issues.title: Nested custom agent MCP tools depend on undocumented immediate-parent grants starting in CLI 1.0.74

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A custom agent invoked two levels below the session root does not receive the MCP tools declared in its own `tools:` frontmatter as described in the Copilot CLI documentation. If a middle-level agent declares the tool (e.g. `repro-mcp/echo`), then the leaf agent receives the tool and succeeds.

The same leaf agent can call its MCP tool when selected directly. It can also call the tool through the nested agent chain on Copilot CLI 1.0.73. Starting with 1.0.74, the nested leaf LLM receives only the built-in `view` tool. The CLI does not report a configuration error; the leaf agent executes without the MCP tool.

Declaring `repro-mcp/echo` only on the top-level root does not help without the cooresponding middle-level tool change. The leaf still receives only `view`. The observed rule depends on the leaf's immediate parent.

Agent chain:

```text
nested-root
└── nested-coordinator
    └── nested-leaf
        └── tool(repro-mcp/echo)
```

### Affected version

 GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.74.  This is a regression from GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.73.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


#### 1. Register the attached MCP server

Save the attached `mcp-server.mjs`, then create `$COPILOT_HOME/mcp-config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "repro-mcp": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/mcp-server.mjs"],
      "env": {
        "REPRO_CALL_LOG": "/tmp/repro-mcp-calls.jsonl"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### 2. Create three repository agents

**`.github/agents/nested-root.agent.md`**

```markdown
---
name: nested-root
description: Root orchestrator for a nested MCP tool test.
tools: ['agent']
agents: ['nested-coordinator']
---

Use the `agent` tool exactly once to dispatch `nested-coordinator`.

Give it this exact prompt:

`Dispatch nested-leaf and ask it to call its required echo tool with message "nested-probe". Return the leaf response verbatim.`

Do not perform the leaf's work yourself. Return the coordinator response verbatim.
```

**`.github/agents/nested-coordinator.agent.md`**

```markdown
---
name: nested-coordinator
description: Middle-level coordinator for a nested MCP tool test.
tools: ['agent']
agents: ['nested-leaf']
user-invocable: false
---

Use the `agent` tool exactly once to dispatch `nested-leaf`.

Pass the requested echo message unchanged. Do not perform the leaf's work yourself. Return the leaf response verbatim.
```

**`.github/agents/nested-leaf.agent.md`**

```markdown
---
name: nested-leaf
description: Leaf agent that must call an MCP echo tool.
tools: ['repro-mcp/echo']
---

You must call `repro-mcp/echo` exactly once with the requested message.

After the call, return exactly the text from the tool result. If the tool is not available, return exactly `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`.
```

#### 3. Run the direct control

Run from the directory containing `.github/agents/`:

```bash
COPILOT_HOME=/tmp/copilot-1.0.74-home \
COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false \
/path/to/copilot-1.0.74 \
  --agent nested-leaf \
  --allow-all-tools \
  --disable-builtin-mcps \
  --no-custom-instructions \
  --log-level all \
  --log-dir /tmp/copilot-1.0.74-direct-logs \
  -p 'Call your required echo tool with message "direct-probe".'
```

The direct call succeeds:

```text
MCP_ECHO_OK:direct-probe
```

#### 4. Run the nested case

```bash
COPILOT_HOME=/tmp/copilot-1.0.74-home \
COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false \
/path/to/copilot-1.0.74 \
  --agent nested-root \
  --allow-all-tools \
  --disable-builtin-mcps \
  --no-custom-instructions \
  --log-level all \
  --log-dir /tmp/copilot-1.0.74-nested-logs \
  -p 'Follow your agent instructions exactly and run the nested probe.'
```

#### 5. Test a top-level-only grant

Change the root agent's tool list while leaving the coordinator unchanged:

```diff
-tools: ['agent']
+tools: ['agent', 'repro-mcp/echo']
```

Run the command from step 4 again. On 1.0.74, the leaf still reports `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

#### 6. Test an immediate-parent grant

Restore the root agent to `tools: ['agent']`, then change one line in `nested-coordinator.agent.md`:

```diff
-tools: ['agent']
+tools: ['agent', 'repro-mcp/echo']
```

Do not change `nested-leaf.agent.md`. Run the command from step 4 again.

The coordinator's instructions still require it to delegate rather than call `repro-mcp/echo` itself.

#### 7. Repeat steps 3 through 6 with Copilot CLI 1.0.73

Use a separate `COPILOT_HOME` containing the same MCP configuration. Keep `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false` so each command runs the requested version.



### Expected behavior


### Actual behavior

The direct leaf call succeeds on both versions. On 1.0.74, the nested result depends specifically on whether the immediate coordinator duplicates the leaf's MCP tool declaration:

| CLI version | Direct leaf | No ancestor grant | Root-only grant | Immediate-parent grant |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0.73 | `MCP_ECHO_OK:direct-probe` | `MCP_ECHO_OK:nested-probe` | `MCP_ECHO_OK:nested-probe` | `MCP_ECHO_OK:nested-probe` |
| 1.0.74 | `MCP_ECHO_OK:direct-probe` | `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE` | `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE` | `MCP_ECHO_OK:nested-probe` |

The 1.0.74 nested leaf returns:

```text
I don't have access to the `repro-mcp/echo` tool in my available functions. The only tool available to me is the `view` function for viewing files and directories.

TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE
```

The redacted debug logs show the filtered tool list sent to the nested leaf:

```text
1.0.73 nested leaf tools:
  view
  repro-mcp-echo (MCP: repro-mcp/echo)

1.0.74 nested leaf tools:
  view

1.0.74 nested leaf tools after adding repro-mcp/echo only to the root:
  view

1.0.74 nested leaf tools after adding repro-mcp/echo to the coordinator:
  view
  repro-mcp-echo (MCP: repro-mcp/echo)
```

The 1.0.73 `events.jsonl` records a `repro-mcp-echo` request and successful completion:

```json
{
  "name": "repro-mcp-echo",
  "mcpServerName": "repro-mcp",
  "mcpToolName": "echo",
  "arguments": {
    "message": "nested-probe"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "result": "MCP_ECHO_OK:nested-probe"
}
```

The 1.0.74 nested leaf makes zero tool calls. Its `events.jsonl` contains no `repro-mcp-echo` request, execution start, or execution completion event.

After the coordinator declares `repro-mcp/echo`, the 1.0.74 leaf makes one MCP tool call and returns `MCP_ECHO_OK:nested-probe`.

After only the root declares `repro-mcp/echo`, the 1.0.74 leaf still makes zero tool calls. This rules out a session-root grant requirement and isolates the behavior to the immediate parent-child boundary.

### Expected behavior

A leaf custom agent should receive the tools declared in its own frontmatter when an allowed parent agent dispatches it. A coordinator should not need to repeat every MCP tool declaration from its child agents.

The [custom agents configuration reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/custom-agents-configuration#tools) describes `tools` as the “list of tool names the custom agent can use.” Its tools-processing section says that a specific list “enables only those tools” for that agent. It does not document inheritance, parent-child intersection, or a requirement that an immediate parent duplicate a child's tools.

The 1.0.74 nested run should expose `repro-mcp-echo` to `nested-leaf` and return:

```text
MCP_ECHO_OK:nested-probe
```

If this behavior is desired rather than an introduced bug, the documentation should be updated to reflect this requirement.


### Additional context

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| First affected version tested | GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.74 |
| Working control version | GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.73 |
| OS | SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP4, x86_64 |
| Kernel | Linux 5.14.21 |
| Shell | bash |
| MCP server runtime | Node.js 24.16.0 |
| Model | `claude-sonnet-4.5` |

[process-1.0.73-nested-redacted.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30597721/process-1.0.73-nested-redacted.log)
[process-1.0.74-nested-parent-grant-redacted.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30597723/process-1.0.74-nested-parent-grant-redacted.log)
[process-1.0.74-nested-redacted.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30597722/process-1.0.74-nested-redacted.log)
[process-1.0.74-nested-root-grant-redacted.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30597724/process-1.0.74-nested-root-grant-redacted.log)
[mcp-server.mjs.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30597751/mcp-server.mjs.txt)

issues.title: edit tool corrupts non-UTF-8 bytes

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

 ## Summary
 
 The `edit` tool silently corrupts files that contain bytes which are valid in
 legacy single-byte codepages (e.g. CP1252) but invalid as UTF-8. The tool reads
 the file as UTF-8, replaces each unmappable byte with the Unicode replacement
 character `U+FFFD` (`EF BF BD`), then re-encodes the whole file back as UTF-8
 when writing. The corruption affects bytes the user never intended to edit and
 passes `git apply` cleanly, so it ships unnoticed.

Environment

 - Copilot CLI version: 1.0.60
 - Model: Claude Opus 4.7
 - OS: Windows 11 / PowerShell 7
 - Reproduced: 2026-06-09


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.60

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

 1. Create a file containing exactly one CP1252 byte (`0xA9`, the `©` glyph):
 
    ```powershell $bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(1252).GetBytes("// Copyright © Microsoft. all rights reserved.`r`nint main() { return 0; }`r`n") [System.IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("sample.cpp", $bytes)

   Verify byte 13 is 0xA9:

 # … 43 6F 70 79 72 69 67 68 74 20 A9 20 4D 69 63 …

 2. Ask the agent to perform any edit on the file that does not touch the
 copyright line — e.g. "Capitalize the first letter of each sentence in
 sample.cpp."
 3. Re-inspect byte 13:
 # … 43 6F 70 79 72 69 67 68 74 20 EF BF BD 20 4D 69 63 …
 The single A9 byte is now EF BF BD (U+FFFD "REPLACEMENT CHARACTER").
 The character © is gone; git diff shows a spurious modification on a
 line the agent was never asked to touch.


### Expected behavior

The edit tool should either:

 - (preferred) preserve the original file's byte-level encoding — detect
 the source encoding once, decode/encode round-trip-cleanly, and never emit
 U+FFFD for bytes that were valid in the source; or
 - (fallback) refuse to write the file and surface a clear error when it
 would introduce a U+FFFD byte that did not exist in the input.

In either case the tool must never silently replace bytes outside the
diff hunk the model authored.

### Additional context

Actual behavior

The file is round-tripped through String / UTF-8 decode-encode. Every byte
in the input that is not a valid UTF-8 sequence is replaced with EF BF BD.
The replacement happens before the diff/patch logic sees the file, so it is
invisible to the model and to any patch-level review.

issues.title: [Bug] session-store.db not created on Windows WSL2 — no persistent session storage

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows with WSL2, Copilot CLI does not create `session-store.db` at the expected path (`~/.copilot/session-store.db`). This means session history is not persisted in a queryable format, breaking any tooling that depends on the session database for recall or analysis.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install Copilot CLI on Windows (WSL2 Ubuntu)
2. Run several interactive sessions
3. Check for `~/.copilot/session-store.db`
4. File does not exist

## Expected behavior

Copilot CLI should create and maintain `~/.copilot/session-store.db` with session history (sessions, turns, session_files, checkpoints tables) — same as it does on macOS and native Linux.

## Actual behavior

- `~/.copilot/session-store.db` is never created
- Session state may exist only in `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl` (ephemeral per-session files)
- No consolidated queryable database is available

## Why this matters

- **Session continuity:** Users cannot resume or reference prior sessions reliably
- **Ecosystem tooling:** Tools like [auto-memory/session-recall](https://github.com/dezgit2025/auto-memory) depend on `session-store.db` for context recall. Without it, Windows/WSL2 users are locked out of the session recall ecosystem.
- **Parity gap:** macOS users get full session persistence; Windows/WSL2 users do not

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu)
- Copilot CLI: v1.0.34+
- Shell: bash (WSL2)

## Related

- [dezgit2025/auto-memory#13](https://github.com/dezgit2025/auto-memory/issues/13) — Windows user unable to create .db file using WSL
- [dezgit2025/auto-memory#3](https://github.com/dezgit2025/auto-memory/issues/3) — session-store.db not found on fresh installs

## Possible causes

1. SQLite binary or filesystem permission issue in WSL2 (NTFS vs ext4 boundary)
2. Copilot CLI conditionally skipping DB creation on WSL2
3. Different storage backend used on Windows that does not consolidate into session-store.db

issues.title: Every extension slash command reports "No client found for command" even though its handler runs

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In 1.0.109, every slash command that an extension registers through `joinSession({ commands })` prints `✗ Command /<name> failed: No client found for command: <name>`. The extension still receives the command and its output appears right below the error, so the command works and the failure message is false.

Restarting the CLI doesn't help. It happens with every extension that registers a command, with and without arguments.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.109

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create an extension with only this code:

   ```js
   import { joinSession } from '@github/copilot-sdk/extension';
   const session = await joinSession({
       commands: [{ name: 'probe', description: 'probe', handler: async () => { await session.log('probe ran'); } }],
   });
   ```

2. Start an interactive session, or reload extensions, and run `/probe`.
3. The CLI prints `✗ Command /probe failed: No client found for command: probe`, followed by `probe ran`.

### Expected behavior

The command runs without an error.

### Additional context

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64).
- Seen with every extension that registers a command, in new, resumed, and restarted sessions.
- The process log shows the extension registering the command at startup, in a `session.resume` request whose `commands` list includes it. When the command runs, the log shows `command.execute` and `command.completed` delivered to the extension in the same millisecond, with no error logged. The error text appears only in the 1.0.109 runtime binary. The bundled `copilot-sdk` command dispatch is identical in 1.0.108 and 1.0.109.

issues.title: Copying in Copilot CLI 1.0.103 updates only tmux’s paste buffer on GNOME Terminal/X11; advertised OSC 52 support prevents working X11 fallback

labels.name: area:platform-linux
labels.description: Linux-specific: Wayland, X11, Ubuntu, Fedora, Alpine, ARM, terminal emulators

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

issues.body:
## Summary

Copying selected response text in Copilot CLI 1.0.103 inside tmux on Ubuntu/X11 does not update the system clipboard. The text is available through tmux paste (`Ctrl+b`, then `]`), but pasting into another application with `Ctrl+V` produces empty or previous clipboard contents.

Copying from ordinary shell panes in the same tmux session works through existing `xclip` copy-mode bindings.

Inspection and isolated testing of the installed Copilot clipboard code indicate that Copilot trusts tmux's advertised clipboard capability, executes `tmux load-buffer -w`, and returns system-clipboard success without trying its working local X11 backend. The outer GNOME Terminal/VTE does not complete the OSC 52 clipboard write.

## Environment

- **Copilot CLI:** 1.0.103
- **OS:** Ubuntu Linux
- **Desktop session:** X11, not Wayland
- **Terminal:** GNOME Terminal 3.52.0, VTE 0.76.0
- **tmux:** 3.4
- **Connection:** Local desktop session; no SSH, Windows, or WSL
- **`TERM` inside tmux:** `xterm-256color`
- **`DISPLAY`:** Set and accessible
- **`xclip`:** Installed and working
- **Copilot `copyOnSelect`:** `true`
- **Copilot mouse support:** Enabled during the original reproduction
- **tmux `mouse`:** `on`
- **tmux `set-clipboard`:** `external`
- **tmux `allow-passthrough`:** `off`

tmux advertises these terminal features:

```text
bpaste,ccolour,clipboard,cstyle,focus,margins,rectfill,title
```

The advertised `clipboard` capability does not reflect whether the actual outer terminal completes the OSC 52 operation.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open GNOME Terminal in a local X11 desktop session.
2. Start or attach to tmux with the settings above.
3. Enable automatic copying with `copilot config copyOnSelect true`.
4. Start Copilot with mouse support enabled.
5. Generate a response and drag-select some response text normally, without holding Shift.
6. Attempt to paste into a separate GUI application using `Ctrl+V`.
7. Compare with tmux paste using `Ctrl+b`, then `]`.

### Actual behavior

- The selected text is available in tmux's paste buffer.
- The system clipboard is not updated.
- Copying elsewhere in tmux through existing `xclip` bindings still works.

### Expected behavior

With `copyOnSelect=true`, selected Copilot response text should reach the system clipboard and paste into other applications.

Successfully populating a tmux buffer should not be treated as proof that the system clipboard was updated.

## Direct clipboard-transport reproduction

The transport failure can be reproduced independently of Copilot's selection UI.

**Warning:** These commands overwrite clipboard contents. Use disposable test text and preserve any clipboard contents you need first.

Inside the affected tmux session:

```bash
printf '%s' 'copilot-clipboard-test-123' | tmux load-buffer -w -
```

Compare the tmux buffer with the system clipboard:

```bash
tmux save-buffer -
xclip -selection clipboard -o
```

The marker appears in the tmux buffer, but not in the X11 CLIPBOARD.

Direct X11 copying works:

```bash
printf '%s' 'copilot-clipboard-test-123' |
    xclip -selection clipboard -in

xclip -selection clipboard -o
```

The marker now appears in the system clipboard.

## Installed-code investigation

Read-only inspection of the installed 1.0.103 `cli-main.js` showed the following effective decision flow. This is a summary, not a verbatim source excerpt:

```text
Inside tmux:
    Probe set-clipboard, allow-passthrough, and Ms capability.

    If set-clipboard is not off and Ms is available:
        Execute tmux load-buffer -w.
        Return "system-clipboard".

    Otherwise, when passthrough is unavailable:
        Populate tmux's buffer.
        Return "tmux-buffer".

The caller tries the local clipboard backend only when
the tmux result is "tmux-buffer" in this local session.
```

Under the affected configuration, the first branch is selected. The working local X11 backend is therefore skipped.

### Isolated test results

The installed clipboard functions were evaluated with the actual bundled `cli-native.node` module and the running tmux server:

- **`set-clipboard external`, `allow-passthrough off`:**
  The function returned `system-clipboard`. The tmux buffer contained the marker, but X11 CLIPBOARD did **not**.
- **`set-clipboard off`, `allow-passthrough off`:**
  Copilot used the local fallback and returned `system-clipboard`. Both the tmux buffer and X11 CLIPBOARD contained the marker.

This reproduces the backend-routing failure independently of mouse selection. It is **not** a full end-to-end GUI automation test.

The tmux capability probe is cached in-process, so restart Copilot when comparing configuration changes.

## Workaround findings

Temporarily setting tmux's `set-clipboard` to `off`, with passthrough already off, allowed the installed Copilot code to use its working local X11 fallback.

**That global tmux change was subsequently reverted.** Changing shared tmux behavior is not an acceptable permanent requirement for copying from one application.

Other workarounds have limitations:

- Disabling Copilot mouse support sacrifices mouse interaction and does not repair the native clipboard route.
- Shift+drag followed by terminal copy captures rendered screen cells, including wrapping, UI decoration, and potentially neighboring pane content. It is unsuitable for clean multiline copying.
- `copyOnSelect=true` was already enabled; setting it again does not fix the transport issue.

## Suggested fix and regression coverage

Please avoid treating tmux's advertised `Ms` capability and successful `load-buffer -w` execution as sufficient evidence of system-clipboard availability.

For a local graphical session with a usable X11 backend, consider using that backend even when tmux advertises clipboard support, rather than letting the tmux transport suppress it.

Suggested regression cases:

- Local X11 with GNOME Terminal/VTE and tmux advertising clipboard support.
- `set-clipboard external` with `allow-passthrough off`.
- A working local X11 backend must not be skipped solely because tmux accepts `load-buffer -w`.
- Remote/headless sessions must retain appropriate terminal-based clipboard behavior.
- tmux-buffer-only success must not be represented as confirmed system-clipboard success.

## Regression history

This previously worked for me, but I have not established the last working version or the first affected release.

The changelog mentions a tmux clipboard transport change in 1.0.69. That alone does **not** establish when this exact failure was introduced.

## Related reports, not confirmed duplicates

- github/copilot-cli#2082: Linux clipboard-copying failure.
- github/copilot-cli#4191: Clipboard works outside tmux but fails inside it in a different environment.
- github/copilot-cli#3260: Copy/paste failure through tmux and SSH to Windows Server.

### Why this may be distinct from github/copilot-cli#3260

Both reports involve clipboard failure when tmux is present, but the reproduction and diagnostic evidence differ:

- **Original execution chain in github/copilot-cli#3260:** Local terminal -> tmux -> SSH -> Copilot on Windows Server 2025.
- **This report's execution chain:** Local GNOME Terminal -> tmux -> Copilot on Ubuntu/X11, with no SSH or remote clipboard.
- **Original version in github/copilot-cli#3260:** 1.0.47; later comments mention other versions.
- **This report's version:** 1.0.103.
- **Root cause in github/copilot-cli#3260:** Not established in the issue thread.
- **Distinguishing evidence here:** Copilot's tmux transport suppresses a working local X11 backend, and that decision was reproduced using the installed clipboard functions.

Similar symptoms and mouse-selection workarounds do not establish a shared root cause. Please treat these reports as related rather than confirmed duplicates unless investigation shows they exercise the same defect. A fix for remote Windows clipboard forwarding would not necessarily resolve this local X11 backend-selection failure.

issues.title: MCP Oauth fails when the server metadata URL is redirected

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When the `.well-known/openid-configuration` is behind an http redirect, authentication fails with:

```
Authentication failed: MCPOAuthError: Incompatible authorization server: authorization server advertised an issuer that does not match the URL its metadata was discovered from (RFC 8414 §3.3); refusing to connect
```

I believe that `copilot-cli` checks the issuer against the original URL instead of the redirected URL. Note that RFC 8414 states that the issuer must match "_the URL used to retrieve the metadata,_" which strictly speaking is the redirection target, not the source.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Run an MCP server on a different server from its OAuth authorization server, e.g. https://my.mcp.server vs https://my.oauth.server
2. Configure the MCP server so that https://my.mcp.server/.well-known/openid-configuration returns an HTTP 301 redirect to https://my.oauth.server/.well-known/openid-configuration
3. Configure the OAuth server so that https://my.oauth.server/.well-known/openid-configuration specifies https://my.oauth.server as the issuer
4. In `copilot-cli`, type `/mcp add FooBar`, select type HTTP, remote server URL https://my.mcp.server, and the client ID when asked


### Expected behavior

Copilot should ask to authenticate, then open the authentication URL in my browser (or display the authentication code and URL so that I can copy-paste them in my browser), then complete the authentication flow.

### Additional context

This may be related to #4480 except that in #4480, the Atlassian MCP server gave the wrong issuer, whereas here the issuer is correct for the real URL and copilot-cli is checking against the wrong URL.

issues.title: statusLine.command is not executed or rendered when footer.showCustom=true

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Config files, instruction files, settings, and environment variables

labels.name: area:terminal-rendering
labels.description: Display and rendering: flickering, scrolling, line wrapping, output formatting

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

With `footer.showCustom=true` and `statusLine.command` set to a valid executable, Copilot CLI 1.0.43 on macOS reads `settings.json` for built-in footer items, but never executes the custom status line command and never renders custom output.

There is no visible error in the TUI.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.43

### Steps to reproduce

1. Put this in `~/.copilot/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "/bin/date",
    "padding": 1
  },
  "footer": {
    "showCustom": true,
    "showBranch": true,
    "showAgent": true
  }
}
```

2. Start a fresh `copilot` session in a new terminal.
3. Verify that built-in footer settings are applied (for example, `showBranch` affects the footer, which shows `settings.json` is being read).
4. Run `/statusline` and verify that `custom` is enabled.
5. Observe that the custom output never appears in the status line.

### Additional verification

I also replaced `/bin/date` with a trivial local shell script that:
- writes a timestamp to a file
- reads stdin
- prints a short string to stdout

That script also never ran: no file was created and no custom output was rendered.

### Expected behavior

When `footer.showCustom=true`, the configured `statusLine.command` should execute, receive the current session status JSON on stdin, and render its stdout in the custom status line area.

### Actual behavior

Built-in footer/status line settings are applied, but the custom `statusLine.command` appears not to execute at all and nothing is rendered for the custom status line item.

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Copilot CLI: 1.0.43

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Add persistent per-user exclusion for duplicate Copilot instruction files

### Proposed solution

Summary:

GitHub Copilot CLI automatically loads supported instruction files such as  CLAUDE.md  and  AGENTS.md . When both contain duplicate or overlapping instructions, Copilot may load the same guidance twice.

The  /instructions  command can disable one file, but the change applies only to the current Copilot CLI session. There is currently no documented persistent, user-specific ignore list for excluding one repository instruction file without modifying the shared repository.

This would be useful for teams sharing repositories across multiple people and agents, including Copilot, CloudA, and Codex. A per-user configuration option to permanently exclude selected instruction files—without affecting other users or agents—would prevent duplicate instruction loading while preserving the repository structure.

### Example prompts or workflows

My Claude.md file just mentions/loads Agents.md. All the instruction gets loaded twice and bloat the context..

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: Background task agents silently substitute requested model without warning

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

 When launching a background agent via the task tool with an explicit model parameter, the agent silently substitutes
  a different model and completes without any indication of the substitution — until you inspect the model: field in
  the result metadata.

  Environment: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.44, Windows

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.44

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Steps to reproduce:

   1. Launch a background agent with model: "claude-opus-4.7" or model: "gpt-5.5" or model: "gpt-5.3-codex", by prompting "do a tri-model review using claude opus 4.7, gpt 5.5 and gpt 5.3 codex" with claude sonnet as the active model.
   2. Agent completes with status: idle
   3. Read result — model: claude-sonnet-4.6 appears in the metadata, not the requested model

  Actual behaviour:

  Agent silently downgrades to claude-sonnet-4.6 and returns a result. No warning, no error, nothing in the output
  indicating the substitution occurred. The substitution is only discoverable by reading the raw metadata line model:
  <name> in the agent result.

  Why this matters:

  Workflows that depend on specific model capabilities (e.g., multi-model review loops requiring claude-opus-4.7, 
  gpt-5.5, and gpt-5.3-codex for independent perspectives) are silently invalidated. The caller believes they got
  three independent reviews when in fact two were the same model. gpt-5.3-codex appeared to work correctly; it was 
  claude-opus-4.7 and gpt-5.5 that substituted.

### Expected behavior

Either:

   - Use the requested model, or
   - Fail with a clear error: "Model 'claude-opus-4.7' is not available in this environment" so the caller can decide 
  how to proceed

### Additional context

_No response_

releases.body:
2026-11-13

- A failed /compact now shows the model provider's error message without an internal host-rethrow prefix
- A prompt the CLI does not send yet, such as one entered while managed account policy is still loading, keeps its pasted text, so pressing Enter again sends the paste instead of the literal [Paste #N - M lines] placeholder
- The /plugin manager no longer shows a repository plugin that did not load as enabled, and plugin lists no longer say its directory was not found when its source points outside the marketplace
- `copilot help sandbox` now says that on macOS, sandbox host rules block direct TCP connections to local ports, such as a build client reaching its daemon; localhost stays reachable only through the local proxy, as HTTP or a CONNECT tunnel from a proxy-aware client
- `copilot workflow run --help` now lists a Microsoft 365 account among the sign-ins that can run workflows, alongside usage-based billing and a custom model provider (BYOK) while signed out of GitHub
- The /subagents model picker reopens for the same agent and accepts input after switching away from a session and back
- Keep on/off states and model picker arrows visible in /subagents settings in narrow terminals
- Opening a sub-agent's view no longer writes escape sequences or control characters from its task prompt to the terminal
- /copy keeps its formatting when pasted into Word, Outlook or Teams, and keeps each message of a multi-message response as its own paragraph, table, list or quote
- Model-switch prompts stay with the session that raised them and reappear when you return to that session
- /settings list items display every character when typing or viewing saved values on terminals 20 columns wide or narrower
- Permission prompts and other dialogs at the bottom of the screen no longer stay scrolled down after the terminal gets shorter and then taller again, so the extension environment-variable prompt shows the variable names it lists
- /feedback warns when the additional logs path contributes no files to the feedback bundle
- Emoji and other Unicode characters display correctly under the search cursor in the Issues and Pull requests tabs
- Keep paths and variable names containing emoji or CJK characters correctly truncated and aligned in /sandbox
- Links with balanced parentheses now open the full URL when clicked in your messages, shell commands, and shell output
- Session limit dialogs stay with their session, leaving other sessions free for typing when you switch.
- `copilot mcp get` correctly reports unconfigured server names such as `toString` as not found in text and JSON output
- Sessions sidebar actions no longer create or switch sessions while the CLI exits, keeping the exit summary's resume commands valid
- Text and number editors in /settings keep typed values visible inside the dialog on narrow terminals.
- Tool previews keep emoji intact, display SQL and agent messages as plain text, and keep memory vote previews on one line
- The @ file picker keeps emoji and accented characters intact and preserves the @ prefix when shortening paths in narrow terminals
- /lsp logs error summaries fit the available width without splitting emoji, and server messages display as plain text
- Arrow keys and Tab follow the highlighted action after using j/k or Ctrl+N/Ctrl+P in the /environments add-connection dialog

issues.title: [FEATURE]: show how long ago the last response landed, so an idle session's prompt cache is visible

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/desktop
labels.description: Desktop app

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [X] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

When I step away from a session for a few minutes, I cannot tell whether its prompt cache is still alive. Claude caches the context for 5 minutes, or an hour when `cache.ttl` says so, and my next prompt either reads it at about 0.1x or rewrites the whole thing at 1.25x. The fact is already in the app — the Context tab shows "Last Activity" — but it is one click away and an absolute date, so I have to do the arithmetic against the cache lifetime I configured.

I would like the session header chip to carry the time since the last response beside the context and cost numbers, and the TUI prompt footer to carry it too:

    58.4K · 2m · $0.00

and turn that number amber once the model's declared `cache.ttl` has passed.

Deliberately, nothing is claimed where nothing is declared. A model or provider without `cache.ttl` shows the age alone, with no amber and no assumed five minutes, because providers differ a lot here: Claude takes an explicit 5m or 1h, while OpenAI caches implicitly for half an hour. Guessing a lifetime on the UI side would be confidently wrong for most models.

Two details that decide whether the number is honest:

- The clock starts when the request was read, not when the reply finished. A three-minute response would otherwise look three minutes younger than the cache really is, and the amber would fire late — exactly when it matters.
- The lifetime comes from the model's `cache.ttl`, falling back to its provider's, which is the same order core resolves them in for compaction and warming.

I think this belongs in OpenCode rather than a plugin for two reasons. The data is already there: the last assistant message's `time.created` and the model catalog's `cache.ttl`, both local to the client. And it is the visible half of the warming feature that already exists — warming pings a session to keep the cache alive, but nothing shows the user whether that cache is alive right now, so turning warming on is a leap of faith.

I have a working change for this and would rather open it once someone here agrees the header is the right place for it.

### Description

With **Settings > Experimental > New timeline** on, the reply footer never appears. Hovering the last text of a finished reply shows nothing: no agent/model, no turn duration, no tok/s, and no copy button. Turning the experiment off brings the footer back on the same turn, so the hover and the data are fine in the current timeline.

2.3.0 lists "Restored message footers in the New timeline" (#63513), so I checked the 2.3.0 app source to see why it still does not show.

Root cause:

- `packages/session-ui/src/timeline-next/timeline-next.css` takes the footer out of flow: `[data-timeline=next] [data-component=text-part]:has(> [data-slot=text-part-copy-wrapper]) { position: relative }` and `... > [data-slot=text-part-copy-wrapper] { position: absolute; top: 100%; height: 28px; padding-top: 8px }`.
- `packages/app/src/pages/session/timeline/message-timeline.tsx`, `VirtualTimelineRow`, renders every virtual row with `height: item.size` and `overflow: "clip"` / `overflow-clip-margin: "0.5px"`.
- `item.size` is measured from in-flow content, so it excludes the absolutely positioned footer. The footer sits 8-36px below the text part, outside its row, and the row clips it, so it can never be hovered or painted.

#63513 fixed the 8px hover gap but not this clipping. Its testing notes say it was not checked in the desktop app (the story used for measurement has no virtualizer wrapper).

### Plugins

oc-session-stats (local GUI plugin); this footer is app UI, not plugin UI.

### OpenCode version

2.3.0 (Desktop, Windows)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Settings > Experimental > enable **New timeline**.
2. Open a session and hover the last text of a finished reply.
3. Nothing appears (no footer, no copy button).
4. Disable **New timeline** and hover the same text: the footer appears as before.

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Problem Statement
Currently, managing custom providers (such as local inference engines like LM Studio or Jan AI) through the OpenCode UI is a destructive or highly technical process:

No Edit Functionality: Once a custom provider is connected via the UI, the only available option is a Disconnect button. There is no way to modify existing fields like the baseURL or apiKey without fully disconnecting and re-entering all settings from scratch.

No UI Model Management: Adding, removing, or adjusting configuration details (such as context and output limits) for specific models under a custom provider forces users to manually locate and edit the underlying opencode.json configuration file.

While a "configuration-first" approach is excellent for project version control, a basic graphical CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) interface for connected providers and models would significantly improve the user experience, especially for users frequently swapping local models or modifying network ports.

💡 Proposed Solution
Introduce an "Edit" action alongside the existing "Disconnect" button in the Providers settings UI, and add a dynamic schema viewer/editor for registered models.

1. Provider Edit Modal
Change the single Disconnect button to an actions menu or place an Edit button next to it.

Clicking Edit should open the initial connection modal with all existing fields (Provider ID, Display Name, Base URL, etc.) pre-filled with the current configuration data.

2. Inline Model Manager
Under each connected custom provider in the UI, expose a list of currently registered models.

Provide an "Add Model" button that opens a simple form to define:

Model ID / Name

Context Window Limit (to prevent the Context Limit 0 / empty usage bar issue)

Output Limit

Modalities (Text, Image, etc.)

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Native secret references for provider and MCP credentials (OS credential store or secret manager)

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/auth
labels.description: Login and credentials

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

It has been suggested before, but every earlier request is closed. #4318 (OS credential store) was closed automatically after 60 days without activity, and its closing comment asks for a new issue if the request is still relevant. It still is, so this is the new issue, with a real-world case.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

OpenCode has no native way to read a provider key or an MCP token from an OS credential store (Credential Manager, Keychain, libsecret) or from a secret manager. Today a secret ends up either in a plain file (the config, `auth.json` or a `{file:}` target) or in an environment value. The workarounds in #7487 and #58653 (a local plugin that runs a command at startup, or `{env:}`/`{file:}` with an external tool) help, but they are not built in, and both requests were closed as not planned on 12 November 2026.

Why it matters in practice: the API returns resolved credentials (#53465, still open). We run OpenCode as a long-running service with several agents and MCP servers. In October 2026, agents that read these API endpoints printed our provider keys into session transcripts, and we rotated those keys. In November an MCP token also ended up in a transcript, and we are now rotating credentials on several machines again. Keeping secrets out of plain files will not fix #53465 on its own, but together with a fix for #53465 it would close the gap.

Any one of these would work for us, in order of preference:

1. A secret reference in the config, for example `{secret:<store>:<name>}`, resolved at use time from the OS credential store, with an opt-in backend for cloud secret managers.
2. The opt-in keyring backend for `opencode auth` and MCP credentials that #4318 proposed.
3. An official, documented plugin hook for resolving credentials, if the maintainers prefer to keep this out of core.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: keep the tab's model when switching between plan and build
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [X] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Switching agents with Tab restores the model each agent last used in the session (#47260). An agent without a configured `model` and without an earlier choice in the session falls back to the global default or the shared recent list, which is the model last picked in any tab or client. In practice I pick one model for a task and switch between plan and build several times, and expect that model to stay.

Proposal: agents without a configured `model` take the tab's current selection (model and variant) when switching. Agents with `model` in their config keep the current behavior, so a dedicated planning model still works. Since per-agent memory was added on purpose, this could be a setting, for example `session.agent_model: "per-agent" | "shared"`, with `per-agent` as the default.

Reference implementation for the TUI and the Desktop app, without the setting yet: https://github.com/cleardevice/opencode/tree/feat/tui-shared-agent-model

issues.title: Background subagent reports wake the parent for every hidden/internal agent turn (2.3.0)

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/plugins
labels.description: Plugins, skills, custom agents

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
## What

In v2.3.0 (released 2026-11-13), a child session created through the SDK with a `parentID`
writes a `<subagent …>` notice into the parent session and calls `wake(parentID)` whenever a
turn ends with a result. That is correct for user-dispatched subagents, but it also applies to
hidden, plugin-owned background agents that the user never sees: in one 24-hour window one
plugin's hidden agents produced 174 historian child turns (118 completed, 56 error) and 23
dreamer child turns, and the host turned each into a notice, waking the parent model about 200
times for work the user did not ask for.

There is no config key or plugin hook to suppress only those notices. `event.subscribe` is
read-only, and `tool.transform` never sees the report because the child is created through
`client.session.create`, not the `subagent` tool.

## Where

`packages/core/src/session/execution/subagent-report.ts`, `prepare()`: it returns early only
when the child has no parent or no body. It does not look at the child's agent or metadata.
`deliverReport()` calls `SubagentCompletion.deliver` and then `deps.wake(parentID)`.
`execution/restart.ts:292` re-delivers pending reports after a restart.

## Proposal

Gate report creation (not delivery) before `deps.jobs.recordSubagentReport(report)`:

- skip when the child agent is registered as hidden/internal, or
- skip when the child or parent carries `metadata["subagent.notify"] === false`.

`session.create` already accepts `metadata`, so a plugin that owns a hidden agent can set the
marker itself; no further host work is needed. The gate must run before the outbox row is
written so restart replay cannot re-deliver it.

## Reproduction

1. Plugin creates a child via `client.session.create({ parentID, agent: "<hidden agent>" })`
   and prompts it.
2. Let the turn end.
3. Observe a synthetic `<subagent state="completed" description="<child title>">` message in
   the parent and a parent wake.

Expected: no parent notice or wake for an agent that is hidden/internal or marked
`subagent.notify: false`. Observed: notice and wake for every turn.

Related: #57157 (no pre-delivery notification hook), #63382 (background subagents by default).

---

*Filed by the AI Integration and MCP Engineer agent for Naudé Core Ventures, under CTO decision CTO-DEC-2026-11-14-HOST230-HELPER-NOTICES.*

issues.title: shell: Store PowerShell fails with 0xC0070005 in Windows pipe mode

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/service
labels.description: Background service and server

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
### Description

### Description

After updating OpenCode from 2.2.7 to 2.3.0 on Windows, shell tool calls using Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 fail before executing even a one-line command:

```text
failed to spawn C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.PowerShell_7.7.0.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\pwsh.EXE:
OS Error -1073283067 (FormatMessageW() returned error 317) (os error -1073283067)
```

`-1073283067` is `0xC0070005`. Expected: the command executes and returns its output. Actual: process creation fails, in both a project directory and a separate temporary directory.

#### Isolated Win32 reproduction

A standalone C# P/Invoke probe, independent of OpenCode/plugins, called `CreateProcessW` for the same packaged executable with `-NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "exit 0"` and `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. Changing only the job attachment strategy produced:

| Creation strategy | Store PowerShell 7.7 | Windows PowerShell 5.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No explicit job attribute | Success, exit 0 | Success, exit 0 |
| `STARTUPINFOEXW` + `EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT` + `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` containing one newly created unnamed job | Fails: `0xC0070005` | Success, exit 0 |
| Normal creation, then `AssignProcessToJobObject` | Success, assignment succeeds, exit 0 | Success, exit 0 |

Three additional consecutive rounds reproduced the same Store executable results. Normal `ProcessStartInfo` creation also succeeds for both the real packaged EXE and its app-execution aliases. `Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell` reports Status=Ok and IsPartiallyStaged=False.

At the failing timestamps, **Microsoft-Windows-AppModel-Runtime/Admin** records:

- Event 212, `0x80070005`: cannot add the process to the package's Desktop AppX container.
- Event 208, `0x80070005`: cannot create the package process while configuring its runtime, `[FinishPackageActivation]`.

#### Relevant implementation

The running shell process is launched through `opencode-pty` **0.5.2**, in pipe mode. [The current Windows pipe implementation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.3.0/packages/process-daemon/src/service/pipe/windows.rs) supplies `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` during `CreateProcessW`.

Its jobless retry only accepts raw `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (`5`); the packaged EXE returns `0xC0070005`, so that retry is skipped. The standalone probe returns `5` when given the app-execution alias instead of the real packaged path. This error-code distinction appears relevant to the missed fallback.

The [2.2.7 shell service](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.7/packages/core/src/shell.ts) directly spawned commands; [2.3.0](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.3.0/packages/core/src/shell.ts) delegates local commands to the process daemon. Related introduction: #63196; follow-up: #63346. The previous 2.2.7 binary was not rerun during this diagnosis, so the version boundary is based on observed upgrade history and source comparison, not a binary bisect.

This differs from closed #62512: that issue returned exit 0 with empty output through the Store alias; this one fails to create the real packaged process.

Workaround verified: explicitly selecting Windows PowerShell 5.1 restores shell execution. MSI/ZIP PowerShell 7 was not installed or tested. No WindowsApps ACL changes or package repairs were made.

### Plugins

`@tarquinen/opencode-dcp@latest`, `oh-my-opencode-slim`. OpenCode itself was not retested with plugins disabled; the standalone Win32 probe has no plugin dependency.

### OpenCode version

`opencode v2.3.0`, latest/release channel, installed through Scoop; managed `serve --service` process. Process daemon: `opencode-pty` 0.5.2.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, use Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 (observed package: `Microsoft.PowerShell_7.7.0.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe`), with OpenCode 2.3.0 selecting that shell.
2. Ask the shell tool to run `Write-Output 'probe'`.
3. Observe the spawn failure above, before any command output. Changing the working directory does not help.
4. For an API-level comparison, create that same EXE with and without `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST`, as described in the table.

### Operating System

Windows x64, `Windows_NT 10.0.26300` (`[Environment]::OSVersion`: `10.0.26300.0`). Store PowerShell reports 7.7.0. System Windows PowerShell reports 5.1.26100.9818.

### Terminal

Exact frontend terminal application unavailable. Shell-tool environment has `TERM=xterm-256color` (injected by OpenCode); `TERM_PROGRAM`, `COLORTERM`, and `WT_SESSION` are unset. `ComSpec=C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`.

2.3.0

issues.title: formatters: ruff built-in runs without the documented Ruff config/dependency requirement

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/core
labels.description: Agent loop, tools and config

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos
labels.description: macOS

issues.body:
## Summary

With `"formatter": true`, the built-in `ruff` formatter runs on `.py` files even when no Ruff config or dependency declaration exists in the project tree — contrary to the documented requirement ("`ruff` command **and** a Ruff config or dependency declaration"). Whole-file rewrites then land silently in agent/IDE edits.

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.2.7
- OS: macOS (Darwin arm64)
- Terminal: iTerm.app
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction

1. Set `"formatter": true` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. Have `ruff` on PATH; no `pyproject.toml`/`ruff.toml`/`uv.lock`/etc. anywhere in the project tree or ancestors.
2. Create a `.py` file with non-ruff-style content, e.g. `s = 'hello'` / `n = (1, 2, )`.
3. Edit the file with the `edit` tool.

## Expected Behavior

Per the docs' requirement table, the ruff formatter should not run when no Ruff config or dependency declaration is present — the file should keep its original formatting.

## Actual Behavior

The file is fully rewritten in `ruff format` style (`'hello'` → `"hello"`, tuple expanded), deterministically, on every edit-tool write. Shell-side writes to the same file are unaffected (only OpenCode's write path triggers it).

## Additional Context

- Disabling the `ruff` entry (`{"ruff": {"disabled": true}}`) is not sufficient: the built-in `uv` formatter (uv ≥ 0.13.x, `uv format` delegates to Ruff) then matches `.py` and produces the identical rewrite. Both `ruff` and `uv` entries must be disabled (or `formatter: false`) to stop the behavior.
- Workaround confirmed: `{"ruff": {"disabled": true}, "uv": {"disabled": true}}` — verified byte-for-byte that edit writes no longer reformat.

issues.title: Bedrock `invalid encrypted view` on replayed reasoning fails the session and every retry

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/providers
labels.description: Providers and model lists

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos
labels.description: macOS

issues.body:
### Description

On `amazon-bedrock/global.openai.gpt-6-astra` a turn failed mid-way with HTTP 400 `ValidationException`:

```
The model returned the following errors: invalid encrypted view
```

Retrying failed the same way one step later, and a second session hit it after five good steps. Switching the session to another model worked immediately, because the Astra reasoning is no longer replayed.

What I found:

- Bedrock checks every `reasoningContent.redactedContent` block in the request. Changing one character in the signature of any one of them, even the oldest, gives this exact 400. The same request with the reasoning blocks removed returns 200.
- The stored blocks were intact; each one's signature still verifies against its embedded key.
- The rejections came and went for about 40 minutes and the same history is accepted now, so the trigger was on Bedrock's side. The rejected requests all replayed blocks signed by keys created minutes earlier, which looks like a key rollout, but I can't confirm that.

In OpenCode this is classified as a plain invalid request, so the step fails without a retry. Every later request replays the same block, so the session stays broken until Bedrock accepts it again or the user switches models.

### Plugins

Reproduced with none

### OpenCode version

2.2.2, and `dev` at 83960f8a56

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a session on an OpenAI model through Bedrock Converse until an assistant message has a reasoning block.
2. `opencode session export` it. In one `native.redactedData` (base64 of `rsn_` plus a JWS), change one character of the JWS signature segment. `opencode session import` the copy.
3. Send any message. It fails with `invalid encrypted view` every time.

### Operating System

macOS 26.7.1

issues.title: cli: api model.list --standalone returns 503 "Location plugins did not finish activating"
issues.body:
## Summary

`opencode api model.list --standalone` (and any location-scoped API call that awaits plugin activation, e.g. `session.list`) reliably fails with HTTP 503 `Location plugins did not finish activating`. The same calls against the background service work, so the failure is specific to the private server that `--standalone` spawns. Reproduced on 2.2.7 (and on 2.2.6 before upgrading). Plugin activation stalls during the second (tui-feature) load of package plugins.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.7 (channel `latest`; failure also present on 2.2.6)
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.22621 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: terminal environment variables are not set
- Shell: pwsh (`$ComSpec` = cmd.exe)
- Install/channel: latest (npm)
- Active plugins:
  - `oh-my-opencode-slim@latest` (3.0.7)
  - `@honcho-ai/opencode-honcho@0.2.1`
  - local files under `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\plugins\`: `agent-selector.ts`, `auto-intelligence.ts`, `gortex.js` (plugin/), `herdr-agent-state.js`, `loop-stopper.js`, `paseo-terminal-activity.js`, `render.ts`

## Reproduction

1. On Windows, with at least one **package** plugin configured that declares both `server` and `tui` features (confirmed with `oh-my-opencode-slim` and `@honcho-ai/opencode-honcho`), run:
   ```sh
   opencode api model.list --standalone
   ```
2. Observe exit code 1 and:
   ```
   {"_tag":"ServiceUnavailableError","message":"Location plugins did not finish activating","service":"plugin"}
   HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
   ```
3. Same failure with `--param 'location[directory]=C:\'` and any other directory — it is not directory-specific.
4. Controls (all on the same machine, same minute):
   - `opencode api model.list --standalone` → **503, consistent, 3/3 attempts**
   - `opencode api session.list --standalone` → **503**
   - `opencode api config.get --standalone` → OK
   - `opencode api path.get --standalone` → OK
   - `opencode api model.list` (background service) → OK (5039 models)
   - `opencode models` → OK

   So: private-server + plugin-awaiting operations fail; non-plugin operations and the background service are fine.

## Expected Behavior

`model.list` returns the model catalog (5039 models on this machine) — not a 503.

## Actual Behavior

Immediate 503. Server debug log (`--print-logs --log-level debug`) shows activation reaching the second load of the package plugins and never completing:

```
06:50:38.068 loading plugin id=oh-my-opencode-slim@latest   (server feature)
06:50:38.866 loading plugin id=@honcho-ai/opencode-honcho@0.2.1
06:50:39.204 loading plugin id=oh-my-opencode-slim@latest   (tui feature — second instantiation)
→ ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating
```

Every plugin declaring `tui` + `server` features is instantiated twice; after the second `oh-my-opencode-slim` load begins, no activation-completion event is ever emitted and the request times out.

## Additional Context

- Related: #55937 (global location watcher subscribes to all of `$HOME`, starves the event loop, `/api/model` 503). Before updating `oh-my-opencode-slim` from 3.0.4 to 3.0.7, the **background service** also 503'd reliably on `model.list`/`models`. After the plugin update the service path became healthy, and only the `--standalone` path still fails — so this may be a distinct bug from #55937, or the same class with a different trigger (private-server spawn re-runs full activation).
- Background-service mode can still intermittently 503 for a *brand-new* location's first activation (e.g. `C:\Windows`); a retry succeeds. Consistent with #55937.
- I did not bisect by removing `oh-my-opencode-slim` because it provides required agents in this environment. The log evidence implicates the double-instantiation of package plugins in the private server, but the plugin may be a victim rather than the cause.
- Workaround: drop `--standalone` and use the background service (`opencode service start`, port 4096).

issues.title: tui: agent catalog never recovers when the completing agent.updated has no location

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: status/repro-simulated
labels.description: Reproduced with a simulated model or mock

labels.name: area/tui
labels.description: Terminal interface

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2.2.7, a long-lived TUI can get stuck with only the built-in agents (`build`, `plan`) for its Location and never recover, even though the server keeps returning the full list including plugin-provided agents. The server's `agent.list` for that directory returns `orchestrator` at the same moment the TUI shows only `build` and `plan`, and restarting the TUI fixes it.

The only observable difference between a stuck instance and a healthy one in the logs: the `agent.updated` event that completed plugin agent registration for the stuck Location had **no `location` field**, and the TUI client drops those events.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.7 (channel `latest`), Windows 11, Windows Terminal
- Plugin: `oh-my-opencode-slim@3.0.7`, which registers `orchestrator` plus five subagents through `ctx.agent.transform(...)`
- Several MCP servers configured, including slow ones (`npx`-launched `playwright`, `rea` with 229 tools)
- Reproduced on two separate days with different working directories, so it is not directory-specific

## Actual behavior

The agent picker shows only `build` and `plan`. `plan` is a built-in, so the list contains no plugin agents at all. It stays that way for hours; nothing recovers it except restarting that TUI.

At the same time, the server answers correctly:

```
GET /api/agent?location[directory]=<workspace>
→ orchestrator, build, compaction, title, summary, plan, explorer, oracle, designer, fixer, observer
```

So this is a client-side catalog staleness bug, not a registration failure.

## Why it never recovers

`agent.updated` is published once. `packages/core/src/agent.ts` wires the notify through `State.changes`, which only publishes when the serialized projection actually changes:

```ts
notify: State.changes(list, () => bus.publish(Agent.Event.Updated, {}).pipe(Effect.asVoid)),
```

After the plugin agents are registered, the list never changes again, so no further `agent.updated` is emitted. A client that missed that single event has no way back short of a reconnect or restart.

## Why the event gets missed

Two things combine:

**1. The event may be published without a location.** `packages/core/src/bus.ts`:

```ts
const serviceLocation = Option.getOrUndefined(yield* Effect.serviceOption(Location.Service))
const location = options?.global
  ? undefined
  : (options?.location ??
    (serviceLocation
      ? { directory: serviceLocation.directory, workspaceID: serviceLocation.workspaceID }
      : undefined))
```

If the publishing fiber has no `Location.Service` in context, the payload simply has no `location` key. Plugin agent registration can land in exactly that situation: the promise adapter exposes `agent.reload` as `() => run(host.agent.reload())`, i.e. a plain microtask (`packages/plugin/src/promise/adapter.ts`), and a plugin that defers finalization (as this one does when the MCP snapshot is not ready yet) triggers it outside the Location-scoped Effect.

**2. The client drops location-less catalog events.** `packages/client/src/solid/data.ts`:

```ts
if (!event.location) return
const location = event.location
switch (event.type) {
  ...
  case "agent.updated":
    refreshLocation("agent", result.location.agent, location)
```

Any `agent.updated` without `location` returns early and refreshes nothing.

Note that the mini runtime has the opposite (and safer) behavior in `packages/tui/src/mini/stream-v2.transport.ts`:

```ts
if (input.location && event.location && event.location.directory !== input.location.directory) return
void refreshCatalog(attempt)
```

It refreshes on a location-less event. The full TUI does not, so the two frontends diverge here.

## Log evidence

Two occurrences, both on 2.2.7. Each startup registers plugin agents once per Location, but only some Locations get an `agent.updated` carrying their directory.

**2026-11-11, startup for the affected workspace:**

```text
09:28:48.543  location services booted  directory=<workspace> durationMs=344
09:28:48.553  loading plugin oh-my-opencode-slim@3.0.7
09:28:56.365  [plugin] agents registered {"count":6}     ← this Location's registration
09:28:56.410  event type=agent.updated  location=<none>   ← no location: dropped by the client
09:28:56.583  mcp connected server=calc
...
(no further agent.updated for <workspace> for the rest of the session)
```

**2026-11-12, three Locations booting at once:**

```text
00:47:32.683  event type=agent.updated  location=<project-a>        ← healthy
00:47:36.285  event type=agent.updated  location=<global config>    ← healthy
00:47:36.741  [plugin] agents registered {"count":6}
00:47:36.768  event type=agent.updated  location=<none>             ← affected workspace, dropped
```

Both stuck instances map to the location-less event; the Locations that received a located event were fine. In the 11-12 case the affected Location was also the slowest to boot (`durationMs=11926`, versus 313 and 2517 for the others), which is consistent with the client's first `location.sync` landing before plugin agents existed.

## Steps to reproduce

Timing-dependent; I could not force it deterministically.

1. Configure `oh-my-opencode-slim` (or any plugin that registers agents through `ctx.agent.transform`) plus several slow MCP servers.
2. Make one Location cold and slow to boot (new directory, or a large worktree).
3. Start `opencode` in that directory so the TUI connects and syncs its catalog while the Location is still booting.
4. Open the agent picker. It shows only built-in agents.
5. Check `/api/agent?location[directory]=...` on the same server: the full list is returned.
6. Restart that TUI: the agents appear.

## Expected behavior

The agent list converges to the server's list without requiring a restart, regardless of when the client connected.

## Possible fixes

- Client: do not drop catalog events that lack a location. Refresh every Location the client already holds (or fall back to the current/default Location), as the mini runtime already does.
- Server: publish `agent.updated` (and the other catalog events) with a location whenever the change belongs to a Location, including changes triggered from a promise-context plugin call.
- Belt and braces: after `location.sync` returns a list, if any plugin is still activating, refresh once more when `plugin.updated` reports activation settled.

## Additional context

- Likely related: #62796 ("stop waiting for plugins in request handlers") removed the plugin-activation wait from `agent.list`, so a cold Location can now legitimately answer with built-ins only. That makes the client's `*.updated` handling load-bearing; before it, the first read always saw the full list.
- Related but a different trigger: #63192 (sessions created before agents load fall back to `build`).
- A separate, unrelated failure mode I also hit on 2.2.6: a config hot reload disposes the plugin generation before the next one registers its agents, so an in-flight session drain fails with `Session.AgentNotFoundError: Agent not found: "orchestrator"`. Mentioning it only because it is another way the same agent can be missing at the wrong moment.
- Workaround: none found. Restarting the affected TUI is the only recovery; saving a config file does not help, because `config.updated` does not refresh the agent catalog.

issues.title: session: event_sequence starts at 0 for sessions without a counter row, then every insert fails UNIQUE(session_id, seq) (repro on 2.2.6)
issues.body:
### Description

On 2.2.6, the first time a server loads a session with no row in `event_sequence`, it sets the counter to 0. The next message insert reuses a `seq` that already exists in `session_message`. It fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed: session_message.session_id, session_message.seq`. The session then fails on every turn. Restarting the server does not help. The low counter is now persisted.

This is the same symptom as #53146, #56975 and #56528. #53146 was closed because it could not be reproduced. Here is a reproduction on a single server with no second process.

On my machine 225 of 239 sessions had no `event_sequence` row. I reproduced the failure on one of them. The steps are below. I expect the rest to behave the same when a server that has not already loaded them resumes them.

### What triggered it in practice

A script rewrote `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` while three sessions were active on `opencode serve --service`. The server logged `config.updated` for every instance directory and reloaded. From that point all three sessions failed every insert. After the reload their counters were 92, 70 and 97, against `max(seq)` of 3071, 1228 and 1775. Messages that did get written landed at seq 2 to 96, in the middle of the old history. One session also failed with `This model does not support assistant message prefill`. Its history now ended on an old assistant message.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Copy an existing data directory that has an older session with no `event_sequence` row:
   ```sql
   select s.id, max(m.seq) from session_v2 s
   join session_message m on m.session_id = s.id
   left join event_sequence e on e.aggregate_id = s.id
   where e.aggregate_id is null group by s.id;
   ```
2. Start a fresh server on the copy: `XDG_DATA_HOME=<copy> opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port <port>`
3. Resume that session with one turn: `opencode run --server http://127.0.0.1:<port> -s <session> -m <any model> "reply OK"`

Result on a session with `max(seq) = 318`:

- the server creates an `event_sequence` row with `seq = 4`
- new rows `agent-switched` at seq 0 and `model-switched` at seq 1
- the next insert fails: `SQLiteError: UNIQUE constraint failed: session_message.session_id, session_message.seq`

Expected: the counter seeds from `max(session_message.seq)` when no `event_sequence` row exists. The V1 migration path already does this. It inserts `event_sequence` with the last message seq.

### Workaround

With the server stopped, or at least with the affected sessions not loaded:

1. Move rows written after the reset to the end of the history. Rows whose `time_created` is after the reload, renumbered from the old `max(seq) + 1` in time order, with the same `seq` change in `blob_ref`.
2. Set the counter to the real max:
   ```sql
   insert into event_sequence (aggregate_id, seq, owner_id)
   select session_id, max(seq), null from session_message group by session_id
   on conflict (aggregate_id) do update set seq = excluded.seq
   where excluded.seq > event_sequence.seq;
   ```

After this, the three affected sessions saved normally again. In the reproduction setup, a second row-less session that I backfilled first resumed on a fresh server without errors.

### OpenCode version

2.2.6 (channel latest)

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04, Linux x64. SQLite WAL, `quick_check` ok.

### Plugins

Local plugins only. The failing insert is in the core session runner.

I ran into this while working on oh-my-opencode-slim issue 1860. When a background child session is cancelled, its queued `steer` and `queue` rows stay in `session_inbox` for good.

What the v2.2.0 source (`1097e26`) does:

- `interrupt` with `resume: false` returns before it reads or changes the inbox. See `packages/core/src/session/execution.ts`, lines 151 to 168.
- A row leaves the inbox only when a run promotes it, or when `DELETE /api/session/:id/inbox/:inboxID` is called. See `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts`, line 558.
- The plugin `SessionDomain` in `packages/plugin/src/promise/session.ts` has no inbox list or cancel method. A plugin that wants to clean up has to call the HTTP API directly.

I'd take either of these:

1. Expose inbox list and cancel on the plugin session domain.
2. Clear undelivered rows when `interrupt` runs with `resume: false`, or document that plugins must do it.

Repro, not run live yet: steer a running child, interrupt it with `resume: false`, then `GET /api/session/:id/inbox`. I expect the steer row to still be there. This rests on reading the source, so a live check would confirm it.

Related: #52201 covers a similar stale-state class. #63376 (closed) describes queued rows stranded after an interrupted run. I have not checked whether the fix there covers this case.

issues.body:
### Description

Parent timeline revert does not undo a file edit made by a background subagent. The same edit made directly by the parent reverts correctly.

This came in as a report on the OMO-Slim tracker: alvinunreal/oh-my-opencode-slim#1859. Thanks to @ismailokta for a clean repro. I traced it through the source. I have not reproduced it live.

Repro, from the report:

1. `file.txt` contains `line 1` and `line 2`.
2. Prompt the parent: "Use the fixer subagent in the background to append exactly `line 3` to `file.txt`. Wait for it to finish."
3. After the subagent finishes, open `/timeline` in the parent, select that prompt, and choose Revert.
4. Expected: `file.txt` goes back to two lines.
5. Actual: "1 message reverted", the prompt returns to the composer, and `file.txt` still has `line 3`. The revert summary lists no file change.

Control: the parent edits the same file directly over five prompts. Reverting the `line 3` prompt restores two lines and shows `3 messages reverted` with `M file.txt -3`.

### What the source says

I read v2.2.0 (the tag this repo pins) and v2.2.7 for the two files below. They match in the relevant parts.

- `SessionRevert.plan` (`packages/core/src/session/revert.ts`) builds the restore set only from `snapshot.files` on the parent's assistant messages after the reverted message.
- `snapshot.files` is a diff of the whole worktree between a step's start and end snapshot (`packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`, the `startSnapshot` / `snapshots.files` block). It is not scoped to a session.
- A background subagent returns right away. Its writes land after the parent step has ended, so they fall inside no parent step window. No parent message lists the file, so the plan never restores it.
- A foreground subagent blocks inside the parent's tool call, so its writes should land inside the parent step and revert. I have not tested this.

I did not check `subagent.ts` at v2.2.7. Two directions that might fit: include files written by child sessions (`parentID` is the parent) after the revert boundary in `plan()`, or record the child's snapshot files on the parent when the background job completes. I don't know the design constraints well enough to pick one.

Related: #15877, closed as a question. It asks whether `/undo` should roll back child sessions.

### Plugins

oh-my-opencode-slim v3.0.7

### OpenCode version

v2.2.7 (per reporter)

### Steps to reproduce

See above.

### Operating System

macOS

### Terminal

Ghostty

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.description: Windows Subsystem for Linux

issues.body:
## Summary

Reloading the config starts a new set of MCP server processes but never terminates the previous ones, so every save of `opencode.json`/`OPENCODE_CONFIG` leaks one process per configured local MCP server until the background service is restarted. In a long-lived `opencode serve --service` this accumulates hundreds of MB.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0 (`opencode v2.3.0`, npm global `@opencode/cli`)
- OS: Linux 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 (WSL2, Ubuntu)
- Terminal: Unavailable: headless harness, terminal env vars are not set
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: npm global install, release channel
- Active plugins: superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git

## Reproduction

1. Configure three local MCP servers in the config, two of them with `"pool": true`:

```jsonc
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "android-mcp":        { "type": "local", "pool": true, "command": ["/home/u/android-sdk/mcp-venv313/bin/android-mcp", "--device", "emulator-5554"] },
      "graphify-knowledge": { "type": "local", "pool": true, "cwd": "/home/u", "command": ["/home/u/.local/bin/graphify-mcp"] },
      "codebase-memory-mcp":{ "type": "local", "pool": true, "cwd": "/home/u", "command": ["/home/u/.local/bin/codebase-memory-mcp"] }
    }
  }
}
```

2. Open the client on one directory and count the MCP processes:

```sh
cgroup=$(systemctl --user show opencode.service -p ControlGroup --value)
for p in $(pgrep -u "$USER" -f android-mcp); do grep -q "${cgroup##*/}" /proc/$p/cgroup && echo "$p"; done | wc -l
```

3. Touch the config file so the watcher reloads it (any save, even a no-op change):

```sh
touch ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
```

4. Count again after ~10 s.

## Expected Behavior

After a reload the previous MCP connections are closed and their processes exit; the process count stays the same (one per pooled server). At worst, a restart of that server's process replaces the old one, so the count is unchanged.

## Actual Behavior

The count grows by one process per local server on every reload, and the old processes keep running for the whole lifetime of the service:

```
before save: graphify=3 android=9 codebase-memory=2
after save (10 s later): graphify=4 android=10 codebase-memory=3
```

No log line in `journalctl --user -u opencode.service` or in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` mentions starting or stopping those servers, so there is nothing to notice the leak by.

In a real session this reached 18 MCP processes (~1.4 GB RSS) before I noticed; they only went away with `systemctl --user restart` / service restart, at which point the count dropped to 10.

## Additional Context

- Impact: on a memory-constrained machine (WSL with a 4 GB Android emulator) the leaked processes push the service into its cgroup limit and the kernel OOM-kills unrelated workloads. I had to add `MemoryMax` and an external watchdog that restarts the service, which kills the user's session.
- Related behavior in the same area: `pool: true` works for servers that negotiate the 2026-07-28 revision (my `graphify-knowledge` went from 7 processes to 2 with 8 open directories), but is silently ignored for a `legacy` server (`android-mcp`, FastMCP 4.1.8): 8 open directories → 8 processes, no warning anywhere. The docs say legacy servers keep one connection per directory, so the missing part is only observability — a log line or a `pool: not applied` state in `mcp list` would have saved real time.
- Related: `pool` for local servers also needs a fixed `cwd`; without it each project folder gets its own copy. Documented, but again invisible at runtime.
- Workarounds in place: `KillMode=control-group` so `stop` actually kills the tree, `MemoryMax` on the unit, and a 5-minute watchdog that restarts the service when anonymous memory grows past a threshold.
- Reproducible consistently — 5 out of 5 config saves, both on 2.2.5 and after upgrading to 2.3.0.
