issues.body:
## Summary

Two back-to-back `/goal resume` turns on a thread running `cliproxy-responses/opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` via a custom OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint failed instantly at provider request time with "The request contains invalid parameters. Check the request body for any errors or inconsistencies." No agent work ran; the thread flipped to `failed` twice.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-43-generic (linux x64, local reporter machine `imbios-baltimore`); failing thread runs on linked remote env `myrehat-dev.asia-southeast1-a.c.myrehat-dev.internal` (linux x64, T3 server `0.1.10-nightly.20261113.4656`)
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color, TERM_PROGRAM unset, COLORTERM unset
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: opencode latest (local reporter); failing provider instance: `opencode` driver via cliproxy `http://127.0.0.1:8317/v1` responses model `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`
- Active plugins: ecc-universal

## Reproduction

1. Thread `8fe319ab-c791-45ac-91fd-36ef3a95387b` ("Support DeepSeek Harness in with-fh") completes run ordinal 3, then goes idle.
2. Send `/goal resume` (run ordinal 4, requested `2026-11-14T01:54:28Z`).
3. Immediately send `/goal resume` again (run ordinal 5, requested `2026-11-14T01:56:28Z`).
4. Both runs terminate ~3-8s after request with `status: failed` and an `error` item titled "Provider error" containing only "The request contains invalid parameters. Check the request body for any errors or inconsistencies."

## Expected Behavior

Resuming an idle thread with `/goal resume` should start a normal provider turn (or surface a retryable, specific validation error identifying the offending parameter).

## Actual Behavior

Both resume attempts fail before any agent/tool activity: `recentRuns` shows ordinal 4 `requestedAt 01:54:28 / completedAt 01:54:31 failed` and ordinal 5 `requestedAt 01:56:28 / completedAt 01:56:36 failed`, each followed by a bare `error` item (`status: failed`, title `Provider error`, text `The request contains invalid parameters...`). Same provider/model succeeded on earlier ordinals in the same thread, so this looks like a request-construction/validation regression keyed to the (bare, short) resume payload rather than a persistent model outage.

## Additional Context

- Failing thread link: `[Support DeepSeek Harness in with-fh](t3-thread://v2/c78fd245-ab83-4648-9212-5480be266bcf/8fe319ab-c791-45ac-91fd-36ef3a95387b)`; failing `latestRunId` is `run:thread:8fe319ab-c791-45ac-91fd-36ef3a95387b:ordinal:5`; `pendingRequestCount: 0`, no pending approvals/questions.

issues.body:
> This issue was drafted by an AI agent (Claude, using OpenCode's built-in report skill) and reviewed by me before posting.

## Summary

When the TUI is started with `--session <id> --prompt <text>`, the first new tab opened afterwards (clicking `+` in the tab bar) submits the `--prompt` text again. That runs the startup prompt a second time in a brand-new session.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0
- OS: Linux 6.18.62 x86_64 (NixOS)
- Terminal: Ghostty, with OpenCode running inside tmux (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`)
- Shell: zsh
- Install/channel: release 2.3.0, packaged with Nix
- Active plugins: four local plugins (lsp, notifications, speech, usage); none of them touch prompts or tabs

## Reproduction

1. Create a session ahead of time:
   `opencode api post /api/session --data '{"title":"repro","location":{"directory":"/tmp/x"}}'`
2. Start the TUI in a tmux pane:
   `tmux split-window -h "exec opencode --session <id> --prompt 'Reply with only: pong'"`
3. Wait for the prompt to run in that session. This part works as expected.
4. Click `+` in the tab bar.

## Expected Behavior

The new tab opens an empty home prompt.

## Actual Behavior

The new tab submits `Reply with only: pong` again, which creates a second session that runs the startup prompt. A second `+` click opens an empty tab, so only the first new tab is affected.

When `--prompt` is a slash command (`/start-ticket ABC-123` in our case), the whole command, model calls included, runs a second time.

## Additional Context

- **Frequency:** it seems to depend on timing. It reproduced reliably with the `split-window` launch above, but on two attempts where opencode was the tmux session's own command and the new tab was opened with `<leader>n`, the new tab came up empty. A user also saw it in one of two similar TUIs.
- **Possible cause (unverified):** this comes from reading the minified 2.3.0 bundle. The home route fills its prompt from `args.prompt` once, guarded by a module-level flag, and it has an effect that submits whenever the prompt text equals `args.prompt`. With `--session`, the app navigates to the session at mount, so the home prompt may never fill. The first later home view (the new tab) then fills the text and submits it. `args.newSessionID` already has take-once semantics (`takeNewSessionID`); giving `args.prompt` the same treatment once the startup navigation uses it would probably fix this.
- **Workaround:** send the prompt through the API instead of `--prompt`, then start the TUI with only `--session`:
  `opencode api post /api/session/<id>/command --data '{"name":"start-ticket","text":"ABC-123"}'`
- **Real-world launcher** where this showed up: https://github.com/Geometer1729/nixos-config/blob/a1fb9dd2cd71a2b9257a6bfb380c5e8c6744d217/modules/home/work/start-ticket.sh#L130-L139

issues.body:
### Description

The "Locations" section of the config docs says "Managed settings have the highest precedence, so users and projects cannot override the values they set, and managed preferences override the system directory." For permissions this does not hold. A project that sets `allow` rules on an agent, including the built-in `build` agent, overrides a managed `ask` and a managed `deny` for that agent. Agents without project rules keep the managed values, and a project's top-level permissions lose to the managed ones.

`packages/core/src/config/plugin/agent.ts` appends each agent's own rules after every document's top-level rules, and `packages/core/src/permission.ts` takes the last match. The permissions docs say "agent rules are appended last", which matches this behaviour. A managed `agents.<name>.permissions` block wins again, but only for agent names that the managed config lists.

### OpenCode version

2.3.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. `/etc/opencode/opencode.json`:

   ```json
   { "permissions": [
       { "action": "example_mcp_tool", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
       { "action": "skill", "resource": "example*", "effect": "deny" }
   ] }
   ```

2. In a project's `opencode.json`:

   ```json
   { "agents": { "build": { "permissions": [
       { "action": "example_mcp_tool", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
       { "action": "skill", "resource": "example*", "effect": "allow" }
   ] } } }
   ```

3. Run `opencode debug agents` in that project. For `build`, the project's `allow` rules come after the managed rules, so both resolve to `allow`. The built-in `general` agent has no project rules and keeps `ask` and `deny`. I checked the effective rules only and made no tool call.

Expected: managed permission rules win, as the config docs say. Alternatively, the docs state this exception and give managed config a way to keep its rules in force for every agent.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04 (Linux)

Related: #22292 (V1, closed as not planned), #55267 (managed config precedence).

issues.title: tui: previous/next user message ignores trackpad scrolling and jumps from the last selection
issues.body:
## Summary

In the TUI, after jumping with "previous/next user message", scrolling the transcript with a macOS trackpad does not invalidate the stored navigation message. The next shortcut continues from the last jumped message instead of the visible scroll position, so it can jump many messages away (for example, seeing message 13 and pressing previous jumps to message 6).

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.2.6 (also reproduced on current `dev`, 06aa6da22e)
- OS: macOS 14.5 (Darwin 23.6.0, arm64)
- Terminal: Ghostty, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /opt/homebrew/bin/bash
- Install/channel: release
- Active plugins: `./plugins/cmux` (local; not involved)

## Reproduction

1. Open a TUI session long enough to scroll (16 user/assistant turns in the harness).
2. Bind `session.message.user.previous` and `session.message.user.next` (their defaults are `none`). Use previous to jump up to a known message, for example message 7.
3. Scroll with a macOS trackpad until a different message is visible, for example message 13.
4. Press "previous user message".

## Expected Behavior

Navigation should be relative to the visible transcript: previous should go to the nearest user message above the viewport, and next to the nearest user message below it. It should not depend on a message selected before the reader scrolled away.

## Actual Behavior

It jumps to message 6 (`7 - 1`), ignoring the current scroll position. From the same position, "next user message" goes to message 8 (`7 + 1`), not message 14.

Clicking "jump to latest" first makes navigation use the viewport again, because `toBottom()` clears the stored navigation message.

## Additional Context

- `scrollToMessage` passes `currentID: navigationMessage()` into `findMessageBoundary` (`packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:864-874`).
- `findMessageBoundary` returns `visible[currentIndex ± 1]` whenever `currentID` is present, without reading `scrollTop` (`packages/tui/src/routes/session/message-navigation.ts:44-47`).
- `navigationMessage` is set by `alignMessage` after a jump (`index.tsx:846-861`).
- Trackpad/wheel scrolling goes through `onMouseScroll`, which only clears navigation when `firstJump()` is set (`index.tsx:1547-1552`); scrollbar changes only call `updateAwayFromBottom` (`index.tsx:1530`).
- Keyboard `moveTranscript` and `toBottom` clear it, so the stale state is specific to trackpad/wheel scrolling and likely scrollbar dragging.
- TUI harness output: jump cursor to prompt 7, trackpad-scroll to prompt 13, press previous -> prompt 6.

Suggested fix: treat `navigationMessage` as valid only until the next user scroll. Invalidate it on trackpad/wheel and scrollbar drag, then use the existing geometry fallback to choose the target. Do not recompute and overwrite it on every scroll event; keep `navigationSlack` handling separate so clearing it cannot clamp the viewport.

prs.title: fix(core): seed missing event sequence from stored events and session messages
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62523

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A session whose `event_sequence` counter row was missing started at seq `0`, while `session_message` already held seqs up to e.g. 318. The projector's `INSERT` then failed `UNIQUE(session_id, seq)` on every turn — permanently, because the low counter row is what the next insert reads.

`packages/core/src/bus.ts` treated a missing counter as `-1`, so the next durable event took seq `0`. The fix adds `persistedMax()`, which takes the maximum of the counter **and** the rows that are actually stored (`max(event.seq)`, and for sessions `max(session_message.seq)`), and uses `max(counter, persistedMax)` in `commitDurableEvent`, `publishAll` and `latestSequence`.

A missing or stale counter now resumes above the rows that exist, and the next write persists the healed counter through the existing upsert, so the session repairs itself. This also covers V1-migrated sessions whose events were deleted while their messages remained.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test in `session-projector.test.ts`: it seeds projected messages with no counter row and then delivers an inbox message. Before the fix this reproduced the `UNIQUE constraint failed` error from the issue; after it the message lands at seq `3` and the counter heals to `3`.
- `tsc -b packages/core` → clean.
- bus tests 64/64, projector tests 46/46 (including the new one), v1-migration + session-title + state-replay 60/60.

prs.title: fix(core): give claude-agent a larger image budget
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #63870

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Gives `claude-agent` a larger image budget in `boundImages`: the cut triggers at 96 MiB and drops to 64 MiB, instead of 25/15 MiB.

claude-agent keeps the history, images included, in its own Claude Code session and only sends what's new. When the cut replaces an old image, the fingerprint of that message group changes, the session branches before it and replays everything after as new input. So each cut rewrites almost the whole prompt cache (~$2.40 at 350k context on Opus). With screenshots that happens every ~40 images.

The larger budget keeps a bound, which matters when a fresh or rebuilt session sends the whole history in one catch-up, and stays under Anthropic's 128 MB request limit with room for the text. Cuts become rare enough that compaction normally comes first. The larger budget only applies when Claude Code reports Anthropic's own API (`account.apiProvider === "firstParty"`) and no `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is set; on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, gateways or an unknown backend, claude-agent's request hooks apply the normal 25/15 MiB cut first. Other providers keep 25/15 MiB. It's a provider check like the existing `xai` one in the same file, passed the same way (`model.model.provider`). Per-model limits (#61563 / #62688) could replace the constant later.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Test in `packages/core/test/session-model-request.test.ts`: 27 MiB of images passes through untouched for `claude-agent` and is still cut for `anthropic`. For `claude-agent`, 96 MiB isn't cut and 99 MiB drops the oldest 12 images, leaving 63 MiB. It fails without the fix.

prs.title: fix(core): repair V1 global sessions left by completed imports
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #49827 for people who already upgraded.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

#56322 attributes V1 global sessions to their folder's project during the import, but only for imports that hadn't finished. Anyone who already upgraded still has those sessions under `global`, where the per-folder session lists can't find them.

This adds a one-time repair that runs in the background on server start, after the import:

```text
if the import is completed and the repair hasn't run:
    for each folder of V2 sessions still under global that came from V1:
        look up the folder's V2 project (same lookup as the import: 5s limit, stop after a timeout)
        nothing found, or it's global again -> skip
        one transaction:
            insert the project row if missing (never replace)
            set project_id + path, only where the session is still global; time_updated is kept
    mark the repair done
```

- Only touches `session_v2` rows that are still `global`, have no workspace, and also exist in the V1 `session` table. Sessions created in V2 are left alone.
- Lookups run outside transactions, and each folder is its own short transaction. If it stops partway, finished folders stay fixed and the next start does the rest.
- If the repair hits a database error it logs a warning, leaves the migration status alone, and retries next start.
- Fresh imports mark the repair done in their completion transaction, since they already attribute sessions.
- Undoable: the V1 `session` table still has the original `global` project ids.

Also points the orphan-session test at a missing folder inside its own temp dir instead of `/tmp/orphan`, which could exist on a machine.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test: a completed import with V1 global sessions in a plain folder, a git repo subfolder, a missing folder, plus a V2-native global session. Only the first two move, time_updated is kept, and the repair is marked done. Fails without the change.
- Ran the repair on a copy of a real already-migrated database (kv, project, session, session_v2 only): 346 sessions moved in about 100ms, 9 new projects, no other session column changed, no non-global session changed, 138 stayed global because their folders are gone.
- `bun run check` passes; `v1-migration` and `project` tests pass with `--rerun-each 3`.

prs.title: fix(core): share the root cache affinity across nested forks and children
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55243

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`SessionAffinity.get` looked only one link up (`parentID ?? fork.sessionID ?? id`). In a chain P → M → G, M sent `prompt_cache_key` P but G sent M, a key never used before, so G's first request rewrote the whole prompt into the cache. A grandchild subagent had the same gap through `parentID`.

`SessionAffinity.get` now takes a session ID and a loader and walks `parentID` / `fork.sessionID` up to the root, like the subagent tool walks `parentID` for its depth limit. If a source session no longer exists, the walk stops at its ID, which keeps today's key for a fork of a deleted session. `SessionModelRequest` loads through `SessionStore`, and the OpenAI, ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot plugins through `ctx.session.get`, so the body key and every session header get the same root. This removes the "persist cache lineage" TODO without a schema change: the walk costs one primary-key read per ancestor per request.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added two session runner tests: a fork chain P → M → G sends P as `promptCacheKey` and in the affinity headers for all three sessions, and a grandchild sends the root, while `x-parent-session-id` keeps its direct parent. prs.title: fix(app): open the server directory as a project on a fresh client
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55222

Port of #41138 (closed when `dev` moved to V2). Same bug as #37096 (V1).

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Running `opencode serve` in a project folder and opening the web UI in a fresh browser shows no projects and "Nothing here yet". The sidebar reads the per-server project list, which lives in browser storage, and nothing fills it. The server already knows the folder: `GET /api/location` returns it.

On connect, this fetches the server's location and adopts its directory as a project, but only when that server has no open projects. Folders the user closed stay closed, filesystem roots are skipped, and desktop sidecars are skipped because the desktop app starts them itself. It waits for `servers.hydrated()`, like the Home selection does, so adopting into the empty pre-hydration list can't overwrite stored projects on desktop. Only the location is tracked, so closing the last project mid-session does not bring the folder back.

It calls `sdk.api.location.get()` directly, as the folder picker and "Add project" do. `sync.data.path` stays empty in this flow, so it can't be used.

**Design and alternatives**

- Chosen: adopt on the client when the stored list for that server is empty. The project list lives in browser storage per server, so the client is where it is empty.
- Not chosen: reading `sync.data.path`. It stays empty in V2, so it never sees the directory.
- Not chosen: seeding projects from the server's project inventory. That changes how the sidebar is built for every client; #53752 takes that route.
- Not chosen: tracking the project list in the effect. Closing the last project would then re-adopt the folder.
- Deferred: skipping the server's home folder. `/api/location` does not report home, so this needs the server to expose it first (see the review thread).

prs.title: fix(core): preserve embedded MCP prompt text
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55181

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

MCP prompt commands can return an instruction together with an embedded text resource containing the document, code, or other reference material the instruction depends on. OpenCode currently keeps the instruction but silently drops the resource body when it converts the MCP response into a session prompt. If the resource is the only message in the response, the generated prompt text is empty.

For example, a `prompts/get` response containing `Review this policy:` followed by an embedded JSON resource with `text: '{"region":"EU"}'` currently submits only `Review this policy:`. With this change, the session receives both pieces in order: `Review this policy:\n{"region":"EU"}`. A resource-only response likewise retains its text instead of becoming an empty prompt.

The problem is in `promptMessageText` in the built-in command plugin. The surrounding code already walks all returned messages and joins their converted content, but the helper recognizes only ordinary text messages. Embedded resources are a valid MCP prompt content type and may already carry the complete body in `resource.text`. There is no need to read the URI again or change MCP discovery, transport, or session admission to preserve that body.

This PR adds a text-resource branch to that helper and gives its parameter the existing `Mcp.PromptResult` message-content type. The response is already validated by the MCP client, so the helper can distinguish the supported content forms directly instead of accepting `unknown` and repeating generic object and property checks. Ordinary text still returns `content.text`; an embedded resource with a `text` field returns `content.resource.text`; the remaining content forms retain the existing empty-string result.

The check is based on the resource representation, rather than a `text/plain` MIME restriction. JSON, Markdown, and source files can all be represented as text resources, and the server has already supplied their text. The mixed-message regression uses `application/json` specifically to protect this behavior. The resource body is passed through directly, consistent with the existing text-resource handling in the MCP client. This does not add a URI prefix or otherwise change prompt formatting.

The scope is deliberately limited to embedded text resources. Images, audio, and resources represented by base64 `blob` fields are not decoded or turned into prompt text. This PR does not introduce media attachments, additional network requests, or changes to message-role handling. The fix is shared by callers of the built-in MCP command path.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added two regression cases to the existing command-plugin test file. They register and execute the real command through `Command.Service`, provide controlled MCP responses using the existing test fixture, and capture the resulting session prompt. This checks the full conversion path rather than a separate copy of the helper's logic.

The cases cover an instruction followed by an embedded JSON text resource and a prompt containing only an embedded plain-text resource. Both assert the exact text submitted to the session. The original built-in `init` and `review` command test also continues to pass.

Validation:

- `cd packages/core && bun test test/plugin/command.test.ts`: all 3 tests passed with the focused resource regressions and the existing built-in command test.
- `cd packages/core && bun typecheck`: passed for the changed core source and tests, with `GOMAXPROCS=2` and `GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB`.
- Prettier check for both changed files and `git diff origin/dev --check`: passed.

The change touches only the command conversion and its regression tests.

prs.title: fix(app): drop removed queued attachment references
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55179

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

This fixes the replacement prompt sent when a queued message with ordinary text and a path attachment is edited. Removing the attachment card now removes its generated path reference from the replacement text. Keeping the card while changing the prompt text produces one reference instead of two. Review and browser comment notes attached to the original queued message continue to accompany the edit.

The composer restores the original message's display text separately from its attachment cards. The full model-visible text contains more than that display text: `buildPromptRequest` appends path references and comment notes. Before this change, `editedPromptInput` rebuilt the replacement request from the editor, then copied the original text's entire suffix back as retained notes. That suffix included the original path references. As a result, a removed attachment survived in the request text even though its metadata was empty, while a retained attachment appeared both in the newly built request and in the copied suffix.

For a concrete example, editing `summarize data` with `/repo/confidential.csv` to `Use only public data` and removing the card previously submitted the new instruction followed by the old file reference. With this change, the old reference is absent. If the card remains, the replacement still refers to `/repo/confidential.csv`, but only once.

The change uses the existing `readPromptPresentation` decoder to identify an app-owned presentation when there is a hidden suffix to retain. It then reconstructs that suffix from the decoded comments using the existing file-comment and note-comment formatters. The current request remains responsible for generating references for the attachments actually present in the editor. This separates the two kinds of generated content without parsing or rewriting the user's prompt text.

Messages from another client may have display text and additional context without the app's structured comments list. Their opaque suffix remains unchanged. A user-typed phrase such as `Attached file: /repo/user-typed.txt` also remains in the edited text. Stored file context continues through the existing admission path, so preserving a review note does not discard the file that note refers to.

The production change is confined to the suffix handling in `queue.ts`, where the app already has both the original presentation and the newly built request. It applies to queued messages with non-empty display text and a hidden generated suffix. This keeps ownership clear: current composer attachments generate path references, and original structured comments generate retained notes.

### How did you verify your code works?

Extended the existing `session-queue.spec.ts` keeper with a two-case table for removing and retaining a path attachment. Each case checks the actual replacement request text, its attachment metadata, retained review and browser comments, a literal attachment-looking phrase in the user's text, and the review comment's stored file URI. The assertions confirm that removing the card removes its generated reference and retaining it sends that reference exactly once.

A further keeper case verifies that opaque suffix context from another client survives editing. The five focused browser checks, including the existing deleted-file-mention and comment-only cases, pass locally in Chromium 143. The comment-only test now waits for the editor to gain focus before sending its editing keys, matching the queue's asynchronous focus restoration.

Package-level `bun typecheck` passes, with the tracked custom-element declaration symlink resolved locally for the Windows check. Focused linting of the two changed files reports no warnings or errors, and `git diff --check` passes.

prs.title: fix(app): honor project permission overrides for unloaded sessions
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55176

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

This fixes project-level permission auto-accept overrides for sessions that the app has not loaded. When the app-wide default is On and a project's override is Off, a permission request from an unknown session currently receives an automatic `once` reply. After this change, the app first obtains that session's project ID and leaves the request pending when the project's setting requires manual approval.

The failure comes from the early return in `consider()` in `packages/app/src/session/requests/auto-approve.ts`. Its `covers(undefined)` condition checks the global default without knowing the request's project. If that default is On, the function calls `approve()` immediately. For an unknown session, `approve()` cannot recover a project ID from the local store either, so its final settings check also uses the global default. The explicit project override is never considered. Cached sessions do not exhibit this problem because their project ID is already available.

The production change removes that global-default shortcut. The cached-session branch continues to call `approve()` directly. Every unknown session instead follows the session-get branch that already exists, and the returned project ID is passed to `approve()`. That function remains responsible for checking the server-scoped project setting, suppressing duplicate replies, and respecting disposal and retry behavior. The fix therefore changes when the project is resolved rather than introducing a second policy implementation.

The observable result is consistent approval behavior before and after a session is opened. An explicit Off override leaves its request pending, while an On project still receives an automatic reply. Restoring a project to the default continues to approve requests when the default is On. The additional work is a session GET for a request whose session metadata is absent; requests from cached sessions keep the existing direct path.

The regression coverage extends the existing project-override case in the multi-server keeper. After the initial settings sweep, it adds two sessions without publishing events that would populate the app's session cache. One belongs to an On project and one to an Off project. It then delivers permission events, checks the exact automatic replies, confirms that the blocked session was fetched, and opens that session to verify that the permission remains visible. Finally, it restores the Off project to the default and checks that all remaining requests are released. This covers the missing cache state within the existing owner of project and server approval behavior.

### How did you verify your code works?

The complete `e2e/regression/multi-server.spec.ts` keeper passes all five cases. The extended override case checks exact outgoing replies and confirms that the Off project's request remains available for manual approval. The other cases also exercise remote-server settings, unfocused sessions and children, reconnect sweeps, and permissions discovered when a session opens.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52122
Refs #41329, #54022

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Third-party packagers (Nix, AUR, Homebrew) ship their own desktop build from the released binary, but the bundled updater only checked the compiled channel. A repackaged release is always the `prod` channel, so it still ran automatic update checks and could offer a release the package did not install. `autoupdate: false` in config does not apply to the desktop app.

This gates the desktop updater on `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE`, the variable the CLI already honors, so one setting disables updates for both. When it is set, the updater starts in its `disabled` state — no automatic check at startup, no ten-minute re-check, and the Check for updates menu item stays unavailable — matching `dev`-channel behavior.

The decision moves to `updaterEnabled` in `packages/gui-extensions/src/updater/enabled.ts` so the packager-facing contract is unit-testable.

The repo's own Nix desktop derivation now passes `--set OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE 1` to its Linux and macOS wrappers, so a Nix install no longer arms the production updater (#52122). The environment variable table also notes that the variable covers the desktop app.

`generatedMigrations` in `packages/core/script/migration.ts` splits a `Bun.Glob` result on the forward slash:

prs.title: feat(app): render voice call delegations as Voice messages
prs.body:
## What

Prompts that the OpenCode iOS app's voice calls send into a session showed up in the desktop/web timeline as raw text: the `Voice delegation.` header (or the shorter `Voice delegation (continued).` marker), then the JSON body with `instruction`, `transcript_delta`, `context` and so on.

They now render the way the iOS app shows them, as a **Voice message**:

- The bubble shows the voice agent's framing (`voice`). If there isn't one, it shows the user's own words (`instruction`).
- A small waveform badge sits on the bubble's top leading corner, with the tooltip and accessible name "Voice message".
- When the call log was attached (`call_log_attached`, or a trailing `Attached file:` line naming a `voice-call-….json` upload), a quiet "Call log attached" caption appears under the bubble.

The session still receives the full prompt unchanged. Only the display is different. Prompts sent from this app's composer carry presentation metadata, so they're never parsed as voice delegations.

## Before / after

Desktop app with mocked server data, dark theme:

![before and after, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/577e12db117af7aeb375cb6b0aee97ddedeee86d/.pr-shots/compare-dark-1100.png)

Narrow window, light theme:

![before and after, light narrow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/577e12db117af7aeb375cb6b0aee97ddedeee86d/.pr-shots/compare-light-520.png)

Badge detail:

![badge detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/577e12db117af7aeb375cb6b0aee97ddedeee86d/.pr-shots/crop-after-dark.png)

## How

- `session-ui/src/message/voice-delegation.ts` parses the prompt. It follows the iOS app's `VoiceHandoff.parse`: it matches the header opening, decodes the JSON body with Schema, and strips trailing `Attached file:` lines.
- `SessionUserMessage` parses only when there's no app presentation metadata, then passes the display text and a `voice` flag to `CurrentUserMessageDisplay`.
- Adds `waveform` and `paperclip` icons and two English i18n keys.
- Adds a `Voice messages` story with fixtures in the exact formats the iOS app sends.

## Tests

- `bun test src/message/voice-delegation.test.ts` (session-ui) covers framing, falling back to the instruction, both ways the call log can be flagged, and non-delegation prompts that must be left alone.
- A component test in `session-message-projection.spec.ts` checks that the story renders the badge, the caption and the display text, with no raw JSON. I confirmed it fails without the change.
- `bun typecheck` passes in session-ui, ui and app. The session-ui and ui unit suites pass.

Not covered: the queued-prompt panel still shows a queued voice delegation's raw text. That text is also what gets edited, so I left it alone. Copy copies the displayed text, same as the iOS app's default Copy.

Requested by: @neriousy (Filip via Slack)

### Issue for this PR

Closes #55084 (the narrowed split-cache case confirmed in the issue).

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Server-listed TUI packages were resolve-only, so a client with a separate/empty npm cache silently skipped `./tui`. Allow installation for package sources; local sources stay unchanged. `Npm.add` reuses cached installations rather than forcing an update.

The regression uses a real local Git package, separate server/client caches, the real Npm service, and the production TUI renderer. It observes the plugin's toast and verifies that inventory refresh does not rerun setup. No duplicate `cli.json` entry is required. Private Git packages still require client-side access.

AI-assisted. No unrelated dependency/type/lint fixes are included.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New split-cache cases fail on unchanged source and pass with the fix (empty and populated client caches).
- Latest focused run: **127 tests pass across 9 plugin/lifecycle files**, including both new cases.
- Prettier and `git diff --check` pass.
- Ran the required root `bun run check`: `oxlint` panics in `oxc_allocator::pool::fixed_size`. The same command panics on the exact unchanged `dev` base `c1615b1`, with the entire tracked tree restored to that base for comparison.
- Retried the affected TUI `bun typecheck` with reduced Go concurrency/memory pressure. Early attempts were killed. The completed run reports Node API type errors (`Process.getBuiltinModule`, `node:module.registerHooks`, and `node:sqlite`). **The unchanged base reports the same errors in the same environment.** This does not claim a green current typecheck.
- Earlier scoped typecheck passed; the current clean-install validation and its baseline comparison above supersede that result.

Full repository tests, Windows, and private-Gitea authentication were not exercised. The live application validation below uses a local Git repository, not a private Git service.

### Screenshots / recordings

No layout changes. Also ran the actual OpenCode CLI/server and interactive TUI from source with the repository's Solid preload/tsconfig, a local Git-hosted plugin declared only in the server's isolated global `opencode.json`, and a separate client HOME/npm cache. No plugin entry was added to the client config and no API/plugin inventory was mocked.

The live server `/api/plugin` inventory reports the package active with server and TUI features. With the unchanged `dev` TUI production source, a fresh client never executes `./tui` and the toast is absent. With this fix, another fresh client installs its own package, executes TUI setup exactly once, and renders `QA Git TUI plugin loaded`. The setup record points to the client cache, distinct from the server's installed package. A second fixed TUI with that populated cache also loads once and reuses the exact same installed package path.

The terminal was a 150-by-38 PTY with standard capability replies. I captured the actual output and a marker written by the fixture's TUI setup. The process was stopped with SIGINT after observation (exit 130 is expected). The server used built-in simulation network mode with model fetching disabled. No provider traffic or paid model call was needed for plugin startup.

Live raw terminal recordings, API inventory and setup records are attached below. The scope remains the cache/loading regression, not private-repository authentication or model behavior.

releases.name: v2.3.0
releases.body:
### Highlights

- **Background Subagents by Default**: Subagents now return immediately, continue in the background, and report back whenever they become idle. You can keep working in the parent session while multiple subagents run concurrently. ([#63382](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63382))
- **Quieter Transcripts by Default**: The TUI now summarizes each run of tool calls and thoughts into one collapsible activity row, so the answer is easier to follow. To see every step again, set **Verbosity** to `medium` or `high` in settings, or set `session.verbosity` in your TUI config; an existing setting is kept. ([#63207](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63207))
- **Jump to an Earlier Prompt**: In the desktop app, open **Jump to message** from the command palette or press `Cmd+Alt+G` (`Ctrl+Alt+G` on Windows and Linux) to search prompts across the current session and jump directly to one. ([#63585](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63585))

### Core

#### Improvements

- Subagents now always run in the background, return their session ID immediately, and report results to their parent whenever they become idle. ([#63382](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63382))
- Added experimental support for MCP events, behind the `mcp_events` flag. ([#63254](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63254), [#63261](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63261), [#63269](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63269))
- Shell commands now survive server handoffs and keep their output when interrupted.
- Added experimental support for moving a shell command to the background when its timeout expires, behind the `shell_timeout_background` flag. With the flag on, an explicit timeout on a background command stops it. ([#63024](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63024), [#63703](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63703))
- Local Windows shell commands now run through the process daemon.
- Added support for freeform tool input on compatible models.
- Added LM Studio decision-model support.
- Agents are now told when their session is a fork. Thanks @hasta84. ([#63235](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63235))
- Tool output truncation now keeps the beginning of the output and preserves a usable preview if the full output cannot be saved.
- Tail reads no longer load the entire file into memory.
- Providers can present a client certificate for gateways that require mutual TLS. Set `settings.tls` with `cert`, `key` and an optional `passphrase` on the provider; values accept `{file:}` and `{env:}` like `apiKey`. ([#61832](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61832))
- When a subagent goes idle while its own background work is still running, its report to the parent now says it is still running, so the parent waits for the final report instead of treating the partial answer as done. ([#63675](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63675))
- Code Mode gets simpler structured results from file and skill tools: `write` and `edit` return their confirmation as a string, `patch` returns an empty result, and `skill` returns the skill's directory and content. ([#63616](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63616), [#63635](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63635), [#63618](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63618), [#63623](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63623))

#### Bug fixes

- Fixed case-only file renames in patches on case-insensitive filesystems.
- Fixed stale thinking being retained after Claude Agent prompts or tools change.
- Fixed directly driven child sessions not resuming after a restart.
- Fixed plugin replacement stopping when cleanup of an earlier plugin fails.
- Fixed MCP OAuth refreshes and localhost redirects when a server rewrites `127.0.0.1`.
- Fixed saved API keys being omitted from local-model discovery.
- Local model discovery (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) waits up to 15 seconds per request instead of 1, so remote or tunnelled endpoints list their models, and a slow endpoint no longer delays other endpoints or config reloads. ([#63700](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63700))
- In Code Mode, calling a namespace as if it were a tool now suggests up to three real tools under it. ([#63697](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63697))
- Fixed retryable provider streams losing completed work when interrupted.
- Fixed GitHub Copilot requests using the wrong endpoint before models finish loading.
- Fixed exhausted request rate limits being treated as terminal. Thanks @Kyle-j-bush. ([#59816](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59816))
- Fixed LM Studio models with a null context length and accepted decision-type models. Thanks @tomzhu1024. ([#56214](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56214))

### TUI

#### Improvements

- Transcript verbosity now defaults to `low`, which summarizes each run of tools and thoughts into one activity row. A `session.verbosity` you already set is kept. ([#63207](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63207))
- Session IDs found in messages can now be opened directly.
- Activity tabs are clickable and open the correct view.
- Shell mode has its own prompt color under the new designs.

#### Bug fixes

- Restored pasted text when undo brings back its placeholder.
- Restored the live draft after browsing prompt history.
- Fixed copying a paste from within the prompt selection.
- Preserved the Mini composer caret when closing the command palette.
- Prevented image bytes from being retained in transcript storage when image previews are disabled.
- Fixed paste-chip contrast across light and dark themes.
- Fixed plugin-provided themes updating live.
- Session lists now open at the top rather than at the current session.
- Mini scrollback now shows the subagent card instead of obsolete launch instructions.

### Desktop

#### Improvements

- Added **Jump to message** to the command palette with `Cmd+Alt+G` / `Ctrl+Alt+G`, including prompts not yet loaded in the timeline. Thanks @usrnk1. ([#63585](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63585))
- Added the experimental **Recent** sessions sidebar, with cross-server recency, local pins, reordering, and standard session-row actions.
- Recent sessions are limited to the last seven days and 30 rows, and can be hidden or muted.
- Added an experimental customizable sessions sidebar.
- Mermaid diagrams can now be maximized for zooming and panning. ([#59250](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59250))
- Added `Alt+Enter` to place a follow-up first in the queue and `Mod+Enter` to steer the next queued prompt.
- Holding the modifier key now shows tab shortcut numbers.
- Each server’s terminal shell can be selected from its menu.
- Added a free-limit panel in place of the composer when applicable.
- Session IDs are easier to find and copy.

#### Bug fixes

- Recent sessions now keep stable recency ordering through list reloads, renames, and completed runs.
- Fixed browser panes not retrying after server plugins finish loading.
- Fixed mention suggestions being recreated while typing.
- Fixed SSH prompts failing to advance or close after connection.
- Fixed pasted provider-auth redirect URLs being rejected.
- Restored message footers in the New timeline.
- Fixed links whose labels contain inline code.
- Fixed the desktop main process freezing while probing the login-shell environment.
- Fixed the drag region after changing layout direction.
- Fixed vertical-tab previews snapping to the wrong tab.
- Fixed the file-tree sidebar opening animation.
- Fixed pairing QR-code contrast in light themes. Thanks @ssskay. ([#63220](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63220))
- Fixed activity-tab navigation and click handling. Thanks @OpeOginni. ([#60168](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60168))

### SDK

#### Improvements

### What do you want to change?

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.5.2 (the current `latest`, and `packages/coding-agent/package.json` on `main`) depends on `undici` at exactly `8.12.3`. Please move it to 8.12.4 or later, or relax the exact pin to a range such as `^8.12.4` so that installs pick up undici patch releases, and cut a patch release.

### Why?

Six undici advisories published on 2026-11-05 affect 8.12.3. All six are fixed in 8.12.4:

- GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32 (CVE-2026-116592, high): cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure via intermediate redirect hops
- GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg (CVE-2026-120474, medium): cross-user cache disclosure via same-origin redirect
- GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954 (CVE-2026-116630, medium): cross-user information disclosure via cross-origin redirect revalidation
- GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f (CVE-2026-120415, medium): cross-origin credential disclosure via array-of-tuples headers bypassing redirect stripping
- GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2 (CVE-2026-120222, medium): denial of service via an unhandled exception in cache-interceptor response replay
- GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc (CVE-2026-120423, medium): Subresource Integrity bypass via whitespace in integrity metadata

A project that depends on pi-coding-agent gets a nested undici 8.12.3 and has to add its own `overrides` entry to receive these fixes. Users who install pi directly cannot do that.

issues.body:
### What happened?

On Windows (PowerShell in Windows Terminal), after exiting pi following a long conversation, the PowerShell prompt floods with echoed escape sequences whenever I move the mouse or press keys:

```
[<35;69;10M^
<35;68;11M^
199,5u ...
127:129u ...
```

These are SGR mouse reports (`ESC[<35;69;10M` = motion, no button) and Kitty keyboard CSI-u reports (127 = Backspace, 32 = Space). The `^` is conhost's caret notation for ESC in cooked-mode echo. The window is unusable until the modes are cleared manually.

I measured this while it happened: pi's console input mode was already back at cooked+ECHO while the terminal still had `?1000/?1002/?1003/?1006` mouse tracking and Kitty keyboard reporting enabled.

1. Windows Terminal, PowerShell, run `pi`.
2. Have a long conversation (large transcript).
3. Exit pi (Ctrl+D).
4. Move the mouse over the window / type at the PowerShell prompt.

Easier with a shorter transcript: stop pi while its stdout write queue is congested (e.g. during heavy rendering), or just exit right after a big final screen repaint.

### Expected behavior

pi disables all input-reporting modes (mouse tracking, Kitty keyboard, modifyOtherKeys, bracketed paste) before the console input flips back to cooked+ECHO, and those disable sequences survive `process.exit()`. On Windows, `process.stdout.write()` to the console is asynchronous and `process.exit()` drops unflushed writes, while `setRawMode(false)` takes effect synchronously — so the disables are currently racing the echo flip and/or get truncated on exit.

### What happened?

pi never sends `reasoning_effort` to `github-copilot/gemini-4-argon` or `github-copilot/gemini-3.8-flash`, so the `--thinking` flag has no effect on those models. The bundled catalog sets `compat.supportsReasoningEffort: false` for every Copilot model on `openai-completions` (and `kimi-k3`). It looks like Copilot supports it, though:

```json
// GET /models
{
  "id": "gemini-4-argon",
  "capabilities": {
    "supports": {
      "reasoning_effort": ["low","medium","high"]
    }
  }
}
```

Separately, Copilot reports reasoning tokens as top-level `usage.reasoning_tokens`, but `openai-completions.js` only reads `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`, so `usage.reasoning` is always 0 for these models.

pi already calls Copilot's `/models` to fill `availableModelIds`. Reading `capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort` from that same response would keep `compat` from going stale. I'm happy to send a PR for either fix, but let me know.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run with `low`:

    ```
    pi -ne -p --mode json --no-session --model github-copilot/gemini-4-argon:low "How many primes are there between 100 and 200?"
    ```

2. Run it again with `high`:

    ```
    pi -ne -p --mode json --no-session --model github-copilot/gemini-4-argon:high "How many primes are there between 100 and 200?"
    ```

3. Observe that both runs send the same request without `reasoning_effort`, and both report `usage.reasoning: 0`.

### Expected behavior

The thinking level maps to `reasoning_effort` for Copilot models whose `/models` entry, and `usage.reasoning` reflects Copilot's `usage.reasoning_tokens`.

### Version

1.5.0

### Notes

Found via AI, authored by a human :smile:.

issues.title: Session with >~120k entries after the last compaction fails to load: RangeError in  buildContextEntries

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

A long session stopped working. Every context rebuild threw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`, and so did every extension call to `ctx.getContextUsage()`. After that, `pi --session  <file>` crashed on startup with the same error, even with `-ne`.

The session had 120,432 entries on the branch after its last compaction. Most were `context_edit` and custom entries, which add no messages: the context was only 402 messages.


The cause is the spread push in `buildContextEntries`:

```typescript
contextEntries.push(...path.slice(compactionIdx + 1))
```

This passes every entry after the compaction as a separate argument. The limit depends on stack depth. It fails at about 120k–150k entries at startup and below 80k when called from inside an extension event handler.

```bash
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
     at buildContextEntries (dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-VEJDBY3O.js:521:2551)
     at buildSessionProjection (...:521:3299)
     at _SessionManager.buildSessionProjection (...:529:4822)
     at _SessionManager.buildSessionContext (...:529:4947)
     at createRuntime (...:1239:14996)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate a session with 150k entries after a compaction:

```sh
node -e '
const fs=require("fs"),t=new Date().toISOString();
const
L=[{type:"session",version:3,id:"00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001",timestamp:t,cwd:process.cwd()},

{type:"message",id:"u1",parentId:null,timestamp:t,message:{role:"user",content:[{type:"text",text:"hi"}
],timestamp:Date.now()}},

{type:"compaction",id:"c1",parentId:"u1",timestamp:t,summary:"s",firstKeptEntryId:"u1",tokensBefore:10}
];
let p="c1";for(let
i=0;i<150000;i++){L.push({type:"custom",customType:"repro",data:{},id:"x"+i,parentId:p,timestamp:t});p=
"x"+i}
fs.writeFileSync("big.jsonl",L.map(x=>JSON.stringify(x)).join("\n")+"\n")'
```

2. Run `pi -ne --session ./big.jsonl`
3. Pi exits with the RangeError above. With 50k entries, the same file loads fine. 

### Expected behavior

The session loads. The number of entries should not be limited by the call stack. Appending in a
loop, or using `concat`, fixes it:

```typescript
for (const entry of path.slice(compactionIdx + 1)) contextEntries.push(entry); 
```

### Version

pi 1.5.2, Node v26.12.1, macOS 26.6.2

issues.title: MCP HTTP resumes response streams after tool calls are cancelled or time out
issues.body:
### What happened?

MCP Streamable HTTP continues resuming a tool's response stream after the tool call has been cancelled or timed out. The caller has already received `AbortError` or `McpTimeoutError`, and the server has received `notifications/cancelled`, but Pi still starts new resumption GETs. A late result then produces:

```text
Received response for unknown MCP request 2
```

Each test made only one `tools/call` POST. This is unnecessary response-stream recovery, not repeated tool execution.

### Steps to reproduce

Using the real `McpClient` and `StreamableHttpTransport` with a local HTTP fixture:

1. Complete MCP initialization. Set `openGetStream: false` to isolate response resumption from the independent notification stream.
2. Start `client.callTool()`.
3. Return a complete SSE priming event, then end the response normally:

   ```text
   id: initial
   retry: 100
   data:

   ```

4. Abort the call before its first resumption, or set `timeoutMs: 40`.
5. Record call settlement, cancellation notifications, and subsequent GETs. Have the fixture return further priming events on the first two GETs and the original result on the third.

Three runs against the unmodified implementation gave the same results:

| Scenario | Call outcome | New resumption GETs after settlement | Late error |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Abort | `AbortError` | 3 | Unknown request |
| Timeout | `McpTimeoutError` | 3 | Unknown request |
| No cancellation | Success after resumption | 0 | None |
| Close the whole connection | `McpConnectionClosedError` | 0 | None |

The three GETs reflect the fixture's response sequence, not a universal retry count. A subsequent `ping` succeeds after both abort and timeout. Cancellation is best-effort on the server; the problem here is that the client initiates new recovery requests after local cancellation has completed.

These are local HTTP integration tests without model APIs or external services, not full Pi TUI or third-party-server tests.

### Expected behavior

Stop recovery for an abandoned request without closing the shared transport or disrupting other calls and the independent notification stream.

In `client.ts`, removing the pending request aborts its send controller. However, `streamable-http.ts` starts `consumeResponseStream()` without that signal; its recovery loop checks whether the result arrived or the transport closed, not whether the request ended.

I plan to propagate request cancellation through the response stream's lifecycle:

- End the reconnect wait and prevent later resumption GETs.
- Stop the request's active response reader or resumption GET and release its resources.
- Avoid dispatching late results or synthetic errors for the removed request.
- Preserve other concurrent requests and the notification stream.

A temporary copy with cancellation checks before resumption reduced subsequent GETs from 3 to 0 for abort and timeout, removed the late errors, and preserved successful normal resumption. This validates the cause, but is not a complete fix: cancellation during an active read or an already-started GET still needs coverage.

I will add regression tests for normal resumption, cancellation during backoff and active reads, timeout, concurrent-request isolation, and full transport close. Assertions will use request traces and resource completion rather than precise timing thresholds.

I am confident I can complete this focused implementation and its regression tests. Would you be willing to give this work an `lgtm` so I can submit the PR?

### Version

Source commit `58c0b02ce552adab76014e7ed712ab7981359aa8`; Node.js 24.20.0; macOS. Dynamic tests used that local revision. Upstream commit `676af1d777ef6f04b6bc8daf4cf3b9b1799cff4d` still has the same missing signal propagation (source inspection only).

issues.title: openai-codex SSE retries a non-retryable HTTP error when provider retries are enabled

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
# openai-codex SSE retries a non-retryable HTTP error when provider retries are enabled

### What happened?

`openai-codex-responses` retries terminal HTTP errors on the SSE transport. With `retry.provider.maxRetries = 3`, a 400 response is sent four times with 1s/2s/4s backoff before the error reaches the caller.

The retry loop in `packages/ai/src/api/openai-codex-responses.ts` parses a non-retryable response and throws the friendly error inside the same `try` whose `catch` retries transport failures:

```ts
const info = await parseErrorResponse(fakeResponse);
throw new Error(info.friendlyMessage || info.message); // caught below
} catch (error) {
  // Network errors are retryable
  if (attempt < maxRetries && ...) {
    await sleep(delayMs, options?.signal);
    continue;
  }
```

The catch cannot distinguish this deliberate terminal error from a network error. It re-sends the same request until the attempts are exhausted. The `usage limit` string check in the same condition handles one symptom of this misclassification.

This is not specific to 400. A 401, 403, or 404 takes the same path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `retry.provider.maxRetries` to `3` in `settings.json`:

   ```json
   { "retry": { "provider": { "maxRetries": 3 } } }
   ```

2. Use the `openai-codex` provider with the SSE transport.
3. Return HTTP 400 with `{"error":{"code":"invalid_request_error","message":"bad request"}}` from the responses endpoint.

Actual: four POST requests, then `bad request`.
Expected: one POST request, then `bad request`.

A focused test with a mocked `fetch` makes 4 calls on commit `21e4cb80d`; it makes 1 call with the fix.

### Expected behavior

A terminal HTTP status should surface immediately and not re-enter the transport retry branch. Provider retries should only cover transport failures and retryable statuses.

I'd be happy to submit a minimal fix and regression test, pending maintainer approval.

### Version

1.5.2 / source commit `21e4cb80d`; Node.js 24.20.0; macOS.

issues.title: Aborting during tool execution leaves unanswered tool calls in the session
issues.body:
### What happened?

When I abort while a batch of tools is running, the tool calls after the abort point never get a result. The ones that already started are answered (real results or "Operation aborted"), the tail just disappears from history. No error is shown.

Both executeToolCallsSequential and executeToolCallsParallel in packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts break out of their loop on abort and skip the remaining calls.

Requests built afterwards are padded by closePendingToolCalls (packages/ai/src/api/transform-messages.ts) with a "No result provided" error, so the model never learns the tools were aborted, it just sees a generic error for calls it did make. The gap in the session file is permanent, and anything reading session entries directly (compaction, external tooling) has to cope with it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne`, any model with tools
2. ask for a batch of slow calls, e.g. run `sleep 10` three times
3. press Esc while the first one runs
4. quit and check the session jsonl: `tool_use` with no `tool_result` after it

### Expected behavior

The skipped calls should get an error `tool_result` ("Operation aborted") recorded in history, same as the started ones.

I have a fix with tests ready and would like to send a PR once this is approved.

Related: #9124 is the same symptom on the dispose/exit path (fix pending in #9126), this is the mid-session abort path. #8378 asked for resuming interrupted turns, a different thing.

issues.title: pi-ai: wire stream timeoutMs on google-vertex and classify mid-stream ECONNRESET / timeout aborts as retryable
issues.body:
## Summary

While running multi-turn coding agent evaluations on `google-vertex` (`@earendil-works/pi-ai@1.5.2` + `@earendil-works/pi-durable@1.5.2`), we found three related issues in `pi-ai` that cause stalled or reset Vertex AI streams to either hang indefinitely or fail without triggering `retryAssistantCall` / Pi Durable's `GenerationTask` retry loop:

### 1. `google-vertex` (and `google-generative-ai`) ignores `options.timeoutMs`
- `StreamOptions` / `SimpleStreamOptions` (and `pi-durable`'s `HarnessSettings.stream.timeoutMs`) pass `timeoutMs` into `stream` / `streamSimple`.
- However, `packages/ai/src/api/google-vertex.ts` (`buildParams`) never reads `options.timeoutMs`, nor does the `for await (const chunk of googleStream)` loop enforce a per-chunk idle timeout.
- When Vertex AI stalls mid-SSE stream (especially after a transient connection drop under load), `for await (const chunk of googleStream)` hangs indefinitely until the caller's outer process/task timeout kills the entire run.

### 2. Timeout aborts via `config.abortSignal` are not classified as retryable
- If a caller attaches `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` to `config.abortSignal` (via `onPayload` / `beforeProviderRequest`), `@google/genai` catches the abort and throws `Error: This operation was aborted` (stripping `TimeoutError`).
- If `options.signal` itself is aborted by a timeout, `google-vertex.ts` sets `output.stopReason = options?.signal?.aborted ? "aborted" : "error"`, which is treated as a user cancellation and never retried.
- Even when `stopReason === "error"`, `"This operation was aborted"` does not match `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN` in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts`, so `isRetryableAssistantError` returns `false`.

### 3. Bare `ECONNRESET` / `EPIPE` / `ETIMEDOUT` error strings in `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN`
- `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN` in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts` matches `"fetch failed"`, `"connection.?refused"`, and `"connection.?lost"`, but does not include `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, `ETIMEDOUT`, or `ECONNABORTED`. When a mid-stream socket reset surfaces without the `fetch failed` prefix (e.g. `read ECONNRESET`), `isRetryableAssistantError` returns `false`.

## Proposed Fix
1. Enforce a per-chunk stream idle timeout from `options.timeoutMs` in `google-vertex` / `google-generative-ai` that aborts the underlying `@google/genai` request while recording `stopReason: "error"` and `errorMessage: "Request timed out after <N>ms"` (when the caller's own `options.signal` was not aborted).
2. Add `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, `ETIMEDOUT`, and `ECONNABORTED` to `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN` in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts`.

issues.title: Steering messages re-injected at every turn boundary instead of consumed once

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
# Steering messages are re-injected at every turn boundary instead of consumed once

## Description

A single queued steering message is re-delivered into the model context at *every* subsequent turn boundary while a run is in progress, instead of being consumed after first delivery. A one-off note ("you can use root SSH if needed") appeared as a user turn repeatedly over a span of several hours and dozens of tool-call turns, without ever being removed from the queue.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a run that involves many tool calls (a long multi-step task).
2. While it's running, queue **one** steering message (e.g. "note: X").
3. Observe the agent's subsequent turns: the steering text is present in the model context as a user message at *every* turn boundary, not just the first one after it was queued.
4. Inspect the session file (`~/.pi/agent/sessions/.../....jsonl`): the steering message does not appear as a persisted user message at all (only genuine user input is recorded). In the repro session, exactly 20 user messages were persisted; the re-injected steering note appears in none of them, despite being visible to the model across many turns.

## Expected behavior

Per `docs/how-pi-works.md`: *"Steering messages enter after the current assistant turn."* A single queued steering message should be delivered **once** and then removed from the queue (consumed on first delivery).

## Suggested fix / options

- **Consume on delivery**: dequeue the steering message when it enters context.
- **TTL**: drop queued steering messages after a configurable age, so a stale note can't linger and re-appear hours later (contradictory or outdated steering is worse than noise).
- Optionally persist steering messages to the session with a distinguishing type so they're auditable.

## Impact

Low severity: it's context noise that makes the model repeatedly believe the user is re-emphasizing something ("I keep thinking I'm being told this"). But a stale steering note re-appearing hours later (e.g. "use the old API key", "ignore the tests") could actively mislead the agent mid-task, and each re-injection also adds tokens to every request.

## Version

pi 1.5.2 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`)

issues.title: Streaming assistant output renders late and arrives in large chunks: every delta triggers a full O(n²) markdown re-render on the synchronous event path
issues.body:
# Title: Streaming UI falls behind the LLM (bulk text output, long `working...`) due to per-delta full markdown re-render on the synchronous event path

## Summary

With streaming providers (verified with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint delivering ~25 SSE chunks/s), the TUI visually falls behind the model: `working...` persists much longer than the model's actual response time, and the assistant message appears to arrive in large bursts instead of streaming from the first token.

## Root cause: every delta triggers a full synchronous re-render

For **every** `message_update` delta:

1. `agent-loop.ts` emits one `message_update` per `text_delta`/`thinking_delta` (no coalescing).
2. `interactive-mode.ts` `case "message_update"` synchronously calls `streamingComponent.updateContent(message, true)` + `requestRender()`.
3. `assistant-message.ts` `updateContent` clears the container and rebuilds a new `Markdown` component for every text block.
4. `markdown.ts` — the render cache only hits when `cachedText === text`, which is never true while streaming, so each delta runs a full `marked.lexer()` parse of the entire accumulated message.

Cost per delta is O(total message length) → O(n²) over a response. All of this runs synchronously in the event-handler path (the tui's 16ms render throttle does not cover it).

## Consequence beyond cosmetics: it starves the event loop's macrotask phases

Because the delta → updateContent → render chain runs as continuous synchronous/microtask work, the event loop rarely reaches poll/timer phases while deltas are flowing. This has a serious side effect: **an abort requested during active streaming does not take effect until the provider finishes the response naturally** (see the companion issue about Esc not stopping requests). Inserting macrotask boundaries in the update path (e.g. coalescing updates with `setTimeout`) empirically restores prompt abort behavior.

## Suggested fix

Coalesce `message_update` handling: store the latest message and apply `updateContent` at most once per interval (e.g. 50–100ms) via a timer, flushing on `message_end`. This both fixes the O(n²) rendering cost and yields to the event loop so I/O (including aborts) is processed during streaming. Alternatively, make `AssistantMessageComponent.updateContent` incremental.

Verified on 0.84.4 (current main): with an 80ms coalescing patch the UI streams smoothly and aborts become responsive; without it, output visibly lags and arrives in chunks.

issues.title: Theme switch leaves stale colors in header, tree labels, and markdown default-style prefix (0.84.2)
issues.body:
### Environment
- pi 0.84.2 (npm), Linux x86_64, tmux 3.4 (also reproducible outside tmux), TERM=xterm-256color

### Symptom
Switching the theme in a running interactive session leaves **stale old-theme colors** in parts of the screen. The new theme applies to most of the UI, but these regions keep the previous theme's colors until pi restarts:

1. **Top chrome**: the `pi v0.84.2` logo/version line, the compact hint bar (`escape interrupt · ctrl+c/ctrl+d clear/exit · …`), and the onboarding hint lines.
2. **Session tree labels**: `[Context]`, `[Themes]` group headers and item names keep old colors.
3. **Transcript**: messages that use a default text style emit a *stale color prefix*. In the pty capture the old foreground SGR is emitted immediately followed by the new-theme SGR (e.g. `38;2;205;214;244m` + `38;2;101;123;131m`), i.e. an old-color sequence is re-emitted forever.

The bug reproduces both via `/settings` → Theme (apply) and via theme-file hot reload (same code path: `setTheme` → `onThemeChange` → `ui.invalidate()`).

### Root cause (two mechanisms)
1. **`Markdown.getDefaultStylePrefix()` cache never invalidated** (`packages/tui/src/components/markdown.ts`): the style prefix is computed from the theme at first render and stored in `defaultStylePrefix`. `invalidate()` clears `cachedText/cachedWidth/cachedLines` but **not** `defaultStylePrefix`, so the old theme's SGR prefix is reused after a theme switch.
2. **Header + tree label strings built once with theme colors**: `builtInHeader` (`ExpandableText`) is constructed once in `interactive-mode.ts` with `theme.fg(...)` already applied to the string; on theme change `Text.invalidate()` clears the wrap cache but the `text` field still contains the old SGR codes, so the re-render produces identical (old-colored) lines and the differential renderer skips them. Tree entry labels are likewise colorized at tree-build time and not rebuilt on theme change.

### Reproduction (headless pty)
- Copy a session into a sandboxed `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, copy the active theme to `glitch-test.json`.
- Run `pi --session <id> --use-theme glitch-test` in a pty (110×40), accept the trust prompt.
- After the initial render, overwrite `glitch-test.json` with a different palette (name unchanged) → hot reload applies the new theme.
- In the last rendered frame after the switch: **35 old-palette SGR occurrences across 15 lines** remain (title line, hint lines, tree rows, and ~11 transcript lines), while 9119 occurrences use the new palette.

Repro script: [repro.py](https://gist.github.com/) — happy to attach; it drives everything automatically and parses SGR truecolor codes per line.

### Expected
After a theme switch, the very next frame should contain zero colors from the previous theme.

### Notes
- The stale transcript spans are exactly the `defaultStylePrefix` artifact (old SGR immediately followed by new SGR on the same span).
- Header staleness self-heals if the startup help is expanded/collapsed (`ctrl+o`), because `setExpanded` rebuilds the text via `theme.fg` — confirming the baked-string diagnosis.

issues.title: Anthropic message threads: thinking blocks dropped (prefix_binding_mismatch) on every thread_not_found resend after a string-typed numeric tool arg
issues.body:
### What happened?

With Anthropic message threads on (default for `api.anthropic.com` since 1.5.1), every full resend after a `thread_not_found` fallback warns:

```
Anthropic dropped 3 thinking blocks: prefix_binding_mismatch at messages.5.content.0; ...
```

The same blocks are dropped again on every later fallback. In one session that was 7 times, once per idle gap over ~5 min. Requests that continue a thread never show it.

What the session shows:

- Early in the session the model called `bash` with `timeout: "20"` (a string; the schema says number). It was the only string-typed numeric argument in that session.
- The dropped blocks are exactly the thinking blocks generated in that thread after that tool call. The thinking before it is kept.
- On the first fallback resend, cache read stopped at that assistant message (31,144 tokens vs 43,935 on the last request before the gap). Later fallbacks read the full prior prefix, so nothing new diverges. The original blocks are just dropped again each time.
- Two other sessions show the same pattern, each right after a string `timeout` in a bash call.

Hypothesis (I did not capture the request payload): pi keeps the parsed arguments as the model sent them (`"20"`) and replays them as `tool_use.input`. `validateToolArguments` only coerces a copy (`pi-ai/dist/utils/validation.js`). The server's thread copy of that turn seems to differ from what pi replays (maybe the input normalized to the schema type, maybe something else), so thinking bound inside the thread no longer matches the prefix on a full resend.

Impact is low: some old reasoning is lost, plus an extra 404 round trip per idle gap. But the warning repeats for the rest of the session.

Possible workaround (not tested): `models.json` → `providers.anthropic.compat.supportsMessageThreads: false`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Anthropic model with thinking, threads on (default).
2. Get the model to call `bash` with a string `timeout` (e.g. `"20"`), then do a couple more thinking + tool turns.
3. Stay idle for more than 5 minutes, then send another message.
4. The resend after `thread_not_found` reports `prefix_binding_mismatch` drops, and so does every later idle resend.

I haven't re-run this with `pi -ne` or built a minimal repro yet.

### Expected behavior

A full resend after a thread fallback should match what the server bound in the thread, so no thinking is dropped. That could mean storing the tool input the same way the server does (e.g. the schema-coerced args) or replaying it byte for byte. At minimum, the same drop shouldn't repeat on every fallback.

### Version

pi 1.5.2 (macOS), claude-sonnet-5-5, thinking high

issues.title: Add packages.minimumReleaseAge for extension install and update

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Make the extension side of the #4929 decision real and uniform: add `packages.minimumReleaseAge` (days), applied when pi installs and updates extension packages, and honoured by the update check so the startup banner stops advertising versions that install will not select.

Escape hatches: `0` disables it, `packages.minimumReleaseAgeExclude` for named packages that should track fresh, and `--min-release-age=0` on `pi install` / `pi update --extensions`. Self-update stays opted out; this is extensions only.

The default value is a policy call, not an implementation one — same plumbing at any number. Current defaults in the wild: npm 11 and bun 0, pnpm 1440 minutes (1 day), Yarn 4.12+ `"1w"`, Dependabot cooldown and Renovate's `security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm` preset 3 days. I'd argue for matching the automated updaters at 3, or pnpm at 1 if you want the smallest behaviour change. Dependabot exempts security updates from its cooldown; pi has no notion of a security release, so the exclude list is the equivalent.

### Why?

#4929 concluded "extensions honor minimum age". Today that only holds by accident of which package manager is on PATH, and the update check contradicts it: the same pi, same extensions, gets no window at all on npm/bun and a week on Yarn.

Extension packages run in-process with pi's full trust, which is a reason to own this number rather than inherit it.

The check side is worse: `npmHasAvailableUpdate` calls `npm view <pkg> version`, which ignores age gates, while the following `npm install <pkg>@latest` obeys them. pi announces an update, installs nothing, then prints "still X (registry reports Y)". Reported in #7741, #8373, #9029, #8792; #6126 proposed the settings-based version of this and was closed `no-action`.

The `-e` temporary-source refresh path (`core/package-manager.ts`, `npmHasAvailableUpdate` then `installNpm …@latest`) is already an automatic extension update, and it is ungated for npm/bun.

### How? (optional)

Forward the setting to the manager in its own unit instead of resolving versions in pi, so transitive deps are covered: npm `--min-release-age=<d>`, pnpm `--config.minimumReleaseAge=<d*1440>`, bun `--minimum-release-age=<d*86400>`, Yarn `npmMinimalAgeGate` (`<d>d`). Yarn is the one to check: its global config may need a different spawn than `yarn global add`.

For the check, filter registry `time` against the cutoff before picking the target version. PR #8377 did this by reading npm's effective `before` from `npm config list`; the same shape works for the other managers.

I want to implement this myself. Asking for `lgtm` before opening a PR.
