issues.title: Transient socket errors (ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT/EPIPE) during streaming abort the whole turn instead of retrying
issues.body:
### What happened?

A one-second blip during a streamed provider turn kills the whole run instead of retrying. The retry classifier in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts` matches message text like "fetch failed", "socket hang up", "timed out" — but Node's bare socket error codes don't match any rule: `read ECONNRESET`, `connect ETIMEDOUT 140.82.113.3:443`, `write EPIPE`. `ETIMEDOUT` contains "TIMEDOUT", not "timeout", and the `timed? out` rule needs a space, so nothing hits. `retryAssistantCall` returns the error and the task dies. Same thing as point 3 in #12070.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a long turn against any streaming provider
2. Drop the network for a second mid-stream (or have the edge close the connection): `read ECONNRESET`
3. Turn fails with the raw socket error — no retry, no backoff

### Expected behavior

Transient transport codes (ECONNRESET / ECONNABORTED / ETIMEDOUT / EPIPE) should retry with backoff. `ECONNREFUSED` should stay non-retryable (nothing is listening, retrying the same request is pointless), and Esc-aborts should stay non-retryable too.

### Version

0.0.3, main @ 275dde4

Fix is written and tested (30 lines, `retry.ts` + its tests, 49 tests pass incl. 3 non-retry cases). It sat in #12127 which the gate auto-closed. I'll bring it back as soon as this gets a look.

issues.body:
### What happened?

When I quit pi from the TUI (double Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D or /quit), the terminal goes back to the shell, but the process keeps running. Its detached subagent children stay alive too. I found 6 of these at the same time on one machine, the oldest one running for over 3 days.

`kill -TERM` kills them right away, so the signal path works. Only the interactive quit hangs.

From what I see in the code (main):

- In `interactive-mode.ts`, the interactive branch of `shutdown()` stops the TUI and then awaits `runtimeHost.dispose()` (around L4506).
- `dispose()` emits `session_shutdown`, and `runner.emit()` (`runner.ts:1103`) awaits each handler one by one, with no timeout.
- If one handler never resolves, `emit` never returns, so `process.exit(0)` (L4513) is never reached. Handlers after it, like `runner.cancelAll`, never run either.
- `killTrackedDetachedChildren()` is only called on the signal / uncaught paths (L4519, L4549, L4586), not on a normal quit, so the children survive.

I haven't confirmed which handler hangs. My best guess is the MCP connection teardown.

(English is not my first language, I used AI to help translate this.)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `pi`
2. Quit with Ctrl-D (same with double Ctrl-C or `/quit`)
3. The shell prompt comes back, but the process is still there:

```
$ ps -Ao pid,etime,command | grep 'bin/gentle-shell'
15330  03-03:29:40  node .../gentle-shell
45676     22:20:13  node .../gentle-shell
86430     02:42:59  node .../gentle-shell
```

It happened 3 times in the same day. `kill -TERM 15330 45676 86430` kills all of them immediately.

### Expected behavior

The process exits on quit. The shell prompt should come back only after the process is gone, and `ps` should show nothing left behind.

| Component | Version |
| --- | --- |
| pi (binary) | 1.5.2 |
| pi core where observed | 1.4.0 (inside gentle-shell 4.5.0) |
| pi core, same code pattern checked | 1.5.0 (vendored by gentle-pi 4.7.0) |
| gentle-ai | 4.4.0 |

### Version

pi binary 1.5.2

issues.title: Expose `ctx.executeTool()` (bounded) to event handlers, at least `before_agent_start`

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Let event handlers — at minimum `before_agent_start` — call tools the way tool `execute()` and command handlers already can: expose `ctx.tools` and a `ctx.executeTool()` on the handler context (bounded, see How).

### Why?

Today the docs are explicit: "All handlers receive `ctx: ExtensionContext`. Tool `execute()` receives `ExtensionToolContext`, which adds `ctx.tools` and `ctx.executeTool()`" — and `before_agent_start` gets the base context. So the one hook that runs *before the model wakes up* is the only context that cannot call a tool. That is exactly where fetching data deterministically matters most: pre-injecting context instead of hoping the model remembers to fire off an MCP tool.

Without it, every extension that needs pre-turn data goes around Pi's pipeline, three ways, all bad:

- spawn its own MCP client: extra processes + handshake every session. Measured on my
  side (Windows, stdio server): 0.5–0.7 s spawn+initialize, and the proxy chain costs
  ~84 MB private per session;
- speak the backend's private protocol directly: fast, but it breaks the day that
  undocumented protocol changes;
- shell out to a CLI and lose the structured result.

All three skip what `executeTool` already enforces: argument validation, `tool_call` / `tool_result` handlers, permission gates, and the bounded `nestedCalls` records. So the current workaround is not just inconvenient — it moves extension calls *out* of the audited pipeline.

### How? (optional)

Reuse what exists — nested calls already validate arguments, run the `tool_call`/`tool_result` handlers, carry `parentToolCallId`, and keep the bounded `nestedCalls` record. The open design questions I see, all solvable with existing pieces:

- servers may still be connecting when the hook runs; the MCP extension already solves late-registering with `reachesTools` in `tool_call`, so the same semantics would let a handler declare what it needs and wait within the per-server timeout Pi already supports;
- a slow server must not stall every prompt: bound it (per-call timeout / overall hook budget);
- optionally scope it: read-only-hint tools only, or an explicit opt-in on the server config.

issues.title: A mid-run change to the selected tool set moves the head of the system prompt and re-bills the conversation
Terminal color replies are matched per read chunk, so an emulator that answers in one write types them into the editor

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## What happens

Starting pi inside a terminal emulator that answers its color queries in a single write leaves escape junk in the editor:

```
b:7676/7676/7676d
```

That is the tail of the `OSC 4` reply for palette entry 8 (`#767676`; on another run the same box showed `gb:e7e7/4848/5656` for entry 9). The same pi in Windows Terminal is clean.

## Why

`pi-tui` asks for the colors on startup (`TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY`: `OSC 10;?`, `OSC 11;?`, 16 × `OSC 4;N;?`, then `CSI c`) and matches the replies against whole read chunks:

- `dist/terminal-colors.js`: `/^\x1b\](?:(1[01])|4;(\d{1,3}));([^\x07\x1b]*)(?:\x07|\x1b\\)$/i`
- `dist/tui.js`: `DEVICE_ATTRIBUTES_RESPONSE_PATTERN = /^\x1b\[\?[\d;]*c$/`

A terminal may answer all of that in one write, and a pty then delivers it as one read. Measured in our emulator:

```
chunk 1 +14ms len=511 "\x1b]10;rgb:cccc/cccc/cccc\x1b\\\x1b]11;rgb:0c0c/0c0c/0c0c\x1b\\\x1b]4;0;…\x1b\\…\x1b[?61;4;6;7;14;21;22;23;24;28;32;42;52c"
done, 1 chunks in 2508ms
```

Nothing matches, so the bytes fall through to `handleInput` as typing and the editor receives them.

It is worse on Windows: ConPTY parses what the terminal writes into its input pipe and keeps only what it can turn into keys — text, control bytes, CSI. An `OSC` is dropped, so the replies never arrive at all, and pi silently uses its own colors. (Measured: `S1` arrives, the `OSC 4` reply right after it does not; `abc` + `OSC 4` + `def` arrives as `abcdef`; `CSI A` and `\x03` do arrive.)

## Suggested fix

Do not treat a read boundary as a message boundary. Accumulate the bytes that do not parse as a key and split replies on their own terminators (BEL / ST for OSC, `c` for DA1), then match each piece — a handful of lines in the query path. That makes color detection work on every terminal, including ones that batch, and also makes the query robust when the reply is cut in half by the read.

## Environment

- pi: latest (2026-11-13), Windows 11, inside a terminal built on libghostty-vt over ConPTY
- Same pi in Windows Terminal: no junk

(For reference: the terminal side was patched to answer replies one per write, which fixes it here, but the read-chunk assumption will still bite other emulators — e.g. any that write all replies at once.)

issues.title: P2 drops WebSocket close code 1009 for oversized frames

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

P2's `/chord` socket closes oversized messages with `1006` instead of `1009`, so clients cannot distinguish a rejected large message from a broken connection. `limitedSocket()` terminates the socket on every error, interrupting the close handshake that `ws` has already started.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a loopback `WebSocketServer` with `maxPayload: MAX_CLIENT_FRAME` and wrap accepted sockets with P2's `limitedSocket()`.
2. Send a binary message containing `MAX_CLIENT_FRAME + 1` bytes (1,048,577 bytes).
3. Observe the client's close code: `1006`.

The existing oversized-message case in `apps/p2/test/p2/socket-limits.test.ts` already expects `1009`. This reproduction uses only `ws` and `limitedSocket()`, without extensions or model calls.

### Expected behavior

The client should receive `1009`. Skipping `terminate()` when `readyState === CLOSING` preserves the handshake; Chord's HTTP upgrades implementation already uses this guard. Local assertions returned `1006` before the change and `1009` after it.

I can submit this small fix after maintainer contribution approval (`lgtm`).

### Version

Reproduced on main `d36266e06669c6991a7c9509d1da04d18d30378d`; the affected source is unchanged on current main `275dde410065080d291de45fbe2110272d10de23`. Node 26.13.1, ws 8.21.0, macOS.

The GitHub Copilot catalog hardcoded `supportsReasoningEffort: false` for its Gemini and Kimi models, so the thinking level was never sent. It now comes from models.dev. prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report diagnostics that appear on session replacement
prs.body:
Related to #11264. Complements #11973.

## Problem

`main.ts`'s runtime factory runs at startup and again on every session replacement: `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, import, RPC `new_session`/`switch_session`/`fork`, and extension `ctx.newSession()`/`switchSession()`/`fork()`. It returns diagnostics: settings errors, project-trust warnings, extension load errors and warnings, session option warnings, and (since #11973) model scope warnings. `AgentSessionRuntime` stores them in `runtime.diagnostics`, but only `main.ts` reads that list, once at startup. After a replacement, the new diagnostics are discarded.

Trace (RPC, before this change):

1. Start `pi --mode rpc` with `enabledModels: ["fake/fake-model"]`. No warning.
2. Change settings to `["fake/fake-model", "github-copilot/missing-model"]`.
3. Send `new_session`. It succeeds, with nothing on stderr and no event.

The same happens with `/new` in the TUI, and when `/resume` moves to another project whose extensions fail to load or whose settings are invalid.

## Fix

- `AgentSessionRuntime.takeUnreportedDiagnostics()` returns the current runtime's diagnostics that were not reported yet and marks them reported. The constructor marks the first runtime's diagnostics reported, because the host shows those at startup.
- Each mode calls it in its rebind callback, which runs after every replacement:
  - interactive: in the chat, like startup diagnostics (shared `showRuntimeDiagnostics()`)
  - print/JSON and RPC: stderr, in the CLI's existing format. `main.ts`'s `reportDiagnostics()` moved to `modes/diagnostics-stderr.ts` so the modes can share it. RPC never writes these to stdout.

De-duplication: a diagnostic with the same type and message as one already reported (at startup or after an earlier replacement) is not repeated. An unchanged settings warning is not shown again on every `/new`. A problem that is fixed and then reappears with the same text is not shown again either; that seemed preferable to repeating every warning.

The new method is an addition to the exported `AgentSessionRuntime` class. Nothing existing changes shape.

## Verification

| Mode | Check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RPC | `test/rpc-replacement-diagnostics.test.ts`: valid settings, `new_session`, add a bad pattern, `new_session` twice | Warning on stderr exactly once, never on stdout. Fails on main (zero warnings). |
| Runtime | `test/agent-session-runtime-diagnostics.test.ts`: startup diagnostics not returned, a new one returned once after `newSession()`, unchanged ones not repeated | Passes. Fails on main. |
| Interactive, regular | tmux: start with valid settings, add a bad pattern, `/new`, `/new` | First `/new` shows `Warning: No models match pattern "github-copilot/nope"` in the chat above "New session started". The second does not repeat it. Screen clean. |
| Interactive, fullscreen | Same | Same |
| Print/JSON | Same callback and code path as RPC | Covered by code review only. No print-mode replacement test exists, since it needs an extension that replaces the session. |

Existing tests for print mode, RPC semantics, runtime events, #2860 and #11973 pass. `npm run check` passes.

Not covered: `/reload` does not create a new runtime, so it is unaffected. Interactive mode also shows `modelFallbackMessage` only at startup; that is left as is.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): don't crash when rendering very large self-rendered tool results
prs.body:
`ToolExecutionComponent.render()` added the rendered lines of tools that draw themselves (`renderShell: "self"`, which includes the built-in `edit` tool) with `lines.push(...contentLines)`. A large edit diff can wrap to hundreds of thousands of display lines. One example is an edit to a file with a multi-megabyte line, such as exported HTML. Spreading that many lines into a single call goes over V8's limit on function arguments, so pi exited with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. The diff is saved in the session, so the crash came back every time that session was resumed.

This change appends the lines in a loop instead, the same way `Container.render` in pi-tui already does. Nothing changes in what is rendered or saved.

Testing:
- I made a session file whose edit result has a diff with two lines of about 12 MB each and opened it with `pi -ne --session <file>` at 100 columns. Before the fix pi crashed in `ToolExecutionComponent.render` on load. After the fix the session opens and accepts input.
- `npm run check`: this change adds no errors. The only errors are type errors in pi-ai tests, which fail the same way on the base commit.

Fixes #8036

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(coding-agent,durable): keep read's non-vision image warning out of what the model gets
prs.body:
When `read` loaded an image while a text-only model was selected, it appended `[Current model does not support images. The image will be omitted from this request.]` to the tool result's text. That text is saved in the session. After switching to a vision model, the next request sent the image together with this note, which was no longer true.

The model doesn't need the note. When a request is built, pi-ai's `downgradeUnsupportedImages` already replaces tool-result images with `(tool image omitted: model does not support images)` for models without image input. The note was mainly a hint for the user, and the read renderer only showed it after the result was expanded.

This change:
- **coding-agent `read`:**
  - The result text no longer mentions the model's image support.
  - When the selected model has no image input, the tool records that model's id in `details.imageUnsupportedByModel`. `details` is shown in the TUI but never sent to the model.
- **read renderer:** draws `[<model> does not support images; it saw a placeholder instead]` from that field, both collapsed and expanded. The warning names the model that read the image, so it stays accurate after a model switch.
- **durable `read`:** it had the same problem as an `info` diagnostic ("The current model does not support images; it sees a placeholder instead."). Diagnostics are rendered into the tool result the model sees, so this diagnostic and its unused `vision` field are removed, and the README paragraph is updated.

Both packages get changelog entries.

Left unchanged:
- The stored image is still resized with the `inputLimits.images.resize` of the model selected when it was read. That adds no false text to the session.
- The HTML export draws read results from their text, so it no longer shows the warning.

**Testing**
- `packages/coding-agent/test/tools.test.ts`: new test. It reads a PNG with a text-only `ctx.model` and checks:
  - the text is exactly `Read image file [image/png]` and the image block is kept;
  - the real `ToolExecutionComponent` shows the warning, collapsed and expanded.

  It fails without the source change.
- `packages/durable/test/tools-images.test.ts`: now expects only `Read image file [image/png].` and checks that the image is kept.
- `npm run check` passes. Both test files pass (114 and 34 tests).

Fixes #12131

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(ai): retry provider errors that report only a Node socket error code
prs.body:
When a provider call failed with an error whose message held only a Node socket error code, pi did not retry it. Examples are `read ECONNRESET`, `write EPIPE`, and `connect ETIMEDOUT 140.82.113.3:443`. None of these matched `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN` in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts`. `ETIMEDOUT` has no space, so `timed? out` misses it. As a result `isRetryableAssistantError` returned false and the turn ended.

**When this happens:** the case I confirmed is Amazon Bedrock. The AWS SDK's HTTP handler (`@smithy/node-http-handler` on `node:https`) passes Node's socket error through unchanged. That error has no `cause`, so `formatBedrockError` reports just `read ECONNRESET` when the connection is reset before a response arrives.

The fetch-based APIs were already retried. Their SDKs wrap the socket error, and `withCauseDetail` adds the code after the wrapper text:

| API | Reset before the response | Reset mid-stream |
|---|---|---|
| anthropic-messages, openai-completions, openai-responses | `Connection error.: read ECONNRESET` | `terminated: read ECONNRESET` |
| google-generative-ai | `fetch failed: read ECONNRESET` | `terminated: read ECONNRESET` |
| mistral-conversations | `fetch failed` | `terminated` |

Extension providers that copy `error.message` straight into `errorMessage` can also produce a bare code.

**The change:** it adds `ECONNRESET`, `ECONNABORTED`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `ETIMEDOUT`, and `EPIPE`, plus Node's wording "connection reset by peer", to the transport section of the pattern.
- **No partial matches:** the codes have word-boundary guards, like the status-code rule, so a code inside a longer identifier does not match.
- **ECONNREFUSED is included on purpose:** the pattern already retries `connection.?refused`, and the node-fetch case "connect ECONNREFUSED" is already retryable. Leaving the bare code out would treat the two forms of the same error differently.

coding-agent and durable both use this shared classifier, so they get the fix with no other change. The Codex Responses transport already retries network exceptions on its own path.

Left unchanged: other socket codes such as `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ENETUNREACH`, and `UND_ERR_SOCKET` are still not retried. The codes match case-insensitively, like the rest of the pattern.

**Testing**
- `packages/ai/test/retry.test.ts`:
  - The six new forms (the five codes plus "connection reset by peer") now classify as retryable. These cases fail without the fix.
  - Three lookalike identifiers (`EXECONNRESET`, `ETIMEDOUTX`, `ERR_EPIPE_ID`) stay non-retryable.
- `node ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/retry.test.ts`: 49 passed.
- `npm run check`: passes.
- Pointed each built-in API at a local TCP server that resets the connection. That produced the messages above, and the Bedrock stream returned `errorMessage: "read ECONNRESET"`. `isRetryableAssistantError` on that message returns false on `main` and true with this change.

Fixes #12128

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): /copy skips turns that ended without an answer
prs.body:
Closes #12119.

**Problem.** `getLastAssistantText()` takes the last assistant message, skipping only aborted messages with no content (#351). Two common cases leave a last assistant message without text:

- After Esc during a tool call, the last messages are a tool-call-only message and an empty one.
- After a provider error, the last message is an empty error message.

So `/copy` says "No agent messages to copy yet." while the previous answer is on screen. RPC `get_last_assistant_text` returns `null` in the same cases.

**Fix.** Skip assistant messages without text whose turn did not end normally (`stopReason` other than `stop`: aborted, error, toolUse, length). This generalizes the existing aborted-and-empty check, in the same function.

A reply that ended normally stays the last reply, even without text. That keeps `/copy` from silently copying an older answer, and keeps the evals harness unchanged: it relies on an empty final reply giving no text to report "Agent run produced no assistant text."

The RPC doc for `get_last_assistant_text` notes the skipped messages.

**Validation** on main `d36266e066`:

- New `test/suite/regressions/12119-copy-after-abort-or-error.test.ts`, using the faux provider:
  - Esc during a tool call returns the previous answer.
  - A provider error returns the previous answer.
  - A normal reply without text still returns `undefined`.
  - The first two fail without the fix. The third passes before and after.
- These pass: `interactive-tui.test.ts`, `rpc.test.ts`, the 8409 abort regression, and `packages/evals` `harness.test.ts`.
- `npm run check` passes. In `./test.sh` the only failures are unrelated to this change:
  - The find tool tests fail because fd is not installed here, and the test config sets `PI_OFFLINE=1`, which prevents downloading it.
  - The pi-env tests need cargo, which is not installed here.
  - One `auth-storage` test also fails on main.

prs.title: fix(ai,coding-agent): make system the default instruction role in openai-completions
prs.body:
TLDR:
On chat-completions api, change the default instruction role from developer to system.

Inspired by: #12101 by @qoli

---
The trigger was #10741: Groq's qwen/qwen3.8-27b failed on the first message:
`400: minijinja: rendering failed: raise_exception: Unexpected message role.`

Problem: openai-completions sent the system messages of every reasoning model with the `developer` role unless the catalog turned it off. `developer` is OpenAI's role; many other hosts' chat templates reject it, as Groq's Qwen template does.

Every new OpenAI-compatible provider or reasoning model hit the same bug until someone added `supportsDeveloperRole: false` to the catalog; about 20 provider files carried that line. Nothing in models.dev says which role a model accepts, so the catalog could not get this right on its own.

Solution: detectCompat() now defaults supportsDeveloperRole to true only for api.openai.com. Every other host gets `system`. This applies to the initial system prompt and to mid-conversation system messages.

Built-in models whose role changes from developer to system:
- groq: 5 (gpt-oss and Qwen)
- xiaomi, xiaomi-token-plan-*: 9 MiMo models
- openrouter: 89 openai/* and anthropic/* models; 12 of them (newer GPT models) also support mid-conversation system messages (supportsMidConvoSystemMessages), which change role too All other built-in Chat Completions models already sent `system`.

Why the default is only api.openai.com:
- api.openai.com keeps `developer` because OpenAI documents it as the role for its reasoning models. In practice this rarely matters: the built-in OpenAI models all use the Responses API, so it only affects custom models that call OpenAI through openai-completions.
- Azure is excluded. Its built-in OpenAI models also use the Responses API; its only built-in Chat Completions model is DeepSeek, which needs `system`.
- OpenRouter is excluded: its Chat Completions reference accepts `system` ("System message for setting behavior") and `developer` with the same fields, and gives no reason to prefer `developer` for any model (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/chat/create-a-chat-completion). The openai/* and anthropic/* exception came in with #5309 without a reported need.
- compat.supportsDeveloperRole still overrides the default.
- The Responses API has its own setting and is unchanged.

The now-redundant `supportsDeveloperRole: false` lines are removed from the catalog and the llama extension.

How we checked it is safe: live requests to the affected hosts, each model given the same instruction once as `developer` and once as `system`:
- Groq qwen/qwen3.8-27b: developer 400, system OK. Groq gpt-oss-20b: both OK.
- Xiaomi mimo-v2.6-pro and mimo-v2.6-flash: both roles OK.
- OpenRouter openai/gpt-5-mini, openai/gpt-oss-20b, anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, moonshotai/kimi-k2.6, qwen/qwen3.6-plus, deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro: both roles OK.
- OpenRouter openai/gpt-5.4-mini and openai/gpt-5.5 with an instruction added mid-conversation: both roles OK.

Released clients: they fetch new catalogs from pi.dev and still default supportsDeveloperRole to true, so the removed `false` lines would make them send `developer` to hosts that reject it. MINIMUM_PI_VERSION is raised to 1.5.3 so they keep the last catalog published for them.

closes #10741 #12101

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): share the auth.json lock across symlinked paths
prs.body:
`FileAuthStorageBackend` locked `auth.json` with proper-lockfile and `realpath: false`, so the lock directory was `<path as given>.lock`. Reads and writes follow symlinks to the same real file, but each path alias got its own lock. For example, an agent dir whose `auth.json` is a symlink to a shared file used a different lock than the real file. Two pi processes could then enter the credential-modification section at the same time and refresh the same OAuth token concurrently.

This change drops `realpath: false` from the sync and async lock calls, so proper-lockfile resolves the path and every alias of the file uses one lock. Resolving the path needs the file to exist, which is already the case: `ensureFileExists()` runs before either lock is taken.

The same `realpath: false` pattern is also in `settings-manager.ts`, `trust-manager.ts`, and `package-manager-cli.ts`. This change leaves those alone.

## Testing

- I added a test to `test/auth-storage.test.ts`. It holds the lock on the real `auth.json`, then checks that a backend opened through a symlink alias waits in `withLockAsync` until aborted, and gets `ELOCKED` from `withLock`. Neither path runs the mutation. Without the fix the test fails because the async call enters the lock; with the fix it passes.
- `node ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/auth-storage test/settings`: 151 tests pass.
- `npm run check` passes.
- With the reproduction script from the issue, current main prints `symlink alias: ENTERED`; with this change it prints `symlink alias: BLOCKED`. The same-path control prints `BLOCKED` in both cases.

Fixes #11655

Requested by @badlogic

prs.title: fix(ai): retry bare socket error codes such as ECONNRESET
prs.body:
## Problem

`isRetryableAssistantError()` in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts` covers fetch and gateway transport wording ("fetch failed", "socket hang up", "connection lost", …) but not the bare Node socket error codes. When a connection drops mid-stream, the SDK often reports only the code:

- `read ECONNRESET` on a dropped response stream
- `connect ETIMEDOUT 140.82.113.3:443` on a stalled connect
- `write EPIPE` when the child process or socket is already gone

None of those strings match: `ETIMEDOUT` contains `TIMEDOUT`, not `timeout`, and `timed? out` requires a space. So the classifier returns false, `retryAssistantCall()` returns the first error, and the run dies on a transient network event instead of backing off and retrying. Reported in #12070 (point 3), also seen with `google-vertex` streams under load.

## Fix

Added the socket codes to the transport section of `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN`:

```
(?<![a-z0-9])(?:ECONNRESET|ECONNABORTED|ETIMEDOUT|EPIPE)(?![a-z0-9])
connection reset by peer
```

- The lookaround guards follow the status-code rule from #11057: a code inside a longer identifier (a request id, `ERR_…` name) must not match.
- `connection reset by peer` is Node's message text for `ECONNRESET`, which some SDK wrappers send without the code.
- `ECONNREFUSED` is deliberately not retryable: nothing is listening, so restarting the same request does not help. It is covered by a non-retryable test case.

Aborts stay terminal: `retryAssistantCall()` never retries `stopReason: "aborted"`, so classifying these error strings cannot turn a user cancellation into a retry.

Out of scope here, left for #12070: wiring `options.timeoutMs` into `google-vertex` / `google-generative-ai` stream loops (point 1) and classifying SDK-swallowed timeout aborts (point 2).

## Tests

`packages/ai/test/retry.test.ts`: added the six code/message forms above as retryable, and three non-retryable lookalikes (`EXECONNRESET`, `ETIMEDOUTX`, `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9`).

- `test/retry.test.ts`: 49 passed.
- Full `packages/ai` suite: the failure set is identical to a baseline run with these two files stashed (6 files in `anthropic-message-threads`, `lazy-module-load`, `models-entry`, `openai-completions-cache-control-format`, `pi-messages`); none touch retry. `openai-chatgpt-oauth` failed once in a concurrent run and passes on its own.
- `biome check --error-on-warnings` on both changed files: clean.
- Root `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in `packages/ai`; the 5 remaining errors are pre-existing, in `packages/chord/test/examples/61-tutorial`.

Note for reviewers running these on a fresh clone: `packages/ai/src/providers/data/` is gitignored, so `npm run hydrate-model-data` is needed before `packages/ai` tests and the root typecheck will produce meaningful results.

---

CONTRIBUTING.md asks new contributors for an `lgtm` before opening a PR. Submitting this anyway so the diff is on the record for #12070; if the gate closes it, it can be reopened after review.

issues.title: ci: pick_runner routes fork-internal PRs to the upstream ECS fleet and queues forever
issues.body:
### Problem

`pick_runner` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` decides self-hosted vs hosted from two inputs only: `SAME_REPO` (`github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`) and `AUTHOR_ASSOCIATION`. Neither of them says the canonical repository is `QwenLM/qwen-code`.

Open a PR *inside a fork* — base and head both `alice/qwen-code`, not a fork-to-upstream PR — and GitHub reports `github.repository = alice/qwen-code` and `head.repo.full_name = alice/qwen-code`, so `SAME_REPO = true`; the fork owner's association is `OWNER`, so `trusted_author = true` as well. Both branches that admit the self-hosted fleet are taken, in a repository that has no such runner.

### Failure path

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` computes `SAME_REPO` and nothing else about the repository identity.
- The `SAME_REPO`/trusted-author branch then sets `ubuntu_runner` to `["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "ecs-qwen"]`, and the ephemeral-pool branch below inherits the same labels into `pr_test_runner` and `lint_runner`.
- Those outputs are consumed by the downstream jobs' `runs-on` (`ubuntu_runner`, `pr_test_runner`, `lint_runner`).
- A fork has no runner carrying those labels, and a job's timeout does not start until a runner picks it up, so the run queues indefinitely instead of failing.

### Evidence

I extracted the merged `pick_runner` shell from `origin/main` (`2229baf860`) and executed it with the fork-internal PR inputs (`SAME_REPO=true`, `AUTHOR_ASSOCIATION=OWNER`, `EVENT_NAME=pull_request`):

```text
ubuntu_runner=["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "ecs-qwen"]
pr_test_runner=["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "ecs-qwen"]
lint_runner=["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "ecs-qwen"]
```

### What is already covered

#17178 added `github.repository == 'QwenLM/qwen-code'` to the classifier's own routing, so `classify_pr` finishes on a hosted runner. The bad outputs are what it hands downstream afterwards, which is why the run looks like it started and then stalls.

### Test gap

`.github/scripts/ci-runner-routing.test.mjs` models only `sameRepo` (and the association); there is no `repoName` input, so `sameRepo=true` with a non-canonical `repoName` cannot be expressed and is never exercised.

### Suggested fix

Pass the canonical repository signal into `pick_runner` and require it before any of the three outputs may take the self-hosted fleet. Add the fork-internal matrix case (`sameRepo=true`, `repoName=alice/qwen-code`) to the routing test so the gap cannot come back.

### Context

Found while reviewing #17180; deferred rather than widened into that PR.

issues.title: [Feature] Add WeCom group-webhook delivery to Channels and Web Shell

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/integration
labels.description: External integrations

labels.name: roadmap/background-automation
labels.description: Roadmap: Background and automation

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add outbound **WeCom group-webhook delivery** (officially called Message Push, formerly group robots) to the existing Channel system, including the shared Web Shell configuration and Scheduled Tasks destination flow.

A user should be able to choose **WeCom → Webhook sending**, configure a named Channel with a sensitive webhook URL, save and start it, and select its configured group as a delivery destination. No Bot ID/Secret, application credentials, public inbound callback server, contact discovery or manually entered chat ID should be required. Preserve the existing WeCom intelligent-bot and callback-application integrations.

Use `markdown_v2` for readable task results, including tables, fenced code, lists and ordinary text, within the documented platform limits.

### Why is this needed?

Users who only want task results posted to an internal WeCom group currently lack the URL-based sending mode already available for DingTalk and Feishu. The existing WeCom integrations serve different setup and interaction needs; they do not accept a group Message Push webhook URL.

This is an established notification use case, with concrete feature-parity precedent. As checked on 2026-11-14, **Uptime Kuma (93,920 stars)** and **Apprise (17,762 stars)** both implement DingTalk, Feishu and WeCom group-webhook senders. Their WeCom implementations POST to `qyapi.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/webhook/send?key=…`, rather than using a WeCom application API. Their source is evidence of adoption and platform coverage, not a replacement for the official protocol or Qwen Code's existing delivery guarantees.

The completed WeCom intelligent-bot issue #6208 explicitly excluded group-webhook-only support. DingTalk (#16751; #16802 / #16804) and Feishu (#16997; #17012 / #17013) have already established the backend and Web patterns needed for this extension.

### Additional context

**Implementation boundaries**

- Add a separate sending plugin type, such as `wecom-webhook`, and present it as an additional method under WeCom. Follow the existing DingTalk/Feishu pattern; reorganizing the separate WeCom Callback entry is outside this issue.
- Reuse the current `outboundOnly` / `defaultDeliveryTarget` metadata, adapter-owned logical target, `user/chat + id` delivery format, workspace ownership checks, worker lifecycle and secret storage. Tasks reference the Channel's logical target, never its webhook credentials.
- Reuse existing Notify, explicit prompt-result and supported scheduled-result delivery paths. Platform payloads, byte limits and business-response handling belong to the adapter; no new scheduler-specific sender or generic notification framework is proposed.

As with the previous platforms, implementation can be reviewed as an adapter/backend PR followed by a small Web integration PR. This issue is complete when both parts are delivered.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Users can create, edit, save, start, stop and restart a named webhook Channel. Validate the supported official endpoint and required key; keep the whole URL sensitive, including readback, diagnostics and configuration editing. Starting prepares local sending resources without sending a test message or claiming remote credential verification. The group URL supplies the credential; do not add an unrelated application secret or copy another platform's HMAC-signing fields.
2. Shared Web Shell groups the new method under WeCom, omits receive/pairing settings for this send-only mode, and supports configured-target selection without contact discovery or a manual ID. Target create/edit/clear/read round trips and unavailable saved targets work as for the existing webhook modes. The same controls are available in `qwen serve` and `WebShellWithProviders` when the host enables the relevant pages and supplies a daemon workspace.
3. Send results with `msgtype: "markdown_v2"`. Verify readable headings, lists, links, fenced code, tables, ordinary text, Chinese and emoji; document the supported subset and older-client plain-text rendering. The official format does not support mentions: task text must not unexpectedly trigger individual or all-member mentions. Configurable mentions and member lookup are excluded.
4. Validate the final message content against the documented **4096 UTF-8 byte limit**, in addition to existing shared delivery bounds. This is a content limit, not Feishu's full-JSON-request limit. Send at most one request per attempt, report oversize content explicitly, and do not introduce silent adapter truncation or automatic splitting.
5. Report HTTP/network failures, malformed business responses and nonzero WeCom `errcode` as bounded, sanitized delivery failures. HTTP 200 alone is insufficient. Cover credential rejection and throttling, document the **20 messages/minute per webhook** limit, and preserve single-attempt delivery semantics. Successful API acceptance is not a recipient/read receipt.
6. Honor the resolved workspace proxy and existing bypass behavior; bound request time, cancel in-flight requests on stop and release request resources. Reuse suitable existing helpers while preserving current WeCom, DingTalk and Feishu behavior.
7. Add focused protocol/lifecycle tests, shared Web interaction coverage and user documentation. Document that Message Push targets internal groups and creation depends on group/admin permissions. Do not assume enterprise certification is universally required or universally exempt.
8. Record real-platform E2E verification separately from fixture tests: configured-target scheduled delivery, Markdown rendering, edits/restart and failure reporting. Access to a permitted test group/webhook is an implementation-validation dependency, **not a prerequisite for proposing or accepting this feature**. No live WeCom delivery is claimed by this issue.

**Out of scope**

Inbound events, changes to the intelligent-bot or callback-application protocols, dynamic recipients, attachments, interactive cards, configurable mentions, automatic retry/outbox/splitting, new task lifecycle events, changes to current per-run/manual-trigger delivery semantics, a separate test-send UI/API, Generic Webhook and other platform adapters.

**References**

- [Official Message Push protocol](https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/91770): endpoint, formats, UTF-8 limits and rate limit.
- [Official setup and creation conditions](https://open.work.weixin.qq.com/help2/pc/14931): internal groups and administrative permissions.
- Uptime Kuma: [DingTalk](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/blob/4f6661cfa83a06be0353d5536ef3d9ee0064f534/server/notification-providers/dingding.js), [Feishu](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/blob/4f6661cfa83a06be0353d5536ef3d9ee0064f534/server/notification-providers/feishu.js), [WeCom](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/blob/4f6661cfa83a06be0353d5536ef3d9ee0064f534/server/notification-providers/wecom.js).
- Apprise: [DingTalk](https://github.com/caronc/apprise/blob/c6f76f3599ec9bc1591abfd4fc8c27a5124f88fa/apprise/plugins/dingtalk.py), [Feishu](https://github.com/caronc/apprise/blob/c6f76f3599ec9bc1591abfd4fc8c27a5124f88fa/apprise/plugins/feishu.py), [WeCom](https://github.com/caronc/apprise/blob/c6f76f3599ec9bc1591abfd4fc8c27a5124f88fa/apprise/plugins/wecombot.py). Both reference WeCom implementations currently send plain text; Markdown scope above is based on the official documentation.
- Current [WeCom](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/114694062b83f69093a936a3caea4c35bdbeb41d/docs/users/features/channels/wecom.md) and [WeCom Callback](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/114694062b83f69093a936a3caea4c35bdbeb41d/docs/users/features/channels/wecom-callback.md) documentation.

Repository baseline: `114694062b83f69093a936a3caea4c35bdbeb41d`, checked 2026-11-14. Implementation should recheck platform details against the current official documentation.

中文摘要：在已完成的钉钉、飞书 Webhook 能力上，补齐企业微信内部群「消息推送」出站适配器及共享 Web 配置流程，保留现有智能机器人和应用回调方式。复用现有逻辑目标、凭证和生命周期管理，采用支持表格与代码块的 markdown_v2，并验证正文 4096 UTF-8 字节限制及业务错误。Uptime Kuma、Apprise 均已实现三平台群 Webhook，作为功能覆盖的参考。真实账号及群 Webhook 的可用性属于后续 E2E 验证条件，不阻塞提出需求；不扩展测试发送、重试、分片、mentions 或通用 Webhook。

labels.name: priority/P3

labels.name: category/integration
labels.description: External integrations

issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up tracking for the non-blocking suggestions from the `/review` round on #17136 (managed DingTalk adapter, H5d of #12827). All nine **critical** findings were fixed in `6928d9c33f`, along with a first batch of suggestions (credential/poll-interval validation, pairing rejection, `QWEN_HOME` test isolation, deps tests, webhook body-read deadline, design-doc decisions, stale enablement docs). The items below are the remaining test-coverage and hygiene suggestions, deferred to keep the adapter slice focused. None is a correctness blocker.

## Deferred suggestions (from /review R1 on #17136)

- **R1-12** — Export `MANAGED_DINGTALK_OUTBOUND_LIMIT = 64` from `managed-state.ts` and use it in both the validator and the adapter's `.slice(-64)`, so the two caps cannot drift.
- **R1-14** — Strengthen the orphan-drop witness to assert the dropped entry is gone from persisted `state.outbound` (not just which deliveries settled), so keeping the entry reds the case.
- **R1-16** — Extract a shared `createManagedChannelCommand` helper so `managed-email.ts` and `managed-dingtalk.ts` stop being near-verbatim copies.
- **R1-17** — Assert the `HttpManagedChannelControlPlane` constructor mapping (tenant/actor/workspace/channel-id/cwd-relative) in the CLI test so a swapped wiring reds it.
- **R1-18** — Add a fake-lock `onCompromised` test asserting the adapter goes inert when ownership is lost.
- **R1-19** — Type and assert the register request payload (platform/accountId/accountGeneration/policy) in the adapter test.
- **R1-20** — Make the webhook cache evict the least-recently-seen conversation (delete-then-reinsert on update) instead of the first-inserted key.
- **R1-24** — Key the state directory on the control-plane identity (clientId + pinned channel id) rather than the mutable display name, so one robot app cannot get two owners and a rename does not orphan acked claims.
- **R1-26** — Add a `replayed: true` + held-claim witness proving the refusal streak is NOT reset on a replayed answer (email R8-1).
- **R1-29** — Move the byte-identical `validManagedReceipt` validators beside the shared `ManagedReceipt` type in `channel-base` so the two providers cannot drift.
- **R1-32** — Require a usable reply target (cached or committed `sessionWebhook`) in the admission gate so a frame that can never be answered is not admitted.
- **R1-33** — Add `managed-state.test.ts`: save/load round-trip, one rejection case per validated field, ENOENT → undefined, corrupt file → throw.

## Acceptance

Each item lands with a witness that reds when the corresponding guard is removed, mirroring the mutation-verified approach used for the critical fixes in #17136.


## Added from /review R2 on #17136 (commit 01e65f66e5 fixed the R2 criticals)

- **R2-6** — Make the CJK clamp witness land the byte limit mid-code-point so the code-point walk is actually exercised (the current 25,000×'中' case lands exactly on a boundary).
- **R2-7** — Pin the `pollLoop` default (the real adapter polls only because of it); the production caller omits the option.
- **R2-8** — Test the `instanceRefusals ?? 0` upgrade for a pre-field state file (without it the counter becomes NaN and poisons the saved state).
- **R2-9** — Pin that `stop()` aborts the in-flight poll delay so a large `pollInterval` does not turn shutdown into a hang.
- **R2-10** — Test the `managed-dingtalk` subcommand registration so dropping it reds the suite.
- **R2-11** — Test the credential-hygiene guard, the `pollInterval` clamp and the `privatePolicy: 'pairing'` refusal (the email package pins the analogous rules).
- **R2-12** — Extend `createStreamClient` coverage to the frame-logging suppression and the ack ordering (the connect/stop paths are now pinned by `managed-dingtalk-stream.test.ts`).


## Added from /review R3 on #17136 (commit 976f2d6b03 fixed the R3 criticals)

Deferred under the review's convergence posture (round 3, non-blocking):
- `packages/channels/dingtalk/src/index.ts:5` — reverting the package's new export block leaves every affected test green (add an export-surface witness).
- `packages/channels/dingtalk/src/managed-dingtalk-adapter.test.ts:310` — the CJK clamp test's byte limit lands exactly on a character boundary, so the code-point walk is never entered (same as R2-6; land the limit mid-code-point).


## Added from the /verify-pr round on #17136 (head 976f2d6b)

- **Duplicate pending claim on redelivery** — since the R3-3 fix makes acceptance the commit point (overflow acks LATER and relies on provider redelivery), a frame redelivered while its claim is still pending (admission answer lost) could be queued a second time before `recent` is updated. Add a dedupe guard at queue/admit time keyed on the platform event id, with a witness.
- The F1 astral/character-cap item previously deferred here is now **fixed** (high-surrogate back-off at the UTF-16 cap, witness added).


## Added from /review R4 on #17136 (commit e3554528cc fixed the R4 criticals)

Deferred under the review's convergence posture (round 4, non-blocking):
- A transient 409 `workspace_unavailable` destroys one message; the outer 409 arm needs the transient-code exemption.
- Persist-before-send is unpinned: moving the outbound append below `sendWebhook` keeps the suite green.
- The `senderStaffId` → `senderId` fallback has no witness and would lose a message silently.
- `controlPlane.disconnect()` in the teardown is unasserted.
- The 0600-in-0700 state mode is called load-bearing but no test asserts it.


## Added from /review R5 on #17136 (commits d5f4d032d9 + 1b63ed83e2 fixed the R5 critical and both suggestions)

The R5-1 stall-durability critical, the first-connect credential suggestion, and the rejection-receipt batch suggestion are all **fixed** (each mutation-verified). The registration-refusal backlog arm that qqqys raised as a question was **reproduced and fixed** in `1b63ed83e2` (not deferred). One bounded lifecycle item is deferred under the round-5 convergence posture:

- **SDK heartbeat timer cleanup** — the pinned `dingtalk-stream-sdk-nodejs` 2.0.4 keepalive/autoreconnect pair creates a heartbeat interval on each socket open; `close` does not clear it and the next open overwrites the only stored timer handle, so the old interval keeps pinging the replacement socket. A probe through this PR's production wrapper and the real SDK (fake network/endpoint and timers only) observed active intervals: first open 1 → close 1 → reconnect open 2 → wrapper disconnect 1. Cleanup should retire the old interval on close/reconnect (in the wrapper, or upstream). Bounded: the CLI calls `process.exit()` after the channel handler returns, so this does not establish a CLI shutdown hang. Land with a timer-count witness.

issues.title: ci: pin the cron side of the failure-report schedule arm
issues.body:
### Problem

The failure-reporting suite pins the schedule arm in one direction only, so a lane can silently lose its nightly trigger and the suite stays green.

`scripts/tests/main-ci-failure-issue-workflow.test.js` derives the schedule arm's workflow names from `main-ci-failure-issue.yml` and asserts every one of them exists in `watchedFiles` (around line 104-118). That covers "a name in the arm is a real watched lane". It does not cover the mirror: nothing asserts that a watched lane which is supposed to run on a cron still carries its `schedule:` block.

### Why it matters

`e2e.yml` carries `schedule: cron '0 4 * * *'`, which #5859 added because a busy merge window keeps cancelling the push run, and it is in `watchedFiles` as `E2E Tests`. Delete that `schedule:` block and the whole suite stays green: `E2E Tests` still appears in the watch list and in the schedule arm, so no assertion moves. The nightly full regression would simply stop running, and the loss would be invisible until someone noticed the absence of the signal itself.

### Suggested fix

In the same test, read each watched lane's YAML and assert the ones that own a nightly signal are in the schedule arm — and pin `e2e.yml`'s `0 4 * * *` so its removal fails here rather than in production. Roughly 3-4 lines next to the existing loop, no production change.

### Context

Deferred from #17180 (review suggestion R4-1), whose guard closed the "name in the arm is watched" direction. The merged guard is valuable; this is the other half.

prs.title: fix(mcp): repair the MCP connection torn down by an aborted tool call
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Aborting an in-flight MCP request can tear the transport down: the SDK's `onerror` fires and the server flips to `DISCONNECTED`. The abort path used to return early without repairing anything, so a session that survived the cancel kept a dead connection. The abort path now arms a status listener and rethrows immediately; when the server actually reports the teardown, the listener reconnects and reloads the tool registry once, best-effort. The cancelled call is still never replayed.

## Why it's needed

Without the repair, every later MCP call in a session that survives the cancel inherited the dead connection: roughly 90s until the health monitor's `30s × 3` budget expired, and indefinitely when the client had already left the manager's `clients` map.

The repair cannot read the status inside the abort catch. The transport reports the failure only after the server reacts to `notifications/cancelled`, one round trip after the local rejection, so a status read there always sees `CONNECTED`. Keying the repair to the `CONNECTED → DISCONNECTED` transition through the existing `mcp-status` registry replaces that race rather than re-timing it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit level only: run the file below and confirm the three cases — an abort whose server then reports `DISCONNECTED` reconnects exactly once and does not re-issue the cancelled call, an abort whose server stays `CONNECTED` arms no repair, and a call that is not aborted still takes the existing cannot-safely-replay path.

A live-server run is what would settle the ordering claim, and it has not been done. Pool mode (`McpClientManager` pool entries, which run their own status listener before this one) has also not been driven.

```sh
# from packages/core
npx vitest run src/tools/mcp-tool.test.ts
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Added a regression test: an abort followed by the server reporting `DISCONNECTED` reconnects once and does not re-issue the cancelled call.
- Added the counterpart: an abort whose server stays `CONNECTED` performs no repair and leaves no listener behind.
- Updated `does not classify a parent abort wrapped by the MCP SDK as a timeout`, which pinned "abort ⇒ no MCP work at all" and so conflated "do not replay" with "do not repair". It now asserts the repair happens once and `callTool` still runs once. The timeout classification it guards is unchanged.
- The shared `expectNoRetry` helper keeps its `ensureTool` assertion: its default signal is never aborted, so the new branch is unreachable from either call site.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only; no dev server or sandbox.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the repair fires on any `CONNECTED → DISCONNECTED` for that server within 60s of an abort, so it cannot by itself tell a teardown the abort caused from one that happened nearby, and it carries no liveness check. Duplicate repairs from concurrent cancels collapse because `discoverMcpToolsForServer` already coalesces discovery per server. #12161, open on the same issue, is about `onerror` writing `DISCONNECTED` for sessions that may still answer a ping; if that lands, this trigger inherits its false positives, which cost one bounded, coalesced rediscovery.
- Not validated / out of scope: not reproduced end-to-end against a live HTTP/streamable MCP server; the ordering claim is source-derived and unit-covered only. Pool mode has not been driven. Not run: full `npm run build`, and the full repository test suite.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

### Local checks run

- `npx vitest run src/tools/mcp-tool.test.ts` — 187 passed (whole file, not just the changed tests).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in `packages/core` — clean.
- `npx eslint` on the two changed files — clean.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12160

prs.title: fix(core): hoist the real functionResponse from behind an intervening model turn
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Teach the orphaned-tool-use repair to look for a genuine `functionResponse` outside the adjacent window before it gives up and synthesizes a placeholder.

The scan behind `planRepair` only walks the consecutive `user` run that follows a `model[functionCall]` turn: its skip loop advances over degraded-placeholder *model* turns only, so one ordinary `model[text]` turn ends the window. A real `functionResponse` that landed behind such a turn — a late submitQuery that answered after a follow-up prompt — is therefore invisible to the scan and the id is classified unmatched.

A new `adoptLateResponses` pass runs between the decision and mutation phases. For each id the window left unmatched it searches the rest of history, adopts the first genuine (non-synthesized, via `isSynthesizedRepairPart`) copy as the hoist survivor, and feeds that through the existing `hoistedParts` / `removalTargets` / `droppedDuplicates` path — no parallel mutation path was added. Synthesis now happens only when no genuine copy exists anywhere. `applyRepair` additionally drops a source user turn left empty by a late removal, since the existing empty-turn sweep never reaches beyond the scanned window.

This restores the behaviour the canonical note in this file already documents — "HOIST the real fr into the immediately-adjacent user turn when it landed in a non-adjacent later turn" — which the implementation previously honoured only inside an unbroken user run.

## Why it's needed

Two failure shapes came out of the same bug, and both were reachable on `main`:

- **The model is told a finished tool was never recorded.** A synthesized `error` placeholder is injected next to the call while the real result stays orphaned two turns down. That is the parent symptom of #15297: the agent re-runs a tool that had already succeeded, or apologises for data it actually has.
- **The wire carries two `tool_result` blocks for one id.** The orphaned genuine copy is still emitted as a stray second tool message further down the history, which is a malformed `tool_use` ↔ `tool_result` shape for Anthropic-compatible backends.

The second is also why the fix cannot be scoped to the resume path. The inline per-send pass runs the same helper, and without the widened search its fallback shape is exactly a sentinel adjacent to the call plus a genuine copy further down — the same wedge class this subsystem exists to escape. Relocating the genuine response into the canonical adjacent slot keeps the invariant intact in both passes.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The first new test is a self-contained reproduction of the issue's fixture. The transcript is `[user[text], model[functionCall], user[text], model[text], user[functionResponse]]` — call `call_behind_model`, one ordinary model turn in between:

```ts
repair([
  userText('open /tmp/long.txt'),
  content('model', readCall('call_behind_model', { path: '/x' })),
  userText('actually, summarize first'),
  modelText('Summarizing the plan.'),
  resultTurn('call_behind_model', 'real file contents'),
]);
```

Run it with `npx vitest run packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.test.ts -t "hoists the real functionResponse"` from `packages/core`. On `main` the assertions fail on the first one; on this branch all pass. What a reviewer should confirm:

- `result.injected` is `[]` — no sentinel was planted.
- The user turn adjacent to the call now *heads* with the genuine response (`{ output: 'real file contents' }`), followed by the follow-up text that was already there.
- No entry after `history[3]` carries a `functionResponse` for that id — the orphan is gone, so there is exactly one `tool_result` for it on the wire.
- `history.length` is 4, not 5: the source turn held nothing but the late response, so it was dropped.
- A second `repairOrphanedToolUseTurns()` returns `{ injected: [], droppedDuplicates: [] }` — the pass is idempotent.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Same fixture, same four observable properties:

| | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result.injected` | `[{ callId: 'call_behind_model', name: 'read_file' }]` | `[]` |
| user turn adjacent to the call | `[functionResponse(error placeholder), text 'actually, summarize first']` | `[functionResponse('real file contents'), text 'actually, summarize first']` |
| entries after the model turn | genuine `functionResponse` still present — orphaned | none |
| `tool_result` blocks for the id | 2 (malformed) | 1 |
| history length | 5 | 4 |
| model sees | tool "was not recorded" | the real output |

Non-user-visible, so the before/after is the transcript rather than a screenshot. Eight regressions in `packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.test.ts` pin the surrounding contract:

- `hoists the real functionResponse from behind an intervening model turn (#15411)` — the fixture above, plus idempotence.
- `synthesizes the still-missing id while hoisting a late real copy of its sibling` — parallel calls, one late copy and one genuinely missing id: both are handled in one pass, in that order inside the adjacent turn.
- `hoists the first genuine late copy and drops later duplicates for the same callId` — first-copy-wins survives the widened search; the duplicate is reported in `droppedDuplicates`.
- `keeps synthesizing when only a synthesized placeholder sits behind the model turn` — a placeholder is never adopted as the survivor.
- `keeps preserved call ids untouched even when a genuine late copy exists` — `preserveCallIds` still filters before the widen pass.
- `leaves later genuine copies alone when the window already has the first copy` — an in-window survivor suppresses widening entirely.
- `leaves a later call intact when the hoisted source turn sits directly above it` — the emptied source turn is dropped even when a `model[functionCall]` turn follows, so the two assistant turns become adjacent (Anthropic/OpenAI merge them); the later call and its pairing both survive.
- `keeps the source turn text when a late response sits behind a model turn` — cleanup drops only turns whose every part is a `functionResponse`; a source turn with the user's own text survives as text-only.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

✅ tested · ⚠️ not tested

Windows is the unit suites, eslint, prettier and `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`. macOS and Linux are covered by CI, not by a local run.

### Environment (optional)

`npx vitest run` under `packages/core` on Node 22. No sandbox, daemon or network; the repair helpers are pure functions over a `Content[]` history, which is why the fixture can be written inline.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: widening is not gated to the resume path. The inline per-send pass now also relocates a genuine response across an intervening model turn, which is a history rewrite at send time rather than recovery-only. The bet is that the repair pass is already an explicit, logged history-rewrite recovery step, and that putting the genuine response into the canonical adjacent slot is strictly closer to the documented invariant than leaving a sentinel plus a duplicate. If that bet is wrong, the blast radius is any send that hits the repair path, not just resumed sessions.
- Not validated / out of scope: only the two-pass repair contract is tested. I did not run a live Anthropic-compatible backend against the malformed two-`tool_result` shape, so the "backend rejects it" half of the motivation is from the wire shape, not from an observed API error. The "exactly one `tool_result` on the wire" guarantee holds only for ids the window left *unmatched*: an id the window already matched can still ship a later genuine copy twice (same on `main`), which is outside the widen pass's contract. Deep-history cost is O(ids × remaining turns) per repair; measured on the fixtures only, not profiled on a long session.
- Review follow-up (F1): the empty-source-turn cleanup originally removed a turn by its absolute index inline with the part-splices, so a late-hoist drop could read an index shifted by an earlier splice and delete a following `model[functionCall]` turn. The drop decision is now taken against the unmutated history (only turns whose every part is a `functionResponse`) and applied after all part-splices, still descending, so no index can go stale. The two-adjacent-model-turn shape that leaves behind is pinned as intended.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No public signature change; `repairOrphanedToolUseTurns` returns the same shape, and `injected` still reports synthesized ids only.

## Linked Issues

Part 1 of #15411 — deliberately **not** using a closing keyword. The issue stays open for Part 2 (the cancelled-continuation site in `use-llm-stream.ts` consulting `getSynthesizedRepairCallIds`), which is why this PR does not auto-close it. #15308 has since merged, so Part 2 is actionable independently of this one.

Related: #15297 is the user-visible symptom this addresses; this PR does not close it.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

**这个 PR 做了什么**

让孤立 tool_use 修复逻辑在放弃并合成占位符之前，先到相邻窗口之外找一找真实的 `functionResponse`。

`planRepair` 背后的扫描只遍历 `model[functionCall]` 之后那一段连续的 `user` 序列：它的跳过循环只会跨过退化的占位符 *model* 轮次，所以一个普通的 `model[text]` 轮次就会终止这个窗口。真实 `functionResponse` 如果落在这类轮次之后——例如一个晚到的 submitQuery 在后续提问之后才给出结果——对扫描来说是不可见的，该 id 于是被判定为未匹配。

新增的 `adoptLateResponses` 阶段插在决策与变更两个阶段之间。对每个被窗口判为未匹配的 id，它在剩余历史中搜索，把第一份真实副本（非合成，通过 `isSynthesizedRepairPart` 判定）采纳为 hoist 幸存者，并送入既有的 `hoistedParts` / `removalTargets` / `droppedDuplicates` 路径——没有新增并行的变更路径。只有当历史中任何位置都不存在真实副本时，才会合成。此外 `applyRepair` 会删除因晚到移除而变空的源 user 轮次，因为既有的空轮次清扫逻辑到不了扫描窗口之外。

这恢复了本文件中那段规范注释早已写明的行为——「当真实 fr 落在非相邻的后续轮次时，把它 HOIST 到紧邻的 user 轮次」——而此前实现只在没有被打断的 user 序列内遵守这一点。

**为什么需要**

同一个 bug 引出两种故障形态，且在 `main` 上都可达：

- **模型被告知一个已经完成的工具「没有被记录」。** 合成的 `error` 占位符被注入到调用旁边，而真实结果被孤立在两轮之后。这正是 #15297 的父级症状：agent 会重跑一个已经成功的工具，或者为它其实已经拿到的数据道歉。
- **线上出现同一个 id 的两个 `tool_result` 块。** 被孤立的真实副本仍然作为一条多余的第二个 tool 消息更靠下地被发出去，对 Anthropic 兼容后端而言这是畸形的 `tool_use` ↔ `tool_result` 形态。

第二种形态也正是为什么本修复不能只限定在 resume 路径。内联的 per-send 流程会用同一个 helper，若无这次的加宽搜索，它的兜底形态正好就是调用旁边一个哨兵占位、而真实副本更靠下——与本子系统存在的意义所要逃离的那类畸形相同。把真实响应搬回规范的相邻槽位，在两条流程中都保持了不变量完整。

**Reviewer 验证计划**

**如何验证**

第一个新增测试是 issue fixture 的自包含复现。对话形态为 `[user[text], model[functionCall], user[text], model[text], user[functionResponse]]`——调用 `call_behind_model`，中间隔着一个普通 model 轮次：

```ts
repair([
  userText('open /tmp/long.txt'),
  content('model', readCall('call_behind_model', { path: '/x' })),
  userText('actually, summarize first'),
  modelText('Summarizing the plan.'),
  resultTurn('call_behind_model', 'real file contents'),
]);
```

在 `packages/core` 下用 `npx vitest run packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.test.ts -t "hoists the real functionResponse"` 运行。在 `main` 上第一条断言就会失败；在本分支上全部通过。Reviewer 应确认：

- `result.injected` 为 `[]`——没有注入哨兵。
- 紧邻调用的 user 轮次现在以真实响应打头（`{ output: 'real file contents' }`），其后是原本就在那里的后续提问文本。
- `history[3]` 之后的任何条目都不再携带该 id 的 `functionResponse`——孤立副本消失，线上该 id 只有一个 `tool_result`。
- `history.length` 为 4 而非 5：源轮次里只有那条晚到的响应，因此整轮被删除。
- 再调用一次 `repairOrphanedToolUseTurns()` 返回 `{ injected: [], droppedDuplicates: [] }`——该阶段是幂等的。

**证据（改前 / 改后）**

同一 fixture、四项可观测属性：

| | `main` | 本 PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result.injected` | `[{ callId: 'call_behind_model', name: 'read_file' }]` | `[]` |
| 紧邻调用的 user 轮次 | `[functionResponse(error 占位符), text 'actually, summarize first']` | `[functionResponse('real file contents'), text 'actually, summarize first']` |
| model 轮次之后的条目 | 真实 `functionResponse` 仍在——被孤立 | 无 |
| 该 id 的 `tool_result` 块数 | 2（畸形） | 1 |
| history 长度 | 5 | 4 |
| 模型看到的内容 | 工具「没有被记录」 | 真实输出 |

非用户可见改动，因此用对话形态而非截图来呈现改前改后。`packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.test.ts` 中新增八个回归用例锁定周边契约：

- `hoists the real functionResponse from behind an intervening model turn (#15411)`——即上方 fixture，外加幂等性。
- `synthesizes the still-missing id while hoisting a late real copy of its sibling`——并行调用，一个晚到副本加一个确实缺失的 id：同一趟里都处理掉，且在相邻轮次内的顺序也正确。
- `hoists the first genuine late copy and drops later duplicates for the same callId`——first-copy-wins 在加宽搜索后依然成立；重复项记入 `droppedDuplicates`。
- `keeps synthesizing when only a synthesized placeholder sits behind the model turn`——占位符永远不会被采纳为幸存者。
- `keeps preserved call ids untouched even when a genuine late copy exists`——`preserveCallIds` 仍在加宽阶段之前过滤。
- `leaves later genuine copies alone when the window already has the first copy`——窗口内已有幸存者时完全不做加宽。
- `leaves a later call intact when the hoisted source turn sits directly above it`——抽空的源轮次即使在下方紧跟 `model[functionCall]` 时也会被删除，于是两个 assistant 轮次相邻（Anthropic/OpenAI 会合并它们）；后续的调用及其配对都完整保留。
- `keeps the source turn text when a late response sits behind a model turn`——清理只删除「每一部分都是 `functionResponse`」的轮次；源轮次里带有用户自己文本时，该轮次保留为纯文本。

**测试环境**

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

✅ 已测 · ⚠️ 未测

Windows 上跑的是单测套件、eslint、prettier 和 `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`。macOS 与 Linux 由 CI 覆盖，未在本地运行。

**环境（可选）**

在 Node 22 下 `npx vitest run`（位于 `packages/core`）。不需要沙箱、daemon 或网络；修复辅助函数是对 `Content[]` 历史的纯函数，这也是 fixture 可以内联书写的原因。

**风险与范围**

- 主要风险或取舍：加宽搜索没有限定在 resume 路径上。内联的 per-send 流程现在也会跨一个中间的 model 轮次去搬移真实响应，这意味着在发送时做历史改写，而不只是在恢复路径上做。这里的判断前提是：修复流程本身已经是一个显式、有日志的历史改写恢复步骤，而把真实响应放进规范的相邻槽位，严格来说比「留下一个哨兵加一份重复」更接近文档化的不变量。若该前提有误，影响面是任何走到修复路径的发送，而不只是 resume 的会话。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：只验证了两趟修复的契约。我没有对着畸形的双 `tool_result` 形态跑过真实的 Anthropic 兼容后端，所以「后端会拒绝」这半个动机来自线形态推断，而非观测到的 API 报错。「线上该 id 只有一个 `tool_result`」的保证只对被窗口判为*未匹配*的 id 成立：窗口内已经匹配的 id 仍可能把稍后的真实副本发两遍（`main` 上同样如此），这属于加宽阶段的契约之外。深历史下每次修复的成本是 O(ids × 剩余轮次)，仅在 fixture 上量过，未在长会话上做过 profile。
- 审查跟进（F1）：抽空源轮次的清理原本用绝对下标、内联在 part-splice 里删除整轮，晚到 hoist 的删除可能读到被前一次 splice 挪移过的下标，从而误删紧随其后的 `model[functionCall]` 轮次。现在删除决策在未变更的历史上判定（只删「每一部分都是 `functionResponse`」的轮次），并在所有 part-splice 之后、仍按降序应用，任何下标都不会过期。由此留下的「两个 assistant 轮次相邻」形态已按预期钉住。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。没有公开签名变更；`repairOrphanedToolUseTurns` 返回结构不变，`injected` 仍然只报告合成出来的 id。

**关联 issue**

本 PR 是 #15411 的第 1 部分——**有意**不使用关闭关键字。该 issue 为第 2 部分（`use-llm-stream.ts` 中取消续流位置对 `getSynthesizedRepairCallIds` 的运用）保持打开，因此本 PR 不会自动关闭它。#15308 已经合入，第 2 部分可以独立于本 PR 推进。

相关：#15297 是本 PR 所针对的用户可见症状；本 PR 不关闭它。

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): defensive resume cached reset, telemetry mirror clear, and test pins
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Follow-up to #12066. This is a defensive reset plus test pins, not a user-visible staleness fix. When resume seeds the prompt and output counts, it now also clears the process-global telemetry mirror of the cached-content count, and keeps a defensive reset of the per-chat cached slot. Tests pin both clears after a real usage report (finite and non-finite seed inputs), and a `/context` case pins the fallback to the global cached count when no session chat exists yet.

## Why it's needed

The other review items from #12066 are already on `main`; this PR carries the remaining delta. `seedResumeTokenCounts` always runs on a freshly started chat, so the per-chat cached slot is already `0` at that point: the per-chat reset is an invariant guard, and `/context` output is unchanged between BASE and HEAD for that field (confirmed by the maintainer's real-TUI A/B run). The value that does go stale on an in-process `/resume` is the global telemetry mirror: it kept the previous session's cached count next to the newly seeded prompt count (for example prompt 12000 from session B with cached 64653 from session A). Every other writer of the per-chat cached slot already clears that mirror, and this brings the resume seed in line. The only reader of the mirror today is the no-chat fallback in `/context`, which had no test for a nonzero global value either.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/llm-chat.test.ts`: 530/530 pass. The resume case records a usage report with `cachedContentTokenCount: 64_653`, calls `seedResumeTokenCounts` with non-finite and then finite inputs, and after each call expects the per-chat cached slot to be `0` and `uiTelemetryService.setLastCachedContentTokenCount` to have last been called with `0`. With the new telemetry line removed, this case fails (`expected last "spy" call to have been called with [ +0 ]`).
2. `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/commands/contextCommand.test.ts`: 49/49 pass. The no-chat case expects the displayed cached figure to be the global `1_000` when the chat is not initialized (this pins existing behavior).
3. `cd packages/core && npm run typecheck` and `npx eslint src/core/llm-chat.ts src/core/llm-chat.test.ts`: both clean.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for the TUI: `/context` output is the same on BASE and HEAD. The observable difference is the global telemetry mirror after an in-process resume: before, it holds the previous session's cached count; after, it reads `0` until the next API usage report.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ |

### Environment (optional)

N/A (unit tests only).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: after resume, the global cached mirror reads `0` until the next API usage report instead of a value from a different session. The per-chat slot behaves as before.
- Not validated / out of scope: restoring the cached figure on resume (the transcript records `cachedContentTokenCount`, but `ResumeTokenCounts` does not carry it); the daemon deferred-session path.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #12066. Relates to #12047.

- 未验证 / 范围外：resume 时恢复缓存数（transcript 记录了 `cachedContentTokenCount`，但 `ResumeTokenCounts` 不携带它）；daemon 延迟会话路径。
- 破坏性变更：无。

## 关联 Issue

#12066 的后续，关联 #12047。

prs.title: fix(web-shell): preserve typing focus for ask-user prompts
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When an AskUserQuestion prompt becomes active in the web shell, it now leaves keyboard focus in an editable composer target when the user is already typing. The prompt remains reachable by Tab or click, while the existing option-focus behavior is preserved in all other cases.

## Why it's needed

### Problem
A question prompt can appear while the user is typing. Its activation focus handoff moves focus to an option, so Enter, Space, digits, or typed text can select or submit an answer the user did not choose.

### Root Cause
The activation focus handoff ran as a passive `useEffect` without checking whether the active element was editable. Keyboard shortcuts already had an editable-target guard, but the activation focus path did not.

### Solution
Use a layout effect, inspect the shadow-aware active element, and yield when it is an editable target. This mirrors the related ToolApproval follow-up in #9609 without touching that PR's files.

### Changes
- Add a panel ref for resolving the document or shadow-root active element.
- Run the activation focus handoff in `useLayoutEffect`.
- Skip the handoff for inputs, textareas, contenteditable targets, CodeMirror editors, and keyboard scopes.
- Add a regression test for a focused textarea when the question appears.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start the web shell with a workspace that can produce an `ask_user_question` prompt.
2. Focus the composer textarea and type without submitting.
3. Trigger an AskUserQuestion prompt while the composer still has focus.
4. Confirm that focus remains in the composer and no option is selected or submitted by the in-progress keystrokes.
5. Press Tab or click the question to enter its option controls, then confirm the normal arrow, digit, Enter, and Space behavior remains available.
6. The deterministic regression command is `npm test --workspace=@qwen-code/web-shell -- client/components/messages/AskUserQuestion.test.tsx --run`; the final result was 71 passed.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the repository triage reproduction identifies the unconditional focus grab on main; a focused editor can be redirected to the question option during the same overlay activation.

After: the new `yields focus when the question appears while the user is typing` regression passes, and the full AskUserQuestion file passes 71/71. No screenshot or video is included because this run used deterministic jsdom focus tests rather than a live browser session; a real-browser manual flow is not validated.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS | ⚠️ |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ |
|  🐧 Linux | ⚠️ |

### Environment (optional)

Windows 11 environment, Node v24.12.0, npm 11.6.2, Vitest v3.2.4, jsdom unit tests. The risk-matched web-shell suite ran 192 files: 125 passed and 67 failed because the sparse checkout lacks `@qwen-code/webui/daemon-react-sdk` generated artifacts and `packages/web-shell/dist/index.js`.

## Testing

- Baseline focused test: 70 passed.
- Final focused test: 71 passed.
- Prettier check on both changed files: passed.
- ESLint on both changed files: passed.
- Risk-matched web-shell suite: 125 files passed, 67 failed on missing generated SDK/dist artifacts; the changed AskUserQuestion suite passed in that run.
- Web-shell typecheck: not verified; the checkout has missing generated SDK artifacts and existing cross-workspace type errors.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Compatibility/Risk

When the question appears during active typing, focus intentionally stays in the editable target and the question remains reachable by Tab or click. Existing focus behavior is unchanged when no editable target is active, when the panel is reactivated, or when `keyboardActive` is false. No public API or data format changes are introduced.

## Notes for Reviewer

The layout effect is intentional: the composer is hidden in the same commit that mounts the overlay, so a passive effect can run after browser style recalculation has already dropped composer focus. #9611 is a follow-up to #9609; the two PRs touch different files and should be sequenced without combining their diffs.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #9611

## Linked Issues

- Fixes #9611.
- Follow-up to #9609, which covers the sibling ToolApproval dialog.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

当 Web Shell 中的 AskUserQuestion 提示变为活动状态时，如果用户已经在可编辑的 composer 输入框中打字，提示不会再抢走键盘焦点。提示仍然可以通过 Tab 或点击进入；其他情况下原有的选项聚焦行为保持不变。

## 为什么需要它

### 问题
当用户正在打字时，问题提示可能出现。激活时的焦点交接会把焦点移到一个选项上，因此 Enter、Space、数字键或正在输入的文字可能选择或提交用户没有选择的答案。

### 根因
激活焦点交接使用了被动的 `useEffect`，没有检查当前焦点元素是否可编辑。键盘快捷键已经有可编辑目标保护，但激活焦点路径没有。

### 方案
使用布局 effect，读取 shadow-aware 的当前活动元素；如果当前元素是可编辑目标，就让出焦点。这与相关的 ToolApproval 后续修复 #9609 保持一致，但不修改那个 PR 的文件。

### 修改内容
- 添加 panel ref，用于解析 document 或 shadow root 中的活动元素。
- 在 `useLayoutEffect` 中执行激活焦点交接。
- 当焦点位于 input、textarea、contenteditable、CodeMirror 编辑器或键盘作用域时跳过交接。
- 添加问题出现时 textarea 保持焦点的回归测试。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 启动能够产生 `ask_user_question` 提示的 Web Shell 工作区。
2. 聚焦 composer textarea，开始输入但不要提交。
3. 在 composer 仍保持焦点时触发 AskUserQuestion 提示。
4. 确认焦点仍在 composer 中，正在输入的按键不会选择或提交任何选项。
5. 按 Tab 或点击问题进入选项控件，然后确认原有的方向键、数字键、Enter 和 Space 行为仍然可用。
6. 确定性回归命令是 `npm test --workspace=@qwen-code/web-shell -- client/components/messages/AskUserQuestion.test.tsx --run`；最终结果为 71 项通过。

### 前后证据

修改前：仓库 triage 复现确认 main 上存在无条件的焦点抢占；浮层激活的同一过程中，已聚焦的编辑器可能被重定向到问题选项。

修改后：新增的 `yields focus when the question appears while the user is typing` 回归测试通过，整个 AskUserQuestion 文件 71/71 通过。本次没有附截图或视频，因为验证使用了确定性的 jsdom 焦点测试而不是实时浏览器会话；真实浏览器手动流程未验证。

### 测试平台

| 操作系统 | 状态 |
| :------: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ |

### 环境

Windows 11，Node v24.12.0，npm 11.6.2，Vitest v3.2.4，jsdom 单元测试。风险匹配的 web-shell 套件运行了 192 个文件：125 个通过，67 个失败，原因是稀疏 checkout 缺少 `@qwen-code/webui/daemon-react-sdk` 生成产物和 `packages/web-shell/dist/index.js`。

## 测试

- 基线 focused 测试：70 项通过。
- 最终 focused 测试：71 项通过。
- 两个修改文件的 Prettier 检查：通过。
- 两个修改文件的 ESLint：通过。
- 风险匹配的 web-shell 套件：125 个文件通过，67 个文件因缺少生成的 SDK/dist 产物失败；修改涉及的 AskUserQuestion 套件在该运行中通过。
- web-shell typecheck：未验证；checkout 缺少生成的 SDK 产物，并存在跨 workspace 类型错误。
- `git diff --check`：通过。

## 兼容性/风险

当问题在用户正在输入时出现，焦点会有意留在可编辑目标中，问题仍可通过 Tab 或点击进入。没有可编辑目标、重新激活 panel 或 `keyboardActive` 为 false 时，原有焦点行为不变。不引入公开 API 或数据格式变化。

## 给评审者的说明

使用布局 effect 是有意的：composer 与浮层在同一次提交中被隐藏和挂载，被动 effect 可能在浏览器样式重算已经丢失 composer 焦点之后才运行。#9611 是 #9609 的后续；两个 PR 修改不同文件，应按顺序合入，不需要合并 diff。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #9611

## 关联 Issues

- Fixes #9611。
- 后续跟进 #9609，它覆盖同类的 ToolApproval 对话框。
