prs.title: fix(desktop): allow MCP App sandbox frames in the navigation policy
prs.body:
## What this PR does Extends the webview navigation policy in `packages/desktop` so the MCP App sandbox frames of generated UI (the `generated_ui_show` card in packages/web-shell) can actually load in the Desktop app. Concretely, `is_allowed_navigation` now accepts, in addition to the daemon's exact same-origin URL: (1) the loopback alias host the Web Shell rewrites `127.0.0.1` to (`localhost` / `[::1]` on the daemon's own port, same scheme), (2) the ephemeral `.localhost:` sandbox listener the daemon 302-redirects to, and (3) `data:` guest documents (data-mode sandbox), only after the daemon's origin has been recorded. Every allowance is scoped: foreign ports, foreign `*.localhost` subdomains on the daemon's port, and any other scheme stay denied, and new unit tests pin the positive and negative boundaries. ## Why it's needed Generated UI cards (the `generated_ui_show` MCP tool) are stuck on "Loading the interactive view…" forever in Qwen Code Desktop, while the exact same session works in a regular browser. Root cause, documented with evidence in #16766: the webview's `.on_navigation` policy allows only the bootstrap URL and the exact same-origin `http://127.0.0.1:`, and wry applies it to **every** navigation action, including subframes. The sandbox chain needs one hop the policy cancels before any network request: the same-origin iframe is addressed at `localhost:` (a client-side alias, which is why zero 302s ever reach the daemon), the 302 target is `.localhost:`, and the data-mode guest loads from a `data:` URL. Both sandbox modes therefore die inside the webview. A plain WKWebView completes the full handshake with zero console errors on the identical payload (capture in the issue comment), so it is the policy, not WebKit, that is at fault. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify - Unit tests (the primary verification for this PR; PR-CI does not compile the Tauri crate): run `cargo test` from `packages/desktop/src-tauri`. New tests: `allows_mcp_app_sandbox_frames`, `mcp_app_sandbox_allowances_do_not_leak`, `data_guests_require_the_origin_to_be_recorded`, plus the adjusted `srcdoc_exception_does_not_allow_other_navigation`. Output: ``` running 44 tests test tests::allows_bootstrap_but_not_a_runtime_url_before_origin_is_set ... ok test tests::allows_bootstrap_even_after_origin_is_set ... ok test tests::allows_mcp_app_sandbox_frames ... ok test tests::allows_only_the_daemon_origin_in_the_main_window ... ok test tests::allows_only_the_recorded_origin_once_it_is_set ... ok test tests::allows_saved_preview_srcdoc_frames ... ok test tests::command_origin_gate_accepts_only_bootstrap ... ok test tests::data_guests_require_the_origin_to_be_recorded ... ok test tests::mcp_app_sandbox_allowances_do_not_leak ... ok test tests::srcdoc_exception_does_not_allow_other_navigation ... ok … test result: ok. 44 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out ``` - Manual (if you build the app): open a session in a Desktop build from this branch and ask the agent to show a generated UI card (the `generated_ui_show` tool); the card should render instead of staying on "Loading the interactive view…". I verified the full handshake with a plain WKWebView harness serving a byte-identical 0.26.9 daemon payload (evidence comment linked below); I did not do an end-to-end run inside a Tauri build — see Risk & Scope. ### Evidence (Before & After) Before: the card is stuck on "Loading the interactive view…"; the daemon's own log shows **0×302 + exactly one 200** (data-mode only) for `/mcp-app-sandbox` across the whole session lifetime; the same payload in a plain WKWebView completes `ui/initialize` with 0 lines in any console-error class (241-line capture). After: `cargo test` passes (output above). Full capture and daemon-log evidence: #16766, [evidence comment](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/16766#issuecomment-6750447524). ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :----: | | 🍏 macOS | ✅ | | 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested | | 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested | ### Environment (optional) macOS 26.6.2 (aarch64), Rust 1.96.0, `cargo test` in `packages/desktop/src-tauri`. ## Risk & Scope - Main risk or tradeoff: the policy is widened, and the `data:` allowance is deliberately the broadest of the three (any `data:` URL once the origin is recorded). This matches what the browser Web Shell already loads (there is no such policy in a browser; the guest document is sandboxed with `allow-scripts` without `allow-same-origin` and the daemon applies its CSP), and `data:` performs no network fetch. The main-frame protection the policy exists for is unchanged: the origin gate still applies. Note that the previous `srcdoc_exception_does_not_allow_other_navigation` test explicitly asserted `data:text/html,

preview

` is denied — I changed that test intentionally, for the reason above; the alternative would be to apply the policy to the main frame only, which is a larger change to how the wry hook is used. - Not validated / out of scope: an end-to-end run inside a real Tauri Desktop build (PR-CI does not compile the desktop crate, and cross-compiling Tauri from macOS is blocked by ring 0.17.14's native build). Windows/Linux behavior of the `*.localhost` ephemeral listener is assumed from the daemon code (`mcp-app-sandbox.ts` binds a raw server under that host) — not tested on those platforms. - Breaking changes / migration notes: none. ## Linked Issues Fixes #16766
中文说明 ## What this PR does 扩展 `packages/desktop` 中 webview 的导航策略，使 generated UI（packages/web-shell 的 `generated_ui_show` 卡片）的 MCP App 沙箱框架能够在 Desktop 应用中真正加载。具体来说，`is_allowed_navigation` 现在除了 daemon 的精确同源 URL 之外，还接受：(1) Web Shell 将 `127.0.0.1` 改写成的 loopback 别名主机（daemon 自身端口上的 `localhost` / `[::1]`，同 scheme），(2) daemon 302 重定向到的临时 `.localhost:` 沙箱监听器，(3) `data:` 来宾文档（data 模式沙箱）——仅在 daemon 的 origin 被记录之后。每个放行都有限定范围：外部端口、daemon 端口上的外部 `*.localhost` 子域名以及任何其他 scheme 仍然被拒绝，新的单元测试固定了正面与负面的边界。 ## Why it's needed generated UI 卡片（`generated_ui_show` MCP 工具）在 Qwen Code Desktop 中永远卡在 "Loading the interactive view…"，而完全相同的会话在普通浏览器中正常工作。根因（已在 #16766 中附证据记录）：webview 的 `.on_navigation` 策略只允许 bootstrap URL 和精确同源的 `http://127.0.0.1:`，而 wry 会把它应用到**所有**导航动作，包括子框架。沙箱链需要一个策略会在网络请求发出前取消的额外跳转：同源 iframe 使用 `localhost:` 寻址（客户端侧别名，所以 302 从未到达 daemon），302 目标是 `.localhost:`，data 模式的来宾从 `data:` URL 加载。因此两种沙箱模式都在 webview 内死掉。普通 WKWebView 用完全相同的 payload 能零 console 错误地完成完整握手（issue 评论中有抓取），所以是策略的问题，不是 WebKit 的问题。 ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify - 单元测试（本 PR 的主要验证方式；PR-CI 不编译 Tauri crate）：在 `packages/desktop/src-tauri` 下运行 `cargo test`。新测试：`allows_mcp_app_sandbox_frames`、`mcp_app_sandbox_allowances_do_not_leak`、`data_guests_require_the_origin_to_be_recorded`，以及调整后的 `srcdoc_exception_does_not_allow_other_navigation`。输出： ``` running 44 tests test tests::allows_bootstrap_but_not_a_runtime_url_before_origin_is_set ... ok test tests::allows_bootstrap_even_after_origin_is_set ... ok test tests::allows_mcp_app_sandbox_frames ... ok test tests::allows_only_the_daemon_origin_in_the_main_window ... ok test tests::allows_only_the_recorded_origin_once_it_is_set ... ok test tests::allows_saved_preview_srcdoc_frames ... ok test tests::command_origin_gate_accepts_only_bootstrap ... ok test tests::data_guests_require_the_origin_to_be_recorded ... ok test tests::mcp_app_sandbox_allowances_do_not_leak ... ok test tests::srcdoc_exception_does_not_allow_other_navigation ... ok … test result: ok. 44 passed; prs.title: feat(cli): add ui.startExpanded to start the TUI in expanded detail mode
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds `ui.startExpanded` (boolean, default `false`). When `true`, the terminal UI starts with thinking blocks and tool output expanded instead of requiring Ctrl+O / Alt+T in every session.

The setting only seeds the initial value of the existing app-wide expansion flag. The toggle still owns the state afterwards, so Ctrl+O in an expanded session collapses it exactly as before. Both renderers are covered (ink `AppContainer`, OpenTUI `start-opentui-ui`).

```json
{ "ui": { "startExpanded": true } }
```

## Why it's needed

Retiring `ui.compactMode` left no way to express "I always want the reasoning visible", so the only option was to press the toggle at the start of each session. This restores that preference as a start-up default rather than a mode the toggle has to fight.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```
npx vitest run src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx       282 passed
npx vitest run src/config/settingsSchema.test.ts   67 passed
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/cli                  clean
eslint / prettier --check on all five changed files  clean
```

The two new `AppContainer` cases are `startExpanded: true` seeds `allExpanded` and unset keeps it `false`. Reverting the `AppContainer.tsx` change turns the first one red (`expected false to be true`).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no terminal capture. The new cases assert the context value both renderers read rather than a live session, so there is no screenshot to pair.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

Only macOS was run locally; the interactive TUI was not driven manually with `ui.startExpanded: true` set. CI covers the rest.

### Environment (optional)

Local `vitest` and `tsc` only. No sandbox, no live terminal session.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: The setting only seeds the initial value, so it cannot conflict with the toggle. A user who never presses Ctrl+O now sees reasoning from the first frame, which is the intent of the option.
- Not validated / out of scope: No manual run of the interactive TUI with `ui.startExpanded: true` — the behaviour is asserted through the context value the renderers read, not through a live terminal session. No full `npm run build` and no full unit suite; only the two affected test files were run.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. The key is new and defaults to `false`, so existing configurations are unaffected.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #9670

prs.title: fix(core): send a current MCP OAuth bearer token on every request
prs.body:
## What this PR does

OAuth-protected HTTP and SSE MCP servers now get a current access token on every request instead of the one captured when the transport was created. The transport's fetch is wrapped so each request asks for the token; the token is cached in the wrapper and only re-read from storage (and refreshed if due) once it is close to expiry, so steady-state requests never touch token storage. Refreshes for one server are deduplicated within the process, so concurrent requests crossing the expiry buffer trigger exactly one refresh request.

While doing this, three edge cases found in review are covered: tokens that live less than the five-minute expiry buffer are refreshed at half their lifetime instead of on every request; a dynamically registered client configured as `oauth: { enabled: true }` without `clientId` refreshes with the client id stored at registration; and every code path for a server presents the same OAuth config (the user's `oauth` block plus the stored client id), because the deduplicated refresh uses the first caller's config.

## Why it's needed

`createTransport()` and `createTransportWithOAuth()` pin `Authorization: Bearer <token>` into `requestInit.headers` at connect time. A pooled connection lives much longer than a typical access token (ours: 1 hour), so after expiry the next tool call is sent with the stale token and gets a 401. The pool then treats it as a silent transport drop, tears down the session's MCP view, and the in-flight call fails. The background reconnect refreshes the token successfully, but the session's MCP tools are not re-registered, so the rest of that session has no tools from the server (same symptom as #13796). Users hit this roughly once per token lifetime in any long session.

`getValidToken()` already refreshes proactively inside its expiry buffer; it was simply never called again after connect.

Why a fetch wrapper rather than the SDK's `authProvider: { token() }`: in `StreamableHTTPClientTransport._commonHeaders()` the headers from `requestInit` are spread after the `authProvider` token, so the existing connect-time `Authorization` header (and any user-configured `Authorization` header) would override it; and with an `authProvider` set, a 401 is raised as `UnauthorizedError` from the auth path, which changes what the existing 401 handling in `connectToMcpServer` (`probeMcpServerForOAuth`, the OAuth challenge bookkeeping) sees. The wrapper keeps both of those behaviors unchanged. Happy to switch if maintainers prefer the `authProvider` route.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit tests (from `packages/core`):

```
npx vitest run src/tools/mcp-client-oauth-token.test.ts src/mcp/oauth-provider.test.ts src/tools/mcp-client.test.ts src/tools/mcp-pool-key.test.ts src/tools/mcp-transport-pool.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
```

The new `mcp-client-oauth-token.test.ts` drives the real SDK transports and a real `MCPOAuthProvider` against an in-memory token store and a fake authorization server that rotates refresh tokens and rejects replays with `invalid_grant`. It covers: the rotated token is sent after the buffer; five concurrent requests trigger one refresh and no credential deletion; two transports for the same server share one refresh; short-lived (300 s) tokens are not refreshed per request; a DCR client without `clientId` in config refreshes; stored-credential paths refresh with the configured client secret; a failed refresh resolves all waiters to null; a failed storage read keeps the still-valid cached token; custom headers and the headers of a `Request` input are preserved; SSE requests carry the refreshed token. With `mcp-client.ts` reverted to `main`, 11 of the 12 new transport tests fail (the remaining one, "no token → request untouched", passes on `main` by design); with the in-flight dedupe removed, the concurrency tests fail (`called once, but got 5 times`).

Manual scenario: see `.qwen/e2e-tests/2026-10-26-mcp-oauth-per-request-token.md`. In short: a Streamable HTTP MCP server behind an OAuth authorization server with short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens; authenticate once via `/mcp`; in one session, call a tool, wait until the token is inside its refresh buffer, call a tool again in the same session.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (Qwen Code Desktop 0.26.1, same session, first call after the 1-hour token expired; debug log, server name redacted):

```
08:08:36.847Z [ERROR] [MCP] MCP ERROR (example-mcp): Error POSTing to endpoint: {"error":"token verification failed: \"exp\" claim timestamp check failed"}
08:08:36.847Z [ERROR] [McpPool:Entry] PoolEntry example-mcp::unpooled-1 silent transport drop (prev state='active', localStatus→DISCONNECTED). Transitioning to 'failed'; evicting from pool.entries + pooledConnections (W122 R20).
08:08:36.849Z [DEBUG] [McpPool:View] SessionMcpView[<session>/example-mcp] torn down
08:08:36.864Z [INFO] [MCP_OAUTH] Refreshing expired token for MCP server: example-mcp
08:08:37.221Z [INFO] [MCP_TOOL] Successfully reconnected to MCP server 'example-mcp'
```

The tool call failed, and a retry in the same session found no tools from the server.

After (`qwen serve` built from this branch, same session, the client-side token expiry moved forward so the refresh buffer is crossed a few minutes after connect; reverse-proxy access log in front of the authorization server and the MCP server, paths redacted):

```
18:37:08 "POST /mcp HTTP/1.1" 200       <- first tool call in the session, token not yet due
18:41:03 "POST /token HTTP/1.1" 200     <- second tool call: one refresh first ...
18:41:04 "POST /mcp HTTP/1.1" 200       <- ... then the call with the new token
```

No 401, no reconnect handshake, no `silent transport drop` / `torn down` entry, and the tool call returned normally. The refreshed token was persisted to `mcp-oauth-tokens.json`.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ |

### Environment (optional)

Windows 11, `npm run build && npm run bundle`, `node scripts/cli-entry.js serve --port <port> --workspace <dir>`, Web Shell. MCP server: Streamable HTTP; authorization server: node-oidc-provider with DCR, PKCE, RFC 8707 `resource`, 1-hour access tokens, rotating refresh tokens.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: token reads and refreshes for one server are now deduplicated per process; concurrent callers share one result. All callers for a server now present the same config, so a shared result is correct for each of them.
- Not validated / out of scope: refresh races across processes sharing one token store (the dedupe is per process; with rotating refresh tokens, if another process deletes the credentials while this one's refresh is in flight, the new token is not saved and the user has to re-authenticate); a token stored without `expiresAt` is never refreshed, so for an authorization server that omits `expires_in` the per-request guarantee does not apply; re-registering a session's MCP tools after a pool teardown (#13796) — this PR removes the expiry trigger for it, but a genuine server-side 401 still tears the view down.
- Credential deletion: before this PR any refresh error deleted the stored credentials; now only an explicit `invalid_grant` does, and only if the stored refresh token is still the one presented. `invalid_client`, `invalid_request`, `invalid_scope`, code-less 400/401, 403, 429, 5xx, timeouts and network errors keep them.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15649

Related: #13796, #8170

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

受 OAuth 保护的 HTTP 与 SSE MCP 服务器，现在每个请求都带当前有效的访问令牌，而不是建传输时取到的那一枚。传输的 fetch 被包了一层，每个请求发出前取一次令牌；令牌缓存在这层包装里，只在接近过期时才重新从存储读取（到期就续签），所以平稳运行时的请求完全不碰令牌存储。同一进程内对同一台服务器的续签会去重，多个并发请求同时跨过过期缓冲线时只发一次续签请求。

顺带覆盖了审查中发现的三个边界情况：有效期短于 5 分钟过期缓冲的令牌，改为在剩余有效期过半时续签，而不是每个请求都续签；配置为 `oauth: { enabled: true }` 但没写 `clientId` 的动态注册客户端，用注册时存下的 client id 续签；同一台服务器的所有代码路径都传同一份 OAuth 配置（用户的 `oauth` 配置块加上存储的 client id），因为去重后的续签用的是第一个调用方的配置。

## 为什么需要

`createTransport()` 和 `createTransportWithOAuth()` 在建连接时把 `Authorization: Bearer <token>` 写死在 `requestInit.headers` 里。连接池里的连接活得比常见访问令牌（我们是 1 小时）长得多，令牌过期后，下一次工具调用就带着过期令牌发出、收到 401。连接池随后把它当作传输静默断开处理，拆掉会话的 MCP 视图，正在进行的调用失败。后台重连能成功续签，但会话里的 MCP 工具不会重新注册，于是这个会话后面再也用不到这台服务器的工具（与 #13796 的症状相同）。任何长会话里，用户大约每过一个令牌有效期就会碰到一次。

`getValidToken()` 本来就会在过期缓冲期内提前续签，只是建连之后再也没有被调用过。

为什么用 fetch 包装而不用 SDK 的 `authProvider: { token() }`：在 `StreamableHTTPClientTransport._commonHeaders()` 里，`requestInit` 的请求头展开在 `authProvider` 令牌之后，所以现有的建连时 `Authorization` 头（以及用户配置的 `Authorization` 头）会把它覆盖掉；而且设置了 `authProvider` 后，401 会从鉴权路径以 `UnauthorizedError` 抛出，这会改变 `connectToMcpServer` 里现有 401 处理（`probeMcpServerForOAuth`、OAuth 质询记录）看到的东西。fetch 包装让这两处行为都保持不变。如果维护者更倾向 `authProvider` 方案，可以改。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

单元测试（在 `packages/core` 下）：

```
npx vitest run src/tools/mcp-client-oauth-token.test.ts src/mcp/oauth-provider.test.ts src/tools/mcp-client.test.ts src/tools/mcp-pool-key.test.ts src/tools/mcp-transport-pool.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
```

新增的 `mcp-client-oauth-token.test.ts` 用真实的 SDK 传输和真实的 `MCPOAuthProvider`，配内存令牌存储和一个假的授权服务器（会轮换 refresh token，重放时返回 `invalid_grant`）。覆盖：过了缓冲线后发出的是轮换后的新令牌；5 个并发请求只触发一次续签、不删凭证；同一服务器的两个传输共享一次续签；短有效期（300 秒）令牌不会每个请求都续签；配置里没有 `clientId` 的动态注册客户端能续签；走存储凭证的路径续签时带上配置里的 client secret；续签失败时所有等待者都拿到 null；读存储失败时继续用仍然有效的缓存令牌；自定义请求头和以 `Request` 传入时自带的请求头都被保留；SSE 请求带的是续签后的令牌。把 `mcp-client.ts` 回退到 `main` 后，12 个新增传输测试中有 11 个失败（剩下的「拿不到令牌时不改动请求」按设计在 `main` 上也通过）；去掉进行中去重后，并发测试失败（`called once, but got 5 times`）。

手动场景：见 `.qwen/e2e-tests/2026-10-26-mcp-oauth-per-request-token.md`。简而言之：一台 Streamable HTTP MCP 服务器，挂在签发短效访问令牌、轮换 refresh token 的 OAuth 授权服务器后面；通过 `/mcp` 认证一次；在同一个会话里先调一次工具，等令牌进入续签缓冲期，再在同一个会话里调一次。

### 证据（修复前后）

修复前（Qwen Code Desktop 0.26.1，同一会话，1 小时令牌过期后的第一次调用；调试日志，服务器名已脱敏）：

```
08:08:36.847Z [ERROR] [MCP] MCP ERROR (example-mcp): Error POSTing to endpoint: {"error":"token verification failed: \"exp\" claim timestamp check failed"}
08:08:36.847Z [ERROR] [McpPool:Entry] PoolEntry example-mcp::unpooled-1 silent transport drop (prev state='active', localStatus→DISCONNECTED). Transitioning to 'failed'; evicting from pool.entries + pooledConnections (W122 R20).
08:08:36.849Z [DEBUG] [McpPool:View] SessionMcpView[<session>/example-mcp] torn down
08:08:36.864Z [INFO] [MCP_OAUTH] Refreshing expired token for MCP server: example-mcp
08:08:37.221Z [INFO] [MCP_TOOL] Successfully reconnected to MCP server 'example-mcp'
```

该次工具调用失败，同一会话里重试也找不到这台服务器的工具。

修复后（用本分支构建的 `qwen serve`，同一会话，把客户端记录的令牌过期时间提前，使建连几分钟后就跨过续签缓冲线；授权服务器与 MCP 服务器前面反向代理的访问日志，路径已脱敏）：

```
18:37:08 "POST /mcp HTTP/1.1" 200       <- 会话里第一次工具调用，令牌尚未到期
18:41:03 "POST /token HTTP/1.1" 200     <- 第二次工具调用：先续签一次……
18:41:04 "POST /mcp HTTP/1.1" 200       <- ……再带新令牌完成调用
```

没有 401，没有重连握手，没有 `silent transport drop`／`torn down` 记录，工具调用正常返回。续签后的令牌已写回 `mcp-oauth-tokens.json`。

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ |

### 环境

Windows 11，`npm run build && npm run bundle`，`node scripts/cli-entry.js serve --port <port> --workspace <dir>`，Web Shell。MCP 服务器：Streamable HTTP；授权服务器：node-oidc-provider，开启动态客户端注册、PKCE、RFC 8707 `resource`，访问令牌 1 小时，refresh token 轮换。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：同一进程内对同一台服务器的令牌读取与续签会去重，并发调用方共享同一结果。由于同一服务器的所有调用方现在传同一份配置，共享结果对每个调用方都是正确的。
- 未验证或不在范围内：共用同一令牌存储的多个进程之间的续签竞争（去重只在进程内；refresh token 会轮换时，若本进程续签途中另一进程删掉了凭证，新令牌不会保存，用户需要重新认证）；存储时没有 `expiresAt` 的令牌永远不会续签，所以对不返回 `expires_in` 的授权服务器，「每个请求带当前令牌」的保证不成立；连接池拆除后把会话的 MCP 工具重新注册回去（#13796）——本 PR 去掉了令牌过期这个触发条件，但服务端真的返回 401 时视图仍会被拆。
- 凭证删除：本 PR 之前，续签出任何错都会删除存储的凭证；现在只有明确的 `invalid_grant` 才删，而且只在存储里的 refresh token 仍是本次提交的那个时才删。`invalid_client`、`invalid_request`、`invalid_scope`、不带错误码的 400/401、403、429、5xx、超时和网络错误都保留凭证。
- 破坏性变更或迁移：无。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #15649

相关：#13796、#8170

</details>

auto_merge.commit_title: fix(core): send a current MCP OAuth bearer token on every request (#15650)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(core): send a current MCP OAuth bearer token on every request

createTransport pinned the access token obtained at connect time as a
static Authorization header. A pooled connection outlives the 1 hour
token, so later requests got 401, the pool tore down the session view
and the in-flight tool call failed; only a new session recovered.

Wrap the transport fetch (Streamable HTTP and SSE, including the
post-authentication transport) so each request carries the current
token. The token is cached in the wrapper and re-read through the
provider only once it passes the storage's expiry buffer, so ordinary
requests do not touch token storage.

MCPOAuthProvider gains getValidOAuthToken, which returns the full token
and shares one in-flight read/refresh per server across the process.
Authorization servers that rotate refresh tokens would otherwise see
concurrent refreshes replay a consumed token, fail with invalid_grant
and have the stored credentials deleted.

* fix(core): harden per-request MCP OAuth token refresh

- Decide when a cached token is due from its real lifetime (the storage
  buffer, but never earlier than half of the lifetime), so tokens that live
  under five minutes are not refreshed on every request.
- Refresh dynamically registered clients with the client id from the stored
  credentials when the config has none.
- Make every caller for a server present the same OAuth config (the user's
  oauth block plus the stored client id), because the shared in-flight
  refresh uses the first caller's config.
- Seed the token cache with the token obtained at connect time, keep using
  the cached token when a due re-read fails, and keep the headers of a
  Request passed as the fetch input.
- Add an e2e test plan.

* fix(core): only the fetch wrapper writes the MCP OAuth bearer header

Keep the OAuth Authorization header out of requestInit so a request made
when no usable token is left carries no stale connect-time bearer. A due
token that cannot be refreshed is kept until it actually expires.

* fix(core): keep MCP OAuth credentials through slow, failing or raced refreshes

A refresh that hangs, fails transiently or loses a race with a
re-authentication no longer wipes or overwrites the stored credentials:

- the token endpoint request times out after 10s, and a request waits at
  most 5s on a due refresh before using the still-valid cached token; a
  failed attempt is retried after 30s instead of on every request;
- credentials are deleted only when the authorization server rejects the
  refresh (400/401), and only if they still hold the presented refresh
  token; a refresh that succeeds after a re-authentication saves nothing;
- a re-authentication drops the shared in-flight refresh, so later callers
  read the new credentials instead of joining the stale one.

Adds tests for the SSE stream-open request and the SSE OAuth retry
transport, two servers refreshing concurrently, tokens without expiry and
credential retention on the failure paths.

* fix(core): delete MCP OAuth credentials only on invalid_grant

Token endpoint errors are now parsed as JSON or form-encoded and keep their
RFC 6749 error code. invalid_client, invalid_request, invalid_scope or a 400
without a code no longer wipe a refresh token that may still be valid.

* fix(core): keep the Agent Plugin redirect refusal for OAuth-only servers

MCP client 2.4.0 resolves a same-origin 30x in its own layer, against
requestInit.redirect, before the compatibility fetch is called. The redirect
refusal introduced with the 2.4.0 bump asked "does requestInit carry a
credential", but this branch moved the OAuth bearer out of requestInit into
the withBearerToken fetch wrapper. For an Agent Plugin server that
authenticates only with OAuth and has no configured headers, no requestInit
was created at all, and even when one existed it had no authorization header,
so the SDK replayed the bearer to another path of the same origin.

Both Streamable HTTP paths (createTransport and createTransportWithOAuth) now
build requestInit through one function that asks agentPluginForbidsRedirect
as if the bearer were present whenever the wrapper is installed. The
criterion is the wrapper, not whether a token was obtained this time, so a
failed refresh cannot turn the refusal off. requestInit is only created when
it is not empty. The compatibility fetch's own check is unchanged: it sits
inside withBearerToken and still sees the header.

Legacy SSE needs no change: Agent Plugin v1 rejects the sse transport type.

* fix(core): adopt a late MCP OAuth refresh and tighten the redirect tests

When a due refresh outlived the 5s wait, the getter fell back to the cached
token and pushed its next attempt 30s out. If the shared refresh then
succeeded, this connection kept sending the old access token for up to 30s,
which a server that revokes the old token on refresh answers with a 401.
The late result is now written back through the same adopt path as a normal
success (cache and next due time), only when it expires later than what is
cached, so a stale result cannot overwrite a newer token. A failed read
changes nothing.

The comment on the wait claimed the token endpoint request had no timeout;
it has one (10s) in oauth-provider. It now says why waiting has a shorter cap.

Tests: the redirect refusal test now sends a real request after the token
became unobtainable and checks the init the base fetch receives, instead of
asserting the static requestInit, so dropping the refusal per request when
there is no token is caught. The same-origin replay test also asserts the
first hop carried the current bearer.

* test(core): pin the 10s MCP OAuth refresh timeout

The hang test checked that the token refresh request carries an abort
signal, but not its delay: raising TOKEN_REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS to 600s left
the suite green. It now asserts the delay passed to AbortSignal.timeout.
That timer is not driven by fake timers, so the value is checked where the
refresh sets it instead of being waited out.

* fix(core): adopt a late MCP OAuth refresh whatever its lifetime

A refresh that finished after the 5s wait was adopted only if its token
expired later than the cached one. A refresh may return a shorter
expires_in, so a valid new token could be dropped and the old one sent
until the retry delay ended. The late result is now adopted whenever it is
a different token. No ordering check is needed: a read that loses a race
with a re-authentication returns the stored, newest credentials.

The late-adoption test now also runs with a 60s refreshed token that
expires before the cached one; it fails on the previous rule.

* fix(core): order late MCP OAuth reads and back off once the token expired

A read can return the snapshot it took when it started (the provider's
early return for a stored token that is not yet due), so a read that
finished after a later one was adopted, e.g. across a re-authentication,
could put an older token back. A read's result is now adopted only if
nothing was adopted since the read started; this replaces the "different
token" check, which no test exercised.

When no usable token was left, a failed refresh did not back off, so every
request read storage and called the token endpoint. The 30s retry delay
now applies there too, and a cached token past its expiry is never sent.

Tests: a slow storage read that returns another process's token after a
re-authentication was adopted, and a failing refresh after expiry. Each
fails with its fix reverted.

* fix(core): order late MCP OAuth reads by start and return replaced credentials

Counting adoptions did not order two reads that started before either was
adopted: a slow read from before a re-authentication that finished first
was adopted, and the later read with the new credentials was then dropped.
Reads are now numbered as they start, and a result is adopted only if no
later-started read was. A request that waited on a dropped result sends the
usable cached token rather than the cached one unchecked.

A refresh rejected because another process or a re-authentication rotated
the refresh token returned null, so the caller backed off for 30s while a
usable token was stored. It now returns the stored credentials, as the
success path already does when it finds them replaced.

Tests: the late-read case also runs with the later read finishing while the
slow one returns; it fails with adoption counting. The provider tests for a
re-authentication during a rejected refresh now expect the new token.

---------

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the /mcp action cursor on its action when the list rebuilds
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The OpenTUI `/mcp` server-detail dialog now remembers the highlighted action by its key instead of its row index. When an action succeeds and the host rebuilds the list with fewer rows, the cursor stays on the same action, or falls back to the first row when that action is gone.

## Why it's needed

The cursor belongs to an action, but the host can rebuild the action list after an operation. Retaining only its old row index can select a different action when rows disappear. The ink dialog already tracks the active item by key and falls back to the first entry (`useSelectionList`); this restores parity for the opt-in OpenTUI renderer.

The component regression demonstrates the wrong-action risk using a disconnected server with cached tools. That fixture is broader than the normal product state: disconnected servers drop their tools. The reachable product transition is a four-row to three-row list, where Enter should use the first-row fallback instead of retaining the old index. [wenshao independently verified that real TUI transition](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14661#issuecomment-6527646220); I did not run that live session.

Fixes #14655.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```console
cd packages/cli
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialogs-mcp.test.tsx -t "keeps the cursor on its action"
```

On `91a7f9e481` this fails with `expected "spy" to not be called with ... "toggle-disable"` because the second Enter falls through to Disable. On this branch it passes.

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Before (component fixture with cached tools): after Reconnect succeeds, the next Enter calls `onServerAction(server, 'toggle-disable')`.
- After: the cursor falls back to View tools, so Enter opens the tool list and `toggle-disable` is never called.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

Original local macOS validation (before the later three regression additions): the dialog test file (19 passed), the related OpenTUI dialog suites (53 passed across `dialogs-mcp`, `opentui-dialog-mount`, `batch-cursor`), `tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier on the changed files.

The current head has 22 dialog tests; [wenshao verified 22/22 at head and trial merge, with two failures against base production](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14661#issuecomment-6527646220). This is reviewer evidence, separate from my original local run.

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only. No live TUI session was run, so no screen recording is attached.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the change only affects the opt-in OpenTUI renderer (`QWEN_TUI_RENDERER=opentui`); the ink path is untouched.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live keypress session and non-macOS platforms.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14655

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

OpenTUI 的 `/mcp` 服务器详情页原来用行号记录高亮动作，列表变化后可能选中另一动作。组件回归用“断开但仍有缓存工具”的夹具展示误触 Disable；真实产品断开时会清空工具，因此不能将该夹具原样描述为真实 TUI 故障。可达产品路径是四行变三行后应回落到第一行。wenshao 已独立验证该真实 TUI 路径；我未运行该会话。ink 版的 `useSelectionList` 已按 key 记录并回落。

本 PR 把详情页光标改成保存 `action.key`，渲染时再换算成行号；动作消失时回落到第一行。新增回归测试：base 上第二次 Enter 会调用 `toggle-disable`（19 个测试中 1 个失败），分支上 19 个全过；相关的 OpenTUI 对话框套件 53 个测试通过，`tsc --noEmit`、eslint、prettier 均通过。未跑真实 TUI 会话和非 macOS 平台。

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): open the highlighted /mcp server when grouping reorders rows
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`/mcp` now selects servers by identity instead of by a display index. `ServerListStep` reports the selected server object, and `MCPManagementDialog` stores its name and resolves it against `servers` — the same name-based selection the OpenTUI dialog already uses.

## Why it's needed

Rows are grouped by source while `servers` stays in configured order. Top-tier servers (`--mcp-config`, ACP/IDE session, bundled Mem0) render under "User MCPs" but sit last in `servers`, so passing a row index made the dialog open a different server; Disable, Clear Authentication, Reconnect and Approve then applied to that server. Removing the index means the two orderings can no longer be confused.

Fixes #14651.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```console
cd packages/cli
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/ui/components/mcp
```

The current MCP suite contains 47 tests, including the two added regressions. [wenshao independently verified 47/47 at the current head](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14653#issuecomment-6528151819), with the two added regressions failing on base. My original local run below predates those additions and covered 45 tests. The mixed-source test fails on `9135d45910` because the callback receives the row index, and passes here because it receives `cliSrv`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Before: selecting `cliSrv` (row 2) called `onSelect(1)`; the dialog used `servers[1]` = `projectSrv`.
- After: the callback receives the `cliSrv` object; the dialog resolves it by name.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

Original local macOS validation: `components/mcp` suite 45 passed (before the two later regressions), `tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier on the changed files. No live TUI session was run.

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only. No screen recording is attached because no live TUI session was run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: `ServerListStepProps.onSelect` changes signature; it is internal to the MCP dialog package (`ServerListStep`, `MCPManagementDialog`, tests).
- Not validated / out of scope: live TUI keypress flow and non-macOS platforms.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none (internal type only).

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14651

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

`/mcp` 原来按行的显示位置传索引，但列表按来源分组后的顺序与配置里的 `servers` 数组顺序不同：`--mcp-config`、ACP/IDE 会话和内置 Mem0 在数组里排在项目服务器之后，显示时却归到 "User MCPs"。选中第二行可能打开另一台服务器。

本 PR 改为按身份选择：`ServerListStep` 把选中的 server 对象交给回调，`MCPManagementDialog` 保存 `selectedServerName` 并用 `servers.find(...)` 解析，与 OpenTUI 版已有的做法一致。新增的混合来源测试在 base 9135d45910 上失败（回调收到行号），最初本地 `components/mcp` 套件 45 个测试通过（早于后续新增的两个回归）；wenshao 在当前 head 独立验证了 47/47、两个新增回归在 base 失败，该 47 项不是我本次执行；`tsc --noEmit`、eslint、prettier 均通过。未跑真实 TUI 会话和非 macOS 平台。

</details>

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): address the post-merge review notes on the loop schedule slice
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Follow-up to #17088 (the fixed-interval `/loop` schedule slice for Managed Sessions), addressing the round-3 review suggestions and the non-blocking observations left by the approving reviewers. It memoizes a complete deferred wake-recovery proof so a pending input beside a future-dated wakeup no longer re-proves the journal from revision zero on every scan; assembles the `cron_list` / `cron_delete` tool descriptions from the creators each profile actually declares so a Session is never steered toward a tool it does not have; pins the creator-actor derivation against the real schema and the empty-creator refusal; tightens the `cron_list` label test to read the rendered text rather than the whole committed payload; binds the live-state filter as a SQL parameter; documents the internal automation controller's auth boundary; and corrects the design-doc acceptance citation in both languages.

Round 2 of this PR's own review tightened the description assembly further: the exported `HOSTED_CRON_*` constants are now the `(true, true)` composition of the description helpers, so the served wording has a single producer (no constant/composer literal copies held together only by a test); the call sites compose unconditionally; `cronDeleteDescription` dropped its never-read `hasCronCreate` parameter; and the cursor paging test was renamed to promise only what it pins (paging under the live-state filter, not the bound-vs-literal form). The served wording is byte-identical before and after this refactor across all four creator corners and both constants.

## Why it's needed

These are the residual notes from the #17088 review that were not blocking but are real: the wake-proof early return skipped memoization (a measurable re-proof cost every 30s scan while a pending input sits beside a deferred wakeup); the per-profile declaration trim added in #17088 covered `cron_create` only, leaving `cron_list` / `cron_delete` naming `loop_wakeup` on files/4 and team-lead/2 and `cron_create` on shell/3 — a model following that text emits a tool the admission chain refuses, failing the whole turn; the creator-actor read (the single fact the three internal routes stand on) had only a mocked test; and the label test's assertions could be satisfied by the payload rather than the rendered text. Each fix carries a committed test, and the load-bearing ones are mutation-verified.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Wake proof memoization: `WakeRecoveryStoreTest#aCompleteDeferredProofIsMemoizedAcrossScans` drives one future loop input plus one due monitor input through the counting template and asserts two `contains(true)` answers with no journal re-read on the second call. Restoring the pre-fix early return reddens it (mutation verified). The same suite runs against a real MySQL 8.4 container as `WakeRecoveryMySqlIT` (30/30 green), covering the changed recovery caching on the real database.
- Per-profile declarations: `hosted-workspace-tool-turn.test.ts` "the cron union declarations name only the creators the profile declares" walks shell/4, files/4, team-lead/2 and shell/3, asserting `cron_list` / `cron_delete` (and the delete id description) name `loop_wakeup` / `cron_create` exactly when the profile declares them. The constants are the `(true, true)` composition, so dropping the `cron_create` clause from `cronListDescription` reddens files/4, team-lead/2 and shell/4 alike (mutation verified).
- Creator derivation: `AutomationScannerTest#creatorActorReadsTheSessionRowFromTheSchema` reads the real `ma_session.creator_actor_key` (and empty for a missing Session); `#anEmptyCreatorActorRefusesTheInternalMutation` asserts the 403 `session_operation_forbidden` refusal.
- Label test: emptying the goal slice in the `cron_list` text template now reddens "cron_list labels distinguish same-cron schedules and cut on code points" (mutation verified) — it previously stayed green because the payload satisfied the assertions.
- Cursor paging: `AutomationScannerTest#listSessionPagesWithACursorUnderTheLiveStateFilter` retires one definition, then pages the three live ones with limit 2; the retired row sorts after the cursor (pages order by creation time descending), so dropping the live-state filter from the cursor arm leaks it into the second page and reddens the page-size assertion (mutation verified).
- Suites: `WakeRecoveryStoreTest` 29, `AutomationScannerTest` 86, `ManagedStoreDecompositionTest` 5, `ClassSizeRatchetTest` 1, tool-turn 639 — all green; Managed Agent checkstyle (CI command) 0 violations; prettier clean.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI (recovery caching, tool declarations, tests, docs).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local unit tests (vitest, H2 via the verification module), a real MySQL 8.4 container for `WakeRecoveryMySqlIT`, and the Managed Agent checkstyle gate; no real-model turn.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the declaration text changes are model-facing wording; the per-profile assembly is covered by the declaration test across all four profiles, and the round-2 refactor is byte-neutral on the served text.
- Not validated / out of scope: a real `/loop` model-turn E2E and the managed loop skill asset remain out of scope (as declared in #17088). The web-shell smoke flake observed on #17088's CI was independently fixed on main by #17187 and is not touched here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

prs.title: ci(release): retry the Docker integration test suites once
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The release Docker integration script now runs its `cli` and `interactive` suites through a single helper and retries a failed suite once when the step is still within its retry budget. Before the retry it removes the containers labeled with its own job owner, so a container leaked by the first attempt cannot affect the second. A sandbox-image build failure now emits an `::error::` annotation stating that the Docker tests did not run, and a suite that fails again after the retry emits its own `::error::`; both become check-run annotations instead of leaving only "Process completed with exit code 1."

## Why it's needed

This is release-lane hardening, not the fix for the nightly failure it was originally drafted against. The motivating incident — `integration_docker` exiting 1 after 38m37s of a 120-minute job for `v0.27.1-nightly.20261110.c238beb56f` (run 42902215339, job 130132787607), with the previous nightly failing the same way (#16769) — turned out to be a **deterministic sandbox `$HOME` crash**, not shared-host transient pressure. The failed job's log is readable with a repo-scoped token (only anonymous access 403s), and the defect was fixed in #16878, which closed #16861. A bounded retry cannot change a deterministic failure's outcome: both attempts fail and the lane stays red (pinned by the `keeps the lane red when the motivating 38-minute cli failure repeats` case).

What the release lane actually lacked, and this PR adds, is the resilience and diagnosability the `sandbox:none` E2E leg already has (#10355): a suite-level retry for genuinely transient failures, and explicit build-versus-test failure annotations. The release job has 120 minutes, so a failed attempt early in the step leaves room for one more; the E2E Docker leg's 60-minute job cannot fit two attempts, which is why it does not retry. The build failure path is made explicit but deliberately not retried, because the build holds the shared host build mutex.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused script suite; it drives the real release Docker script against stubbed `git`, `node`, `docker`, `npm`, `npx`, `date`, `timeout`, and `flock` binaries. The cases simulate a first-attempt suite failure followed by a pass, the same for the second suite, a second failure after the retry, a failure after the retry budget is spent, a build failure, and check that job-owned containers are removed before the retry.

Expected: 135 tests collected. On Linux all 135 run; on macOS 134 pass and 1 pre-existing platform-conditional case skips (`executes the workspace wipe against guard branches`, which needs GNU `realpath -m`).

Then inspect the script: a failed suite is retried once only when `elapsed_seconds + max(attempt_seconds, expected_suite_seconds) + remaining_suite_seconds <= DOCKER_TEST_STEP_BUDGET_SECONDS` — a 6600s step budget, with `expected_suite_seconds` 2400s for `cli` and 1260s for `interactive`, and 1260s reserved for `interactive` when retrying `cli`. A failure that would overrun the budget exits with the budget `::error::` instead of retrying, and a build failure prints the new annotation without running vitest.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for screenshots: this changes CI orchestration, not a user-visible or interactive surface. The before/after behavior is pinned by the script harness's call log and the mutation probes listed in the E2E report.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Linux container without a Docker daemon or socket. Build, typecheck, lint, the focused script suite, and ShellCheck 0.11.0 were run; the real Docker integration lane was not run locally because the daemon is unavailable.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a genuinely transient suite failure can add one extra suite run (roughly 30–40 minutes) before the step finishes. The budget gate refuses a retry that would overrun the 120-minute job, and a deterministic failure still fails both attempts, so the step cannot turn green on a real defect.
- Not validated / out of scope: the exact self-hosted Docker lane under real transient load. The motivating nightly failure was a deterministic sandbox `$HOME` crash, fixed in #16878, not a transient this retry absorbs; this change hardens the lane against genuinely transient failures and makes future build-versus-test failures visible through check-run annotations. Build failures are not retried because the build holds the shared host build mutex.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No product code, settings, or user-facing behavior changes.

## Linked Issues

Part of #16861 (closed by #16878, the deterministic sandbox `$HOME` fix; this PR is release-lane hardening, not that fix).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

发布 Docker 集成脚本现在通过一个辅助函数运行 `cli` 和 `interactive` 套件，并在步骤仍处于重试预算内时，对失败的套件重试一次。重试前，它会删除带有本任务 owner 标签的容器，避免第一次尝试泄漏的容器影响第二次。沙箱镜像构建失败现在会输出 `::error::` 注解，说明 Docker 测试没有运行；重试后再次失败的套件也会输出自己的 `::error::`；两者都会成为 check-run 注解，而不是只留下 "Process completed with exit code 1."

## 为什么需要这个改动

这是发布流水线的加固，而不是它最初所针对的那次夜间发布失败的修复。触发事件——`v0.27.1-nightly.20261110.c238beb56f` 的 `integration_docker` 在 120 分钟任务的第 38 分 37 秒以退出码 1 结束（运行 42902215339，任务 130132787607），且前一次夜间发布也以同样方式失败（#16769）——最终查明是**确定性的沙箱 `$HOME` 崩溃**，而不是共享宿主机瞬时压力。失败任务的日志用仓库作用域 token 可读（只有匿名访问才 403），该缺陷已在 #16878 修复，#16861 随之关闭。有界重试无法改变确定性失败的结果：两次尝试都会失败，流水线保持红色（由 `keeps the lane red when the motivating 38-minute cli failure repeats` 用例固定）。

发布流水线真正缺少、而本 PR 补上的，是 `sandbox:none` E2E 流水线早已具备的韧性与可诊断性（#10355）：针对真正瞬时失败的套件级重试，以及显式的「构建失败 vs 测试失败」注解。发布任务有 120 分钟，因此步骤早期的失败尝试仍留有一次重试的空间；E2E Docker 流水线的 60 分钟任务装不下两次尝试，这正是它不重试的原因。构建失败路径被显式标注，但有意不重试，因为构建持有共享宿主机的构建互斥锁。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

运行聚焦的脚本测试套件；它用桩程序 `git`、`node`、`docker`、`npm`、`npx`、`date`、`timeout` 和 `flock` 驱动真实的发布 Docker 脚本。用例模拟第一次套件失败后通过、第二个套件同样失败后通过、重试后再次失败、重试预算耗尽后的失败、构建失败，并检查重试前会删除本任务的容器。

预期：收集 135 个测试。Linux 上全部 135 个运行；macOS 上 134 个通过、1 个既有的平台条件用例跳过（`executes the workspace wipe against guard branches`，需要 GNU `realpath -m`）。

然后检查脚本：失败的套件只有在 `elapsed_seconds + max(attempt_seconds, expected_suite_seconds) + remaining_suite_seconds <= DOCKER_TEST_STEP_BUDGET_SECONDS` 时才重试一次——步骤预算 6600 秒，`expected_suite_seconds` 对 `cli` 为 2400 秒、对 `interactive` 为 1260 秒，重试 `cli` 时为 `interactive` 预留 1260 秒。会超出预算的失败将带着预算 `::error::` 退出而不是重试；构建失败会打印新注解且不运行 vitest。

### 证据（改动前后）

截图不适用：这改变的是 CI 编排，不是用户可见或交互式界面。改动前后的行为由脚本 harness 的调用日志和 E2E 报告中列出的变异探测固定。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

本地 Linux 容器，没有 Docker daemon 或 socket。已运行构建、类型检查、lint、聚焦脚本套件和 ShellCheck 0.11.0；由于 daemon 不可用，本地未运行真实 Docker 集成流水线。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：真正的瞬时套件失败可能会在步骤结束前多跑一次套件（大约 30–40 分钟）。预算门限会拒绝将超出 120 分钟任务的重试，确定性失败仍然会让两次尝试都失败，因此步骤不会因为真实缺陷而变绿。
- 未验证 / 范围外：真实瞬时负载下的确切自托管 Docker 流水线。触发的那次夜间发布失败是确定性沙箱 `$HOME` 崩溃，已在 #16878 修复，不是本重试能吸收的瞬时故障；此改动加固流水线以应对真正的瞬时失败，并通过 check-run 注解让未来的构建失败与测试失败可见。构建失败不重试，因为构建持有共享宿主机构建互斥锁。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。没有产品代码、设置或用户可见行为变更。

## 关联 Issue

Part of #16861（已由 #16878 关闭，即确定性沙箱 `$HOME` 修复；本 PR 是发布流水线加固，不是该修复）。

</details>

prs.title: test(ci): stabilize the macOS nightly CI legs
prs.body:
## Problem

The nightly `schedule` leg of Qwen Code CI has been red for 10+ consecutive nights (runs 43491119975, 43289039867, 43086181053, 42884117073, …). The macOS unit-test matrix only expands on `schedule`, so these failures never surface on push or PR runs. Four distinct signatures recur:

| Leg | Signature | Nights observed | Class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| scripts | `qwen-autofix-workflow.test.js:714` — `AssertionError: expected NaN to be 120` | 11-10 … 11-13 (every night since #16777) | deterministic |
| cli 2/3 | `SubscriptionDialog.test.tsx` — `switches account with the keyboard (canCheckAgain=true)`, spy 0 calls | 11-10, 11-12, 11-13 | load flake |
| cli 1/3 | `session-pr-refresh.test.ts` — Aone `mr view` case (`updated: 0, aoneConsumed: undefined`) and the rotation sweep case (view 1× instead of 2×) | 11-10, 11-11, 11-12, 11-13 | load flake |
| core 2/2 | `file-changed-watcher.test.ts` — real-file cases, 0 notifications within 5s (three different cases) | 11-12, 11-13 | load flake |

## Fixes (one commit each)

1. **`test(ci): gate the autofix staleness derivation witness on GNU date`** — the witness executes the workflow's `date -u -d "N minutes ago"` lines on the host; macOS BSD date rejects the relative string, both timestamps come back empty, and the gap reads `NaN`. The production step only runs on Linux runners. Adds a `hasGnuDate` host probe in the file's established `hasBashMapfile`/`hasSha256sum` shape and gates only the executed derivation; all text pins stay unconditional.
2. **`test(cli): align SubscriptionDialog waits with the AuthDialog budget`** — all 11 bare `vi.waitFor` calls (1s default) now use `WAIT_FOR_TIMEOUT = 5000`, the same constant the sibling `AuthDialog.test.tsx` already uses. The Enter→handler→render chain exceeds 1s on the contended 3-core macOS hosts.
3. **`test(cli): deflake the session-pr-refresh nightly cases`** — (a) the Aone origin probe spawns real git under a 5s budget and degrades to `undefined` when the spawn times out under load; the delegating spy now retries the REAL resolution once inside the single spy call (per-sweep call-count pins stay 1), the same retry-under-load shape `removeTempTree` uses. (b) The rotation sweep case: the re-entrancy guard skips an interval whose predecessor's refresh tail is still in flight, and `waitFor`'s fake-time budget cannot reach the next 60s interval; the test now advances intervals until the second view lands (skipped ticks do not advance the rotation counter, so the order stays [42, 43]) and both view waits use the sibling case's explicit 10s budget.
4. **`test(core): widen the real-file watcher waits for contended hosts`** — `waitOptions` 5s → 15s: FSEvents delivery plus the watcher's `awaitWriteFinish` stability polling (200ms threshold, 50ms poll) stretches past 5s under saturation; 15s matches the repo's other contended-host waits.

## Verification

- **GNU-date gate, 4 arms** (byte-level restore checked with `sha256sum -c`): Linux host green with the executed witness running; BSD-date shim fronting PATH green (gate skips); shim + gate removed red with the exact nightly signature `AssertionError: expected NaN to be 120`; Linux + tier-collapse mutation on the unpinned first cutoff line red (`0` vs `120`), proving the executed witness still bites.
- **SubscriptionDialog budget, 2 arms**: with a 1.2s delay injected into the production `onUseAnotherAccount` path, the old 1s budget fails and the new 5s budget passes (both `canCheckAgain` variants); component restored byte-identical. Full file: 11/11 green; test-title set unchanged.
- **session-pr-refresh**: Aone describe (all cases) and the rotation sweep case green; full file 94 passed with 3 pre-existing `drainNow` failures that fail identically on the unmodified `origin/main` file in this environment (stale symlinked dist; unrelated to this change).
- **watcher**: full file 28/28 green on Linux. The macOS-load stall itself cannot be reproduced on a Linux host; the budget widening follows the repo's established contended-host precedent.
- `prettier --check` passes on every touched file; `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors in the touched files (the checkout's symlinked dist produces unrelated baseline errors in `acp-integration`/`channel` files; PR CI builds fresh).

## Test plan

From the repo root:

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/qwen-autofix-workflow.test.js -t 'runs scheduled autofix as a 10-minute multi-target fan-out worker'
cd packages/cli && CI=1 ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/ui/auth/SubscriptionDialog.test.tsx src/serve/server/session-pr-refresh.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
cd packages/core && CI=1 ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/hooks/file-changed-watcher.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
```

The nightly macOS legs are the authoritative witness; the next scheduled runs after merge should clear these four signatures.

prs.title: test(ci): name the shape the tree-ref encoder actually guards
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Clears the two Suggestions left on #16747 and the review rounds that followed. Test-only, no production change: corrects false statements in test comments, pins the ref encoders with one all-hazards sample asserted per site, gives each half of the truncated-tree guard its own witness, and covers the two wiring points nothing watched — `main()`'s base-ref hand-off and the ci.yml fixture's merge-base argument.

## Why it's needed

The comment on the slash case said an unencoded ref containing `/` would 404, so the narrowing would throw into the fail-closed catch and keep the verdict — "a false red rather than a false green". That is wrong, and it was the only written justification for `encodeURIComponent` on that path.

Measured against the live API with a real slash-named branch:

```
git/trees/agent/agent-view-commands?recursive=1    -> 200  sha=6f32d53c…  8638 entries
git/trees/agent%2Fagent-view-commands?recursive=1  -> 200  sha=6f32d53c…  8638 entries
```

Same tree. The 404 originally cited for `release/1.0` was simply a branch that does not exist.

What the encoder actually guards is `#` and `%`, both legal in a git branch name. An unencoded `#` starts the fragment and takes `?recursive=1` with it, so the request answers for a **different ref** instead of failing:

```
git/trees/main#frag?recursive=1    -> 200    42 entries   (top level only)
git/trees/main%23frag?recursive=1  -> 404
git/trees/main?recursive=1         -> 200 16226 entries
```

That is a silent wrong-tree read, not a fail-closed refusal. The hazard matters because of how the false comment reads: someone who checks it against a real slash-named branch finds it untrue, concludes the encoder is decoration, and deletes it — at which point a `fix#1`-style base ref stops being refused and starts reading the wrong tree. `BASE_REF` is wired to `github.event.pull_request.base.ref`, so such a name reaches this path verbatim.

### The second Suggestion: each truncated-tree arm needs its own witness

The truncation case shared one `truncated` flag across both trees, so the guard's two halves were indistinguishable. Measured before changing anything:

```
keep baseTree.truncated only  -> 74 pass / 0 fail
keep headTree.truncated only  -> 74 pass / 0 fail
```

Both arms survived their own removal. The fixture now takes per-side flags (`truncated` remains shorthand for both) and the case runs once per shape. Each arm has a sole witness:

```
keep base only -> ✖ (only the head tree)   75 pass / 1 fail
keep head only -> ✖ (only the base tree)   75 pass / 1 fail
```

Production behaviour is unchanged and was already correct on all three shapes — this only makes the two halves separately enforceable.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```
node --test .github/scripts/check-lint-gate-freshness.test.mjs
```

Expect 82 passing on this base (also with CI's `--test-concurrency=1`).
```
ℹ tests 82 / pass 78 / fail 4
✖ a base ref containing a hash is URI-encoded in the tree path
  AssertionError: expected an encoded tree ref, got [ … "/git/trees/fix#1?recursive=1" … ]
✖ a base ref containing a percent is URI-encoded in the tree path
✖ every prettier-path URL encodes a ref carrying every hazardous character
✖ a base ref containing a slash is URI-encoded in the tree path
```

The logged path shows the unencoded `fix#1` reaching the request, which is the shape that misbehaves in production. Source restored byte-identically afterwards (SHA-256 compared).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

清掉 #16747 上遗留的两条 Suggestion 以及随后几轮评审的发现。纯测试改动、生产代码不变：订正注释中的错误陈述、用一个全危险字符样本按站点钉住各 ref 编码器、让截断守卫的两半各有独立见证，并补上两处此前无人看守的接线——`main()` 的 base ref 传递，以及 ci.yml 夹具的 merge base 参数。

## 为什么需要

斜杠用例的注释原本写「含 `/` 的 ref 不编码会 404，收窄抛进 fail-closed catch 保留判定——是假红而非假绿」。这是错的，而它是该路径上 `encodeURIComponent` 唯一的书面依据。

用真实含斜杠分支对线上 API 实测：`git/trees/agent/agent-view-commands?recursive=1` 与编码形式**都是 200、同一 tree sha、同样 8638 条**。当初引用的 `release/1.0` 404 只是因为该分支不存在。

编码器真正防的是 `#` 与 `%`（二者都是合法分支名字符）。未编码的 `#` 会被当作 fragment 起点并吞掉 `?recursive=1`，请求于是返回**另一个 ref**而不是失败：`main#frag` → 200 / 42 条（仅顶层），`main%23frag` → 404，纯 `main` → 200 / 16226 条。这是静默读错树，不是 fail-closed 拒绝。

危险在于这条假注释的读法：维护者拿真实含斜杠分支一验发现不成立，就会判定编码是多余装饰并删掉；此后 `fix#1` 这类基线 ref 不再被拒绝，而是开始读错树。`BASE_REF` 接的是 `github.event.pull_request.base.ref`，这种名字会原样到达该路径。

### 第二条 Suggestion：截断守卫的两半各需独立见证

截断用例原本两侧共用一个 `truncated` 标志，守卫的两半无法区分。改动前实测：只保留 `baseTree.truncated` → 74 通过 0 失败；只保留 `headTree.truncated` → 同样 74 通过 0 失败——两臂都从自己的移除中存活。

夹具改为按侧取标志（`truncated` 保留为「两侧」的简写），用例按形状各跑一次。现在每臂都有唯一见证：只留 base 臂 → 恰好打红「仅分支截断」（75 通过 1 失败）；只留 head 臂 → 恰好打红「仅基线截断」（75 通过 1 失败）。

生产行为不变、三种形状本来就正确；这只是让两半分别可被强制。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

运行 `node --test .github/scripts/check-lint-gate-freshness.test.mjs`，本基线上预期 82 条通过（带 CI 的 `--test-concurrency=1` 亦然）。已按父提交用例标题集合核对：无丢失；新增 hash 与 percent 两条 ref 用例、ci.yml 收窄自身编码器的用例、在两条路径上按站点断言的全危险字符样本、`main()` 原样传递 `BASE_REF` 的源码钉，以及 ci.yml 夹具的第二个不同 merge base，并把原先单条截断用例有意拆成三种形状（两侧 / 仅基线 / 仅分支）。

斜杠用例保留：它仍钉住编码后的字符串，注释现在如实这么说，而不再声称 404。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A —— 无用户可见 surface，证据是上面的 API 实测与变异输出。

Linux 上 Node v24.22.1。单元套件加线上 API 探针，不涉及构建或沙箱。

prs.title: fix(core): do not call a command read-only when a redirection hides part of it
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The read-only shell classifier no longer calls a command read-only when part of the command is hidden inside a redirection node.

- **A file redirection followed by more words.** `git branch < /dev/null -D main` and `find . 2>&1 -delete` now classify `unknown`. A redirection that carries more words than its operator takes is not read-only: one for every operator except `<&-` and `>&-`, which close a descriptor and take none, so `find . >&- -delete` is `unknown` too.
- **A heredoc followed by more on the same line.** Whatever shares the heredoc's first line is now judged: a redirection or a statement by the existing rule for its kind, a plain word as `unknown`. `cat <<EOF > out.txt` and `cat <<EOF && rm x` now classify `write`; `cat <<EOF | sh` classifies `unknown`.
- **A command in a heredoc body.** When the delimiter is unquoted, bash expands the body, and the parse tree does not show what it expands: a backtick substitution is plain text there, and so is `$(...)` behind leading whitespace. The body is therefore read from its own text. Every expansion bash performs in a heredoc body starts with `$` or a backtick, so an expandable body holding either is `unknown`. `detectCommandSubstitution` in `shell-utils.ts` already scans a heredoc body's text this way for `$(` and a backtick; this is the same test on the AST path, widened to any `$` because `$[x]` and `$((x))` run a command held in `x`. With a delimiter quoted as a whole (`'EOF'`, `"EOF"`, `\EOF`) the body stays read-only. A delimiter that is neither one plain word nor quoted as a whole, such as `${X:-'E'}` or `$X`, is `unknown` whatever the body holds.

A redirection with one word, a heredoc with nothing after it, and a heredoc piped into a read-only command stay read-only.

## Why it's needed

A read-only verdict is an allow with no prompt and no classifier call (`ShellToolInvocation.getDefaultPermission`, `if (isReadOnly) { return 'allow'; }`). tree-sitter-bash files the words after a redirection under the redirection node, so `getArgumentNodes` never returns them and no rule reads them. #16856 has the mechanism and the first set of cases.

**Behaviour change to accept on purpose:** `cat <<EOF > file` is how an agent often writes a file. On `main` it classifies read-only, so it takes the read-only fast path. With this PR it is a `write` like any other output redirection.

While fixing the issue I found two more shapes that are not in it:

- `2>&1` in the middle of a command hides the words after it the same way as `<`.
- A heredoc hides the rest of its first line. The redirection, the pipeline or the next command of a list is a child of the `heredoc_redirect` node, and `evaluateRedirectionSafety` only looked inside that node for command substitutions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

`packages/core/src/utils/shellAstParser.test.ts`, `describe('words after a redirection in the middle of a command')`. The new cases fail on `main`'s source (39 failures) and pass with the change; the controls pass on both.

A sweep outside the test file: each of 27 redirection spellings and 7 heredoc spellings inserted at every word boundary of 7 write commands (`find . -delete`, `git branch -D main`, `sed -i …`, `git push …`, `git remote add …`, `sort -o …`, `tee out`), plus heredocs followed by those commands and heredoc bodies that run something. 1,291 commands: 357 classify read-only on `main`, none on this branch.

A second sweep for heredoc bodies, with real bash as the reference: 26 delimiter spellings × 4 operator forms × 9 bodies (backtick and `$(...)` commands at line start, behind a tab, behind a space and on an indented second line, `$[x]` and `$((x))` with `x` holding a command, and `${V:-$(...)}`), closed both by the delimiter as written and by its quote-removed form. Each body creates a marker file when bash runs it. Of 1,548 commands, 207 on `main` classify read-only while bash (3.2.57) runs the body's command; none do on this branch.

### Evidence (Before & After)

`classifyShellCommandSafety`, measured on `main`'s classifier and on this branch (heredoc rows show the first line; the body and the closing `EOF` follow):

| Command | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `git branch < /dev/null -D main` | read-only | unknown |
| `git < /dev/null push origin main` | read-only | unknown |
| `git remote < /dev/null add origin <url>` | read-only | unknown |
| `find . < /dev/null -delete` | read-only | unknown |
| `sed < /dev/null -i 's/a/b/' f` | read-only | unknown |
| `git branch 2>&1 -D main` | read-only | unknown |
| `find . 2>&1 -delete` | read-only | unknown |
| `find . >&- -delete`, `find . <&- -delete`, `find . 2>&- -delete` | read-only | unknown |
| `git branch <<EOF -D main` | read-only | unknown |
| `cat <<EOF \| sh` | read-only | unknown |
| `cat <<EOF` with `` `id -u` `` in the body | read-only | unknown |
| `cat <<EOF > out.txt` | read-only | write |
| `cat <<EOF && rm x` | read-only | write |
| `cat <<EOF \| tee out.txt` | read-only | write |
| `cat <<EOF \| git push origin main` | read-only | write |

Unchanged (asserted by the new tests):

| Command | Both |
| --- | --- |
| `git status < /dev/null`, `git status 2>&1`, `git status 2>&1 \| head`, `git status >&-`, `git status <<< x` | read-only |
| `cat < a.txt < b.txt`, `cat < "my file.txt"` | read-only |
| `cat <<EOF`, `cat << EOF`, `cat 3<<EOF`, `cat <<EOF # note`, `cat <<EOF \| grep hi`, `cat <<EOF \| grep hi \| wc -l` | read-only |
| `cat <<'EOF'` with a backtick in the body | read-only |
| `git branch -D main < /dev/null`, `git branch > out.txt -D main`, `< /dev/null git push origin main`, `git branch <<< x -D main` | write |

Local run: `shellAstParser`, `shellReadOnlyChecker`, `shell-utils`, `plan-mode-shell-policy`, `coreToolScheduler`, `tools/monitor`, `tools/shell` and all of `permissions/`: 23 files, 3,753 tests passed at `ecf4814f4e` (`main` merged at `5916929761`). ESLint and Prettier are clean on the two changed files.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only. The classifier was called directly from the source tree; I did not run an end-to-end AUTO session.

## Risk & Scope

- **Design choice for the words after a file redirection.** The issue offered two directions: collect those words back into the argument list, or refuse read-only when they are present. This PR takes the second. Collecting them would give exact verdicts (`git < /dev/null push` would be `write`, not `unknown`), but it means rebuilding the argument list bash hands the program, with ordering across several redirections to get right. Refusing needs no model of bash, so it cannot be wrong about one. If you prefer exact verdicts I can do the first as a follow-up.
- **Why the heredoc is handled differently.** Refusing everything after a heredoc would also stop `cat <<EOF | grep hi`, which is common and harmless. The pipeline, command or redirection inside the heredoc node is a complete node of a kind the classifier already judges, so it is passed to the existing rule. Only a bare word is refused, and so is any node the classifier has no rule for.
- **Main risk or tradeoff:** more prompts. A harmless command that puts words after a redirection, such as `cat < a.txt b.txt` or `grep foo < in.txt -r .`, now classifies `unknown`. And `cat <<EOF > file` goes from the read-only fast path to a `write`, as described above. A heredoc with an unusual delimiter (`"$X"`, `E"O"F`, `$'EOF'`) is `unknown` even where bash would leave its body alone; only the three whole-delimiter quotings are vouched for. A heredoc under a plain delimiter whose body holds any `$`, such as `$HOME`, is `unknown` too, although a bare variable runs nothing.
- **Not in this PR (review finding R1-3):** `extractCommandRules` builds the "always allow" rule from the same shortened argument list, so approving `git < /dev/null push origin main` offers the rule `git`. On `main` that dialog never appears because the command is read-only; with this PR it can. What rule should be offered for such a spelling, or whether none should be, is a separate decision in a different function, and I would rather a maintainer made it than widen this PR.
- **Not in this PR (review finding R3-1):** the dialog's rules are built per line, so a heredoc body line becomes a rule of its own. That is already the case on `main` for `cat > f <<EOF` and `tee f <<EOF`; it is written up on #17001, where the fix for that path is planned.
- **Not validated / out of scope:** the regex fallback (`isShellCommandReadOnly`) is unchanged; it already answers not-read-only for every row of the first table. The git-config risk check also reads `getArgumentNodes`; it derives a config warning from it, not a read-only verdict, and is unchanged.
- **Related:** this also covers the remaining finding on #14360 (R11-3, `git remote < /dev/null show <url>`), which the new tests include.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none in the API.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16856

prs.title: feat(cli): add OpenTUI agent creation and read-only details
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Replaces the OpenTUI agent-creation placeholder with manual and Qwen-guided creation, including location, description, tools, color and explicit save confirmation. Adds read-only agent selection and details that work both immediately after saving and after restarting the CLI. Existing Ink color selection now persists canonical color ids accepted by the parser.

Pending generation and save results lose authority when their configuration owner changes or the dialog closes. Cancelling generation retains the editable description; a late response cannot advance the form or overwrite a newer request. Persistence stays with the existing manager and its commit checks. No Core implementation changes are included.

This PR builds on #17148, #15948, #15950 and #15951. Its feature series starts at the current #15951 head and includes the CI follow-up. The increment is 18 files, +2736/-101; the current cumulative upstream-main diff is 33 files, +3565/-152 (gross 3717). Prerequisite changes remain visible until the stack is integrated.

## Why it's needed

OpenTUI exposed `/agents create` as an unusable placeholder, while `/agents manage` could not open a selected agent's details. Users could not complete the existing Ink creation workflow in the native renderer. The existing Ink selector also emitted the display label `Blue` instead of the serialized id `blue`.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Open `/agents create`, cancel at the location screen, and confirm neither agent store changes.
- Choose Manual Creation, enter a name, prompt and description, select tools and Blue, then inspect the confirmation. There must be no file before Save; saving creates the exact project Markdown with `color: blue`, without changing user-level agents or sending a model request.
- Use the deterministic guided interactive case to hold the first generation request, cancel it, and release its response late. The description must remain editable and both stores unchanged. A second explicit generation must populate the review flow through the existing schema, without saving until confirmation.
- Open `/agents manage`, select the new agent and View Agent. Check its description, prompt and color, back out, quit, restart, and inspect the same details and file. Viewing must not mutate either store; both public quits must finish naturally.
- Retain the owner-change, duplicate-submit and stale-completion regressions when reviewing the asynchronous paths.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Cropped actual PTY viewport text from the source-bundle runs:

```text
Before:
Subagent Create
Define a new subagent (name, tools, prompt).

After:
Step 2: Choose Generation Method
› 1. Generate with Qwen Code (Recommended)
  2. Manual Creation

Step 6: Confirm and Save
Name: owned-guided-proof
Tools: *
Color: blue
Description: Use this agent when validating owned guided creation.
System Prompt: You are an owned guided test subagent. Reply only OWNED_GUIDED_REPLY.
```

Initial feature validation: normal build, typecheck, lint and formatting passed, together with 116 tests across six affected whole CLI files. All six complete public cases passed on one source bundle: manual and guided creation under Node/Ink, Bun/Ink and strict Bun/OpenTUI. They completed twelve natural exits; manual cases made zero model requests, and guided cases made six owned loopback requests total, comprising three cancelled and three completed schema responses. A separate E2E report comment records the scope and commands.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Darwin arm64 source bundle: Node 24.19.0/Ink, Bun 1.4.4/Ink, strict Bun 1.4.4/OpenTUI 0.5.10 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested for this increment |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ Exact-head GitHub Actions checks passed; no local Linux run is claimed |

### Environment (optional)

Vitest 3.2.7; isolated owned homes, workspaces and temporary directories; deterministic loopback model fixture; zero test retries. Original 120-second cases and 12-second observation limits are retained. The six public runtime cases belong to the source bundle before the documentation-only status update, matching all thirteen production/test files in the initial head 72447e43. The follow-up 726fe086 changes only a stable ref-object alias in production and updates the virtual-list geometry fixture; those six cases were not rerun on that follow-up. No post-commit installed artifact or final merged-main qualification is claimed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: asynchronous work can outlive its UI owner. Generation and save have explicit ownership checks; already-started filesystem writes cannot be rolled back by closing the dialog.
- Not validated / out of scope: model quality or real external-provider behavior, real user-level overwrite, agent execution/tool enforcement, native manager editing/deletion, external editing, installed/npm/npx/standalone artifacts and full platform migration acceptance.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none intended. Valid lowercase color ids are persisted; legacy in-memory display labels still preview, but invalid `color: Blue` files are not made valid by Core. Renderer defaults and Ink availability are unchanged.

Designs: [manual EN](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/72447e43e59ff1791ee9efbff4d02572a474380f/docs/design/2026-11-13-opentui-manual-agent-creation.md), [manual 中文](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/72447e43e59ff1791ee9efbff4d02572a474380f/docs/design/2026-11-13-opentui-manual-agent-creation.zh-CN.md), [guided EN](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/72447e43e59ff1791ee9efbff4d02572a474380f/docs/design/2026-11-13-opentui-guided-agent-creation.md), [guided 中文](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/72447e43e59ff1791ee9efbff4d02572a474380f/docs/design/2026-11-13-opentui-guided-agent-creation.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Prerequisite PRs: #17148, #15948, #15950, #15951. This PR does not close the overall Ink→OpenTUI migration.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

将 OpenTUI 的 Agent 创建占位面板替换为手动及 Qwen 引导创建，包含位置、描述、工具、颜色及明确保存确认。新增只读 Agent 选择与详情，支持保存后立即查看和 CLI 重启后查看。已有 Ink 颜色选择现持久化 parser 接受的规范颜色 id。

配置 owner 变化或对话框关闭时，待完成的生成与保存结果会失去权限。取消生成保留可编辑描述；晚响应不能推进表单或覆盖更新的请求。持久化仍由已有 manager 及提交检查负责，不包含 Core 实现改动。

本 PR 基于 #17148、#15948、#15950 和 #15951。功能提交序列从当前 #15951 head 开始，并包含 CI 修正。新增量涉及 18 文件，+2736/-101；当前相对上游 main 的累计差异为 33 文件，+3565/-152（gross 3717）。依赖栈整合前，这些前置改动仍会显示在差异中。

## 为什么需要

OpenTUI 的 `/agents create` 原先只有不可用的占位界面，`/agents manage` 也无法打开所选 Agent 的详情，用户不能在原生 renderer 完成 Ink 已有创建流程。已有 Ink 颜色选择器还会输出显示名称 `Blue`，而非序列化 id `blue`。

## 审查者测试计划

### 验证方式

- 打开 `/agents create`，在位置页取消，确认两个 Agent 存储均不改变。
- 选择 Manual Creation，输入名称、提示词与描述，选择工具和 Blue，再检查确认内容。Save 前不应有文件；保存后生成包含 `color: blue` 的精确项目 Markdown，用户级 Agent 不变且无模型请求。
- 使用确定性引导交互用例挂起首次生成请求，取消后晚释放响应。描述应保持可编辑，两个存储不变。第二次明确生成应通过已有 schema 填入检查流程，确认前不保存。
- 打开 `/agents manage`，选择新 Agent 及 View Agent，检查描述、提示词与颜色，返回、退出、重启，再检查相同详情和文件。查看不改变两个存储，两次公开退出均应自然完成。
- 审查异步路径时，保留 owner 变化、重复提交和过期完成结果的回归测试。

### 前后证据

源码 bundle 真实 PTY viewport 的裁剪文本：

```text
Before:
Subagent Create
Define a new subagent (name, tools, prompt).

After:
Step 2: Choose Generation Method
› 1. Generate with Qwen Code (Recommended)
  2. Manual Creation

Step 6: Confirm and Save
Name: owned-guided-proof
Tools: *
Color: blue
Description: Use this agent when validating owned guided creation.
System Prompt: You are an owned guided test subagent. Reply only OWNED_GUIDED_REPLY.
```

初始功能验证：正常 build、typecheck、lint、格式检查和六个受影响 CLI 整文件中的 116 项测试均通过。同一源码 bundle 上六个完整公开用例均通过：Node/Ink、Bun/Ink 和严格 Bun/OpenTUI 下各运行手动与引导创建。共完成十二次自然退出；手动用例无模型请求，引导用例合计六次 owned loopback 请求，包含三次取消及三次完成的 schema 响应。另行发布的 E2E 报告评论记录范围与命令。

### 验证平台

| OS | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Darwin arm64 源码 bundle：Node 24.19.0/Ink、Bun 1.4.4/Ink、严格 Bun 1.4.4/OpenTUI 0.5.10 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 本增量未测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ 精确 head 的 GitHub Actions 检查通过；未声称本地 Linux 运行 |

### 环境

Vitest 3.2.7；隔离 owned HOME、工作区和临时目录；确定性 loopback 模型 fixture；零测试重试。保留原 120 秒用例和 12 秒观察限制。六个公开运行用例对应文档状态更新前的已测源码 bundle，与初始提交 72447e43 的十三个生产及测试文件字节一致。后续提交 726fe086 的生产改动仅为稳定 ref 对象别名，并修正虚拟列表的几何 fixture；没有将旧六案冒充该后续提交的新运行。不宣称提交后的安装产物或最终 merged-main 验收。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险与权衡：异步工作可能晚于 UI owner 完成。生成与保存均有明确权限检查；对话框关闭不能撤回已经开始的文件写入。
- 未验证及范围外：模型质量或真实外部 provider、真实用户级覆盖、Agent 执行与工具权限、原生 manager 编辑和删除、外部编辑、安装/npm/npx/standalone 产物及完整平台迁移验收。
- 兼容性与迁移说明：无预期破坏性变化。持久化有效的小写颜色 id，旧内存显示名称仍可预览，但 Core 不会因此接受无效的 `color: Blue` 文件。Renderer 默认及 Ink 可用性保持不变。

设计：[手动英文](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/72447e43e59ff1791ee9efbff4d02572a474380f/docs/design/2026-11-13-opentui-manual-agent-creation.md)、[手动中文](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/72447e43e59ff1791ee9efbff4d02572a474380f/docs/design/2026-11-13-opentui-manual-agent-creation.zh-CN.md)、[引导英文](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/72447e43e59ff1791ee9efbff4d02572a474380f/docs/design/2026-11-13-opentui-guided-agent-creation.md)、[引导中文](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/72447e43e59ff1791ee9efbff4d02572a474380f/docs/design/2026-11-13-opentui-guided-agent-creation.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联事项

前置 PR：#17148、#15948、#15950、#15951。本 PR 不关闭整体 Ink→OpenTUI 迁移。

</details>


## CI follow-up / CI 修正

726fe086 reproduces and corrects the initial zero-warning ESLint failure and dialog-layout failure without suppressing warnings or increasing waits. Full build, typecheck, all 116 affected unit tests, formatting, zero-warning ESLint and bundle passed after the correction. The exact native layout script passed all original bounded geometry/resize checks, now navigating the virtual agent list with real arrow keys. The full component script remains unqualified locally: the command-registry script stalled before its first matrix output on Darwin/Bun even with the CI-isolated settings; the exact import/initialization boundary is unknown, so both interrupted attempts and forced group cleanup are retained. The exact-head CI completion is recorded below; these interrupted local attempts remain unqualified.
