issues.body:
### Summary

Let OpenClaw subscribe to the events an MCP server in `mcp.servers` advertises (MCP Events draft), and start an agent run for each event, the way a `hooks.mappings` entry does.

### Problem to solve

An MCP server connected through `mcp.servers` can be called by the agent, but it cannot start a run. On current `main` the client advertises `elicitation` and the MCP Apps extension (`buildMcpClientCapabilities` in `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts`), and the only server notification it acts on is `notifications/tools/list_changed`, which refreshes the tool catalog.

So when a server knows that something happened (a new file, a finished transcript, an incident), getting the agent to react takes a second path into the Gateway: a separate process that POSTs to `/hooks/agent` with the hooks token and can reach the Gateway's port, plus a mapping for each source. The server's existing MCP connection and auth can't be used for it.

Concrete case: a meeting recorder whose MCP server announces `transcript.created` when a new transcript is saved. A ChatGPT agent can subscribe to it and write the minutes on its own. In OpenClaw the same server can be connected for its tools, but the event can't start anything.

### Proposed solution

Implement the client side of the MCP Events draft from the Triggers & Events Working Group, starting with the two delivery modes that need no inbound endpoint:

- **poll**: `events/poll` with a persisted cursor, honouring `nextPollMs` with a floor
- **push**: `events/stream`, with `notifications/events/event` and a heartbeat

Webhook delivery (`events/subscribe`) needs a public https callback, so it can come later or not at all.

Each subscription would reuse the action fields that `hooks.mappings` already has, so an event takes the same path as a mapped hook: an isolated session, external-content wrapping, the agent allowlist and the same delivery options. Rough config shape, for a hypothetical meeting-recorder server that emits an event when a transcript is ready:

```json5
mcp: {
  servers: {
    recorder: {
      url: "http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp",
      events: [
        {
          name: "transcript.created",
          arguments: {},
          action: "agent",
          agentId: "notes",
          messageTemplate: "A new meeting transcript is ready: {{data.title}} ({{data.url}}). Read it and write the minutes.",
          channel: "telegram",
          to: "<chat id>",
        },
      ],
    },
  },
}
```

- `eventId` becomes the run's idempotency key, so a replay after a restart doesn't start a second run.
- Off unless a server entry lists `events`.

### Alternatives considered

- **An external process POSTing to `/hooks/agent`.** It works today, and it's what we'd tell OpenClaw users to do meanwhile. It's weaker because every event source re-implements delivery, retries and dedup, needs its own hooks token and network path to the Gateway, and can't describe its events to the operator, even when the source is already an MCP server the agent uses.
- **Watching a specific source, e.g. `gog drive changes poll --on-change` → `/hooks/agent`.** Covers Drive only, not other event sources.
- **#21251 (`resources/subscribe` for plugins).** Closed for inactivity after the author solved their case another way. Resource update notifications carry no payload and don't start a run, so they don't cover this.

### Impact

- Affected: operators who connect MCP servers that front event sources (recorders, issue trackers, monitoring, mail)
- Severity: blocks event-driven use of an MCP server without extra glue
- Frequency: every event-driven integration
- Consequence: a separate webhook sender per source, or cron/heartbeat polling that spends a model call on quiet ticks

### Evidence/examples

- MCP Events design sketch (Triggers & Events WG, draft, not yet an official spec): https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/experimental-ext-triggers-events/blob/main/docs/design-sketch-proposal.md
- ChatGPT consumes MCP events (webhook delivery) to start agent runs: https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-events
- Hermes Agent has an open proposal for the same, poll and stdio push first: NousResearch/hermes-agent#130124

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

The spec is still a draft and the capability shape may change, so this could live behind an experimental flag.

issues.body:
## Summary
Signal replies can never be native voice notes. TTS output sent to Signal always arrives as a plain audio-file attachment, even when the file is Ogg/Opus.

## Evidence (OpenClaw 2026.9.8, @openclaw/signal 2026.9.8, signal-cli 0.14.7)
- `docs/tools/tts.md`: native voice messages are limited to Feishu, Matrix, Telegram, WhatsApp; "Every other channel receives an audio attachment."
- `@openclaw/signal` `send` (dist/.setup/send-*.mjs) builds `params.attachments = [path]` and never sets a voice flag. `grep -ri "voice\|opus"` over the whole plugin package returns nothing. `payload.audioAsVoice` (honoured by the Telegram outbound adapter as `asVoice`) is ignored on Signal.
- signal-cli supports it: `signal-cli send --help` lists `--voice-note` (added in its CHANGELOG), so the transport can do it.
- `tts.convert` with an ElevenLabs provider returns `outputFormat: mp3_44100_128`, `voiceCompatible: false` for a Signal target. There is no ElevenLabs `outputFormat` config key, so the format cannot be forced to Opus via config either.
- A hand-converted Ogg/Opus file sent as media on Signal still arrives as a file attachment.

## Expected
When a reply payload has `audioAsVoice: true` (or the Signal channel advertises voice-note support), TTS should choose a voice-compatible format (Opus), and the Signal plugin should pass the voice-note flag to signal-cli so the recipient sees a voice message.

## Related, not duplicate
#132736 (closed; Signal TTS supplement hang), #70439 (Signal inbound voice-note transcription).

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), npm global install, node v24.16.0; gateway as systemd user unit, Ubuntu (kernel 7.0.0-3x), single host
- 15-agent organization; mixed tool profiles (`full` and `coding` per agent; root tools.profile=coding); `tools.sessions.visibility=all`; `agentToAgent` enabled
- Session kinds in daily use: main lanes, an interactive dashboard lane, isolated cron runs, collector subagents

## Symptoms
1. The agent-side `automations` tool (documented in docs/automation/cron-jobs/managing-jobs.md) disappeared from the per-turn tool inventory of **every** observed session: a `full`-profile main lane, a `coding`-profile main lane, and a **fresh isolated minimal-context subagent probe** (lightContext, ~200 input tokens).
2. The flip happened **mid-session during normal operation**: last confirmed successful tool call 2026-10-04 ~13:0x local; first confirmed absence 2026-10-05 ~01:4x. In that window: **zero gateway restarts, zero host restarts, zero config-file changes** (config mtime 2026-10-04 12:12 precedes the last successful use — the tool worked after that write).
3. **Persistent across cold restarts**: a host reboot (10-06 12:39) and a gateway-only restart (10-07 06:16) did not restore the tool.
4. **Silent**: no error/warn lines in gateway logs at flip time; post-restart boot logs show no registration errors; plugin inventory identical across four gateway generations spanning the window (15 plugins, stable list).
5. Discovered days later only because an agent reported "tool absent in all turns today"; the org had silently fallen back to the CLI.

## Code-level gate (read from the installed dist bundle)
- Tool-injection filter (agent-tools module) drops `automations` when `!(cronCreatorAuthorityResolver || cronManagementGrant)`.
- Resolver binding: `cronCreatorAuthorityResolver = bindActiveCronCreatorAuthorityResolver(options?.runId)` (agent-runtime-identity-token module) — a **per-run authority binding**.
- State DB: table `worker_turn_tool_authorities` (session_id, environment_id, owner_epoch, placement_generation, claim_id, run_id, tool_names_json, updated_at_ms) holds **0 rows** — no per-run tool authority is persisted for any session.
- `device_auth_tokens`: single operator token with scopes `operator.admin/approvals/read/write`, **unchanged for ~3.5 weeks** (long before the flip) — operator auth stable.

## Non-causes excluded (with evidence)
- **Config deny/allow**: full-text config grep for "automations" = 0 hits; per-agent deny lists cover browser/canvas/messaging/calendar tools only; `agents.defaults.tools=null`; `agents.defaults.experimental=null` (lean mode not set).
- **Plugin registry**: boot-line plugin inventory identical across four gateway generations before/after the flip.
- **Context-size tool trimming**: fresh minimal-context isolated probe also lacks the tool.
- **Operator auth**: device token unchanged since well before the flip.
- **Version**: same build (2026.9.4 / 3a9d69d) throughout — the tool was present under the identical binary hours before the flip.

## Expected vs actual
- Expected: `automations` availability stable for authorized sessions (as it had been for weeks), and any entitlement flip to be logged/auditable and recoverable (restart or re-auth).
- Actual: silent, org-wide, mid-session flip; no audit trail (authority table empty); unrecoverable across cold restarts; only the per-run resolver outcome appears to have changed.

## Mitigation in place (our side)
- Org-wide migration to `openclaw cron` / `openclaw automations` CLI — full functional parity for our usage (one-shot `--at`, `--delete-after-run`, `--model`, best-effort delivery, agent-run wrapped payloads). Zero operational loss, but in-turn tool ergonomics are gone and the entitlement state remains flipped.

## Asks
1. What populates `worker_turn_tool_authorities`, and what does `bindActiveCronCreatorAuthorityResolver(runId)` resolve against? Under what condition does it start returning falsy for **all** runs, persistently, with no config change, no restart, and no log line?
2. Should entitlement flips emit an audit/log event? Is there a supported re-grant or re-auth path short of a version upgrade (e.g., operator.admin re-authentication)?
3. Known issue in releases after 2026.9.4?
4. Domain-separation note: filed separately from #166035 (supervisor child-process accumulation) and #166137 (egress sentinel substitution) — distinct subsystems, separate issues for triage hygiene.

issues.body:
### Bug

The main Telegram DM session stops taking new turns. Its follow-up queue retries the same failure every 5 seconds and never admits the owner's messages.

### Observed

OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (`847611d`). Session `agent:main:telegram:direct:alex`.

From 2026-11-14 09:21 Asia/Bangkok through at least 09:58, the gateway log repeats:

`followup queue drain failed for agent:main:telegram:direct:alex: Error: channel restart recovery requires source-keyed user-turn admission`

430 failures in that window, about one every 5 seconds. The session status stays `done`. The transcript has no user turn after 09:24. Messages the owner sent at 09:28, 09:30 and 09:54 were not answered. The last delivered reply was 09:24.

Just before the first failure the log has `recorded message-tool-only run outcome` and `agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only)`.

### Expected

A follow-up that cannot be admitted is dropped or parked once, and the owner's next message still starts a turn.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (`847611d`), Gateway on Linux, Telegram DM, `messages.visibleReplies: message_tool`.

### Evidence scope

Observed in `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-11-14.log` and the session transcript. Not induced. Not tried: a Gateway restart. The error text is the restart-recovery path itself, so a restart is not assumed to clear it.

issues.body:
### Summary

Move the generated Control UI translation memory (`ui/src/i18n/.i18n/*.tm.jsonl`) out of `main` so the repository's history stops growing by ~4 MB file versions on every locale refresh.

### Problem to solve

The translation-memory files are now most of the repository's clone size. In a full clone of `openclaw/openclaw` (all branches, 105k commits, 5.24 GiB pack), the on-disk blob size breaks down as:

| Path | On-disk size |
|---|---|
| `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` | **3.53 GiB** |
| everything else | 1.30 GiB |
| `mantis/` QA gifs (`qa-artifacts` branch) | 0.08 GiB |
| committed Swift `.build/` caches | 0.06 GiB |
| committed `.serena/` cache | 0.01 GiB |

On `origin/main` alone:
- 20 TM files, 85 MB in the current tree (~4 MB each)
- 813 commits touching them since 2026-04-05 (343 `github-actions[bot]`, 327 `openclaw-mantis[bot]`)
- 9,307 distinct TM blob versions

Each refresh only changes a few lines per file (for example, #165213 is +100/-20 across 20 files, and #165010 is +20/-20). But every refresh stores a new version of each ~4 MB file, and the `control-ui-locale-refresh` workflow runs on a daily cron plus on pushes. That adds up to 20 large blob versions per run, indefinitely.

#159032 reported the clone size and was closed as needing a GitHub-side repack. That repack would help existing clones. This issue is about the source-side cause, which a repack doesn't fix: the workflow keeps adding history at this rate.

### Proposed solution

Keep the translation memory out of `main`'s tree. Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. **Dedicated orphan branch or separate repo for TM** (for example, `i18n-memory`). The locale workflow reads and writes TM there and only commits the generated `ui/src/i18n/locales/*.ts` output to `main`. The TM history still exists but no longer comes with every clone of `main`, and `--single-branch` clones skip it entirely.
2. **Store TM as a CI artifact or cache** (Actions cache or a release asset), restored at the start of `control-ui-locale-refresh.yml` and saved at the end. This only works if TM loss is recoverable, for example by retranslating with the existing "retranslate every source string" input.
3. **Git LFS for `*.tm.jsonl`.** This is the smallest workflow change, but it adds an LFS dependency for contributors and bandwidth costs on GitHub.

`ui/AGENTS.md` already treats these files as generated and workflow-owned rather than hand-edited, so moving them shouldn't affect contributors.

### Alternatives considered

- **GitHub support repack only (#159032):** shrinks the current pack (the reporter there saw 6.2 GiB → 1.2 GiB after a local repack) but does nothing about future growth.
- **History rewrite (filter-repo) to purge old TM versions:** would fix past history too, but breaks every fork and open PR. That seems out of proportion.
- **Shrinking each file (shard per namespace, drop `updated_at`):** reduces per-version cost but keeps the unbounded growth.

### Impact

- **Affected:** anyone doing a full clone. That includes contributors, forks, people self-hosting from source, and CI jobs without `--filter`/`--depth`.
- **Severity:** annoying to workflow-blocking on slow or metered connections or small disks.
- **Frequency:** every full clone. Growth continues on every locale refresh (at least daily).
- **Consequence:** multi-GB clones and fetches, slow `git gc`, and disk pressure on dev machines.

### Evidence/examples

Measured on a full clone fetched 2026-10-05:

```sh
# on-disk blob size by category
git rev-list --objects --all \
  | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectsize:disk) %(rest)' \
  | awk '$1=="blob" && $3 ~ /\.tm\.jsonl$/ {s+=$2} END {printf "%.2f GiB\n", s/2^30}'
# -> 3.53 GiB

git log --oneline origin/main -- 'ui/src/i18n/.i18n/*.tm.jsonl' | wc -l          # 813
git rev-list --objects origin/main -- ui/src/i18n/.i18n/ | grep -c 'tm.jsonl$'   # 9307
```

Workflow: `.github/workflows/control-ui-locale-refresh.yml`. It stages `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/${LOCALE}.tm.jsonl` (around line 205) and publishes `*.tm.jsonl` via the `automation/control-ui-locale-refresh` branch (around line 277). The cron is `23 4 * * *`.

Related: #159032 (clone size report, closed as needing a GitHub-side repack).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Separately from this change, a server-side repack via GitHub support (as #159032 suggested) would still be worthwhile for the existing history. Until then, contributors can use `git clone --filter=blob:none` or run `git repack -a -d -f --depth=50 --window=250` locally.



---

**Update 2026-10-08 — still reproducible on `main`** (v2026.10.1-beta.2 @ `e73b64b7f62`):

- Workflow unchanged. `.github/workflows/control-ui-locale-refresh.yml` still crons on `23 4 * * *` (line 36), stages `*.tm.jsonl` (line 207), and publishes via the `automation/control-ui-locale-refresh` branch (lines 276–279).
- 20 `.tm.jsonl` files currently tracked on `main`, totalling **84.1 MiB** (`git ls-tree -l -r origin/main ui/src/i18n/.i18n/`).
- **13 refresh commits touching `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` on `main` since this issue was filed on 2026-10-05** — the daily cron keeps running and keeps adding ~4 MB × 20 blob versions per refresh.
- No mitigation landed: no `.gitattributes` LFS rules for `*.tm.jsonl`, no orphan-branch migration, no alternative storage!

issues.body:
Observed on installed OpenClaw 2026.9.8. A bounded isolated cron test used a collector-mode profile spawn, explicitly collected its result, and continued in the parent to commit a verification marker through native automation scratch CAS. The requested terminal outcome was silent (`NO_REPLY`), with no child announcement.

Actual: child completion and parent continuation were verified, but the cron run ended after approximately 68 seconds with `Agent couldn't generate a response` and a warning that tool actions may already have occurred. Parent Gateway diagnostics reported `stopReason=stop`, `hasLastAssistant=yes`, `hasCurrentAttemptAssistant=yes`, `payloads=0`, `tools=6`, `replaySafe=no`. This was not a timeout. We have not rerun potentially side-effectful work.

Evidence limit: native history did not expose the parent final message, so we cannot independently assert that its authored final text was exactly `NO_REPLY`; zero terminal payloads and the completed parent marker are observed.

Installed-source candidate: `shouldTreatEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` delegates to `shouldSkipNonVisibleTurnRetry`, which rejects any retained `acceptedSessionSpawns`. `hasAcceptedSessionSpawn` checks nonempty length, regardless of collection/settlement; the incomplete-turn exemption instead checks `hasCompletionMessageSessionSpawn`, false for a collector (`expectsCompletionMessage:false`). Could a settled collector therefore block optional silence without owning a future completion message?

Expected regression coverage: completed collector + parent consumes result + permitted silence finishes successfully without announcement; outstanding collector/failed child/required-visible final retain their correct non-success or visible-response behavior. Do not blindly exempt every accepted spawn.

Related: #141556 / #141957 and #130675 concern silent terminal classification, but their documented causes differ. Please confirm whether this accepted-spawn variant is already tracked or fixed. This source analysis is based on installed shipped code, not a claim of reproduction on current upstream main.

Private prompts, tokens, channel IDs, session/job IDs and task data are deliberately omitted.

### Summary

The Liquid AI setup step tells readers to restart the Gateway after installing the local plugin, even though a plugin install already applies through a running Gateway.

### Affected docs path(s) or URL(s)

docs/providers/liquid-ai.md (Set up the provider section, lines 20-26); published page https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/liquid-ai

### Steps to reproduce / verify

1. Open docs/providers/liquid-ai.md
2. Go to the section Set up the provider (near line 20)
3. Line 22 reads: From that checkout, install the local plugin and restart the Gateway:
4. The code block runs pnpm openclaw plugins install ./extensions/liquid-ai and then pnpm openclaw gateway restart (lines 25-26)
5. Compare docs/cli/plugins/install.md lines 15-16, which state that install applies through a running local Gateway for every supported plugin source

### Expected docs behavior/content

The step should install the local plugin only; the following models auth login --provider liquid-ai then runs against the applied install. Sibling provider pages already omit the restart, for example docs/providers/gmi.md lines 40-41.

### Actual docs behavior/content

The section instructs an extra pnpm openclaw gateway restart right after pnpm openclaw plugins install ./extensions/liquid-ai, and the sentence above the block says to restart the Gateway.

### Impact

Operators on the development-checkout path restart a healthy Gateway for no reason, and the page contradicts the install reference, which states that install applies through a running Gateway for every supported plugin source. The same stale step already exists on other pages (#194414, #198612).

### Evidence

- docs/providers/liquid-ai.md lines 22-26: the sentence asks readers to restart the Gateway, and the code block runs pnpm openclaw plugins install ./extensions/liquid-ai followed by pnpm openclaw gateway restart
- docs/cli/plugins/install.md lines 15-16: When a local Gateway is running, plugins install applies every supported plugin source through that Gateway and returns its applied generation. With no local Gateway, it saves the installation for the next start.
- docs/plugins/manage-plugins.md lines 281-286 (Apply changes and inspect): Control UI actions and the Gateway plugin-management RPCs apply plugin changes without restarting the Gateway. Ordinary CLI install, enable, disable, and uninstall commands use the running local Gateway when available.
- docs/providers/gmi.md lines 40-41: Installation applies to a running Gateway automatically; otherwise it takes effect on the next startup.


### Additional information

Same defect class as #194414 and #198612 (BytePlus section). A focused docs PR will remove the restart step from this section only.

issues.body:
### Summary
`openclaw backup create --all` fails with `ETIMEDOUT` on large state dirs because the SQLite header probe spawns one worker over **every** discovered path with a fixed 10s timeout.

### Where
`src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.ts` → `probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders()`: `childProcess.spawnSync(..., { timeout: 1e4 })` (dist `backup-sqlite-snapshot-*.mjs`, 2026.11.1 / 4ffdd20).

### Repro
- State + workspace with ~640k files (agent workspace scratch output).
- `openclaw backup create --all` → probe takes ~10.9s → `spawnSync ... ETIMEDOUT` → whole backup aborted.
- Scheduled backups fail silently every run.

### Suggested fix (any of)
1. Pre-filter candidates by extension/name (`*.db`, `*.sqlite`, `*.sqlite3`, `-wal`/`-shm` siblings) before header probing.
2. Chunk the probe into batches (e.g. 10k paths) with a per-batch timeout instead of one 10s budget for all paths.
3. Scale timeout with path count, or make it configurable.
4. Honour an exclude list for workspace scratch dirs.

### Workaround
Move bulk non-DB files out of `~/.openclaw` to get under the limit.

issues.body:
# Issue: memory_search tool always times out (15s) while CLI `openclaw memory search` works fine

**Repo**: openclaw/openclaw
**Labels**: bug

---

## Description

The `memory_search` tool always fails with a 15-second timeout error, even though the underlying embedding provider and vector index are healthy. The CLI equivalent `openclaw memory search` works correctly.

## Environment

- **OpenClaw**: 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)
- **OS**: Windows 10 (28000) x64
- **Node**: v24.15.0
- **Embedding provider**: openai-compatible (Zhipu embedding-3 at `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4`)
- **Model**: xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro
- **Channel**: feishu (direct)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `memorySearch` in `openclaw.json`:
```json
{
  "memorySearch": {
    "provider": "openai-compatible",
    "model": "embedding-3",
    "remote": {
      "baseUrl": "https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4",
      "apiKey": "..."
    }
  }
}
```
2. Start gateway
3. Use the `memory_search` tool from any session

## Expected

`memory_search` returns results or empty array (like the CLI does).

## Actual

Always returns:
```json
{
  "disabled": true,
  "unavailable": true,
  "error": "memory_search timed out after 15s"
}
```

## Diagnostics

- `openclaw memory status --deep`: **Embeddings: ready**, **Vector store: ready**, 174/174 files indexed, 1518 chunks, 2048 dims
- `openclaw memory search "test"` (CLI): works, returns results in <1s
- Direct `curl` to the embedding API: returns 200 in ~0.09s
- Gateway restart: does NOT fix the issue
- The 15s timeout appears to be a hardcoded tool-level limit that cannot be configured

## Analysis

The CLI path and the gateway-internal tool path appear to use different code paths for memory search. The CLI successfully queries the same embedding provider and vector store, but the gateway tool layer has a 15-second timeout that is too short or hits a different bottleneck.

Possible causes:
- The gateway tool path may re-index or warm up on first call, exceeding 15s
- The gateway may use a different HTTP client with stricter timeouts
- There may be a locking or concurrency issue in the gateway's embedding call path

## Request

1. Is the 15s tool timeout configurable? If not, can it be made configurable?
2. Is there a known difference between the CLI and gateway memory search paths?
3. Any workaround to get `memory_search` working in gateway sessions?

issues.body:
### Summary

In a `claude-cli` session, the user's message sometimes appears twice in Control UI and `sessions_history`. The second copy is the Claude CLI import of the prompt, and its text starts with the internal gap note:

`[OpenClaw: N messages occurred outside this Claude session from … Their contents are not included here. Before answering …, call mcp__openclaw__sessions_history({...}) …]`

The UI renders this copy as a user bubble, so it looks like the user typed the note. `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` ("Sessions", "History account boundaries") says imported user turns are correlated with the local row and that generated resume notes are removed from the display copy. That doesn't happen in this case.

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d), macOS, `claude-cli` backend (Claude Code subscription login, no stable account id → reseed reason `auth-unknown`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an agent session on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` with the `claude-cli` runtime.
2. In the same OpenClaw session, have at least one user-visible text reply come from a different model (here a user message answered by `xai/grok-4.7`, plus heartbeat turns on an OpenAI model).
3. Switch back to the Claude CLI model and send a message.
4. The prompt passed to Claude CLI is assembled as:
   `<"Recorded completion events and your replies …" ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧ block>` + `\n\n` + `<[OpenClaw: N messages occurred outside this Claude session …]>` + `\n\n` + `<user text>`
   (`resumeContext` from `renderCliPreservedTurns` is prepended outside the `sessionGapContext`.)
5. Open chat history. The local user row is followed by a second row (`__openclaw.importedFrom: "claude-cli"`, no `seq`/`provenance`/`idempotencyKey`) containing the gap note plus the user text.

### Expected

The imported turn matches the local user row and is deduplicated, or at minimum its display copy has the gap note stripped.

### Actual

The gap note is not stripped, the comparable text doesn't match the local row, and the imported copy is shown as an extra user message.

### Root cause (from reading the 2026.11.3 dist)

`stripCliPromptDecorations` (`src/gateway/cli-session-history.prompt-text.ts`) removes the gap note with a regex anchored at `^`:

```js
text.replace(/^\[OpenClaw: \d+ (?:messages occurred outside this Claude session|…) from [^\n]+\. Their contents are not included here\.[^\n]*\]\r?\n\r?\n/u, "")
```

This runs **before** the leading ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧ replay block is removed (that happens later, in `stripInboundMetadata` via `extractComparableText`). When `resumeContext` and `sessionGapContext` are both present, the gap note isn't at position 0, so the anchored regex misses it. `cleanClaudeCliImportedUserDisplay` uses the same function, so the display copy keeps the note too.

I replayed `stripCliPromptDecorations` over every note-bearing prompt in my local Claude Code transcripts. In all 7 prompts where the gap note came first, it was stripped correctly. The 1 prompt with a replay block before the note leaked.

### Suggested fix

- Strip prompt decorations to a fixed point regardless of order: leading ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧ blocks (including the "Recorded completion events" replay label), the gap note, the drift note, and system-event lines. Or remove the leading inbound-metadata/replay block before applying the gap-note regex.
- Add a test covering `resumeContext + sessionGapContext + user text`.
- The same ordering issue likely affects the drift note (`OpenClaw resumed this CLI session after prompt content changed …`) and the `messages recorded in this chat since your last reply here (possibly already in this session)` variant when either follows a replay block. For example, the next ordinary turn after a subagent announce could hit this. I found that path in the code but haven't observed it.

### Workaround

Setting `agents.entries.<agent>.heartbeat.isolatedSession: true` stops heartbeat turns from adding other-model turns to the main session, so it removes the most frequent trigger. It doesn't fix the strip-order bug for other-model replies or completion replays.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A recurring isolated cron job recovered from a tool error, successfully sent its Discord report, saved its checkpoint, and ended with `NO_REPLY`; the scheduler nevertheless recorded a tool-warning error and ran it again, producing a second report.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

The observed production sequence is below. It has not been replayed in isolation, so these are observations rather than a claimed minimal reproduction.

### Expected behavior

The job explicitly sends and verifies its report before saving its checkpoint and returning `NO_REPLY`; an auxiliary error that it handled before completing should not turn that completed run into a failure. Merged #152165 describes this outcome for confirmed visible message-tool delivery and intentional silent completion.

### Actual behavior

On 13 November 2026 (UTC), with `agentTurn`, isolated session, `delivery.mode: none`, and a recurring 01:00 / 10:00 / 17:00 schedule:

- 01:13:28: `web_fetch` returned an error (`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`). The agent continued; at 01:16:24 the native `message` send succeeded, the checkpoint write succeeded, and at 01:16:59 the final assistant response was `NO_REPLY`.
- 01:17:02: the run receipt recorded `error: "⚠️ Web Fetch failed"`. A second run started at 01:18:02, one minute later and well before the next scheduled slot.
- In the second run, a read-only `process` search exited 1 after returning paths; the agent continued and used a located result. At 01:25:01 its native `message` send succeeded, then its checkpoint write succeeded and at 01:25:14 it ended `NO_REPLY`.
- 01:25:19: the second receipt recorded `error: "⚠️ Process failed"`. The recipient received two reports; a failure-streak alert also fired.

The installed scheduler contains a one-minute transient retry at the applicable error count; the interval and schedule are consistent with a retry after the first false failure. The exact warning metadata and reason the delivery suppression did not apply have not been established.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3, official core commit `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`; no local source patches.

### Operating system

Windows 11 x64

### Install method

Official global npm package, native Windows Gateway.

### Model

Effective model identifier omitted.

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw cron → isolated agent turn → OpenAI Codex harness / Responses API → native Discord message tool.

### Logs and evidence

Times and outcomes above were read from the original session transcript events and scheduler receipts. Both session records show completed turns; the second scheduler receipt also records `delivered: true` alongside error status. Full private evidence has been retained; inbox content and private identifiers are omitted here.

The installed `resolveCronPayloadOutcome` excludes `NO_REPLY` from visible recovery text and can retain a structured tool warning as fatal. The finalizer can record a fatal run independently of message delivery. Those source observations are consistent with the receipts, but do not prove the warning's provenance or which delivery metadata reached the classifier in this Codex-harness run. No current-main reproduction has been run.

### Impact and severity

Two completed reports appeared in the same Discord channel for one scheduled slot, followed by an erroneous failure alert. This sequence was observed once across the original run and its repeat; broader frequency is unknown. Repeating an agent turn after it has performed side effects can repeat those effects.

### Additional information

Related: #155597 covers delivery status in failure alerts; #152165 addressed confirmed delivery followed by a silent finish; draft #180922 proposes broader recovery for silent turns after tool errors. This observation adds a confirmed native send and a repeat run with a second report. A useful regression target is a recovered tool error followed by confirmed native delivery, successful checkpoint, and `NO_REPLY`: record success and do not retry; preserve genuine runtime and delivery failures.

Prepared with AI assistance (Codex).

issues.body:
> **Form note (edited 2026-10-09):** this was filed with `gh issue create --body-file`, which bypasses the issue form. It is a feature request and is restructured here to the `feature_request.yml` fields; the original sections below are kept verbatim as Problem to solve / Evidence, and the missing fields are appended.

## Summary

An `exec` tool call runs its command as a child of the Gateway with **no marker of which agent's
turn initiated it**. On a multi-agent install where the leashed agents run
`tools.exec.mode: "allowlist"`, that means an operator-written wrapper script — the standard way to
give one agent a narrow slice of a CLI — cannot know its own caller. The only handle left is the
*path* the allowlist matched, so identity has to be encoded in the binary's location: one wrapper
file per (agent × wrapped tool).

This is a missing primitive rather than a misbehaviour: nothing documented promises the identity is
there. Filing it because the workaround does not scale and because it silently weakens exactly the
boundary `tools.exec.mode: "allowlist"` exists to draw.

The security half is concrete. Any CLI the wrapper fronts that takes an identity flag will accept
whatever the model wrote, because the wrapper has no ground truth to compare it against.
`openclaw cron add --agent <id>` is the case that prompted this: it is an `operator.admin` surface,
so the Gateway is right to trust it, but a wrapper handed to a leashed agent cannot tell
`--agent self` from `--agent <an agent with full exec>`. The turn it schedules then runs under the
other agent's tool posture. The same shape applies to `--account <id>` (which channel identity
speaks) and `--session-key agent:<other>:...` (whose live session the turn lands in).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two agents, one leashed:

   ```jsonc
   "agents": { "entries": {
     "narrow": { "tools": { "exec": { "mode": "allowlist" } } },
     "wide":   { "tools": { "exec": { "mode": "full" } } }
   } }
   ```

2. Write a wrapper and allowlist it for `narrow` only:

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   # /opt/wrappers/show-identity
   env | grep -iE 'agent|session' || echo "no identity in env"
   ```

   ```bash
   openclaw approvals allowlist add --agent narrow "/opt/wrappers/show-identity"
   ```

3. Have `narrow` run `show-identity` through its `exec` tool.

## Expected behavior

Something in the child's environment names the agent whose turn is running — e.g. a read-only
`OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID`, alongside the session key already used for routing. A wrapper could then
compare an identity flag against it and refuse a mismatch, and one wrapper would serve every agent.

## Actual behavior

The child sees only Gateway/service variables. Measured from inside the `exec` tool of the leashed
agent itself — the wrapper printed variable **names** only, and the credential/service entries are
elided here:

```
CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION
DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS
OPENCLAW_CLI
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_SERVICE_PID
OPENCLAW_PATH_BOOTSTRAPPED
OPENCLAW_SERVICE_KIND
OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER
OPENCLAW_SHELL
OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT
--- total vars: 58 ---
```

58 variables, and not one identifies the calling agent, the session, or the turn. `docs/concepts/user-model.md` states
for the related case that contributor trailers "are not exported through the process or shell
environment", so this reads as deliberate for attribution — but it leaves authorization with no
in-process anchor either.

Consequence in practice: the wrapper has to be told who it is by where it lives.

```bash
# scripts/wrappers/narrow-cron — the entire content is the id
exec /opt/skills/cron-pinned narrow "$@"
```

## Environment

- openclaw 2026.8.1 (`ea80657`), installed via `npm -g` at `~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`
- Linux 6.17.2-1-pve, x64, node v22.23.2
- 6 agents, `agents.defaults.model: null`, per-agent models; 4 agents on
  `tools.exec.mode: "allowlist"`, 2 on `"full"`
- Model on the turn that found this: `claude-cli/claude-opus-5`

## Provider / routing chain

Discord channel message → agent turn (claude-cli runtime) → `exec` tool → exec approvals allowlist
match on the resolved path → child process spawned by the Gateway. The identity is present at every
step up to the last one.

## Additional setup details

Ours, disclosed so it can be separated from upstream behaviour: a small `exec-guard` script that
diffs the approvals store against a declared manifest, and per-agent wrapper scripts under
`scripts/wrappers/`. No `dist` patches are involved in this report and none are carried for it.

## Impact and severity

- **Maintenance:** 10 wrapper files on this install exist only to carry an agent id — 4 for one
  scheduling CLI, 6 for a memory-write script. Every new agent multiplies by the number of wrapped
  tools, and every wrapper is a file that can drift from the mechanism it shims.
- **Security:** until each wrapper strips them by hand, an identity flag on a wrapped CLI is
  caller-supplied. On this install that was `openclaw cron --agent`, where a leashed agent could
  schedule an agent turn under another agent's tool posture. It is closed here by refusing the flag
  in the wrapper; it stays open for anyone who wrapped the same CLI without noticing the flag.
- **Time to notice:** the cron wrapper had been in use since June and the flag was found while
  auditing something else. Nothing surfaces it — the created job simply carries the requested
  `agentId`, which is indistinguishable from an operator scheduling it.

## Alternatives considered

- **Identity encoded in the wrapper path (what we run today).** One wrapper file per (agent × wrapped tool); 10 such files on this install, described under Impact. Works, does not scale, and every file can drift from the mechanism it shims.
- **Refuse the identity flag inside each wrapper.** This is how the `openclaw cron --agent` case is closed here. It protects only the wrappers whose author noticed the flag.
- **Use the native Gateway tool instead of a wrapped CLI.** The ClawSweeper review of 2026-09-03 points out that the native Automations tool already prevents the cross-agent cron target on the supported path. That covers scheduling; it does not cover the other wrapped CLIs (the memory-write script, `--account`, `--session-key`), which have no native equivalent here.
- **Do nothing and document that exec children carry no caller identity.** Acceptable if the maintainer decision is that wrapper-level authorization is unsupported; the docs would then need to say so where `tools.exec.mode: "allowlist"` is described.

We accept the review's point that an env variable is advisory and cannot authenticate a later Gateway call. The request is the advisory marker for wrapper ergonomics and refusal of mismatches, not an authentication primitive.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only. This crosses the security boundary the review flags (`clawsweeper:needs-security-review`, `needs-product-decision`); we will not open a PR unless a maintainer decides the contract and asks for one.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Common mistakes in a `mcpServers` entry produce the diagnostic
`$.mcpServers.<name>: Invalid input` with no field or reason.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `openclaw templates create ./mcp-diag`
2. Add any one of these under `mcpServers` and run `openclaw templates validate ./mcp-diag`:
   ```yaml
   s: { url: "https://x.example/mcp" }                  # transport missing
   s: { url: "https://x.example/mcp", transport: http } # unknown transport
   s: { command: node, args: [8080] }                   # non-string argument
   s: {}
   ```

### Expected behavior

A diagnostic that names the field and the rule, for example
`$.mcpServers.s.transport: required for a remote server (sse or streamable-http)`.

### Actual behavior

`$.mcpServers.s: Invalid input` for all four.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3 (82123cd), source checkout of `main`

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Darwin, arm64)

### Install method

Source checkout (`pnpm openclaw ...`), isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`

### Model

N/A (a local mock OpenAI-compatible server, only so Template Add's opening turn can run)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
See the captured output under "Screenshots, recordings, and evidence".
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Reproduced with the CLI. All four inputs print the same line:
  ```
  $ openclaw templates validate ./mcpdiag
  ERROR invalid_manifest $.mcpServers.s: Invalid input
  [exit 1]
  ```

- `src/templates/schema.ts:417` is a `z.union`; `diagnosticsFromZodError` (`:606`) keeps only the top-level `issue.message`.
- `transport` is required for remote servers at `:393` but optional in native config, so authors copying a working config entry hit this.
- Custom refinements (unpinned `npx`, literal env values) do report properly.

### Impact and severity

Authors cannot tell what to fix. Low severity, high frequency during authoring.

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows 2026.10.7: every boot blocks the main thread ~100 s in main-session startup orphan marking, then ~190 s more in a second direct agent-DB reservation (both `outcome=error`)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: impact:crash-loop
labels.description: Crash, hang, restart loop, or process-level availability failure.

issues.body:
## Summary

On every gateway start (clean or after a crash), `sidecars.main-session-recovery` runs main-session startup orphan marking. It takes a **synchronous `direct` agent-database reservation on the main thread** (`threadId 0`, `isMainThread: true`). The reservation waits on a worker task, the task times out after ~100 s, and the reservation ends with `outcome: "error"`. For that whole time the event loop is blocked:

- `plugins.runtime-post-bind` is reported as 97–101 s, but it is only waiting behind the stall.
- HTTP `/health` and WebSocket upgrades hang. Clients time out (`closed before connect`, `handshake: pending`).
- The liveness monitor reports `event_loop_delay` for 102 s, and the health monitor then restarts every channel (`reason: stopped`).

A **second** main-thread `direct` reservation follows. It ends with `outcome: "error"` after **183–195 s**. In the 2026-11-13 boot, `/health` began answering about 9 s after it finished. Total main-thread blocking per boot is about 5 minutes.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.7 (157d8c2)**, npm global install, Node 24.22.1, Windows 10 22H2 (19045), x64, 32 GB RAM, local SSD.
- Gateway runs as a Scheduled Task. `gateway.bind=loopback`, `gateway.tailscale.mode=serve`.
- 8 plugins: anthropic, device-pair, discord, memory-core, openai, openrouter, telegram, xai. 10 agents. 6 Telegram accounts and 1 Discord account.
- Agent DB sizes (WAL mode): main 443 MB, second agent 334 MB, others 223 / 216 / 121 MB. Shared state DB 77 MB.

## Reproduction

Restart the gateway. It happens on every boot. Two consecutive boots:

| boot | orphan marking fails at | 1st reservation | 2nd reservation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-12 22:00 (clean restart) | +97.7 s | `elapsedMs: 97661`, error | `elapsedMs: 182627`, error |
| 2026-11-13 16:33 (after `restart_close_failed`) | +101.2 s | `elapsedMs: 101745`, error | `elapsedMs: 195090`, error |

## Log excerpt (2026-11-13 boot, trimmed)

```
16:33:43.887 startup phase: http.bound 0.0ms total=45269.2ms
16:33:44.006 startup phase: sidecars.main-session-recovery starting total=45388.3ms
16:33:44.012 startup phase: plugins.runtime-post-bind starting total=45393.8ms
            -- no log output for 101 s --
16:35:25.117 startup phase: plugins.runtime-post-bind 101104.2ms total=146498.0ms
16:35:25.138 WARN liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=74584ms elapsed=104584ms; deferring recovery decisions
16:35:25.141 WARN liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization interval=102s degradedFor=102s
16:35:25.148 [discord:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)
16:35:25.219 [telegram:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)   (x5 accounts)
16:35:25.228 WARN main-session startup orphan marking failed before channel startup: WorkerTaskError: worker task timed out
16:35:25.228 startup phase: sidecars.main-session-recovery 101221.2ms total=146609.5ms
16:35:25.241 WARN slow agent database reservation {"operation":"direct","outcome":"error","threadId":0,"isMainThread":true,"reentrant":false,"elapsedMs":101745,"queueWaitMs":0,"writerExecutionMs":101745,"completionDelayMs":0}
16:35:25.374 http server listening (8 plugins ...; 119.2s)
16:35:28.938 WARN closed before connect ... {"durationMs":3587,"handshake":"pending","phase":"ws_upgrade_started"}   (x4, incl. the Android app)
16:35:28.981 WARN slow SQLite transaction hold {"database":"...state/openclaw.sqlite","operation":"placementJournals.prune","elapsedMs":3595,"phases":{"sqlMs":1,"hostAdmissionWaitMs":3594}}
...
16:38:44     WARN slow agent database reservation {"operation":"direct","outcome":"error","threadId":0,"isMainThread":true,"elapsedMs":195090,...}
16:38:53     GET /health -> {"ok":true,"status":"live"}   (first success)
```

The `slow SQLite transaction hold` warnings are a side effect. Their `sqlMs` is about 1 ms, and all the time is `hostAdmissionWaitMs` spent queued behind the blocked main thread.

## Expected

- Main-session orphan marking (and any startup recovery) never holds a synchronous agent-DB reservation on the main thread. It should run in a worker or be async, with a bounded wait.
- If the worker task times out, the failure should not keep the event loop blocked for the full timeout. HTTP, WebSocket and liveness should keep running.
- The startup phase log should attribute the stall to the phase that causes it, not to `plugins.runtime-post-bind`.

## Possibly related

- #186631: a full `integrity_check` in a fresh opener holds an agent's write queue, with the same `slow agent database reservation ... outcome=error` signature (Linux, worker threads). It may be the reason the worker task here times out.
- #162211: a startup event-loop block (40–200 s) is misread as a disconnect by the health monitor. We see the same channel restarts.
- #185452: slow agent database reservation on session-sqlite worker open.
- #164294: the state DB's WAL auto-checkpoint never completes because a long-lived in-process worker connection pins it (reported on 2026.9.7, also seen on this host). That's a different DB and a different symptom. The possible link is the shared pattern of an in-process worker holding SQLite while the main thread waits on it. Not confirmed: during the 11-13 boot the state WAL was only ~0.5 MB.
- #170956 / #170928: slow Windows startup.

## Evidence available

Full gateway logs for both boots, the stability bundle from the 11-13 crash (`restart_close_failed`), and DB file sizes. Happy to run a debug build or add instrumentation.

issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #177387 and #186331, both of which were closed as "already implemented on `main`". That implementation **still has not shipped**: the newest published release, **v2026.10.10 (published 2026-11-03)**, ships the same Preview-only identity check. Every release published since the fix was merged on `main` reproduces the bug.

This issue reports the **new** fact — a release published *after* those closures also lacks the fix — rather than re-reporting the original defect.

## Affected published releases (verified against the shipped npm artifact, not the changelog)

| Release | Published | `MINIMAX_M31_MODEL_ID` in shipped build | Accepts GA id? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v2026.10.8` | 2026-10-27 | `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` | no |
| `v2026.10.9` | 2026-10-29 | `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` | no |
| **`v2026.10.10`** | **2026-11-03** | **`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`** | **no** |
| `main` | — | `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (+ separate preview id) | **yes** |

### Verification 1 — the published npm tarball for v2026.10.10

```bash
curl -sL https://registry.npmjs.org/openclaw/-/openclaw-2026.10.10.tgz -o o.tgz
tar -xzOf o.tgz package/dist/thinking-Dg9lPaiN.mjs | grep -n 'MiniMax-M3.1-Flash'
```

```js
// package/dist/thinking-Dg9lPaiN.mjs  (openclaw@2026.10.10)
const MINIMAX_M31_MODEL_ID = "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview";
...
function isMinimaxM31ModelId(modelId) {
	return modelId.trim().toLowerCase() === MINIMAX_M31_MODEL_ID.toLowerCase();
}
```

### Verification 2 — the release tag source

`extensions/minimax/thinking.ts` at `v2026.10.10` is **byte-identical** to the same file at `v2026.10.9`:

```bash
diff <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/v2026.10.9/extensions/minimax/thinking.ts) \
     <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/v2026.10.10/extensions/minimax/thinking.ts)
# no output
```

### Verification 3 — runtime behaviour of the shipped build

```js
import("file:///path/to/openclaw/dist/thinking-Dg9lPaiN.mjs").then(m => {
  console.log(m.r("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash"));                       // false
  console.log(JSON.stringify(m.i("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash")));       // {"levels":[{"id":"off"},{"id":"adaptive"}],"defaultLevel":"adaptive"}
  console.log(JSON.stringify(m.i("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview"))); // {"levels":[{"id":"low"},...{"id":"max"}],"defaultLevel":"max"}
});
```

The GA id and the Preview id resolve to **different** profiles in the same build.

## Impact (unchanged from #177387, still live)

Two symptoms, one one-line identity check in `extensions/minimax/thinking.ts`:

1. **No level choices.** `resolveMinimaxThinkingProfile("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash")` falls through to the plain-M3 rule → adaptive-only profile (levels `off`/`adaptive`, default `adaptive`). The five-tier ladder MiniMax exposes on M3.1 is unreachable for the GA id.
2. **Effort never reaches the wire.** `wrapMinimaxProviderStream` in `extensions/minimax/stream.ts` gates the Anthropic-compatible payload patch on the same `isMinimaxM31ModelId(model.id)` check, so `output_config.effort` is never sent for the GA id. The request goes out with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` and no effort bound, and the model self-selects maximum reasoning.

The affected id is not a typo — it is the id MiniMax's live catalog returns and the id the bundled catalog documents. `main` already accepts both ids.

### Wire contract (verified live against `api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1/messages`)

- `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` → `200 OK`, `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` varies by level
- `off` → `400` `invalid reasoning_effort: "off" (allowed: low, medium, high, xhigh, max) (2013)`
- `adaptive` → `400` `invalid reasoning_effort: "adaptive" (allowed: low, medium, high, xhigh, max) (2013)`

Both `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` and `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` are accepted by the endpoint. Note `adaptive` is **not** a valid `output_config.effort` value — unbounded adaptive behaviour is obtained by omitting `output_config` entirely, which is exactly what the plain-M3 path does.

## Proposed fix

Publish #176955 (`ed5a99e0`). The resulting profile on the GA id:

```
MiniMax-M3.1-Flash         levels=["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] default=max
MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview levels=["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] default=max
MiniMax-M3                 levels=["off","adaptive"]                   default=adaptive
MiniMax-M2.7               levels=["off","minimal","low","medium","high"] default=off
```

### Root-cause fix preferred

#182110 proposed keying the profile off the model **family** rather than a fixed id list, so M3.1 Pro and future M3.x get the same five effort levels without needing a release each time. That would prevent this whole issue class from recurring — the id list has now needed changing at least three times (GA id added, Pro added, preview deprecated).

## Note on release-branch divergence

Release tags appear to be cut from a branch that does not contain `main`'s merge commits as ancestors, so a fix merged on `main` does not automatically reach a release. Concretely, for `v2026.10.10` the merge commit of #176955 is *not* an ancestor of the tag, and the shipped artifact still carries the pre-fix check.

This also means the release changelog is **cumulative** — `CHANGELOG/2026.10.10.md` is 3,089 lines versus 88 lines for `2026.10.9.md`, and it re-lists already-shipped PRs. For example it advertises MiniMax OAuth work (#160089 models-list, #160459 regional token renewal, #168957 discovery refresh) whose **content is byte-identical between the 10.9 and 10.10 npm artifacts** — i.e. it was already live in 10.9. The MiniMax OAuth entries in the 10.10 changelog therefore do *not* indicate MiniMax received attention in this release; the GA-id fix is the only MiniMax behavioural delta, and it is absent.

Because of that, please verify release content against the shipped artifact or the tag source rather than the changelog when triaging MiniMax reports.

## Workaround in use

Until the fix ships, operators patch the installed build (one-line id widening, mirroring `ed5a99e0` exactly). This must be re-applied after every `openclaw update`, since an update reinstalls `dist` and reverts it.

issues.body:
### Summary

The docs say the bundled `claude-cli` backend passes eligible skills to Claude Code as a temporary `--plugin-dir` plugin. They also say managed Claude turns load no Claude skills or plugins. On ordinary managed turns only the second statement holds.

### Affected docs path(s) or URL(s)

- `docs/tools/skills.md` ([L751-L756 at b556fdf](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf/docs/tools/skills.md#L751-L756))
- `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` ([L336](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf/docs/gateway/cli-backends.md#L336) versus [L240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf/docs/gateway/cli-backends.md#L240) and [L249](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf/docs/gateway/cli-backends.md#L249))

### Steps to reproduce / verify

1. Read `docs/tools/skills.md` L751-L756: "For the bundled `claude-cli` backend, sessions without library selections materialize eligible skills as a temporary Claude Code plugin, passed via `--plugin-dir`."
2. Read `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` L336: the bundled backend "prefers Claude Code's native skill resolver" and passes a temporary plugin via `--plugin-dir` when the snapshot has a materialized skill.
3. Read the same file at L240 ("`Skill` is not offered because managed turns load no Claude skills") and L249 ("Managed isolation stays in force: Claude settings, hooks, plugins, slash commands ... remain excluded").
4. On a live install, run an ordinary turn on the bundled `claude-cli` backend with default MCP bundling and no personal-library selections. Inspect the Claude Code process arguments. There is no `--plugin-dir`, and the arguments include `--tools ToolSearch` and `--disable-slash-commands`. The model receives OpenClaw's `<available_skills>` prompt catalog and has no native `Skill` tool and no `skills_search`/`skills_read`.

### Expected docs behavior/content

- `docs/tools/skills.md` and `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` L336 should state when the `--plugin-dir` path applies. They should say plainly that ordinary managed `claude-cli` turns use the bounded OpenClaw prompt catalog, not a native Claude plugin. Having no library selections is not enough to get the plugin.
- The skills docs should say which runtimes expose `skills_search`/`skills_read`. They should also warn that skills omitted by `skills.limits.maxSkillsPromptChars` / `maxSkillsInPrompt` are **not** discoverable on managed `claude-cli` turns.

### Actual docs behavior/content

Two pages describe a native-plugin skill path for `claude-cli` as the default ("sessions without library selections", "prefers Claude Code's native skill resolver"). The managed-isolation section of `cli-backends.md` says managed turns load no Claude skills or plugins. The source agrees with the managed-isolation section.

### Impact

Operators planning skill-catalog size for agents on `claude-cli` can conclude that skills cut from the prompt by the catalog budget stay reachable through Claude's native `Skill` discovery. We nearly applied a `maxSkillsInPrompt` cap on that basis. On managed turns that would have made the omitted skills unreachable: no native `Skill`, no `skills_search`, no `skills_read`.

### Evidence

Source at `b556fdf` agrees with the managed-isolation statement:

- [`src/agents/cli-runner/prepare-tool-policy.ts` L102-L124](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf/src/agents/cli-runner/prepare-tool-policy.ts#L102-L124): `ordinaryClaudeMediation` is true for `claude-cli` with bundled MCP and exact tool enforcement (not a side question, exec host not `node`). That sets `cliToolAvailability`.
- [`src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` L1198-L1206](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf/src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts#L1198-L1206): a defined `cliToolAvailability` skips `prepareClaudeCliSkillsPlugin`. The inline comment reads: "Exact Claude execution strips native plugins; keep selected skills in the host prompt instead of suppressing them for an unusable plugin."
- [`src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` L1370-L1373](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf/src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts#L1370-L1373): with no plugin arguments, `resolveCliSkillsPrompt` supplies the prompt catalog.

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (`b556fdf`), Claude Code 2.1.318, macOS arm64, bundled `claude-cli` backend, `tools.profile: "full"`, no personal-library selections:

- The process arguments have no `--plugin-dir`, and include `--tools ToolSearch` and `--disable-slash-commands`.
- The prompt catalog is present (79 entries, compact format, just under the default 18,000-char budget). The model's tool list has no `Skill`, `skills_search` or `skills_read`.
- About 3 days of gateway logs show no Claude skills-plugin warnings. This is consistent with the plugin being skipped on purpose, not with a plugin build failure.

### Additional information

This is a docs-only defect. We are not asking for managed isolation to be weakened or native plugins re-enabled.

Related, separate request (happy to open it as its own feature issue if preferred): give managed `claude-cli` turns the host-owned, policy-filtered `skills_search`/`skills_read` tools over the admitted catalog. This would match the embedded runner, the Codex harness and Gateway cloud turns (`docs/tools/skills.md`, "Search installed skills"), and would make the bounded catalog safe to shrink on Claude too.

Related: #184068 (skills_read and Tool Search), #185336 (native Skill load accounting), #160554 (claude-cli skill exposure).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Media sent from a plugin tool via the sanctioned `toolContext.delivery.send({ mediaUrl })` capability (introduced in #127098) reaches the outbound channel but does not appear in the OpenClaw Control UI, while media produced by the built-in `image_generate` tool through `details.media.mediaUrls` appears in both.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a plugin whose tool factory receives `toolContext.delivery` and, in `execute()`, calls `delivery.send({ mediaUrl: <absolute-path-to-workspace-image> })` for one or more images.
2. Configure a chat channel (e.g. Telegram) for the agent so `deliveryContext` is populated with `channel`, `to`, `accountId`.
3. Invoke the plugin tool from a chat that has the Control UI open on the same session.
4. Compare the resulting turn on the chat channel and in the Control UI assistant reply.

### Expected behavior

The image that appeared on the chat channel also appears inline in the Control UI assistant reply for that turn — matching the built-in `image_generate` tool (`src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.execution.ts`), whose `details.media.mediaUrls` are ingested via `pendingToolMediaUrls` into the assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls` that the Control UI renders.

### Actual behavior

Image is delivered to the chat channel. The Control UI shows only the text portion of the assistant reply for that turn; no image, no attachment entry.

Code trace on `main` @ `c1ead4b71e0`:

- `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts:161-207` — `delivery.send` calls `runMessageAction` with `forceCoreDelivery: true, skipQueue: true, dryRun: false`. This is a live, ephemeral push through the core outbound owner and never populates the tool-result media queue.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-media.ts:102` — `TRUSTED_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA` is a hardcoded set. Plugin tool names are not members, so `details.media.mediaUrls` returned from a plugin tool is stripped by `filterToolResultMediaUrls()`.
- Result: both established Control UI ingest routes (trusted tool-result media, or assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls`) are closed to plugin `delivery.send`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (main @ `c1ead4b71e0`)

### Operating system

macOS 12.7.6

### Install method

pnpm dev (source checkout of main)

### Model

Not model-dependent (defect is in the tool-result → transcript pipeline, before the model round-trip)

### Provider / routing chain

Not routing-dependent

### Additional provider/model setup details

N/A — the defect is in the tool-result → transcript pipeline, not in inference routing.

### Logs

N/A — no error is emitted; the media silently does not appear in the Control UI.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Code references above are sufficient for grounded verification against `main` @ `c1ead4b71e0`:

- `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts:161-207`
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-media.ts:102`
- `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.execution.ts` (baseline: native tool whose media does appear in Control UI)

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any plugin tool that returns media via the sanctioned `toolContext.delivery.send` capability from #127098.
- Severity: Behavior bug. Chat channel delivery works; Control UI users lose visibility of media the same turn produced.
- Frequency: Every invocation.
- Consequence: Control UI reviewers cannot see plugin-generated media without switching to the chat channel; degrades review, debugging, and audit workflows.

### Additional information

Follow-up to #120718. Of the three solutions proposed there, #127098 implemented Option C (a sanctioned `delivery.send` abstraction). Option A (extending `TRUSTED_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA` for plugins) was not implemented, and the Control UI path continues to depend on it.

Two directions that would close the gap:

1. Mirror `delivery.send`-sent media into the assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls` for the current turn so the Control UI renders what the chat channel received.
2. Ship Option A from #120718 — allow plugins to declare a tool as trusted local-media producer so returning `details.media.mediaUrls` from the tool result also survives `filterToolResultMediaUrls()`.

Either would restore parity with the native `image_generate` tool's Control UI behavior.



---

**Update 2026-10-08 — still reproducible on `main`** (v2026.10.1-beta.2 @ `e73b64b7f62`):

- `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts` still calls `runMessageAction` for `delivery.send` with `forceCoreDelivery: true, skipQueue: true, dryRun: false` — media never enters the tool-result media queue.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-media.ts` still exposes `TRUSTED_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA` as a hardcoded set; plugin tools are not members, so `filterToolResultMediaUrls()` continues to strip plugin-tool `details.media.mediaUrls`.
- No mirror from `delivery.send` into assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls` has landed on `main`. (See clawsweeper's 2026-10-08 review of this issue: `deliver-transcript.ts:45` passes `text` only, with mediaUrls flattened to filename text — confirming the mirror boundary is still the loss site.)
- Linked fix PR #156613 remains **open and unmerged**, blocked on merge conflicts (`mergeable_state=dirty`).

issues.body:
## Summary

In 2026.8.1, exec `SecretRef` resolution requires the resolver command to be owned by the invoking uid. On macOS the canonical way to read a keychain secret is `/usr/bin/security`, which is root-owned like every system binary, so **every keychain-backed SecretRef fails and the Gateway will not start**.

The plugin install-policy path in the same release allows root-owned commands. The secrets path does not. That inconsistency looks unintentional.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.8.1 (upgraded from 2026.7.1-2, where this worked)
- macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), node 26.5.0
- Gateway as LaunchAgent, loopback bind

## Reproduce

Configure any exec secret provider that shells out to a system binary:

```json
{
  "secrets": {
    "providers": {
      "keychain": {
        "source": "exec",
        "command": "/usr/bin/security",
        "args": ["find-generic-password", "-w", "-s", "my-service", "-a", "my-account"]
      }
    }
  },
  "gateway": { "auth": { "mode": "token", "token": { "source": "exec", "provider": "keychain", "id": "gateway-token" } } }
}
```

Then:

```
$ openclaw secrets audit --allow-exec
Secrets audit: unresolved. plaintext=0, unresolved=3, shadowed=0, storeResidue=0, legacy=1.
- [REF_UNRESOLVED] /Users/<user>/.openclaw/openclaw.json:gateway.auth.token Failed to resolve
  exec:keychain:gateway-token (secrets.providers.keychain.command must be owned by the
  current user (uid=501): /usr/bin/security).
```

The Gateway then fails startup:

```
[secrets] [SECRETS_PROVIDER_DEGRADED] exec:keychain: secret provider failed.
Affected owners: cold gateway:ingress-auth.
Gateway failed to start: Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable.
```

`/usr/bin/security` is `uid 0, gid 0, mode 755` — root-owned and **not** group- or world-writable, i.e. the case the check should be accepting.

## Root cause

Two code paths in the same build disagree.

`dist/install-policy-*.js` — allows root:

```js
if (process.platform !== "win32" && typeof process.getuid === "function" && stat.uid != null) {
  const uid = process.getuid();
  if (stat.uid !== uid && stat.uid !== 0)
    throw new Error(`${params.label} must be owned by the current user (uid=${uid}) or root: ${effectivePath}`);
}
```

`dist/resolve-*.js` (secrets exec resolution) — missing the root exemption:

```js
if (process.platform !== "win32" && typeof process.getuid === "function" && stat.uid != null) {
  const uid = process.getuid();
  if (stat.uid !== uid)
    throw new Error(`${params.label} must be owned by the current user (uid=${uid}): ${commandPath}`);
}
```

Both already reject group/world-writable commands just above this, which is the property that actually matters for hijack resistance. Root ownership is the *safe* case.

There is also no escape hatch — the Windows branch of the same function states "there is no provider-level bypass".

## Impact

Any macOS user with keychain-backed secrets is hard-blocked on upgrade: the Gateway will not boot, and because the gateway token itself is typically keychain-backed, it cannot report the failure through its own channels either. Same applies to any Linux setup pointing an exec SecretRef at a system binary.

## Suggested fix

Add the `&& stat.uid !== 0` clause to the secrets resolver so it matches the install-policy check.

## Workaround

A user-owned wrapper satisfies the check:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
exec /usr/bin/security find-generic-password -w -s "$1" -a "<account>"
```

`chmod 700`, own it as the invoking user, and point `secrets.providers.*.command` at it with the service name as the argument. `openclaw secrets audit --allow-exec` then reports `unresolved=0`.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a Template is created from chat, the review and the published `CLAW.md` drop the `agent.description` the agent wrote in the manifest whenever the draft's top-level `description` is still the seeded `""`, and they rewrite an explicit `agent.name` (`Follow-up Writer` becomes `Follow Up Writer`, `macOS Release Notes` becomes `MacOS Release Notes`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Gateway with Templates enabled in Labs and sign in to ClawHub.
2. Create a draft with `templates.drafts.create` (also used by `openclaw templates draft` and the create-template skill). The seeded draft JSON has `"description": ""`.
3. Save a proposal whose manifest frontmatter has `agent.name` and `agent.description`, and keep the seeded top-level `description`.
4. Call `templates.drafts.review`, then `templates.drafts.publish` with the choices the Control UI builds from that review.

I ran this on a real Gateway built from main `f4b43b47147`, calling the methods through `openclaw gateway call`. Only ClawHub was replaced, with a loopback server that answers `whoami` and saves the uploaded package. The saved manifest had `agent.name: Incident Follow-up Desk` and `agent.description: Triage incoming incidents and hand off with evidence.`:

```text
seeded draft description: ""
review: displayName "Incident Follow Up Desk", description ""
uploaded CLAW.md frontmatter:
---
schemaVersion: 1
agent:
  id: incident-triage
  name: Incident Follow Up Desk
metadata: {}
workspace:
  bootstrapFiles: {}
  files: []
...
```

Control: with the top-level draft `description` set to the same text, the same run publishes `description: Triage incoming incidents and hand off with evidence.`, so the harness does observe a kept description.

Calling the review preparation directly with other explicit names:

```text
"Follow-up Writer"         -> "Follow Up Writer"
"macOS Release Notes"      -> "MacOS Release Notes"
"GPT-5 code_review helper" -> "GPT 5 Code Review Helper"
```

### Expected behavior

`prepareTemplateDraft` already falls back to the manifest's `agent.description` when the draft has no description of its own (`src/templates/draft.ts:234-235`), and `skills/create-template/references/draft-format.md` puts `name` and `description` in the manifest. `docs/cli/templates.md` says the review Name is "defaulted to readable title case". The review should show the description and name the author wrote, publish them unchanged, and title-case only the default derived from the package slug.

### Actual behavior

- Description: `createTemplateDraft` seeds every draft with `description: ""` (`src/templates/draft.ts:48`). The fallback uses `??`, which does not skip `""`, so the empty value wins and `agent.description = description || undefined` removes the authored description. The fallback and the seed were added together in #173346, so the fallback has never applied to a draft created by OpenClaw.
- Name: `titleCaseTemplateName(draftManifest.agent.name ?? draftName)` (`src/templates/draft.ts:233`) title-cases the explicit manifest name as well as the slug default. It replaces `-` and `_` with spaces and upper-cases the first letter of every word.

The Control UI copies both values into its publish choices, so the uploaded package carries the changed name and no description.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5-beta.2 (same code on main `f4b43b47147`)

### Operating system

Windows 11 (the logic is platform-independent)

### Install method

pnpm dev (source checkout)

### Model

Not applicable (no model call; the draft content is written directly)

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable

### Impact and severity

A Template published from chat loses its author's description and can carry a misspelled name. Neither the review nor the publish response says the values were changed.

issues.body:
## Problem

The database-worker ratchet contributes several minutes to `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`. In [run 43429268180](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43429268180/job/131899001202), its current/base analysis took about 307 seconds. The current-tree credential-writer phase alone occupied about 55 seconds.

## Proposed scope

Remove the credential guard's second full syntax-tree traversal by collecting import-binding expression/name pairs during its existing first traversal, then resolving them afterward in the same source and preorder sequence. Preserve every declaration, binding, diagnostic and compiler query; do not narrow analysis or change allowlists.

## Validation and acceptance

Use the real full-tree inventory, frozen baseline/candidate analyzer revisions, identical input/output digests, and five interleaved fresh-process samples per revision. Require at least 5% lower median inventory time; CPU and peak RSS must remain within 10% of baseline. Record p95/spread, compiler request counts, and separate instrumented traversal-count runs. Reject the experiment if it does not meet these criteria. Existing credential, dynamic-import, worker-boundary and ratchet tests must remain green.

## Result: rejected

[The complete comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198364) met input/output parity and correctness checks, but missed the predeclared performance requirement. Five alternating fresh-process samples per revision measured median inventory time of 61.781 seconds baseline versus 60.846 seconds candidate: **1.51% faster**, below the required 5%. Median CPU improved 0.83%; peak RSS improved 0.22%.

The candidate removed 34.89% of credential-guard AST visits while leaving compiler requests unchanged. All 230 focused tests passed. The PR is closed without merging; no production optimization or billed CI saving is claimed.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install Android `ai.openclaw.app.debug` built from `54b059c478f39289fba83fb361271dd72ccc963f` (versionName `2026.8.2-debug`, versionCode `2026080201`).
2. Connect it to a Gateway that has two configured models with aliases. This run used `lab/alpha` alias Alpha and `lab/beta` alias Beta.

The induced hold is a transport delay in a disposable proxy. The payload bytes were unchanged. It is a separate setup from the airplane-mode steps.

### Expected behavior
The chip keeps the alias already shown for that selection. With the catalog loaded, the same sessions show `Alpha` and `Beta`, which is `selectedCatalogModel.name`.

### Actual behavior
The chip text changes to the raw id, `beta` while offline and `alpha` or `beta` during the catalog gap. The picker selection and the session model do not change.

`ChatScreen.kt` `selectedModelLabel` uses the catalog name when that entry exists, and otherwise `selected.substringAfterLast('/')`. Clearing the catalog on disconnect, and at a new chat scope before `models.list` returns, makes that fallback visible.

### OpenClaw version
Android `2026.8.2-debug` from `54b059c478f39289fba83fb361271dd72ccc963f`. Gateway CLI `2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)`, Node 24.22.1.

Android 16, API 36, `sdk_gphone64_x86_64` emulator. Gateway on Linux, Node 24.22.1.

Local play debug APK. Gateway from the npm global CLI, disposable state directory.

### Model
`lab/beta` (alias Beta). Also observed for `lab/alpha` (alias Alpha).

### Provider / routing chain
Android app to a disposable local Gateway. Models came from a configured `lab` provider. No inference call was made.

### Additional provider/model setup details
`models.mode` merge. Provider `lab`, two text models, aliases Alpha and Beta. Both reported `available`.

### Logs
Airplane-mode observation is the UI change from alias `Beta` to raw `beta` when the app shows Gateway offline. No model-selection RPC is required for that change.

Induced catalog-gap example, `chat.metadata` held 10 seconds: Gateway handler `chat.metadata` 23 ms, 24670 bytes, id `2e0b969b…`. `models.list` was not requested until 10.060 seconds later, id `52419e97…`, 1043 bytes. The chip showed `alpha` until that catalog publish, then `Alpha`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Observed on the emulator during the #192252 reproduction. Offline frame: header New chat, body Gateway offline, chip `beta`. Induced frame: body Ready when you are, picker only Default model, chip `alpha`, then alias `Alpha` after the catalog returned.

Affected: Android chat composer while the catalog is empty.

Frequency: every observed disconnect in this run, and for the full duration of each induced catalog gap (3 seconds and 10 seconds, both `chat.metadata` and `models.list`).
Consequence: the chip disagrees with the alias shown in the picker and with the chip text from a moment earlier.

### Additional information
Related to #192252, which is the delayed picker. This report is only the label fallback. The regression baseline is unknown. This was not compared with an older Android build.
