issues.body:
## Summary

Include the effective date range, timezone and active filters in Usage JSON exports so a saved report remains understandable after the browser selection is gone.

## Problem to solve

Suppose I select one agent, a calendar range and local time in Usage, then download the JSON to compare it with another report next week. The file contains the usage data, but not a dedicated record of the choices that produced it. The filename records the export date rather than the selected reporting period.

Rows cannot reliably reconstruct those choices. Days with no activity do not establish the requested boundaries, and a selected session can also happen to be the only session with activity. Two reports with identical totals can therefore represent different reporting periods or selections.

This makes an otherwise portable report depend on a separate note or the original browser state. It matters when comparing saved reports, investigating a usage spike, or passing a report to someone else.

## Proposed solution

Add a small, versioned report-context object alongside the existing JSON fields. Capture the effective export request once and use it for both the data request and the saved context.

The context should describe:

- The requested date boundaries and timezone interpretation, including the resolved timezone when local time is selected.
- Agent scope, session grouping and any active creator, search, day, hour or session selections that determine the report.
- When the export was generated and the version of this metadata format.

Keep `sessions`, `totals`, `aggregates` and `daily` at their existing locations. An additive field lets consumers keep reading the current structure while newer consumers can explain the report's scope. The exact field name can follow the existing export conventions.

Metadata should describe the effective selection, with unfiltered values represented consistently. Transient table pagination and the rest of the browser or Gateway configuration are not report context.

## Alternatives considered

- **Put the range in the filename:** useful for browsing files, but insufficient for timezone, grouping and selections, and easily lost when a file is renamed.
- **Save a separate note:** works manually, but the explanation can become detached from the data.
- **Infer scope from exported rows:** cannot recover an empty part of the requested period or distinguish an explicit selection from coincidentally matching data.

## Impact

This improves the existing JSON export workflow for people comparing, archiving or sharing usage reports. The benefit appears when a report is opened outside its original Usage view; it removes the need to reconstruct the selection manually. It is a report-interpretation improvement, with no change requested to usage accounting or export availability.

## Evidence/examples

Source inspection at `82e8cded772dcfc01c4f470b58f123ec7cb22266`:

- [The export controller](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82e8cded772dcfc01c4f470b58f123ec7cb22266/ui/src/pages/usage/export.ts) captures `selectedQuery` and uses it for the request, but builds the downloaded JSON from `sessions`, `totals`, `aggregates` and `daily`. Its filename uses the current date.
- [The request builder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82e8cded772dcfc01c4f470b58f123ec7cb22266/ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts) translates date, timezone, scope and selection fields into the effective `sessions.usage` request.
- [The export type](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82e8cded772dcfc01c4f470b58f123ec7cb22266/ui/src/pages/usage/usage-state-types.ts) currently has the four data fields above.

Related work protects different properties: #140567 concerns mixing session instances, #152741 aligns exported rows with the selection, and #171613/#171679 protect export completeness. This proposal preserves those behaviors and records what the exported report represents.

## Additional information

Acceptance examples:

- A report opened without its original browser state identifies its requested range, timezone and active selections.
- Two selections that produce identical totals remain distinguishable through their context, including a range containing days without activity.
- Changing the view after an export starts cannot attach a newer selection to the earlier request's data.
- Existing JSON fields, row identities, selected totals and incomplete-export checks retain their behavior. CSV exports are unchanged.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

  Blocked actions: 1

agent from the same Template as soon as they configure that secret.

Since the scheduled CI on `main` switched to Boat mode on 2026-11-12, two jobs run on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` instead of Blacksmith. Everything in them runs about 2-3× slower, and two time limits sized for Blacksmith now fail about half the time. Between the 15:26 and 16:26 UTC runs that day, preflight shows `CONFIGURED_RUNNER_PROFILE` changing from `hybrid` to `boat`. #193038 sends these lanes to `ubuntu-24.04` in Boat mode on purpose.

**1. `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway`: was `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`**

`ui/src/e2e/model-key-save-check.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("reports a rejected key where it was entered and keeps the field editable") failed in 16 of the last 47 scheduled runs, always on the first key: `sk-synthetic-revoked: expected 2045 to be less than 2000` (failures from 2015 to 2599 ms).

- It failed in none of the 16 runs on Blacksmith and in 16 of the 31 on `ubuntu-24.04`.
- Everything in the job slowed at the same run. The median Gateway readiness went from 5-7 s to 8-15 s, and this test from 6.5-11 s to 13-20 s.
- Product code didn't make it slower. Reverting #197784, the one change on this path near the first failure, doesn't make the first save faster when both builds run side by side locally (1797 ms with it, 1967 ms without).
- Only the first key comes close to the limit because it is the only save that changes config: the Gateway writes the config and waits for it to apply. Later keys find nothing to change and return in about 30 ms.

**2. `agentic-control-plane-http-plugin-ws`: was `blacksmith-8vcpu-ubuntu-2404`**

`src/gateway/server.plugin-reload-send-continuation.product.test.ts` hits its 120 s limit in 7 of the scheduled runs checked. It isn't hung: every stage advances, and the last of its three Gateway scenarios runs out of time.

- On an idle 4-CPU VM it takes 64 s.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`CLAW.md` accepts `timeout` and `connectTimeout` on an MCP server, so
`templates validate`, `build` and publish succeed. OpenClaw config rejects both
keys as retired aliases, so Add fails when it writes the server, after the new
agent is already committed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `openclaw config set gateway.controlUi.experimental.templates true`
2. `openclaw templates create ./mcp-timeout`
3. Add to the `CLAW.md` frontmatter:
   ```yaml
   mcpServers:
     s:
       command: node
       args: ["s.js"]
       timeout: 30
   ```
4. `openclaw templates validate ./mcp-timeout` (passes)
5. `openclaw templates add ./mcp-timeout --json`

### Expected behavior

Either the manifest rejects `timeout` / `connectTimeout` at validate time with a
message naming the supported keys, or Add maps them to `requestTimeoutMs` /
`connectionTimeoutMs`.

### Actual behavior

Validate passes. The MCP write returns
`Config invalid after MCP set (mcp.servers.s: Unrecognized key: "timeout").`
Add ends `partial`; the agent exists and its automations are never scheduled.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3 (82123cd), source checkout of `main`

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Darwin, arm64)

### Install method

Source checkout (`pnpm openclaw ...`), isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`

### Model

N/A (a local mock OpenAI-compatible server, only so Template Add's opening turn can run)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
See the captured output under "Screenshots, recordings, and evidence".
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Reproduced end to end with the offline CLI (Gateway stopped). A control Template without `mcpServers` completes with exit 0.
  ```
  $ openclaw templates validate ./mcptimeout
  Valid Template project: .../mcptimeout
  Package: mcptimeout@0.1.0
  $ openclaw templates add ./mcptimeout
  Added agent: mcptimeout
  Workspace: <state>/workspace-mcptimeout
  Config invalid after MCP set (mcp.servers.s: Unrecognized key: "timeout"). The agent was already made available and was kept. Continue setup in this agent; do not add another copy.
  [exit 1]
  $ openclaw mcp list
  No OpenClaw-managed MCP servers configured in <state>/openclaw.json.
  ```
  `openclaw agents list` then shows `mcptimeout`.
- `src/templates/schema.ts:351-355` accepts both keys.
- `src/templates/mcp.ts:80` passes the declaration to config unchanged.
- `src/config/zod-schema.mcp-server.ts:76-91` rejects both as retired aliases.
- `src/templates/schema.test.ts:64` asserts the manifest accepts `timeout: 30`; no test writes it to config.

### Impact and severity

Any published Template that sets an MCP timeout installs a half-configured agent
for every user. The author gets no warning before publishing.

### Additional information

_No response_

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

### Summary
In the browser Control UI, **Sort by: Last updated** is visibly selected, but the visible agent-main/Home-style sidebar rows remain in a largely fixed/alphabetical roster order despite conversation activity.

### Steps to reproduce
Observed on an existing multi-agent installation (not yet reproduced in a clean profile):
1. Open the browser Control UI sidebar containing multiple agents' main/Home-style conversations.
2. Use owner filter **All owners** and **Status: Active**.
3. Open **Filter & sort** and inspect **Sort by: Last updated**; this selected value was confirmed in the DOM, not inferred from the row order.
4. Observe the visible roster while conversations on the current agent and other agents receive activity.
5. The rows remain in the same largely fixed/alphabetical order rather than visibly surfacing recently updated conversations.

### Expected behavior
The visible **Last updated** selection should make it clear which visible conversations it orders, and recently active conversations in that scope should surface by recency. If agent-main/Home rows or agent group headers are intentionally exempt and only ordinary sessions within groups are sorted, that distinction should be explicit rather than implying the visible roster is sorted by update time.

Reference: `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` at commit `bc061f935bfd` describes Created/Updated/Owners sorting and says nested sessions follow the selected sort, with recently active children first for Updated. It also distinguishes Home/main conversations from ordinary session rows. That distinction is important here; this report does **not** establish that the ordinary-session comparator is faulty.

### Actual behavior
The current agent stays first, followed by rows that remain largely alphabetic/fixed. Sanitized illustrative labels for the observed shape: `Current agent -> Agent A -> Agent B -> Agent C -> ...` (not actual private labels). Updates did not produce the expected visible recency ordering.

These rows appear to represent agent main/Home conversations or agent headers, not necessarily ordinary session rows. Whether the selected sort is intentionally limited to regular sessions within those groups is not established. No root cause has been established.

### OpenClaw version
UI and Gateway: **2026.11.5-beta.1**, commit **bc061f935bfd**, build dated **November 3, 2026**.

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

- Direct browser observation plus DOM confirmation that **Sort by: Last updated** was selected; **All owners** and **Status: Active** were visible.
- A working/activity ring was visible on the current agent row.
- Two actual screenshot crops are attached below: the original observed sidebar and a later capture with the real Filter & sort menu showing Last updated and Active. Names, avatars, previews, and the conversation area are redacted/cropped; row positions and the actual sort/status controls are preserved. These show roster appearance and control selection, not a controlled before/after experiment, update chronology, or a failure of the ordinary-session comparator.
- Original observed sidebar (privacy-redacted, 380 × 675):

  ![sidebar-original-redacted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5289a918-be9e-4daf-bea5-0d91b4c391a6)

  ![sidebar-sort-redacted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04e43e07-590f-487d-97d8-aa2895eaf10e)

### Impact and severity
Affected: the observed multi-agent browser installation. Severity: navigation/discoverability friction; no data loss demonstrated. Frequency: the order stayed fixed during the observed activity; cross-profile/version frequency is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. Consequence: the user cannot rely on the selected Last updated view to find recently completed replies in this visible roster.

Related discoverability observation, **not a separately proven unread-tracking defect**: the user could not readily distinguish conversations with finished unread replies. No obvious unread dots were visible on the other inspected rows, but no controlled unread/read test was performed, and those rows' main/Home/group semantics may matter. The docs describe unread dots; this report does not claim unread tracking is absent.

Duplicate search covered sidebar sort, last updated, alphabetical ordering, and unread reports (open and closed). Related but not exact duplicates: #146383 concerns custom agent roster order, #124273 concerns sort selection persistence, #158442 concerns read acknowledgements changing timestamps, and #184170 concerns Home indicators/menu. issues.body:
### Summary

Allow custom Control UI sidebar groups to contain subgroups, creating a hierarchy for organizing sessions and projects.

### Problem to solve

Sidebar groups are currently flat. Once users maintain many long-running sessions across several areas, the list becomes long and hard to scan. For example, top-level areas such as Work and Personal cannot contain project groups such as SAP, Finance, Family, or School. Prefixes and emoji only imitate hierarchy; they do not provide structural grouping or independent collapse state.

### Proposed solution

Support hierarchical custom sidebar groups.

Suggested behavior:
- A group can optionally have a parent group (at least two levels; arbitrary depth would be even better).
- Sessions can be assigned to any group in the tree.
- Parent and child groups are independently collapsible, with collapse state persisted.
- The UI can create, move, rename, reorder, and delete nested groups, including sensible handling of children when a parent is removed.
- Existing session/group tools and APIs expose the hierarchy.
- Existing flat groups remain valid root groups with no migration work required.

### Alternatives considered

Name prefixes such as `WORK / SAP` or emoji section headers help visually, but they remain one flat list and cannot be collapsed as a unit. Separate agents or workspaces provide isolation, but are too heavyweight when the need is only navigation and organization.

### Impact

Affected: Users with many concurrent or long-running sessions/projects.
Severity: Persistent UX friction; it does not block work, but makes navigation increasingly cumbersome.
Frequency: Constant once the sidebar contains more than a handful of groups.
Consequence: More scrolling, slower session switching, and manual naming conventions to simulate hierarchy.

### Evidence/examples

A representative sidebar may already have root groups such as OpenClaw, SAP, Local First Stack, Blog+Social, Finance, Health, Family, and School. Several naturally belong under broader folders such as Work or Personal, but the current flat model cannot express that.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Please preserve backward compatibility: existing groups should behave exactly as root-level groups. A stable parent reference would avoid coupling hierarchy to display-name separators, but the implementation is flexible.

issues.body:
## What happens

In the 47 hourly scheduled `main` CI runs from 2026-11-11 23:25Z to 2026-11-13 21:26Z, 36 mocked Control UI shard jobs hit the 20-minute limit of the `Test Control UI end-to-end` step, in 21 of the 47 runs. Some of them had passed every test: [shard 6/7 of run 43501562872](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43501562872/job/132149228843) finished all 151 files (608 tests) in 1,198 s, and the step was killed at 1,202 s.

Which runner the job lands on decides whether it fits:

| Runner (CPU reported by the job) | Jobs | Timeouts | Test step p50 / max |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404` | 102 | 0 | 638 / 926 s |
| `ubuntu-24.04`, AMD EPYC 7763 | 63 | 35 | 1,202 / 1,213 s |
| `ubuntu-24.04`, Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C | 7 | 1 | 1,180 / 1,213 s |
| `ubuntu-24.04`, other CPUs (EPYC 9V45/9V74, Xeon 8573C/6973P/6975P) | 110 | 0 | 837-1,045 / 1,193 s |

30 of the 47 runs ran these jobs on `ubuntu-24.04`. The work is CPU-bound (about 3.6 of 4 cores busy), and the EPYC 7763 runners take 1.31-1.36 times as long as the plan predicts. Shards 4 and 6 fail most often (12 and 10 of the 36). Each drew a 7763 runner 12 times, against 8-11 for the other shards, and shard 4 also holds the compiled-worker borrowers (below).

## Why the shards don't fit

1. **Each shard is planned to about 960 s of a 1,200 s step.** The weighted sequencer balances the shards well: re-running it on the inventory of run 43501562872 gives 916 s of file weight per shard, and on fast runners the six shards finished within about 10% of each other. Adding the costs it doesn't price, every planned cold shard is about 959 s on current `main`. That leaves no room for a runner that is 30% slower.
2. **Two costs are not priced.** Every shard builds the Control UI bundle and launches Chromium before its first file (21-31 s). The shard that holds a compiled-worker borrower also prepares the 12,701-input subprocess generation during its 4-worker phase: 31-60 s on Blacksmith, 61-124 s hosted. Neither appears in the per-file timings, because Vitest's file durations leave out collect time. Serial projects are priced correctly (full file time, one worker).
3. **The compiled-worker generation is prepared twice per run, sometimes more.** `ui/src/e2e/guest-person-identities.e2e.test.ts` borrows the generation but is not in `UI_E2E_SHARED_WORKER_FILES`, so its shard prepares a second copy in every run (57-98 s of collect). `route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts` did the same on some runs; #197854 adds it to the group.

Shutdown after the run is about 1 s, so it is not a factor. The compiled-worker Actions cache is not a fix today: its restore misses even on the Node shards that enable it ("Cache not found").

## Proposed fix

- Price the cold costs in the UI E2E sequencer: a per-shard startup and a one-time preparation charge on the compiled-worker affinity group.
- Add `guest-person-identities` to `UI_E2E_SHARED_WORKER_FILES` so each run prepares the generation once.
- Run nine mocked Control UI shards (ten rows with the browser-extension row) instead of six. The full-inventory plan already reserves thirteen rows, so the registration ceiling is unchanged. The plan drops to 649 s per cold shard: about 883 s on an EPYC 7763 runner, 26% under the limit.
- Add a test that runs the real planner on the hourly-main inventory with the committed timings and fails when a planned cold shard exceeds 700 s.

This keeps the 20-minute step budget and every test. Raising the step timeout would also stop the failures, but it would hide the next growth step too.

## Follow-up worth considering

The UI E2E inventory grew from 878 to 987 files in two weeks, so a fixed shard count goes stale within weeks. Preflight installs no dependencies on ordinary runs, so it cannot run the sequencer to choose the count today. Moving the project lists the sequencer needs into a dependency-free module would let preflight size the matrix from the planner, the way it already sizes the Windows rows.

Related: #197854 (fixture and compiled-worker ownership), #198212 (timing refresh; with its timings, nine shards plan 637 s).

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (d48be80), macOS app host, `memory-core` slot.

## What happens

After a Gateway start, memory files and sessions are not indexed until an
agent calls `memory_search`. In `extensions/memory-core/manager-runtime.js`, only a
`default`-purpose manager calls `ensureWatcher()`, `ensureSessionListener()`
and `ensureSessionStartupCatchup()`. Nothing creates one at boot. Every Gateway
memory RPC (`memory.search`, `memory.search.owner`, used by
`openclaw memory search`) builds a `cli`-purpose manager, which is transient:
it syncs memory files once and never indexes sessions or starts a watcher.

## Reproduction

1. Restart the Gateway (or reinstall the app).
2. Edit a file under `memory/` and add messages to a session. Do not call `memory_search` from an agent.
3. `memory_index_sources` gets no new rows for either source, and no `[memory]` log line appears.
4. `openclaw memory search x`: memory rows update, but sessions do not.
5. `openclaw gateway call tools.invoke --params '{"name":"memory_search","args":{"query":"x"}}'`: sessions catch up and the watcher starts.

Observed on 2026-11-05: indexing stopped at 07:42 when the app relaunched at 07:48, and stayed stopped for about ten hours.

## Expected

The Gateway starts the default memory manager (watcher, session listener,
startup catch-up) at boot, as `resolveSyncConfig()` (`watch: true`,
`onSessionStart: true`) implies. Failing that, a `cli` search should not leave
sessions unindexed.

## Related

openclaw#177685 (CLI search-triggered sync lost on exit), openclaw#177686
(memory watcher ends without logging).

issues.body:
## Problem

Since the scheduled CI run at 07:25 UTC on 2026-11-13, every hourly `main` run fails the four cancellation variants of `controls a real native consultation without client control` in `src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts` (shard `bun:agentic-gateway-server-isolated-hosted-*`, for example [job 132180366602](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43510639112/job/132180366602)). After a cancelled consultation, the next consultation (`after-cancel`) should send "Real runner consultation completed." but sends the fallback "I need a moment to verify that before answering." instead.

This is not a flake and not specific to Bun or compiled workers. It fails 4/4 on every run, locally too, on both the pinned Bun fork and Node 24.

## Cause

Two current contracts conflict:

1. **#135423** (decision in #133855): Talk stores each generated consult prompt with `excludeFromContext: true` (`src/gateway/talk/client-agent-runtime.ts`), so it is sent in its own request and dropped from later turns.
2. **#198100** (`bf0b8002c2b`, first in the 07:25 run): every request in a session must extend the previous one. `test/setup.shared.ts` now defaults `OPENCLAW_PROMPT_CACHE_ASSERT=1`, and `beginPromptCacheObservation` throws on any history rewrite outside the rebuild points and known exceptions listed in `docs/reference/prompt-caching.md#session-prefix-stability`. Talk's excluded consult input is not on that list.

So the **second** real consult in a Talk session always rewrites history at the position of the first consult's prompt:

- Request 1 (cancelled consult): `[consult prompt 1 (excluded), runtime-context carrier 1]`
- Request 2 (`after-cancel`): `[carrier 1, consult prompt 2 (excluded), carrier 2]`, which gives `historyRewrite(message 0 (user) differs from the previous request ...)`

The assertion throws inside the runner, the runner retries (each retry also reorders history), the run ends with an error payload and no model request, and `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts` speaks the fallback text. The test's completed variants pass only because they run a single real consult.

With `OPENCLAW_PROMPT_CACHE_ASSERT=0`, all four cancellation variants pass unchanged: one model request per consult, no retries, completed result delivered. In production the assertion is a warning, so users get the answer, but each later Talk consult misses the prompt cache from the earlier consult's position onward.

Commit `f52d9254a99` (#198248) noted these "four post-cancel history failures overlapping #179237". #179237 proposes retaining consult input and is waiting on the owner decision requested in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179237#issuecomment-6354621771.

## Decision needed

Which contract should win for Talk consult input?

- **Retain consult input** in later model history (the #179237 direction). This keeps prefixes append-only and fixes the test without touching it, but reverses the #135423 exclusion.
- **Keep the exclusion** and add context-excluded current-turn input to the documented prefix-stability exceptions, declared like compaction and pruning. This keeps #135423 and accepts one cache rewrite per later consult.

Either choice leaves the test's cancellation variants and completed-result assertion as they are.

## Related

- Speech folded into a consult prompt as "Earlier unanswered user message" is replayed as its own message on the next request, which is a second rewrite (also covered in #179237).
- #197649 reports the same red job as unrelated to its change.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading from 2026.9.7 to 2026.10.10, every agent turn in a large, long-lived Telegram direct-chat session fails because the SQLite worker repeatedly dies on its 512 MB heap limit (ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY): 11/11 turns failed, and the worker was recreated 13 times in ~50 minutes.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (npm global, gateway as a systemd user service) on a Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB RAM) with one long-lived Telegram direct-chat session for the main agent: ~127k transcript events, main agent DB ~1.06 GB (WAL).
2. Upgrade to 2026.10.10 with the managed updater; the gateway restarts.
3. Send any message in that Telegram chat that starts an agent turn. Reproduced with the codex harness and with the claude-cli backend.
4. Watch the gateway log: within 7 s to 10 min, the SQLite worker is recreated (ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY / integrityGateReason=stale-lease-full) and the turn fails.


### Expected behavior

Turns in this session complete and the reply is delivered, as on 2026.9.7 the day before on the same host, session and DB: 47 inbound Telegram messages, 79 successful outbound sends, and zero occurrences of "admission is closed", "stale-lease-full", "session.rowTranscript.backfill" or "ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY" in that day's gateway log.


### Actual behavior

Every agent turn in that session fails: 11/11 since the upgrade (codex harness and claude-cli backend), 7 s to 10 min after the turn starts.
- In ~50 min after the restart, the agent-DB worker was recreated 13 times (new threadId each time). Each time, the main and writer DBs were reopened with integrityGateReason=stale-lease-full and a full integrity check (main: 3.8–27.8 s, outcome healthy).
- 7 of these were logged explicitly as "SQLite worker stopped before its result was received: Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory | ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY".
- In-flight turns fail with "Agent database execution admission is closed", "Codex session generation is no longer current" (AgentHarnessSessionSupersededError) or the worker OOM error. Exec completions fail with SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError.
- User-visible: "Something went wrong while processing your request", "This Codex session changed before your message could run. Please send it again." and "OpenClaw couldn't finish this request". Replies that had finished generating were not delivered.
- Dispatch of one inbound message failed with "telegram dispatch failed: SqliteWorkerError … JS heap out of memory"; that message was processed only ~5 min later.
- Before the earlier crashes, session-sqlite logged session-actor commands blocked on worker op session.rowTranscript.backfill for 6.5–31.7 s (that session only; 61 startup backfills of other sessions took ~3.9 s each). Later crashes happened with session.actor.read / session.actor.patch in flight.
- Switching the harness (codex -> claude-cli) and /new (sessionId unchanged) did not change this.


### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10 (7dc3350)

### Operating system

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), kernel 6.18 aarch64, Raspberry Pi 5 Model B (8 GB RAM)

### Install method

npm global, gateway as a systemd user service; upgraded with the managed updater

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra and claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 (both affected)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> codex app-server (ChatGPT OAuth) -> OpenAI; openclaw -> claude-cli -> Anthropic

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: the main agent's Telegram direct chat (one large session). The writer agent DB is reopened on every crash too.
Severity: High – blocks the primary chat. Generated replies are lost or followed by error notices.
Frequency: 11/11 turns since the upgrade; a worker crash every few minutes while the session is active.
Consequence: the chat is unusable; messages have to be resent.


### Additional information

Last known good: 2026.9.7. First known bad: 2026.10.10.
Same failure class as #185953 (reported on 2026.10.7, closed as fixed on main); still reproduces on 2026.10.10.
The worker heap cap is hard-coded (maxOldGenerationSizeMb ?? 512 in createWorkerTaskHost); no config override found.
The host was under memory pressure (swap ~3.9/4 GB). Freeing ~1.2 GB shortened stalls but did not stop the crashes.
Related: #159789, #162579, #159438

issues.title: [Bug]: Update stuck in 'validating' for hours: recovery-baseline walk inventories the whole agent workspace (millions of files) with per-directory ancestor probing, and reports no progress

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Emergency: data loss, security bypass, crash loop, or unusable core runtime.

labels.name: impact:ux-release-blocker
labels.description: A non-technical user is blocked without terminal, logs, config, or support.

issues.body:
## Summary

A Control UI-triggered `openclaw update` from **2026.10.10 → 2026.11.3** (npm-global, Linux, systemd user service) has sat in the `validating` phase for **80+ minutes** with no progress visible in the UI or in `openclaw update status`. The driver process is not hung. It is pinned at ~100% CPU on its main thread, walking every entry under the agent workspace (`~/.openclaw/workspace/**`). The workspace is inside the state dir, and agent scratch trees there hold several million files.

## Environment

- Installed: OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), npm global install, Node 24.22.1, Linux x64
- Target: 2026.11.3 (`--channel stable`), trigger `control-ui`
- Gateway: systemd **user** service; the update runs in its own transient `openclaw-update-<uuid>.service`
- State dir `~/.openclaw` with the default agent workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace`. That tree holds **~8.7M entries** in total. ~8M of them are two coding-agent scratch trees (mutation-test tmp dirs) under `workspace/.state/`, which are still being written while the update runs.

## What the run record shows

`openclaw update status --json`, `activeRun`:

- `phase: "validating"`, `status: "running"`, `updatedAtMs` unchanged for 75+ minutes
- Last steps: `staging` completed → `candidate-admission` completed (one config warning) → `validating` in_progress → `updater-runtime-retention` completed in ~54 s (`entries: 45746`)
- Nothing is recorded after that. The UI shows "2 of 7 phases complete", and the last step detail is "Preparing the updater", which has completed.
- The handoff log also stops at that point. Its last lines are repeated `[infra:temp-artifacts] Runtime retained at …/openclaw-update-runtime-*: Could not inspect OpenClaw processes: Error: Could not classify PID …: could not read package identity`, logged once for each of ~11 retained runtimes.

## What the driver is actually doing

The `openclaw update` driver PID, after ~75 min:

- ~4,260 CPU-seconds, RSS ~3 GB, main thread state `R`
- `/proc/<pid>/io`: `rchar` ≈ 58 GB, `wchar` ≈ 14.8 GB
- `strace -f` (10 s sample): no writes. On the main thread, ~113k `statx` calls and ~15k `readlink` calls. Libuv threads issue `openat`/`getdents64` on workspace subdirectories in sorted (lexicographic) order. Each visited directory gets a `statx` of every ancestor up to `/home`, plus a `statx` probe for `.openclaw-private-update-capture` in every ancestor:

```
statx("/home/<user>/.openclaw/workspace/.state/<scratch>/…/tmp/<dir>") = 0
statx("/home/<user>/.openclaw.update-captures") = 0
statx("/.openclaw-private-update-capture") = -1 ENOENT
statx("/home/.openclaw-private-update-capture") = -1 ENOENT
statx("/home/<user>/.openclaw-private-update-capture") = -1 ENOENT
statx("/home/<user>/.openclaw/.openclaw-private-update-capture") = -1 ENOENT
statx("/home/<user>/.openclaw/workspace/.openclaw-private-update-capture") = -1 ENOENT
… (one per ancestor, repeated for every directory visited)
```

That pattern matches `isUpdateCapturePath()` (`update-capture-paths-*.mjs`) being called once per visited directory. In 2026.10.10 it is called from the `visit()` walk in `captureUpdateRecoveryBaseline()` (`update-recovery-baseline-capture-*.mjs`). Measured throughput is roughly 1k entries/s, so an 8.7M-entry tree takes hours.

## Problems

1. **The walk reaches the agent workspace.** The workspace holds user/agent files, not OpenClaw state. Arbitrary coding-agent scratch (pytest tmp dirs, git worktrees, `node_modules`, `.venv`) can put millions of entries there. A recovery-baseline or capture walk should be bounded to the resources it needs. If the workspace has to be inventoried at all, it should be excluded or capped.
2. **Per-directory ancestor probing is O(depth) syscalls per directory.** The capture-marker check repeats the same ancestor `statx`/marker probes for every directory under the same parent. Memoizing results per ancestor would remove most of the syscalls.
3. **No progress or budget signal.** The run record shows no step for this walk, and its `updatedAtMs` doesn't advance. From the UI it looks hung, so operators cancel it, and a rerun repeats the same multi-hour walk.
4. **The source tree changes during the walk.** Agents keep writing to these trees throughout the update. If the baseline is later revalidated against the source, a tree this busy can't produce a stable result.
5. **Possible manifest-bound interaction.** `visit()` throws `Original update resource inventory exceeds its manifest bound.` at `observed.size >= 1e6`. If this is that walk, it should already have failed. If it is a different walk, that walk has no bound at all. Either way, an 8.7M-entry state dir should get a fast, clear refusal or a skip, not hours of silent CPU.

## Expected

- Update validation should finish in minutes regardless of how many files the agent workspace holds. Workspace contents should be excluded from recovery-baseline/capture inventory, or declared through an explicit allowlist.
- Any unavoidable long scan should report progress in the run record (entries visited, elapsed time) and enforce a bounded budget with a clear refusal reason.

## Workaround

Move large scratch trees out of `~/.openclaw` before updating. A finished-job move of ~1.08M files out of `workspace/.state` did not help this run, because the inventory was already under way and the remaining live agent scratch is ~8M entries.

issues.body:
## Summary
On macOS the generated gateway LaunchAgent launches the runtime through a **version-pinned** absolute path (`~/.openclaw/runtime/<version>/bin/bun`). Because macOS TCC associates removable-volume permissions with the *resolved binary*, every update introduces a new binary path and the user must manually re-approve access ("bun wants to access files on a removable volume") after each upgrade — even though a stable `runtime/current` symlink already exists.

## Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.10.8 (release 5413218d77df)
- macOS: 26.1 (arm64)
- Update channel: Managed by OpenClaw.app (bundle id ai.openclaw.mac)
- Gateway: local, LaunchAgent `ai.openclaw.gateway`

## Reproduction
1. Run the gateway via the generated LaunchAgent on macOS.
2. Grant TCC permission for removable-volume access to `bun` (e.g. a media library under /Volumes/...).
3. Update OpenClaw (a new versioned runtime directory is created).
4. The gateway restarts -> macOS prompts again.

## Mechanism
The generated `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` runs:
```
/bin/sh
  -> ~/.openclaw/service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway-env-wrapper.sh  (header: "Generated by OpenClaw. Do not edit while the gateway service is installed.")
  -> ~/.openclaw/service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway.env
  -> ~/.openclaw/runtime/<VERSION>/bin/bun --no-install ~/.openclaw/runtime/<VERSION>/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 18789
```
- Label: ai.openclaw.gateway; KeepAlive true; RunAtLoad true; WorkingDirectory ~/.openclaw
- The wrapper is generic (`exec "$@"`).
- A stable symlink `~/.openclaw/runtime/current` -> current version exists, but the launcher does not use it.

## Impact
- Recurring manual approval after every update for anyone whose gateway touches an external/removable volume.
- Breaks unattended/headless operation until someone clicks "Allow".

## Related (all CLOSED; none covers the launcher's per-version bun path)
- #69799 [closed] Ship a dedicated/bundled Node binary so macOS TCC permissions (FDA, Accessibility) are scoped to OpenClaw only.
- #78049 [closed] macOS launchd-managed Gateway cannot reliably access TCC-protected folders via CLI tools.
- #98798 [closed] Add macOS Node TCC install preflight (record the stable resolved binary).
- #186107 [closed] fix(macos): iMessage replies stop after app updates until Automation is re-granted (keep the grant across app updates).
These addressed TCC scoping/preflight, but the gateway LaunchAgent still pins the versioned `bun` path, so removable-volume grants are still lost on every update.

## Proposed fix
Launch the gateway under a stable identity/path so TCC keeps the same grant across updates:
1. Launch through the signed OpenClaw.app bundle (stable code signature).
2. Or invoke the runtime via the stable symlink (`runtime/current/...`), if macOS does not resolve the symlink for TCC.
3. Or ship a `bun` at a non-versioned path used by the launcher.
The service generator should apply it (plist/wrapper are regenerated on update).

issues.body:
### Summary
Treat persistent sessions created from another session as ordinary, independently organized conversations, distinct from delegated subagent runs.

### Problem to solve
The Control UI sidebar renders persistent dashboard sessions and subagent runs as equivalent child rows. Nested rows cannot be dragged to another group, and their menus omit Move to group. This prevents users from organizing a separate follow-up task where it belongs.

### Proposed solution
Persistent conversations appear as sidebar peers and can be moved, ungrouped, and pinned independently. Real subagent runs remain beneath their navigation parent, labeled as subagents. Retain existing parent/source navigation and all creation, sandbox, workspace, and completion-owner metadata; sidebar organization must not rewrite runtime relationships.

### Alternatives considered
Allowing dragging alone leaves category removal reattaching sessions and pinning still blocked. Clearing parent metadata would incorrectly change lineage and control relationships. Keeping origin as a backlink separates provenance from sidebar placement without a new persisted layout mode.

### Impact
Users who create persistent follow-up sessions can organize them without losing their source relationship. Subagent execution remains inspectable under its parent, rather than looking like another ordinary conversation.

### Evidence/examples
Verified source at ea1c52fcb4996fb7dd2b12310004bde79dfa3f60: app-sidebar-session-row-render.ts disables dragging for every isChild row; session-menu-actions.ts disables group actions for the same flag. The tree already promotes categorized dashboard children but nests them again when their category is cleared, while actual subagents remain nested. Focused projection reproduction confirmed all four cases. Browser regression and before/after screenshots will accompany the implementation PR.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

### Additional information
Maintainer-requested implementation and landing after a design discussion. No runtime ownership, permissions, storage schema, or completion-delivery changes are intended. Cross-agent subagent discovery in #95295 is related context, not the same defect.

## Summary

`openclaw update cleanup` never retires Doctor's `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<id>.bak` groups on installations that are upgraded outside `openclaw update`. That covers a global `npm install -g openclaw@<version>`, or an image or package that ships a newer install. A group becomes a candidate only after update history records a succeeded update that started after the migration completed. Outside upgrades never write that history, so every group stays `protected` forever. Each upgrade then adds another full copy of every session database.

Version: 2026.10.6 (`fe06181`), npm-global install, Linux container.

## What happens

`openclaw update cleanup --dry-run --json` on a long-running instance:

```
candidateBytes: 0
protectedBytes: 2195857408
verificationRequiredBytes: 265563980
```

| Group | Migration `completedAt` | Outcome / reason |
|---|---|---|
| A | 2026-10-16T07:39Z | protected / `awaiting-later-completed-update` |
| B | 2026-10-23T01:58Z | protected / `awaiting-later-completed-update` |
| C | (no manifest) | protected / `unmanifested-recovery-original` |

Group A stays protected even though a newer startup migration, B, completed on a newer version a week later, and the Gateway has been healthy on that version since.

## Why

In `dist/doctor-session-sqlite-retirement-*.mjs`:

```js
laterUpdateStartedAt = Math.max(0, ...listUpdateRuns({ limit: 100 }, …)
  .filter((run) => run.status === "succeeded" && run.finishedAtMs !== null)
  .map((run) => run.createdAtMs));
…
classify("protected", "awaiting-later-completed-update")  // unless laterUpdateStartedAt > completedAt
```

`docs/cli/update/repair-and-recovery.md` says the same thing: groups "become eligible only after Doctor verifies migration completion and update history records a successful update that started later."

On an installation upgraded with npm directly, `state/openclaw.sqlite` had no `update_runs` table at all. The only way to get a row is to upgrade through `openclaw update`. We tried that on the same kind of instance (`openclaw update --tag 2026.10.6 --yes --no-restart` from 2026.10.4). The package install worked (16.5s). Candidate validation, running beside the live Gateway, was then OOM-killed in a 4 GiB container. Many deployments run smaller containers than that. Deployments that bake OpenClaw into an image can't route upgrades through `openclaw update` at all without giving up the offline image install.

There is no supported command to record an upgrade that something else performed (`adopt-immutable` is only for sealed release installations). Writing `update_runs` directly would depend on private schema.

## Ask

Either of these would make `cleanup` work for outside upgrades without weakening its guarantees:

1. **Accept a later completed startup migration as the evidence.** A group could become a candidate when a different, newer startup-migration manifest for the same database has a `completedAt`, written by a newer OpenClaw version than the one in the older group's manifest. Doctor already verifies that manifest. The newest group would stay protected as it is today, so the rollback copy for the current generation is kept.
2. **Add a supported way to record an outside upgrade**, for example `openclaw update record --from <version> --to <version>`. It would write a succeeded run (`trigger: "external"`) after Doctor confirms the installed version, so `laterUpdateStartedAt` reflects it.

Option 1 needs no operator action and matches what the history check is trying to establish ("a later generation started and finished successfully"). Option 2 keeps the history-based rule and gives package managers and image builders a way into it.

## Workaround today

Downstream, we keep the newest group per database and delete older groups only when the newest manifest has `completedAt`, the Gateway is healthy on the current version, and no process has the file open. It works, but it is a second retention policy outside OpenClaw's intent records. We'd rather `cleanup` owned it.

Related: `unmanifested-recovery-original` groups (group C above) stay protected permanently. If option 1 lands, it may be worth treating an unmanifested group that is older than a completed, manifested newer group the same way. That is separate and optional.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash / run failure

### Summary

On 2026.11.1, sending `/think medium` in the same Telegram topic while an ordinary agent turn is running kills that turn with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` ("SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>"). The directive itself is applied and acknowledged, but the in-flight turn fails right after its first model response: the completed model output is discarded, the user gets "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request…", and the original request is dropped until the user resends it.

This is #192522 with a different command. PR #192585 fixed only `/status`: it marks status replies `contextFreeCommand` and states that "ordinary commands retain their existing behavior". Directive acknowledgements (`/think`, `/reasoning`, `/verbose`, `/fast`, `/elevated`, `/model`, `/queue`, …) still go through the same delivered-command recorder as context-bearing rows, so typing any of them mid-turn has the same effect.

### Observed sequence

2026.11.1 (`4ffdd20`), Linux, Node 26.12.1, Telegram polling, direct chat with forum topics, built-in `openclaw` runtime, `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, default queue mode. All times UTC, 2026-11-07, from the gateway log:

1. 03:59:46.377 inbound user request (411 chars) in a DM topic; agent turn `runId=0f7a6dbe…` starts on `lane=session:agent:main:telegram:direct:<peer>:thread:<topic>`.
2. 03:59:59.984 inbound `/think medium` (13 chars) in the same topic, ~14 s later, while the turn's first model request is in flight.
3. 04:00:02.880 directive reply "Thinking level set to medium." delivered (`sendRichMessage`) and recorded as a delivered command exchange.
4. 04:00:47.909 the first model response returns (`request=1`, promptTokens≈177k).
5. 04:00:48.821 `lane task error: lane=main durationMs=61856 error="SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>"`, and the same for `lane=session:…`.
6. 04:00:49.065 `Embedded agent failed before reply: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>`.
7. 04:00:49.400 `message dispatch completed … outcome=error`; 04:00:50.237 the user receives "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request…". No answer to the original request; the user had to send "Continue" manually.

The same install hit the same failure on 2026-11-06 11:13 UTC, also on 2026.11.1: a 792-char request, then a 7-char command in the same topic 19 s later (acknowledged within 4.6 s), then the conflict 18 s after that, at the first model response. The command text isn't in the log, but its length matches `/status`. That is consistent with #192585 not having shipped yet (see release status below).

### Why (source)

- On `main`, the only producers of `contextFreeCommand` reply metadata are `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-status.ts` (`markStatusReply`) and the unknown-subcommand branch in `commands-info.ts`. `directive-handling.impl.ts` sets nothing, so a `/think` acknowledgement is recorded by `recordDeliveredCommandExchange` as a context-bearing command input plus reply.
- The active turn's prepared assistant append then fails the transcript fence when the first response is committed. The installed build checks this in the session-turn worker: `append.preparationVersion` against the version read in the transaction, which includes `rawSeq` and `transcript_updated_at`.
- The embedded runner rethrows it as fatal (`if (isSqliteTranscriptMutationConflict(promptError)) throw promptError`), and model fallback classifies it as `coordination`. So there is no retry or continuation, and the already-paid model response is lost.

The throwing call site wasn't instrumented. The timing (failure at the first assistant commit, after the directive exchange was recorded) and the #192522 analysis both point to the prepared-assistant fence.

### Release status

#192585 (merge `c2cb56c665e3c0a84f21f30369731563e05c37fa`) is not in `v2026.11.1` (latest stable) or `v2026.11.5-beta.1`: `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.transcript.ts` contains no `contextFreeCommand` at either tag, and the installed 2026.11.1 `recordDeliveredCommandExchange` has no such handling. Even after it ships, it won't cover `/think`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A Telegram (or any channel) session on an embedded-agent runtime with SQLite transcript storage.
2. Send a request that keeps the first model call busy for 10 s or more (a long answer or a large context).
3. While that call is in flight, send `/think medium` in the same chat/topic. `/think low`, `/reasoning on` or `/verbose on` should behave the same way.
4. Expected failure: the directive is acknowledged, then `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` fires at the first model response, the user sees "couldn't finish this request", and the original request never gets an answer.

Control cases: the same request without the directive completes normally, and the same directive sent after the turn finishes is harmless.

This was observed twice in production, not in an isolated harness. Rough frequency: any directive typed mid-turn by a user who adjusts settings while waiting.

### Expected

A settings directive sent while a turn is running should apply to the next turn (or at a safe boundary) without failing the turn in flight. User-visible commands shouldn't be able to destroy an in-progress answer.

### Suggested direction

- General fix, preferred over per-command marking: let the prepared-assistant fence rebase over delivered command exchanges that land mid-turn, or defer recording those exchanges until the active turn on that session lane settles. Marking commands context-free one at a time is whack-a-mole; there are dozens of slash commands and any of them can be typed mid-turn.
- ~~Narrow fix: treat directive-only acknowledgements like `/status`.~~ Withdrawn: #169026 (`289d859c`) deliberately keeps `/think`, `/model`, `/reasoning` etc. in later model context, and the slash-commands docs keep `/status` as the only exception. The fix should keep the directive exchange in history and context but stop it from invalidating the turn already in flight, for example by recording it after that turn's prepared answer commits, or by letting the fence accept a delivered command pair that arrived after the turn's input.
- Safety net, only if the above is not enough: recover the already-received answer when the sole intervening rows are a delivered command exchange. Not a blanket replay, which could admit unrelated newer input or repeat tool side effects.

### Related

- #192522 / #192585: `/status` variant, fixed on `main` only for `/status`.
- Same error family with other concurrent writers: #184909, #176235, #174994, #145551, #148280.
- Closed-unmerged #185939 ("recover rewrites from concurrent appends") is the general approach.

issues.body:
### Summary
After a Slack bot token rotation (edited in panel/config and persisted to `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`), the running Slack provider does not reliably reload the new token. The cached token in `@slack/bolt`'s `singleAuthorization` keeps returning the old value, so every inbound event fails `auth.test` with `invalid_auth`. Symptom looks like "Slack integration broken" — messages stop routing — even though the new token on disk is valid.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.5.6 (downstream managed instance, single container)
- Channel: Slack (Bolt)

### Repro
1. Running gateway with a working Slack channel.
2. Edit `channels.slack.botToken` in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (or via panel "save Slack config") to a freshly rotated token.
3. Observe gateway logs around the edit timestamp.

### Expected
`[gateway/channels] restarting slack channel` fires within the inotify debounce window, the `App` instance is rebuilt with the new token, and `auth.test` succeeds on the next inbound event.

### Actual
- Earlier edits in the same session (e.g. 14:34, 14:54 UTC on 2026-05-10) did trigger the restart line.
- A later edit (15:35 UTC, same file, same key) did **not** trigger any restart line — the old token stayed cached in memory.
- All inbound events from then on hit `invalid_auth` against `auth.test`, even though a direct `auth.test` against the on-disk token succeeded.
- Workaround: `docker restart <container>`. After restart, Slack reconnected clean and stayed healthy.

### Suspected cause
- `@slack/bolt` `singleAuthorization` caches `authorization.botToken` per `App` instance. The provider reuses the existing `App` rather than tearing it down and rebuilding when only the bot token changes.
- The inotify-based config watcher / `config.patch` path appears to debounce or skip the restart for some edit shapes (token-only change while other fields are unchanged).

### Asks (either fixes the user-visible bug)
1. **Reliable channel restart on token change.** Gateway should always emit `[gateway/channels] restarting slack channel` when `channels.slack.botToken` (or `appToken`) actually changes on disk, regardless of the surrounding edit shape.
2. **Or:** the panel's "save Slack config" path should explicitly call gateway/channels restart-slack after persisting, so we don't depend on the watcher firing.

### Notes / not this bug
- This is **not** "multiple Slack sessions" or "message routing splitting." A user-side hypothesis ("OpenClaw is creating multiple Slack sessions per user") was reported but did not match the logs. The actual symptom is a single stale `App` instance holding a cached token.
- Loosely related (different code path, already merged): #70720 *fix(gateway): restart channels after secret reload* — that fix targets SecretRef refresh; this issue is about plain token-string rotation in `channels.slack.botToken` not triggering a restart.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On Windows, every time the Gateway (re)loads the plugin registry it materializes a fresh capture of the bundled Codex plugin package, including @openai/codex-win32-x64 (~461 MB, codex.exe alone is 354,558,768 bytes), into state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/openclaw-plugin-build-*/package-N/node_modules/... The copy + per-file verification runs synchronously on the main thread, so the whole Gateway freezes for 20-50 s per load (up to ~3 min late in the day): no replies, Control UI websocket drops and reconnects, channel connections (Zalo) restart. Registry loads happen at the start of each agent turn (prepareWorkspacePluginRegistries), when the Control UI asks for the tool list, and on every config reload, so the freezes recur every few minutes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11, OpenClaw 2026.11.3 installed via npm into a local app folder, custom state dir, Codex plugin installed (state/extensions/codex with @openai/codex-win32-x64).
2. Start the Gateway and use the Control UI webchat normally (send messages, open sessions).
3. Watch state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/: a new openclaw-plugin-build-* directory with a full copy of codex.exe appears at each freeze.
4. Measure: first tools/list call from the UI takes 25-31 s, an immediate repeat takes ~2 s (cache hit), next registry rebuild freezes again.

### Expected behavior

Plugin generation capture should reuse an existing materialized package (or hard-link / reference the native executable) instead of copying hundreds of MB per registry load, and heavy capture work should not block the Gateway event loop.

### Actual behavior

Gateway event loop blocked 20-50 s per registry load, growing to ~170 s over a long-running process. Over ~9.5 h the old process reloaded config 100 times; RSS grew to ~3.6 GB (JS heap only ~520 MB). tmp/plugin-captures grew to ~4.7 GB / ~24k files with 10+ copies of codex.exe; in one 25-minute window after a restart 13 new 461 MB copies were created, each timestamp matching a freeze (22:03, 22:04, 22:05, 22:12, 22:13, 22:15, 22:16, 22:20). Windows Defender scanning each new codex.exe copy makes it slower.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 x64, Node v24.19.0

### Install method

npm (local prefix install, custom OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR), Gateway run as Windows scheduled task

### Model

claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 (issue is model-independent)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> claude-cli (not relevant to the bug)

### Additional provider/model setup details

No custom provider routing involved; bug is in plugin loading, independent of model/provider.

### Logs

```shell
CPU profile (CDP Profiler, 60.8 s sample during one freeze), inclusive time:
52.5s prepareWorkspacePluginRegistries  prepared-model-runtime.facts-*.mjs:252
52.5s acquireAgentRuntimePluginRegistry  runtime-plugins-*.mjs:276
52.5s loadOpenClawPluginsCore            loader-runtime-load-*.mjs:1226
52.4s loadRuntimePluginCandidate / loadPluginModule  loader-runtime-load-*.mjs:749/1017
50.7s bindPluginInstanceModuleLoader     plugin-setup-module-*.mjs:1002
49.8s createPluginGenerationArtifact     plugin-generation-artifact-*.mjs:972
45.1s materialize                        plugin-generation-artifact-*.mjs:1029
44.9s copyPackage -> copy                plugin-generation-artifact-*.mjs:1001 / 134

Copies of codex.exe (354,558,768 bytes each) under state:
state/extensions/codex/node_modules/@openai/codex-win32-x64/vendor/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/bin/codex.exe
state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/native/admission-*/content/vendor/.../codex.exe (x2)
state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/openclaw-plugin-build-*/package-2/node_modules/@openai/codex-win32-x64/.../codex.exe (many)
state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/openclaw-model-catalog-*/openclaw-plugin-build-*/package-2/.../codex.exe
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: any Windows install with the Codex plugin installed. Severity: high - the Gateway becomes unresponsive for minutes repeatedly, chat and channel connections drop. Frequency: every agent turn / tool-list request / config reload that rebuilds the plugin registry. Consequence: assistant unusable until the plugin is disabled or the Gateway is restarted, and restart only resets the growth.

### Additional information

Workaround under consideration: disable the Codex plugin. Possibly related: config reload triggered 100x in one day also rebuilds the registry each time. Disk: purging state/tmp/plugin-captures frees several GB.

issues.body:
- **Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)
- **Beta release blocker:** No

## Summary

The `sessions.usage` RPC builds each session row's `modelProvider` / `model` fields **only** from the session store entry:

```js
// dist/usage-<buildhash>.mjs — session row assembly
modelProvider: merged.storeEntry?.modelProvider,
model: merged.storeEntry?.model,
```

Sessions that never persisted a session-level model/provider — deleted-session tombstones, heartbeat / cron / subagent sessions, and sessions whose model was resolved per turn — therefore return `modelProvider: null`. The Control UI Usage page reads the provider column from exactly that field (`provider: e.modelProvider ?? e.providerOverride`) and falls back to the generic "unknown" label, so those sessions show up as an **unknown provider** even though the same row carries the real provider one level deeper in `usage.modelUsage[].provider`.

Measured on **2026.11.3 (847611d)**, RPC `sessions.usage` with `{agentScope:"all", limit:900, startDate:"2026-11-01", endDate:"2026-11-14"}`:

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| session rows returned | 789 |
| rows with `modelProvider == null` | **623** (≈ 79 %) |
| rows with `modelProvider == null` in a 24 h window | 66 → 70 (grows with every new session) |
| `usage.modelUsage[]` entries | 894 |
| `usage.modelUsage[]` entries with `provider == null` | **0** |

Provider distribution of the `modelUsage[]` entries for the same window: `minimax` 377, `opencode-go` 311, `lmstudio` 89, `openclaw` 73, `openrouter` 44 — i.e. the provider is **always** available at that level; only the session-level field is missing.

**Scope note:** `aggregates.byProvider` is *not* affected. It is built from `usage.modelUsage[].provider` and contains no "unknown" bucket at all. The defect is limited to the per-session `modelProvider` / `model` fields returned by the RPC.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d) with a mix of session types (interactive chat, cron/heartbeat, subagent spawns) and some deleted sessions in the history.
2. Call `rpc sessions.usage` with `{agentScope:"all", limit:900, startDate:"<d>", endDate:"<d+1>"}`.
3. Inspect `sessions[]`: count rows where `modelProvider === null` and compare with the `usage.modelUsage[]` entries of the same rows.

## Expected behavior

A session row whose usage was measured against a provider should report that provider, even when the session record itself has no persisted `modelProvider`.

## Actual behavior

`modelProvider` is `null` for those rows (623/789 in the measurement above), and the Usage page renders them under "unknown".

## Suggested fix

Fall back to the provider of the **dominant** `usage.modelUsage[]` entry (largest `totals.totalTokens`) when the session-level value is missing — for `modelProvider` and `model` alike:

```js
const dominantModelUsage = Array.isArray(usage?.modelUsage) && usage.modelUsage.length > 0
  ? usage.modelUsage.reduce((best, current) =>
      ((current?.totals?.totalTokens ?? 0) > (best?.totals?.totalTokens ?? 0) ? current : best))
  : null;

modelProvider: merged.storeEntry?.modelProvider ?? dominantModelUsage?.provider ?? null,
model: merged.storeEntry?.model ?? dominantModelUsage?.model ?? null,
```

The fallback is a no-op for rows that do carry a session-level provider, and it stays `null` for rows that genuinely have no measured usage (empty session shells).

## Verification

Applied the fallback above locally on 2026.11.3 (847611d) and re-ran the same RPC:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| rows with `modelProvider == null` | 623 | **4** |
| rows with `modelProvider == null` in a 24 h window | 66 → 70 | 0 |

The 4 remaining rows have `totalTokens = 0` and `modelUsage = null` (empty session shells with no measured usage) — there is genuinely no provider to report for them.

## Impact

On a 14-day window this affects ~79 % of all rows. Any per-provider spend/token attribution built from the session rows is unusable, and the Usage page shows a growing "unknown" provider group that operators cannot break down or attribute.

## Related

- #194260 — *different* root cause: that one is about `usageReport.state === "unavailable"` hiding range totals. This issue is only about the missing provider/model attribution on the session rows.

### What happens

When `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set **only in the environment of the spawned Claude CLI process** (for example a skill or backend-specific env override), and not on the Gateway process itself, a second turn in the same conversation starts a fresh session instead of resuming.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: current `main` and `4f8df80`
- Claude Code CLI: `2.1.323`
- Node: `24.22.1`
- Isolated Gateway, fresh `claude.ai` login, subscription `max`
- Default `~/.claude/projects` left empty to make the transcript location visible

### Steps

1. Start the Gateway without `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in its own environment.
2. Configure the Claude agent so the child process gets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/some-dir` (skill env override).
3. Run two turns in one conversation.
4. Restart the Gateway and run a third turn.

### Observed

On `4f8df80`:

- two turns produced **two different transcript UUIDs**,
- the second turn did not use `--resume`,
- the log contains a missing-transcript entry.

With the change we tested internally on the same setup:

- both turns produced **one transcript UUID**,
- after the Gateway restart the next turn issued `--resume` for that same UUID,
- the default `~/.claude/projects` stayed empty.

### Why this is separate from #175549 and #198337

`#175549` fixed the cases where `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set on the Gateway process or through `env.vars`; we verified those work on current `main`. `#198337` covers the Control UI history case.

This report is only about the child-process-only override, which the closing comment on #145895 mentioned as untested and out of scope for now.

### Question

Is this setup in scope? I can share the reproduction script and the patch we used if you want to look at it.

labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
## What happens

When you scroll up through a chat with many finished tool calls, the text you are reading jumps up, against the scroll direction, by up to several hundred pixels. This is the jump most people hit in long agent sessions.

Measured on an isolated Gateway with a synthetic history of 280 turns, half of them with settled `read`/`exec` tool calls (Chromium, 1280×900, frames sampled after each paint):

- On `main` (`480389e1`), a frame trace of a fast upward scroll shows the text moving 206.5 px against it.
- A scripted wheel run on the same history moved the text against the scroll in 11 frames, by up to 618 px. That run used `d1c800bf` plus a fix for the late-content case below.

## Reproduce

1. Open a session whose history has many settled tool calls. Each turn should have one or more `read` calls with a few lines of output, followed by a short answer.
2. Start at the end of the transcript.
3. Scroll up quickly with a mouse wheel or trackpad (for example 1,100 px wheel steps about every 55 ms).

Expected: the text moves down steadily with the scroll. Actual: every few frames it jumps up.

## Why

- A settled tool row is estimated at 240 px but renders at about 34 px.
- The transcript lays out its visible rows in normal flow, starting at the first row's estimated offset.
- A row scrolled into view above that content enters the flow at its real size in a frame where the flow's start still counts its 240 px estimate. Everything below it moves by the difference before the correction lands.
- On an iOS user agent, virtual-core defers its own scroll correction while the reader scrolls, so the jump stays visible longer.

## Also: late content inside the top visible message

The same text also moves when content renders late inside a message already on screen. Measured on `main` (`d1c800bf`) with synthetic messages in the Control UI e2e harness, with the message's top above the viewport and its last line 40 px below the top edge:

| Late content | Reader text moves |
| --- | --- |
| Mermaid diagram renders above the text | 378 px down |
| Raw tool details open above the text (hidden toggle) | 440 px down |
| Remote Markdown image (blocked by policy) | 0 px |
| Local image decoding late | 0 px |

To reproduce the Mermaid case:

1. Use a history whose message has a Mermaid block followed by text, and hold the Mermaid module so it renders late.
2. Scroll so the message's top is above the viewport and its last text line is near the top.
3. Release the module.

Expected: the text stays where it is. Actual: it moves down by the diagram's height.

Why:
- The transcript turns native scroll anchoring off (`overflow-anchor: none`), so the app keeps the reader's place itself.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-reader-anchor.ts` corrects size changes of rows entirely above the viewport. It does nothing for growth inside the row that crosses the top edge, where late content above the reader's text lands.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-interaction-anchor.ts` keeps the clicked control's row top in place. When that control isn't laid out or is off screen, the content it opens pushes the visible text down instead.

## Related

- #197549 removed the automatic browser preview cards, one earlier trigger. The jumps above still happen without them.
- #192101 covers a separate problem: one owned measurement switches compensation off for the whole next resize delivery.

issues.body:
### Summary
When the primary model fails with a failover-class error (provider usage limit) **after the turn has already delivered progress messages** to the channel, the turn ends with the generic "stopped" reply and the configured model fallback is never attempted.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d), macOS, Telegram direct chat
- Primary: `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5` (Claude CLI subscription auth)
- Fallbacks: `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` (Codex OAuth, usage 100% left), `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`

### What happened
1. Long tool-using turn (~488 s, computer-use) that had sent several `message(action=send, final=false)` progress updates.
2. Claude CLI returned the 5-hour usage limit:
   `diagnostic FailoverError lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner:… durationMs=488274 error="You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 6pm"`
3. ~1 s later the generic progress-stopped reply was delivered.
4. No attempt on `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` (or any fallback) appears in the log for the next ~57 minutes. The agent stayed silent until the user sent a new message.

### Suspected cause
In the installed build, `cli-run-recovery-*.mjs` (~L48-50) returns `finishDeliveredFailure` before the retry/throw path when delivery evidence exists, and `cli-runner-*.mjs` (~L422+) builds an error result with the progress-stopped text. Prior progress delivery turns a FailoverError into a returned error result, so the fallback loop never sees it.

### Expected
A FailoverError (usage/rate limit) should still advance to the next fallback candidate even if progress messages were already delivered. At minimum, continue on the fallback model with a resume note instead of ending the turn silently.

### Related
Possibly related to #176183 (fallback abandoned after first candidate), but this is the CLI-runner delivered-progress path, not continuation sub-runs.
