issues.title: Devices page: gateway role badge uses theme accent color and reads as a red error dot

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
## Summary

On the Control UI **Devices** page, every paired device row shows a status chip — green `connected` / gray `offline`. The **gateway row's chip is not a status chip**: it is a role badge rendered with the theme *accent* color. On themes whose accent is red-ish (e.g. the built-in `miami` theme, `--accent:#ff5c5c`), a perfectly healthy gateway displays a **red dot** next to "gateway", directly contradicting the green dots on every other row.

Because it sits in the exact position and shape of the status dots used by all other rows, users reliably read it as "the gateway is in an error state" — and then go hunting for a health failure that does not exist.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d), npm install, Fedora Linux (bare-metal systemd user service)
- Control UI dark mode, theme `miami` (accent `#ff5c5c`)
- Gateway health genuinely healthy: `health` RPC `ok: true`, `openclaw doctor` 0 error findings

## Repro

1. Run a gateway with any red-accented theme (miami, claw).
2. Open Control UI → Devices.
3. Observe: `● gateway` chip on the gateway row is red while `● connected` chips on node rows are green — even though everything is healthy.
4. Switch theme → the "status" dot changes color (e.g. to amber/pink), proving it is not status-driven.

## Actual vs expected

| | Actual | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway row chip color | theme accent (`--theme-chip-accent` → `--accent`) | a status color (green when healthy), or a visually distinct badge treatment that cannot be mistaken for a status dot |
| Chip semantics | role badge ("gateway" vs "unpaired") | users read it as health status because every sibling row uses that exact pattern for status |

## Where it lives

In the devices page chunk, the gateway presence chip is rendered with `kind: "accent"` (vs `"muted"` when unpaired), and CSS maps it to the theme accent:

```css
.chip--accent { background: var(--theme-chip-accent); } /* --theme-chip-accent: var(--accent) */
```

Node rows use `kind: "ok"` (green) / `"muted"` (gray) — genuine status.

## Why it matters

This cost a full afternoon of debugging a non-existent gateway fault: we chased dead-lettered delivery entries, security-audit findings, and a reboot cycle before discovering the dot was cosmetic. Silent cosmetic/status ambiguity is worse on a self-hosted admin surface where the red dot's only other meaning in that UI *is* error. (The docs page for the Devices feature also describes the gateway dot as a health indicator, which reinforces the misreading.)

## Suggested fix

Either (a) render the gateway badge with a neutral/ok treatment and reserve accent for non-status decoration away from the dot position, or (b) make it an actual health indicator so the color means what users assume it means.

Related but distinct: #151504 (badge/indicator consolidation epic) — this issue is about the specific status-misreading hazard of the accent-colored gateway dot, not general badge geometry.

Happy to provide a repro driver or screenshots on request.

issues.title: Design review: durable closed-session snapshot contract for opt-in external memory export

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:feature
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

issues.body:
## What problem this solves

OpenClaw deployments that use an external durable-memory system need a safe way to export **only a finalized, authorized session generation** for later indexing. Today, terminal-write draining and closed-turn reads do not establish a restart-safe, closed-session snapshot. Treating either as one can export incomplete, resumed, or deleted content.

This blocks a default-off, opt-in OpenClaw → external-memory bridge and forces deployments to retain duplicate native semantic indexes or lose reliable cross-session recall.

## Requested design acceptance

Please accept or amend the following storage/lifecycle contract before implementation:

1. A host-owned, generation-bound durable settlement receipt is created only after all accepted producers for that occurrence have durably succeeded. It is invalidated by resume, replacement, reset, or deletion.
2. At settlement, the host copies the bounded finalized payload into the agent database; it is not a mutable/live transcript anchor.
3. Any future external bridge is default-off and requires an explicit source allowlist. It redacts content and metadata before creating any export intent or embedding request.
4. Deletion/revocation semantics are delete-wins for pending local intents. A delivered external copy is not represented as retracted unless the downstream sink has a verified deletion/revocation contract.
5. Export uses a same-agent-database outbox and stable event IDs; sink idempotency must be verified before dispatch.

## Evidence

- Existing `drainAgentRunTerminalWrites` uses `Promise.allSettled` and does not yield a durable-success receipt.
- Existing closed-turn reader validates bounded turn anchors, not permanent session closure.
- Agent-session lifecycle storage and ordinary delivery-queue storage are separate databases, so queue insertion is not atomic with a session snapshot.
- Model/regression tests cover writer failure, delete, replacement, resume/re-close races (10 focused cases).

## Proposed review packet

- Branch: https://github.com/dlmccoy/openclaw/tree/task/durable-terminal-snapshot
- Commit: `712136734f0`
- `CLOSED-SNAPSHOT-REVIEW-DIFF.md` details schema/transaction alternatives, storage seams, and activation/rollback gates.
- `TERMINAL-SETTLEMENT-PLAN.md` records lifecycle/race assumptions.

No production API, schema migration, transcript export, deployment, or memory setting change is proposed by this issue. Once the contract is accepted, I can prepare the narrow default-off implementation and focused race tests for review.

issues.title: [Bug]: cron: automations created without `payload.model` get no inference binding when `agents.defaults.subagents.model` differs from the agent primary → "Automation has no recorded inference account" on first run

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: impact:auth-provider
labels.description: Auth, provider routing, model choice, or SecretRef resolution may break.

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.11.3 (847611d), macOS, Gateway local.

**Summary**

When an `agentTurn` automation is created without `payload.model`, the creation-time inference capture and the run-time model selection resolve **different default models**. Capture binds nothing; the run then forwards an auth profile and is refused. One-shot (`at`) jobs are disabled on that first error, so the reminder is silently lost.

**Config that triggers it**

```json5
agents: { defaults: {
  model: { primary: "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5" },          // claude-cli runtime, native login
  subagents: { model: { primary: "openai/gpt-6-astra" } }   // Codex runtime, forwards auth profile
}},
auth: { order: { openai: ["openai:pool"] } }
```

**Steps**

1. Create an automation without a model, e.g. via the `cron`/automations tool from an agent session:
   `{ schedule: { kind: "at", at: "<+5m>" }, sessionTarget: "isolated" | "session:<key>", payload: { kind: "agentTurn", message: "…" } }`
2. Wait for it to fire.

**Expected:** it runs on the model it resolves at run time (here `openai/gpt-6-astra` via `openai:pool`), or creation fails/warns that no account could be recorded.

**Actual:** run fails in ~100 ms with
`Automation has no recorded inference account. Explicitly select its account with a model@profile update before running it.`
Run history shows `provider: openai, model: gpt-6-astra`. One-shot gets `autoDisabled: consecutive-failures`.

**Cause (from the built dist)**

- Creation: `captureCronCreatorSession` (src/gateway/server-methods/cron-input-validation.ts) → `captureCronInferenceForCaller({ model: job.payload.model, … })` → `captureCronInferenceBinding` → `resolveSimpleCompletionSelectionForAgent({ modelRef: undefined })` → falls back to the **agent primary** (`agents.defaults.model`). That is claude-cli, which does not accept profile forwarding → returns no binding.
- Run: `resolveCronModelSelection` (src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts) resolves payload → gmail hook → stored automation-session override → **`agents.defaults.subagents.model`** → default. With no session override yet, a fresh job lands on `openai/gpt-6-astra` (Codex) → `resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId` returns `openai:pool` → `trigger === "cron" && !binding && authProfileId` → refusal (src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts for isolated; src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-cli-candidate.ts for `session:<key>`).
- The startup diagnostic `describeCronInferenceMigration` (src/gateway/server-cron-inference.ts) already uses the run-time precedence (`payload.model ?? hooks.gmail.model ?? subagents.model`), so capture is the odd one out.

**Not affected:** legacy jobs that already have a stored automation-session `modelOverride` (e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` from earlier runs) keep resolving to it and run fine without a binding.

**Suggested fix:** in `captureCronCreatorSession`, resolve the capture model with the same precedence as `resolveCronModelSelection` (at minimum `job.payload.model ?? subagents.model primary`, and the target session's `modelOverride` for `session:<key>` targets), or fail creation with an actionable error instead of storing an unbound job that cannot run.

**Related, not the same:** #192555 (creation accepts session-targeted jobs that can never run on a CLI-login session — same class: creation and run resolve different routes), #192327 (plugin service `add()` passes no binding), #195887 (legacy claude-cli jobs unbound after upgrade, not flagged), #188761 (preflight when the default model changes), PR #195890 (refuses edits that leave a job unbound — does not cover `add`), #193855 (feature: follow the agent's account). Here the job is created through the Gateway's own `cron.add`, and the capture runs, but on the wrong default model.

**Workaround:** `openclaw automations edit <id> --model 'openai/gpt-6-astra@openai:pool'` (records the binding; the model does not change).

issues.title: [Bug]: Remote-access setup retains Connecting warning after relay becomes online

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:bug
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The **Turn on remote access** completion dialog retains a yellow **Connecting <claw>** warning after the relay has become online and accepted a remote browser, because its relay result is a one-time snapshot with no reconciliation while the completed dialog remains open.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed once on the affected build; the delayed-relay state transition also reproduces deterministically with the existing runner and fake actions (no live service changes):

1. Enable the OpenClaw ID lab and start **Turn on remote access** as an administrator through a verified personal trusted-proxy connection.
2. Complete the name/recovery-kit ceremony and publish successfully while the relay is not online at the first status read.
3. The completion card shows a green signing step, green hostname-registration step, and a yellow **Connecting <claw>** step.
4. Allow the Gateway's existing relay retry to succeed, then connect remotely. The warning remains the completion card's stored result; there is no subsequent relay read in this dialog's setup sequence.

Minimal synthetic check, run using the repository's existing TypeScript runner from the repository root:

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { runLinkSteps } from './ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/link-steps.ts';

let online = false;
let reads = 0;
const states: Record<string, unknown> = {};
await runLinkSteps({
  sign: async () => {},
  commit: async () => ({
    state: 'published', ownerAccountId: 'synthetic', snapshotSeq: 1,
  }),
  relayOnline: async () => { reads++; return online; },
}, {
  notPublished: () => 'not published',
  relayOffline: 'relay not connected yet',
}, (id, state) => { states[id] = state; });

online = true;
await Promise.resolve();
assert.equal(reads, 1);
assert.deepEqual(states.relay, {
  state: 'warning', message: 'relay not connected yet',
});
```

Control: initializing `online = true` reports `{ state: 'done' }`. Both synthetic assertions passed against the unmodified affected source. This is a runner/source reproduction, not a new browser replay of the production ceremony.

### Expected behavior

While the completion dialog remains open, reconcile the connection step with current relay status: once the Gateway reports online, show success (or explicitly label the warning as a historical initial check rather than current connection status). The same runner already reports success when the first read is online.

### Actual behavior

Remote access succeeded, but the completion card retained its connection warning. The Gateway became relay-online 8.044 seconds after the successful setup commit. A remote peer was subsequently admitted and served the Control UI with HTTP 200. A later read-only status call reported a running, online tunnel with one connection and zero restarts.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3; full commit `3991f8f22494afea4a9b2ac8c48b47e7386928b2`; build `2026.11.3-3991f8f22494-2026-11-13T21-01-41.582Z`.

The relevant runner, dialog, sign-in service and method handler are unchanged between this revision and upstream main `649ca5f879f1e4349a2c5cf9872e30366962a595`, checked November 13, 2026. No exact existing tracker/fix was found in live issue/PR searches for the status text, `stepRelayOffline`, `runLinkSteps`, and remote-access setup warnings.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0 (26A428), arm64; Node v26.12.1.

### Install method

Native source build, supervised by a macOS LaunchAgent.

### Model

Not applicable; no model request is involved.

### Provider / routing chain

Control UI → verified personal trusted proxy → Gateway setup; Discovery publication → outbound iroh relay → remote browser.

### Logs

Sanitized event excerpts, November 13, 2026 (UTC−06:00); private account/profile/peer identifiers and hostname omitted:

```text
15:14:12.860 openclaw-id: remote access commit success route=personal_admin via=trusted-proxy profile=<redacted> user=<redacted>
15:14:12.861 openclaw-id: remote access link_profile failure code=sign_in_not_held route=personal_admin via=trusted-proxy profile=<redacted> user=<redacted>
15:14:20.904 tunnel: relay online
15:16:20.901 tunnel: admission allowed: peer=<redacted> path=relay
15:16:21.531 tunnel: http peer=<redacted> GET / -> 200 (32ms)
```

Later read-only `openclawId.status` excerpt (unrelated/private fields omitted):

```json
{
  "status": {
    "state": "on",
    "tunnel": {
      "state": "running",
      "relayOnline": true,
      "relayDenied": null,
      "connections": 1,
      "restarts": 0
    }
  }
}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The user-supplied screenshot showed the completed card with green **Securing <claw>** and **Setting up <hostname>**, yellow **Setting up your access** and **Connecting <claw>**, and a **Close** footer. The original screenshot is not uploaded because it includes the user's remote hostname.

Source at the exact affected revision:

- [One-shot relay read and terminal warning state](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3991f8f22494afea4a9b2ac8c48b47e7386928b2/ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/link-steps.ts#L72-L78).
- [Dialog invokes the sequence once, then enters done](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3991f8f22494afea4a9b2ac8c48b47e7386928b2/ui/src/components/openclaw-id/make-reachable-dialog.tsx#L313-L327).

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed administrator setting up OpenClaw ID remote access. Severity: misleading onboarding status, not a demonstrated tunnel outage or data loss. Frequency: one production incident; deterministic delayed-relay runner reproduction with an initially-online control. Consequence: the user believed setup may have failed and required log/status tracing to distinguish a stale connection warning from an actual profile-link warning.

### Additional information

**Scope distinction:** the separate **Setting up your access** warning in this incident corresponds to a real `sign_in_not_held` profile-link refusal. It is not evidence that the relay failed and is not claimed to be a second bug here. The exact reason that particular browser sign-in was not held is unknown from retained logs; do not infer token expiry, profile mismatch, or restart causality from the shared refusal code.

[PR #198349](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198349), already present in the affected build, intentionally leaves remote access enabled when profile linking is refused. [PR #197998](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197998), also already present, changes the E2E test for warning completion and explicitly makes no production behavior change; it does not add relay-status reconciliation.

Regression status: unknown; no last-known-good or introducing change is established. No live configuration, service, recovery keys, memberships, or source code were changed during this investigation.

issues.body:
## Subagent completion delivery: final answer lost (`truncated-by-retention` stub) + duplicate settle events; `deliveryStatus` stuck `pending`

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)
- Linux 7.0.12-linuxkit (arm64), Node v24.19.0, Docker
- Main session: `agent:main:main`

### Steps to reproduce
1. `sessions_spawn` a subagent with `mode=run`, `runtime=subagent`, `context=isolated` (long-running task, ~20 min).
2. Let the child complete.

### Observed
Child run: `205c4277-af22-4977-959b-f99ec38e5fd4` (child session `agent:main:subagent:da061934-8121-41e3-94cc-e5c8251f3955`, label `flux-audit`).

1. **Final answer lost.** The completion event arrived with `status: ok` but the child result body was only:
   ```
   [truncated-by-retention: complete child answer unavailable]
   The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions.
   ```
   The child had actually produced work (files on disk) but its final report text was unrecoverable to the parent.

2. **Same settle event delivered multiple times.** The identical inter-session settle message for this run was received by the parent at least 3 separate turns apart (~18:41, ~18:55, ~19:1x UTC), each claiming "Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled" — after which further completion events for that run were (correctly) impossible, so the duplicates had no data but did cause redundant re-processing.

3. **`deliveryStatus` stuck.** `subagents(action=list)` reported `deliveryStatus: "pending"` for the task across all three deliveries, i.e. the pending flag never cleared even though settle notifications kept arriving.

### Expected
- The child's final answer is delivered intact (or, if retention truncation is intentional, the truncation happens at a known boundary and the full answer is retrievable by path).
- One settle/completion event per run.
- `deliveryStatus` transitions `pending -> delivered` once the parent actually receives the result.

### Impact
Parent loses the only structured handoff from a long-running child; must reconstruct results from side-channel artifacts (scratch files). Duplicate settle events risk double-processing or masking genuinely lost results (the "is it done or broken?" ambiguity).

### Workaround used
Child instructed to write all artifacts to a fixed workspace path before exit; parent verifies artifacts on disk instead of trusting the completion message.

Happy to provide more detail or test a patch if useful.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a bot sends files in a Teams channel, allow automatic resolution of the team's own SharePoint site instead of requiring a hardcoded `sharePointSiteId`.

## Problem to solve

Bots that send files in Teams channels must configure `channels.msteams.sharePointSiteId` pointing to a single SharePoint site. The native Teams file card uses `webDavUrl`, which requires the recipient to be a member of that SharePoint site. In multi-team deployments, team members who are not members of the configured site see "request access" when clicking a file the bot sent — even though they are members of the Teams team the file was sent in.

This is a real production issue: a bot deployed across four Teams teams uploaded all files to a private SharePoint site. Members of one team could not open files the bot sent because they had no access to that site. The bot operator had to either manually grant every team's M365 group read access to the site, or maintain per-team `sharePointSiteId` overrides — neither of which scales.

## Proposed solution

When `sharePointSiteId` is absent from config:
1. Resolve the team's M365 group ID from the activity (already cached by `resolveTeamGroupId`)
2. Call `GET /groups/{groupId}/sites/root?$select=id` to get the team's backing SharePoint site ID
3. Cache the result (site IDs are stable)
4. Upload files there instead

Files then land on the team's own SharePoint site where all team members already have read access. `webDavUrl` in the file card works without additional permission grants.

Additionally, make the upload folder name configurable via `sharePointFolder` (default: `OpenClawShared`) so deployments can customize it.

`sharePointSiteId` remains as an explicit override for deployments that want a central upload site.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use the org-wide sharing link in the file card instead of `webDavUrl`**: OpenClaw already creates an org-scoped sharing link via `createLink`, but the file card uses `webDavUrl`. Switching to the sharing link would make files accessible to anyone in the org, removing per-team privacy isolation. This is a weaker solution for enterprise deployments.
- **Require operators to grant site access per team**: Manual, does not scale, and grants broader access than needed (entire site vs just uploaded files).
- **Per-team `sharePointSiteId` in config**: Verbose, requires operators to resolve site IDs manually for every team. Dynamic resolution removes this burden.

## Impact

- **Affected**: Multi-team msteams deployments where the bot sends files
- **Severity**: High — file sends appear to work but recipients cannot open the files
- **Frequency**: Every file send in every team except the one whose site matches the config
- **Consequence**: Users see "request access" on files the bot sent; operators must manually manage SharePoint site permissions per team

## Evidence/examples

Production deployment across 4 Teams teams. File sent by bot in Team A's channel → uploaded to `/sites/bot-private` → Team A member clicks file card → "request access" because they are not a member of `/sites/bot-private`. The bot operator can open it fine because they are a site admin.

With the proposed change, the same file would upload to `/sites/TeamA/` (the team's own backing site) where the team member already has read access.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

## Additional information

- Requires `Sites.Read.All` or `Sites.ReadWrite.All` on the bot's app registration (most deployments already have `Sites.ReadWrite.All` for uploads).
- The `resolveTeamGroupId` cache from `team-identity.ts` is already populated on every inbound message, so the group ID is available without an extra API call.
- Site ID resolution adds one Graph call per team on first file send; the result is cached for the process lifetime.
- Backward-compatible: `sharePointSiteId` still works as before when set.

issues.body:
## Summary

With a `claude-cli/*` model, the system prompt's Tooling section lists tools by their bare names (`read`, `exec`, `edit`, `write`, ...) and says "Names case-sensitive; call exact." The only callable names in that runtime are the MCP-prefixed ones (`mcp__openclaw__read`, ...). A one-line hint about the prefix is appended at the very end of the prompt, so the model sees an explicit instruction to call `read` long before it sees the correction.

## What happened

First tool call of a session: `read`. Result:

    Error: No such tool available: read

Retrying as `mcp__openclaw__read` worked. It costs one wasted turn and a visible tool error, and it is easy to repeat because the prompt tells the model to use the bare name.

## Where it comes from

`extensions/anthropic/cli-tool-naming.ts` (`appendClaudeCliToolNamingGuidance`) appends this section to the end of the assembled system prompt:

    ## OpenClaw tool names in Claude Code
    OpenClaw MCP: `mcp__openclaw__<name>`. Deferred: ToolSearch `select:mcp__openclaw__<name>` first.

The Tooling list earlier in the same prompt is built for all runtimes and is not rewritten for the CLI runtime, so the two sections contradict each other. Observed on 2026.11.2.

## Suggested fix (any of these)

1. When the CLI runtime appends the naming section, also rewrite the Tooling list entries to the prefixed names (or prefix them at build time for `claude-cli`).
2. Change the "call exact" line for this runtime to say names carry the `mcp__openclaw__` prefix.
3. Move the naming hint up next to the Tooling list instead of the end of the prompt.

Option 1 is the cleanest: the list then matches what is callable, and the end-of-prompt hint becomes redundant.

## Workaround

A line in the workspace `AGENTS.md` ("under claude-cli, call the `mcp__openclaw__` prefixed names") helps only if the model reads it before the first call; it does not remove the contradiction.

## Searched first

No open or closed issue found for: "mcp__openclaw", "claude-cli tool prefix", "claude-cli system prompt tool names", "No such tool available". Happy to send a PR for option 1 or 2 if the maintainers say which they prefer.

2026-11-13T17:52:05.563-04:00 templates.add.apply failed: Agent hopper deletion is in progress; new work is unavailable.
2026-11-13T17:52:05.563-04:00 ⇄ res ✗ templates.add.apply 139ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Could not add this Template. Review Gateway logs before retrying.

issues.body:
Versions: 2026.10.7 and 2026.11.2 (same logic).

What happens
A client starts an agent run over the gateway WebSocket (`sessions.create` with `message`, or `chat.send` / `agent`). The agent makes tool calls, all succeed, and its final message is `NO_REPLY` (the caller accepts silence). The run's final assistant message in the transcript is instead:
"The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions."
The caller cannot tell this from a real answer without matching the English string, so a run that meant to stay silent reads as a completed run with odd content (or, to callers that check content, as a failure).

Why (source: src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.ts, src/agents/reply-completion.ts)
1. Gateway-started turns resolve as reply "required": `resolveReplyExpectation` returns "optional" only for an explicit `terminalReplyExpectation`, heartbeat, `inputProvenance.kind` inter_session/internal_system, `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent`, or a trigger other than user/manual. The gateway agent attempt sets `trigger: "user"` (dist 2026.11.2 attempt-execution.runtime-*.mjs:336).
2. With "required", an explicit NO_REPLY stop after settled, error-free tools triggers the text-only settled-turn finalization (`resolveSettledToolTerminalContinuationInstruction`, allowEmptyStopContinuation). When finalization is empty twice (MAX_EMPTY_SETTLED_FINALIZATION_ATTEMPTS) or throws, and `preparedAttempt.silentExpected !== true`, the fallback text replaces the answer (2026.11.2 embedded-agent-*.mjs:7463 and :7518; 2026.10.7 :7338 and :7392). Native cron runs get `SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN` here (`runParams.trigger === "cron"`) and also run with `terminalReplyExpectation: "optional"`; gateway-started runs get the English text.
3. There is no supported way for a gateway client to say the reply is optional:
   - `SessionsCreateParamsSchema`, `AgentParamsSchema`, `ChatSendParamsSchema` and `sessions.patch` are closed and carry no reply-expectation field (packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-create.ts and siblings).
   - `silentExpected` is internal only (memory flush, experience review, recall) and also suppresses all visible output.
   - The in-process gateway path carries `replyExpectation`, but it is stripped before WebSocket transport (2026.11.2 in-process-gateway-*.mjs:136).
   - `agents.defaults.silentReply.group` applies to group chats; gateway chat is direct.
   - The only reachable lever is claiming `systemInputProvenance` / `inputProvenance` kind internal_system or inter_session, which is admin-only and changes how the turn is recorded and shown (system actor, "Internal system input", run-wait transcript-artifact filtering, skill selection). That is a provenance claim, not a reply policy, and not something a client should fake.

Repro
1. Over the gateway WS: `sessions.create { agentId, label, message: "<prompt that calls a tool and then answers NO_REPLY when there is nothing to report>" }`.
2. Agent runs one or more tools without error, final message `NO_REPLY`.
3. `sessions.get`: the last assistant message is the fallback text, with `__openclaw.idempotencyKey` = `<runId>:settled-finalization-fallback`.

Ask (any one would do)
A. A per-run reply expectation on the gateway API: e.g. `terminalReplyExpectation: "optional" | "required"` on `sessions.create` (initial turn), `chat.send` and `agent`, with the same semantics native cron gets (empty / NO_REPLY is a silent completion, no settled-turn fallback text).
B. Or: when a run's final assistant turn is an explicit NO_REPLY after settled tools, use `SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN` as the fallback for every trigger, not only cron (the cron branch already shows the intent).
C. In any case: a documented, stable marker that a final message is the synthesized fallback (today only the `:settled-finalization-fallback` idempotency-key suffix, which is an implementation detail), so clients can tell "agent produced no final answer" from a real answer without matching English text.

Related: #174620 (closed: optional turns now complete silently; this issue is that a gateway client cannot make a run optional), #188984 (same resolution problem for unmentioned group turns).

issues.body:
### Summary

On a container install, after swapping the image to a new release the bundled-channel plugin copies (matrix, signal, perplexity, voice-call) keep serving the old version, and there is no documented way to update them while the Gateway runs. The commands that look right either refuse or exit non-zero even though they work.

### Environment

Docker, image 2026.11.3 (previously 2026.11.2), state directory bind-mounted, Gateway running, commands run inside the Gateway container.

### What happens

1. After the image swap, `openclaw plugins list` shows the four external plugins still at 2026.11.2 while core is 2026.11.3.
2. `openclaw plugins update <id>` refuses with "requires exclusive offline state ownership". With the Gateway stopped there is no running container to run it in, and a one-off container cannot take the Gateway lease (see #196846).
3. `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/<id> --force` from inside the running Gateway container does work, but it takes about 1 to 1.5 minutes per plugin and exits with rc 1. Output (abridged):
   - `Plugin operation failed during drain: plugin <id> admitted work did not settle within 60s; the previous plugin generation stays active. Use `openclaw plugins reload <id> --wait` ...`
   - `Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.`
   - `Plugin "<id>" installation is saved. Fix the reported issue, then run `openclaw plugins reload <id>`. | UNAVAILABLE`

   The new files are on disk afterwards, and a full Gateway restart applies them.

### Why it is confusing

- The rc 1 and "replacement not applied" wording reads as a failed install; it actually saved the new version and only the live swap was refused. Scripts and operators cannot tell success from failure without re-listing.
- The suggested `--wait` can wait forever when the caller's own agent turn is what holds the plugin (the case in #162115, where the turn waits on its own lease).
- Nothing in the upgrade or Docker docs mentions that bundled-channel plugin copies can lag the image after an upgrade, or which command to use for it.

### Suggested

- Document the Docker upgrade sequence: swap image, `plugins install --force` per plugin (or an equivalent `plugins update` that works online), then one restart.
- Either make the install exit 0 with a "saved, restart to apply" notice when the live swap is deferred, or print that distinction explicitly.
- Consider having the entrypoint's doctor step converge external plugin copies to the image version, so a plain image swap needs no manual step.

Happy to test any of this on our setup.

Allow an automation owner to explicitly authorize separate provider/account bindings for a cron job's primary model and fallback models.

## Problem to solve

My configuration uses an OpenAI primary with an xAI fallback so scheduled work can continue when the primary hits a usage limit or becomes unavailable. After upgrading a Windows npm installation to official OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (`7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be`), adopting an OpenAI account for a cron job does not authorize its configured xAI fallback.

The shipped binding stores one provider/account. Both execution paths reject a candidate from another provider. Selecting a new `model@profile` changes the job's binding; it does not approve a second account for fallback.

This request concerns jobs with an explicitly selected primary account. It is separate from the older-job missing-account adoption problem tracked in #188761.

## Proposed solution

Provide a supported authoring flow to approve the primary and each fallback's model, provider, account and compatible runtime/authentication route for one scheduled job.

- Preserve explicit ownership and current authorization checks for every approved candidate.
- On ordinary availability or quota failures, allow the configured fallback to use its own approved account.
- Preserve the existing refusal behavior for revoked, missing or incompatible authorization; an account-authority refusal must not become a way to bypass the original permission boundary.
- Show incompatible or unapproved fallback routes during job creation/editing, with a supported way to approve them.

The exact API/storage design is for maintainers to choose. Credential values should remain in their existing owners.

## Alternatives considered

- A same-provider fallback on the bound account does not cover a provider-wide outage or that account's subscription limit.
- Manually changing the primary account requires intervention when the purpose of the fallback is unattended recovery.
- Separate provider-specific jobs require coordination outside the single scheduled turn.

## Impact

This prevents the intended OpenAI → xAI fallback policy for an account-bound scheduled job, even though the fallback remains configured. The requested capability is useful to operators who deliberately use multiple providers and approve the account used for each one.

Scope: source/configuration verification on 2026.10.10, not a forced live fallback test. No outage was induced, no production job was replayed, and no claim is made that every configured cron job has already reached this failure branch. Current xAI authentication also needs independent validation before claiming a successful live fallback.

## Evidence/examples

Exact released source:

- [One provider/account in `CronInferenceBinding`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/cron/inference-binding.ts#L5).
- [Provider-mismatch guard in `prepareCronRunInference`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/cron/run-inference.ts#L47).
- [Equivalent guard in the isolated fallback executor](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts#L371).
- [Documented inference-account continuity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md#L189).

The source error is:

```text
Automation candidate is incompatible with its recorded inference account and route.
```

The comparison is between provider IDs, not the company that authored a model. This request does not claim that every model from another company is prohibited.

Related account-continuity work: #172590 and #173411. The latter explicitly addresses an unintended provider switch after an account-adoption refusal. This proposal requires deliberate approval of each fallback account rather than changing that refusal policy.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

AI assistance: configuration/source investigation and issue drafting with Codex.

issues.body:
### Summary
On macOS, gateway discovery through `dns-sd -L` cuts off any TXT value that contains a space. A gateway display name shows up as `Peter’s\` instead of `Peter’s Mac Studio`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. On a Mac whose computer name contains a space, run a gateway with Bonjour discovery on.
2. From another Mac, run `openclaw gateway discover`.
3. Compare with `dns-sd -L "<instance>" _openclaw-gw._tcp local.`, which prints `displayName=Peter’s\ Mac\ Studio`.

### Expected behavior
`displayName` is `Peter’s Mac Studio`.

### Actual behavior
`displayName` is `Peter’s\`, and the rest of the value is dropped.

### Source-level repro
- `src/infra/bonjour-discovery.ts`: `parseDnsSdResolve` splits the TXT line with `line.split(/\s+/)` before unescaping.
- Apple's `ShowTXTRecord` (mDNSResponder `Clients/dns-sd.c`) prints spaces and shell metacharacters in TXT values as `\<char>`, so escaped spaces become token breaks.
- `decodeDnsSdEscapes` only handles `\DDD`, so the trailing `\` survives.
- `displayName` is also decoded twice (in `parseTxtTokens` and again later in `parseDnsSdResolve`).
- The existing test fixture uses `\032` inside TXT, which `dns-sd -L` never prints for TXT values, so the tests don't catch this.

This was found by reading the source against Apple's `dns-sd` output format; I haven't captured it on a second Mac yet.

### Proposed fix
- Split the TXT line on unescaped whitespace only, and decode `\<char>`, `\\` and `\xHH` once per value.
- Keep `\DDD` decoding for DNS names.
- Add a fixture using real `ShowTXTRecord` output.

I'm happy to open a PR for this.

### Impact
Wrong gateway names in discovery, and any TXT value containing a space (for example `cliPath`) is cut off. Affects only the macOS `dns-sd` path.

### Version / OS
`main` @ 2a226d93; macOS (`dns-sd`).

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
The sqlite-vec KNN path for memory search selects `vec_distance_cosine(v.embedding, ?) AS dist` after vec0 has already run the KNN. On a 650-chunk index that recompute takes about 1.1 s per query; using vec0's own `distance` column instead takes about 8 ms with the same top-5 ranking.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Enable memory search with the vector store on (`memory.search.store.vector.enabled: true`) and an embedding provider (observed with Gemini `gemini-embedding-001`, unit-normalized vectors).
2. Index a few hundred memory chunks (observed: 650).
3. Run `memory_search` and time the KNN SQL, or run the same statement directly against a copy of the index DB with sqlite-vec loaded.
4. Swap `vec_distance_cosine(v.embedding, ?) AS dist` for `(v.distance * v.distance / 2) AS dist` and run the same queries.

### Expected behavior
KNN distance comes from the vec0 MATCH result, so the query cost is dominated by the KNN itself (single-digit ms at this size).

### Actual behavior
Each candidate's embedding is materialized and cosine is recomputed. Warm SQL p50/p95 was 1089/1410 ms with the current expression and 8.22/9.99 ms with the vec0 distance. The ordered top 5 matched on 21/21 checked queries; the largest first-hit distance difference was 1.49e-6. A freshly built vec0 index over the same 650 vectors took 666/845 ms on the unchanged path.

The expression was at `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-knn.ts:113` on 2026.10.10-beta.3 and is now at `src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector.ts:114` on main (777007b), passed as `distance` to `nearest()`.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.10-beta.3 (621f020); expression still present on main 777007b

### Operating system
macOS 27.0 (arm64)

### Install method
From source (git checkout, built locally)

### Model
gemini-embedding-001 (memory search embeddings)

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw memory-core -> Gemini embeddings API; KNN in local sqlite-vec (vec0)

### Additional provider/model setup details
vec0 tables are created as `embedding FLOAT[N]` with the default L2 metric (`src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-memory-search-fragments.ts`). For unit-normalized vectors, cosine distance = L2² / 2, which is why `(v.distance * v.distance / 2)` preserves both ranking and score.

Two possible fixes:
- Declare the vec0 column with `distance_metric=cosine` and select `v.distance` directly. No normalization assumption, but existing indexes need a rebuild.
- Keep L2 and derive cosine as `v.distance * v.distance / 2`, valid only while every stored and query vector is unit-normalized.

### Logs
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Timings above come from a scratch copy of the index with sqlite-vec loaded in a child process, the same way the KNN child runs it. Warm DB open, pragmas and extension load totalled under 4 ms, so the SQL dominates. The probe doesn't separate embedding materialization from the cosine math itself.

### Impact and severity
Affected: memory search users with the vector store enabled.
Severity: slow tool calls (about 1 s added per memory_search at 650 chunks, growing with candidate count).
Frequency: every vector search.
Consequence: higher latency for agent turns and voice consults that call memory_search. Workaround: `memory.search.store.vector.enabled: false`, which uses the worker cosine scan (about 30 ms at this size).

### Additional information
Related: #69680 introduced the sqlite-vec KNN path. #172092 (closed) is about a different JSON scan in engine storage.

issues.body:
## Feature request

Make the `MEMORY.md` size budget used by `memory-core` Dreaming promotion configurable instead of fixing its maximum at 10,000 characters.

## Current behavior

`DEFAULT_MEMORY_FILE_MAX_CHARS = 1e4` in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory-budget.ts` caps the promotion writer even when an operator has explicitly configured a larger per-file bootstrap budget. `resolveMemoryPromotionFileMaxChars` can lower that 10,000-character cap to a smaller consumer `bootstrapMaxChars`, but cannot raise it. Once the final rendered `MEMORY.md` cannot fit after permitted compaction, promotion candidates are deferred and do not become durable in that file.

A fixed, conservative default is sensible for safe bootstrap injection. The request is for an **explicit opt-in** for deployments that choose a larger memory/context budget, without changing the default or silently overflowing the effective bootstrap limit.

## Proposed behavior

- Expose a documented `memory-core` Dreaming/promotion configuration setting for the maximum final `MEMORY.md` character count (for example, `plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.phases.deep.memoryFileMaxChars`; exact name/location is up to maintainers).
- Keep 10,000 characters as the default when unset, preserving existing behavior.
- Permit an explicitly configured value above 10,000 when compatible with the consuming agent(s)' per-file bootstrap budgets. Continue resolving the smallest applicable budget for shared workspaces, or reject an incompatible configuration with a clear diagnostic instead of silently writing an uninjected tail.
- Retain current safeguards: preserve user-authored content, compact only eligible generated promotion sections within the loss limit, and defer candidates without marking them promoted when the final write cannot fit.
- Document the interaction with `bootstrapMaxChars`, `bootstrapTotalMaxChars`, and character counting; test the default, a larger opt-in budget, a smaller consumer budget, and the overflow/deferral path.

## Observability / acceptance criterion

A configurable cap alone does not address silent saturation. When one or more otherwise eligible Dreaming promotion candidates are deferred **because the effective `MEMORY.md` budget cannot be satisfied**, expose a distinct, actionable warning in the Dream Diary / promotion result and memory health/status surface (including the effective limit, current/final projected size, number of deferred candidates, and whether compaction was exhausted). Do not report an ordinary sweep with zero eligible candidates as a budget failure. Provide a durable health signal that operators can alert on, without generating a notification on every subsequent sweep for the same unchanged condition.

This should make it obvious that Dreaming phases still run but durable promotion is blocked; the operator can then curate memory or explicitly change the budget. Please include a regression test for over-budget deferral surfacing the warning and for a normal zero-candidate sweep not surfacing it.

## Why this matters

Operators with ample context space can intentionally reserve more than 10,000 characters for durable promoted memory. Today, raising `bootstrapMaxChars` alone does not allow Dreaming to use that space, so eligible memories eventually stop being promoted to `MEMORY.md` even though the deployment could accommodate them.

## Related work

- #73691 introduced the safe size cap to prevent unbounded growth; this proposal keeps that protection by default.
- #142393 / #142545 fixed deferral and consumer-budget enforcement; this proposal should preserve those guarantees.
- #71330 requests a configurable *target file*, which is a different feature from configuring the size budget of `MEMORY.md`.

Source in v2026.9.6: [`memory-budget.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/extensions/memory-core/src/memory-budget.ts#L30-L64).

issues.body:
## Problem

The Signal channel fully supports **inbound** mention detection: `requireMention` gating (with per-group overrides) and `groupChat.mentionPatterns` text fallback — the mention-gating section of `docs/channels/signal.md` covers inbound matching only. There is no way for an agent to **send** a native mention: the message tool has no mentions field, and the managed-native send path attaches no mention metadata. Agent replies in group chats always render as plain text.

## Use case

Multiple OpenClaw agents share a Signal group with `requireMention=true` (a natural agent-collaboration setup). Agents need to address each other explicitly. Human members tag agents with native mentions via the Signal mention picker; agents cannot answer in kind. The text-pattern fallback gates correctly, but:

- it renders as plain text, not a mention highlight;
- it bypasses the platform's native mention semantics;
- every agent in the group must maintain mirrored `mentionPatterns` instead of relying on the native mechanism.

## Current workaround and why it fails

signal-cli >= 0.14 supports outbound mentions: `signal-cli send --mention start:length:recipient`, and the JSON-RPC `send` method accepts a `mentions` array (string format `start:length:uuid`, UTF-16 code units). Calling signal-cli directly beside OpenClaw is not viable: the gateway's managed-native transport holds the signal-cli config lock permanently, so any side-channel invocation blocks forever ("Config file is in use by another instance"). Taking the transport down to free the lock brings the whole channel down with it. The capability is unreachable through supported paths.

## Request

Extend the Signal send path and the message tool with an optional `mentions` parameter on sends:

```json
{
  "action": "send",
  "channel": "signal",
  "target": "group:<id>",
  "message": "@name — hello",
  "mentions": [{ "start": 0, "length": 5, "recipient": "<uuid>" }]
}
```

- ranges in UTF-16 code units, matching signal-cli's `start:length:recipient` format;
- the managed-native transport passes them through to signal-cli (CLI `--mention` or JSON-RPC `mentions`).

## Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), signal-cli 0.14.4.1, managed-native transport, receiveMode manual.

issues.body:
**Summary**

`openclaw health` reports a delivery-queue warning that can never clear on an older install:

```
Delivery queue: warning (dead-lettered entries — outbound: 15, outbound-prepared-v1: 3; oldest 121d ago)
```

**Cause**

Records live in `delivery_queue_entries` in the shared state database. The legacy `outbound` queue persists its terminal records with `completionRetention` set to the string `"permanent"`:

```
queue_name=outbound  status=failed  recovery_state=completed_permanent
entry_json = { "id", "enqueuedAt", "retryCount", "failedAt",
               "recoveryState": "completed_permanent",
               "completionRetention": "permanent" }
```

These are payload-free tombstones (no message body, no target, no error text) — but they are retained indefinitely, and the health snapshot counts them as dead-lettered. Our oldest dates to 2026-06-01 (121 days), and the count never decreases.

The newer `outbound-prepared-v1` queue behaves correctly and self-expires:

```
completionRetention = {"idPrefix":"cron-direct-delivery:v1:","maxAgeMs":86400000,"maxEntries":2000}
```

so this looks specific to the legacy `outbound` queue's retention policy.

**Reproduction**

1. Run an 8.x Gateway long enough to accrue failed `outbound` entries.
2. `openclaw health` → `Delivery queue: warning (dead-lettered entries — outbound: N …; oldest …)` where N never falls.

**No supported remediation**

- `openclaw channels dead-letters` covers **inbound** events only (`list` / `resubmit` per channel account).
- There is no `deliveryQueues` retention/prune schema path — a config schema lookup for `deliveryQueues` returns `schema_path_not_found`.
- Deleting rows by hand from a live shared-state database is unsupported and requires a Gateway stop.

**Expected**

Any of:

- apply bounded retention to legacy `outbound` terminal records the way `outbound-prepared-v1` already does;
- exclude permanently-retained completed records from the health dead-letter count; or
- expose a supported prune/acknowledge command.

**Impact**

Cosmetic but permanent: every health check on an older install reports a warning that cannot be resolved, which trains operators to ignore the queue-warning line. Diagnosed on 2026.8.2.

issues.body:
### Summary

`memory-lancedb` should register a memory search `runtime`, so the Control UI Memory page works when it owns `plugins.slots.memory`.

### Problem to solve

With the official `@openclaw/memory-lancedb` as the memory slot owner, the Control UI Memory page can't show or search anything. The plugin only registers `publicArtifacts`:

```js
// extensions/memory-lancedb/dist/index.js (2026.9.4 installed; 2026.9.6 from npm is identical)
api.registerMemoryCapability?.({ publicArtifacts: { async listArtifacts(params) { /* … */ } } });
```

Without a `runtime`, `ensureMemoryRuntime` returns `{ searchRuntimeRegistered: false }` and every host-side memory search call fails:

```
$ openclaw gateway call doctor.memory.status --params '{"agentId":"main"}'
{ "agentId": "main", "searchRuntimeRegistered": false,
  "embedding": { "ok": false, "error": "memory plugin unavailable" } }

$ openclaw gateway call memory.search --params '{"query":"test","agentId":"main"}'
Gateway call failed: memory plugin unavailable
```

Since #155117 the Overview shows a neutral "Host memory search is unavailable — memory-lancedb does not provide a host memory search runtime" hero instead of a failure. That is accurate, but the page is still empty and the Memories tab search still fails.

Meanwhile the memory system itself is healthy, so this is purely an operator-visibility gap:

- `openclaw ltm stats` / `ltm search`: LanceDB store OK, vector recall OK.
- `openclaw memory search "…" --agent main` and the agent's `memory_search` / `memory_get` return hits from the memory-core file index. memory-core's tool opens its manager through `getBuiltinMemorySearchManager` directly, not through the slot owner.
- `memory_recall` / `memory_store` / `memory_forget` and auto-recall work.

The agent can search its memory, but the operator can't see it from the UI. The only config-level "fix" is setting the slot back to `memory-core`, which drops the LanceDB tools and auto-recall and cuts off the stored memories. So users of the featured first-party memory plugin are left with a Memory page that never works.

### Proposed solution

Have `memory-lancedb` pass a `runtime` in `registerMemoryCapability`, like memory-core does (`createLazyMemoryRuntime`):

- `getMemorySearchManager(params)` returns a manager backed by the plugin's LanceDB store. It embeds the query with the configured embedding provider, runs the agent-scoped vector search it already uses for `memory_recall`, and maps rows to the result shape the Memories tab renders (text, score, source, id).
- `closeMemorySearchManager` / `closeAllMemorySearchManagers` release the table handles.
- Optional hooks (`authorizeSearchHits`, `classifyWorkspaceMemoryPaths`, `supportsWorkspaceMemoryReadSources`) can stay unset at first.

Plugin authors have already pointed out that a third-party slot owner which registers a `runtime` gets a working Overview and search (see #138366). The first-party plugin would then be the reference implementation of that seam.

### Alternatives considered

- **Fallback in core**: when the slot owner registers no runtime, `memory.search` and the Memories tab fall back to the builtin file-index manager, labelled as such. That mirrors what the agent's `memory_search` tool already does, and it would also help third-party slot owners without a runtime. But it would still show nothing of the LanceDB store itself, which is where `memory-lancedb` keeps its memories. It works as a complement, not a replacement.
- **Slot back to `memory-core`**: the UI works (file index only), but the LanceDB tools and auto-recall are lost. Not viable.

### Impact

- Affected: every install using `memory-lancedb` (featured in the plugin catalog) as the memory slot owner.
- Severity: annoying to workflow-blocking for operators. Nothing in the Memory page can be inspected, and the only way to audit memories is the CLI (`ltm list` / `ltm search`) or asking the agent.
- Frequency: always, by design of the current registration.
- Consequence: memories can't be reviewed from the UI, which makes it hard to spot bad or stale auto-captured entries.

### Evidence/examples

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Docker on Linux, `plugins.slots.memory = "memory-lancedb"`, Ollama embeddings; memory-core loaded as the dreaming sidecar. Startup log: `memory plugin not selected for the memory slot; skipping its indexing runtime and recall registration (consolidation lifecycle preserved) (plugin=memory-core)`.
- Discussed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138366#issuecomment-5844801270. The issue author agreed it is a separate gap from the Dreams provider and preferred a `runtime` in `memory-lancedb` over a core fallback.
- Related: #153016 (same symptom with a third-party slot owner, closed by the neutral hero in #155117).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Should stay backward-compatible: `memory-core` as slot owner is unchanged, and the runtime only exists when `memory-lancedb` holds the slot.

issues.body:
## Summary

Two tool schemas — `automations` and `skill_workshop` — alternate between two different capability profiles across turns **in the same session, with no config change**. The tool roster is unaffected: same 51 tools, same names, same order.

This is primarily a **capability-correctness** problem, not just a caching one. In profile A the `automations` tool offers `add`; in profile B it does not. The same agent in the same session can create an automation in one turn and be unable to in the next, with nothing explaining the change.

It also invalidates the entire prompt cache on each flip, because tool definitions sit at the front of the cached prefix. Observed cost on one flip: `cacheRead=0`, `cacheWrite=340,830`.

## Relationship to #146902

**#146902 is very likely the same root cause, observed one level down.** That report describes same-session tool-set churn where two variants share a tool *count* but differ in *membership* (43A vs 43B, different tool names). This report describes variants that share count **and membership and ordering** — all 51 names identical, in the same order — yet still produce a different `toolDigest`, because two tools' *schemas* differ.

So `"tool set changed with same count"` covers at least two distinct situations, and `toolNames` alone does not distinguish them.

If the per-attempt `toolsAllow` mechanism identified there (`resolveCodingToolConstructionPlanForAllowlist`) also gates *which actions a tool advertises*, that would explain both reports with one fix. This report adds the schema-level evidence and, more importantly, a functional consequence not covered there: an action silently disappearing from a tool the agent had just used successfully.

That report's request 4 (the redaction gate blocking prompt capture) independently matches what I hit here and in #155685; confirming it from a second host and OS.

Other related but distinct: #155685 (a `sessionId` above the cache boundary — different cause, same symptom). #148304, #95610, #112986, #125064 concern volatile *prompt* content; this is volatile *tool schema* content.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.9.5 (also observed on 2026.9.4) |
| Node | v24.21.0 |
| OS | Linux 7.0.14-5-pve (x64) |
| Provider / API | `anthropic` / `anthropic-messages` |
| Model | `claude-opus-5` |
| `cacheRetention` | `long` |

## The two profiles

Captured by dumping raw `context.tools` on both sides of a flip. Same session, same `sessionKey`, no config change between them.

### `automations` — profile A has 5 more actions

```
A (10):  status list get add update remove run runs next_check wake
B  (5):  list get update run remove
```

- Actions absent in B: **`status`, `add`, `runs`, `next_check`, `wake`**
- Properties absent in B: `contextMessages`, `in`, `mode`, `sessionKey`, `text`
- `additionalProperties`: `true` in A, absent in B
- Description: **5,603** chars in A, **459** in B

B's description redirects the caller elsewhere: *"Use the Automations page for other actions."*

### `skill_workshop` — profile B has 6 more actions

```
A (14):  create prepare_patch patch update read revise list inspect
         evaluate apply reject quarantine history restore_collection
B (20):  … the same 14, plus share unshare transfer activate remove rollback
```

- Properties added in B: `delete_files`, `expected_revision`, `files`, `revision`, `skill_id`, `target`
- `additionalProperties`: `false` in A, `true` in B
- Description: **1,990** chars in A, **2,774** in B

### Everything else is byte-identical

All other 49 tools match exactly between captures, including `browser`, `exec`, `message`, `image_generate` and `video_generate`.

## Observations

Aggregate `toolDigest` for the 51-tool policy takes exactly two values: `314e0eefc8…` (profile A) and `30309afb5d…` (profile B).

| time (UTC) | run | toolDigest | cacheRead | cacheWrite |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| 09-21 19:07 | `d0661d5b` | B | 167,986 | 7,844 |
| *gateway restart* | | | | |
| 09-21 19:18 | `012e14f4` | **A** | 0 | 208,710 |
| 09-21 19:28 | `eff56d49` | A | 231,173 | 1,855 |
| 09-21 19:29 | `3f79ee5f` | **B** | 49,039 | 187,636 |
| 09-22 10:23 | `4798c171` | **A** | 0 | 250,779 |
| 09-22 10:38 | `5d3f6b09` | **B** | 0 | 249,145 |
| 09-22 11:04 | `2483d9e6` | B | 257,034 | 2,545 |
| *gateway restart* | | | | |
| 09-22 11:47 | `90ec896d` | **A** | 325,891 | 820 |
| 09-22 12:36 | `2005f6fd` | **B** | 0 | 340,830 |

Every digest change costs a full re-cache; stable digests hit normally.

The profile alternates in **both directions**, with and without an intervening Gateway restart. Full sequence for this session (`A` = `314e0eefc8`, `B` = `30309afb5d`):

```
18:28 B ×7 … 19:07 B | restart | 19:18 A  19:28 A | 19:29 B  19:33 B
10:23 A | 10:37 B  11:04 B  11:16 B  11:23 B | restart | 11:35 A  11:47 A
12:36 B  12:37 B  12:43 B | 13:08 A
```

Note `13:08 A` and `12:36 B`: both flips occurred with **no** Gateway restart. A restart is therefore not required to change profile, and neither profile is "the" steady state.

## What is NOT established

**Whether the two tools' changes share a cause.** They co-vary in all four captures that contain both tools, and never appear mixed:

| capture | tool policy | `automations` | `skill_workshop` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11:47:46 | 51 tools | A (10 actions) | A (14 actions) |
| 12:05:12 | 47 tools | A | A |
| 12:10:00 | 44 tools | A | A |
| 12:36:27 | 51 tools | B (5 actions) | B (20 actions) |

That is only **one observed transition**, so co-variation here is equally consistent with a single shared cause and with two independent changes that happened to fall in the same window. It should not be assumed the two are linked.

**The trigger.** An initial hypothesis — that a run under a different tool policy mutates shared schema state — was tested directly and **refuted**.

Controlled experiment, with the session in profile A:

```
13:08:10  main session   51 tools  314e0eefc8   A
13:08:46  main session   51 tools  314e0eefc8   A
13:09:14  main session   51 tools  314e0eefc8   A
13:09:14  subagent       34 tools  109c63e5e8   <- deliberate perturbation
13:09:24  main session   51 tools  314e0eefc8   A  (unchanged)
```

A subagent run under a genuinely different tool policy did not change the parent session's profile.

A second candidate — the 30-minute heartbeat (`agent:main:main`) — is also ruled out as a sufficient cause. Those runs carry a perfectly stable `toolDigest` (`0ca6c99476`) across 38 consecutive executions, while the main session's profile flips only on some of them and in both directions.

No deterministic trigger has been identified. The profile holds for a few consecutive runs and then alternates, which is consistent with nondeterministic resolution of the two schemas at build time (for example an async capability lookup that sometimes resolves before the tool set is assembled), but that mechanism is **not** established here and should be confirmed from the source side.

A related anomaly, possibly the same root cause: one run in this same session (09-21 19:05, `70b48498`) presented a third digest, `92f7c97a3b`, with a **tool count of 36** rather than 51. So the roster itself can also vary within one session, not only the two schemas described above.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Anthropic model, `cacheRetention: long`, `diagnostics.cacheTrace.enabled: true`.
2. Restart the Gateway, take a turn. Note `toolDigest` in the `cache:state` snapshot, and that `automations` accepts `action: "add"`.
3. Continue taking turns over the next several minutes.
4. `toolDigest` changes with `toolCount` unchanged; `cache:result` reports `tool set changed with same count` and `cacheRead` collapses.
5. `automations` no longer accepts `action: "add"`.

I could not reproduce on demand — the interval varied from 12 to 49 minutes — so this needs whatever drives the two profiles to be identified from the source side.

## Diagnostic gap that made this expensive to find

`cache:state` records `toolDigest`, `toolCount` and `toolNames`, but never the schemas. Since the roster is identical across the flip, the trace can report *that* tools changed but never *which* tool or *what* changed.

`collectPromptCacheTools()` already computes per-tool `descriptionDigest` and `schemaDigest` — and discards them, keeping only the aggregate. **Including per-tool digests in the `cache:state` snapshot would have reduced this investigation to one diff.** That seems a cheap, high-value change.

Identifying the tools required patching `onModelRequest` to dump raw `context.tools`, because by the time the array reaches `beginPromptCacheObservation` it has already been reduced to digests.

(The same run also hit the `system`-field redaction described in #155685, which prevented capturing prompt text without a patch.)

```
[warn] SQLite session write failed operation=session-entry.patch elapsedMs=9 err="subagent session-effects owner retired before session commit"
[warn] failed to persist subagent session timing err="subagent session-effects owner retired before session commit" runId=…
```
Later the delivered completion text is prefixed with `[truncated-by-retention: complete child answer unavailable]` even though the child's full terminal reply exists in `completion.terminalReply.text` (e.g. `37 × 29 = 1073`).

**Expected**: the late session-effects patch should either be accepted by the new owner or dropped silently as telemetry; the retention note should not be shown to the end user when the terminal reply is available in the registry.

issues.body:
## Summary

Cross-filed from https://github.com/garrytan/alphaclaw/issues/102. That report describes OpenClaw 2026.9.3 on a mature Render installation with a consolidated repository layout:

```text
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/data/.openclaw
/data/.openclaw -> /data/repository/agent
```

The operator reports repeated worktree idle-cleanup failures:

```text
[agents/worktrees] idle cleanup failed … repository does not own worktree
```

`git worktree list` invoked through the repository's real path does list those worktrees. Nineteen Doctor sessions started with `worktree:true` left 152,243 entries / 5.8 GB under the managed worktrees directory. Eleven older scratch checkouts remained under `workspace/.openclaw/`; nine reportedly no longer had live git metadata. This accumulated state subsequently prevented the next upgrade backup.

The same install reports `openclaw config set` failing with:

```text
Atomic replace parent must be a real directory
```

## Requested upstream investigation

1. Canonicalize the repository/state-root identity before comparing worktree ownership, without following or weakening checks on arbitrary interior symlinks.
2. Ensure completed Doctor/worktree sessions dispose of their clean managed worktrees. Preserve dirty work rather than deleting user changes; make retained work and its cleanup policy visible.
3. Allow `config set` to use a symlinked state root by resolving its parent before the atomic write.

## Regression coverage

Start a worktree session in a repository reached through a state-root symlink, complete it, then run idle cleanup. Assert ownership resolves to the same repository and clean managed worktrees are removed without the ownership error. Also run `config set` against the symlinked state directory and verify the real config changes while the state-root link remains intact.

## Evidence boundary and downstream mitigation

The cleanup failure and sizes above are the operator's production observations in the linked issue, not a local reproduction by this cross-filing run. AlphaClaw is adding complete preflight counts, scratch exclusions, canonical child-process state/config paths, `.env` exclusion, and single-pause backups. Those mitigations do not repair OpenClaw's worktree completion/idle-cleanup implementation.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in, single-owner escalation provider for Active Memory so a plugin can decide whether to start deep recall after the deterministic lane has no strong hit.

## Problem to solve

Active Memory has a sound two-lane architecture: the deterministic lane is cheap, while the deep lane runs a blocking embedded agent only when escalation is warranted. In the default escalate mode, however, the escalation decision is closed inside the bundled plugin and based on a built-in lexical intent matcher.

That leaves operators with only three choices:

- off: never run deep recall;
- always: pay for a blocking recall agent on every eligible turn;
- escalate: depend on the built-in matcher.

The matcher has already required language-specific repairs, including CJK support and the current PT-BR work in #135085 and #136502. A third-party plugin cannot replace only this decision: prompt-build hooks compose rather than claim the decision, and replacing the bundled Active Memory plugin also means taking ownership of its session isolation, privacy rules, timeouts, cleanup, caching, circuit breaker, status and deep-recall orchestration.

The missing capability is not another recall engine. It is a supported extension point for the small decision immediately before deep recall.

## Proposed solution

Expose an optional, lifecycle-aware Active Memory escalation provider through the plugin SDK.

Conceptually:

- a plugin registers one provider by id;
- Active Memory selects it through an optional escalationProvider config field;
- the provider runs only in escalate mode, after the deterministic lane has no strong hit and before the embedded recall agent starts;
- it returns recall, skip, or abstain;
- the provider receives an AbortSignal and a short bounded timeout;
- absent, missing, timed-out, failed or abstaining providers fall back according to an explicit, documented policy;
- off, always and strong deterministic hits retain their current behavior;
- existing configurations and defaults remain unchanged.

A dedicated provider is preferable to a general accumulating hook because exactly one component should own this decision. The SDK contract should not require or bundle any model. Implementations could be deterministic, local learned classifiers, or another policy chosen by the operator.

I plan to open a focused PR containing the SDK contract, registry/lifecycle handling, Active Memory integration, config/schema/UI hints, documentation and tests. It will not add a model, weights, network request or new runtime dependency.

## Alternatives considered

### Keep adding language-specific matcher rules

This preserves zero-dependency behavior but does not provide a scalable customization path. The PT-BR gap demonstrates that operators cannot currently supply a better policy without replacing the whole plugin.

### Run a generic LLM completion before recall

This adds another serial model request, authentication/failure surface, cost and latency to the path whose purpose is deciding whether to pay for deep recall.

### Replace the bundled Active Memory plugin

OpenClaw supports config plugins overriding bundled plugins, but this forces a third party to duplicate and track the full deep-recall implementation merely to change one decision.

### Use an ordinary prompt-build hook

Prompt-build hook results compose and do not offer a single-winner handled/cancel contract for this decision.

## Impact

Affected users and systems:

- multilingual personal-assistant deployments;
- operators with local or domain-specific recall-intent policies;
- latency-sensitive agents that cannot use always mode;
- plugin authors who want to improve escalation without owning memory retrieval.

Severity: medium. The current default works for covered formulations, but uncovered language or semantic forms can silently skip deep recall, while always mode adds a blocking agent run to ordinary turns.

Frequency: every eligible conversational turn reaches this policy after a weak deterministic result.

Consequence: either missed historical context, unnecessary latency, or downstream maintenance of a private Active Memory replacement.

## Evidence/examples

- PT-BR recall-intent gap: #135085
- PT-BR matcher repair: #136502
- Prior CJK matcher repair: #117419
- Blocking Active Memory latency report: #72015
- Active Memory documents that lane 1 makes zero model calls and lane 2 is a real agent turn:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/concepts/memory-architecture.md
- Current decision is internal to:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/active-memory/escalation.ts

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

The intended PR is additive and opt-in. It preserves the current built-in policy as the default and keeps model selection, datasets and classifier artifacts outside OpenClaw core. I will include focused provider lifecycle, sync/async, timeout, error, missing-provider, mode, strong-hit and embedded-run boundary tests.

prs.title: perf(sessions): report facts backfill timing per progress interval
prs.body:
## Problem

The transcript facts backfill (#194519) is running on Team r326. Its progress line reports only running maxima since the backfill started: maximum batch and maximum admitted writer execution. A running max only ever rises, so operators can't tell whether a foreground append hold at 05:10 coincided with a slow backfill write or with an older one. The line also says `0/17661 sessions visited` after 64k rows. That reads like no progress, but the counter only advances when a session completes, and discovery puts the largest recently active session first.

## Change

Diagnostic only, in `session-transcript-facts-backfill.ts`. Each progress line (every 60 s, plus pass completion) now reports for the interval since the last line:

- number of batches
- maximum batch (in-transaction work)
- maximum and total admitted writer execution

Total over 60 s gives the backfill's writer duty cycle for that minute. The counter is renamed `sessions completed`, and while a session is in progress the line adds `current at position P of E active events`. Positions are dense, `0..active_event_count-1`.

Pacing (`delayMs`) is unchanged. The line carries no session ids or content.

Example from the fixture:

```text
session: transcript facts backfill progress: 7 rows filled, 0 rows skipped, 0/1 sessions completed (current at position 16 of 40 active events), 734 payload bytes, 0 lock-contention pauses; since last report: 1 batches, 10.9 ms maximum batch, 1407.4 ms maximum and 1507 ms total admitted execution
```

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest run src/config/sessions/session-transcript-active-facts-backfill.test.ts`: 5/5 pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: clean. oxlint and oxfmt: clean.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean.

Closes #198515

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI agent roster stays in configured order when users select **Last updated**, even after another agent's conversation becomes more recent.

## User Impact

User impact: unpinned agents follow their latest conversation activity and update as activity arrives, including after a cached sidebar reload. Pins, stable ties, other sort modes, and selecting an agent's main conversation keep their existing behavior. Recency uses the existing shared 300-session window, excluding archived sessions; it is not an all-history ranking.

**Draft:** focused behavior is verified, but UI typecheck and performance-budget proof remain incomplete. This is not a live deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing canonical conversation-activity clock instead of metadata update times, apply ordering only in the unpinned roster's Last updated view, subscribe directly to activity updates, and retain display-only recency in cached sidebar snapshots. Existing snapshots without recency remain readable.
