prs.title: refactor(browser): keep one document-interception session per tab
prs.body:
Related: #198317

## What Problem This Solves

Prepares the fix for #198317. Every guarded browser navigation or action creates its own CDP session for document interception and tears it down afterwards, so nothing owns a tab's interception between actions and a policy for that gap has nowhere to live. This moves ownership to the tab without changing what is allowed or blocked, so the fix (#198452) is a small policy change on top of it.

## User Impact

User impact: none intended. Interception still runs only while a guarded navigation or action is in progress, with the same policy decisions, redirect-hop checks, source-page preservation and error precedence.

Three differences worth a reviewer's attention:

- After its first guarded navigation or action, a tab keeps one CDP session and its iframe auto-attach instead of creating them per action. A new out-of-process iframe in that tab is resumed by this session between actions too.
- A frame that attaches after an invocation lost its authority is resumed instead of left paused. Its documents are still refused and the invocation still fails with the authority error.
- An action can return slightly before a nested out-of-process iframe commits, because cleanup has fewer protocol round trips. The redirect authority live test waits for that commit instead of reading it immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

- One tab fence per Playwright `Page` owns the session, its frame targets and the document tracking. `installNavigationAuthorityFence` keeps its signature and registers a claim: the invocation's policy, document handler and failure state.
- A paused document goes through the claims that existed when it arrived, in turn, and continues only if each one resumes it. With one claim this is the same decision as on `main`.
- Releasing the last claim sends `Fetch.disable` and `Network.disable`, and cleanup returns when they are answered, as on `main`. The next claim sends `Fetch.enable` and `Network.enable` only after that answer, and a claim whose enable fails fails its invocation. The extension relay refuses `Fetch.enable` while its `Fetch.disable` is unanswered, so sending the two in call order is not enough there.
- Cleanup that cannot confirm cancellation keeps its closed claim, which refuses every document until the tab closes, and clears the documents it was waiting on so later invocations on that tab do not wait for them.
- The fence file is edited in place (+187/−93) so the diff shows what moved from the invocation to the tab.

One accepted edge: a browser connection that stays open but never answers `Fetch.disable` fails that cleanup at the navigation timeout, and the next invocation on that tab waits until the tab or the connection closes. There is no code for it.

## Evidence

- **Back-to-back invocations:** a unit test delays the `Fetch.disable` answer and refuses `Fetch.enable` until it arrives, as the extension relay does. Without the wait, cleanup returns before the answer, the next invocation's enable is refused and dropped, and it runs with interception off. With it, cleanup returns after the answer and the next invocation ends with interception on. A second test covers a refused enable failing the invocation.
- **Unit tests:** 119 of 119 pass in the six browser test files that cover the fence and its callers. Targeted typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Live tests (real Chromium):** 27 pass: redirect authority (10), page-cancelled interception (3), download policy (7), current-document download (5) and native CORS (2).
  - Three native-CORS cases need `127.0.0.2`, which macOS does not route; they time out there on `main` as well.
  - The two nested-iframe redirect cases fail in this environment and fail the same way on `main` (10 of 10 runs). A trace shows the test's click inside the nested frame starts no navigation, so the fence has no redirect to see.
- **Independent review:** a reviewer who did not write the change looked for an interleaving of overlapping and back-to-back invocations, frame targets attaching or detaching, a late or missing answer, and tab or session loss in which an invocation starts with interception off. It found none.
- **Test changes:** the fence lifecycle tests assert a released claim instead of a detached session; one case that tested listener removal before detach is replaced by one that a document arriving after release loads; one case covers a later invocation not waiting on documents a timed-out cleanup left behind.

Not checked: a real extension relay (the relay's refusal is reproduced in a unit test, not in a browser with the extension), the full Gateway with a real agent and model, Linux and Windows, and remote-CDP profiles.

Refs #195982, follow-up to #198424

## What Problem This Solves

Each is over the 64 B build-variance allowance in `control-ui-performance`.

## User Impact

- The phase view (starting label, permission-hint delay, listening and finishing rows) moves to `composer-dictation-status.tsx`. It loads lazily inside the same `ChatLazyBoundary` other optional composer parts use. The boot bundle keeps only a `Show` on `dictation.active`.

- Phase labels wrap instead of being cut off with an ellipsis. This drops the separate override rule for the permission hint. "Listening…" and "Finishing dictation…" are short enough that this changes nothing in practice.

prs.title: fix(templates): keep pre-upload ClawHub failures retryable in draft publication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #198548. `templates.drafts.publish` can fail **before the artifact is uploaded** — for example when the ClawHub sign-in has expired (`whoami` returns 401) or the registry is unreachable. Those failures are raised as `ClawHubRequestError` (not `TemplateProjectError`), which `draftError` treated as unknown. The publish response therefore carried no `templatePublication` metadata, and the Control UI concluded the submission was `unconfirmed` — showing "Submission unconfirmed", blaming the draft's contents, and disabling both Publish and Retry with no recovery short of reloading the page.

The fix makes pre-upload ClawHub failures a **known, retryable, not-published** outcome: the response now reports `templatePublication.effect: "none"` with a named sign-in or network message, so the UI shows "Not published" and keeps Publish/Retry available.

## Solution

- `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.ts` — `draftError` now treats `ClawHubRequestError` as a known error. Its code becomes `clawhub_request_failed`, it stays retryable (`effect: "none"`), and the message names the actual cause: a 401 maps to "Your ClawHub sign-in has expired. Sign in again and retry publishing."; other statuses map to "ClawHub could not be reached. Check your network connection and retry publishing.".
- `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts` — the publication fixture gains an `identity.unauthorized` flag that makes `whoami` answer 401; a new regression test publishes after sign-in expiry and asserts the failure is retryable with `effect: "none"`, zero uploads, and zero registry posts.

## Evidence

- **Regression test (RED → GREEN):** with the old `draftError`, the new test fails (it saw `code: "templates_disabled"` and no publication metadata). With the fix, the full `templates-drafts.test.ts` suite passes — 31/31 tests.
- **Behavioral contract:** a pre-upload 401 now yields `{ code: "INVALID_REQUEST", retryable: true, details: { templatePublication: { effect: "none", code: "clawhub_request_failed" } }, message: "Your ClawHub sign-in has expired. Sign in again and retry publishing." }`, and the test asserts `posts === 0` and zero uploads — nothing is ever submitted to the registry in this path.
- The Control UI already maps `effect: "none"` to the "Not published" state with Publish/Retry enabled (`creator-flow.ts`), so no UI change is needed; this is a protocol/response-contract fix on the Gateway side.
- No credentials, tokens, or private data appear in this PR.

prs.title: perf(models): skip JSONC scans for generated catalogs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated model catalogs currently pass through two JSONC regex scans before parsing, although their writer emits strict JSON. This creates avoidable transient allocation in catalog workers.

## User Impact

Try strict JSON first only for already-identified generated catalogs. Authored root catalogs keep their existing parser, and imported generated JSONC retains the same fallback and validation. This adds no user setting, RPC wait, or loading UI.

## Evidence

Draft experiment; no worker-level improvement is claimed yet.

- Dependency-free parser checks pass for strict JSON, quoted comment/comma text, JSONC fallback, and malformed input.
- 49 focused parser/registry/invalid-cost tests passed, along with the matching agent test TypeScript leaf. Full independent local review is clean after removing a stale import. One fixture escape reported by lint has been corrected; final lint and built-worker measurement remain pending.
- The experiment is now based on `730ce41827c40c9075685e5601e0371687ff05fa`, including the landed provider-selection optimization from #198591. This measures incremental benefit; dependency manifests and the parser/registry base files did not change during that rebase.
- A parser-only exploratory probe favored strict parsing by roughly sixfold. Applying that shortcut globally regressed a large trailing-comma catalog by 29%, so authored root catalogs deliberately retain their original path.

Acceptance rule, recorded before worker comparisons: at least 5% lower median warm allocated bytes, identical catalog/runtime hashes, and no 20% median/p95 latency or retained-heap regression. Use at least five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs of the committed catalog-worker retention workload, with allocation and timing measured separately. Drop the experiment if it does not meet the rule.

prs.title: perf(build): halve warm rebuilds with hook filters, parallel asset hooks, cache-hit fixes and an optional worker bundle
prs.body:
## Problem

A warm rebuild after a one-line source edit (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build`) takes about 4 minutes on a loaded 32-core Mac, mostly in work that repeats unchanged results:

- Twelve build plugins register unfiltered `transform`/`load` hooks that match one or a few exact files. Rolldown therefore sends every module of ~90 configs through JavaScript, and several hooks `realpath` each id.
- `plugins:assets:build` runs its plugin Control UI hooks one at a time (each a short esbuild process).
- `external-plugins:local-dist` hits its per-plugin caches but still re-hashes the same SDK and core sources once per plugin: 66,258 file reads per pass for 12,965 unique files, done twice.
- A `ui:build` cache hit still runs the report-only Control UI performance check (~20 s of gzip/brotli measurement) on bytes it already measured.
- Runtime-only builds always build the sealed cloud-worker deploy bundle, about half of tsdown's CPU, and `check-cli-bootstrap-imports` then walks it.

## Solution

- **Hook filters.** Each exact-match hook declares its match as a native Rolldown filter (`scripts/lib/rolldown-id-filter.mts`); handler bodies are unchanged. The Bun standalone source adapter evaluates the same two filter shapes (id RegExp, code substring) and still rejects any other shape.
- **Plugin asset hooks.** Build-phase hooks run four at a time; each writes only its own package's assets. Every running hook is joined before the step reports. Copy-phase hooks stay serial.
- **External plugin signatures.** `hashInputFiles` accepts an optional per-run file-digest map. The step shares it across plugins and drops a plugin's own entries after its build, so regenerated package files are re-read.
- **`ui:build` hit.** The report-only performance check runs only after a real build. The precompressed-assets check still runs on every hit, and restores still use APFS clones (`COPYFILE_FICLONE`).
- **Worker deploy bundle.** `OPENCLAW_BUILD_WORKER_DEPLOY_BUNDLE=0` skips the sealed deploy entries, only together with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1`. Declaration, package and release builds always build them, and the local process helpers in `dist/worker/` are always built. tsdown's output clean removes any earlier bundle. Preparing a worker bundle from such a dist fails with the existing "OpenClaw worker deploy artifact is missing" error. The bootstrap check skips the worker artifact only when the flag is set and the entry is absent.

Not changed: `runtime-postbuild` and `check-cli-bootstrap-imports` read tsdown's fresh output, so a content-keyed cache would miss on every source edit; the bootstrap check is ~1 s once the worker walk is skipped.

## Impact

Measured on Studio (M3 Ultra, shared, load 40-80), `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build`, warm caches, base `77a0a8426513` vs this branch with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_WORKER_DEPLOY_BUNDLE=0`:

| Warm rebuild | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| one `src/` edit (run 1) | 4m 04s | 1m 36s |
| one `src/` edit (run 2) | 4m 15s | 2m 09s |
| one `extensions/` edit | 3m 35s | 2m 01s |
| no change | 3m 45s | 2m 28s |

Per step for the `src/` edit: tsdown 91 s -> 32-42 s, `ui:build` 47-50 s -> 23-27 s, `plugins:assets:build` 16-25 s -> 4-5 s, `external-plugins:local-dist` 22-40 s -> 11-15 s, `check-cli-bootstrap-imports` 10-16 s -> ~1 s.

Full cache-off `pnpm build` (declarations, worker bundle built): 6m 16.8s -> 4m 45.2s.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current main `d1dc63bac00c962065e88826dc915f1f5fc3e635` (clean, no conflicts); the measurements below were taken on base `77a0a8426513`, and the tests and `tsgo` were rerun on the rebased head.

- **Byte-identical full tier:** cache-off full `pnpm build` on base and branch, every dist file hashed: 28,193 files each; the only 10 differing files are build identity (`.buildstamp`, `.runtime-postbuildstamp`, `build-cache-inputs.json`, `build-info.json`, `cli-startup-metadata.json` help text with the commit id, Control UI `index.html`/`sw.js*`, and one Control UI source map that embeds the checkout path).
- **Hook filters alone:** no-declaration tsdown step on base vs filters, 3 alternating pairs: 23,424 files, 0 differing in every pair; CPU 189 s -> 179 s.
- **Worker skip:** after the skipped build, `dist/worker/` holds only `github-exec-launcher.mjs`, `service-child-group-anchor.mjs`, `service-child-relay.mjs`, `workspace-rsync-receiver.mjs` and the Windows helper; `prepareWorkerBundle` on that checkout rejects with "OpenClaw worker deploy artifact is missing; build the running package at …"; an isolated Gateway (private state, loopback, token auth) on that dist reports healthy in 17 s.

## What problem this solves

Template Add opens a pending chat but waits for all declared dependencies before the agent can speak. A slow dependency stalls the opening, and the composer handoff can lose queued input or require a reload to show the new agent.

## What changes

Finalize the prepared agent and ordinary session before dependency setup, attach chat, and start its opening while dependency work settles. The existing session continuation owns both branches and serializes checkpoints. A dependency-results turn follows the opening; Retry preserves the same agent, files and settled work. Existing UI owners retain drafts, attachments and queued input.

Source resolution reuses verified acquisition. Optional timing diagnostics use debug severity. Referenced ClawHub plugins remain recommendations, not automatically installed or enabled. Explicit denies, consent and installation policy are unchanged.

Stacked above https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198603, which independently contains the shared input leaf, bootstrap citation and truthful stale-Retry repair.

prs.title: perf(models): reduce catalog normalization allocations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing large model catalogs repeatedly resolves the same provider hooks for every model, creating avoidable worker allocation and CPU pressure.

## User Impact

The measured two-provider catalog workload allocates 39% less memory per refresh, runs warm requests 16% faster, and retains 3.51 MiB less worker heap. Cold-request median is effectively unchanged. No new setting, disabled feature, worker-pool consolidation, or persistent cache.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse successful provider selections within one synchronous catalog pass, then discard them. Existing handle logic retries model-specific misses. Every model still runs its hooks; configured-provider isolation, in-place model updates, fallback order, and same-origin transport restrictions remain intact.

## Evidence

### Validation

- 95 focused tests passed: provider runtime, the four new catalog-normalization cases, transport-origin restrictions, agent model discovery/membership/synthetic auth, and prompt-prefix stability.
- Type-aware lint passed for all six changed files, including generated SDK declarations. Formatting and line-cap checks passed.
- Both frozen-base and candidate `sourcePerformance` builds passed, including built plugin/control-plane checks. This profile does not claim full package/release qualification.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete range through `f0e58c37cdb7` with no actionable findings; independent source review also found no remaining issue.
- Runtime builds and the 95-test suite used `e68e8ab3c854`; later commits only correct the test fixture. Final head `cc462fa2cab4` passes all four normalization tests, type-aware fixture lint, and the exact `core.test.plugins-platform` TypeScript leaf that caught a missing `workspaceDir` field in CI. Production inputs are identical, so the benchmark and broader behavioral proof remain valid.
- Ordinary `models.list` reads still serve published rows while catalog discovery refreshes in the background. This PR adds no RPC wait or UI loading state. Existing first-snapshot picker loading presentation is a separate follow-up.

### Benchmark

Frozen base: `9cb3c14855e5a5216148a1c125f9240c5da1f6de`. The acceptance rule was recorded here before comparisons: at least 15% lower median warm allocated bytes, identical catalog/runtime hashes, and no 20% median/p95 latency or retained-heap regression. All measured metrics meet it.

40 independent built-worker runs: five AB allocation pairs, five AB retained-heap pairs, and ten timing pairs (five AB plus five BA). Each run uses two workspaces, two providers, 5,000 overlay rows, 1,000 discovered rows per provider, and four task rounds. There are seven warm requests after the first cold request. Sampling and timing runs are separate. All catalog and runtime hashes match.

| Metric | Base median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 | Median change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Warm allocation / 7 requests (MiB) | 705.51 / 707.25 | 428.29 / 434.71 | -39.3% |
| Warm request (ms) | 79.49 / 163.08 | 66.40 / 119.45 | -16.5% |
| Cold request (ms) | 977.94 / 1712.95 | 969.30 / 1557.50 | -0.9% |
| Worker CPU / 7 requests (ms) | 556.02 / 803.10 | 413.70 / 600.16 | -25.6% |
| GC / 7 requests (ms) | 26.52 / 51.16 | 26.31 / 35.96 | -0.8% |
| Peak worker heap (MiB) | 120.18 / 161.15 | 110.12 / 115.49 | -8.4% |
| Post-GC worker heap (MiB) | 74.42 / 74.43 | 70.91 / 70.91 | -4.7% |
| Harness process RSS (MiB) | 657.57 / 709.48 | 630.02 / 708.23 | -4.2% |

Allocation corresponds to 100.79 → 61.18 MiB per warm request. The first allocation profiles attribute 154.61 → 0.06 MiB to provider-selection preparation and 57.45 → 0.06 MiB to runtime lookup preparation.

Ranges: warm requests 48.88–220.94 → 39.07–175.29 ms; cold requests 654.65–1712.95 → 728.44–1557.50 ms; allocation 696.18–707.25 → 416.92–434.71 MiB; retained worker heap 74.34–74.43 → 70.84–70.91 MiB. Host load ranged 7.8–15.8. The initial five AB timing pairs showed a 7.2% slower cold median; five BA pairs were declared before running to counterbalance order, and every original sample remains in the combined results.

Reproduction, for each base/candidate build:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/catalog-worker-retention-measure.ts   --output <new-fixture-directory> --built-worker <build-root>   --workspaces 2 --providers 2 --models 5000 --discovery-models 1000   --task-rounds 4 --runtime-plugin --measure-tasks
```

Add `--sample-allocation` for the allocation pass. Omit `--measure-tasks` for post-GC retained-heap collection after each round.

This exercises the real catalog worker, not a full Gateway/client workload. Process RSS includes the TypeScript harness; the isolated retained-worker-heap result is the useful residency comparison. No claim of 39% lower Gateway RSS.

prs.title: fix(templates): read the package BOOTSTRAP.md with its own bound in build
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A package-root `BOOTSTRAP.md` between 1 MiB and 2 MiB passes `openclaw templates validate` and then makes
`openclaw templates build` (and `dev`) fail with a bare `too-large` error that names neither the file nor the limit.

Both sides read the same file with different bounds, so the 1–2 MiB band is accepted by one and rejected by the other.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace bootstrap owner already declares the bound for this file and says it must be shared — "Keep every read path
on the same bound" (`src/agents/workspace-bootstrap-read.ts:4-6`, `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES = 2 MiB`).
`validate` (`src/templates/reader.ts:336-341`) and `add` (`src/templates/bootstrap.ts:52`) both read with it. `build` did
not: `readSelectedProjectFile` applied `MAX_MANAGED_FILE_BYTES` (1 MiB, the generic selected-file cap) to every file it
re-read, `BOOTSTRAP.md` included — so a file validate had just accepted failed on the way into the artifact.

`readSelectedProjectFile` now takes an optional bound, and the `BOOTSTRAP.md` call passes the bootstrap owner's constant.
Every other selected file keeps the generic 1 MiB cap.

## User Impact

`templates build` and `templates dev` accept a package-root `BOOTSTRAP.md` that `templates validate` accepts, so the
1–2 MiB band no longer turns a validation-approved package into a build failure. Files above 2 MiB still fail, and now fail
in `validate` first where the diagnostic names the file and the byte limit.

## Evidence

New case in `src/templates/project.test.ts`: a project whose `BOOTSTRAP.md` is 1.5 MiB must pass `validateTemplateProject`
and then build.

- base (`main` @ `0b7cd35571e`): **fails** with `Serialized Error: { code: 'too-large', category: 'policy' }` — the same bare
  error the report describes.
- with this change: the new case passes, and the whole file reports **28 passed | 1 skipped**.
- `oxlint` on both touched files: no findings. Test lines are inside the 400-line allowance, so no allocation entry is
  needed.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from the issue report; the author reviewed the change and its evidence.

prs.title: fix(browser): pages reach SSRF-blocked addresses by navigating after an action's 250 ms guard
prs.body:
Closes #198317

Stacked on #198638, which moves document interception from each invocation to the tab without changing behaviour. This PR's own change is the second commit, [`a4b66c09617`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198452/commits/a4b66c09617c9d52574784c6f6d852e3424b8df4): about 170 added source lines. The first commit is #198638's, and the third applies #198638's claim and release ordering to this branch; both belong to that PR's review.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a page reaches an address the browser SSRF policy blocks by navigating more than 250 ms after a browser action, because document interception ends when each action's guard window does.

## User Impact

User impact: in a tab OpenClaw has navigated or acted on, a document the page requests between actions is checked against the configured `browser.ssrfPolicy` and stopped before any request leaves the browser when the policy denies it.

What someone using that browser notices:

- Typing a blocked address into such a tab (or reloading or going back to one) shows Chrome's blocked page instead of loading it. To open it anyway, use a new tab or add the host to `browser.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames`.

  ![Chrome's "localhost is blocked" page after typing a blocked address into a tab the agent used](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7b36f51d4cdc951616a86b2f7cb7959d983dcb45/images/2026/11/6fd29ee9-9a0f-43c0-9333-9abdcba90bf5.png)

- A page keeps loading documents from the origin it is already on, so a localhost dev page opened under the automatic loopback exception can reload itself and follow its own links between tool calls. A different loopback port is a different origin and is stopped.
- A blocked navigation that a page script requested is cancelled silently and the tab keeps its page.
- Each document request in such a tab makes one round trip through the Gateway before it loads, between actions as well as during them.

Not covered, and listed in the docs: a popup's first request, Service Worker traffic, `fetch`/XHR and other subresources, tabs OpenClaw has not navigated or acted on, the time the Gateway's connection to the browser is down (a tab is covered again from its next guarded action), and speculation-rules prefetch on browsers OpenClaw did not launch.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Interception stays on for the tab's lifetime instead of only while an invocation claims it. With no claim, the tab's standing policy decides each document: the configured policy without invocation-scoped grants such as the loopback exception, which end with the invocation. Interception stays document-only, so CORS preflights and subresources stay on Chromium's native path.
- The standing policy is one small module, `pw-session-navigation-standing.ts`; the fence itself changes by about 45 lines.
- The fence never sends `Fetch.disable`, so the extension relay's refusal of `Fetch.enable` during a release, which #198638 handles, has no release to meet here. A claim only starts document tracking (`Network.enable`), after the last release is answered, and a claim whose tracking fails to start fails its invocation.
- Same-origin documents are allowed because a page can already `fetch()` its own origin, so they reach nothing new.
- Whether a denial shows the blocked page or is cancelled silently depends on whether the navigation looks browser-initiated (no page request event, no referrer, top-level). A page can imitate that, so the check only picks how the denial looks; the request is denied either way.

One tradeoff for reviewers: the same-origin allowance is checked ahead of `blockedHostnames`. A tab already on a host that a config reload later blocks keeps loading that origin. `main` enforces nothing between actions, so this is not a widening against `main`.

## Evidence

- **Reproduction:** a real-Chromium test presses a key, and the page navigates to a denied address 500 ms later while a fixture server at that address counts requests. On `main` the server receives the document and it becomes the tab's page. With this change it receives nothing and the tab keeps its page.
- **Live tests (real Chromium):** 32 pass: the between-actions suite (5), redirect authority (10), page-cancelled interception (3), download policy (7), current-document download (5) and native CORS (2).
  - Three native-CORS cases need `127.0.0.2`, which macOS does not route; they time out there on `main` as well.
  - The two nested-iframe redirect cases fail in this environment and fail the same way on `main` (10 of 10 runs). A trace shows the test's click inside the nested frame starts no navigation, so the fence has no redirect to see.
- **Unit tests:** 142 of 142 pass in the seven browser test files that cover the fence, its callers and the navigation guard, including a release answered late and a claim whose tracking fails to start. Targeted typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Checked on a prior revision of this change with the same standing-policy logic, not rerun on this head:**
  - In a headed Chrome, a blocked address typed into the real address bar of a tab that had been through a guarded action showed the blocked page above with no request reaching the server; the next action on that tab worked, and a typed allowed address and Cmd+R loaded normally.
  - Independent adversarial runs: 34 page-initiated navigation vectors (top-level, frames, out-of-process and nested iframes, redirects, rapid and overlapping navigations) reached a denied server on an unfenced tab and none did on a fenced one. A loopback port hop, a same-origin redirect to a denied port, and a page imitating a typed navigation were each stopped before any request.
  - Page loads, cross-site iframes, reload and back, CORS preflights, downloads, form POSTs, allowed redirects, and `blob:`/`data:`/`srcdoc` frames behaved between actions as on an unfenced tab.

Not checked: the full Gateway with a real agent and model (the proof drives the browser action functions directly), Linux and Windows, and extension-relay or remote-CDP profiles.

prs.title: fix(ci): recover npm qualification with its dependent receipt
prs.body:
## Problem
An npm qualification job that fails also fails its dependent `Seal artifact producer receipt` job. The continuation planner counts these as two independent failures and refuses recovery, even though GitHub's single-job rerun already includes the dependent seal.

Observed during approved 2026.11.5-beta.3 qualification: a dependency-check checkout failed with `bad pack header`; package preparation and the other npm checks passed, while sealing failed solely because the npm stage failed.

## Changes
- Select the one failed npm qualification job when the only other failure is its dependent producer receipt.
- Retain the existing single-job rerun, live admission, attempt adoption, original prepared-artifact checks, and strict final verification.
- Continue refusing multiple independent failures; do not waive either failure or submit a second receipt retry.
- Document the supported recovery shape.

## Evidence
- Regression fails on the base at the real `continueFailed` boundary.
- Canonical tooling suite: 142/142 passed, including one exact job retry, no failed-jobs retry, and final verification.
- Scoped type-aware lint, tooling typecheck, formatting, diff checks, and full docs-content checks passed.
- The three patched files are identical to the tested private repair after transplant onto main; no relevant base-file changes.
- Self-review and simplification completed; no independent review was requested, per the release owner's explicit instruction.
- Production change: 11 lines. No new state or transport.

## Remaining proof
The live release has not been retried with this change. The non-release post-merge proof broker and deliberate tooling selection remain required before live use. Existing release failures remain blockers.

`check:changed` is red on `main` since #194519 (72f90dde). Knip's script unused-export scan reports `prepareTranscriptFactsBackfillStress` in `scripts/perf/transcript-facts-backfill-stress-preload.mjs`. Perf lanes branching from `main` inherit the failure.

## Why the export stays

No in-repo module imports this function by design. The module header explains the contract: a task-local `--gateway-preload` module imports it and passes the campaign root plus the operator's original TMPDIR. These paths can't reach the stress Gateway any other way:

- `createGatewayBenchEnv` builds the Gateway env from an allowlist, so extra env vars are dropped.
- `team-shape-stress` creates its output directory fresh (`mkdirSync` without `recursive`), so a pre-written options file is impossible.

## Change

Tag the export `@public` with that reason, following the existing precedent for out-of-repo consumers in `scripts/lib/docs-markdown.mjs`. No runtime change.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts` with `main`'s file: the script unused-export scan reports `scripts/perf/transcript-facts-backfill-stress-preload.mjs: prepareTranscriptFactsBackfillStress`.
- Same command with this change: `Knip script unused-export scan passed with 0 entries.`

prs.title: fix(backup): prevent concurrent cleanup from interrupting verification
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent backup cleanup can acquire a live backup's scratch token during its retirement handoff, interrupting otherwise valid archive verification or restore.

## User Impact

Draft: this head contains the deterministic regression only. A backup-only exclusive-admission repair is prepared locally and remains uncommitted pending baseline proof and a fresh-review decision. No schema version, DDL, migration, persisted-format, config, public API, retention, or durability-policy change is planned.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator currently rolls back its IMMEDIATE transaction before acquiring EXCLUSIVE retirement custody. The regression schedules a real second SQLite connection in that released-lock interval. The intended repair gives backup scratch exclusive creator custody from initial admission; nested snapshot owners retain their existing reader-sharing behavior.

Related evidence: [Node backup restore failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43533287147/job/132256802841), using Node 24.22.1 and two test-file workers. That historical error identifies scratch retirement, but does not identify the competing process. The new regression exercises that admissible ownership counterexample separately; its runtime result is pending.

## Evidence

- Frozen base: `b6390c7d0adb64830aaa807356018023d3c49e6e`.
- Regression head: `95745c77d860d4614ad328b27a2d505c367ae714`; production delta 0, tests +46.
- Independent read-only regression review: GO; cleanup finding addressed by covering payload creation with the existing `finally`.
- `git diff --check`, formatting, and native commit checks passed.
- Expected-red runtime proof: pending [baseline full-validation CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43559326432). Preflight passed and its logs verify target checkout `95745c77d860d4614ad328b27a2d505c367ae714`; the scratch test job is still queued. The original schema-1/schema-17 create-to-restore cases remain unchanged.
- [Earlier dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43559079629) failed before tests because `validation_tier=main` rejects a separately targeted SHA. It supplies no test evidence; the supported full-validation dispatch above corrects that input.
- Prepared local production diff: +11/-5 across `backup-scratch.ts` and `sqlite-staging-token.ts`; backup-only `exclusiveCreate`, existing generic defaults unchanged. Three-file formatting passed. This production diff is not in this PR head and has no runtime proof yet.
- Boat execution refused before allocation because the configured private visibility requires missing `BOX_ORG`; the temporary source checkout was removed. Local test dependencies are unqualified, so the repository's draft/CI proof route applies.
- Local autoreview did not launch: its input policy rejected the public `sqlite-staging-token.ts` context as a sensitive filename. This is unavailable review, not a clean automated verdict. The fresh production-review leaf paused without inspecting the final diff because replacing the refused capture route would bypass that restriction. Earlier regression-only review does not cover the production changes; a human review or an explicit scoped fresh-review waiver is pending.

prs.title: feat(state): upgrade state by copy and swap at Gateway startup
prs.body:
## Problem

Upgrades migrate state in place. Every step of the v13..v40 chain, the STRICT rebuild, the scoped pre-migration snapshots and the `.bak` custody exists to make writing the live file safe, and that machinery is itself the top source of state failures in the field. Of 2,720 classified real upgrade failures, 351 are in the state-database layer (7 with data loss), led by migration gates and snapshot/backup custody:

| Cause (state-db layer) | Reports |
| --- | ---: |
| legacy exec-approvals migration gate deadlock | 18 |
| candidate state snapshot failed | 15 |
| startup migration gate blocks on legacy leftovers | 12 |
| database schema preflight refused update | 12 |
| retained session migration source changed | 12 |
| SQLite backup probe timed out during update | 5 |

A Gateway started on real prior-release state refuses today, for example on 2026.7.1:

```
OpenClaw state database schema migration required (audit-events-v2) at …/state/openclaw.sqlite; run openclaw doctor --fix to migrate it.
Gateway failed to start: … gateway.maintenance_required
```

## What changed

Gateway startup now owns the state upgrade, by copy and swap. It runs in `prepareGatewayRunBootstrap`, before the config guard or any database reader, under file-only state ownership (`acquireGatewayLock({ databaseAccess: "none" })`).

It runs only when the start would be admitted: the same `getGatewayStartGuardErrors` check is asked with the raw config file (`gateway.mode`, `--allow-unconfigured`). A start that the guard refuses leaves every state file unchanged, so the previous package can still read it (the read-only admission contract from #141451).

When the shared state DB or any agent DB is older than this build:

1. **Copy.** The state directory is copied into a private shadow (`<state>/.upgrade-<version>/`). SQLite files use `VACUUM INTO` from a read-only connection, so committed WAL frames are included and the live file is never opened for writing. A database that a crash left with a hot rollback journal is copied with its journal and rolled back privately. Other files are copy-on-write clones. A symlink is copied as the file or directory it points to, so nothing written to the shadow can reach a live target. Configured workspaces, `tmp/`, `locks/`, earlier generations and old backups are skipped. BLOB values in TEXT columns are decoded on the copy (#110186).
2. **Chain.** This build's Doctor (`doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`) runs against the shadow only. Absolute paths into the live tree are pointed at the shadow for the run and back afterwards.
3. **Validate.** Every upgraded database must reach this build's schema version and pass `integrity_check` and `foreign_key_check`. Per-table row conservation compares source and result counts; tables the chain is known to merge or retire are listed in `CHAIN_TRANSFORMED_TABLES`. A mismatch logs, records and pins the old generation; it does not fail the upgrade.
4. **Fallback.** If the chain fails (any step, or validation), the shadow databases are discarded and rebuilt by the generic engine: the current schema, name-matched columns cast to the declared type, defaults for new columns, the shipped row-moving steps on a private scratch copy (state: v12/v13 fold-ins, which carry `voicewake_triggers` and `installed_plugin_index`; agents: the pre-v14 session migration into `session_nodes`/`session_windows`), a small map for the one released rename (v36 `claw_*` → `template_*`, including renamed columns, enum values and record versions), newest row kept on key collisions, and rows that do not fit (constraints, missing parents, removed tables) set aside into `diagnostic_events` (`upgrade.set-aside`). Leases are dropped. Doctor's migrated config is kept so this build can read it. When only an agent database is outdated, a copy of the current shared database joins the swap, so the report, set-aside rows and pin are kept. The old generation is pinned and a warning names the failed step. The Gateway still starts.
5. **Swap.** This process's handles on the shared database (opened while the environment was selected) are released. The diff between the shadow and the live tree becomes a plan that is written and fsynced before any live file changes. Applying it hard-links each replaced or retired live file to `<name>.pre-<version>`, removes stale WAL/SHM/journal/seal companions, renames each new file into place and fsyncs the directories. Every step is idempotent, so the next start finishes an interrupted plan.
6. **Retention.** One prior generation is kept. Older `.pre-*` copies and the backups the in-place migration left (`*.pre-startup-migration-*`, `*.scoped.bak`, `*.sqlite*.bak`, `openclaw-media-persistence-recovery-*`) are pruned, except pinned generations.

A report row (`upgrade.report`) records the mode, failed step, source versions, conservation result and set-aside count. The chain's output is kept as `logs/state-upgrade-<version>.log`.

Rollback to the previous release is a rename: `<name>.pre-<version>` back to `<name>` (and `<name>-wal.pre-<version>` back to `<name>-wal`).

## Proof

All runs use this build's real Gateway (`node openclaw.mjs gateway run`) on copies of real prior-release state written by each release's own writers and CLI (populated corpus, now committed as `test/fixtures/state-corpus-populated/`), with an isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, no inherited `OPENCLAW_*`, and a free port.

Before (base `b6c6aef`, 2026.7.1 corpus): `Gateway failed to start: OpenClaw state database schema migration required (audit-events-v2) … gateway.maintenance_required`.

After, on head `62c8ded` (built with `ocx build`) unless noted. "Values" = every value the release wrote and REPORT.md located, found in the upgraded tree (`.pre-*` excluded). "Old bytes" = SHA-256 of every original DB and WAL equals its `.pre-2026.11.3` copy.

| Run | Mode | Start | Values | Old bytes | Report |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026.7.1 | chain | listening, ready | 42/42 | identical | no mismatches, 0 set aside |
| 2026.7.1-blob | chain | listening, ready | 41/41 | identical | no mismatches |
| 2026.7.35 | chain | listening, ready | 41/41 | identical | no mismatches |
| 2026.8.35 | chain | listening (`8c2453d`), ready (e2e test) | 48/48 | identical | no mismatches |
| 2026.9.37 | chain | listening, ready | 47/47 | identical | no mismatches |
| 2026.10.10 | chain | listening (`8c2453d`), ready (e2e test) | 47/47 | identical | no mismatches |
| 2026.10.10 | forced fallback | listening, ready | 46/46 | identical | `failedStep: injected-step`, 7 set aside, pinned |
| 2026.8.35 | forced fallback | ready (e2e test) | all | identical | `failedStep: injected-step`, pinned |
| 2026.7.1 | forced fallback | listening; sessions refused (legacy JSON, see edge cases) | 41/41 | identical | `failedStep: injected-step`, 2 set aside, pinned |

Fault proof (2026.7.1 corpus; `kill -9` via a crash-point seam on `8c2453d`. That seam was an `OPENCLAW_TEST_*` environment name and has since been removed with the other upgrade seams; the plan, apply and resume code it exercised is unchanged):

| Fault | After the fault | Next start |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kill -9` after copy | live files identical, no plan | upgrades, ready, 42/42 |
| `kill -9` after build | live files identical, no plan | upgrades, 42/42 |
| `kill -9` after plan written | live files identical, plan present | finishes the plan, 42/42 |
| `kill -9` after 1st and 6th applied step | old bytes identical (live or `.pre`) | finishes the plan, 42/42 |
| `kill -9` after all steps, before cleanup | old bytes identical under `.pre` | resumes, listening, 42/42 |
| `kill -9` of the Gateway while the shadow Doctor runs | live files identical | discards the attempt, upgrades, 42/42 |
| 40 MiB APFS volume with ~2 MiB free (on `62c8ded`) | `State upgrade to 2026.11.3 stopped: disk I/O error. Nothing in … was changed. Free disk space … and start the Gateway again.`; live files identical; no work directory left | after freeing space: upgrades, 42/42 |

Commands (scripts kept with the evidence): `probe/e2e.sh <release> <run>`, `probe/kill9.sh 2026.7.1 <step>` (needs the removed seam), `probe/diskfull.sh`, `probe/verify.py`, and `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/state-upgrade.e2e.test.ts` (5/5) plus `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/state/sqlite-copy-swap.test.ts` (23/23).

Review-fix proof, on head `901f316` (later heads change only guards, comments, test seams and the content-version stamp owner) (built with `ocx build`; script `probe/round2.sh`, 2026.9.37 corpus unless noted):

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Outdated state, `gateway.mode: remote`, no `--allow-unconfigured` | Start refused (exit 78, the previous `run openclaw doctor --fix` message). Every `*.sqlite` and `openclaw.json` byte-identical; no upgrade ran. |
| `state/openclaw.sqlite` is a symlink to another directory, chain | Listening, ready. The external target keeps its SHA-256 (`4ea36156…`); the live name is now the upgraded file, and `openclaw.sqlite.pre-2026.11.3` is the old symlink. |
| Same, forced fallback | Listening, ready, 7 set aside, pinned; external target unchanged. |
| Shared DB current, one agent DB at v27 (from 2026.10.10), forced fallback | Listening, ready. The shared DB gained `upgrade.report` +1, `upgrade.pin` 1, `upgrade.set-aside` 2 (before: 1, 0, 0). Before the fix this run failed with `SQLite database file identity changed before existing-only open`; the state handle opened during environment selection is now released before the swap. |
| Shared DB in rollback-journal mode with a hot journal (a torn 2,000-row write) | Chain upgrade, listening, ready, `user_version` 40, torn rows and table absent. `openclaw.sqlite.pre-2026.11.3` and its journal equal the pre-start bytes. Before the fix discovery stopped the start with `attempt to write a readonly database`. |

E2E lane: `test/state-upgrade.e2e.test.ts` 5/5 on head `3719be1` (forced fallback now runs in process; see Tests) (the corpus now stores its device keys with an encoded PEM marker; the test restores it on its copy). `src/state/sqlite-copy-swap.test.ts` 23/23 (agents now go through the production fallback entry). `src/cli/gateway-cli/pre-bootstrap.process.test.ts` 23/23. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` clean. Locally passing: Kysely guardrails, export-name collisions, private-key scan, test-lines ratchet, assertion-safety ratchet, env-var count (461/461), database-dialect ratchet (0/0/0 with the classifications below).

Earlier failures this proof found and fixed: BLOB-typed keys broke the chain's STRICT rebuild on the `-blob` corpus (decoded on the copy with foreign keys off); a resumed plan left WAL-mode files that a read-only opener could not admit (swap files now use a rollback journal); the fallback lost the chain-created credential store and migrated config (now kept).

## Tests

- `src/state/sqlite-copy-swap.test.ts` (23 tests): generic rebuild of every corpus database through the production entries (`buildStateDatabaseByCopy`, `buildAgentDatabaseByCopy`; state and agents, 7.1 through 10.10, including the BLOB variant). Asserts the bytes of the input copy are unchanged, per-table conservation (`copied + setAside = source`), integrity, and that no user-data column is dropped. A data-rule group covers BLOB decode and invalid bytes, newest-row-wins, constraint and removed-table set-aside, and the guard: a renamed user-data column without a map entry fails; with the entry it passes. Another case carries a released `claw_mcp_server_refs` row into `template_mcp_server_refs` with its renamed value and record version.
- `test/state-upgrade.e2e.test.ts` (e2e lane, prebuilt dist): starts the Gateway on 7.1-blob, 8.35 and 10.10 corpora through the chain. For 8.35 and 10.10 it also forces a chain failure: it runs `upgradeStateDirectory` with this build's Doctor followed by a throwing step, then starts the Gateway on the result. Asserts it starts, every value the release wrote survives, the old files are byte-identical under `.pre-<version>`, the report and set-aside rows match, and no work directory is left.

## Accepted edge cases

- The admission check reads `gateway.mode` from the raw config file. A mode set only through `$include` reads as missing, so that start is not upgraded and keeps the previous path (Doctor), as before this PR.
- A database inside a symlinked directory is not upgraded by the swap (a rename cannot cross it); it keeps the previous path. The shadow copies the directory's content, so the chain still cannot write the live target. A symlinked database file is upgraded; the live name becomes a regular file and the old symlink is kept as `.pre-<version>`.
- No dedicated test covers the agent fallback's pre-v14 session migration: the committed corpus has no pre-v14 agent sessions (7.x stored them as JSON). The step is the shipped `migrateSessionNodesAndWindows`, run on a scratch copy; a failure there is rolled back and its rows are set aside.

- Files Doctor writes outside the state directory (configured workspaces, config `$include` files outside the state dir) are not part of the swap.
- A `kill -9` while the shadow Doctor runs leaves that child to finish in the work directory, which the next start discards.
- The shadow copy needs free space about equal to the state directory (copy-on-write makes it nearly free on APFS, Btrfs and XFS). On a full disk the upgrade stops, the live tree is untouched and the next start retries.
- Values the shipped chain itself retires are retired here too (native CLI-shaped OAuth profiles, expired pending pairing requests); the in-place Doctor drops the same values. The running Gateway consumes its one-shot restart sentinel after the swap.
- The fallback cannot run Doctor's file imports. A 7.x install whose chain fails starts, but agents with legacy session JSON stay unavailable until `openclaw doctor --fix`; the old generation is pinned. If the chain fails before Doctor writes the credential store or config, the Gateway reports `run openclaw doctor --fix` instead of starting.
- The corpus plugin was installed from a path that exists only in the generator container. With it configured, Doctor (in place or in the shadow) defers the 7.x session import; the e2e test removes that config entry.

## Guard classifications for maintainer review

The upgrade works on SQLite files, so it adds engine-specific SQL. The dialect guard asks for maintainer review of these scoped classifications (`scripts/lib/sqlite-dialect-constructs.mts`, `scripts/database-dialect-inventory.mts`):

- `SQLITE_PRIMITIVE_OWNERS` gains `sqlite-copy-swap.ts`, `state-upgrade-tree.ts`, `state-upgrade-validate.ts` and `state-upgrade.ts` as the SQLite file upgrade owner (private `VACUUM INTO` copies, catalog PRAGMAs, `integrity_check`/`foreign_key_check`, WAL checkpoint before the swap). Callers do not repeat this SQL.
- File-private constructs: `rowid` in `sqlite-copy-swap.ts` (collision and foreign-key set-aside address rows by identity) and `typeof` in `state-upgrade-tree.ts` (BLOB-in-TEXT decode and path rewrite touch only values of one storage class). PostgreSQL stores never take this path.
- Mechanical debt is zero: the two upserts use `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE`, and `user_version` reads go through `readSqliteUserVersion`.
- The Kysely raw-SQLite allowlist gains the same modules plus the two `*-db-swap.ts` map files.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

This PR adds the single owner; it does not yet delete the in-place machinery, because two callers still migrate live files in place and depend on it:

1. **Doctor** (`openclaw doctor --fix` run by hand) still migrates the live databases with its scoped snapshots and `.bak` custody. Next PR: route Doctor's version-migration entry (`prepareDoctorDatabaseMigrations`) through `upgradeStateDirectory`, then delete `src/infra/sqlite-migration-scoped-snapshot.ts` (665 lines), the version-migration path of `src/commands/doctor-migration-backup*.ts`, `src/state/schema-migration-backup-*.ts`, and `database restore-migration-backup`.
2. **The updater** still runs candidate Doctor against live state and rolls databases back after a failed activation (`update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts`, base PR commit `91930dc`). These files belong to the update-thread PRs; once they stop migrating live state, the Gateway is the only migrator and that rollback becomes a rename of `.pre-<version>`.
3. **CLI runtime opens** (`ensureOpenClawStateRuntimeSchema` outside the Gateway) can still apply bounded migrations in place. After 1 and 2, they should refuse an outdated schema and name the Gateway as the upgrader; the STRICT pass and bounded runner then run only inside the shadow.
4. **Collapse the unreleased v23..v40 steps** (separate PR, as agreed).

Together these remove about 6,000 lines of migration-safety code and about 2,500 lines of per-version steps.


## Size

Production +2,291 / -3 under `src/` (new owner; the deletions it enables are listed above), guard scripts +19 / -1, tests +430 (`config/test-lines-allocations/198389-state-copy-swap-upgrade.txt` records the 30 lines over the allowance: the corpus generic-rebuild proof and the e2e start test), fixtures about 12,600 lines of text plus SQLite files (6 real state directories).

prs.title: fix(telegram): suppress duplicate DM transcript windows while preserving delivery-only context
prs.body:
Related: #89855, #112548, #130551, #172711, #179399

## What Problem This Solves

In an existing plain Telegram DM, recent assistant turns reach the model twice: once through canonical session replay and again through a supplemental session `chat_window`. Telegram already suppresses its native DM window in this case, but the shared transcript-context owner then rebuilt the same turns from the session transcript.

## User Impact

The model sees already-delivered answers (including Cron announcements) twice in the same request, which encourages repeated or stale answers. A November 8 report on this PR describes a real DM installation re-sending already-delivered finals; its `dmHistoryLimit: 0` workaround also drops Cron announcement context.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Telegram keeps its existing plain-DM suppression predicate and passes `deliveryOnly: true` on `SessionTranscriptContext`.
- The shared transcript reader selects its bounded recent window first, then keeps only transcript-only delivery mirrors (Cron direct delivery, message-tool source replies) that normal replay excludes.
- Fresh DMs, explicit replies, topics and groups keep their current selection. No config, schema or storage change.
- `deliveryOnly` is an additive optional field on a type the plugin SDK exposes transitively through `BuildChannelInboundEventContextParams.sessionTranscript`. It is source-compatible for every existing caller and grants no new authority; maintainers accept it as the narrow Telegram-to-core selection signal.

## Evidence

Live Telegram Test Server E2E (real Gateway, TDLib user, deterministic Chat Completions mock that logs each model request). Scenario: DM `PING:one`, a real Cron job announcing `PONG:cronnote`, then `PING:after`. The judged request is the one answering `PING:after`.

- **main `8ebe740925ca` (reproduced):** replay contains `assistant: PONG:one` and `assistant: PONG:cronnote`, and the same request also carries a "Conversation context" session window repeating both rows (`PONG:one` x2, `PONG:cronnote` x2).
- **head `826864b3be9c` (built from this exact commit):** replay contains both assistant rows once; no supplemental window is added (`PONG:one` x1, `PONG:cronnote` x1). The Cron announcement stays in context.
- Focused tests on this head pass: `session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts`, `bot-message-context.prompt-context.test.ts`, `session-transcript-context.runtime.test.ts`. The SQLite regression fails on the original parent and passes with the fix.
- CI on `826864b3be9c` is green.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): member roles come from gateway.roles.definitions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway hardcodes what the OpenClaw ID member roles `operator` and `viewer` allow, so an owner cannot change them or add a role of their own.

## User Impact

User impact: an owner can edit what Operator and Viewer members may do, and can define more member roles, by editing `gateway.roles.definitions`. OpenClaw ID is a Labs feature and is off by default; with it off, nothing here runs.

Changes an owner will notice:

- Turning on OpenClaw ID, or starting a Gateway with it on, writes missing `operator` and `viewer` definitions into the config file. It writes no `default`, so the claw's other sign-ins behave as before. **This rewrites the config file as JSON and removes JSON5 comments**, as every config write does.
- Viewer members are limited to conversations (`operator.sessions.read`). They no longer read logs or the user directory.
- A member whose role has no definition cannot connect. Deleting a definition cuts off its members until an owner gives them another role.
- A member role has no ceiling in code. A definition that includes `operator.admin` or `operator.pairing` gives its members those scopes. No preset includes them.
- `users.setRole` with a role name is refused for an OpenClaw ID member's profile. A member's role comes from membership.

Known limit: a Viewer cannot open the Access page, because loading plugin pages needs `operator.read`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- A member's role name is looked up in the current `gateway.roles.definitions` on every admission and authority check: WebSocket connect, Gateway HTTP, the tunnel API, retained and recovered runs, sandbox streams and session continuations. Editing or deleting a definition closes the affected members' connections and stops their retained work.
- The membership role takes precedence over any named role, default role or GitHub mapping on the member's profile.
- Presets are ordinary definitions. They are written only when missing, never overwrite an edited preset, and are not written again after an owner deletes one until OpenClaw ID is next turned on or the Gateway restarts.
- At startup the presets are installed before the runtime config is published, so existing members keep access after upgrade in every reload mode. If a running Gateway cannot apply the saved definitions (`gateway.reload.mode: "off"`), the OpenClaw ID status says a restart is needed.

## Evidence

- New tests cover: edited presets and custom roles; unknown role refused on all surfaces; Viewer can read conversations and cannot read logs, list users or send; a custom admin role gets admin scopes; live eviction when a definition is edited or deleted; retained runs and sandbox streams losing an edited role's authority; preset writing on activation and at startup, with existing definitions, default and assignments preserved; nothing written with OpenClaw ID off; `users.setRole` refused for members.
- One unmocked Gateway test proves that turning on OpenClaw ID does not refuse a device-token-only reconnect.
- Focused runs: 281 backend tests in 21 files and 85 UI tests in 4 files for the first commit; 61 tests in 6 files for the second. Targeted typechecks, lint, format and ratchets pass.
- Independent review of the first commit found no P0, one P1 and two P2. The second commit fixes the P1 (with config reload off, presets written at startup could reach disk without reaching the running Gateway, leaving existing members refused until another restart) and one P2 (a profile merge during `users.setRole` could skip the member check). The other P2 is the comment removal stated above. A second review of the fix commit found nothing.

Test lines: this PR adds 1,386 net test lines, 986 over the 400-line allowance. The allocation record is `config/test-lines-allocations/member-role-definitions.txt`. The tests cover separate transport, retained-authority and config-lifecycle boundaries, each of which can fail on its own.

Rebased onto main after #197697 and #197712 merged; five commits. The fourth adapts to main: it keeps the membership role when the access policy is re-evaluated during a transient failure (regression test added, seen failing first), follows main's newer publication grant call, and gives delegated-ingress fixtures an explicit catalog. After the rebase: 601 of 603 tests passed across 55 files, and the two failures plus one follow-up fixture failure were repaired and rerun green with their affected suites (26 tests in 3 files). The 55-file run was not repeated as a whole after the repairs.

The fifth commit fixes the first CI run: the `users.setRole` handler export is renamed to avoid a name collision, a perf script passes the new options object, and five fixtures with OpenClaw ID members gain role definitions. No assertion changed. 666 tests in 62 files pass with the static checks and ratchets.

Live proof on head `bd9bd69be165` (isolated Gateway, staging testnet): 9 of 10 checks passed; see the proof comment. The tenth, refusing `users.setRole` for a member's profile, was not reached because of a test-harness selector error and is covered by unit tests only. The Gateway was restarted once after enabling OpenClaw ID, because enabling it without a restart leaves the Access page unloaded; that behavior is the same on main.

CI on that head, two failures, neither from this PR:

- `checks-ui (1/3)`: two saved-credential badge cases in `chat-model-preferences.test.tsx` fail identically on the CI merge base `e80a6dd9` and on current main (18 pass, 2 fail on each). This PR does not touch the file.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-small-6`: the checkout step failed five times before any test ran.

Not run: the full repository suite and browser end-to-end tests.

prs.title: perf(update): replace the candidate canary with a runtime contract check
prs.body:
## Problem

Before activation, `openclaw update` rehearses the candidate: it copies all SQLite state and plugin payloads into a scratch directory, runs the candidate's `doctor --fix`, `doctor --lint`, `config validate` and `plugins list` against the copy, then boots a private Gateway on it. On a real 26-minute update this took 10–15 minutes (about 46%).

#197851 made that rehearsal redundant. Post-activation rollback now always has a pre-activation SQLite schema baseline, and `--no-restart` updates boot the activated release once (`activated-gateway-startup`) and roll back when it cannot become ready. Doctor and Gateway startup are proven on real state after activation, with rollback.

## Change

The driver no longer rehearses. Before activation it runs only the candidate's recovery worker once: `update-migrated-finalize --check` (step `candidate-recovery`). That one stateless call already produced every canary output used later:

| Canary output | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `candidateSchemaVersions` (activation schema baseline, PostgreSQL baseline gate, post-Doctor schema check) | `--check` `state`/`agent` |
| `gatewayRestartCompletion` | `--check` `gatewayRestartCompletion` |
| `doctorConfigWrites` (delegated Doctor config writes) | `--check` `doctorConfigWrites: "pid-start-v1"` |
| `doctorConfigChanges` (keys merged into a refusal message; warning step for candidates without delegated writes) | Removed. Activation Doctor reports its own `configChanges` and refusal keys. |
| `validatedConfigSnapshot` | Unchanged: the config read before the check |
| Observed canary Gateway startup ms (previous-Gateway readiness window) | Removed; the existing five-minute floor or `--timeout` applies |
| Missing worker → "uses the current updater" advisory | Kept as-is |

Call sites:

- `openclaw update` (`validateUpdateCandidateWithProgress`): `checkUpdateCandidate`; the progress-writer/state-worker scaffolding that kept WAL readable during the copy is gone.
- `openclaw update preflight` (external supervisors): reads config, runs `--check`; receipt `coverage` changes from `isolated-core-startup` to `candidate-runtime` so a supervisor can tell the weaker proof apart. `--source-root` is still accepted.
- Immutable activation: `--check` before drain and before rollback; the post-start private canary and its second observation are removed (live readiness verification and rollback are unchanged).
- `snapshot-space-preflight` keeps only the activation database backup/rollback space check; the scratch-copy capacity refusal is gone.
- Automatic-update backoff: now keys on repeated identical activation failures (`openclaw doctor`, `post-update verification`, `activated-gateway-startup`) instead of `candidate-doctor`, which no longer runs.
- Previous-Gateway readiness budget no longer scales with the canary's startup time; it uses the existing floor (5 min, 90 min on Windows) or `--timeout`.
- **Fix found by E2E:** `captureUpdateDatabases` retires idle state-read workers before acquiring capture ownership. A reader started before activation lazy-imported `gateway-owner-lease.worker` by its old hashed chunk name; when the target rehashes that chunk the ownership check fails and automatic restore is disabled.
- **Fix found by E2E:** the no-restart `activated-gateway-startup` boot (#197851) writes Gateway boot bookkeeping to real state. Database rollback then saw "changes after Doctor" and refused to restore (`state-migrated-no-rollback`, Gateway left broken). `adoptUpdateBootDatabaseWrites` attributes the boot's own writes to the update when nothing else wrote since Doctor, so the failed boot rolls back. Accepted edge case: a foreign write during the boot window is attributed the same way. Covered by the `activated-boot` entry of the database rollback matrix (`update-command-database-rollback.test.ts`): a migrating Doctor succeeds, the activated boot writes state and fails, and the pre-migration databases are restored. This entry fails when boot-write adoption is disabled.

### What was removed

- Driver: `update-candidate-canary.ts` (708), `update-candidate-canary-commands.ts` (107), the canary-only lint/failure/config helpers, Git startup-runtime selection (`onOwnedStartupRuntime`, `resolveManagedServiceStartupRuntime`), and the validation wrapper scaffolding.
- Tests: the canary suites and their test-support (`canary.test`, `.cleanup`, `.exit.process`, `.integration`, `.lint`, migration/mocks/progress/readiness/harness support, candidate-validation budget tests).
- Production: **-1316 / +310** lines (net about -1000). Tests: **-5006 / +375**. Docs: -65 / +102.

### What stays, and why

Released updaters, including the current stable 2026.11.3, still rehearse whatever candidate they install, using **the candidate's** state-copy worker (`update-candidate-state.worker`), its rehearsal-aware Doctor and lint, `update-candidate-rehearsal`/`-snapshot`, plugin-tree copy, and `--update-canary` startup progress. Deleting those would break upgrades from every shipped version, so this PR keeps the candidate-side support and removes only the driver. That is why the production deletion is ~1k lines rather than the ~4.9k the canary family totals. The candidate side can go once no supported update source runs the canary. Historical step identities (`candidate-doctor` etc.) also stay so existing `update_runs` history still renders.

## Evidence

Harness: real `openclaw update --yes --no-restart` on a Git checkout, from BASE to BASE+fault commit, state seeded by published `openclaw@2026.11.3` then BASE Doctor. Isolated `env -i` HOME/state, never the live Gateway. Faults: `gateway-crash` (Gateway throws at boot), `config-transform` (Doctor writes an invalid `gateway.port`), `migration-broken-v41` (state migration adds a column, then throws), `committed-migration` (new: state migration v41 commits, then Doctor throws, so the database baseline must be restored), `plugin-crash` (acpx throws at load).

main = `da0e0ba`. Head runs: `91930dc` (first pass) and `b6c6aef` (current head; production code identical except the stale-reader retirement). "Healthy" = a fresh Gateway on the post-update state reaches `/readyz`. Schema = state `user_version` after the run (base 40, fault target 41).

| Fault | main (canary rehearsal) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gateway-crash | refused at `candidate-gateway-startup`; HEAD base; schema 40; healthy | `91930dc`: activated, Doctor ok, `activated-gateway-startup` failed, **database rollback ok**, `git-runtime-rollback` ok; HEAD base; schema 40; healthy. `b6c6aef` rerun queued. |
| config-transform | refused at `candidate-doctor`; HEAD base; schema 40; healthy | queued on `b6c6aef` |
| migration-broken-v41 | refused at `candidate-doctor`; HEAD base; schema 40; healthy | queued on `b6c6aef` |
| committed-migration | refused at `candidate-doctor`; HEAD base; schema 40; healthy | **Not proven; see Gaps.** `91930dc`: Doctor committed v41 then failed; capture had disabled restore, so **HEAD stayed on target with schema 41** (Gateway boots). `b6c6aef`: code rolled back (HEAD base, schema 40, healthy), but via an earlier updater failure before Doctor ran, so the DB restore path was not exercised. |
| plugin-crash | update ok (plugin failure recorded); healthy | queued on `b6c6aef` |

Before the boot-writes fix (`8a82856`), gateway-crash activated, the boot failed and **rollback was refused** ("Databases changed after openclaw doctor"), leaving the target checked out and the Gateway failing. That run is why the fix is in this PR.

Wall-clock on this shared host (load 20–140) is not comparable; main's canary fault runs took 25–56 min.


Timing: see Gaps.

Config preservation on refusal (`update-cli.config-convergence.test.ts`): the candidate refuses through the `--check` result contract (a `candidate-recovery` failure fact), and the test asserts that recorded refusal plus unchanged authored config bytes. A thrown error cannot satisfy it.

## Accepted edge cases

- Problems that only Doctor or Gateway startup reveal are now found after activation. The update rolls back to the previous release and restores the pre-activation database baseline instead of refusing before activation. That costs one activation/rollback cycle (restart path: a brief Gateway outage) in exchange for 10–15 minutes saved on every successful update.
- `--no-restart` with a Gateway still running on the old code: the activated release is not booted (reported), as in #197851.
- PostgreSQL: the activation baseline is still captured only when the candidate reports its schema versions; `--check` reports them, so behavior is unchanged.
- External supervisors using `update preflight` get less proof (`coverage: "candidate-runtime"`) and must verify readiness after activation.

## Gaps

- **Blocker: committed-migration database restore is not proven on Git installs.** After activation, long-lived workers in the *updater* process (started from the live `dist/` before the swap) lazy-import chunks by their old hashed names. When the target build rehashes state chunks, those imports fail (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND …/dist/state/openclaw-state-read-…-<hash>.mjs`). Retiring idle readers before capture fixed the first instance; the `b6c6aef` run then failed on another stale import in post-update verification. This is a retained-runtime problem (workers created outside the retained runtime generation), not part of the canary removal, but this PR makes post-activation rollback the primary safety net, so it now matters. Likely addressed by #198375 (runtime slots / frozen launcher). Decision needed: land after #198375, or fix worker binding here.
- **Clean-update timing main vs head is pending.** The shared host ran at load 40–140 during these runs (other pueue work), so wall-clock comparisons are not meaningful. Will run alternating main/head clean updates (≥3 each) on a quiet host and add the table with load averages and per-step durations.
- npm-global path: npm-global `openclaw@2026.11.3` (its own updater, which still runs the canary) to this branch's packed tarball (`8a82856`): **ok**, state schema 22→40, Gateway healthy. Its `candidate-state-snapshot`/`candidate-doctor`/`candidate-gateway-startup` steps ran against the candidate-side support this PR keeps (the shipped-updater compatibility contract). The npm path for the *new* updater (head → head+1) is not exercised; the Git path above covers the new driver.
- Plugin-crash: accepted as on main (plugin load failures are recorded, not refused).
