prs.title: fix: reduce Gateway stalls under filesystem pressure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Synchronous filesystem lookups in request and timer paths can turn a host I/O stall into a Gateway-wide pause. This change removes redundant polling and moves necessary filesystem work to the existing asynchronous or worker owner. It reduces the Gateway’s exposure; it does not fix the underlying host I/O pressure or eliminate every synchronous runtime path.

Session reads, pending-input lifetimes, history, maintenance, workspace reads and skill preparation carry facts captured by their existing owners. Retained guards use live in-memory authority; workers retain the original candidate roster, absence and physical identity checks at the effect boundary. Lock mutual exclusion, FIFO ordering, cancellation, accepted-work settlement and replacement refusal remain required contracts. Workspace bootstrap reads remove the content cache and use the existing guarded worker reader, trading retained bytes for additional bounded reads.

The final integration also repairs periodic transcript backfill introduced by [#194519](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194519). Its startup inventory guard became recurring main-thread `statSync` work. Backfill now carries the startup admission’s original file/key/birthtime through the existing worker read-custody contract. The calibrated real-startup scheduler regression goes from **3 synchronous target checks to 0**. The real worker proof permits closing and reopening the same file, then refuses a physical successor without changing its database, WAL, SHM or journal bytes. The focused 37 cases pass; finite reconciliation and page-cache checks retain their physical guards.

## Measurements and limits

**The following Gateway census is INTERMEDIATE c37 evidence, not a result for the current candidate.** On the synthetic Linux/btrfs fixture (35 GiB agent database, 5,000 sessions, 62,000 workspace files), selected main-thread kernel filesystem syscalls fell from **39,322/min to 2,893/min (−92.64%)**. Five after-windows were 2,908/2,893/2,893/2,893/2,893. Only the fifth baseline window has complete tracing and the matching six measured turns.

**K** means selected kernel syscalls per fixed 60 seconds; **J** means intercepted main-thread filesystem API calls per workload window; **O** means a separate owner workload. These denominators are not interchangeable or additive. Later focused guards do not establish a new Gateway after-total.

| Owner | Retained before → after evidence | Scope / remaining qualification |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway/state locks | K root lock 1,836 → 0; projection lock 1,980 → 0 | Redundant held-lock polling removed; subprocess mutual exclusion and worker-loss cases exercised. Client lock activity was not independently reproduced. |
| DB admission, reads and history | K agent DB 2,574 → 266; state DB 485 → 54; O pending lifetime 6 → 0 | c37 still contained 320 DB/session identity API calls. Later retained-source, history, patch and subagent guards passed; final census pending. |
| Maintenance and native leases | K state/WAL 20 preads + 25 pwrites + 1 fsync + 1 fstat → 0; later O cold/warm/removal guards pass | Later owner tests cover maintenance and scheduling; integrated counts and costs pending. |
| Skills, sandbox and docs | K skills tree 1,686 → 42; O projection 1,094 main-thread calls → 0 | c37 retained J docs 324 and mount 18. Later docs and prepared-mount guards pass; final census pending. |
| Workspace bootstrap | c37 J 72/window; later real-loader guards pass | Cache removed; complete guarded reads stay with the worker. Additional reads and allocation costs remain to measure. |
| Directory/skills observation | O registration 1 access + 1 stat + 136 readdir → 0; 60 edits/min: 60 stat → 0 | Separate synthetic owner proof, not an incident-rate reproduction. |
| Credentials and GitHub configuration | O metadata 198/18 operations → 0; GitHub reads 252/18 → 0; HTTP path 198/18 → 0 | Writer-owned rotation preserved. The directory component is generated from independent 16 random bytes, not a GitHub token; no value was printed. |
| Executable and Git preparation | O safe-bin 756/18 → 0; commands 72/18 → 0; shell 54/18 → 0 | Physical preparation stays with the existing command/Git worker. |
| Logging, pricing and installation | K log 135 → 0; models 82 → 0; runtime artifact 12 → 0 | Logging worker, prepared pricing facts and asynchronous installation observation. |
| WSL and CPU observation | c37 J WSL 18 and CPU 24/window; later focused guards pass | Final Linux counts and CPU-reader cost remain pending. |

Costs are material. The directory/skills owner’s cold wall time increased 1,048 → 1,446 ms and total CPU 1,074 → 1,297 ms. Historical detached-transcript tests added 0.54–0.65 ms/read and 41–43 KB sampled main-thread allocation/read. Hourly cleanup’s separate three-artifact workload increased wall time 6.578 → 246.209 ms and cumulative isolate allocation 1.008 → 118.113 MB; cold loader work also increased. These are separate owner measurements, not per-turn Gateway costs. Final owner-cost qualification is pending.

Completed baseline A1/A2 controls drifted by +25.51% main CPU, +30.86% process CPU and +1.68% sampled main allocation as host load rose. The synthetic fixture accumulated changes and required upstream schema migration; it was not reset or downgraded. Request schemas/bytes also differ across versions. There is **no causal whole-Gateway CPU, allocation or latency improvement claim**, and no final untraced B timing result yet. The c37 observer lacked its completion marker; bounded sample coverage and clean primary/tracer exits are retained rather than treating observer teardown as complete evidence.

Remaining exposure is explicit: cold plugin preparation measured 28 synchronous API calls, plus uncounted native SQLite/retirement work; new plugin generations can reenter that path. Update transaction and cold legacy/unowned paths remain. Native memory diagnostics still caused K `/proc/self/stat` 55 → 62 opens/min outside the API wrappers; moving them would change the exact main-isolate telemetry contract. This is not an all-runtime-zero or outage-immunity claim.

## Scope and prerequisite merges

The exact recount against integrated main `6ff27cbe` is **+8,545 runtime lines in this PR and +10,241 across the lane**, including +1,696 from the fifteen merged prerequisites. Three build-entry lines are classified separately. **The requested net ≤0 expectation is not met.** Growth carries existing authority and lifecycle contracts across worker boundaries and completes their callers; redundant polling and the workspace content cache are deleted. The exact 905-path census records +12,545 test/helper lines and +4,852 other lines. Canonical test growth is 12,294 lines, covered by 11,894 allocated lines and the unchanged single 400-line allowance; the actual-PR line and test ratchets pass.

The lane adds no new configuration option or its own SQLite schema change. Integration retains upstream state 39 → 40 and agent 41 → 42 migrations; older code must not be run against upgraded state. Fresh-install and upgrade proof remain required.

These fifteen prerequisites are merged; that status is not proof of the final composition: [warm borrowing #197446](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197446), [writer admission #197461](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197461), [lock ownership #197455](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197455), [directory observation #197445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197445), [credential reads #197460](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197460), [GitHub profile writes #197546](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197546), [ClickClack reads #197545](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197545), [safe-bin preparation #197539](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197539), [command preparation #197634](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197634), [installation observation #197584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197584), [readiness/diagnosis #197975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197975), [logging worker #197586](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197586), [default logging target #197742](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197742), [prepared pricing #197599](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197599), and [Gateway measurement #197504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197504).

## Evidence

Published head `a4955cafcd7dbc2a364826a107fc0f1b81e1bbb8` binds the reviewed tree `776ddc68095dc08b6bffe735ac11545b23da7e69`, integrating main `6ff27cbe`. The calibrated backfill regression and 37 focused cases pass, as do the Gateway server type graph and four page-cache cases. Fresh Codex review covers all 173 integration changes in ten passes with zero findings; it supplements the retained full prior-head review and its source-backed disposition. All three affected UI cases pass, including real-Gateway worker admission, with unchanged source and no unhandled errors.

The native incremental changed-check remains **40 of 43 stages passing**, exit 1. All current export and lint failures reproduce on exact main `6ff27cbe`: `MAX_COMPLETION_CLAIMS` in production/full-tree export scans ([#197471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197471)); `prepareTranscriptFactsBackfillStress` in script exports and startup-finish's 701/700 file cap ([#194519](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194519)); and the runtime manifest cap, first crossed by this lane's earlier [#197586](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197586), then increased by #197634 and #194519. The manifest is 706 lines on the parent and 702 here. These are four named main regressions, not noise or green checks. The line-growth failure against the prior integration head is separately resolved against the actual PR base: both native line and test ratchets pass. Exact-parent local evidence does not establish an exact-head CI exception.

Before landing: build and pack this exact head with full declarations; run final B kernel/API counts, untraced timing and required owner CPU/allocation costs; qualify all five Doctor roles, including fresh install and latest-stable upgrade; obtain exact-head CI disposition and a final-head ClawSweeper review with zero open items. Completed A/A controls remain immutable. No final artifact, current-head Gateway performance result, overall CI-green status or merge is claimed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat progress messages add decorative ellipses to creation, startup, working, approval and recovery labels.

## User Impact

Progress labels use plain text while retaining their spinner, elapsed time, live announcements and loading behavior. User and model messages, CSS truncation and unrelated placeholders are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Update the canonical English copy and remove the two renderers that appended punctuation. Update exact consumers rather than strip punctuation from transcripts.

Stacked on [Template Add responsiveness #198637](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198637), above [creation #198070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198070) and [setup #198603](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198603). The diff is only this presentation layer and its consumer repairs.

## Evidence

Matched built Control UI creation state at4seconds. Browser harness uses synthetic Gateway responses. Proof was inspected and delivered before the first push; these are retained unchanged-patch images, not fresh final-stack live proof.

| Before | After |

prs.title: fix(beam): avoid blocking mirror cleanup on a captured response tee
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Beam mirror upload runs while diagnostic HTTP capture is enabled (`OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED=1`) and the receiver responds slowly, the upload's cleanup stalls and the connection slot stays unreturned for up to 10 seconds per poll retry. The `finally` block in `createBeamMirrorRunner`'s upload path discards the ignored response body with `await response.body?.cancel()`, but capture has already tee'd the response through `response.clone()`, so awaiting the caller's branch cancel waits for the capture branch to settle (bounded by the capture reader's 10s idle deadline). The dispatcher `release()` that reclaims the connection slot sits behind that wait — exactly the "retain connection slots across poll retries" outcome the adjacent comment says the cancel exists to prevent.

- Problem: `extensions/beam/src/mirror.ts` awaited the caller's tee-branch cancel before releasing the dispatcher, so a held capture branch delayed cleanup on every upload poll retry.
- Solution: fire-and-forget the cancel (`void response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`), matching the canonical owner `cancelUnreadResponseBody`, then release the dispatcher in `finally` exactly as before.
- What changed: one word in the upload `finally`; the existing lifecycle-abort regression test now holds the cancel to model a live capture tee branch.
- What did NOT change: the `finally { await release() }` ordering (shutdown still waits for guarded cleanup), the cancel being initiated on every path, redirect blocking, throttled warnings, timeouts, and every behavior with capture disabled (the default).

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adopts the repository's canonical form for discarding an unread, possibly-tee'd response body. `cancelUnreadResponseBody` (`src/infra/http-response-body.ts:10`) documents the invariant — "A capture tee must not delay errors or the caller's bounded dispatcher release" — and implements it as `void response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`. The same form was merged for the marketplace capture path in #191675 and is under review for the xAI OAuth challenge path in #198219; the Beam mirror call site was a remaining caller that awaited the cancel directly. An extension cannot import the core owner file (plugin boundary), so the call site adopts the owner's expression verbatim. The nearest in-extension precedent states the reason outright — `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts:83` keeps a local copy of the helper with the comment "Do not await: debug capture can tee the stream and deadlock a waiter."

Best fix: yes. It reuses the established owner form rather than adding a new guard, and keeps the production change to a single word. Alternative considered: passing `capture: false` for the mirror upload fetch; rejected because it would remove diagnostic visibility for mirror traffic and diverge from the owner-level invariant that callers must not await a tee-branch cancel. Risk: the cancel is now best-effort, but the dispatcher release still aborts the request controller and closes the transport, so the unread body is reclaimed by the existing release path.

## User Impact

Operators running Beam session mirroring with diagnostic capture enabled no longer have a slow receiver hold a dispatcher connection slot (up to 10s) between upload polls: cleanup releases the slot immediately while the ignored body is still being discarded. With capture disabled (the default), the cancel already resolved instantly and behavior is unchanged. Service shutdown still waits for the guarded response release to finish before settling.

## Evidence

| Mirror-upload cleanup metric | Before (`await cancel()`, origin/main) | After (`void cancel()`, this head) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shipped built Gateway running the real Beam mirror service, capture on, receiver holds the body 3000 ms — transport closed after response headers | 3023 / 3006 / 3003 ms | 15 / 4 / 4 / 4 ms |
| Shipped, capture on — transport still closed before the held body drained (`closedBeforeBodyRelease`) | false on every in-run upload | true on all 4 uploads |
| Shipped, capture disabled (the default) — same measurement | 30 / 2 / 2 ms (inert) | 50 / 2 / 3 ms (inert) |
| Real mirror POSTs delivered per run (receiver-recorded request bodies) | 4 | 4 |
| Guarded-fetch transport call in isolation, capture on — dispatcher `release()` reached after | 2993 / 2996 / 2999 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 ms |
| Committed regression (held capture-tee cancel) at the real Beam call site | FAIL — `Error: Test timed out in 120000ms` | PASS |
| Cancel initiated | once | once (unchanged) |
| Warnings surfaced | none | none (unchanged) |

### Shipped end-to-end: built Gateway running the real Beam mirror service

The built artifact from this head (`dist/index.js`, produced by `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime` in this branch's worktree) was started as a real isolated Gateway — its own scratch `HOME`, state dir, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, config with `plugins.entries.beam.config.mirror` and the anthropic native session catalog — by a `node` harness that also:

- synthesizes a Claude-style transcript in the catalog's explicit project root and appends a turn every 8 s, so each 10 s poll produces a new fingerprint instead of a deduplicated no-op;
- runs a local `node:http` receiver as the mirror endpoint that flushes `200` + `{"ok":true` and then holds the rest of the JSON body open for 3000 ms, recording per request when the client's transport closed relative to that held release;
- sets `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED=1` so the guarded fetch really tees the response through the capture branch (`src/proxy-capture/runtime-response-body.ts:140-161`).

The before cells are the *same built file* with only the one-word cancel form restored (`await c.body?.cancel()…`), and each output echoes the snippet it actually ran (`distCancelForm`), so the two forms cannot be confused:

After (this head):

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/beam-shipped-mirror-proof.mts  # LABEL=head CAPTURE=1 UPLOADS=4 HOLD_MS=3000
{"label":"head","captureEnabled":true,"holdMs":3000,"uploadsSeen":4,"distCancelForm":".ok}finally{c.body?.cancel().catch(()=>void 0);await l()}}","root":"/tmp/beam-shipped-H8xy0R","uploads":[{"bytes":449,"closeDelayMs":15,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true},{"bytes":512,"closeDelayMs":4,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true},{"bytes":574,"closeDelayMs":4,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true},{"bytes":699,"closeDelayMs":4,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true}]}
```

Before (origin/main cancel form):

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/beam-shipped-mirror-proof.mts  # LABEL=base CAPTURE=1 UPLOADS=4 HOLD_MS=3000
{"label":"base","captureEnabled":true,"holdMs":3000,"uploadsSeen":4,"distCancelForm":"nally{await c.body?.cancel().catch(()=>void 0);await l()}}","root":"/tmp/beam-shipped-hnCYEh","uploads":[{"bytes":449,"closeDelayMs":3023,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":false},{"bytes":574,"closeDelayMs":3006,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":false},{"bytes":637,"closeDelayMs":3003,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":false},{"bytes":762,"closeDelayMs":57,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true}]}
```

`closeDelayMs` is measured on the receiver: headers arrived, then the connection stayed open for the whole 3000 ms body hold in the before cells, while the after cells close within 4-15 ms of the response — the mirror's `finally` reached `release()` while the receiver still held the body. Both runs log the same real upload path (`beam mirror active: claude -> http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) and deliver 4 real POST bodies (449-762 bytes). The last before-cell row (`57 ms`) is the harness's own teardown: the loop stops and sends `SIGTERM` as soon as it observes the requested upload count, so that final exchange's close is shutdown-driven rather than cleanup-driven; the same truncation does not appear in the after cells because their cleanup never waits.

Control with capture disabled (the shipped default) — both forms close in single-digit tens of milliseconds, so the change is inert unless diagnostic capture is on:

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/beam-shipped-mirror-proof.mts  # LABEL=base CAPTURE=0 UPLOADS=4 HOLD_MS=3000
{"label":"base","captureEnabled":false,"holdMs":3000,"uploadsSeen":4,"distCancelForm":"nally{await c.body?.cancel().catch(()=>void 0);await l()}}","root":"/tmp/beam-shipped-6PwtMp","uploads":[{"bytes":449,"closeDelayMs":30,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true},{"bytes":512,"closeDelayMs":2,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true},{"bytes":574,"closeDelayMs":2,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true},{"bytes":699,"closeDelayMs":2,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true}]}
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/beam-shipped-mirror-proof.mts  # LABEL=head CAPTURE=0 UPLOADS=4 HOLD_MS=3000
{"label":"head","captureEnabled":false,"holdMs":3000,"uploadsSeen":4,"distCancelForm":".ok}finally{c.body?.cancel().catch(()=>void 0);await l()}}","root":"/tmp/beam-shipped-tmrSqh","uploads":[{"bytes":449,"closeDelayMs":50,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true},{"bytes":574,"closeDelayMs":2,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true},{"bytes":637,"closeDelayMs":3,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true},{"bytes":699,"closeDelayMs":1,"closedBeforeBodyRelease":true}]}
```

### Dispatcher-release timing at the transport call

The same invariant was measured from inside the cleanup block itself: the mirror upload's transport call (`fetchWithSsrFGuard` with the mirror's own `url` / `timeoutMs` / `policy` / `auditContext: "beam.mirror_upload"` / `maxRedirects: 0` / POST body) and its `finally` replayed verbatim in a standalone `node` run against a real loopback receiver that holds the body open for 3000 ms, with the same capture flag. Only the cancel form differs between runs.

After (this head) — `void response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` then `await release()`; `bodyStillHeldAtRelease: true` is the discriminator, the slot is reclaimed while the receiver still holds the body:

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs beam-cancel-tee-proof.mts  # FORM=head CAPTURE=1 UPLOADS=3 HOLD_MS=3000
{"form":"head","captureEnabled":true,"holdMs":3000,"uploads":3,"rows":[{"upload":1,"result":true,"cleanupElapsedMs":17,"releaseReachedAfterMs":0,"releaseElapsedMs":17,"bodyStillHeldAtRelease":true,"receiverHeldBodyMs":3000},{"upload":2,"result":true,"cleanupElapsedMs":2,"releaseReachedAfterMs":0,"releaseElapsedMs":2,"bodyStillHeldAtRelease":true,"receiverHeldBodyMs":3000},{"upload":3,"result":true,"cleanupElapsedMs":1,"releaseReachedAfterMs":0,"releaseElapsedMs":1,"bodyStillHeldAtRelease":true,"receiverHeldBodyMs":3000}]}
```

Before (origin/main) — the same run with `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`, so `release()` is reached only after the held capture branch settles:

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs beam-cancel-tee-proof.mts  # FORM=base CAPTURE=1 UPLOADS=3 HOLD_MS=3000
{"form":"base","captureEnabled":true,"holdMs":3000,"uploads":3,"rows":[{"upload":1,"result":true,"cleanupElapsedMs":3003,"releaseReachedAfterMs":2993,"releaseElapsedMs":10,"bodyStillHeldAtRelease":false,"receiverHeldBodyMs":3000},{"upload":2,"result":true,"cleanupElapsedMs":2997,"releaseReachedAfterMs":2996,"releaseElapsedMs":1,"bodyStillHeldAtRelease":false,"receiverHeldBodyMs":3000},{"upload":3,"result":true,"cleanupElapsedMs":3001,"releaseReachedAfterMs":2999,"releaseElapsedMs":2,"bodyStillHeldAtRelease":false,"receiverHeldBodyMs":3000}]}
```

With a longer hold the awaited form blocks up to the capture read idle bound (10s, `CAPTURED_RESPONSE_BODY_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`); the held-for-3s case was chosen so one run stays inside the 15s upload timeout.

### Committed regression at the real product call site

The existing lifecycle-abort test in `extensions/beam/src/mirror.test.ts` ("forwards lifecycle abort and waits for guarded response cleanup without warning") was extended so the response body's `cancel` returns a promise that never settles — structurally identical to a live capture tee branch holding the caller's side of the tee (no wall-clock assumptions). On origin/main production code the upload's `finally` awaits that cancel and never reaches `release()`, so the test's cleanup barrier never starts and the test times out; on this head the cancel is initiated and discarded, `release()` runs immediately, and the same assertions (cleanup started while cancel is still pending, shutdown settles only after the release barrier completes, cancel invoked exactly once, no warnings) all pass.

RED — base production code (byte-identical `origin/main` file) with the extended test:

```console
$ vitest run extensions/beam/src/mirror.test.ts -t "forwards lifecycle abort"
 FAIL   extensions  extensions/beam/src/mirror.test.ts > createBeamMirrorRunner > forwards lifecycle abort and waits for guarded response cleanup without warning
Error: Test timed out in 120000ms.
 ❯ extensions/beam/src/mirror.test.ts:258:3

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 19 skipped (20)
   Duration  169.11s
```

GREEN — this head, full file:

```console
$ vitest run extensions/beam/src/mirror.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
   Start at  07:46:16
   Duration  14.08s
```

### Corroboration on the sibling call site of this anchor

The same owner-form fix under the same anchor was measured end-to-end in a shipped product session for the xAI marketplace capture path in sibling PR #198219 (real `openclaw models list --refresh` CLI child process over real TLS through a local capture proxy: transport closed in 4-14ms with the body held versus ~3005ms without the fix), and the merged precedent #191675 established the owner form. This PR applies that fix to the remaining Beam mirror call site, with the Beam-specific shipped matrix and committed regression above.

What was not tested:

- The shipped cells drive the real `createBeamMirrorRunner` service (activation, poll scan, catalog read, fingerprint dedup, guarded POST upload, cleanup) inside a built Gateway, but the mirrored transcript is a synthetic Claude-format JSONL file and the receiver credential is a synthetic bearer token; no operator's real Beam endpoint or real conversation data was involved. The guarded-fetch transport, the diagnostic capture tee, the dispatcher release and the cancel paths all run unmodified.
- The final upload of the before/capture-on cell is closed early by the harness's own `SIGTERM` teardown (the loop stops at the requested upload count), so it reads 57 ms instead of ~3000 ms; the three in-run uploads carry the before/after comparison and the after cells are unaffected by the same teardown.
- A hold longer than the capture read idle bound (10s) was not run live, because the 15s upload timeout would make the two forms differ only by which error they surface; the bounded-stall behavior is the capture owner's existing contract, unchanged here.
- Local `oxlint` could not run in this environment at all: its config loads `./tools/solid-lint/index.mjs`, which imports `eslint-plugin-solid`, and that package is a dangling symlink in the local install (`node_modules/eslint-plugin-solid` -> an unmaterialized `.pnpm` entry). Lint therefore relies on CI `check-lint`. `oxfmt` and the affected test suites were run locally and are clean (`git diff --check` empty; `extensions/beam/src/mirror.test.ts` + `mirror-retry.test.ts` = 23 passed).

### Open PR collision check

Swept against the submission-day open-PR snapshot two ways. Changed files: the 60 most recently updated open PRs were enumerated with their file lists and none touches `extensions/beam/*` at all, let alone `extensions/beam/src/mirror.ts` / `mirror.test.ts`. Title/body search: `mirror in:title` returns 6 open PRs (replay admission, telegram final deliveries, usage double-count, plugin-sdk write assertion, imessage echo cache, session mirroring feature) and none of their files include `extensions/beam`; `capture tee` returns this anchor's sibling #198219, which changes only `extensions/xai/*` (zero file overlap). The merged precedent #191675 (`src/plugins/marketplace.ts`) established the owner form, and `origin/main` still has `await response.body?.cancel()` at this call site, so the bug is live and uncovered.

prs.title: fix(update): retrying an update from a dev checkout is refused after a killed update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after an update from a linked dev checkout is killed partway through, every later update from that checkout is refused, and the installation has no package at its path until someone moves a link back by hand.

## User Impact

User impact: an installation left in this state is repaired by running the same update again from the checkout. The updater prints `Restored the npm package link an interrupted update left at <path>.` and continues. `--dry-run` reports the link it would restore and moves nothing.

Updaters without this fix keep refusing that retry, so an affected installation needs an updater that contains it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switching a linked dev checkout to a published package replaces npm's package link with a directory. A directory cannot be renamed over a link, so the swap first renames the link to `.openclaw.package-backup-<pid>-<time>`, then renames the staged package into place. Linked roots are outside the activation journal, because its descriptor records tree fingerprints that an operator-owned checkout does not have.

An updater killed between those two renames leaves no package at its path, the link beside it under the backup name, and an `openclaw` launcher that no longer resolves. Nothing deletes that link. The defect is the retry: the npm destination gate sees a launcher it cannot resolve and refuses the update as an uninspectable destination (`unreadable-layout`).

When the package path is empty, the gate now first puts back a link left under the swap's live backup name, but only when it resolves to the checkout running the update. Inspection, activation, rollback and retirement then follow the existing linked-root path. Links to other checkouts, retained package directories, and the retired `.openclaw-package-backup-*` name are left where they are. A backup entry that disappears during the scan matches nothing.

Accepted edges:

- A link to this checkout kept by an earlier failed cleanup is restored the same way.
- A restore that fails, for example `EACCES` on the rename, ends in the gate's existing refusal.
- For this state, `--dry-run` does not inspect the launcher, so a foreign launcher is reported only by the real run.
- The crash window itself stays. Closing it needs a journal record for links or an exchange rename that Node does not expose.

No journal, schema, or protocol change.

## Evidence

**Reproduction.** `update-command-package-destination.interrupted-link.test.ts` runs the real linked swap in a child process that kills itself with `SIGKILL` once the link has left the package path, then asks the destination gate.

| Production files | Result |
| --- | --- |
| From `main` at `27d9e69` | The gate returns `unknown` / `unreadable-layout`. The new dry-run case fails because a dry run moves the link. 2 of 23 tests fail. |
| This branch | The gate returns `owned`, the same link is back, and the retried swap activates. A dry run leaves the link under its backup name and stages nothing. 23 of 23 pass. |

`package-update-swap.integrity.test.ts` also passes (25 tests); its linked-swap helpers moved to the shared test support with no case or assertion changed.

**Wider checks** on the rebased head: all 43 `src/infra/package-update-*.test.ts` files except the e2e one, plus every test that uses the destination gate or the swap test support: 58 files, 815 tests passed, 1 existing skip (the ACL case in `package-update-permission-drift.test.ts`). `pnpm tsgo:all` passes. `oxlint` and the docs format check passed on the authoring branch.

The process-death case is skipped on Windows; the dry-run and vanished-entry cases are not.

**Review.** An independent review of the first commit found that a dry run would restore the link and that a vanished backup entry would fail inspection; the second commit fixes both, each with a test that failed first. No autoreview pass: the helper could not run on the authoring machine.

prs.title: fix(cli): show session-target remedies for attach failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An operator who points `openclaw attach` at a short session reference gets no actionable output. `openclaw attach "https://gw.example/dashboard/main/movies-a1166b81" --url wss://other.example` prints only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` plus `For help, run openclaw doctor.` — the remedy the resolver already composed ("pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both") never reaches the terminal, and the doctor hint sends the operator to the wrong next step. The same collapse hides the formatted ambiguity table for a colliding prefix, the `No session found` hint, and the gateway-unreachable / stored-device-auth recovery lines.

- Problem: `resolveSessionTarget` in `src/cli/session-target.ts` raises its operator remedies as plain `Error`s. `attach` awaits it directly, so they bubble to the root CLI renderer, which prints the message only for expected CLI errors and a narrow show-reason whitelist that does not include `attach`.
- Solution: raise those remedy sites through the canonical `throwExpectedCliError` / `ExpectedCliError` owner in `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`, message text verbatim.
- What changed: `src/cli/session-target.ts` (+16/−9) — six returned remedy errors and three thrown remedy errors now carry `humanOutput`. Regression assertions folded into the existing cases in `src/cli/session-ref.test.ts` and `src/cli/session-target.test.ts` (net −4 test lines, no new test file).
- What did NOT change: every message string, the exit code (1), the JSON failure envelope (`formatCliJsonFailure` already kept the message), `openclaw tui` output, and the internal-invariant error at `session-target.ts:199` ("Gateway returned a session without a consistent agent identity.") which stays a plain `Error` because it names a branch that should not happen.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-target owner already writes these remedies for one purpose — telling the operator what to do next — and one of its two consumers honours that contract while the other discards it. `src/cli/tui-cli.ts:96-105` catches around the same `resolveSessionTarget` call and prints the formatted message; `src/cli/attach-cli.ts:103` awaits it unwrapped, so the identical remedy is visible under `tui` and invisible under `attach` for the same input. That asymmetry is the strongest signal this is a missed site rather than a deliberate choice, and it is the same reasoning accepted in the merged dns CLI fix #192127 and the hooks CLI fix #190366, which adopted exactly this per-site shape.

Alternatives considered and rejected: adding `attach` to the renderer's show-reason whitelist would print raw reasons for every attach failure including unforeseen internal errors, a larger blast radius than one guard needs. Putting the conversion in the `attach` action instead would leave the second consumer (and any future one) re-deriving the contract that the owner already owns. Constructing `ExpectedCliError` inline at each of the six `shapeTargetError` return sites would triplicate the long remedy templates in a three-field constructor call, so those sites share one local factory over the owner class; the three throw sites call `throwExpectedCliError` directly.

## User Impact

Operators running `openclaw attach` with an ambiguous short reference, a mistyped reference, a conflicting URL and `--url`, or an unreachable gateway now see the remedy — including the already-formatted candidate table and the `sessions list` hint — instead of a generic failure and a doctor pointer. Successful and JSON-mode invocations are untouched, and every affected path still exits 1.

## Evidence

| Case (shipped entry, same isolated profile) | Before (`origin/main` `5bdadab2c73`, owner file reverted) | After (this head `14a4ec8219f`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attach <session URL> --url wss://other.example` | generic title + doctor hint, remedy hidden (exit 1) | `pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both` (exit 1) |
| `attach <ref> --url` to a port nothing listens on | generic title + doctor hint (exit 1) | transport line + `Could not reach gateway wss://127.0.0.1:18307. Check whether the gateway is down and whether its tailnet or SSH tunnel is reachable.` (exit 1) |
| `tui` with the same two inputs (control) | remedy printed | byte-identical remedy printed — the fix changes nothing on the consumer that already worked |
| owner unit suite (38 cases) | 9 failed / 29 passed | 38 passed |

Live runs use the shipped source entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`) with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` on a scratch directory holding a minimal config, so no real state or config is touched; the unreachable cells hit a genuine TCP refusal on loopback port 18307 (nothing listening) and travel the real `callGateway` transport, with no mocks. All eight runs exit 1, and the two `tui` control outputs diff byte-identical between base and head.

After (this head), conflict cell:

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts attach "https://gw.example/dashboard/main/movies-a1166b81" --url wss://other.example
pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both
(exit 1)
```

Before (same command, `origin/main` version of the owner file):

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts attach "https://gw.example/dashboard/main/movies-a1166b81" --url wss://other.example
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
(exit 1)
```

After, unreachable cell (real `ECONNREFUSED`, remedy plus the transport detail the operator needs):

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts attach "https://127.0.0.1:18307/dashboard/main/movies-a1166b81" --token dummy-token
Gateway not reachable at wss://127.0.0.1:18307 (ECONNREFUSED).
Start it with `openclaw gateway run` or check `openclaw gateway status`.
Gateway target: wss://127.0.0.1:18307
Source: cli --url
Config: /tmp/oc307/openclaw.json
Could not reach gateway wss://127.0.0.1:18307. Check whether the gateway is down and whether its tailnet or SSH tunnel is reachable.
```

prs.title: fix(models): surface the auth login device-code conflict remedy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw models auth login --device-code --method password` rejects the conflicting flags but prints only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` followed by a doctor hint — the remedy the guard already composed (`--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.`) never reaches the operator. This change throws the conflict as an expected CLI error so the root failure renderer prints the remedy line directly.

- Problem: the conflict guard in the `models auth login` action throws a plain `Error`. The root failure renderer prints `humanOutput` only for expected CLI errors, and `models` is not on the show-reason whitelist, so the message collapses to the generic failure title plus `For help, run openclaw doctor.`
- Solution: replace `throw new Error(...)` with the canonical `throwExpectedCliError(...)` from `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`, keeping the message verbatim.
- What changed: `src/cli/models-cli.ts` (one import, one throw) and a regression assertion folded into the existing `--device-code` mapping test in `src/cli/models-cli.test.ts` (net 0 test lines, no new test file).
- What did NOT change: the guard condition, the message text, the exit code (1), machine/JSON output, and every other command path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer already owns the remedy-printing contract: an expected CLI error carries `humanOutput`, and `formatCliFailureLines` prints it verbatim before any generic fallback. Reusing `throwExpectedCliError` is the established per-site remedy for this exact anti-pattern — the dns CLI fix #192127 adopted the same shape, including the `rejects.toMatchObject({ humanOutput })` guard-test form reused here. Alternatives considered and rejected: adding `models` to the show-reason whitelist would widen reason printing for every models failure (a larger blast radius than this one guard), and constructing `ExpectedCliError` inline would duplicate the owner. The production delta is +1 line (the import); the throw itself is a one-for-one replacement.

## User Impact

Operators who combine `--device-code` with an incompatible `--method` now see the actionable remedy line directly instead of a generic failure and a doctor hint. Valid invocations are untouched, and the command still exits 1 on the conflict.

## Evidence

| Case | Before (base 25559c4) | After (this head) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models auth login --device-code --method password` | generic title + doctor hint, remedy hidden (exit 1) | remedy line printed verbatim (exit 1) |
| same command, `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` | `Reason:` + stack: plain `Error` at the guard (`src/cli/models-cli.ts:586`) | remedy line only, no Reason/stack (expected-error early return) |
| `models auth login --help` (control) | exit 0, help text | exit 0, identical help text |

Live runs through the shipped entry point (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts ...`), both sides on the same isolated profile: `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` point at a scratch directory with an empty config, so no credentials or configuration are written (the conflict guard is the first statement of the action handler). The service-probe warning and the log-append note in the outputs below are artifacts of that isolated profile and appear identically on both sides.

After (this head):

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts models auth login --device-code --method password
Installed Gateway service state and config paths could not be verified. Inspect the service environment with `openclaw gateway status --deep` before repairing plugin state.
[openclaw] log file append failed; records dropped; check that the path is a writable regular file; file=openclaw-2026-11-13.log
--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.
(exit 1)
```

Before (base, owner file reverted via `git show`, test kept):

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts models auth login --device-code --method password
Installed Gateway service state and config paths could not be verified. Inspect the service environment with `openclaw gateway status --deep` before repairing plugin state.
[openclaw] log file append failed; records dropped; check that the path is a writable regular file; file=openclaw-2026-11-13.log
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
(exit 1)
```

Before with `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` shows the hidden remedy and proves the plain-Error envelope (excerpt, stack path normalized):

```console
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: --device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.
[openclaw] Stack:
[openclaw] Error: --device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.
[openclaw]     at OpenClawCommand.<anonymous> (src/cli/models-cli.ts:586:15)
```

Unit invariant, same folded test with the owner file swapped: on base the plain Error carries `message` but no `humanOutput`, so the guard assertion fails (1 failed | 21 passed); on this head the full file passes (22 passed).

```console
FAIL src/cli/models-cli.test.ts > models cli > maps --device-code to the provider device-code auth method
AssertionError: expected Error: --device-code cannot be combined w… to match object { Object (humanOutput) }
- Expected
+ Received
- {
-   "humanOutput": "--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.",
+ Error {
+   "message": "--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.",
  }
```

Open PR collision check (submission-day sweep, 2026-11-13): scanned the 60 most recent open PRs plus keyword searches (`device-code`, `throwExpectedCliError`, `expected-cli-error`, `failure-output`, `models auth login`) and compared changed-file lists. #190482 and #198294 also touch `src/cli/models-cli.ts`, but their hunks (fallbacks-list `--agent` rejection near L422; `withModelsRuntime` near L38) are disjoint from this import/guard change and merge cleanly; #191233 and #191237 are sibling per-site fixes of the same anti-pattern in `security-cli.ts` / `worktrees-cli.ts`; #184579 is a headless device-code feature in the commands layer, not the CLI registration guard. No open PR touches `failure-output.ts` or `expected-cli-error.ts`, and the defect is still present on current `origin/main`.

What was not tested: local lint and typecheck. The repo wrapper rejects this worktree's symlinked `node_modules` ("Declaration input escapes checkout"), and the direct oxlint binary fails loading the config's JS plugin because the shared install's `eslint-plugin-solid` peer-hash symlink is stale. Both lanes were attempted; the change is byte-identical to the canonical pattern already compiling on main (the import line matches seven sibling `src/cli` files; the call shape matches `dns-cli.ts`), so lint/type verification is left to CI on this head.

prs.title: fix(ui): Control UI freezes in WebKit when a picker replaces an opening menu
prs.body:
Related: #196820

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI freezes in Safari and the macOS app when one menu or picker opens while another anchored menu is still opening and the layout changes. One example is opening the sidebar Agent menu, then quickly toggling Home and opening a settings picker. Scrolling still works, but nothing else responds until the app reloads.

## User Impact

User impact: switching quickly between overlays in WebKit no longer freezes the Control UI. The one visible difference: an overlay that had flipped to fit the viewport may return to its default side during its 100–200 ms fade-out.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a surface in an exclusive group (here the opening Agent menu) closes because another one opens, WebKit keeps re-resolving the closing surface's `position-try-fallbacks` and never finishes style resolution. Every later style flush hangs the page: our `getAnimations()` calls, and also WebKit's own rendering update. A closing surface is only fading out, so it no longer needs fallbacks. `overlay.css` now sets `position-try-fallbacks: none` on any surface with `data-phase="closing"`. It uses `!important` because several surfaces declare their own fallback lists with more specific selectors. The rule is in `overlay.css`, which shadow-hosted overlays inline as well.

Chromium was unaffected. The rule applies in every engine to keep overlay behavior the same across browsers.

## Evidence

- **New regression test.** `ui/src/e2e/overlay-menu-swap-webkit.e2e.test.ts` replays the swap in Playwright WebKit through the real Control UI and mock Gateway, in the same frame the Agent menu reaches the top layer. Without the fix it fails both times with "WebKit stopped answering after the menu swap". With the fix it passes 4 of 4. It's registered in the CI `webkitSuites` list and in `test/scripts/ci-ui-browser-dependencies.test.ts`, which passes 7 of 7.
- **System WebKit (macOS 27.2, WebKit 22625.2.8.11.9, the engine the Mac app uses).** A WKWebView harness ran the production Control UI build. The same sequence hung 3 of 3 before the fix and 0 of 3 after, at three timings and with both the real Home button and the Home toggle event. A randomized fuzz run (one seed, 8 tries) hung 5 of 8 before and 0 of 8 with the rule. The hung process's stack matches the user's four freeze samples: `Element::getAnimations` → `Document::resolveStyle`, with `TreeResolver::resolve` repeating `invalidateForResumingAnchorPositionedElementResolution`.
- **Existing overlay coverage.**
  - Chromium browser lane (overlay anchor, overlay lifecycle, popover, overlay style, menu navigation): 113 passed.
  - WebKit browser lane (select picker, sidebar rail and Agent menus, menu surface, tooltip): 88 passed.
- **Changed-file checks.** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passes. I skipped the dead-export scan, because it fails on files this branch doesn't touch (`scripts/perf/transcript-facts-backfill-stress-preload.mjs`, `extensions/workboard/src/store-evidence.ts`).
- **Bundle size.** `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` passes against the parent commit: total CSS raw +59 B, within the 64 B allowance. The first CI run failed this check at +70 B, so the selector is now `[data-phase="closing"]` without the class. The +423 B JS gzip difference CI reported came out as −202 B locally, so it is build variance.
- **Review.** Codex autoreview of the branch came back `scoped-clean` at P0.

Screenshots (Playwright WebKit, mock data):

| Before: last frame painted, then frozen | After: the swap completes |
| --- | --- |
| ![Agent menu open; the UI stops repainting after Home and the font picker are clicked](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f6cf06d-117c-4468-82b6-66f9c4bde47f) | ![Agent menu closed, Home panel open, UI responsive](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31ea5d41-277a-4ef9-87eb-a604451669e4) |

A frozen page can't paint a new frame, so "before" shows the frame it freezes on. In "after", the font picker's menu is open below the fold after the layout shift; the test asserts that state.

**Gaps**
- **Not yet in the installed app.** I haven't run the fix in the installed Mac app; the system-WebKit harness uses the same engine and production build.
- **Theme-switch freeze not reproduced.** The issue's freeze during a theme switch fits the same pattern: a `getAnimations()` call from the overlay close path in a microtask. I didn't reproduce that path separately.
- **Not reported to WebKit yet.** I haven't filed a WebKit bug; I don't have a reproduction without OpenClaw's own code yet.

prs.title: fix(cli): surface the capability inspect remedy in --json failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw capability inspect --name bogus --json` exits 1 and prints only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` plus ``[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.`` on stderr, so a script or agent driving the CLI is told nothing about the mistake; the actual reason, `Unknown capability: bogus`, is trapped in the stdout JSON envelope. Without `--json` the same command does print the reason.

This change routes that one check through the CLI's expected-failure owner, so both output modes print the remedy on stderr.

- Problem: the unknown-capability check threw a plain `Error`, which the root failure renderer treats as "the CLI command failed", while the text path had already printed the message locally
- Solution: throw `ExpectedCliError` through the existing `throwExpectedCliError()` helper, the same owner every other argument guard in this command group uses
- What changed: one throw site in `src/cli/capability-cli.ts`; the existing `capability metadata` test case now also asserts the unknown-id rejection type
- What did NOT change: the message text, the exit code, the stdout JSON envelope, and every other capability command

## Why This Change Was Made

The root renderer (`src/cli/failure-output.ts`) prints the producer's own remedy for expected failures and the generic "command failed / run doctor" pair for everything else. `runCommandWithRuntime` prints the message locally only when JSON mode is off, which is why the two lanes disagree for this check today.

#198471 converted this command group's argument guards to `throwExpectedCliError()` and kept runtime failures on the generic path; validating `--name` against the capability table is an argument check, so this site belongs with the ones already converted. Fixing it at the producer reuses the existing owner instead of adding a second rendering rule, and keeps the machine-readable envelope byte-identical.

Alternatives considered and rejected: special-casing the string in the root renderer (duplicate policy, grows the cold path); leaving it as-is because `--json` consumers can read stdout (the remedy then stays invisible in the stream that carries errors, and the text lane keeps contradicting it).

Risk is limited to this command's failure formatting. No schema, config, state, or exit-code change; nothing else reaches this throw.

## User Impact

- `openclaw capability inspect --name <id> --json` now prints `Unknown capability: <id>` on stderr alongside the unchanged JSON envelope, so a mistyped or unsupported capability id is self-explanatory in pipelines and agent logs
- Text output is unchanged, including for a valid id and for `capability list`
- No new flags, config keys, or documentation changes are needed

## Evidence

Two arms, two lanes, shipped source entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`) against an isolated state directory, no mocks. BASE is `origin/main` at `94cc426fb0b`; HEAD is this branch.

| Case | Before (`94cc426fb0b`) | After (this head) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capability inspect --name bogus` — stderr | `Unknown capability: bogus` (271 B) | `Unknown capability: bogus` (271 B, unchanged) |
| `capability inspect --name bogus --json` — stderr | `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` + doctor hint (324 B) | `Unknown capability: bogus` (271 B) |
| `capability inspect --name bogus --json` — stdout | 104 B envelope with the message | 104 B envelope, byte-identical |
| `capability inspect --name image.edit --json` — stdout | 497 B, exit 0 | 497 B, exit 0 (control unchanged) |
| `capability list` — stdout | 3256 B, exit 0 | 3256 B, exit 0 (control unchanged) |

BASE, text lane — the remedy is visible:

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts capability inspect --name bogus
Unknown capability: bogus
$ echo $?
1
```

BASE, `--json` lane — stderr loses it, only stdout carries it:

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts capability inspect --name bogus --json
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts capability inspect --name bogus --json 2>/dev/null
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Unknown capability: bogus"
  }
}
```

HEAD, `--json` lane — the same remedy now reaches stderr, envelope unchanged:

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts capability inspect --name bogus --json
Unknown capability: bogus
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts capability inspect --name bogus --json 2>/dev/null
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Unknown capability: bogus"
  }
}
```

Regression test, folded into the existing `it.each(["list", "inspect"])` case in `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` (net −1 test line, no new file):

```text
# unfixed source, new assertion only
× capability cli > queries capability metadata through inspect
AssertionError: expected Error: exit 1 to be an instance of ExpectedCliError

# fixed source
vitest run src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  117 passed (117)
```

Sibling suites that touch the same renderer and command group, all green on HEAD:

```text
vitest run src/cli/capability-cli.help.test.ts src/cli/capability-cli.lazy.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  7 passed (7)

vitest run src/cli/failure-output.test.ts src/cli/failure-output.contention.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  26 passed (26)
```

Open PR collision check: re-run against the submission-day open-PR snapshot, both by changed file and by keyword (`capability`, `ExpectedCliError`); no open PR touches `src/cli/capability-cli.ts`, `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`, or `src/cli/failure-output.ts`. The nearest family members in review (#198345, #196073, #191233, #197254, #198333) change other command groups with zero file overlap.

What was not tested: no Windows or macOS run, and no real Gateway (this command reads only the local capability table). The repository lint binary could not resolve its JS plugin in the isolated worktree, so `oxlint` was not run locally; formatting was verified with the repo formatter on both changed files.

Related: #198471 converted the sibling argument guards in this command group to the same owner; this is the remaining `--name` check it left on the generic path.

prs.title: perf(build): emit tsdown declarations in one native compiler command-line pass
prs.body:
## Problem

`write-unified-entry-dts` is the slowest step of a full build (~2 min on a 32-core Mac). The native declaration emitter routes every compiler read through the TypeScript 7 API's filesystem callbacks and forces `singleThreaded` emit. A plain `tsgo` pass over the same roots emits the same declarations in 17-27 s in parallel, versus 44-52 s single-threaded.

## Solution

- tsdown declaration builds run one `tsgo -p <leaf config> --listFiles` pass. The leaf config sits beside its base, so `${configDir}`, relative overrides and default type roots keep the compiler's interpretation; the default type roots are bounded to the checkout.
- Emit is parallel when `stableTypeOrdering` is on (the unified build sets it), otherwise single-threaded as before. The readonly-modifier race that motivated `singleThreaded` does not occur with stable type ordering: 12 emits of the full declaration graph (10 parallel at load 60-89, 2 single-threaded) produced 15,803 `.d.ts` files with one combined hash.
- Inputs come from `--listFiles`. The checkout boundary is now a post-check: every file the compiler read must be physically inside the checkout, and escaped inputs are reported before type errors.
- The writer's cache key now covers every `package.json` and `tsconfig*.json` plus `pnpm-lock.yaml`, because the command line does not report consulted manifests or failed resolution probes.
- API baselines (`diagnostics: "declarations"`, sometimes a historical compiler) keep the API path unchanged.

### Behavior changes (intentional, pinned by tests)

1. **Parent-install shadowing now fails loudly.** An optional SDK relative import that reaches a parent-directory `node_modules` used to be hidden by the virtual filesystem; it now fails with `Declaration input escapes checkout: <path>`. Test: `fails closed when optional SDK relative imports reach a parent install`.
2. **A parent-directory package link that resolves back into the checkout now builds.** The compiler reports the real path it read, which is checkout content, so the output is correct; the old path refused the outside spelling. Test: `builds through a parent package link that resolves back inside the checkout`.

Test rewrites: receipts no longer list consulted `package.json` files; the directory-alias test now proves that editing such a manifest re-keys the cache (`cache miss`). The cold-sibling build-order test sequences on the compiler subprocess instead of patching `Program.prototype.emitToString`.

## Impact

Full cache-off `pnpm build`, one earlier run each at load 36-45: `write-unified-entry-dts` 2m 4.7s -> 1m 20.3s, `tsdown-packages` 59.9 s -> 32.7 s, total 6m 27s -> 5m 24s. A 2-round alternating measurement at low load is running and will be added here.

## Evidence

- Earlier full build: 403 `.d.ts` files, 0 differing from main; the other 10 differing dist files are build identity (stamps, build info, Control UI service worker and maps).
- Tests: `native-declaration-boundary`, `tsdown-declaration-resolution`, `native-declaration-subprocess`, `extension-boundary-cache`; `tsgo` on `tsconfig.scripts.json` and `test/tsconfig.json`.
- Pending here: 2-round alternating timings, byte-identical `.d.ts`/dist proof on this head, local ClawSweeper.

The boundary tests are in the declaration-boundary owner's area; requesting their review for the two behavior changes.

prs.title: fix: queued follow-ups drop the implicit reply target
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
-->

Closes #142268

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Queued follow-up answers on resolver-less channels (Telegram after restart, no live dispatcher) dropped the implicit reply target, so `reply_to_message_id` was missing.

This PR restores that injection for same-channel external/legacy turns. It does **not** claim ordinary overlapping-turn parity through a live Telegram Test Server run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued follow-up delivery already stores `messageId` / `originatingReplyToId` at admission. Payload resolution only applied reply tags and never ran the same implicit-injection helper the live path uses.

Queued payloads now go through `resolveReplyThreadingPayloads`. Implicit `currentMessageId` is injected only for resolver-less channels, with the same origin/provenance exclusions as `routeReply` (same-channel external or legacy user turns). Channels that own `resolveReplyTransport` keep correlation at `routeReply`, so empty/`replyToId` opt-outs survive. Restart-sentinel still keeps `originatingReplyToId`. Explicit `replyToId` still wins. `replyToMode` `off` / `first` / `all` stay authoritative.

## User Impact

On resolver-less transports, queued follow-up answers reply to the triggering same-channel message. Cross-channel and internal/inter-session IDs are not forwarded. Channels with a transport resolver still decide correlation at final routing.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. Head SHA: `c6f38a93c8f7f9266efe7d3b39dbfd1aa799494b`. Marker: `PROOF_OK_c6f38a93`.

Focused Vitest after this revision (`test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts`): `followup-delivery.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.channel.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts` + `followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts` + `followup-turn-admission.test.ts` — **137 passed**.

Coverage:

- same-channel queued `messageId` still injects `replyToId` on resolver-less channels
- Discord-origin / Slack-destination IDs are withheld at decision time
- inter-session child announcements stay unthreaded
- restart-sentinel keeps `originatingReplyToId`
- explicit `replyToId` survives excluded implicit IDs
- empty `replyToId` opt-out survives decision and delivery through the real channel resolver
- decision-to-delivery matrix matches those exclusions through the real channel resolver
- core tests use a fixture channel; they no longer import `extensions/qa-channel`

Sabotage: switching decision injection back to unguarded `resolveFollowupCurrentMessageId` turns the foreign-channel and inter-session tests red.

Runtime observation on `ba68eaeb` used the real Gateway + Telegram transport after restart and recorded the queued answer referencing message 11. That remains the dispatcher-less recovery proof. Telegram Test Server E2E for ordinary overlap was **not** rerun (no Convex QA broker credentials on this fork).

## Maintainer refresh — September 14, 2026

Refreshed onto `82a9bef596011a6145d7f639d9773ff5e7267f7d`, preserving the original patch and contributor authorship. Current candidate: `6d592e236f8d40d33c911391ad795ed59062b439`.

Fresh review exposed an empty-target regression on channels without a transport resolver. The shared threading owner now distinguishes an absent reply target from `replyToId: ""`; the latter remains an explicit opt-out. Inline explicit-reply directives still override that implicit-threading opt-out. This is an owner-level condition change, not a follow-up-specific workaround.

Verification:
- Added regressions failed on the pre-repair candidate: **3 failed, 46 passed**.
- Repaired candidate: **183 passed across 7 suites**, covering queued delivery, channel boundaries, admission/provenance, resolver delegation, shared threading, empty/false opt-outs, inline override, first-reply slot accounting, and deduplication.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.channel.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-admission.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-plumbing.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-threading.test.ts`
- `git diff --check` passed. The repair adds one net production line (an explanatory comment) and 61 test lines. Full changed-surface static checks and hosted CI are tracked separately; this section does not claim they have completed.
- This is deterministic owner/channel-boundary proof, not new authenticated live-channel proof.

Review adjudication: the fresh autoreview returned four reports, not a scoped-clean result. The index-only empty-target finding is resolved in the committed candidate. Two resolver-owned issues were verified as unchanged baseline behavior and recorded as follow-ups: **resolver-owned empty/false opt-out consistency** and **separating explicit inline current-message resolution from implicit correlation policy**. The reported QA dedupe mismatch was not established: that resolver returns a native message reference without `threadId: null`, while the dedupe owner treats `replyToId` as a conversation thread only for the explicit-null transport contract. No new unresolved P0–P2 regression was independently confirmed in this candidate.

prs.title: test(codex): prompt hook test fails on main after the collaboration policy change
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Codex test "applies prompt hooks once per build without duplicating continuity input" fails on `main`, so pull requests whose CI selects the Codex extension shard are red for a reason they did not cause.

## User Impact

User impact: none. This changes one test file.

## Why This Change Was Made

#187856 made managed collaboration guidance part of the immutable thread policy (`buildCodexThreadGenericInstructions` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-requests.ts`). The guidance now sits between the hook's system prompt and the plugin-injected system context.

That order is intended. Refreshable content, including plugin context, has always followed the immutable policy so the stable prompt prefix does not change, and #187856 regenerated the canonical prompt snapshots with it. The test was missed.

The test pinned the system prompt and the plugin contexts as adjacent, which is not what it is about, and its `toContain` never checked "once". It now asserts that the system prompt and the plugin contexts each appear exactly once, in that order.

## Evidence

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.bounded-continuity.test.ts`

| Tree | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `61405c9`, parent of #187856 | 2 passed |
| `35b544c` (#187856) and `main` at `009fcd9` | 1 failed: the collaboration block sits between the system prompt and the plugin context |
| This branch | 2 passed |
| This branch, with `thread-requests.ts` changed to join the refreshable instructions twice | 1 failed: "expected [ …(3) ] to have a length of 2". The previous assertion passed in that case. |

`oxfmt` and `oxlint --type-aware` pass on the file. The test file was read in full; nothing else in it changed.

Related: CI on #198489 hit this failure.

prs.title: fix: finish Gateway shutdown after plugin scope retirement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown refusing memory and channel cleanup when it inherits an expired plugin invocation scope, and waiting for the hard deadline after cleanup has already rejected and settled.

## User Impact

Memory, channel transports, and shutdown hooks close under the Gateway lifecycle owner. A settled cleanup failure wakes the run loop and bounds any remaining process tail after CLI finalization, without using SIGKILL. Pending persistence and genuinely retained resources still keep their hard deadline. Restart markers and transcripts keep their existing settlement order.

## Why This Change Was Made

The close boundary cleared the current plugin call but left its enclosing invocation scope attached. Clear both at the owner boundary, including the full close prelude and hooks. The cleanup owner now notifies the loop when an asynchronous rejection settles, replacing a later failure check that could not wake the sleeping loop.

Deadline retirement follows retained resources rather than a failed result. Generic failed status `1` uses default SIGUSR2 after the existing one-second settled tail watchdog; SIGTERM would hide failure from an on-failure supervisor. Special supervisor exit codes remain report-only. Production code grows by 7 lines (+29/-22) to carry the owner notification and failure signal; no new config, cache, or schema.

## Evidence

- Three regressions fail on exact base `0b7cd35571e7cbfb7544305379c7c4a1dac26b03`: expired-scope memory/four-channel close; settled failed close with a leaked handle; rejected log cleanup leaving the loop asleep. The fixed real Gateway case also verifies all four shutdown hooks.
- 214 focused CLI tests and 4 Gateway memory/channel/hook tests pass. Process tests preserve pending-cleanup deadlines, special exit codes, restart custody, and finalizer durability.
- Build passed. `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD` completed; an introduced unused test import was removed and core typecheck re-passed. All remaining failures are the two exact-parent dead exports listed below. Targeted lint/format and other selected guards passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings on the final candidate. Its earlier failure-status finding was fixed before the final review.
- Built Gateway pilot on synthetic 35 GiB SQLite, 5,026 stored sessions, and 62,000 workspace files / 1.1 GB: 16 streaming chats, 2 active exec children, 4 cron runs, 4 pending RPCs, and four mock channel transports. Baseline and candidate exited naturally after SIGTERM, stopped all four transports, left no child alive, and persisted/resumed all 18 sessions exactly once with durable partial text/tool receipts and cron outcomes. Pilot stop times were 3.14 s / 2.60 s; differing host load means this is not a speedup claim.

The serial campaign passed all 12 runs: two baseline A/A controls, then five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs. Every run exited naturally with code 0, stopped all four mock transports, settled both children, recovered all 18 sessions exactly once, and preserved partial text, tool receipts, and cron outcomes.

| Metric (five samples per head) | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 | Baseline range | Candidate range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SIGTERM to process exit | 2,073 / 2,796 ms | 2,053 / 2,190 ms | 1,379–2,796 ms | 1,636–2,190 ms |
| Gateway-close owner | 1,021 / 1,484 ms | 1,096 / 1,324 ms | 131–1,484 ms | 215–1,324 ms |
| Main-thread CPU after signal | 750 / 997 ms | 632 / 737 ms | 693–997 ms | 626–737 ms |
| Sampled main-isolate allocation | 158.6 / 166.5 MiB | 155.0 / 171.1 MiB | 156.3–166.5 MiB | 153.8–171.1 MiB |

p95 is the nearest-rank maximum with n=5. The A/A controls were 9,353 / 2,409 ms to exit, 1,432 / 813 ms CPU, and 176.5 / 172.4 MiB sampled allocation. That spread prevents a speedup claim. The Gateway-close median increased 74 ms and allocation p95 increased 4.6 MiB; both are reported rather than hidden. The measured benefit is removal of the reproduced failure/idle-wait paths, with normal loaded durability preserved.

Rerunnable workload: `TMPDIR=<safe-synthetic-root> node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/shutdown-loaded-measure.ts --checkout <built-head> --fixture <shutdown-loaded-fixture-root> --output <new-directory> --channel-transports --allocation`. Allocation sampling uses 32 KiB intervals and includes collected objects. CPU/allocation cover the main isolate, not workers or children. A separate candidate CPU profile was captured with `--cpu-profile`.

Evidence limits: mock transports exercise the real registry/channel lifecycle, not the bundled Discord/Slack/ClickClack/X adapters. The expired-scope injection establishes a failure mechanism, not the provenance of a production signal's scope. Large-fixture storage is a temporary APFS sparse image on APFS; Linux/btrfs proof is unavailable because the configured remote provider could not allocate without its credential.

### Existing main regressions

Both unused-export failures reproduce on the clean exact parent with `node --import tsx scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts`; neither file is changed here:

| Export | Introducing commit / PR |
| --- | --- |
| `prepareTranscriptFactsBackfillStress` | `72f90dde293d5e99d6852545a0d7b2590a5aa56e` / #194519 |
| `MAX_COMPLETION_CLAIMS` | `c1ca2d7b14c6de87939ec0e1207808cf1816d434` / #197471 |

The existing pending-close process test also contained a main-thread file-write interception made ineffective by the worker logging migration in `5358d05ca2c1dc8c8a4770704a03c1a8f89b5f78` (#197586). That assertion failed on the exact parent. This PR removes the obsolete interception while keeping the real pending-close watchdog test; accepted logging writes remain covered by the finalization process suite.

auto_merge.commit_message:
Run the full Gateway close under its lifecycle owner's plugin context so an
expired requesting invocation cannot refuse memory, channel or hook cleanup.
Wake the loop when retained cleanup rejects, and retire deadline watchdogs
once no resource remains pending. Bound generic failed exits after CLI
finalization with a failure signal while preserving special supervisor codes.

Keep pending persistence, retained resources, restart markers and transcript
settlement with their existing owners. Add regressions that fail on the base
and extend the loaded shutdown fixture with four synthetic channel transports.

prs.title: fix(ui): Control UI hides the bounded-context warning for channel conversations
prs.body:
Closes #181772

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI hides the bounded-context warning that channel users receive.

## User Impact

Control UI shows the same warning as a System notice when you watch a channel conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bounded-seed host now publishes `context_bounded` to the run event bus before its advisory channel callback. The Gateway forwards that event to authorized session viewers, and the UI reuses its system-warning notice. A pane that started the run keeps its existing status reply, so nothing shows twice.

## Evidence

Real in-process Gateway and real Chrome Control UI. A `context_bounded` event is emitted for a hidden channel run while the pane views the session. The page text is checked for the warning.

Before (base):

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ericcurtin/openclaw/34f154c1914a0e7307f19a47fe454fc8eca275e1/before.png)

After:

![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ericcurtin/openclaw/34f154c1914a0e7307f19a47fe454fc8eca275e1/after.png)

- Page contains the warning: base `false`, fix `true`.
- Gateway, host-seed and UI tests are red on base and green with the fix.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt pass.
- The screenshot harness emitted the event directly. The recorded parent proof below exercises a real Codex bounded-seed run; the refreshed head retains those production blobs. Reload persistence is outside this live-warning change.

### Parent behavior proof and refreshed baseline

The real behavior proof ran against signed parent `4e4a2208b3bb7954430860fd4f009edbecbcc935`, tree `b9800b4319cb384f829eb88e9ee06be9f27630cd`. The current hosted head is signed `b723dbb038b5f371f6e2863fb31bfa117a317d07`, tree `99a716af01f189cf34e15cd6aeed447bab2ed8ee`. Its first parent retains the contributor commits, host event repair, test formatting, and prior one-line picker assertion correction. Its second parent is official main `ccf468fd4705fe6250257736a650698d39d639b4`. Main had independently fixed that stale picker test in PR #198546 with `role="option"` and a stronger selected-row check. The native one-file conflict resolution selected main's exact test blob, so the current PR diff has only the seven warning-fix paths. Every warning-fix production blob is unchanged from the parent proof. This is inherited behavior evidence, not an execution on the current head. A secretless AWS run used native Codex `0.164.0`, a mock model provider, QA channel, real Gateway, and authenticated Control UI browser. The single browser test passed; the selected viewer saw one System warning, the channel received its warning and final reply, native model input omitted the old transcript marker, and SQLite retained that old history. Focused host, Gateway, and UI tests and the private QA build also passed.

```json
{"verdict":"pass","candidateTree":"b9800b4319cb384f829eb88e9ee06be9f27630cd","servedUiDocumentHash":"3e8f354c1cc2c042df7f34461b1d84070fa3c1c0c7d20b1587e996c57aaf4009","servedUiEntryHash":"25dd521c68b67e516b03a553b26f7fa0d2080d20029ae4083b1ac2a72ae84c88","hostEvent":true,"viewerSystemWarning":true,"channelWarning":true,"nativeInputBounded":true,"oldHistoryRetained":true}
```

The browser test process exited 0 and reported 1/1 passed. Two configured reporters printed the same verdict twice, so a post-test script that expected one printed line exited 1. Independent review accepted the typed verdict and a clean post-run tree check; the AWS lease was released with cleanup complete. Previous exact-head CI on `5b523e01c5c65fbed425b71193fec5704c2829e0` passed all 74 jobs, including UI and PostgreSQL conformance. Native merge admission then found the independent main picker-test change; the signed baseline refresh resolved that sole conflict while keeping the seven warning-fix blobs byte-identical. The queued same-input main comparator never ran, so no main-red claim is made. Fresh CI and reviews for `b723dbb038b5f371f6e2863fb31bfa117a317d07` remain merge gates.
