prs.title: fix(macos): keep Apple Event permission probes off the cooperative thread pool
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On 2026.9.3 the macOS app periodically goes dead while still running: the paired node shows **offline** in the Gateway dashboard although the Mac is on and the TCP session to the Gateway is still ESTABLISHED (32 KB of unread bytes sitting in the receive queue), the menu bar item stops opening its menu, and the process ignores SIGTERM (needs SIGKILL). It "fixes itself" only when the app is relaunched.

## Root cause

`AppleEventPermissionProbe.state` runs the blocking `AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget` in `Task.detached`, which schedules onto the Swift cooperative thread pool. The call blocks until Terminal answers the Apple Event handshake (and, when `askUserIfNeeded`, until the user answers tccd). `MacNodeModeCoordinator` re-probes permissions on every refresh trigger (`UserDefaults.didChangeNotification`, config change, permissions change, app activation, reconnect probe), so a slow Terminal under system load lets probes stack up.

A 3 s `sample` of the wedged process showed **all 16 cooperative threads** parked here, main thread idle:

```
DispatchQueue_18: com.apple.root.user-initiated-qos.cooperative
  closure #1 in AppleEventPermissionProbe.state(askUserIfNeeded:)
    AppleEventPermissionProbe.determineTerminalPermission(askUserIfNeeded:)
      AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget
        _dispatch_semaphore_wait_slow
          semaphore_wait_trap
```

Terminal automation was already **granted** in TCC (`kTCCServiceAppleEvents ai.openclaw.mac → com.apple.Terminal = 2`), so this was not a pending prompt. Once the pool is exhausted nothing async in the app can run, including the gateway websocket receive and the status item, and any continuation the AE reply needs can never be scheduled.

## Fix

- Run the blocking probe on a dedicated `DispatchQueue` (concurrent, so a prompt is never queued behind a hung passive check), bridged with a `CheckedContinuation`, so it never pins a cooperative thread.
- Single-flight concurrent callers per `askUserIfNeeded` value through a small actor (`AppleEventPermissionProbeCoordinator`), so at most one probe blocks at a time regardless of how many refreshes fire.
- Bound passive (non-prompting) probes with a 10 s timeout that surfaces as `.failed(errAETimeout)` → capability `.unknown`, instead of hanging the caller. Prompting probes keep waiting on the user.

No change to call sites; `AppleEventPermissionProbe.live` and `TerminalAutomationPermission` keep their API.

## Evidence

- `concurrent passive checks share one blocking probe`: 32 concurrent passive `state` calls → exactly one `determine` call, all callers get the result.
- `a hung passive probe times out instead of blocking callers`: a `determine` that never returns yields `.failed(errAETimeout)` in ~200 ms with a 200 ms timeout.
- `interactive prompts are never timed out`.
- Existing suite unchanged and green (12/12).
- Live observation, 2026-09-09: reproduced twice on the same Mac (2026.9.3 release build). Both times `netstat -anv -p tcp` showed the OpenClaw-owned socket to the Gateway ESTABLISHED with 32,778 and 52,617 bytes in Recv-Q, and `sample <pid> 2` showed 16 and 17 frames in `AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget`. The second occurrence started within 60 s of a Gateway restart, i.e. on the reconnect refresh path. `pkill -9` + relaunch cleared it each time.

`swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` ✅, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` ✅, `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` ✅ (Xcode 26.6 / Swift 6.3.3).

## Review follow-up (revision 3)

Both P2 findings are addressed:

- **Retain the in-flight operation after a caller times out.** The coordinator now keeps the operation in `inFlight` until the native call actually returns. Caller deadlines are measured from the operation's start, so once the deadline has passed later passive callers answer `errAETimeout` immediately and never enqueue a second native call. When the target replies, the tracked operation drains and the next probe runs fresh. Covered by the new test `timed-out callers never enqueue a second native call behind the hung one` (second caller answers in < 150 ms with `callCount == 1`, operation still in flight; after release the next probe runs and `callCount == 2`).
- **Synchronize overlapping callers before releasing the test probe.** The concurrency test now waits until all 32 callers are parked on the coordinator (`waiterCount == 32`) before releasing, and `BlockingProbeGate.release()` opens the gate permanently so every native call a test started completes during cleanup.

The probe queue is concurrent so an interactive prompt is never queued behind a hung passive check.

## After-fix native proof

Debug build of this branch on a second Mac (macOS 26.4.1, Xcode 26.6), run in a throwaway app profile pointed at a remote Gateway URL that refuses connections (so every reconnect attempt builds a manifest and evaluates permissions). Terminal.app, the Apple Event target, was frozen with `SIGSTOP` so the probe could not get a reply, then resumed with `SIGCONT`. The passive probe returned `noErr` on this host: its TCC database already holds an allowed `kTCCServiceAppleEvents` row for bundle id `ai.openclaw.mac` → `com.apple.Terminal`, which the debug build shares, so recovery shows as a normal `returned 0`.

| Phase | `sample` probe frames | Cooperative-pool frames in the probe | `openclaw-mac status` (control socket) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0 | 0 | ok |
| Terminal frozen, 55 s | 1, on `DispatchQueue: ai.openclaw.apple-event-permission (concurrent)` | 0 | ok |
| Terminal resumed, 50 s later | 0 | 0 | ok |

Unified log (`ai.openclaw`/`AppleEventPermissionProbe`), timestamps relative to the freeze:

```
-27 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.172922083 seconds
-19 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.033881875 seconds
-10 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.208797417 seconds
  0 s     Terminal.app frozen (SIGSTOP)
+17 s  E  probe ask=false timed out after 10.0 seconds; operation retained
+58 s     Terminal.app resumed (SIGCONT)
+58 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 50.992712958 seconds
+66 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.032903625 seconds
+97 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.137408166 seconds
```

No second native call started while the first was hung (the only lines between the freeze and the resume are the single timeout), the retained call returned as soon as Terminal answered, and the probes after it ran fresh.

The app answered its control socket throughout, kept exactly one blocked thread (on the private queue, never the cooperative pool), released it when Terminal answered, and quit within 1 s of `SIGTERM` afterwards. On the release build the same condition ends with 13 to 17 cooperative threads blocked, a dead status menu, and `SIGTERM` ignored (openclaw/openclaw#146030).

Filtered test run (`swift test --filter AppleEventPermissionTests`, private HOME, throwaway profile, `--skip-build`): 13 tests, 0 failures. Full native suite left to the `macos-swift` CI job per `apps/macos/AGENTS.md`.

### Signed-bundle run (signing provenance)

The run above used the bare SwiftPM debug binary (ad-hoc signed). Repeated on the same Mac with a full `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` bundle of head `621a4a4d8`, signed through `scripts/codesign-mac-app.sh` with a real Apple Development certificate and kept at the fixed path the permissions guide asks for (`<checkout>/dist/OpenClaw.app`). Provenance, identity details redacted:

```
Identifier=ai.openclaw.mac.debug
Format=app bundle with Mach-O thin (arm64)
CodeDirectory v=20500 flags=0x10000(runtime)
Authority=Apple Development: <redacted>
Authority=Apple Worldwide Developer Relations Certification Authority
Authority=Apple Root CA
TeamIdentifier=<redacted, set>
Sealed Resources version=2 rules=13 files=42384
codesign --verify --deep --strict: OK
```

`ai.openclaw.mac.debug` has no Automation grant on this Mac, so the passive probe's real answer is `-1744` (`errAEEventWouldRequireUserConsent`), returned without a prompt once Terminal answers. Same procedure (throwaway profile, refusing Gateway URL, Terminal `SIGSTOP` for 55 s, then `SIGCONT`):

| Phase | `sample` probe frames | Cooperative-pool frames in the probe | `openclaw-mac status` (control socket) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0 | 0 | ok |
| Terminal frozen, 55 s | 1, on the private queue | 0 | ok |
| Terminal resumed, 50 s later | 0 | 0 | ok |

```
-28 s  I  probe ask=false returned -1744 after 0.207445334 seconds
  0 s     Terminal.app frozen (SIGSTOP)
+14 s  E  probe ask=false timed out after 10.0 seconds; operation retained
+58 s     Terminal.app resumed (SIGCONT)
+58 s  I  probe ask=false returned -1744 after 54.768811875 seconds
```

One blocked native call, no second call queued behind it, bounded caller wait, control socket answering throughout, the retained call returning the moment Terminal resumed, and the app quitting within 1 s of `SIGTERM` afterwards.

## Release note

Fix the macOS app wedging (node offline while TCP alive, menu bar item unresponsive, ignores SIGTERM) when concurrent Terminal Automation permission probes exhausted the Swift cooperative thread pool.

Diagnosed and written with Claude Code: https://claude.ai/code/session_014TmTvgdhcL7bPCwg3f8B6G
Review follow-up, after-fix proof, and this revision: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RW45HgmUaFSiM4DSZGrVSp

prs.title: fix(cli): stop interrupted exec approval grants list reads
prs.body:
## Problem

`openclaw approvals grants list` issues the `exec.approval.grants.list` RPC without an abort signal. A Ctrl+C during the request waits out the full gateway timeout, then prints a stale grants table after the command appears to have ended.

## Solution

Thread the command's AsyncWorkScope abort signal into the RPC and drop the result once the scope begins closing, matching the `get` (#198626) and `pending` (#198631) read fixes from the same parent.

To keep the CLI module under its line cap while the guard lands, the display helpers (`describeGrantState`, `escapeApprovalTextForTerminal`, id formatting, resolver formatting) move to a coherent sibling module `exec-approvals-display.ts`.

## Evidence

Discriminating test `prints no grants list that lands after Ctrl+C` on real remote node 24.18 vitest:

- **base** (PR-B head cli, no signal): `exec.approval.grants.list` settles after `beginClose`, stale table still printed → **FAIL** (31 passed / 1 failed)
- **head** (this PR): signal aborts the read, nothing printed → **PASS** (32 passed)

```
base:  × prints no grants list that lands after Ctrl+C
head:  ✓ prints no grants list that lands after Ctrl+C
```

## Precedent

#197815, #198254, #198626, #198631 — read-only CLI commands stop with the command.

prs.title: feat(macos): join an OpenClaw ID claw as a member with an invite
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves A member who picked a claw in the Mac app's OpenClaw ID sign-in hit a dead end ("Ask for an invite to "), and someone with only an invite link had no way to join from the Mac at all. ## User Impact An invited member can now join a claw from the Mac: sign in with OpenClaw ID, paste the owner's invite link, ask to join, and wait while an owner approves it in the Control UI's People. The Mac then opens the dashboard with the invite's role (operator or viewer). Members get **no node**: the assistant can't use the Mac's commands, screen or camera, and the native owner-only actions (tools toggle, Remove this Mac, recovery kit, approvals) are not shown. If an owner removes the member, the Mac shows "This Mac no longer has access to " and tells them to ask for a new invite. ## Why This Change Was Made This is the "mac: member invite join (no node)" step of the sign-in-first plan. It reuses the existing pieces instead of adding new ones: - **Protocol:** the Mac produces the same `InviteRedemption` as the browser loader (`claw-loader/src/loader/join.ts`): D self-signs `{claw_id, invite_id, account_id, device_pub, peer_key, label, proof, requested_at}` with the HMAC proof from `invites.ts`, and mails it to the Gateway through Discovery. Nothing on the Gateway, Control UI or Discovery changes. The owner approves in the existing People flow. - **Claw id:** an invitee can't read the claw's descriptor yet, so the Mac gets the claw id for the link's hostname from Discovery's existing `POST /v1/join-tickets` (the loader's join route), or from `listClaws` when the account is already a member. The id is not trusted: the proof covers it, and admission is verified against fp(R) from the link. - **Admission:** the Mac joins only when the claw's K_gw-signed snapshot lists its W as a member under the pinned root. The role comes from that verified snapshot. - **Pending:** the request (not the link secret) is saved before the redemption is sent, so closing the window or a lost response keeps the same keys, and reopening sign-in resumes the wait. Only a definite Discovery refusal or **Cancel request** deletes the keys. A request expires after seven days, but only after admission has been checked. - **Join completion and removal** go through the existing owners (`MacOpenClawIDJoinCompletion`, `MacOpenClawIDDeviceStore.remove`). For a member, a 404 from Discovery's descriptor read means the account no longer belongs to the claw, so it counts as removal. This only applies when the saved session is the member's own account. Another account's session is asked to sign in again instead. - **No deep link:** the invite link is an https claw URL that opens the browser loader; the app has no handler for it today, so this PR uses paste. "Open in OpenClaw for Mac" from the loader is a possible follow-up. Accepted limits: - A member can't remove their own Mac. The protocol lets only R or an owner device sign revocations, so Settings says to ask an owner. - An owner never sends a decline to the requester, so a declined request stays pending until the user cancels it or it expires. - Discovery's join-ticket call also issues a one-minute loader ticket, which the Mac doesn't use. ## Evidence - **Wire format:** `OpenClawIDMemberJoin.json` is generated from the TypeScript reference (`buildInviteLink`, `parseInviteFragment`, `deriveInviteProofKey`, `computeRedemptionProof`, `signStatement`, and checked with `verifyInviteRedemption`). The Swift redemption body is byte-identical, and both signatures verify. - **OpenClawKit** (`swift test --filter OpenClawID`, MacBook Pro): 55/55 pass. That includes link parsing, the join-ticket → redeem → pending → approved flow with a scripted Discovery, refusal of a claw under another root, and a member's hidden claw counted as removal. - Red/green: on the base `OpenClawIDDeviceRoute.swift`, the member case fails (`OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccountError(404)` thrown instead of `.notAdmitted`). It passes with the fix. - **macOS** (`swift build --build-system native --build-tests` + focused tests, MacBook Pro): 41/41 pass across 8 suites (`OnboardingOpenClawID*`, `OpenClawIDRemovalTests`, `DashboardOperatorRouteTests`, `MacNodeOpenClawIDSelectionStoreTests`, `OnboardingFirstRunTests`). New cases cover: - paste → request → pending → joined with role `viewer`, no node, `approvedWith: .invite`; no node description is ever requested; - resume after closing and cancel forgetting the keys; - another account not resuming someone else's request; - expiry only after the admission check; - a lost mailbox answer keeping the request while a Discovery 400 forgets it; - member removal copy. - **Checks:** `scripts/lint-swift.sh all` passes for Sources (pinned SwiftLint), `scripts/format-swift.sh all` reports 0 files to format, and `native:i18n:baseline` + `native:i18n:verify` pass (inventory updated). - **Review:** an independent review found three P2s, all fixed: keys deleted after an ambiguous send, an approved request discarded after seven days, and a wrong-account session misread as removal. - **Not yet run:** the live staging proof (an owner invites a second staging account, Josh joins on the Mac, then we confirm no node, the role and member removal). It is prepared and waits for approval to use staging. ### Device label (after #198575) Rebased on main after #198575 (member devices) landed. The redemption now carries the required `label`, the Mac's display name, the same ≤64-character label it already gives `bindDevice`. `OpenClawIDMemberJoin.json` was regenerated from main's protocol (`2c8ffdcfd7af`) and passes `verifyInviteRedemption`. The proof is unchanged because it doesn't cover `label`. The member-join tests now check that both the Swift fixture and the redemption sent through Discovery include the label. **Pending:** the Swift build and tests on this rebased head haven't run yet because the MacBook build host went offline. The results above are from the previous head. ### Screenshots (real SwiftUI/WebKit views, fixture data, rendered in the isolated render sandbox) **Before:** picking a member claw was a dead end, and the picker had no way in with an invite. **After:** the claw picker, invite entry, join request, waiting, and joined screens. **Settings and removal for a member:** no tools toggle, no Remove this Mac. 🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(agents): long sessions lose the prompt cache when a wake, subagent turn or replay changes sent bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long sessions lose their provider prompt cache in the middle of a session when a wake, subagent turn, silent reply, replayed history or a long transcript changes bytes that were already sent.

## User Impact

User impact: more warm turns read the provider cache instead of writing a new one, on every built-in transport. There is no config, schema or persisted-format change. The sent prefix is kept in Gateway memory only, so a rollback needs no data repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier fixes pinned one prompt input at a time (#197835, #197893, #197925, #198100). Each was correct, and each time the next input broke the same rule. This PR enforces the rule in one place instead:

- **One owner per session** (`session-prefix-owner.ts`) sends every foreground model request. It keeps the entries it already sent (by identity: role + timestamp, or tool-call id) and re-sends their exact bytes. Only new entries are appended. Upstream drift is absorbed and logged once per session (`[prompt-cache] re-derived history changed ...`), so each source can be found and removed later.
- **Closed rebuild list.** A series starts again only on a new route or system prompt (model/provider switch, compaction, `/new`, `/reset`), on a log that no longer extends the sent log by identity (compaction, reset), or on a declared rebuild: provider rejection repair, context-overflow truncation, idle pruning after cache expiry, or a tool-policy config change.
- **The tool set is frozen per series.** Wakes and handoffs build wider tool surfaces than user turns. Those tools are no longer added mid-series; tools a turn did not build stay listed and refuse their calls (existing pin stubs). Tool definitions (name, description, schema) stay as first sent until a rebuild; a tool-policy config change is a declared rebuild.
- **Commit on accept.** A request joins the series only after the provider accepted it, so a rejected request and its retry are not held to each other's bytes.
- **Silent replies stay in replay** (from draft #198183). Chat Completions and Bedrock merge adjacent user turns, so dropping a silent reply rewrote an already-sent user message.
- **Prompt series survives a bounded transcript window.** The series history id read the newest compaction entry from the loaded window. After the session outgrew the window, the id became null, the series restarted and the whole system prompt was re-rendered. It now falls back to the newest system-prompt checkpoint's history id.

<details>
<summary>Contract (one page, checked against provider docs)</summary>

- A request is `P + L`. `P` = request settings + tool definitions + system prompt, fixed when the series starts. `L` = model-visible messages; a request may only **append** to `L`. Cache markers are not part of the bytes.
- All four provider families chain `tools -> system -> messages` and need an exact prefix match. On Anthropic preserved-thinking models a changed earlier block can fail the prefix check; OpenAI drops reasoning items after a prefix change. So this is a correctness rule, not only a cost rule.
- Allowed in `P`: model/route/thinking/tool-choice settings; the session's tool definitions in fixed order; static instructions and workspace files **as read at series start**.
- Not allowed in `P`: clocks, per-turn trigger or provenance, the current run's tool grants, node presence, memory recall, exec/subagent status, delivery route.
- Mid-session changes ride `L` as update entries (in-history system message where supported, otherwise a user-role note).
- Rebuild points: new session (`/new`, `/reset`), compaction (incl. overflow recovery), model/provider switch, one repair after a provider rejects replayed history.
- Not rebuild points: exec/tool/subagent wakes, cron/heartbeat turns, inter-session sends, skill/file/memory edits, node changes, tool grants, silent replies, retries.
- Misses outside the contract (TTL expiry, minimum cacheable size, provider routing/isolation, provider-side thinking stripping, proxy account rotation) are measured separately and never attributed to OpenClaw bytes.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cause list from raw request bytes</summary>

Wire-byte diffs of consecutive requests from one production gateway, captured at the proxy (metadata only: first differing byte, structural path, usage; raw bodies deleted). 6,153 consecutive request pairs, 87 prefix breaks, 21.1M tokens written at breaks.

| Breaks | Tokens written | First changed part | Cause |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 16 | 7.0M | system: deferred tool schema list | tool list differs by turn kind (wake / UI turn / skills) |
| 15 + 2 + 1 + 1 | 4.4M | system: workspace / project context | workspace file re-read mid-session |
| 11 | 0.57M | earlier assistant tool-call id | two tool-call id rules disagree (side-question fork vs replay) |
| 9 | 2.2M | system: subagent "Rules" | per-turn subagent context text |
| 11 | 3.3M | earlier assistant message | tool calls dropped or turned into text on replay; aborted-turn repair; inserted text row |
| 3 | 0.46M | earlier user message | user entry re-projected |
| 3 + 2 | 1.5M | system: Tooling / deferred list text | tool list text |
| 3 | 0.36M | tool description | tool description changed |
| 7 + 3 | 1.2M | `messages[0]` | compaction (allowed) |

System and tool causes were already addressed on `main` by the pin (#197925, #198100) but not yet deployed on that gateway. Replay drift inside a session (dropped or converted tool calls, aborted-turn repair, re-projected entries) was not fixed on `main`; the owner absorbs it here, and the root fixes are listed below as not in this PR. The tool-call id flip is between a side-question fork and its parent, and this PR does not fix it (see below). The in-process `[prompt-cache]` detector reported most of these only as `systemPromptSuffix`, because it compares pre-translation messages.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Comparison with Pi and Hermes (same 11 scenarios on fake servers)</summary>

| | Pi (custom model ids) | Pi (Claude 5 path) | Hermes | OpenClaw `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefix owner | re-renders head on change (`collapseSystemMessages`) | in-history system messages | builds once, persists sent bytes, replays them | pin + deltas, history re-derived every attempt | pin + deltas + one owner of sent bytes |
| Breaks in 11 scenarios | tool add/remove, `/reload`, compaction | compaction | compaction, model switch | compaction, model switch | same as `main` on these scenarios |
| Production causes absorbed | – | – | – | system/tools | + replay drift inside the session (tool-call drop, re-projected entries) |

Hermes makes tool-set changes and context reloads unrepresentable mid-session; Pi absorbs them as append-only deltas only on its Claude-5 path. Neither re-reads context files per turn. The long-term shape (persist each entry's sent bytes, as Hermes does) is phase 2 below.

</details>

## Evidence

**Randomized invariant test** (new, `test/prompt-cache-prefix-randomized.<transport>.e2e.test.ts`): seeded 23-step journeys over 15 turn kinds (user, image input, image tool result, tool, parallel tools, thinking tool, exec wake, subagent, inter-session send, skill added, workspace edit, tool policy change, silent reply, model switch, compaction) through a real Gateway against fake servers for all five wire formats. Each request is canonicalized (cache markers removed) and must extend the previous request of the same session, except at the first request of a rebuild step. Same seeds on both builds; `main` = this branch's test commits on the same `main` base, without the fixes.

| Transport | `main` seed 1 | `main` seed 2 | `main` seed 3 | this PR (seeds 1-3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat Completions | pass | FAIL: tools grow on a subagent turn | FAIL: tools grow on a subagent turn | 3/3 pass |
| Anthropic Messages | FAIL: earlier image user turn re-projected | FAIL: tools grow on a subagent turn | FAIL: tools grow on a subagent turn | 3/3 pass |
| OpenAI Responses | pass | FAIL: tools grow on a subagent turn | FAIL: tools grow on a subagent turn | 3/3 pass |
| Google Generative AI | pass | FAIL: tool set changes on a subagent turn | FAIL: tool set changes on a subagent turn | 3/3 pass |
| Bedrock Converse | FAIL: silent reply merged into the next user turn | FAIL: silent reply merged into the next user turn | FAIL: earlier user turn rewritten on an exec wake | 3/3 pass |
| **Total** | **3/15** (seeds 1-3) | | | **15/15** |

`main` failures name their cause: `skills_read`/`skills_search` join the tool list on a subagent turn (all transports), a silent reply merged into the next user turn (Bedrock), and on current `main` an image user turn re-projected at the next request (Anthropic seed 1). The owner holds the series tool set and re-sends sent entries, so none of these reach the wire on this branch. Two `main` seeds and two seeds of this branch first hit a Gateway request timeout under host load (not a prefix result); they were rerun one at a time and the table shows the reruns.

The matrix ran on 234f349c. Later commits narrow a cast in `session-prompt-history-id.ts` (same behavior; the window regression test and Chat Completions seed 3, the seed that exercises that path, rerun on the final head) and change tests only: typing, and two unit tests that encoded the old behavior (a silent reply dropped before a user turn; a mid-series tool description change sent without a rebuild). The new randomized harness adds 615 net test lines; `config/test-lines-allocations/198410-prompt-cache-session-prefix-owner.txt` records the 215 lines over the allowance, because these journeys are the invariant gate that the earlier per-scenario prompt-cache tests did not provide.

**Real route** (full build of this head's runtime source, throwaway Gateway with an isolated state dir and scrubbed environment, one 12-step session: plain turn, read + parallel exec, background exec wake, inter-session send, skill added, workspace file edit, silent reply, subagent spawn + settle, `/compact`, two turns after compaction). Anthropic Messages (Claude Opus 5.5) through an Anthropic-compatible proxy route; provider-reported usage:

| Build | Requests | Byte breaks | cacheRead | cacheWrite |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `main` (before the rebase) | 12 | 0 | 374.0k | 59.8k |
| this head | 12 | 0 | 393.9k | 64.6k |

- This journey is already byte-clean on `main` after #198100, so it shows no regression rather than the gain; the gains need the randomized mix (tool growth, replay drift). Request counts and model tool choices vary per run, so totals are not a like-for-like cost comparison.
- The one partial miss (request 2, ~19.6k written once per session) also happens with a byte-identical replay of the same bodies; it is provider/proxy-side, not OpenClaw bytes.
- Before the rebase, the same head on OpenAI Responses (gpt-5.4-mini): 16 requests, 1 break at compaction (an allowed rebuild), cacheRead 317.8k.

**Unit / focused:** `session-prefix-owner.test.ts` (absorb drift, rebuild by identity, frozen tools, accepted thinking removal, commit on accept), `session-prompt-state*.test.ts` (history id from the checkpoint when the window drops the compaction entry), `replay-history.test.ts` (silent replies): 132 tests across 5 files pass (vitest-source). `oxfmt`/`oxlint` on changed files clean; line-cap ratchet OK (`session-prompt-state.ts` shrinks). Full build + packed smoke: self-contained package tarball integrity check passes; the installed package runs `--version` and `gateway --help`.

<details>
<summary>Postmortem: seven prompt-cache fixes in three days</summary>

- #197074 merged on a loopback-mock proof for a cost claim and was reverted (#197175) after a real-route measurement. #197835, #197874, #197893, #197925 and #198100 each fixed the input that the previous day's production logs named; each time the next input broke the same rule.
- Why: the bug was a design property (about 35 live prompt inputs and 20 history transforms rebuilt every request) treated as a list of inputs; attribution came from an in-process detector instead of wire bytes; each PR proved only its own scenario; fixes merged faster than they deployed, so "still breaking" looked like "new cause".
- Process change, one gate per invariant: (1) a written contract before code, (2) a cause list from wire-byte diffs, (3) seeded randomized journeys over every turn kind on all five transports, (4) provider cache read/write before and after on real routes, (5) a production canary with the daily cache audit, (6) a cache PR names the contract clause it enforces and adds its turn kind to the randomized test.

</details>

## Not in this PR

- **Scope-2 root fixes** (each needs its own randomized case and real-route proof):
  - one tool-call id rule for the transport, replay and side-question forks. Inside a session's own series the owner re-sends the ids it sent, but a side-question fork (for example the Advisor plugin) still spells an id differently from its parent (for example `call_30_0` vs `call300` on Chat Completions), so the fork misses the parent's cache. `main` does the same;
  - one producer for subagent standing instructions, from durable inputs only (the "Rules" toggles);
  - the sources of the replay drift that the owner absorbs today (an inserted assistant text row, aborted-turn repair), so the absorb path can be deleted.
- **Phase 2: persisted sent bytes** next to each transcript row, so a restart, a worker turn and a fork replay the same bytes, and the per-attempt re-derivation layer (about 3.6k non-test LOC) can be deleted. This needs a persisted-log schema decision first.
- Worker-turn system prompt pin (draft #198201) and the session-human series key (draft #198221) stay separate.
- Translator prefix-property tests (string/array marker shape, opening system marker, late tool-result relocation).

prs.title: fix: contain expired channel cleanup callbacks
prs.body:
Related: #198645, #198245, #198338.

## What Problem This Solves

Completes the narrator crash stop in #198645: dispatch can finish without stopping its narrator, and expired plugin callbacks can still throw from typing cleanup timers or deferred acknowledgment removal.

## User Impact

Expired optional progress work stops without dropping connected users or interrupting unrelated runs. Plugin authorization and closed-scope rejection remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing visibility error boundary now uses the narrator's turn cancellation owner, so it aborts in-flight narration as well as clearing retries. Narration-clear callbacks contain synchronous throws. Discord cleanup stops narration even when dispatch produces no final reply. Typing cleanup seals its controller before invoking plugin cleanup; typing-stop and acknowledgment-removal callbacks catch synchronous exceptions and asynchronous rejection, including an expired error-reporting callback.

Neither #198245 nor #198338 changed PluginInvocationScope or PluginInstance lifetime. The production closed-scope check predates both; the string added by #198245 was in a regression test. Both authorization fixes remain unchanged. Presence scheduler and typing keepalive timer boundaries were inspected; their callbacks already run under synchronous/asynchronous error handling.

## Evidence

- Four new dispatch/typing/ack regressions fail on exact baseline `52e231b703f7e2fb1f4287dd0ff5b2ebf03c6d7a`. The corrected real-plugin narrator regression fails at `PluginInvocationScope.assertOpen → run → maybeRun → retry timer` with that baseline's narrator source; the scope, instance, bindings and narrator sources are byte-identical between that baseline and the original branch parent. Direct closed-scope calls still throw after the fix; the pending timer stops without invoking the plugin or model again.
- Focused candidate proof: 98 passing tests across narrator, core/channel typing, acknowledgment/status reactions and Discord dispatch cleanup. Final integrated narrator suite: 30/30 pass in 39.04 seconds including cold compilation; all production files are byte-identical to that tested candidate. Main's existing narrator regression is retained alongside the real-plugin boundary proof.
- Full `pnpm check:changed --base 94cc426fb0b412746f83715b80093faaa5a0fd43`: typechecks, lint, formatting and all other checks pass; dead-export scan fails on the two inherited exports below. It is not reported green. The overlapping hotfix was integrated from main parent `5116e8d42292ea2f1dd307df5ce77183015a4021`; production bytes did not change during conflict resolution. Broad final-head proof is PR CI.
- Both dead-export failures reproduce through the canonical scanner on exact main parent `5116e8d42292ea2f1dd307df5ce77183015a4021`: `scripts/perf/transcript-facts-backfill-stress-preload.mjs: prepareTranscriptFactsBackfillStress` introduced by `72f90dde293d5e99d6852545a0d7b2590a5aa56e` / #194519, and `extensions/workboard/src/store-evidence.ts: MAX_COMPLETION_CLAIMS` introduced by `c1ca2d7b14c6de87939ec0e1207808cf1816d434` / #197471. These are main regressions, not ignored noise. The baseline replay additionally reports five unused voice type exports not present in the candidate failure; those additional diagnostics are not used as landing exceptions.
- Independent Codex review of the original complete local change: scoped-clean through P2 (confidence 0.87). Integrated-range review against `5116e8d42292ea2f1dd307df5ce77183015a4021`: scoped-clean through P2 (confidence 0.86).
- No Control UI imports of the changed owners were found. No config, schema, dependency, public API or scope-lifetime change.
- Simplification: existing turn/controller cancellation and promise boundaries own cleanup; no new lifecycle manager or cache. Against the integrated main parent, production grows by 12 lines for error boundaries and terminal cleanup; tests grow by 79 lines, docs by 2.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): report discrawl export errors without a traceback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`discrawl-normalize.mjs` crashes with a raw Node traceback for every rejected export — channel-name resolution, guild mismatch, bad `--threads`, bad timestamps, `discrawl status` failure — because the run rejects out of the top-level `await` with no CLI boundary catch. The sibling script `chat-transcript.mjs` in the same skill already reports the same class of input errors as a single clean line (#197307 open; merged siblings #196398, #196440).

The output stream ordering had the same validate-after-open shape as #196440: `createWriteStream(output)` ran before channel/guild/threads validation, so a rejected export raced the stream open against process teardown for the user's previously preserved JSONL.

Precedent: #197307 (same file family, same "reject without a traceback" shape; this PR covers the Discrawl normalizer), #196440 (validate before touching output).

## Why This Change Was Made

- `run()` gained the same CLI boundary catch as `source-manifest.mjs`/`#197307`: print only `error.message`, `process.exitCode = 1`. No stack, same exit code.
- Destination creation moved after every input validation and after `database.prepare`, so a rejected export never opens (and truncates) the output file — the #196440 ordering.
- The `finally` now destroys a non-stdout destination so a rejected export cannot leave the open stream holding the event loop (without this, the new `exitCode`-only exit would hang on validation errors).

No new validator, option, config, or policy. Valid exports take the identical code path apart from stream creation happening after validation instead of before.

Production LOC is +11/-4 (1 file); test +75/-0 (1 new file).

Classification: `behavior-completing` (completes the reject-without-traceback shape for the Discrawl normalizer; same boundary pattern as the sibling scripts).

## User Impact

A rejected Discrawl export now prints one diagnostic line (e.g. `Channel name resolved to 0 rows; supply --channel with the stable channel ID`) and exits 1, instead of a multi-frame Node traceback. A pre-existing preserved `messages.jsonl` can no longer be truncated by a rejected run. Valid exports are byte-identical before and after (control run below).

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `c5cf853931feaa51f9be651a2535103368c34de2` (branch `fix/knowledge-discrawl-validate-first`)
- Current-main RED baseline: `91db919f2de1675ec62da6524f3bda0415f9f8b9` (discrawl-normalize.base.mjs = `git show origin/main:…/discrawl-normalize.mjs`)
- Production entry: `node discrawl-normalize.mjs --config x --channel nope --since 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z --before 2026-10-02T00:00:00Z --output <pre-existing file>` (script file itself; node:sqlite builtin)
- Canonical owner exercised: `run() in extensions/knowledge/skills/knowledge-source-ingest/scripts/discrawl-normalize.mjs`
- Recorder/readback boundary: exit code / stderr line count / pre-existing output file bytes
- Cleanup: isolated tmp dirs only; no Gateway/session/token/config touched

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

Shipped script file in docker `lexiflow-all:latest`, Node v24.22.1, fake `discrawl` CLI on PATH returning a fixture archive. Base = current-main file, head = this branch. Full harness output:

```text
== RED (base, invalid channel, pre-existing output) ==
base  exit=1 stderr_lines=12 traceback=true preserved=true
base  stderr: "file:///ws/discrawl-normalize.base.mjs:84\n        throw new Error(\n              ^\n\nError: Channel name resolved to 0 rows; supply --channel with the stable cha"
== GREEN (head, invalid channel, pre-existing output) ==
head  exit=1 stderr_lines=1 traceback=false preserved=true
head  stderr: "Channel name resolved to 0 rows; supply --channel with the stable channel ID"
== control (valid channel, base vs head byte-compare) ==
base  exit=0 rows=1 summary={"provider":"discord","source_key":"discord:9:100",...,"item_count":1,"watermark":"7",...}
head  exit=0 rows=1 summary={"provider":"discord","source_key":"discord:9:100",...,"item_count":1,"watermark":"7",...}
control_identical=true
```

Note on the original truncation claim: with a small fixture archive the stream-open vs process-teardown race on current main does not truncate within the measurement window (5/5 runs preserved); the deterministic, reproducible defect is the traceback, which the boundary catch fixes. The reordering removes the race class entirely (open cannot precede validation) and is required so the `exitCode`-only exit cannot hang on the dangling stream — the test suite's preserved-file assertion guards the ordering.

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge/src/discrawl-normalize.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/source-manifest.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 4 passed (clean-error RED here; successful-export coverage stays in source-manifest.test.ts per review)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge/src/chat-transcript.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/source-manifest.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/skill-packaging.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 7 passed (sibling scripts unaffected)
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts` — OK; `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs` — OK
- Not tested: `--output` into a missing directory still surfaces a stream-level error (pre-existing behavior, separate concern); mid-iterate DB errors keep their existing crash class.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: +11/-4 (1 file)
- Test LOC: +121/-0 (1 new file)
- Existing-solutions preflight: mirrors the `source-manifest.mjs` boundary pattern cited in #197307; no new helpers
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none

prs.title: fix: retain minified lazy parser targets in standalone builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Standalone plugin preparation fails to load its embedded Acorn parser when the minifier spells static strings as constant templates. The native dependency resolver recognizes only quoted literals, so the lazy module lookup falls through to a removed node_modules tree. Fetched Teams and TypeScript plugins report a missing Acorn package.

## User Impact

Retain the existing lazy ESM parser dependency in standalone executables without requiring the original source package. Package-map helpers stay lazy, and plugin contracts and parser identity stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teach the existing native module-resolution owner to read constant template specifiers and export conditions alongside quoted strings. This preserves the private parser loader instead of changing its module format or adding a runtime fallback. The earlier CJS-loader proposal in this PR was disproved by a signed artifact and has been replaced.

## Evidence

- The regression runs the real source through dependency discovery, native transformation and image-loader rewriting, removes node_modules, then scans a plugin import. Before the fix, the literal control passes and the minified-template case fails with the real missing-package error; both pass afterward. Distinct ESM/CJS export targets guard parser identity.
- 35 focused native/parser and source-inspection tests pass. Tooling test typecheck, scoped lint, formatting and diff checks pass. The normal candidate build passes.
- Codex autoreview of the complete candidate from base `e883a78ec5f3563cb755da1a460f815f3bfabb1d` to the staged patch committed as `8c4111ac68ebe79eb5eebe7b95a220886787ae04` is P2 scoped-clean, with no accepted findings.
- A byte-matched qualification copy passes signed AOT core smoke, Teams install/load, CJS/ESM/published/local TypeScript, all 34 late API checks, SDK identity, npm child/re-entry, PDF Worker and real Codex activation/turn. The existing query-resolution limitation remains visible as the sole failed wrapper gate; it is not presented as a full compatibility pass.
- Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43557937540) and [Darwin tooling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43557937360) are green. No admin exception.
- Stock-main AOT separately fails in compiler Lower on the full graph. No compiler workaround, production pin or default-AOT change is included.

prs.title: docs: propose a linked package root and staged candidate handoff for updates
prs.body:
Related: #145252

## What Problem This Solves

Update reliability work has no written plan for its two structural causes: a package update moves the running release off its path, and the installed updater drives the whole run, so a fix in a new release cannot help the release that is failing.

## User Impact

User impact: none. This is a design proposal for maintainers to accept, change, or reject. It adds one page under `docs/reference/` and changes no behavior.

The page records seven decisions, which a maintainer accepted on November 13, 2026. Decision 2 was revised the same day, from extending the activation journal to not extending it. Three are ones this repository reserves for explicit approval: recording a pointer intent in the activation journal, the retention rule for release directories, and the package marker that #197922 adds. Accepting them sets the direction; each slice still needs its own review.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197922, now merged, implements the first slice of this plan, and its reviewers had no place to see where it leads. The page records:

- The recommendation: on OpenClaw-owned prefixes, the installed package directory keeps its path and becomes a link to a release directory. Activation and rollback are one rename each. A staged transfer of update work to the candidate sits beside it.
- Four approaches that were considered and rejected, with the source facts behind each: a launcher in the npm package, extending the immutable installation owner to user installations, rebinding the service to a new package root, and describing the candidate handoff as moving an existing one.
- Step timings from a published-updater Docker run, with the swap step broken down. The link can remove at most about 32 s of the 139 s that run took.
- A first-hop table, including what a published updater does when it meets a linked package root. That case has now run for `2026.10.9` and `2026.11.3`: the update passes and the link stays, but the updater rewrites the release directory behind the link in place. The page predicted the link would be replaced by a directory, and it now adds a release identity rule to the recommended route because of the result.
- A correction to the second slice, from two source traces at `649ca5f879f1e`. No handoff rule is needed for a linked package root, because the updater already rebinds its post-core child to the activated root. A later design pass recommends against extending the activation journal for the link switch, and decision 2 is revised to match: the link is the record, and the update run record gains one optional field naming the two releases. The page records that design, the order of an activation, what each crash point leaves, and what it does not cover.
- What was not traced or measured.

This is the fourth version of the page. The third recommended rebinding the service to a release path. That rested on a wrong premise, which the page states under rejected approaches.

It follows the form of the existing `team-immutable-update-design.md`. Like that page, it is not listed in `docs/docs.json`.

## Evidence

Docs-only change. Run against this page at `526f6d63cab40`:

- `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` on the page: passed.
- `oxfmt --check` on the page: clean.
- `markdownlint-cli2` with the repository config: 0 issues.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Links: the page links to six pages and two anchors on other pages, unchanged from the previous version, and five anchors within itself. All resolve.

Not run: `pnpm docs:check-links`. The worktree is a sparse checkout without installed dependencies, so the audit could not start there.

The design comes from reading source, from two tests with toy packages on macOS (Node resolving a linked entry, and npm's handling of a linked global package), from the Docker runs recorded on #197922, and from one new Docker test.

**Published updaters on a linked package root.** In the published-driver update cell on linux/arm64, I moved the installed release into `releases/<version>/` and left a relative link at the package path, then ran a normal update to a build of `089d8b8`.

| Published updater | Result | Package path after | Directory behind the link after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026.11.3 | PASS, Gateway ready, version and sessions verified | Same link | Holds the new build |
| 2026.10.9 | PASS, Gateway ready, version and sessions verified | Same link | Holds the new build, under the old version's name |

The cell's installed-tree budget check refuses a linked root, so I pointed it at the link's target for these runs; the harness copy with that change and the layout recording was not committed. Not covered: rollback after a failed update on a linked root, a second update, a Gateway-initiated update, older updaters, and Windows.

The link switch itself has not run on an OpenClaw installation. The page's "Evidence limits" section lists the rest.

prs.title: fix(templates): honor the workspace bootstrap byte limit when building packages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`templates validate` accepts a `BOOTSTRAP.md` that `templates build` later rejects. The reader (`src/templates/reader.ts`) snapshots a package-root `BOOTSTRAP.md` with the workspace bootstrap byte limit (`MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES` = 2 MiB), but the builder (`src/templates/project-build.ts`) reads the same file back through `readSelectedProjectFile` with the generic managed-file limit (`MAX_MANAGED_FILE_BYTES` = 1 MiB). A `BOOTSTRAP.md` between 1 MiB and 2 MiB passes `templates validate` (issue #198559 reproduces with a 1,680,008-byte file) and then fails `templates build` with `file exceeds limit of 1048576 bytes`.

## Solution

Make `readSelectedProjectFile` use `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES` (2 MiB) for `BOOTSTRAP.md`, matching the reader's limit for the same file, while all other managed files keep `MAX_MANAGED_FILE_BYTES` (1 MiB). This keeps validate and build consistent for the entire accepted range.

## Evidence

### Regression test (RED → GREEN)

New test `builds a package bootstrap between the managed-file and workspace-bootstrap byte limits` in `src/templates/project.test.ts`: writes a 1,680,008-byte `BOOTSTRAP.md` (between the two limits), asserts it passes `validateTemplateProject`, then `buildTemplateProject` packages it and the extracted artifact contains the full contents.

- **RED**: before the fix the new test fails with `FsSafeError: file exceeds limit of 1048576 bytes (got 1680014)` at `project-build.ts:23` → `buildTemplateProject` at `:116`.
- **GREEN**: after the fix all 55 tests pass (3 files: `project.test.ts`, `project.bundled.test.ts`, `reader.test.ts`) plus 7 CLI tests in `templates-cli.project.test.ts`.

### Real CLI execution (post-fix, head `3876a79aecb`)

prs.title: fix(talk): voice consults rewrite the cached prompt on every question
prs.body:
Closes #179236

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated Talk hand-offs remove previously submitted consult input from later model history. Speech finalized during a consult can also move into earlier history. Source-built runtime proof found a further case: speech immediately before a consult was folded into its generated prompt, then replayed separately on the next call. These changes rewrite conversation prefixes and can increase cache writes.

## User Impact

Later voice questions retain the consult-containing conversation prefix and genuine spoken clarifications. Generated consult input remains hidden from chat and voice-background previews.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current head: `bbb9caa27a628cbea73cdb1f3429d1fae91b9c1d`.

- Tag and retain native and client-tool-call consult input already sent to the backing model.
- Replay speech finalized during a tagged consult after that consult's last row; preserve ordinary chat order.
- Keep speech preceding a tagged consult as distinct history, including speech committed while write admission waits. Preserve ordinary unanswered-message and restart recovery.
- Hide generated input from pending voice background before the first model response.
- Keep earlier excluded records excluded without rewriting stored data.

The PR integrates upstream `54dd1c6d` with its native package identity 2026.10.6. No version or saved configuration metadata was edited to bypass downgrade protection.

**Maintainer decision required:** scoped generated-consult retention changes the earlier contract from #135423. The [owner decision request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179237#issuecomment-6354621771) remains open.

## Evidence

[23 October source-build report and durable JSON receipts](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/blob/4baba2d09836fd192b11fcbd04dfc2adf034f9de/evidence/talk-consult-prompt-cache/2026-10-23/README.md)

| Requirement | Verified result |
| --- | --- |
| Exact original upstream-base regression | Browser/native producer cases on `390d7993` fail only at intended retention assertions; strict expected-failure gate passed. Original fixed-source integration passed 134 tests at `4dddbb7d`. [Run 39879508535](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/actions/runs/39879508535). |
| Additional preparation defect | All three intended negative cases fail on `5c86a193`. Repaired source passed **47 tests across five files**, covering native recorder/prepared/browser provenance, late speech, ordinary recovery and mandatory tool-prefix stability. [Run 39930234710](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/actions/runs/39930234710). |
| Built Gateway / actual agent requests | **Passed** with native source build at `8b6f6011`: pending reconnect before response bytes, generated background suppression, exact retained prompt count, clarification after the answer, and exact contiguous HTTP input prefix through the first consult. [Run 39931480192](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/actions/runs/39931480192). |
| Latest-stable pre-existing mixed-data upgrade | **Passed** from published 2026.10.6 through the native updater to candidate `98239851`. Typed question/reply and genuine speech survive in order; legacy generated input stays hidden. Candidate and installed build identities and all **18,522 application-file hashes** match. Current-source upgrade fixture tests also passed **93 tests**. [Run 39930703485](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/actions/runs/39930703485). |
| Current-head upstream checks | **Passed** for `bbb9caa2`: CI gate, security-sensitive review and dependency review all successful. [CI run 39932582291](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39932582291). |

Both upgrade manifests declare 2026.10.6; build identity and the complete file inventory establish candidate activation. Official latest stable was rechecked as `v2026.10.6` at 2026-10-23T09:59:51Z.

Proof candidates have identical product source and docs to the PR. The PR adds only two user-role guards inside the new regression test to satisfy the message-union type check; strict assertions remain equivalent. The linked report records the exact source correspondence and earlier failed attempts rather than counting them as proof.

### Wire-proof scope

The first **three contiguous actual Responses input items**, through the generated consult, replay unchanged. The first/second requests have four/seven input items; the first answer is at index 3 and the clarification at index 4. The provider intentionally rebuilds its trailing per-turn runtime-context item, which is outside this compared prefix. No filtering or normalization is applied to compared items.

This synthetic source-build lane uses the real Gateway, producer and agent loop with a controlled external HTTP provider. It does not claim whole-request/system/tool/header equality, live provider cache hits or microphone/audio testing. Native producer coverage also uses public plugin registration and real session/history owners in the linked integration tests.

### Earlier live observations

The [22 October live report](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/blob/499bfbe1547071b8a8dc67dbbb416484f72e34ce/evidence/talk-consult-prompt-cache/2026-10-22/README.md) covers actual OpenAI/GPT and Google/Gemini Talk routes with Anthropic Claude, clarification recall and mixed typed/voice recall. Individual follow-up first requests showed 96.3%, 97.5% and 97.8% cached input. These observations used a compiled-JavaScript port on an existing patched beta image, not a full source build or guaranteed savings. The manual reconnect attempt was inconclusive; the source-built pending test above adds deterministic coverage.

Fresh independent reviews found no P0–P2 findings in the current repair and proof. The shared autoreview CLI is unavailable on the server; no helper-isolated autoreview run is claimed.

All new source proof ran in secretless fork CI with synthetic state. Chief and its live configuration, data, volumes, environment and image were untouched.

The requested technical receipts are submitted. Scoped retention still requires a maintainer decision; fresh ClawSweeper review is requested after this body/evidence update.

prs.title: fix(agents): completion relays report spurious failures on tool-free turns
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #198584

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users would receive "the task failed / I'm blocked" reports for subagent work that actually completed, whenever the completion was relayed on a degraded path (unverified handoff envelope, restart recovery, CLI execution provider, or raw-model run). On those turns every execution tool is disabled by design, yet the announce prompt still instructed the model to "require continued work or a follow-up in the kept child session" — so the model burned tokens on blocked tool attempts and then escalated the relay's own authority loss as a child task failure.
- **Related:** #198584 (this issue); #198204 touched the same instruction builder for a different defect (duplicate delivery) — complementary, no overlap. clawsweeper labels on the issue: `queueable-fix` / `fix-shape-clear` / `source-repro`; its Codex review asked to "qualify shared completion guidance by available tools", which is exactly this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** the completion guidance a relay turn receives matches the tool surface that turn actually resolved. Restricted relays (tools disabled, or allowlist collapsed to `["message"]`) now get relay-only wording: preserve the child outcome, relay it truthfully, state any needed follow-up for a subsequent normal turn, and do not report the turn's own tool restrictions as a task failure. Trusted in-process handoffs that retain the requester's tools keep the existing continuation guidance unchanged.
- The instruction is frozen into the announce prompt at compose time, while the tool-surface decision (`resolveCompletionToolPolicy`) is only made later at run time — so the rewrite is applied at the run seam in `runAgentAttempt`, the single place that authoritatively knows the surface. One condition (`isSubagentAnnounceHandoff && !completionRetainsRequesterTools`) covers both the `disableTools` and message-only cases, for the CLI and embedded paths, across the prompt text and the task-completion internal events (which feed runtime-context fragments).
- **Out of scope:** the tool restriction itself (intentional privilege separation, unchanged); model-free relay for unverified paths (issue's costlier option 2); persisting the capability envelope across restarts (option 3); the settle-into-busy-parent and `sessions_send` A2A paths, which run with tools and keep the original instruction.
- **Highest-risk area:** prompt text substitution on completion handoff turns.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The rewrite is an exact-match `replaceAll` of one frozen constant; text that does not contain it is byte-identical. The trusted-handoff regression test asserts the continuation guidance survives untouched when tools are retained.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** on a restricted completion relay turn, the model-facing prompt and runtime-context fragments contain the relay-only instruction and no longer contain the "require continued work or a follow-up" continuation clause; users stop receiving spurious failure reports for completed child work, and tokens are no longer wasted on blocked tool attempts. Trusted completion handoffs behave exactly as before.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.ts` (the `completionRelayOnly` seam after `resolveCompletionToolPolicy`), `src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-instructions.ts` (new relay-only constant + rewrite helpers), and the regressions in `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts` ("rewrites completion guidance to relay-only on a restricted relay turn", "keeps continuation guidance on a trusted completion handoff turn").

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** isolated worktree at `origin/main` (72f90dde293) + patch, Node v26.12.1; vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run` against the real `runAgentAttempt` seam with only the CLI/embedded runners mocked (the tool-policy resolution, handoff verification, and prompt composition under test are real).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/command/attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts \
    src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-instructions.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check <changed files> && pnpm exec oxlint <changed files>
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts > completion relay guidance matches the resolved tool surface > rewrites completion guidance to relay-only on a restricted relay turn
  ✓ attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts > completion relay guidance matches the resolved tool surface > keeps continuation guidance on a trusted completion handoff turn
  ✓ subagent-completion-instructions.test.ts (5 tests: relay-only rewrite of composed prompt text, private-completion instruction, and task-completion internal events; non-matching text untouched)
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** on the unverified-handoff (restricted) relay turn, `runCliAgent` receives `disableTools: true` with a prompt containing `SUBAGENT_COMPLETION_RELAY_ONLY_INSTRUCTION` and no continuation clause, in both `prompt` and `runtimeContextFragments`; on the trusted turn the prompt is unchanged and still carries the original continuation instruction.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** RED on the same regression (pre-fix, unverified handoff): `AssertionError: expected '[Inter-session message] …' to contain 'This completion ends one child run, n…'` — the received prompt still carried "Reviews, failed checks, and other in-scope fixable blockers require continued work or a follow-up in the kept child session" while `disableTools: true`.
- **What was not tested:** no live model run against a real gateway restart (the degraded path is exercised through the real `runAgentAttempt` seam with an unverified handoff envelope, which is the same `resolveCompletionToolPolicy` branch a restart recovery lands on). `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this host at all — its `tsrs` native binary requires `GLIBC_2.32`+ and the host has glibc 2.31 — so type checking is left to CI. One pre-existing test in `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts` ("restricts completion tools for a capability without persisted child lineage") fails identically on untouched `origin/main` on this host (verified by control run); it is unrelated to this change. Full CI lanes pending.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (behavioral regressions through the real run seam, RED on main → GREEN on head, before/after contrast above).
- **Proof limitations:** none for the prompt/fragment rewrite behavior; the end-to-end user-visible "false failure" framing depends on live model behavior and is argued from the instruction text the model receives.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): members add and approve their own devices
prs.body:
Related: OCF-338 (Linear)

## What Problem This Solves
An invited OpenClaw ID member can only use the one browser that accepted their invite. They can't add another browser or a native app, and a member who switches laptops quietly loses access.

## User Impact
Members can approve their own additional devices from a device they already have. New devices inherit the member's role, and members can remove their own devices. Owners see each member's devices on the People page, with who approved each one, and can remove any of them. Removing a device also removes the devices it approved, directly or indirectly; the confirmation shows the count. Owners are notified when a member adds a device. Missing or duplicate device labels now include a stable short fingerprint, so rows, approval provenance, confirmation buttons and removal notices identify the same device.

**Breaking (unshipped v1-draft protocol, revised in place with no compatibility path):** invite redemptions now carry a required `label`. Members admitted before this change can still connect, but can't approve devices until they're removed and re-invited. The macOS member join (#198499) adds `label` once this lands.

## Why This Change Was Made
- **Protocol:** member device records now keep each device's signing key, label and approver. A new `add_member_device` op has no role field, so new devices inherit the member's role.
- **Who can sign it:** one of the same member's own listed devices, an owner device with `manage_members`, or R.
- **Members as signers:** they may sign only `add_member_device` and `revoke_device`, only for their own account, and only directly over the tunnel (never through the mailbox).
- **Unchanged:** the relay snapshot keeps its shape, so admission doesn't change.
- **Tunnel API:** members get an account-scoped membership view and may submit those two statements. Invite routes stay owner-only, and sign-out stays open to every admitted peer.

## Evidence
- Rebased onto `0b7cd35571e7cbfb7544305379c7c4a1dac26b03` (main); dropped the empty CI-trigger commit. The rebase preserves upstream owner/node expiry and this PR's member-device behavior. Pushed using an exact lease on the previous PR head.
- Fresh targeted proof:
  - protocol package: **245 passed**, including generated-vector parity;
  - Gateway HTTP, owner expiry, owner notices, real SQLite persistence and remote sign-out: **35 passed**;
  - rebase-affected node authority, membership service, store capacity and tunnel suites: **27 passed**;
  - People page and formatting: **30 passed**;
  - Chromium browser flow: **passed at 1280, 820 and 400 px**, including cascade confirmation, owner-signed submission, notice text, and no horizontal overflow.
- Gateway/protocol test and browser typechecks, targeted lint, format and whitespace checks pass. Earlier i18n proof remains applicable; this repair changes no translation keys.
- Stable-identity regression: on the rebased pre-fix source, two HTTP tests fail because a metadata-free device has an empty label, a signed whitespace label stays blank, and two `Chrome on Linux` devices are indistinguishable. Both pass with the fix. The owner and member views agree, the People projection has the same label, and stored signed labels remain unchanged. Browser tests cover the row, `Approved by …`, cascade confirmation and removal notice consumers.
- Existing independent reviews found and repaired approval-cycle counting and confirmed owner capability/account scope. Fresh independent OpenClaw subagent autoreview covered the complete 46-file local snapshot against base `0b7cd35571e7cbfb7544305379c7c4a1dac26b03`, at P0–P2. It found one P2: the existing membership regression still expected a blank label. That expectation was updated without weakening removal assertions; its suite and the other rebase-affected suites now pass (27 tests). No additional verified P0–P2 findings. This was instruction-based read-only review, not helper-enforced isolation; external Discovery/loader/native-app behavior was not independently rerun.
- Test growth is **+955 lines**, with a justified allocation of 555 beyond the default 400, across authority, HTTP/removal, persistence capacity and browser boundaries. The additional 26 lines strengthen existing identity regression paths rather than add a parallel harness.
- **Simplification:** one existing projection owns device display identity; no caller-side fallback or numbering state, schema change, cache, compatibility layer or permission restriction was added. The short fingerprint is display-only; full keys remain authoritative. Whole-PR production delta: +754/-101; tests, fixtures and test scaffolding: +1062/-25. This repair alone: production +13/-2 and tests +54/-28. The protocol/Gateway/People changes remain one requested functional slice.
- [Live staging proof on `0e762df16464`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198575#issuecomment-6871056927) passed the owner/invite/SAS gate and all 10 member-device checkpoints through deployed Discovery #16 and loader #32: self-approval, role inheritance, provenance/notice, descendant cascade, crafted cross-account/role rejection, and owner removal. That is prior-head integration evidence, not a final-head replay. Full staging was not rerun for this display-only repair; the new browser proof uses the bundled UI with a synthetic Gateway response, paired with real Gateway HTTP projection tests. Companion PRs: openclaw/discovery (self mail), openclaw/claw-loader (routing and member devices).

### CI and inherited failure evidence
Final-head CI: [CI run 43555905292](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43555905292) **passed** for `10ed7da328255d08483783465781b0dda60753e2`: **47 successful jobs, 25 scope-skipped jobs, zero failures**; `openclaw/ci-gate` is green. All three UI shards, both UI e2e shards, `check-test-types` and its five core shards passed. No inherited-failure exception is needed for this final run. An older metadata-only `PR context and evidence` run was cancelled and superseded by successful runs. The branch is conflict-free.

[ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198575#issuecomment-6870194780) completed on this exact head: **no findings, nothing required before merge, ready for maintainer review**. It confirms the previous display-identity finding is resolved and accepts reuse of the live staging evidence after comparing the unchanged core blobs. Exactly one [re-review request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198575#issuecomment-6871703559) was posted after the branch, body and focused proof were ready and CI had started. This PR remains open and unmerged.

On untouched detached main `0b7cd35571e7cbfb7544305379c7c4a1dac26b03`, `chat-view.test.ts:2998` reproduces the exact earlier [UI shard 2 failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43544829932/job/132294056803): `expected <div …> to be an instance of HTMLButtonElement`. The unchanged renderer creates a `div[role=option]`; neither it nor this test is touched by this PR. Same pinned Bun build, Node 24.22.1, lockfile and owning UI config; the two model suites finish **1 failed / 127 passed**, with only that assertion failing. This is an attributed inherited failure, not a green check or a fix pushed to main.

Reproduction on that main commit:
```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config ui/vitest.config.ts --project unit \
  ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts \
  ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control-view.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1
```

The old responsive assertions at 2313/2398 (and the same CI job's 568×320 assertion) **pass** on main; all 59 responsive tests pass. The old [UI shard 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43544829932/job/132294056785) `model-control-view.test.tsx:103` failure also **passes** on main. Upstream #198532 refreshes the responsive fixtures; #198535 memoizes model names. These failures are not claimed as currently inherited merely because they once failed. The rebase includes those upstream changes; final-head CI is the broad verification. Local replays are bounded, not a recreation of full-shard ordering.

### Stable device identity — before and after
Synthetic fixture: three devices named `Chrome on Linux`, plus one unlabeled device. No real accounts or device keys are shown.

Before (blank row and indistinguishable devices):

![Before: blank and duplicate member device labels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78a1fb13-d873-4b3f-bead-0bdfd1dcabcf)

After (shared projection supplies stable identities):

![After: distinct member device identities](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f17bb67b-f41a-47bf-8650-2b03fc681f7a)

![Mobile cascade confirmation with stable device identity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02ee960d-0ae7-4b63-ba6d-8c23b94d6de2)

Removal confirmation with cascade count:

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session roster refreshes copy the selected-session map even when every selection remains valid.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Selection identity, deletion confirmation, pending-deletion rollback, and successor protection stay intact. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Defer the copy until reconciliation removes the first entry. Source-derived selected-map constructions per reconciliation fall from **1 to 0 when all entries are retained**; removals still make one copy. The current-row map and validation pass remain. These are source-derived operation counts, not measured heap allocations or timing improvements.

## Evidence

- Tested base: `2110db5a1d1c4d15ef746e788b623ef3e49582b6`; prepared commit: `4cf8747cacaa4a11cb362ce2885e6fa64ad14823`. Committed TypeScript hashes equal the tested source.
- AWS proof: 8 observed CPUs, 16,371,773,440 bytes physical RAM. Canonical private-QA runtime and matching UI built successfully; the selected test reused the native current build. Before/after build-file hashes match; this is not a served-byte or latency measurement.
- Scope suite: **11 passed**. Four selection-owner sibling files: **60 passed**. Exact real-Gateway case, `reconciles captured selections across real refresh, removal, and successor updates`: **1 passed**, 0 failed, 1 unrelated sibling filtered out of 2 discovered. It covers refresh, captured references during confirmation, removal, successor identity, and exactly one UI delete request with the original expected session identity.
- The initial real-Gateway run failed its final roster assertion. Source inspection identified missing test synchronization: optimistic disappearance preceded deletion settlement. The test now awaits the matching successful delete response before the independent client reads the roster, preserving every assertion. This does not establish a production deletion defect or retrospectively determine the original request outcome.
- Canonical focused format/parity, lint/parity, production UI and affected test types, and test-line checks passed on the applicable source. Source-identical helper evidence covers 18 baseline/candidate executions (9 per version), including order, references, pending callbacks, multiple removals, and exception propagation.
- Fresh canonical local autoreview of the complete change against the pinned base, **P0–P3**: **scoped-clean, zero findings**. Included unchanged owner/caller/deletion lifecycle context. Reviewed patch SHA-256: `a3c3c2b2d8dbcaf24a2cf9093f006e560c153aee56f4f5196a1aa883a2fb79ae`; committed patch is identical.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop interrupted pending approvals reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw approvals pending` keeps its three parallel Gateway list reads (`exec.approval.list`, `plugin.approval.list`, `openclaw.approval.list`) alive after Ctrl-C/SIGTERM, then prints a late result after the interrupt.

## User Impact

Ctrl-C/SIGTERM stops a pending `pending` list read promptly and exits 130/143 without printing a late list. Normal reads and empty-list outcomes retain their behavior. Interrupted writes (`set`/`resolve`) still report their admitted receipts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pending list reads did not join the command work scope, so nothing aborted them on interrupt. Forward the command signal through the shared pending reader, reject aborted reads before printing, and suppress canceled output.

The pending list reader moves to a sibling module (`exec-approvals-pending.ts`) so the approvals CLI file stays under its line budget while gaining the cancellation path (the file was already at its oxlint max-lines ceiling).

Stacks on #198626 (same CLI file's `get` cancellation and snapshot split); this PR covers the `pending` command.

## Evidence

Product HEAD: `0ce4f6122d39`; acceptance-red BASE: `85a9f5245a1d` (PR-A head, no pending cancellation).

- **Discriminating regression** (`prints no pending list that lands after Ctrl+C`): an `AsyncWorkScope` is created, the `*.approval.list` Gateway mock calls `beginClose()` while the reads settle, and the command runs inside `work.run(...)`. The assertion checks `defaultRuntime.writeJson` was never called and no runtime errors surfaced.
  - BASE: test **FAILS** — 30 passed / 1 failed (late pending list still printed).
  - HEAD: **31 passed** (aborted reads exit without output).
- **Controls on both revisions:** the existing 30 tests (including the `get` cancellation from #198626) pass unchanged.

Ran on the remote test host (docker, Node 24.18, `vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`). Line-cap ratchet passes.

## Not tested

Native approvals node paths on real hosts, Windows/macOS, production Gateway load. The pending command always routes through Gateway RPCs regardless of `--gateway`/`--node`/local mode.

## Impact surface

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/cli/exec-approvals-pending.ts` | new sibling module: pending list reader (signal-aware) |
| `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.ts` | forward `getAsyncWorkSignal()` into `loadPendingApprovals`; suppress aborted output |
| `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts` | +16 lines discriminating regression |
