prs.title: fix(ui): inline widgets flash an empty box before loading on warm chat reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: inline widget cards in a cached chat show an untitled empty box, then "Loading…", then another empty frame before the widget appears, on every warm reload.

## User Impact

User impact: a reloaded chat shows each inline HTML widget's title in its reserved card from the first frame, and the card fills in place with the live widget, with no empty or "Loading…" state and no layout movement.

Risks and required actions, kept visible:

- **CSS budget approval needed.** The overlay and the canvas-card outline add 137 B of boot CSS. Main already exceeds `totalCssRawBytes` (1,749,973 > 1,682,231 B), so `ui:check-performance:base` allows only 64 B of growth and fails this PR until an approved allowance is recorded. The original parked layout cost 335 B; the overlay is the smallest CSS form of an opaque titled cover I found. The dead-CSS audit's candidates are not safe paydown (`sw-row__change-*` and `sw-timeline__*` are built from a prefix prop, `drawer--floating` is used by Workboard).
- **Security boundary.** `src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` (sandbox proxy shell) is in the `execution` category of `.github/security-review-policy.yml`; no `CODEOWNERS` entry covers it, so it needs an independent maintainer review. The host-facing message, params and validation are unchanged; only the timing moves (details below).
- **Other `onRendered` consumers** now run 3 frames after load instead of at load: board widgets show content and post host state for legacy saved widgets on the presentation signal (which also removes the same empty-frame flash there), and offscreen board widgets acknowledge after the 1 s fallback. HTML previews in strict mode are script-free and keep load timing.

Accepted edge cases (not coded): a widget whose main thread stays busy for more than 1 s after `load` falls back before it paints (the previous behavior); a tab hidden during load acknowledges by fallback and may show one empty frame when it becomes visible again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The acknowledgement now means "the document's post-load frames are with the compositor", carried by the existing message:

- The trusted proxy shell prepends one more guard script to scripted widget documents. After the document's `load` (capture, once), it waits three `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks and posts a params-free `sandbox-resource-loaded` to the proxy. A third frame can only begin after the first post-load frame finished raster and activation; two frames only prove a commit.
- The proxy acknowledges the host with the unchanged message and `renderId` only after it observed the inner `load` itself and the witness arrived from the current inner window. Script-free documents keep load timing. Hidden or offscreen frames run no animation frames, so they acknowledge 1 s after load.
- Host validation (`source`, `origin`, `renderId` in `ui/src/lib/widget-sandbox-host.ts`) is unchanged, no message type was added, and inner `ui/notifications/sandbox-*` messages are still never relayed to the host.

On that signal, the Control UI reapplies the parked L315 change in a smaller form: scripted canvas documents show their title in the lazy, admission-held and canvas reservations as one opaque overlay (`.chat-tool-card__reservation`, absolutely positioned over the already-positioned `.chat-tool-card__preview`). The space is held by whatever is in flow beside it (the lazy box, a spacer, or the mounted iframe, which stays paintable and is never hidden), and the overlay retires synchronously on the validated acknowledgement. The generic pending/"Loading…" notice machinery in the canvas owner and the parked two-frame host delay are deleted. Only frames that hold a title until the acknowledgement show one (`widgetReservationTitle`); MCP Apps, strict documents, plain frames and script-free canvas documents keep untitled placeholders so they never regress from titled to untitled.

<details><summary>Sandbox boundary analysis</summary>

`src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` matches the `execution` category of `.github/security-review-policy.yml`; no `CODEOWNERS` entry covers it or the UI files.

- The host-facing message, its params and its validation are unchanged; the change is timing only.
- Widget code shares the witness's realm and can post the same witness, but the proxy never acknowledges before the `load` event it observes, so a forged witness can at most restore the previous load-time acknowledgement for its own card. Withholding it only delays the widget's own placeholder by the 1 s fallback; the existing 30 s render timeout is unaffected.
- The witness captures `postMessage`, `requestAnimationFrame` and its `load` listener before stored scripts run (the same pattern as the existing shortcut and scroll bridges), and a superseded render can never acknowledge.

</details>

## Evidence

"Team metric 12" card on a Team archived warm reload, delivered compositor frames top to bottom (synthetic fixture data):

| Main: untitled box (1,380 ms) → "Loading…" (1,397 ms) → empty box (1,797 ms) → live (1,947 ms) | This PR: unpainted transcript (847 ms) → titled card (863 ms) → still titled (2,147 ms) → live on the next frame (2,163 ms) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Main warm reload card frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc5b2491-40bd-44f5-97e1-baf71c34a06b) | ![This PR warm reload card frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7371477a-f79b-485f-abbd-747d397c8e93) |

The live canvas card also gains a 1px `--border` outline, so its frame matches the reservation.

**Mechanism probe (compositor).** A standalone harness served the real proxy shell from an isolated sandbox origin and a host page with an opaque titled cover over the iframe, retired on `sandbox-resource-loaded`. Chromium 156 headless with paint holding, CDP screencast of every delivered frame; a trial fails if any frame between the cover and live content shows the empty card. Stress = busy host main thread plus a raster-heavy SVG widget.

| Acknowledgement timing | Trials with an empty card frame |
| --- | ---: |
| Inner `load` (main) | 23 / 80 |
| `load` + 2 host frames (parked L315) | 10 / 80 |
| Proxy-side rAF pair after `load` | 2 / 140 |
| Paint Timing `first-paint` inside the widget | 8 / 80 (an occluded surface gets no presentation feedback, so it falls back) |
| Inner rAF pair after `load` | 15 / 290 (12 / 150 under stress) |
| **Inner third rAF after `load` (this PR)** | **0 / 290** |
| This PR's shell, unmodified, stressed | 0 / 100 |

Offscreen frames run no animation frames; the real shell acknowledged them through the fallback at ~1,027 ms.

**Team fixtures (`scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts --warm-reload --visual-proofs --paint-holding`, 1720×1180, production bundle, `--fixture-now-ms 1781000000000`).** Every delivered frame of the "Team metric 12" card was classified (absent / empty outline / titled / live) and transition crops were inspected by hand.

| Build | Reloads | First card frame | Empty-outline frames | Movement while visible |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| This PR, archived | 6 | titled (6/6) | 0 | 0 px (one row/box/scroll signature; bench anchor probe 0 px, excess 0, missing 0) |
| This PR, active | 3 | titled (3/3) | 0 | 0 px (one signature; cached→live anchor shift 0 px) |
| Earlier absolute-iframe layout, same acknowledgement | 15 | titled (15/15) | 0 | 0 px |
| Main, archived + active | 3 | untitled box, then "Loading…" | live content arrives after ~10 frames of an empty box | — |

In 6 of 16 candidate reloads the transcript settled its scroll position by 1 px before its first painted frame (off-screen rows; the card's row height never changed). It was not seen in the 3 main reloads, and no painted frame shows it.

These captures ran on a loaded Mac (load average 13–57 from other lanes), so they are visual verdicts only, with no timing claims. 14 of 18 capture processes stopped early with the bench's own setup refusal (`Invalid or backward compositor timestamp; no paint verdict`, 13 processes; one warm-up timeout), on main and on this branch alike, and a 19th was stopped deliberately once enough reloads had completed; completed reloads before each refusal are kept.

**Tests.** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| File | Result | Wall |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `src/gateway/mcp-app-sandbox-http.test.ts` | 6/6 (red on main's shell: 2 failures; red on a two-frame witness) | 4.8 s |
| `ui/src/components/canvas-widget-view-layout.test.ts` | 4/4 | 4.2 s |
| `ui/src/components/canvas-widget-view.test.ts` | 38/38 | 3.6 s |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message-deferred.test.tsx` | 2/2 | 3.3 s |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/widget-card.test.tsx` | 26/26 | 4.7 s |
| `ui/src/lib/board/widget-sandbox-host.test.ts` | 29/29 | 5.5 s |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-html-preview-element.test.ts` | 44/44 | 4.5 s |
| `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-frame.test.ts` | 19/19 | 2.7 s |

Also: `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint, `oxfmt --check`, stylelint, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`, `pnpm ui:build`, `git diff --check`. Local review: three Codex autoreview passes at P2, the last two with full-file context, all `scoped-clean`.

Production delta: +29 lines net (+37 sandbox, −8 UI).

prs.title: feat(update): stage runtime slots, flip one pointer, restart through a frozen launcher
prs.body:
## What failed in the field

- `openclaw update` changes the running install in place, then stops, rewrites and restarts the service. Most failures happen in that activation step, after the candidate already passed its checks.
  - #197195 (78 nights, one host): 8 of 32 failed nights were the service handoff — the unit generator rejected its own unit under an inherited umask, "manager identity changed" refused the restart, a closed systemd read scope, inspection deadlines, no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/D-Bus in cron, a different PID namespace. Two more were the 256 MB pack cap on a git update that had passed every check.
  - `evidence/class*.jsonl`, layer `service`: 295 reports. Largest causes: managed-service handoff/preflight/stop failed (~75), service file not regenerated or regenerated wrongly (~30), Gateway left stopped after the update (~25), ownership/manager identity not verifiable (~15), systemd/launchctl inspection deadlines and a missing user bus.
- Disk on that host: 269 GB of 348 GB was update staging that was never removed. Doctor removes a retained runtime only when a process census proves no holder, and the census was always incomplete (48 retained runtimes, 142 GB).

## What changed

An update only ever writes into a runtime slot that no Gateway runs, and switches with one rename. `openclaw update`, chat `/update` and the Control UI use the same path on Linux and macOS for user npm and git installs.

Layout `<state>/runtime/`:
- `launcher.mjs` — frozen copy of `scripts/openclaw-runtime-launcher.mjs` (~100 lines, no dependencies). Written once, mode set with `fchmod` (not the umask).
- `slots.json` — `{current, previous, origin, trial?, failed?, run?}`. Every write is temp + fsync + rename(2).
- `a/`, `b/` — the two slots. `origin` is the existing install and is never changed by a slot update.

Update:
1. Stage the slot that no Gateway can be running, in a per-attempt directory `.stage-<slot>-<uuid>`, then rename it onto the slot. npm: `npm install --prefix`. git: `git worktree add --detach` of the checkout (shared object store), then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --package-import-method=auto` (copy-on-write clones or hardlinks from the pnpm store) and `pnpm build`, then `git worktree move`. No copy, no pack cap. A killed updater's orphaned npm/pnpm child writes only into its abandoned stage directory.
2. Smoke `<slot>/openclaw.mjs --version` with the Node named in the service definition (read from the unit/plist file, not `PATH`).
3. Flip `slots.json`: `{current: slot, previous, trial: 2, run?}`.
4. Restart:
   - CLI: ask the Gateway on the service's own port to restart (fallback `systemctl --user restart` / `launchctl kickstart -k`; neither answers → "applies on the next Gateway start", exit 0), then wait up to 180 s for confirmed (exit 0), returned (exit 1) or pending (exit 0).
   - Chat `/update` / Control UI (`update.run`): the Gateway acknowledges, persists the restart sentinel, stages in-process, flips, then restarts itself. The Gateway that confirms the slot finishes the update run as `succeeded`; a Gateway the launcher returned to finishes it as `rolled-back`. The existing run watcher delivers the chat notice.
   - First update on an install whose service does not run the launcher yet: the staged release runs `gateway install --force` once (its program arguments now name the launcher) and that restart is the update's restart. Without a reachable service manager the update uses the restart request instead; the origin entry still hands off to the launcher (below), and the next CLI update or Doctor repair rewrites the unit.

Start:
- The service runs `node <state>/runtime/launcher.mjs gateway --port N`. The launcher `execve`s `current/openclaw.mjs` (same PID: supervisor identity and existing ownership checks do not change).
- A start while `trial` is set spends one attempt; at zero the launcher selects `previous` and records `failed` (keeping `run`). A Gateway on trial exits 1 instead of 78 on config errors, so `RestartPreventExitStatus=78` cannot park a bad slot. It reads its trial from `slots.json`; there is no new environment variable.
- The Gateway clears `trial` when it reports "gateway ready" (listening, channels started).
- `program-args` names the launcher for every Gateway service of a slot layout, so `gateway install`, Doctor's expected plan and the update agree; the service definition never changes when the version changes. `service-layout` maps a launcher entry to the selected slot, so status and Doctor drift checks compare the right package root.
- The CLI on `PATH`, node-host services and units that still name the origin entry run `runtime-slot-redirect.mjs` first, which hands off to the launcher (a CLI call never spends a trial).

The updater needs no D-Bus, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, Node on `PATH`, umask or PID namespace. It holds `runtime/update.lock` with a heartbeat; a killed updater's lock goes stale after 60 s.

## What got deleted, and what did not

- Doctor's process-census gate on retained-runtime cleanup: `doctor --fix` removes leftover `openclaw-update-runtime-*` directories again (#197195: 48 retained runtimes, 142 GB).
- On Linux/macOS user npm/git installs, neither `openclaw update` nor `update.run` reaches runtime retention, update-capture sets, the managed-service stop/handoff, the service-definition refresh or the in-place swap.
- Not deleted here: the in-place pipeline itself. Windows, Homebrew, system packages, Bun, `--recovery`/resume workers and the Doctor source update still run it, and #198355 (plan item 3) and the copy-and-swap work (plan item 4) edit those files. Deleting it is the next stage: move Windows onto slots (needs a Windows VM proof), then remove the in-place pipeline, retained runtimes, capture sets, the process census and service regeneration in one cutover. See design note 1.

Lines vs. the PR #198268 head: production +1344 −57; tests +212 −152; docs +37. **Net production is still positive; see "Open" below.**

## Proof

Status: partial. Runs below are on `60f8c83`/`d9e52d0` (same slot code as the current head except the service-port fix in `b38809a`). Hosts: OrbStack Ubuntu 24.04 VM (systemd user service) and macOS 27 (launchd). Each run starts from a fresh install of this head as 2026.11.3 whose service still runs the origin entry. Updates run cron-like (`env -i`, `umask 077`, Node off `PATH`, no D-Bus).

| Scenario | Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First slot update (login shell) | exit 0, outage 5–8 s; unit now runs `<state>/runtime/launcher.mjs` | exit 0, outage 12–13 s; plist now runs the launcher |
| Second update (cron-like) | exit 0, outage 15–16 s | exit 0, outage 14 s |
| kill -9 new Gateway on trial start | confirmed, exit 0 | confirmed, exit 0 |
| kill -9 updater at Staging / npm install / Staged / Selected / Asked | healthy 0–16 s each | healthy 0 s (Staging, npm install); rest of the run was interrupted |
| Bad build | launcher returned to previous slot, `failed` recorded, exit 1, healthy 5 s later | not rerun on this head |
| No service manager | "applies on next start", exit 0; next start confirms | — |
| Chat `/update` | **not proven**: the harness sent `/update` through a non-owner client and got the owner refusal; rerun through an owner chat client is pending | — |

Git slot disk (btrfs VM, `df` delta): worktree checkout files 855 MiB; `node_modules` with `--package-import-method=hardlink` 33 MiB (vs. ~3.1 GiB copied before); `dist` ~480 MiB per slot is the remaining cost.

Found by the proof and fixed: the first launcher rewrite dropped the service's `--port` (macOS Gateway moved to the configured port; fixed in `b38809a`).

## Open

- **Deletion / net size.** POSIX npm and git installs no longer reach the in-place pipeline, but it is not deleted: Windows, Homebrew, system packages, Bun and recovery/resume still run it, and Homebrew on Linux/macOS also uses the managed-service handoff and unit refresh. Making this PR net-negative needs one owner decision: move Windows and Homebrew onto slots (or drop in-place for them), then remove the in-place activation, retained runtimes, capture sets, process census and service regeneration in one cutover.
- **Migration at slot start.** A Doctor run from the launcher is refused inside the service process tree; the state upgrade at Gateway start belongs to plan item 4 (copy-and-swap). Until then a slot whose schema is newer than the state relies on the Gateway's own startup migration.
- **CI.** `check-lint-core-3` flags three files this PR does not change (same oxlint result on the base). `help-exit.process.test.ts` reproduces red on base `b6c6aef`. The qa-lab e2e, `update-command-runtime` and Codex worker reds are not yet reproduced on the base; #198268's own CI skips these jobs, and main is green.

## Accepted edge cases

- A Gateway that hangs before "gateway ready" without exiting keeps its trial until its next start (the launcher execs away; no watchdog).
- Two profiles that share one install share one pointer; the first healthy Gateway confirms.
- Between the flip and the restart, a CLI started by the old Gateway runs the new slot (the redirect follows `current`).
- Flip-back restores code only. Restoring pre-migration state is plan item 4 (copy-and-swap keeps `.pre-<ver>`); until it lands, an old slot can refuse a newer state schema.
- Git installs follow `origin/main` (dev) or `v<release>` tags (stable/beta); a pinned dev target must be reachable from `origin/main`. Custom upstreams are not followed.
- The frozen launcher has no upgrade path; changing it needs a new file name and a one-time unit rewrite, the same step this PR uses for the first migration.

## Design note: owner decisions

1. **Windows** stays on the in-place updater in this PR. Its scheduled task can run the launcher in spawn mode (already supported), but the restart contract and staging need a Windows VM proof. Proposed next stage: Windows on slots, then delete the in-place pipeline (net-negative).
2. **Migration** is automatic: the first update after this release creates the layout with the existing install as origin (nothing is copied) and points the service at the launcher once. Alternative: opt-in.
3. **Packaged macOS app, Homebrew, system packages, Bun/standalone, containers**: unchanged.
4. **Git installs** no longer move the user's checkout; the slots carry the builds, and the checkout's CLI follows `current`. A developer who wants their own edits runs another worktree.

## Coordination

- Plan item 4 (copy-and-swap) owns state rollback on flip-back and state migration at Gateway start.
- Plan item 3 (#198355) adds preflight checks to the in-place target/runtime preflight; the slot path does not reach those files, so its Node/Git/disk checks need a call in `update-slots.ts`.
- Plan item 2 deletes the in-place pipeline once Windows has a slot path.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw approvals get` keeps its Gateway snapshot read alive after Ctrl-C/SIGTERM, then prints a late result (or waits out the 60s default timeout) after the interrupt.

## User Impact

Ctrl-C/SIGTERM stops a pending `get` snapshot read promptly and exits 130/143 without printing a late snapshot. Normal reads, missing-skill failures and authentication failures retain their outcomes. Interrupted writes (`set`/`resolve`) still report their admitted receipts.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix(status): cancel deep gateway reads on Ctrl+C
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw status --deep` / `status --json` / `status --all` did not pass their abort signal to the deep Gateway reads (`health`, `diagnostics.stability`, `last-heartbeat`). Ctrl+C or SIGTERM while one of those replies was pending left the read running: the CLI hung until the cleanup deadline force-killed it (exit 137), or the read timed out and the report printed late.

The sibling reads in the same command were already fixed: the scan probe/readiness wait (#197969, #197909) and the `status` projection read (#197909) forward the signal. `status-runtime-shared.ts` — the shared deep-read helper already importing `getAsyncWorkSignal` for `reportStatusScanFailureUnlessInterrupted` — was the remaining signal-blind read path in the status family.

Precedent: #197909 (same command, scan-phase reads), #196976 (channels status), #197174 (models catalog diagnostics — same helper-level `signal?.throwIfAborted()` shape), #198083 (hooks).

## Why This Change Was Made

- `queryStatusGateway` now takes `getAsyncWorkSignal()` and forwards it to `callGateway`, with `signal?.throwIfAborted()` on both the fulfillment and rejection arms, so an interrupted RPC rejects with the canonical abort reason instead of being mapped into a `{ kind: "request" }` failure (which `status --all` rendered as a report error and `status --json` rendered into its output via health suppression).
- `resolveStatusRuntimeSnapshot` re-throws through the JSON `suppressHealthErrors` catch when the work signal aborted (real probe failures still collapse into the JSON error object as before), and checks the signal once more before returning so a late interrupt cannot publish a half-built snapshot.
- No consumer changes: `status.command.ts` / `status-json-command.ts` / `status-all.ts` keep their existing interrupt plumbing; the abort now reaches it through the shared helper.

No new validator, option, config, or policy. Normal (non-interrupted) behavior is unchanged: the same RPCs with the same timeouts; a fulfilled read returns the same values.

Production LOC is +16/-3 (1 file); test +35/-0 (1 file).

Classification: `behavior-completing` (completes the interrupt-forwarding shape for the last signal-blind read path in the status family).

## User Impact

Interrupting a pending deep Gateway read now stops the read promptly and exits with the normal SIGINT/SIGTERM status, without printing a late report error line. Non-interrupted failures keep their current rendering. No configuration, storage, protocol, or migration changes.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `ff705c1a667f46457bf6fc352b85b842cd738706` (branch `fix/status-deep-read-cancel`)
- Current-main RED baseline: `91db919f2de1675ec62da6524f3bda0415f9f8b9`
- Production entry: `resolveStatusGatewayHealthSafe` / `resolveStatusRuntimeSnapshot` in `src/commands/status-runtime-shared.ts:60` (drives `openclaw status --deep`, `status --json`, `status --all`)
- Canonical owner exercised: `queryStatusGateway` forwarding `signal` into `callGateway`
- Decision surface: abort vs. `{ kind: "request" }` failure mapping; JSON `suppressHealthErrors` swallow
- Recorder/readback boundary: rejected promise identity (`rejects.toBe(reason)`) + `callGateway` call-args readback (`signal: scope.signal`)

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

Current main vs. this branch, same three tests (new in this PR), `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/status-runtime-shared.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:

```text
BASE (production change stashed):
 × forwards the work signal to deep gateway reads
 × propagates an interrupt instead of reporting a request failure
 × does not let JSON health suppression swallow an interrupt
      Tests  3 failed | 16 passed (19)

HEAD (stash popped):
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

The three failures are the expected assertion points: `callGateway` receives no `signal`; an abort is mapped to `{error: ...}` instead of propagating; JSON suppression swallows the abort into a `{error: String(AbortError)}` value.

Consumer suites: `status.command-report.test.ts` (2), `status-json-command.test.ts` + `status-json.test.ts` + `status.command-sections.test.ts` (15) — all passed unchanged, including the exact-call assertion `toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith({method, params, config, timeoutMs})`, confirming no-signal callers are unaffected.

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/status-runtime-shared.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 19 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/status.command-report.test.ts src/commands/status-json-command.test.ts src/commands/status-json.test.ts src/commands/status.command-sections.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 17 passed
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts` — OK (net +37, allowance 400); `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs` — OK
- `npx oxfmt --check` on touched files — clean
- Not tested / proof ceiling: a pty-level `openclaw status --deep` SIGINT timing trace was not feasible on the remote test host (no usable dist build there; kernel 3.10 limits the E2E lane). Evidence therefore matches the bar the sibling merged fixes for this exact command carried (#197909 merged with mocked-transport command tests of the same class); the forwarding predicate itself is identical to the merged `readSelectedGatewayModelCatalog` pattern in #197174. The `status-all.ts` overview-path catch (still on the non-interrupt `reportStatusScanFailure` variant) is intentionally left out — that file is at its line cap and the path overlaps open channels-status work.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: +16/-3 (1 file)
- Test LOC: +35/-0 (1 file)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `getAsyncWorkSignal`/`AsyncWorkScope` and `callGateway`'s existing `signal` option; no new helpers, exports, or reporting paths

prs.title: feat(memory): add CJK bigram companion FTS index for two-character queries
prs.body:
Resolves #170997

## What Problem This Solves
When using `store.fts.tokenizer: "trigram"`, SQLite FTS5 requires query terms to be at least 3 characters long. As a result, two-character CJK queries (ubiquitous in Chinese and Japanese, e.g. "設定", "記憶", "台北") cannot be matched by FTS5 and currently fall back to an unranked substring scan. This causes:
1. **Zero BM25 ranking**: Keyword scores contribute 0, leaving result ordering purely arbitrary or vector-dominated.
2. **Slow fallback**: On larger corpora, fallback substring scanning is significantly slower than index-backed lookups (901 ms vs 99 ms on 1,301 chunks).

Because `node:sqlite` does not allow registering custom FTS5 tokenizers at runtime, an in-engine "bigram" tokenizer cannot be added.

This PR adds an opt-in companion Han bigram FTS index (`memory.search.store.fts.cjk: "bigram"`).

### Design
- **Companion Table**: `memory_index_chunks_cjk_fts` uses `tokenize='unicode61'`. Han runs in chunk text are encoded as overlapping character bigrams separated by spaces.
- **Two-Character Query Routing**: Queries consisting of 2-character Han terms bypass the trigram leg and query the companion table directly via `cjkBigramQuery`, providing full BM25 ranking.
- **Mixed OR Recovery**: When searching under `matchAny: true` with mixed Han and short ASCII terms (e.g. `設定 AI`), results are combined across companion BM25 hits and substring candidates via bounded UNION ALL.
- **Non-Regression**: ASCII terms, single-character terms, and queries with 3 or more characters continue using their existing trigram/unicode61 execution paths.
- **Derived State & Lifecycle**:
  - Enabling or disabling `store.fts.cjk: "bigram"` rebuilds only the FTS index leg without requiring any re-embedding. When disabled, `dropDisabledMemoryFts` drops the companion table.
  - Batched writes derive companion rows directly from the write plan using Kysely batch operations without rereading canonical chunks.
  - Deletions via `purgeForgottenMemory` and full resets via `MEMORY_INDEX_DERIVED_TABLES` ensure forgotten chunks are completely expunged from the companion index.
  - Reused schema admissions skip redundant schema scans or DROP queries.
- **Encapsulation & Architecture**: Companion SQL generation is strictly internal to Memory Core (`manager-search-shared.ts`). No implementation SQL builders or table-specific query generators are exported through the public Plugin SDK.

## Evidence

### Benchmarks
Measured on a CJK-heavy corpus (1,301 chunks, 93% with Han text), across 400 two-character terms:
- **Trigram only (baseline)**: Recalled 400/400, BM25-ranked 0/400, 901 ms total (unranked substring fallback)
- **With CJK bigram companion**: Recalled 400/400, BM25-ranked 400/400, 99 ms total (10x faster + BM25 ranked)
- Storage overhead: Companion index adds 0.84 MB alongside the 3.89 MB trigram index.

### Shipped CLI & Gateway Behavior Proof
Demonstrating execution of the shipped `openclaw` CLI binary against a production workspace upgraded from latest stable (`v2026.11.2`) with existing settings, chunks, and embeddings:

#### 1. Binary Version & Environment
```console
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.2
$ node --version
v26.3.1
$ git rev-parse HEAD
5b9b11183cd58525b5832a8ba71f3a228229f3d9
```

#### 2. Shipped CLI Search Execution (Short Han Query `設定`)
```console
$ openclaw memory search --query "設定"
0.673 MEMORY.md:335-337
## AI Agent 操作守則（2026-09-07 新增）

- **MEMORY.md 只放守則/原則/決策記錄**（短）。**詳細 SOP / 設定 / 踩坑 → Dify KB 查詢**（`dify-search` skill）

0.499 MEMORY.md:227-229
## Audio / TTS + STT

- **TTS**：OpenClaw 內建 `tts` tool，用 Microsoft Edge `zh-TW-HsiaoChenNeural`（`messages.tts.provider = microsoft`）

0.484 MEMORY.md:218-218
- **M2.5 fallback**（太慢/太貴時切）

0.479 MEMORY.md:41-42
- 改 WAL mode / 刪 WAL / fsck
```
Hits are ranked and sorted with positive BM25 scores (0.673, 0.499, etc.), surfacing the target "設定" note directly at Rank #1 instead of being buried by unranked rowid fallback.

#### 3. Upgrade & Compatibility Proof
- **Zero re-embedding**: Existing vector embeddings and canonical chunks in SQLite (`memory_index_chunks`) remained intact upon upgrade and enabling `store.fts.cjk: "bigram"`.
- **Zero drift**: Disabling the flag drops `memory_index_chunks_cjk_fts` cleanly via `dropDisabledMemoryFts` without leaving orphan database tables or corrupting agent state.

### Automated Test Suite
- Dedicated test suite `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search.cjk-bigram.test.ts` (9/9 passed):
  - ranks a two-character Han query with BM25
  - recalls a two-character Han query that trigram cannot match
  - keeps three-character Han queries on the trigram leg
  - keeps ASCII queries on the trigram leg
  - keeps single-character Han queries unranked
  - falls back to the substring plan without the companion index
  - keeps the companion index aligned with the chunk writer
  - recovers mixed Han and short terms under matchAny
  - drops the companion index when the option transitions to off
- Reused admission & schema lifecycle tests:
  - `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema-admission.test.ts` (10/10 passed)
- Ratchet checks verified against latest `upstream/main`:
  - `pnpm check:assertion-safety --base upstream/main --no-merge-base` (OK: 0 violations)
  - `pnpm check:database-dialect-ratchet --base upstream/main --no-merge-base` (OK: 0 growth)
  - `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main --no-merge-base` (OK: slack 40)

The host-remediation browser test opens the command palette settings summary, then waits for project rows that are only rendered after selecting Workspace. Both desktop and phone cases time out.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Restore the missing Workspace click so the test exercises unavailable computers in both selectors. All tooltip, selection, and no-session-created assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

Both original cases fail at the project-row locator on the base and pass after the one-line change. Default tsrs, targeted lint and formatting, whitespace checks, and independent review pass. No sleeps, timeout changes, or weaker assertions. Production delta: zero lines; test delta: one line.

## Exact-head CI

[Run 43547288763](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43547288763), attempt 1, completed with six failures in `checks-ui (2/3)` and `checks-ui (3/3)`; the aggregate failed because of those two leaves. The tested merge was `969ae8a3d0ce75fd63ecd2a119593346f5a1184b`, with ordered parents `9bf3e79c823a51b098ab892d2f8f505931cd5671` and this PR head `5a2ae40548c521517972a43b8ed309a47256bf31`. Each failed test and its inspected production owners/helpers is byte-identical between that actual baseline and tested merge. This PR only changes the separate host-remediation E2E fixture.

Five failures match the exact cases and assertions from scheduled main run 43540514362:

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` — `chat responsive browser layout > keeps the composer bottom controls, attachment, and primary action aligned at 568x320`; `keeps short-landscape composer adjunct rows scroll-reachable`; `keeps short-landscape slash menu visible inside the bounded composer` (tracked by #198532).
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts` — `chat model controls > applies model, reasoning, and speed for the session that opened the picker` (obsolete physical-button assertion, tracked by #198546).
- `ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control-view.test.tsx` — `keeps one mounted model view live without depending on draft revisions` (tracked by #198535).

The sixth is `ui/src/pages/cron/cron-page.lifecycle.test.ts > preserves catalog provider identity through model selection and save (catalog-needed)`: the unchanged case timed out waiting for its lazy editor, before model selection or save. The focused two-case replay and all 33 lifecycle cases pass unchanged; that passing replay does not establish a fix. Open PR #185707 overlaps by removing the group; this is recorded as overlap, without endorsing deletion as a repair. The unresolved readiness failure is independent of the host-remediation change.

These attributed inherited failures are retained as failed CI under the authorized maintainer exception. The two original host-remediation cases pass with the one-line repair; no timeout or assertion was weakened.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep model picker interactions stable
prs.body:
Related: #157466 (picker curation; this does not implement hidden models).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes model-picker interactions that unexpectedly close the picker, fail to retain dragged provider order, or leave Favorites stale until reopening.

## User Impact

Users can favorite and browse models without shifting rows or accidentally changing the selected model, reorder providers in Chat and New Session, and use a quieter, slightly narrower picker with working keyboard shortcuts. Mobile sizing and context-window values are preserved; no migration or configuration change is needed.

Desktop stars remain pointer-hover-only, including when a star button receives keyboard focus, as explicitly requested during design review. This retains the known accessibility tradeoff of an invisible focused star button; touch stars remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker and composer now respect each other’s click, drag, and keyboard ownership. Favorites membership stays live while provider-row ordering retains its opening snapshot. The change reuses existing preference and browser-local provider-order owners.

The presentation pass uses one trailing star/check column, centers provider glyphs, shows short provider lists fully, removes numeric keycaps while retaining numeric activation, reuses the shared scrollbar, fades clipped list edges, and centers the desktop overlay when space permits. Context-window controls match the adjacent 11px metadata without reducing their hit targets. Desktop width changes from 440px to 416px; automatic-account copy becomes “Account: Auto” in the trigger and “Automatic” in its menu. Short desktop viewports now fit the popup to the available side of its trigger rather than overlapping it.

The account control’s existing active-run lock and chevron are unchanged. The idle account menu works; the reported no-op click was not independently reproduced in the requester’s original state.

## Evidence

- Initial focused proof: 55 unit tests, 42 Chromium picker/shared-shortcut tests, 23 real-app Chat/New Session scenarios, and all six combined capture scenarios pass. These cover native provider drag/reload, live Favorites, pointer/keyboard behavior, touch/context hit targets, empty/loading catalogs, and idle/actual-send account states.
- UI build, UI typecheck, scoped semantic lint, stylelint, formatting, i18n baseline, test-line allocation, and whitespace checks pass. No thresholds were raised.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete local delta against `9bf3e79c823a51b098ab892d2f8f505931cd5671`, with relevant unchanged owners supplied: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Reviewed candidate: `f489a1525136e1fda3e977034f6b504d22399860`. Subsequent typography, placement/CSS, and shortcut corrections each received fresh independent delta review with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The reviewers did not execute tests; test results are separate executed evidence.
- Typography regressions failed at 12px/13px versus adjacent 11px metadata, then passed at 1280px desktop and 390px emulated touch. Both refreshed capture scenarios pass.
- CI remediation: both short-viewport placement regressions, all 25 account lifecycle tests, and three desktop/touch star scenarios pass. Shortcut activation now shares the registered-shortcut owner instead of duplicating slash/digit dispatch. Its 37 Chromium picker tests and scoped checks pass. The exact prior CI merge-context performance comparison exits 0: boot JavaScript is 459 normalized gzip bytes smaller; total CSS is 7 raw bytes smaller and 36 gzip bytes larger, within the existing allowance. Prior-head GitHub `control-ui-performance` also passed in [43556981033](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43556981033). Existing baseline ceiling warnings remain; limits are unchanged.
- Final mechanical repair: a new main-branch fixture conflict was resolved without changing the approved absent-keycap behavior, provider-local numeric activation, or 8px placement. Main’s model-name memoization and dictation changes are retained. The inert-space test now uses a center-top native click target instead of the corner that CI reported as intercepted by `<body>`; all interaction assertions remain. All 37 Chromium picker tests (14.51s) and all seven New Session catalog scenarios (20.89s), scoped formatting and whitespace checks pass. Published head `eb4043ccc8e267ed8c678f6cc1ec6c7c10dad575` is tree-identical to tested local candidate `3a8325579498dac7118bd029fea6f88c12680fe0`.
- Exact-head CI [43557689189](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43557689189) is pending. Earlier failed runs and prior-head passes are not current-head green proof. The previously observed `chat-view.test.ts:2998` element-type assertion also failed identically on main run [43551669456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43551669456), job `132315665357`; this does not establish inheritance for other failures.
- Proof uses real app components with synthetic Gateway data and emulated 390px touch—not live-provider traffic or a physical phone. Local WebKit startup did not reach tests; the new native click target still needs exact-head WebKit CI proof. A separate synthetic geometry probe did not establish the earlier rounded-corner explanation.

<details>
<summary>Review disposition, proof correction and test cost</summary>

ClawSweeper’s account-label and CSS-budget findings are repaired. Its focus-visible recommendation conflicts with the explicitly requested desktop hover-only behavior, so that product choice is retained with its accessibility limitation stated above; arrow navigation and numeric model activation remain intact. Executed real-app interaction regressions cover drag/reload, live Favorites, inert clicks and slash/numeric ownership. Existing screenshots are visual proof, not recordings of those transitions. No WebKit or live-provider result is claimed.

The earlier combined capture run’s failed active-run assertion used session-roster flags that did not establish a local running turn. Exercising the actual composer send establishes the disabled account state; the corrected scenario passes. A misleading source-map excerpt pointed at a favorites line, but the named failed test and assertion were the active-run fixture. The first conflict-check E2E command referenced a nonexistent configuration and ran no tests; the supported invocation passed all seven scenarios.

Simplification removed the separate numeric-keycap renderer and desktop/mobile star copies, dropped 45 lines of capture-only scaffolding from maintained regressions, consolidated repeated favorite selectors, and removed duplicate shortcut dispatch. The 119-line test allocation above the standard allowance covers distinct native drag, keyboard-capture, touch-hit-target, virtual-scroll, and computed typography boundaries that unit tests cannot prove. Typography assertions reuse existing desktop/touch scenarios rather than adding new launches.

</details>

### Short-viewport repair

After: the menu fits below its trigger in the 1280×320 regression viewport, leaving an 8px trigger gap and 8px bottom margin. This is the actual application with synthetic models and the existing placement fixture positioning the trigger near the top; it is not a live session or a natural composer-layout capture.

![After: model menu fits below its trigger in a short viewport](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfcef635-1df6-4bfd-88f3-8978c1c86204)

### Before and after

Matched automatic-account menu, current-main baseline `72f90dde293d5e9` versus the reviewed change. Real UI, synthetic Gateway/model/account data.

| Before | After |

| ![Before: 440px picker with long automatic-account labels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b400da2f-1438-4338-8d2f-0e021d4bec3b) | ![After: 416px picker with concise automatic-account labels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8493e10-b2e1-4edc-af80-9e258e48a891) |

<details>
<summary>Desktop Favorites, mixed-provider scrolling, and emulated touch</summary>

![Desktop: live Favorites and a fixed star/check slot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1e555dd-d78f-4530-a56a-d6b5df649824)

![Mixed-provider search: context values and clipped-edge fades](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1601bd5-e52e-469c-8146-4bd6448adaa3)

![Previous touch presentation, before the typography correction](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f71f785-deea-4e51-8674-5129a9c49ce0)

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): invalidate Gateway-cached MCP runtimes on mcp reload
prs.body:
Closes #164642

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw mcp reload` reported "Disposed cached MCP runtimes", but it only disposed CLI-local runtimes. The Gateway process owns its own cached session MCP runtimes, and the CLI command could not reach across the process boundary — so the Gateway's stdio MCP server kept serving the stale runtime and subsequent agent turns never saw the new MCP config.

## What Changed

- New gateway method `mcp.reloadRuntimes` (`mcp-app` family, `operator.write`): disposes the Gateway-side session MCP runtimes via the existing `disposeAllSessionMcpRuntimes` owner.
- The CLI's `mcp reload` dispatches the method before the local dispose and degrades gracefully when no Gateway is reachable (the CLI-local dispose always runs; the log states which side was disposed).

## Evidence

- Handler regression (`mcp.reload-runtimes.test.ts`): the method disposes all session MCP runtimes and acknowledges `{ ok: true }`. Red on `origin/main` (no such method).
- Suites: recovery 222/222, `session-accessor.readonly` 26/26, `server-startup-post-attach` 115/115; `tsc` core clean in all touched files.
- The reporter's source inspection (CLI-local dispose only) matches the pre-fix behavior; the gateway-side dispose reuses the same owner the server-close path already calls.


## Update — 2026-10-04 (Rev 3 rework)

- **Lease-preserving reload**: the handler now runs the Gateway's own config-reload path (`reloadSessionMcpRuntimes`, the same one the hot-reload flow uses) instead of the shutdown-grade `disposeAllSessionMcpRuntimes` — admitted calls keep their runtimes; only stale ones rebuild on the next turn. The manager's `reloadConfig` propagates per-runtime reload failures (no swallowed errors).
- **Authority revalidation**: the handler reads the request's mutation authority and asserts it current immediately before the reload — a caller revoked during the acquisition wait can no longer trigger it.
- **CLI output**: the failure branch now states which side was disposed and that the Gateway-side reload was **not confirmed** (no more misleading "active agents use new config" assurance when the reload did not run); the no-Gateway case is labeled explicitly. The import-boundary assertion follows.
- Handler tests: reload shape (`reloadPlugins: false`), authority revalidation observed, and the failure path responding with an error shape.

Still open: the authority-chain live evidence (allowed reload, read-only rejection, queued revocation preventing closure, discovery/active-call survival) and the command-scope framing — the reload semantics now match the Gateway's own hot-reload behavior rather than a Gateway-wide teardown.


## Update — 2026-11-06 (Rev 5 findings)

- **Unconfirmed cleanup joined into the reload outcome** (`src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime-parts.ts`): a session-parts reload that retires servers now throws when the recorded cleanup failure is outstanding, so a Gateway-level reload cannot resolve successfully while a retired transport's cleanup is unconfirmed. The hot-reload caller already degrades a rejected reload to a warning (`disposeMcpRuntimesWithTimeout`); the RPC path now surfaces it as an error response.
- **Unapplied config reported, not claimed** (`src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.ts`, `src/cli/mcp-cli.reload.ts`): the handler response carries `configApplied` next to `reloaded`. With `gateway.reload.mode=off` the command rebuilds runtimes from the published snapshot but leaves pending on-disk edits unapplied, and the CLI prints that caveat instead of promising new config.
- **Discovery order**: `mcp.reloadRuntimes` moved out of the legacy advertised prefix into the additive section (frozen-prefix assertion green again), and `since` follows the protocol guard's current train (`2026.11`).
- **CLI + docs**: the reload command moved to a sibling module (`mcp-cli.reload.ts`) per the line-cap ratchet; `docs/cli/mcp/registry.md` now states that reload contacts the configured Gateway and rebuilds from the published snapshot.
- Regression: `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime-parts.reload-cleanup.test.ts` — a reload whose retired part fails cleanup rejects; red against the prior revision (verified by checkout-swap).

prs.title: fix(dns): publish CoreDNS config atomically so failed writes keep the operator's files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #184888. `openclaw dns setup --apply` rewrote the operator's existing CoreDNS `Corefile`, the generated `.server` files, and the zone bootstrap through a truncating in-place write: `fs.writeFileSync` directly on the final path, or `sudo tee` (which also truncates) for root-owned paths. An ENOSPC, crash, or kill between truncation and write completion left the operator's CoreDNS configuration empty or partial, with no recovery copy anywhere — the file lives outside OpenClaw's state directory, so OpenClaw held none.

## User Impact

An operator running wide-area discovery DNS setup on a host that already runs CoreDNS could lose their entire CoreDNS configuration to a mid-write failure, breaking LAN-wide DNS resolution until the file was restored by hand. With this change, a failed or interrupted publication leaves the previous `Corefile` byte-for-byte intact, no longer restarts CoreDNS on a failed path, and the command reports the failure instead of silently proceeding.

## Why This Approach

Publication goes through the repo's atomic-write convention (`@openclaw/fs-safe` `replaceFileAtomicSync`): a same-directory staged file + rename, fsynced, parent dir synced. Root-owned paths fall back to a privileged staged publish. The already-safe zone publisher (`replaceWideAreaZoneFile`) is unchanged.

### Review findings, addressed one by one

Round 1 (reviewed head `5b0061eb`):

- **[P2] Resolve file symlinks before invoking the atomic publisher** — fixed. `resolvePublicationTarget` walks the destination's symlink chain (bounded at 32 hops, dangling links included) to the final target before publication, restoring the plain write's follow-the-link semantics while leaving the operator's link in place. A dangling link resolves to its missing target, which the plain write would have created.
- **[P2] Preserve ownership on the ordinary atomic path** — fixed. A rename publishes a new inode, so the staged file receives the operator's uid/gid before it replaces theirs. Setting a group outside the invoking account's memberships fails EPERM, which the publication router treats as a permission failure and re-runs through the privileged path (which chowns under sudo) — privilege is used only when necessary.
- **[P1] Create privileged staging files privately before writing content** — fixed. The privileged path creates the staging sibling exclusive and mode 0600 (`sudo install -m 600 /dev/null`) *before* any configuration byte exists, then `sudo tee`s into that existing private file, applies preserved uid/gid/mode, and renames.
- **[P2] Respect the operator's umask for newly created files** — fixed. Both publishers create fresh files with `0666 & ~process.umask()` (the plain write's contract) instead of a hardcoded 0644.
- **[P2] Narrow the mocked tee destination before writing it** — fixed in `5401ceca`.

Round 2 (reviewed head `5048abb1`):

- **[P1] Keep ordinary staging private until ownership is restored** — fixed in `5503e4e8`. The atomic writer now stages with mode 0600, so the configuration bytes are never readable by an account outside the operator's readership — not even in the window between writing them and publishing them. The operator's uid/gid and final mode are restored on the staged file immediately before the rename. New regression observes the staged file at the ownership hand-off (the moment it holds the bytes) and requires it to still be 0600 there.
- **[P2] Flush privileged staging before publishing it** — fixed in `5503e4e8`: the privileged path flushes the staged file before the rename and the parent directory after it.
- **[P2] Match the actual sudo tee command in the regression** — fixed in `5503e4e8`: the regression matched `" sudo tee "` against a joined command string that never carries that prefix, so the ordering assertion could not hold on any POSIX run. It now matches the structured executable and argument fields.
- **[medium] Verify staging confidentiality across the ownership transition** — the mechanism is fixed in `5503e4e8`, and the macOS run below samples the staged file itself.

Round 3 (reviewed head `5503e4e8`):

- **[P2] Wait for the privileged staging file to finish synchronizing** — fixed in `c6cf53f1`. macOS `sync` ignores pathname operands and only schedules a global sync that may return before the flush completes, so the previous repair did not provide the promised crash-safety on the supported platform. The privileged flush now synchronizes the descriptor explicitly: it opens the staged file (and the parent directory after the rename) and fsyncs it through the same runtime that owns the command, so the rename cannot outrun the flush. The regression asserts the flush happens before the rename and the directory flush after it.

Round 4 (reviewed head `c6cf53f1`):

- **[P1] Preserve existing macOS ACLs before replacing configuration files** — fixed in `63dae340`. macOS carries a per-file access policy beside the mode, and a replacement inode does not inherit it, so restoring uid/gid/mode alone dropped a file-specific denial. The publication now captures the policy entries (`ls -lde`) before replacing the file and restores them on the staged file (`chmod +a`) right before the rename, on both the ordinary and the privileged path. The macOS run below shows the deny entry surviving the publication with the account still denied, and a regression runs the real `chmod +a`/`ls -lde` round-trip on the macOS CI shard.
- **[P2] Match the executable before the eval flag in flush assertions** — fixed in `63dae340`. The regression looked for `["-e", execPath]` while the publisher invokes sudo with `[execPath, "-e", script, path]`, so the assertion could not hold; it now matches the real command, which is why the exact-head CI run failed it.

Round 6 (reviewed head `b54b8b3c`):

- **Findings: none** — the review confirmed the three prior code findings resolved with no remaining introduced defect. The remaining items are proof: the interrupted-restoration case above (run 41296608480, case 7) and the capture-failure regression below.
- **ACL-capture failure** — a regression on the macOS CI shard simulates a failed `/bin/ls -lde` capture and asserts the publication aborts with the operator's file byte-identical, its deny entry still present, and no staging sibling left behind (`aborts the publication when the access policy cannot be captured`).

Round 8 (against the round-7 findings, head `b3b64649`):

- **[P2] The capture-failure regression never exercised the capture failure** — fixed in `b3b64649`. The regression spied on the default `child_process` export, but production imports the named `spawnSync`, which the mock factory routes through its own wrapper, so the injection never reached it. The failure is now injected through `spawnSyncMock` itself, wrapping the existing implementation and returning a correctly shaped failed result for `/bin/ls`.
- **Ordinary-path coverage** — new regression in `b3b64649`: a non-permission failure (ENOSPC) from the atomic publisher aborts the publication **without** routing to the privileged fallback; the operator's file stays untouched, no staging sibling remains, and CoreDNS is not restarted. This is the ordinary path the CLI transcript cannot reach on a root-owned target.
- **Leftover check** — the harness now lists hidden entries (`ls -1A`), so a leftover `.Corefile…` / `.openclaw-dns-config…` sibling is actually detected; the earlier `ls -1` listing silently excluded them.

Round 7 evidence (against the round-6 proof gap, head `b54b8b3c` / `04be35d4`):

- **After interruption, on both publishers** — case 7 covers the privileged publisher and the new case 8 covers the ordinary one: the managed symlink target (published through the ordinary path) was denied by a file-specific ACL and made immutable, so the final rename failed after the restoration completed. The managed target stayed byte-identical, its printed policy entry is unchanged (`user:dnsproofreader deny read`), the excluded account is still refused, no staging sibling survived, and CoreDNS was not restarted.
- **Preventing restart** — cases 2, 7 and 8 assert the failure output never reaches the restart step ("Starting CoreDNS" absent) and the CoreDNS service PID is unchanged across the failure.
- **ACL-capture failure** — covered by the in-process regression on the macOS CI shard (`04be35d4`): a failed `/bin/ls -lde` capture aborts the publication with the operator's file byte-identical, its deny entry present, and no staging sibling. An external CLI-level capture failure is not constructible on a healthy host because production pins the system `/bin/ls` precisely so user-installed ls builds cannot enter this path.
- **Through restoration** — the restoration runs entirely inside the staged file's private 0600 mode (chown → chmod +a → grant mode), which is the ordering fix from `b54b8b3c`; the in-process boundary test observes the staged file at that transition on the macOS CI shard, and the external samples of the staged file (mode 600, reader denied) bracket it.

### Data-model compatibility

This change touches no config, state, or database schema. The compatibility surface is the operator's on-disk CoreDNS configuration, and it is pinned by regressions (mode, ownership, symlink, dangling link, umask) and by the macOS run below: a configuration published by the latest stable release keeps its contents, ownership, permissions and symlink after the upgrade to this build.

## Evidence

### Real macOS behavior proof (run)

A macOS-14 runner drove the shipped CLI (`pnpm openclaw dns setup --domain openclaw.internal --apply`) as an unprivileged account against a root-owned, group-restricted `Corefile`, so the privileged staged publication ran with real sudo. An independent local account (`dnsproofreader`, outside the operator's group) stood in for the unauthorized reader. (harness: `proof/macos-dns-publication-proof.sh`, fork branch `proof/macos-dns-publication`)

```
=== case 1: successful privileged publication ===
after publication: mode=640 owner=root:staff; reader denied
=== case 2: a failed privileged publication preserves the operator's Corefile ===
failed publication exit status: 1
Reason: sudo install -m 600 /dev/null /opt/homebrew/etc/coredns/.Corefile.openclaw-15596.tmp failed: install: ...: Operation not permitted
operator Corefile after the failed publication: unchanged (.:53 {|  errors|  log|}|# marker-before-interruption|)
=== case 6: an ACL-denied principal stays denied across the publication ===
policy before the publication:
 0: user:dnsproofreader deny read
reader denied before the publication
 0: user:dnsproofreader deny read
reader denied after the publication
=== case 7: an interrupted publication preserves the operator's file and policy ===
interrupted publication exit status: 1
Reason: sudo mv /opt/homebrew/etc/coredns/.Corefile.openclaw-9268.tmp /opt/homebrew/etc/coredns/Corefile failed: exit 1
operator Corefile after the interrupted publication: unchanged
reader still denied the operator's Corefile
no staging sibling survived
=== case 8: an interrupted ordinary publication preserves the managed target and policy ===
Reason: sudo mv /opt/homebrew/etc/coredns/.managed-Corefile.openclaw-9535.tmp /opt/homebrew/etc/coredns/managed-Corefile failed: exit 1
managed target after the interruption: unchanged; policy: user:dnsproofreader deny read
reader still denied the managed target
no staging sibling survived; CoreDNS not restarted
=== case 2 restart assertion ===
CoreDNS not restarted across the failed publication (service PID unchanged)
=== case 3: symlinked Corefile keeps its link ===
link preserved: managed-Corefile; managed target updated
=== case 4: latest stable configuration survives the upgrade ===
latest stable exit status: 0
after the upgrade: mode=640 owner=root:staff content=ok
=== PROOF PASSED ===
```

Runs: <https://github.com/syxscott/openclaw/actions/runs/41296608480> (cases 1-4, 6-7), <https://github.com/syxscott/openclaw/actions/runs/41297533034> (case 8 ordinary-publisher interruption and the restart-suppression assertions), and <https://github.com/syxscott/openclaw/actions/runs/41313384334> (the same suite with the leftover check covering hidden staging files). Case 7 fails the final rename after the restoration completed (immutable Corefile), which exercises the interruption point that matters: the operator's file stays byte-identical, its deny entry is still printed, the excluded account is still refused, and the CLI cleaned its staging sibling.

What that establishes, on the supported platform:

- The publication succeeds end to end and the operator's file keeps its **contents, mode (0640) and owner (root:staff)**; the group-excluded account still cannot read it.
- A **failed** privileged publication exits non-zero with the cause (`sudo install ... Operation not permitted`) and leaves the operator's Corefile **byte-identical** with its mode and ownership untouched — the interruption case.
- A **file-specific deny ACL** (`user:dnsproofreader deny read`, not expressible in the mode) survives the publication and the account remains denied — before and after. This is the access-policy preservation that `63dae340` adds.
- A **symlinked** Corefile keeps its link and the managed target is updated instead.
- The configuration published by the **latest stable release** (`openclaw@latest`) still loads and keeps its contents, ownership and permissions after the upgrade to this build.

**The staging window** (the configuration bytes sitting in the sibling file before the rename) is milliseconds long in the real command and cannot be sampled reliably from outside the process — eleven harness iterations established that empirically (PATH interception, NODE_OPTIONS preload, and directory-permission forcing each failed to yield a deterministic sample). That window is therefore covered where it is deterministically observable: the in-process boundary tests run on this PR's macOS CI shard against the real fs and the real fs-safe publisher — `keeps the staged configuration private until the operator's mode is restored` observes the staged file at the ownership hand-off (the moment it holds the bytes) and requires it to still be 0600, and `keeps the operator's macOS access policy across a publication` runs the real `chmod +a`/`ls -lde` policy round-trip through the publication. An earlier run of the external harness did sample the staged file live at `mode=600` with the unauthorized reader denied (<https://github.com/syxscott/openclaw/actions/runs/41172290366>); the deterministic coverage is the CI shard.

### Regression suite

- Red on base / green on fix: on `main`, an injected ENOSPC during Corefile publication left the Corefile truncated mid-import-line (the issue's damage scenario); with the fix the previous bytes survive and CoreDNS is not restarted.
- POSIX regressions (this PR's CI ubuntu + macOS shards): mode preservation (0640 stays 0640), private staging until the ownership hand-off, macOS access-policy round-trip, symlinked-Corefile publication to the managed target, dangling-link target creation, and the forced-privileged-path publication.
- Windows host note: the development host cannot execute the POSIX-only regressions locally — Windows has no POSIX mode semantics, so the atomic writer's staged-file chmod fails with EPERM and the command routes to the privileged path on this host, and NTFS drops the group/other bits the mode assertions check. Those regressions are verified in this PR's CI; the platform-neutral suite passes locally (10 passed, 11 POSIX/darwin-skipped).
- Checks: `pnpm vitest run src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts src/infra/widearea-dns.test.ts src/infra/widearea-dns.boundary.test.ts`, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:core`, the cli test-typecheck config, and both ratchets — all clean locally; the full matrix runs in CI.

### Latest head (`5bf22fcb7e`)

Three independent reviews of the publication path (not the hosted bot) found defects that are fixed on this head, and the test mock had drifted from the production contract it stood in for:

The head also merges `origin/main`: the test-line ratchet measures a pull request's merge tree against its merge base, and this branch's base was six days old, so main's own test-line drift was charged to this change. With main merged the lane measures this change alone (`Test lines OK: 6623658; ceiling: 6623949; slack: 291`) and the allocation still covers exactly this change's measured growth. The scalar reconciliation that drift had motivated (#194489) is no longer needed and was closed with its measurement: at `origin/main` (`28b82d78e1`) the tree is 292 lines under its ceiling.

- The privileged inspection replayed the inherited entries at the **parent directory's** ACL indexes; the restore inserts at the recorded position, so those indexes do not exist on the staged file — the publication aborted instead of restoring the policy. The entries are renumbered contiguously now, like the unprivileged reader.
- Stripping the inheritance flags left the separating comma on the entry (`group:admin deny write,`), which is not a valid access policy — any directory with a `file_inherit` grant failed to restore. The separator goes with the flags now.
- The inspection treated every stat failure as a missing destination and continued past a symlink chain it could not resolve; only `ENOENT` is a first creation now, and an unresolved chain aborts.
- The privileged helper scripts ran `process.execPath`, which in the standalone build is the OpenClaw executable itself: it cannot evaluate a script, so the privileged publication failed there and the CLI was briefly run as root. A Node or Bun runtime is resolved now, and the scripts read their path from the last argument.
- The mock re-implemented the inspection script and returned bare strings where the script returns `{ position, entry }` records, so the privileged policy restore was never exercised. The mock now runs the production script, which pins the contract instead of imitating it.

New regressions on this head: the inspection script reports positional records with the inherited entries renumbered; the privileged publication hands the staged file the operator's captured ids before the rename; a failing privileged publication (`sudo mv`) leaves the operator's file byte-identical, removes the staging sibling and does not restart CoreDNS; and the access-policy **order** survives a replacement — the same entries at the same positions, which is what `chmod +a#` exists for (`chmod +a` canonicalizes the order and can put an allow in front of a deny).

### Accepted edge cases

- The staging file's name carries a random component, so another account that may write the destination directory cannot place a file at a known staging path before the privileged steps run. An account that may write that directory can still substitute the staged file between the privileged steps; the operator's directory permissions are the boundary there, and the truncating write this replaces exposed the destination path itself, so the substitution was easier to arrange before, not harder.
- The privileged runtime stays the operator's own toolchain. An account that can replace that runtime could already run it with sudo; the publication does not add a new privilege to it.
- The macOS proof harness runs on this fork's macOS Actions quota, which is currently exhausted (the dispatch on this head was cancelled with zero steps). The macOS regressions therefore run in this PR's upstream macOS CI lane, which executes `src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts` on a macOS runner.

prs.title: improve(backup): capture PostgreSQL and SQLite stores in parallel
prs.body:
Related: #183094

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup create` waits for the shared state PostgreSQL export to finish before it starts the SQLite agent snapshots, even though neither depends on the other's data, so capture takes about as long as both added together.

## User Impact

User impact: `backup create` and `backup create --verify` finish capture sooner when the shared state store is on PostgreSQL. On the 183094 fixture capture dropped from about 53-57 s to about 33 s, and `backup create --verify` from about 226 s to about 199 s. The archive format, compression, per-store consistency and every integrity check are unchanged. Hosts with slow disks may see less gain, because the two captures then compete for the same disk.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared state export now runs in its worker while the other stores are captured, still one at a time, so at most two captures are in flight. Their plan is built before the export supplies the agent registry. When the exported registry only names agent stores that plan already owns under the same path (the usual case: agents at their default paths), those snapshots are kept. Otherwise they are discarded and the stores are captured again from the inventory sealed with the registry, as before. So the archived registry is still the image that chose which agents were captured.

Only SQLite captures overlap the shared export. Every PostgreSQL export takes the local state owner on the state database, so another PostgreSQL-backed store (for example a retained Matrix account root) awaits the shared export before it exports, as on main.

If either side fails, the other stops: the export worker is aborted and joined, and the store loop stops before its next store (a SQLite snapshot already in progress finishes first). The first error is reported after both have settled, so nothing writes into the scratch directory after cleanup starts. Manifest order is unchanged (shared store first, then plan order).

`docs/cli/backup.md` now says the shared export runs alongside the other stores instead of "one after another". The legacy audit retry wrapper moved to its own file, unchanged, to keep `backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts` under the line cap.

## Evidence

- New `src/infra/backup-sqlite-snapshot.concurrent.test.ts` (real SQLite capture and planning; only the PostgreSQL worker is faked):
  - agent stores are captured while the export is still running, manifest order is unchanged, and the archive walk reuses the capture's header probes. Fails on main (the agent capture waits for the export).
  - the exported registry decides reuse: a new agent store, or a known agent at another path, discards the concurrent snapshots and captures from the registry; a registry naming fewer agents keeps them; a registry giving a planned store to another agent is refused, as before. Each case checks that the archived shared image is the export the registry was read from and that every registered store was archived.
  - a failing agent store aborts the export and waits for it to settle, even when the worker settles later. Fails on main (hangs).
  - a failing export stops the agent captures.
  - a second PostgreSQL-backed store never exports while the shared export runs.
  - Mutation checks: not waiting for the export, or always reusing the concurrent snapshots, each fail the matching tests.
- New PostgreSQL conformance test `src/infra/database-engine/backup-parallel-capture.postgres.test.ts`, with the real database-backup worker and a real PostgreSQL export (see below).
- `src/infra/database-engine/matrix-roots.postgres.test.ts` (three PostgreSQL-backed state roots): passes on PostgreSQL 17 (2 of 2 runs on the final commit). The previous head failed it every time with `GatewayStateOwnerContentionError`, because a second export took the state owner while the shared export held it.
- Backup unit suites (`src/infra/backup-create*.test.ts`, `src/infra/backup-sqlite*.test.ts`, 15 files): 146 passed, 6 skipped.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed.
- Fixture timings: see below.

<details><summary>Real export worker: SQLite capture failure while the export runs</summary>

`backup-parallel-capture.postgres.test.ts` puts the shared state store on PostgreSQL 17 (20,000 rows of about 2 KB) and keeps the main agent store on SQLite. It runs `createBackupArchive` with the real database-backup worker. The SQLite agent capture throws as soon as the worker has a PostgreSQL connection open on the test database. The test asserts this order:

1. export worker run started
2. SQLite capture failed while the export was active
3. export worker run rejected
4. export worker pool close called, then joined
5. scratch cleanup started, with no export backend left in `pg_stat_activity`
6. scratch cleanup finished
7. `createBackupArchive` rejected with the SQLite error

After cleanup, the test checks for 1 s that the scratch directory stays absent. Any later write would have to recreate it.

The test does not import `database-suite-workers.test-support`, because that support shares one backup pool per worker URL and replaces its `close()` with a no-op.

The same scenario, run with timestamps and a recursive `fs.watch` on the scratch root. Paths are shown relative to the scratch directory, and the times are milliseconds from test start:

```text
3519  export worker run started (real database-backup worker, PostgreSQL export)
3706  fs.watch rename <scratch>/.../openclaw.sqlite.postgres/.pending (exists)
3834  fs.watch rename <scratch>/.../openclaw.sqlite.postgres/anchor.sqlite (exists)
3923  SQLite agent capture throws; PostgreSQL export backends active: 1
3980  export worker run settled: rejected (Error)
3980  export worker pool close called (runBackupTask finally)
3982  export worker joined; PostgreSQL export backends now 0
3986  scratch cleanup started; export backends 0
3995  fs.watch rename <scratch>/... (absent)   [11 removal events]
3995  fs.watch rename <scratch>/owner.sqlite (exists)
3996  scratch cleanup finished
3998  createBackupArchive rejected with the SQLite capture error
4046  fs.watch rename <scratch> (absent)
8040  scratch absent (ENOENT); export backends 0
```

The export had already written its `.pending` directory and anchor when the capture failed. After cleanup started, the only event for a path that still existed was the scratch's own `owner.sqlite` lock, which is removed with the directory at 4046. The scratch directory was still absent 4 s later. The scenario passed every run on this branch and on the previous head: 3 assertion-only runs and 2 timestamped runs on the final commit, plus 8 earlier runs.

</details>

<details><summary>Fixture timings</summary>

Synthetic 183094 fixture on a Mac Studio: shared state on PostgreSQL 17 (about 2.1 GB, 1 GiB blob rows), agent SQLite stores of 4.0, 1.0 and 0.5 GiB, about 4.8 GB workspace. `backup create --verify`, base and branch runs alternated, phases timed in a disposable instrumented build. Page cache was warm (no purge available), so disk-bound hosts will see different absolute numbers.

| run | capture | archive write | total (real) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main 1 | 57.1 s | 154.1 s | 226.3 s |
| branch 1 | 32.7 s | 152.7 s | 198.2 s |
| main 2 | 53.5 s | 159.5 s | 226.9 s |
| branch 2 | 32.8 s | 153.5 s | 199.7 s |

On the branch the export (about 26 s) overlaps the agent snapshots instead of preceding them. All four archives verified. The last branch archive was restored with `backup restore --target` into a fresh directory (`ok: true`, SQLite inventory verified), and the restored agent databases pass `PRAGMA quick_check`.

</details>
