prs.title: improve(backup): faster PostgreSQL export hashing for blob-heavy stores
prs.body:
Related: #183094

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL backups and database ports of blob-heavy stores spend much of their export time turning every BLOB into hex inside JSON just to hash the row.

## User Impact

`openclaw backup create`, update rollback captures and `openclaw database port` export PostgreSQL stores faster when they hold large BLOB rows. On a state store with 1 GiB of BLOB rows, the PostgreSQL export phase drops from about 24 s to about 18 s.

Existing backups and exact captures verify and restore with this build, including ones written by the published 2026.11.3 release. Port receipts in the old format still verify.

Downgrade limit: export manifests written by this build record `verification.digest: "typed-v1"`. Published releases with PostgreSQL support (2026.11.1 through 2026.11.3, Workboard only) read that object strictly, so their reader refuses these manifests with `Unrecognized key: "digest"`. The refusal happens before any PostgreSQL namespace or anchor is written. In practice this applies to exact captures and port captures. In 2026.11.3, `backup restore` of an archive from this build extracts the PostgreSQL capsule as files without importing it, `backup git restore` has only `--global` and `--agent` scopes, and an upgraded state directory is refused anyway (state schema 39, while 2026.11.3 supports 22). Whether that limit is acceptable is a maintainer decision. `docs/cli/backup.md` states it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every table digest used to hash `JSON.stringify` of each row with BLOB cells hex-encoded. The digest now hashes typed raw bytes: one tag byte and 8 bytes per value (integer, real, or byte length), then the TEXT or BLOB bytes as they are. Values cannot run into each other, and null, empty text, empty BLOB, integer, real, text and BLOB stay distinct. Integral numbers still hash as integers, as before, because PostgreSQL returns `integer` and `boolean` columns as JavaScript numbers while SQLite returns bigints; the SQLite and PostgreSQL sides of a port therefore still produce the same digest.

New digests are recorded with `verification.digest: "typed-v1"`. A stored proof without that id (an exact export, Git or archive capture, or a port receipt from an older build) is checked with the old JSON digest, so update rollback and port recovery across an upgrade keep working. The id only matters where a stored digest is compared: exact restores, and the database port staging and `verify` steps.

Across an update, the in-process updater retains the running package and binds every worker it starts, including the database backup worker, to that retained copy before replacing the package. Its update captures and rollback restores therefore read and write one manifest format. If retention fails, workers load the new package, which reads both formats.

## Evidence

Upgrade from published 2026.11.3, run locally on macOS arm64 with PostgreSQL 17.11:

- Installed `openclaw@2026.11.3` from npm (build `847611d`) into an isolated prefix and state directory. Through a running 2026.11.3 Gateway, created a board with settings (name, description with non-ASCII text, icon, color), five cards with labels, priorities, comments, a status change and a 16418-byte binary attachment. Moved Workboard to PostgreSQL with the 2026.11.3 `openclaw database port --to postgres`, then added a second board and five more cards on PostgreSQL. `openclaw backup create --verify` succeeded. Its Workboard manifest has profile `user-backup`, schema 3 and no `digest` field.
- Switched the same state directory and database to this build (`899504c`). `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` passed and kept the 2026.11.1 Workboard-only PostgreSQL setting. The Gateway served both boards and all ten cards with their comments and attachments. A per-table fingerprint (row count and MD5 of every row) of all 17 Workboard tables matched the pre-upgrade fingerprint. The same build then wrote a third board with cards and an attachment.
- Pre-upgrade backup restored with this build: `openclaw backup verify` and `openclaw backup restore` accept the 2026.11.3 archive. A 2026.11.3 archive has no PostgreSQL capsule inventory, so archive restore extracts the capsule as files and says so (behavior this PR does not touch). Restoring that extracted 2026.11.3 capsule by calling this build's matched-export restore functions directly produced a namespace whose 17 table fingerprints, board settings and attachment SHA-256 values are identical to the pre-upgrade store. A fresh installation of this build pointed at the restored anchor served the restored boards, cards, labels and the 16418-byte attachment.
- Exact capture written by 2026.11.3: on a second 2026.11.3 installation, interrupted `openclaw database port --to sqlite` after it had written its exact PostgreSQL capture (profile `exact`, no `digest`). This build's matched-export restore functions, called directly, verified and restored that capture, so exact verification on the legacy JSON digest passed. (This build's `database port --resume` and `--rollback` cannot take over that interrupted port for an unrelated reason: under the 2026.11.1 Workboard-only setting they ask for `--family`, which they also reject.) The restored rows match that installation's fingerprint. The same capture relabelled `typed-v1` is refused with `Exact PostgreSQL export verification differs from its manifest.` No anchor is written and no namespace is left behind.
- New backup with this build: `openclaw backup create --verify` writes `digest: "typed-v1"` and Workboard schema 4. `openclaw backup restore` of that archive imported a namespace identical to the live store, table by table.
- 2026.11.3 against a manifest from this build: its packaged reader refuses the Workboard capsule with `unrecognized_keys: digest`, writes no anchor and creates no namespace. 2026.11.3 `backup verify` of the whole archive passes, and its `backup restore` extracts files only. Pointed at the upgraded state directory, it refuses to start the restore because of the state schema.

Unit and integration tests:

- SQLite digest tests through `inspectDatabasePort`: 14 single-row variants hash differently (`["a","b"]` vs `["ab",""]` vs `["ab",null]`, null vs empty text vs empty BLOB, `1` as integer, text and BLOB vs `1.5`, one changed byte in a 70 KB BLOB, swapped values, one vs two rows), and reordered schema columns change the digest. The legacy digest of a fixed table matches the value the unpatched build computes. The typed digest matches an independent implementation of the format.
- The typed encoder matches an independent unbuffered reference encoder for values of 65527 to 65545 bytes (around the 64 KiB scratch buffer), 20,000 small rows spanning many buffer flushes, multibyte UTF-8, and empty text vs empty BLOB. Integers outside 64 bits are refused.
- Port `verify` accepts a receipt in the old format and refuses both old and new receipts after a row changes. Port staging against a source proof in the old format succeeds, records an old-format receipt that then verifies, resumes, and still refuses changed rows (this staging test fails on the previous revision).
- PostgreSQL round trip: an exact export rewritten to the old format restores; new digests without the id are refused.
- PostgreSQL conformance on PostgreSQL 17 (CI image and extensions), 16 files and 91 tests: port provider, state, agent and logbook ports, archive restore, Git backup with and without secret exclusion, port command (integration, mixed, recovery, refusals), backup, update candidate state and update preflight. Changed-file typecheck, lint and format pass.

Performance, state store ported to PostgreSQL 17 with 1024 rows of 1 MiB BLOBs, `openclaw backup create`, PostgreSQL export phase (`capturePostgresBackup`):

| build | run 1 | run 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 24.9 s | 23.6 s |
| after | 18.2 s | 17.9 s |

Row copy and verification inside it (`materializeDatabasePort`): 21.1 s / 20.2 s before, 14.7 s / 14.5 s after. The exact capture used by update rollback took 22.6 s before and 16.8 s after. Small rows are not slower: one million rows of text, integer, null and real hash in 5.1 to 5.8 s, against 5.8 to 9.6 s before, on a loaded machine.

prs.title: fix(agents): retract running deferred dispatcher when nested target starts
prs.body:
Fixes #194168

## What Problem This Solves

Discord progress mode with `toolProgress: true` renders **two identical rows** for each deferred tool call while it runs: one for the `dispatch_action` dispatcher and one for its nested target. Both rows share the same label and `running` status at the same time, even though the transcript records a single execution. This fix retracts the dispatcher row as soon as its nested target starts, so the live draft shows exactly one row per tool call. Independent tool calls with identical labels remain separate.

## Problem

With Discord progress mode and `toolProgress: true`, a deferred tool call dispatched through `dispatch_action` renders as **two identical rows** in the live draft while it runs: one for the dispatcher and one for its nested target. Both rows show the same label and the same `running` status at the same time.

The transcript shows each tool call executed exactly once.

## Root cause

`dispatch_action` is a pure forwarding wrapper. It publishes its own visible prepared item (`tool:<dispatcher-call-id>`) when it starts, and its nested target (`tool_call:<parent>:<name>:<seq>`, `parentToolCallId` = dispatcher id) publishes a second visible item with an identical label. The existing wrapper suppression (`resolveCompletedActivityWrappers` / `finalizeToolActivity`) only collapses a completed wrapper **at run termination**, so while the target is still running both rows stay on the draft.

## Fix

Represent a deferred dispatcher and its nested target as one live operation at the producer (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.start.ts`):

- When a nested target starts (`lifecycleProvenance: "nested"`) **with a visible activity**, look up its parent dispatcher from the tracked tool starts.
- If the parent is a `dispatch_action` wrapper that is still visible, retract its row by emitting an `update` item event with `hideFromChannelProgress: true` (the channel progress compositor clears the row by item id).
- Persist `hideFromChannelProgress` on the parent's start record so the dispatcher's terminal event stays hidden too — the run-termination collapse in `finalizeToolActivity` is unchanged.

A nested target whose activity is hidden (for example a routine `progress_card`, or a `wait`/`process.poll` child) does **not** replace the dispatcher: the shared activity owner (`resolveCompletedActivityWrappers`) keeps a wrapper visible when none of its children contributes a visible row, so the dispatcher stays visible until terminal collapse. This matches the routine-wrapper preservation policy established in #165358 and avoids leaving neither the dispatcher nor a hidden routine target countable.

A `dispatch_action` that fails to dispatch (no nested target) keeps its own visible row with the error, so no information is lost. Independent tool calls with identical labels stay separate because they have no parent/child relationship.

## Evidence

### Regressions (each fails on the prior head, passes with the fix)

1. `retracts a running deferred dispatcher once its nested target starts` — a visible `web_search` target replaces the running dispatcher row.
   - Before: the dispatcher receives no retraction update → assertion `expected [] to have a length of 1` fails.
   - After: exactly one `phase: "update"` item event with `hideFromChannelProgress: true`, and the target row stays visible.

2. `keeps a running deferred dispatcher when its nested target is routine` — a `progress_card` target (hidden activity) does not replace the dispatcher.
   - Before: the dispatcher is retracted anyway → assertion `expected [ { itemId: 'tool:dispatcher', ... } ] to have a length of +0 but got 1` fails.
   - After: no retraction update is emitted and the dispatcher stays visible.

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  15 passed (15)
```

### Related suites (all pass)

- `src/infra/agent-activity-events.test.ts` — 25 passed
- `src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts` — 59 passed
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.rest.test.ts` — 16 passed

### CI-equivalent checks

- `oxlint --type-aware --deny=warn` — clean
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` — clean
- `check-test-lines-ratchet` — pass (new test lines covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/issue-194168-deferred-dispatcher.txt`, 87)
- `check-test-mock-exports --prune` — 6387 → 6387, no new violations
- typecheck on changed files — 0 errors

## What was not tested

No live Discord round trip was run in this environment. The regression exercises the producer event stream (`handleToolExecutionStart`), which is the source both channels and the Control UI consume; the Discord draft-preview test suite confirms the retraction path (`hideFromChannelProgress` + item id) is honored by the compositor.

prs.title: fix(ios): chat fails with thinking "off" on Claude CLI reasoning opt-out
prs.body: Closes #198642 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: iOS chat sends fail with `Thinking level "off" is not supported` when a Claude CLI model's config row opts out of reasoning. ## User Impact User impact: chat on Claude CLI models with a `reasoning: false` config row works from the iOS app again. The thinking picker shows the runtime's levels and sends one of them, matching the web Control UI. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway keeps a configured `reasoning: false` on Claude CLI rows while publishing the runtime's mandatory thinking levels, which do not include `off`. The shared chat client treated `reasoning: false` alone as "thinking off", so it hid the picker and sent `off`, which the Gateway rejects as an explicit unsupported level. The client now gates to `off` on the opt-out only when the published levels include `off` or no levels are published, the same rule the web Control UI uses. Models with an `off` level and models without Gateway metadata keep their current behavior. ## Evidence - New `ChatViewModelTests` case: a `reasoning: false` model with levels `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `ultra` and default `medium`. prs.title: fix(auto-reply): keep emoji whole in group thread tool reply capture
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent posts a long reply in a group chat, the copy saved for the next round can end in half an emoji. That saved copy is invalid UTF-16, and it is the text the other agents are prompted with next round. The saved copy now stops at a whole character.

- Problem: `finalizeGroupThreadToolReply` captured the outgoing reply with `content?.slice(0, 4_000)`; a raw slice at a fixed offset splits a surrogate pair and keeps half a character.
- Solution: cap through the repository's existing UTF-16 owner, `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, which drops a dangling high surrogate instead of storing it.
- What changed: `src/auto-reply/group-thread-context.ts` (one import, one assignment) plus one send folded into the existing `it.each(["telegram", "slack", "discord"])` case in `src/agents/tools/message-tool-execution.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the 4,000-unit cap, the `{ observed, text }` capture contract, reply labeling, channel delivery, and the payload handed to `recordReply`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel already received a correct message; only the copy recorded for later rounds was corrupted, so the repair belongs at the capture boundary that owns the cap.

- Best fix: reuse the shared truncation owner (`src/auto-reply/fallback-state.ts` already imports it) rather than open-code a boundary check.
- Alternative rejected: `[...content].slice(0, 4_000).join("")` allocates a 4,000-element array per captured reply and silently changes the measured unit from UTF-16 code units to code points.
- Not subsumed by merged #198200: that PR made the later caps in `group-thread.ts` safe, but `truncateUtf16Safe` returns its input unchanged when `input.length <= limit`, so an already-split 4,000-unit capture passes through untouched. `git show origin/main:src/auto-reply/group-thread-context.ts` still contains `content?.slice(0, 4_000)`, and no open PR touches this file.
- Risk / non-goals: a reply that would have ended on a high surrogate is now 3,999 units instead of 4,000, never longer; `undefined` still yields `undefined`. No claim is made about how channels render a 4,000-unit reply.

## User Impact

Group-thread agents now carry the text they actually sent into the next round with the final character intact, and that recorded copy stays valid UTF-16. Exported group-thread turns no longer end in a replacement glyph. Replies under the cap are unaffected and channel delivery is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway + Slack send path: red on base, green on this head

Isolated Gateway built from `dist`, real Slack channel adapter on the repo's e2e transport, two-agent broadcast (`maxRounds: 2`), an injected `message_sending` observer, and the QA mock model scripted to send a reply whose astral character straddles the cap. Alice's round-1 `message` tool send runs core `sendMessage` -> `applyMessageSendingHook` -> `runMessageSending` -> `finalizeGroupThreadToolReply`. Round 2 is read back through the shipped `chat.history` RPC: the persisted transcript the next turn is prompted from. Only the model layer is mocked.

| Round-2 observation | Before (`origin/main`) | After (this head) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alice's recorded sibling copy, `isWellFormed()` | `false` | `true` |
| Same copy, lone-surrogate scan | `lone: true`, `0xd83e` | `lone: false` |
| Same copy, unit after the 3,985-char run | `0xd83e` | `0xa` |
| Same copy, JSON tail | `"aaaaaa\ud83e\n\ncha"` | `"aaaaaa\n\nchan"` |
| Bob's recorded sibling copy (shorter label, control) | well formed, pair intact | well formed, pair intact |
| Reply units at `message_sending` | 4016 / 4018, astral intact | 4016 / 4018, astral intact |
| Round-2 outbound provider request | 9142 units, tail `aaaaaa\nmes` | same digest bytes |
| Group-thread `message` tool tests | `3 failed \| 65 passed (68)` | `68 passed (68)` |

The provider request is deliberately not the observation point: every transport runs `sanitizeSurrogates`, which deletes unpaired surrogates, so the round-2 payloads match on both arms once the run's temp dir and `sentAt` are normalized. The recorded transcript is where the difference survives. Bob's label is two units shorter, so his pair lands inside the cap and stays whole on both arms: a built-in control.

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
    test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/channel-progress-presentation.e2e.test.ts \
    -t "keeps the group-thread tool-reply capture whole at its cap"
```

Base arm (`group-thread-context.ts` reverted, runtime rebuilt, harness unchanged):

```console
 FAIL  ... > keeps the group-thread tool-reply capture whole at its cap
AssertionError: the recorded sibling copy must stay whole where the next round reads it
- Expected  []
+ Received  [ { sibling: 'Alice (alice):', aRunLength: 3985,
+               aRunNextUnit: '0xd83e', aRunTail: '"aaaaaa\ud83e\n\ncha"',
+               lone: true, loneUnit: '0xd83e', wellFormed: false } ]
      Tests  1 failed | 15 skipped (16)
```

This head, same harness:

```console
 ✓ ... > keeps the group-thread tool-reply capture whole at its cap 52172ms
      Tests  1 passed | 15 skipped (16)
```

### Regression test: red on base, green with the fix

The new send is folded into the existing three-channel `it.each` case, so it runs through the real `message` tool, `runMessageSending` hook and group-thread scope.

```console
$ npx vitest run src/agents/tools/message-tool-execution.test.ts
# base:  Tests  3 failed | 65 passed (68)   (telegram / slack / discord)
# head:  Tests  68 passed (68)
```

Sibling suite exercising the same scope (`src/auto-reply/group-thread.test.ts`): `Tests 28 passed (28)`.

### What was not tested

No live Telegram/Slack/Discord round-trip with leased credentials was run. The Gateway harness is a local proof lane, not committed; the committed regression is the folded `it.each` send.

Per review, the proof now observes the recorded sibling copy through `chat.history` on a real Gateway + Slack run, red on base and green on this head.

prs.title: feat(cron): back automation off when a provider pushes back
prs.body:
Related: #196859

Depends on #197394 for the shared automation limit.

## What Problem This Solves

Automation bursts can keep replacing completed runs at full capacity even when a provider repeatedly rate-limits requests that eventually succeed through retries.

## User Impact

- Backoff applies only with `cron.dynamicConcurrency` on (#197394). With it off, the default, automation keeps its fixed eight and nothing here changes it.
- A provider rate-limit or overload signal halves automation capacity when more than eight automation agent sessions are active, with a floor of eight.
- Each minute without pushback adds one slot back, until the limit is whole again. With runs queued, the scheduler picks up the new slot within about a minute.
- Conversations remain independent, and running automations finish normally.
- Each reduction is logged as a Gateway warning. This PR adds no setting of its own.

Backoff makes a backlog drain more slowly. The ceiling is process-wide, so pressure from one provider can also slow jobs using other providers and command or script jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run-slot owner observes classified model-attempt failures. It reacts to attempts rather than final job status because runtime retries can turn a rate-limited attempt into an `ok` job.

The ceiling is a reduced value plus one slot per minute since the last pushback, so recovery needs no growth bookkeeping and no signal from the run queue. One burst causes one reduction: while the sessions already in flight exceed the ceiling, their further pushback holds it where it is instead of halving it again; pushback once they have come down to it halves again. Pushback that cannot lower the ceiling, with eight sessions or fewer in flight, also holds it, so every step up follows a full minute without pushback.

Accepted tradeoffs:

- Automation-agent lane activity determines reductions, while the resulting ceiling applies to every job type.
- Hook turns and internal session events share that lane.
- CLI, ACP, compaction, and other model calls that emit no supported failure event do not drive backoff.
- Memory pressure does not drive backoff.
- Reductions are not persisted across Gateway restarts.
- Recovery is gradual: returning from eight to 32 slots takes about 24 minutes without pushback.

For automations whose parent has no workspace binding, parent replacement can still permit owner-authorized work on main. The [main prompt executor installs its parent-source guard only for workspace-bound children](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/220ca12e0732ab599c5a9b6434ac699f6750728f/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts#L212). The slot wait lengthens that interval; these PRs do not introduce the behavior. Maintainers may choose separate hardening. This observation is not a blocker for this PR.

## Evidence

The scheduler regression, with the setting on, an agent limit of 30 and 32 due jobs: a provider rate limit halves 22 automation sessions to 11, a second pushback from the same sessions does not halve again, a run ending does not hand its slot on, the ceiling rises to 12 after a minute, a pushback holds it for a minute, and it climbs back to the whole 30 without further pushback. A second regression cuts nine sessions to eight, then sends another rate limit at eight sessions 50 seconds later: the ceiling stays at eight for a full minute after that pushback before it rises to nine. The #197394 regressions for both modes also pass here. The two targeted files (41 tests) and the core typecheck pass.

[Current-head real Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197395#issuecomment-6871873637) at `368ae7bf8b775a6ce42e20b4df903d80e2c193bc`: twenty due agent-turn jobs admitted sixteen; one synthetic-provider HTTP 429 reduced the ceiling to eight. Another 429 at eight active sessions restarted the quiet minute. A newly due job stayed unstarted, and no queued request started for that full minute. Actual recovery reached nine concurrent requests 75.979 seconds and ten concurrent requests 135.396 seconds after the floor pushback. All 21 jobs completed successfully, with 23 provider requests including two retries.

The selected new quiet-minute regression failed against the immediate parent's run-slot implementation (expected eight, received nine) and passed against the restored head implementation. Each run selected one test and skipped fourteen unrelated tests.

## Validation Limits

The focused Gateway run used a synthetic HTTP provider and real elapsed time. Default-off admission, stable-data upgrade, and the full suite were not repeated. Real provider services, overload responses, active config reload, production user data, and durable restart recovery were not exercised. The maintainer policy decision and required CI remain separate.

prs.title: fix(workboard): a retried card's first run can complete it with a stale result
prs.body:
Closes #198450

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Workboard card's first run that finishes after its retry has started completes the card with its own old result, and the retry's attempt is marked succeeded.

## User Impact

User impact: when an operator retries a quiet card, only the retry can complete it. A late call from the replaced run is refused with an error that tells the worker to report its result in its reply, and the card stays running on the retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

A retry claims the card for the same agent and usually reuses the session, so the claim check (which compares agent ids) let the replaced run through. The Workboard card tools pass the calling run's id from the tool context, and the store's claim check refuses writes from a run that is recorded as an earlier attempt on the card. The check sits in the store's single mutation guard, so it covers completion, block, proof, comments and the other card writes made through those tools.

Known gaps, accepted rather than coded around:
- Workboard workers run in subagent sessions, where a background command's exit does not start a wake turn; it is queued as a system event for the session's next turn. After a retry that next turn is the retry run itself, which is current and may write, so a model that reports the replaced run's output as its own result is not caught by this check.
- A card that has dropped that run's attempt from its bounded attempt history no longer recognizes the run.

## Evidence

- New test in `extensions/workboard/src/tools.test.ts`: dispatches a card, retries it, then calls `workboard_complete` from the first run. It fails on `main` (the old run's completion is accepted) and passes with this change: the old run is refused, the card stays running on the retry, and the retry's own completion succeeds.
- Workboard suite: 369 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed.
- Extension and extension-test typecheck, lint and format on the touched files: clean.
- Not run live: the original report came from a controlled comparison run with real model workers; this change was not replayed against a live Gateway.

## What Problem This Solves

Adding a downloaded Template with an invalid manifest reports only a generic failure, hiding the field and reason needed to fix it.

prs.title: fix: recover agent database verification after native retirement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated agent-database verification after restart when an earlier full check completed but a later native retirement revoked its proof. Also fixes background verification of legitimately admitted runtime stores that are absent from the configured startup roster.

## User Impact

A running Gateway can earn fresh verification after an unclean native retirement and carry it through the existing clean-close seal. Subsequent clean starts reuse that proof. Unclean or unverified closes still cannot publish a seal. No schema, storage format, configuration, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The background owner retained a settled attempt for the whole Gateway lifetime, even after its verification was revoked. Runtime admission now replaces that completed attempt when its admitted facts lack verification. Pending and inconclusive attempts still share the existing owner, preventing scan loops during worker churn.

The same owner distinguishes configuration-selected startup work from already-admitted runtime stores. The former keeps configuration removal/move checks; the latter keeps its physical database identity and Gateway lifetime checks without requiring startup-roster membership. The error previously reported as a configuration change did not inspect SQLite pragmas.

This reuses the existing writer publication and seal machinery. Runtime production delta: +11 lines; the growth carries the missing admission distinction and renewed-verification decision. A genuinely unclean retirement still requires another full scan; this repairs when that debt can be paid, not the scan's intrinsic cost.

## Evidence

Acceptance: one completed verification per valid admission generation, no seal after unverified closure, a seal after successful re-verification, and zero full scans on subsequent clean process starts. Warm filesystem samples are serial with A/A controls and counterbalanced A/B order; timings and CPU/allocation are reported separately from scan counts.

prs.title: feat(templates): finish Add in a retryable setup conversation
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Template Add can create the agent but its tools-disabled opening cannot finish the declared setup or recover a failed opening without repeating creation.

## What changes

After creation, one hidden setup turn uses the new agent’s ordinary tools and retained permissions. It greets in the Template’s voice, creates declared automations paused, reports MCP sign-in needs, and shows exact-package plugin cards without installing or enabling those plugins. Explicit tool denies and operator ceilings remain authoritative.

The ordinary session owns the retryable setup continuation. Retry uses the same agent, workspace and conversation without reinstalling dependencies. When its one-shot receipt has already been consumed, Retry returns a truthful partial/unverifiable outcome instead of inventing readiness or creating another agent. Plugin inventory includes canonical package identity so the agent does not infer a plugin ID from its package name.

This layer follows https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198070. Early-opening/dependency concurrency and composer responsiveness remain a separate follow-up.

## Evidence

### Current repair qualification

Head `577e12a6b457945be951b6e97a753b9c2cfebaef`, base `9ed5a58794db142be41f5e142e68a5cd92d72bd0`:

- Promotes the existing stale/concurrent Retry fix into this independently landable layer. Three Gateway regression cases fail before the fix with false complete/ready results. After the fix the complete owning request suite passes **14/14**, exit0 (144.61s wrapper): `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add-chat.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The same agent, workspace, edited files and dependency-install counts are preserved. External registry/model I/O is fixed; admission, config, workspace, session, rollback and retained setup ownership remain real. No new test seam or mock was introduced.
- Moves the unchanged setup input contract into a type-only leaf and updates all three consumers. Both runtime and Madge import-cycle guards now report **zero cycles**. The leaf does not prematurely add the responsive follow-up callbacks.
- Adds the incident reference beside the bootstrap exception, without changing model-facing prompt bytes.
- Six-file **type-aware lint**, formatting and diff checks pass. Test-line ratchet is **+281 <=400**, no setup allocation or global-limit changes.
- Seven existing setup commits were restacked onto the creation allocation-only repair. UI source and performance inputs are unchanged from the prior setup qualification below; prior results are reused, not claimed as fresh executions. Exact-head hosted compiler/build/CI and completed re-review remain required.

### Retained prior qualification

Prior setup `e68f2ecdbc3b54fea242e6ca545d1f0830bc0aff` above `b7235cc095dff0eebd90cd268b2695ca96f98a08`:

- Complete strict paired production-UI performance passes, exit0: document **14,019 B <=14,026 B**; chat JS **1,315,006→1,315,005 B**, New Session **818,001→818,000 B**, startup **90,860 B unchanged**. Requests and CSS unchanged. Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts b7235cc095dff0eebd90cd268b2695ca96f98a08`.
- Owning Gateway14/14 and setup prompt6/6, complete two-shard command exit0 (161.15s). Explicit denies and operator ceilings remain authoritative.
- Deletes the old tools-disabled outcome prompt and uses the existing session continuation owner, not a parallel Template ledger.

The prior hosted native Talk and UI failures were compared with scheduled main run43540514362 and have identical failure signatures; they are not passing CI. New-head checks still need reconciliation. No inherited-failure qualification covers an introduced defect.

## Real product evidence and remaining gap

Earlier integrated Travel Copilot proof, not this exact head: baseline creation opened chat at19.9s, failed on a disabled referenced plugin at35.6s, leaving an empty workspace. Earlier integrated creation/setup opened pending chat in104ms and produced output at52.2s, preserving original CLAW.md and goplaces while leaving Expedia disabled and Travel Themes uninstalled. The later retained responsiveness recording showed the original-chat card without narration and working review navigation without installation; that follow-up is not part of this PR.

These historical screenshots do not prove the current setup head, completed plugin installation, latest-stable upgrade preservation, or final combined-head video. The historical live-card omission is addressed by the current foundation and its three producer-to-renderer paths. Fresh combined-head real Add/install/caption/video proof remains open before final delivery. No production Gateway was changed.

prs.title: fix(templates): second Template Add blocked once its MCP env var is set
prs.body:
Closes #198541

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: adding the same Template a second time reports `mcp_server_collision` when its MCP server uses an environment reference such as `STATUSPAGE_TOKEN: "${STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}"` and that variable is set.

## User Impact

A Template that declares an MCP secret the documented way can be added again after the secret is configured: Add reuses the matching shared MCP server and creates another agent. `openclaw templates add`, `templates add --dry-run`, and `templates dev` all stop reporting the false conflict. A Template whose declaration really differs is still blocked.

## Why This Change Was Made

Template Add now compares a manifest's MCP server with the server as the config file declares it, using the `authoredConfig` that `listConfiguredMcpServers` already returns (`openclaw mcp doctor` reads the same field). No new option, helper, or state.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

A manifest keeps `${VAR}` references. On main, planning (`src/templates/lifecycle.ts:569`), install (`src/templates/mcp.ts:58`), and rollback (`src/templates/mcp.ts:124`) digest it against `listConfiguredMcpServers().mcpServers`, which comes from the config after environment substitution. With the variable unset the placeholder survives substitution and the digests match; once it is set they differ.

The four places that feed existing servers into planning (`templates add`, `templates dev`, and the Gateway `templates.add.plan` / `templates.add.apply` handlers) and the install and rollback reads now use the authored entry. Rollback still passes the substituted entry as `expectedServer`, because the config writer compares that argument against substituted values.

The comparison came in with #102406, whose description says exact declarations are reused and `${ENV_VAR}` references are preserved, so matching by declaration is the intended behavior. The existing reuse test (`src/templates/schema.test.ts:712`) passes the manifest's own server object as the existing config, and `src/templates/mcp.test.ts` uses literal servers, so substitution never ran in tests.

</details>

## Evidence

Built `main` (6d5e2dfb1b8) and this branch, then ran the shipped CLI (`pnpm openclaw`) with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. A local OpenAI-compatible stub answers Add's opening turn; nothing else is stubbed. The Template is the MCP example from `docs/cli/templates.md`.

- Main, `STATUSPAGE_TOKEN` set after the first Add: `templates add --dry-run`, `templates dev`, and `templates add` each exit 1 with `mcp_server_collision`. Same result when the variable is set before the first Add.
- This branch, same commands: all exit 0, `envmcp-2` is created, `openclaw mcp list` shows one `statuspage`, and `openclaw.json` still holds `"${STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}"`.
- Control, both trees: with the variable unset the second Add plans with no blockers.
- Control, both trees: a Template that declares `${OTHER_STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}` for the same server, with both variables set to the same value, is still blocked.

<details>
<summary>Main (RED), trimmed to the commands and result lines</summary>

```
$ export STATUSPAGE_TOKEN=dummy-value
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/envmcp --dry-run
Agent: envmcp-2
MCP servers: 1
  MCP statuspage: npx --yes @acme/statuspage-mcp@1.0.0
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.statuspage: MCP server "statuspage" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates dev <run>/proj/envmcp
Template dev preview: envmcp@0.1.0
Agent: envmcp-2
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.statuspage: MCP server "statuspage" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/envmcp
Agent: envmcp-2
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.statuspage: MCP server "statuspage" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]
$ grep STATUSPAGE_TOKEN openclaw.json
          "STATUSPAGE_TOKEN": "${STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}"
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>This branch (GREEN) and the different-reference control, trimmed the same way</summary>

```
$ export STATUSPAGE_TOKEN=dummy-value
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/envmcp --dry-run
Template add preview: envmcp@0.1.0
Agent: envmcp-2
MCP servers: 1
  MCP statuspage: npx --yes @acme/statuspage-mcp@1.0.0
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates dev <run>/proj/envmcp
Template dev preview: envmcp@0.1.0
Agent: envmcp-2
Blocked actions: 0
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/envmcp
Added agent: envmcp-2
Workspace: <run>/state/workspace-envmcp-2
[exit 0]

$ export OTHER_STATUSPAGE_TOKEN=dummy-value
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/otherref --dry-run
Agent: envmcp-3
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.statuspage: MCP server "statuspage" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]

$ openclaw mcp list
OpenClaw-managed MCP servers (<run>/state/openclaw.json):
- statuspage
$ grep STATUSPAGE_TOKEN openclaw.json
          "STATUSPAGE_TOKEN": "${STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}"
```

</details>

Tests:

- `src/cli/templates-cli.state-owner.test.ts` (real config loading): `templates add --dry-run` plans without blockers for an existing `${VAR}` server once the variable is set.
- `src/templates/mcp.test.ts` (real config loading): install reuses the server, a different reference with the same value is rejected, and rollback removes the Template-introduced server.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add.test.ts` (planner mocked): the `templates.add.plan` and `templates.add.apply` handlers hand the planner the authored entry, not the substituted one.
- With only the production lines reverted, `pnpm test` on those three files: 4 failed (2 failed, 28 passed in the Gateway file; 2 failed, 23 passed in the other two). On this branch: 55 passed.
- `pnpm test` over the touched files and their consumers (Template planning, Gateway Add handlers, Template and MCP CLI, MCP config): 12 files, 258 tests pass. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, targeted oxlint and format, and `git diff --check` pass.

Gaps:

- The Gateway `templates.add.plan` / `templates.add.apply` handlers were not driven live: they accept only ClawHub or bundled sources, and no bundled Template declares an MCP server. The handler test above covers the two changed lines with the planner mocked. Both handlers read the same `listConfiguredMcpServers` result as the CLI; it builds a fresh snapshot per call (`src/config/io.runtime.ts:314`), and a snapshot of an existing valid config always carries `authoredConfig` (`src/config/io.snapshot.ts:282`).
- The rollback comparison is covered by the test only. Add rolls MCP servers back only before the workspace is exposed and the agent config is committed (`src/templates/add-stateless.ts:414`), and it installs them after both (`src/templates/add-stateless.ts:665`), so the CLI does not reach it with an installed server. The line changed so all three comparisons use the same entry.

Production delta +9/-7; test delta +69/-2 against main.

Merge risk: two-way door; no config, state, or schema change, and reverting restores the prior behavior. Blast radius is Template Add and dev planning plus MCP install when an existing `mcp.servers` entry contains a `${VAR}` reference whose variable is set. An authored escaped literal (`$${VAR}`) no longer matches a Template's `${VAR}` reference.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): stop narration when a retried visibility check throws
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Team (r325, 52e231b7) crash-looped on an uncaught exception: `Error: Plugin invocation scope is closed`. It crashed at 03:54:36Z, 04:22:43Z and 04:25:26Z (the last 44 s after startup). Each crash: failed close → hard-exit watchdog SIGKILL → systemd restart, about 2 min dark, with active turns and agent child processes killed.

Stack (from the stability bundle):

```
PluginInvocationScope.assertOpen
PluginInvocationScope.lookup
PluginInstance.run
<plugin member Proxy apply>
maybeRun            (src/auto-reply/reply/progress-narrator.ts)
Timeout._onTimeout  (scheduleRetry setTimeout)
```

The narrator's retry timer outlives the channel plugin's invocation scope. When it fires, the plugin-wrapped `isProgressDraftVisible` predicate throws, and the throw escapes a bare `setTimeout` and kills the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the minimal crash stop. A throwing visibility check now ends narration for the turn: disable, clear the retry timer, log verbose. The scope-lifetime root cause (likely related to #198245) is being investigated separately by the lane that authored it.

## User Impact

The Gateway no longer crashes when a narration retry fires after the channel turn has ended. Narration simply stops for that turn.

## Evidence

- New regression test: it fails on main ("promise rejected 'Error: Plugin invocation scope is closed'") and passes with the fix.
- `progress-narrator.test.ts`: 29/29 pass.
- Production LOC: +12 (try/catch guard). Test: +25.

prs.title: fix: allow controller adoption after journal retirement
prs.body:
Related: #198574, #198624.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes controller adoption getting stuck after successful native forward recovery retires the activation journal but leaves a completed historical adoption gate.

## User Impact

Operators can adopt a newer reviewed four-file controller closure in steady state without restarting the Gateway. Complete-pair adoption remains required; this does not deploy a Gateway release, migrate databases, or change scheduling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing adoption source owner only accepted a retained incident or a particular operator-accepted retirement. `steady-successor` uses the same locked publication and replay owner with an absent canonical journal, the exact completed installed closure, its immutable source archive, and current process/release-pointer bindings. It preserves the old gate and four-file closure with recorded old/new hashes. Completed entry admission remains independent of the adoption-time process, so subsequent deployments and controller adoptions work normally.

Production grows by 27 lines to admit the missing state. No new publication owner, cache, configuration option, SQLite schema or migration is introduced.

## Evidence

- Synthetic Linux fixture installs the exact #198574 controller closure, completes historical native-update adoption and forward recovery, then exercises steady adoption, interrupted publication/replay, a normal deploy through the installed successor, and another steady adoption after the process changes. Adoption itself performs no restart. Old closure and gate history remain intact.
- Existing `prepare` reproduces the absent-journal ENOENT. The new regression fails on exact parent `0b7cd35571e7cbfb7544305379c7c4a1dac26b03`, then passes with the fix.
- Negative controls cover an active/newly appearing journal, wrong action surface, incomplete completion, changed process generation, release pointers and installed closure; incomplete adoption excludes ordinary controller entry.
- Filesystem operations, SQLite and exclusive Linux FD9 locking are real; Gateway/systemd/build observations are synthetic. No live server was accessed. This is controller-boundary proof, not a live Gateway deployment rehearsal.

- Focused Linux suites: 73/73 existing adoption tests and 4/4 affected recovery/steady cases, zero skips. The exact historical-closure rehearsal separately passed 1/1.
- `pnpm check:changed`, syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed. No UI import boundary is touched.
- Simplification kept the existing publication owner; production +27 lines, tests +116, documentation +60.
- Codex autoreview of the final local snapshot against `0b7cd35571e7cbfb7544305379c7c4a1dac26b03`, with full production owner and test context, completed P0–P2 review with zero findings (two complete passes). Reviewed bytes were committed as `81b1689b2323`; no source changes followed review. Hosted ClawSweeper and exact-head CI are required before landing.

prs.title: fix(update): refuse missing host prerequisites in one line and record a cause per attempt
prs.body:
Stacked on #198268 (`perf/update-remove-candidate-canary`): that PR rewrites `update-candidate-snapshot.ts` and `update-failure-facts.ts`, which this change also touches. Retarget to `main` after #198268 lands.

## What failed in the field

From 3,782 classified upgrade issues and 783 auto-filed update failure reports:

- **Unsupported Node: 99 failures, the largest single cause.** 83 of them read `npm error [openclaw] error: this OpenClaw release requires Node >=24.22.1 …` under `Reason code: global-install-failed`. The npm preinstall check found the problem after the update had started. All came from updaters at or below 2026.10.9. Main has refused before staging since #180769. But that refusal is a 40-line wall: 5 `Failing check` lines, recovery steps, a triage run, 3 failure JSON files and a diagnostics zip, with the instruction buried in the middle.
- **Old Git: #197195.** System Git 2.43 failed with the opaque `preflight-no-good-commit`. Nothing told the operator "Git ≥ X required".
- **Full disk:** nothing refused an update on a nearly full disk. There was only a soft `Low disk space … may fail` warning.
- **Causes hidden in reports.** 276 reports read `Reason code: global-install-failed`. That code names the place where the update failed, not the reason. Their failing-check codes read `[redacted-code]` (147) or `Error` (126). Phase names are redacted as `[redacted-command]`, because a step name with a space looks like a shell command.

## What changed

1. **Prerequisite preflight.** Before staging, `openclaw update` refuses with one `Update refused: …` line that says what to install or free, and changes nothing:
   - **Node**: the existing engine check reads the service's Node from its launchd plist, systemd unit or Windows task. It now leads with one line that names the target's `engines.node` and which Node is too old (the service or the updater), followed by the recovery owner's own numbered steps (profile, version-manager install, absolute launcher continuation, and the service-definition owner's step when this updater cannot refresh it). If no supported Node release satisfies the target, it says to pick a compatible OpenClaw version instead.
   - **Git** (new): Git-checkout updates need Git ≥ 2.31. Older Git echoes `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute` back instead of failing, so `prepareGitCandidateTransfer` gets a wrong object directory after the service is prepared for mutation. The check runs the same Git as the updater. The updater puts its Node's directory and `/usr/bin` ahead of the shell's `PATH`, so the refusal names the Git that it found.
   - **Disk**: the soft low-disk warning becomes a refusal sized from the target's registry `dist.unpackedSize`, read with the target metadata the updater already fetches (one more field, no install measurement). The floor is 4.4× that size: for 2026.11.3 (263 MiB unpacked) a fresh global install with dependencies took 662 MiB (2.5×) and npm's cache 490 MiB (1.9×). Metadata without `dist.unpackedSize` (some mirrors) skips the check. It runs after the existing measured state-copy check (`snapshot-capacity-insufficient`), which now leads with its instruction line.
   - These refusals skip triage. A repair agent cannot install Node or Git or free disk space.
2. **One cause per attempt.** `finishUpdateRunRecord` is the single place that writes a terminal update-run record. It now sets `origin.cause` to one value of a closed enum (`none`, `node-unsupported`, `git-unsupported`, `disk-full`, `permission-denied`, `network`, `config-invalid`, `install-failed`, `state-migration-failed`, `plugin-failed`, `service-failed`, `interrupted`, `refused`, `unknown`). Machine facts (an npm `ENOSPC`, `EACCES` or network code) win over the site code. The saved report and the auto-filed failure report print `Cause: …`. Origin compaction keeps the enum intact, so an oversized record stays readable. The Control UI report renderer prints the stored cause and does not bundle the classifier. Because the set is closed, redaction never hides it. It is stored in `origin_json`, as `nextAction` already is, so there is no SQL schema change. The wire schema gains one optional enum field.

Replaying the 783 auto-filed reports through the classifier gives: 271 install-failed, 129 state-migration-failed, 107 service-failed, **97 node-unsupported** (before: all hidden behind `global-install-failed`), 80 unknown, 27 plugin-failed, 27 refused, 15 config-invalid, 13 interrupted, 11 permission-denied, 6 network. The script reconstructs facts from the redacted text, so the real unknown share is lower: new records get their facts before redaction.

## Deleted / replaced

- `createLowDiskSpaceWarning` and its `disk-space-preflight` warning step are replaced by `describePackageStagingShortfall`.
- The `snapshot-capacity-insufficient:` prefix line in the state-copy refusal is gone.
- For a fresh prerequisite refusal, the terminal shows the refusal line, the recovery steps and the report path. The `Failing check` dump, triage run, triage prompt, diagnostics zip and two extra failure JSON files are gone. The report file keeps every detail. Re-rendered history (update status, Control UI) keeps the existing saved-advice qualification.

Production delta: +309 / −43 lines (excluding the regenerated `predicates.js`, whose +2829/−2813 is renumbered check ids from adding one optional field; that file is most of GitHub's +3k count). Most of the growth is the cause map in `src/infra/update-run-cause.ts`, which is data. The rest is the Git check (+32) and the refusal layout. I found no duplicate Node check to delete: the early engine check and the later activation-runtime check answer different questions (`engineOnly` versus capability and identity).

## Proof: real `openclaw update` against throwaway installs

Setup, all on Studio (macOS) with isolated state:
- The target is a local registry (verdaccio) serving `openclaw@2026.11.9` with `engines.node: >=24.22.1 <25 || >=26.12.1`.
- The installed package is this branch, packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --skip-build` and installed with `npm i -g` into a throwaway prefix.
- Each run uses `env -i` with `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=prq` (label `ai.openclaw.prq`) or a throwaway `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
- The base runs use the same setup at #198268's head.

**A. Old Node service.** A real LaunchAgent Gateway (`openclaw gateway install --runtime-path ~/.nvm/…/v24.20.0/bin/node`) is serving `/readyz`. The updater also runs on Node 24.20.

Before: 38 lines, starting with `⚠️ OpenClaw could not complete the update. A required system check failed.` and then 5 `Failing check` lines, recovery steps and a triage run.

After (final head `497c2f38`, real LaunchAgent on nvm Node 24.20, target needs ≥24.22.1):
```
⚠️ Update refused: openclaw@2026.11.10 needs Node >=24.22.1 <25 || >=26.12.1, but the Gateway service runs Node 24.20.0 at /private/tmp/prq/oldnode/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/bin/node. No changes were made.
Report: ~/.openclaw-prq/update-reports/938f9d14-….md
1. Use the same service account and keep the existing OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH overrides throughout recovery.
2. Run `export OPENCLAW_PROFILE=prq OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=19437 OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL=ai.openclaw.prq …`.
3. Run `nvm install 24.22.1 && nvm use 24.22.1`.
4. Run `node /private/tmp/prq/A/prefix/lib/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs --profile prq update --tag 2026.11.10`.
```
- Record: `failed|finished|preflight-node-runtime-incompatible|node-unsupported`; `openclaw update status --json` gives `cause: "node-unsupported"`.
- The Gateway kept serving `/readyz` on the old build.

**B. Old Git.** The fixture is a Git checkout with a newer commit on its origin. Git 2.23.0 is built from source and placed next to the updater's Node (the directory the updater puts first on `PATH`).

Before: the update fetched, then failed in `validating` with `target-metadata-preflight: The Git target manifest or revision could not be inspected. Check Git remote access…` (`git show <sha>:package.json exited 128`). It then printed `Update recovery could not prove a runnable installation … Run openclaw update repair` and ran triage.

After:
```
⚠️ Update refused: Git 2.23.0 at <scratch>/node-oldgit/git is too old for Git-checkout updates. Replace it with Git 2.31 or newer, then retry openclaw update. No changes were made.
```
- Record: `git-version-unsupported|git-unsupported`.
- HEAD unchanged.

**C. Near-full disk.** Install, npm cache, temp files and state all live on one 2 GiB APFS image with 279 MiB free.

Before: the update printed only `Low disk space … may fail`, then started `package-install` and filled the disk to 29 MiB. It failed with `update-failed`, and `Update report could not be saved: ENOSPC`. The update was left as `Update recovery remains pending`. A 174 MiB `.openclaw.update-stage-*` directory stayed on disk.

After (final head `497c2f38`; local registry serves `dist.unpackedSize` 300,114,914 B, so the floor is about 1.2 GiB; 4 GiB volume):
```
⚠️ Update refused: 991 MiB free on the volume holding /private/tmp/prq/C/vol/prefix/lib/node_modules; this package update needs about 1.2 GiB. Free 268 MiB there, then retry openclaw update. No changes were made.
```
- Record: `failed|finished|preflight-insufficient-space|disk-full`. Nothing staged.
- With the filler removed (2.8 GiB free) the same command passed the check and completed: `✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.9 (from 2026.11.3)`, `update status` → `succeeded`, `cause: "none"`.
- Verdaccio does not compute `dist.unpackedSize` (npmjs does), so the proof writes the real file-byte sum into the local registry's version metadata.

Scenario B (old Git) ran on `ebae345f`; its code path is unchanged since.

Focused tests:
- `update-run-cause.test.ts`: the terminal record stores the cause, including npm `ENOSPC` behind `global-install-failed`.
- `update-run-cause.test.ts`: the auto-filed report prints `Cause: disk-full` even when the step text is redacted.
- `update-run-ledger.test.ts`: the cause enum survives origin compaction (red without the codec fix: the stored `disk` fails validation).
- `update-check.test.ts`: both metadata readers return `dist.unpackedSize`.
- `update-run-report.test.ts`: a fresh refusal leads with its block and steps; re-rendered history does not announce a fresh refusal.
- `update-runner-git-commands.test.ts`: the Git version verdict.
- `disk-space.test.ts`: the refusal sized from the unpacked size.

Consumer suites still pass: node-engine preflight, target settlement, triage, ledger and snapshot-space cleanup. `pnpm protocol:check` and `gateway:validators:gen` regenerated `predicates.js`. Most of that diff is renumbered check ids.

## Accepted edge cases

- **The disk floor is an estimate.** 4.4× `dist.unpackedSize` comes from one measured release; a release with a very different dependency weight shifts it. A warm npm cache needs less, so a host near the floor may be refused although it would have finished; the message names the exact amount to free. Registries without `dist.unpackedSize` skip the check and keep the install's own ENOSPC handling.
- **The original-state capture still runs before target admission.** It wrote about 3 MiB under `<state>.update-captures/` for each refusal above, and it keeps that copy. Moving it after preflight changes initialization order, so it is left for a follow-up.
- **The check looks where the updater looks.** The updater searches its Node directory and `/usr/bin` before the caller's `PATH`. An old Git that only appears later in the shell's `PATH` is neither used nor flagged.
- **Targets given as a tarball or file spec still skip the engine check**, as before. Only registry metadata carries `engines.node` before staging.
- **A future reason code missing from the map records `unknown`.** It is a single data table to extend.



## CI

- `control-ui-performance` failed on earlier heads, and that was this PR: the Control UI imports `update-run-report.ts`, which then pulled in the cause classifier, growing three bundles by about 0.8 KiB gzip past the base (the base itself is already over the cap, so no growth is allowed). The renderer now prints the stored cause instead, and the check passes.
- `checks-ui-e2e (2/6)`: `route-asset-requests` timed out in `beforeAll` (`Hook timed out in 180000ms`) on several heads, passed on #198268's head run [43467658704](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43467658704/job/132052081630), and passed locally in isolation on this head. The same test timed out the same way on `main` in scheduled run [43472686357 (4/7)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43472686357/job/132049216911), and passed on this PR's `497c2f38` run. It depends on shard layout, not this change.
- `checks-ui-e2e (5/6)` `home-readonly.real-gateway` (120 s timeout; 108 s on #198268's head) passed on later heads.
- ClawSweeper: the input scanner flagged a pre-existing credential-shaped URL fixture in `update-failure-report-prepare.test.ts` (TruffleHog `URI` detector), scanned because this PR touched that file. The PR no longer touches it; TruffleHog over every changed file now finds nothing. The re-review ran and raised four P2 findings, all addressed in `497c2f38`: cause enum preserved through origin compaction, recovery steps kept under the Node refusal, the no-supported-Node case, and saved-versus-fresh refusal rendering.

prs.title: feat(sessions): show per-session token and cost usage from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #192616

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway records per-session token and cost attribution and the Control UI shows it, but the terminal could not: `openclaw gateway usage-cost` prints one aggregate number, so a headless operator could not see which session, agent, or model burned the tokens.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions usage [sessionKey]` prints one row per session (label, agent, model, messages, tokens, cost) plus range totals, with `--agent`, `--all`, `--range`, `--start/--end`, `--max-rows`, and `--group-family` selectors. `--json` returns the raw `sessions.usage` response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical `sessions.usage` owner and only shapes output: conflicting selectors are rejected before dispatch, and the report's `partial` status is printed instead of hidden, so a time-budgeted answer is never mistaken for "no usage".
- The row cap flag is `--max-rows` rather than `--limit`, because the parent `sessions --limit` list-row cap owns that name (the sibling search command follows the same naming after review feedback).
- Registration rejects the parent list selectors, matching the other gateway-backed verbs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-usage.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 27/27 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and run against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000 --json
{ ..., "startDate": "2026-10-06", "endDate": "2026-11-04", "cacheStatus": {"status": "partial"},
  "partial": { "reason": "time-budget", "message": "Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; ..." } }

$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000
Session usage (2026-10-06 → 2026-11-04)
No session usage recorded in this range.
Totals: $0.0000 · 0 tokens · in 0 / out 0
Partial report: Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; narrow the date range or select a session.

$ openclaw sessions usage --agent x --all          → exit 1 (conflict)
$ openclaw sessions usage --end 2026-10-31         → exit 1 (missing --start)
$ openclaw sessions usage --max-rows 500           → exit 1 (cap exceeded)
```

The live response's `partial` reason surfacing in text mode is the behavior the review asked to prove: an incomplete answer is labeled, never silent.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, ledger, or config changes.

prs.title: feat(agents): explain the effective tool set for a session
prs.body:
Closes #192712

## What Problem This Solves

When a tool the agent expects is missing, the operator had to guess why. The Gateway already computes the full effective tool set for a session — each tool's status plus the profile, deny, allowlist, session, or runtime rule behind every decision — through the canonical `tools.effective` RPC, but no CLI verb exposed it.

## User Impact

`openclaw agents tools <sessionKey>` prints the effective profile, the Gateway's filtering notices, and one row per tool with its status and the deciding reasons; `--json` returns the raw diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical owner and only shapes output; blank selectors are rejected before dispatch and transport failures exit non-zero in both output modes.
- Registered under `agents` because the `tools` root is deliberately reserved.
- The command defaults its runtime to `defaultRuntime`, matching the other agents commands that are invoked without an explicit runtime from the registration wrapper.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/agents-tools.test.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts` → 32/32 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and exercised against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`). The first live run exposed a real defect (the command was invoked without a runtime, crashing the error paths) which was fixed before this head; the fixed build shows the correct failure contract:

```text
$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "unknown session key \"agent:main:main\"" },
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:main" }            (exit 1)

$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
Tools diagnostics failed: unknown session key "agent:main:main"
                                                (exit 1)
```

The Gateway log confirms both live requests (`⇄ res ✗ tools.effective ... errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown session key`). The isolated store has no sessions, so the populated table rendering is covered by the unit tests.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, tool-policy, or config changes.

## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.

- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix(agents): resume yielded parents after restart retires completion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes parent sessions remaining parked after a restart when they were waiting for a paused subagent whose old completion authority was retired.

## User Impact

Affected parents resume through ordinary restart recovery, inspect saved results, or continue retained child tasks through fresh admission. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registry restore deliberately retires completion authority from the previous process. Yield reachability checked that fact only for non-yielded terminal children. Apply the same existing check before following message or nested waits, preserving retirement and the current recovery owner. Production line count is unchanged.

## Evidence

The actual Gateway regression uses a deterministic external provider, real tools and SQLite, and graceful process shutdown. It verifies that the original yielded parent survives shutdown. On exact pre-fix main `3cd6a3ed497469fcce9288b1621df968244c2e7c`, startup reports `resumed: 0` / `parked: 2` and the parent never resumes. With the fix, the parent resumes, continues the saved child, and receives its result. Siblings cover a child completing before restart, a child on another agent, and an interrupted child.

All six Gateway scenarios pass together. A separate credentialed OpenAI model replay of the parked-parent flow also passes using synthetic sessions and constrained tool choices (27.8 seconds of behavioral execution). Focused owner, stable-record recovery, sweep and requester-receipt tests pass. The real retired-store rejection already records a visible durable failure on the baseline; its new regression preserves that behavior. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2.

`pnpm check:changed` has unrelated unused-export failures reproduced on the exact main parent: `REQUIRED_ACTION_STOP` (introduced by #196951 / `de0ea1efe5f9`), `resolvePackageDistCommonJs` (#198567 / `5f99927e134e`), and `prepareTranscriptFactsBackfillStress` (#194519 / `72f90dde293d`). These are tracked main regressions, not ignored failures.

<details>
<summary>Synthetic owner measurement</summary>

Linux btrfs, Node 24.22.1, 4 CPUs / 12 GiB; synthetic 35.13 GiB database, 10,000 sessions, one million transcript events, and 62,000 workspace files (1.116 GB). Five counterbalanced pairs, ten calls per sample, separate timing/allocation A/A controls.

Baseline admits one of four parents and leaves three parked; fixed admits all four. Both perform 14 transcript-worker tasks per call. Median process CPU rises from 188.4 to 209.7 ms and sampled main-isolate allocation from 10.34 to 11.99 MB for the three additional recovery admissions. Allocation A/A differs by −0.37%. Wall medians are 142.6 versus 155.1 ms, with substantial A/A drift; no latency improvement is claimed. Worker allocation is outside the inspector sample. Model execution is outside this owner benchmark.

</details>

prs.title: ci(i18n): add non-publishing native locale refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected preflight support was removed: guards inside branch-controlled YAML cannot independently guarantee secret isolation. Manual runs use the trusted main workflow definition.

## User Impact

No direct user-facing change. Maintainers gain a review-only native translation refresh path that cannot push, open a PR, or enable auto-merge, while non-publishing source selection requires current exact-head review approval.

## Evidence

### November 2 review-readiness repair

- Removed the branch-selected preflight mode and restored the main-only dispatch contract, addressing the P1 workflow-boundary finding without adding another execution path.
- Focused workflow contract regression: fails on the previous head at the branch-admission condition; passes after the repair (1 test, 4.97s runner wall).
- Workflow validation passed, including pinned tooling fallback and zizmor.
- Changed-surface checks passed: formatting, root-test typechecks, dependency/coercion/dead-export guards, and script/test lint. `git diff --check` passed.
- Repair delta: 12 insertions / 37 deletions across workflow and guard test; removed the separate preflight input, scheduling branch, and branch-dispatch route.
- Local autoreview of this repair against `7bf16b8fd47f07612777b4957b1a14bbc66eba42`: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings.
- Remaining integration proof: no new credentialed translation run was dispatched. The earlier hosted translation/artifact run predates the current approval checks, so it does not prove approved and revoked-source behavior for this head. That remains an explicit pre-merge validation gap.

### CI integration repair

- Integrated main `1f01f4944d45` to resolve a concrete CI failure: the new non-publishing upload step retained an old action pin while main's canonical workflow helper required the updated pin.
- Both upload steps now use main's existing upload-artifact v7.0.2 pin; the dispatch/security repair is unchanged.
- Focused workflow regression: 1 passed on the integrated candidate. Full workflow validation, including zizmor, passed. `git diff --check` passed.
- Current head: `ae494551c445`; replacement exact-head CI is pending. Prior failed run is not claimed passing.

Related: #142663

## What Problem This Solves

`/tools verbose` advertises automation creation during management-only turns, even though execution rejects `add`. Inventory construction has no run ID, so deriving its description and schema from an exact-run execution grant incorrectly falls back to the unrestricted surface.

## User Impact

Discovery inside an admitted management-only turn no longer advertises creation. Fresh remote administrator turns retain creation through the existing `callerScopedCreation` distinction. Execution authorization is unchanged.

This fixes the discovery mismatch only; the reported Telegram creation rejection is not claimed fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `resolveCronToolManagementMode` reads admitted scope, deployment policy, liveness, and any supplied run ID without requiring an execution grant.
- `bindCronManagementGrant` reuses that classification while retaining its exact-run, live caller authority and operational-instance checks.
- Automation descriptions, schemas, and compact summaries use the admitted mode. Summary wording stays in the existing description-presets owner, keeping `cron-tool.ts` within its line limit.
- Discovery outside an admitted turn still describes the configuration surface, not per-turn execution authority.

## CI Repair

Rebased onto upstream `24e758688a6db34e1f9079f65faff3269bf15978`, which contains [#181647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181647), `05d779c0c931c8c0bbccf9cce93a47fbb54e6ef9`. That upstream repair distinguishes the admitted restart source ID from the interrupted execution run ID, addressing the three failures previously reproduced on CI's upstream base without this PR.

Removed this PR's duplicate exact action-enum assertion, which had become stale when upstream added `bind`. The real command-handler regression remains; existing schema and authority tests protect permitted actions and the creation boundary. No upstream assertions, skips, retries, or approval gates were changed by this PR.

## Evidence

- Real command-handler regression covers `/tools verbose` in an admitted management-only scope. Authority coverage distinguishes discovery from execution grants and preserves fresh remote creation.
- 128 focused tests passed using repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`: 20 restart-continuation cases plus 108 authority, tool, inventory, and prefix-stability cases across the six affected suites.
- [New-head native CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40344290316), including `checks-node-changed-5` and the native `openclaw/ci-gate`. The final rollup had 66 passing checks and none pending; only the maintainer-approval commit statuses remain red.
- Standalone command smoke outside Vitest, with isolated state and synthetic admitted scopes: management-only output omits `add job`; fresh remote creation output includes it. This is command-boundary proof, not a live Gateway/model session.
- Targeted production and touched-test typechecks, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks.
- Fresh independent review was attempted, but both reviewer processes failed at service capacity; no fresh review verdict is claimed. The authority implementation is unchanged from the previously reviewed patch. This update rebases that patch, removes the duplicate enum assertion, and relocates the unchanged summary expression.

The security-sensitive guard still requires current-head approval from a maintainer with `maintain` or `admin` access. A previous-head approval would not carry over after this rebase.
