prs.title: fix(codex): retain native thread reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Summary

- retain Codex App Server's effective reasoning effort from thread start, resume, and fork responses
- update the same live and durable binding from matching `thread/settings/updated` notifications
- report the effective native setting through the existing `turn_starting.effort` diagnostic when a supervised turn intentionally has no per-turn collaboration override

## Root cause and canonical fix

OpenClaw's manual response types and durable session binding omitted Codex's response-backed reasoning effort. The notification controller also discarded settings notifications emitted before `turn/start` returned a turn id. Supervised attempts therefore reported a null effort even when the native thread had an effective setting.

The repair records the fact where Codex owns it: start/resume/fork responses initialize it, and `thread/settings/updated` changes it. All binding writers carry the same nullable field. Existing generation and thread guards prevent stale clients from moving live or durable state.

This current-main rewrite does not add `thread_ready.reasoningEffort` or another event field. It fills the long-standing `turn_starting.effort` field only when the per-turn request intentionally omits an override. The live harness independently verifies the effective native effort and the absent collaboration override.

## Dependency contract

The integrated plugin pins `@openai/codex` 0.164.0. The sibling Codex source was inspected directly at commit `fdf23b4097bf19adf2286c64316da2d2a9fedae6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` defines response-backed nullable `reasoning_effort` for thread start/resume and `ThreadSettings.effort` for settings updates. Native thread facts remain separate from per-turn overrides.

## Coverage and change shape

Regressions cover response capture across start/resume/fork and supervised materialization, pre-turn settings updates, durable-owner rejection, effective turn-start diagnostics, and the live supervised/native assertion boundary.

No new configuration surface, schema migration, protocol version, fallback, or parallel path. The positive production delta propagates one native fact through the existing binding writers; notification writes use the connection's current authority.

## Validation

- Current head: `ae1b83e6b0bd`; integrated main: `1f01f4944d45`.
- 89 tests passed across three affected files during conflict repair.
- After the final current-authority adaptation: all three reasoning-effort regression cases passed; extension production types and targeted lint passed.

prs.title: feat(system-agent): let the system agent report backup status
prs.body:
Fixes #192657

## Summary

The system agent could report `health`, `status`, `doctor`, `models`, and `plugins`, but had no way to answer backup questions ("when did the last backup run, did it succeed, are the offsite schedules working?"). The Gateway already summarizes that through the canonical `backup.status` projection; only the model-facing surface was missing.

This PR adds a read-only `backup-status` system-agent operation plus the `backup_status` tool action, wired through the same four-step chain the `health` action established: operation type → executor case → tool action enum + `SIMPLE_ACTIONS` → assistant-prompt lists. The executor reuses the projection's own helpers (`readBackupRuns`, `summarizeBackupTargets`, `summarizeBackupSchedules`, `listStorageLocations`, `buildBackupStatusValue`), so no new projection or state access is introduced. The typed-command parser accepts `backup status` / `backup` / `backups`.

Revision 2 (`2118837348c`) closes the remaining P2 from the earlier review: when the selected Gateway is not this host (`gateway.mode=remote`), the loader now asks that Gateway's `backup.status` handler for the projection instead of reading the client's own SQLite ledger, cron partition, and storage registry. The rendered headline now states where the rows came from (`Source: local process state` or `Source: selected Gateway ws://…`), so an operator can tell which host answered.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: the `backup_status` system-agent operation now renders the recorded backup-run ledger — freshness headline, per-target `kind/target/status/age` table, enabled schedules, storage locations, plus the existing backup doctor hints — instead of having no action at all; and with `gateway.mode=remote` it renders the selected Gateway's projection rather than the client's local one.

**Real setup tested**: Windows 11 host, OpenClaw run from TypeScript source on this PR's head (`2118837348c`). Two isolated state directories, no user state touched: Gateway host `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix` (real pre-existing `state/openclaw.sqlite`, 2.0 MB, with two recorded runs) and remote client `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote` whose own ledger holds **0 rows**. The Gateway ran on `ws://127.0.0.1:18817` with token auth, started only for this proof and stopped afterwards.
- **Runtime**: node v24.22.1, invoked as `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` (no `dist` rebuild, so the tree under test is exactly this branch's source)
- **Selected-Gateway transport**: the shipped `backup.status` RPC over the real Gateway WebSocket, exercised through the shipped `createSystemAgentTool()` object and its `backup_status` action (not by calling `backupStatusCommand` directly, and not through a stubbed transport)

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:

```bash
# Gateway host: isolated state with real ledger rows, real Gateway on 18817
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix/openclaw.json"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18817

# Local mode (no gateway.mode): the same tool object the agent calls
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-backup-status.ts     # createSystemAgentTool({surface:"cli"}).execute({action:"backup_status"})

# Remote mode: client has gateway.mode=remote -> backup.status on the selected Gateway
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote/openclaw.json"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-backup-status.ts

# What the client's own ledger contains (0 rows), so the two rows below can only
# have come from the Gateway's backup.status response
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-ledger-rows.ts
```

The two probe files contain no stubs: they build the shipped tool with `createSystemAgentTool({ surface: "cli" })`, prepare runtime config through `captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader`, and print the tool's real text result.

**After-fix evidence**:

```text
# local mode, isolated state with two recorded runs (newest first)
Backup status last attempt failed 20h ago (external)
Source: local process state
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| Kind     | Target                                                             | Status | Age     |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| external | nas-b                                                              | failed | 20h ago |
| external | nas-a                                                              | ok     | 20h ago |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
----- tool result meta -----
{"ok":true,"parts":1}
```

```text
# gateway.mode=remote, client ledger has 0 rows — rows come from the selected Gateway
Backup status last attempt failed 20h ago (external)
Source: selected Gateway ws://127.0.0.1:18817
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| Kind     | Target                                                             | Status | Age     |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| external | nas-b                                                              | failed | 20h ago |
| external | nas-a                                                              | ok     | 20h ago |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
----- tool result meta -----
{"ok":true,"parts":1}
```

```text
# the remote client's own ledger, proving the two rows above crossed the RPC boundary
{"clientLedgerRows":0,"targets":[]}
```

The local-mode run took 254.6 s and exited 0; the remote-mode run took 142.6 s and exited 0. Both are real terminal runs, not test output.

**Observed result after the fix**: the headline moves from `Backup status none recorded` to `last ok` / `last attempt failed`, the table lists every recorded target newest-first with the ok row still visible behind a later failure, and in remote mode the same rows are rendered from the Gateway while the client's own ledger is empty. Exit code is 0 for the populated, single-row, and empty cases alike — the empty state is a normal state, not an error. `Source:` makes the answering host explicit in both modes.

**What was not tested**: no live LLM agent turn was run (this host has no model credential wired for a paid run), so the model's own tool-selection step — choosing `backup_status` and formatting its answer — is covered only by the contract assertions in `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts`, not by an executed agent session. Schedule rows were not exercised in this session: the isolated state has no cron backup jobs, so the "Schedules:" line did not appear (the code path is the same helper the `health` action already uses). The remote run used a loopback Gateway with token auth; a TLS/tunnel Gateway was not exercised.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: the runs used TypeScript source via the `tsx` loader rather than a `tsdown`-built `dist`, so the evidence is byte-identical to this branch's source but not to a packaged release artifact. The Gateway was started for the proof only and stopped afterwards; the isolated state directories and the loopback token never touch the user's real `~/.openclaw`.

## Gateway-target fix (revision 2)

| Scenario | Before this revision | After this revision |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.mode=remote`, client ledger empty, Gateway has a failed `nas-b` run | client prints `none recorded` (its own empty SQLite ledger) | client prints `last attempt failed … nas-b`, `Source: selected Gateway ws://…` |
| Transport used | none — local file reads only | canonical `backup.status` on the selected Gateway (`callGateway`, `operator.read`) |
| Failure mode when the Gateway is unreachable | silently wrong local answer | explicit error naming the Gateway URL; no silent local fallback |
| Doctor hints | built from the client's local ledger | built from the same projection the headline/table used |

`isImplicitLocalGatewayTarget(config)` chooses the path: implicit local keeps today's local reads (no Gateway required for CLI use), `gateway.mode=remote` routes to `backup.status`. `loadBackupStatusSnapshot` is the only decision point; `renderBackupStatus` and the hint builder are shared, so both modes describe one projection.

## Tests and validation

- Unit tests landed with the PR (recorded when the branch was pushed, not re-run in this evidence session): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/system-agent/operations-parse.test.ts src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts` → 114/114 passed, covering the new `backup status` parse rows and the schema/description assertions.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src/commands/backup-status.ts src/commands/backup-health.ts` → 0 warnings / 0 errors; `oxfmt --write` applied to both files.
- Type checking: a workspace-wide `tsgo` run in this checkout is red on pre-existing `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` dependency drift (`src/acp/*`, unrelated to this branch); it reported exactly one error in the touched files on the first pass (`OpenClawConfig` imported but unused), which is fixed in the pushed head.
- The end-to-end behaviour above is production code (tool dispatch → executor → projection → renderer → Gateway RPC), not a unit-test fixture.
- Read-only throughout: no backup runs, schedules, storage writes, or Gateway mutations; the operation returns `{ applied: false }` like the other reporting actions.

## Risk checklist

- **Does this change user-visible behavior?** Yes, but only additively: the system agent gains one read-only action (`backup_status`), the tool description grows by two words, and every rendered status now carries a `Source:` line. No existing action semantics change.
- **What is the release/rollback risk?** Low. The new code path is a branch inside one loader; reverting it returns to local reads without touching the ledger, the cron store, or the RPC, which remain the canonical owners.
- **Could this corrupt state or break an existing surface?** No state is written. In remote mode the command now performs a read-only `backup.status` RPC with the configured client credentials; the local path is unchanged. A defect would surface as wrong output or an explicit connection error, not as data loss.
- **Auth/secret handling**: the Gateway token is read from the existing `gateway.remote` config through `buildGatewayConnectionDetails`/`callGateway`; it is never printed, logged, or embedded in the body.

## Current review state

- **Addressed in revision 2**: the P2 "Read backup status from the selected Gateway" — `gateway.mode=remote` now routes through the selected Gateway's `backup.status`, and the evidence above shows the empty-client-ledger scenario the review described (2 rows from the Gateway, 0 rows locally).
- **Addressed in revision 1**: the "Add real behavior proof" blocker — populated, single-row, and empty states were already shown; revision 2 additionally shows the actual system-agent tool dispatch and the selected-Gateway transport the earlier review asked for.
- **Still open (author-known)**: no live LLM agent turn, no cron schedule rows, and no packaged-`dist` run (see What was not tested).
- **Next step**: maintainer review. I will not claim the remote path is release-proven until a packaged build runs against a non-loopback Gateway.

## Before / After

| State | Before this PR | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Agent action | no `backup_status`; fallback guidance lists doctor/status/health only | `backup_status` registered; parser maps `backup status` / `backup` / `backups` |
| Operation type | `operation-types.ts` has no backup case (0 hits on `origin/main`) | `{ kind: "backup-status" }` (1 hit) |
| Executor | no `backup-status` case (0 hits on `origin/main`) | dispatches to `backupStatusCommand` (2 hits) |
| Rendered output | — | freshness headline + source + per-target table + schedules/locations + doctor hints |
| Remote Gateway | local ledger read regardless of `gateway.mode` | `backup.status` on the selected Gateway; explicit error instead of a silent local answer |

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

| Shorthand before | Shorthand after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Shorthand before the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9596a8ed-17fd-4809-9c45-f0bc359d40af) | ![Shorthand after the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd794946-ed7c-4567-a1bf-4862d23afb6d) |

The Environment row uses the host control wrappers and explicit plugin icon/diff styling. The following synthetic browser captures show the repaired layout.

prs.body:
# Prompt presence checks for frozen injection expectations

Implements the approved PRI-1119 minimal design v1.2 (Tier B): bounded, fact-only presence checks that verify whether a frozen injection expectation's full body text appears inside the **pre-submission request object**, on both the `openai-responses` and `openai-completions` paths.

## What this does

- **Pure bounded checker** (`packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-check.ts`): three mutually exclusive outcomes — `full_hit` / `checked_missing` / `unknown` with explicit reasons (`assembly_truncated`, `body_over_limit`, `expectations_over_limit`, `scan_region_over_limit`, `cumulative_scan_over_limit`, `unparseable_content`, `check_failed`). Caps: per-body 64 KiB, per-message region 8 MiB, expectation count 64, message count 512, and a **cumulative UTF-8 scan cap (32 MiB) covering legal AND wrong-role regions — exceeding it never outputs `checked_missing`** (owner condition 1).
- **responses path**: the existing egress observer frame computes `presenceCheck` (with per-attempt index) when the request carries a frozen expectation set (options-keyed carrier). The `provider.prompt.observed` event gains `presenceCheck` (+ `requestIndex` stamped by the runner wrapper).
- **completions path** (previously zero observation): a checkpoint after `onPayload` replacement and before `encodeBody` emits the same event channel with `egress: "completions"`, `attemptIndex: 0`.
- **runner**: per-run `requestCount` on the run-scoped prompt state (incremented once per attempt assembly), expectation set frozen by the prompt-build phase **after the size guard**, carrier bound per request, `requestIndex` stamped on emitted events.
- **plugins**: optional structured `injectedExpectations` field on the before_prompt_build result (validated passthrough; merged by concatenation across plugins).

No request mutation. No body persistence. Requests without frozen expectations are unaffected: no carrier → no `presenceCheck` field → no measurable added cost.

## Owner acceptance conditions — where implemented

1. Cumulative scan cap (32 MiB default) over legal AND wrong-role regions; exceeding yields `unknown:cumulative_scan_over_limit`, never `checked_missing`.
2. Expectations carry `bodyComplete`; truncated-assembly fragments force `unknown:assembly_truncated` and can never yield `full_hit`. The injecting plugin freezes expectations after its size guard and marks completeness by containment.
3. Event identity reuses existing fields: envelope `runId`, wrapper-stamped `requestIndex` (run-scoped ordinal, incremented per attempt assembly), egress-closure `attemptIndex` + `payloadVariant`. Tests cover same-run multi-request, concurrency isolation, and retry attempt indexing.
4. Event size measured in UTF-8 bytes (table below).

## Measured on the implementing machine (script: `packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-measure.mts`)

| fixture | runs | median | p95 | event bytes (UTF-8) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| representative: 18 expectations × ~2.2 KiB bodies, 58k-char system region | 30 | 0.111 ms | 0.192 ms | 2,994 |
| representative: 1 expectation, same region | 30 | 0.008 ms | 0.010 ms | 249 |
| boundary: 64 expectations × 64 KiB bodies (under limits) | 10 | 128.620 ms | 129.286 ms | 10,702 |

## Tests

- `packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-check.test.ts` — 20 fixtures (containment, roles, parts, no-concatenation, prefix-not-hit, limits, cumulative cap, truncated-assembly rule, exception fail-open, completions roles).
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/provider-prompt-state.presence.test.ts` — 6 tests (carrier binding + event stamping, same-run multi-request ordinals, concurrency isolation, absent-expectation untouched events, truncated-assembly rule through the real transport chain, retry attempt indexing).
- Regressions green: existing observer/transport suites 36/36; runner-side scoped tsc clean for touched files.

## Trust boundary

The check runs inside the host process (host-recorded, not third-party). It observes the pre-submission request object — the exact object `encodeBody` serializes into the wire body via body-override. It does not prove network-peer bytes or model-context inclusion.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation custody store** in the per-agent database persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts, and hands each delegate off to the subagent run registry before spawn (RFC `docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md` §5.4). The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **Durable custody**: delegates and their replay state live in the continuation custody store, with one transactional authority for replacement and a pre-spawn handoff to `subagent_runs` (upstream has removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime, #159179) - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → custody record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from the custody store (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` (tree `53363f7964f31a47109cf0575aa23f31eefa0338`), the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. It was reached by fast-forward on 2026-11-05. Every earlier presented head, including `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba`, remains an ancestor; no presented history was rewritten. ### Receipts bound to this exact head Each is a separate receipt in the preserved exact-head packet, [`PROOFS/a22bd9c05c…/`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb) (docs `main` at `9ba5518b`). | gate | ruling | scope | |---|---|---| | Recipient-authority row (`R-CD-RECIPIENT-AUTHORITY`) | PASS-candidate ([docs#620 comment 6651745479](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/pull/620#issuecomment-6651745479)) | the gate-3 fire only; the row stays `partial` until a corpus fold review | | Mode-B and the locally run cut shards | PASS-candidate ([karmaterminal/openclaw#1271 comment 6653747059](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/issues/1271#issuecomment-6653747059)) | the candidate-owned regression gate; it doesn't claim Mode-B was green | | Fold source review of the `2907e656 → a22bd9c05c` delta | PASS-candidate ([#1271 comment 6655365352](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/issues/1271#issuecomment-6655365352)) | source review only | **Mode-B** [`41927761314`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/41927761314) ran on product `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` with workflow `a768f04231bd0a6f94cc7b845aecaec28a4a4c9e`, from 2026-11-04 22:43Z to 2026-11-05 04:47Z. It finished terminally **non-green**: 91 jobs (53 succeeded, 27 failed, 3 cancelled, 8 skipped) and 218,033 tests passed / 220 failed. - Its receipts are valid, routed equals planned, and every hosted job ran on the project's own runner pool. - **Its 64 distinct failing tests are exactly the previous accepted head's set** (the same sorted-set sha256 `185b6dea…`), and none is new. - The four shards the workflow cuts at 90 minutes were run locally at this exact SHA, serially with one worker: - two were clean; - two carry only baseline or test-order failures, each classified in the receipt with counterfactual runs. **Packet status: preserved, NOT acceptance-complete, NOT terminal.** Of 37 required rows, **0 pass, 1 partial (the recipient-authority row above), and 36 missing**. No live row has fired at this SHA, because no deployment runs it yet: the deployed fleet is on a separate, older line. Running live rows here needs a deployment whose runtime has this SHA as an ancestor. That is a migrating cut (an agent-schema step), gated on its own timed restore rehearsal. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` does not point at this packet, and nothing here is a terminal rollup claim. ### Earlier evidence: provenance, not exact-target proof The live behavior observed on earlier heads, and the earlier corpora, are ancestry and materiality evidence for this head. They aren't exact-target execution, and no row is carried over from them as a pass: - Mode-B [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) at `3821eaef72`, 2026-09-18; - corpora [`7cb9d71f…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) and [`139e3657…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393). The behaviors those corpora observed are the ones this feature exists for: - stale ambient backlog suppression; - typed and bracket `continue_work` wakes with granted provenance and Tempo model-call spans; - cost-cap rejection; - max-chain, scheduler, durable recovery and delegate surfaces. They are re-fired against this head's runtime once one is deployed. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. - [Exact-head packet for `a22bd9c05c`: README, status and limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md: identities and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md: how the packet was built](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/METHOD.md) - [Gate 4 receipt: Mode-B and the local cut shards](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/gates/GATE-4-MODE-B-AND-LOCAL-SHARDS.md) - Historical corpora (provenance only): [`7cb9d71f…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567), [`139e3657…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - `139e3657…` packet files: [README](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) · [RESOLVED-SHA](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) · [METHOD](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) · [TRANSPOSED-FROM](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) · [manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) ### PROOFS METHOD Live rows use a Grafana k6 proof harness. Each packet's `METHOD.md` carries the exact reproducer commands. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers, because OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access. Structural completeness is not proof: a row counts only with an authoritative receipt at the exact SHA. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially host Cron plus / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A tool adapter over durable flow records is also not a lifecycle host, and upstream has since removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime (#159179) that such an adapter would have called. Marking a stored record as running neither reacquires a session lane nor invokes the model; continuation needs the turn machinery itself to own which session runs next, how child results return, and what survives finalization. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix(templates): invalid MCP declarations report only "Invalid input"
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #198554

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where Template authors writing an `mcpServers` entry in `CLAW.md` would see only
  `ERROR invalid_manifest $.mcpServers.s: Invalid input` from `openclaw templates validate` — with
  no field and no rule — for four ordinary authoring mistakes: a remote server missing `transport`,
  an unsupported `transport` value, a non-string entry in `args`, and an empty declaration. Authors
  could not tell what to fix, so a low-severity typo cost a guess-and-retry loop on every run.
- **Related:** #198556 is a distinct diagnostic-loss boundary (`readVerifiedArtifactSource`
  replacing all manifest diagnostics with one fixed message) and is intentionally not addressed
  here. Fix signal labels on the issue: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`,
  `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** a malformed MCP declaration reports the offending field and the rule it
  broke, e.g. `$.mcpServers.s.transport: Invalid option: expected one of "sse"|"streamable-http"`,
  in both the text and `--json` modes, while every manifest that is accepted today stays accepted
  and every manifest rejected today stays rejected.
- Zod collapses a failed `z.union` into one valueless `invalid_union` issue and nests each branch's
  field-level reasons under `issue.errors`. `mcpServerSchema` is the union of the stdio and remote
  shapes, and `diagnosticsFromZodError` mapped issues 1:1 from `issue.message`/`issue.path` only, so
  the nested branch detail was dropped. The fix expands an `invalid_union` issue into the branch
  that got furthest through the schema (uniquely the fewest issues) and re-roots each of its issues
  at the union's own path. When no branch is the clear match, the existing union-level diagnostic is
  kept rather than guessing which shape the author meant.
- This mirrors how the same Zod collapse is already handled elsewhere in the repo —
  `src/config/validation-issues.ts` ("Zod collapses the useful ACP branch issue behind a generic
  union-level 'Invalid input'") and `src/infra/exec-approvals-config.ts`.
- Diagnostics-only: no schema, no default, no accepted value and no hand-written error text changed
  — the messages forwarded are Zod's own. Refinement-based diagnostics (unpinned `npx`, blocked env
  keys, non-HTTPS remote URLs) already carried field paths because a refinement makes its branch
  dirty, so Zod returns that branch's issues instead of collapsing; that path is untouched.
- **Out of scope:** #198556's artifact-source diagnostic propagation; native (non-Template) config
  MCP schemas; any change to which declarations are accepted or rejected.
- **Highest-risk area:** branch selection picking a misleading branch when both branches are equally
  close. **How is that risk mitigated?** Expansion only happens on a unique fewest-issue branch; a
  tie falls back to today's behaviour, so the change can only add precision, never invent a field.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** `openclaw templates validate <dir>` (and `--json`) rejects each of the four
  reported declarations with exit status 1 and a diagnostic whose `path` names the offending field
  (`transport`, `args[0]`, `command`) instead of stopping at the server name; valid stdio, `sse` and
  `streamable-http` declarations still validate with exit status 0.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/templates/schema.ts` — `closestUnionBranchIssues`,
  `locatedIssues` and `diagnosticsFromZodError`; and the regression test
  `names the malformed MCP field for %j` in `src/templates/schema.test.ts`, whose four fixtures are
  the declarations from the issue report.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux host (`Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64`, glibc 2.31), Node v26.12.1,
  pnpm 12.15.0, worktree at PR head `b5531419e17`. Every case is a real Template project on disk
  (`package.json` + `CLAW.md` under `/tmp/mcp-cli-198554/<case>`), validated by **spawning the shipped
  CLI entry point as a real process with real argv**:
  `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts templates validate <dir> [--json]`. `src/entry.ts` is
  the exact module tsdown bundles into `dist/entry.js`, which the `openclaw` bin (`openclaw.mjs`)
  imports — so argv parsing, commander routing (`src/cli/templates-cli.ts:52-55`), the
  `runTemplatesValidateCommand` action handler, project discovery, manifest validation,
  `formatTemplateDiagnostics`, text/JSON output and the process exit status are all shipped code
  paths, run out-of-process, with stdout and `$?` captured verbatim. Runs used a throwaway
  `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-cli-198554/state`; no real OpenClaw state was touched. (The
  `[openclaw] log file append failed` line inside the transcripts is that throwaway state dir's
  file-log transport: it appears 7× in the BEFORE run and 7× in the AFTER run, so it is unrelated to
  this change.)
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1. one Template project per case from the issue report (+ 3 valid controls)
  bash build-fixtures.sh /tmp/mcp-cli-198554

  # 2. shipped CLI entry point, real argv, both modes, stdout + exit status per case (at head)
  bash run-cli-entry-matrix.sh "AFTER (PR head b5531419e17, shipped CLI entry src/entry.ts, real argv)" \
    after-cli-entry-matrix.txt

  # 3. committed regression suite at head -> GREEN
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=900000 \
    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/templates/schema.test.ts          # 49 passed (49)

  # 4. base leg: temporarily restore the unmodified schema.ts, re-run the same suite and matrix
  git checkout origin/main -- src/templates/schema.ts                     # blob sha256 287aa25a...
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/templates/schema.test.ts
  #                                                                       -> 4 failed | 45 passed (49)
  bash run-cli-entry-matrix.sh "BEFORE (unmodified origin/main schema.ts, shipped CLI entry)" \
    before-cli-entry-matrix.txt
  git checkout HEAD -- src/templates/schema.ts                            # sha256 back to edcec60a...
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** verbatim stdout of the shipped CLI at head, one reported case per mode:
  ```text
  $ openclaw templates validate /tmp/mcp-cli-198554/non-string-arg
  ERROR invalid_manifest $.mcpServers.s.args[0]: Invalid input: expected string, received number
  [exit 1]
  ```
  ```json
  {
    "schemaVersion": "openclaw.templateProject.v1",
    "stability": "experimental",
    "ok": false,
    "root": "/tmp/mcp-cli-198554/non-string-arg",
    "diagnostics": [
      {
        "level": "error",
        "code": "invalid_manifest",
        "phase": "schema",
        "path": "$.mcpServers.s.args[0]",
        "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received number"
      }
    ]
  }
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** all four declarations from the report now name the field and the
  rule, in both CLI modes, and all four still exit 1 (nothing was made permissive). Both columns are
  the shipped CLI entry point with real argv; only `src/templates/schema.ts` differs between them:

  | Case (`mcpServers.s`) | unmodified `origin/main` (blob `287aa25a`) | head `b5531419e17` (blob `edcec60a`) |
  |---|---|---|
  | `{ url: "https://x.example/mcp" }` | `$.mcpServers.s: Invalid input` · exit 1 | `$.mcpServers.s.transport: Invalid option: expected one of "sse"\|"streamable-http"` · exit 1 |
  | `{ url: …, transport: http }` | `$.mcpServers.s: Invalid input` · exit 1 | `$.mcpServers.s.transport: Invalid option: expected one of "sse"\|"streamable-http"` · exit 1 |
  | `{ command: node, args: [8080] }` | `$.mcpServers.s: Invalid input` · exit 1 | `$.mcpServers.s.args[0]: Invalid input: expected string, received number` · exit 1 |
  | `{}` | `$.mcpServers.s: Invalid input` · exit 1 | `$.mcpServers.s.command: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` · exit 1 |
  | valid stdio / `sse` / `streamable-http` (controls) | `Valid Template project: …` · `ok: true` · exit 0 | unchanged · `ok: true` · exit 0 |
- **Before evidence:** on unmodified `origin/main`, all four cases print the identical valueless line
  reported in the issue, in both modes (`--json` reports `"path": "$.mcpServers.s"`,
  `"message": "Invalid input"`), confirming the reproduction:
  ```text
  ERROR invalid_manifest $.mcpServers.s: Invalid input
  [exit 1]
  ```
- **Committed regressions fail on the base and pass on the head:** the same suite
  (`src/templates/schema.test.ts`, unchanged between the two legs) was run against both versions of
  `src/templates/schema.ts`:
  ```text
  base  (schema.ts from origin/main, blob 287aa25a):
    × parseTemplateManifest > names the malformed MCP field for {"server":{"url":"https://mcp.linear.app/mcp"}, …}
    × parseTemplateManifest > names the malformed MCP field for {"server":{"url":"https://mcp.linear.app/mcp","transport":"http"}, …}
    × parseTemplateManifest > names the malformed MCP field for {"server":{"command":"node","args":[8080]}, …}
    × parseTemplateManifest > names the malformed MCP field for {"server":{}, …}
    AssertionError: expected [ { level: 'error', …(4) } ] to deep equally contain ObjectContaining{…}
      - Expected: { path: "$.mcpServers.remote.transport", message: StringContaining "expected one of \"sse\"|\"streamable-http\"" }
      + Received: [ { code: "invalid_manifest", level: "error", message: "Invalid input",
                      path: "$.mcpServers.remote", phase: "schema" } ]
    Test Files  1 failed (1)   |   Tests  4 failed | 45 passed (49)   |   VITEST_EXIT=1

  head  (b5531419e17, blob edcec60a):
    ✓ the same four cases (9ms / 6ms / 6ms / 6ms)
    Test Files  1 passed (1)   |   Tests  49 passed (49)   |   VITEST_EXIT=0
  ```
- **Affected neighbours also pass at head:** one runner invocation over the six suites that touch this
  surface — `src/templates/{schema,schema-conformance,project,reader}.test.ts` and
  `src/cli/templates-cli{,.project}.test.ts`:
  ```text
  |unit|  Test Files 4 passed (4)   Tests 97 passed | 1 skipped (98)   Duration 145.36s
  |cli|   Test Files 2 passed (2)   Tests 28 passed (28)               Duration 35.90s
  [test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 189.15s   VITEST_EXIT=0
  ```
- **Lint/format:** `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/templates/schema.ts src/templates/schema.test.ts` →
  `All matched files use the correct format.` (exit 0); `pnpm exec oxlint` on the same two files →
  exit 0.
- **What was not tested:**
  - `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this host at all: the native `tsrs` binary requires
    `GLIBC_2.32`/`GLIBC_2.33`/`GLIBC_2.34` and this host has glibc 2.31
    (`/lib64/libc.so.6: version 'GLIBC_2.34' not found`), so no typecheck evidence is available locally.
  - The repo lint wrapper `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` (CI's path) aborts in oxlint 1.89.0's Rust
    allocator pool on this 4.19 kernel — `thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at
    crates/oxc_allocator/src/pool/fixed_size.rs:112`, exit 134 — and reproduces identically on
    untouched files such as `src/templates/project.ts`, so it is environmental rather than caused by
    this change; the direct `pnpm exec oxlint` run above exits 0.
  - The bundled artifact itself was not exercised: the local tsdown build is refused on this host
    (it requires a ≥4352MB heap and peaks near 4.7GB). The proof above runs `src/entry.ts` — the
    module that build bundles into `dist/entry.js` — so the only unexercised layers between it and an
    installed `openclaw` binary are the bundling step and `openclaw.mjs`'s Node-version/compile-cache
    gating, neither of which this change touches.
  - CI lanes pending on this head: its workflow runs (`CI`, `CodeQL`, `CodeQL Critical Quality`,
    `Workflow Sanity`, `OpenGrep — PR Diff`, `macOS Periphery Dead Code`) are queued as
    `action_required` awaiting maintainer approval for a fork PR, which is why the `openclaw/ci-gate`
    status currently reports `failure` ("CI must complete successfully; review updates
    automatically"). No CI job has run and failed on this head.
- **Proof tier:** L3 for the reported behaviour — real Template projects on disk, the shipped CLI
  entry point spawned out-of-process with real argv, both output modes, exit statuses, before/after
  across two versions of the single changed file, plus a red/green run of the committed regressions.
- **Proof limitations:** none for the diagnostic paths, messages and exit statuses above. The
  typecheck, repo lint wrapper and bundled-binary gaps listed under "What was not tested" are host
  limitations and are left to CI.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI authorization + maintainer review.
