prs.title: fix(cron): refuse ownerless operator job edits through chat
prs.body:
Related: #187195

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway-owner chat edit through the `automations` tool from Code Mode can save an operator-created, ownerless trusted job that scheduled admission always refuses.

In the production incident, the agent inspected the job and twice updated its prompt while re-sending the full agent-turn payload, including `toolsAllow: ["*"]`. Both updates succeeded. The job acquired `final-executable-surface` provenance with an `unknown` caller origin, retained `trusted` policy and no owner session, then failed every scheduled admission and eventually auto-disabled.

## User Impact

Chat now refuses changes to what an ownerless trusted automation runs, including from Gateway-owner management turns, with the existing plain recovery message: create a new automation in the conversation or use the Automations page. Lifecycle management remains available. Direct operator administration remains available through the page, CLI or Gateway API.

No schema, config option or migration changes. The production job was already repaired; this change prevents another edit from creating the invalid authority combination.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root is `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-job-access.ts:99` on the base: `cronUpdateNarrowsTrustedJob` excludes every `manageAll` caller. That bypasses the existing ownership refusal at `cron.ts:268`. Meanwhile, `cron.ts:355` passes no account policy for management without a creator capture, and `cron.ts:478` still passes the caller's tool provenance to the mutation owner. An explicit `toolsAllow` resave stamps the capture in `src/cron/service/jobs-tool-policy.ts:401`. `src/cron/run-authority.ts:27` consequently selects requester admission, and its workspace check at line 46 refuses the missing owner session.

The caller's management grant grants Gateway-wide job management, not local execution origin. Remote user admission intentionally records `unknown` at `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-creator-authority-admission.ts:93`; the tool's final-surface capture is forwarded into its caller identity at `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts:239`. Recording that chat as a local operator would widen authority.

Chosen contract: refuse the edit (option ii). The existing narrowing decision now also applies to management callers when the trusted job has no owner conversation. Its existing ownership guard rejects the edit both during preparation and against the locked job before persistence. This follows #187195's refusal for an owner whose account cannot be proven, without inferring a session/account from routing or transferring creator attribution. The job never receives the requester stamp from a refused edit.

`explicitlyMutatesToolsAllow` remains unchanged: an explicit resave can reauthorize the surface even when the list is equal, and the prompt itself changes the executable definition. Treating the equal cap as omitted would not establish valid requester ownership.

Simplification kept the existing Gateway authority owner and refusal path: one net production line, 114 net test lines, three net documentation lines; no new helper, owner or state machinery.

## Evidence

Base: `4f7b426a4e3fb3d2275df8f8b5a75b19c1496b6f`. Fixed head: `d2350c5c7042eee541a25670cf0daf020828c0bf`.

One regression uses the real `automations` tool and its live management-grant machinery, the real Gateway handlers and SQLite cron service. Only the transport is replaced. It seeds the ownerless trusted operator shape, performs get → prompt/full-payload update → repeated update with a final-surface capture and unknown origin, then reads stored state and exercises both production admission functions. The existing ownership matrix is updated for the refused ownerless/trusted management case.

Red with base production code (the final fixture uses the current canonical `session:<key>` target):

```sh
timeout 120s pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'unknown-origin owner chat'
```

```text
Tests  1 failed | 4 skipped (5)
Expected: "operator-schedule"
Received: "requester-schedule"
Received: "Requester-scoped automation can only use its owning conversation’s workspace."
Stored provenance: { version: 1, source: "final-executable-surface", callerOrigin: { kind: "unknown" } }
Both updates accepted; stored prompt = "edited again"; owner absent; policy trusted.
```

Green with the fix, including all existing tests in the affected consumer file:

```sh
timeout 120s pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       5 passed (5)
New regression: 1270 ms
All test bodies: 3282 ms
Vitest duration: 69.16 s; wrapper wall time: 77.29 s
```

Wall time is dominated by repository worker compilation/import preparation; the regression itself is about one second and the complete file's test bodies stay below five seconds. CI seconds are pending.

Touched-file typecheck (temporary config extending the repository test shard config with only the two changed TypeScript roots), oxlint, formatting and diff checks passed:

```sh
timeout 120s pnpm exec node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .artifacts/tsconfig.automations-owner-edit.json --pretty false
timeout 60s pnpm exec node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/gateway/server-methods/cron-job-access.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts
timeout 60s pnpm format:check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- docs/automation/cron-jobs/managing-jobs.md src/gateway/server-methods/cron-job-access.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts
timeout 10s git diff --check
```

Completed `pr-simplify`, then the requested local Codex autoreview against the base-to-working-tree snapshot that became this commit:

```sh
timeout 600s python3 ~/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine codex
```

Result: `scoped-clean`, no accepted/actionable findings at the helper's default P0 scope. No P1/P2 coverage is claimed. The first fixture attempt double-redeemed a management grant and failed setup; that was corrected before the defect was reproduced. Typecheck also caught fixture typing issues, corrected before the final green run.

This is tool/Gateway/service boundary proof; it does not boot the Code Mode kernel, run a live model or exercise scheduler auto-disable. Admission is tested directly against the job read back from SQLite. No full suites, Docker or browser tests were run.

prs.title: chore(ui): catch clipped row-menu actions in WebKit
prs.body:
Related: #196567

## What Problem This Solves

A WebKit visual proof (2026-11-07) found the last Secrets row's action menu with **Delete** cut off, while its menu-bounds check still passed. No committed test covered that case in WebKit, and the shared visibility check could not see a row clipped inside the menu.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The clipping itself is already fixed on `main` by #196567. This PR makes a regression fail in both Chromium and WebKit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cause was in the shared overlay stylesheet that every `Menu` uses, so other long lists with row menus had the same exposure. Before #196567, `max-height` used `calc(100% - 16px)`, and inside a `position-area` that `100%` is the space beside the trigger. A menu near the window edge shrank into that space and scrolled its own rows instead of flipping above. WebKit hit this on Secrets because the first keyboard focus at the bottom of Settings moves the last row down 72px, leaving 64px below a 66px menu. Chromium kept the row higher, so the menu still fit below.

This PR changes only tests:
- `expectItemVisible` now measures each row against the menu's scrollport (`clientTop`/`clientHeight`), not the menu's outer box.
- A new short two-item `bottom-end` menu at the window edge must show every action in full, above its trigger.
- `overlay-style.browser.test.tsx` joins the WebKit browser lane. The whole file already passes there.

## Evidence

![Before (main without #196567) and after (current main), WebKit 1440x1000, last Secrets row menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1780ce5d-35c2-4a43-bf90-44d383d4ef05)

Synthetic data only, captured headlessly from production bundles with the perf lane's own Secrets proof harness (200 rows, keyboard-opened last-row menu). Top: current `main` with #196567's overlay CSS reverted. The menu sits at y=939.8 and is 48.2px tall around 66px of content (the same numbers as the 2026-11-07 report), and the harness's wrapper-bounds check still passes. Bottom: current `main`. The menu flips to y=833.8 at its full 66px. Chromium is unchanged between the two because the row has room below.

- With #196567's CSS reverted, the new test fails in both engines: `Edit: expected 592 to be less than or equal to 588`. The menu wrapper itself still fits the viewport, which is the gap the lane reported.
- On `main`, `overlay-style.browser.test.tsx` passes in Chromium (13/13, 5.5s) and WebKit (13/13, 6.6s).
- `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt pass on the touched files. Autoreview (Codex) found nothing at P2 and above.

Not covered: the 72px WebKit scroll-range drop on first focus near the bottom of Settings is a separate layout shift. This PR doesn't change it.

prs.title: fix: bound shared Git content searches before lazy fetching
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes excessive downloads and promisor-pack creation when agents search the entire history of a shared partial clone, or when content prefetch cannot finish.

Related: #197259, #197448.

## User Impact

Recognized pickaxe, patch/stat/numstat logs, range diffs, revision grep, and blame fetch at most one bounded blob batch, then read offline. If content is still missing, agents get guidance to narrow the pathspec, use revision-specific `git grep`, or add a `--since` bound (a revision range for blame). Already-hydrated histories remain readable. Speculative `show rev:path` hydration retains its existing behavior. Use `--` before scoped pathspecs; implicit log paths, explicit rename/copy forms, and `log.follow=true` path history retain their existing native handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous implementation bounded each fetch to 2,048 objects but allowed an unlimited number of batches. Incomplete discovery and failed prefetch also fell through to native lazy fetching. Apply the existing discovery budget to every recognized content search and retain offline execution after preparation, including its failure paths. Remove the unlimited batch loop. Native blame implicitly follows edited renames, so preparation expands bounded predecessor paths from deletions in the same commits, including rename chains, before its one blob fetch. Internal discovery preserves literal filenames and root-relative paths even with caller pathspec/relative modes. This conservative set may include other deletions in those commits. Production code is net **+53 lines** (124 added / 71 removed); the growth preserves native blame rename/range behavior, existing log path/follow contracts, and supported Git 2.43 operation under the bounded execution policy. No new configuration, cache, schema, or dependency.

The exact unscoped command `git log --oneline -S selectThemeSettings` engaged batching on Git 2.56, but reproduces the tiny-pack storm on Ubuntu 24.04 Git 2.43: the original shim created **65 packs / 6,159 bytes in 1.28 seconds** before a 64-pack observation cap terminated it. The candidate returns actionable guidance in 119.9 ms with zero packs or fetches. This is a capped baseline observation, not completed-search latency. The source fixture has 20,001 commits and 62,001 files.

On the tested Git 2.43, `cat-file --batch-check` aborts on a missing promisor blob instead of printing a missing row, even with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` and protocol denial; the old pipeline treats the empty result as no missing blobs, skips explicit prefetch, and permits native lazy fetching. Missing-blob inspection now uses offline `rev-list --objects --no-walk --ignore-missing --missing=print` on the bounded known blob roots and subtracts present roots. It neither walks history nor scans the object database. An inconclusive speculative show probe also proceeds to bounded preparation. No Git-version branch or new configuration.

The actual production Git version was not inspected, so the production-specific attribution remains conditional. The same mechanism is reproduced through the unchanged original shim on the large synthetic fixture.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: an oversized cold search must return actionable guidance with zero new packs and transport attempts; a fully hydrated search must preserve native output. Small scoped reads must retain one-batch behavior.

The following large-history Git 2.56 measurements are retained from initial candidate `2c7b7c56a50c`; they precede the rename and legacy-inspection repairs. Final-code Git 2.43 and warm-read measurements follow below.

Synthetic fixture: 20,001 commits, 62,001 files, 1.116 GB materialized workspace, isolated linked worktree metadata in a `blob:none` clone. Five paired A/A controls and five alternating A/B pairs; `maintenance.auto=false`, `gc.auto=0`, no partial-clone maintenance. Linux container, Git 2.56.0, 4-CPU / 8-GiB limit, overlay filesystem; this is Git-owner proof, not a database or btrfs latency claim.

| Cold exact pickaxe | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Wall median / p95 | 3,392.5 / 4,459.2 ms | 90.5 / 128.4 ms |
| Command-tree CPU median / p95 | 3,557.9 / 4,750.9 ms | 87.6 / 125.5 ms |
| New promisor packs / transports | 10 / 10 | 0 / 0 |
| Maximum RSS median | 78,897,152 B | 27,373,568 B |

A/A control medians: 4,399.9 vs 4,754.2 ms wall; 4,588.5 vs 4,614.9 ms CPU. All controls produced identical output and pack counts. The candidate intentionally refuses this oversized cold search; these are not equivalent successful-search latency numbers. Independent macOS samples show 17,732.4 → 145.0 ms median and 10 → 0 packs (macOS CPU accounting is incomplete).

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/agent-git-probes.mts --scratch-parent <scratch> --bounded-history --commits 20000 --files 62000 --samples 5 --baseline-shim <pre-fix-shim>`. Add `--warm` for hydrated controls; `--allocation-preload <counter.so>` for a separate allocation run.

Pack-count regression is red on baseline: `-S`, `-G`, and `log -p` each create 3 packs and request 4,098 blobs; blame creates a lazy-fetch pack. Candidate creates zero. Focused shim tests cover output/path scope, linked-worktree overlap, offline reads, failed prefetch, grep exit 1, narrowed searches, and hydrated oversized history. Final focused suites: eight tests pass on Git 2.56, and all six history tests pass on Git 2.43. These include edited rename chains, literal pathspec flag/environment, and subdirectory relative-diff regression cases. Rename behavior is red on the first PR head and green with the repair. On Git 2.43, small search/rename tests fail at head 779d1bea and pass after the nonhydrating inspection repair; all existing one-pack assertions remain intact. The failed-prefetch baseline creates 11 lazy-fetch packs; candidate creates zero. Source-aware Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Warm searches preserve byte-identical output: median wall 658.5 → 414.2 ms, command-tree CPU 664.0 → 411.8 ms, zero packs for both. Warm A/A control wall medians: 639.4 / 634.8 ms. Separate instrumented cold runs reduce malloc/calloc/realloc calls from 3,939,342 to 218,766 and cumulative requested allocation bytes from 11,946,259,143 to 457,625,228 (medians; not retained memory). A/A allocation controls agree exactly at 3,939,316 calls / 11,945,885,586 bytes. The counter calibration reports exactly 3 calls / 110 requested bytes. 


`pnpm check:changed` completed: all checks pass except the unrelated dead-export scan. The initial test-local shadowing lint findings were fixed and the focused lint/test checks pass. The same dead-export findings reproduce on the exact main parent `4cffd43ee043275f6a4c693aaacee8d8e5a61288`; no findings touch this diff. Source attribution:

| Finding | Introducing change |
|---|---|
| `TELEPORT_PT`, `QA_UX_STREAM_END_MARKER` | `858b5b01338e` / #198293 added unused exports |
| `adoptTelegramDmTopicMessage`, `TELEGRAM_DM_TOPIC_ADOPT_WINDOW_SEC` | `90c620b8e554` / #169444 added exports without production consumers |
| `mergeNodeRepositoryPublication`, `WorkspaceTransferOperation` | `8e6768f91235` / #193873 added the export/re-export |
| `RELAY_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`, `RELAY_GRACE_MS` | `d4e80ac038cd` / #198474 added exported constants used locally |
| `ChatModelPickerTargetOption` | `cd61ce32dd28` / #180824 moved its last external consumer into the defining module but retained the export |
| `ChatModelRuntimeControl` | `56ca2fae9015` / #192137 added an exported component used locally |

These are inherited main regressions, recorded for their owners; the scan was not skipped or reported green.


## Measured implementation and warm-read decision

These measurements are pinned to `777063446191`; the final edge repairs reuse them because these workloads use explicit paths, have no `log.follow` configuration, and have nonempty history discovery. The added endpoint/native-path branches do not run and introduce no new Git operations in these workloads.

Ubuntu 24.04 / Git 2.43, local container limited to 4 CPUs / 8 GiB, 600 commits, 62,000 files (1.116 GB), five paired A/A controls and five interleaved A/B pairs. Each cold sample starts with fresh shared partial-clone metadata. Output is byte-identical; these are completed searches.

| Cold operation | Baseline wall median / p95 | Candidate wall median / p95 | CPU median before → after | New packs before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Path-scoped patch log | 10,541.9 / 11,112.9 ms | 76.3 / 105.7 ms | 8,424.5 → 67.4 ms | 599 → 1 |
| Blame | 10,967.5 / 21,363.0 ms | 61.2 / 68.4 ms | 8,809.7 → 60.9 ms | 600 → 1 |

Cold A/A wall medians: log 10,379.3 / 10,220.9 ms; blame 20,618.2 / 14,937.3 ms. Shared-host timing spread is disclosed; control outputs and pack counts agree. Median maximum process RSS: log 8,151,040 → 7,364,608 bytes; blame 8,126,464 → 7,331,840 bytes.

Separate allocation runs reduce public malloc/calloc/realloc calls: log 4,905,699 → 111,844; blame 5,261,711 → 104,134. Cumulative requested bytes: log 1,927,520,027 → 206,240,479; blame 1,972,682,334 → 206,026,521. These are not retained memory. A/A allocation controls agree exactly within each operation (log 4,905,100 calls / 1,927,012,505 bytes; blame 5,261,711 / 1,972,682,334).

Warm reads retain identical output and zero packs, but cost more. **The campaign performance owner accepted this tradeoff; see the verbatim decision below.**

| Final-code warm operation | Linux Git 2.43 median before → after | macOS Git 2.56 median before → after |
|---|---:|---:|
| Patch log | 30.95 → 32.10 ms | 94.29 → 116.67 ms |
| Blame | 27.14 → 31.38 ms | 77.94 → 109.54 ms |

Warm blame A/A medians: Linux 24.01 / 23.79 ms; macOS 79.44 / 79.43 ms. Warm log A/A: Linux 32.10 / 30.50 ms; macOS 98.54 / 95.02 ms. Git starts increase 5→6 for log and 5→7 for blame. Linux whole-command-tree CPU: warm log 30.05→31.05 ms, blame 26.76→31.93 ms. macOS CPU accounting is incomplete and is not compared. The warm-read cost pays for shared-clone detection and rename-safe preparation before unconditional offline execution. All six history tests pass on both Git versions; both general shim tests also pass on final code. Full-source/delta Codex autoreviews are scoped-clean. Reviewed head `b6eed12ef1c86c263b2318d9c2b909affcf6da97` landed through native scripts/pr as `ff0a22cd21177f3f9971049e8735c9fbb472b8aa` on 2026-11-14 at 03:45:13Z. Exact-head CI run43551030434 reached GREEN; the latest ClawSweeper review on that head had zero open items and zero findings. Both prior heads `0246f328386e` and `6fc0c66b86ce` had exact-head GREEN CI. `check:changed` was rerun at6fc0c66b86ce and again failed only the identical attributed dead-export set; every other check passed. Unchanged checks were reused for the final one-line log.follow override, whose affected tests, lint/format and fresh review passed.


The unchanged-range regression is red before repair and now fetches endpoint content in one bounded pack. Git's existing revision parser supplies the positive endpoint; the fallback runs only after complete, empty blame discovery. Implicit `log.follow` path history follows the existing explicit `--follow` native contract. Implicit paths without `--` reuse unresolved-path facts already established by revision preparation, including paths with spaces; no extra probe was added. Unscoped pickaxe remains bounded even with `log.follow=true`. The failed-batch injector now rejects `fetch` specifically and records that it ran, so `rev-list --stdin` cannot accidentally satisfy the failed-prefetch test.


## Performance owner acceptance

> Lead decision (campaign perf owner; Peter delegated these calls): ACCEPTED. Warm macOS patch-log latency goes 94→117 ms and blame 78→110 ms. In exchange, the whole-history pickaxe lazy-fetch storm goes from 65+ tiny packs (production: 38 tiny packs, then 1.12 GB over 18 min, a 9.9 s commit and 20% PSI) to 0 packs with actionable narrowing guidance, and scoped cold reads go from 10–11 s to 61–76 ms.

This is the owner's explicit acceptance of the measured warm-read cost. Production figures above are supplied observations, not measurements from the synthetic fixture.


## Second-attempt and failed-preparation proof

The original shim has no explicit whole-command retry loop. It does have unconditional native execution after best-effort blob preparation: a failed batch, incomplete discovery, or ownerless-lock timeout can return and reach unrestricted `exec git`. Process snapshots alone cannot distinguish that fallthrough from an external second invocation or another shim on PATH; noop-negotiation `fetch origin --stdin` occurs in both explicit prefetch and Git's lazy-fetch machinery. No additional production access was used to infer the launcher.

At retry-proof head `0246f328386e`, `prepared_blobs=1` is assigned in the parent shell before preparation (line 409). Returns or a terminated fetch inside the preparation subshell cannot clear it. The caller runs native Git with both no-lazy-fetch and protocol denial (lines 621–627), then exits; it cannot reach the unrestricted exec. A fresh invocation applies the same policy again.

A supplemental real-Git 2.43 reproduction runs the exact `git log --oneline -S selectThemeSettings` twice against the same shared partial clone. On the 20,001-commit fixture, the original creates **64 then 66 additional packs**, each stopped at the observation cap; final code creates **0 then 0 packs**, returns exit 2 with actionable guidance in **122.7 and 117.2 ms**, and starts no fetches. These are censored baseline observations, not successful-search latency comparisons.

On a bounded 100-commit fixture, an injected first-fetch failure and a SIGTERM of the first fetch each return exit 2 with guidance and zero packs. Repeating the same command after that one-shot failure succeeds with **one explicit batch / one pack**, with no native lazy-fetch children. An actual ownerless-lock wait expires after **31.8 seconds**, returns exit 2 with guidance and zero packs; retry after removing the fixture-owned lock succeeds with one batch / one pack. Existing committed failed-prefetch pack-count regression is red on the original source (11 lazy packs) and green on the fix. No additional source change was required.


## Combined diffs and root-blame compatibility

The final hosted review identified two additional native Git contracts, both reproduced red before repair. Combined raw diff records contain one mode/object pair per parent plus the result; discovery now includes every object within the existing bound. Blame discovery explicitly includes root changes even when `log.showRoot=false`, while leaving user log presentation unchanged. Regression coverage compares real native output and requires one pack for `diff HEAD^!`, explicit multi-parent `diff`, and historical root blame. These corrections add five production lines and no Git processes, fetches, caches or configuration; the previously measured ordinary raw records and default root inclusion cover the same objects.


Internal blame discovery also overrides `log.follow=false` so caller log preferences cannot make its metadata-only --full-diff query fail. The actual user command retains the original setting. The existing rename fixture now covers log.follow=true, with native output and one-pack/13-object assertions: red on6fc0c66b86ce, green after the one-line repair. Final eight focused tests pass on Git2.56 (82.06s including compilation), all six history tests pass on Git2.43 (4.32s), and fresh Codex delta review plus targeted lint/format pass. The completed check:changed result at6fc0c66b86ce is reused for unchanged checks; its one remaining failure is the identical attributed dead-export set. No new production lines, Git processes or default-workload objects were added by this final configuration override.

prs.title: feat(exec): keep durable background commands running across Gateway restarts on macOS
prs.body:
Fixes #197443

## What Problem This Solves

Durable background commands are unavailable on macOS, preventing sessions from keeping work running across Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

macOS users can run Gateway-host background commands with `durable: true` and resume observing their output and completion after a Gateway restart. This requires a logged-in GUI session; logout and reboot still end the jobs. Descendants that leave the command's process group are outside its timeout and stop handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use transient launchd jobs behind the existing durable-process registry. A wrapper tracks the command's process group, enforces its timeout, and records its outcome and duration. Failed job observations remain unknown and are retried. The launch environment is stored in a private spec file and removed before command execution. Doctor excludes these jobs from its stray-service scan.

Accepted edge cases, kept simple on purpose (named in code comments):

- If the wrapper is killed from outside while its command runs, OpenClaw does not signal the orphaned process group itself. Stop reports "not confirmed" and points at `launchctl list`; the run settles as outcome unknown once the group ends.
- If the wrapper cannot write its status file after starting the command (for example, a full disk), the wrapper exits and the command runs on without supervision. OpenClaw reports the outcome as unknown and asks to check output and side effects before repeating work.
- The existing completion-notification crash window remains: a Gateway crash immediately after recording notification settlement can lose the completion wake.

## Evidence

- Targeted tests at this head: `src/agents/bash-process-launchd.test.ts`, 4 passed. The file no longer sleeps in the test process; the wrapper case still starts real subprocesses (a 0.2 s background child and a 0.3 s timeout).
- The PR adds 154 net test lines, under the 400-line allowance, so no test-lines allocation record is needed.
- Live macOS run, recorded at `efb41c8` in a logged-in GUI LaunchAgent on macOS 26.6.2: [run summary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197474#issuecomment-6836801128) and [durable-evidence.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34770920/durable-evidence.json). A durable command survives a Gateway restart and delivers its completion wake; a command completes while the Gateway is down; the wrapper enforces the timeout while the Gateway is down and keeps the measured duration; killing the wrapper leaves the command running and later reports an unknown outcome; another session cannot stop the job, the owning session can.
- Not run live at this head: the stop loop was simplified and the two edge-case branches above were removed after that run. Broad CI, Linux live execution, logout/reboot behavior, and macOS privacy-permission behavior were not checked here.

prs.title: fix(ui): show recorded tool actions and preserve chat lifecycles
prs.body:
## Latest pushed revision

`248ef462567c1e0ca6c8dd39269470a121d915a0` fixes the subagent panel crash by keeping operations and their object-keyed context maps in the same snapshot. Deferred steering inputs retain A/B/C order and identity while local messages become accepted custody and then persisted history, including an acknowledgment arriving before the next send.

The first tool call now keeps its invocation, activity-group and disclosure identity through hydration and appended calls. One activity renderer handles ordinary, inline and standalone segments. A shared presentation timer holds a newly arriving group for 200 ms (bounded to one second during a continuous burst), preventing a transient wrapper from flashing its label or chevron. Recorded outcomes and urgent failures remain immediate; completed work does not retain a running shimmer. Settled singleton operations use their direct row.

Summaries name skill searches and reads semantically, resolve chat and wait targets from already-loaded names, retain useful childless Code Mode purposes, and distinguish running commands from completed executions regardless of exit status. The automation transcript consumer also uses factual summaries and no longer exposes “Raw details” as an activity. Launch/lifecycle terminology is unchanged pending the maintainer's decision.

**Validation:** 252 focused tests across 14 files, eight Chromium disclosure/interaction tests, and all three bundled operation/headline cases passed. UI types, focused lint/format, i18n verification and controller guards passed. The independent code review found no actionable regressions. The production UI build succeeds with six budget violations: document gzip (+8 bytes), largest JavaScript gzip, total CSS raw/gzip, chat boot JavaScript gzip and new-chat boot JavaScript gzip. No budget or baseline was raised.

The duplicate inline activity renderer was removed; the existing activity owner now handles segmentation and snapshot consistency. The new regression coverage exercises the reproduced crash, steer-order transitions, disclosure identity and initial visibility, rather than freezing styling.

No new recordings or real-model Gateway runs were made for this revision. The maintainer will pull and test it against their real Gateway. This remains a draft and does not claim zero jitter across untested real workflows. All media below belongs to the explicitly listed earlier revisions.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode titles and execution wrappers hide the operations that actually happened. Opening “Worked for” adds a counter, hiding narration can merge separate batches, and completing a run can remove the paragraph being read. The live tool buffer also discarded early calls after 50 entries, so an expanded batch could lose operations and recover them only after history reconciliation.

## User Impact

- Groups describe recorded work as a sentence, such as “Ran commands, read files, edited files, searched”. Recorded Code Mode children use the ordinary grouping rules; their original input and output remain available through inspection. Routine hidden polling does not reappear as an extra wrapper row. An execution without representative children keeps its descriptive purpose, or a factual fallback when no purpose was recorded.
- Narration, permission requests, questions, session launches and rich output keep their places. Hiding narration preserves its boundaries. Only the eligible tail segment presents live activity.
- Changing the selected action has a short cadence; its recorded outcome updates immediately. Expanding a group puts the command on its operation row instead of repeating it in the heading and output body. Full commands remain readable on narrow panes.
- Failed attempts remain inspectable, including outcomes whose raw call is not in the loaded page. A failure does not mark the whole group as failed or imply that a matching later call recovered it.
- Completion preserves an above-tail reader’s open work and reading anchor. A reader following the end gets the folded “Worked for” heading and final answer. Cold history retains the normal folded default.
- Explicitly blocking questions use the native inline panel; asynchronous questions retain the composer dock. Subagent and child-chat launches have distinct labels and recorded outcomes; parent return does not imply child completion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Execution identity and visual grouping have different jobs. This change resolves recorded operations before grouping, retains live calls until the existing history/run cleanup replaces them, and reuses the existing disclosure, scroll-anchor, permission, question and media owners. Known containers stay available as inspection evidence without becoming recurring transcript rows. The optional `blocking` question field comes from owners that actually wait; polling and narration do not infer it.

The remaining production growth serves segmentation around standalone lifecycle events, native question placement, operation labels and missing-raw-call outcomes. Against pinned base `9d28854c4322`: production +1763/−625 lines across 51 files; tests +1682/−609 across 25 files; docs +32/−11. No new durable store or recovery protocol.

## Evidence at prior revision 087f37e

Evidence revision: `087f37e59bdc0c24795f973e56d50ceea559c5ae`. The six recordings below include five after captures from this head and one explicitly labeled prior-head comparison. They use the real Control UI in isolated task-owned environments. Deterministic Gateway streams and the real-model execution are identified separately. The old recordings are retained at the end as historical evidence, not evidence of this head.

| Real model, isolated Gateway, disposable calculator project | 10 Code Mode executions, 24 recorded child operations and four narration blocks; 13/14 tests failed before repair, independent rerun passed 14/14; eight long-running batches completed. |
| Routine polling in that real run | Three completed wrappers whose children were hidden; 33 eligible UI samples, zero residual “Executed code” summaries. |
| Above-tail reading during completion | Same fixture as prior PR head `94b0f154680`: before, scroll moved −803 px and the paragraph disappeared; after, paragraph moved only −0.5 px and work stayed open. |
| Following the tail during completion | Distance from the end stayed 0 px; work folded and the final answer stayed visible. |
| 60-operation stream, completion and reload | 20 → 40 → 60 during streaming, then 60 after completion and 60 after reload; the same operation signatures, order and three batch memberships. |
| Interactions and narrow layout | Returned parent with still-running child, native permission, blocking inline question, async composer question with retained draft, playable media/overlay; 96-character command wraps into three lines at a 390 px viewport without duplication or clipping. |

## Validation and Limits

The DOM proof maps recorded call IDs to visible operation signatures, batch membership and order. It does not establish individual identity for identical command strings by text alone, or claim that a DOM node survives reload. Reload checks saved content/order; it does not assert persistence of scroll position or open disclosures. Expanded output still uses the existing bounded, independently scrollable group, so output below its viewport requires scrolling within that group.

prs.title: improve(ui): show dictation feedback on click and a live voice level while listening
prs.body:
Refs #195982

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI dictation feels stuck when it starts: after the click the composer shows a long "Waiting for microphone access…" notice, and while listening it shows only a "Listening…" label with no sign that the microphone hears anything.

## User Impact

User impact: the moment dictation starts, the composer shows pulsing bars and "Starting microphone…", and while it listens, bars beside "Listening…" follow the live microphone level. The browser-permission hint appears only when opening the microphone takes longer than a second, which is when a permission prompt is the likely cause, and it wraps to its full text in narrow composers.

This covers the start and listening part of #195982. Progress after Send and dropped transcripts are not addressed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The dictation session already measured the input level, but nothing displayed it. The dictation owner keeps that level and the status row renders it with the same bar meter Talk uses.
- The dictation audio context starts while the browser opens the microphone instead of after it. In a VM test with a fake microphone, the step from "microphone open" to "Listening…" dropped from about 100 ms to under 10 ms. Microphone errors still take precedence over an unsupported-audio error.
- Accepted limit: in the main chat composer, a tap starts Talk and dictation needs a press and hold, so dictation itself starts only after the 0.5 s hold threshold. The hold ring is the feedback for that half second; this PR does not open the microphone during the hold.

## Evidence

Before (current main), New Session dictation: the permission notice while the microphone opens, then a plain "Listening…" label.

![Before: "Waiting for microphone access" notice, then a plain "Listening…" label](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/0a75e528e33fbb0241f702f7b2b0bda21166751b/images/2026/11/914e9cd3-8c9f-4d9e-b82b-175656386c8f.png)

After: pulsing bars with "Starting microphone…", then bars following the voice level beside "Listening…".

![After: "Starting microphone…" with pulsing bars, then live level bars beside "Listening…"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/0a75e528e33fbb0241f702f7b2b0bda21166751b/images/2026/11/a279afbd-0560-45ad-9dc4-ef8e8626d25a.png)

Slow microphone access in a 320 px wide composer: the permission hint wraps and stays readable.

![320 px composer: the full "Waiting for microphone access. Bring this tab to the foreground and allow access if prompted." hint wrapped beside the starting bars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/48b90d4cc81245c0b6abb680948b4efd12ac00ae/images/2026/11/52b89834-5278-4dac-8afb-76f3d8af75fc.png)

- Live run in a macOS VM: current main and this branch built side by side, Control UI e2e harness with Playwright Chromium, a simulated Gateway with a transcription provider, and a fake microphone playing speech-like audio. New Session click and main chat hold both reach listening with the bars moving and the transcript landing in the draft. Click to "Listening…" over 7 runs each: median 236 ms on main, 171 ms on this branch.
- `browser-dictation-status.e2e.test.ts`: 13 passed, including a new 320 px case that holds microphone access pending and checks the permission hint is not clipped. That case fails against the first commit of this branch, where the hint is cut to "Waiting for microphone access. Bring …".
- Unit tests: `composer-dictation.test.ts`, `composer-direct-dictation.test.tsx`, `chat-composer.test.ts`, `chat-composer-microphone.test.ts`: 75 passed. The `chat-composer.test.ts` case for the starting label, its bars and the delayed permission hint fails against main's dictation sources. Two outbox cases in `chat-composer.test.ts` failed intermittently on a heavily loaded machine and passed on rerun, on both main and this branch.
- `tsgo` for the UI project, oxlint, format checks and `git diff --check` on the changed files: clean.
- Not tested: a real microphone, a real Gateway with a real transcription provider, and non-English locales (the new "Starting microphone…" string is English-only until translation runs).

prs.title: fix(ui): let expired OAuth profiles reconnect
prs.body:
Closes #148323.

Supersedes #148325. **Still Draft:** conflict repair, public-code review and synthetic browser validation are complete; real expired-xAI authorization and credential persistence have not been exercised.

## What Problem This Solves

An expired OpenClaw-managed OAuth account in Models has no profile-level action to restart its provider's advertised authorization flow.

## User Impact

Reconnect opens the existing Gateway-owned OAuth/device-code wizard for an eligible expired account, then refreshes its status after completion. It does not change the active model. The recorded test demonstrates that UI path with fictional data, not compatibility with the real xAI service.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing login runner already owns authorization, mutation admission, cancellation and stale-result handling. This change reuses that owner instead of adding a credential store or authentication RPC.

Reconnect requires an expired OAuth profile, a positive Gateway `reconnectSupported` ownership capability, exactly one advertised OAuth/device-code route, and existing write/busy admission. Config display provenance and logout eligibility are not ownership authority. External or inherited profiles, missing local-ownership metadata and ambiguous routes fail closed; the Gateway excludes external IDs even if they overlap the local set. Existing logout behavior is unchanged.

### Conflict repair — 2026-10-25

Conflict-repair head: `ac5c975754f91d342e1cbe6de6557954c49f01c6`.
Merged actual upstream main `9629838ec1aab5d0917828453335473bfa385847` into prior published head `a6519de67ed551eec6b3c16553f9d55043dd805a`, preserving both parents and the original PR.

Resolved the two conflicts in the login controller and its browser suite. Reconnect now lives in current main's inline `providerActions` getter; removed single-use helper wrappers were not restored. The current model-access scenarios and their exact request/no-activation assertions are retained. The contribution remains 11 files (+518/-44) against that main commit; this is not a new feature expansion.

## Evidence

### Hosted review and remaining decision — 2026-11-14

The [ClawSweeper review of `269903e49e`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150688#issuecomment-5710314969) completed on November 6 with no actionable code findings. The [CI gate was skipped](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42165727120/job/127721659223) while this PR remained Draft.

Models and auth owners still need to decide when credential health warrants interactive sign-in. Real expired-xAI authorization, credential persistence, and refreshed status with the same active model are unverified. The recorded browser proof uses a mocked Gateway and fictional accounts. The [linked report's administrative closure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/148323#issuecomment-6670010644) did not record a fix. Please consider a `no-stale` hold on this draft while the owner decision and live proof are pending.

### Current main integration — 2026-11-06 (`269903e49e6db2a954c8716e5d43ce1544d8a1f6`)

Merged main `7349fd516c645ec49ca0708e94f8527988e2a9cf` into the original branch, preserving `91c80e7d53ef01e63a01acb5110ddc07bbc39d92` as a parent. The account-action conflict now retains both the existing API-key Replace action and the OAuth Reconnect action. Browser coverage follows main's current native-permissions step and completion copy. Shared completion-model selection stays in the existing login-provider module; no separate login state or model activation is introduced.

Validation on this candidate:
- **60/60 UI tests** across six owning suites, **53/53 Gateway auth-status tests**, and **7/7 Chromium browser tests** passed. The browser suite builds the production UI and uses a mocked Gateway with fictional expired/restored xAI profiles and device code. It exercises Reconnect, wizard completion, restored-profile readback, and ordinary login/native-permissions siblings.
- UI and targeted Gateway typechecks, typed UI/core lint, formatting, English i18n verification, diff checks, and the test-line budget passed. The scoped allocation records the contribution's 416 net test lines; the shared budget baseline is unchanged.
- Fresh independent Codex review of all 12 public contribution files plus the public owner contracts completed **P0–P2 scoped-clean (1/1)**. The reviewer did not execute tests; the runs above are separate local evidence.
- Initial checks exposed an over-budget login controller, outdated browser completion text, and a capture aimed at a non-painted modal host. These were corrected; the final frozen candidate passed without raising limits, extending timeouts, or weakening behavior assertions.
- Reviewed/committed tree: `838f72dc9d988039e236f3f934efe9598abf88ea`. Contribution-file SHA-256: `ec8adae779256f821b57ce473f8920fc4f6ac8e25cb85af70abcdc939428226f`.

**Remaining gates:** fresh hosted CI/review is separate from these local results. The maintainer decision on routine expiry versus credential-health-driven reconnect eligibility remains open. Real expired-xAI authorization, credential persistence, and real-provider readback have not been performed; the PR remains Draft. No real accounts, private user data, credentials, workflow secrets, or Orca source were used. Historical captures and runs below retain their original commit/date scope.

### Latest review follow-up — 2026-10-27

Current head: `91c80e7d53ef01e63a01acb5110ddc07bbc39d92` (two test files, +4/-20; production behavior unchanged).

Addressed the [latest ClawSweeper test-value feedback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150688#issuecomment-5710314969): remove the standalone config-bound positive-presence component case. The stronger registered-page config-bound scenario still exercises the advertised route, completion, Close, and restored-status readback; external/config/inherited/saved missing-ownership controls and the inherited/removable overlap remain.

- Both affected files pass **30 tests** (Vitest 2.68s; wrapper wall time 4.07s), plus targeted typed lint, formatting and diff checks.
- The initial two-file run had three immediate button-enabled assertion failures (27 passed / 3 failed). The tests now await the same observable enabled condition before clicking, preserving the existing async configuration-owner admission contract. No timeout, production code, ownership guard, auth-route assertion or readback assertion changed.
- Fresh canonical independent **P0–P2 review of this two-file delta completed scoped-clean**, 1/1 pass with complete usage reporting. It assessed the diff and public configuration-owner/harness context; runtime coverage comes from the separate executed tests.
- The prior 59-UI/51-Gateway integration proof and production review remain attributed to `f0104df14`, whose production bytes are unchanged. They are not claimed as additional new-head runs. New-head hosted CI and review are separate.

**Still Draft:** the latest advisory also asks the maintainer to decide whether Reconnect should apply to routine access-token expiry or only unusable-sign-in credential facts, preserving automatic-refresh messaging. That product decision and authorized real-Gateway expired-xAI recovery through persistence/readback remain unresolved. This test-only follow-up does not change the proposed eligibility rule or perform real account authorization. No private data, real logs or secrets were used or shared; maintainer edits/secrets access remain disabled.

### Current main integration — 2026-10-27

Current integration head: `f0104df14db38c1c838d88a52d9eb49648e0a922`. This merge preserves original PR head `1630a2cd749e6bf826b69f530d82956f03348dc0` and actual main `4d8806c8c2e297af9bc06f5cc73d4b0a3a8f949b` as its two parents.

The shared sign-in start has two production callers (picker and Reconnect); both pass the Gateway-advertised brand, and Reconnect still does not request model activation. The obsolete single-use completion helper is removed rather than restored.

- **59 UI tests across five files pass** on the integrated candidate (latest wrapper wall time 13.06s, Vitest 10.34s), covering the registered page, existing login/activation/default selection, completion refresh, profile controls and fail-closed reconnect ownership.
- Two registered-page logo regressions fail before brand forwarding for the intended missing provider badge, then pass after repair. Both the ordinary picker and direct Reconnect path retain main's Grok/xAI brand. The intended red run was 6.23s wall time; earlier fixture setup and busy-loop attempts were not counted as product proof.
- The existing **51 Gateway auth-status/logout tests pass** (120.94s wrapper wall time, including first worker compilation). These use fictional configuration/credentials and exercise production auth-status projection, not a real provider authorization.
- Full UI and targeted Gateway production typechecks, targeted typed lint, formatting, i18n verification, and contribution diff checks pass. The local default Bun attempt could not start because the supported macOS SQLite library was unavailable; the documented Node 24.22.1 test mode was used without changing guards. An interim extraction widened `selectModel` to boolean; formal types and independent review caught it, and an explicit `{ selectModel?: true }` annotation resolves it. The final types and review pass; no guard, baseline or assertion was weakened.
- Fresh canonical independent **P0–P2 review of the final public candidate completed scoped-clean**, 1/1 pass with complete usage reporting, after the type repair. Review did not execute project code or validate a real account.
- Frozen contribution diff SHA-256 against that main: `9b215c997491268708a2835b9fca0ef2900829e931e9071ba5105eef54cacf09`. Only the original 11 contribution files differ from main.

**Still Draft:** current-head checks report 13 successes and 85 skips, with no failed or pending check. The skipped Draft lanes are not passing test proof. Hosted review is still in progress; independent local review above is complete. Prior Chromium captures and execution evidence below remain tied to their recorded older heads; no new production-browser capture, real expired-xAI authorization, credential replacement/persistence, or real-provider status readback was performed for this integration. Maintainer product acceptance and authorized live recovery remain open. No private Orca code, personal notes/configuration, real logs or secrets were used; maintainer edits/secrets access remain disabled.

### Historical validation and captures

### Latest review follow-up — 2026-10-25

Current PR head: `1630a2cd749e6bf826b69f530d82956f03348dc0`.

Addressed the latest [ClawSweeper test-value feedback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150688#issuecomment-5710314969) with a test-only change (+2/-15, one file): remove seven duplicate missing-ownership variants from the component-level fixture loop. The registered-page tests still cover missing capability for external/config/inherited/saved profiles and the inherited/removable overlap. The retained non-expired and non-OAuth controls now have `reconnectSupported: true`, so each exercises its intended status/type guard rather than passing because ownership is absent. Write-permission, busy-state, credential-owner routing and unavailable/ambiguous-route checks are retained.

- **27/27 focused UI tests pass** across the changed component test and registered-page reconnect suite (Vitest 4.66s; wrapper wall time 8.08s). No hosted CI time is claimed for this new head.
- Targeted UI/E2E typecheck, typed lint of the changed test, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Fresh isolated independent **P0–P2 review of this test-only delta is scoped-clean**, with complete usage reporting. It assessed the full public component and overlapping page tests; it did not execute project code.
- No production code, Gateway behavior, auth flow or browser scenario changed. The 9/9 browser captures and prior production-contract evidence below are reused unchanged-input evidence from `ac5c975754`, not newly executed end-to-end tests on this test-only head.

The latest hosted ClawSweeper review of `ac5c975754` found no actionable correctness defects, but still requires **maintainer product acceptance** of the added account-row action and **authorized real-Gateway expired-xAI recovery through persistence/readback**. Those requirements are not claimed resolved. Hosted Codex's separate attempt failed with an unknown service error, not a code verdict; the independent local workflow review above is a separate result. Keep Draft and maintainer edits disabled; no real account authorization is performed.

### Retained conflict-repair validation

The following conflict-repair results were recorded at `ac5c975754f91d342e1cbe6de6557954c49f01c6`, using merged candidate tree `c3e55272164f394fd183f75aa5bc2b2ade713867` on task-only Node 24.22.1 with current main's frozen dependency lock, including Solid rc.18. The frozen-lock install passed; no dependency or lockfile change was authored.

- The existing Gateway auth-status/ordering/logout test file and **55 tests across five relevant UI files passed** in two Vitest shards (57.89s). They cover positive local/config-local ownership and fail-closed external, inherited, overlapping and missing-metadata cases, alongside existing login, completion and refresh behavior.
- **Recorded production-UI Chromium E2E: 9/9 passed** (Vitest 240.45s; test file 136.196s; production UI build 91s). This includes Expired → Reconnect → fictional device-code wizard → completion → Close → expand → restored-account readback, plus browser-callback and all three existing model-access/default-preservation cases. - The first recorded attempt was **6 passed / 3 failed**, not hidden or counted as a passing run. One extra typecheck attempt encountered an active dist-artifact lock from the concurrent lint owner; it was rerun successfully after that owner finished, without deleting the lock or bypassing ownership.

prs.title: fix(github): publication fails with PostgreSQL session or state stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes GitHub publication requests failing when either shared state or the source session uses PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

Publication works with SQLite, PostgreSQL, and mixed engine configurations. A concurrent source writer remains excluded until publication settles. No configuration, schema, permission, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publication worker read the SQLite identity anchor instead of the configured session store and reserved the destination anchor instead of its PostgreSQL connection. Use the existing engine opener and transaction owner, retain admitted engine identities, and keep receipts attached to the existing anchors. Empty lock attempts release acquired reservations before retrying.

This reimplements the intent of `ada7d22ab01` against current main rather than importing its patch. Simplification keeps PostgreSQL lock acquisition with the PostgreSQL transaction owner and removes the anchor-only data path; no new state owner or production test hooks.

## Evidence

- Real disposable PostgreSQL, all four SQLite/PostgreSQL state/session pairs: the conformance proof now exercises the production requester, canonical identity/profile, operator role/session policy, source reservation and durable-admission owners. It demonstrates authorized creator success, rejection of an equally scoped foreign principal, and committed runtime-policy revocation while a separate request waits on its real source reservation. Final durable assertions retain the authorized requester snapshot and exclude the denied publication.
- Pinned negative control: reverting only the six affected production owners to the original parent produces 3 failures / 1 pass (`session_nodes` missing or unavailable source reservation). The candidate passes 24/24: four mixed-engine authority flows and 20 source-fence regressions. Those six baseline owners are unchanged in the inspected current-main context. This is an owner-reversion control, not a complete baseline checkout run.
- Gateway publication consumers: 42/42 passed, including a fresh continuation run. The combined continuation runner timed out after its Gateway shard passed and before the infra shard completed; the separate source-fence rerun passed 20/20. The timeout is retained as an observation, not relabeled a passing combined run.
- Existing deferred-commit proof verifies PostgreSQL and SQLite source-writer exclusion through destination settlement. Rollback, cancellation, aliasing, contention and lost-reply regressions remain covered.
- Fresh full-candidate independent autoreview at P0–P2 with 13 production-owner contexts: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Core/infra-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Published proof commit `c7393f4518f24f985f8c7aa0b39baa37f1ac884d` directly extends the previously reviewed head. Its entire tree and all three changed blobs match the tested local candidate; the human co-author trailer is preserved. New-head CI was attached and pending at publication; no final-green claim is made here.

November 14 proof submission and new hosted execution: the bullets above are historical original-implementation evidence, not fresh verification of the corrected head. Exact signed candidate `551e25b7f93d81dd82e0b10f8e75379f16f2e6ef` was published through the native proof-purpose route. New-head [CI run 43547547121](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43547547121), attempt 1, completed successfully. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed, and the four publication cases passed without target-case skips: SQLite/SQLite, PostgreSQL/PostgreSQL, PostgreSQL/SQLite, and SQLite/PostgreSQL state/session stores. prs.title: feat(ui): edit an agent's thinking default from its Overview
prs.body:
Closes #198371

## What Problem This Solves

The agent Overview page shows an agent's **Thinking default** as plain text, so setting one agent's level (for example a `coder` agent) means using the config editor or the CLI.

## User Impact

Operators who can edit config can pick an agent's thinking default in **Agents → agent → Overview → Model selection**. The menu lists only the levels that agent's model accepts, plus **Inherit default (level)**, which removes the agent's own setting. Choices save to `agents.entries.<id>.thinkingDefault` through the page's existing autosave and affect only that agent. Message and session thinking overrides still take precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The levels come from the agent's row in `agents.list` (`thinkingLevels`), which the Gateway already resolves for that agent's model and runtime.
- **Schema change (additive):** `agents.list` agent rows gain an optional `thinkingInheritedDefault`. The Gateway sends it only when the agent sets its own `thinkingDefault`. It is the level that clearing the override resolves to, using the same resolver as runs: per-agent model params, shared model params, the global default, the model's own default, then clamping to the model's levels. The core resolver gains an option to skip only the agent's own `thinkingDefault`. Existing clients can ignore the field; the Swift and Kotlin protocol contracts are unchanged. The protocol changelog is release-owned, so this description records the schema change.
- Restricted model views (a model selection policy) drop `thinkingInheritedDefault` along with the other thinking fields, because it is resolved from the agent's hidden model. Their `thinkingDefault` is the agent's own override, so with an override and no inherited level the option reads plain **Inherit default** and names no level.
- The **Inherit default (level)** label shows `thinkingInheritedDefault`, or the agent's resolved level when it has no override. Example: global Low, a per-model param of High and an agent override of Medium give "Inherit default (High)", which is what clearing produces.
- Level names come from one helper, `thinkingLevelLabel` in `ui/src/lib/chat/thinking.ts`, which this page and the Models page share. It uses the `quickSettings.model.thinkingLevels.*` translations through each page's reactive translator. The five standard levels that had no key (Minimal, Extra high, Adaptive, Maximum, Ultra) gain canonical English, and the translation pipeline supplies other locales. Provider-specific levels keep their own label.
- A saved level that the current model does not offer stays visible and selected, but greyed out, instead of being rewritten.
- The row reads the real config even when the model catalog restricts model choices, because thinking is not a model choice.
- Before config has loaded, or for users who cannot read config, the row is disabled and shows the resolved level the way the read-only row did.

**Known gaps:**

- The level list belongs to the agent's saved model. Right after changing the primary model, the list still shows the old model's levels until the agent list refreshes. Any level picked meanwhile is valid config, and the Gateway clamps it to the new model at run time.
- On a model whose only level is a harness Ultra, an agent with an Ultra override shows "Inherit default (Ultra)", though clearing it leaves no default. This is rare, and the level is visible and recoverable.

## Evidence

Live run on an isolated Gateway built from this branch, inside a macOS VM, with made-up config: agent `coder` on a stand-in reasoning model. A headless browser drove the Control UI, and the script checked the config file after each step.

Before choosing: the menu offers `Inherit default (Medium)`, `Off`, `Minimal`, `Low`, `Medium`, `High`, `Ultra`.
This frame is from the run before the label-only fix; that fix does not change this frame.

![Thinking default showing Inherit default (Medium)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/d30dfd561bd40d9d49bfcc1ede37da3223a5f32f/images/2026/11/7c8b9ed5-7cfe-458d-b194-92cec8158493.png)

After choosing **High**, the config file has `agents.entries.coder.thinkingDefault: "high"` and `agents.defaults` is unchanged; after a page reload the row still shows High:

![Thinking default showing High after reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/d30dfd561bd40d9d49bfcc1ede37da3223a5f32f/images/2026/11/83758db8-eb60-4cfc-b579-436be268c6af.png)

Choosing **Inherit default** again removes the key from `agents.entries.coder`; after a reload the row reads Inherit default (Medium):

![Thinking default back to Inherit default after reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/d30dfd561bd40d9d49bfcc1ede37da3223a5f32f/images/2026/11/b566695d-70fb-4e73-b53d-2eeb8c48b717.png)

Second live run, same VM setup: global Low, a per-model `params.thinking` of High, and coder's own Medium.
- **Upgrade from latest stable (2026.11.3):** stable shows the read-only row. The update runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` with this build, then starts on the same state. coder's entry and the defaults are unchanged. `agents.list` reports `thinkingDefault: "medium"` and `thinkingInheritedDefault: "high"`, and the inherit option reads "Inherit default (High)". Choosing it removes the override, and after a reload the agent resolves to High.
- **Model-restricted operator:** a trusted-proxy person whose role has `modelPolicy.allow: ["standin/stand-in"]` and admin scope. The projected roster carries the override as `thinkingDefault` with no inherited field, and the inherit option reads plain "Inherit default".

![Stable 2026.11.3: Thinking Default medium, read-only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/d14cac6ebc379e191d36e1e4456e6067dc41150d/images/2026/11/d7fd05a9-2a99-47fb-944e-a97d032896c6.png)
![After clearing on the upgraded branch: Inherit default (High)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/d14cac6ebc379e191d36e1e4456e6067dc41150d/images/2026/11/e72038cb-67c1-4659-8c41-b91d83204381.png)
![Model-restricted operator: Thinking default editable, model choices policy-owned](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/d14cac6ebc379e191d36e1e4456e6067dc41150d/images/2026/11/5614497f-12de-42a6-b9f7-445ff6dd3366.png)

Tests and checks:
- `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.test.ts`: 21 passed; `ui/src/pages/agents/model-config.test.ts`: 13 passed; the Models page view, locale and page tests and `ui/src/lib/chat/thinking.test.ts` pass with the shared helper. They cover the levels offered, saving and clearing, inherited labels (global Low, per-model High and override Medium labelled "Inherit default (High)"; the same override on a restricted roster labelled plain "Inherit default"), a saved level the model does not offer, a restricted model catalog, and the disabled state without config. The tests that pinned the row as a read-only fact were replaced.
- `src/gateway/session-utils.agent-models.test.ts`: `agents.list` reports `thinkingInheritedDefault: "high"` for that case and omits it for an agent without an override; the real restricted projection of that roster drops the field and reports `thinkingDefault: "medium"`. The UI and Gateway tests each fail without their fix and pass with it.
- `src/gateway/session-utils-model.thinking-default.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-list.test.ts` and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agents-models-skills.test.ts`: pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, the gateway test typecheck, oxlint and format on the touched files, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` and `pnpm protocol:check` (Swift and Kotlin contracts unchanged): pass. In a German locale the selector reads "Inherit default (Hoch)", "Aus", "Niedrig", "Mittel", "Hoch".
- Not run: the full test suite (left to CI).

prs.title: feat(a2a): implement the A2A protocol v1.0 specification
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR upgrades the `extensions/a2a` channel plugin from partial 0.3-era support to a **conformance-validated implementation of the A2A protocol v1.0 specification**, tested against the official [a2a-tck](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-tck) conformance suite (remaining failures are limited to scripted-reference-SUT-only scenarios — see Evidence). All configuration remains backward compatible with the original plugin.

## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/a2a` plugin currently implements only a partial, 0.3-era subset of the A2A protocol. A2A has since shipped **v1.0** with breaking changes and new requirements:

- **New method surface**: `SendMessage`/`GetTask`/`ListTasks`/`CancelTask`/`SendStreamingMessage`/`SubscribeToTask` replace the 0.3 dotted methods, plus push notification config CRUD and `GetExtendedAgentCard` — v1.0 clients calling a 0.3-era server get `Method not found`
- **HTTP+JSON (REST) binding** at `/a2a/v1/rest` (spec §5.4) with gRPC-transcoding-style path bindings — required for REST-native clients, previously absent
- **Revised error model**: codes `-32001..-32009` with `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` details, and new HTTP status mappings (`TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE` → 409, `CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` → 415, `INVALID_AGENT_RESPONSE` → 502) — the old mappings no longer conform
- **Capability, media-type, and required-extension validation** (spec §3.3.4, §3.1.1, §4.6) — previously not enforced
- **Agent Card caching** (ETag/304, §8.6.1) and the **Extended Agent Card** — previously absent
- **Push notification webhooks** with idempotent delete (§3.1.10) and SSRF protection — previously absent

In short: without this change, the plugin cannot interoperate with A2A v1.0 clients and fails the official conformance suite. With it, it passes (see Evidence below) while every pre-existing config key keeps its name, semantics, and default.

## Evidence

### a2a-tck conformance suite (official, black-box against a live instance)

Round 10 (latest, HEAD `086867253` — the stream-order fix — both declared transports `jsonrpc` + `http_json`, Bearer auth; [full rendered report](https://gist.github.com/beeven/d00d70490e12cea4d1450b26f472da37)):

- **Overall: 70.0% / MUST: 71.2%** — the only MUST requirements still failing are the two scripted reference-SUT contracts (`DM-ART-001`/`DM-MSG-001`)
- Per-transport: `agent_card` 10/10; `jsonrpc` 62P/5F; `http_json` 57P/5F — every remaining failure is a scripted-contract case
- `STREAM-ORDER-001` (round-9 finding: state-sequence regression when a reused messageId lands on a completed task) **passes on both transports** after `086867253`, with a regression test in the suite
- Round-to-round: 51.3% -> 65.8% -> 67.9% -> 69.1% -> 73.9% -> 75.0% -> 73.9% -> 71.4% -> 71.2% MUST. Round-over-round variance is coverage, not behavior: the real LLM returns COMPLETED or INPUT_REQUIRED non-deterministically for TCK's fixed prerequisite text, so requirements move in and out of the denominator between runs
- Round-9 confirmation traces (live gateway, token redacted):

```
# REST push-config list route — the round-8 regression, now fixed
GET /a2a/v1/rest/tasks/<uuid>/pushNotificationConfigs
-> 200 {"configs":[],"nextPageToken":"","pageSize":0}

# STREAM-ORDER-001 reproduction (reused messageId on a completed task)
jsonrpc  first stream : ok     [WORKING, WORKING, COMPLETED]
http_json reuse       : regress [COMPLETED, WORKING, COMPLETED]   <- before fix
http_json reuse       : ok     [WORKING, COMPLETED]               <- after 086867253
```

- Reproduction (public repo layout, local plugin injects Bearer auth which upstream TCK lacks):

```
cd a2a-tck && PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python ./run_tck.py \
    --sut-host http://localhost:38789 --transport jsonrpc,http_json -- \
    -p tck_local_openclaw --timeout=45 --timeout-method=signal
```

Artifacts: `reports/compatibility.json` / `compatibility.html` / `junitreport.xml`.

### Behavior proof over the real transport

Captured against a real Gateway built from this branch (`19e3466d0`) — real HTTP/SSE on the wire, real agent dispatch to a live model backend, real webhook POSTs to a local receiver (localhost endpoints and placeholder tokens throughout, nothing to redact). Full traces in [#issuecomment-6659323864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179380#issuecomment-6659323864); summary:

- **Allowed delivery**: three ordered webhook POSTs (WORKING → artifact → COMPLETED), all 200, per-task ordering held
- **Foreign peer refused**: unknown bearer → HTTP 401, no task, zero webhook POSTs
- **No POST after deletion in the real retry window**: registration deleted via REST inside the 250 ms backoff → receiver saw exactly one failed POST, no retries
- **No POST to the old URL after replacement in the retry window**: same config id re-registered to a new URL during backoff → old receiver silent, new receiver got the retries
- **No POST after shutdown**: SIGTERM while a delivery chain was live → terminal update delivered while the account was still stopping, then zero POSTs after `shutdown completed` with the receiver healthy for 17 s
- **Disabled extended card**: authenticated peer gets `-32004` UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION pointing at the config
- **Stream ordering (v4 contract)**: `SendStreamingMessage` = opening Task snapshot (WORKING) → updates → terminal close; subscribing to an INPUT_REQUIRED task folds all pre-subscription transitions into the snapshot and streams only post-subscription events
- **Follow-up retry identity**: identical messageId retry while the resumed turn was running resolved to the same task, history contains the answer exactly once
### Unit tests and typecheck (this repo)

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/a2a
Test Files  13 passed (13)
     Tests  151 passed (151)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test   # typecheck: green
```

New coverage added alongside the review fixes: REST binding HTTP tests (push-config create/list, shared per-peer rate limit -> 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, malformed body -> INVALID_ARGUMENT), per-subscriber stream queues each observing the full event sequence, replay-before-subscribe, interrupt-released blocking sends, `statusTimestampAfter` filtering, task-eviction observers expiring push registrations, 429 webhook retry, and the stream-order regression above.

### Config compatibility

- All pre-existing config keys verified unchanged (name/semantics/default) — existing deployments upgrade without touching config
- New keys are opt-in; `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` regenerated via `pnpm config:channels:gen` and the metadata sync check passes

## What's implemented

### Core protocol (§3)
- All **11 JSON-RPC methods** defined in v1.0: `SendMessage`, `GetTask`, `ListTasks`, `CancelTask`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `SubscribeToTask`, the four push notification config CRUD methods (`SetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `GetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `ListTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig`), and `GetExtendedAgentCard`
- Backward-compatible **0.3-era dotted method aliases** (`message/send`, `message/stream`, `tasks/get`, `tasks/list`, `tasks/cancel`, `tasks/subscribe`, ...) so existing clients keep working
- **Agent Card** served at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` with ETag / Last-Modified / Cache-Control caching and `If-None-Match` → 304 handling (§8.6.1)
- **Extended Agent Card** served behind the `extendedAgentCard` capability

### Transports
- **HTTP+JSON (REST) binding** at `/a2a/v1/rest` per §5.4, with gRPC-transcoding-style URL path bindings (path parameters take precedence over body fields)
- **SSE streaming** with resumable task updates
- **gRPC-style HTTP status mappings** per §5.4: `TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE` → 409, `CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` → 415, `INVALID_AGENT_RESPONSE` → 502

### Error model
- Full v1.0 error codes **-32001..-32009** with `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` details (reason / domain / metadata); JSON-RPC reserved codes (-32700..-32603) carry no ErrorInfo, as required

### Push notifications (§3.1.10)
- Full config CRUD with **idempotent delete** (repeated deletes succeed silently, per spec)
- Webhook delivery with **SSRF protection** (private-network targets blocked unless explicitly allowed)
- Configurable authentication schemes (bearer, basic, apikey)

### Validation
- **Capability validation** (§3.3.4): calling a method whose capability is disabled returns `-32004` `UnsupportedOperation`; enabling `extendedAgentCard` without configuring it returns `-32007`
- **Media-type validation** (§3.1.1): raw/url part media types checked against `inputModes` (with `type/*` and `*/*` wildcard support) before text-part checks, returning `-32005` with ErrorInfo metadata
- **Required extensions** (§4.6): extensions declared with `required: true` that are not activated via the `A2A-Extensions` header return `-32008`

### Outbound agent-to-agent client
- Full `Message | Task` oneof parsing with ErrorInfo reason surfacing in thrown errors

## Configuration compatibility

- **No breaking changes**: every pre-existing config key keeps its name, semantics, and default
- New v1.0 features are **opt-in** via new keys: `capabilities.*` (skill discovery, extensions, push), `pushNotifications.*` (auth, webhook options), `rest.enabled`, `extendedSkillDescriptions`
- `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` regenerated via `pnpm config:channels:gen` so core startup validation accepts the new keys
- Config-surface budget: this consciously raises the `channel` baseline by **+30 entries** (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`, channel 3975 → 4005) — exactly the new opt-in A2A v1.0 keys (`capabilities.*`, `pushNotifications.*`, `rest.*`, `extendedSkillDescriptions`, and peers/auth knobs); no existing keys changed

## Notes

- Rebased onto latest `main` (`65fc2f00d`); the diff is limited to `extensions/a2a/` + the regenerated config metadata file, and upstream's `wait()`/`buildContext` refactors from #178508 are integrated
- Happy to split into smaller commits or adjust scope per maintainer feedback

prs.title: fix: preserve bindings and static imports in standalone builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Standalone workers fail with numeric URL errors, and Gateway startup cannot find bundled packages, when minified output reuses an import alias or expresses a static import as a constant template.

## User Impact

Standalone packaging preserves ordinary worker callbacks and bundled package imports, restoring the behavior needed for Doctor and Gateway startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The import rewriter matched `createRequire` calls by spelling, including unrelated nested callbacks, and treated every template import as computed. Use the existing lexical binding owner for factory calls and the existing static-string reader for literal and constant-template specifiers. Computed imports, CommonJS imports and generated aliases keep their existing routing.

## Evidence

- Seven shadowing regression cases and five constant-template/alias regression cases fail before their fixes; all 76 focused tests pass with both fixes.
- Tooling and script test typechecks, focused lint and formatting pass. Independent review of the complete staged candidate is clean.
- The real emitted heartbeat worker keeps its one factory call instead of twelve wrappers. Its signed AOT Doctor gate passes with the binding fix.
- Both real emitted Gateway and cleanup modules retain their static package imports with the template fix.
- Full signed artifact requalification is incomplete. A separately reproduced stock compiler lowering failure is outside this fix; this PR does not claim full stock-compiler compatibility.
