prs.title: fix: templates build rejects BOOTSTRAP.md that passes validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`templates validate` accepts a package-root `BOOTSTRAP.md` up to the 2 MiB workspace bootstrap limit, but `templates build` rereads the same file under the generic 1 MiB managed-file cap. A valid 1,680,008-byte file therefore passes validation and then fails to build. Fixes #198559.

## Why This Change Was Made

The build path now uses the existing `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES` limit when rereading package-root `BOOTSTRAP.md`. Other managed files keep their existing limit.

## User Impact

Template packages with package-root `BOOTSTRAP.md` files between 1 MiB and 2 MiB can build after validation. Files over 2 MiB still receive the existing `package_bootstrap_too_large` diagnostic.

## Evidence

### Production-boundary reproduction

Before: base `dcd2afb07a1bec66341d4f82eef5e462bbf6d68e` validated the 1,680,008-byte fixture, then build failed with `file exceeds limit of 1048576 bytes`.

After: HEAD `b5d0ae83052745264a234de0c8dc6b7e389fb1f2` validated and built the same fixture; artifact creation succeeded.

Negative-control: a 2,097,153-byte `BOOTSTRAP.md` remains rejected with `package_bootstrap_too_large`.

### Focused regression

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/templates/project.test.ts -t 'package-root BOOTSTRAP' --reporter=dot` (2 passed).

<details>
<summary>Proof reproduction source</summary>

Run from the repository root with the local OpenClaw CLI available:

```bash
set -eu
ROOT="$(mktemp -d)"
FIXTURE="$ROOT/valid-large"
OVERSIZED="$ROOT/oversized-control"
cp -R test/fixtures/templates/project-v1 "$FIXTURE"
cp -R test/fixtures/templates/project-v1 "$OVERSIZED"
head -c 1680008 /dev/zero | tr '\0' x > "$FIXTURE/BOOTSTRAP.md"
head -c 2097153 /dev/zero | tr '\0' x > "$OVERSIZED/BOOTSTRAP.md"
mkdir -p "$ROOT/home" "$ROOT/state"
printf '{}' > "$ROOT/config.json"
export HOME="$ROOT/home"
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$ROOT/state"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$ROOT/config.json"
pnpm openclaw templates validate "$FIXTURE"
pnpm openclaw templates build "$FIXTURE" --out "$ROOT/valid.tgz"

  echo "unexpected success for oversized control"
  exit 1
fi
grep -F "package_bootstrap_too_large" "$ROOT/negative.log"
```

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full CI can run the same repository-wide formatting check in both `check-lint` and the required `check-docs` job. Each check runs oxfmt and pinned Bun parity, duplicating two complete formatter passes.

## User Impact

No product behavior change. Current-revision CI runs formatting once when docs owns the required check. Docs-skipped runs retain lint's check, and frozen release targets retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate lint's existing formatting invocation on whether the required docs job already owns it. Both formatter implementations and the aggregate docs failure gate remain intact.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, recorded before measurements: on this committed checkout, compare two fresh `CI=true pnpm format:check` invocations (baseline combined work) with one (candidate), in five interleaved pairs with a warm filesystem and one excluded warm-up per arm. Every invocation starts a fresh process. Require matching formatter diagnostics/status, four formatter children becoming two, at least 30% lower median combined wall and CPU time, and no >20% peak RSS regression. This measures formatting work, not whole-pipeline latency or invoiced savings.

Validation completed:
- The new regression fails on the original condition with two formatting invocations instead of one, and passes on the final head.
- All three workflow suites passed in 373.0 seconds on `d653fc737860`. The final follow-up only narrows two test fixture literals; the focused regression and tooling typecheck pass on `80129cd18963`.
- Targeted lint, `pnpm check:workflows`, and oxfmt/Bun parity for the touched files pass on the final head.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `80129cd189635ac54d5b7f98dc0749cc9c48cd78` found no actionable findings.

Five paired samples passed. Combined formatting work: four formatter children → two; all 15 measured invocations succeeded with identical diagnostics.

| Metric | Baseline (two invocations) | Candidate (one invocation) | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median wall | 27.053 s | 12.409 s | -54.1% |
| p95 wall (5 samples) | 30.532 s | 14.607 s | -52.2% |
| Median CPU | 100.61 s | 46.77 s | -53.5% |
| p95 CPU (5 samples) | 113.87 s | 54.89 s | -51.8% |
| Median peak RSS | 235.6 MiB | 266.5 MiB | 13.1% |
| p95 peak RSS (5 samples) | 251.8 MiB | 279.8 MiB | 11.1% |

Wall ranges: baseline 23.573–30.532 s; candidate 11.515–14.607 s. Memory increased but stayed within the predeclared 20% bound. Five samples make p95 the largest observation. The parent CPU profile was dominated by synchronous formatter child execution (10,305 sampled hits in `spawnSync`).

Reproduce with `CI=true pnpm format:check`, serial fresh processes, one excluded warm-up per arm, then five AB pairs (two invocations per A, one per B). Measure each with `/usr/bin/time -f '%U %S %M'`; sum wall/CPU across each arm and take its maximum RSS. Profile: `node --cpu-prof scripts/run-format.mts --check`.

Isolated Boat proof: lease `cbx_a4774b636525`, run `run_cc8e2bc747dcaf126cfd1ba42f3bfb83`, exit 0. Exact-head hosted CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43550957220 (completed; inherited UI failure documented below).

CI attribution: `checks-ui (2/3)` fails `chat model controls > applies model, reasoning, and speed for the session that opened the picker`, expecting `HTMLButtonElement` but receiving a `div`. The identical case and assertion fail on scheduled main run [43546371724](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43546371724/job/132298929515). This is an inherited failure, not green CI. All lint shards and the artifact build passed. All 76 jobs are complete; the only failing jobs are this inherited UI shard and the aggregate CI gate.

prs.title: fix(litellm): LiteLLM proxy chat models are hidden from model lists and refused as not chat
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198581

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with the LiteLLM provider, the chat models the proxy lists are hidden from model lists, and turns on them are refused.

- `openclaw models list --provider litellm --refresh` lists only the plugin's built-in `claude-opus-4-6`, even for a model just set as the default.
- `openclaw agent --model litellm/<model>` fails with "This model doesn't support chat; pick another model." and sends nothing to the proxy.

It started with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198288 (merge `2110db5a1d1c`). With the same proxy, the commit before that merge lists the proxy's chat models and sends the turn.

## User Impact

User impact: LiteLLM models that the proxy lists with `mode: "chat"` are back in model lists and run again. Embedding models and models without `mode` stay out of chat choices.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198288, a discovered row whose id is not a known chat model needs a declared chat capability, or it is kept as not chat. A configured model the proxy lists then inherits that, so it is refused too. LiteLLM declares chat in its own field: each `/v1/models` row has `mode: "chat"`, set from LiteLLM's model map or from `model_info.mode` in the proxy config. The shared discovery does not read `mode`.

The LiteLLM plugin now projects its rows before the shared discovery: a row with `mode: "chat"` gets `capabilities: { chat: true }`, and every row then goes through the shared rules unchanged. This is where `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/model-catalogs.md` puts provider-specific capability fields, as the Anthropic and Baseten projections do. Reading `mode` in the shared discovery instead would change admission for every OpenAI-compatible provider whose rows carry a `mode`, and none of the others was checked.

The LiteLLM provider docs now say which models are chat choices and that a chat deployment the proxy lists without a mode needs `model_info.mode: chat`.

## Evidence

Tested at this PR's head (base `main` `211bc77fff45`).

**Setup:**

- The OpenClaw CLI from source (`pnpm openclaw ...`) on Linux x64. Each run has its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
- A real LiteLLM 1.109.1 proxy (with the proxy extra), bound to 127.0.0.1, with five deployments:
  - `gemini-2.5-flash` (`gemini/gemini-2.5-flash`) and `claude-opus-4-6` (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`);
  - `text-embedding-004` (`gemini/text-embedding-004`);
  - `local-qwen`, OpenAI-compatible, with `model_info.mode: chat`;
  - `local-unlabeled`, OpenAI-compatible, without a mode.
- No provider key was set for the proxy. It lists its models, but it answers every completion with 500 "Missing Gemini API key". **No completion was sent on either side.**
- The proxy's own `GET /v1/models`, one row per line (the same on both sides):

```text
{"id": "gemini-2.5-flash", "object": "model", "created": 1677610602, "owned_by": "openai", "mode": "chat", "max_input_tokens": 1048576, "max_output_tokens": 65536}
{"id": "claude-opus-4-6", "object": "model", "created": 1677610602, "owned_by": "openai", "mode": "chat", "max_input_tokens": 1000000, "max_output_tokens": 128000}
{"id": "text-embedding-004", "object": "model", "created": 1677610602, "owned_by": "openai", "mode": "embedding", "max_input_tokens": 2048}
{"id": "local-qwen", "object": "model", "created": 1677610602, "owned_by": "openai", "mode": "chat"}
{"id": "local-unlabeled", "object": "model", "created": 1677610602, "owned_by": "openai"}
```

- Each run, on both sides:
  1. `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health --auth-choice litellm-api-key --litellm-api-key <proxy key> --custom-base-url http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1`;
  2. `openclaw models set litellm/gemini-2.5-flash`;
  3. `openclaw models list --provider litellm --refresh --json`;
  4. `openclaw agent --local --model litellm/gemini-2.5-flash -m "Say hi"`.
- Every run on both sides also prints "log file append failed" lines. They refer to the default log file outside the isolated state directory.

Before (base `main` `211bc77fff45`). `...` marks omitted lines:

```text
== openclaw models list --provider litellm --refresh --json
Gateway is not running. Refreshing the local model catalog.
...
{
  "count": 1,
  "models": [
    {
      "key": "litellm/claude-opus-4-6",
      "name": "Claude Opus 4.6",
      "input": "text+image",
      "contextWindow": 1000000,
      "local": true,
      "available": true,
      "tags": [
        "configured",

      ]
    }
  ],

    {
      "provider": "litellm",
      "status": "ready"

exit=0
== openclaw agent --local --model litellm/gemini-2.5-flash -m 'Say hi'
...
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=litellm/gemini-2.5-flash candidate=litellm/gemini-2.5-flash reason=format next=none
...
This model doesn't support chat; pick another model.
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.

```

After (this PR), with the same omission marks; the request ids are shortened to `...`:

```text
== openclaw models list --provider litellm --refresh --json
Gateway is not running. Refreshing the local model catalog.
...
{
  "count": 3,
  "models": [
    {
      "key": "litellm/gemini-2.5-flash",
      "name": "gemini-2.5-flash",
      "input": "text",
      "contextWindow": 1048576,
      "local": true,
      "available": true,
      "tags": [
        "default",
        "configured"
      ]
    },
    {
      "key": "litellm/claude-opus-4-6",
      "name": "Claude Opus 4.6",
      "input": "text+image",
      "contextWindow": 1000000,
      "local": true,

      "tags": [
        "configured",

      ]
    },
    {
      "key": "litellm/local-qwen",
      "name": "local-qwen",
      "input": "text",
      "contextWindow": 128000,
      "local": true,
      "available": true,
      "tags": []
    }
  ],
  "providerOutcomes": [
    {
      "provider": "litellm",
      "status": "ready"
    }
  ]
}
exit=0
== openclaw agent --local --model litellm/gemini-2.5-flash -m 'Say hi'
...
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=litellm api=openai-completions model=gemini-2.5-flash status=500 elapsedMs=4284 ...
[provider-error] Model request failed ... provider=litellm model=gemini-2.5-flash name=Error status=500 code=500 type=internal_server_error
...
[agent/embedded] transient retry window elapsed for litellm/gemini-2.5-flash after 6/8 retries; stopping same-model retries
...
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=litellm/gemini-2.5-flash candidate=litellm/gemini-2.5-flash reason=server_error next=none
⚠️ The AI service is having trouble. Please try again in a moment.
...
exit=1
```

The proxy log during the After turn, one of its seven requests:

```text
INFO:     127.0.0.1:<client port> - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
... LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: ... litellm.APIConnectionError: Missing Gemini API key. ...
ValueError: Missing Gemini API key. Set the GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY environment variable.
```

**Observed result:**

- **Base:** `"count": 1`, only the built-in `claude-opus-4-6`. `gemini-2.5-flash`, set as the default one step earlier, and `local-qwen` are missing. The turn is refused with "This model doesn't support chat; pick another model." (`reason=format`), and the proxy logged no `POST /v1/chat/completions` during the run.
- **This PR:** `"count": 3`: `gemini-2.5-flash` (tags `default` and `configured`, context window 1048576 from the proxy's row), `claude-opus-4-6` and `local-qwen`. `text-embedding-004` (`mode: "embedding"`) and `local-unlabeled` (no mode) are not listed. The turn is sent to the proxy: the proxy logged seven `POST /v1/chat/completions` answered 500 for the missing provider key, and OpenClaw ended with "The AI service is having trouble." No completion was sent.
- **Where it started**, same proxy and steps:
  - at `3bf446ef4475`, the commit before the https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198288 merge: `"count": 4` (`gemini-2.5-flash`, `claude-opus-4-6`, `local-qwen` and `local-unlabeled`), and the turn reaches the proxy and gets its 500s;
  - at `2110db5a1d1c`, the merge: `"count": 1` and "This model doesn't support chat; pick another model.".

Full captures:

- Before: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261114-198288-litellm-chat-rows-hidden/before.txt
- After: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261114-198288-litellm-chat-rows-hidden/after.txt
- Proxy log: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261114-198288-litellm-chat-rows-hidden/proxy-log.txt
- Before the merge of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198288: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261114-198288-litellm-chat-rows-hidden/pre198288.txt
- At that merge: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261114-198288-litellm-chat-rows-hidden/at198288.txt

**Checks:**

- `extensions/litellm/index.test.ts` "discovers models from %j at %j" (5 base URL cases): the stubbed `/v1/models` row now has LiteLLM's shape, `{ id: "proxy-model", object: "model", mode: "chat" }`, and the test expects the discovered row not to be marked as not chat. All 5 cases fail on base with `expected [ [ 'proxy-model', false ] ] to deeply equal [ [ 'proxy-model', undefined ] ]` and pass here. The file's other 8 tests pass on both.
- Consumer tests pass: 5 files, 80 tests. They are the LiteLLM plugin tests (`index`, `onboarding`, `image-generation-provider`, `image-generation-provider.url`) and `src/agents/agent-command-local.test.ts`, the only test outside the plugin that names it.
- `pnpm tsgo` passes.
- `pnpm check:changed`:
  - format, lint, typecheck and the repository guards pass;
  - the dead export scan fails on 9 exports in files this PR does not touch, such as `scripts/lib/ios-behavior-grade.mts` (`TELEPORT_PT`). All of them are on base.
- Size against base: production +20/−2 lines in `extensions/litellm/index.ts`, docs +5 lines, test lines net −1.
- The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

Test cost, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local:

| File | Tests | Local wall | Vitest | New or changed test | CI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/litellm/index.test.ts` | 13 | 8.53 s | 6.85 s | 117 ms (5 cases) | not yet run |

Local review: autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, high), base `211bc77fff45` to head `684048e2d1ca`, priority P0–P1. Its context was the shared live-row admission (`src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-normalize.internal.ts`), its public runtime barrel, the Anthropic projection, the configured-model merge (`src/agents/models-config.merge.ts`) and the model catalog docs. Result: scoped-clean, no findings.

<!-- openclaw-preflight:v1
{"v":1,"repo":"openclaw/openclaw","base":"211bc77fff4533cfba01950553c2aeefd486804f","head":"684048e2d1caa718009982722f05ae0b7ebfff0e","tool":{"name":"autoreview","version":"source-a120e048f9fc"},"completion":"complete","summary":"Threshold P1; lower priorities not assessed; status scoped-clean; accepted 0; priority-filtered 0; scope/attribution-rejected 0; missing-required 0. Self-reported; see native report."}
-->

**Not covered:**

- Models the proxy lists without `mode` (an alias LiteLLM's model map does not know, on a deployment without `model_info.mode`) were chat choices before https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198288 (`local-unlabeled` above). They stay out of chat choices, as since that merge; the docs now say to set `model_info.mode: chat` for them.
- Rows with `mode: "completion"` or `mode: "responses"` are not translated and stay out of chat choices; no such deployment was run.
- The model menu of interactive `openclaw onboard --auth-choice litellm-api-key` reads the raw `/v1/models` rows, not the projected ones. It is unchanged and was not run.
- A custom OpenAI-compatible provider pointed at a LiteLLM proxy does not use the LiteLLM plugin and was not run.

prs.title: fix(templates): ClawHub Template Add says the manifest is invalid without saying why
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Adding a published ClawHub Template with an invalid CLAW.md fails with only "Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid.", in the CLI, the Control UI and the Gateway log.

## User Impact

User impact: users and Template publishers now see what is wrong (for example a retired `packages` key or a missing `openclaw.template` selector) and what to change, instead of a reason-free error. Nothing else about the failure changes: same error code, still fails closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest reader already returns specific diagnostics with fix text, but the ClawHub download path dropped them. The error message now carries up to three of them (code, path, message) plus a count of the rest. Reader messages that name a file by its absolute Gateway cache path are rewritten relative to the package root (realpath and link path, longest first), so clients do not see the Gateway host's home directory. Diagnostics can quote publisher-controlled text, so each reported diagnostic goes through `sanitizeTerminalText` before it reaches Gateway RPC clients and the CLI (local and Gateway-owned Add).

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/templates/clawhub-source-artifact.test.ts`: a retired `packages` key is named in the message; an unparsable CLAW.md is named as `CLAW.md` without the cache path, also when the cache root is a symlink whose realpath contains the link path (as `/private/tmp` does `/tmp` on macOS). All fail on origin/main and pass with the fix.
- `src/cli/templates-cli.test.ts` (local Add) and new `src/cli/templates-cli.gateway-add.test.ts` (Add through a running Gateway, real `templates.add.plan` handler): a manifest key containing U+202E and U+009B is named in the error, and neither control character reaches the CLI output. Both fail without the sanitization.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/templates/clawhub-source-artifact.test.ts src/templates/clawhub-source.test.ts`: 58 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: everything passes except the dead export scan, which fails the same way on origin/main in files this PR does not touch.


In a sweep of the 28 third-party ClawHub Templates, 7 failed this way (5 retired format, 2 missing selector) and none of them said why.

### Real CLI runs

Built from source: before = merge-base `82123cd17bd` (main), after = this PR (`91c887117db`). Each run used a fresh isolated state dir with Templates enabled. Mode A has a Gateway running, so the CLI routes the Add through it. Mode B has no Gateway, so the CLI does the Add itself. The state dir path is shortened to `<state dir>`.

**Published Template with a retired `packages` key** (`@etzelm/job-application-coordinator` 0.1.2 on ClawHub)

Mode A, before (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator
Gateway owning <state dir> on local port 19583 could not complete templates.add.plan for Template configuration and provenance: Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid.. The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying. No local fallback was attempted.
```

Mode A, after (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator
Gateway owning <state dir> on local port 19583 could not complete templates.add.plan for Template configuration and provenance: Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid. retired_template_configuration at $.packages: Move native settings into CLAW.md agent and exact ClawHub references into skills/plugins. Use automations for scheduled work; remove packages, profiles, cronJobs, and metadata.openclaw.config; keep schemaVersion: 1.. The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying. No local fallback was attempted.
```

The Gateway log line for the failed `templates.add.plan` carries the same reason after the change.

Mode B, before (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator --acknowledge-clawhub-risk
Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid.
```

Mode B, after (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator --acknowledge-clawhub-risk
Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid. retired_template_configuration at $.packages: Move native settings into CLAW.md agent and exact ClawHub references into skills/plugins. Use automations for scheduled work; remove packages, profiles, cronJobs, and metadata.openclaw.config; keep schemaVersion: 1.
```

In mode B the local Add asks for `--acknowledge-clawhub-risk` before it downloads this release, so the flag is passed in both runs. Nothing was installed.

**Reason text with control characters** (local test package served by a loopback registry stub)

The package's CLAW.md has an unknown key `evil` + ESC `[31m` + `key` + U+202E (right-to-left override) + U+009B (C1 CSI) + `31m`.

Mode A, after (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @acme/demo-agent
Gateway owning <state dir> on local port 19583 could not complete templates.add.plan for Template configuration and provenance: Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid. invalid_manifest at $: Unrecognized key: "evilkey". The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying. No local fallback was attempted.
```

Mode B, after (exit 1):
```
$ openclaw templates add @acme/demo-agent
Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid. invalid_manifest at $: Unrecognized key: "evilkey"
```

A byte check of the captured terminal output and the Gateway log found no ESC, U+202E or U+009B in the reason line. Before this change, both modes stopped at "Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid." with no reason for this package.

The "outcome may be partial" wording in mode A is a separate issue and is not changed here.

prs.title: fix(agents): agents.delete stalls while another agent's model catalog builds
prs.body:
Closes #198543

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `agents.delete` stalls until another agent's model-catalog build finishes, which can take seconds (up to the 180 s catalog budget). Right after Gateway start this pushes the request past the 10 s client timeout, as in the hourly CI failures of `server.config-patch.test.ts`.

## User Impact

User impact: deleting an agent, or re-creating a deleted one, does not wait for unrelated work in the model-catalog worker.

Accepted edge case: a read of the deleted agent's database that is running at the moment of deletion fails with a closed-handle error instead of delaying the delete.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion asks every worker to close the deleted agent's database handles and waits for every answer. On `main`, a worker answers only after its current task, which for the model-catalog worker is usually a catalog build for a different agent. The deleted agent's own database work and catalog runtime are already retired before this step, so these closes don't need to wait.

`serveOwnedWorkerTasks` gets an option for resource keys whose close can skip the running task. Such closes still run after earlier closes, and later tasks still wait for them. `src/infra/worker-task-server.ts` applies it only to deleted-agent closes and revives. Offline-maintenance closes keep waiting, because the running task may hold those handles.

Not covered: the catalog worker blocks its own event loop for a few seconds while it loads plugins synchronously, and a close that arrives in that window waits for the rest of it (see #198543).

## Evidence

[Live Gateway RPC proof with terminal capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198547#issuecomment-6869567912): one completed main-versus-head comparison in a disposable macOS arm64 VM, through `node openclaw.mjs gateway run` and real protocol-v4 WebSocket RPCs.

| | `agents.delete` round trip | Same-ID `agents.create` round trip | Catalog metadata requests pending at the replies |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Main `d2bfdb0d9a52` | 19,415.9 ms | 540.0 ms | 0 / 0 |
| PR `4a3cdf9276d7` | 1,569.8 ms | 562.1 ms | 8 / 8 |

The bundled Ollama provider performed real catalog discovery against a synthetic local metadata endpoint (96 new models, two seconds per metadata response, eight concurrent requests). Both agents were warmed first. On the PR, delete and recreate acknowledged while main's catalog work remained unfinished; its last metadata response arrived 17.163 seconds after recreation. The survivor subsequently published all workload models, and the recreated agent appeared in `agents.list`. The capture includes client timing, pending metadata requests, and Gateway WS response logs. No Gateway or worker source was modified for the run. The VM and synthetic state were destroyed.

Focused regression proof:
- The deleted-agent scheduling regression fails on the base and passes with the fix.
- `src/infra/worker-task-server.test.ts`: 9/9; `packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-server.test.ts`: 4/4; `src/infra/agent-database-readers.test.ts`: 7/7.
- The three targeted agent create/update/delete and large-shrink Gateway tests pass with the fix.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`, and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Independent review covered running handles, revive/close ordering, worker closers, and host-side receipts without finding a concrete defect.

The live comparison does not cover model inference, a real Ollama installation, synchronous plugin-loading stalls, Windows file removal, or offline-maintenance closes. Maintenance serialization remains covered by the focused regression. The exact-head CI run still requires maintainer authorization; the live proof does not replace required CI.

prs.title: fix(pairing): browser pairing command reaches the wrong Gateway when several run on one host
prs.body:
Closes #198462

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the **Pair this browser** page tells you to run `openclaw pair CODE`, which fails with "No browser is waiting for this code" when the page comes from a Gateway running under a named profile and another Gateway runs on the same host.

## User Impact

User impact: a Gateway running under a named profile shows its pairing code with that profile in front, such as `work:ABCD-EFGH`, and a plain `openclaw pair work:ABCD-EFGH` reaches that Gateway without `--profile`. The default profile keeps plain `ABCD-EFGH` codes, and plain codes are still accepted everywhere. While it waits, the pairing screen shows only that command, the waiting status and Cancel.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page cannot know which profile the Gateway runs under, and the command it showed went to whatever profile the shell selected. The Gateway that issues the code knows its profile, so it returns the command with the code as shown (`openclaw pair work:ABCD-EFGH`).

On the CLI side, the profile is chosen by the same early argument parser that handles `--profile`, before config and state paths are fixed. For `openclaw pair`, it reads the profile from the code's prefix:

- The prefix is untrusted routing only. It must be a valid profile name, or the command stops before connecting. A prefix that contradicts `--profile` is refused.
- The prefix is not part of the code. The eight random characters after it are what the Gateway checks, unchanged.
- Before asking, the command prints a **Gateway profile** line, so the operator sees which Gateway they are approving on.
- The code is found the way Commander reads it, so `openclaw pair -- work:ABCD-EFGH` routes (and is checked against `--profile`) like the plain form.
- With a container target (`--container` or `OPENCLAW_CONTAINER`), the host CLI selects no profile from the code: the Gateway's command is `openclaw --container <name> pair work:ABCD-EFGH`, and the CLI inside the container routes the prefix there. Container targeting keeps its precedence over profiles.

The command is the only place the page shows the code, so the CLI asks the operator to approve only if the page in front of them shows that code.

Accepted edge cases, not handled in code: a shell with its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` keeps it even with a prefixed code, the same as with `--profile`. The early parser lists `openclaw pair`'s options to find the code, so a new option with a value needs adding there too.

## Evidence

Two Gateways on one host in a macOS VM (default, and `--profile work`), Control UI in headless Chromium with no token. The page from the `work` Gateway shows the prefixed code:

| Base (`df0d49f58d1`) | This PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Pairing page on the base shows openclaw pair HS4M-5HUZ for a Gateway running under the work profile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/6e5fdb00d3c28ca81d40115402215af316580317/images/2026/11/3d0f9a38-4f62-4beb-9c46-09a148eb342c.png) | ![Pairing page with this PR shows only openclaw pair work:5P95-2KZN, the waiting status and Cancel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e7b26235d382bc717643132c95ac71d226574923/images/2026/11/c0af696c-1e78-4e4a-b093-292c1c324dfe.png) |

Running the command as shown, with no `--profile` and the default Gateway also running:

```
$ openclaw pair work:DU9F-SHKA --yes
A browser is asking to pair with administrator access to this Gateway.

  Gateway profile    work
  Code               DU9F-SHKA
  Address            127.0.0.1
  Page (reported)    http://127.0.0.1:28831
...
Approved. The waiting browser connects by itself.
```

The browser connected by itself, and the new device is listed only on the `work` Gateway (`openclaw --profile work devices list`), not on the default one.

![After approval the browser opens the Control UI chat on the work Gateway](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ae6158daabf67658e2979a5ef7d2fbd469ba72ca/images/2026/11/9dbdf73d-7888-44e8-a851-fc6c1a9947c9.png)

Tests:

- `src/cli/profile.test.ts`: 37/37. The pairing-code cases select `work` from `pair work:ABCD-EFGH` (also after `--yes`, after `--timeout 5000`, and after `--`), leave plain codes, other commands and container targets alone, and refuse an invalid prefix or one contradicting `--profile` (also after `--`). On the base, 8 of them fail.
- `src/cli/run-main.profile-env.test.ts`: 8/8. `openclaw --container demo pair work:ABCD-EFGH` reaches container dispatch without selecting a host profile; on the base it stops with "--container cannot be combined with --profile/--dev".
- `ui/src/components/login-gate-browser-pair.test.ts`: 23/23; on the base the page shows `openclaw pair ABCD-EFGH` instead of the Gateway's command.
- `checks-ui` shards 2 and 3 fail in this PR's CI on chat, model-picker and new-session tests that the PR does not touch. The same tests fail on current `main` without this PR (`draft-submission-title`, `hosted-environment`, `model-control-view`, `chat-pane-session-controls`, `chat-view`, `chat-pane-unmaterialized-settings`) and pass on this branch before the merge with `main`. `checks-ui-e2e` passes.
- `src/cli/pair-cli.test.ts`, `src/cli/run-main.exit.test.ts`, `src/gateway/browser-pair-http.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server.browser-pair.test.ts`: pass.
- Typecheck (core, UI) and format pass; lint reports nothing in the touched files.

prs.title: perf(test): batch legacy agent schema fixture creation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Historical database fixtures repeatedly create the frozen agent schema using per-statement autocommit. This experiment tested batching that setup work.

## User Impact

**Rejected; not for landing.** The matched runs did not establish a repeatable runtime benefit. All 18 existing cases passed in every run; the candidate preserves their isolated databases and assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Batch only the frozen legacy schema seed in the existing synchronous SQLite transaction helper, following the current-schema fixture precedent. Foreign-key configuration, version adjustments, admission and registration remain in order. The source review was clear, but the performance acceptance rule was not met.

## Evidence

Frozen base `3cd6a3ed497469fcce9288b1621df968244c2e7c`; candidate `510c4f235be0a8835e38068e04372761bdaaa496`. One native checkout, identical dependencies and runtime, only the fixture file switched between the two exact versions. Serial command on macOS arm64: `pnpm test -- src/commands/doctor-agent-deletion-journal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Five interleaved pairs; all runs passed 18/18 cases.

| Pair | Baseline wall (s) | Candidate wall (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 85.257 | 60.286 |
| 2 | 58.601 | 81.522 |
| 3 | 94.707 | 62.181 |
| 4 | 118.812 | 146.659 |
| 5 | 133.760 | 139.672 |

Pair 1 is excluded from the matched warm aggregate: baseline compiled workers (24.700s) while candidate reused them. Pairs 2–5 all reported worker-cache hits. Their wall-time medians were **106.760s baseline / 110.597s candidate (+3.59%, slower)**; three of four warm pairs were slower with the candidate. The wide ranges (58.601–133.760s / 62.181–146.659s) prevent a reliable causal speedup claim. The extra 21-case migration proof was not run after performance acceptance failed.

A separate initial cold candidate proof passed 18/18 (94.61s outer test command, including 26.708s worker preparation). Independent review and complete local ClawSweeper review were clear. No broader CI dispatch or testbox lease was created. These are local test runtimes, not Blacksmith billable usage. No savings claimed.

prs.title: fix: plugin revision requested before the final answer is ignored after the run called a tool
prs.body:
Closes #167862 Related: #164355 (quotes the same refusal line), #125531 (earlier attempt, closed by the stale bot), #160297, #140743 ### What Problem This Solves Fixes: a plugin's `before_agent_finalize` `revise` answer is dropped, and core finalizes the draft the plugin rejected, when the run called any tool outside the replay-safe allowlist (`exec`, `write`/`edit`-class tools, plugin tools, session spawns) before the final answer. ### User Impact User impact: plugins that validate or correct final replies through `before_agent_finalize` get their one more model pass on turns that used tools too, as `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` already describes, instead of the rejected draft being finalized (in the deployment where this was observed, the plugin had already replaced that draft with a fallback service message, which then reached the user instead of the corrected reply). No config, SDK or hook-contract change. Risk, stated up front: a revision retry on a tool turn is a model pass over the same transcript; a model could call a tool again despite the retry prompt's "Do not repeat completed work or rerun tools unless the request explicitly requires it". Core never re-executes anything by itself (see Evidence), and the 3-revision ceiling still applies. ### Why This Change Was Made The revise branch of `onBeforeTerminalDelivery` refused the revision whenever `event.hadDeterministicSideEffect` was set. That guard protects against replaying an attempt, but a revision does not replay anything: settlement appends one `leaf` control row to the rejected draft's parent (`attempt-settle.ts`, "Keep persistence append-only while excluding the rejected draft and every trailing descendant from the hidden retry's active branch"), so the tool call and its result stay on the branch, and the retry is a hidden prompt over that branch. #160297 already continues a turn after side effects on the same basis ("a same-prompt follow-up, not a replay or draft rewind"). The change removes only that condition from the revise branch (production: +3/-6). The `hadDeterministicSideEffect` event field and everything that reads the underlying flag stay: incomplete-turn recovery, the compaction-continuation retry, the `abandoned` liveness derivation. The "no persisted assistant entry" refusal and the revision ceiling are unchanged. I left the now-unread event field in place because the lifecycle test pins it as part of the callback's contract; happy to drop it (types, lifecycle handler, test support) in this PR if maintainers prefer. Docs: `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` now states the contract explicitly: the embedded runner honors a revision after tool calls, including side-effecting ones; it rewinds only the rejected draft, completed tool calls and results stay in the transcript and are not replayed; the revision pass is still a normal model turn, so the model can call tools again, and the revision prompt (and the plugin's `reason` / `retry.instruction`) asks it not to repeat completed work. One existing test pinned the old rule: the `side-effecting hook revision` row of the plan-completion policy table in `attempt-plan-completion.test.ts` expected the revision to be refused and to fall through to the plan-completion check (3 model requests). It now expects the revision to be recorded (reason and entry id set, the tool result kept, no completion check: 2 requests). This is the intended behavior change, not a side effect of it. Answer to the review concern on #125531 (the guard "intentionally protects users from unsafe re-execution"): that PR added a `forceRevision` bypass together with step-level checkpoints and rollback, which truncate and redo work. This change adds no bypass flag, no rollback and no new API; it relies on the draft-only rewind core already performs, which is why nothing is re-executed. ### Evidence Where the change was checked, and what was not: 1. **Unit tests, `main@114d443b2f8e`** (the branch sits on `main@432ade6f500d`; the three touched files are byte-identical on both) (sparse tree, Node v24.21.0, pnpm 12.5.1, vitest 5.0.1; `pnpm test` could not be used in a sparse tree, so `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=1` with the repo's own config): - Test changes applied, production change reverted: 1 of 65 fails, the new `honors a revision as a draft-only rewind (hadDeterministicSideEffect: true)` case (since renamed `honors a revision after side effects as a draft-only rewind`): `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { suppressTerminalDelivery: true }`. - With the fix: the two touched files and the neighboring suites that read the same flag, `Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 138 passed (138)`: `attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts`, `embedded-agent-subscribe.before-terminal-delivery.test.ts`, `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts`, `incomplete-turn-recovery.test.ts`, `incomplete-turn-resolution.test.ts`, `attempt-nested-tool-activity.test.ts`. - `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the three touched files clean; `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0. - Not run locally, left to upstream CI (the sparse tree has no `extensions/`): `pnpm build`, `pnpm check`, the full `pnpm test`, and any test under `extensions/`. - Follow-up commit (`ab7d6ce4`: the plan-completion policy row above, the hook docs, the new gate test reduced to its side-effect case, and, in `6ff572f0`, the duplicate ceiling test dropped) was validated by upstream CI only, not re-run in the sparse tree: [job 113934012927](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37963861296/job/113934012927) on `6ff572f0` (`attempt-plan-completion.test.ts` + neighbor, `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 25 passed (25)`, including `preserves side-effecting hook revision policy with 0 completion checks`); `openclaw/ci-gate` green. - New tests: a revision is honored with `hadDeterministicSideEffect` set; a revision without a persisted assistant entry is still ignored with the flag set; the revision ceiling with a tool turn is covered by the existing plan-completion `hook budget exhausted` case; after a real tool run the callback still receives `hadDeterministicSideEffect: true` and the subscription's replay state still reports `hadPotentialSideEffects` (a replay-safe `read` leaves both `false`). The attempt-replay paths that must keep respecting the flag are pinned by existing tests that stay green: `does not retry an empty turn after side effects` and `keeps accumulated deterministic side effects from being marked abandoned`. 2. **Real behavior, on the published `2026.9.2` build**, same one-condition change applied to the dist (the revise branch has the same shape on `main`; this is not a `main` build). Scripted turns `tool call; invalid draft; corrected reply` against a plugin whose `before_agent_finalize` handler returns `revise` for the invalid draft. Stock vs. lifted for the foreground `exec` turn: stock makes 2 model requests (tool call, draft) and finalizes the rejected draft (here as the plugin's fallback message); lifted makes 3 (tool call, draft, revise pass) and delivers the corrected reply once.
Container log lines, stock vs. lifted ``` # stock 2026-10-08T17:06:46.689+00:00 orchestrator-channel: reply revise errorClass=unknown_key attempt=1/2 2026-10-08T17:06:46.742+00:00 [agent/embedded] before_agent_finalize requested revision after potential side effects; finalizing runId=3e43a6ac-b2d5-4a9b-83cf-dbc989605aab sessionId=8e22f1a1-b8f9-42c8-968c-312997d0400b # model requests of the run: 2 (tool call, draft); the rejected draft is finalized (here as the plugin's fallback message) # lifted 2026-10-08T17:03:14.720+00:00 orchestrator-channel: reply revise errorClass=unknown_key attempt=1/2 2026-10-08T17:03:14.869+00:00 [agent/embedded] before_agent_finalize requested one more pass: runId=…f99d sessionId=a2d380cd-2e6f-4fa9-841f-40a5cceb9774 attempt=1/3 # model requests of the run: 3 (tool call, draft, revise pass); the corrected reply is delivered once ```
Transcript rows of the lifted exec turn `ACTIVE` = on the session's active branch; the tool call and result stay active, only the rejected draft and the `leaf` control row are dead. | seq | parent | branch | type / role | |---|---|---|---| | 5 | 4 | ACTIVE | message / assistant (`toolCall:exec(...)`) | | 6 | 5 | ACTIVE | message / toolResult (`(no output)`) | | 7 | 6 | **dead** | message / assistant (the rejected draft) | | 8 | 7 | **dead** | leaf (`rewinds to seq 6`) | | 9 | 6 | ACTIVE | custom_message / `openclaw.runtime-context` | | 10 | 9 | ACTIVE | message / assistant (the corrected reply) |
Matrix: five tools plus a no-tool baseline `exec` foreground appending a line to a file, `schedule_list`, `notification_create`, `sessions_spawn` with its announce run, background `exec` with its exit-event heartbeat run. The side-effect counter read exactly 1 for every tool over the whole session including a `docker restart`; the tool-call and tool-result rows stayed active; the retry request carried the tool call and output and no draft; the next turn's request was byte-identical (sha256 per input item) before and after the restart; the tool-call and output items hash identically in the retry request and both replays (`exec`: `55c021f9c660` / `74643e04a8cd`); the announce and heartbeat runs revised normally.
3. **Not covered, stated plainly:** (a) no run on a build of this PR / `main` (the real-behavior numbers above are `2026.9.2` plus a two-line backport of #140743, which `main` has natively); (b) the corrected reply was scripted, so the runs show that core does not re-execute tools and do not show whether a real model obeys "do not rerun tools" in the retry; (c) `write`, `edit`, `memory_search` were not run (same flag, same tool-independent rewind); (d) one revision per run only, the ceiling was not exercised with tools; (e) everything outside the six files above is covered by upstream CI only (see the "Not run locally" bullet in 1). Full capture set (row listings, request dumps with per-item sha256, side-effect counters, stock control) is available on request; the issue carries the same tables.

prs.title: feat(web-fetch): assess unusable pages with opt-in Decision model
prs.body:
Related: #166688

## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` can return a successful-looking login, access-denied, bot-check, or navigation shell that provides no source material for the user's question.

## User Impact

Default behavior is unchanged. Operators who enable Decision assistance, select a Decision model, and set `tools.web.fetch.decisionQuality: "shadow"` get a page-quality judgment while retaining content. `"apply"` can withhold text at an unusable-page probability of at least 0.90, only when both the fetched result and evaluated excerpt are complete. Unavailable or uncertain judgments retain the page.

A hosted Decision provider may receive a bounded page excerpt and charge for each evaluation. The five-second evaluation deadline is unchanged. The threshold is experimental, not calibrated for production false-drop rates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses the existing Decision runtime after direct/fallback extraction and outside the shared fetch cache. Evaluation includes at most 6,000 characters of wrapped extracted text plus bounded metadata, not request URL/headers or generated private spill locators. The original result remains cached. The owning agent's consent, selected model, mode and invocation authority are checked around inference; cancellation/source loss remains terminal, and accepted usage is completed only for retained judgments. This does not promise cancellation of already-admitted work or exactly-once final tool delivery.

Real opt-in apply and shadow are both preserved. The one additional core config path is intentional; core placement, page-data transfer/cost and experimental withholding policy remain upstream maintainer decisions. `web_search`, page-change monitoring, provider/dependency changes and production activation are out of scope.

## Evidence

### October 26 integration refresh — `a85c0ff8907832ff0138f007f03560130e5f8c63`

Rebased onto `09104d524ce1a89968716367b8691c4081f7397b` for demonstrated conflicts. Preserves upstream #183797's execution-owned fetch/cache/spill closures rather than restoring the retired request parameter bags. Regenerated config baseline is current-main core +1; channel/plugin counts are unchanged. Fourteen other feature files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head. Pre-publication main `31c6d5440b24b91929e9d472d17f652901e7c133` advanced 163 paths with no overlap in the 17 PR paths; merge preview is clean.

- **83 selected tests passed; one unchanged macOS sandbox fixture failed** because it invokes GNU `stat -c` on BSD/macOS. This includes quality/accepted-usage, config, assembly, fallback and prompt-prefix checks. No skip, command shim or weaker assertion; Linux CI remains the platform gate.
- Production and agents-tools test types, scoped type-aware lint, changed-file formatting, generated-config, line-cap and whitespace checks passed.
- **Independent clean-context native integration review: PASS**, no actionable P0–P2 findings; previous full 17-file review remains applicable to unchanged feature bytes. Local AutoReview CLI is unavailable and is not counted as completed review.
- **Exact clean-head runtime build passed** (runtime profile, 1m28.8s), including bundles, built plugin closures and UI. Both runtime stamps identify this clean head.
- **Built Gateway + built CLI agent proof passed all four strict cases**, using actual registered local TypeSafe/Clef inference. A credential-free scripted local agent transport selected the real registered `web_fetch`; this was not `--local` or a helper-only call. Each CLI turn exited 0 and took 4.3–4.7 seconds after Gateway startup.

| Scenario | Unusable probability | Result | CLI exit |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| default-off-junk | not evaluated | original text retained | 0 |
| shadow-junk | 0.9482 | original text retained | 0 |
| apply-junk-short | 0.9515 | withheld; complete marked 200-character recovery notice | 0 |
| apply-useful | 0.0481 | original text retained | 0 |

These are warmed synthetic integration observations, not classifier-accuracy or universal latency measurements. A separate real local model warmup took 6.3s, outside the unchanged five-second evaluation deadline. No credentials, hosted/paid inference, new dependencies or production service/config changes. Isolated proof listeners were stopped.

- Supplemental source registered-provider controls: consent removal and model reassignment retain the page; invocation revocation rejects. Actual transport observations counted **zero provider requests** for all three pre-admission controls. This is source-boundary proof, not built-Gateway capture-stall proof.
- **Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review: pending after publication.** Previous head `20e7790a` completed CI without failures and final hosted review with zero findings/sufficient shipped-entry proof; those results are historical, not coverage of this head.

Author simplification retained the existing schema/assembly seams to bound oversized owners and reused upstream's local character-budget value. Full diff: 17 files; source +348/-96 including mechanical moves, tests +479, docs +41, generated +3/-3. No new policy owner, manager or framework. The full apply contract and distinct consent, truncation, cache, cancellation and accepted-usage regressions remain coherent as one optional consumer.

### Acceptance / rollback

Maintainer acceptance is still required for the core setting, page-data transfer/privacy/cost and experimental 0.90 withholding policy; no merge is implied. A broader independently labelled corpus showing useful-page drops would falsify the threshold's suitability. Historical small development/held-out sets are not a rerun corpus on this refresh.

Unset `tools.web.fetch.decisionQuality` to disable the feature. Original content remains in the fetch cache. AI-assisted implementation/review: yes.

Related: #198510, #198578

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: main CI dependency checks reject a private Stop label and a shared package resolver whose real consumer is omitted from the script audit.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Manual-step Stop/Ready behavior and package-inventory CommonJS resolution stay unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep REQUIRED_ACTION_STOP private to its owner, without changing its value or manual-step behavior. Preserve the genuinely shared resolvePackageDistCommonJs export and include its existing runtime-chunks consumer in the script audit entry/project graph, beside the existing bootstrap consumer. Extend the existing executable-root configuration contract. No ignore, baseline, dummy consumer or broad source glob is added.

## Evidence

- [Natural main run 43546371724, dependency job 132298930665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43546371724/job/132298930665) reports these exact two findings. The other two findings are independently fixed by #198578 and are not duplicated here.
- Complete owner/caller inspection confirms Stop is local-only and the resolver has a real external production consumer. Runtime/declaration/behavior-test bytes are preserved.
- Pinned formatting, syntax and diff checks passed. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues.
- [Exact-head CI 43549881603](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43549881603) passed for `83a23498de9c5143b86c1f40b5072711e1a616c0` through merge checkout `2f93ec9f4c2045928aa53f56fa40880d61ab0d76`. Actual logs prove 15 normalization cases and 35 ask-user cases passed, including Ready/Stop/cancel/expiry/pending handling.
- [Deadcode configuration regression job 132310119749](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43549881603/job/132310119749) executed all 31 cases successfully, including “keeps the script unused-export scan scoped to real executable roots,” which requires both bootstrap consumers in entry and project.
- Gaps: local named tests, scoped lint and typecheck were unavailable in the sparse implementation checkout. The successful PR run admitted no full dependency/Knip scan; an after-fix green script export graph is unproven. Natural-main dependency qualification remains separate from merge.

Contributor credit: @obviyus and @steipete.

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. A fresh bundled no-op or forced override cannot stand in for the original bug. The 56 owner declarations do not directly cover `install(target:)` success/compatibility-failure selection paths. The published discovery regression now asserts persistence from initially unset keys before inspection, but its new assertions still need native execution; the historical 56-declaration run predates them.
- **Existing-state upgrade:** A disposable latest-stable-to-candidate app upgrade with existing settings/data retained remains unrun. No preference/schema format changed, and source review found no data-model incompatibility; the missing upgrade run is a proof gap, not an established migration defect.
- **Current composition:** The fixtures emit `v24.22.1`, which satisfies the current runtime requirement; the 24 October change addressed the higher minimum inspected at that time. This two-line fixture-only repair is published at `4298606`; native execution of the current composition remains unverified. This does not relabel the pinned original-head result or establish a production incompatibility.

### Retained real coexisting-installation proof

[Run 37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616) compared earlier product `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b` with baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9`, governed by corrected QA workflow `b166bce6b7ee4fc86631cb491fd7c17990be6362`. The candidate preserved external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset: one native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The baseline failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected other failures.

Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations with verified published SHA-512 integrity on disposable hosted macOS runners. Cleanup, preference/environment restoration, and pristine-source checks passed. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain selection cells, installation identities, logs, and strict verification summaries. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. Previously reported formatting, whitespace checks, and scoped Codex AutoReview remain historical proof, not a fresh review of the current head.

</details>

Maintainer review remains separate. The fixture-only follow-up changed no production source. The current head also includes the 2 November main merge. Swift owner tests, real installation, and app upgrade remain unverified for the current head; skipped CI lanes do not supply that proof.

prs.title: improve(ios): polish native chat, floating composer, and sidebar
prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. Current synthetic screenshots show keyboard-visible content and preservation of the reader’s position: | Typing | Reading older history | | --- | --- | | | | Original before/after layout comparison: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | These original layout captures use synthetic data on the same simulator. The baseline fixture’s model label was normalized for publication; its layout is unchanged. Physical-device, iPad, largest Dynamic Type, and macOS visual comparisons remain unverified. Shared macOS compilation and chat tests are covered. Maintainer product acceptance of the floating composer and placement of advanced controls is still pending.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: feat: failed updates offer a prompt for source repair
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A failed Gateway update shows a report, but offers no way to hand that evidence and a safe source repair task to a coding agent.

## User Impact

Users can copy a prompt that asks an agent to determine whether the update guard was correct or the updater is defective, preserve the installed service, and open a source pull request for a verified defect. The action appears on unreconciled Gateway-managed failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompt includes redacted, bounded installed and requested version identities before the bounded update report. It redacts source fields before the report shortens diagnostics, so a cut-off private key cannot evade masking. Clipboard feedback uses the existing shared copy behavior.

Main has since ported the update run view to Solid and now shows a failed run the Gateway has moved past as history without recovery actions. This branch merges main (no rebase) and follows both: the action lives in `update-run-view.tsx`, and it is hidden for historical runs, just as Retry update is. It also stays hidden for acknowledged abandoned runs and OCM-managed installs. Copying never retries the update.

## Evidence

Current head `96d082d4e0c` (merge of main `6d7a74ecd3f`):

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/update-run-view.test.ts ui/src/app/update-confirmation.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 2 files, 53 tests passed, 13 s wall time. The update view file has 15 tests; the repair-prompt cases cover identities ahead of early-failure diagnostics, token redaction, complete and truncated PEM masking, eligibility (succeeded, OCM, acknowledged abandoned, historical vs. current serving), and feedback that survives a same-revision refresh but clears for a newer revision. Removing the historical guard makes the eligibility test fail.
- `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/update-run.e2e.test.ts` (mocked Gateway, Chromium): 6 tests passed, 87 s wall time including the UI build. The repair-prompt flow took 2.26 s. It reads the clipboard after the click and checks that `update.run` was requested only once. The four saved-failure projection cases now also check that Copy agent prompt appears only when Retry update does.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` (all 8 shards) passed. `oxfmt --check`, oxlint on the touched files, stylelint on `update-run-view.css`, and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed.
- Not run: the full suite and `check:changed`. CI on this head is the remaining gate.

Earlier head `69d504dfc25`: 31 focused tests passed, and the browser flow passed in 74.52 s. ClawSweeper accepted the screenshot proof on that head.

The before capture is the user's real failed update dialog, which has no repair action. The after captures are from this head's mocked-Gateway browser run, with the dialog rendered by the Solid view. They do not prove a repair of the user's live upgrade.

**Before — user's failed update dialog**

**After — desktop (head 96d082d4e0c)**

![Failed update dialog with Copy agent prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4adf2d7c-f009-415f-909b-78189f8d2e09)

prs.title: improve(browser): show the agent a Browser panel note only during take-over
prs.body:
Closes #198449

## What Problem This Solves

Take-over (#197928) is opt-in by design. The operator-control module states its own contract: "Nothing changes until someone clicks Take control in the Browser panel", and #197928 promised users "Nothing changes for anyone who doesn't click the new button. Agents keep using the browser exactly as before."

The 60-second recent-use note breaks that contract. Any click or keypress in the Control UI Browser panel, with no take-over, changes what the agent receives: its browser results for the next minute carry "the user used this browser from the Browser panel N seconds ago… Check the page before acting on it." A user who only looks at or uses the panel, and never opts into take-over, still changes the agent's tool results and the text added to its context.

## User Impact

Using the Browser panel without taking control leaves the agent's browser results exactly as they are without the panel. While the user holds control, the agent still gets the take-over note on results it can still get (snapshots, screenshots), and actions still answer `user_has_control`. Take control stays the one way for a user to signal the agent that they are in the browser.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser tool adds a note only while someone holds take-over control of that browser, so the opt-in contract holds for every result. The last-input time that only fed the 60-second note is removed. Marked panel input still restarts the 5-minute idle timer of a held take-over. The Browser panel docs no longer describe the recent-use note.

## Evidence

Tests in `browser-tool.operator-control.test.ts`, through the real `browser` tool against a host browser's operator-control state:
- After panel input without take-over, an agent `act` result carries no note. This test fails on `main` (the result contains the Browser panel note) and passes with the fix.
- During take-over, a `snapshot` result ends with the take-over note, and `act` and `stop` answer `user_has_control`.

Suites run: the operator-control tool and route tests and `browser-tool.test.ts`, 105 passed. Typecheck of the extensions and their tests, lint and format of the changed files, and the assertion-safety check pass.

Live Gateway, Control UI, and real-model proof on `d0bf21a45656901fb6aa0e50e53eb50bc632fbf0`: [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198454#issuecomment-6869218602). Both cases ran in one macOS 26.6.2 VM Gateway process and agent session, with a synthetic local page. I checked the browser tool messages sent back to the model.

Without Take control, a panel click followed by the agent's click changed the count from 1 to 2. All three browser results carried no panel-use note; the last reached the model 7.213 seconds after panel input.

![Ordinary panel input: agent action succeeds without a Browser panel note](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/068f28329ddae1f1052dd01911faedbbba21d6ba/images/2026/11/09cf973d-70e5-42fe-b357-81918a6aff76.png)
