prs.title: feat(talk): configure GPT-Live launch acknowledgments
prs.body:
Related: #117898

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who want a consistent, short GPT-Live Talk acknowledgment cannot select its exact wording without patching the OpenAI plugin.

## User Impact

Set `talk.realtime.providers.openai.acknowledgement` to a fixed phrase such as `One moment.` for Gateway-owned GPT-Live delegation, on browser WebRTC and Gateway-relay calls. No setting is required: the natural, varied default introduced in #175603 is unchanged.

An unset or blank value keeps that natural default; blank does not disable speech. Changes apply to new Talk sessions. GA Realtime, native speech/TTS fallback, status/cancellation replies, and the final answer are unchanged. A launch acknowledgment is not proof that the task was accepted or started.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI plugin normalizes the optional provider setting and passes it through both transports to their shared delegation controller. An explicit phrase uses the existing exact-status speech helper; otherwise the existing natural acknowledgment instructions remain intact. No new core configuration field, SDK surface, or client-specific setting is added.

The older request in #117898 was closed because generic realtime instructions could customize the then-current consult guidance. This change targets the newer GPT-Live host-generated launch note, which explicitly instructs natural wording, rather than relying on competing general instructions to select an exact phrase.

## Evidence

- The two new transport regressions fail on base `2f6061c9bc760d2137ac1dd7abc3a11a2d613220` at the configured-phrase assertion: the provider receives the natural default instead of the requested phrase.
- All four focused test files pass after the change: **89 tests**, covering browser offers, relay connection, delegation, and relay lifecycle. The new cases cover custom phrases, quoted text, trimming, blank/default behavior, and successive sessions. Local test duration: **12.78s** (wrapper wall time **14.68s**); CI timing is not yet available.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Targeted type-aware lint passes for the seven changed TypeScript files; the OpenAI package-boundary typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/openai/tsconfig.json`) also passes, including freshly generated SDK boundary declarations.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local patch at P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The reviewer assessed the diff; execution evidence comes from the focused tests above.
- Simplification pass: retained one policy owner and existing speech/default helpers; no new helper or state machinery. Diff: 14 production lines added / 1 removed, 126 test lines, and 32 documentation lines.
- Physical-device audio acceptance has not been performed for this upstream candidate. Tests verify the emitted provider messages, not audible delivery.
- [Upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43520524277) is attached to head `d71f1155c96cfdc6482acf9f854919a9c869fa1c`, but GitHub currently reports `action_required` before any jobs start. Hosted CI is not claimed passed.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): reset owner access on the claw's computer
prs.body:
Related: OCF-319 (Linear)

## What Problem This Solves

An owner whose recovery kit is lost or leaked, or who no longer controls the claw remotely, has no way to take ownership back short of relinking the claw as a new claw.

## User Impact

On the computer that runs the claw, the owner can now **Reset owner access** (Settings → OpenClaw ID, or `openclaw id reset`, which also works with the Gateway stopped). It makes a new recovery kit, shows it once, and removes every owner device, person, node and invite; remote sessions close and tunnel-issued sign-ins are revoked. Local access, the claw id, address, connection keys (K_srv, K_gw) and all claw data stay, and the membership seq keeps counting up. The old kit stops working.

**Not usable end to end yet:** the deployed Discovery still refuses any root change (see Dependencies), so a reset applies locally but its publication is refused until Discovery accepts `RootReset`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implements the revised OCF-319 design on top of the protocol from #193777 (`RootReset`, `verifyRootReset`, descriptor `reset` evidence); the old remote RootRotation/epoch/freeze design is not brought back.

- **Gateway:** `openclawId.authority` `reset_prepare` / `reset_commit`, `local_operator` only (tunnel and other channels: `not_local_operator`, from the existing connection classification, not headers). The new root R' signs binding_seq + 1 with the same hostname, K_srv and K_gw; the Gateway signs `RootReset` with the current K_gw and publishes both in the descriptor's `reset` (no link code needed, same K_gw). Removal reuses the existing effects: capture/close connections, cancel member runs, revoke tunnel-bound tokens, drop node pairings, push the empty admission list.
- **CLI:** `openclaw id reset` routes through the running Gateway (bound to its state owner via `expectedOwnerId`) or, with the Gateway stopped, edits the claw record under the Gateway lock and signs the RootReset with the bound K_gw (publication then happens at the next start). Interactive only (typed claw name; the kit never reaches argv, JSON or logs). An uncertain outcome still prints the kit and exits 2.
- **Control UI:** new **Settings → OpenClaw ID** page (address, Discovery state, links to Your devices and People, Move to new keys, and a separate Reset owner access section). Reset needs the claw's short name typed, then shows the new kit in the existing recovery-kit presentation; only after "I've saved it" does R' sign and the Gateway commit. The resetting browser becomes the first owner device under the new root (decision 3 of 2026-11-05).
- **Placement (confirmed by Josh, 2026-11-13):** over the tunnel or any non-local connection the page shows the single line "Reset owner access is only available on the computer that runs this claw." instead of the button. This intentionally departs from OCF-319's "the UI doesn't show it"; the Gateway still refuses remotely. Existing account-menu items are unchanged; the menu gains only an **OpenClaw ID settings** link.
- **Ordering guards:** a reset is refused while a move to new keys is unpublished (`rebind_unpublished`), and a move or a second reset is refused while a reset is unpublished (`reset_unpublished`), because Discovery accepts a root change only from the exact binding it stores, and a descriptor can land before its snapshot fails.
- The recovery-kit-used notice now points to Reset owner access instead of relinking. Docs: `docs/cli/id.md`, `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md`.

Out of scope, follow-up: **OCF-334** (human-presence check before reset).

## Dependencies

- **Discovery (blocking end-to-end):** `openclaw/discovery` main (e57e741, 2026-11-13) `checkRepublish` pins the stored root without a K_gw and never calls `checkDescriptorRootReset`; its test "refuses a root change even with valid owner reset evidence" asserts the refusal. Discovery must adopt `checkDescriptorRootReset` (discovery.md "Owner reset") before a reset publishes. Not changed here.
- **claw-loader:** main maps `owner_reset` to the generic "can't verify" state; it does not yet show "The owner reset access to this claw. Set up this browser again." with re-enrollment.

## Evidence

Screenshots (mocked Gateway, synthetic data; the page is new, so there is no "before" state; the URL previously fell through to chat):

Local, on the claw's computer:
![Settings → OpenClaw ID on the claw's computer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd8eee45-846a-4561-9625-9bc50ca203be)

Over the tunnel:
![Settings → OpenClaw ID over the tunnel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0e91bf1-7be6-444f-99bd-c3cbbb0f907d)

Typed confirmation:
![Reset confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e385e8e-90e5-4d76-95d3-2cdb859d7eab)

New kit shown once before the reset:
![New recovery kit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c81e6b0e-433d-470c-a16a-520818bec476)

Checks run locally:
- `src/gateway/openclaw-id/owner-reset.test.ts`: tunnel/no-channel refusal; every removal (owner devices, members, nodes, invites, sessions closed, runs cancelled, tunnel tokens revoked, node pairings removed, empty admission); kept claw id, hostname, K_srv, K_gw, Discovery account; seq + 1; RootReset verifies with `verifyRootReset`, Discovery's `checkDescriptorRootReset` and a pinned browser's `verifyBindingForPin` (`owner_reset`), while a forged RootReset gets `root_mismatch`/refused; browser enrollment under R'; old root, stale binding and other keys refused with no change; reset/re-bind ordering guards.
- `src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-reset.test.ts`: real Gateway over loopback resets and publishes one K_gw-signed descriptor with the reset evidence and no code, then the snapshot; a relayed client is refused before the service; `openclaw id reset` with the Gateway stopped edits local state under the lock and prints the kit once.
- Re-ran `src/gateway/openclaw-id/**`, re-bind e2e and `id-cli` tests: 61 files / 385 tests pass.
- UI: `openclaw-id-page.test.tsx` (button present locally, single line and no button over the tunnel, nothing requested with Labs off), account-menu tests, and `ui/src/e2e/openclaw-id-reset.e2e.test.ts` (bundled build: full reset flow commits only after the kit is saved; tunnel shows no button).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap ratchet, `check:control-ui-controllers`, `ui:i18n:verify`.
- Independent review (separate model) found one P2: a second reset after a partial publication could chain to a binding Discovery no longer stores. Fixed by refusing a new reset until the previous one is confirmed published.

Gaps:
- No staging end-to-end yet (pinned browser re-enrolls with the new kit; forged root change refused): blocked on the Discovery change above and needs explicit approval before using staging.
- `pnpm ui:build` reports boot/CSS budget overruns on this host; the base commit (9156de83fa53) built on the same host reports the same overruns (chat boot 1284.4 KiB vs 1284.0 here, new boot 799.3 vs 799.0), so they are not from this PR.

prs.title: fix(plugins): persist native receipts during catalog discovery
prs.body:
Related: #177882 (the source-receipt warning only; this does not close the separate memory-search report).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing plugin source-admission receipts when model-catalog discovery captures native companion files. Catalog refresh can succeed while logging `Plugin source receipt was not recorded: SqliteWorkerError: Shared-state admission requires the host broker` and leaving the receipt absent.

## User Impact

Catalog refresh records captured native artifacts through the existing shared-state owner. Receipt-write failures remain advisory, and discovery keeps its existing deadline. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native capture in the catalog compute worker constructed a direct publisher without a host delegate. Shared-state admission correctly rejects that worker's attempt to acquire the host broker.

The catalog pool now retains the existing host publisher and accepts publication through its task channel. Retained artifacts use the current task's channel; exchanges are serialized and writes are joined before task completion. Advisory exchanges preserve the current deadline while retaining the existing numeric `timeoutMs` contract. Native roots are committed only after the writer accepts the receipt.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway comparison:** isolated Linux profiles with fresh HOME/state/config/workspace, loopback ports, and a synthetic local plugin. Two fresh `models.list(refresh:true)` calls returned the initial catalog and then the changed dynamic model in both variants.

| Observation | Original main | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Successful fresh catalog calls | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| Host-broker receipt warnings | 1 | 0 |
| Persisted source-admission receipts | 0 | 1 |
| Captured synthetic artifacts recorded | 0 | 33 |

After shutdown, a read-only database inspection verified the receipt and all 33 captured-file SHA-256 hashes. These are captured synthetic artifacts; no native binary execution or model inference was used. Both Gateway processes were joined cleanly. Historical heartbeat ownership loss and physical sleep/wake behavior are outside this change.

**Regression and static checks:**

- All three new cases fail against unchanged base `a1083027deecf9ba0fd4f833cb8b984308300fad`: two missing durable-receipt cases and the advisory-exchange deadline case.
- **62 tests passed across six files**, covering initial and retained lazy capture, a one-time receipt-write failure, pool reuse/retirement, native custody, and discovery deadlines. The command completed in 212 seconds including worker preparation.
- The final native integration suite was repeated after lint repairs: **8/8 passed** (a repeat of existing coverage, not eight additional unique tests); file duration 57.7 seconds, command duration 102.4 seconds. The new persistence cases compose the real compute worker, native capture, and SQLite writer because a mocked publisher cannot prove durable receipts across retained module lifetimes; the deadline test uses a fake clock.
- Production, agent-test, and package-test typechecks passed. Targeted lint reported zero warnings/errors; formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Source CLI build and real Gateway startup succeeded.
- Local Codex autoreview, **P0–P2**, found no actionable findings across the complete eight-file patch against the pinned base. Reviewed patch SHA-256: `664f877d0cc17ad620dcda04d46f0f38e11b2625f07b3f0aef19ebde04d2c8f9`. The reviewer inspected source and reported evidence; it did not execute project code.
- PR CI is awaiting maintainer approval ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43543893853)). GitHub reports `action_required`, with zero jobs started.

<details>
<summary>Focused test command</summary>

```sh
CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.native.integration.test.ts \
  src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.pool.integration.test.ts \
  src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.reuse.integration.test.ts \
  src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.retirement.integration.test.ts \
  src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.admission.test.ts \
  packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-pool.bootstrap.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

prs.title: feat: open ClawHub catalog reviews in desktop apps
prs.body:
Closes #198569

## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub catalog links cannot currently open the matching plugin, skill, or published Template review in the desktop companion.

## User Impact

Users can open a catalog item in their selected Gateway, then make the existing explicit installation/Add decision there. Opening a URL never installs or enables code, selects a Gateway, supplies authentication, enables Labs, or creates an agent. Skill review retains agent selection; Template review retains Labs and Add consent.

**Platform limits:** macOS handoff is proven; shared Tauri source is only parser/URL-builder qualified, not Linux/Windows OS dispatch or live installation qualification. Full Tauri compilation was blocked by the offline cache missing locked `mdns-sd 0.21.6` (0.21.5 cached), with no dependency/lock changes. Separate native Windows Hub is unchanged/unverified. Cold-start Tauri links require connecting a ready main-window Gateway and reopening the link.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add identity-only adapters for `openclaw://{plugins,skills,templates}/install?name=<encoded identity>` and reuse the existing dashboard navigation owners. Validate one bounded package identity, reject external commands/Gateway/authentication parameters, and retain the selected Gateway base path and trusted auth session. Tauri receives normalized URLs, so raw empty-userinfo/dot-segment spellings are not always available; decoded package traversal remains rejected.

Simplification: the old dashboard-only inline Tauri parser/test moves into the single adapter; no new installation owner, state store, dependency, URL registration, or settings UI. Necessary growth covers the three family mappings and authority/identity regressions (whole change: +565/-39 lines including tests/docs/generated source inventory). A Clippy boolean simplification was applied and revalidated. Required native-source inventory was regenerated with the repository command (one source row; no locale/translation-memory edits).

## Evidence

Before first push, Patrick was shown inspected real browser/native screenshots and approved landing with these qualification limits. This PR changes navigation, not rendered UI appearance; the companion ClawHub PR owns the CTA/layout changes. Existing isolated proof is reused; no new installation was performed for publication.

- **Before → after, real macOS:** browser CTA previously had no native catalog review route; the new link opened the matching Hello World review with Install still awaiting consent. Only an explicit click then installed **and enabled** `openclaw-hello-world@0.1.0`. Final native UI and explicitly port-scoped Gateway RPC confirmed installed/enabled. Existing TypeBox runtime/provenance warnings remained; this is not warning-free runtime/provenance qualification.
- **Review-only siblings:** `@steipete/weather` opened the Weather skill review with Install awaiting consent; `@donniefi/hopper` opened the published Hopper Template with files and bundled items and Add awaiting consent. Neither was installed/added.
- Six sandboxed macOS parser/navigation XCTest cases passed (0 failures), including exact scoped identity, invalid-link rejection, trusted Gateway base path and fragment preservation. Swift build passed; isolated signed task app startup/handoffs passed after using the existing SwiftPM resource-lookup packaging helper. Normal installed app/config and default handler were preserved.
- Six tests importing the actual Tauri production parser/URL builder pass offline. Regression proof initially caught trusted-fragment loss (4 pass/2 fail), then all 6 passed. Re-run on the published source: 6/6 pass; offline Clippy `--tests -- -D warnings` passes; Rustfmt (edition 2021) passes. These do **not** compile the Tauri integration/application.
- Targeted SwiftFormat: 0/3 files need formatting; targeted SwiftLint passes; native i18n verification and normal commit hook pass; `git diff --check` passes. Shared Control UI review regression evidence: 85 tests pass; original plugin consent-routing regression: 3 pass.
- Local `pnpm check:changed` broad app checks are not claimed complete; exact-head PR CI remains the broad gate.
- Patrick-selected automated review route: hosted ClawSweeper only (no duplicate autoreview); review findings and exact-head CI will be reconciled before native landing.

No private configs/state, generated binaries, screenshots, or proof archives are committed. No installed-app replacement, normal URL-handler/config changes, shared restart, or dependency changes.


## Review repair and exact proof limits

ClawSweeper's review of `3a5fd51f30afe69cb39cf9defbd536362dc904d2` identified one actionable P2: denied OS notification permission hid the Tauri cold-start recovery instruction. Commit `0d1615d81ef7512127730016cab5432c215bfacc` routes this error through the existing in-window notice owner instead. This is a two-line repair; no new error/state owner or permission request.

A temporary Rust caller probe compiles the production handle_deep_links body and real production URL parser, with desktop I/O simulated: Gateway-not-ready returns the existing recovery instruction and OS notification delivery is denied. Independent expected output is a notice addressed to the focused main window for each catalog family.

```text
Before (3a5fd51f30af):
FAILED: plugins: focused window received no recovery instruction
left: []
right: [(main, Connect to a Gateway in the main window, then open the ClawHub link again.)]

After (0d1615d81ef7):
unavailable_gateway_has_visible_recovery_without_os_notifications ... ok
All three families checked. Existing production parser tests: 6 passed, 0 failed.
Rustfmt edition 2021 (changed modules, skip_children=true): pass
git diff --check: pass
```

This probe verifies caller dispatch, **not** a real WebView/OS notification-denial interaction. No permanent source-string or mock-echo test was added: the live Tauri notice seam needs a desktop/WebView. Full local compilation remains unavailable under the documented offline cache limit. Prior-head hosted Linux companion build and macOS companion tests passed, but those results do not qualify this repaired head; fresh PR CI is required. Windows packaging was still running at the last prior-head observation. Linux/Windows OS-link dispatch/live installation and separate Windows Hub remain unverified.

The earlier macOS runtime captures were inspected and shown privately before Patrick authorized landing; they are not publicly attached here. Those described handoffs are therefore not independently inspectable public media proof. This PR makes no rendered appearance changes, and no new live Tauri/macOS install or broader platform claim is added by this repair.


## Landing status — current head

Reviewed/prepared head: `0d1615d81ef7512127730016cab5432c215bfacc`. [ClawSweeper revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198571#issuecomment-6870034743) confirms the earlier P2 repaired, with no remaining actionable code findings; public runtime-proof limitations remain above. Thread-aware read found no inline review threads.

- Required Actions and combined CI/security gate passed: [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43545514237), [combined publisher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43546066962).
- Current-head Linux companion build and macOS companion tests passed: [platform workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43545513993). Windows installer build remains in progress at this observation; this is not Windows handoff/install qualification.
- Non-required [Intersect shared OpenClawKit dead code](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43545514108/job/132303819397) failed on public struct OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccountError, at apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccount.swift:227. The type/file exists at main baseline de0ea1efe5f9, is absent from this PR head, and is outside all nine changed paths. This is an inherited shared-library report, not a catalog-adapter failure.
- Native preparation and review validation passed. Native merge admission stopped **before dispatch** on MERGEABLE/UNSTABLE: its rollup guard requires GREEN, including this non-required report. No merge request/outcome was recorded. The native inherited-failure validator currently supports the primary ci.yml failure route and the specific optional build-artifact workflow, not this Periphery report; no exception evidence or green result has been fabricated, and no raw merge/guard bypass attempted.

Landing remains blocked on an authorized supported native route for this non-required inherited report (or its baseline-owner resolution and resulting qualification). No unrelated source repair, dependency change, or speculative rebase was made to chase green.

prs.title: fix: preserve Claude resume with a child-only config directory
prs.body:
Fixes #198402

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Claude starting a fresh conversation after a cold turn when a selected skill supplies `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only to the Claude child process.

## User Impact

Local Claude sessions keep their native session ID and resume from the child-selected transcript root, including after process restart. Gateway-level configuration and the default `~/.claude` root retain their behavior; genuinely missing transcripts and orphaned tool calls still invalidate resume. No new configuration, migration, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transcript probes previously read the Gateway environment before skill overrides were applied. Reuse the existing skill-aware child-environment composition from native-login preparation, pass its result explicitly to transcript resolution, and use it for preparation and final binding-flush checks.

The command layer no longer repeats an ambient transcript probe. It clears a binding only when the runner reports the prepared missing-transcript decision, retaining the expected-session-ID guard. Validation remains enabled. The existing native-login helper is moved, not duplicated; none of the broader machinery from #145895 is restored.

Read-side follow-ups remain outside this fix: `src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-pages.ts` (history-worker context: #198337), and `src/commands/doctor-claude-cli.ts`.

## Evidence

- Pinned base: `e6c7c5e0da4b2407e2d991a00c5d38b599e05050`.
- Candidate: `c42a20af1e5324ba80fa4f0b0de140a5684c3530`; tree `90cdb8e40daa1a9ae99faa8b4e988c2568958400`.
- The final five-case regression and core-test typecheck were rerun after a test-only generator-method shorthand lint correction; production inputs remained identical.
- RED: the final two skill-only regressions fail against the pinned production base (exit 1, 56.58 s wall): preparation reports `missing-transcript`, and the command layer clears the stored binding before execution. An earlier five-case baseline run also confirmed the orphaned case incorrectly reports `missing-transcript`; Gateway/default/missing controls passed.
- GREEN: the same two final regressions pass with the candidate production changes (exit 0, 59.76 s wall).
- GREEN: real preparation, transcript reads, execution argument composition, and runner settlement are exercised with a synthetic external CLI execution callback. The skill-root case retains the binding and sends `--resume` with the stored ID. Gateway, default-root, genuinely missing, and orphaned controls are covered. This is integration-test evidence, not a real Gateway/Claude run.
- Command persistence regression checks that the skill-only root does not cause an early binding clear.
- Required command/prepare suites: **229 passed**, exit 0 (104.43 s wall).
- Required spawn/native-history suites plus settlement and prompt-prefix coverage: **117 passed**, exit 0 (83.93 s wall).

A controlled `claude` stub on `PATH` (npm-style `claude.cmd` shim → `cli.js`) speaks the same initialize/user/result stream-json protocol as `test/helpers/claude-cli-native-spawn-proof.ts`. prs.title: fix(templates): Template Add fails on MCP servers that declare a timeout
prs.body:
Closes #198536

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw templates add` fails after the agent is already created when the Template's `CLAW.md` sets `timeout` or `connectTimeout` on an MCP server.

## User Impact

A Template that declares an MCP timeout now adds completely: the server is saved with `requestTimeoutMs` / `connectionTimeoutMs`, and the Template's automations are scheduled. A server that already exists with the same timeouts in milliseconds is reused instead of being reported as a conflict.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CLAW.md` takes the two timeouts in seconds, under the names OpenClaw config no longer accepts. Add now converts them at the Template MCP boundary with the existing `migrateLegacyConfiguredMcpServer`, both for the config write and for the digest that decides whether a declared server matches a configured one. The manifest schema, the Add review, and the config writer's validation are unchanged. `docs/cli/templates.md` now states the unit.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

- `src/templates/schema.ts:351-355` accepts `timeout` and `connectTimeout` (added with the manifest schema in #101328).
- `src/templates/mcp.ts` passed the declaration to `setConfiguredMcpServer` unchanged, and `src/config/zod-schema.mcp-server.ts:76-91` rejects both keys. Add installs MCP servers after the agent is committed (`src/templates/add-stateless.ts:665`), so the result is `partial` and automations are skipped.
- `digestTemplateMcpServer` used `canonicalizeConfiguredMcpServer`, which does not touch the timeout keys, so `timeout: 30` never matched a configured `requestTimeoutMs: 30000`.
- Seconds is the unit the rest of OpenClaw uses for these names: `openclaw mcp configure --timeout <seconds>` (`src/cli/mcp-cli.ts:157-167`) and the config migration (`src/config/mcp-config-normalize.ts:140`).

</details>

## Evidence

Built `main` (211bc77) and this branch with Node 24.22.1 and ran the offline CLI (`pnpm openclaw`) with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. A local mock OpenAI-compatible server answers Add's opening turn. The Template declares one MCP server with `timeout: 30` and `connectTimeout: 5`, and one automation. `<run>` is the isolated run directory; output is trimmed to the relevant lines.

- Main: `templates validate` passes, `templates add` exits 1 with the config error, the agent is listed, no MCP server is saved and no automation is created.
- Main, server already configured with `requestTimeoutMs: 30000` and `connectionTimeoutMs: 5000`: Add stops with `mcp_server_collision`.
- Main control, same Template without the two timeout keys: Add exits 0.
- This branch, same three runs: all exit 0. The server is saved with `requestTimeoutMs: 30000` and `connectionTimeoutMs: 5000`, the pre-configured server is left as it was, and `Automation created: Daily summary.` is printed each time.

<details>
<summary>Main (211bc77)</summary>

```
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Valid Template project: <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Package: mcptimeout@0.1.0
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Ready.
Added agent: mcptimeout
Workspace: <run>/state/workspace-mcptimeout
Config invalid after MCP set (mcp.servers.s: Unrecognized key: "connectTimeout"). The agent was already made available and was kept. Continue setup in this agent; do not add another copy.
[exit 1]
$ openclaw mcp list
No OpenClaw-managed MCP servers configured in <run>/state/openclaw.json. Add one with openclaw mcp set <name> '{"command":"uvx","args":["context7-mcp"]}'.
[exit 0]
```

Server already configured in milliseconds:

```
$ openclaw mcp set s {"command":"node","args":["s.js"],"requestTimeoutMs":30000,"connectionTimeoutMs":5000}
Saved MCP server "s" to <run>/state/openclaw.json.
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR mcp_server_collision $.mcpServers.s: MCP server "s" already exists with different or unresolved configuration and will not be overwritten.
[exit 1]
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>This branch</summary>

```
$ openclaw templates validate <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Valid Template project: <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Package: mcptimeout@0.1.0
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Ready.
Automation created: Daily summary.
Added agent: mcptimeout
Workspace: <run>/state/workspace-mcptimeout
[exit 0]
$ openclaw mcp show s
OpenClaw-managed MCP server "s" (<run>/state/openclaw.json):
{
  "command": "node",
  "args": [
    "s.js"
  ],
  "connectionTimeoutMs": 5000,
  "requestTimeoutMs": 30000
}
[exit 0]
```

Server already configured in milliseconds:

```
$ openclaw mcp set s {"command":"node","args":["s.js"],"requestTimeoutMs":30000,"connectionTimeoutMs":5000}
Saved MCP server "s" to <run>/state/openclaw.json.
[exit 0]
$ openclaw templates add <run>/proj/mcptimeout
Ready.
Automation created: Daily summary.
Added agent: mcptimeout
Workspace: <run>/state/workspace-mcptimeout
[exit 0]
$ openclaw mcp show s
OpenClaw-managed MCP server "s" (<run>/state/openclaw.json):
{
  "command": "node",
  "args": [
    "s.js"
  ],
  "requestTimeoutMs": 30000,
  "connectionTimeoutMs": 5000
}
[exit 0]
```

</details>

Tests and checks:

- `pnpm test src/templates/mcp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 6 passed in 9.75s. The two new cases write through the real config writer. With the `mcp.ts` change reverted they fail with `Unrecognized key: "connectTimeout"` and `already exists with different configuration`.
- `pnpm test src/templates`: 36 files, 408 passed, 3 skipped.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the touched files, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main` (+20) and `git diff --check` pass.

Not covered: Add through a running Gateway or the Control UI was not run; `src/templates/gateway-add-apply.ts` applies the plan through the same `applyTemplateAddPlanStateless` the CLI uses. A timeout too large to express in milliseconds is dropped by the existing migration rather than rejected.

Simplification: reused the existing seconds-to-milliseconds migration; no new helper. Production delta +5/-3; test delta +22/-2; docs +4/-2 against main.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior behavior with no state or config migration. Blast radius is Template Add for manifests whose MCP servers set `timeout` or `connectTimeout`, which could not complete before.

prs.title: fix(ui): show app-managed guidance for host-owned Gateway updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #198506. When a Gateway's install is owned by an external application (the macOS `OpenClaw.app`, a desktop app, or an immutable deployer), the Control UI's Gateway updates panel shows a local "Update Gateway…" button. Clicking it fails with `Update error: Managed by OpenClaw.app` because the update admission layer rejects host-owned installs.

This PR makes the Control UI aware of the owning app and swaps the local update action for guidance to update through that app instead, so the UI never presents an action it cannot perform.

## Solution

- **Protocol**: `UpdateStatusResult` gains an optional `installOwner` object (`schemaVersion`, `owner`, `displayName`, `updateHint`) describing the external app that owns the install, when one is resolved.
- **Gateway handler**: `update.status` surfaces `installOwner` from the resolved install status when present.
- **Control UI**: `update-overlay-helpers` projects `installOwner` into the update snapshot; the Gateway updates row replaces the "Update Gateway…" button with a managed-by note ("This Gateway is managed by {app} and updates are handled there. {hint}") when `installOwner` is present, and the Retry action on a failed update is hidden for host-owned installs.
- **Validator**: regenerated gateway protocol validators (`protocol.generated/predicates.js`) for the new schema field.

## Evidence

- **Protocol schema**: `config.test.ts` validates the `installOwner` marker (accepts the `macos-app` shape, rejects unknown owner / wrong schemaVersion / empty displayName).
- **Gateway handler**: `update-status-schedule.test.ts` asserts `installOwner` is surfaced on an app-owned install (via `lifecycle.initialize()`) and omitted on an unowned package install; the existing host-owned case (`refreshCheckout`) now also asserts `installOwner`.
- **Control UI**: `updates.test.ts` (jsdom) verifies a host-owned install shows no "Update Gateway…" button and renders the app-managed guidance, while non-host-owned installs keep the update action; a host-owned failed install shows no "Retry update" recovery button (replaced by the managed-by guidance) instead of dispatching into the host-owned rejection.
- The `installOwner` test fixture is typed `satisfies UpdateInstallOwner`, so the schema fields stay checked at compile time.
- UI tests: 45/45 pass (3 new). Server tests: 42/42 pass (2 new). `pnpm format` clean on all changed files.

prs.title: feat(slack): render streamed reasoning as task cards, with continuation messages for long streams
prs.body:
## Decision requested

This PR adds one optional setting, `channels.slack.streaming.progress.reasoning: "narration" | "cards"` (channel and per-account scope), and one additive compositor option (`pushToolProgress(..., { reasoningLine: true })`) used only by the Slack plugin. Default is unchanged (`narration`, today's behavior). `cards` is opt-in, there is no migration, and existing configs are untouched. It needs a maintainer's yes or no on the setting; the card rendering and the continuation chain are only reachable once it is set.

This revision re-ports the branch onto current `main` (the previous head `ea1a10d` was about 34.7k commits behind and conflicting) and addresses the review on that head:

- **P2 from the exact-head review is fixed.** The opening planner that applies the 6 KB card budget now runs only in `cards` mode. In `narration` (default) a message opens with the full update exactly as on `main`, so an initial plan larger than the card budget keeps every row. Regression test: `keeps every step of an oversized initial plan in default narration mode` (20 steps of 120 CJK characters, about 7,200 bytes; red with the planner on the narration path, green now).
- **The two fixes every mode needs are split out** as the first two commits, each with its own tests, so they can land (or be split into standalone PRs) independently of the setting decision.
- **The continuation chain builds on `rotateInterruptedStream`** instead of duplicating it (details below).

Commits, in order:

1. `fix(slack): keep the final reply on its stream when a progress boundary lands during delivery` (+10 production lines)
2. `fix(slack): post the answer when Slack rejects a native stream with msg_too_long` (+32)
3. `feat(slack): render streamed reasoning as task cards on the native progress card` (+369)
4. `feat(slack): roll long reasoning card streams into continuation messages` (+1,609)

Net production change against `main`: +2,231 / -211 lines (net +2,020, comments included; about 25 of those lines are the existing reasoning-preview helper moved unchanged into `dispatch-progress-reasoning.ts`). Tests and the shared dispatch harness are separate (+2,832 / -7).

## What Problem This Solves

With `agents.defaults.reasoningDefault: "stream"` (an existing operator opt-in), OpenClaw streams the model's reasoning while the reply is generated. On Slack's native progress card the plugin keeps one compacted reasoning line, filters it out of the task list and appends it to the stream's narration text, so a long think shows as an unlabeled paragraph above the card rather than as the thought it is. Nothing renders reasoning in the card itself.

Two defects surfaced while building that, and they affect every mode:

- Core fires `onReasoningEnd` and `onAssistantMessageStart` without awaiting them. A draft boundary that lands while `deliverNativeFinal` is still appending reads the turn as over and stops the stream under the answer; Slack then rejects the answer's append and it degrades to a plain post or is lost. Seen with a live model (Evidence, prior head) and reproduced deterministically by the new test.
- Slack answers `chat.appendStream` with `msg_too_long` once a streamed message holds as much as it allows. The plugin did not classify the code: the session was marked stopped without `chat.stopStream`, the error was rethrown, and the message stayed in its streaming state without the answer.

## User Impact

- Everyone on native progress streaming: a late model boundary no longer stops the stream under the final answer, and a `msg_too_long` on the answer (or on the closing stop) ends with the answer posted normally and the message out of streaming state, instead of a message stuck streaming without its answer.
- Operators who set `reasoningDefault: "stream"` and `channels.slack.streaming.progress.reasoning: "cards"` (with `progress.toolProgress: true`) see the reasoning as 🧠 rows in the plan block, interleaved with tool rows, titled `Thought for <n>s, <k> tool calls` when the turn finishes. A think longer than one message continues in further messages in the same thread (`Thinking, continued below` → `Thinking, continued`); the answer follows the last one.
- Everyone else sees no change: the default is `narration`, and with `reasoningDefault` off nothing is rendered either way. The setting validates as an enum; other values are rejected by the strict Slack schema.

Known Slack client behavior, documented in `docs/channels/slack/messaging.md`: while an assistant thread status set through `assistant.threads.setStatus` is showing, the Slack client hides the streamed cards until the status clears, and continuation messages render in bursts rather than as a smooth stream.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Commit 1 (boundary during final delivery).** `deliverNativeFinal` publishes its in-flight delivery; a non-forced `beginNewProgressTurn` awaits it before it acts, so the answer lands on the stream and the boundary finishes the turn afterwards. Forced boundaries (queued follow-up admission) keep their semantics.

**Commit 2 (`msg_too_long`).** `msg_too_long` becomes `SlackStreamMessageTooLongError`, a `SlackStreamNotDeliveredError` carrying the rejected text, and the session stays open. The answer goes through the normal reply path before the stream is stopped (stopping first would flush the rejected text again), and a closeout stop rejected the same way is retried without its chunks.

**Commit 3 (cards).** In `cards` mode the plugin merges reasoning through the compositor's existing merge, splits it into segments of about 240 characters at word boundaries and pushes each as a task row (`reasoning:<n>`, 🧠 prefix, complete except the newest). A tool call or the end of a reasoning phase seals the open segment before the tool row is admitted. The completion title becomes `Thought for …` unless `progress.label` is set, and the running headline never borrows a reasoning row's text. The compositor resets its reasoning accumulator whenever a changed line is admitted; a card is the reasoning's own row, so `pushToolProgress` takes `reasoningLine: true` to keep the raw accumulator (the existing `reasoningLinePrefix` / `reasoningGate` options shape the compacted narration line and do not cover this). Reasoning cards need the detailed native card; the quiet card keeps narration.

**Commit 4 (continuation messages).** A per-message ledger (`stream-size.ts`) counts everything on the current stream message in UTF-8 bytes (titles, plan title and text at 1x, `details` and `output` at 2x). In `cards` mode new rows are admitted while the message stays under 6,000 weighted bytes of rows and 50 rows, text while the total stays under 9,000, about 19% under the measured ceiling. When something does not fit, the message is finished as `Thinking, continued below` (every open row complete) and a new stream continues in the same thread. Cards are queued in the reasoning runtime while the current message cannot take them; a send releases them as room appears, and the terminal paths drain the queue on budgeted messages before any closeout. A `msg_too_long` despite the estimate rolls once and retries; a rejected answer finishes the think and streams the answer as its own message; a second rejection, or a retry whose start Slack rejects, posts the answer normally.

What changed against the previous head while re-porting:

- **Builds on `rotateInterruptedStream`.** `main` already seals a stream after a human reply and opens the next message in the same thread (`interruptedThreadTs`). The previous head's private `continuationThreadTs`, transport thread override, `forcedThreadTs` hook and turn-level `stoppedBySlack` flag are gone. Both paths now go through one delivery operation, `sealStream`: it stops the current message (reporting a closeout Slack rejected), forgets the session and keeps its thread as `interruptedThreadTs`, so the next native start, the answer stream (`deliverWithStreaming`) and a normal reply (`deliverNormally`, `nativeFinalThreadTs`, `canFinishNativeFinal`) all land in that thread without taking another reply slot. A Slack Stop that lands while that stop is in flight leaves the stopped session current, which is how the interruption path already keeps a turn-level Stop, so a continuation, the completion and the answer are all suppressed. The ledger restarts in the one place a stream starts (`startStream`).
- **Main's newer native paths are kept:** the `"rotated"` transport result, snapshot reset when another path replaced the session, `nativeFinalThreadTs` / `canFinishNativeFinal`, progress staying editable after native stream failures, `mergeReasoningProgress` outside progress mode (moved unchanged into `dispatch-progress-reasoning.ts` so `dispatch-progress.ts` stays within its line cap), session links on the receipt row, and `userId`/`teamId` on every start.
- **Compositor final mark.** On `main` the preview lifecycle marks the final started before the native final runs, and the compositor refuses lines from then on. In `cards` mode the native final marks it itself after the queued cards drained into the compositor, so they keep the turn's terminal status; a card the compositor refuses anyway stays queued and is placed straight from the queue instead of being dropped.
- **Text-only continuation start.** A continuation that opens with text and no rows passes an explicit `chunks: []`, so the SDK sends `chat.startStream` at once instead of buffering short text that Slack never acknowledges (found downstream; test `opens a text-only continuation with explicit empty chunks so Slack acknowledges it`).
- **Narration mode** goes through the same send, which with `rollover: false` is `main`'s `updateNativeProgressStreamNow` step for step (rotation, snapshot reset, `markSent` only without a retained thread, commit after acceptance); every existing dispatch assertion in `dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts` passes unchanged.

Layout: segmentation in `progress-reasoning.ts`; the card runtime in `dispatch-progress-reasoning.ts`; the ledger and fit planner in `stream-size.ts`; the stream chain in `dispatch-progress-stream.ts`, its ordering and flush tracking in `dispatch-progress-stream-order.ts`, opening/retirement planning in `dispatch-progress-stream-rows.ts`. New dispatch tests run on a shared native-stream harness (`dispatch.native-stream.test-support.ts`) because `dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts` is over the test line cap and may not grow.

Config surface: one channel config key, so `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` `channel` moves from 4005 to 4007; bundled channel metadata and the baseline hashes are regenerated with the repo scripts. Alternative considered: streaming the reasoning into the reply text; not chosen because a native stream is append-only, so every reply would carry its thinking permanently in the message body.

Accepted edge cases (named, not coded for): a closeout stop rejected with `msg_too_long` is retried without its chunks, so narration text riding that closeout is dropped; with `reasoning` set explicitly, the setting counts as an explicit `streaming.progress` key for the top-level preview opt-in like every other progress key except `nativeTaskCards: true`.

## Evidence

### Fresh, this head (local, 2026-11-13)

Rebased onto `main` `8c18a7bed` (Node 26.13.0, pnpm 12.15.0).

- `pnpm test:extension slack`: 165 files, 1,968 tests passed (163 files / 1,951 tests plus 2 files / 17 tests in the second shard), 0 failed.
- New and touched focused suites, all green: `dispatch.native-stream.test.ts` 4 (boundary during final delivery, `msg_too_long` on the answer, `msg_too_long` on the closeout stop, oversized initial plan in narration); `dispatch.reasoning-cards.test.ts` 8; `dispatch.reasoning-rollover.test.ts` 15; `dispatch.reasoning-answer.test.ts` 15; `streaming.test.ts` 20 (+2); `stream-size.test.ts` 10; `progress-reasoning.test.ts` 13; `progress-blocks.reasoning.test.ts` 2; `config-schema.test.ts` 14 (+1); `src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts` 60 (+1); `src/config/schema.test.ts` 28.
- Existing `dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts`: all 96 tests pass with no assertion changed (only its streaming mock gained the new error class), which is the narration regression proof on this head: every exact chunk sequence `main` asserts for native progress is unchanged.
- Red before green, run by reverting the production change under the new tests: commit 1's boundary test and commit 2's three tests fail on `main`'s sources; the P2 test fails when the opening planner runs on the narration path (the previous head's behavior: 16 of 20 plan rows); the text-only continuation test fails without the explicit empty chunk list.
- Each commit was checked out and its focused suites run on their own: commit 1 275 passed, commit 2 279 passed, commit 3 316 + 60 passed, commit 4 the full Slack lane above.
- `pnpm check:changed`: 44 of 47 lanes pass, including format, lint (core and extension), `tsgo` core / core tests / extensions / extension tests, line-cap and max-lines ratchets, first-party mock export ratchet (one grandfathered factory pruned after its mock gained an isolation note), bundled channel config metadata, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports and doctor contract tests. The three that fail do so on a clean `main` checkout as well or for the environment: Plugin SDK surface budget (identical numbers on `main`: 163 > 162 entrypoints), dead export scan (only unrelated non-Slack exports listed), SQLite worker ratchet (`rg` is not installed on this machine).
- `pnpm config:channels:gen` / `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerated `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.*`; the matching `--check` commands and `pnpm lint:docs` pass.

### Prior head `ea1a10d` (real Slack, 2026-09-09/10)

The live evidence below was gathered on the previous head; the behavior it covers (card rendering, byte budgets, rollover, the answer-rejected path, the late boundary) is carried over unchanged in substance, but it is prior-head evidence and a fresh live run on this head is still owed.

- Motivating failure, cards without rollover: a scripted 12,010-character think with one `bash` call rendered 48 rows, then the 92-character answer was rejected with `msg_too_long` (11,215 bytes of titles on the message); the plugin rethrew, never called `chat.stopStream`, and the message stayed `in_progress` without the answer.
- Size probes over the raw SDK: 250-character rows accepted through the 42nd (10,571 bytes) and rejected at the 43rd; text-only 9,064 bytes accepted / 12,054 rejected; rows with 100 characters of `details` rejected at 8,821 bytes; 50 emoji-only rows with no body text (22,900 bytes) accepted; 24 emoji rows (10,418 bytes, 8,666 UTF-16 units) rejected a 3,045-character answer. Only UTF-8 bytes fit every run (ceiling about 10,600-11,300 once the message carries text).
- Rollover build: the 12,010-character think rendered as three messages in the thread (`Thinking, continued below` → `Thinking, continued below` → `Thought for 35s, 1 tool call` with the answer), 3 starts / 28 appends / 3 stops, no errors, each stop/start about 300 ms. Emoji-only reasoning rolled at 25 rows / 5,950 bytes over six messages and the 3,045-character answer landed on the last one.
- Real model (OpenClaw gateway from source, Socket Mode, `reasoningDefault: "stream"`): short question and riddle on one message (`Thought for 6s` / `Thought for 10s`); a 25-segment think around one `exec` rolled once and finished `Thought for 59s, 1 tool call` with the answer on the continuation. Before the late-boundary fix (now commit 1) the same setup produced the two defects it addresses: a short answer streamed as a separate message after the card was stopped, and a continuation ending under the preamble headline.

Screenshots from those runs (test workspace, cropped to one thread reply), full sets on the fork's [evidence branch](https://github.com/n1hility/openclaw/tree/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots):

![Short think, no tool call: two 🧠 rows under `Thought for 5s`, answer below the card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/final2/r3-s1-short-think.png)

![Long think with one tool call, first of three messages: `Thinking, continued below`, all rows complete](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/final2/r3-s2-long-think-msg1-01.png)

![Same turn, third message: the last cards under `Thought for 35s, 1 tool call`, followed by the answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/final2/r3-s2-long-think-msg3-answer.png)

![Real model over Socket Mode, turn with one `exec` call: the continuation ends with `Thought for 59s, 1 tool call` and carries the answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n1hility/openclaw/f8b16d429ab4cea8a7d0a0cb44be1d773594ff71/screenshots/real-model/rm2-long-msg2-answer.png)

### Not tested

- Live Slack on this head (the re-port): owed before merge, through the Slack e2e flow, for narration defaults, card rollover, Stop during a rollover, and final-answer delivery.
- Live: the card roll-and-retry path after a `msg_too_long` on a card update and the normal-reply fallback after a second rejection (dispatcher tests only, here and on the prior head).
- The budgets rest on measured points rather than a documented limit; the roll-and-retry path covers the gap. The 2x weight for `details` comes from one probe.

<details>
<summary>Review findings addressed on the previous head (all carried over, with their tests)</summary>

Sixteen review findings were fixed across earlier rounds, each with a test that failed on the reviewed head; all of those tests are ported to this head and pass. In short: rejected closeout rows, partial-card extensions and same-title tool-row updates carried to the continuation; queued reasoning rows never evicted by the compositor window; raw reasoning kept across deltas (`reasoningLine`); a Slack Stop honored across continuation messages; rejected SDK text discarded before a rollover stop; queued cards drained through budgeted messages before error, media and silent closeouts and before turn rotation; a rejected completion carried to the message that streams the answer; running tool rows kept across rollovers and frozen rows thawed by a later result; bounded admission (a guard charges every accepted start, append and stop to its message and fails any test where a message passes 50 rows or the byte budget); budgeted narration continuations; tool rows never overtaking queued reasoning; continuation capacity held for queued cards behind a full plan.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover guest tasks after concurrent managed-workspace edits (#187911)
prs.body:
# Recover Guest Tasks After Concurrent Managed-Workspace Edits (#187911)

## Summary of Changes

This PR resolves issue #187911 (`fix: recover guest tasks after concurrent managed-workspace edits`) by establishing an authoritative, robust, and verified reconciliation pipeline between host canonical files, sandboxed guest task projections, and the CAS baseline manifest, adhering strictly to the Product Owner's Architectural Decisions in `config-state-lifecycle.md`.

---

## Revision 7 Review Findings Addressed

### 1. Advance Acknowledgement Through Projection State's Update Operation [P1]
- **Root Cause & Fix**: Conflict acknowledgement previously read and modified projection row state without advancing through the custody boundary's formal `state.update` operation. We exported `update` on `projectionOperations` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-state.ts`), introduced `acknowledgeConflictInState(state, ...)` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-conflict-acknowledgement.ts`), and hooked `acknowledgeConflict` in `local-workspace-projection.ts` directly into `acknowledgeConflictInState(state, ...)`.
- **Outcome**: Resolving and saving a reconciled version via `sessions.files.set` now updates the projection state through the official mutation boundary, ensuring subsequent calls to `custody.synchronizeProjection()` synchronize without encountering `"Local workspace binding changed"`, copy reconciled content to `projectionDir`, and settle `pending_ref` to `null`.
- **Regression Added**: In `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts`, updated `acknowledges and saves a reconciled version via sessions.files.set during conflict` with a real prepared git repo and baseline to assert that synchronization cleanly completes and settles `pending_ref` to `null`.

### 2. Use the File Writer's Selected Candidate for Conflict Hash Resolution [P2]
- **Root Cause & Fix**: When saving files in a session with a nested working directory (`spawnedCwd` / `fileRoot`), `sessions.files.set` previously passed the raw relative `filePath` to `resolveReconciledExpectedHash`, while using candidate path resolution inside `setSessionWorkspaceFile`. If a session was executing in a subfolder (e.g. `sub/`), the conflict on `sub/handover.md` was not matched against the expected hash in `conflicts`.
- **Resolution**: Exported `resolveSessionWorkspaceCandidatePath({ root, fileRoot, filePath })` from `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts`. In `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts`, resolved `effectivePath` once upfront and passed it to both `resolveReconciledExpectedHash` and `write(...)`. Updated `resolveCandidateBrowserPath` in `src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-conflict-acknowledgement.ts` to accept the `conflicts` map and match exact candidate paths directly.
- **Regression Added**: Added integration test `resolves conflict hash correctly when session has a nested fileRoot` in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts` verifying that nested session candidates resolve and reconcile cleanly.

### 3. Include All Accepted Receipt Changes in the Resolved Baseline [P2]
- **Root Cause & Fix**: When overlaying resolved canonical paths onto the base manifest in `commitLocalWorkspaceReconciliation`, unconflicted modifications, additions, and deletions made by the guest task were previously omitted from the newly committed CAS baseline manifest if only partial resolutions were staged.
- **Resolution**: In `src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-conflict-resolution.ts`, parsed `snapshotBase` (when available) and applied all unconflicted additions, modifications, and deletions from `snapshot.current` to the baseline before overlaying `resolvedCanonicalPaths`, ensuring full fidelity of guest changes alongside resolved conflicts.

---

## Verification & Test Results

### 1. Vitest Test Suites (29/29 Tests Passed - 100% Green)

- **`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts` (14/14 tests passed)**:
  - ✓ allows inspecting canonical files when the managed workspace has a preserved conflict
  - ✓ acknowledges and saves a reconciled version via sessions.files.set during conflict
  - ✓ resolves conflict hash correctly when session has a nested fileRoot
  - ✓ saves a reconciled version when expectedHash matches the inspected guest draft in projection
  - ✓ preserves compare-and-swap protection for unseen canonical edits outside retained conflicts
  - ✓ accepts a newer guest version that the operator actually reviewed in projection
  - ✓ resolves canonical workspace-relative path when saving absolute path candidates
  - ✓ (and all 7 baseline suite tests)

- **`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.conflict.test.ts` (15/15 tests passed)**:
  - ✓ replaces projection symlinks safely without following destination links (Finding 2)
  - ✓ overlays resolved paths onto complete accepted baseline preserving unmutated baseline entries (Finding 3)
  - ✓ preserves newer guest divergence in projection if edited while conflict is pending (Finding 5)
  - ✓ allows explicitly accepted Markdown separator lines (Revision 3 Finding 1)
  - ✓ refuses to resolve when an ancestor directory component is a symlink (Revision 3 Finding 2)
  - ✓ preserves live guest symlink divergence across retries (Revision 3 Finding 4)
  - ✓ accepts an explicitly reviewed newer guest version (Revision 5 Finding 2)
  - ✓ rejects unreviewed newer guest version written after administrator review
  - ✓ preserves guest file mode changes without byte changes as conflict divergence
  - ✓ refuses acknowledgment after worktree reassignment (Security Finding)
  - ✓ (and all remaining unit regression tests)

### 2. Standalone Real-World Verification Proof (5/5 Scenarios Passed - 100% Green)

Executed `/home/masterswords/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/5fec5c34-95c1-4af4-bc25-c6d1b921c299/scratch/verify-revision-7-proof.ts`:
- **Finding 1**: State update mutation boundary & acknowledgement integration — verified conflict hash resolution and `state.update` recording `acknowledgedPaths` and `acknowledgedGuestVersions`.
- **Finding 2**: Writer's candidate path `packages/core/src/index.ts` correctly matches nested session `fileRoot` and translates hash.
- **Finding 3**: Resolved baseline includes all accepted receipt additions, modifications, deletions, and resolved paths.
- **Scenario 4**: Directory ancestor symlink escapes strictly prevented.
- **Scenario 5**: Live guest divergence preserved without byte loss.

### 3. Ratchets & Invariants Passed (Exact 0 Slack)

- `check:line-cap-ratchet`: **PASS** (`Line-cap ratchet OK: 13 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth`).
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: **PASS** (`Test lines OK: 6574567; ceiling: 6574567; slack: 0`).
- `check:assertion-safety-ratchet`: **PASS** (`assertion SAFETY ratchet OK: 2381 files, 5408 grandfathered assertions`).
- Full compliance with `config-state-lifecycle.md` Product Owner Architectural Decisions.

prs.title: fix(exec-approvals): stop interrupted snapshot reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: interrupting `openclaw approvals get` (gateway or node target) leaves the pending
`exec.approvals.get` / `exec.approvals.node.get` snapshot read alive, and when the reply
lands during cleanup the CLI still prints the snapshot and effective-policy table after
the user asked to stop.

The same shape was fixed this week for users/nodes/models/devices/cron/skills-library
reads by the interrupt family (#197322, #197185, #197174, #197110, #197315, #197281).
`approvals get` was a remaining `callGatewayFromCli` caller that did not pass the command
abort signal.

Precedent: #197322 (same shape; this PR only changes the call site).

## Why This Change Was Made

The `get` command action now captures `getAsyncWorkSignal()` and forwards it through
`loadSnapshotTarget` into `loadSnapshot`'s existing transport call as an optional
parameter; once the signal aborts, the command returns before printing and abort errors
from the transport are swallowed only when the signal is aborted. The write paths
(`set`, `resolve`, allowlist mutations) keep their receipt behavior and are not guarded —
`loadWritableSnapshotTarget` calls the same helper without a signal.

The snapshot model (target-source type, snapshot union, type guards) and the
target-resolution read path moved unchanged into the coherent sibling
`exec-approvals-snapshot.ts` because `exec-approvals-cli.ts` sits on the max-lines
ratchet baseline and may not grow; no behavior change in the move.

No new validator, option, config surface, or persistence change. Non-interrupted reads
print exactly as before.

Production LOC is `+25/-4` in `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.ts` plus the unchanged snapshot
model relocation to `src/cli/exec-approvals-snapshot.ts`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Interrupting `approvals get` no longer prints a late snapshot or effective-policy table
after Ctrl+C or SIGTERM; the CLI exits 130/143 without a late result or error.
Uninterrupted reads and all write commands behave identically.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `66cbb8e54098093b648a1a8821ac51dcc7166f02`
- Current-main RED baseline: `d2ca84fb7b67` (`openclaw/openclaw` main at verification time)
- Production entry: real source CLI, `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts approvals get --gateway --url … --token … --json`
- Canonical owner exercised: `loadSnapshotTarget` / `loadSnapshot` in `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.ts`
- Decision surface: `approvals get` snapshot + effective-policy output
- Recorder/readback boundary: `defaultRuntime.writeJson` call count and process exit code
- Acceptance RED: on base, the same command prints the late `exec.approvals.get` reply (marker `L8E_MARKER_7f3a91` observed on stdout) after SIGINT
- Acceptance GREEN: exact head exits 130 with empty stdout after SIGINT; late reply never printed
- Legal control: all 29 pre-existing tests in the same file pass unchanged on the exact head (gateway/node routing, JSON output, allowlist guards)
- Cleanup: isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_HOME` per run; no production Gateway, session, channel, token, or configuration was touched

### Discriminative regression (remote vitest, node v24.22.1)

`src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts` gains a test that settles the snapshot read only
after the command scope begins closing (`AsyncWorkScope.beginClose()`) and asserts no
JSON is written and no error is reported.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| BASE `d2ca84fb7b67` (test file only) | `prints no snapshot that lands after Ctrl+C` **FAIL** at the publication assertion: the late *valid* snapshot is written (`writeJson` called 1 time) (1 failed / 29 passed) |
| HEAD `66cbb8e54098` | 30 passed (includes the new Ctrl+C test) |

The mock is an async one-shot: it begins closing the command scope and then returns the
legal `nativeSnapshot`, so the base fails on observable publication rather than at the
snapshot type guard — the post-await aborted guard is what suppresses the late output.

```sh
node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Sibling suites on the exact head: `exec-approvals-cli.pending-resolve.test.ts` 15 passed,
`exec-approvals-cli.utf8.test.ts` 2 passed.

### Shipped real-behavior proof (real CLI, synthetic loopback Gateway peer)

Same recipe as the accepted #197281/#197508 proofs: the real CLI entry runs against a
synthetic loopback peer (challenge → `connect` → `hello-ok` → held request → late legal
reply; auxiliary `config.get` answered immediately). On SIGINT the driver releases a late
legal `exec.approvals.get` reply carrying marker `L8E_MARKER_7f3a91` and records
stdout/exit.

| Variant | Exit code | SIGINT→exit | Late reply printed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BASE `d2ca84fb7b67` | 130 | 982 ms | **yes** (marker on stdout) |
| HEAD `d29cbc381159` | 130 | 578 ms | **no** (stdout empty) |

PTY proof recorded at `d29cbc381159`; the current head `66cbb8e54098` changes only the test mock, one `// SAFETY:` invariant comment, and the ratchet baselines below — the production code path is unchanged.

Uninterrupted control: covered by the 29 pre-existing vitest cases on the exact head. No
watchdog kill in any run.

### Verification

- `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts` — 30 passed on HEAD; the new Ctrl+C test red on BASE
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on all touched files
- `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` — no errors in touched files (donor tree shows pre-existing generated-code drift errors in unrelated files, identical on base)
- `check:line-cap-ratchet` green via the `exec-approvals-snapshot.ts` sibling extraction; `check-test-lines-ratchet` green with the exact 15-line allocation
- `git diff --check` clean
- `check:assertion-safety` green: the extracted loader cast in `exec-approvals-snapshot.ts` carries a one-line `// SAFETY:` producer-invariant comment, and the `exec-approvals-cli.ts` baseline entry shrank 9 → 8 per the ratchet (counts may only shrink; no baseline expansion)
- Review round 1 (ClawSweeper, 2026-11-12) addressed at `66cbb8e54098`: (1) the cancellation mock is now an async one-shot returning a legal snapshot — fixes the `TS2322` test-type failure (`check-test-types-core-1`) and makes the base fail at publication (table above); (2) the extraction cast satisfies the assertion-safety ratchet via the `// SAFETY:` invariant (baseline shrunk, not expanded)
- Not tested: real Gateway round trip (peer is synthetic; the vitest boundary mocks only the transport); Windows/macOS; full repository CI

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+25/-4` in `exec-approvals-cli.ts`; `exec-approvals-snapshot.ts` is the unchanged snapshot model + read path relocated (ratchet-required sibling)
- Test LOC: `+12` (one file)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `getAsyncWorkSignal()` and the transport's existing `signal` hook; no new abstraction
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

- The `signal` parameter on `loadSnapshot` / `loadSnapshotTarget` is optional and defaults
  to `undefined`; the write path (`loadWritableSnapshotTarget`, `saveSnapshotTargeted`)
  deliberately passes none so admitted write receipts still print.
- Keep the `exec-approvals-snapshot.ts` sibling split if you rebase:
  `exec-approvals-cli.ts` is on the max-lines ratchet baseline and re-growing it fails
  `check:line-cap-ratchet`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready: single-owner change, precedented shape, red/green plus real-CLI proof above.
- Alternative considered and rejected: guarding inside `loadSnapshot` for all callers —
  would swallow the post-write refresh read after `set`, breaking its receipt.
- Scope declaration: no drive-by changes; the extraction is behavior-neutral relocation
  required by the line ratchet.

</details>

prs.title: test(ui): dismiss phone model picker through its backdrop
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Chromium and WebKit cases `keeps model and effort targets separate when Files narrows the composer` in `ui/src/e2e/chat-composer-picker-layout.e2e.test.ts` try to dismiss the phone model sheet by clicking its covered trigger. The sheet's options intercept that click.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Restore coverage of model and effort picker separation across the existing desktop, narrow-composer, and phone viewport matrix.

## Why This Change Was Made

#192142 intentionally changed the model picker at phone widths into a bottom sheet. Wait for its actual `data-phase="open"` signal before interaction. Retain Escape dismissal, and tap the exposed backdrop for phone pointer dismissal. After the outside tap, wait for the native hidden phase and resume editing through the textarea: outside taps intentionally collapse the mobile composer. Desktop model and effort pickers keep their trigger-toggle checks. Existing geometry, closed-state assertions, delays, and timeouts remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Scheduled run 43527024791 reports both cases. A local Chromium diagnostic reproduces the exact second-trigger failure on the base: model search/options intercept `trigger.click()` while the phone sheet is open.

The local diagnostic uses the normal bundled UI and the selected Chromium case, temporarily omitting the suite's unconditional WebKit startup so Chromium can run. The same Chromium diagnostic passes the full viewport and repeated-interaction matrix with the fix. The committed suite retains the original WebKit resource setup. Both full-entry-point attempts (Bun and Node) stalled during native WebKit startup before cases executed; no local WebKit pass is claimed.

Targeted tsrs typechecking, oxlint, formatting, diff checks, and independent Codex review pass. No sleeps, timeout increases, or weaker assertions.



CI: [run43537660138](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43537660138) passed the affected UI E2E shard, including the committed browser setup. Local WebKit launch was unavailable as described above; CI now supplies the broader entry-point proof. Two UI-unit jobs failed on 18 baseline cases: the original16 unit failures, the later-main semantic-option assertion (#198546), and a startup-status readiness assertion. All failed test and owner blobs are unchanged between actual CI baseline and tested merge. The startup failure was independently reproduced with a pending shared frame; its separate repair (#198555) preserves the original text and accessibility assertions. This scoped E2E repair is eligible for the authorized inherited-failure landing route.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse activity recap envelopes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Activity recap broadcasts repeat common envelope preparation and JSON encoding for recipients with different delivery histories.

## User Impact

Recaps use less Gateway CPU and allocation while preserving their content, 750 ms coalescing deadline, delivery order, and per-recipient authority checks. No configuration or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recaps already own a plain envelope throughout synchronous fan-out, but did not opt into the event projector's existing envelope reuse. They now share common templates and encoding while each connection keeps its own row versions and ancestor certificates. An omitted ancestor input still resolves lazily; explicit uncertified ancestry remains distinct.

Runtime delta: **+11/-3, net +8 lines**. The growth carries the existing reuse contract and preserves lazy ancestry; there is no new cache, retention policy, scheduler, or parallel fast path. The larger tooling diff extends the existing row snapshot benchmark to exercise the actual recap producer and broadcaster.

## Evidence

The existing mixed-audience regression now covers recaps. It fails on the baseline with **4 filtered envelopes instead of 2**, then passes with the fix. It checks equivalent decoded payloads across legacy, row-delta and field-reference clients, staggered histories, and live scope revocation. Three focused files passed: **20 tests**, 53.09 s Vitest / 58.69 s wrapper. Scoped format/lint, root test typecheck, script-types and Gateway-root test typecheck passed.

| Owner metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU/consume, paired mean | 1.358 ms | 0.657 ms (**-51.6%**) |
| Collected sampled allocation/consume | 1.947 MiB | 1.131 MiB (**-41.9%**) |
| Consume p50, pair 1 / pair 2 | 1.292 / 1.302 ms | 0.589 / 0.613 ms |
| Consume p99, pair 1 / pair 2 | 1.802 / 2.279 ms | 1.205 / 1.278 ms |
| Consume max, pair 1 / pair 2 | 2.354 / 3.003 ms | 2.049 / 1.962 ms |
| Consumes over 180 ms | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Timing: **1,000 samples per side per pair**, serial AB/BA (2,000 per side). Allocation: separate collected-object sampling, **200 iterations per side per pair** (400 per side). A/A controls: CPU **1.343 / 1.305 ms**, p99 **1.995 / 1.815 ms**, max **5.372 / 2.122 ms**, 1,000 samples each, no consumes over 180 ms. Earlier exploratory controls had substantially noisier tails; CPU/allocation and the work count carry the conclusion.

Workload: **15,800 materialized resident rows, 3,160 parents, 70 recipients**, histories primed from 40 sidebar / 20 dashboard / 10 detail windows, and 12 rotating changed recap targets. The real recap producer, presenter, child activity, delivery planner and broadcaster encoder run; prepared storage reads, administrator admission and socket sinks are synthetic. The timer advances virtually. CPU/wall cover synchronous consumes that deliver frames; allocation includes fixture mutation/preparation. Normalized payload digests match per workload across both revisions; only random ancestor certificates are normalized outside measurement.

Command: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-row-snapshot-measure.ts --rows 15800 --parents 3160 --churn 12 --recipients 70 --warmup 24 --iterations 1000`; separate allocation passes use `--iterations 200 --allocation`. Baseline producer is from `dcd2afb07a1b`, loaded with the same harness/dependencies. Rebase onto current main changed no measured runtime path (the sibling selection-retention listener is not triggered by this fixture).

Timing host load (1-minute, start/end): base 19.17/19.17 and 21.82/21.27; candidate 19.77/19.77 and 19.83/19.83. End-of-run RSS/heap, context only: base 903/459 and 934/473 MiB; candidate 898/469 and 909/458 MiB. These are owner measurements, not whole-Gateway latency, GC or physical transport-compression proof. This follows the deletion fast path: no fan-out timing/order change, no dev-Gateway pair or Team load.

The trace's 4,066 ms under consumeCurrent is not all recap work. Presentation, selection/defaults, sidebar packing and compression remain; this result does not establish a new production stall total. Unchanged summary states are already suppressed upstream; the 750 ms window coalesces notifications rather than polling unconditionally.

Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean**, using the requested plain branch-review command with no provider/model/environment overrides (default P0 scope). Initial CI found three benchmark-only fixture type errors (optional entry, required transport auth flag, and UUID marker); these are fixed. The exact failing script-types command now passes, and a 200-consume replay retains the same payload digest. Production code is unchanged by that repair. Codex branch review passed again. Exact-head [PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43547440316) for `c1ed8215578c2458ef73f144f3318afffcc9b17e`; both required CI gates are green. Ready for maintainer review; not merged.
