prs.title: fix(android): large videos never send and keep dropping the Gateway connection
prs.body:
Closes #193810

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Android, sending a video between about 12 and 20 MB never sends, keeps dropping the Gateway connection, and holds back every later message in that chat.

## User Impact

User impact: Android now refuses a video that cannot fit in one message when it is picked, a message already stuck from an earlier version shows "Failed — too large to send" with Delete, and later messages in the chat send normally. The new limit is 11.8 MiB; videos over 12 MiB could never be sent, and the small gap leaves room for the message text in the same frame.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat.send` carries attachments inline as Base64 in one WebSocket message, and OkHttp refuses any message that would grow its outgoing queue past 16 MiB, closing the socket. Android admitted videos up to 20 MiB, and the refused send was treated as a transient connection problem, so the row was replayed on every reconnect.

- Video admission now uses the attachment budget of one 16 MiB message, computed with the same formula the Gateway uses for its own frame limit (`src/shared/chat-attachment-frame-budget.ts`): 12,386,304 bytes. The composer, the outbox and the camera recorder already read that one constant.
- A request larger than the socket accepts fails permanently before it reaches OkHttp, so the connection stays up, the row parks as Failed with a size message, and later rows proceed through the existing failed-row handling.

Not changed here: a picked file over its limit still shows the existing generic notice "Could not stage an attachment for sending.", the same one videos over 20 MiB and images or documents over 8 MiB get today; the picker drops the failure reason for every kind. Naming the limit in that notice touches every attachment kind and adds a translated string, so it is better as its own change; this PR keeps to making every admitted video deliverable.

## Evidence

Real app (third-party debug APK built from each commit) on an Android 16 (API 36) x86_64 emulator, paired by setup code to an isolated Gateway built from the same commit, no model configured (the failure happens before any model call). The video is chosen through **+ → Gallery → system photo picker**.

### Full-product repro on main

`main` at `f7a46e85d26`, a 13,498,225-byte MP4, then a text in the same chat. App screen (uiautomator dump) and Gateway log:

```
bubble 1: 18.mp4                  Sending…                          (2+ minutes)
bubble 2: hello after the video   Queued — sends when reconnected

08:56:41.212 [ws] → close code=1001 durationMs=240144 handshake=connected lastFrameMethod=health
08:56:41.315 [ws] client connected client=openclaw-android mode=ui role=operator
08:56:44.197 [ws] → close code=1001 durationMs=2897 handshake=connected lastFrameMethod=sessions.list
08:56:44.234 [ws] client connected client=openclaw-android mode=ui role=operator
... (one close + reconnect about every 2 s)
08:56-09:01 UTC: 94 closes with code=1001, 0 chat.send
```

Control on the same build: a 7,484,429-byte MP4 sends (`[ws] ⇄ res ✓ chat.send 1651ms`), 0 closes.

### Live run with the fix

Same emulator and Gateway. The app was updated in place over the stuck `main` install (data kept), then Retry, a text, a new 13.5 MB pick and the 7.5 MB control:

```
stuck row after update + Retry:  18.mp4  Failed — too large to send; delete it and send a smaller file
text after it:                   hello after the video  (sent)
new 13.5 MB pick:                Could not stage an attachment for sending.   (nothing queued)

09:16:29.063 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ chat.send 660ms   (the text)
09:18:07.600 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ chat.send 668ms   (7.5 MB control)
09:15-09:19 UTC: 0 closes with code=1001
```

Proof artifice: taps and typing were driven over adb from the screen hierarchy (uiautomator) instead of by hand; the device is an emulator, not a phone; the MP4s were generated with ffmpeg (test pattern, constant bitrate); the Gateway had no model configured, so replies are a sign-in error.

Tests (`:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest`, Robolectric, real OkHttp + MockWebServer):

- New `GatewaySessionReconnectTest.oversizedRequestFailsWithoutDroppingTheSocket`: fails on main (the request comes back as the retryable "not enqueued" failure that parks the row as Queued), passes with the fix.
- `GatewaySessionReconnectTest`, `RoomChatCommandOutboxTest`, `ChatComposerDraftTest`, `ChatControllerOutboxTest`: 242 passed, 0 failed. `:app:ktlintCheck` passed.

Test lines: +35/-2 Kotlin (one new test; two assertions that pinned the old 20 MiB constant removed); no TypeScript test lines.

prs.title: feat(plugins): let an operator run a memory plugin beside the memory slot owner
prs.body:
Closes #198445

## What Problem This Solves

A memory plugin that does not own `plugins.slots.memory` is disabled before it registers anything, so an operator cannot keep memory-core and also run an external memory plugin.

## User Impact

An operator can set `plugins.entries.<id>.memory.sidecar: true` to load that memory plugin beside the slot owner. The mode is an explicit operator opt-in. The plugin keeps its hooks, tools and corpus supplements. The slot owner keeps `memory_search`, the memory runtime, the recall grant and memory lessons. A turn now carries a host-minted memory audience when a loaded sidecar can use it, so a sidecar that routes recall and retain by audience works next to memory-core. Configs without the setting load and behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registrar already strips slot-owner fields from a memory capability registered by a plugin that is not the owner (the dreaming sidecar relies on this), so the missing piece was the load decision. The setting is per plugin entry, so an operator accepts the cost of a second memory system for each install. `openclaw plugins enable` keeps the current slot for a sidecar entry, so enabling one does not replace memory-core.

Every sidecar lookup reads `plugins.entries` through the canonical policy id, so a manifest id such as `MiXeD-memory` matches its lowercase entry `mixed-memory`. Root help admits a sidecar only when the normalized memory slot is not `none`.

Memory audiences are minted by the host, not by plugins. The embedded runner minted one only when the slot owner was a native provider, so next to memory-core (a legacy runtime) a sidecar saw no audience and skipped recall and retain. The gate is now: native slot owner, or at least one loaded memory plugin that is not the slot owner and has `memory.sidecar: true`. The audience comes from the same `resolveMemoryAudienceFromEntry` call with the same owner, sender and lineage checks, so it grants nothing a native owner would not. A config with no sidecar entry returns before any registry read, so legacy-only turns still take no session lease and read no lineage. The other native-only paths (project memory bootstrap, post-compaction refresh, memory flush) talk to the slot owner's provider and are unchanged.

Config surface: `plugins.entries.*.memory` and `plugins.entries.*.memory.sidecar` are counted once per plugin entry, so the generated plugin path count in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` rises from 5081 to 5455. No other config paths change.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `PluginEntrySchema`: `memory.sidecar` (boolean), with label and help text.
- `normalizePluginsConfig`: `entries[id].memorySidecar`; `isMemorySidecarEnabled` reads it by canonical policy id.
- `resolveMemorySlotDecision`: `sidecar` parameter; enabled and not selected when the slot names another plugin; still disabled for `slots.memory: "none"`; a case variant of the owner id is not a sidecar.
- Callers: runtime loader, config validation, CLI root descriptors, plugin root contributions.
- `applySlotSelectionForPlugin`: drops the `memory` kind for a sidecar entry, so enable does not move the slot.
- `hasLoadedMemorySidecar` (`src/plugins/memory-state.ts`): true when a loaded `memory` plugin other than the slot owner has `memory.sidecar` on; never loads a plugin.
- `resolveEmbeddedAttemptMemoryAudience`: mints when the owner is native or `hasLoadedMemorySidecar` is true.
- docs/plugins/manifest.md: one line on the setting.

</details>

## Evidence

Builds: main `4cffd43ee04`, this branch before the audience change (`a3fca384bdb`) and with it (`e4597199264`), built from source. The external plugin is `@etzelm/openclaw-memory-hindsight` 0.9.0 from npm (manifest id `hindsight-native`, kind `memory`, `slotMode: sidecar`). `hindsightApiUrl` points at a loopback mock that logs every request and answers recall with one canned memory (`PROOF-CANARY-7731: the operator's test color is teal.`); no real credentials.

The head `3e696edd18f` merges main (`9bf3e79c823`) on top of `e4597199264`. On that merged tree, the 94 tests in the changed test files pass and `pnpm config:docs:check` is OK.

Chat turns: each build ran as an isolated scratch Gateway (own HOME, state dir, config, loopback port and token) with the repo's QA mock-openai server as the model, `plugins.slots.memory: "memory-core"`, and two `chat.send` turns on `agent:main:main`.

| Run | `plugins inspect hindsight-native` | `tools.catalog` | `memory.status` provider | Requests at the Hindsight mock | Canary in the model prompt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, plugin enabled, no `memory.sidecar` | disabled: `memory slot set to "memory-core"` | `memory_search`, `memory_get` | `memory-core` | none | no |
| `a3fca384bdb`, `memory.sidecar: true` | loaded | + `hindsight_recall`, `hindsight_reflect`, `hindsight_retain` | `memory-core` | none (`auto-recall skipped: this session has no memory audience`) | no |
| `e4597199264`, `memory.sidecar: true` | loaded | + `hindsight_recall`, `hindsight_reflect`, `hindsight_retain` | `memory-core` | per turn: `POST .../memories/recall` and `POST .../memories` (retain) | yes, both turns |

Gateway log, `e4597199264`:

```
[plugins] memory-hindsight: running as a sidecar beside memory-core; memory_search and memory_get stay with it
[plugins] memory-hindsight: auto-recall source=fresh
```

No `no memory audience` lines appear. The `hindsight_*` tool factories return null only for the sessionless `tools.catalog` call, which has no audience by design, and not during the turns. The model sees a compact tool list in this setup (`tool_search`, `tool_describe` and core tools), so neither `memory_*` nor `hindsight_*` tools are listed directly and no tool call was exercised.

Upgrade from the latest stable release (npm `openclaw@2026.11.3`), one scratch HOME and state dir:

- Stable: `onboard --non-interactive`, `plugins install` and enable of the 0.9.0 plugin, slot kept on memory-core, `config validate` passes, Gateway starts healthy with `memory.status` provider `memory-core`, `doctor --non-interactive` exits 0.
- Branch on the same state and config, without `memory.sidecar`: `config validate` passes with the config unchanged. The state written by stable needs `doctor --fix` before the Gateway serves sessions (the agent database schema moved on main), and `doctor --fix` exits 0. After it, `doctor --non-interactive` exits 0, the plugin stays disabled (`memory slot set to "memory-core"`), and the Gateway starts healthy with `memory.status` provider `memory-core` and no `hindsight_*` tools.
- Branch with `config set plugins.entries.hindsight-native.memory.sidecar true`: `config validate` and `doctor --non-interactive` exit 0, the plugin is loaded (`enabled in config`), the Gateway lists `hindsight_*` beside `memory_search` and `memory_get`, and `memory.status` stays `memory-core`.
- Round trip: `config get plugins.entries.hindsight-native.memory` returns `{"sidecar":true}` before and after an unrelated `config set logging.level info`. The file on disk keeps `"memory":{"sidecar":true}` and `config validate` still passes.
- Stable 2026.11.3 refuses the same state dir afterwards because the branch (main) state database is at schema 40 and stable supports 22.

Tests (`pnpm test` on the changed test files): 84 passed across `loader.memory-sidecar`, `config-state`, `slot-selection` and `plugin-root-contributions`. The case-variant slot check asserts a literal decision (`{ enabled: false, reason: 'memory slot set to "mixed-memory"' }`). Audience gate: `attempt-memory-audience.sidecar.test.ts` (native owner granted; legacy owner without sidecar none, with no lineage read or lease; legacy owner with a loaded sidecar granted; sidecar setting off or plugin not loaded none; a turn the owner checks deny stays denied) and `memory-state.sidecar.test.ts`. The new tests fail on `a3fca384bdb` (3 failed: `expected undefined to deeply equal { kind: 'owner-private', ... }` and `hasLoadedMemorySidecar is not a function`) and pass with the change; with the neighbouring audience and memory-state suites, 93 passed.

`pnpm check:changed` on the branch: every step passes except the dead export scan. Its findings are all in files this branch does not touch (`scripts/lib/ios-behavior-grade.mts`, `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/mock-openai-ux-stream.ts`, `extensions/telegram/src/dm-topic-adopt.ts`, `src/node-host/node-worker-*.ts`, `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/link-steps.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-*.tsx`).

Not covered: a model-initiated `hindsight_*` tool call during a turn (the mock model does not call tools here), and a real Hindsight server (a loopback mock stands in).

prs.title: fix: preserve non-GitHub credential helpers in worker turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workers using a non-GitHub HTTPS remote can lose its configured credential helper when a turn prepares the managed GitHub identity.

Fixes #198461

## Why This Change Was Made

Worker turns now reset and install the credential helper only for `https://github.com`, preserving helpers for other HTTPS hosts. This follows the existing `managedGitHubIdentityEnvironment` and `GITHUB_PUBLIC_HOST` contract.

## User Impact

Managed GitHub operations keep using the turn identity, while other HTTPS remotes can authenticate through their configured helpers.

## Evidence

- The committed test launches the production worker CLI (`src/entry.ts worker`) with a fake Gateway, then runs real `git ls-remote` requests through a loopback TLS/CONNECT proxy. The checkout fetch and both HTTPS requests use that proxy; only GitHub and Forgejo are allowed. Credentials are random per run and no external network is used.
- Before: the validation-base binding runtime authenticated GitHub but Forgejo authentication failed.
- After: exact head `e4cd40e3070bfd5485c8cdca145243354f79a8f3` authenticated both hosts. The assigned GitHub identity and profile permissions were checked inside the active turn; the token was not printed or recorded in transcripts.

```text
$ pnpm test src/worker/worker.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testNamePattern='runs the worker CLI with the turn GitHub identity'
base 4cffd43ee043275f6a4c693aaacee8d8e5a61288: worker CLI authenticated GitHub; Forgejo authentication failed.
head e4cd40e3070bfd5485c8cdca145243354f79a8f3: worker CLI authenticated HTTPS: forgejo-authenticated, github-authenticated; loopback CONNECT: github.com=4, forgejo.example=2; profile active and assigned identity matched.
negative-control: GitHub helper remained !gh auth git-credential; credentials were absent from output and transcripts.
```

<details>
<summary>Repro: committed worker CLI proof</summary>

```ts
// src/worker/worker.runtime.test.ts
it.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")(
  "runs the worker CLI with the turn GitHub identity and authenticates managed Git access without publishing its token",
  async () =>
    await runManagedWorkerGitIdentityProof({ setup }),
);
```

The committed `worker-runtime-github-identity-proof.test-support.ts` starts the CLI process, holds the temporary profile checks inside the turn, and routes checkout and shell Git traffic through the constrained local proxy.
</details>

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): name invited members from their email and ask who they are on first visit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Someone invited to a claw through OpenClaw ID arrives as "Person c33358cb" when their account reports no display name, and stays that way in sessions, mentions and presence until they find Settings → Profile.

## User Impact

User impact: a newly approved member is named from the part of their email before the `@`, and on their first visit lands on a new session that asks for a name and then a photo before it offers a composer.

- Only invited OpenClaw ID members who have not chosen a name see the step. Owners, members whose account reports a name, and other sign-ins are unaffected.
- **Skip for now** keeps the email-derived name. The answer is saved with the member's profile on this Gateway, so they are not asked again on another device.
- The step replaces the composer on the new-session page and the chat page, and hides the starter prompts, so there is no other place to type. Nothing is sent to the agent or written to a transcript.
- An existing nameless member is named from their stored email on their next sign-in. A name someone chose is never replaced.
- Gated by the existing OpenClaw ID Labs switch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The name and photo are stored only in this Gateway's own profile. OpenClaw ID keeps holding just the account email; nothing is sent back to it.

The email-derived name is written to the profile when the member is approved, the same way an email sign-in is named, so every surface that shows a display name picks it up without a protocol change.

A member who still owes the step is taken from the default landing to a new session, because the main session is shared history. An explicit link to another session is kept, and the step replaces that session's composer.

## Evidence

**Before**: a newly approved member lands in the main session with an ordinary composer.

![A newly approved member in the main session with an ordinary composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f244bf98-8f16-4a6c-8adc-ce355559e7b5)

**After**: the same arrival lands on a new session and is asked for a name, then a photo.

![The new-session page asking a new member for their name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86eb191c-a27e-4329-8d7d-e72adceffb7e)

![The photo question after the name is saved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/727b9cd9-0d41-4c17-9e72-322636c71b95)

![The name question in a phone-sized chat page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55ea2dff-a666-4200-af35-1c9671ed10e3)

The screenshots are from the live runs below and show throwaway staging accounts. The "before" capture is from an earlier commit of this branch in which the chat page was still unchanged.

**Live proof.** An isolated Gateway on a Mac Studio, linked as a throwaway staging claw, with real Chromium browsers for the owner and two invited members over the tunnel against staging OpenClaw ID. 12 of 12 steps passed on `ca209c9d44cc`:

- an approved member is named from their email, never "Person";
- the member lands on `/new` with the name field focused and no composer rendered at any point before answering;
- name and photo reach the Gateway profile and the owner's Access page shows the new name;
- a reload goes straight to the composer;
- a second member on a phone-sized browser skips and keeps the email-derived name;
- an owner device gets the ordinary composer.

That run predates the rebase and the three review fixes below; it was not repeated on the final head.

**Tests on `8af5af5bf4fc`:**

- `src/state/user-profile-openclaw-id.test.ts`: the new naming case fails without the worker change and passes with it.
- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/member-welcome.test.ts`: who is due the step, the answer saved with the profile and honoured in another browser, dismissal when browser storage cannot be written, the one-time landing, and re-asking after a reconnect (fails without its fix).
- `ui/src/e2e/openclaw-id-member-welcome.e2e.test.ts`: the built Control UI against a mocked Gateway at 1280 and 390 px, covering landing, both steps, keyboard activation of the photo button, the kept explicit link, and reload.
- Existing new-session, chat composer, bootstrap and OpenClaw ID member suites, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint on changed files, the Solid guard, i18n verify and format check pass.

**Review.** One independent agent review (GPT-6 Astra, high reasoning) of the full diff at `7d95b4259654` against its merge base, with a read-only checkout. No P0 or P1 findings; three P2 findings, all verified and fixed in `bde3f05985ac`:

1. A page mounted before the bootstrap config arrived kept the composer.
2. A status read lost to a dropped connection was not retried after reconnect.
3. The photo upload could not be reached from the keyboard.

The fixes were not re-reviewed. Local ClawSweeper was not run.

**Follow-up to the hosted ClawSweeper review of `bde3f05985ac`** (in `b8d4f0d1e2e8` and `8af5af5bf4fc`):

1. Chosen name equal to the email's local part: the member's answer is now a profile preference (`ui.openclawId.memberWelcomeAnswered`), read before the step is offered, so naming or skipping on one device ends it everywhere. A member whose account reports a name equal to their email's local part, and who has never answered, is still asked once.
2. Dismissal no longer depends on browser storage; a failed write is ignored.
3. Avatar validation failures show recovery copy instead of the internal code.
4. The welcome modules are assigned to the existing boot groups (`ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json`), which restores the chat boot request counts. The byte budgets are still exceeded; see Gaps.
5. Upgrade: no schema or stored-format change. The profile test covers an existing nameless profile being named from its stored email on the next sign-in, and a chosen name being kept.

CI unit failures on `bde3f05985ac` in `chat-composer-video.test.ts`, `chat-composer-context-retention.test.tsx` and `hosted-environment.test.ts` were caused by this PR and pass now: the composer crashed where a test supplies an application without a config owner, and the new-session composer is now handed through untouched when no welcome stands in.

**Gaps:**

- Control UI byte budgets: `main` already exceeds each cap, so the check allows no growth. This PR adds under 1 KiB gzip of JavaScript and about 0.4 KiB gzip of CSS. No budget was raised.
- These tests fail identically on `main` when run locally and are not changed here: three cases in `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`, and the e2e files `composer-layout`, `mobile-new-conversation`, `chat-composer-size`, `new-session-page.model-catalog` and `new-session-page.prompt-attachments`.
- Dark theme and Safari were not captured.
- A failed photo upload is not covered by a test.
- The late-config fix has no test of its own.
- A member whose first page is neither chat nor new-session sees no step until they open one of those.
- Mention chips and message sender labels written before a member chose a name keep the old text; that is unchanged here.

prs.title: perf(sessions): backfill historical transcript facts after readiness
prs.body:
Approved by Peter (2026-11-07, question tool): "Approve + merge". Ships in the next Team build after landing.

**Refreshed onto `51c2f42a8e029f667829c753d7098af911dd7f70`. New cron-model measurements and refreshed validation are identified first under Evidence. All other runtime measurements below remain historical evidence from `fe435de371195768a35f26bfe9f4875c8482ef50` or their explicitly named earlier head. The previously reported multi-second shutdown tail remains unresolved; this refresh does not claim to resolve it. The TS session merges after validation.**

## What Problem This Solves

Schema 41 (#193682) accelerates transcript hydration through active-event facts, but ordinary appends populate only a recent window. Long sessions written before the upgrade retain uncovered historical rows and miss the full benefit. This adds the separately requested paced backfill within the existing database worker and post-ready maintenance owners.

## User Impact

Backfill starts after the existing startup-methods barrier and restart recovery, never inside database opening, migration or readiness. It processes recently updated sessions first (seven days), largest paths first within that group, then older paths by size. Each session stays selected until covered or skipped. Live runs and unrelated Background/root work do not require global idleness; background writer admission waits outside the foreground FIFO until existing work drains. The supplied Team observations found full idleness in only 0.97% of samples (median 14 active items). That factor no longer multiplies completion time: after recovery, eligibility depends on foreground writer admission and pacing, not active-run count. Measured busy-workload rates remain conditional; continuous foreground writes can still delay background admission.

One Gateway-lifetime callback deduplicates canonical physical database paths across normal and deferred startup. Each pass retains one V2 client and closes it on completion, failure or shutdown abort. Progress reports include filled/skipped rows, visited/remaining sessions, payload bytes, maximum batch time and contention pauses. Restart derives coverage from the existing facts primary key; there is no durable cursor or sidecar.

Transactions use the writers' existing derivation helpers and recheck current active-row identity/payload together. They skip cold, rebuilding, ineligible, changed and malformed rows; missing remains unknown, while `{}` remains a known non-candidate. The identity query finishes before inserts, retaining at most 512 small identities. Payload work targets 10 ms, at most 16 rows and 128 KiB before yielding. An indivisible payload read or commit can exceed those soft limits.

Cadence charges the larger of native transaction duration and **complete admitted publication execution**, including preparation and reply delivery but excluding foreground FIFO wait. The next delay is at least 250 ms and twenty times that cost; lock-contention backoff reaches five seconds. A foreground arrival can still wait behind one admitted publication. These are pacing controls, not a hard transaction or shutdown deadline.

The backfill uses the existing empty derived-cache write scope: equivalent facts preserve semantic actor/replica tokens, while native mutation witnesses and database-wide write tracking remain intact. Ordinary transcript mutations still invalidate. There is **no schema, index, stored-shape, configuration or retention change**. This background pass is SQLite-only; PostgreSQL retains ordinary writer population and reader fallback pending a separately measured locking protocol.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing readers substitute these facts for the same payload-derived byte counts and dependency navigation. Filling them therefore removes repeated historical payload work without changing hydration results. The implementation reuses existing scheduling, admission, transaction and invalidation contracts rather than introducing another maintenance manager.

Qualification found two consequential boundaries. Native batch timing omitted admitted preparation/reply cost, so pacing now charges the complete publication. Facts-only inserts also unnecessarily invalidated semantic session state. Merely declaring an empty scope was insufficient while a native identity iterator remained open: the observer correctly treated nested writes conservatively. Finishing that bounded query before inserts preserves the intended derived-cache contract without weakening any observer or reader. This changes batch work and requires fresh final-head measurements.

Runtime production growth is **+532 lines** (+536/−4), necessary for the requested maintenance operation, lifecycle integration and observability. The requested broader non-test/non-doc filter is **+2,774 lines** (+2,825/−51), including reproducible performance tooling; the exact regression allocation is **558 lines**.

## Evidence

**2026-11-13 refresh — current-head proof.**

Rebase replayed the existing twelve lane commits cleanly. Main is now agent schema 42 (the opt-in tool-usage table); active-facts storage and semantics are unchanged, and the backfill has no schema-41 equality assumption. Auditing every active-row mutation owner found no new writer: append callsites now add mention membership and tool-usage side effects, and cold restore changed its execution custody, but all preserve the same facts derivation/invalidation owner. Existing append/rewrite/branch/delete and cold/archive/restore interleaving tests cover those transitions.

The backfill kernel, pacing wrapper, worker-store addition and startup-session scheduler are byte-identical to the approved head. Background FIFO admission and post-ready/RestartRecovery gates remain compatible with main's lifecycle changes. No selection, schema, stored-shape, or pacing change was needed; the conditional direct-owner contention rerun was therefore not triggered. Earlier foreground/Gateway/shutdown numbers are retained below, not presented as remeasured.

**Refreshed cron-model facts evidence**

Production source was rebased onto `51c2f42a8e029f667829c753d7098af911dd7f70` before these runs (refreshed production head `091dc56a38a55e19f62a70b2a55f8bb8ed392f8c`; final head `129b947470a5fc282eb9bca554c5257613625bb1` adds only the proof tools). The backfill kernel and pacing were unchanged. Node 26.12.1; source/probe hashes, each raw sample, process receipts and host loads are retained beside this report. The final `inspect` mode was added after comparative measurement. A subsequent script-only typing fix uses a static import for the cohort unique symbol and binds the first result before comparison callbacks; neither changes the measured workload or production code.

These fixtures use real `persistSessionTranscriptTurn` writes and `SessionManager.appendCompactionAsync`, then copy the closed synthetic database on SF1 and delete facts outside the last 512 active rows. They contain alternating ordinary user messages and excluded assistant dashboard posts in historical rows, with an ordinary final tail. This is a declared synthetic composition, not an inference about Team’s excluded-row fraction. There are no unresolved pending automation results, custom/reset/branch-summary events, malformed rows, cold archives or off-path branches.

| Shape | Stored rows | UTF-8 bytes | zstd bytes | Compactions | Final retained tail | Excluded historical rows / UTF-8 bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| frv | 48,111 | 624,353,820 | 220,095,076 | 15 | 726 rows / 9,165,745 B | 23,685 / 307,983,172 B |
| shellbench | 13,971 | 136,515,581 | 48,025,825 | 18 | 181 rows / 1,791,835 B | 6,886 / 67,473,136 B |

Tail counts include one compaction summary: FRV has 725 retained messages plus summary; ShellBench has 180 plus summary. The header is additional. The production default cron limits are 1,024,000 bytes and 10,000 events, so the open deliberately returns less than the whole tail.

The measured entry point is `SessionManager[sessionManagerOpenTranscriptCohort]` with caller `cron-model`, the production limits and an empty-ID/message-presence cohort. This matches the owned-reader branch of `attempt-session-prepare`, without an initial user-turn entry lookup. It dispatches the real `readSessionTranscriptHydrationRequest` worker and `readSessionTranscriptBoundedActiveContextCore` owner. The alternate `SessionManager.openAsync` smoke produced exactly equal entry hashes, model-message hashes, VFS bytes and facts counts in all three states.

Five fresh-native-reader opens per state ran in ABC/CBA order, serially. Closing the DB owner between opens also includes worker preparation in CPU/wall. All first samples are retained; no OS cache eviction is claimed. Exact-target VFS xRead bytes are **logical SQLite I/O**, not physical disk reads; repeated reads count. The opt-in probe forces xFetch misses so mmap cannot bypass counters. Atomic counters capture worker reads. Physical process counter deltas are separate and include code/supporting activity.

| Shape/state | VFS logical bytes/open, median | SQLite read spans | CPU ms, median [min–max] | Wall ms, median [min–max] | Hydrated events / manager entries / model messages |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| frv / before | 204,197,496 | 49,873 | 2095.0 [1915.5–6424.6] | 2507.3 [2173.5–9209.1] | 82 / 81 / 81 |
| frv / after | 19,000,952 | 4,659 | 1867.0 [1696.2–2261.0] | 2180.9 [1934.4–2852.5] | 82 / 81 / 81 |
| frv / natural | 19,000,952 | 4,659 | 1903.2 [1782.2–1916.3] | 2239.1 [2075.4–2472.8] | 82 / 81 / 81 |
| shellbench / before | 38,778,652 | 9,495 | 2003.1 [1821.2–5627.6] | 2316.1 [2157.8–7285.8] | 104 / 103 / 103 |
| shellbench / after | 6,784,796 | 1,684 | 1852.1 [1787.2–2226.4] | 2200.5 [2114.1–2548.5] | 104 / 103 / 103 |
| shellbench / natural | 6,813,468 | 1,691 | 1933.4 [1896.9–2105.5] | 2385.7 [2248.1–2557.2] | 104 / 103 / 103 |

Before means 512 natural-window facts. After means completed production backfill. Natural means all facts left by real writers. Every returned entry and final model message is hash-identical across states. All first before/after reads had 77,824 extra VFS bytes (19 spans) versus subsequent reads; these are retained. The FRV natural control is exactly equal to backfilled steady I/O; ShellBench natural differs by 28,672 B (seven spans), consistent with different fact-table page packing rather than missing semantics.

FRV VFS reduction is 90.69%; ShellBench 82.50%. CPU/wall include worker preparation and other fresh-open work; those components were not independently timed. The byte reduction is the decisive result, not a claim of equivalent production latency reduction.

**Residual reads and selection**

The completed reads do **not** collapse to only the post-compaction tail: FRV still reads 19.00 MB versus a 9.17 MB complete tail; ShellBench 6.78 MB versus 1.79 MB. They do eliminate the historical payload fallback. This is already the natural-writer result, not rows missed by the backfill.

Inspection repeats the real cohort open and asserts its entry and model hashes against all recorded samples. It finds:

- frv: header plus latest summary at raw seq 47,393 plus 80 messages at raw seq 48,031–48,110. All 48,110 active rows have facts; 47,598 were filled, zero skipped. There are zero off-path identities, pending automation-result facts, cold archives, custom/reset/branch-summary events or unknown facts. Full backfilled facts equal natural writer facts row-for-row. Relevant metadata tables and indexes occupy 29,745,152 B; the facts table alone occupies 10,698,752 B.
- shellbench: header plus latest summary at raw seq 13,798 plus 102 messages at raw seq 13,869–13,970. All 13,970 active rows have facts; 13,458 were filled, zero skipped. There are zero off-path identities, pending automation-result facts, cold archives, custom/reset/branch-summary events or unknown facts. Full backfilled facts equal natural writer facts row-for-row. Relevant metadata tables and indexes occupy 9,469,952 B; the facts table alone occupies 3,080,192 B.

`session-accessor.sqlite-active-context.ts` still builds the dependency CTE over excluded active rows (23,685 / 6,886), irrespective of compaction boundaries. With facts present, the CASE reads companion navigation and byte counts; its correlated transcript payload subqueries are not evaluated. Ordinary eligible identities are excluded from that candidate set. All generated excluded posts are non-pending, so there are zero materialized dependency payloads. The reader separately loads the selected header/latest summary/newest messages, gets logical parents and retention ranges from identities, and probes custom/reset cache-TTL metadata (none in these fixtures). Off-path and cold-storage reads do not occur.

This source-backed row attribution distinguishes selected payloads from history-sized metadata scans. The `dbstat` values are storage footprints, **not** an exact allocation of the 19.00/6.78 MB VFS reads to individual statements or objects. No per-object I/O trace was claimed. No backfill selection change or new stored shape is needed for this case; further shrinking the metadata scan belongs to the bounded reader.

**Ordinary-history control and Team implication**

A separate real-writer 2,001-row, three-compaction control with **no excluded history** returns 104 hydrated events / 103 manager entries / 26 model messages. Its VFS median is exactly 1,384,702 B and 365 spans before, after and natural. This explains the earlier neutral cron result: ordinary indexed history is already filtered before dependency payload reads. Missing facts matter for excluded history, not every old compacted transcript.

| Conditional workload at 30 opens/hour | Before | After backfill | Natural control |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| frv synthetic mix | 6.126 GB/h | 0.570 GB/h | 0.570 GB/h |
| shellbench synthetic mix | 1.163 GB/h | 0.204 GB/h | 0.204 GB/h |

These are bytes/open × 30, in decimal GB. The synthetic FRV baseline is below the reported 11–16 GB/h on Team; this does not prove Team’s exact excluded-row mix, fragmentation, context budget, pending-result retention or physical I/O rate. If Team’s excess reads arise from this same missing-fact dependency fallback, covering those rows should remove that payload traffic. The remaining metadata and selected-context reads persist. Unresolved pending automation results intentionally retain their payloads and were not modeled here.

Entry loads were FRV 23.86–27.05, ShellBench 19.24–24.65, ordinary control 28.96–38.12; no measured post-open load exceeded 40. A later non-timing FRV inventory attempt refused load 48.48 before opening and is preserved; a fresh inventory retry passed and joined. All comparative and inventory workers joined. Cleanup completed: 36 exact synthetic DB/WAL/SHM files removed (5,077,254,144 logical bytes; physical reclaim not measured). All JSON/Markdown reports, probes, scripts, raw logs and process receipts remain. `cron-cleanup-receipt.json` verifies every target absent.

Refreshed validation: 146 focused tests passed with one pre-existing skipped test across the worker/admission, native and real-worker facts/interleaving, cold restoration, scheduler/startup and restart-recovery files. Strict agents-sessions, state-logging, gateway-server and gateway-root test graphs passed, as did all four strict root partitions (`pnpm tsgo:test:root`) and the fixed-protocol export guard. The first refreshed CI found a proof-script typing error in its separate `tsconfig.scripts.json` graph: dynamic destructuring widened a unique symbol, and the result array was captured before inference. Both were fixed without casts or behavior changes; that exact scripts graph now passes locally, along with the repeated four root partitions. Changed-file formatting and script lint passed. Scoped production lint has only size-limit observations: startup-finish 701 lines (main 688 plus the approved integration) and worker manifest 706 (main already 703 plus the approved registration), against 700. The repository's existing GitHub policy makes these size rules advisory; no lint config, suppression, baseline or environment was changed. Main CI `43540256697` for the rebased base is green; these are local size observations, not an invented inherited failed-CI claim. No production code changed after the clean rebase.

Local Codex P0–P2 reviews of the proof tools and subsequent typing fix returned no accepted findings. An independent evidence review reconciled all 45 main/control opens and cleanup. Exact requested branch command `python3 ~/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --engine codex` completed clean on `129b947470a5fc282eb9bca554c5257613625bb1` (helper default P0 scope), with no provider/model overrides or inherited AUTOREVIEW_/CODEX_ overrides. The final new proof tools also passed the local P0–P2 review. Exact-head [CI 43545292660](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43545292660) completed successfully on `129b947470a5fc282eb9bca554c5257613625bb1` (53 successful jobs, 25 skipped), including `check-test-types` and all PostgreSQL conformance jobs. The TS session owns merging; this lane has not merged the PR.

Cleanup verified 36 task-owned DB/WAL/SHM files absent, 5,077,254,144 logical bytes removed (physical reclaim not measured). All 17 fixture/probe commands settled; the one inventory load refusal is retained separately. Reports, raw samples, source/probe hashes and receipts remain under `.local/buf706/revision6/`. No Team access, writes, load, deployment or database copies were used for this refresh.

**Historical qualification below.** These are the retained November 7 measurements, not new runs on the refreshed head.


**November 7 source and validation.** The previous handoff used head `fe435de371195768a35f26bfe9f4875c8482ef50`. Fresh Codex P0–P2 review and the exact requested branch review are scoped-clean. Five backfill cases pass on the final head, with strict session types and changed lint/format. The 28 projection/replica consumer cases passed before the final cursor correction; that correction does not execute in those cases, so this is reused earlier-head consumer evidence. Earlier admitted-timing validation passed 38 focused cases, relevant strict state/session configurations and all four strict root typecheck shards. Exact-head [CI 42391976242](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42391976242) completed **successfully on this exact head**. That November 7 CI gate passed; the older cancelled PR-context run was superseded by a successful same-head run. At that handoff, the separate harness PR had a documented inherited test-line-ratchet failure; no CI was rerun to chase green.

Regressions cover historical coverage, restart, writer interleavings, cold transitions, malformed data, readiness/recovery ordering, live-work progress and shared-physical-store deduplication. The original post-ready regression fails on the schema-41 base. Timing regressions distinguish 1,000 ms of FIFO wait from 100 ms of admitted work and preserve publication success/original failure if observation throws. Final native and real-V2 regressions prove facts growth with an unchanged semantic token and advancing database revision; an actual transcript rewrite still invalidates. The token regression fails on the preceding implementation.

**November 7 Gateway qualification.** Baseline is `4f132c9f661b714cb2786da748294cd30dfd972f`. Separate tooling uses the canonical harness plus [#194563](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194563), `bf33a13ead512afb903ca191dfece9b6accd2bef`, for bounded retryable startup-sidecar refusal handling; that repair is not part of this branch. All proof is synthetic and isolated on SF1. Entry load must be ≤40; pauses/outliers are retained.

| Final native-owner measurement | `fe435de3` result |
| --- | --- |
| 49k-path missing facts filled; transaction count | 48,488; 6,208 |
| Paced wall / CPU; native hold p50/p99/max, n, holds >50 ms | 27.515 min / 54.536 s; 10.447 / 16.688 / 148.116 ms, n=6,208; 3 holds >50 ms |
| Logical reads/writes; process physical reads/writes | 1,739,554,816 / 72,905,624 B; 1,476,481,024 / 282,144,768 B |
| WAL peak / checkpoint snapshots; RSS / heap; host load | 523,272 B; both complete, zero consecutive blocks/no warning at capture; 323.44 / 94.03 MiB; 4.23–35.77 |
| Restart covered-prefix work; completed-path rescan wall/CPU | 20 batches, 10,240 identities, zero payload/fills; 48.248 ms native / 57.295 ms CPU. Full rescan: 96 batches, 24.308 s paced / 345.167 ms CPU, zero payload/fills/logical writes |
| Native-model rows/hour and conditional missing-row durations | 105,734/hour; 49k path's 48,488 missing rows: 27.515 min; 1M: 9.46 h; 6.27M: 59.30 h. **Not a Team forecast or host cadence** |

The native fixture has 10M active rows, 40,236 sessions, fragmented overflow chains, four 20k–49k paths and a 21.75 GB file. Only selected paths are filled. Final runs use production NORMAL synchronization and disabled automatic checkpoints, with a fresh process at the predeclared restart. Native modeled cadence is distinct from the real host's admitted-publication cadence. Materialized-but-unconsumed identity rows count toward measured CPU/I/O even when excluded from `rowsVisited`. No hydration warmup ran; OS cache state was uncontrolled, so this is not a paired comparison with the earlier warmed native campaign. All 6,208 sampled loads were ≤40. Native holds over 50 ms were 55.916, 86.480 and 148.116 ms; the largest used 10.686 ms CPU and 10.764 ms kernel time, with the remaining elapsed time unattributed. Mean batch CPU was 7.763 ms and mean modeled delay 253.328 ms (max 2,962.315 ms). Process physical writes include diagnostics; checkpoint snapshots are not cumulative blocked-attempt counts. WAL was zero after both native closes. Only this selected path was filled, not all 10M rows. Scaling this native shape to 6.27M missing rows implies about 117.5 CPU minutes, 224.94 GB logical reads and 9.43 GB logical writes. These are conditional estimates, not Team physical I/O measurements. Tiny paced transactions and repeated identity/current-row checks cost substantially more CPU and page writes than the earlier coarse 512-row proposal; that prototype is not an equivalent production algorithm.

| Final foreground proof: four A/A pairs + AB/BA + one predeclared extra pair, 1,000 append/read samples per arm | Idle → backfill / signed paired delta |
| --- | --- |
| Append request p50/p99; writer execution p99; queue p99/max | 7.090→7.557 / 26.213→44.144 ms; 26→39 ms; 0→10 ms paired queue p99; candidate queue maxima 257/110/257 ms |
| Nonresident read p50/p99; writer execution/queue p99 | 5.956→6.297 / 22.060→42.172 ms; execution 22.333→38 ms; queue 0→10 ms, candidate maxima 111/159/108 ms |
| A/A request-p99 delta ranges; load | Append −12.100…+16.292 ms; read −16.164…+6.837 ms. All gates qualified; in-window load 9.89–35.45 |
| Actual host-paced rows/hour; conditional missing-row durations | Mean 49,983/hour; 49k path with 512 facts: 58.21 min; 1M: 20.01 h; 6.27M: 125.44 h. **Direct-actor shape, not a Team forecast** |

Queue-p99 target ≤15 ms passes on the signed three-pair mean; individual append queue p99 values were 7/15/8 ms and read values 7/16/7 ms. The 16 ms read arm remains included. Initial request baselines differed by >6×, triggering exactly one predeclared extra pair. All three request-tail differences were positive: append +22.314/+29.709/+1.768 ms; read +17.070/+38.595/+4.672 ms. The observed mean request increases (+68.4%/+91.2%) exceed numeric adverse thresholds, with noisy A/A controls limiting causal precision. This is **not a neutral result**. The queue target passed, so no slower pacing curve was triggered and runtime pacing stayed unchanged.

| Host-paced candidate arm | Midpoint / measured fills | Returned delay mean / max | Rows/hour |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AB | 100 / 372 | 465.155 / 5,154.416 ms | 43,743 |
| BA | 286 / 596 | 424.248 / 3,190.603 ms | 42,990 |
| Extra | 99 / 413 | 425.168 / 5,158.898 ms | 63,217 |

Delay medians were 250 ms. Arm BA added three more facts during drain, excluded from its measured rate. All arms started with 512 facts and remained unfinished. The backfill's domain reservation explicitly blocked all six maximum-queue observations; maximum batch publication occupancy was 258/110/258 ms, distinct from native transaction timing. Cadence includes that occupancy, but does not bound an individual foreground wait. Seven sparse 49k reads per arm were context-only: median 171.270/180.245/171.503→179.177/195.630/176.388 ms, with initial/max reads up to 22.481 s retained. The 600-row foreground append tails are not long-session append tails. All fourteen children joined and their copies were deleted.

**Final whole-Gateway result.** All eight ≥10-minute arms completed: timing AB/BA and separate allocation AB/BA, with 320 primary turns/tool calls/results and 80 distinct completed native children total. Every arm retained all four long transcript paths and completed 40 primary turns/tools plus 10 native children. Candidate backfill progressed strictly inside every measured interval and remained unfinished at shutdown.

Timing CPU was 8.256→8.133% with opposite pair signs; this is **not a verified CPU win**. GC was 0.214587→0.179349 s/min. Append queue p95 was 32.5→27.5 ms; p99 rose 235→280.5 ms but is context at 660 samples/arm. Endpoint RSS/main heap rose 77.018/39.098 MiB; old-generation growth rose 26.059 MiB and settled old generation rose 3.335 MiB. These are distinct observations, not interchangeable memory statistics.

Allocation was 29.861974→31.171270 and 30.554461→30.199522 MiB/s: mean **30.208217→30.685396 MiB/s (+1.58%)**, with opposite signs, so **inconclusive**. Host imbalance limits causal interpretation of apparent timing improvements. The final allocation baseline had two sampled minutes over load 40 (maximum 42.06), after passing its premeasurement gate at 11.20; they remain included under the predeclared entry-gate/no-mid-window-filtering protocol. Traced latency/GC is context only. No predeclared extra GC/pause A/A condition triggered; per-kind totals, counts and both maxima are retained below.

Strict timing fills of 20,250/26,636 over actual 600.013/600.007-second intervals imply 121,497/159,814 rows/hour, mean **140,656/hour**. These are conditional estimates, not measured Team physical-I/O throughput or continuous 99%-busy occupancy. The direct-actor proof's 49,983/hour (58.21 min / 20.01 h / 125.44 h) and fragmented-native proof's 105,735/hour are different workload models, not a confidence interval. Four identical-base A/A pairs were 174/140, 121/127, 128/622 and 138/131 ms: means 140.25→255.00 (+114.75 ms), medians 133→135.5, maxima 174→622; original loads/timestamps remain separate.

The original fourth candidate took **6,276 ms**, including **5,378 ms in plugin-service cleanup**. Its following baseline was refused at load 50.14, making that whole pair invalid; the slow candidate remains a standalone observation. The baseline's 902 ms cleanup is not a measurement. A fresh whole pair replaced it, without erasing or re-pairing that tail.

Five symmetric diagnostic pairs on exact base/final head were 165/159, 130/637, 122/640, 184/285 and 134/129 ms (means 147→370, +223 ms; maxima 184→640). All expected spans completed without drops. Facts-client closes were approximately 7 ms, and native closes approximately 18–57 ms; these spans overlap and are not additive. Two candidate runs had unexplained 531/533 ms gaps between native close and first plugin service. A later untraced baseline also had a roughly half-second delay. Normal logs omit individual steps below one second. **No diagnostic run reproduced the multi-second plugin-service stall, so its cause is unresolved and no causal fix is claimed.** Instrumented runs are not pooled with untraced qualification. All diagnostic and shutdown children joined and private temporary state was removed.

Earlier dedicated shutdown pairs included a 9.4-second candidate tail: base/candidate means 1,115.8/2,978.4 ms. Four quieter A/A pairs and a 533→256 ms diagnostic pair did not explain it; plugin-service cleanup was the aggregate location, not a proven backfill cause. Those results predate the final correction and do not establish unchanged final shutdown or a causal fix for the old outliers.

No Team writes, load, deployment or database copies occurred. All final Gateway children joined and private temporary state returned to zero. The five 21.75 GB native fixture databases and ten sidecars have been deleted (108.736 GB logical size, with APFS sharing; physical reclaim not measured). Cleanup also removed 470 arm fixture directories, six template fixture directories and eight task-owned runtime build archives (35.063 GB logical files; physical reclaim not measured). All targets are verified absent. Reports, raw evidence and ten allocation profiles remain; shared dependencies and UI attribution evidence were preserved. Peter approved this PR on 2026-11-07; the unresolved shutdown observation remains an explicit gap retained for the TS session's merge review.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native catalog adoption changing after an unchanged transcript notification, and avoids rebuilding the full local catalog snapshot on every such poll.

## User Impact

Catalog entry order and adopted-session links remain stable across unchanged notifications. Real title, timestamp, usage, binding, roster and configuration changes still refresh metadata. When multiple eligible sessions bind one native source, the adoption helper now consistently selects the greatest UTF-8 binary session key; this also resolves legacy cross-agent duplicates deterministically instead of using notification/enumeration order. Explicit ownership filtering and current delivery authorization are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The row owner deleted and reinserted every index membership on `put`, even when receiving the same row. That moved rows to the end of agent/store sets, while adoption selected the last matching row. The broad selection revision also retired snapshots for unchanged publications. Index replacement now changes only memberships whose keys changed, and the existing catalog cache retires through accepted selection publications. There is no second cache, new schema or configuration option.

Runtime production code grows by 39 lines because preserving index position requires distinguishing unchanged memberships from retired session-ID, parent and URL-slug memberships; duplicate-source resolution is now explicit. The repeated delete/reinsert path is removed. The older owner microbenchmark fixture also publishes the selection notification, preserving its cold/retention comparisons. The event-mix measurement script carries the reproducible event-mix workload in its own header; no shared perf README changes.

## Evidence

- Regression is red on current-main baseline `5f99927e134e19edee859794ae34a15f3c7b7b7e` (1 failed / 8 passed, 50.72 s wrapper), including #198566: an unchanged transcript notification changes the adopted key from `agent:main:second` to `agent:main:adopted`. Candidate preserves both order and snapshot identity; committed writes replace the snapshot. Replay response hashes intentionally differ because provider-visible catalog order is now stable; no byte-identical-output claim is made for the buggy reorder case.
- Seeded mixed-write differential test compares cached entries with the full-rebuild path across 120 timestamp/title/usage/binding/add/remove/config/fallback-agent steps. The same five-test snapshot file also passes with main’s original snapshot implementation (51.13 s wrapper), while the notification/adoption regression fails on main. Index coverage includes singleton alias isolation and session-ID, parent and URL-slug replacement. Deletion tests warm the snapshot before retiring an agent.
- Seven focused files: 54 tests passed, including real catalog handlers, selection/list ordering and real sidebar delta delivery. Final three amended files: 19 tests passed. Wrapper times: 245.19 s and 80.28 s respectively (compiler/setup dominates).
- Changed-file formatting/lint, production scripts typecheck, script-root test typecheck and matching gateway/plugin test typechecks passed. No new benchmark lint suppressions.
- Initial CI caught two no-op replay callbacks missing the connection-ID parameter in the production scripts type program. Reproduced locally and fixed their signatures; both script typecheck programs now pass. No cast widening/suppression or runtime change was needed.
- CI also caught a request-closure retention edge: the projection listener kept the first planning roster alive after replacement. Reproduced locally (2 retained objects), then isolated listener construction from request scope. Existing retention and snapshot tests pass (9 tests); after rebasing over #198566, all 18 catalog/resident/retention tests pass. Independent repair review is clean.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings, including the final test amendments. The configured autoreview route failed provider preflight because its provider did not match operator configuration; configuration was not changed.

Two separate five-round A/A-control/B passes, 240 catalog polls per arm: **1,200 calls per variant per instrumentation mode; 7,200 measured calls total**. Refreshed after the retention repair and rebase: base `5f99927e134e19edee859794ae34a15f3c7b7b7e` (includes #198566), candidate `fa47d7a5390c5e8ba756268ae2269cf8adefdfd3`. Each arm has 5,000 persisted rows across two agents, 16 active rows, 12 synthetic sidebar clients, unchanged runtime/transcript publications, automation publications, and real timestamp/title/usage commits. 24 polls represent one virtual minute; replay wall time is compressed.

| Metric (median of five rounds) | Base | A/A control | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Full rebuilds / virtual minute | 24 | 24 | 2 |
| Handler main-thread CPU, ms/call (untraced) | 2.1249 | 2.1305 | 0.7218 (−66.0%) |
| Handler wall p50, ms (untraced) | 2.0693 | 2.0590 | 0.5323 |
| Handler wall p95, ms (240 samples/arm, untraced) | 2.7157 | 2.7848 | 2.4638 |
| Snapshot-owner sampled allocation, MB/call | 2.4255 | 2.4219 | 0.6105 (−74.8%) |
| Whole-replay sampled allocation, MB/call | 4.8416 | 4.8533 | 3.0034 (−38.0%) |
| Total GC, ms/call (untraced) | 0.2704 | 0.2843 | 0.1537 (−43.2%) |
| RSS after, MiB (untraced; context) | 1253.4 | 1215.4 | 1170.0 |
| Heap after, MiB (untraced; context) | 315.7 | 324.2 | 282.7 |

Untraced signed paired mean CPU delta: −1.4239 ms/call (−66.0%); total GC delta: −0.1228 ms/call (−44.5%). Candidate CPU, total GC and handler wall p95 improved in every round. Round 5 A/A control was noisy (wall p95 8.39 ms, loop p99 88.60 ms); retained without exclusion. Every candidate max GC pause was under 15 ms and below max(50 ms, 2×base max). Loop p99 has fewer than 1,000 samples per arm and major GC has one collection per arm, so these are context only. Allocation-traced timing is also context only. No measurement samples or windows were discarded. A local orchestration print error after the first untraced arm was repaired; its completed JSON and all preceding arms were retained, then the remaining arms resumed.

The existing owner microbenchmark passes cold work-count checks (zero temporary mapped arrays) and retains **0 of 65 retired catalog arrays**. The real projection retention regression additionally proves publication releases the old roster without a subsequent request. Runtime production delta: **+39 lines**; total non-test/non-doc delta: **+132** (+91 benchmark tooling, +2 exact test-line allocation record).

Reproduce each allocation arm:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-catalog-selection-measure.ts \
  --event-mix --operations 240 --yield-ms 0 --allocations \
  --state-dir <fresh-synthetic-dir> --output <arm.json>
```

Omit `--allocations` for the separate timing/GC pass. Use the pinned base owners above for A/control and the candidate owners for B; same harness in both.

prs.title: feat(message): recommend one exact ClawHub plugin in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Template setup needs to recommend the exact plugin its author named, rather than a fuzzy search result. Server-started setup can also publish a card before live chat adopts its run ID; that card was saved but dropped from the live view.

## User Impact

Agents can show one exact ClawHub plugin card by package name, including during server-started setup without reloading. Official plugins keep Install; community plugins offer View details for normal review. Unknown packages show no card. Verified cards no longer add a redundant generated status caption; explicit caller text and lookup errors remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an exact-package option alongside existing ClawHub search, keeps intermediate card publication non-final when requested, and admits only native sequenced producer-owned intermediate replies before local run adoption. This is the foundation of the chat-based Template Add stack.

## Evidence

- Initial exact-card layer: 61 focused tests pass; five integration cases fail without the production change.
- Live admission repair: recorded-row regression changes zero cards to one; repository-standard integrated runner passes 65/65 across four files. UI typecheck and focused lint/format pass on that earlier snapshot.
- [Real full-stack before/after and View details proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198065#issuecomment-6843632949): real model, Travel Copilot 0.2.8, isolated Gateway. One community card appears in the original chat without reload, and View details opens the correct review page. No plugin installation or enablement occurs.
- Pending chat 120ms; durable admission event 6.28s; first visible reply 56.5s. These are different timing boundaries.
- The recorder preserved a stale-selector harness error after successful live-card assertions; screenshots confirm navigation. Intermittent screencast-size corruption means clean final-head video proof is still pending, not claimed complete.
- Production Gateways were unchanged. Existing screenshots cover the earlier live-card repair, not fresh final-stack installation or clean final-head video.

### Repair qualification at `c1c471f63b56ad6e5908058d4bebf4e87e080454`

The composition regression uses the supported `.node.test.tsx` lane and a narrowly scoped profile mock. Live admission and card decoding retain producer ownership, strict finality, imported-row exclusions, and serialized card field order. One required main integration updates the fixture to the current renderer API; no further main refresh is included merely for age.

- The complete strict paired UI performance command passes against `6d5e2dfb1b8919386abeb7442fa9152cdffc1485`: generated document **14,027 → 14,017 bytes**, below its unchanged **14,026-byte** cap. Chat JS is **1,315,225 → 1,314,978 bytes (−247)**; 21 requests remain 21. CSS bytes and its three requests are unchanged. Solid's native named-export lazy option removes the redundant promise/export adapter. No budgets were raised or generated files hand-edited.
- Affected card/lazy tests pass **26/26**, including the current listing while its body is pending. The current-renderer composition proof passes all **three** history/live/live-before-adoption cases. Earlier unchanged reader/admission/projection/boundary proof remains recorded separately: 97 passing cases.
- The owning line-cap gate caught outbound send growing from 700 to 702 counted lines. Moving its unchanged attachment-type normalizer into the existing payload-normalization module restores the gate without removing behavior. Existing payload contracts pass **21/21**, and execution/accepted-result tests pass **56/56** across three files. Their multi-lane wrapper reached its 120-second bound before completing the final message-tool integration lane: **77 passing cases, not a full command pass**.
- Line-cap and first-party mock-export ratchets pass. The isolation reason now sits immediately above its mock. The supported 116-line allocation explains independent transport/projection/admission/history/live/lazy boundaries; no assertions were removed. Four-file syntax lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- The delegated changed-check attempt reached its 150-second local-host bound after reporting the two repaired gate details. Narrow type-aware lint reached package declaration generation but hit its 90-second bound without source diagnostics. Full canonical compiler, lint, architecture and exact-head hosted checks remain required; they are not reported green.
- All five observed UI failures in [prior PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43544874316) match [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43540514362) by complete test name, assertion values and source location. The comparison uses actual tested merge `b42967fd7c785e798140b05275fd0eb1633e5b88`, not only the PR head. Failing test files, responsive styles, picker/view/controller helpers, test configuration and lockfile match; this attributes those observed signatures, not every transitive input or the new head's full CI.
- Caption repair retains paired handler proof: three unexpected-caption failures become **10/10** passing integration cases; 87 outbound/message cases passed on that saved patch. Final shipped caption proof and final-stack real installation/video remain open. No permissions, consent or installation policy changed.

prs.title: improve(ui): simplify Cmd+K project selection and mobile mode tabs
prs.body:
Related: #198316

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing a project in Cmd+K Compose requires opening New session settings first, and the mobile Search/Compose tabs fill the entire footer.

## User Impact

The project picker sits immediately to the right of Settings and opens directly. Agent, New worktree, and Remember settings remain in Settings. On mobile, Search and Compose are compact, content-width controls with the same icons, labels and selected-tab styling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing project and machine choices into their own popover, using the same draft selection and preference owners. Remove the nested Back navigation and its unused styling. Locked placement retains its existing explanation and recovery in Settings. Mobile mode tabs reuse the existing compact styling, and the footer height drops from 56px to 44px.

## Evidence

- 30 existing unit tests passed. All eight palette-creation E2E scenarios passed across the main run and the final focused device-case replay.
- Desktop (1280px, dark) and phone (390px, light) browser checks passed: direct opening, exclusive Settings/Project menus, search, Enter, Escape and return of focus.
- Selecting a destination updated the trigger and produced one creation with the expected device/workspace scope and complete prompt, while preserving the foreground conversation and draft.
- UI production build, scoped typechecks, lint, stylesheet lint and formatting passed. Independent P0–P3 review of the project-picker change found no actionable issues.
- After the mobile-only CSS adjustment, both existing mode-switch E2E cases and three browser scenarios passed (390px light, 320px dark and 1280px desktop). Touch activation preserves the draft, the tabs stay separated and desktop styling is unchanged. Mobile tabs are 32px tall rather than 40px and no longer stretch across the footer.
- The browser evidence uses the actual Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses. No live inference or physical-device test is claimed.

prs.title: fix(openclaw-id): reopening an approved invite link is refused as already used
prs.body:
Related: OCF-536 (Linear)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an approved OpenClaw ID member who reopens their already-used invite link from the same browser has the redemption refused as `invite_used`, with only a warn log on the Gateway and nothing on the owner's Access page.

## User Impact

User impact: a member who re-sends the invite they already redeemed, from the same account and the same device and peer keys, is accepted as a no-op instead of being refused. Reuse by a different account, by new keys, or by a removed peer is still refused, and the Gateway log now says whether the sender is already a member and whether the keys match. Invites approved before this change didn't record the approved keys, so reuse of those stays refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The protocol authority refused every redemption for an invite that wasn't open, and approval discarded the pending account, device and peer keys, so an exact replay couldn't be recognized. The approved keys are now kept on the invite record for the rest of the invite's lifetime. An exact replay is still fully signature-verified, then accepted with no state change and no events, and the Gateway skips the pending-request and report writes for that case. The browser still gets no reply telling it the outcome; the protocol docs now describe that gap. The loader-side fix is separate (claw-loader, OCF-535).

## Evidence

- Regressions in the protocol (`invite-replay.test.ts`) and `mailbox-reader.test.ts` failed before the fix and pass after it.
- Scoped runs: 31 protocol test files with 243 tests, plus the `mailbox-reader`, `service.invites`, `authority` and `claw-store.persistence` suites with 35 tests. All passed.
- The portable protocol, core production and affected test type checks passed. Lint and format on the touched files passed.
- An independent Astra review found no verified P0–P2 findings.
- Not tested: live browser and native-iroh paths (the iroh binding isn't available locally).
- After merge, claw-loader's vendored `openclaw-id-protocol` needs a sync to this commit.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: perf(sessions): expire idle transcript payloads
prs.body:
**Ready for TS review; this lane has not merged the PR.** Exact-head CI and independent review are clean. The measured benefit is a small reduction in idle message-content residency. Maximum-pause discrimination remains inconclusive because completed identical-build controls also trigger the safeguard; this is not a speedup or a clean maximum-pause claim.

Exact reviewed and CI-green head: `7b4c1c3537ce9d462400d9c666bbc38a43b6a767` (CI run `40761649914`).

## What Problem This Solves

Recent message bodies remain in the session actor replica after their sessions become idle, even when metadata readers are the only remaining consumers.

## User Impact

A small reduction in idle Gateway memory. Transcript bodies expire five minutes after the last actor handle closes; active handles and entry/snapshot facts remain intact. The first transcript read after expiry uses the canonical reader, so infrequently reopened sessions trade a cache hit for a reload.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing replica owner now owns one detached, unreferenced expiry timer. Metadata reads and receipt replacement do not extend idle message residency. This releases the history projection at its owner, without adding independent caps to provider conversion memos or changing transcript storage.

Runtime production delta: **+56 lines** (**+259 total non-test/docs**, including +202 measurement support and one extraction-inventory entry). The growth implements the missing idle lifetime; existing value-preparation helpers moved unchanged to keep the owner within its line limit. Test consolidation preserves every distinct assertion and offsets the regression: **net test lines −1**, ceiling unchanged. Benchmark support adds 202 lines to the existing harness, with usage in its header.

## Evidence

Frozen baseline: `76fc97e3765d8865a00e036e9868927ca6f1910e`; candidate artifacts contain only this runtime change on that base. The PR was rebased afterward; the changed runtime sources and harness are byte-identical to the measured versions.

The isolated built-Gateway reproduction used 10,800 background session rows, 40 bundled plugins, 170 long histories (73 child sessions), and four active turns during the final minute of a six-minute idle window. Each history contained 40 reasoning/tool cycles with 16 KiB signatures and 16 KiB tool-output payloads.

| Post-idle metric | Base | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Idle resident transcripts | 21 | 0 |
| Active handles | 4 | 4 |
| Retained actor snapshots | 25 | 25 |
| Owner-held physical content | 1.466 MiB | 0.128 MiB |
| Inclusive transcript data | 2.708 MiB | 0.140 MiB |
| Forced-GC main heap | 460.443 MiB | 457.796 MiB |

This is a **small 2.65 MiB live-heap improvement**. Post-work heaps matched within 17 KiB, and owner content matched exactly before idle and after reopening. Heap snapshots attribute the released content to the global actor pool → cells → transcript → message-content path. Content/data figures are inclusive physical unions, not exclusive dominator savings; native Blob backing is not included.

Both arms verified 344 primary provider requests. All 170 complete seeded historical wire prefixes matched across initial, held-active, and reopened turns, and across builds. Instructions/tools/pre-history digests changed zero times. All 170 history presentation prefixes stayed append-only. The regression also compares canonical stored event rows before and after expiry/reload; the live run did not separately reread raw durable encoding bytes. Live provider proof uses the mock Responses transport, not Anthropic.

Two counterbalanced pairs per mode, 6,000 measured reads per arm/mode. Timing and allocation sampling ran separately. CPU was mixed (+9.57%, −0.82%; mean-cost +4.34%); allocation fell 0.80%. These do not establish a speedup.

The canonical harness ran eight original arms: two AB/BA timing pairs and two separate AB/BA allocation pairs, at least ten minutes per arm, with 10,800 rows, 40 plugins, 65 WebSocket clients, four concurrent mock-provider turns, tool calls, native subagents, and sidebar/list/search churn. A longer untraced follow-up completed two efficacy pairs plus four identical-build A/A pairs: **12 arms, at least 20 minutes, 20 measured rounds and 80 primary turns per arm**. All completed telemetry, maintenance windows and pauses are included.

**The longer client list p99 increased 46.09% (37.608 → 54.940 ms), with sufficient samples.** Server handler means were approximately neutral (+0.014 ms / +0.21%, mixed signs), and handler maxima improved in both pairs. Identical-code controls also showed substantial client-tail variation. This does not prove the client effect is zero; it is disclosed rather than rejected on client list/loop p99 alone. Per-arm server latency and host load are below. Server histogram p99s are window ranges with roughly 113–128 observations/window, not pooled, sample-qualified arm p99s.

Original paired GC increased **40.688 ms/min**; longer paired GC increased **7.207 ms/min**, both below the 50 ms/min absolute materiality rule. CPU and allocation establish no speedup. Endpoint RSS/heap are not forced-GC retention measurements and are not a separate retained-memory claim.

**Maximum-pause discrimination remains INCONCLUSIVE, not passed.** Original base → candidate GC maxima were 72.527 → 508.273 ms and 37.050 → 37.419 ms. Longer base → candidate GC maxima were 90.885 → 193.062 ms and 39.860 → 71.932 ms. Protocol history is retained: the short controls stopped after two complete pairs when identical-code maxima already breached. During the longer campaign, a provisional first-arm maximum was mistakenly read as final; the complete pair is **309.254 → 389.799 ms**, which does **not** breach 2×. That interpretation was corrected, and the remaining predeclared arms were completed without discarding or repeating the four completed arms. The continuation source/side mapping was declared before its results and preserves efficacy AB/BA and control AB/BA/AB/BA order. A local launcher preload forwarded the existing fixed-round option only to the measurement harness; built Gateways did not inherit it. Artifact/source hashes and every arm’s 20-round/80-turn/duration acceptance were verified.

The verified few-MiB retention benefit is the reason to propose this change. The ~5% CPU/allocation exception is not met or invoked. The larger production heap-growth hypothesis remains unexplained. This lane requests TS review of the small memory win with the client-tail observation and inconclusive maximum-pause attribution explicit; it does not claim all performance metrics improved.

prs.title: fix: progress-card updates discard unrelated session caches
prs.body:
Related: #178731

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: updating or clearing a progress card invalidates cached session facts even when no session entry or transcript changes.

## User Impact

Progress-card updates and dismissals retain valid session-scoped cache receipts. Schema changes and real session mutations still invalidate them; authorization, commit admission, rollback, and dismissal revision checks are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

This is a narrow write-classification repair, not a demonstrated fix for the Codex child-completion authority failure discussed in #178731.

## Why This Change Was Made

The card writer leaves its affected session scopes unspecified, so card-only writes conservatively invalidate every tracked session scope. Certify an empty session-impact set only around the two card-row mutation sites. Keep lazy schema creation and the enclosing transaction outside those scopes, and restore any caller's enclosing session-write scope afterward.

The incognito memory actor is unchanged. No new cache, authority owner, retry, or guard exception is introduced. The production change is seven net lines; the existing worker regression is extended rather than adding another Gateway fixture.

## Evidence

- Before the repair, the public progress-card tool/RPC-handler path through the actual durable worker fails token preservation for both default and custom stores. The memory-kernel regression independently fails on the warm card update.
- After the repair, all 34 focused tests pass across the card kernel (11), real durable worker (7), incognito actor adapter (3), and SQLite scope owner (13). The final worker fixture also passes all seven cases after removing an unnecessary SQLite-only schema-admission call.
- Coverage preserves cold-schema invalidation, warm updates and clears, stale dismissal CAS, reset clearing, global write-revision advancement, enclosing session mutation invalidation, commit-denial rollback, FIFO behavior, and non-replay after a lost committed reply.
- Core production typecheck and the canonical other and gateway-root test typecheck scopes pass. Changed-file typed lint, formatting, whitespace, line-cap and test-line checks pass. The dedicated 64-line allocation covers the new receipt/scope-restoration regression and extensions to the existing real-worker test; the shared baseline is unchanged.
