prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.
- Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
```

prs.title: feat(compaction): make the summary character cap configurable
prs.body:
Closes #194408

## What Problem This Solves

`MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS` (16,000) is hard-coded: every persisted compaction summary — including preserved turns, split-turn context, tool failures, and workspace sections — must fit inside it, and no config key reaches it. The reporter's long-context production agent compacted 120k–241k-token sessions into ~4k-token summaries, with the `[Compaction summary truncated to fit budget]` marker on 66% of 117 compactions and 532 safeguard loss events over 22 days.

Plain language: the "keep a shorter version of the conversation" step writes its notes into a fixed-size notebook. On a big-window model the notes get cut off constantly, and there was no way to ask for a bigger notebook. Now there is one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cap is threaded from config instead of remaining a module constant: `agents.defaults.compaction.maxSummaryChars` (default 16000, schema-bounded 2000–200000) flows through `SettingsManager` → `CompactionSettings` → `CompactionPreparation.settings`, and now bounds the summary fitter (`fitCompactionSummary` gains an explicit bound parameter), the derived preserved-turns/split-turn budgets in the safeguard, the request-budget reserve probe, and the final persisted-summary cap. Explicitly setting `compaction.model` or unrelated behavior is unchanged; omission preserves the exact current behavior.

## User Impact

Operators on long-context models can raise the cap so compaction summaries stop losing summary tails, preserved-turn heads, and suffix content. Default behavior is byte-identical when the key is absent. Config docs and schema help text document the key.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on the latest main content this change is based on (every changed file verified as `main` + exactly this delta, byte-compared; config doc baselines regenerated from the same tree):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `settings-manager.test.ts` new test: `maxSummaryChars` override exposed via `getCompactionSummaryChars()` / `getCompactionSettings()` | green |
| `compaction-summary-cap.test.ts` new test: fitter honors a configured 4,000-char bound | green |
| `compaction-safeguard.test.ts` new test: preserved-turns section truncates with the configured bound and reports the `preserved-turn-head` loss | green |
| Red checks: reverting the fitter bound / the safeguard threading / the settings passthrough each makes exactly the corresponding new test fail | confirmed ×3 |
| Existing suites: `compaction-safeguard.test.ts` 33/33, `compaction-summary-cap.test.ts` 2/2, `agent-session-compaction.test.ts` 19/19, `settings-manager.test.ts` + `settings-storage.test.ts` 49/49 | all green |
| `docs/.generated/config-baseline.*` regenerated; counts = main + exactly the new core key (core 2639, channel 4003, plugin 5018) | verified |
| `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.core.json`: zero errors in changed files | verified |

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and git diff to analyze issue #194408, trace the constant's consumers through the safeguard, agent-core fitter, settings manager, and request budget, and implement the config plumbing. The implementer understands the code: `CompactionPreparation.settings` is the single seam that carries the configured cap to every budget consumer. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(tui): anchor delayed peer prompts before the earliest surviving reply
prs.body:
Fixes #131993

## What Problem This Solves

When a peer's prompt reaches the terminal after the reply it belongs to, the TUI prints that prompt *below* the reply instead of above it, so the scrollback reads out of order. The prompt now lands above the earliest reply of its run that is still on screen.

- Problem: `ChatLog.finalizeAssistant` rebuilt the run's tracked-reply set from the streamed/frozen segments only (`new Set(run.frozen)`), so finalizing a second reply for the same run dropped the earlier reply out of `run.finalized`. `addLiveUser` anchors a delayed peer prompt at the first component it still tracks for that run, so with the earlier reply untracked the anchor collapsed onto the newer reply.
- Solution: carry the run's already-finalized, still-rendered segments forward when it finalizes again.
- What changed: `src/tui/components/chat-log.ts` (one expression plus its comment) and the anchoring regression test, which now covers the retained *and* the pruned scrollback variants.
- What did NOT change: no new API, no change to session ownership or admission semantics, and no change to how a fresh stream replaces a previous reply (`updateAssistant` still clears the finalized set).

## Why This Change Was Made

The ownership contract already states that a delayed persisted peer prompt belongs before every surviving reply from the same run, including the earliest-surviving-reply anchor in `ChatLog.addLiveUser`. The tracked set was rebuilt instead of accumulated, so that anchor silently degraded to the newest reply.

- Best fix: accumulate the surviving finalized segments, which is where the contract already points. The only new input is the set the run already maintained one line earlier.
- Alternative considered: re-deriving the anchor from `userComponents`/transcript order at insert time. More code, second source of truth for the same ordering, and it would leave `run.finalized` still wrong for every other consumer.
- Risk / non-goals: a run now keeps tracking its visible replies for as long as they are rendered, so `run.finalized` is proportionally larger; entries are pruned when their component leaves the log and the run entry is released once it is empty. Cross-turn accumulation does not occur because `updateAssistantSegment` clears the set when a new stream starts. Not addressed: prompt ordering relative to *other* runs in the same scrollback.

## User Impact

Terminal users keep a causally ordered transcript: a prompt that arrives late — after a reconnect, replay, or peer continuation — is shown above every reply of its run rather than appearing after them.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(text): settle ownership after completed paragraphs
prs.body:
Fixes #181696

## What Problem This Solves

A streamed reply that began with a completed leaked plain-text tool call and then a paragraph re-projected the entire retained reply on every later delta. Visible output remained correct, but a 32 KB reply blocked the Gateway thread for roughly 12 seconds locally.

## User Impact

Completed tool calls now settle at the blank-line boundary, so ordinary prose after them streams with bounded work. The 32 KB repro drops from 12.3 s to 0.38 s and output remains identical to the canonical sanitizer. Nonblank LF and CRLF continuations retain the ownership cache instead of reintroducing repeated parsing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint ownership cache reused parsed ownership across a newly created blank line. The cached `retainStart` still pointed at the completed tool call, so `findTextCheckpoint()` kept returning the opening line and `projectPlainTextToolCallBlocks()` rescanned the whole reply for every delta.

The checkpoint now refreshes ownership on a genuine blank-line completion, treating a CRLF split across chunks as one line ending and ignoring ordinary nonblank lines. The shared reuse predicate remains stable, so settled XML output does not rescan the cumulative reply after each paragraph.

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway proof

A temporary E2E harness exercised the real Gateway `agent` / `agent.wait` path and reconstructed the `chat` subscriber stream. It used a mock OpenAI-compatible provider that emitted 4-character deltas. The completed-tool-call case sent `[tool:read] {}\n\n` followed by 29,717 characters of ordinary prose; the Gateway subscriber received the exact 29,701-character visible reply in 4,445 ms, with `containsToolCall: false` and the expected trailing `Done.`.

```text
GATEWAY_STREAM_PROOF {"label":"tool-call-prose","elapsedMs":4445,"deltaEvents":45,"inputCharacters":29717,"outputCharacters":29701,"outputSha256":"68486157a2e817c71dff9748a3ceeb7c417bb995bbefef4eddf08f52eacc719b","outputPrefix":"Answer paragraph with ordinary prose and no tool markers. Answer paragraph with ","outputSuffix":"no tool markers. Answer paragraph with ordinary prose and no tool markers. Done.","containsRuntimeMarker":false,"containsToolCall":false}
```

The same run also streamed 262,144 ordinary characters with exact output and exercised a split runtime marker; the marker was stripped. The temporary proof harness was removed after capture.

### Regression and work bounds

The original P2 finding is fixed at `14e30dd4`. A follow-up P2 showed that putting the blank-line invalidation in the shared predicate also disabled settled XML reuse; that is fixed at `8804f3ee` by refreshing only the checkpoint ownership cache. Production-projector assertions cover nonblank multiline tool-call continuations for both LF and CRLF.

```text
Base 9fae: LF 18671 ms -> expected 2 to be >= 512
Base 9fae: CRLF 16661 ms -> expected 2 to be >= 512
Base 9fae: reusable LF 7303 ms -> expected 512 to be +0
Base 9fae: reusable CRLF 7006 ms -> expected 512 to be +0
Base 9fae: split CRLF -> expected false to be true
Head 14e30dd4: 5 passed, 25 skipped
Head: LF 196 ms, CRLF 159 ms, reusable LF 21 ms, reusable CRLF 17 ms, split CRLF 2 ms
```

```text

fixed 8804f3ee: <16 rejected ownership-reuse checks
```

```text
base: 114,261,817 projected characters (budget 120,916)
head: 257,000 projected characters
```

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

prs.title: fix(text): bound brace checkpoint activation
prs.body:
Closes #182562.

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary JSON and brace-containing prose cause repeated whole-reply tool-call scans during streaming, delaying visible replies.

## User Impact

Ordinary braces keep their visible text without activating canonical tool-call checkpoints. Split calls are still removed, while fenced, inline, and indented code examples remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace bare-brace activation with a bounded incremental bracket-header probe beside the canonical parser. The probe delegates completed headers to that parser; the canonical transform retains ownership of valid names, payloads, Markdown protection, and removal. Existing Harmony/XML activation and replacement resets remain unchanged.

The complete PR adds 58/removes 3 production lines (net +55), adds 66/removes 2 test lines (net +64), and adds the 53-line benchmark. The bounded header/whitespace state avoids retaining or rescanning an accumulating reply. The follow-up adds no production code: it replaces overlapping terminal-only examples with a compact split-point parity table and retains the distinct long-whitespace regression. Original contribution by @xiaopan-xydt; contributor history is preserved.

## Evidence

At head `29d943b772f19e61b13c98ec59359b5a7cb89755`:

- A differential experiment ran **167 adversarial sources, 14,498 chunk schedules, and 45,893 observed prefixes** through the production visible-stream filter chain. Every two-chunk split plus one- and four-character chunkings matched the batch canonical transform in both projected text and delta replay. It includes tool/named headers, 119–121-character names, CRLF/CR, malformed headers, JSON prose, and literal code. The same corpus has zero divergence on the baseline. The committed 12-row parity table also has independent final-text expectations.
- The work-budget regressions fail on the baseline: 4 KiB ordinary JSON causes **2,048** canonical checkpoints and brace prose **2,044**. Both cause **zero** with this PR and preserve the expected text.
- **134 focused tests pass**, covering the parser, plain-tool text, production subscriber, streaming work, and the new parity table. Wrapper wall time: **54.44 s** across four shards. The new parity file took **1.45 s**, with about **0.12 s** of test work. The existing streaming-work shard took 33.94 s; the added table stays outside that expensive suite.
- Full `pnpm build` passed (11m 55.7s). Scoped production/test typecheck, type-aware core/script lint, formatting, diff checks, and max-lines/line-cap/assertion-safety/timeout-race/mock-export/config-doc/plugin-inventory ratchets pass. Independent Codex P0–P2 review of the complete canonical owner and branch diff found no actionable findings.

### Fresh performance comparison

Rerun the committed workload with:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/plain-tool-brace-measure.ts
```

Same workload frozen into baseline/candidate ESM bundles, five fresh processes per arm in serial ABAB order, 32 KiB inputs in 8,192 four-character deltas; Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64. Baseline `29423b6550865b31a2ef0ca635d0f11818801eda` has byte-identical measured streaming owners to fetched main `d9a5304a0c1dfeaf9a9ced403696537a40337e28`. Candidate production bytes match the current head. No builds, tests, typechecks, or lint ran in this checkout during the samples.

| Input / phase | Baseline median / p95 ms | Candidate median / p95 ms | Thread CPU median ms, before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| JSON / cold | 77.85 / 169.67 | 28.31 / 52.70 | 70.48 → 27.52 |
| JSON / warm | 58.27 / 94.43 | 22.07 / 31.53 | 55.51 → 21.29 |
| Brace prose / cold | 1862.58 / 2176.46 | 21.26 / 33.33 | 1719.19 → 19.80 |
| Brace prose / warm | 1743.07 / 3050.05 | 20.50 / 35.40 | 1689.86 → 19.45 |

Ranges (ms): JSON cold 63.65–169.67 → 27.80–52.70; JSON warm 52.71–94.43 → 21.59–31.53; prose cold 1692.50–2176.46 → 20.27–33.33; prose warm 1676.32–3050.05 → 20.30–35.40. Empirical p95 is the maximum of five samples. All samples preserved exact output and emitted zero replacement frames. Median process maxRSS fell from 169,856 to 115,456 KiB. The shared host's one-minute load was 61.1–63.6, so CPU and work counts support the wall-time comparison; these are not production Gateway latency estimates.

### Fresh shipped CLI and real local-model control

The final implementation passed a task-isolated `pnpm openclaw --profile probe-sweeps agent exec ... --config <fixture-config> --state-dir <isolated-state> --code-mode direct --thinking off --timeout 90 --json` run with the embedded OpenClaw runtime pinned on the provider.

The deterministic loopback Responses provider handled **one request**, sending **29 four-character deltas** declaring `final_answer`: brace prose remained, the CRLF-split tool call disappeared, and the fenced example remained byte-for-byte. The same fixture also passed on the baseline. No runner or sanitizer was mocked.

A second run forwarded OpenClaw's actual prepared request to local Ollama **qwen2.5:7b**. The model's unchanged answer was framed by the loopback Responses adapter as **30 four-character final-answer deltas**; the shipped CLI returned the exact original fenced JSON. This is a real local-model response to the actual OpenClaw request, with synthetic Responses framing to exercise the changed subscriber path. The adapter buffers the local response before rechunking; this does not prove native Ollama streaming/tool transport or Gateway throughput.

All state, workspaces, and provider listeners were isolated. The final CLI payload verifies delivery behavior; the committed prefix parity and work-budget tests verify the streaming contract and avoided scans. Validation is local macOS; no Windows timing claim is made.

Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40262333159) passed, including its `openclaw/ci-gate` job. The aggregate [`openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40263099772) is also green on this head.

ClawSweeper reports no code findings on this exact head; its remaining proof-only hold asks for inspectable CLI output beyond the summaries above. Local captures are retained for maintainer review; no additional proof/review cycle is being started.

prs.title: fix(infra): age crash-truncated lock files by mtime before declaring them stuck
prs.body:
fix(infra): age crash-truncated lock files by mtime before declaring them stuck

Closes #192981

## What Problem This Solves

A crash between lock-file creation and payload write leaves a 0-byte lock that `shouldRemoveDeadOwnerOrExpiredLock` never treats as stale (no pid, no createdAt), so the WhatsApp channel — and every other file-lock consumer — waited the full lock timeout and stayed down until the file was removed by hand.

## User Impact

After a power loss or hard kill in that window, the next start reclaims the abandoned lock once it is older than the stale grace instead of blocking the channel for 39 minutes; recovery also stops accumulating repeated restart failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

A payload with neither pid nor createdAt cannot prove an owner, but the current code keeps such locks forever. This change ages them by the lock file's mtime with the same stale grace an expired createdAt receives, and stays conservative when no mtime is available. Locks whose payload has a pid, or whose file was written recently, keep the exact previous behavior, so the legitimate create-then-write race is preserved.

## Evidence

- Focused run on latest main content: src/infra/stale-lock-file.test.ts 11/11 passed, including new cases (empty and `{}` payloads older than the grace are removed; fresh mtime and missing-mtime payloads are kept).
- Red check: reverting only the mtime branch fails exactly the new stale-empty cases (1 failed | 10 passed); restoring passes.
- file-lock.ts gains a statSync-based mtime read passed into the reclaim callback; adjacent file-lock-sync suite stays green (21/21 with the change).

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and module tracing to analyze issue #192981, locate the missing branch in src/infra/stale-lock-file.ts, and implement the mtime-based aging mirroring the existing createdAt-expiry semantics. The implementer understands the code: the create-then-write race is preserved by requiring the mtime to exceed the same staleMs grace. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep quoted-message media from redefining source_modality
prs.body:
fix(channels): keep quoted-message media from redefining source_modality

Closes #192253

## What Problem This Solves

A text-only Telegram reply to a photo reported `source_modality: "image"` in its per-turn Conversation info: quote media are merged into the turn's media list before the modality fallback derives from it, so the field described the quoted message instead of the current one.

## User Impact

Per-turn metadata that the prompt presents as reliable context now describes the actual message: a text-only reply no longer tells the model it came from an image. Channels that merge quote media without self-quote suppression (Telegram) stop mislabeling every such reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The derivation order made merged quote media win the fallback. This change pins SourceModality from the message's own media before quote media merge — defaulting to "text" for a text-only reply — and factors the media-to-modality mapping into a shared helper used by both the finalize path and the template fallback, so the rule exists in one place.

## Evidence

- Focused runs on latest main content: src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts and src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts, 49/49 passed, including new cases (text-only reply to a photo pins "text"; own media keeps its own modality).
- Red check: reverting only the pin fails exactly the two new pin cases (2 failed | 16 passed); restoring passes.
- Broader suites: src/auto-reply/reply and src/channels/inbound-event green (one pre-existing timing flake reproduced identically on pristine main without this change).

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and module tracing to analyze issue #192253, locate the quote-media merge in src/channels/inbound-event/context.ts and the modality fallback in src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts, and implement the pin with a shared media-to-modality helper. The implementer understands the code: quoted media merge into the same list the fallback derives from, so the pin must happen before the merge. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(slack): admit accessGroup senders in the direct-message gate
prs.body:
fix(slack): admit accessGroup senders in the direct-message gate

Closes #191048

## What Problem This Solves

Slack direct-message authorization lowercases the allowlist before matching, which turns `accessGroup:<name>` entries into unmatched literals. A group that admits a sender on Slack's command path (shared ingress) still leaves their DMs rejected.

## User Impact

A person listed through an access group can now direct-message the bot on Slack without being added as a literal allowlist entry — matching how the command path already admits them, and how other channels treat groups.

## Why This Change Was Made

`accessGroup:` refs are matched case-sensitively against the raw config list, so the lowercased DM list cannot express them. The edit expands the raw allowlist through the shared access-groups runtime (plugin-sdk `expandAllowFromWithAccessGroups`, the same helper the shared direct-DM path uses) and appends the sender's concrete id when a referenced group admits them. Unmatched groups keep the existing rejection and pairing flow; the Matrix half is covered by #191118.

## Evidence

- Focused run on latest main content: extensions/slack/src/monitor/auth.test.ts 30/30 passed, including two new cases (sender admitted through `accessGroup:` + `message.senders` group; sender outside the group still rejected and routed to the existing unauthorized flow).
- Red check: reverting only the expansion in dm-auth.ts fails exactly the admission case while the rejection case keeps passing.
- Full monitor suite runs green alongside the change (auth.test.ts 30/30; ingress suite exercised separately).

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and module tracing to analyze issue #191048, locate the lowercasing gate in extensions/slack/src/monitor/dm-auth.ts, and implement the expansion with the existing plugin-sdk helper. The implementer understands the code: the shared expansion matches `accessGroup:` refs case-sensitively, so the raw list must be consulted before the lowercased DM list. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(sessions): log unreadable transcript probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session activity monitoring silently ignores an unreadable transcript, so operators cannot tell a persistent permission or locking failure apart from an idle conversation.

When the transcript file cannot be opened for a reason other than "missing", the probe is now reported through the existing `plugins/session-catalog` logger. It remains retryable and is still not classified as missing.

## User Impact

Operators can see why activity detection has stopped working for an adopted Claude or Pi session, receive a concrete recovery step, and know that probing continues automatically. Healthy sessions and missing-transcript cleanup continue to behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared JSONL activity reader intentionally keeps non-`ENOENT` failures distinct from a missing transcript because marking them missing could eventually remove a recoverable upstream link. It previously returned `undefined` without logging, which made that deliberate distinction invisible.

The change adds a warning with recovery guidance at the existing catch site. It does not change the activity result, retry policy, marker, or link lifecycle. The focused test mock now documents its process-global logger isolation, and duplicate non-`ENOENT` table rows were removed.

## Evidence

Head-green focused regression:

```text

```

prs.title: fix(gateway): isolate scheduled runs from worker refresh scope
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Workboard automation nudges fail with "Plugin runtime changed" when a script-payload cron job runs after the worker that nudged it has ended.

In plain terms, a card-completion event could schedule the board's owner job, but that job inherited a permission lifetime from the worker that had just finished. The job therefore started and immediately lost permission to call its first tool. Scheduled and manually started runs were unaffected.

## User Impact

Event-driven Workboard automations now start with their own scheduler-owned lifetime instead of inheriting the ended worker's refresh scope. Scheduled runs, manual runs, tool restrictions, cancellation, and stale-tool rejection keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler already replaces Gateway caller, plugin registry, and request scopes, but it intentionally preserved unrelated ambient async context. One of those inherited contexts was the agent plugin-runtime refresh owner, so a queued run captured the closing worker's owner and every tool call rejected it.

The scheduler boundary now clears only the plugin-runtime refresh field before running detached work. A real agent run still creates its own refresh owner through the existing embedded-runner path.

## Evidence

Base-red behavior probe using the production refresh and scheduler owners:

```text
refresh_assert=Error: Plugin runtime changed. Continue with the refreshed tool catalog; do not repeat completed actions.
```

Head-green with the same probe:

```text
refresh_assert=ok
```

Focused regressions:

```text
src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts                    2 passed
src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.plugin-runtime-refresh.integration.test.ts  17 passed
```

The new regression holds the scheduled callback until the originating refresh owner closes, then verifies the callback no longer inherits that closed owner. The adjacent integration suite verifies real agent runs still reacquire generations and preserve run authority, committed work, and terminal results.

- `pnpm test src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.plugin-runtime-refresh.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/plugin-runtime-refresh.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/plugin-runtime-refresh.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Focused typecheck remains unavailable in this container because the pinned `tsrs` binary requires `GLIBC_2.34`; the host loader fails before project checking starts. A full Workboard card lifecycle was not run against a live Gateway, but the regression and production probe exercise the exact scheduler/refresh boundary that produced the reported error.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Codex). The scope came from #170985 and was validated against the real scheduler and refresh owners. No production data, credentials, or external services were used.

Closes #170985

prs.title: fix(setup): preserve the current model when activating saved auth
prs.body:
Related to #167381

## What Problem This Solves

Activating a previously saved auth profile failed with `The candidate route does not match the selected model` when the saved credential's starter model differed from the current agent model. The activation path staged the stored starter model instead of the model the agent was already using, so route verification rejected the candidate. If the models happened to match, activation could also overwrite the user's current model with the starter model. Discovery had the same mismatch: Model Setup forwards the discovered candidate model explicitly, so fixing activation alone was bypassed by the normal UI flow. Provider-qualified aliases such as `openai/Fast` must also be resolved to their canonical model identity or the same route check rejects a valid current model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Saved-auth discovery and `stageSavedAuthCandidate` now share the same model-selection decision:

1. An explicitly supplied `modelRef`.
2. The canonical current agent route model, when it belongs to the same provider as the saved credential.
3. The saved credential's stored model, preserving the existing cross-provider fallback.

Both paths call `resolveCurrentModelRefForSavedAuth`, which uses the existing setup route resolver. Configured aliases therefore resolve to the same concrete model identity used by the model-selection updater, and discovery advertises that canonical current model to Model Setup. The trailing auth-profile suffix is removed before comparing providers. API-key header configuration is applied to the provider of the resolved model rather than always using the saved starter model's provider. Credential and auth-profile binding behavior is unchanged.

The saved-auth route lookup is also scoped to the setup target. Previously it always resolved the primary route and cached by provider alone, so a credential chosen for the utility target could advertise the primary model and ordinary activation could promote a utility-only model to primary. Discovery and `stageSavedAuthCandidate` now pass `modelTarget` (`primary` or `utility`) into the shared resolver, and the discovery cache is keyed by provider plus target. A utility-only configuration therefore keeps its utility model while saved-auth activation still persists the selected starter model as primary.

## User Impact

Users can switch back to a saved sign-in without a spurious route mismatch, and activation no longer resets their current model to the provider's starter model. Cross-provider saved credentials retain the previous fallback behavior.

## Evidence

- Full target suites on the final head: `43 passed` across `setup-inference-activate.test.ts` and `setup-inference-saved-model.test.ts`, including both `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and the configured `openai/Fast` alias; `19 passed` in `setup-inference-detect.test.ts`.
- Discovery-to-activation regression: both cases call `setup.detect()`, assert the saved-auth candidate advertises the canonical current model, activate that candidate as Model Setup does, and verify the persisted model and inference call.
- Discovery base-red: with the previous discovery selection restored, both cases advertise `openai/starter-model` and fail before activation.
- Role-isolation regression: with only `agents.defaults.utilityModel` configured, detection advertises the saved starter model and activation persists that model as primary while leaving `utilityModel` unchanged.
- Type-safety hardening: the API-key header target uses the resolved model provider when a model is present and otherwise falls back to the saved provider, so `parseInferenceRef` never receives an optional model reference. The final-head model regressions pass (`2 passed | 40 skipped`).
- Formatting and lint: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` passed for all changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- Logs: `180832-final.log` (43 + 19 passed) under `contributions/pr-evidence-20261025/180832/` in the contributor workspace. Earlier logs remain under `contributions/pr-evidence-20261023/`, and the upgrade readback files are under `180832-live-proof/upgrade-20261023e/`.

### Real CLI behavior proof

On 2026-10-23 I exercised the shipped `openclaw` CLI in an isolated state directory against a local loopback OpenAI Responses provider. The state had an active `openai:baseline` credential and a saved replacement `openai:saved-proof` credential whose recorded model was `openai/starter-model`; the current agent model was `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`.

- A baseline `openclaw agent --local` turn authenticated with the baseline credential and returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1` on `gpt-5.4-mini`.
- `openclaw models auth activate openai:saved-proof --agent main` printed `Inference verified: openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and `Sign-in verified and saved.` It authenticated the probe with the saved credential, not the baseline credential.

prs.title: fix(update): report corrupt restart sentinel rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A present-but-unreadable restart sentinel row was treated as absent by the managed update helper. Operators lost the recovery context without any corruption-specific guidance. The helper now reports the shared reader's `invalid` state, keeps the row intact, and does not replay unverified context.

Closes #153501

## User Impact

After a failed managed update, corrupt JSON in `continuation_json` or `stats_json` now produces an actionable warning instead of silently dropping recovery context. Safe service recovery still proceeds, the malformed row remains available for inspection, and the warning is persisted in update history.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared reader already distinguishes `missing`, `valid`, and `invalid` rows. The helper consumed that state but returned silently. This change reuses the existing owner result rather than parsing or rewriting the corrupt payload.

The warning is logged and recorded as a run warning:

`Restart sentinel metadata is unreadable; preserved the row and skipped its unverified recovery context. Run openclaw update repair on the Gateway host, then retry the update.`

For a failed standalone CLI handoff without notification or exported triage metadata, outcome recording can finish before failure triage reads the sentinel. The helper now performs that existing failed-update capture before the terminal writer snapshots `runWarnings`, so the corruption diagnostic is included in the persisted run steps instead of only appearing in console output. That pre-terminal capture is best-effort: if reading the sentinel fails, the helper logs the diagnostic failure and still finalizes the recorded updater outcome instead of replacing its exit code.

## Evidence

- Added a managed-handoff regression test that writes truncated `continuation_json`, asserts the repair hint appears, and verifies the sentinel row is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The terminal-ordering regression asserts the persisted update run contains `warning:restart-sentinel-unreadable` with the repair guidance before the run is finalized.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-triage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14 passed. Both before- and after-recovery diagnostic read failures retain updater exit 7, finalize terminal state, and skip unavailable triage.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "persists a corrupt restart-sentinel diagnostic"`: 1 passed, 70 skipped.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 13 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm test src/infra/restart-sentinel.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 39 passed.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet pass.
- Test and core typechecks report only the pre-existing unrelated `src/snapshot/local-repository-directory-policy.ts:351` (`isVolumeRoot`) failure on `main`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): serve readiness probes through trusted proxies
prs.body:
Closes #182798

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: reverse-proxy readiness and startup checks return `403 proxy_attribution_required` when a configured trusted proxy cannot supply a forwarded client address.

## User Impact

Operators can health-check healthy Gateway backends from Traefik, ALB target groups, and other trusted proxies without fabricating an `X-Forwarded-For` header. Public probe responses stay aggregate-only; detailed readiness/startup diagnostics still require a local or authenticated caller, and every non-probe route retains proxy-attribution rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Headerless health checks have no client identity to attribute. The Gateway now serves the existing bounded ready/startup handlers before rejecting unattributable proxy ingress. `/livez` is also accepted as a liveness alias, matching the path reported in the issue and the documented liveness behavior.

## Evidence

- Base-red: the new trusted-proxy regression failed with `GET /ready: expected 403 to be 503`; see `contributions/pr-182798-evidence/base-red.log`.
- Fixed: the regression covers GET/HEAD for `/ready`, `/readyz`, `/startup`, `/startupz`, `/health`, `/healthz`, and `/livez`, including reduced bodies and `Content-Length`; a protected node route still returns `403 proxy_attribution_required`.
- Real listener proof: the shipped `startGatewayServer` was started on a loopback TCP port with a trusted loopback proxy entry. Requests carried a loopback `X-Forwarded-For` value, so ingress was classified as unattributable. All 14 GET/HEAD probes returned 200; `/ready` and `/readyz` returned `{"ready":true}`, `/startup` and `/startupz` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"started"}`, and the liveness aliases returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`.
- The same listener rejected the protected `/api/nodes/watch/node-1` request with `403` and `proxy_attribution_required`, proving the probe exception did not widen authenticated routes.

```json
{
  "entrypoint": "shipped startGatewayServer with a real loopback TCP listener",
  "probeCount": 14,
  "probeStatuses": { "GET": 200, "HEAD": 200 },
  "protectedRoute": {
    "path": "/api/nodes/watch/node-1",
    "status": 403,
    "type": "proxy_attribution_required"
  }
}
```

- Focused suites: `server-http.probe.test.ts`, `ingress-attribution.test.ts`, and `auth.test.ts` passed, 83 tests total; see `contributions/pr-182798-evidence/final-tests.log`.
- `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `check:changed` passed all runnable gates. Its typecheck lanes cannot run on this host because the bundled `tsgo` requires glibc 2.29 while the host provides 2.28; the dead-export lane also reports the existing repository-wide Knip baseline unrelated to these files. See `contributions/pr-182798-evidence/check-changed.log`.

prs.title: fix(sessions): reuse PostgreSQL model-context navigation cache
prs.body:
Closes #183363

## What Problem This Solves

Bounded conversation reads repeatedly project the full PostgreSQL transcript even after its model-context navigation has been cached.

## User Impact

Warm PostgreSQL history reads reuse existing navigation, and an append refreshes only the changed range. Writable transactions still bypass the cache.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared cache guard treated every PostgreSQL transaction as dirty. The existing registered read-only snapshot scope already identifies transactions that cannot publish writes, so the fix uses that owner rather than introducing another cache or transaction flag.

Original implementation and regression by @xiaopan-xydt. The simplification pass retained the focused two-file change. Production delta: +2 lines (the explanatory comment); test delta: +44 lines.

## Evidence

- Independently reproduced against unchanged main owner code using a disposable PostgreSQL 17 database: the new regression fails because the read-only snapshot is classified as dirty; six sibling tests pass. With the fix, all seven tests pass, including one navigation row read across two snapshots and a bypass inside a writable transaction.
- Command: `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <disposable-database> -- src/infra/postgres-sync/read-facts.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Base wall time 356 seconds; fixed wall time 390 seconds (Vitest duration 320 seconds), dominated by cold worker preparation; the fixed regression itself takes 250 ms.
- Native SQLite schema-fact suites pass: 109 tests, three skipped; 395 seconds wall time including worker preparation.
- Targeted core oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.
- Exact-head CI is GREEN at `a1c81243296c1ca2ff0127271704cc82b62a9e26`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40173229348.
- Contributor-supplied public `SessionManager.openModelContextAsync` proof reports first/warm/append navigation-query counts of 1/0/1, an append-only `(8,9]` refresh, and an unchanged eight-message prefix.

### Shipped Gateway/CLI trace

Fresh run at `a1c81243296c1ca2ff0127271704cc82b62a9e26` on this host, against a disposable PostgreSQL 16.15 database and an isolated Gateway. Statements were observed through the documented `openclaw.database.statement` diagnostics channel; the counted query is the model-context navigation projection (`WITH context_input AS MATERIALIZED ...`). Loopback addresses, DSNs, tokens, and local paths are omitted.

| Read | Shipped entry point | Navigation-projection statements |
|---|---|---|
| Cold | `openclaw agent --session-key ... --message "fork source one"` (new session) | 2 |
| Warm, no append | `openclaw gateway call sessions.fork` on the unchanged source | 0 |
| Post-append | next `openclaw agent` turn (`"fork source two"`) | 1 |
| Warm after append | second `sessions.fork` on the same source | 0 |

The fork returned the unchanged source context (`editorText: "fork source one"`) both times. The post-append turn refreshed navigation for the new message only; the following read reused it without another projection.

Fresh targeted PostgreSQL regression on this host: `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <disposable-database> -- src/infra/postgres-sync/read-facts.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 7/7 tests passed, including `reuses model-context navigation facts across PostgreSQL read-only snapshots`.

prs.title: fix(android): bind chat to an allowed agent roster
prs.body:
Fixes #182638

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Android Chat targeting an excluded Gateway default after restart, even though the operator's agent picker contains only an allowed agent.

## User Impact

On startup Android waits for the role-filtered roster, then chooses the allowed default or the first selectable agent. An empty roster shows “No agents available for this role” and keeps Chat unavailable. Failed discovery stays visible and can be retried through the existing Gateway connection action. A remembered explicit selection retains its existing reconnect behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hello and `agents.list` routing metadata remain Gateway-wide, preserving the shipped contract from #161019. Android owns choosing a usable target from discovery.

The maintainer rewrite preserves @xiaopan-xydt's commits and regression intent while removing the extra connection epoch, retry loop, bootstrap flags, and unchecked `mainKey` fallback. Discovery uses the existing connection-catalog lifetime, propagates cancellation, and initializes Chat on a successful retry even when its canonical session key is unchanged. Chat's production transport waits for runtime readiness so manual history refresh cannot bypass failed or empty discovery.

## Evidence

**Final head `571716ebe65d7b069e4df311d574c05c99d599ea`: all selected CI jobs passed.** [Play tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139347410/job/121007794327) passed in 10m07s job wall time; [third-party tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139347410/job/121007794296) passed in 10m06s. Wear, both native-access jobs, Android ktlint, localization, docs, security-fast, and the CI gate also passed.

- Confirmed the original defect on main: `NodeRuntime` bound `hello.mainSessionKey` before discovery and later accepted a fallback absent from the returned roster.
- Owner regressions cover excluded hello defaults, cancellation before readiness, failed-discovery retry with the same session key, an empty allowed roster, and a newer notification conversation selected during initial discovery. The first exposes main's premature binding; the retry and cancellation cases expose the original contributor bootstrap defects. Regression execution is delegated to PR CI; no local red/green run is claimed.
- Updated the synthetic Gateway roster responses used by Android lifecycle, appearance, UI, and Wear tests without weakening their original assertions or timeouts.
- Static Kotlin formatting and lint use the repository-pinned ktlint 1.8.0 and Android `.editorconfig`; documentation formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Contributor Gradle/build/test code was not executed locally.
- Live Gateway/Android e2e and upgrade proof were skipped per maintainer policy. PR CI is the broad gate, including both Android test flavors.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview completed with no accepted findings. Its one omitted-catalog finding was rejected after checking `replaceGatewayMethods(hello.methods)`: the existing owner marks the connection present even when the optional catalog is null. The incremental repair autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2; the final matching Wear fixture update also received independent source review. Exact-head [CI 40139347410](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139347410) is green at `571716ebe65d7b069e4df311d574c05c99d599ea`, including both Android test flavors and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- Change versus integrated main: production +97/−46, tests +227/−23, docs +5/−2. Local test timing is unavailable because contributor code was not executed; hosted timings remain in CI.

The rewrite removes the new epoch/backoff machinery. Necessary production growth covers readiness, visible discovery failures, and the Chat transport hold; no Gateway, protocol, config, or persistence schema changes.

The first maintainer-head CI run ([40134316442](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40134316442)) reached the Android job limit after fixture readiness failures: those synthetic Gateways returned `{}` or unsupported-method for the newly required discovery request. The repair gives those fixtures their existing `main` roster and preserves every assertion. This was PR-caused fixture fallout, not an inherited failure; no blind rerun or timeout increase was used. The discovery hold also uses the existing not-enqueued error classification so unsent messages remain queued.

ClawSweeper reviewed the complete Android rewrite at `1d7692c379c2e775bfb6ac47755eb427f5d4784e` with zero code findings and confirmed the prior P2s resolved. Its remaining live-proof-only hold is superseded by the maintainer validation policy above.

The second run ([40137760546](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40137760546)) completed with Play **3,583 passed / 1 failed** and third-party **3,715 passed / 1 failed**. The remaining notification-reply failures exposed an initial-discovery ordering bug: selecting a conversation after socket admission retired the pending roster result, leaving startup incomplete. Initial discovery now completes while the existing binding owner preserves the selected conversation; ordinary later refreshes still reject stale selection results. The held-roster regression would fail on `94efb23e6897` at its Connected assertion because that head discards the initial roster; it covers this path, and the unchanged notification tests remain the receiving proof. This incremental repair passed static lint and scoped-clean P0–P2 autoreview.

prs.title: fix(cli-runner): clean failed temporary MCP config writes
prs.body:
Closes #179555

## What Problem This Solves

A failed temporary MCP-config write leaks the directory allocated by `writeTemporaryBundleMcpJson`. The caller receives cleanup only after success. A partial Claude `mcp.json` write can therefore leave resolved header credentials in an orphaned temporary file; Gemini's atomic settings writer has the same directory-lifetime defect.

## User Impact

Failed preparation removes its temporary tree and propagates the original write error. Successful configuration and caller cleanup keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The allocating helper now catches write failures and removes its own tree before rethrowing. Cleanup errors do not replace the original write error. Both atomic and non-atomic callers share this owner, so no caller-specific guard or new configuration is needed.

Thanks @xiaopan-xydt for the fix and shipped-CLI reproduction, and @YangManBOBO for the related partial-write reproduction in #179756.

## Evidence

- Fresh base run: both regressions fail with an orphaned directory. One writes a partial synthetic credential file before throwing ENOSPC; the other exercises the real atomic writer with an invalidly long filename.
- The regressions use a private tracked temporary root, preserve the original non-atomic error, and verify the root is empty after failure. No global temporary-directory scans or serializer-only failure substitute is used.
- Production +9/-4 (net +5): the necessary catch-and-cleanup boundary. No useful adjacent deletion was found; the existing writer and successful cleanup owner remain intact.
- The contributor's recorded shipped-CLI run used `node openclaw.mjs agent exec ...` with a disposable 8 KiB tmpfs filled to zero free bytes. Directory creation succeeded, then the real Claude adapter's write failed. The helper returned ENOSPC, removed its directory, and never invoked the fake Claude executable.
- No fresh packaged CLI or model round-trip was run in this pass. The earlier CLI proof is retained below; fresh tests cover partial writes and the atomic sibling on the integrated source.

```text
Recorded contributor run, head 89a7835a79cec63262b1e6b00df8634a0159cc06:
proof_status=PASS
tmpfs_available_bytes_before_run=0
exit_code=1
enos_observed=yes
mcp_json_events_observed=3
mcp_json_max_observed_size=0
leftover_openclaw_cli_mcp_dirs=0
fake_claude_invoked=no
ENOSPC: no space left on device, write
```

Fresh integrated-head regression tests: 2/2 pass. Typed oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Tests +46/-0. The simplification pass retained the small write-owner error boundary; the two tests cover distinct write paths without a new harness.

Existing Claude and Gemini success-path checks also pass: 2 selected tests across `bundle-mcp.test.ts` and `bundle-mcp.gemini.test.ts`, with 21 unrelated cases filtered out. These exercise real generated configuration files through both callers.

Independent P0–P2 review of the final staged candidate: no actionable findings.

Fixes #194078

## What Problem This Solves

MCP servers launched over stdio were not enrolled in host-loss termination: if the Gateway host process disappeared abruptly, the subprocess custody anchor could wait for a lineage-close receipt instead of retiring the server decisively, leaving orphaned MCP server processes behind. In plain terms: when the manager dies suddenly, the helpers it started should be shut down right away, not left waiting for a goodbye message that never arrives.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OpenClawStdioClientTransport` calls `createOwnedStdioProcess` without `terminateOnHostLoss`, so the stdio path only gets best-effort host-loss handling. The Claude CLI owner path (`extensions/anthropic/cli-process.ts`) already arms `terminateOnHostLoss: true` on the same owned-stdio custody. Normal transport `close()` ends stdin explicitly, which is exactly the contract the flag requires, so the stdio MCP path can adopt the stronger behavior without changing graceful shutdown.

## User Impact

MCP stdio servers are killed decisively when their host is lost, matching the Claude CLI owner behavior. Normal connect/close flows are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Real-runtime custody behavior behind the flag (shipped machinery, unmodified): `service-child-group-anchor.input-lifetime.test.ts > "host-loss distinguishes protocol EOF from host loss"` — 4/4 pass; host-loss mode ends the child with SIGKILL while EOF modes exit cleanly (code 0).
- Wiring regression: `mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts > "arms host-loss termination for owned stdio custody"` asserts the transport passes `terminateOnHostLoss: true` into owned stdio custody; the suite passes 26/26.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean; oxlint reports 0 warnings and 0 errors on the changed files.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the repository test harness to analyze issue #194078, locate the missing flag in mcp-stdio-transport.ts, and mirror the existing Claude CLI owner path. The implementer understands the code: normal close ends stdin explicitly, and the flag makes host loss kill the child instead of waiting for lineage-close confirmation. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(infra): skip the exec-approvals deletion fence where the journal table is absent
prs.body:
fix(infra): skip the exec-approvals deletion fence where the journal table is absent

Closes #192227

## What Problem This Solves

Saving node exec approvals failed with "no such table: agent_deletion_journal": the mutation fence queried the journal in the agent database that stores node-scoped approvals, but that table only exists in the shared state database.

## User Impact

`openclaw approvals allowlist add --node <id>` and the Control UI node approval save persist again, instead of failing with UNAVAILABLE while reads kept working.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deletion fence protects against mutating approvals while an agent deletion owns them; the journal recording those deletions lives in the shared state database. Node-scoped approval databases predate the table, so the fence now checks for the journal table's presence through the existing engine-aware `tableExists` owner and only enforces the fence where the journal itself exists. Databases with the table keep the exact previous fencing behavior.

- PostgreSQL keeps working: `tableExists` consults admitted PostgreSQL physical catalog facts instead of a SQLite-only `sqlite_master` query.
- No per-mutation schema probing: `tableExists` consumes the admitted per-database schema facts cache; discovery stays with the schema owner.
- Safety: a database without the journal table has never recorded a deletion, so there is no in-progress deletion this fence could miss on that database; the unchanged query path keeps fencing every store where deletions are recorded. If a maintainer prefers refusal for unknown history, dropping the presence guard restores the original behavior — the reported saves then need the journal initialized through the schema owner instead, which is an owner decision I am happy to implement.

## Evidence

- Focused run on latest main content: src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts 30/30 passed, including the new case asserting the fence is skipped on a database without the agent_deletion_journal table.
- Red check: reverting only the presence guard fails exactly that case (1 failed | 29 passed); restoring passes.
- Neighboring suites stay green: agent-deletion-journal.fence (14/14), exec-approvals-policy (29/29), and the earlier exec-approvals-config/store.read-worker set (76/76).

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and module tracing to analyze issue #192227, locate the fence query in src/infra/exec-approvals-sqlite.ts, and implement the presence guard. The implementer understands the code: the fence queries a state-database-only table, while node approvals persist in agent databases that never had it; presence is now checked through the shared `tableExists` owner. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.body:
Closes #182773

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw database port --dry-run` reports an opaque `validation or I/O failure` when the local client credential receipt is bound to a different shared database file, and then suggests `--resume/--rollback` even when no recovery manifest exists.

## User Impact

Operators now see the failed fact (a credential receipt bound to another shared database file), the supported repair (`openclaw backup restore`), and only advice that applies to the current run. A preflight dry run no longer tells an offline operator to stop a Gateway or use a recovery manifest it did not create.

## Why This Change Was Made

The credential mismatch is now a typed error consumed by the database-port refusal owner instead of falling through to the catch-all as an unknown I/O failure. Refusal guidance now depends on whether a Gateway was observed and whether a recovery manifest actually exists. Unexpected failures still use the existing redacted-code path.

## Evidence

New regression in `src/infra/database-engine/port-command.credentials-local.test.ts` enters through `doctorDatabasePort({ family: "state", dryRun: true })`, corrupts only the local receipt's shared-file identity, and asserts the actionable message without changing either database.

Base-red on unmodified sources:

```text
Received: "... observed validation or I/O failure; required successful verified phase; preserve the recovery directory. Stop the Gateway first; correct this fact and retry, or use --resume/--rollback with .../manifest.json."
Expected: /local credential receipt bound to a different shared database file.*openclaw backup restore/u
Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)
```

With the fix:

```text
✓ database port local credential ownership (4 tests)
✓ database-port admission and existing doctor database-port tests (17 tests)
Test Files  3 passed (3)
```

### Shipped CLI proof

The current branch was run through `src/entry.ts` by invoking the real command below against an isolated state directory:

```text
openclaw database port --family state --to sqlite --dry-run
```

The local credential receipt was changed only in its recorded shared-file identity. Both database files remained byte-identical, and no recovery manifest existed:

```json
{
  "entrypoint": "openclaw database port --family state --to sqlite --dry-run",
  "exitCode": 1,
  "message": "Database port preflight: .../matrix/accounts/active/matrix.example__user/0123456789abcdef/client/credentials.sqlite; observed local credential receipt bound to a different shared database file; required a receipt matching this shared database; restore the archive with openclaw backup restore. Correct this fact and retry.",

  "recoveryManifestCreated": false,

}
```

After creating the actual recovery manifest, the same shipped command retained manifest-dependent recovery guidance:

```json
    "resumeOrRollbackAdvicePresent": true,
    "output": "Database port preflight: .../openclaw.json; observed OWNER_UNAVAILABLE; required successful verified phase; preserve the recovery directory. Correct this fact and retry, or use --resume/--rollback with .../recovery/database-port/manifest.json."
  }
}
```

After the merge, the focused regression suite passed 14 tests across 3 files (`port-command.credentials-local.test.ts`, `doctor-database-port.test.ts`, and `doctor-database-port-memory.test.ts`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: reopening a short Control UI session URL returns a bare 404 while the UI is still resolving its session key.

## User Impact

Users can reload generated short-session URLs, including newly created chats with composer focus. Authentication and the selected session still come only from the pathname. Unknown, duplicate, and malformed query parameters remain rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The return-path parser omitted both `__openclawSessionKey` and the `__openclawComposerFocus` hint emitted alongside it by new-session navigation. One query-validation table now accepts these existing hints and preserves the dashboard, draft, recovery, and preferred-face rules. It replaces repeated per-key checks without adding a UI parameter or configuration option.

Thanks to @xiaopan-xydt for the original fix and running-Gateway evidence.

## Evidence

On current main `9141755ddadb`, the two regressions fail: the URL generated with a short session key and composer focus returns 404 instead of the app shell, and the authenticated handoff never serves the app. The other 41 tests pass. On the candidate, all 43 tests pass across `control-ui-session-entry.test.ts` and `control-ui-public-chat.http.test.ts` (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <both files> --maxWorkers=1`). The contributor supplied a final-head shipped-Gateway trace for the combined key/focus URL, in addition to the earlier trace below. The independent local build attempt failed before listening, as recorded below. No operator Gateway or private state was used.

The generated short-session URL with both `__openclawSessionKey` and `__openclawComposerFocus=1` returned the 122,672-byte app-shell/login-handoff document with the expected missing-session 404. Duplicate key, duplicate focus, blank key, and unknown query parameters returned the 9-byte `Not found` rejection; `/chat` returned 200. prs.title: fix(ui): replace stored secrets from config forms
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Form mode can type a new sensitive value, but a stored secret arrives as the server redaction sentinel and remains read-only. The disabled reveal button leaves no way to replace that credential from Form mode.

Sensitive scalar fields now offer an explicit **Replace stored value** action. It opens an empty, masked input without revealing or committing the sentinel. Abandoning the replacement restores the concealed state; typing replaces the stored value normally.

## User Impact

Operators can rotate a stored token from Settings and channel forms without switching to Raw mode or exposing the existing secret. Opening and abandoning the replacement does not clear the credential.

Structured `SecretRef` values remain raw-mode-only, and non-masked reveal behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`getSensitiveRenderState` intentionally prevents the redaction sentinel from becoming editable. The scalar renderer now tracks a local replacement transition: the sentinel stays concealed, the input renders empty as `type=password`, and the first input marks the replacement as intentional. Blur without input cancels the transition.

The existing sensitive-field button becomes the explicit replacement entry point when the value is sentinel-redacted; otherwise it keeps its reveal/hide behavior.

The secret wrapper now also remains mounted while that replacement transition is active. Channel forms configure masking without a reveal callback, so deriving the wrapper only from `sentinelRedacted` removed it after the first character and replaced the focused input. The regression types a two-character credential and asserts that the same input remains focused and both characters reach `onPatch`.

## Evidence

Base-red on `origin/main` with the new browser coverage: 3 failures. The replacement action was absent, and the sentinel remained locked. The new no-reveal regression additionally failed on the previous head after the first replacement character.

Head-green:

```text
config-form-scalar-integrity.browser.test.ts  37 passed
config-form.browser.test.ts                   43 passed (adjacent suites, 2 files)
```

## What Problem This Solves

A fresh dashboard conversation can fail its first message with `Codex thread <id> is claimed by active work; stop it first.` before any native `turn/start`, while MCP/app discovery still holds its preliminary thread lease.

Fixes #182549

## User Impact

First replies can start while app discovery retains its preliminary thread. Genuine claimed work and incoming native-tool-disabled policy changes retain their existing refusal paths. No configuration, protocol, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preliminary app preparation creates a restricted native thread. First-reply startup needs a replacement with the full native tool surface, but the predecessor release guard treats discovery protection like a claimed turn. The lifecycle now leaves a protected, unclaimed restricted predecessor with its existing discovery lease while starting the authorized replacement. Releasing that lease returns the predecessor to normal idle eviction; no second cleanup owner is introduced.

Closes #179557

## What Problem This Solves

A directory or manifest-write failure while building the Claude CLI skills plugin leaves its temporary tree behind. The caller receives the cleanup callback only after a successful preparation, so it cannot remove a failed preparation's tree.

## User Impact

Failed preparation removes the allocated tree and still returns the original filesystem error. Successful preparation keeps its existing lifetime and caller-owned cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The allocating helper owns cleanup until it hands the tree to its caller. The fix adds error cleanup there, using the same recursive removal as the normal cleanup path, without adding a new temp owner or changing configuration.

Thanks @xiaopan-xydt for the fix, regressions, and shipped-CLI reproduction.

## Evidence

- Fresh base run: both regressions fail because the allocated directory remains after EACCES during directory creation or ENOSPC during manifest writing. Both still observe the original error.
- Each test uses a private temporary root and real filesystem cleanup; no global temp-directory scans.
- Reused contributor shipped-CLI proof on the same cleanup behavior: `node openclaw.mjs agent exec --isolated --cwd <synthetic-workspace> --model claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6 --json hi`. A long private temp path lets allocation and directory creation succeed, then fails the manifest write with ENAMETOOLONG. Before: one leftover tree. After: zero, with the same ENAMETOOLONG reported. No application or filesystem mock was used in that recorded CLI run.
- No fresh packaged CLI or model round-trip was run on this loaded host; the original CLI trace is retained below, with fresh focused filesystem tests for the integrated source.

```text
Before (main 502a942ca53):
```
