prs.title: fix(agents): keep main-agent auth usage out of inherited recording after store relocation
prs.body:
fix(agents): keep main-agent auth usage out of inherited recording after store relocation

Closes #193576

## What Problem This Solves

After the shared auth store migrates to the state database, the main agent's own successful runs are recorded as inherited usage, which skips `lastUsed` and `lastGood` updates. The documented OAuth round-robin order freezes and acts like fixed failover: the first profile gets every automatic session pin while the remaining profiles are never picked.

## User Impact

With multiple OAuth profiles per provider, automatic session pins resume round-robin distribution after the shared-store relocation instead of pinning to the first profile until cooldown. Idle profiles get refreshed on schedule instead of expiring unused.

## Why This Change Was Made

`usage-write.ts` identified the main agent by `localPath === sharedPath`, which held before relocation (both pointed at the main agent's own database) but breaks after the shared store moves to the state database. The fix adds `localPath === legacyPath` — the main agent's own database path — to the main-agent check, so main-agent successes are no longer misclassified as inherited. Subagent callers still match the inherited path because their local databases differ from both the legacy and relocated paths.

## Evidence

- Focused run on latest main content: src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.inherited-owner.test.ts 10/10 passed; src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts and src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-kernel.test.ts also green.
- Red check: reverting the fix restores the old `localPath === sharedPath` comparison; the existing inherited-owner suite passes identically (the post-relocation main-agent path was not previously covered by tests, which is consistent with the regression going unnoticed).
- The reporter provides a minimal unit repro: two `markAuthProfileSuccess` calls for the main agent dir — with agent-db credentials `lastUsed` updates; with the relocated state-db layout it does not.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and module tracing to analyze issue #193576, locate the main-agent classification in src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-write.ts, and implement the path comparison fix. The implementer understands the code: the shared-store relocation broke the path-identity check that previously identified main-agent callers. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(android): distinguish chat metadata refresh failures
prs.body:
Fixes #183031

## What Problem This Solves

Android stored a single `chat.metadata` refresh failure notice for the combined metadata and model-catalog read. When `chat.metadata` failed first, the controller skipped `models.list` but still told the user that models had failed to refresh. The banner therefore named the wrong operation and made a recoverable session-metadata race look like a model/provider problem.

## User Impact

An initial `chat.metadata` failure now reports:

```text
Could not refresh chat metadata. Tap Refresh to try again.
```

If metadata loads and `models.list` fails, the existing model notice is unchanged:

```text
Could not refresh models. Tap Refresh to try again.
```

The failure path does not start a model-catalog request after metadata has failed, and it retains the last accepted model choices. A successful refresh clears either notice without overwriting unrelated session or settings errors. Authorization and publication guards are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fetchChatMetadata` now records whether the metadata read completed before entering the catalog read. Its shared failure handler uses that state only to choose the accurate notice. The metadata and catalog success paths clear both transient notices, while the existing `Refresh` action preserves them until a refresh succeeds or fails with another error.

Superseded-read retry policy was intentionally left unchanged. The issue's requested user-visible distinction is repaired without broadening this PR into Gateway retry behavior.

## Evidence

`base-red.log` runs the new metadata regression against the current production code and fails with the incorrect model notice:

```text
expected:<Could not refresh [chat metadata]. Tap Refresh to try...>
 but was:<Could not refresh [models]. Tap Refresh to try...>
```

The regression also verifies that the failed metadata read does not increase `models.list` calls and that the accepted catalog choices remain unchanged. A second regression keeps model failures labelled as model failures. Both verify that a later successful refresh clears the notice.

The focused catalog suite passes 4/4, and the ClawSweeper-requested adjacent acceptance commands pass 58/58 and 13/13. The final Android static checks pass:

```text

BUILD SUCCESSFUL
```

This change was developed with AI assistance under contributor direction and review.

Closes #124705

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor` reports `channels.telegram` as being in first-time setup mode when a multi-account Telegram setup already configures `groups` for every active account.

## User Impact

Configured multi-account Telegram users no longer receive this parent-scope false positive. Accounts that actually lack group configuration still warn at their own scope, and configurations that rely on an implicit default account keep the first-time guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor inspects configuration without starting channels, so the live channel registry can be empty. Account-id resolution now falls back to Doctor's config-driven read-only plugin loader for bundled and configured external channels, and forwards the active Doctor environment.

The Telegram parent container is not itself an account. Telegram's extra warning hook now suppresses first-time guidance only when an explicit default account exists, at least one child account is active, and every active child configures `groups`. With an implicit default account, the container remains the only scope that can carry the guidance, so the warning is preserved.

## Evidence

- Focused Doctor and Telegram tests pass: 3 Vitest shards, 5 test files, including new coverage for config-driven account discovery and the parent/child warning cases.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.

- Shipped CLI proof: `pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive` was run from this head with isolated `HOME`/state/config/workspace and `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`. The issue's reported two-account config no longer prints `Telegram is in first-time setup mode`; four retained-guidance controls still do (missing child groups, single account with no `accounts` block, top-level-token implicit default, and environment-token implicit default). These are synthetic diagnostic configs only; no live Telegram credential or message delivery is claimed.

```text
child account missing groups                 first-time warning: retained
single account, no groups                    first-time warning: retained

env token, implicit default                  first-time warning: retained
```

- Latest-stable config upgrade: published `openclaw@2026.10.5` normalized the issue config, then the same isolated state was run through this head's shipped `doctor --fix`. Stable printed the reported false positive; head completed without it and wrote no config change.

Fixes: `before_dispatch` handlers cannot distinguish which Control UI connection sent a turn when multiple clients share the same session.

## User Impact

Plugins can correlate an inbound turn with the requesting authenticated Control UI connection through an optional `connId`. It is a narrow correlation hint, not authentication, authorization, or a delivery capability; channel-originated turns omit it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already captures a `GatewayUiCommandTarget` for authenticated Control UI turns. The dispatcher now forwards only its trimmed connection identifier into the existing `before_dispatch` context. This follows the issue's additive seam and ClawSweeper's recommended narrow contract without changing host-owned delivery or authority.

The `before_dispatch` types were moved to a focused sibling module and re-exported from `hook-types.ts` to satisfy the existing line-cap ratchet.

## Evidence

- Base-red: the gateway-turn regression failed with `expected undefined to be 'control-ui-conn-42'`; see `contributions/pr-182691-evidence/base-red.log`.
- Fixed regression covers two distinct Control UI connections and verifies channel-originated turns omit `connId`; 3/3 passed. See `contributions/pr-182691-evidence/final-conn-tests.log`.
- Real authenticated proof: two Control UI WebSocket clients shared `agent:main:proof:shared`, each called `chat.send`, and a registered plugin `before_dispatch` handler observed the matching distinct connection IDs. A normal authenticated gateway client did not receive `connId`.

```json
{
  "entrypoint": "authenticated Gateway WebSocket chat.send",
  "hook": "registered plugin before_dispatch",
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:proof:shared",
  "controlUi": [
    { "helloConnId": "4d230506-2114-405f-a076-7ef046810a94", "hookConnId": "4d230506-2114-405f-a076-7ef046810a94" },
    { "helloConnId": "f306f9d3-5f9a-4b4d-a2fe-37957088802c", "hookConnId": "f306f9d3-5f9a-4b4d-a2fe-37957088802c" }
  ],
  "distinctControlUiConnections": true,
  "nonControlUiHookHasConnId": false
}
```

- Adjacent dispatcher and hook suites passed: 25 tests across `before-dispatch-conn-id`, `question-custody`, `ordinary-hook-route-change`, and `hooks.before-dispatch`; see `contributions/pr-182691-evidence/final-tests.log`.
- `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet passed.
- `check:changed` passed every runnable gate. Its typecheck lanes cannot run on this host because the bundled `tsgo` requires glibc 2.29 while the host provides 2.28; see `contributions/pr-182691-evidence/check-changed.log`.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

prs.title: fix(ui): match sidebar file search across NFC and NFD text forms
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar file viewer searches file contents by lowercasing both the typed query and each line without Unicode normalization, so a line stored in one form (for example decomposed `cafe` + U+0301) is not found by a query typed in the other form (precomposed `café`), and vice versa. `computeFileMatches` returns no match for visibly identical text.

## User Impact

Users searching file contents with accented or composed characters (café, résumé, José, 中文, etc.) silently get no matches, or miss lines that should be highlighted, forcing them to guess the exact normalization form of the text they are looking for.

## Why This Change Was Made

`computeFileMatches` filters each line with `.toLocaleLowerCase().includes(normalizedQuery)` where both sides are only lowercased. Canonicalizing the query and each line with `.normalize("NFC")` makes NFC and NFD spellings equivalent, matching the shared Unicode-matching convention already applied across the UI (model picker, sharing, activity, dashboards, session owner search, chat context search, plugin settings, etc.).

## Evidence

### Unit proof (`chat-sidebar-file-view.test.ts`)

The jsdom `it.each` normalizes both the file content and the typed query, so each iteration exercises one direction (NFC content with an NFD query, and NFD content with an NFC query), plus case-insensitive matching across forms.

**Green with the fix:**

```text
✓ |unit| chat-sidebar-file-view.test.ts > computeFileMatches > matches file lines across NFC content and the other normalization form query 15ms
✓ |unit| chat-sidebar-file-view.test.ts > computeFileMatches > matches file lines across NFD content and the other normalization form query 2ms
✓ |unit| chat-sidebar-file-view.test.ts > computeFileMatches > keeps matching case-insensitive across Unicode forms 1ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Red on the unpatched code** (normalize removed) — both directions fail:

```text
× |unit| chat-sidebar-file-view.test.ts > computeFileMatches > matches file lines across NFC content and the other normalization form query
  → expected [] to deeply equal [ 2 ]
× |unit| chat-sidebar-file-view.test.ts > computeFileMatches > matches file lines across NFD content and the other normalization form query
  → expected [] to deeply equal [ 2 ]
Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
```

- The fix is confined to `computeFileMatches` (a pure helper); the branch is based on current `main` and the diff is only the two-line production change plus this test.

## Merge Danger

Low. Two-line production change confined to the `computeFileMatches` search predicate; existing behavior for already-canonical (ASCII) names is unchanged. No config, schema, or state impact.

prs.title: fix(tavily): allow a baseUrl override on a private or internal host
prs.body:
Supersedes #139868 (closed by the stale bot). Same change and contract, rebased onto current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who set the Tavily plugin's `baseUrl` (`plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.baseUrl` or `TAVILY_BASE_URL`) to a Tavily-compatible endpoint on a private or internal host would find every `tavily_search` and `tavily_extract` call refused before it left the process. The documented override exists for self-hosted gateways, policy proxies and test doubles, and those endpoints are normally addressed by private names such as `*.internal`, `*.local` or an RFC 1918 address, or by a loopback address on the same machine. Routing through an env proxy does not change the outcome, and no plugin setting affects it.

## User Impact

Operators can point the Tavily plugin at a Tavily-compatible endpoint on a private, internal or loopback host and use `tavily_search` and `tavily_extract` against it, directly or through an env proxy. Users of the default endpoint see no change. Cloud-metadata destinations remain unreachable, and a configured name whose DNS answer is loopback, link-local or metadata remains refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The client posts through the trusted-endpoint guard mode, whose policy pins the hostname but keeps the private-network checks on. This change treats `baseUrl` as operator authority and trusts the host named in it by exact name, under this contract:

- The configured host is honored as typed, including loopback and private addresses and `localhost`-style names.
- Cloud-metadata destinations are always refused: `169.254.169.254` and other link-local literals, `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`, their mapped and embedded encodings, and `metadata.google.internal`. A `baseUrl` naming one of these is routed to the strict guard, which refuses it before any DNS lookup or request in direct and env-proxy mode alike.
- A configured name whose DNS answer is loopback, unspecified, link-local or cloud-metadata is refused, because that answer was not the operator's choice.
- Off-host redirects are refused. A redirect that stays on the configured host is followed.
- With an env proxy, name resolution belongs to the proxy, as for all trusted calls; the exact-host rule still applies to every hop.
- The default `api.tavily.com` endpoint keeps the trusted-endpoint mode unchanged.

The guard gains an internal helper that combines the existing fake-IP hostname allowlist with the existing exact-host `allowedHostnames` policy for the request URL's host, after checking the host against a new `isCloudMetadataHostnameOrIp` classifier in `src/infra/net/ssrf.ts` that reuses the guard's metadata hostname and the `net-policy` metadata and link-local IP classifiers. `postTrustedWebToolsJson`'s request shape, error handling and response parsing move into a shared helper, and `postPinnedTrustedHostWebToolsJson` is the one new export, on the local-only `plugin-sdk/provider-web-search` subpath, used by the Tavily client when the resolved base URL's host is not `api.tavily.com`. Because the subpath is local-only, the public plugin SDK surface budgets do not change. The Tavily docs state the contract under "Custom base URL".

Alternative considered: an explicit `webSearch.selfHosted` opt-in flag. Not chosen because an operator who sets `baseUrl` has already named the host, and anyone able to write `baseUrl` can write the flag, so it adds a setting without adding a control.

Also note: an invalid custom `baseUrl` still fails before any request, as on current `main` ("reject malformed endpoints instead of switching hosts"); this change only chooses which guard mode a valid URL is posted through.

## Evidence

Head commit on base `main` `cd61ce32dd28e92003b213f8d2014608504515fb`. Original authorship and the existing co-author credit are kept.

Rebase notes relative to #139868:

- `extensions/tavily/src/tavily-client.ts`: kept `main`'s `resolveEndpoint` (no fallback to the hosted API for malformed URLs) and added `usesDefaultTavilyHost` on top of it.
- `extensions/tavily/src/tavily-client.test.ts`: `main` rewrote this file; the routing assertions were ported into its current shape (hosted URL variants stay on `postTrustedWebToolsJson`; `https://tavily.gateway.internal` search and `http://10.0.0.5:8080/tavily/` extract go to `postPinnedTrustedHostWebToolsJson` with the same parameter shape). Both new routing tests fail on `main` and pass with the change.
- `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-common.ts`: adapted to `main`'s `createLazyPromise` loader and `SearchConfigRecord` shape.
- `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-common.test.ts`: the two pinned-helper tests were appended to `main`'s rewritten file; the non-2xx assertion now matches `main`'s `ProviderHttpError` (`message` and `status`).
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts`: no change. `provider-web-search` is a local-only SDK subpath, so the public export counts are identical with and without the new export (verified by running `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` on both).

Focused tests on this head:

- `pnpm test:extension tavily`: 4 files, 43 passed.
- `src/agents/tools/web-guarded-fetch.test.ts`, `web-guarded-fetch.pinned-endpoint.test.ts`, `web-search-provider-common.test.ts`: 3 files, 74 passed. These cover the exact-host policy shape, cloud-metadata literals and `metadata.google.internal` refused before any lookup or request (direct and env-proxy), loopback/link-local/metadata DNS answers refused after one lookup, private answers reached, off-host redirects refused and same-host redirects followed, env-proxy delivery without local DNS, the request timeout, and a real loopback server receiving the pinned `POST` with the same headers while `postTrustedWebToolsJson` is refused.
- `pnpm test:contracts:plugins`: 49 files, 1028 passed; 2 files, 62 passed.
- `oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean on the changed files; `git diff --check` clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), plugin boundaries, Plugin SDK package exports, lint core/extension changed files and the other lanes pass. Two lanes fail identically without this change: "Plugin SDK surface budget" (public entrypoints 163 > 162, exports 3888 > 3867, callable 2243 > 2236, wildcard reexports 1 > 0 on base `main` too) and "dead export scan" (unused exports in `scripts/lib`, `extensions/qa-lab`, `extensions/telegram`, `src/node-host` and `ui`, none touched here).

Historical local run from #139868 (original head, same transport code; not re-run on this head):

Local run: a Tavily-shaped stub (`POST /search`, `POST /extract`) on `127.0.0.1:18080`, a logging HTTP proxy stub on `127.0.0.1:18090` that records every `CONNECT` and absolute-URI request, tunnels `CONNECT` to the stub's port and answers 403 to any other tunnel, and the real plugin client (`runTavilySearch`, `runTavilyExtract` from `extensions/tavily/src/tavily-client.ts`) driven from source. The driver records every local `dns.lookup` call. The private name is redacted.

```
=== (a) baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:18080, no proxy
[client] tavily_search: ok provider=tavily count=1
[dns] local lookups during tavily_search: 1 (127.0.0.1)
[client] tavily_extract: ok provider=tavily count=1
[dns] local lookups during tavily_extract: 1 (127.0.0.1)
--- stub log (new lines: 2)
[stub] method=POST route=/search status=200 auth=bearer-present x-client-source=openclaw body-bytes=48
[stub] method=POST route=/extract status=200 auth=bearer-present x-client-source=openclaw body-bytes=37
--- proxy log (new lines: 0)

=== (b) baseUrl=http://169.254.169.254:18080, no proxy
[security] blocked URL fetch (url-fetch) targetOrigin=http://169.254.169.254:18080 reason=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
[client] tavily_search: rejected name=SsrFBlockedError message=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
[dns] local lookups during tavily_search: 0

[client] tavily_extract: rejected name=SsrFBlockedError message=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
[dns] local lookups during tavily_extract: 0
--- stub log (new lines: 0)
--- proxy log (new lines: 0)

=== (c) baseUrl=http://169.254.169.254:18080, HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:18090
[security] blocked URL fetch (url-fetch) targetOrigin=http://169.254.169.254:18080 reason=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
[client] tavily_search: rejected name=SsrFBlockedError message=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
[dns] local lookups during tavily_search: 0
[security] blocked URL fetch (url-fetch) targetOrigin=http://169.254.169.254:18080 reason=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
[client] tavily_extract: rejected name=SsrFBlockedError message=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
[dns] local lookups during tavily_extract: 0
--- stub log (new lines: 0)

=== (d) baseUrl=http://<private-host>:18080, HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:18090
[client] tavily_search: ok provider=tavily count=1
[dns] local lookups during tavily_search: 0

[dns] local lookups during tavily_extract: 0

[stub] method=POST route=/search status=200 auth=bearer-present x-client-source=openclaw body-bytes=48

--- proxy log (new lines: 2)
[proxy] CONNECT <private-host>:18080 (host received as written: <private-host>)
[proxy] CONNECT <private-host>:18080 (host received as written: <private-host>)

=== (e1) default endpoint (baseUrl unset), HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:18090
[client] tavily_search: rejected name=TypeError message=fetch failed cause=Request was cancelled. <- Proxy response (403) !== 200 when HTTP Tunneling
[dns] local lookups during tavily_search: 0
[client] tavily_extract: rejected name=TypeError message=fetch failed cause=Request was cancelled. <- Proxy response (403) !== 200 when HTTP Tunneling
[dns] local lookups during tavily_extract: 0
--- stub log (new lines: 0)
--- proxy log (new lines: 2)
[proxy] CONNECT api.tavily.com:443 (host received as written: api.tavily.com)
```

(a) The operator-configured loopback endpoint is honored: both calls succeed and the stub receives exactly two requests. (b) and (c) A metadata `baseUrl` is refused before any lookup or connection, with or without an env proxy; the proxy log stays empty. (d) A private name is delivered through the proxy: one `CONNECT` per call, the name arrives at the proxy unresolved, and the stub receives exactly two requests. prs.title: perf(state): reduce worker imports for machine-state reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared-state read workers load the host-side reader and pool graph when fallback query handlers are first used.

## User Impact

Experiment closed without merging. The built worker saves only about 20 KiB of retained heap (0.13%), too little to justify this as an RSS optimization. No production behavior changes were shipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the two internal machine-state command helpers into their existing worker reader module. The fallback dispatcher then consumes worker-safe code instead of the host reader façade. Extend the worker-spawn benchmark to read a persisted machine-state fixture through the actual worker transport.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, recorded before measurement: compare the frozen base and candidate with five interleaved fresh-worker samples each, using `worker-spawn-measure.mjs --worker openclaw-state-read --state-task machine-state`. Require identical admitted fixture replies and a repeatable decrease in retained heap after GC and loaded modules; report cold import, first-task and total allocation/CPU, median and p95 latency separately. Any 20% latency regression stops landing. No whole-process RSS or universal workload claim follows from this isolate benchmark. Also run the default admit workload to check startup regressions.

Both revisions passed the `sourcePerformance` runtime build and bootstrap import checks. Measurements used Node 26.13.0 on an 18-core macOS host. Initial load averages were 8.63/8.10/6.01. Each arm received five samples, alternating AB/BA. All persisted-read replies matched the fixture and reported source admission.

### Built runtime results

Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worker-spawn-measure.mjs --worker openclaw-state-read --state-task machine-state --built --build-dir . --compare-build-dir <baseline-build> --samples 5 --output <report>`.

| Metric | Base median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retained heap, MiB | 15.657 / 15.658 | 15.638 / 15.641 |
| Spawn to first reply, ms | 67.608 / 86.688 | 67.190 / 70.769 |
| Cold import, ms | 48.880 / 66.475 | 50.179 / 53.024 |
| First task, ms | 10.536 / 11.717 | 9.043 / 9.478 |
| Total thread CPU, ms | 58.877 / 63.779 | 58.403 / 61.785 |
| Total allocated, MiB | 73.709 / 75.977 | 73.284 / 74.008 |

Evaluated built modules: 120 → 118. Retained heap reduction: 20,656 bytes. The default admit workload also completed five paired samples; total latency median was 49.86 → 50.53 ms and p95 60.86 → 51.63 ms.

### Why this was rejected

The source-loader experiment looked more promising: 0.46 MiB less retained heap, 1,303 → 1,276 modules, and first-task allocation about 36.1 → 8.2 MiB. One source sample also breached the latency acceptance threshold. The native built-worker comparison removes loader effects and shows that bundling already removes almost all of the supposed memory win. Do not use the source result as a shipped RSS claim.

Independent source review and local ClawSweeper found no actionable defects over `9cb3c14855e5..03fd4915c21f`. The commit hook, benchmark syntax check, and whitespace checks passed. The focused Vitest suite was not run: its Testbox allocation queued and was stopped, with the workflow confirmed cancelled. Additional qualification was stopped after the built memory result ruled out the candidate; this PR is not ready to merge.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A node approved together with an owner device keeps access after the device’s explicit certificate expiry.

## User Impact

The device and its bound node now lose access together at the chosen expiry. Independent descendant devices, invite-enrolled nodes, and unrelated local approvals keep their own lifetimes.

Renew before expiry to preserve the existing node pairing. After expiry cleanup, renewing the certificate alone requires explicitly pairing the node again, or removing and re-enrolling its listing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound-node admission now uses the existing owner certificate validity check. The existing expiry lifecycle closes both peers, retires ID-derived pairing and tokens, and removes the inactive node from snapshots and active listings without deleting its provenance.

This adds no state, migration, or configuration option. Default certificates without an expiry retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Both new expiry regressions fail on the base for the intended reasons and pass with the repair; 29 focused tests pass.
- Typed lint passes for all eight changed TypeScript files; formatting and diff checks pass.
- Independent OpenAI API autoreview of the complete nine-file snapshot against `ea4697cc4fe9383ccf3dbcceb65404b6546c73f5` (now committed unchanged as `7707c6ada5006b491012f9d405781fa39db050c5`): no actionable P0–P2 findings. Runtime evidence is separate from this static review.
- Follow-up `d97c8a9ccd0` only places the assertion invariant comments next to their casts. The assertion-safety ratchet, formatting, and diff checks pass; the reviewed and replayed runtime logic is unchanged.
- Gateway and package test typechecks pass; all 18 sibling tests pass across four files.
- The complete `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` build passes, with source verification before/after the build and after replay.
- Independently verified compiled-application replay passes through normal browser owner linking/member approval and signed combined enrollment, with the source-built native transport. Captured result:

```text
pre-expiry pairing: present; command: ok; existing connection: open
post-expiry fresh human: not_a_member; fresh node: not_a_member
existing node: revoked (code 2), after expiry
expired node pairing: absent
renewed certificate: human/node HTTP 200; node handshake: PAIRING_REQUIRED
explicit node removal: not_a_member
independent owner/member health: 200
cleanup: joined
```

The isolated runtime uses a source-built native transport and deterministic external fixtures. Deployment, fresh/npm installation, full declaration/release packaging, and physical iOS behavior are not qualified by this work.

## What Problem This Solves

This draft currently conflicts with main. The candidate below predates the current Talk admission and CLI authority lifecycle; it needs to be adapted and revalidated before the behavior can be claimed on current main.

Browser Talk consultations fail with an Anthropic API-key error when the selected model uses `claude-cli`, without trying the configured fallback. This revision also closes the terminal-event gap found in the submitted adapter when session-read or model-lock preflight rejects.

## User Impact

Browser Talk honors model-scoped CLI routing and the configured fallback chain, including CLI-only setups without a direct provider API key. Caller permissions, generated-prompt visibility and cancellation stay with the existing owners. No configuration or public SDK changes are required.

This covers the Control UI/native GPT-Live consultation path. Meeting, voice-call and FaceTime plugin consultation paths are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser consultation enters the canonical admitted turn/fallback owner and selects the runtime for each candidate. It retains one admission, transcript recorder and terminal result across attempts. Non-steerable CLI turns use GPT-Live's existing joined replacement path; revoked or foreign authority remains a hard failure. The correction requested in the [landing review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164229#issuecomment-5969946723) now puts fallible session-read/model-lock preflight and selection inside the existing terminal backstop's try/catch/finally. [Scripts, sanitized observations, review receipts and exact source hashes](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/tree/d530ab2f733aaf74a1e4dc1585e546b4c9f7943d/proof/issue-161885-terminal-repair)

prs.title: fix: recover retained native updates after config edits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained native-update controller adoption and recovery when a held database has been archived and a normal atomic config edit occurred after migration completed.

## User Impact

Operators can adopt the complete controller closure and recover the already-serving candidate without restarting it. The original journal, session witness, migration receipt and backup remain intact. This change requires complete-pair adoption; it does not deploy a Gateway or change SQLite schemas.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native receipts can include held databases even though Doctor leaves them unmigrated. Receipt validation now resolves their original paths through the existing owner-safe archive check while retaining exact device/inode identity. Live database identity checks remain strict.

For a migrated `ROLLBACK_FAILED` candidate, current config replaces the obsolete receipt inode only after runtime ownership/mode/path checks and proof that the Gateway has applied that exact revision. The controller matches the native config revision token to current file bytes, rejects stale or unapplied snapshots, records drift in the existing adoption intent, and shares the same proof with canonical recovery. This exceptional single-file reconciliation refuses included-file revisions; ordinary same-schema and stopped migration/restore contracts remain unchanged.

## Evidence

The new historical-successor regressions fail independently on #198513 (`f7bb28768b7cb31374bb45f927ccffea481b6429`): the archived receipt entry fails at the missing live pathname; the atomic config rewrite fails at the migration-time config identity check.

The Linux adoption suites pass 73/73 with no skips. `pnpm check:changed` passes. Independent Codex review through P2 reports zero actionable findings. All three incident-specific end-to-end recovery cases pass (0 skips): atomic config rewrite alone, rewrite plus archived held receipt, and refusal controls. They verify complete adoption → apply → context → recover → journal retirement without restart and retain the original witness/receipt/backup/closure. Affected fixture siblings pass 21/22; the remaining inherited fixture failure is detailed below. Exact-head [CI run43544290646](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43544290646) passed on `65305b565394bd379178e0adc17fef67a92a1837`; security-sensitive review and dependency review passed. The fixture executes actual controller/library/SQLite/filesystem operations and Linux FD9 locking; process, systemd and Gateway responses are synthetic. No live deployment rehearsal is claimed.


The broader recovery run exposed inherited fixture failures: direct journal creation omitted mandatory FD9 locking introduced by #193647 (`3efe1deca653acf8f13a321af0bc80770a722c7e`), and a stale registry-schema assertion contradicted the physical-schema owner established by #169752 (`aee12b63234c`). This patch repairs those fixture callers and expectations.

Two inherited main regressions remain in the unverifiable native-candidate rollback cases (`D_VERIFYING` and `ROLLBACK_FAILED`): the fallback reaches suspension handoff with an empty process-instance token. The live-native rollback composition was introduced by #169841 (`3e3a9a87e58be5b8d291d7bf448e1b7e8f7ba947`). Exact-parent reproduction and focused results are retained with this lane's evidence. These failures are not treated as passing or noise; this patch does not modify that fallback.

Production grows by 91 lines to share one live-config revision proof across adoption and recovery. No new cache, configuration, schema or parallel recovery owner is added.

The remaining `prepared steady profile closes with its original pre-selection inspection` fixture has a second raw Node invocation (`startup-profile inspect`) without FD9. The repaired journal setup exposes this existing caller, which still hits the mandatory lock guard from #193647. The exact parent fails the same test at its earlier missing-FD9 journal setup; both raw callers predate this patch. This is an inherited main fixture regression, preserved as a failure, not a passing replay. No controller lock is weakened.

prs.title: fix(ui): tweakcn theme imports are lost in other browsers and devices
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, who is the intended reviewer for this change.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/883de5f4-29a0-436b-9b14-bd0167001845)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e6c2c44d-1746-4a0f-8948-6e93174b160d)

Related: #184960 (theme discovery and personal-theme removal; it keeps this importer unchanged)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a theme imported from tweakcn in Settings → Appearance disappears in every other browser or device, and after browser storage is cleared, even when the person is signed in to a Gateway profile.

## User Impact

User impact: when you are signed in with a profile you can edit, a tweakcn import is saved as a personal theme. It appears in the theme grid like agent-created themes, is selected right away, and follows you to other browsers and devices. Importing the same tweakcn theme again updates that personal theme instead of adding a duplicate.

Existing users keep their imports. The importer shipped in stable releases (v2026.10.2 through v2026.11.3), so a browser that still holds an import from an earlier version moves it to the profile the next time it connects with write access. If it was the active theme, it stays active. If the save fails, the browser keeps its import and retries on the next connection.

Without a profile or without write access, nothing changes: the import stays in the browser-local slot with its Replace and Clear controls.

**Decision for review:** the docs from #152460 promised that existing browser-local imports are “never uploaded automatically.” This PR intentionally reverses that promise, as requested, and the docs now describe the one-time move. Please confirm this is acceptable.

Fonts that exceed the portable theme limits, such as tweakcn’s long system font stacks, are replaced by the default theme fonts. All 19 semantic colors are kept.

## Why This Change Was Made

The importer stored one derived token map in browser settings under the special `custom` theme, which profile sync deliberately skips. Signed-in imports now go through the existing `themes.import` Gateway method, the same path agents use, as `user/tweakcn-<id>`. The imported token map still contains the original tweakcn colors and fonts, so one small mapping produces the personal theme definition for new imports and for the one-time move.

The import response primes the theme catalog before the new theme is selected. Without this, switching from a theme such as Knot briefly rendered Claw while the catalog refreshed. No storage layer, schema, or Gateway change is added. The browser-local slot stays only for connections that cannot write to a profile, so its Replace and Clear controls are still used there.

Known gap: Appearance has no control to delete a personal theme on `main`. Before this change, signed-in people could clear their one browser-local import. Now an import becomes a personal theme, like agent-created themes. #184960 adds personal-theme removal.

## Evidence

The before screenshots come from current `main` (`e6c7c5e0da4b`); the after screenshots come from this branch. Both use the real Control UI against a real local Gateway with a signed-in trusted-proxy profile that has write access, in dark mode with a 1440×1000 viewport. The tweakcn response is the real `amethyst-haze` payload, served by a Playwright route. No Gateway RPCs are mocked.

### Before: a fresh browser on the same profile after importing Amethyst Haze

The import is missing and Claw is selected.

![Before: fresh browser on main shows Claw and no imported theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac355c88-050a-45f9-bf76-5fe36d83d664)

### After: a fresh browser on the same profile after importing Amethyst Haze

Amethyst Haze is a personal theme and is selected, and the appearance scope reads “Saved to your profile”.

![After: fresh browser shows the Amethyst Haze personal theme selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36c52ffa-ddde-4c87-a79b-6ff529685bd7)

<details><summary>The importing browser, right after import</summary>

Before: the import fills the browser-local slot (Replace and Clear controls, “Stored in this browser only”).

![Before: importing browser on main with the browser-local slot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/755dd567-13ca-4757-a2a9-8166457659b5)

After: the import is a personal theme card, and the Import card stays available for the next import.

![After: importing browser with the personal theme card and the Import card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b28c167-bf6c-4bd6-a4ce-7edd27da13b3)

</details>

- **Red on base, green with the fix:** `config-page.custom-theme.test.ts` › “saves a signed-in import as a personal theme instead of browser storage” failed on `main` (`themes.import` was never called, and the palette was written to browser settings) and passes on this branch.
- **New focused tests:** a test proves that the real tweakcn payload is saved with all 19 original colors, that the derived palette matches the import, and that an over-long font stack falls back. Another test proves that a browser-local import is moved to the profile on a writable connection and that the selection follows it.
- **Real Gateway run:** importing while on Knot went straight from Knot to the new theme, with no Claw flash. A reload and a second browser context both kept the personal theme.
- **Checks passed:** `pnpm test` on `custom-theme.test.ts`, `theme-catalog.test.ts`, `config-page.custom-theme.test.ts`, `view-appearance.browser.test.tsx`, `bootstrap-theme.palette.test.ts`, and `server-prefs.profile.test.ts` (all passed, about 1–4 s per file). `pnpm tsgo:ui` and the UI app and pages test typecheck shards passed. oxlint and oxfmt passed on the changed files, as did `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` and `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` (no baseline drift).
- **Local review:** autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, branch mode) found nothing actionable.
- **Not run locally:** the full UI and E2E suites. The existing mocked-Gateway Appearance E2E covers the connection without a profile, whose behavior is unchanged; PR CI covers the broad suites.
- **Seen but not changed:** while a personal or imported theme is active, the Import card looks light grey. Imported palettes derive `--bg-hover` from the muted text color. This already happens on `main` whenever an agent-created theme is active, so it is left for a separate fix.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes desktop standalone packaging failing on the current build output before it reaches executable compilation.

## User Impact

Standalone packaging can select the current runtime chunks and capture its fixed workspace programs consistently.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chunk selection sent every relative-looking literal, including ordinary strings such as `.` and `.sqlite`, through native filesystem resolution and exhausted Bun's resolver storage. Reuse the existing package-inventory CommonJS resolver, preserving extensionless files, directory indexes, and package main entries while preventing unrelated build-host files from changing retention.

The next packaging stage still searched an old `workspace-manifest-*` filename for the workspace-path-exclusions program. Remove that exception so it uses the current owner filename, like the other fixed programs.

## Evidence

The repaired selector produces the same 19,647-file selection as the original algorithm under Node and completes under Bun where the original panics. Its regression test fails before the fix because an unlisted manifest changes retention. The three code-generation fixtures reproduce the missing-owner failure before the filename correction and pass after it; the real staged output captures all six fixed programs with no residuals.

All 76 affected packaging tests pass. Targeted core, tooling and gateway typechecks, lint and formatting pass. Independent review found no actionable issues. The full normal build also passes on the final candidate. The stock compiler now reaches native AOT compilation, where it independently panics in `Lower` on the LinkeDOM/CSSOM chunk; this PR does not claim to repair that compiler failure. Carried-compiler qualification continues separately. Exact-head CI remains required before landing.

prs.title: feat(agents): support required manual-step handoffs in chat
prs.body:
Related: #192713 (effective-tool CLI diagnostics, a separate entry point).

## What Problem This Solves

Agents can end an authorized task when a required human step blocks them, and completing sign-in can leave the waiting task with its old unauthenticated tool catalog.

## User Impact

The existing chat question panel explains the observed blocker and supported manual step, optionally opens a verified link, and keeps the original task waiting. **Ready to recheck** refreshes available tools and resumes that task for authoritative verification; it never grants permission or declares success. **Stop this task**, Skip, and expiry leave the requirement unresolved and stop dependent work.

Existing OAuth, approval, native-permission, and desktop-ownership controls remain authoritative. There is no new configuration, approval layer, or durable restart ledger. Unsupported prerequisites still block the task, and the agent must verify completion before dependent effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing `ask_user` contract with `requiredAction`, preserving its attributed human-input wait, navigation, reconnect, cancellation, and expiry behavior. Advertise the built-in handoff in deferred Code Mode descriptions; client-overridden question tools do not inherit core semantics. After manual Ready, the tool requests the existing runtime-refresh continuation so newly authorized plugin tools become discoverable without restarting the Gateway or replaying completed work. Ordinary decision answers and unresolved manual steps do not request refresh.

The six-file follow-up repairs two gaps observed against reviewed head `723eef051b8954c7ff62686a6a8f2c768884de34`: handoff discovery and post-OAuth catalog refresh. It adds no Linear-specific policy or connector workaround.

## Evidence

### Original-flow replay with a real model and human OAuth

An isolated Linux Gateway used Linear plugin **1.0.1**, deferred Code Mode, the supplied screenshot, and the original uncoached request, “can you try this? for the isntalled linear plugin”. The real-account replay restricted Linear tools to read operations and instructed the agent against writes.

- **Before catalog-refresh repair:** the agent naturally displayed a manual-step card; human OAuth reached **Connected**, but Ready resumed with zero Linear tools. The original task remained blocked.
- **With the final repair:** the agent naturally displayed the card; after human OAuth and Ready, the same original run acquired authenticated tools, successfully called **`linear__get_user`**, finalized `done`, and displayed its success reply. No Gateway restart; zero active work or pending inputs. Run `2dd3c7d6-bab0-4193-b189-668de4096b7f`, completed **2026-11-14 00:33:52 UTC**.
- **Premature Ready without OAuth:** settled as still unauthorized, no repeated card or Linear operation. **Stop this task:** settled with zero subsequent tool calls. Both left no active work or pending input.

This proves the reported browser-account path on the tested configuration. It does not establish recovery for every provider/channel, an unavailable capability, or a plugin-bundled connector that the standalone `mcp login` CLI cannot resolve. Ready remains a recheck instruction; actual credential state determines catalog availability.

### Regression checks and review

- **125 focused tests pass**, covering manual/ordinary answers, Ready with and without a refresh consumer, Stop/cancel/expiry, creator-scope capture, deferred core discovery versus client overrides, normalization, existing runner continuation, and prompt-prefix stability. The repair regression failed before the fix.
- Targeted production/test types, lint, formatting, whitespace, and the full build including SDK declarations pass. The tests reuse the existing refresh lifecycle; real acquisition is established by the live replay above. Local timings: ask-user 35 cases, 11.29 s runner time; Code Mode/prefix 58 cases across two shards, 55.68 s combined wall time (51-case Code Mode/description owner: 52.36 s including cold transform/import). Broad hosted CI is recorded separately below; it is not green.
- Independent full-candidate **autoreview**, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium, P0–P3: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings, confidence 0.83, range `da533397..f4524367` (published as the identical-tree `57ca0021667`). The reviewer inspected supplied source; it did not independently execute the runtime proof. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its checkout has no built runtime/dependencies; the workflow fallback uses autoreview and an exact-head hosted re-review after publication; [that review completed with no findings or before-merge actions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196951#issuecomment-6784290250).

prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.

prs.title: fix(channels): unblock ingress after a transient shutdown release failure
prs.body:
Closes #193019

## Main compatibility refresh — 2026-11-06

Published merge head `3e7a10e467cf355f5a02d71b899efa3eb4068832`, integrating main `b11b610d173cc6ff87eb026b6506c20fc7e5fd62` without rewriting PR history. The single `ingress-drain.ts` conflict is resolved preserving upstream failure callback extraction, queue-cap drops, selective custody retirement and test consolidation.

**Updated scope:** main #193423 already mitigates the old indefinite hold by retiring failed drains and permitting recovery of known never-adopted claims after disposal. This PR retains the bounded, token-fenced native cancellation-release retry before disposal; it does not claim current main remains indefinitely blocked. Pinned-main production overlay fails the focused retry regression (one release instead of two). Exhaustion coverage now follows upstream recovery after joined disposal; uncertain outcomes remain fenced.

**New-head verification:** 180 tests across 13 affected files passed; final worker handoff rerun 12 passed, coordinator independent rerun 12 passed. Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, source-line ratchet and scoped whitespace passed. Independent exact-head semantic review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Frozen pnpm 12.15.0 install used target-identical manifests/lockfile. Test-line ratchet retains main's 25-line debt: pinned main is 25 over, candidate is 25 over, and the PR adds exactly its existing 182-line grant. No shared ceiling was changed. New-head CI is not claimed green.

**Proof provenance:** all Telegram/Claude live evidence below remains historical at `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. Writer bytes are equivalent, but upstream custody/disposal, dependencies and test contracts changed; no live-proof equivalence or new-head live run is claimed. No production restart or new Telegram traffic occurred.

Later observed main `c63b3a2e58c45e82ea4d4955c1ac3bbb6a275d2e` also merge-probes cleanly; intervening changes are iOS tooling, so no additional merge was introduced.


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: queued channel messages remain blocked when a pre-adoption cancellation release fails once during shutdown and the retained old drain continues holding its claim.

## User Impact

A transient known release failure can recover automatically so a replacement monitor can deliver the queued conversation. Cancellation preserves delivery retry history. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained cancellation after abort now joins at most three token-fenced release attempts, with 1s and 2s backoffs. The existing settlement owner holds custody throughout. Explicit disposal prevents another attempt; failed completion, ordinary abandonment, standalone drains, and uncertain write outcomes keep their existing safety behavior. Exhaustion or an uncertain cancellation write remains observable and retains custody. The bounded retry can add up to three seconds of backoff to shutdown, plus storage I/O.

## Evidence

- A real production ingress monitor stop/restart with an actual isolated SQLite-backed queue fails on the unchanged base and passes with the repair. One known failure is injected before the native release write; the lifecycle callback is invoked only once. The replacement processes same-lane events in order, rejects stale-token writes, and does not replay already-adopted unrelated work.
- Focused drain, monitor, handoff and claim-owner suites: 73 tests passed. Added checks cover exhausted retries, nested uncertain outcomes, explicit disposal during backoff, takeover during retry, standalone cancellation and ordinary abandonment. Existing failed-completion and retry-history controls pass.
- Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, line-cap/test-line ratchets and whitespace checks are recorded in the local handoff.
- Independent shared autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning, P0–P2, one pass over the complete uncommitted candidate against `06d4059a3d06` and supplied unchanged owner context; no actionable findings. This is evidence-based review, without a repository mount or test execution in the reviewer sandbox. Subsequent test edits only added required braces and an explicit already-completed return and removed a redundant default type argument. The coordinating parent independently inspected the final source and clean commit and reran all 10 boundary cases successfully.

**Initial test scope (historical; supplemented by the real Telegram/model run below):** proof here is the owning monitor/SQLite boundary with a synthetic pre-write failure. Actual SQLite locking, a complete Gateway process, a real agent/model, and Telegram transport were not exercised; no live outage reproduction is claimed. Exact live Gateway channel stop/restart under an actual storage lock remains a broader integration gap. No external API or transport contract changes here.

The dedicated allocation grants exactly 182 added test lines for this recovery regression and its distinct custody bounds; the shared baseline is unchanged. The change reuses existing owners and removes redundant release wrappers; production code grows by 12 lines. The four-suite run took 41.92s including worker preparation; the final boundary file took 4.63s in Vitest (50.61s wrapper including compiler preparation), and the parent independently measured 4.92s (53.90s wrapper). CI timing is unmeasured before publication.


## Additional shipped-entry-point evidence — 2026-11-05

The earlier Evidence section describes the initial monitor tests. This additional run used the real built CLI/Gateway, its plugin loader, and the public `channels.stop` / `channels.start` RPCs. It was **not another in-process monitor test**. The channel was a task-only local diagnostic plugin (`ingress-proof/default`), not Telegram. Its delivery callback deliberately calls synthetic `onDeferred` / `onAdopted`; **no real agent/model response or external transport was exercised, so this does not claim the root real-agent/model E2E gate is fully satisfied**.

**Isolation and provenance.** Separate task HOME, config, SQLite state, workspace and loopback ports; only the diagnostic plugin enabled; no provider credentials copied, no production Gateway restart/config/state change, no real-channel messages. The same fixture and one-shot fault wrapper ran against head `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2` and runtime inputs from base `06d4059a3d06e1a34a3cacfd3f635b93fe803a38`. For the base run, only the two owner files were temporarily restored byte-for-byte from the base and rebuilt through the CLI; all other runtime inputs matched base (only the new test/allocation differed). This was a documented base-runtime overlay in the head checkout, not a Git checkout whose HEAD changed. Original source was restored afterward.

The external plugin uses public SDK `createChannelIngressMonitor` and `api.runtime.state.openChannelIngressQueue`. It throws exactly once **before** calling the native release operation, logs refresh only after the real queue returns `true`, and reads the committed queue via the public API. There is no SQLite method mock, SQL reset, forced owner retirement, manual second cancellation callback, or claimed actual `SQLITE_BUSY`. The fixture SHA-256 is `d1d039654e952e53eff1e39baa8680360637a26f3e8cf0bad372773df0b7fcb3`.

**Base observation.** Real Gateway PID `95449`: the channel stop RPC reported `stopped: true`, but the internal joined monitor stop rejected the injected error. Starting the replacement channel did not drain its lane. Only `unrelated` was synthetically adopted; `task` remained claimed and `waiting` pending. Committed `claimedAt` values advanced at `2026-11-05T11:03:19.612+09:00`, `2026-11-05T11:03:21.614+09:00`, and `2026-11-05T11:03:58.706+09:00`; heartbeat commit counts were `[4, 6, 43]`. This is a bounded observation of continued old-owner renewal, not an empirical claim that it can never recover.

```text
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":95449,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-abort","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":95449,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-rejected","generation":1,"pid":95449,"message":"Error: Synthetic known cancellation release failure before native write","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback-returned","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":2}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:58 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
```

**Head observation.** Real Gateway PID `93148` remained the same across channel generation 1→2. One cancellation callback caused one known pre-write failure, then release attempt 2 committed about one second later and joined stop succeeded. The replacement synthetically adopted `task`, then `waiting`; the already-adopted `unrelated` was not replayed. The old token's release/complete/refresh all returned `false`, the successor token differed, and re-enqueue of `unrelated` returned `completed`. Final pending and claimed sets were empty.

**Shipped command path.** Under each task-only environment: `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`; then `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call` with `--expect-url` pinned to that task's configured loopback Gateway, using `ingressProof.seed`, `ingressProof.arm`, `channels.stop`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, `channels.start`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, and `ingressProof.dedupe` (head). Public lifecycle params were `{"channel":"ingress-proof","accountId":"default"}`. All these RPC commands exited 0; the base's reported stop success is distinguished above from its monitor failure. Both task Gateways later handled SIGTERM and exited 0 with clean shutdown. No commit/push was required for this instrumentation.

**Interpretation and limits.** A generally slow model cannot explain this comparison because no model runs; identical fixture, queue, lane and fault behavior plus the advancing native timestamps distinguish a retained old-owner claim from a delayed initial read. However, the fixture deliberately supplies deferred/cancelled work and observes its own callback receipts. Its synthetic adoption is not evidence of agent execution, outbound send, Telegram acceptance, or user-visible response. It does not prove an actual database lock, indefinite blockage beyond the observed interval, every channel adapter, or a whole-Gateway process restart. It proves a real Gateway-hosted local channel stop/replacement through shipped entry points with actual SQLite persistence. Whether this layer satisfies the requested real-behavior gate remains for review; the broader real agent/model/transport gap is explicit.


## Real Telegram and real model recovery evidence — 2026-11-05

**Observed result:** recovery eventually succeeded through the production Telegram adapter, real Claude CLI agent/model, and Telegram Bot API. It did **not** succeed on the first replacement: the task relay refused two overlapping local polls and the adapter automatically restarted twice before both replies completed. The human operator confirmed in the Telegram client that the replies arrived in A → B order. Per-event counts below are backed by the queue, transcript and Bot API receipts; the human confirmation specifically establishes client-visible order.

Pinned PR head: `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. The requesting user confirmed their dedicated bot was unused elsewhere, then sent a fresh exact handshake and prescribed A/B prompts manually in the verified private DM. No automated user account or team QA pool was used. The isolated Gateway had task-owned config/state/workspace/ports. A parent-owned, destination-bound protected HTTPS relay consumed the stored token sentinel; no credential value was extracted or copied into the Gateway. The operator Gateway was untouched.

Temporary instrumentation held only A before real admission and injected one known error before the original claim's native cancellation release write. It never invoked synthetic adoption. Native cancellation, the PR's existing bounded writer retry, real Telegram replay, real agent/model execution and outbound delivery remained production paths. Setup `deleteWebhook` was a recorded local no-op after verified empty webhook; no upstream webhook deletion or queue flush occurred. Command-menu deletion attempts were refused locally.

Measured timeline, KST:

```text

13:31:58.907  bound B observed by real Telegram poller
13:32:36.938  read-only task SQLite: A claimed, B pending; same lane; attempts=0
13:32:38.283  one known pre-write release failure for original A token
13:32:39.285  second release attempt for that same token (+1002ms)
13:32:40      manual channel replacement starts
13:32:41      local concurrent-poll refusal; automatic restart scheduled
13:32:47–48   first automatic restart also hits local poll guard
13:32:58      second automatic restart starts
13:32:59.308  real A adoption/completion write commits with new claim token
13:33:03.954  Telegram accepts final A response
13:33:04.053  real B adoption/completion write commits
13:33:06.414  Telegram accepts final B response
```

The old long-poll request remained in the relay until its bounded upstream request returned after the downstream client was cancelled. The relay's single-poll guard refused the two successor attempts rather than starting another upstream poller. This was task relay lifecycle behavior, not a second bot consumer or a newly fixed PR behavior. No queue reset, forced retirement, manual second cancellation callback or failed-send retry was used to recover.

Final read-only SQLite inspection found exactly A and B, both `completed`, both attempts=0, with no pending/claimed work. The real agent transcript contains exactly two assistant records matching the prescribed A and B responses in order, both `provider=claude-cli`, `api=cli`, with actual usage: A input10/output181/cache-write11936; B input10/output81/cache-read11936/cache-write710. Telegram returned two distinct accepted message receipts, A then B; no duplicate-send refusal or uncertain-send event occurred. Native launch/probe/maintenance subprocess counts are not misrepresented as exactly two model requests. The separate one-shot provider setup qualification is excluded from this recovery proof.

The native Claude child used its existing login without copying credentials, with global home file writes denied by an OS policy, tools/customizations and native session persistence disabled. Gateway/OpenClaw state stayed task-owned. This was a real provider, not mock-openai or synthetic `onAdopted`. Source instrumentation was restored byte-for-byte, Git was clean at the pinned head, and the uninstrumented head build completed successfully. The Gateway logged a clean shutdown in82ms; its launcher group received SIGTERM and reported-15, so that wrapper is not reported as exit0. Parent verified the protected relay ended code0 and both task ports closed. No live task processes remain; persistent review Remote is retained.

**Client observation:** on 2026-11-05 at 13:43 KST the human operator confirmed the replies arrived in order. This is a human client observation, not an inference from Bot API acceptance.

**Limits:** Actual SQLite locking, every transport/provider, and whole-Gateway restart were not tested or required for this known pre-write failure. The earlier base/head Gateway comparison and existing safety regressions are separate supporting evidence. This run establishes eventual real-channel/model/outbound recovery with the explicit transient relay failures above; it is not presented as a clean first-restart run or proof of all client-rendering behavior.
