prs.title: fix(cron): withdraw ownerless access change pending reproduction
prs.body:
This proposal is withdrawn pending reproduction. Do not merge: the original access change did not repair the reported admission failure and expanded ownerless-job access. The follow-up commit reverses that change, its test, and its documentation. The resulting tree is identical to the original base, `de0ea1efe5f960aa52891395ee05025b5fb1375e`.

## Problem and diagnosis

The reported failure is an operator-created, trusted automation with a human owner profile but no conversation `owner`. An interactive agent prompt edit reportedly stamps `final-executable-surface` provenance with an unknown caller origin. With no `owner.sessionKey`, that state is requester-admitted and then rejected for its conversation workspace.

The admission mechanism is confirmed in `src/cron/run-authority.ts:27` (non-local provenance selects `requester-schedule`) and `:46` (missing owner session fails workspace ownership). The provenance writer is `src/cron/service/jobs-tool-policy.ts:244-253`. The production mutation route remains unverified.

The proposed human-owner route cannot authorize that agent edit on this base:

- `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-human-owner.ts:31` excludes agent runtime identities from direct human clients; `:41` also excludes them from human-owner matching.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts:230-232` requires an agent runtime identity to construct the caller scope; `:265-268` takes the final-surface stamp from that identity.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ts:156` applies caller-scope visibility before human-owner management at `:165`. The original trusted-job check requires a recorded owner session (`cron-caller-scope.ts:393`, `:435-441`). Matching the human profile cannot override it.

## Boundary evidence and stop decision

A temporary diagnostic probe exercised the real agent cron tool and Gateway router/cron service/store, with the Gateway transport mocked to carry the tool's caller identity. The operator-created job had no conversation owner, trusted policy, wildcard tools, and the same registered human profile as the conversation. Its interactive agent edit carried final-surface/unknown provenance. The Gateway returned “Automation not found” and the stored job was unchanged. A direct human-owner prompt edit succeeded, wrote no requester provenance, and remained `operator-schedule` with no workspace ownership error.

The first diagnostic attempt failed during fixture setup because the synthetic profile was not registered. After correcting the catalog setup, the probe passed against the unchanged original production base:

```text
timeout 120s pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/cron.gateway-policy.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'probes whether a matching human owner'
✓ probes whether a matching human owner admits an ownerless prompt edit from the agent tool
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed | 21 skipped (22)
```

This is a diagnostic result, not a red-to-green regression. The temporary probe was removed from the candidate; no test or policy change is presented as a fix. Per the coordinator's explicit stop condition, neither owner binding nor refusal semantics were added. A deployed source revision and the actual admitted RPC envelope (identity, management-grant presence, capture marker, and patch shape; no secrets) are needed to establish the accepted mutation path. A distinct management capability or deployed-code difference remains unexcluded.

## Rollback impact and validation

The rollback removes the routing-based access widening from `cron-caller-scope.ts`, the test for that widening from `cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts`, and the corresponding `managing-jobs.md` text. There is no net production, test, documentation, schema, or configuration delta against the original base. No automation is repaired by this PR.

Focused checks ran serially, each with `timeout`:

```text

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       4 passed (4)

exit 0

[tsgo:core-test-gateway-methods] passed in 3.5s

timeout 120s pnpm lint:core --files-json '["src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts","src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts"]' --threads=2
[oxlint:core] passed
```

`pr-simplify` removed the entire unsupported proposal: 96 net lines removed relative to its first revision, zero net lines against the original base. `timeout 600s python3 ~/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine codex --max-priority P2 --no-web-search` (with task context and unchanged owner modules supplied) returned `scoped-clean`, with no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings. This PR remains draft and must not be merged as a fix.

prs.title: improve(sessions): reuse list selections after usage updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session lists repeatedly rebuild unchanged selections and people facets when an active session publishes only usage or other display metadata.

## User Impact

Lists retain the same contents, ordering, visibility, and current row details while doing less main-thread work after display-only updates. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selection index already distinguishes selection facts from display facts, but broad publication invalidation discarded completed selections before that distinction could help. Carry that existing facts revision through the publication owner. Indexed entry references and displayed rows still update; incomplete publications, deferred archives, changed Board facts, and selection changes still invalidate. Existing viewer/query keys, temporal bypasses, expiry, and cache bounds remain authoritative.

Runtime production delta: **+21 lines**. The added handoff preserves the required distinction between updating indexed entries and invalidating their selection; no additional cache or retained state is introduced. The benchmark extension adds 18 lines, and the existing regression adds 13 lines with an exact allocation record.

## Evidence

On 25,000 synthetic sessions across eight agents, replaying a people-facet list after each `inputTokens` update:

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread list CPU, mean of five timing arms | 23,413 µs/call | 805 µs/call (−96.6%) |
| Timing iterations per side | 10,000 | 10,000 |
| Sampled allocation, two separate arms | 3,547,379 B/list | 980,290 B/list (−72.4%) |
| Allocation iterations per side | 4,000 | 4,000 |
| Replay throughput, mean | 39.4 lists/s | 597.6 lists/s |
| Median of each arm's list p95 | 26.68 ms | 1.51 ms |
| Untraced total GC per list, mean | 99.3 µs | 35.6 µs |
| Owner projections over 70 measured replay calls | 1,750,002 | 2 |

Timing order was AB/BA/AB/BA/AB, with identical restored synthetic fixtures. CPU ranges were 21.73–26.87 ms/call on base and 0.73–0.90 ms/call on candidate. Host load varied from 18 to 43; these are owner measurements, not whole-Gateway throughput claims. One timing pair's GC rose by 0.0126 ms per list; the five-pair mean decreased. Allocation uses separate counterbalanced passes with collected objects included: base 3.54–3.55 MB/list and candidate 0.979–0.982 MB/list. Allocation-pass GC is not used as an untraced timing gate.

Native V8 call coverage over 142 total list requests (including warmup and initial/final captures) counted 141 → 1 calls to both `selectSessionEntries` and `filterSessionEntries`; presentation selection remained at 147 calls. This removes recomputation while preserving preparation retries.

The 70-call differential replay produced identical canonical response bytes (timestamps and transport revision fields are normalized by the existing harness). The extended viewer regression fails on base with 128 unexpected owner projections and passes with zero; surrounding assertions cover interleaved viewers, changed visibility, clock expiry, and profile rename. Focused list-page/invalidation/viewer tests passed (17 tests), plus retained-selection and accepted-record tests. Strict root-script and Gateway-test typechecks passed. Formatting and scoped lint passed. [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43543470778) passed on exact head `4b28bb943d2e2fc5bd599fc895a3d1536ca9a62c`, without failures or retries.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean through P2. The configured helper refused its provider route; the fallback reviewed the diff and owning contracts in fresh context limited to supplied source bundles. No reviewer configuration was changed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the owner replay</summary>

Create a clean fixture with `--list-shape people --sessions 25000 --updates-per-list 0`, then restore that same fixture before each arm:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs \
  scripts/perf/session-prepared-list-measure.ts \
  --state-dir <synthetic-fixture> --reuse-fixture \
  --sessions 25000 --iterations 2000 --warmup 70 \
  --updates-per-list 0 --list-shape people \
  --row-updates-per-list 1 --row-update-field inputTokens --mode timing
```

Use `--source-ref 51c2f42a8e029f667829c753d7098af911dd7f70` for base. Repeat with `--mode allocation` in a separate process. Use `--mode verify --count-visits --iterations 70` for work counts and differential response digests.

No live server load, local Gateway stress, model turns, or new retained-heap claim is included: focused owner proof directly counts the removed scan. Dynamic search/activity-pulse selections keep their existing bypasses and are not claimed as improved. PR CI supplies broad validation.
</details>

prs.title: improve(workers): reuse verified prepared snapshots and worker code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh cloud sessions repeat completed snapshot setup and worker-code extraction instead of reusing verified prepared content.

## User Impact

Fresh, unpinned default-branch sessions can reuse a compatible completed snapshot only when its revision belongs to admitted default-branch history. Explicit refs and pinned sessions retain exact-source preparation. Seed-only requests prepare the requested revision without running an unauthorized setup recipe. The actual completed base reaches preparation, inspection and binding; current repository access remains required.

Verified worker packages are reused through exact aliases; damaged or missing code falls back to verified archive installation. Legacy peers retain registration-time verification. Only negotiated peers defer verification to first binding with its full timeout; exact binding replay preserves private edits.

**Status:** `3825a67…` is published for **proof**, not landing. Broad CI, shared Swift-kit Periphery and OpenGrep precise scan **attempt 2 succeeded** after separately diagnosed download failures. At the November 9, 16:41 UTC readback, all **167 latest check runs were terminal: 124 success, 42 skipped, one neutral**, with no failed or pending checks. OpenGrep's parser-coverage limitations are recorded below. AUTH-2, UPGRADE-3 and dependency #193873 remain open. No consumer merge or server deployment occurred.

**Landing dependency:** older-snapshot behavior requires [managed publication recovery #193873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193873). Publication is not dependency acceptance. Capture normalization and diagnostics are separately covered by #193776.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, prepared-workspace and installer owners serve this flow. Strict registration requests exclude receipt-only fields. Negotiated verification stages preserve old/new peer compatibility without a protocol-version bump. Actual-base propagation, main's preparation callback, memoization, capture verification and diagnostics remain intact.

The admitted repository/account owner checks snapshot ancestry. Missing or oversized comparisons decline optional reuse only after repository/account revalidation; authentication, revocation, cancellation and transport failures still fail closed. The metadata size limit is unchanged.

Original PR and contribution: @galiniliev. Workflow recovery and contributor-credit support were requested with @vyctorbrzezowski. Automated repair and qualification: @roboclaw-bot.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev and @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1f24e3f3-e7d6-4966-b666-e5868987619d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/70153122-6ab4-4eea-96e9-a8b689da6467)
- [Implementation and verification — first-bind and seed-only regressions](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/649d3ef7-7e03-41fc-b728-f1e3cc134da1)

- [Implementation and verification — landed native workflow prerequisites](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4e21df81-705a-4c4f-8051-ce41b210e29d)
- [Verification — authenticated baseline candidate](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/94d52650-602b-4d45-952b-682817c03e9e)

## Evidence

### Published source

- **Head:** `3825a67949692994c8c09733379bcda88992df5e`; **tree:** `d689db82d1bd50a160e0086c818371eace8753ab`.
- Native proof publication fast-forwarded `e67f9b520ca4c19fb34a01e5a5bb7080e9181661` to this exact candidate. Receipt: `PUSH_PURPOSE=proof`, `PUSH_REPLACED_HOSTED_ANCESTRY=false`, pending `AUTH-2,UPGRADE-3`.
- The sole new blob is `config/test-lines-allocations/prepared-snapshot-residual.txt`: **3 owned LF**, reconciling complete PR growth **1,019** against prior grants **1,016**. Tests, runtime, checker and shared scalar are unchanged. Exact hosted composition reproduced red **6,593,452 / 6,593,449**, then green **6,593,452 / 6,593,452** with this record. No inherited-debt credit or padding was added.

- The prior native baseline `c7266a4…` preserves `b6faccd…` as first parent and authenticated `1bc50e0…` as second parent. It used landed #195476/#195662 tooling without changing signing trust or rewriting history.

### Source-pinned local proof and review

These are separate executing-source receipts, not a summed final-head suite:

| Source | Completed proof |
| --- | --- |
| `32b13317…` | **93-test** correction proof and immutable bundle. |
| `adbf95d3…` | **175** owner/direct-consumer tests; **321** routing checks. |

Fresh complete canonical review: **29/29 passes, scoped-clean, zero findings**, with 206 complete owner bodies per pass and six historical composition datasets. |

| **`3825a679…`** | Exact allocation-only correction independently reviewed **scoped-clean, zero findings**. Native checker red→green on the exact hosted composition; actual merge-tree equals the tested repaired tree. No runtime source changed, so earlier runtime evidence is retained under its original source identity. |

Pre-fix runs reproduced verification-stage/budget incompatibility, seed-only rejection, topic-only retention and unavailable/oversized comparison failures. Repairs retain strict wire and fail-closed authority behavior. Historical composition datasets are not current execution proof.

**Recorded limitation:** the historical pinned-Bun startup fixture had `spawnSync sh ETIMEDOUT` before its fence assertion. Supported-Node replay passed; this is not a claimed Bun repair.

### Exact-head hosted CI and recovery

All runs below bind to `3825a679…`; tested merge `f0376f49490d960bb746b90a5b98c4b89f36372a` has parents `92798ae…` and this head. Earlier red runs remain historical evidence, not relabeled green.

- [Broad CI 42569113831, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42569113831/attempts/2): **completed, success**. Attempt 1 failed downloading pinned Temurin 21 with HTTP 504 before Android ktlint executed.
- [Periphery 42569113955, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42569113955/attempts/2): **completed, success**. Attempt 1 exhausted Periphery download retries with HTTP 504 before the iOS build/scan. Its false completion sentinel and missing-artifact failure were downstream effects. Recovery produced `shared-periphery-ios-42569113955-2`, reused the original successful macOS artifact `…-1`, and passed the iOS shared scan and intersection.
- [OpenGrep precise scan 42569113927, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42569113927/attempts/2): **completed, success**, including actual scanning and both SARIF uploads. Attempt 1's five scanner-download HTTP 504s and exit 22 remain preserved. The new log reports **109 rules on 60 files, zero findings**; the downloaded SARIF has **145 rule definitions, zero results** and `executionSuccessful: true`. Artifact `opengrep-pr-diff-sarif` was produced and inspected.
- **OpenGrep coverage limitation:** 10 files were only partially analyzed due to parser warnings (including modern TypeScript `using` and import-type syntax); 23 files matched existing `.semgrepignore` patterns. The successful gate is not a claim of an error-free complete parse of every changed file.
- Each workflow received its first bounded failed-job recovery only after its setup/download cause was diagnosed. No source was changed or pushed for these recoveries. Passing recovery supplies missing coverage; it does not prove a network repair.
- Complete paginated check-run readback at 16:41 UTC: **124 success, 42 skipped, one neutral, zero failed/pending**. Separate `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review commit statuses were success. These are exact-head observations, not installed production acceptance.

### Important proof gaps

- **AUTH-2 — IMPORTANT:** exercise the real registered `RepositoryIntegration.withIdentity` policy with an admitted isolated repository/account, including revocation and reassignment during provisioning and zero prepared-content execution afterward. Synthetic fixtures do not close this requirement; access to the deployment-selected policy and owner-supported fixture remains missing.
- **UPGRADE-3 — IMPORTANT:** complete installed stable/mixed-peer/provider acceptance through actual owners. The supported survivor harness needs Docker; rootless Podman preflight is not installed acceptance. Stable-package acquisition was refused by unchanged release-age policy; no safeguard was bypassed. #193873 remains an unsatisfied landing dependency.
- Retain the stated scanner/runtime coverage limitations and satisfy ordinary review/acceptance/landing requirements. Mergeability remains an observation, not a guarantee against later main movement.

Native assessment remains **NEEDS WORK**, proof-purpose only. No Platinum rating, live cloud latency result, ready transition or consumer merge is claimed.

prs.title: feat(update): new releases run their own pre-update rehearsal
prs.body:
Related: #145252

## What Problem This Solves

A fix to the pre-update rehearsal cannot help the update that needs it. The installed updater runs its own copy of the state snapshot, Doctor rehearsal, test Gateway, and their time budgets before the new release takes over, so a corrected check only reaches users one update later.

## User Impact

User impact: once an installation runs a release with this change, later releases rehearse themselves, so rehearsal fixes and budget changes take effect on the update that ships them. A successful update otherwise looks the same, apart from one output line saying the candidate ran its own checks.

- Updates from releases published before this change behave as they do today. Those updaters ignore the new marker.
- This adds a package marker, `openclaw.updateRehearsalProtocol: 1`, and a hidden `openclaw update rehearse` command. **The marker is a protocol addition. A maintainer accepted it on November 13, 2026 (decision 5 in #197949).**
- If the candidate's rehearsal crashes, goes silent, times out a check, stalls its private Gateway before it is ready, fails its state copy, sends a report the updater cannot read, or returns an invalid result, the updater names the reason in its output and runs its own rehearsal. The worst case is that the rehearsal runs twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

After staging, the updater runs the candidate's `openclaw update rehearse --request <file>` in place of its own rehearsal. The candidate receives the config source the updater resolved in a private `0600` file, holds no update authority, and touches copied state only.

A candidate refusal stays binding, and the candidate refuses only when its Doctor rehearsal or its private Gateway fails on the copied state. A pass grants nothing: the installed updater still owns drain, activation, verification, and rollback.

Two existing guarantees carry across the process boundary:

- **Committed progress before forward work.** The candidate sends each progress and step receipt, then waits for the updater's answer on its stdin before it continues. The updater answers only after its ledger write has completed. A refused receipt or a lost updater stops the candidate before the announced check. This keeps the contract from #162098.
- **Custody of check processes.** Each rehearsal check runs in its own process group, and so does each command that inventories or copies state. Stopping the candidate does not reach them. The candidate reports those processes, and the updater stops any still running after the candidate exits, crashes, or is forced to stop. It signals a process only while it still has the start time it had when reported.

One rule is new with this protocol: **a receipt is answered or the rehearsal ends.** The candidate's heartbeat would otherwise hide a wait on a receipt the updater never read. The updater closes the candidate's stdin and takes the rehearsal back when it receives an event line it cannot read, including one its line reader dropped for length. The candidate does not send a receipt longer than that reader accepts. An unknown event that carries no receipt number is still ignored, so protocol 1 can gain events. After the updater is gone, the candidate still removes its own state copy.

| Update | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Any published updater to a release with this change | Unchanged. The old updater runs its own rehearsal. |
| Updater with this change to a candidate with the marker | The candidate rehearses itself and the updater applies its verdict. |
| Updater with this change to a target without the marker | The updater runs its own rehearsal. This is the downgrade case. |
| Candidate rehearsal ends without a usable result | The updater logs the reason and runs its own rehearsal. |

Tradeoffs worth a reviewer's attention:

- The updater does not impose a work deadline on the candidate. It detects a dead or blocked candidate by silence: the candidate sends a heartbeat every 15 seconds, and 15 minutes without any output returns the rehearsal to the updater. An explicit `--timeout` still ends it.
- On cancellation the candidate gets five minutes to remove its temporary state copies before it is forced to stop, matching the existing cleanup allowance.
- The immutable activation path keeps the updater's own rehearsal. `updatePreflightProtocol` and the external-supervisor `update preflight` command are unchanged.

## Evidence

All Docker runs used `scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh` locally (linux/arm64) with packages built by `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`.

**Both sides marker-aware, packaged.** This run predates the rebase onto `a83f743`; `git range-diff` shows both commits unchanged by it. The installed updater was this branch at `27f3c52`, and the candidate was a second build of the same tree with a different build identity. The harness is written for a published updater, so I seeded this build through its driver seed cache, using the same in-container `npm install --global --prefix` step that CI uses to seed a published release.

```text
PASS published 2026.11.3 → candidate 2026.11.3 (c1c7f08eb4e854981e572b287be391aaf9fac7b2): finished, readyz=200, running version verified
```

The label says "published" because that is the harness's wording; the updater was the local build. The update's output contains `The candidate release ran its own update checks.` once and no fallback line. All eight rehearsal steps were relayed with exit 0, the run finished `succeeded`, and the harness's durable and incognito session checks before and after the update passed.

**Published updaters to this change.** On the pushed head `758582e`, one cell per published updater, plus two control cells with unmodified `main` at `a83f743` as the candidate:

| Candidate | Published updater | Result | Recorded steps | Updater's own rehearsal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this branch | 2026.11.3 | PASS, Gateway verified | 139.1 s | 21.0 s |
| this branch | 2026.11.2 | PASS, Gateway verified | 138.0 s | 21.3 s |
| this branch | 2026.10.9 | PASS, Gateway verified | 171.4 s | 32.7 s |
| this branch | 2026.10.1 | PASS, Gateway verified | 168.1 s | 29.2 s |
| this branch | 2026.9.9 | FAIL, `post-update-failed` | 178.3 s | 24.2 s |
| `main` | 2026.11.3 | PASS, Gateway verified | 141.3 s | 21.9 s |
| `main` | 2026.9.9 | FAIL, same step and message | 180.0 s | 23.8 s |

Each published updater ran its own rehearsal, as designed: `The candidate release ran its own update checks.` appears in no output of these cells.

The `2026.9.9` failure is not caused by this change. Both candidates fail at the same step after the package swap, with the same message:

```text
openclaw doctor --fix: Shared state migration did not finish: expected schema 40, found missing.
```

In both runs the new Gateway serves the candidate version with `readyz: true`, the run is recorded as failed, and rollback is not attempted (`state-migrated-no-rollback`). The cause is not established.

**Rerun after the third commit.** The same five published-updater cells, with the candidate built from `b285a37` (the third commit plus a merge of `main`):

| Candidate | Published updater | Result | Recorded steps | Updater's own rehearsal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this branch | 2026.11.3 | PASS, Gateway verified | 170.5 s | 25.6 s |
| this branch | 2026.11.2 | PASS, Gateway verified | 168.9 s | 26.1 s |
| this branch | 2026.10.9 | PASS, Gateway verified | 204.0 s | 39.6 s |
| this branch | 2026.10.1 | PASS, Gateway verified | 199.6 s | 35.3 s |
| this branch | 2026.9.9 | FAIL, same step and message as before | 203.6 s | 28.3 s |

`The candidate release ran its own update checks.` appears in no output of these cells. The machine was doing other work during this run, so these timings are not comparable with the first table.

The two-sided cell was rerun as well. The installed updater was the `b285a37` build, seeded the same way as before, and the candidate was the next head, `b3d920d` (one further merge of `main`):

```text
PASS published 2026.11.3 → candidate 2026.11.3 (b3d920d032670532f6b50699997c6f3a3cba8d50): finished, readyz=200, running version verified
```

The update's output contains `The candidate release ran its own update checks.` once and no fallback line. All eight candidate steps were relayed with exit 0, including `candidate-state-cleanup`, the run finished `succeeded`, and the session checks before and after passed. Recorded steps came to 188.8 s, of which the candidate-owned rehearsal was 25.7 s.

**Focused tests.** Before the rebase, 174 tests in 8 files passed. On `758582e`, the five test files this change touches pass (58 tests). On `26150c4`, those five files plus `update-candidate-canary.test.ts` and `update-candidate-canary.exit.process.test.ts` pass (169 tests in 7 files). Four cases use a real child process: acceptance, fallback, a refused receipt stopping the candidate before its announced check, and the updater stopping a check process that a crashed candidate left running. I removed each guarded behavior in turn (exit-status and document agreement, commit-before-answer, the refused-receipt stop, silence detection, the inconclusive-outcome rule, and process custody) and confirmed tests fail each time.

**Checks.** On `758582e`: `pnpm tsgo:all`, the mock-export ratchet, and the test-line ratchet pass. On `26150c4`: `pnpm tsgo:all`, the test-line ratchet, and `oxlint --type-aware` and the format check on the files that commit changes pass. The mock-export ratchet was not rerun. `pnpm check:changed` on the first commit reported two failures that this change does not cause: `max-lines` lint errors in files it does not touch, and the Plugin SDK surface budget.

**Review.** An autoreview pass (Codex, P0 and P1 scope) found that the candidate treated a timed-out check or failed state copy as a binding refusal; fixed in the first commit. ClawSweeper then found the two lifecycle gaps described above; the second commit fixes both.

ClawSweeper's re-review of `758582e` found three more defects, and `26150c4` fixes them:

- A candidate Gateway that stalled before it was ready was a binding refusal. It is now inconclusive. Only the Gateway startup step counts, so a timed-out exit or cleanup elsewhere leaves a genuine refusal standing; three control cases cover that.
- A receipt the updater could not parse went unanswered, and the candidate waited behind its heartbeat. The trigger ClawSweeper named, a cleanup progress line longer than the ledger's text bound, is now accepted and bounded the way the ledger bounds it. Any receipt that is still unreadable ends the rehearsal.
- State inventory and copy commands were not in the updater's custody. They are now reported through the existing `CommandProcessCustody` interface.

Each new test failed before its fix. For the cases that reproduce the hang, the failure was the test timing out. I also confirmed the real canary reports a stalled Gateway the way the fixture does: `runtime-verification-failed`, with the `candidate-gateway-startup` step at `termination: "timeout"`.

An independent reviewer agent read the fix before it was committed. It found that my first version of the stall rule voided genuine refusals, and that a candidate could not remove its state copy once the updater stopped answering, because the cleanup waits on a progress receipt. Both are fixed in `26150c4`, with tests. The autoreview helper could not run for the third commit, so that commit has not had an autoreview pass. A maintainer accepted the reviewer-agent pass together with the ClawSweeper re-review in its place.

**Gaps.**

- Windows and macOS service managers were not exercised, and process custody after a candidate crash is untested on Windows.
- No extended-stable updater was run. The harness accepts only updaters that classify as `stable`.
- The Docker cells exercise the passing path only. The third commit's failure paths (a stalled Gateway, an unreadable or oversized receipt, a candidate killed during its state copy, and a lost updater) are covered by unit tests and real-subprocess tests, not by a Docker cell.
- The published-updater cells ran on `b285a37` and were not repeated after the last merge of `main`.
- CI on `b285a37` and `b3d920d` failed three tests that this change does not cause. They are fixed on `main` by #198417 and #198418, which this branch now includes. Each failed the same way on unmodified `main` at `858b5b0`:
  - `telegram-model-picker-prepared-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: "Could not resolve built prepared-model-runtime- module".
  - `gateway-timeout-recovery-subagent.e2e.test.ts`: a child completion delivery list does not match.
  - `extensions/codex/src/node-app-server.runtime.test.ts`: a worker `command/exec` returns exit 1 with empty output. This one passes on macOS and fails on Linux; I compared `main` and this branch in a `node:24.20.0-bookworm` arm64 container, which is not the CI runner.
- The stopping of a state-copy command after a candidate crash is covered in two halves: the candidate reports a real command's process, and the updater stops reported processes. No single test kills a candidate during a real state copy.
- The advisory step `post-activation doctor inspections` exits 1 in every passing cell, including the `main` control. Its JSON is identical between the branch and `main` runs with `2026.11.3` apart from duration and a temporary directory name. It reports 12 `info` findings and no errors or warnings.

<details>
<summary>Test notes</summary>

- Net test lines are +850, above the 400-line allowance, so this adds `config/test-lines-allocations/update-candidate-rehearsal.txt` for 450 lines (319 before the third commit). A maintainer accepted the 450-line allocation on November 13, 2026. The excess covers the updater-side fallback table (nine invalid-result shapes), receipt acknowledgement ordering, liveness and cancellation timing, inconclusive candidate outcomes, the real-subprocess cases, and the regressions for the three re-review defects with their controls.
- In the third commit I read `update-command-preflight.test.ts` and `update-candidate-delegated-rehearsal.test.ts` in full again. No case was removed. The stalled-Gateway case joined the existing inconclusive-outcome table, the state-copy removal check joined the existing refused-receipt table, two cases that shared a title now have distinct titles, and the fake-timer restore moved from the end of one test into `afterEach`.
- Touched test files, each read in full: `update-candidate-delegated-rehearsal.test.ts` (new), `update-candidate-canary-process.test.ts`, `update-command-preflight.test.ts`, `run-main-update-admission.test.ts`, and `update-command-candidate-validation.test.ts`. No existing case was removed. In `run-main-update-admission.test.ts`, two inline per-command conditionals became one lookup table.
- Step timings from the two-sided cell's update run, small fixture state: 177 s of recorded steps in total, of which the candidate-owned rehearsal was 25.5 s.

</details>

prs.body:
## Status: superseded — do not merge

[PR #194807](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194807) already fixed this Systems dependency on main, merged at **2026-11-07 22:13:28 UTC** as `16f02454a7f8bb4e95e1a733d04303ecac193632`. That canonical implementation independently loads measurements through the existing page owner.

This draft was prepared against the older pinned baseline `fa27babf88518f243724fde005b40c90ad8e3f2a`. Current-main inspection caught the overlap. The committed early-content regression also passes when run with the Systems owning modules from inspected main `adca0b0844c71362be6da780008c642d17b2e350`. There is therefore **no additional validated performance opportunity here**, and this alternative must not replace or duplicate the current owner. The branch remains preserved as historical experiment/proof, not a proposed second cutover.

## What Problem This Solves

Historical problem: Systems inventory was hidden until optional node/host telemetry settled. The current canonical main implementation already removes that dependency.

## User Impact

The desired first-content behavior is already on main through #194807. **This superseded draft adds no required user-facing fix.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The original experiment published the canonical inventory early while retaining full-request settlement, selection, cancellation, and live scope/access guards. After reconciling current main, no further production change is proposed from this branch. **Systems only; no unrelated page changes.**

## Evidence

### Historical comparison only

Five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, fresh Node/jsdom process per sample, fixed 250 ms optional host-response delay:

| Component-harness inventory readiness | Old baseline | This experiment |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 204.1 ms | 74.7 ms |
| p95, nearest rank (n=5: maximum) | 204.5 ms | 76.8 ms |
| Min–max | 193.2–204.5 ms | 72.8–76.8 ms |
| Optional telemetry gates before inventory | 1 | 0 |

Baseline `fa27babf88518f243724fde005b40c90ad8e3f2a`; experimental head `0f26ff48829754a5715f340c782f91b55aac712b`. **This table does not compare against today's main and is not evidence of an incremental win over #194807.** It replaces the earlier non-interleaved preliminary table. No deployed/browser latency, CPU, or RSS improvement is claimed.

Committed workload:

```sh
OPENCLAW_PAGE_PERF=0 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/systems/systems-page.test.ts \
  -t 'first content' --maxWorkers=1
```

The old baseline fails the early-readiness assertion; the experimental head passes. Crucially, the same regression passes with current main's Systems owning modules as well, confirming that the opportunity is already covered. No attempt was made to resolve this draft's merge conflict by restoring obsolete machinery.

Historical branch checks: 33 focused tests, production UI typing, UI test type shards, scoped type-aware lint/format/diff checks, test-line and UI ownership ratchets passed. Fresh independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reported no actionable findings on the experimental local snapshot against the old baseline; it did not establish necessity against newer main. Author simplification retained one request owner (production LOC +31; exact 33-line scoped regression allocation, shared scalar unchanged).

Routed Chromium/source-renderer behavior proof used a synthetic Gateway with host statistics held from boot: inventory appeared before any statistics response, with one Systems-navigation statistics request and one separately counted bootstrap request. This is not production timing evidence.

**Superseded draft. Do not merge. No landing is authorized.**

prs.title: test(update): run the published-driver cell on a linked package path
prs.body:
Related: #197949

## What Problem This Solves

The update design in #197949 proposes keeping each release in its own directory behind a linked package path. Nothing tested what an already-published updater does when it meets that layout, which a downgrade would leave behind.

## User Impact

User impact: none. This adds a mode to an existing Docker end-to-end cell, a script to run it, and documentation. No CI workflow selects the new lane, so CI cost does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OPENCLAW_PUBLISHED_DRIVER_LINKED_ROOT=1` makes the published-driver update cell move the installed driver into `releases/<version>/` under the prefix and leave a relative link at the package path before the update. No shipped release produces that layout.

The update, readiness, version, and session assertions are unchanged. Three things differ in this mode:

- The incognito scan also covers the directory behind the link. Published updaters follow the link and keep their backups there, so scanning only beside the link would have checked one location instead of two.
- The installed-tree budget is measured at the link's target, because the budget check refuses a link. The default mode still passes the package path unchanged.
- The cell records where the package path points before and after the update, including after a failed update. That record is an observation and cannot fail a successful update.

Run it with `pnpm test:docker:published-driver-linked-root`. The Docker lane matches its `published-driver-scoped-restore` sibling.

## Evidence

Run locally on linux/arm64 with a candidate built from `e38fbc495a21a`, which is patch-identical to this head before a rebase onto `main`:

| Mode | Published updater | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linked package path | 2026.11.3 | PASS, Gateway ready, version and sessions verified |
| Linked package path | 2026.10.9 | PASS, Gateway ready, version and sessions verified |
| Default (control) | 2026.11.3 | PASS |

In both linked runs the link was unchanged afterwards and the directory behind it held the new build, with the updater's activation control directory beside it. The incognito scan covered two roots in linked mode, the same count as the default mode.

Checks: `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware`, `scripts/check-docker-e2e-boundaries.mts`, the docs MDX check, and the docs link audit pass. Seven lane and workflow test files pass (324 tests). `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts` (18 cases) and one case in `test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts` fail on the authoring Mac with and without this change.

Review: an independent reviewer agent found the incognito scan gap, a layout record that could throw, and three inaccurate doc statements. All are fixed here. No autoreview pass: the helper could not run on the authoring machine.

Gaps: two published updaters, Linux only, one update each. Rollback after a failed update on a linked path, a second update, and Windows are not covered.

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip unused cached child clock views
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated session-row presentation allocates a subagent clock view for each cached parent even when none of its child activity needs recomputing.

## User Impact

Session lists and session events do less main-thread work for unchanged child activity. Returned rows and freshness behavior stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

The clock view creates three maps and query closures, but only the dirty-child loop reads it. Construct it inside that existing branch. Invalidation, expiry, clock rollback, recipient permissions, and synchronous publication stay with their current owners. No new cache, retention, schema, configuration, or deferred delivery. Production LOC delta: **0** (one line moved).

## Evidence

The existing propagation/settlement integration regression now requires a cached parent read to create zero clock views. It fails on the base with one unexpected call and passes with the change. The complete presentation test file passes (13 tests), covering run settlement, child ancestry, recipient permissions, row modes, and response presentation.

Measurements: existing `session-row-snapshot-measure.ts`, 15,800 resident rows with 3,160 parents/four children each, 12 replaced rows per page. Warm clock views: **3,161 → 1 per page**. Exactly 12 rows reproject per page; unchanged row identities remain equal. Timing uses serial AB/BA runs; allocation uses separate sampling passes. These are owner measurements, not whole-Gateway or RPC latency results.

| Owner metric | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU/page, paired mean | 42.41 ms | 34.19 ms | -19.4% |
| Sampled allocation/page, paired mean | 26.28 MiB | 13.21 MiB | -49.7% |
| Timing pages per arm | 2,000 | 2,000 | two pairs |
| Allocation pages per arm | 200 | 200 | two pairs |
| Page p50, pair 1 / pair 2 | 42.29 / 41.68 ms | 35.46 / 32.65 ms | context |
| Page p99, pair 1 / pair 2 (1,000 samples per side/pair) | 243.75 / 74.60 ms | 44.89 / 38.40 ms | context |
| Page max, pair 1 / pair 2 | 931.28 / 474.16 ms | 66.00 / 60.95 ms | context |
| Pages over 180 ms, pair 1 / pair 2 | 19 / 3 | 0 / 0 | context |

A/A controls (100 pages per arm): CPU 43.24 / 43.85 ms; p99 62.25 / 49.74 ms (context only: fewer than 1,000 samples). Shared-host wall tails are noisy; the result is the removed work and lower CPU/allocation, not a claim that production stalls are eliminated.

Timing host one-minute load, start → end: pair 1 base 33.49 → 33.59, candidate 30.68 → 30.03; pair 2 candidate 30.99 → 25.14, base 22.08 → 22.34.

Command on each owner revision: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-row-snapshot-measure.ts --rows 15800 --parents 3160 --churn 12 --warmup 10 --iterations 1000`; allocation passes use `--iterations 100 --allocation`. Base owner: `51c2f42a8e029f667829c753d7098af911dd7f70`; other dependencies are identical. Initial overlapping exploratory candidate runs were not counted in the serial comparison.


Local format/lint and the root script plus Gateway test typechecks: passed: oxfmt and scoped oxlint; `pnpm tsgo:test:root` (all four shards); `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json --incremental`; `git diff --check`. Final focused test: 13/13 passed, 88.24 seconds including cold compilation (101.86 seconds wrapper total). Exact-head [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43542375849) for `3cc50d6dccfa64b1fe96a91543e839ce21e3e527`; both required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks are successful. The two initial lint findings (unbound benchmark method and test-file line limit) were fixed and the checks rerun..

Independent review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), complete local diff and owning context, P0–P2, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The autoreview helper refused the selected provider because it did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed..

Scope: this removes a measured source of unused work; it does not claim to eliminate all long session-row consume tasks. No live server was modified or load-tested. A whole-Gateway stress campaign was not run for this synchronous allocation deletion.

prs.title: fix: deliver child results after the producer runtime lease ends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing child results when the spawning turn's runtime lease ends before an independently retained child completion is delivered, including resumed children.

## User Impact

Parents can receive valid child results after the producing turn finishes, without extending that turn's plugin lease. Real grant revocation, plugin retirement, policy changes and Gateway identity changes still reject completion. No migration, public SDK expansion or deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

A released ambient plugin invocation scope could reject otherwise-current retained continuation authority. The existing independent-continuation capture boundary now supplies a narrow host-issued authority adapter that leaves only explicitly released producer custody. It preserves source identity, scopes, native cancellation, prepared session-source assertions, dynamic model policy, retention and current-role reads, without acquiring another producer lease.

Generic policy registration is byte-identical to the pinned Main; ordinary closed-scope recovery tests are unchanged. Live tracking, overlap, cleanup custody, admission, policy-decision sharing and Gateway ownership checks remain intact. This proves the present mechanism, not attribution of the historical incident.

## Evidence

Frozen reviewed source: `02de164e2fae43e5c671315964656a76f7543691`, tree `61cc52e98ce0b75fb713b4d3f9b9395b0a71c937`, against pinned Main `82123cd17bd0292294cf0de3a140c62018119f96`. The original PR was updated through history-preserving integration `4c5b4cb775e03ccd26ed2b061fbdb085f2f1e5d1`; published head `3ca699da51c586d5964d82aebc63b28932490b06` has the exact reviewed tree and that integration as its sole parent. This update is for exact-head CI; it is not a landing claim.

- A changed-base predecessor was **rejected: 18 passed / 2 failed**, because generic policy assertions incorrectly let ordinary closed callbacks succeed. That candidate was not published or API-reviewed. The replacement restores the generic policy boundary and passes both unchanged Main recovery tests.
- Independent peer review subsequently found **P2 adapter re-wrapping**. The repair tracks factory outputs in a private `WeakSet`, preserving adapter identity on repeated capture. Two actual red-before regression tests now pass; no producer lease or generic-policy exception was added.
- **65 affected tests qualified across eight files: 53 freshly executed tests across six Gateway files plus 12 previously executed tests carried from two unchanged plugin files. This is not 65 fresh executions.** Coverage includes fresh/resumed delivery, live producer custody, suspended retained assertions/retention/role reads, revocation/retirement, policy/Gateway fences, worker/module-identity controls, adapter identity and duplicate-terminal cleanup. Historical 143-test evidence is not presented as qualification of changed semantics.
- The final runtime-changing Gateway run took **124.37s**; its six product scenarios total approximately **58s**. The carried plugin run took **45.524s** wrapper / **41.36s** Vitest. The subsequent product-test receiver annotation is type-only; runtime evidence was retained through type-erasure equivalence, not a new runtime run. CI timing remains pending.
- Canonical exact-delta autoreview of the adapter repair and the subsequent receiver-only follow-up each completed **scoped-clean at P0–P2, zero findings, one complete assessment and exit 0**. The follow-up review took **24.211s**. The parent verified all 61 adapter-repair and 50 receiver-follow-up bindings without mismatch; consumed review scratch was removed. P3 API coverage is not claimed; static review is not test execution.
- **The same independent Fable peer accepted both the adapter repair and final source `02de164e2fae43e5c671315964656a76f7543691` / tree `61cc52e98ce0b75fb713b4d3f9b9395b0a71c937`, with no P0–P2 findings.** Required exact-head CI/security gates remain outstanding.
- Final one-file typed lint passed in **5.47s**; canonical formatting, diff checks and normal commit hooks passed. Test-line ratchet passed against pinned Main: **897 net test lines / 400 allowance / 497 allocation credit**.
- **Broad canonical typechecking remains unverified:** shared-store `tsrs` declaration containment refused before diagnostics. This is not a green typecheck or an established baseline failure; no containment bypass or dependency change was made.
- **Prior published head `d1dceb308c401c63ef43975248e666c17ba5021b` had failing core5 and aggregate CI gates. Its actual CI failure cause remains unconfirmed:** job-log access returned HTTP 403. The receiver annotation addresses a credible static issue but is not claimed as a confirmed diagnosis of that CI failure. **New-head CI/security qualification is pending; no green-CI claim is made.**

The minimum 497-line per-change allocation retains distinct meaningful regression proof rather than weakening the budget or deleting safeguards. The real Gateway/tools/runtime-lease/policy/registry/delivery composition catches the demonstrated lost-completion paths; separate policy configurations and destructive grant/plugin cases require isolated lifetimes. External model responses and the grant backend are private fixtures; policy verdicts, continuations, persistence and delivery remain real. SQLite and update-handoff stores were confined to task-private roots, with processes joined and roots removed. No live Gateway/app/configuration was changed.

prs.title: fix: show plugin-delivered images in Control UI
prs.body:
Closes #156548
Related: #156613 (earlier unmerged candidate; this repair uses the current source-session owners).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin-delivered images missing from Control UI when `toolContext.delivery.send({ mediaUrl })` successfully sends them to the current conversation's channel.

## User Impact

Delivered images appear in the source conversation and survive history reload, without another channel send. Existing filename-only history is preserved rather than backfilled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The confirmed source-reply mirror retained filenames and URLs but did not prepare managed display attachments. The repair carries the sender's existing reader into the managed-attachment and transcript owners, preserves replay identity, and settles attachment custody before publishing history. Uncommitted preparation is cleaned up; committed media survives cancellation.

Relative references also retain the sender-scoped intent of #152219: they resolve against the sender workspace, honor reader denial and never fall back to a same-named Gateway-CWD file. HTTP ingestion is unchanged. No schema, worker, configuration or public plugin API rewrite; the loader moves into its existing preparation sibling to satisfy the line-cap gate.

The cleanup now prunes cases, not just setup: **10 → 3 new media cases**, with the standalone source-mirror test file deleted. Media-test growth against the pinned base falls from the original **387 added lines** (315 after the first cleanup) to **135 added / 6 removed, 129 net**. The inherited Visitor expectation correction remains separate and unchanged: three added/one removed lines. Whole PR: **353 additions / 71 deletions, 282 net**, across 11 existing files; production growth remains 149 net lines, total test growth 131, docs two. No new test file or generic harness remains.

## Evidence

- Published pruning head: `ba85aa6a4107aa1179a863ce7de56f7734370151`, a fast-forward test-only child of `aa2c508c1f7b446bdc6570b2c953e58ef07a0334`. Pinned rebase base remains `8e6768f91235b7b094f7f8dde96735d727a3f748`. No history rewrite or runtime change.
- **Exact-head [CI run 43534799442](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43534799442) completed successfully.** The required `openclaw/ci-gate`, security-sensitive review and applicable security checks are successful. GitHub reports the PR mergeable with a clean merge state. Verified November 14, 2026, 01:01 UTC; nothing merged, bypassed or set to auto-merge.
- Existing plugin, managed-media, privacy/cancellation and transcript-owner coverage passed in the 112-case selection. After final placement in the existing ingestion/recovery suite, all **17 recovery/media-identity cases pass**; the two reader cases additionally fail against the exact old loader and pass with the repair. These counts overlap and are not newly added cases. Gateway-root and agents-sessions test typechecks, scoped lint/format, whitespace and commit gates pass. The line-cap gate rejected growing the large managed-media test file, so the two checks use the existing smaller ingestion/recovery suite and its scoped state fixture instead. No gate was waived.
- The retained plugin-delivery regression still has its proven red/green result: zero display images after database reopen on unchanged pinned-main media source, visible managed image with the repair. The final relocated sender-reader regressions fail for wrong Gateway bytes and acceptance despite sender denial on the old loader, then pass with the repaired loader. Production-identical real-Gateway proof below remains applicable.
- Independent P0–P2 review of the exact final pruning diff against `aa2c508c`: no actionable findings. The committed patch was compared byte-for-byte with the reviewed diff. This is static diff review, separate from executed tests and earlier complete-range review.
- ClawSweeper's completed `d3592fb3` review found no actionable findings and accepted the real Gateway/media evidence. Its existing request is complete; no duplicate hosted request was posted for this test-only push. That hosted review is parent-head evidence; the final pruning has its own independent diff review and exact-head CI above.

<details>
<summary>What was pruned and why</summary>

- **Primary regression retained (one case):** plugin delivery → persisted display image after database reopen, managed-artifact resolution, one send. This catches the reported defect at the caller-to-persistence boundary. Its existing fixture stays at 79 added lines, down from the original 125.
- **Exposed sender-reader bug retained (two cases):** allow/deny variants move into the existing managed-media ingestion/recovery fixture, using different sender and Gateway-CWD bytes. They directly guard the actual review-discovered relative-path authority bypass; no source-session harness is needed.
- **Standalone replay/conflict and released-history cases removed:** the existing transcript media-identity cases already own persisted replay/conflict and literal old-row reopen. Nine net lines strengthen those existing cases for the new display-preparation callback: skipped for old rows, invoked once for concurrent fresh writes, with display content persisted. No new transcript cases or fixtures.
- **Separate absolute-reader-denial and sensitive-media cases removed:** no new absolute-path semantics; the moved denial regression covers the exposed reader bypass. Existing plugin binding/root checks and final-media privacy-owner tests cover the unchanged permission and sensitive-exclusion policy.
- **Three cancellation cases removed:** existing writer tests cover revoked authority before commit and custody completion at the first post-commit async boundary; managed-media tests cover partial-preparation rollback and pending-read abort. The deleted post-commit scenario only aborted after the mirror had already completed, weaker than the existing owner race test.

This deletes the 236-line source-mirror suite rather than relocating its harness. Runtime authorization, replay, cancellation and custody code are untouched. The earlier 80-test selection meant 10 new plus 70 existing cases, not 80 additions.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Separate inherited CI expectation correction</summary>

[Run 43524086665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43524086665), on `d3799e80`, had one failing test plus its aggregate gate: Visitor Access policy-reopen expected `GatewayOperatorAccessDeniedError` but received `GatewayOperatorAccessUnavailableError`. [Earlier run 43519250072](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43519250072) showed the same failure.

The identical 4-pass/1-fail result was independently reproduced on unchanged pinned main and the PR. The native report labels it unknown because no comparable main job exists; direct source-matched reproduction establishes inheritance.

The fixture deliberately deletes the guest `modelPolicy`. Existing runtime semantics classify invalid policy configuration as unavailable, not a decision to revoke the visitor. Commit `d3592fb3` corrects only that expected class, its import and explanatory comment. Valid-policy/uninvited assertions still require denied access. **All five Visitor Access and six policy-invalidation cases pass locally.** This test-only correction is separate from the media fix and unchanged by cleanup; runtime authorization was not relaxed. Old-head CI is not evidence for the cleaned head.

</details>

### Real Gateway/media proof

A built isolated Gateway on production-identical parent `d3799e80` loaded a declared and consented fixture plugin. Its public channel inbound-dispatch path ran the agent and invoked genuine `toolContext.delivery.send`. No Gateway RPC, history response, media response or browser request was mocked, and no transcript rows were injected.

- Authenticated original-image GET: **200**, exact 5,920 source bytes (SHA-256 `e8c7ce0a3a6c52bd904cc55e31a5b3a8b6392dcd70ba9e220ecf0ef1d6bd8c16`).
- The same managed-image URL without its ticket: **401**.
- After source-file deletion, Control UI reload performed another real media GET and decoded the retained image. The destination recorded **one media send**, unchanged after reload.
- Scenario: 7.4 seconds; full focused invocation: 29.37 seconds. Earlier fixture setup/observation mistakes are retained as failed attempts, not product defects.

Only inference and the destination sink were synthetic/local. This is unmocked Gateway/media and browser-transport proof, **not a live external-channel/model-provider test or installed-release upgrade**. No real-user sends or paid services were used. The proof script and receipts remain in the linked work session. Subsequent commits only change tests; runtime source is identical.

![Real isolated Gateway: plugin-delivered image retained after source deletion and history reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f6ea6b0-0131-4c79-be44-940521f9fa3e)

### Original before/after visual proof

**Before**

![Before: plugin-delivered image appears only as a filename](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/784b0dff-8729-4de4-8a77-ab02b93a1c41)

**After**

![After: delivered test image is visible and survives reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39d2d847-b122-45d6-947e-8c809969bce6)

The blue rectangle is the exact synthetic 320×180 regression PNG. These original captures use real persisted projections with mocked Gateway/media transport; the additional capture above uses the real isolated Gateway transport.

Requested and co-authored by @hannesrudolph. Thanks to @NianJiuZst and @Olli0103 for the earlier repair work in #156613 and #156582.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/361d9188-04c9-4379-bd76-be7ea733b8bc)

prs.title: fix(gateway): reduce resident memory on constrained hosts
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## Problem and change

Gateway startup and the first model turn retain unnecessary code and independent readers on memory-constrained ARM64 hosts.

This change shares bounded readers for store discovery, projections and maintenance; retires idle workers under memory pressure; loads optional runtimes on demand; skips empty-store work; and defers optional background work until memory is available. Token-only CLI requests avoid loading credential database machinery.

On hosts with at most 1 GiB of effective memory, Gateway spawns directly instead of retaining the optional default broker. This trades Linux fork latency and optional broker-owned agent-exec cgroup placement for lower resident memory. Command memory monitoring and native database ownership remain active.

Shared queues can delay heavy reads, and first use can load more code. Sustained pressure can delay automatic updates, catalog refresh, cron retention and publication recovery. Manual operations, writer ordering, active work, cleanup and restart authority keep their existing owners. There are no new configuration options, dependencies or persistent formats.

## Runtime proof

Revision `523851ff` passed the original Linux ARM64 acceptance workload with the official source image, Node 24.22.1, a real OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` reply and a 60.382-second healthy soak:

- Authoritative outer peak: **916.641 MiB**, below the unchanged **928 MiB** ceiling.
- Health: 7.345 seconds; reply: 19.498 seconds; client exit: 0.
- No OOM, restart or swap. All 27 controller commands joined and owned resources closed.
- Limits: 768 MiB service, 1 GiB outer/client, one CPU; V8 old/young limits 256/4 MiB.

Later changes repair type-only imports, narrow guards and test fixtures, and add failure-only test diagnostics plus bounded shutdown receipt fields. These measurements remain tied to `523851ff`; they are not a new-head measurement. The physical Cardputer is offline. Physical-device operation and a 512 MiB service are **not qualified**.

## Review and validation

Targeted worker, history, import-boundary, credential, process-lifecycle and configuration checks cover the production changes, including regressions that fail before their fixes. Core types, targeted lint/format, architecture/import checks, native-wrapper closure and database inventory checks passed. The database ratchet remains 167 → 167 live main-thread calls. Fresh independent P0–P2 reviews completed after the production repairs.

At `7b182384`, the guest-dictation test adds only fixed phase names and elapsed times on failure; assertions, execution order, cleanup and the 30-second deadline are unchanged. Its focused test and lint/format pass. The previous 15-file/117-test group passes with eight workers and pinned Bun in CI mode on both `a2d41be5` and baseline `82123cd1`. Passing replays do not establish the cause of an earlier timeout.

At `aca31622`, incomplete close receipts include the existing close flags, available checkpoint health and post-close WAL size. No checkpoint, seal, retry or close-order behavior changes. The pinned-reader diagnostic regression fails before the change and passes after it; 131 state tests pass (one skipped), along with core types, targeted type-aware lint and formatting. Fresh P0–P2 review is clean.

At `a489b610`, the concurrent-admission test holds the existing session mutation until the duplicate request observes pending admission, then joins both requests before cleanup. The callback, response and dispatch assertions are unchanged. Its shared hold helper moved unchanged into the existing session-store test support, reducing the oversized main test file. No production code or timeout changed. The final 62-test file passes in 100.25 seconds including the runner; core types, type-aware lint, formatting and the line-cap ratchet pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is clean.

At `7cbc7bea`, rebased onto `19a88c18` and dropped the superseded lazy-history commit in favor of [the upstream explicit-prewarm implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198512). All 35 retained patches are unchanged. The rebased import, reader-lane, lifecycle, explicit-prewarm and build-graph checks pass: 124 tests, plus core types, type-aware lint, formatting and the line-cap ratchet. The chat-test fix is byte-identical to the reviewed and tested `a489b610` version.

## CI evidence and remaining gaps

[Current-head CI run 43540103758](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43540103758) tests `7cbc7bea` as merge `ce5992e3` over `d2bfdb0d`. All non-PostgreSQL jobs have finished; five test jobs failed while PostgreSQL conformance finishes.

Three failures have baseline attribution: the title fixture leaves independent naming work running across mock resets; the model-auth-refresh fixture retains an old account row (previously reproduced on baseline); and the Visitor fixture expects denial after deleting a required model policy. Their relevant owners and test inputs are unchanged from the actual CI base. The title attribution is source-established; no failing exact-base replay is claimed.

Two jobs remain unattributed:

- Restart handoff exits successfully, but the agent database reports `checkpoint-incomplete` with a 6,163,552-byte WAL, so the required clean-close receipt is missing. The blocking connection and close caller are not identified.
- Session-message events time out for a blocked placeholder and spawn/route metadata. Both cases pass locally on the prepared head; their complete 11-file CI group also passes with the same two-worker setting: 127 tests in 93.60 seconds including the runner. These replays do not explain the CI failure.

No timeout, assertion, checkpoint or durability requirement has been weakened. The original ARM acceptance remains revision-bound as described above. Current CI, required reviews and native merge gates still apply.

[Prior run 43536410184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43536410184) and [earlier run 43529591006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43529591006), including their failed cases and paired baseline/merge replays, remain in native review evidence. The concurrent-admission failure is fixed above; earlier passing replays are not claimed as causal repairs. Two local failures also remain recorded: a skill watcher returning stale content and linked-path cleanup interrupted by logging.

## What Problem This Solves

Teams tests duplicated parts of the inbound runner and attachment policy, while the test isolation guard treated SQLite file URIs as literal paths.

## User Impact

No user-visible production change. This strengthens internal tests and private test support; production LOC delta is zero. The test-line ratchet remains unresolved, so this is not ready to land.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixtures now use the real public inbound runner and isolated session persistence, with dispatch injected at its existing per-turn boundary. Cleanup joins session work and canonical SQLite cleanup before deleting owned roots, while explicit runtime-config reload snapshots remain intact.

Attachment checks assert ordered saved results and adapter forwarding without duplicating media policy or replacing the existing real SharePoint storage path. The SQLite guard checks NUL before canonical decoding and retains physical containment and original opener arguments. Superseded suites and the retired SQLite coordinator remain removed.

The correction is integrated on frozen base 91d08c31d14cd85be17e5ecb4d8a0ec075ef53bb. Final head is f7a21e31e0976f3ea1de083cede24f7965fd8200: 15 test/private-support source files, +500/-197 lines, plus the exact test-line allocation.

- **Final source review:** one complete review of E and its whole owner/caller context found no actionable findings. This was source-only, not another runtime or CI run.
- **Environment:** Darwin arm64, pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1, Node 26.12.1 launcher. The remote backend stopped before receiver/tests; normal trusted-source local fallback supplied these results. No Linux, native Windows or live Teams proof is claimed.

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #163150

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: when a SQLite store worker thread disappears, the worker lifecycle counters call it an
unattributed `exit` and the Gateway log says nothing, so an operator cannot tell a crash from a
retirement the broker asked for.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: a retirement the broker requested now shows its own reason (`closed`, or `failure`
when the slot had already failed) in the stability bundle's `workerLifecycle`, and a worker that
leaves without any request writes exactly one warning line naming its cause to the log file, so a
lost storage worker is diagnosable from the bundle and the log instead of only from a repro.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The lifecycle registry takes the retirement reason from whatever the worker's owner recorded
before native exit; without that record it falls back to `exit`, which
`docs/gateway/prometheus.md` already defines as "an owner did not specify a reason". The task-pool
owners do record it, the SQLite store worker owner never did, so every one of its retirements
landed in the fallback. Reasons are now recorded where this owner asks the worker to leave, and on
the `error`/`messageerror` events that precede native exit. A departure that no one requested has
no other witness, so it is logged once at warn; requested retirements stay silent because their
caller already reports the outcome. Nothing in the broker's failure path changed, and the log line
carries only the redacted error text.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Failing test first, then the fix, on `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts`:

```
 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
    207|       await lifecycle.retire(slot);
  >  209|       expect(retirementCount("closed")).toBe(closedBefore + 1);

 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
  >  253|     expect(retirementCount("failure")).toBe(failureBefore + 1);
```

After the change the same two tests pass, and they check both halves of the symptom against the
real registry and the real log-file transport: a retirement the owner asked for adds a `closed`
count and leaves `exit` unchanged, and a worker that throws on its own adds a `failure` count while
the log file holds one `left without a retirement request` line containing the cause text.

```
 TEST  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts
 ... > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit 87ms
 ... > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause 178ms
```

Adjacent lanes, run locally with the same config:

```

 src/infra/worker-cpu.test.ts             Tests 7 passed with sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts,
                                          Duration 20.95s
```

Local gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files (28ms), `run-oxlint.mjs` on the core tsconfig
reported "Found 0 warnings and 0 errors" (68.1s), `git diff --check` clean, and
`check-line-cap-ratchet.mts` reported "Line-cap ratchet OK: 2 changed source files; no new
violations or over-cap growth". `check-changed.mjs --dry-run` listed the CI gates this diff
selects. Pre-commit hooks ran normally; no hook was skipped.

Cost of the new tests, per the repo validation rules: they add 87ms and 178ms inside a file whose
targeted run takes 26s with a warm transform cache and 212s cold on this machine. Neither test
sleeps, polls, or uses a wall-clock timer; they await the worker `online` event, the slot's own
exit promise, and `flushLogger()`.

Gaps worth naming: the run was Windows, where the six pre-existing cases in this test file already
fail at `fileURLToPath("file:///openclaw/...")` with `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` before this
change and in code this diff does not touch, so those cases are covered here by CI's Linux infra

Fixes excessive transcript decoding when recovering accepted nested tool activity across unrelated messages.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintenance reader decoded every body between the accepted first and last entries before filtering activity. It now uses existing stored metadata to admit candidate compressed SQLite rows before payload decoding. Inline, exceptional, ambiguous and PostgreSQL rows retain their existing decoding path; scope, ordering, admission and malformed-evidence checks stay with their owners.

prs.title: fix(google-meet): cancel interrupted status, transcript and doctor reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: interrupting `openclaw googlemeet status`, `googlemeet transcript`, or
`googlemeet doctor` leaves the pending `googlemeet.status` / `googlemeet.transcript`
request alive. The CLI hangs in signal-exit cleanup (`Waiting for cleanup before
exiting.`) until the 5s gateway timeout, then the watchdog SIGKILLs it (-9) — the
Ctrl+C never owns the exit.

The same shape was fixed this week for extensions CLI reads by the interrupt family
(#197750 codex sessions, #197749 memory-wiki, #195603 team-reports). The Google Meet
CLI reads were remaining `callGatewayFromCli` callers that did not pass the command
abort signal.

Precedent: #197749 (memory-wiki) — same shape, same `callGoogleMeetGateway` /
`callGoogleMeetRuntime` delegation, extension-side `getAsyncWorkSignal` from
`openclaw/plugin-sdk/concurrency-runtime`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`callGoogleMeetGateway` now accepts and forwards an `AbortSignal` into the existing
Gateway transport call. `callGoogleMeetRuntime` captures `getAsyncWorkSignal()` for the
three read-only commands (`status`, `transcript`, `doctor`) and passes it through; once
the signal aborts it returns `undefined` and the action prints nothing, never starting a
local runtime fallback. The write actions (`join`, `leave`, `speak`, `test-speech`,
`test-listen`) keep their receipt behavior and are not guarded, matching the #197750
read/write split.

No new validator, option, config surface, or persistence change. Non-interrupted reads
print exactly as before. Write commands do not pass a signal, so their behavior is
unchanged (guarded by a TypeScript overload that keeps `Result` for writes).

Production LOC: `+76/-21` across `cli-shared.ts`, `cli-command-context.ts`, `cli.ts`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Interrupting `googlemeet status` / `transcript` / `doctor` no longer hangs the CLI in
cleanup until the gateway timeout; the CLI exits 130 immediately without a late result
or error. Uninterrupted reads and the write commands behave identically.

## Evidence

### Discriminative regression (remote vitest, node v24.22.1)

`extensions/google-meet/src/cli.test.ts` gains a test that settles each read only after
the command scope begins closing (`AsyncWorkScope.beginClose()`) and asserts the captured
stdout is empty.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| BASE (unfixed; test file only) | `prints no googlemeet.status/transcript reply that lands after Ctrl+C` **3 FAIL** (reply printed) |
| HEAD (fixed) | 37 passed (includes the 3 new Ctrl+C tests) |

```sh
node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts extensions/google-meet/src/cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

### Shipped real-behavior proof (real CLI, synthetic loopback Gateway peer)

Same recipe as the accepted #198254/#197750 proofs: the real CLI entry
(`node --import tsx src/entry.ts googlemeet status --json`) runs against a synthetic
loopback peer (challenge → `connect` → `hello-ok` protocol 4) that **holds** the
`googlemeet.status` request forever. A PTY sends Ctrl+C once the peer reports the held
read, and the harness measures interrupt→exit. The read is never released, so a cancelled
read is the only thing that lets the CLI exit cleanly.

| Variant | Exit code | Ctrl+C→exit | status read | Watchdog |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BASE (unfixed) | **-9 (SIGKILL)** | **2112.8 ms** | held, not cancelled | no (exits via kill) |
| HEAD (fixed) | **130 (SIGINT)** | **350.1 ms** | cancelled | no |

Base stderr: `Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` — the
pending read holds the signal-exit barrier until the watchdog SIGKILLs it. Head exits 130
immediately with the read cancelled and no late output.

Full receipts: `proof/googlemeet-read-cancel/{base,head}/receipt.json` on the
`proof/googlemeet-read-cancel` branch of the contributor fork (EVIDENCE.md + harness
`drive-peer.mjs` / `drive.py` included).

Uninterrupted control: covered by the 34 pre-existing vitest cases on the exact head. No
watchdog kill in any run.

### Cleanup

Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`HOME`/`TMPDIR` per run, synthetic
token `synthetic-proof-token`, peer on a random loopback port. No production Gateway,
session, credential, or real Meet session was touched.
