prs.title: fix: agent-selected themes keep the previous accent and fonts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the agent selects or applies a different theme, an accent or font chosen earlier in Appearance keeps covering the new theme, so the theme the person asked for does not look like itself. Choosing the same theme in Appearance already resets those overrides, so the result depended on where the theme was chosen.

## User Impact

User impact: selecting a different theme shows that theme's own accent and fonts, whether it was chosen in Appearance or by the agent with the `theme` tool (`set`, or `import` with `apply: true`). Changing only light/dark/system mode, reselecting the current theme, and importing a theme without applying it keep the person's accent and font overrides. Accent or font values sent together with the selection still win, so Appearance behaves exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reset rule lived only in the Control UI, which sends `accent: "theme"` and cleared fonts alongside the new theme. The Gateway `themes.set` and `themes.import` handlers, which both Appearance and the agent tool use, now apply the same defaults whenever the selected theme changes, so there is one owner for the rule. The Control UI keeps its own reset because it also updates the browser immediately and covers connections without a profile; its requests already carry explicit values, so its stored result is unchanged. Tool description and docs now describe the behavior.

Accepted edge case: like Appearance today, choosing a different theme stores `ui.accent: "theme"`, which uses one profile preference key. A profile already at the preference key limit cannot apply a newly imported theme until a key is freed; the existing limit test was adjusted for that.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway and Control UI (synthetic owner profile, no live data). Steps on each build: select Claw, save a custom pink accent (`#ff2d95`) to the profile, then send `themes.set {"id":"phosphor"}` from the CLI, which is the same request the agent's `theme` tool sends. prs.title: fix(infra): preserve git identity for dev install badge detection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two distinct git-identity defects in `resolveDevInstallGitBranch` (the Control UI dev-gateway badge classifier) are fixed together in its 63-line owner:

1. **Qualified refs from same-name tags.** `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns a **qualified ref** (`heads/main`, or `refs/heads/main` when other refs deepen the ambiguity) when the checked-out branch shares a name with a tag. The old code compared that output directly against `HIDDEN_BRANCHES` (`{"main", "master", "HEAD"}`), so a mainline checkout on branch `main` with a same-name tag `main` was **not hidden** — the Control UI sidebar showed a dev-gateway badge carrying a qualified ref (e.g. `refs/heads/main`).
2. **Whitespace-suffixed checkout roots.** `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` output was `.trim()`ed before the toplevel comparison. A checkout whose directory legitimately ends in whitespace (for example `/srv/openclaw `) had its meaningful trailing space stripped, failed the root comparison, and was classified as "not a source checkout" — the dev-gateway badge silently never rendered for that install. This is the same root-cause family already approved in #196654 (`update-check`) and #197973 (`doctor`), and the same predicate wording already shipped on main in `src/projects/project-checkout.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Fix 1 (review follow-up to the prefix-stripping approach, thanks @roboclaw-bot / ClawSweeper):** stripping `heads/` from abbreviated output cannot distinguish a **mainline checkout with a colliding tag** from a **literal branch named `heads/main`** — both abbreviate identically. This revision reads the actual branch identity with `git branch --show-current` (the same owner `session-diff.runtime` already uses) and applies the existing hidden-name check unchanged. No prefix stripping, no normalization.

**Fix 2:** the toplevel comparison now removes only Git's final LF record terminator (`replace(/\n$/, "")`), preserving filesystem characters in the checkout path — exactly matching the shipped `project-checkout.ts` wording and the approved #196654/#197973 predicate. Ordinary paths are byte-for-byte unaffected.

**Fix classification:** Fix 1 is `behavior-preserving` (only the previously-misclassified qualified-mainline case moves to `null`; literal `heads/`-prefixed names keep rendering). Fix 2 is `behavior-completing` (it completes the same approved family as #196654/#197973 for the dev-badge owner). No new helper, export, or config.

## User Impact

- **Qualified refs:** before, a source checkout whose branch shares a name with a tag (e.g. branch `main` + tag `main`) showed a dev-gateway badge (e.g. `refs/heads/main`); after, mainline checkouts stay hidden while genuinely drifted checkouts (including a literal branch named `heads/main`) show their real branch name.
- **Whitespace roots:** before, a source checkout under a whitespace-suffixed directory never showed the badge (misread as a non-checkout); after, the badge appears exactly as it does for ordinary checkouts. A path that merely looks similar after trimming no longer misclassifies.

## Evidence

### Remote red/green on the exact head (real git, both fixes)

Vitest on the real runner (docker `lexiflow-all`, Node v24.22.1, portable git), `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/dev-install-branch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, against this branch's head `c35483fa17db`:

- **14/14 pass** on the exact head, including a new real-git control: `git init` in a temp directory whose name ends in a meaningful space (`whitespace `), feature branch `feat/dev-branch-badge` checked out, only package-root discovery stubbed — the resolver returns `"feat/dev-branch-badge"`.
- **RED control (same tree, predicate short-circuited):** with only the toplevel line reverted to `topRes.stdout.trim()` and everything else byte-identical, the new whitespace control fails (`expected null to be 'feat/dev-branch-badge'`) while the other 13/14 pass unchanged — so the green comes from this diff, not from the environment.
- Legal controls unchanged: mainline/tag-collision, literal `heads/main`, tagged feature branch, detached HEAD, nested package, git-missing, and non-interactive cases all keep their prior classification.

The real-git controls execute the production resolver against real git subprocesses; no git output is mocked in that block.

### Real behavior proof through the shipped Control UI (fix 1)

Real Gateway (`openclaw.mjs --dev gateway`, loopback only) booted from a source checkout with the colliding tag, driven with Playwright against the served Control UI; bootstrap cross-checked at `/control-ui-config.json` in the same page. Loopback-only, synthetic local token, default identity — no credentials or non-public endpoints in captures.

| State | Checkout | `/control-ui-config.json` `devGitBranch` | Sidebar badge |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Before** (base `8f9190485c6` code) | branch `main` + tag `main` | `"refs/heads/main"` | **shown: `refs/heads/main`** (wrong) |
| **After** (this branch) | branch `main` + tag `main` | `null` | **hidden** (correct) |
| **After** (this branch) | literal branch `heads/main` | `"heads/main"` | **shown: `heads/main`** (correct literal name) |

![Badge before/after comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/badge-before-after-compare.png)

- Before, branch `main` + tag `main`: [full capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/before-tagged-main-full.png) — badge `refs/heads/main`.
- After, same checkout: [full capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/after-tagged-main-full.png) — no badge.
- After, literal `heads/main` branch: [full capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/after-literal-heads-main-full.png) — badge `heads/main`.

### Review response

- **[P2] Preserve literal branch names** — fixed by replacing prefix stripping with `git branch --show-current`; the real-git control above (identical abbreviated output, divergent classification) passes.
- **[Needs proof]** — provided via the real Gateway + shipped Control UI captures above, including the visible literal `heads/main` control.

### Local checks

- `check-test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main` — pass (`slack: 0`); allocation `dev-install-branch-identity.txt` raised 70 → 81 for the new real-git control (+9) plus absorbed main drift (+2), per the repo's ratchet contract.
- oxfmt on changed files — clean; `git diff --check` — clean.
- Full `check:changed` / typecheck cannot run on this host (glibc below the tsgo native binary requirement); the PR CI lanes carry them.

## Not tested

- The whitespace control is skipped on Windows (`it.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")`), where Win32 path APIs cannot address a directory whose name ends in whitespace — the same platform gating the approved #196654 family uses.
- Windows/macOS git variants for `branch --show-current` — it has produced the actual branch name across platforms since git 2.22 (the same dependency `session-diff.runtime` already relies on).
- The footer badge element itself is already covered by the existing UI e2e (`ui/src/e2e/sidebar-dev-branch.e2e.test.ts`); the fix-1 proof exercised the real Gateway→bootstrap→UI chain end to end. The whitespace fix is below the UI layer (owner predicate), proven at the resolver boundary with real git.

## Cleanup

No state/config/session/token touched in the product. Fix-1 proof ran in an isolated temp checkout (`/tmp/ocdevproof192034`) with its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; the temp repo and state were removed after capture. Fix-2 red/green ran in isolated remote vitest trees with only package-level dependency overlays. Media for this body lives on the fork's `proof-192034-media` branch.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old comparison. Blast radius is the dev-install badge classification in the Control UI sidebar. Production diff: `src/infra/dev-install-branch.ts` +12/-9; test +76/-0; allocation record +5. Both fixes sit in the same 63-line owner and the same test file, so they ship in one reviewable unit rather than two conflicting PRs.

Precedent: #196654, #197973, `src/projects/project-checkout.ts` (shipped predicate wording), #191047, #191155, #104262

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

- Maintainer edits allowed: yes — address review comments directly on this branch.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready: both predicates are one-line, worded exactly like the already-approved #196654/#197973 family; red/green is reproduced on the real runner with the predicate short-circuit control.
- Alternative: land fix 2 as a separate PR after this one — not recommended; same file, same test file, guaranteed textual conflict.
- Scope declaration: behavior-preserving (qualified refs) + behavior-completing (whitespace roots); no change to badge rendering, only to identity detection.

</details>

prs.title: chore(postgres): qualify notice transcript crash recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The PostgreSQL recovery qualification did not cover a Gateway dying after the recovery notice transcript committed but before its worker reply allowed notice-debt acknowledgement.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. This adds crash-recovery qualification within the existing schema and persistence contracts; it changes no production code, schema/version, DDL, migrations, stored format, config, public API, retention, or durability policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing process-crash table with `notice-transcript-reply-lost`. The preload forwards the exact keyed `session.turn.commit` request and withholds only its successful committed receipt. Candidate/admission frames occur before COMMIT and remain untouched.

An independent PostgreSQL connection must observe one committed notice transcript, completed notice receipt, owed notice debt, and the original failure awaiting settlement. After SIGKILL and restart, debt must be acknowledged, the original failure finalized, the entire transcript stream unchanged, and the synthetic HTTP sink must still contain exactly one notice. The four existing crash windows retain their assertions and shared cleanup.

## Evidence

- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P3), complete local candidate against `961b23b3210da439214ce3381476d1a53c95f87a`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Required owner/worker source supplied. Reviewer did not execute tests; primary separately verified the existing cleanup and 998 counted lines against the 1,000-line cap.
- Static proof: `git diff --check` passes; formatting completed in the pre-commit hook; built-in Node parsing checks all 10 generated crash/restart preload variants.
- Exact candidate `2f8b4df068bc68479ac7da70c81b063250f1ab61`: [manual CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43533287147). Actual source checkout verified in preflight; the run metadata SHA identifies the separate trusted harness. All three PostgreSQL 17 conformance shards passed. [Shard 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43533287147/job/132256776950) executed the new `notice-transcript-reply-lost` case successfully (78.256 seconds), along with the existing crash windows. [Build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43533287147/job/132256776100), lint, production/test types, guards, and SQLite schema baseline checks passed. [PR-only PostgreSQL 16 smoke](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43536823903/job/132268339524) subsequently passed all 12 Gateway tests, including all five crash windows; the new case passed in 46.782 seconds.
- The managed checkout is code-only. The Crabbox wrapper refused the canonical tooling install (`@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.26.13 versus required 0.27.1); proof used CI without installing local dependencies or starting another remote allocation.
- The pre-commit line-cap ratchet could not start: installed oxlint 1.88.0 differs from required 1.89.0. The draft commit used `--no-verify`; CI lint and guard gates subsequently passed.
- Production delta: 0. Tests/support: +46/-10 lines (net +36), reusing the existing suite and preload; no new test-only production seam or registration.
- Limits: synthetic transport, real isolated Gateway and PostgreSQL process-death qualification. No live Telegram, indefinite exactly-once, or newly fixed production-defect claim.

## Broader CI and Follow-up

The manual full-matrix run also reports failures outside this two-file test change: native/UI translation inventories, dependency export inventory, UI browser/E2E behavior, spawn-broker retention, Swift tunnel timing, utility completion, visitor access policy, plugin reload fixtures, process engine-selection isolation, systemd upgrade fixture, and backup/restore scratch cleanup. Those source inputs are unchanged by this PR; this does not claim the whole matrix is green or establish the cause of every unrelated failure. The ordinary PR CI attempt and its failure classifications will be retained separately.

Concrete next persistence audit: [backup/restore scratch retirement fails with `database is locked`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43533287147/job/132256802841) in `src/infra/backup-create.worktrees.test.ts:68` / `src/commands/backup-verify.ts:689`. Investigate transaction/connection cleanup under the same schema embargo; no speculative fix is included here.

A second lifecycle follow-up is [credential-test process-selection isolation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43533287147/job/132256787360): `src/gateway/server-database-engine.credentials.test.ts:35` encounters the existing immutable process-selection guard. The changed PostgreSQL crash suite is absent from that job's logs, and both credential test and selection owner are unchanged. Preserve the runtime guard while investigating the test's initial global selection.

[Exact-head hosted source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198511#issuecomment-6868560918) found no actionable code defect. Its one before-merge move requested actual execution of the five windows plus build/type/lint/format proof; the linked manual CI and static evidence above now supply that proof. The head is unchanged, so no rating-only re-review was requested.

[Ready-PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43536823903) completed successfully: 28 passed, 29 intentional skips, no failures. It tested merge checkout `3b5bd205149a10df1d4303114727032f2e9eda19`, incorporating this exact head into main `a1083027deecf9ba0fd4f833cb8b984308300fad`; preflight checkout was independently inspected. All three PG17 conformance shards and PG16 smoke passed. The job logs confirm all five crash windows executed successfully on both PG17 and PG16. All six applicable security review boundaries passed.

Landed by the native gated squash route as [51c2f42a8e02](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/51c2f42a8e029f667829c753d7098af911dd7f70). No schema or persistence-contract changes are included.

prs.title: fix(templates): publishing a Template from chat drops its CLAW.md description and rewrites its name
prs.body:
Closes #196643

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Template published from chat loses the description written in its `CLAW.md`, and its explicit agent name is rewritten (`Incident Follow-up Desk` becomes `Incident Follow Up Desk`, `macOS Release Notes` becomes `MacOS Release Notes`), when the draft's top-level `description` is still the empty value new drafts start with.

## User Impact

User impact: the Template review shows the name and description the agent wrote in `CLAW.md`, and the published package keeps them. A draft without an agent name still gets the readable title-cased default from its package slug, and editing or clearing the fields in review still takes precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

New drafts are seeded with `description: ""`. The review was meant to fall back to the manifest's `agent.description` when the draft has no description of its own, but it used `??`, which does not skip an empty string. As a result the fallback never ran for drafts created by OpenClaw, and the manifest description was removed. The review also passed an explicit `agent.name` through the title-casing meant for the slug default, which replaces `-` and `_` with spaces and capitalizes every word.

Now an empty draft description falls back to the manifest description, and only the slug-derived default is title-cased. Review choices still win, so an explicit empty description from the review modal clears it.

#196427 (open) makes the review read-only. Once it lands, the manifest values are the only way to set the published name and description, so they need to survive review unchanged.

## Evidence

A real Gateway built from main `f4b43b47147` and from this branch, driven with `openclaw gateway call` through the same sequence the Control UI uses: `templates.drafts.create` → `read` → `save` (manifest with `agent.name: Incident Follow-up Desk` and `agent.description`, seeded top-level `description: ""`) → `review` → `publish` with the choices the Control UI builds from that review. Only ClawHub is replaced: a loopback server answers `whoami` and saves the uploaded package, which is then extracted.

| Build | Review `displayName` | Review `description` | Uploaded `CLAW.md` `agent` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main `f4b43b47147` | `Incident Follow Up Desk` | `""` | `name: Incident Follow Up Desk`, no description |
| this branch | `Incident Follow-up Desk` | `Triage incoming incidents and hand off with evidence.` | `name: Incident Follow-up Desk`, `description: Triage incoming incidents and hand off with evidence.` |

Control on main: the same run with the top-level draft `description` filled in publishes the description, so the harness does observe a kept description.

<details>
<summary>Uploaded CLAW.md frontmatter</summary>

main `f4b43b47147`:

```yaml
schemaVersion: 1
agent:
  id: incident-triage
  name: Incident Follow Up Desk
metadata: {}
workspace:
  bootstrapFiles: {}
  files: []
```

this branch:

```yaml
schemaVersion: 1
agent:
  id: incident-triage
  name: Incident Follow-up Desk
  description: Triage incoming incidents and hand off with evidence.
metadata: {}
workspace:
  bootstrapFiles: {}
  files: []
```

</details>

Focused checks:

- `src/templates/draft.test.ts`: the new case fails on main (`expected { … } to match object { …(2) }`) and passes here. It also checks that an explicit empty `choices.description` still clears the description. 13/13 pass; the existing slug-default case ("Research Brief") still passes.

- Test cost: `pnpm test src/templates/draft.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 6.4 s of test time and 14.9 s wall time locally. The new case adds 33 test lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/template-draft-manifest-identity.txt`; `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes.

prs.title: Preserve complete MP3 audio when creating macOS Opus CAF voice attachments
prs.body:
# Preserve complete MP3 audio when creating macOS Opus CAF voice attachments

## Problem
On macOS, direct MP3 → Opus CAF conversion with afconvert can exit successfully while retaining only the first segment of a concatenated MP3. The synthetic regression fixture decodes to 48.074 seconds, but direct conversion produces only 3.310 seconds.

## Change
For MP3 → CAF only, decode with FFmpeg to mono 24 kHz signed 16-bit PCM WAV, validate its RIFF structure, then encode with afconvert. Probe the resulting CAF and reject unexpected format or frame count. Other input formats continue using direct afconvert. All stages share the existing default 5-second timeout budget; temporary files are cleaned on success and failure.

Long clips now produce complete voice memos when conversion fits the budget, or retain the original MP3 attachment when conversion fails or exceeds it. A loaded host or sufficiently long clip may therefore receive an MP3 attachment rather than a voice memo; previously it could receive a silently truncated voice memo. No per-stage reset extends the total conversion budget. The once-only warning is neutral: a conversion failure does not necessarily mean FFmpeg is missing.

## Tests
- Native macOS regression compares decoded PCM frame counts, allowing one 20 ms Opus packet of padding; it skips on non-macOS hosts or when FFmpeg is unavailable. Both the availability probe and PCM decoder resolve FFmpeg through the same trusted-system `resolveFfmpegBin()` helper as production, not an independent PATH lookup.
- Unit coverage includes malformed WAVs, shared timeout exhaustion, missing FFmpeg, encoder/probe failures, cleanup and non-MP3 routing.
- Focused red run against the original module fails; candidate focused tests pass (39/39); targeted oxlint and git diff whitespace checks pass.
- Re-ran red/green after aligning the native FFmpeg lookup: original module produced 79,440 decoded frames; the fixed module produced 1,154,088 against 1,153,775 input frames (313-frame difference, within 480).
- No full build, full typecheck, full test suite, or live Messages playback was performed.

Patch SHA256: `8c7477de221cb321477eaa91b12e3676ab6de5ff631980d809c57350f4f36f6b`.

## Fixture rights and regeneration
`src/media/fixtures/tts-ten-segment.mp3` is entirely mathematical sine tones generated offline, not speech, recordings, model output or private audio. It is dedicated under CC0 1.0 Universal (including the fallback license): https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode.en . No FFmpeg binary is distributed.

Generation uses ten separate FFmpeg sine inputs at frequencies `440 + 37*n` Hz (n=0..9), mono 24 kHz, libmp3lame VBR quality 2. Segment durations in seconds: `3.3, 5.3, 5.475, 5.2, 4.9, 4.075, 6.55, 4.125, 4.025, 4.375`. Encode each independently, then concatenate the MP3 bytes without remuxing, retaining each segment’s Xing header and delay/padding fields. Set each Xing encoder-identification field to `LAME` followed by five spaces, blank encoder-version digits elsewhere, and remove ID3 and format/stream tags. This is a deliberately constructed triggering layout, not a claim about an original encoder. Other FFmpeg/libmp3lame versions may produce different bytes.

The accompanying `fixture-build.py`, `fixture-README.md` and `fixture-LICENSES.md` provide the generator, detailed construction and rights statement. Fixture size: 166,176 bytes. SHA256: `7b2d8a3b1244383a4cfc3beaa57ba756c0d76c7d485fa80f927a458bdb60c0f0`.


Addresses #197531.

prs.body:
<!-- Title: fix(templates): failed Template Add preview warns the Add may be partial -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when `openclaw templates add` runs against a Gateway and the preview fails, the CLI says "The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying", although a preview never changes anything.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed preview now reports that no local mutation was attempted, so users retry or fix the Template instead of inspecting state for a partial Add that cannot exist.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI routes Add through the Gateway that owns the state dir and treats any error reply without `details.mutationAccepted: false` as an unknown outcome. `templates.add.plan` is read-only but sent no marker on either failure branch. Both its UNAVAILABLE and its FORBIDDEN (Labs disabled) replies now carry `mutationAccepted: false`, as other read-only owner methods already do. Error codes and messages are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add.test.ts`: new cases assert the marker on UNAVAILABLE for a ClawHub source error and a generic error; the existing "Labs switched off mid-request" case now also asserts it on FORBIDDEN. They fail on origin/main and pass with the fix.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add.test.ts src/cli/templates-cli.state-owner.test.ts`: pass.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: everything passes except the dead export scan, which fails the same way on origin/main in files this PR does not touch.
- Live run, `openclaw templates add @etzelm/job-application-coordinator` against an isolated Gateway (preview fails on an invalid manifest):

```
before: ... could not complete templates.add.plan ... The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying. No local fallback was attempted.
after:  ... could not complete templates.add.plan ... No local mutation was attempted. Update the Gateway or fix authentication and retry. ...
```

Known gap: the "after" recovery text still suggests updating the Gateway or fixing authentication, which is the CLI's generic owner-refused wording. Changing that text is out of scope here.

prs.title: fix(memory): start default index managers at Gateway boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194164 asks for memory indexing to be fresh right after a Gateway restart:
with the current demand-driven cold start, an agent's index opens on its
first search, flush, or turn, and until then `memory_index_sources`
receives nothing — the reporter observed roughly ten hours of stopped
indexing after an app relaunch.

The original draft of this PR restored eager boot-time indexing for every
configured agent. Review and history showed why that is the wrong default:
#167756 started Memory Core's index service eagerly on every Gateway start,
and #174718 (`6c050f8043`) deliberately reverted it after startup peak RSS
rose from ~1.1 GB to ~1.8 GB (startup catch-up touches every
session-transcript read lane, each spawning its own worker isolate). This
revision keeps that policy intact and adds an explicit operator opt-in
instead:

```jsonc
// memory.search.coldStart
"demand" // default — exactly today's behavior, unchanged
"eager"  // open every configured agent's index at boot and on later service starts
```

Each agent can override the global default with
`agents.entries.<id>.memory.search.coldStart`; the per-agent value wins over
the global setting in both directions, matching how the memory config
resolver treats other `memory.search` fields. Operators who need fresh
indexes immediately (the reporter's local-GGUF fleet) pay a known,
self-inflicted cost; everyone else sees zero change. The demand default, the
`liveIndexing` retention semantics, and the worker/RSS characteristics of
#174718 are untouched.

## The Change

- `memory.search.coldStart` (`"demand"` default | `"eager"`), registered in
  the config schema, field labels/help, and `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`.
- `memory-core-index` service start resolves the opt-in per agent:
  `resolveAgentConfig(cfg, agentId)?.memory?.search?.coldStart ?? global`.
  `"demand"` (effective) keeps `retainMemoryIndexingAgents` exactly as
  before; `"eager"` opens the agent's index through the existing host-aware
  runtime (`memoryRuntime.getMemorySearchManager`, which supplies the host's
  local-service acquisition — resolving the Revision 1 P2 finding). Manager
  construction marks each agent live, so later reloads retain them like any
  watched index.
- Boundary tests on untouched agents (so acquisition cannot be explained by
  prior demand): a per-agent eager override under a global demand default
  opens only that agent; a per-agent demand override under a global eager
  default keeps that agent lazy. Both fail against the previous
  global-only selector.

## Evidence

- **Unit/boundary tests** (worktree, committed source): `extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts` — 35 passed (2 new per-agent cold-start boundary cases; the previous single eager case was rewritten on untouched agents per review), and `src/config` schema regressions (config.schema-regressions, dead-config-keys, schema.hints) — 263 passed after registering the new field.
- **Regression check:** the two new boundary cases fail on the previous
  global-only selector (2 failed | 33 skipped) and pass with the per-agent
  resolution (35 passed).
- **Live redacted output, built from the committed source** (isolated
  state/workspace, local Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, synthetic data; the same
  state is upgraded in place between scenarios):

  ```text
  ===== SCENARIO 1: coldStart demand (default) =====
  gateway ready (demand)
  # memory file written + chat.send delivered, 45s watcher window, no consumer opens an index
  demand: memory_index_sources rows = 0

  ===== SCENARIO 2: upgrade in place -> coldStart eager =====
  gateway ready (eager)
  # same state, settings and sessions intact, 45s after boot, no consumer call
  eager: memory_index_sources rows = 2
      memory|memory/proof-demand-note.md
      sessions|sessions/main/34d590f2-28ad-4c95-91df-bda672a78c92.jsonl
  eager: memory_search -> {"ok":true,"results":[{"path":"memory/proof-demand-note.md",...
  ```

  Scenario 1 confirms the demand default is byte-for-byte unchanged
  (untouched agents stay lazy). Scenario 2 is the reporter's requested
  behavior, available under the explicit opt-in.

- **Latest-stable → candidate upgrade trace (redacted live output):** a
  dedicated run upgrades a state directory created by released
  **v2026.11.3** (npm, `847611d`) to the candidate built from this PR's
  head, covering both the upgrade-compatibility and data-model items:

  ```text
  ## PHASE S — stable v2026.11.3 (847611d), config without any coldStart key
  [stable] consumer memory_search -> {"ok":true,...}   # demand: index opens on first consumer
  [stable-final] memory_index_sources rows: 2          # memory/upgrade-note-a.md
  [stable-final] memory_index_chunks rows: 2           # + sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl

  ## PHASE C-MIG — candidate refuses unmigrated DB (documented admission guard), then migrates
  "…uses schema version 27; … run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to
   schema version 42 …" | gateway.maintenance_required
  $ openclaw doctor --fix --yes    ->  schema_meta primary = 42
  [post-migration] memory_index_sources: 2  memory_index_chunks: 2   # data survived

  ## PHASE C-A — candidate on migrated stable state, config UNCHANGED (demand default)
  booted healthy; memory_search retrieves the stable-era note
  [candA-final] memory_index_sources: 2                 # demand unchanged: no boot-time growth

  ## PHASE C-B — only delta: memory.search.coldStart = "eager"
  # new file written, then boot with NO consumer call
  [candB] rows BEFORE boot: sources=2 chunks=2
  [candB] rows AFTER eager boot: sources=3 chunks=3     # note B indexed at startup
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-a.md                    # stable-era data intact
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-b.md                    # newly indexed at boot
      sessions|sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl            # stable-era session intact
  consumer memory_search("Post-upgrade synthetic") -> upgrade-note-b.md
  ```

  Existing settings are preserved (the stable-era config carries no
  `coldStart` key; the candidate boots it unchanged under the demand
  default), the stable-written database migrates via the documented
  `doctor --fix` path and loads/works (schema 27 → 42, index rows,
  session transcript, and provenance intact), demand semantics are
  unchanged after upgrade (no growth without a consumer), and the opt-in
  eager mode works on the upgraded state.

  Data-model note: this change adds an optional config field only — no
  stored index, session, or state format changes; the trace above
  demonstrates the stable-release upgrade end to end.

prs.title: perf(ci): avoid a repeated credential-analysis tree walk
prs.body:
## Decision

**Rejected: do not merge.** The measured median inventory improvement was **1.51%**, below the **5%** acceptance threshold fixed before comparison. CPU and memory stayed within their limits. Removing an AST pass alone did not produce a sufficient end-to-end gain.

## Problem and experiment

The database-worker ratchet contributes minutes to `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`. This experiment collected import-binding pairs during the existing first credential-analysis traversal, then resolved them afterward in the same order, removing a second full traversal without narrowing analysis, guards, allowlists, diagnostics, or compiler queries.

Related experiment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198363.

## Reproducible workload and acceptance

`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/database-worker-inventory-measure.mts <analyzer-ref>`

Baseline: `51bdadb343756e358792dd98f5ec14e317326035`.
Candidate: `927f44c025ef3e8d5a41059ec96f69f927b21b36`.

Both arms used one current-tree workload, sorted by path before hashing and analysis. Five fresh processes per arm ran serially in ABAB order. Separate `--count-walks` processes and a separate `--cpu-prof` process were excluded from timing statistics. GNU time captured whole-process user+system CPU, wall time, and peak RSS, including the native compiler.

The unchanged rule required identical ordered input and output, at least 5% lower median inventory time, and no more than 10% regression in CPU or peak RSS. Inventory time excludes source loading/sorting but includes observer overhead; process wall time includes setup.

Boat/ascii-box: `cbx_bded9d11f05f`, run `run_f6e46fdc6a58dc120658bb438a3abdb9`. Requested large tier; observed **8 CPUs by affinity, 16,767,762,432 bytes RAM, Node 24.22.1**. The VM exposed no cgroup v2 CPU/memory limit files; no quota claim is made.

## Results

23,797 source files, 863 inventory rows. Every accepted sample had:

- Ordered input SHA-256: `f685ab32e60877ea48ef6bd308a361b614ad2de66aa3642bc4d87269bcf21bad`.
- Output SHA-256: `12fb0d41bf513df9207c249e883ff479c28ba9fe405ccce9c26d98cdf124d803`.

Each metric cell is **median / p95 / min–max** (p95 is the nearest-rank maximum for five samples).

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inventory seconds | 61.78 / 67.29 / 60.30–67.29 | 60.85 / 63.22 / 59.57–63.22 |
| Process wall seconds | 62.70 / 68.25 / 61.24–68.25 | 61.73 / 64.16 / 60.46–64.16 |
| Total CPU seconds | 107.73 / 112.08 / 105.54–112.08 | 106.84 / 108.07 / 101.91–108.07 |
| Peak RSS MiB | 5799.74 / 5843.66 / 5671.17–5843.66 | 5787.20 / 5901.15 / 5484.07–5901.15 |

Median deltas: inventory **−1.51%**, process wall **−1.55%**, CPU **−0.83%**, peak RSS **−0.22%**.

| Pair | Baseline inventory seconds | Candidate inventory seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 67.295 | 63.216 |
| 2 | 60.302 | 60.846 |
| 3 | 64.975 | 59.964 |
| 4 | 61.781 | 61.804 |
| 5 | 61.490 | 59.569 |

Separate counted runs: AST visits **64,622,899 → 42,074,455 (−34.89%)**. Compiler request counts were unchanged: **240,103 semantic + 809 syntax** per arm.

The separate candidate CPU profile completed with matching input/output hashes. Its largest sampled frame was `read` (24.33%); GC accounted for 9.07%. This profile is diagnostic, not an additional timing sample or a claim about billed CI savings.

## Correctness and review

- All four focused files passed: **230 tests in 10.27 seconds**, covering credential writers, session-repair edges, database compatibility and the ratchet. Boat run `run_04161d9e6691ebcbb92b66e47aa586d4` verified source `0f5282386c291ec5e60a0d849a890fc7b4173328`; the only subsequent change sorted this benchmark's inputs.
- Fresh independent source review and local ClawSweeper review of the original production change found no actionable correctness/security issue. The later benchmark-order correction received an independent read-only review.
- Syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- [Prior-head full CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43462983545) passed build artifacts, core lint/type stripes, central lint, production/root-test types, baseline ratchets, and unused-file scans. It remained red in untouched dependency, PostgreSQL-inventory, Gateway/Talk and native-systemd surfaces; it is not presented as green or as current-head CI.

## Excluded attempts

Two Blacksmith Testboxes queued and were stopped without running tests. Boat setup failures ran no benchmark samples. The initial unsorted counting pair returned identical output but different ordered input hashes because `rg --files` enumerates nondeterministically; those measurements were discarded. The harness now sorts entries, and the complete accepted comparison above uses that corrected committed harness.

The experiment remains below its predeclared performance bar and should be closed without merging.

Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

The unchanged selection keeps its familiar name during disconnects and catalog gaps. Fresh catalog metadata replaces that name; changing Gateway, agent, session, or model clears it. Model selection, availability, eligibility, and request ordering remain unchanged.

prs.body:
<!-- Title: fix(templates): Template Add fails when the state dir path contains a symlink -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Gateway Template Add ends partial with `template_initialization_failed` when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` sits under a symlinked path.

## User Impact

User impact: Templates Add and open normally on hosts where the state dir is reached through a symlink (for example a home folder linked to an external volume). Before, the new agent and chat were kept but the Template's workspace files were never written.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway Add first admits the agent and its workspace, then replans with that admitted workspace. The planner compared the realpath of the target workspace with the raw admitted path, so under a symlink the two differed and the planner reported a workspace collision against the workspace it had just created. The admitted path now goes through the same canonicalizer before the comparison. Identical inputs still compare equal.

## Evidence

- New test in `src/templates/gateway-add-plan.test.ts` symlinks a temp state dir, points `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` at the link and asserts no `workspace_collision`. It fails on origin/main and passes with the fix.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/templates/gateway-add-plan.test.ts src/templates/gateway-add-apply.test.ts`: pass.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: everything passes except the dead export scan, which fails the same way on origin/main in files this PR does not touch.
- Live run, isolated Gateway built from this branch stack, state dir `~/work/.../home/.openclaw` where `~/work` is a symlink to an external volume:

```
before: templates add myfitnessclaw
{"agentId":"myfitnessclaw-2","status":"partial","error":{"code":"template_initialization_failed","message":"The Template changed since review. Preview it again. ..."}}
after:  templates add myfitnessclaw

workspace-myfitnessclaw-2: AGENTS.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md avatars reference skills templates

```

prs.title: fix(ui): stale theme colors return when an older catalog read finishes late
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, who is the intended reviewer for this PR.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/883de5f4-29a0-436b-9b14-bd0167001845)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e7367350-e2f2-4120-a576-3babb785e62a)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI can show outdated theme colors, or bring back a removed plugin theme, when an older theme catalog read finishes after a newer refresh has started on the same connection and profile.

Two reproduced cases on `main`:

1. A first `themes.list` is still pending, a `users.prefs.changed` event starts a second refresh that applies background `#222222`, and the first read then finishes with `#111111`. The older `#111111` palette wins.
2. A `themes.get` for a plugin theme is still pending, a `plugins.changed` refresh removes that theme from the catalog, and the pending read then finishes. The removed theme becomes available and is applied again.

A profile or client change already discarded these late reads; a refresh on the same connection and profile did not.

## User Impact

User impact: after a profile preference change or a plugin reload, the Control UI keeps the newest theme colors and does not reapply a plugin theme that the catalog no longer contains. There is no visual or settings change otherwise.

## Why This Change Was Made

The theme catalog already owned the decision about whether a response may still publish (connection, client, and profile). It now also records a refresh generation: each refresh supersedes earlier list and palette reads, so only reads started under the newest refresh can publish. A palette read also publishes only while the current catalog still lists its theme, because a palette read started during a refresh can otherwise finish after the new list removed the theme. Dropped palette reads are requested again by the existing path, since each refresh already clears the requested set. No new UI, cache, or state layer was added.

## Evidence

- Two regression tests in `ui/src/app/theme-catalog.test.ts` cover the cases above through the real application theme and Gateway store test harness. Both failed on `main` (`e6c7c5e0da4b`): the first kept `#111111` instead of `#222222`, and the second applied `space-pack/xenovessel` instead of staying on `claw`. Both pass with this change.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/theme-catalog.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 20 of 20 tests pass, about 2.6 seconds.
- Consumer tests that import the theme catalog or application theme (11 files, including `bootstrap-theme.palette`, `config-page.appearance-catalogs`, `config-page`, and `appearance-background.browser`): all pass.
- `tsgo:ui` and the `tsgo:test:ui` shards pass; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on both files; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `origin/main` at `e6c7c5e0da4b`, P0–P2, with the catalog, its test file, and `bootstrap-theme.ts` as source context): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Not run locally: broad UI suites and Control UI end-to-end runs; PR CI covers broad proof. This is not a visual change, so there are no screenshots.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(sessions): reduce memory for lightweight transcript reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Lightweight transcript reads load the full history presentation graph when a foreground worker starts, even with Control UI disabled.

## User Impact

Lightweight workers retain about 10 MiB less heap and finish their first lookup sooner. History presentation remains available on demand, and enabled Control UI still uses explicit prewarming. A worker that has not prepared presentation pays the deferred import cost on its first presentation request (about 160 ms in this benchmark). Fully prepared history workers retain about the same heap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the four presentation imports into the existing prewarm request and remove eager foreground-lane startup loading. Let Gateway prewarming reach an already-started lightweight worker, using the existing per-database prewarm deduplication. Separate worker lanes, database admission, and read behavior remain intact. No configuration options are added.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: at least 20% less retained heap for a fresh foreground worker performing a lightweight read, with no 20% regression in total explicit-prewarm latency. Five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, built runtime, Node 26.13.0, one Blacksmith host with 4 CPUs and approximately 16 GiB RAM:

| Workload / metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Lightweight read: retained heap after GC | 29.95 MiB | 19.98 MiB |
| Lightweight read: evaluated modules | 1,253 | 410 |
| Lightweight read: spawn to reply, median / p95 | 272.25 / 308.73 ms | 174.16 / 213.22 ms |
| Explicit prewarm: spawn to reply, median / p95 | 293.98 / 311.94 ms | 272.53 / 308.01 ms |
| Explicit prewarm: retained heap after GC | 30.01 MiB | 29.97 MiB |
| Explicit prewarm: total allocations | 184.30 MiB | 192.07 MiB |

The import cost moves from startup into the first presentation request: measured request-only prewarm median 5.17 → 164.91 ms. The heap result is per-worker retained JavaScript heap, not a measurement of whole-Gateway RSS.

Reproduction: `scripts/perf/worker-spawn-measure.mjs --built --build-dir <candidate> --compare-build-dir <baseline> --worker session-transcript --prewarm-history --transcript-task <sqlite-target|prewarm> --samples 5`, run with Node 26.13.0 through `--import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`.

- Both runtime builds passed.
- Import-timing and existing-worker prewarm regressions fail on their original source and pass with the fix.
- Focused history integration, Gateway prewarm/startup, pool, and lane lifecycle suites passed.
- Targeted lint/format and `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- [Blacksmith validation run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43530360101); task-owned testbox stopped after proof.

Local ClawSweeper 0.3.3 completed a full committed-range review of `91046f7bbbb8..602c92076abe` with no priority filter and no code findings. It identified the deliberate first-presentation latency tradeoff and requested additional live Gateway evidence covering a second foreground worker. The maintainer accepted demand loading after the measured tradeoff was presented. The additional probe now passes through the built Gateway on Node 26.13.0: Control UI disabled and enabled, each with a lightweight `sessions.list` followed by two waves of eight concurrent `chat.history` requests. Both foreground workers served history in each case; all 32 responses succeeded with nonempty seeded messages, and cold/warm message digests matched. The probe used isolated synthetic state and exercised natural request-driven loading (no prewarm tasks were observed). These instrumented functional timings are not a before/after Gateway latency benchmark. The previously queued extra Testbox was stopped; this Gateway proof ran locally in the native PR checkout.


The final follow-up commits document mock isolation for the existing Gateway prewarm test and remove its obsolete baseline entry. The targeted mock-export ratchet passes; production code is unchanged from the reviewed and measured head.

One unrelated existing test (`session-message-events.test.ts`, same-clock avatar revisions) failed at `subscribeMessages` on both baseline and candidate. Its root cause remains outside this change; the focused worker/Gateway suites and real Gateway history proof pass.


### Inherited CI failure

[CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43534842832/job/132262012386) fails four native Talk cancellation variants: a new consultation after cancellation returns the fallback text instead of the expected completion. The worker/history tests in that shard pass. Reproduced all four identical expected/actual failures locally with both candidate and original worker/prewarm production source, using only main's test-fixture correction that asserts the terminal response rather than waiting forever for correct output. The unchanged original fixture times out on both versions. Temporary diagnostic changes were restored. An independent source review confirmed the inherited attribution; the voice defect remains outside this memory change. CI is retained as failed and landing uses the native inherited-failure exception, subject to remaining checks/security.

prs.title: feat: rank MCP tools in the usage-ranked tool index
prs.body:
Related: #197128 ## What Problem This Solves The usage-ranked tool index (#197128) ignores MCP tools, so the bounded MCP tool directory in the `tool_search` description drops descriptions and collapses servers to count lines without regard to the tools an agent actually uses. Large MCP inventories already hit this: Granola plus Linear (~100 tools) overflow the 4,096-byte budget and every description is dropped. ## User Impact With **Settings → Labs → Usage-ranked tool index** on, MCP tools (including MCP servers installed as plugins, such as Granola) learn from successful calls. Their most-used tools keep descriptions, and their names survive when a server would otherwise collapse to a count line, so the model can skip the `tool_search` round trip for them. With the lab off (the default), prompt bytes are unchanged. Renaming an MCP server produces new catalog IDs that start without history; old IDs expire with the existing 90-day retention. Codex-native surfaces stay excluded, and Claude CLI runs keep Claude's native `ToolSearch` (the recorder and ranking live only in the embedded runner). ## Why This Change Was Made #197128 skipped MCP on the premise that the MCP directory requires `tool_describe` anyway, so ranking saves nothing. A listed name still skips `tool_search`, exactly like the ranked deferred-schema directory. This change reuses the same storage, frozen per-series snapshot, newcomer reservation and refresh points: - **Recording:** successful MCP calls count under their exact catalog ID `mcp::`, for direct calls and nested calls through `dispatch_action` and Code Mode `MCP` namespaces. The existing exclusions apply (failed, cancelled, pending, client-delegated, incognito). Bindings stay exact: a bare name shared by an MCP and a native tool, or shadowed by a client tool, is not attributed. - **Ranking:** the MCP directory keeps its budget, sanitization, safe-name rule, per-server count lines, closing line, canonical order and exact IDs. When descriptions don't all fit, higher-scored tools keep theirs first; when names don't fit, higher-scored names survive and the rest of each server becomes `- server: N more tools, names omitted`. Unscored names still favor smaller servers, like the fixed steps. If even per-server counts don't fit, the existing fixed fallback runs unchanged. - **Frozen series:** the snapshot depends on the registered catalog, so the ranked directory is applied when tools are pinned for the series. When in-attempt compaction refreshes the snapshot, the session re-pins its tools before the next request, so the directory changes only at a series boundary. - **Import:** `openclaw tools usage import` now backfills MCP calls. Exact `mcp:` IDs resolve without a live MCP catalog; bare MCP names resolve from the `mcpServer` detail OpenClaw's MCP runtime records on results. Evidence that contradicts a native owner of the same name stays uncounted, as does a server whose safe name needed a collision suffix (accepted edge case, documented). - No schema change: rows reuse `agent_tool_usage` and its retention. ## Evidence - Flag-off byte identity: `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.test.ts` runs the real session-runtime preparation with an overflowing MCP catalog and learned MCP usage; with the lab off, the pinned `tool_search` description equals the unranked bytes and storage is never read. `tool-search-mcp-directory.test.ts` checks that no learned usage, or a directory that fits, returns the original tools array. - Ranking/overflow: description priority, name priority with per-server count lines and closing line, sanitization of a hostile ranked description, and the fixed fallback when count lines don't fit. - Recording: direct, `dispatch_action` and Code Mode MCP calls record `mcp:granola:…`; a failed MCP result does not; same-named native/MCP and client-shadowed names stay unbound. - Import: exact-ID and evidence-based backfill, and refusal for MCP evidence that contradicts a native owner (direct, nested, bare-name dispatch with nested or wrapper results). - Compaction re-pin: after a committed compaction refreshes the snapshot, the session refreshes its tools once and the re-pinned directory reflects the new ranking. - Data compatibility: no schema, migration or storage-shape change. Existing `agent_tool_usage` rows (`openclaw:*` IDs) are read, decayed and ranked by the unchanged reader; MCP rows are new IDs in the same table and retention. The unchanged storage suites (`src/config/sessions/tool-usage*.test.ts`, `session-actor-tool-usage.test.ts`, tool-usage prompt-state and spawn-boundary suites) pass on this head. prs.title: fix(openclaw-id): script widgets render blank for members who open a claw through OpenClaw ID
prs.body:
Related: OCF-531 (Linear). Requires openclaw/claw-loader#28 (merged and deployed to staging).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: script widgets, dashboard widgets and MCP App views render an empty frame ("server IP address could not be found") when a member opens the Control UI through OpenClaw ID remote access.

## User Impact

User impact: members who reach a claw through OpenClaw ID see script widgets, dashboard widgets and MCP App views, with the same isolation as on direct and cloud-ingress connections. Direct, cloud-ingress and unlinked connections don't change. HTML session-file previews that declare their own Content-Security-Policy and load relative resources (the only previews that fetch files from the Gateway sandbox listener) show the existing "does not support relative resources in Preview" notice for tunnel members and render without those resources, instead of a frame that cannot load. Previews without an authored policy keep their images, which the Control UI inlines.

## Why This Change Was Made

Script content loads in a frame on a separate sandbox origin. Tunnel connections fell back to `mcp.apps.sandboxOrigin` or the Gateway host plus the sandbox port, and neither is reachable from a claw origin. On OpenClaw ID tunnel connections with a linked claw, the Gateway now reports the claw-loader sibling origin `sbx--<h>.<domain>`, with `claw=<label>` and `cspv=1` in the URL, and includes its unchanged trusted shell HTML. The Control UI waits for that origin's bootstrap-ready message from the exact frame, sends the shell, and then continues the existing sandbox handshake. Same pattern as #198344, which reports the claw origin for copied links.

This contract assumes the UI and Gateway come from the same build, per `ui/AGENTS.md`; it is not designed for independently hosted older UIs.

## Evidence

- Gateway and protocol schema vitest: 166 passed. UI vitest: 188 passed. Golden host-mapping vectors: 5 passed, identical to claw-loader.
- `pnpm protocol:check` passed.
- Browser contract (`.artifacts/ocf-531/browser-contract.mts`, local) passed in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit against the Worker's real bootstrap response. bootstrap-ready, then proxy-ready, then the widget renders, and a forbidden fetch stays blocked after `document.write`.
- An independent review found no P0–P2 issues. It confirmed the shells this branch generates are byte-identical to the Worker's pinned fixtures, all 22 CSP outcomes match, and the tunnel gating leaves direct and cloud-ingress output unchanged.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane passes except the dead-export scan, which reports `QA_UX_STREAM_END_MARKER`, `adoptTelegramDmTopicMessage`, `TELEGRAM_DM_TOPIC_ADOPT_WINDOW_SEC`, `TELEPORT_PT` and `RELEASE_VALIDATION_WAIVERS`. Those fail identically on `origin/main` fa155ff6f53e, and this PR doesn't touch them.
- Authored-CSP preview fallback (`ad679abcc910`): new `sessions-file-preview.test.ts` covers tunnel members getting `unsupported` with no grant created, and direct connections keeping the grant. The six related Gateway test files pass, and an independent Astra review found no P0–P2 issues.
- **Live staging proof** (claw-loader#28 is merged and deployed): the branch's Gateway `resolveSandboxView` output, loaded in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. The parent page is served as a claw origin; the widget frame goes to the **live** `sbx--` staging Worker (200, `frame-ancestors` limited to that claw). bootstrap-ready, then proxy-ready; the scripted widget renders, and a fetch to a non-allowed origin stays blocked. A synthetic claw host and tailnet name are used to keep private identifiers out.
- **Inherited CI failures (landed through the pre-existing-failure route, run 43526462356 attempt 2):** `checks-ui (2/3)` and `(3/3)` fail in `chat-responsive`, `chat-pane-session-controls`, `hosted-environment`, `draft-submission-title`, `model-control-view` and `chat-pane-unmaterialized-settings`, identically to main's scheduled run 43527024791 at the same base. `chat-audio-preview` ("plays unflagged incoming audio inline at 390 px") failed once on playback timing in an unchanged file and passed 3/3 locally on this head. The macOS Periphery check flags `OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccountError`, added to main by #197630; this PR touches no Swift. An earlier attempt's setup failures were a Launchpad 503 and passed on rerun.
- Not tested: a full Control UI session through a real tunnel to a Gateway running this branch. That happens on the first fsn1 update after merge.

prs.title: fix: recover Gateways in delegated service cgroups
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained controller adoption refusing a serving Gateway that uses the shipped `DelegateSubgroup=gateway` unit configuration. This blocked the native schema-crossing recovery added in #198501.

## User Impact

Operators can adopt the reviewed complete controller closure and recover the already-serving candidate without restarting it on successful forward acceptance. The adoption request and command sequence stay the same; stage the new four-file closure and bind its new descriptors. No SQLite schema, configuration, or deployment change is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process owner now accepts exactly the system unit root or its `/gateway` leaf and preserves the observed path in its witness. Other leaves, nested sandboxes, and other units remain refused. Profiling uses the same main-process rule; the privileged systemd condition separately permits only the root or `/.control`.

Stopped custody accepts the exact runtime-owned delegation boundary while preserving root-owned ancestors and protected population evidence. It consumes the kernel's recursive population bit instead of rejecting empty delegated child directories. Cutover, operator restart, and handoff were audited: they have no separate process-cgroup equality policy.

## Evidence

246 distinct Linux controller tests passed with zero skips: recovery/cutover 14, adoption/retained-runtime/operator and handoff/stopped recovery 226, profiling 6. The delegated fixture completes adoption → canonical recovery → journal retirement with no restart and unchanged archived held bytes/mtime. The delegated adoption, delegated stopped-recovery, and three profiling/condition regressions fail on exact base `e6c7c5e0da4b2407e2d991a00c5d38b599e05050` at their cgroup guards.

The expanded suite exposed two inherited fixture regressions from #193647 (`3efe1deca653`): raw library calls omitted required FD9 custody, and stopped-current setup recreated an existing lock. Both reproduce on the exact base. This PR repairs the shared test runner and forwarding wrapper, and deletes duplicate lock creation; all affected suites now pass.

`pnpm check:changed`, syntax and diff checks passed on the final source. Independent Codex autoreview at P0–P2: the production/test diff through `455e983d312e` and the subsequent fixture-only delta through `20ea92b6ec5c` are both scoped-clean with zero findings. The Linux final capsule matches the final committed controller directory byte-for-byte.

Native I/O is synthetic in these fixtures; this is not a real-systemd or live Gateway deployment rehearsal. Production was not accessed. Linux test cost: repaired sibling group 545.63s wall; this exercises the real multi-phase controller and its subprocesses. No product-performance claim is made. Production LOC +12, tests/support +137, docs +16; growth covers role-specific membership and delegated ownership checks while redundant stopped-subtree scanning is removed.

prs.title: improve(ui): restore composer superellipse corners and tighten its controls
prs.body:
Related: #193621 ## What Problem This Solves The chat composer was the only Control UI surface left on plain circular corners, so its 25px radius read as a pill. Its action row mixed icon stroke weights and uneven gaps. On New Session at phone and narrow widths, the composer rested about 40px taller than its content and the model chevron sat far from the model name. ## User Impact User impact: the composer draws the same superellipse corner as the rest of the app again, its controls read as one evenly weighted row, and New Session's narrow composer rests one line tall with the chevron beside the model name. Safari and other WebKit browsers keep today's circular corners. WebKit 27.3 beta was reported to stop painting a superellipse composer in narrow layouts (#193621), and that fallback now applies only to WebKit instead of to every browser. It covers WebKit at every width because the reported threshold is unknown, and it relies on a WebKit-only CSS probe (`-webkit-nbsp-mode`). Remove it once WebKit paints the shape. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Corners:** the composer's shape token defaults to `superellipse(1.5)` again, with a WebKit-only `@supports` block that keeps `round`. Theme overrides still win. - **Action row:** line icons share one 1.5px rendered stroke (they ranged from 1px to 1.67px). The plus, microphone and send paint a 30px tier and the permission, model and effort chips paint 28px, so the actions stay the taller bookends when a chip is hovered. The send disc and the plus sit 8px from the side and the bottom. Gaps between neighboring controls are 21.5px to 22.75px (they ranged from 17.75px to 25px). The context ring and model mark use even boxes so they center on whole pixels. Hit targets stay 32px and the touch layout keeps its own geometry. - **New Session, narrow:** the writing area no longer carries a taller floor than the shared composer, so it rests at the 92px surface minimum (it was 132px at 390 × 844) and still grows with the draft. The model picker keeps the track between the fixed controls, and the chip inside it hugs its label and chevron. ## Evidence Real Control UI with a mocked Gateway and synthetic content, Chromium. The phone captures use an emulated touch viewport. **Chat composer, 1280px, dark** Before (main `e6c7c5e0da4b`) After **New Session, 390 × 844 touch, dark** Before After **New Session, 580px window with a draft, light** Before After - `ui/src/styles/corner-shape.browser.test.ts`: the composer and its notices are back in the superellipse contract, and a new case satisfies the WebKit probe in Chromium to prove those selectors stay circular there while other surfaces keep the superellipse. 5 cases pass in about 0.5s of test time locally (10.6s shard wall time alongside two other files); CI seconds are not available yet. - Passing composer consumers: `chat-rhythm-alignment`, `chat-composer-mobile`, `chat-composer-overflow` and `composer-editor` browser tests; `new-session-page.model-catalog` "keeps mobile model loading steady" at 320, 400 and 560px (zero layout shift with the hugging chip); `composer-control-ink`, `new-session-page.responsive-welcome` and `new-session-page.keyboard` E2E. - Stylelint and the format check pass on the changed files. - Playwright WebKit 27.2 computes the circular corner with this change and paints New Session at 390px. WebKit 27.3 beta itself was not tested. - Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode) on `origin/main` `e6c7c5e0da4b` → `2d40828a52ab`, priorities P0 to P2: scoped-clean, no findings. The reviewer had no rendered layouts.
Failures that also occur on the base, and coverage gaps These fail locally with the same assertions and values on `e6c7c5e0da4b` without this change: - `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`: "keeps the composer bottom controls, attachment, and primary action aligned at 568x320", "keeps short-landscape composer adjunct rows scroll-reachable", "keeps short-landscape slash menu visible inside the bounded composer". - `chat-composer-picker-layout.e2e.test.ts`: "keeps model and effort targets separate when Files narrows the composer" in Chromium and WebKit. - `new-session-page.model-catalog.e2e.test.ts`: "keeps picker geometry stable while shortcut visibility follows focus". Not covered: Safari 27.3 beta and physical touch devices. The maintainer verification below additionally covers the Fast-mode bolt.
Requested and directed by Vyctor Brzezowski (@vyctorbrzezowski). ### Maintainer browser verification On `822199a42585ac6047bc9eb5f1277a801e29f02b`, eight source-UI scenarios passed in installed Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and Playwright WebKit 27.2: chat at 1280px/390px, and New Session at 390px dark/580px light. The Gateway data was synthetic; no microphone, provider credentials, or inference were used. - The actual `CSS.supports('-webkit-nbsp-mode', 'space')` result was false in Chromium and true in WebKit. No CSS probe was replaced. Chromium computed `superellipse(1.5)`; WebKit retained the `round` token, serialized as `superellipse(1)`, for the composer and its visible notice. - Inputs remained visible and editable. New Session rested at 92px instead of the baseline's 131.95px, and grew to 296px/266px with long drafts at 390px/580px. Send/Start targets remained reachable. - The fixture retained Fast mode in chat at both widths; the bolt is visible in the Chromium capture below. - One ResizeObserver notification was recorded during the WebKit 390px chat scenario, with the same single notification on the baseline. It was not a sustained loop in the observed run, and no painting or interaction failure occurred. - Safari/WebKit 27.3 beta and physical touch devices were not tested. | Installed WebKit 27.2 · 390px · notice and composer visible | Chromium · 1280px · Fast mode retained | | --- | --- | | ![WebKit keeps circular corners and a visible composer and notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/533d75ff-d913-4b89-ae83-ac6577499fd3) | ![Chromium composer with the Fast-mode bolt visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10e1357c-7d38-4334-a82a-441e6cb71cc3) | ### Maintainer correction: narrow composer hit areas Published in the corrected head 5fed90721d28fb6392a59627ecc7e6d57b9c2edb; an independent P0–P3 review of this CSS correction found no actionable issues. The original candidate let the new microphone paint rule override the existing narrow-layout target size. With Files open at 1100 × 729, the microphone overlapped the effort button by 7 × 36px; hit testing sent clicks in that part of the effort button to the microphone. The correction keeps the existing narrow target size and removes the desktop-only context offset in the narrow container. The microphone still paints on the 30px tier; model and effort retain their separate 44px targets. The approved wide layout and the control gaps are unchanged. - On the corrected source, Chromium and WebKit both opened Model and Effort with actual clicks and closed them with Escape. The visible microphone passed click actionability without starting audio capture. - Geometry, labels and context alignment passed at all seven widths from the existing regression scenario in both engines. - Desktop and phone smoke checks retained the same composer heights, corner shapes and Fast mode as the original candidate. - The full existing picker scenario proceeds past the repaired geometry assertions, then reaches the separately reproduced baseline overlay-dismissal failure. That entire scenario is not reported as passing. | Before correction: effort and microphone targets overlap | After correction: separate targets | | --- | --- | | ![Narrow composer before correcting the hit areas](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db50b544-4258-4c62-9305-1b82ae78ffef) | ![Narrow composer after correcting the hit areas](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d2790f5-f06a-4f0a-9225-5083d809586b) | ### CI findings and budget decision The pre-correction [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43532756854) had 27 failed UI/E2E cases. Two exposed the overlap repaired above. The remaining 25 reproduce on the PR baseline, including model/account selectors, short-landscape layout, model-catalog state and native-runtime recovery assertions. The 25 relevant test/owner blobs were also compared with the CI main parent and were unchanged. Local attribution used macOS arm64; CI used Linux x64. The same run measured CSS growth of 2,029 bytes raw and 331 bytes gzip on a baseline already over its cap. The maintainer's standing CSS-budget exception applies; no limit or baseline is changed by this PR. Neither the budget exception nor the inherited-failure attribution is described as green CI. ## Work sessions Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public. - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3a3ae829-e164-417f-a7ce-da0d64c72b63) ## Worked on by - @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(ci): split oversized hosted main test groups
prs.body:
Related: #157302

## What Problem This Solves

Hourly main CI bypasses its existing test-file limits because main validation now requests the complete inventory through PR-mode planning. In [scheduled run 43519241305](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43519241305/job/132209693482), one Gateway group ran 293 files and took 40 minutes before its remaining groups.

## User Impact

Hosted main validation splits Gateway groups into at most 96 files and chat groups into at most 30, retaining every selected test and the existing 77-row non-build budget. This is an internal CI change. The current inventory uses all 77 non-build rows; further growth must still pass the existing cap. Actual completion-time and billing improvements remain unmeasured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing main-specific file envelopes when `mainValidation` is true, while retaining ordinary row packing. The existing storage limit, worker counts, runner routing, ordinary PR plans and full-release plans remain unchanged. Main validation cannot also adopt legacy dedicated-row isolation: that broader candidate exceeded the row cap and was excluded.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: retain the exact selected inventory, configs and worker limits; enforce the 30/96/64-file family bounds; keep the complete main plan within 77 non-build rows.

- Native dependency-free planner proof at `4729152d6fa28d3c38ce6fc117bd829f5bca80ce`: chat 116 files in 4 groups (maximum 30), Gateway 587 in 9 (maximum 96), storage 1,676 in 30 (maximum 64). All three inventories are complete and unique. There are 75 compact non-build rows plus 2 existing worker-proof rows.
- Full main-plan before/after replay retains all 14,532 file/config/prerequisite/environment entries exactly; effective per-file worker limits and plan concurrency are also identical. Total compact rows change from 76 to 77, and complete non-build rows from 76 to 77 after adding the unchanged worker-proof rows.
- Regression proof: the main-validation case fails on the original planner with `expected 116 to be less than or equal to 30`, then both legacy-push and main-validation cases pass with the fix (2/2; 9.43 seconds measured wall time). The production planner test checks exact inventories, configs, prerequisites, worker limits and the row reservation.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper completed a full committed-range review of `e6c7c5e0da4b2407e2d991a00c5d38b599e05050..4729152d6fa28d3c38ce6fc117bd829f5bca80ce` at high reasoning priority with no findings. The execution gaps it identified are now covered by the checks below.
- Native PR-workspace focused regression, tooling-test typecheck, targeted script/test lint, three-file formatting, one-file docs MDX validation, and `git diff --check` all pass.
- Broad PR CI remains the final gate. Actual post-change main timing and billing effects are unmeasured; the next natural hourly run owns that observation.

prs.title: improve(ui): invite questions and tasks in the new-session prompt
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The new-session prompt asks "What should this session work on?", which is framed around OpenClaw's internal concepts and leaves new adopters asking what a session (or a task) is before they have typed anything.

## User Impact

User impact: the new-session prompt now reads "Ask me anything, or hand me something to do", in the selected agent's voice, and the header hint is shortened to "Pick where this session works." English only; other locales update through the normal translation refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw is a personal agent, so the prompt should sound like the agent offering help rather than the product describing its own concepts. The new line covers both halves of how people use it, questions and handed-off work, which matches the range on openclaw.ai/showcase: coding handoffs, daily chores, one-off questions, small builds and errands. Because the prompt now asks for the work, the header hint no longer repeats "then say what to do".

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: fix(ui): match chat context entry search across NFC and NFD name forms
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat context panel filters long context lists (skills, files, tools, deferred entries) by the typed search query, comparing lowercased entry names with the lowercased query without Unicode normalization. A name stored in one form (for example decomposed `Jose` + U+0301) does not match the same name typed in the other form (precomposed `José`), so the context search silently shows no matches.

## User Impact

Users searching the context breakdown for accented or composed names (café, résumé, José, etc.) get no matches when the stored name and the typed query use different Unicode normalization forms, forcing them to guess the exact form of the text they are looking for.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ContextList` filters each entry with `.toLocaleLowerCase().includes(needle)` where the needle is also only lowercased. Canonicalizing both the query and the candidate `name + path` with `.normalize("NFC")` makes NFC and NFD spellings equivalent, matching the shared Unicode-matching convention already applied across the UI (model picker, sharing, activity, dashboards, session owner search, sidebar file search, plugin settings, etc.).

## Evidence

### Unit proof (`chat-context-breakdown.test.tsx`)

The new `it.each` covers both directions through the real search input in a long (>20 entries) context list: NFC stored + NFD typed, and NFD stored + NFC typed.

**Green with the fix:**

```text
✓ |unit| chat-context-breakdown.test.tsx > filters context entries typed in another Unicode form (José vs José) 39ms
✓ |unit| chat-context-breakdown.test.tsx > filters context entries typed in another Unicode form (José vs José) 29ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  15 passed (15)
```

**Red on the unpatched code** (normalize removed):

```text
× |unit| chat-context-breakdown.test.tsx > filters context entries typed in another Unicode form (José vs José)
  → expected [] to include 'José'
× |unit| chat-context-breakdown.test.tsx > filters context entries typed in another Unicode form (José vs José)
  → expected [] to include 'José'
Tests  2 failed | 13 passed (15)
```

- `git merge openclaw/main` into the branch resolves without conflicts; the two touched files differ from main only by this fix (the panel has no prior normalization, and the test file is unchanged on main).

## Merge Danger

Low. Two-line production change confined to the `ContextList` search filter in `chat-context-panel.tsx`; existing behavior for already-canonical (ASCII) names is unchanged. No config, schema, or state impact. The search box only appears for lists longer than 20 entries after "Show all".

Completed chat replies still show a separate output-token count beneath the answer, repeating technical usage information in the main conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Token usage is useful power-user detail, not something a personal agent needs to emphasize after every turn. The existing on-demand surfaces already provide that information.
