prs.title: fix(exec): preserve explicit environment in full access
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: full-access host commands reject explicitly requested environment settings, including `SUDO_ASKPASS`, Git helpers, interpreter options, proxies, and custom `PATH` values.

## User Impact

User impact: effective `security=full` / `ask=off` execution can use the command environment the caller requested, including helper-based authentication and an explicitly empty PATH. Constrained execution, inherited-environment filtering, and owner-scoped credential/routing protections remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply environment restrictions according to effective execution authority rather than adding a special exception for one variable. Resolve plugin and shared-store overrides under the same policy, enforce the execution host's policy on Node and macOS, and keep forwarded approval/fallback paths constrained. Restore explicit Node PATH values after the generated login-shell startup without interpreting them as shell code.

No new configuration or wire-protocol authority flag is introduced.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the broader environment rejection before the fix, then verified real full/elevated-full subprocesses receive the requested values.
- Reproduced three PATH failures before the follow-up fix: empty Gateway PATH and empty/nonempty Node PATH. All pass after the fix, including a real executable in a path containing shell metacharacters.
- Targeted coverage: **196 passed, 2 Windows-only cases skipped** across the host sanitizer, Gateway policy-floor/plugin/store, Node policy/prepare/run, and process-runner suites.
- Core TypeScript checking, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, the repository line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. The existing policy resolver and environment regression group were moved to coherent sibling modules to avoid growing oversized files; affected tests passed again after that move.
- Bounded mutation testing exposed a missing direct full-access shell-wrapper assertion; the regression matrix now covers it. Automatic mutation analysis did not finish, and existing high-complexity sanitizer metrics remain findings rather than a passing quality score.
- Independent policy review completed; its two PATH findings were reproduced and fixed. Final Codex autoreview of the local changes over `d08fbbc5405` (P0–P3) was unavailable because CLI authentication failed; no clean final review report is claimed.
- [CI attached to the published head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43532318712), but GitHub reports `action_required` and no jobs have started; repository approval is still needed. No hosted CI pass is claimed.

prs.title: feat(i18n): prepare pinned external Control UI memory
prs.body:
Related: #165234

## What Problem This Solves

Prepares the Control UI locale refresh to retain canonical translation memory outside main while keeping source checkouts and public-session builds reproducible offline.

## User Impact

After an explicit bootstrap, UI and public-session builds use checked-in digest-pinned catalogs without fetching translation storage. Raw memory is restored only for generation and published to a separately configured, append-only canonical Git repository before the corresponding main pin.

**This PR does not activate or provision production storage.** Until an administrator configures the approved destination/App and lands the generated bootstrap change, the existing tracked-memory workflow remains active. No real destination or credentials are supplied here; no remote migration was performed. Existing reachable Git history is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepared path retains one lossless canonical snapshot, exact revision and SHA-256 pins, and a smaller derived build representation. The same reader serves Vite and public-session runtime/worker builds. Bootstrap validates all raw bytes before local removal; restore validates the complete snapshot before writes; failed canonical publication cannot advance the main revision pin.

This is the smallest coherent preparation stage spanning both build consumers, the existing same-run artifact flow, and the terminal generated-PR publisher. It uses existing Git/GitHub infrastructure with no new runtime dependency. Production ownership/access and the explicit bootstrap remain operator actions documented in `docs/ci/control-ui-memory.md`. No history rewrite, shared repack, translation rewrite or provider call was performed.

## Evidence

- Native local Git fixtures cover bootstrap, byte-exact restore from old/new pins, rejected-push ordering, projection corruption, no new raw-memory objects in future source commits, and unchanged catalog object IDs for metadata-only refreshes.
- Full-roster local cutover: 22 locales, 270,050 translated key/value entries; current-English materialization and public-reader dictionaries are byte-identical. Raw inputs total 114,078,356 bytes; build projections total 46,251,834 bytes. These are logical file sizes, not a clone-pack forecast.
- Both UI builds pass: 4,940 output files byte-identical; only `.build-inputs.json` changes to record the new inputs. Public-reader tsdown module bytes are identical. All original raw files were restored after the local experiment.
- The old public-reader consumer fails the activated-input regression with missing French translations; the reviewed consumer passes. 59 focused locale/tooling tests, 50 Vite build-owner tests, and 225 CI workflow guards pass. Targeted tooling/UI types, typed lint, formatting, workflow validation, docs links and production/full-tree unused-file scans pass.
- Independent Codex autoreview of published head `86733d21e2becf0eb8e27f7ff4e3d581977c3959` against `cd61ce32dd28e92003b213f8d2014608504515fb`: complete P0–P2 branch scope, no actionable findings. It inspected the frozen code/evidence, not live Actions. The native publisher appended a provenance-only commit after reviewed implementation `239a76570fb4972d3f329fe5c4fc18311ad029b4`; local Git verifies both trees are `f644ec19706b60424a32e54bd5d2ce5d9dafcb8c`, so the unchanged implementation proof remains applicable.

Limits: no production repository, GitHub App permissions or authenticated hosted refresh has been exercised. Local fixtures use synthetic destination identities and no network. No visual behavior change is intended; this does not claim to fix GitHub’s existing pack representation or remove historical objects. The draft requires maintainer review of canonical-store ownership, retention and activation.

Prepared at the request of @hannesrudolph. Related issue reported by @NovaUnboundAi.

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

Tested on `upstream/main` `20237d956bb` (2026-11-12) before, and `c50d8b26e1e` (this PR head, rebased onto it) after. Real built CLI, local fake MCP servers on loopback, isolated temp HOME and state dir. Ubuntu 26.04, Node 26.10.0.

`node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning|error`. Exit codes: warning threshold / error threshold.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Healthy server (remote or stdio) | no finding; exit 0 / 0 | no finding; exit 0 / 0 |
| Remote outage: connection refused, HTTP 503, HTTP 401, hang past the 10 s deadline | error; exit 1 / 1 | warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 0 |
| Remote invalid catalog (bad tool entry, repeated cursor) | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Stdio failure: crash at start, missing executable, invalid catalog | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Remote 503 and stdio crash in one config | error + error; exit 1 / 1 | error + warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 1 |

Upgrade check (published `openclaw@2026.10.8`, then this build, same temp state dir, remote HTTP 503): at the error threshold 2026.10.8 gave error, exit 1; this build gave no finding, exit 0. State files stayed byte-identical. Not the `openclaw update` command.
Unit tests (4 files, `--maxWorkers=1`): 55 of 55 pass, including the stdio Doctor tests.
Not tested: real `openclaw update`, a running Gateway, real third-party servers, OAuth, legacy SSE, TLS, human-readable Doctor output, Windows, macOS.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. Current-head PR CI remains separate from these local checks.
- Simplification: failure/retirement projection uses the existing catalog owner; the old duplicate retired-catalog literal is removed. Necessary growth is typed failure provenance and strongest-severity aggregation, plus distinct real transport/ordering regressions; no new manager, database schema or runtime policy option.

prs.title: fix(ui): add document MIME mappings (xlsx/docx/pptx/etc) for chat attachments — Bug #9
prs.body:
## Summary

Downstream bug 9 — a production instance produced an Excel pricing analysis with its AI assistant, but the browser only offered "Webpage Complete" as the Save As format for the `.xlsx`. The file was served with the wrong `Content-Type`, so the browser treated the response as an HTML page.

## Root cause

`ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.ts` infers an attachment's MIME type from a hand-maintained `MIME_BY_EXT` table when MEDIA references come back as plain URLs/paths. That table covered images, audio, video, `pdf`, `txt`, `md`, `csv`, `json`, and `zip` — but **none** of the common Office, OpenDocument, or source-code extensions. For an `.xlsx` upload the lookup returned `undefined`, `mediaKindFromMime(undefined)` returned `undefined` → fell through to `"document"` with no `mimeType`, and the downstream chat serving path emitted the file with a generic/HTML Content-Type. Hence the reported "Webpage Complete" symptom.

## Fix

Extend `MIME_BY_EXT` to cover the full document set called out in the bug:

| Extension | MIME |
|---|---|
| `xlsx` | `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet` |
| `xls` | `application/vnd.ms-excel` |
| `docx` | `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document` |
| `doc` | `application/msword` |
| `pptx` | `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation` |
| `ppt` | `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint` |
| `odt` / `ods` / `odp` | OpenDocument text/spreadsheet/presentation |
| `rtf` | `application/rtf` |
| `html` / `htm` | `text/html` |
| `xml` | `application/xml` |
| `yaml` / `yml` | `application/yaml` |
| `ts` / `js` / `py` / `sh` / `sql` | source-code text MIMEs |

`mediaKindFromMime` (in `src/media/constants.ts`) already classifies anything starting with `application/` or `text/` as `"document"`, so every new entry flows through without further changes — verified by reading the file before editing.

## Tests

Parameterized coverage added to `ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts`:

- Each new Office Open XML, legacy Office, OpenDocument, PDF, and RTF extension produces an attachment with `kind: "document"` and the canonical MIME.
- `xlsx`, `docx`, `pptx`, and `pdf` (the cases called out in Bug #9) are explicitly asserted.
- `html` and `ts` cover the `text/*` and source-code paths.

```
✓ unit-ui ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts (39 tests) 10ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  39 passed (39)
```

`pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` are clean on the touched files.

## What this does NOT fix yet

Even with the correct MIME inferred, the gateway's outgoing-attachment pipeline is image-only (`src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.ts`). Documents still need a managed `/api/chat/media/outgoing/...` URL with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<original>"` to make Save As behave fully. That is **PR B** — `feat/managed-document-attachments-bug-9` — which I'm opening next.

This PR is the small, safe slice that immediately stops Office documents from being misclassified at the chat layer; it should ship soon for the affected user.

## Bug

Downstream bug 9 — production instance, file delivery for non-image documents.

## Review

🚫 Do not merge yet. Tagging Ada/Brian for Codex review per Brian's protocol.



## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: before this PR, `MIME_BY_EXT` in
`ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.ts` had no entry for `.xlsx`,
`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xls`, `.doc`, `.ppt`, `.odt`/`.ods`/`.odp`, `.rtf`,
`.html`/`.htm`, `.xml`, `.yaml`/`.yml`, or common source-code
extensions. Office documents fell through with `mimeType` undefined,
which let the chat surface emit them with a generic/HTML
`Content-Type` and produced the reported "Webpage Complete" symptom.
This PR adds the full document set to `MIME_BY_EXT`.

**Real environment tested**: macOS 25.3.0 (arm64), Node v22.22.0, branch
`fix/document-mime-mappings-bug-9` at commit `119b702b4e`. This PR
touches a UI/TypeScript file; the real-runtime proof is to drive the
actual production build pipeline (Vite production build with
minification + tree-shaking) and inspect the artifact end users'
browsers will load. No mocks, no vitest; the bytes below are the
deployed bundle.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```sh
$ cd ui
$ pnpm build
> openclaw-ui@0.0.0 build /Users/ada/work/openclaw/ui
> vite build
...
../dist/control-ui/assets/index-Cg_uNzWL.js                  1,117.05 kB │ gzip: 323.20 kB
✓ built in 1.75s

$ for ext in xlsx docx pptx; do
    grep -oE "${ext}:\"[^\"]*\"" dist/control-ui/assets/index-*.js
  done

$ for mime in \
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet" \
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document" \
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation" \
    "application/vnd.ms-excel" "application/vnd.ms-powerpoint" "application/msword" \
    "application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet" \
    "application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text" \
    "application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation" \
    "application/rtf" "application/yaml" "application/xml"; do
    printf "%-90s %s\n" "$mime" "$(grep -c "$mime" dist/control-ui/assets/index-*.js)"
  done
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```
$ grep -oE 'xlsx:"[^"]*"' dist/control-ui/assets/index-*.js
xlsx:"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"

$ grep -oE 'docx:"[^"]*"' dist/control-ui/assets/index-*.js
docx:"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document"

$ grep -oE 'pptx:"[^"]*"' dist/control-ui/assets/index-*.js
pptx:"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation"
```

A 1KB window of the minified `dist/control-ui/assets/index-Cg_uNzWL.js`
showing the full MIME table inside the production bundle — every entry
introduced by this PR is present in the same object literal:

```
...mage/heic",heif:"image/heif",ogg:"audio/ogg",oga:"audio/ogg",
mp3:"audio/mpeg",wav:"audio/wav",flac:"audio/flac",aac:"audio/aac",
opus:"audio/opus",m4a:"audio/mp4",mp4:"video/mp4",mov:"video/quicktime",
xlsx:"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet",
xls:"application/vnd.ms-excel",
docx:"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document",
doc:"application/msword",
pptx:"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation",
ppt:"application/vnd.ms-powerpoint",
odt:"application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text",
ods:"application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet",
odp:"application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation",
pdf:"application/pdf",rtf:"application/rtf",txt:"text/plain",
md:"text/markdown",csv:"text/csv",html:"text/html",htm:"text/html",
xml:"application/xml",yaml:"application/yaml",yml:"application/yaml",
json:"application/json",ts:"text/x-typescript",js:"text/javascript",
py:"text/x-python",sh:"application/x-sh",sql:"application/sql",
zip:"application/zip"};function UR(e){const t=e.trim();if(!t)retur...
```

Audit table — every PR-introduced MIME hits the deployed bundle:

| MIME                                                                        | in bundle |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`         | ✓ present |
| `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`   | ✓ present |
| `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation` | ✓ present |
| `application/vnd.ms-excel`                                                  | ✓ present |
| `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint`                                             | ✓ present |
| `application/msword`                                                        | ✓ present |
| `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet`                            | ✓ present |
| `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text`                                   | ✓ present |
| `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation`                           | ✓ present |
| `application/rtf`                                                           | ✓ present |
| `application/yaml`                                                          | ✓ present |
| `application/xml`                                                           | ✓ present |

**Observed result after fix**: the new MIME mappings introduced in
`ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.ts` survive Vite's production
minification + tree-shaking and ship to end users in the actual
`dist/control-ui/assets/index-*.js` bundle the browser loads. When a
chat surface receives an `.xlsx` MEDIA reference, the normalizer now
returns `mimeType: application/vnd.openxmlformats-...spreadsheetml.sheet`
and `kind: "document"`, which is what downstream code requires to render
it as a document attachment instead of falling through to a generic
HTML/octet-stream response.

**What was not tested**: I did not boot the actual control-ui in a
browser tab and click a `MEDIA:` link end-to-end — that requires the
gateway-side fix in #77877 to also be present. This PR is the small,
safe slice that stops Office documents from being misclassified at the
chat layer; the full user-visible Save As behaviour requires #77877 +
#77912 alongside this change.

prs.title: feat(gateway): managed outgoing attachments for documents (xlsx/pdf/docx) — Bug #9
prs.body:
## Summary

Downstream bug 9 — gateway-side fix. PR A ([#77875](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77875)) made the UI infer the right MIME for `.xlsx` / `.docx` / `.pptx` / `.pdf` etc. This PR ensures the gateway actually **serves** those documents with the right `Content-Type` and `Content-Disposition: attachment` so the browser stops offering "Webpage Complete" as the only Save As format.

## Why a sibling module instead of generalizing `managed-image-attachments.ts`

I read all ~1000 lines of `managed-image-attachments.ts`. It is dense with **image-specific** transforms — resize, alpha-channel detection, JPEG/PNG conversion, pixel/dimension limits, inline `Content-Disposition`. Documents must skip every one of those. Threading a `kind` discriminator through that flow would risk subtle regressions to the image happy-path.

Instead, this PR adds **`src/gateway/managed-document-attachments.ts`** as a sibling module that mirrors the public surface but skips every image-specific step:

| Concern | Image module | Document module |
|---|---|---|
| Resize / alpha / jpeg | yes | **no** |
| Pixel / dimension limits | yes | **no** |
| Per-attachment byte limit | 12 MiB | 25 MiB |
| MIME filter | `image/*` | `mediaKindFromMime === "document"` |
| Content-Disposition | `inline` | **`attachment; filename="…"`** |
| Route | `/api/chat/media/outgoing/...` | `/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/...` |
| On-disk dir | `media/outgoing/...` | `media/outgoing-docs/...` |

Auth, scope, transcript-ownership, TTL, and 404/405 logic mirror the image module so behavior is auditable side-by-side.

## What lands

- **`src/gateway/managed-document-attachments.ts`** (new):
  - `createManagedOutgoingDocumentBlocks({sessionKey, mediaUrls, ...})` — saves the document, writes a per-attachment record, returns `attachment`-kind blocks with `kind: "document"` and a stable URL `/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/{sessionKey}/{attachmentId}/full`.
  - `attachManagedOutgoingDocumentsToMessage(...)` — promotes `transient` → `history` retention once the transcript is appended.
  - `cleanupManagedOutgoingDocumentRecords(...)` — sweeps stale records and orphan files using the same TTL + transcript-membership rules.
  - `handleManagedOutgoingDocumentHttpRequest(...)` — serves bytes with the saved `Content-Type` and `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<original>"`.
  - Filters by `mediaKindFromMime === "document"` so it silently drops images / audio / video / unclassifiable content; the image and audio paths continue to own those.

- **`src/gateway/managed-document-attachments.test.ts`** (new, 17 tests):
  - `.xlsx` returns `application/vnd.openxmlformats-...spreadsheetml.sheet` with `attachment; filename="pricing.xlsx"`
  - `.pdf` returns `application/pdf` with attachment disposition
  - filename sanitization strips CR/LF/quote/backslash/slash
  - rejects unauth, cross-session, non-GET, malformed UUIDs
  - device-token bypass still requires transcript membership
  - `attachManagedOutgoingDocumentsToMessage` promotes transient → history
  - `cleanupManagedOutgoingDocumentRecords` honours TTL and transcript references

- **`src/gateway/server-http.ts`**: register the new HTTP stage `chat-managed-document-media` alongside the existing `chat-managed-image-media`.

- **`src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`**: in the assistant reply pipeline, call `createManagedOutgoingDocumentBlocks()` in parallel with the existing `createManagedOutgoingImageBlocks()` so document `MEDIA:` refs get a managed URL. Pair the cleanup and the "attach to transcript message" calls with the document analogs so retention stays consistent.

## Test results

```
✓ gateway src/gateway/managed-document-attachments.test.ts (17 tests) 38ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  17 passed (17)
```

`pnpm tsgo:core` is clean. `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` is clean on the touched files.

The `managed-image-attachments.test.ts` failures in this worktree are pre-existing (`sharp` not installed locally) — verified by stashing the diff and re-running.

## Compatibility

- New endpoint, new on-disk dir — no behavior change for existing image flows.
- Document MIMEs that fall outside `mediaKindFromMime === "document"` (i.e. `application/*` and `text/*`) are silently dropped, matching the image module's symmetric drop of non-images.
- Transcript-membership gating uses the same primitives as the image module (`loadSessionEntry` + `readSessionMessagesAsync`); cache is per-module so the two index caches don't collide.

## Bug

Downstream bug 9 — production instance file delivery for non-image documents.

## Review

🚫 Do not merge yet. Tagging Ada/Brian for Codex review per Brian's protocol. Pairs with [PR A #77875](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77875) — A should land first; B is independent (different files) but the user-visible fix only completes when both land.



## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: before this PR, the gateway had no
managed outgoing-document pipeline — `MEDIA:` references for `.xlsx`/
`.pdf`/`.docx` flowed through the assistant-media path with no
`Content-Disposition: attachment` header and no per-attachment ownership
record. This PR adds `src/gateway/managed-document-attachments.ts` which
saves documents under `media/outgoing-docs/`, returns chat blocks
pointing to `/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/...`, and serves them with
`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="..."`.

**Real environment tested**: macOS 25.3.0 (arm64), Node v22.22.0, branch
`feat/managed-document-attachments-bug-9` at commit `aafec535cb`. Real
`~/.openclaw` state dir; the new module is loaded directly from
`src/gateway/managed-document-attachments.ts` via an esbuild bundle
and exercised through `http.createServer()` — no vitest, no mocks.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```sh
1. Bundle the new module:
node_modules/.bin/esbuild src/gateway/managed-document-attachments.ts \
  --bundle --platform=node --format=esm \
  --outfile=_bug9_doc_bundle.mjs \
  --external:sharp --external:fsevents \
  --banner:js='import { createRequire as __ccr } from "node:module"; const require = __ccr(import.meta.url);'

2. Driver: call createManagedOutgoingDocumentBlocks() with a real .xlsx,
--   then serve handleManagedOutgoingDocumentHttpRequest() on :8766:
cat > _bug9_doc_harness.mjs <<'JS'
import http from "node:http";
import {
  createManagedOutgoingDocumentBlocks,
  handleManagedOutgoingDocumentHttpRequest,
} from "./_bug9_doc_bundle.mjs";
const blocks = await createManagedOutgoingDocumentBlocks({
  sessionKey: "agent:bug9-proof:session:00000000",
  mediaUrls: ["/Users/ada/.openclaw/workspace/bug9-proof/pricing.xlsx"],
  localRoots: "any",
  messageId: "bug9-proof-msg-1",
});
console.log(JSON.stringify(blocks, null, 2));
http.createServer(async (req, res) => {
  await handleManagedOutgoingDocumentHttpRequest(req, res, { auth: { mode: "none" } });
}).listen(8766, "127.0.0.1");
JS
node ./_bug9_doc_harness.mjs &

3. Curl the managed URL (real GET, real handler):
curl -sv -X GET "http://127.0.0.1:8766/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/agent%3Abug9-proof%3Asession%3A00000000/d9ea1437-5c11-41b4-b3ed-aabfe0baa90a/full" -o /tmp/dl.bin

4. Inspect the on-disk record:
find ~/.openclaw/media/outgoing-docs/ -type f
cat ~/.openclaw/media/outgoing-docs/records/d9ea1437-*.json
```

**After-fix evidence**:

Step 1 — `createManagedOutgoingDocumentBlocks()` returned (real call,
real bytes copied to disk):

```json
[
  {
    "type": "attachment",
    "attachment": {
      "url": "/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/agent%3Abug9-proof%3Asession%3A00000000/d9ea1437-5c11-41b4-b3ed-aabfe0baa90a/full",
      "kind": "document",
      "label": "pricing.xlsx",
      "mimeType": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"
    }
  }
]
```

Step 2 — real on-disk artifacts written by the call above:

```
$ find ~/.openclaw/media/outgoing-docs/ -type f
/Users/ada/.openclaw/media/outgoing-docs/records/d9ea1437-5c11-41b4-b3ed-aabfe0baa90a.json
/Users/ada/.openclaw/media/outgoing-docs/originals/2f09ba44-2680-4dba-b2f3-af5f93e7933f.xlsx

$ cat .../records/d9ea1437-5c11-41b4-b3ed-aabfe0baa90a.json
{
    "attachmentId": "d9ea1437-5c11-41b4-b3ed-aabfe0baa90a",
    "sessionKey": "agent:bug9-proof:session:00000000",
    "messageId": "bug9-proof-msg-1",
    "createdAt": "2026-05-05T15:47:06.252Z",
    "retentionClass": "history",
    "label": "pricing.xlsx",
    "original": {
        "path": ".../originals/2f09ba44-2680-4dba-b2f3-af5f93e7933f.xlsx",
        "contentType": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet",
        "sizeBytes": 2058,
        "filename": "2f09ba44-2680-4dba-b2f3-af5f93e7933f.xlsx"
    }
}
```

Step 3 — live curl against the real handler shows the
transcript-membership guard correctly refuses orphan records:

```
$ curl -sv -X GET "http://127.0.0.1:8766/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/.../d9ea1437-.../full"
< HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
< Content-Length: 9
not found
```

Step 4 — wire-format response (post-validation replay over the same
on-disk record, running the IDENTICAL response-shaping code from
`managed-document-attachments.ts` lines 906-925):

```
$ curl -sv -X GET "http://127.0.0.1:8767/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/.../d9ea1437-.../full" -o /tmp/dl.bin
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet
< content-length: 2058
< content-disposition: attachment; filename="2f09ba44-2680-4dba-b2f3-af5f93e7933f.xlsx"
< cache-control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable

$ xxd /tmp/dl.bin | head -1
00000000: 504b 0304 1400 0000 0800 b753 f31e 7cad  PK.........S..|.
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- `createManagedOutgoingDocumentBlocks` saves a real `.xlsx` under
  `media/outgoing-docs/originals/` and writes a record JSON pinning the
  canonical xlsx MIME and `retentionClass: "history"`.
- The block returned to the chat layer carries the new
  `/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/...` URL with `kind: "document"` and
  `mimeType: application/vnd.openxmlformats-...spreadsheetml.sheet`.
- The handler refuses orphan records (404) — transcript-membership
  protection works.
- The post-validation file-serve emits HTTP 200 with the correct xlsx
  `Content-Type`, the new `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="..."`
  header, and `cache-control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable` — the
  live response carries the actual `PK\x03\x04` xlsx bytes saved in step 1.

**What was not tested**: I did not exercise the full assistant chat
pipeline that calls `createManagedOutgoingDocumentBlocks` from inside
the gateway HTTP server with a real session JSONL — that integration is
covered by the existing vitest suite. The transcript-membership guard's
"pass" path therefore is exercised by tests with mocks; this proof
covers the "fail" path with real runtime, plus the file-serve response
shape with a verbatim replay against the real on-disk record.

prs.title: fix(chat): MEDIA: binary file delivery — proper download for xlsx/csv/zip (downstream bug 9b)
prs.body:
# Downstream bug 9b — file delivery for non-image binary files

Bug #9 covered MIME inference (#77875) and the gateway-managed outgoing
document pipeline (#77877). Bug #9b plugs three remaining gaps in the
plain `MEDIA:` → `/__openclaw__/assistant-media` path that produced a "Save as Webpage Complete" fallback for non-image binary files
on a production downstream instance.

## Root cause (one-liner)

`/__openclaw__/assistant-media` streamed xlsx/csv/pdf/zip with the right
`Content-Type` but no `Content-Disposition`, the chat anchor lacked a
`download` attribute, and the new managed `/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/`
URL was being double-wrapped through assistant-media — together that lets
Safari render the response in-tab and offer Save As "Webpage Complete".

## What goes wrong without this PR

1. `/__openclaw__/assistant-media` sets the right `Content-Type` for
   `xlsx`/`csv`/`pdf`/`zip` but **no `Content-Disposition`**. Safari (and
   other browsers under various preference combinations) renders the
   response in-tab; File→Save offers "Webpage Complete" as the only
   option.
2. The document anchor in `grouped-render.ts` uses `target="_blank"` with
   **no `download` attribute**, so even browsers that respect
   `Content-Disposition` are first asked to open the file in a new tab —
   the gateway hint is the only thing keeping it from rendering.
3. The managed `/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/` URL produced by the
   gateway (#77877) is **misclassified as a "local" source** and
   double-wrapped through `/__openclaw__/assistant-media`, discarding the
   managed `Content-Disposition: attachment` header.

## What lands

### Server side (`src/gateway/control-ui.ts`)

- `handleControlUiAssistantMediaRequest` sets
  `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<basename>"` for any
  response whose resolved MIME is not image/audio/video. Images, audio,
  and video keep the default inline disposition because the chat surface
  inlines them. `application/octet-stream` fallbacks also get the
  attachment hint so unclassified content still downloads cleanly.
- `safeAssistantMediaDownloadFilename` mirrors the managed-document
  sibling: strips CR/LF/quote/backslash/slash so the filename is safe
  to interpolate into the header. Unicode is preserved.

### Client side (`ui/src/ui/chat/grouped-render.ts`)

- Document-kind anchors now render with `download=<label>` alongside the
  existing `target=_blank` / `rel=noreferrer` pair, so clicks trigger
  same-origin save-to-disk with the suggested filename. `target=_blank`
  stays as a graceful fallback for browsers that ignore the `download`
  attribute on cross-origin or sandboxed responses.
- `isLocalAssistantAttachmentSource` also recognizes
  `/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/` as a non-local URL so the managed-doc
  response from #77877 isn't double-wrapped through assistant-media and
  keeps its `Content-Disposition: attachment` header.

## Tests

### `src/gateway/control-ui.http.test.ts` (Bug #9b describe block, 6 tests)

- `.xlsx`, `.csv`, `.pdf`, `.zip` each respond 200 with the canonical
  `attachment; filename="<original>"` header.
- `.png` keeps the default inline disposition (no header set).
- Filename sanitization replaces embedded double quotes with `_`.

### `ui/src/ui/chat/grouped-render.test.ts` (3 new + 1 strengthened)

- Existing "verified local assistant attachments" test now asserts
  `download=test-doc.pdf` on the rendered anchor.
- New "binary document attachments (xlsx/csv/zip)" test renders three
  `MEDIA:` refs and asserts `download=pricing.xlsx`, `export.csv`,
  `bundle.zip` plus the standard mediaTicket-bearing href.
- "preserves same-origin assistant attachments" test now asserts
  `download=test-doc.pdf` on the same-origin `/__openclaw__/media`
  anchor.
- New "managed outgoing-doc URLs" test asserts the
  `/api/chat/media/outgoing-doc/` URL renders without re-wrapping
  through `/__openclaw__/assistant-media` and carries
  `download=pricing.xlsx`.

## Test results

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/control-ui.http.test.ts` — 156
  passed (52 × 3 environments)
- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run src/ui/chat/grouped-render.test.ts` —
  37 passed
- All 11 unit-environment chat UI test files (121 tests) pass
- `oxlint` clean on the four touched files
- `pnpm lint:ui:no-raw-window-open` clean

## Related

- Pairs with #77875 (UI MIME mappings, Bug #9)
- Pairs with #77877 (gateway managed document pipeline, Bug #9)
- A separate downstream change covers the spreadsheet
  skill side (bug 9a)
- Reported by a downstream production user, 2026-05-05



## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: `/__openclaw__/assistant-media` previously
served `.xlsx`/`.csv`/`.pdf`/`.zip` with the right `Content-Type` but no
`Content-Disposition` header, so Safari rendered them in-tab and offered
"Webpage Complete" as the only Save As format. After this PR every
non-image MIME gets `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="..."`.

**Real environment tested**: macOS 25.3.0 (arm64), Node v22.22.0, branch
`fix/chat-binary-file-delivery-bug-9b` at commit `70700cf707`. Real
`~/.openclaw` state dir, real on-disk fixture files, no vitest, no mocks.
The handler is loaded directly from `src/gateway/control-ui.ts` via an
esbuild bundle and served through `http.createServer()` listening on
`127.0.0.1:8765`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```sh
1. Build a CJS-compatible ESM bundle of the patched module:
node_modules/.bin/esbuild src/gateway/control-ui.ts \
  --bundle --platform=node --format=esm \
  --outfile=_bug9_control_ui.mjs \
  --external:sharp --external:fsevents \
  --banner:js='import { createRequire as __ccr } from "node:module"; const require = __ccr(import.meta.url);'

2. Tiny harness:
cat > _bug9_harness.mjs <<'JS'
import http from "node:http";
import { handleControlUiAssistantMediaRequest } from "./_bug9_control_ui.mjs";
http.createServer(async (req, res) => {
  const handled = await handleControlUiAssistantMediaRequest(req, res, {});
  if (!handled) { res.writeHead(404).end("not handled"); }
}).listen(8765, "127.0.0.1", () => console.log("listening"));
JS
node ./_bug9_harness.mjs &

3. Real fixture files in ~/.openclaw/workspace/bug9-proof/:
--    pricing.xlsx (PK\x03\x04), data.csv, report.pdf, bundle.zip, photo.png

4. Hit each one:
for f in pricing.xlsx data.csv report.pdf bundle.zip photo.png; do
  curl -sIv "http://127.0.0.1:8765/__openclaw__/assistant-media?source=$HOME/.openclaw/workspace/bug9-proof/$f"
done
```

**After-fix evidence**:

`.xlsx` — gets `Content-Disposition: attachment` (the fix):

```
> HEAD /__openclaw__/assistant-media?source=/Users/ada/.openclaw/workspace/bug9-proof/pricing.xlsx HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet
< Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="pricing.xlsx"
< Cache-Control: no-cache
< Content-Length: 2058
```

`.csv`:

```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/csv
< Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="data.csv"
< Content-Length: 36
```

`.pdf`:

```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: application/pdf
< Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="report.pdf"
< Content-Length: 53
```

`.zip`:

```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: application/zip
< Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="bundle.zip"
< Content-Length: 1028
```

`.png` — does NOT get `Content-Disposition` (proves the fix is targeted):

```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: image/png
< Cache-Control: no-cache
< Content-Length: 69
```

**Observed result after fix**:

| extension | `Content-Type`                                                     | `Content-Disposition`                  |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| `.xlsx`   | `application/vnd.openxmlformats-...spreadsheetml.sheet`            | `attachment; filename="pricing.xlsx"`  |
| `.csv`    | `text/csv`                                                         | `attachment; filename="data.csv"`      |
| `.pdf`    | `application/pdf`                                                  | `attachment; filename="report.pdf"`    |
| `.zip`    | `application/zip`                                                  | `attachment; filename="bundle.zip"`    |
| `.png`    | `image/png`                                                        | *(absent — inline)*                    |

Every binary document now triggers a download with the original filename;
images stay inline as before. This is the wire-level behaviour the reporting
user's browser will see.

**What was not tested**: I did not exercise the full chat anchor click in
a real browser on the production instance itself — I only verified the
gateway response shape end-to-end. The grouped-render `download=` anchor
attribute change is covered by the strengthened `grouped-render.test.ts`
assertions (which run against jsdom).

prs.title: fix(control-ui): restore `has-copy` class on chat bubbles with action buttons
prs.body:
## Summary

Assistant chat bubbles that render the floating `.chat-bubble-actions` (copy + expand buttons) need the `has-copy` class so the matching `.chat-bubble.has-copy { padding-right: 70px; }` rule reserves space for those absolutely-positioned buttons. Without the class, the buttons sit on top of the message text.

A downstream production user reported this exact symptom: the rightmost word of the latest assistant message was visually obscured by the copy/expand icons. Screenshot:

![overlap bug](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/assets/placeholder/bubble-overlap.png)

## Root cause

The class was correctly added by #61872 and #62121 (thanks @jjjojoj) back in April, but an unrelated refactor (`ead8be96fd`, _Add tweakcn custom theme import_) rebuilt the `bubbleClasses` array and accidentally dropped `has-copy`. The CSS rules in `grouped.css` / `layout.css` still exist, so re-adding the class restores the intended padding without any CSS churn.

```ts
// Before (buggy)
const bubbleClasses = [
  "chat-bubble",
  isToolMessage ? "chat-bubble--tool-shell" : "",
  opts.isStreaming ? "streaming" : "",
  "fade-in",
];
```

The `<div class="chat-bubble-actions">` then rendered conditionally based on `canCopyMarkdown || canExpand`, but the bubble never picked up `has-copy`, so the CSS that reserves right-padding for those buttons did not apply.

## Changes

- **`ui/src/ui/chat/grouped-render.ts`** — compute `willRenderBubbleActions` once, before building `bubbleClasses`, and append `has-copy` when the action row will render. Reuse it for the existing `hasActions` variable so the two stay in sync (single source of truth for \"does this bubble show action buttons?\").
- **`ui/src/ui/chat/grouped-render.test.ts`** — regression unit test asserting that an assistant bubble with action buttons carries `has-copy`. **Fails without the fix.**
- **`ui/src/ui/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`** — defensive layout regression: at 320 / 430 / 600 px viewports, `.chat-text` must not visually extend into the `.chat-bubble-actions` rect (catches a future CSS-only regression where the class is present but padding-right is reduced).

## Verification

\`\`\`
pnpm exec vitest run \\
  ui/src/ui/chat/grouped-render.test.ts \\
  ui/src/ui/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts
\`\`\`

→ 55/55 pass with fix; the new unit test fails without the fix (verified with stash → restore).

cc @jjjojoj — restoring your original `has-copy` wiring.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): render chat-bubble-actions as floating chip
prs.body:
## Summary

The hover action icons (open-in-canvas + copy-as-markdown) sit absolute-positioned at the top-right of assistant bubbles. Previously the container had no background, so the SVG glyphs visually overlapped any message text underneath — especially noticeable when a line wraps tightly against the 70px right-padding boundary.

Give `.chat-bubble-actions` an opaque card backdrop, a small radius, a subtle shadow, and a `backdrop-filter` blur so the icons read as a deliberate floating control above the prose rather than glyphs mixed into the text. Light mode gets a faint border instead of relying solely on contrast since the card and bubble backgrounds match.

No layout shift — bubble padding is unchanged; only the existing chip gains a backdrop.

## Reproduction

1. Open an OpenClaw chat session in the control UI.
2. Hover any assistant message whose text wraps close to the right edge of the bubble.
3. Before: the `<>` (open-in-canvas) and copy glyphs render on top of the trailing word with no visible chip.
4. After: the action buttons sit inside a small floating chip with opaque background + subtle shadow.

Reported by a downstream production user.

## Test plan

- `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/ui/chat/grouped-render.test.ts` — 33/33 pass.
- `npx vite build` — clean.
- Visually verified in light + dark themes.

## Related

- Builds on prior fix `e83e147995` ("fix(control-ui): restore has-copy class on chat bubbles with action buttons") which added the bubble-side padding. This PR makes the chip itself visually robust regardless of viewport width.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reject tool input schemas with a top-level union before publishing (openclaw-1azg)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway-managed `claude-cli` run died mid-turn with

```
API Error: 400 tools.2.custom.input_schema: input_schema does not support
oneOf, allOf, or anyOf at the top level
```

immediately followed by `candidate=anthropic/claude-opus-5 reason=unknown next=none` — the whole turn killed with no usable explanation.

Two independent defects:

1. **A tool input schema can reach a provider with a union at its root.** The MCP loopback publish path (`buildMcpToolSchema` in `src/gateway/mcp-http.schema.ts`) flattened only a root `anyOf`/`oneOf`, and only when neither sibling `properties`/`required` had to be preserved. A root `allOf` passed straight through, an empty root union list was published as-is, and the real normalizer's `expandJsonSchemaTypeArray` rewrites a root `type: [...]` into a root `anyOf` after that check could have run. The resulting 400 is request-wide and names only a **tool index**, never a tool name, so the failure is opaque exactly where it needs to be actionable.
2. **The fallback ladder classified that 400 as `unknown`.** A deterministic rejection of a tool *definition* is not a property of the candidate model — every fallback candidate is offered the same tool set and fails identically — so reporting `reason=unknown` both wastes the ladder and reads to an operator as an unexplained dead turn.

Deliberately out of scope: loosening any validator to accept top-level unions silently. Either the shape belongs at the boundary and is declared, or it is flattened or rejected explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Flatten, then assert at the publish boundary.** `flattenTopLevelUnionSchema` collapses every top-level union keyword into the single object schema native tool definitions require. `anyOf`/`oneOf` branches are alternatives, so only a key required by *every* branch of that keyword stays required; `allOf` branches all hold, so their required keys are unioned in. Sibling root `properties`/`required` are kept rather than replaced, and an empty union list is dropped with a one-shot warning naming the tool instead of being left for the provider to reject. `hasTopLevelUnion` now gates on all three keywords rather than two.

**A conjunction keeps its exact intersection, in a scope that does not change what either side accepts.** Root `properties`, each `allOf` branch, and each sibling union keyword all hold at once, so merging them with the *alternative* merger would broaden the tool's contract (the revision-1 finding). Each `allOf` branch and each union keyword is merged into its own map and then combined by `combineConjunctiveProps`, which takes the exact intersection of the two property schemas through `intersectPropertySchemas` (new, in `src/shared/json-schema-conjunction.ts`, next to the existing literal-schema owner).

Three review rounds showed that hand-writing a merge rule per keyword exposes another edge case each time, so that function has **one general rule** instead:

- **A flat schema is published only when one schema can state both constraints exactly.** That holds for *self-contained* keywords — `type`, `enum`/`const`, `format`, `pattern`, the numeric and length and item and property-count bounds — whose assertion reads only the instance. So root `action: {type:"string"}` plus branch constants `"start"`/`"stop"` publishes as `action: {type:"string", enum:["start","stop"]}`, and `allOf` branches constraining `mode` with `["read","write"]` and `["write","delete"]` publish as `enum:["write"]` — the only value satisfying both.
- **Everything else keeps its own evaluation scope, as a nested conjunction `{allOf:[a,b]}` under that property.** `additionalProperties`, `properties`, `items`, `if`/`then` and nested composition are evaluated against *their own* schema's siblings, so copying one of them into the other schema changes what that schema accepts: a branch declaring `{type:"object", additionalProperties:false}` and no properties rejects `{x:"ok"}`, and merging its `additionalProperties` into a root property that *does* declare `x` would advertise that value as valid (the revision-3 finding). Keeping the conjunct boundary is exact, and nested unions are legal in a native tool input schema — only the root is restricted to a single object, which is what `findToolInputSchemaTopLevelUnionError` documents and enforces.
- **`integer` is a subset of `number`**, including inside `type` arrays, so `number` against `integer` narrows to `integer` rather than reporting disjoint type names.
- **Annotations do not constrain a value**, so a differing `description`/`title`/`examples`/`default` never makes a conjunction conflict; the left (root-side) schema's metadata is kept so the published output is deterministic. This is the same distinction `src/shared/json-schema-literals.ts` already applies to alternatives, now shared with the conjunctive path through the new `schemaValidationKeywordsOnly`.

Because the nested conjunction is always available, **no property-level overlap withholds a tool any more** — a tool main serves cannot disappear from `tools/list` (and therefore from `tools/call`) because two conjuncts constrain one key. An overlap that needs the nested form is reported with a one-shot `mcp-loopback` warning naming the tool and the key, so the published shape is never a surprise.

**`allOf` branch-level constraints are carried over or the tool is withheld by name.** Every `allOf` branch holds on every instance, so a branch keyword the flattener does not fold in is a real constraint the published schema would lose (the second revision-2 finding). `additionalProperties` is now resolved across conjuncts: it is republished on the flattened object when no other combined schema contributed a key the declaring conjunct does not list — so `{allOf:[{…, properties:{value:…}, required:["value"], additionalProperties:false}]}` publishes *with* `additionalProperties:false` instead of advertising `{"value":"ok","extra":1}` as valid — and the tool is withheld with a named warning when closing it would be unsound (a conjunct closed to additional properties while another conjunct contributes a key, or two conjuncts closing it differently). Any other branch-level validation keyword (`not`, nested `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`, `patternProperties`, `if`/`then`, `dependentRequired`, `$ref`, …) and a branch `type` that excludes objects now withhold that one tool with a warning naming the keyword, instead of publishing a definition that silently accepts inputs the tool rejects. Pure annotations (`title`, `description`, `default`, `examples`, …) are carried as before.

Alternatives *within* one `anyOf`/`oneOf` deliberately keep the existing upstream contract (compatible literals union; other same-key conflicts keep the first variant and warn) — that behaviour is pinned by `src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts` on main and bundled tools such as `deep_research` depend on it, which the proof run below shows happening live. A branch keyword dropped on that path now at least emits a one-shot warning naming the tool, the keyword and the alternative; whether those alternatives should instead withhold the tool for consistency with the conjunctive path is a product decision left to a maintainer.

**An invariant check at the point the tool is named.** Immediately after the schema is otherwise finalized, `findToolInputSchemaTopLevelUnionError` (new, in `src/shared/json-schema-defaults.ts`, alongside `TOOL_INPUT_SCHEMA_TOP_LEVEL_UNION_KEYWORDS`) re-checks the root and throws if any union keyword survived. Nested unions are legal and unreported. This is not a second normalizer: it fails where the tool is *named*, rather than letting the provider return a 400 that names only an index.

**Classify the provider rejection.** `src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts` adds the exact observed text plus a structural pattern, `/\btools\.\d+\.(?:custom\.)?input_schema\b/i`, to the `format` class — provider request validation that names a published tool definition rather than the conversation. `format` does not consume a transient cooldown probe slot.

## User Impact

A tool whose published input schema would be rejected is named at the boundary that produced it, so the fault is attributable instead of surfacing as an index into a request array. A composed schema that can be projected onto one object schema now publishes with its constraints intact — including a narrowed overlap and a closed branch — so tools that worked before this change keep working and keep their real contract. No tool is withheld because two conjuncts constrain the same property: the published property carries both constraints, flat where that is exact and as a nested `{allOf:[…]}` otherwise, so a tool that main advertises stays advertised and callable. Only a *branch-level* composition that one root object schema cannot carry at all (`not`, nested composition, `patternProperties`, `if`/`then`, a conjunct closed to additional properties while another conjunct contributes a key) is withheld, from that one tool's entry, with a warning naming the tool and the keyword, rather than silently handing the client arguments the tool will reject; the rest of the catalog still publishes. If such a rejection still reaches a provider, the failover ladder reports a tool-definition fault rather than `unknown`, so an operator sees why the turn ended and that retrying another model with the same tool set cannot help.

## Evidence

**Tested head: `37354b136417c2cb7c729ccf804cdc73a1ca1a83`.**

Real behavior proof, driving the production path end to end: a real MCP loopback HTTP listener (`ensureMcpLoopbackServer`), a real `tools/list` JSON-RPC request over a real TCP socket to `127.0.0.1:<port>`, the real grant store and run admission, the real plugin loader reading a fixture plugin from disk through `plugins.load.paths`, real tool resolution, and the real publish boundary `buildMcpToolSchema` reached through `mcp-http.runtime.ts`. No vitest, no mock of any seam on that path, and a throwaway `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` so nothing touches a real state directory or the live gateway. The only interception is a tee on `process.stdout`/`process.stderr` so the run can assert on the real warning lines the production logger emits.

The fixture plugin registers ten tools whose `parameters` carry top-level union keywords — the review's own examples from all three rounds. The three added for this revision are exactly the revision-3 findings: `proof_scoped_overlap` (root property `payload: {type:"object", properties:{x:{type:"string"}}}` against an `anyOf` branch constraining `payload` as `{type:"object", additionalProperties:false}`), `proof_numeric_subtype` (`count: {type:"number"}` against `{type:"integer"}`, plus `size: {type:["number","string"]}` against `{type:["integer","boolean"]}`), and `proof_annotated_constants` (root `action: {type:"string", description:"Command"}` against `anyOf` constants carrying `description:"Start"` / `description:"Stop"`).

Command, run against the same fixture and the same real listener, differing only in which revision of the publisher is on disk:

```
PROOF_MODE=<reviewed|head> node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/proof-197118-mcp-tool-schema-union.ts
```

**Before, `PROOF_MODE=reviewed` — `src/gateway/mcp-http.schema.ts` and `src/shared/json-schema-literals.ts` restored from `ac0e162f9d71d0f2e1f53d897c239dd145428132` (the head ClawSweeper reviewed in revision 3) and `src/shared/json-schema-conjunction.ts` removed. All three revision-3 findings reproduced over the wire, not just read:**

```
[mcp-loopback] tool "proof_numeric_subtype" input schema constrains "count" differently across combined top-level schemas; skipping the tool instead of publishing a weakened constraint
[mcp-loopback] tool "proof_annotated_constants" input schema constrains "action" differently across combined top-level schemas; skipping the tool instead of publishing a weakened constraint

PROOF_MODE=reviewed  tools/list HTTP 200  62 tools served
  proof_scoped_overlap: {"type":"object","properties":{"payload":{"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"additionalProperties":false}},"required":[]}
  proof_numeric_subtype: NOT SERVED (skipped by publisher)
  proof_annotated_constants: NOT SERVED (skipped by publisher)

  PASS  REVIEWED HEAD: finding 1 is real - additionalProperties is copied out of its evaluation scope — payload = {"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"additionalProperties":false} - advertises {"payload":{"x":"ok"}} as valid although the anyOf branch declares no properties and rejects it
  PASS  REVIEWED HEAD: finding 2 is real - number against integer withholds the whole tool — proof_numeric_subtype absent from tools/list although the exact intersection is {type:"integer"}
  PASS  REVIEWED HEAD: finding 3 is real - differing descriptions withhold the whole tool — proof_annotated_constants absent from tools/list although the exact intersection is {type:"string",enum:["start","stop"]}
```

prs.title: fix: show linked OpenClaw ID on tunnel profile pages
prs.body:
Related: #197628

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Profile → Identity asks you to link OpenClaw ID over a personal sign-in even when your profile is already linked, if you open the Control UI through the OpenClaw ID tunnel.

## User Impact

Your saved account and owner label appear through either entrance. Link and Unlink remain available only through an eligible personal sign-in, such as Tailscale. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reading an existing link is separate from permission to change it. The Gateway reads only the caller’s canonical personal profile and rechecks live profile authority after the read; account IDs stay server-side. The UI now checks saved links before deciding what controls to offer. Shared-owner and synthetic callers remain ineligible.

## Evidence

- Reproduced before the fix: the Gateway rejected the tunnel’s link-status read, and the browser displayed the personal-sign-in guidance despite an existing link. Both regressions pass after the fix.
- Focused checks: 5 account-link handler tests, 2 channel-boundary tests, 7 identity-row tests, and all 13 profile-page browser tests pass.
- Core/UI typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and the production UI bundle used by the browser suite pass.
- Browser proof uses the real production UI with a mocked Gateway and synthetic profile data. Handler tests separately exercise server admission and profile selection. No live issuer or production account was changed.
- Independent local review: autoreview with Claude Fable 5, full local diff against base 785706eb8bd; clean, with no accepted/actionable findings. Manual maintainability review found no structural regression. Transient read/authority failures intentionally retain Retry rather than being relabeled as unsupported connections.

**Before — the linked tunnel profile incorrectly asks for a personal sign-in**

![Before: OpenClaw ID displays linking guidance despite a saved link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87088e9b-8a74-40d4-bc52-1825292671b0)

**After — the saved account is shown without unavailable link-changing controls**

![After: OpenClaw ID displays the saved email and owner label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/266ddd5c-01ab-413a-83b4-ff5628c91e0d)

prs.title: feat(agents): let the gateway tool read update status
prs.body:
## Summary

- The agent-facing `gateway` tool can now read the Gateway's update state with `{ action: "update.status" }`, forwarding to the existing read-only `update.status` RPC through the same `callGatewayTool` path that already backs `config.get` / `config.schema.lookup`.
- `update.status` stays available when `allowConfigReads` is false. The restricted tool variant is the one that schedules `update.run`, so it is the one that most needs the read: "why did my update fail?" is a question the restricted agent is expected to answer without handing it config read authority.
- No new RPC and no new write authority: the action is read-only, `update.run` / `restart` / `update.cleanup` admission is untouched, and the change is a single enum + dispatch branch in `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts`.
- The tool description and the Codex prompt snapshot that mirrors it (`codex-dynamic-tools.telegram-direct.json`) move together, per the prompt-prefix contract. Both variants were shortened to 165 chars ("Owner/operator:" replaces "Owner request/operator schedule:") so the tool directory no longer truncates the description.

Fixes #188320

## Linked context

- Issue: #188320 — the `gateway` tool could schedule `update.run` and restart the Gateway but could not read the update state it was about to change.
- Review history on this PR: the 2026-10-30 ClawSweeper round raised three P2s (signal/result assertions, assembled-tool contracts, directory description limit). All three are fixed on this head.
- **This revision answers the one remaining reviewer ask** — *"Provide a successful real agent invocation of `update.status` with configuration reads allowed and withheld; the supplied invocation aborts before the changed tool body"*. The previous revision's `tools.invoke` capture aborted on agent-database admission, so the new forwarding branch never ran. This body replaces that capture with **two successful executions of the real tool object, one per variant**, against a live Gateway (see below), and explains honestly why the `tools.invoke` wrapper path is still blocked on this host.

## Revision note (rebase)

The capture below was taken at head `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`. The branch has since been **rebased onto `origin/main` to clear a merge conflict** (`mergeable: dirty`), so the current head is `8862cfd8bddc482a2ddfbe7caa208b2a9d0fbfd2`. The patch content is unchanged — same 8 files, `+63 −22` — and the only bytes that moved were the generated prompt-snapshot fixtures, which were regenerated with `scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --write` rather than hand-merged (`Prompt snapshots are current (6 files)`). Because the captured `schedule.install.git.currentSha` is literally the checkout's HEAD at capture time, it reads `3c654c1b48f…` and not the post-rebase sha; that is the expected consequence of the rebase and is called out here instead of being silently edited.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Before this patch the assembled `gateway` tool's action enum contained `config.get`, `config.schema.lookup`, `update.run`, `restart` and `update.cleanup` only, so `{ action: "update.status" }` was rejected at the tool boundary and an agent could not read the update state it was about to change or diagnose a failed update. After the patch the same call forwards to the canonical read-only `update.status` RPC and returns the recorded state, and it does so in **both** variants — including the restricted one that has configuration reads withheld.

**Real setup tested**: Windows host, Node v24.22.1, branch `feat/agent-update-status` at head `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`, TypeScript sources executed directly through `scripts/tsx.mjs` (source runtime, not a packaged dist), **brand-new** isolated state directory `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2` (empty before this run, so the agent database is created and migrated from scratch rather than reused), Gateway bound to loopback port 18815 with `--allow-unconfigured`, reaching `post-ready.startup-maintenance` at total 387.0 s before any RPC was issued.
- **Runtime**: node v24.22.1 + `scripts/tsx.mjs` loader (source runtime); no packaged `dist` build was used for this capture.

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2
export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18815
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18815

# (1) Ground truth: the canonical RPC the new branch forwards to.
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway call update.status --timeout 180000 --json

# (2) The changed code path itself, exercised once per variant against the same
#     live Gateway. This is a throwaway harness (NOT part of the patch); it
#     imports the production factory and calls the production tool object.
#     Variant selection is the same input the real assembly passes:
#       src/agents/openclaw-tools.gateway.ts:23 ->
#       createGatewayTool({ allowConfigReads: options?.gatewayConfigReadAllowed === true })
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ./.proof-probe-188321.ts
```

```ts
// .proof-probe-188321.ts — throwaway harness, deleted after the capture
import { createGatewayTool } from "./src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.js";
import { captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader } from "./src/config/config.js";

const variants = [
  { label: "FULL VARIANT (config reads allowed)", allowConfigReads: true },
  { label: "RESTRICTED VARIANT (config reads withheld)", allowConfigReads: false },
];

async function main() {
  const readConfig = captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader({ skipPluginValidation: true });
  await readConfig();
  for (const v of variants) {
    const tool = createGatewayTool({ allowConfigReads: v.allowConfigReads, senderIsOwner: true });
    console.log(`### ${v.label}`);
    console.log(`tool.description = ${tool.description}`);
    console.log(`action enum      = ${JSON.stringify(tool.parameters.properties.action.enum)}`);
    const result = await tool.execute("proof-188321", { action: "update.status" });
    console.log(`RESULT = ${JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}`);
  }
}
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```text
}
```

```text
    "updateAvailable": null,
    "effectiveChannel": "dev",
    "schedule": { "channel": "dev", "autoEnabled": false, "install": { "kind": "git", "git": { "currentSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d", "commitAtMs": 1794477400000, "upstreamSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d", "repositoryUrl": "https://github.com/lsr911/openclaw", "status": "current" } } }
  }
}
```

```text
# (3) RESTRICTED VARIANT (config reads withheld) — elapsed_ms = 210
tool.name        = gateway
tool.description = Read update status; owner/operator: update.run, restart, update.cleanup. Cleanup permanently retires eligible rollback copies; dryRun previews. Use runtime-owned actions.
action enum      = ["update.run","restart","update.cleanup","update.status"]
RESULT = identical canonical status object as (2), same currentSha/upstreamSha/status:"current"
```

```text
# (4) Gateway-side corroboration — one backend connection per variant, both
#     authenticated as an operator, at the moment of the two probes.
[ws] client connected conn=64415c02-… client=gateway-client name=agent mode=backend role=operator auth=device-token
[ws] client connected conn=232a8461-… client=gateway-client name=agent mode=backend role=operator auth=device-token
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `update.status` now executes through the tool object in **both** variants and returns the live Gateway's real update state — `schedule.install.git.currentSha` is `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`, which is exactly `git rev-parse HEAD` of this checkout, and `repositoryUrl` is this fork. That SHA is read out of the running Gateway's own install state, so the payload cannot be synthesized by the calling process. The two action enums are the direct, structural answer to the reviewer's question: the restricted schema is `["update.run","restart","update.cleanup","update.status"]` — `update.status` is present while `config.get` and `config.schema.lookup` are absent — and the full schema is the six-action superset. The restricted variant ran much faster (210 ms vs 8079 ms); the likely explanation is a warm connection on the second call, and I am not claiming more than that — both executions are real calls against the same Gateway, which the per-variant backend connections in (4) corroborate. `lastRun` / `activeRun` are absent because no update was ever run in this fresh isolated state directory; that is the honest shape of a clean Gateway, not a filtered field.

**What was not tested**: a packaged `dist` build of this head (both captures use the tsx source runtime); the **`tools.invoke` wrapper path end-to-end** — it is still blocked on this host by `Agent database execution admission is closed` (see the limitation section below), which fires inside the Gateway's agent-database admission *before* the tool body runs, so it cannot exercise this patch either way; a full model-driven agent turn on Discord/Telegram that selects this action from the model's tool list; a real update run producing `lastRun` / `activeRun` records (no update was deliberately triggered in a throwaway state directory); and any `openclaw update status` CLI surface, which does not exist for this action.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: The `tools.invoke` RPC (which is how the previous revision tried to reach the tool) is gated by the Gateway's agent-database execution admission. On a brand-new state directory that admission still ends in a schema handshake failure — `agent database remains degraded agentId=main … reason="Agent database execution admission is closed"`, with the Gateway log advising `Use the newer install that supports schema 41 or newer`. The `repairHint` is `openclaw doctor --fix`, which is out of scope for this run (it mutates a deliberately throwaway state directory and is not something a contributor should run to manufacture proof). Rather than stop there, the capture above drives the **same production tool object** the assembly builds, so the new forwarding branch genuinely executes and returns Gateway-served data — but it is invoked directly instead of through an agent-mediated turn, and that distinction is stated rather than blurred. Note also that a **successful** `update.status` does not emit a `⇄ res ✓ update.status` line in this build (only failures and the outer `tools.invoke` RPC are logged at that level), so the round-trip evidence here is the backend connection log plus the self-referential `currentSha`, not a `⇄ res ✓` line — I did not fabricate one. No secrets, tokens or real user state were used: every command ran against `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2` on loopback port 18815.

## Tests and validation

- Baseline regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on this head → **`Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 15 passed (15)`, duration 368.90 s, exit 0**. This is the pre-existing suite around the changed file, so it covers "did the patch break the existing actions" rather than only the new branch; the run includes the pre-existing `preserves update diagnostic Unicode in tool results` case alongside the new `update.status` assertions.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.assembly.test.ts src/agents/tool-search.test.ts` → **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the same four files → **All matched files use the correct format.**
- CI on head `3c654c1b48f`: **110 check runs, 0 failures** (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` pass, `openclaw/ci-gate` pass, `pr-failure-report` skipped as expected). The compiled agents-tools suites are covered by CI, not by this Windows host.
- Unit coverage added on this branch: `gateway-tool.test.ts` ("reads update status even when config reads are withheld" — calls the tool with `allowConfigReads: false` and asserts the forwarded method), `gateway-tool.assembly.test.ts` (action present in the coding profile and in the full profiles after `config.schema.lookup`; grants matrix), `tool-search.test.ts` + prompt snapshot (new description text).

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes`)

What is the highest-risk area?
- The risk is the agent tool surface: one more action becomes reachable from a model-driven turn, and that action crosses the Gateway boundary. The action is read-only, but it does expose update channel/schedule state to the restricted tool variant that previously could not read it — the capture above shows exactly that enlarged surface (`update.status` inside a schema that still withholds `config.get`).

How is that risk mitigated?
- The action maps to the existing `update.status` RPC with no parameters and no write admission; it does not touch `update.run`, `restart` or `update.cleanup`. It is enumerated in the schema (no free-form method passthrough), so an unknown action still fails closed at the tool boundary. The restricted-profile availability is intentional and asserted in tests; the full-profile grants matrix keeps the owner/config-read boundary unchanged. The dispatch branch sits *before* the `allowConfigReads` guard rather than inside it, so the read is available without widening the config-read gate.

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Maintainer review (owner decision) on the bounded status action. No author action is pending on the code; this body rewrite is the author action for the proof gap the review named.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?
- Waiting on the maintainer decision requested by the review. Open external proof, stated plainly: a packaged `dist` capture, a model-driven turn that picks the action, and the `tools.invoke` wrapper path (blocked by the agent-database schema handshake on this host).

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?
- 2026-10-30 ClawSweeper P2s: signal/result assertions, assembled-tool contracts, directory description limit — all fixed on this head.
- The 2026-11-12 review's single "Before merge" item ("add real behavior proof … the supplied invocation aborts before the changed tool body") is addressed by the two successful per-variant executions above; the stale "not producible in this checkout" note is retracted.

## Before/After

- **Before**: `{ action: "update.status" }` was outside the tool's action enum in both variants, so the tool boundary rejected it and an agent could only schedule updates, never read their state. The captured "before" is structural — the four-action / five-action enums on `origin/main` — because a live pre-patch build capture would require reverting the patch on a second host.
- **After**: the same call forwards to the canonical `update.status` RPC and returns `{sentinel, updateAvailable, effectiveChannel, schedule}` in both the full variant (6-action enum) and the restricted variant (4-action enum), with `schedule.install.git.currentSha` matching this checkout's HEAD.
- **Boundary**: the action is enumerated in the Zod schema (`stringEnum`), not a free-form method passthrough, so an unknown action still fails tool-input validation before any Gateway call is made — the enum is closed and the new action is an explicit addition, visible in the two enum dumps above.

prs.title: fix: recover catalogs after non-native preparation timeouts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway model catalog stops recovering when a plugin import times out before native verification starts or after verification has finished.

## User Impact

User impact: normal catalog preparation timeouts recover through the existing shared worker lifecycle, while stalled native verification remains terminal for that capture. No configuration, migration, or timeout-budget changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native verifier reports entry, verified-member progress, and exit through one lifecycle owner. The catalog worker forwards start/end immediately and only classifies a timeout as stalled native admission while verification is active. Existing idle deadline renewal still requires new completed members.

Related: #166687. This follow-up does not establish resolution of the separately reported Windows MSIX startup starvation (#167406); preserved Windows replay and caller attribution remain unverified.

## Evidence

- Actual Gateway catalog-worker boundary: eight tests passed, covering imports blocked both before and after verification, ongoing verification progress, terminal verification stalls, and existing catalog refresh siblings. Wrapper wall time: 123.35 seconds.
- Negative controls reproduced both original wrong terminal classifications before their fixes.
- Fresh full-context independent P1 review: scoped-clean; no actionable findings.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged` is running; core typecheck passed and test graph checks are in progress. Cost measurement: `pnpm test src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.native.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all eight tests in 111.47 seconds wall; individual test durations totaled 65.15 seconds (86.99-second Vitest invocation including transformation/setup). This existing native-worker suite must exceed 30 seconds to prove the real compiled worker, import boundary, shared catalog recovery, and terminal native admission—not a helper substitute. Fake timers bound the existing preparation deadline and an explicit import barrier replaces real sleeps; no new per-test Gateway/process boot was added. Hosted CI seconds will be recorded once its selected run completes.
