Fixes #194330 Related: #194338 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Android shows an unexplained total-refresh warning when model discovery fails but a populated model catalog remains available. ## User Impact User impact: users keep their model choices and see a bounded provider or native-discovery warning when that scope is known, with an honest partial-catalog fallback when it is not. Genuine refresh failures remain visible. ## Why This Change Was Made The catalog attempt owner records provider/native failures, including an unknown scope, but previously published only an aggregate flag. This change derives live `refreshFailures` from that owner, carries the facts through the decision adapter and RPC projection, and updates Android to consume them without changing authentication outcomes or model eligibility. Partial recovery now publishes a status change even while another acquisition remains failed. The public projection omits raw errors, credentials, endpoint/profile-shaped labels, and provider identities outside the requested view. Android honors these sanitized scopes rather than recovering hidden labels from legacy outcomes; legacy fallback labels must be present in the returned catalog. **Related work:** #194338 overlaps the same producer and proposes synthesizing `providerOutcomes`. This is an alternative, not a parallel auth-state fix: it retains ready/auth outcomes, distinguishes native and unknown acquisition scopes, and includes Android handling. Reconcile the two approaches before either is merged. #159670 was also inspected; its catalog-auth retention change is not copied here. ## Evidence ### Native Android rendering evidence — November 10 **Native test-fixture rendering, not installed-device/live-Gateway end-to-end proof.** These inspected Android API 34 native-graphics captures exercise the production ChatScreen → MainViewModel → NodeRuntime → ChatController → models.list path, with an isolated in-memory screenshot runtime and controlled Gateway-response I/O. prs.title: fix: preserve Gateway delegation for channel replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repairs a dropped host-ownership handoff that can send channel-origin delegated OpenClaw requests over WebSocket without their private run authority, producing `delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority`.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. Ordinary and fast reply session setup clone the inbound context without copying its privately bound Gateway resolver. Use the existing scope-checked `copyChannelParticipantAdmissionEvidence` helper at both boundaries.
2. A deployment of that first repair still reproduced the error. Further tracing found that Discord's provider supplies the host-bound `buildContext`, but `buildDiscordMessagePreflightContext` dropped it. Message processing then selected the plain fallback builder, so there was no Gateway binding for session initialization to preserve.

**Scope correction (September 17):** that second, Discord-side production correction has since landed upstream independently, in `34f29edb265` — *fix(discord): restore OpenClaw delegation from guild messages* (#143006, September 9). `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight-context.ts` is now byte-identical between this branch and `main`, so this PR no longer carries that production change. What it retains on the Discord side is the **regression test** that pins the forwarding behavior, which upstream did not add. The independent convergence is corroborating evidence that the diagnosis was correct.

**Production surface at the current head** (`git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD`, re-derived this round — the previous four-file list in this section was stale, and named `src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.ts`, which is byte-identical to `main`):

- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-fast-path.ts` — the two session-preparation call sites that copy the admission evidence.
- `src/channels/message-access/admission-evidence.ts` — the fenced resolver stored at preparation.
- `src/plugins/channel-gateway-root-slots.ts` (new) and `src/plugins/registry-runtime-channel.ts` — the channel Gateway slot lifecycle added by rounds 23 and 24. **Corrected this round:** the earlier list here named `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts` and `src/plugins/runtime/gateway-context-binding.ts`; neither is in this PR's diff any more. Main's plugin-runtime consolidation moved the registered-channel owner into `registry-runtime-channel.ts`, and this branch's two later `origin/main` merges put the lifecycle change on that owner. See *Round 25* for the measurement.

It adds no permissions, infers no authority from identifiers, transports no grants over WebSocket, does not weaken the delegation guard, and does not select a global Gateway.

## User Impact

Channel session preparation retains scope-bound Gateway ownership, so calls keep their intended local route. The absent-builder fallback remains unchanged. No configuration or credential changes are required.

## Evidence

### Round 25 — the registry-runtime reconciliation with main, measured

Revision 27's one remaining item asks to reconcile the overlapping registry-runtime changes with main's `registry-runtime-channel.ts` owner, preserve the session-copy and lifecycle fixes, and validate the resulting head. Three facts, each re-derived at the current head `8c569d2c3498ce5fbec55f5f04e6f7bf405ae276`:

**1. The owner reconciliation already landed, after the reviewed head.** Revision 27 reviewed `95c2e8629cd`. Two `origin/main` merges landed on this branch *after* that commit — `2927efa40ed` and `021975dc1b3` — and they are what moved this branch onto main's current owner. Main's plugin-runtime consolidation (#168006, `7008414e344`) and its session-mutation follow-up (#168453, `7924f12c75f`) moved the registered-channel runtime owner out of `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts` into `src/plugins/registry-runtime-channel.ts`. At this head the lifecycle change is applied to *that* file, on main's structure: main's `createRegisteredChannelRuntimeResolver` keeps its `createHostChannelIngressRuntime`, `createHostChannelInboundEventContextBuilder`, `assertSessionEntryPatchAuthority` and `revokePluginRecord` wiring, and this PR adds three `isChannelRecordSuperseded` fences plus the `claimChannelGatewayContext` call inside it. `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts` is no longer in this PR's diff at all.

**2. GitHub reports no conflict.** `gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/pulls/139620 --jq '.mergeable, .mergeable_state'` returns `true` and `blocked` — blocked on checks, not `dirty`. The four-file conflict set recorded in the previous revision of this description is stale and has been replaced in *What is resolved, and what is not* below.

**3. There is almost nothing left to reconcile.** Between the main this branch has merged (`8408f1b5755`, November 11) and `upstream/main` at `33a8ad2b90e` (November 13), upstream changed 7191 files across 642 commits. Exactly **one** of them is also touched by this PR — `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`, where both sides only append shard-lane entries, in regions ~50 lines apart. Upstream changed **none** of this PR's five production files in that window, `src/plugins/registry-runtime-channel.ts` included.

#### The merge was performed and verified locally, and is deliberately not pushed

To test fact 3 rather than assert it, `upstream/main` @ `33a8ad2b90e` was merged into this branch in a worktree:

```sh
git merge --no-ff 33a8ad2b90e -m "Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' into fix/channel-session-gateway-owner"
# -> 502bfa4be30, clean: no conflicts, `git status --short` empty, `git diff --check` clean, signature G
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile   # the merge moves package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml; Packages +8 -3
pnpm tsgo:core                   # exit 0 (61s)
```

**Silent-merge-drop check, the strong form.** A clean merge is not proof, so the topic patch was compared byte for byte across the merge with the base pinned to the merged main sha. `git diff 33a8ad2b90e...<head> -- src test config extensions` is **1333 lines both before and after** the merge, and `diff` reports exactly two changed lines: the blob hashes and the `@@ -716` → `@@ -720` hunk offset of that one shared vitest lane file, caused by upstream's own four added entries above ours. Every other hunk is identical, in all five production files and all nine test files. Reading the merged result confirms the same per function: `copyChannelParticipantAdmissionEvidence(sessionCtxForState, sessionCtx)` is present in the merged `initSessionStateAttemptLocked`; the same copy is present in the merged `initFastReplySessionState`; the fenced `scopedGatewayContext` and its `bindGatewayContextResolver` association are present in the merged `prepareHostChannelContextAdmissionEvidence`; main's owner wiring and this PR's fences coexist in the merged `createRegisteredChannelRuntimeResolver`. The topic file list stays at 15 files and the stat stays at +1111/−21, so the merge does not grow the PR.

**Why it is not pushed.** `pnpm tsgo:core:test` was killed at about 25 minutes, and the nine focused suites never ran, because this host's shared exec memory budget (17 GB across all concurrent work) terminated both. A merge head whose test typecheck and focused suites did not finish is an ungated head, so it was not pushed; the branch is restored to `8c569d2c349` and the merge is recorded as a one-command reproduction. **Nothing in this description is evidence from `502bfa4be30`** beyond the merge-mechanics and `tsgo:core` results stated in this section.

#### CI at this head is red on a file this PR does not touch

Worth stating plainly rather than leaving for the reviewer to find: the run for `8c569d2c349` (`openclaw/ci-gate`, [run 43176727390](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43176727390), November 12) fails in one shard, `checks-node-changed-compact-small-10`, at `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.attachments.test.ts:82` — two cases expecting no `chat` events receive one with `state: "error"`, `errorMessage: "No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one."`. That file is **not** in this PR's diff, and nothing in this PR touches session attachment creation or chat event emission. 17 other checks pass and 11 are skipped. It is unresolved whether that shard is flaky, broken on the November 11 main this branch sits on, or genuinely interacting with this change; the merge above is the natural next probe, since current main is 642 commits past it.

### Round 24 — the slot history no longer owns retired generations

Revision 25's finding: rollback retires a staged candidate but leaves it as the slot's `current` claim with the predecessor still linked to it, so the next claim appends *behind the retired candidate*. Repeated failed replacements therefore extend the chain indefinitely, every `ownsLiveRegistrySlot` check crosses all of it, and because each link's value strongly holds the next record together with its whole registry, no failed generation can be collected while the live owner lives.

Measured, not argued. The harm is cost and retention, **not a wrong answer** — `isChannelRecordSuperseded` returns the same boolean before and after, which is why the regressions here are retention probes rather than behavioral ones.

Fixing it surfaced a second path of the same class, and the round's two commits address one each.

**Commit 1 — compact failed candidates.** `claimGatewayRootChannelSlot` records the claim each generation displaced and walks back from the slot's current claim through retired candidates, so a new claim links from the exact *live* predecessor. Overwriting that predecessor's single successor link is what releases the compacted generations. A retired candidate never owned the slot, so it leaves the history rather than joining it.

**Commit 2 — stop the history owning anything retired.** Revision 26 then reported, correctly, that commit 1's predecessor links were *owning*, and the slot's `current` claim is strongly held, so `pred(C) → B → A` pinned one whole retired registry per **successful** replacement for the Gateway root's lifetime. That one is self-introduced and fixed in the same round. Measuring it turned up an independent half that commit 1 did **not** introduce: the forward successor links are owning too, and they are rooted at whatever still holds an old generation's record — precisely this PR's subject, a long-lived admitted binding. Across seven committed replacements with such a binding held, retained generations measure 5 of 5 identically before commit 1, after commit 1, and with only the predecessor fix, so that half dates from the slot extraction itself. Both are ours.

- Predecessor links are now **non-owning**. The slot's current claim is the authoritative live owner, and a generation nobody else holds can neither own the slot nor be restored to it.
- Successor links stay **owning on purpose**: answering an authority check from weak references would make a live record's fence depend on when the collector last ran. Retired links crossed during the walk are spliced out instead, which cannot change the answer — a retired claim never supersedes — and keeps one stale binding from holding a long chain of committed generations. Only the owning forward link is removed; the spliced generation keeps its own non-owning predecessor link, because it may still be the slot's `current` claim and the next claim reaches the live predecessor through exactly that link.

In an `--expose-gc` child driving the real `createRuntimeBuilder` ingress chain, using the repo's existing `collectForRetentionCheck` fixture (the pattern of `src/process/spawn-broker/proxy-retention.test.ts`):

| Retired generations still retained, 5 tracked by `WeakRef` | Reviewed head `e81523edf20` | Commit 1 | **This head** |
|---|---|---|---|
| six failed candidates, nothing holding an old generation | 5 | 0 | **0** |
| seven committed replacements, oldest generation held by a stale binding | 5 | 5 | **0** |

In every variant the unowned control collects, the oldest generation is still reported **superseded**, and its stale binding still refuses to resolve — so compaction does not soften the fence.

**Controls, each with a distinct failure reason.**

1. Revert only `src/plugins/channel-gateway-root-slots.ts` to the reviewed head → the failed-candidate retention case fails at `retainedGenerations: 5` where it expects `0`.
2. Revert that file to commit 1 → the failed-candidate case passes and the **committed** case fails at `retainedGenerations: 5`. Each case pins its own path independently.
3. Revert that file and run the rollback regression → **3 passed**. Stated plainly: the repeated-failed-replacement case the review asked for is preservation coverage for the restore and committed-rejection semantics, not the pin for the leak.
4. Keep the fix but drop the retired-guard from the back-walk so it can step past a *live* predecessor → all three rollback cases fail with `expected {} to be undefined`; a staged candidate then never fences the predecessor's retained binding.

A fifth result is worth recording because it was a self-caught regression: commit 2's first draft also deleted the spliced generation's predecessor link, which destroyed the back-walk the next claim needs while `current` still points at that retired candidate. It failed the second cycle of the repeated-rollback case with `staged second candidate: expected {} to be undefined`.

### Regression coverage added

`registry-runtime.channel-ingress.rollback.test.ts` gains *"restores the same predecessor after repeated failed replacements"*: three successive stage/rollback cycles with **no traffic to the predecessor in between**, so nothing re-heads the slot history and each candidate genuinely claims behind the one before. After each rollback the originally retained binding redeems the live Gateway again, a fresh admission on the predecessor binds, and a fourth candidate that *commits* still takes the slot and rejects the predecessor's binding.

`registry-runtime.channel-ingress.slot-retention.test.ts` is new and covers both sequences above.

### Round 23 — staged-rollback slot restore

Supersession is derived from lifecycle rather than a permanent mark: a record counts as superseded only while a successor in its chain belongs to an unretired registry, so rollback hands the slot back to the exact predecessor and commit does not. The slot bookkeeping moved into `src/plugins/channel-gateway-root-slots.ts`, which returned `registry-runtime.ts` to its `origin/main` counted size. Full detail is in the round 23 comment on this PR.

### Delegated-authority expiry before final effect (round 22)

The open security ask was whether an **already-prepared** delegated operation is rejected **before it performs I/O** once its channel is unbound, retired, or replaced — with the Gateway itself still running. Round 22 measures that directly, at the production fence, with a real observable effect.

Where the fence is: `bindAgentToolGatewayRequest` captures the retained resolver, and every delegated call then passes through `bindInProcessGatewayContext` (`src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.ts:113-133`), which resolves the binding *before* `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` and throws `Gateway instance unavailable for <method>` when it yields nothing. For work that has already entered a handler, `resolveInProcessGatewayDispatch`'s `assertContextCurrent` is composed into the `sessionMutationCommitGuard` that `handleGatewayRequest` hands every handler, so a revocation that lands mid-await still fires before the handler's final write.

Both runs below drive the same chain of real production functions — `registerChannelIngressHostOwner` → `resolveStableChannelMessageIngress` → `createHostChannelInboundEventContextBuilder` (which runs `prepareHostChannelContextAdmissionEvidence`) → `finalizeInboundContext` → `initFastReplySessionState` (one of the two call sites this PR adds `copyChannelParticipantAdmissionEvidence` to) → `readChannelContextGatewayContextResolver` (exactly what `agent-runner-execution.ts:544` reads) → `withPluginRuntimeGatewayContextResolver` → `bindAgentToolGatewayRequest` → `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` → real `handleGatewayRequest` → a registered method handler whose **final effect is a real filesystem write**. Rejection "before I/O" is measured by that file's absence, not by an exception type alone.

In every scenario the channel host's own `resolveGatewayContext` keeps returning the live Gateway — only the **channel** lifetime is revoked — and a control call bound straight to a live root Gateway reaches its final effect, so each row is a channel-authority result rather than a Gateway-availability result.

| Scenario | Binding copied to sessionCtx | Operation accepted | Handler entered | Handler committed | **Final effect** | Successor Gateway redeemed | Gateway still active |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| allowed, channel live | true | true | 1 | 1 | **PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| unbound context | false | false | 0 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| retired before dispatch | true | false | 0 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| replaced before dispatch | true | false | 0 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| retired **during awaited work** | true | false | 1 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| replaced **during awaited work** | true | false | 1 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |

Rejections: `Gateway instance unavailable for sessions.list` for all four retired/replaced rows. The two mid-flight rows are the sharpest result — the handler had already started and was stopped by the production commit guard before its write.

The `unbound` row is honest about a different mechanism: with no retained binding there is no in-process delegated path to enter at all, so the call degrades to an ordinary authenticated external Gateway client (`gateway sessions.list requires credentials before opening a websocket` in an environment with no configured Gateway credentials). No in-process delegated effect occurs, but that row is *not* produced by the lifetime fence.

**Negative control.** Reverting only `prepareHostChannelContextAdmissionEvidence`'s fenced resolver back to `main`'s `state.gatewayResolverByPreparation.set(preparation, params.owner.resolveGatewayContext)` — and nothing else — flips all four retired/replaced rows from **NOT PERFORMED** to **PERFORMED**, with `handler committed` going `0 → 1` in each. The standalone run exits 1 with 16 assertion failures; the committed regression test reports `4 failed | 2 passed (6)` at `expect(fs.existsSync(effectPath)).toBe(effect)` — `expected false, received true`. The fence, not the harness, is what rejects the stale authority.

That round added `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.delegated-effect.test.ts` so the behavior stays pinned in CI. The standalone `pnpm tsx` proof that produced the table is deliberately **not** committed; it is retained with its logs alongside that round's gate output.

#### Round 22b — the real delegated apply owner

Revision 15 accepted the table above but pointed out that its handler substituted for `sessions.list` and guarded its own write, leaving the real delegated approval/application chain — which has its own authority checks — unexercised. That is a fair hit, and the chain is reachable directly.

`prepareDelegatedSystemAgentApproval` (`src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-approval.ts`) is production code, and its `isAuthorityActive` already consults `callerIdentity.gatewayContextResolver()`. `assertLiveApprovalAuthority` runs at preparation, again inside the proposal resolver, and once more through the `assertCurrent` callback the apply owner invokes immediately before its effect. The repo's existing `system-agent-approval-authority.test.ts` exercises exactly that path — but with a synthetic `() => liveContext` resolver. What was missing was the same path driven by the resolver **this PR copies into the reply session context**.

The new cases build that resolver through the same real production ingress chain, hand it to `withGatewayToolCallerIdentity` with a real claimed run authority (`claimAgentRunDelegatedAuthority`), and drive the real `prepareDelegatedSystemAgentApproval` to its apply. The channel host's own resolver keeps returning the live Gateway throughout, so only the channel lifetime can reject.

| Channel state at apply | Outcome | Apply effect |
|---|---|---|
| live | resolves `{ kind: "completed" }` | performed once |
| retired while the apply owner awaits queued work | rejects `system-agent approval authority is no longer active` | **never performed** |
| replaced while the apply owner awaits queued work | rejects `system-agent approval authority is no longer active` | **never performed** |

**Negative control on the apply owner.** With the same single-line revert, both revoked cases resolve `{ kind: 'completed' }` and the apply effect is performed:

```
× fences the delegated system-agent apply owner when the channel is retired
  → promise resolved "{ kind: 'completed', reply: { …(3) } }" instead of rejecting
× fences the delegated system-agent apply owner when the channel is replaced
  → promise resolved "{ kind: 'completed', reply: { …(3) } }" instead of rejecting
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  6 failed | 3 passed (9)
```

Without the fence, the real apply owner applies a change under expired channel authority. That is the behavior this PR prevents.

The channel-ingress setup shared by both blocks is extracted into a single `prepareChannelBoundResolver` helper rather than duplicated.

### Earlier evidence

- The session regression uses a real host-bound channel context, actual inbound finalization, `getReplyFromConfig`, and real prepared-run admission. Only the embedded runner is stubbed to inspect the admitted resolver. Live, retired, replaced, and deliberately unbound cases retain the existing owner checks.
- The retained Discord regression invokes actual `preflightDiscordMessage` and actual `buildDiscordMessageProcessContext`. Against the pre-fix implementation the injected-builder case lost its callback while the absent-builder case passed; against the current implementation both pass and processing uses exactly the context object returned by the injected builder. Because the production forwarding now comes from `main`, this test guards it against regression rather than proving a change in this diff.
- An additional diagnostic exercises the real Discord DM builder and preflight assembler with private host ownership, retaining the resolver through fast session initialization. The initial simplified session regression did not cover this earlier adapter handoff.
- **Withdrawn, not restated:** earlier revisions of this section carried a "157 focused tests pass" breakdown and a "complete five-file changed-file gate" claim. Both were measured at head `1b2ca891101a45d0ab372231f326526bd4db7006`, three commits and two `origin/main` merges back, and the branch diff is now fourteen files. Neither figure has been re-run, so both are withdrawn rather than repeated. The re-evidenced gate figures are in *Gates* below.

### Gates

Two `origin/main` merges (`5c7e0f141a81`, `671e3911b5dd`) and the round 23 commit (`e81523edf204`) landed after the figures withdrawn above were taken, and this round adds one commit on top. The earlier commands are kept only as a record of what was run then.

Round 24, at this head. Both commits were gated the same way; the figures below are commit 2's run:

```sh
# the round's own delta, staged
pnpm check:changed --staged
# focused suites at the exact staged content
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/plugins/registry-runtime.channel-ingress.slot-retention.test.ts \
  src/plugins/registry-runtime.channel-ingress.rollback.test.ts \
  src/plugins/registry-runtime.channel-ingress.test.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.delegated-effect.test.ts \
  src/channels/message-access/admission-evidence.test.ts
# exit 0 across 35 lanes; 6 shards, 8 files, 166 tests, 0 failed
# mergeability surface, with linuxbrew git 2.55
git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only upstream/main HEAD
```

The branch-wide `pnpm check:changed` run exits 1 on the **line-cap growth ratchet** only, with exactly two rows — `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` 1041 → 1043 and `src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts` 1998 → 2178. Both are reproduced byte-identically by running that lane on the clean reviewed-base tree with this round's changes stashed, so neither is introduced here; CI's `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` treats them as advisory and passed at the previous head with the same rows. Clearing them means extracting ~180 lines out of an upstream-owned test file, which would create new conflict surface in a file this branch does not otherwise own. That is left as a separate decision rather than folded into a finding fix. Because `check:changed` stops at the first failing lane, the later lanes are reported above from the `--staged` run over this round's delta.

```sh
# earlier head 1b2ca891101 — record only, not re-run
pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight-context.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.test.ts src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.test.ts src/channels/message-access/admission-evidence.test.ts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 045524c6f883ca31df7240a107872bd01f2c3378
pnpm build
```

## Related Work and Open Questions

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138596 (previously inspected at `537130294ac2e1360700ab2f094df4b8e9a8b05d`). That PR addresses authenticated CLI/subprocess and worker calls that legitimately cross the Gateway WebSocket boundary, carrying existing host-signed runtime authority. This PR preserves the original local Gateway route at the channel session handoffs. Non-overlapping file sets are not a compatibility proof.

The changes may be complementary, but we have not established that both are required or that either replaces the other. A differential comparison should exercise baseline, this fix, the related fix, and both against the same channel-origin delegation probe. The related PR is not incorporated here.

These production changes are model/runtime-agnostic. Codex enters host tool execution through a native dynamic-tool callback; the bundled Claude CLI MCP handler binds caller identity from its admitted client grant. Those entry paths differ, but no matched successful Claude call has established why the observed behavior differed. No Codex enterprise-policy restriction is demonstrated.

## Post-deployment evidence and remaining validation

On September 8, the operator restarted a real Gateway built from integration `5936dbff50dfbf81c511db450dc1a5be87482e92`, which contains this topic head. A real Discord-origin native Codex turn then invoked the delegated OpenClaw system tool for read-only Gateway status and health. That delegated read completed normally, reported the matching deployed build, and did not fail with the previously observed missing active-run authority error. No configuration, credential, service, or trust changes were made by the probe.

This is successful complete-path **read-only evidence on the combined integration**, not an isolated-topic differential comparison and not evidence of permission to perform mutations. The integration contains other authority fixes, so this observation does not establish which companion fixes are required. Note that the probe ran on September 8, before upstream #143006 landed, so at that time the Discord forwarding under test came from this branch. The probe also predates rounds 23 and 24, so it carries no evidence about the channel Gateway slot lifecycle.

### What is resolved, and what is not

Resolved: rejection before final I/O for retired and replaced channel contexts, including revocation during awaited work, with the Gateway kept active — measured both at the in-process dispatch fence against a real filesystem effect and at the **real delegated system-agent apply owner**, each bound to production by its own negative control. Restoration of the exact predecessor when a staged channel replacement fails (round 23), and a channel slot history that owns no retired generation on either the failed-candidate or the committed path (round 24, both measured 5 of 5 retained → 0 of 5).

Still outstanding:

- **Companion-fix attribution.** The September 8 deployment combined other authority fixes, so it still does not establish which companion changes are required. The differential comparison against #138596 described under *Related Work* has not been run.
- **Unbound is a different mechanism.** An unbound context performs no in-process delegated effect, but because it leaves the in-process path entirely rather than being rejected by the lifetime fence, it is reported separately above rather than folded into the fence result.
- **No booted-gateway probe for the fence rounds.** The Gateway host in rounds 22 and 22b is an in-process object held live for the run, not a booted gateway service, and round 22b's approval engine seam (`resolveOperatorApproval`) is a stub — the *authority chain* around it is production. Every step between channel ingress and the apply fence is production code; the host and that engine seam are not.
- **Merge conflicts: resolved, and re-measured.** The four-file conflict set this section used to report is gone. `gh api .../pulls/139620 --jq .mergeable` returns `true` (`mergeable_state: blocked`, on checks). Between the November 11 main this branch has merged and `upstream/main` @ `33a8ad2b90e`, exactly one file this PR touches was also changed upstream — a vitest shard-lane list, appended on both sides in different regions — and a full `--no-ff` merge of current main is clean with the topic patch byte-identical across it (*Round 25*). No rebase decision is needed.
- **CI is red at this head on an untouched file.** One shard fails at `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.attachments.test.ts:82`, which is not in this PR's diff; see the end of *Round 25*. Whether it is flaky, main-side, or interacting here is not established, and pushing the verified merge of current main is the next probe. That merge is gated but unpushed because this host's shared memory budget killed `pnpm tsgo:core:test` before it finished.

prs.title: feat: recognize personal identity across enrolled devices
prs.body:
Related: #162164

## What Problem This Solves

Approved browsers, native apps, and interactive CLI clients cannot consistently share one Gateway-local personal identity.

## User Impact

Optional enrollment associates approved operator devices with an existing or new personal profile. Identity survives credential rotation and reconnect, while device, personal, and membership permissions remain ceilings. Skipping setup preserves Shared Owner; existing devices and historical authorship are not silently reassigned. Missing or revoked personal authority requires recovery, not fallback to Shared Owner.

**Compatibility:** state schema 40→41 retains main's worker-provisioning migration; agent schema remains 42. Older incompatible readers refuse the upgraded store. Rollback requires supported backup/restore, not only replacing the package. No external account or login provider is introduced. Physical iOS/macOS acceptance for #162164 remains open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse canonical profiles, pairing workers, credentials, and policy owners across browser/CLI enrollment, native operator handoffs, WebSocket/HTTP requests, and OpenClaw ID adapters. Keep node, unattended-service, membership/root, and independent maintenance authority separate. Setup stays in existing onboarding, Profile, Devices, and QR surfaces.

## Evidence

### Current cleanup

**Head:** `131fa24a9d6defe78b3fbdaef9fd3fea8d9d07ce`. **Tree:** `46274caa23184fe8442e57f9daaf5a62c51a2940`. Integrates main `d4e80ac038cdc19ea8d15415ce5eec7db202d7eb`.

- Removed a separate bootstrap-profile worker module by reusing the enrollment validator. Consolidated actor-policy composition, sandbox policy restoration, UI permission checks, and duplicate enrollment subscriptions.
- Consolidated repeated test setup and removed weaker duplicate assertions only where retained browser or Gateway boundary tests cover the same contract. Browser, CLI, native, rotation/revocation, cross-device, and recovery functionality remains in scope.
- Fixed the review's forwarded-HTTP scope defect: both resource and scoped authorization paths now apply the existing personal-policy ceiling before admitting a request. Both regression cases failed before the fix. The binding-owner fixture omissions from the original review were repaired on an earlier revision.
- Resolved ten conflicts with current main, preserving definitions-only role catalogs as unenforced until `roles.default` is configured. Added a regression to the existing UI role-preview test and aligned onboarding. The UI regression failed before its fix. Dropped the superseded Telegram minifier-regex repair in favor of main's parser-based implementation.
- No new dependency, state owner, suppression, test allocation, or relaxed gate.

| PR snapshot | Files | Added / removed | Net lines |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Original handoff | 240 | +12,254 / −2,455 | 9,799 |
| Previous published `6f4f5bfac261` | 288 | +13,374 / −2,886 | 10,488 |
| This candidate | 286 | +13,194 / −2,908 | 10,286 |

Whole-PR source split: production (including generated source) +7,764/−2,525; tests/fixtures +4,926/−71; docs/tooling/other +504/−312. Versus the previous published head, that is −46 production and −156 test/fixture net lines.

This pass reduces the published PR by **202 net lines and two files**, but the full integrated feature remains **487 net lines larger than the original handoff**. These are whole-PR comparisons against each integrated base, not a claim that upstream merge contents are new feature work.

**Current verification (local, self-reported):**

- 133 selected core tests across 12 files, 117 focused UI tests across 11 files, and 8 mocked desktop/mobile browser enrollment/QR tests across 2 files pass. The initial core run had 108 passes and a duplicate-import parse failure; the repaired 25-test role suite then passed. After the final HTTP consolidation, all 16 affected HTTP/bootstrap tests passed again (not added to the unique count).
- Both forwarded HTTP regression cases failed before the fix and now pass. These exercise the actual authorization helpers with synthetic ingress authority, not a live hosted-ID deployment. The real isolated-Gateway owner test passed enrollment, reconnect, WebSocket/HTTP restrictions, and revocation.
- Production/UI build; core/UI production and Gateway-root test typechecks; touched-source/test lint and formatting; zero import cycles; test-line budget +4,662 with unchanged 400 allowance/4,342 feature allocation all pass. Existing advisory UI bundle warnings remain.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): preserve the causal failure when a continuation loses operator authority
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #198360. When a same-session cron continuation loses operator authority before admission, `followup-runner.ts` discarded the failure entirely: it set `completion = { kind: "aborted" }`, logged a constant message, and never propagated the causal error to the internal session-event execution. The result was that a denied continuation recorded a generic "Session event was abandoned before execution" receipt with no actionable reason — even though the original error (e.g. "original operator role changed") was available and the sibling internal-event branch already preserves it via `onFailed`.

## Solution

In the authority-loss branch of `executeFollowup` (src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts), preserve the causal failure through the existing session-event outcome:

- Call `queued.run.internalEventExecution?.onFailed?.(error)` so the cause flows into the session-event handoff's failure (the same channel the adjacent internal-event branch uses).
- Set `completion = { kind: "failed", error: formatErrorMessage(error) }` so the receipt carries the safe, actionable reason instead of a generic abandonment.
- Keep `disposition = { kind: "consumed" }` — the terminal denial and settlement-once semantics are unchanged; revoked input is never replayed or retried.
- Preserve a **distinct secondary authority refusal** too: when the post-failure authority recheck throws its own reason that differs from the original failure, both are reported — `"<original>; authority check: <authority reason>"` — with the original failure kept as the `cause`, so the receipt distinguishes which condition failed instead of hiding it (per the issue's expected behavior).

No conversation content or credentials are exposed: only the already-logged error messages are propagated.

## Evidence

- **RED → GREEN regression**: new tests in `followup-runner.test.ts` — `records the causal failure on an internal event when revoked input is denied` and `preserves a distinct secondary authority refusal alongside the original failure`. On the pre-fix code both fail (2 failed / 28 passed); with the fix all pass.
- Full file suite: `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts` — **30/30 passed** (including the new cases).
- Format: `run-format.mts --check` clean on both changed files.

Closes #198360

prs.title: fix(cli): surface failed systemd dueling-scope probe in `status --deep`
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway status --deep` on Linux could report a healthy Gateway while the systemd dueling-scope check had never run. When the deep probe threw, `findSystemdGatewayInstallation(serviceEnv).catch(() => null)` turned the failure into `null`, so the result carried neither a warning nor an error: "the probe broke" and "no dueling scope found" printed the same thing. The service-mode startup path in `gateway-cli/run.ts` swallowed the same failure.

- Problem: a failed systemd dueling-scope probe was silently dropped on both paths.
- Solution: keep the redacted probe error on the status payload, print it next to the dueling-scope warning it belongs to, and log it during service-mode startup.
- What changed: `status.gather.ts` records `gateway.duelingScopesWarningError`; `status.print.systemd.ts` renders it; `run-systemd.ts` logs it. The print/inspect code moved into sibling modules to stay inside the line-cap ratchet.
- What did NOT change: a successful probe still prints the existing dueling-scope warning; no new flags, config keys, exit codes, or extra probes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Silence is the wrong default for a diagnostic whose job is to catch a misconfigured host; this is the same silent-swallow class as #195977.

- Best fix: carry the error beside the warning it invalidates, redact at the egress boundary with `redactSupportDiagnosticLine`, and print both from one owner so `status` and startup agree.
- Alternative: rethrow and fail the whole `status` command. Rejected: status is a read-only health report, unrelated checks should still print, and the operator needs the partial result plus a named remedy.
- Risk / non-goals: the probe still only runs on Linux with a native service target (default install identity, no port override, healthy service inspection); this does not widen when it runs.

## User Impact

Operators on Linux now see `Could not inspect the systemd gateway installation: <reason> The dueling-scope diagnosis was NOT checked; run openclaw doctor for the full check.` instead of a silent gap, and the startup log names the same reason and remedy.

## Evidence

Before/after on one machine (Linux, systemd 255, Node 24.19, non-root uid 1000). The failure is real, not mocked: `/etc/systemd/system/openclaw-gateway.service` exists while the system manager does not know it, so the probe throws `ServiceInspectionError: busctl --system call: exit 1; Unit openclaw-gateway.service not loaded.` A real `openclaw gateway run` serves port 18899, then a second real `openclaw gateway run` starts in service mode and evicts it:

| Same scenario, real CLI | Before (`46350da`) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Startup evicts a stale gateway, probe throws | eviction logged, inspection failure dropped | eviction logged **and** the inspection warning |
| `gatherDaemonStatus` + real printer, probe throws | error undefined, nothing printed | error recorded, warning printed |
| `gateway status --deep`, probe succeeds | no inspection warning | unchanged: no inspection warning |
| `gateway status --deep`, probe fails mid-run | probe access denied, nothing printed | same denied access, warning printed |

```
$ OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=1 openclaw gateway run --port 18899   # 46350da
[gateway] service-mode: cleared 1 stale gateway pid(s) before bind on port 18899
```

```
$ OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=1 openclaw gateway run --port 18899   # this branch
[gateway] service-mode: cleared 1 stale gateway pid(s) before bind on port 18899
[gateway] service-mode: could not inspect the systemd gateway installation: busctl --system call: exit 1; Unit openclaw-gateway.service not loaded. busctl --system could not be inspected. The dueling-scope diagnosis was NOT checked; check read access to the reported unit and run openclaw doctor for the full check.
```

Focused tests, same test file, base source vs this branch:

```
# 46350da source, this branch's tests
× surfaces a dueling-scope inspection error when the systemd probe fails
  → expected undefined to be defined
      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 53 skipped (55)
```

```
# this branch
✓ reports dueling systemd diagnosis for its native target
✓ surfaces a dueling-scope inspection error when the systemd probe fails
      Test Files  1 passed (1)
           Tests  2 passed | 53 skipped (55)
```

The focused tests above drive the shipped `gatherDaemonStatus` and the shipped `printDaemonStatus`: only the systemd boundary is stubbed, so the collector-to-printer wiring is the real code.

`gateway status --deep` reaches its own probe only after a healthy service inspection, so a mid-run host change is what separates the two failures. Reproduced with the shipped CLI and no stubs: traversal on the user-unit directory was revoked right after the service audit's second `systemctl --user show`, and `strace` shows the deep probe's own discovery call denied 23s later, with no failed inspection in either run.

```
# identical probe syscall, 46350da and this branch
access("[redacted-home]/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service", F_OK) = -1 EACCES
```

```
$ openclaw gateway status --deep      # 46350da
Service: systemd user (enabled)
Runtime: running (pid 280115, state active, sub running, last exit 0, reason 0)
Last shutdown: gateway.stop at 2026-11-10T02:12:06.107Z
```

```
$ openclaw gateway status --deep      # this branch
Service: systemd user (enabled)
Runtime: running (pid 280115, state active, sub running, last exit 0, reason 0)
Last shutdown: gateway.stop at 2026-11-10T02:12:06.107Z
Could not inspect the systemd gateway installation: EACCES: permission denied, access [redacted-path]. The dueling-scope diagnosis was NOT checked; run openclaw doctor for the full check.
```

Per review: use the real daemon-status types instead of a narrow printer type, drop the redundant baseline test, and give the startup warning a recovery step.

prs.title: fix(state): repair private state stores after K8s fsGroup remount
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Kubernetes PVC remount with `fsGroup`, `openclaw gateway run` repairs the SQLite credential store but managed GitHub identities still fail `git push` ("Reconnect or change GitHub Identity") and Codex workers report `Worker Codex configuration directory is unsafe` — their private stores stay group-writable (`2770` dirs / `0660` files) because the startup repair only enumerated `.update-captures`, `client/credentials.sqlite`, and `control/services.sqlite`, missing `credentials/github/<scope>/<profileId>` and `codex-runtime`.

## User Impact

Users running openclaw on Kubernetes or Podman who have enrolled managed GitHub identities or Codex workers keep them after a PVC remount — no reconnect, no re-enroll. Unaffected installations see no change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend `restorePrivateStateStoreModes` to enumerate two minted-store families through their owners' naming contracts:

- **GitHub**: `credentials/github/system`, `credentials/github/personal`, and every 64-hex hashed agent key under `credentials/github/agents/<key>`, then every child matching `isManagedGitHubProfileId` (`ghp_[a-f0-9]{32}`)
- **Codex**: `<stateDir>/codex-runtime` (direct child of state root)

Each minted store is restored as a whole: directory first (descriptor-bound, `O_NOFOLLOW`, uid-match), then every regular file directly inside. `namesPlainDirectoryChainSync` refuses symlinked ancestors above the store so an alias at `credentials` or `credentials/github` cannot lend the repair to another tree.

## Review follow-up: repair owned stores without requiring unrelated ones

The previous revision bailed out entirely when the state directory contained neither `<stateDir>/.update-captures` nor an existing SQLite store, as a workaround for test fixtures that stub `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` at synthetic roots. That pre-check was wrong twice over:

- it probed `<stateDir>/.update-captures`, while the capture root is the sibling `<stateDir>.update-captures`;
- it skipped real stores whenever an unrelated one was absent, including the capture-only layout `main` already repaired.

The pre-check is gone. Every store admits itself through its own descriptor, so a state directory that holds only some stores is repaired for what it holds, and the repair makes no decision about stores it cannot see. Two regressions pin that, both with no SQLite store present: a capture root mounted alone, and minted GitHub/Codex stores mounted alone.

## Evidence

All repair paths run through `openclaw doctor --non-interactive --repair`, which invokes `ensureOpenClawStatePermissions` via `doctor-config-preflight.ts:100` and `gateway-lock.ts:531` (gateway startup path).

### Red/green on the reviewed defect

Same filesystem layouts, same code path, only `src/state/openclaw-state-db-permissions.ts` differs:

| Layout | Before (reviewed head `5cebd16`) | After (this head) |
|---|---|---|
| capture root only (no SQLite) | `2770`, not repaired | `0700`, repaired |
| GitHub profile + `codex-runtime` only (no SQLite) | `2770` / `0660`, not repaired | `0700` / `0600`, repaired |

### Driver-lane GHA upgrade proof (external repo)

Public repo `github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-privatestore-upgrade-proof`, run [42953923900](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-privatestore-upgrade-proof/actions/runs/42953923900), checked out at `42653076a7b7b3ad36e1fcc64ce1a1b138288785`. Recipe: install **latest stable** `openclaw@2026.11.3` → fixtures widened to `2770`/`0660` → driver `doctor` confirms what it can and cannot repair → tarball built from this PR head (stamped `2026.11.4`, see note) → `openclaw update` installs it over the stable driver → candidate `doctor --repair` repairs every private store → data retained.

The candidate carries the version stamp `2026.11.4` because this branch still declares `2026.11.2` in `package.json`; without a stamp above the driver's `2026.11.3`, `openclaw update` would treat the candidate as a downgrade. The stamp is the only change CI makes to the packaged tree — `dist/` and every source file come from this head.

| Fixture | Driver widens | Driver repairs | Candidate repairs | Data retained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SQLite `.update-captures/` | 2770 dir | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `client/credentials.sqlite` | 0660 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| GitHub `credentials/github/system/ghp_*` | 2770 / 0660 | ❌ (not enumerated) | ✅ | ✅ |
| GitHub `credentials/github/personal/ghp_*` | 2770 / 0660 | ❌ (not enumerated) | ✅ | ✅ |
| GitHub `credentials/github/agents/<64hex>/ghp_*` | 2770 / 0660 | ❌ (not enumerated) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Codex `codex-runtime/` | 2770 / 0660 | ❌ (not enumerated) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Capture root only, no SQLite (new) | 2770 dir | —¹ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Minted stores only, no SQLite (new) | 2770 / 0660 | —¹ | ✅ | ✅ |

¹ The two minimal layouts run against the candidate binary, after the upgrade step has replaced the driver. Both contain only the capture root / the minted stores when doctor starts; doctor then creates its own state database inside them, which is why the log later lists `client/credentials.sqlite` beside the repaired stores. The reviewed-head red check for both layouts is in the table above.

<details>
<summary>Raw proof log (trimmed to the permission checks)</summary>


prs.title: fix(agents): keep exec approval followup observation deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an async `exec_approval_followup` run completes on the gateway, OpenClaw keeps observing it for a bounded 6-minute window before deciding whether to resume the originating session. That observation window is budgeted on the wall clock (`Date.now()`) but consumed by the monotonic timer that backs the gateway `agent.wait` RPC. When the system wall clock is adjusted (NTP step, VM clock sync, or a laptop waking from hibernation), the two clocks diverge and the observation window is distorted.

- **Problem**: `waitForAgentFollowupRun` seeds `observationDeadline = Date.now() + timeout` and reads `remainingMs = deadline - Date.now()`, passing that budget into a gateway wait consumed on the monotonic clock (`performance.now()` / `setTimeout`). Budget computed in one clock domain, spent in another.
- **Solution**: align the whole observation budget to the monotonic clock — seed `observationDeadline` and read `remainingMs` / `retryDelayMs` with `performance.now()`, matching the monotonic consumer.
- **What changed**: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-followup.ts` (3 deadline reads `Date.now()`→`performance.now()`; per-wait budget rounded up with `Math.ceil` for the gateway `agent.wait` integer `timeoutMs` schema); the deadline regression test now controls the monotonic clock.
- **What did NOT change**: the transport retry/backoff policy and the observation lifecycle (reason `"deadline"`, `transportErrors` accounting) are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observation deadline is a pure process-local closure (never serialized/persisted/cross-process), so a monotonic clock is the only correct source. The gateway consumer already computes its own monotonic `DispatchDeadline`; passing it a wall-clock-derived remaining budget is a cross-clock-domain mismatch. Switching the three reads keeps the seed and every remaining-budget read on the same (monotonic) domain, zero external contract change.

- **Best fix**: yes — one canonical owner, no new parser/policy branch.
- **Alternative**: keep `Date.now()` and rely on the per-wait `Math.min` cap; rejected because the cap only bounds a single wait, not the total observation window, nor the `retryDelayMs <= 0` exit from a forward wall jump.
- **Risk**: low — `Math.ceil` on the remaining budget never shrinks the observation window and always yields an integer accepted by the gateway validator.

## User Impact

Exec approval follow-ups for async commands now complete on a stable, clock-skew-proof observation window. Under NTP/hibernation clock steps, a healthy agent run is no longer prematurely declared complete (dropping slow terminal output), and a finished run is no longer observed far beyond its deadline.

## Evidence

**1. Shipped exec-host public-entry clock-skew proof, both directions.** Driven through the exec-host **public shipped entry** `sendExecApprovalFollowupResult` (`bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`) — the exact function `exec-host-node.ts` / `exec-host-gateway.ts` call after an approved async exec. It registers the handoff, then `sendExecApprovalFollowup` runs through the **production** `GatewayRecoveryRuntime` the Gateway registers at startup — **no** `registerGatewayRecoveryRuntime` override, **no** internal-function call. Both the `agent` dispatch (production `recovery.dispatchAgent` → real in-process `agent.run`, accepted against a synthetic-provider run that stays pending) and the wait (production `recovery.waitForAgent` → shipped wait transport) are unmodified shipped code. A 30 s wall step (−30 s / +30 s) is injected inside `waitForAgentFollowupRun` via a `Date.now` proxy; a pass-through probe on `recovery.waitForAgent` records the round-1 budget handed to the wait transport. (Observation budget shortened 6 m→20 s as a disclosed control; the per-wait cap cannot mask it.)

```console
# BACKWARD (−30s rewind)
[proof] production recovery runtime present = true (Gateway auto-registered)
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=20000 -> shipped wait transport   # post-fix: BOUNDED
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=49999 -> shipped wait transport   # pre-fix: INFLATED +30s
# FORWARD (+30s jump)
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=20000 -> shipped wait transport   # post-fix: BOUNDED, observation proceeds
[proof] outcome=undefined elapsed=2652ms / NO agent.wait dispatched             # pre-fix: observation ENDED IMMEDIATELY (drops slow output)
```

| leg | skew | production-recovery budget (round 1) | window |
|---|---|---|---|
| post-fix | −30 s | 20000 | bounded |
| pre-fix | −30 s | 49999 | inflated +30 s |
| post-fix | +30 s | 20000 (proceeds) | bounded |
| pre-fix | +30 s | none (ends immediately) | drops slow output |

Keeping the budget on the monotonic clock makes the shipped wait budget immune to wall-clock steps in both directions. The accepted run stays the sole delivery owner (`direct_deliveries=0`; no competing direct delivery), and the integer `timeoutMs` passes the shipped `validateAgentWaitParams`.

**2. Integer-boundary proof (P2).** `performance.now()` is fractional; the `agent.wait` schema requires an integer `timeoutMs`. `sendExecApprovalFollowup` was driven through a recovery runtime whose `waitForAgent` re-runs the shipped validator on the exact params. Same fractional remaining budget (59999.75 ms), before vs after the one-line `Math.ceil`:

```console
before: [waitForAgent] timeoutMs=59999.75 -> shipped validator: REJECT
after : [waitForAgent] timeoutMs=60000   -> shipped validator: ACCEPT
```

`Math.ceil(59999.75) === 60000` never shrinks the budget; `Math.max(1, ...)` keeps the positive minimum.

**3. Regression.** Pre-fix the new test fails (`Number.isInteger(59999.75)` false); post-fix it passes, full suite green (18/18).

Not re-tested here: the clock divergence itself (NTP/hibernation) is injected by the proof, and the direct-delivery and session-resume paths are unchanged and covered by existing suites.

**Collision check**: `origin/main` still has the wall-clock reads (bug live); sibling PR #181942 touches the same three reads for the same defect; #181942 open.

prs.title: improve(cli): show workspace binding in sessions text output
prs.body:
Related to #181155 (this PR covers the Workspace column only; filtering & worktree metadata remain separate)

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions --json` already emits `spawnedWorkspaceDir`/`spawnedCwd`, but the default text table does not surface the workspace binding. With concurrent worktrees, a user scanning the plain `openclaw sessions` output cannot tell which session belongs to which workspace, so session ownership is effectively undiscoverable in the default view.

## Why This Change Was Made

The binding was already computed and available on the display row (`toSessionDisplayRow` exposes both `spawnedWorkspaceDir` and `spawnedCwd`), and the JSON path already projected it; the text-rendering path simply never wired it into a column. Adding the column at the text-rendering boundary is the minimal, owner-respecting fix: it consumes existing fields through the same cell-formatter pattern already used for `Key`/`Age`/`Model`/`Flags`, without a new owner or duplicated state.

The column shows the workspace directory **basename** (via `path.basename`) to keep rows narrow; sessions with no bound workspace render `-`. Managed-worktree sessions persist their binding in `spawnedCwd` and leave `spawnedWorkspaceDir` undefined, so the cell falls back to `row.spawnedWorkspaceDir ?? row.spawnedCwd`.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions` (default text output) now shows a `Workspace` column (next to `Tokens (ctx %)`, before `Flags`) with the basename of each session's spawned workspace, so operators can immediately attribute a session to its worktree across concurrent worktrees without `--json`. Sessions with no spawned workspace render `-`; JSON output is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Gap confirmed on `origin/main` (`src/commands/sessions-table.ts:21` exposes `spawnedWorkspaceDir`; the text table in `src/commands/sessions.ts` had no `Workspace` column).
- New cell formatter `formatSessionWorkspaceCell` added next to `formatSessionModelCell` (same `sanitizeTerminalText` + `theme.muted`/`theme.info` pattern).
- Column wired into the text table render in `src/commands/sessions.ts`, before the flex `Flags` column. The cell consumes `row.spawnedWorkspaceDir ?? row.spawnedCwd` so managed-worktree sessions (which persist `spawnedCwd` and clear `spawnedWorkspaceDir`) render their worktree basename.
- Test extended in `src/commands/sessions.test.ts` (`shows the spawned workspace basename in the text table`): asserts the `Workspace` header, correct basenames (`wt-181155`, `openclaw-main`), `-` for an untethered session, and a `spawnedCwd`-only managed-worktree row (`agent:main:managed`) rendering `wt-189857`.
- The existing `sanitizes persisted identifiers only for terminal output` test was made robust to the narrower `Flags` column by pinning a 240-column terminal (same pattern already used by the `aligns ... columns` test), preserving its sanitization intent.
- Validation: `run-vitest src/commands/sessions.test.ts` → 28/28 passed (incl. new managed-worktree assertion); `run-vitest src/commands/sessions-cleanup.test.ts` → 13/13 passed. Pre-fix (column read only `spawnedWorkspaceDir`, kept new assertion) → managed row failed (RED), confirming the guard.

### Real CLI render (shipped `openclaw sessions`, built from head `11b1cba`)

Real terminal output from the shipped CLI (built from this head, version `2026.10.9 (11b1cba)`) against a real persisted session store with the same producer-contract fixtures (wide PTY):

```
$ openclaw sessions --limit all
Session store: /tmp/.../openclaw-agent.sqlite
Sessions listed: 4
┌────────┬───────────────────────┬───────────┐
│ Kind   │ Key                   │ Workspace │
├────────┼───────────────────────┼───────────┤
│ direct │ agent:main:managed    │ wt-189857 │
│ direct │ agent:main:plain      │ core      │
│ direct │ agent:main:untethered │ -         │
│ direct │ agent:main:wt         │ wt-181155 │
└────────┴───────────────────────┴───────────┘
```

(The full table also carries Age/Model/Runtime/Tokens/Flags columns unchanged; excerpt focuses on the changed `Workspace` column. Workspace basenames and their parent directory are redacted to neutral labels below; each cell is still the real `path.basename` result for that row.)

Fixture mirrors the producer contract: `wt` persists `spawnedWorkspaceDir`; `managed`/`plain` persist only `spawnedCwd`; `untethered` persists neither. The Workspace column renders:
- `agent:main:managed` (`spawnedCwd=<workspaces>/wt-189857`, `spawnedWorkspaceDir` undefined) → `wt-189857`
- `agent:main:plain` (`spawnedCwd=<workspaces>/core`) → `core`
- `agent:main:untethered` → `-`
- `agent:main:wt` (`spawnedWorkspaceDir=<workspaces>/wt-181155`) → `wt-181155`

| Session row (same fixture) | Before (`origin/main`, no `Workspace` column) | After (this head `11b1cba`) |
|---|---|---|
| `agent:main:wt` — `spawnedWorkspaceDir` set | no workspace binding in the text table | `wt-181155` |
| `agent:main:managed` — `spawnedCwd` only | no workspace binding in the text table | `wt-189857` |
| `agent:main:plain` — `spawnedCwd` only | no workspace binding in the text table | `core` |
| `agent:main:untethered` — neither field | no workspace binding in the text table | `-` |

Contrast vs `origin/main` (no `Workspace` column at all): every row gains a readable workspace binding; `managed`/`plain`/`wt` show their worktree basename, `untethered` shows `-`. The fallback (`spawnedWorkspaceDir ?? spawnedCwd`) is what distinguishes `managed`/`plain` (which persist only `spawnedCwd`) from a version reading `spawnedWorkspaceDir` alone (those two would render `-`). JSON output is unchanged by this PR.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): converge NFD titles to the canonical page and preserve released identities
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

An accented memory-wiki title typed in a different Unicode normalization form than the existing page created a **second** page file, so `[[Café]]` in NFC and NFD resolved to different pages. NFC-normalizing the shared `slugifyWikiSegment` helper fixed new vaults but renamed **released** pages on upgrade, orphaning their frontmatter `id` and hand-written Notes. This revision keeps released identity bytes stable and reuses a released page by canonical equivalence: exact NFC/NFD stem, NFC-equivalent stem, or — for hash-truncated long titles — the stored frontmatter `title` as a canonical slug.

## Findings addressed

- Title-fallback reuse is limited to pages the **same producer** wrote (`pageType` / `sourceType`), so an `unsafe-local` import keeps its id, `sourceType`, and `sourcePath` when a look-alike direct ingest arrives. A page at the exact target stem is still reused — it is this writer's own.
- The fallback compares canonical slugs, not raw titles, so a long mixed-form title whose stem is hash-truncated still matches a case or normalization variant.
- The new page `id` is the title's slug; the `-<12hex>` suffix `slugifyWikiPageStem` adds for reserved stems stays a filename concern (`source.index`, not `source.index-e540cdd1328b`).

Not changed: `slugifyWikiSegment` / `slugifyWikiPageStem` output, frontmatter schema and the `id` shape, link parsing. No migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

NFC-normalizing the shared `slugifyWikiSegment` helper was the wrong owner for this fix: it repaired new vaults by rewriting the identity of pages a released version had already written, orphaning their frontmatter `id` and any hand-written Notes. Released identity bytes are the durable contract here, so this revision leaves them alone and instead makes reuse canonical-equivalence aware — exact NFC/NFD stem, NFC-equivalent stem, or, for a hash-truncated long title, the stored frontmatter `title` compared as a canonical slug.

Reuse also has to stay inside one producer. A look-alike title arriving through direct ingest must not adopt a page an `unsafe-local` import wrote, so the title fallback is limited to pages with the same `pageType` / `sourceType`; a page already sitting at the exact target stem is still reused because it is this writer's own. Comparing canonical slugs rather than raw titles is what lets a long mixed-form title match its case or normalization variant even when the stem was hash-truncated. The `-<12hex>` suffix that `slugifyWikiPageStem` adds for reserved stems stays a filename concern, so a page titled `Index` keeps the id `source.index`.

## User Impact

`[[Café]]` typed in either Unicode normalization form now resolves to the same page instead of creating a second file, and a long mixed-form title re-ingested with different casing or normalization reuses its released page rather than duplicating it. Upgrading from a released version keeps every existing page filename, frontmatter `id`, and hand-written Note: no migration, no removed files, and `openclaw wiki lint` stays at `issueCount=0`. An `unsafe-local` import keeps its own id, `sourceType`, and `sourcePath` when a look-alike direct ingest arrives. Slug output, the frontmatter schema, the `id` shape, and link parsing are unchanged, so nothing else about an existing vault moves.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI — new vault (built bundle, isolated state dir)

```console
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title $'cafe\u0301'      # NFD
  -> sources/café.md  id=source.café  created=True
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title $'caf\u00e9'       # NFC, same visual title
  -> sources/café.md  id=source.café  created=False
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title Index
  -> sources/index-e540cdd1328b.md  id=source.index
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title <long mixed-form>     -> …-9197c5785ca8.md  created=True
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title <same, UPPER + NFC>   -> …-9197c5785ca8.md  created=False
```

### Live Gateway + real model (this branch's dist)

```console
# released vault written by openclaw 2026.11.3
  synthesis page: syntheses/cafe<U+0301>.md  id: synthesis.cafe<U+0301>  sha256 8444fbfc…  487 B
  syntheses/: cafe<U+0301>.md, index.md

# isolated Gateway from this branch's dist, model glm-5.2, one agent turn
$ openclaw agent --session-id gw-proof-nfc2 -m 'call wiki_apply create_synthesis, title "café" (NFC)'
  run ok   tools: [wiki_apply, dispatch_action]   calls: 2   failures: 0
  tool result: "Updated syntheses/café.md via create_synthesis. Refreshed 3 index files."
  syntheses/: cafe<U+0301>.md, index.md   id: synthesis.cafe<U+0301>   sha256 f73e904d…  479 B
```

### Shipped CLI — synthesis, lint, cross-form backlinks

```console
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis Menu --source-id source.café --body-file body.md
  # body.md had [café](../sources/cafe<U+0301>.md) and [[cafe<U+0301>]] in decomposed form
  -> syntheses/menu.md  id=synthesis.menu
  menu Related -> Sources: ../sources/café.md
  café Related -> Referenced By: ../syntheses/menu.md
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis Index --source-id source.café
  -> syntheses/index-e540cdd1328b.md  id=synthesis.index
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis $'cafe\u0301' --source-id source.café
  -> syntheses/café.md  id=synthesis.café        # reuses the NFC synthesis page
$ openclaw wiki lint                               -> issueCount=0
```

### Upgrade from released 2026.11.3 (same state dir, same database)

```console
# vault + state written by openclaw 2026.11.3 (npm stable, unfixed); 21 files
  page: sources/cafe<U+0301>.md   id: source.cafe<U+0301>   synthesis: syntheses/menu.md
  hand-written Notes: "UPGRADE NOTE MUST SURVIVE"
# head CLI on that state dir, documented update path first
$ openclaw doctor --fix
  Doctor: database migrations ... pre-migration SQLite backup kept
$ openclaw wiki ingest note.txt --title $'caf\u00e9'
  -> created=False  pagePath=sources/cafe<U+0301>.md  id=source.cafe<U+0301>
  same released page: True   same id: True   Notes preserved: True
  sources/: [sources/cafe<U+0301>.md, sources/index.md]   files removed: []   lint issueCount: 0
```

### Regression runs

```console
# this PR's tests on origin/main (base): 5 failed | 10 passed (15)
  × NFD convergence   × released decomposed reuse   × released mixed-form reuse
  × released hash-truncated NFD reuse   × long mixed-form uppercase reuse
# this PR's tests at the previous head f44f987: 4 failed | 14 passed (18)
  × long mixed-form uppercase reuse   × imported page kept out of ingest reuse
  × synthesis/source id for a title "Index": 'source.index-e540cdd1328b' != 'source.index'
# this commit: 8 test files, 109 tests passed
```

### Before / after

| Scenario (real behavior) | previous head `f44f987` | this commit `c539ab5` |
|---|---|---|
| Released decomposed page re-ingested in NFC | reused (`created: false`) | reused (`created: false`) |
| Released long mixed-form page (`…-9197c5785ca8`) re-ingested as UPPER + NFC | **duplicate page** (`created: true`) | reused (`created: false`) |
| Direct ingest of a title an `unsafe-local` import already owns | **import adopted**: id, `sourceType`, `sourcePath` rewritten | separate page; the import keeps its id and provenance |
| File titled `Index` -> page id | `source.index-e540cdd1328b` (CI red) | `source.index` |
| Released slug bytes and frontmatter `id` shape | unchanged | unchanged |

Checks: `oxlint` 0/0 on the five changed files; `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean; `tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json` reports nothing in `extensions/memory-wiki` (tsgo cannot run in this symlinked worktree; CI's shard is the authority).

## Not tested

The vault has no UI surface (`openclaw.plugin.json` declares only an id and the plugin registers no Control UI view), so there is no screenshot evidence to capture. macOS/iOS paste normalization is Unicode semantics, not reproduced here: this host is Linux/KVM with no macOS environment.

prs.title: fix: adopt recovery controllers after native schema crossings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes controller adoption refusing a retained native-update `ROLLBACK_FAILED` journal after a schema crossing, even when its candidate is selected and serving. The held-store recovery fix in #198303 could not be adopted through that transaction's existing historical-successor path.

## User Impact

Operators can adopt the reviewed complete controller closure and run canonical `--recover`. Successful full acceptance retires the activation journal without a Gateway restart. Held stores remain archived, and the original witness, native backup/receipt and old controller closure remain retained. Adoption does not deploy a new Gateway release. Canonical recovery's existing rollback behavior on failed acceptance is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing adoption owner now accepts an explicit `nativeRecovery` binding only for a completed, nondecreasing schema-crossing native migration in `ROLLBACK_FAILED`. The exact source descriptor binds the journal, candidate and schema pair; additional fields bind the migrated receipt, backup-directory identity and serving process through the existing native custody owner. Historical adoption still archives and installs all four files, including a changed shell. Same-schema adoption and non-retained recovery retain their existing paths.

No SQLite schema, configuration or cache is added. `--prepare-retained-repair` remains a separate operation for building a distinct same-schema repair release.
