prs.title: fix(imessage): preserve literal trailing-space in configured cliPath/dbPath
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A configured iMessage `cliPath` or `dbPath` ending in whitespace was silently rewritten to a *different* path before use. macOS allows trailing spaces in file and directory names, so these are legitimate literal values, and the rewritten spelling is usually another real file: OpenClaw could run the wrong `imsg`, read the wrong `chat.db`, and — through the trimmed remote-host cache key — SSH-stage an attachment to one Mac while executing the RPC on another.

- Problem: the extension applied `.trim()` to configured paths at ~20 call sites, conflating "is this configured?" with "normalize this value".
- Problem, second layer: the plugin-state store trims every entry key, so the recovery cursor for a literal `chat.db ` collapsed onto its trimmed spelling and inherited a high-water measured on a different database — the exact cross-database suppression the cursor identity exists to prevent.
- Solution: blank detection now uses the SDK owner `readNonBlankString`, which returns the original bytes. Path *resolution* keeps `resolveUserPath`'s contract — `OPENCLAW_HOME` first, result absolute — through `resolveIMessageLiteralPath`, without trimming. Cursor keys hash the `(accountId, dbIdentity)` pair, so a literal identity keeps its own slot instead of collapsing onto its trimmed spelling.
- What changed: every configured-path decision point migrated together — `cli-path.ts`, `client.ts`, `send.ts`, `accounts.ts`, `probe.ts`, `actions.ts`, `chat.ts`, `channel.ts`/`channel.runtime.ts`, `setup-core.ts`, `private-api-status.ts`, `message-tool-api.ts`, `approval-handler.runtime.ts`, `cli-output.ts`, `monitor/recovery-cursor.ts`, `monitor/remote-host.ts`. Home-tilde expansion moved to a dependency-free `user-path.ts` because a bare `node` child imports it.
- What did NOT change: business normalizations that are not path identity — `HOME` lookup, shebang/echo matching, configured `remoteHost` validation — keep trimming.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner per responsibility: "blank vs. literal" belongs to the SDK string-coercion owner, not a locally invented helper. An earlier revision of this PR added a private `readLiteralPath` that was byte-identical to `readNonBlankString`; it is deleted, so there is no second implementation to drift.

The cursor key is the `#184862` digest of `JSON.stringify([accountId, dbIdentity])`, which carries the literal bytes: an identity ending in whitespace gets its own slot instead of inheriting the high-water of its trimmed neighbour. The pre-`#184862` NUL-composite key is still adopted when read, so no operator's stored cursor moves on upgrade. (Rebased onto current main, which redesigned these keys; this branch's earlier quoting is superseded.)

Also fixed a regression this PR introduced: `send.ts` stopped capturing `shouldClose` and re-read `opts.client` in `finally`, so a mid-request options mutation could close a borrowed client. The captured flag is restored and covered by the existing custody tests.

Risk / non-goals: the local `dbPath` no longer goes through `resolveUserPath`'s trimming step; `~` expansion, the required-home cwd fallback, and absolute resolution are preserved, all pinned by tests.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a literal trailing-space `cliPath`/`dbPath` get exactly the binary and database they wrote, on the host the wrapper names. Fully-blank values are still treated as unset, so empty or absent config behaves as before. No config migration, no new option, no public SDK export, no lockfile change. A literal database that used to share a cursor row with its trimmed neighbour now keeps its own, so a high-water from the other file can no longer silence it.

## Evidence

Two real `sshd` instances on loopback (`mac-a`, `mac-b`), real `ssh`/`scp` behind wrappers that name one host each, a fake `imsg` that logs the exact bytes of its `argv` and every `--db`, a trimmed neighbour binary that must never run, and an isolated Gateway per tree. The `local` account uses the literal `cliPath`/`dbPath`, the `remote` account a literal wrapper plus a literal remote `dbPath`, the `plain` account ordinary paths.

This head (`a09ad07`), media uploaded through the production staging path:

```console
sshd sessions: mac-b=14  mac-a=0
staged on mac-b: sha256 77db3976… == source 77db3976…
--db seen by the child: [chat.db ]   (trailing space intact)
cursor: literal db -> no since_rowid   ordinary db -> since_rowid 777
```

Same harness on `HEAD^`, the tree the shipped channel is built from (2026.10.8 ships this channel as `@openclaw/imessage`, not bundled):

```console
sshd sessions: mac-a=15  mac-b=0
staged on mac-a: sha256 77db3976…   (the upload hit the wrong Mac)
trimmed neighbour binary executed: yes
cursor: literal db -> since_rowid 888   (the trimmed neighbour's high-water)
```

Upgrade: a state dir created by `openclaw@2026.10.8`, then booted by this head — stored config bytes unchanged (same sha256), the cursor row for an unchanged identity still honoured (`since_rowid 777`), both stored rows still present, and the old trimmed-spelling row no longer reaching the literal database.

### Upgrade from latest stable `v2026.10.10` (Linux/Docker, real Gateway, real `spawn()`)

The reviewer asked for the latest-stable line explicitly. This harness boots the actual `openclaw@2026.10.10` binary on the same state lineage and then this head; the only fake is `imsg` (a Linux container has no Messages host), which records the byte-exact `argv` the product hands it and answers the JSON-RPC protocol.

```console
phase A  2026.10.10  plain + neighbour  -> store: plain\0…=777, neighbour\0…=888
phase B  2026.10.10  literal account    -> self 15 B, --db 17 B, since_rowid 888   (bug reproduced)
phase C  head a09ad07 literal + plain   -> self 16 B, --db 18 B, since_rowid 700 / 777
```

| check | 2026.10.10 | head `a09ad07` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw.json` sha256, before → after the Gateway boot | — | `bb0596aa…` → `bb0596aa…` (byte-identical) |
| `cliPath` handed to `spawn` | `/proof/bin/imsg` (15 B) | `/proof/bin/imsg ` (16 B) |
| `--db` handed to `spawn` | `/proof/db/chat.db` (17 B) | `/proof/db/chat.db ` (18 B, base64 ends `ZGIg`) |
| `since_rowid`, literal account | 888 — inherited from the trimmed neighbour | 700 — its own database watermark |
| `since_rowid`, unchanged account | 777 | 777 — pre-upgrade progress kept |

Stored rows after the head boot, each digest re-derived from the implementation's key material rather than read back from a claim:

```text
"8517ca3ecd5d57d1a3d3c65aa9c68581" = sha256(["plain","local:/proof/db/plain.db"]).slice(0,32)   -> 777   legacy row adopted
"527ad9701aae68ccf95da378dbe8359e" = sha256(["literal","local:/proof/db/chat.db "]).slice(0,32) -> 700   literal identity gets its own slot
"neighbour\0local:/proof/db/chat.db" -> 888                                                        legacy row untouched
"literal\0local:/proof/db/chat.db"   -> 888                                                        written by the buggy release, now unreachable
```

So the upgrade keeps every stored row it must keep, adopts legacy rows whose identity still resolves to the same database, and stops the literal account from seeding `since_rowid` out of its trimmed neighbour.

One operational note found while building this: when the state directory still holds the externally installed `@openclaw/imessage` from the old release, the plugin loader prefers it over the in-repo channel, so the trimmed behaviour survives the CLI upgrade until that install is removed or updated. The harness removes it before measuring — an upgrade step, not a code change here.

### Upgrade from current stable `v2026.11.1` (hashed recovery keys, Linux, real Gateway)

The previous review asked for this line explicitly: v2026.11.1 already writes hashed recovery keys (`sha256(JSON.stringify([accountId, dbIdentity]))[:32]`), so the seed writes hashed keys the way v2026.11.1 did — proving an ordinary hashed cursor survives the upgrade and a literal database is isolated from its trimmed neighbour. The harness boots `openclaw@2026.11.1` (node ≥ 24.22.1) to create the state lineage, seeds hashed-cursor rows plus their legacy NUL-composite counterparts, then boots this head on the same state dir.

```console
phase A  v2026.11.1  gateway ready, imessage channel unavailable (Linux, expected)
phase B  seed        hashed: plain -> 777, local(trimmed) -> 888   + NUL legacy rows
phase C  head a09ad07  channel init on same state dir:
           imsg-plain  watch.subscribe  since_rowid 777   (ordinary hashed cursor honoured)
           imsg-literal watch.subscribe  no since_rowid     (literal db isolated, own fence)
```

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| `openclaw.json` sha256, seed → after head boot | `4e97af09…` → `4e97af09…` (byte-identical, config unchanged) |
| ordinary hashed cursor (plain, no whitespace) | `since_rowid 777` — v2026.11.1 hashed key read back correctly |
| literal database (trailing-space `chat.db `) | no `since_rowid` — does not inherit the trimmed neighbour's 888 |
| literal `--db` reached child | `chat.db ` with trailing space intact (18 B) |
| stored rows after upgrade | all 4 survive: 2 hashed (`8372136a…`=777, `54bb190d…`=888) + 2 NUL legacy |

The key insight: v2026.11.1 and this head use the **same hash algorithm** (`sha256(JSON.stringify([accountId, dbIdentity]))[:32]`). For ordinary paths (no whitespace), trimmed == literal, so the hashed key is identical and the cursor is inherited unchanged. For a literal path with trailing space, v2026.11.1 trimmed it before hashing; this head keeps the literal bytes, producing a different hash — so the literal database correctly gets its own cursor slot instead of inheriting the trimmed neighbour's high-water. The adopt path cannot bridge this gap (it re-derives the NUL key from the current literal dbIdentity, which never matches the trimmed NUL key v2026.11.1 wrote), which is the intended isolation: a literal database must not silently consume a high-water measured on a different file. Existing data still loads and works — every stored row is preserved and readable.

Reproduce: `bash proof3.sh setup && bash proof3.sh stable && bash proof3.sh seed && bash proof3.sh candidate && bash proof3.sh verify` (node ≥ 24.22.1 for the v2026.11.1 binary).

Reproduce: `./run.sh` (single command, ~12 min, Docker + node ≥ 22) regenerates the tables above and fails on any assertion. The macOS-only surface (real `imsg`, Full Disk Access, SSH wrapper transport) is covered by the loopback evidence above, not by this Docker lane.

Unit suites — green with the fix, and both guards red on the base:

```console
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-imessage.config.ts
 Test Files  38 passed (38)
      Tests  352 passed (352)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts recovery-cursor
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

That cursor case and the cache case are the regression guards. On `HEAD^` the cursor readback fails with `expected 888 to be 777` — the literal database inherited the high-water of its trimmed neighbour — and the cache readback fails with `expected { trimmed: true } to deeply equal { literal: true }` because both spellings shared one entry. Other new cases: a literal-vs-trimmed `it.each` for database lookup plus blank-as-unset, an attested-binary resolve returning the literal path, a spawn assertion that the literal `cliPath` and `--db` reach the child, a remote-host case separating two wrappers by SSH destination, a CLI-output assertion that the literal `--db` bytes reach `imsg`, and a spawn-boundary case for the cwd fallback — the parent leaves `~` in place (`/srv/gateway/~/Library/Messages/chat.db`).

## Rebased Onto Current Main

The branch was rebased onto `main` and the resulting conflicts resolved; the PR is a single commit on top of current `main`, so the merge is clean. Where `main` had moved on, `main`'s newer owner won and this branch's overlapping mechanism was dropped:

- `monitor/recovery-cursor.ts` — keeps `main`'s `#184862` digest keys plus the legacy NUL-key adoption, and this branch's `readNonBlankString` path identity. The earlier whitespace-quoting encoding is gone because the digest already carries literal bytes.
- `client.ts` — combines this branch's literal-path resolution with `main`'s `remoteHost` plumbing.
- `cli-path.ts` / new `user-path.ts` — `resolveIMessageHomeDir` and `expandIMessageUserPath` now live in `user-path.ts` (a bare `node` child imports it); `cli-path.ts` re-exports them.
- `send.ts` — keeps this branch's `readNonBlankString` path semantics. The formatter splits the added import across three lines, so the file offset that growth with equivalent consolidations (one `stringValue`-based blank check replacing a hand-rolled `typeof`/`trim()` ternary, and grouped declarations) to keep the line-cap ratchet flat. No behavior change. A second rebase followed `main` extracting `sendMessageIMessageForAccount` (inner) plus the `withIMessageSendFailureStatus` wrapper; the literal-path resolution moved into the new inner function and the `readNonBlankString` semantics survived the split.

Verification on this head (`a09ad07`, rebased onto `main`):

```console
$ node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --base origin/main
Line-cap ratchet OK: 23 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.

$ pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main --no-merge-base
Test lines OK: 6535873; ceiling: 6535908; slack: 35.
This PR's +127 net delta is fully covered by its allocation (`config/test-lines-allocations/imessage-literal-trailing-space-paths.txt` = 127), so it contributes zero over-by of its own.

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-imessage.config.ts
 Test Files  1 failed | 37 passed (38)
      Tests  1 failed | 356 passed (357)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts recovery-cursor
 Test Files  1 passed | 1 skipped (2)
      Tests  5 passed | 1 skipped (6)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts
 Tests  37 passed (37)
```

The new `it.each` literal-vs-trimmed pairs add 127 test lines; `config/test-lines-allocations/imessage-literal-trailing-space-paths.txt` records exactly that share, so the repository-wide test-line ceiling is unchanged for everyone else.

`oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on all 23 changed files. The single remaining imessage failure is `status.test.ts` expecting the English `iMessage: needs setup` while this shell's `zh_CN` locale renders the localized Chinese form of that same status; it reproduces on unmodified `main` in the same shell (locale-dependent), so it is not from this branch.

prs.title: fix(daemon): use monotonic clock for scheduled task settlement deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, stopping or updating the Gateway can hang or bail out early when the system clock is adjusted: the scheduled-task settlement probe computes its deadline and remaining budget from `Date.now()` (wall clock) while the PowerShell probe's `spawnSync` timeout and the poll `sleep` are monotonic timers. A clock jump forward shrinks the probe timeout (a 280s budget collapsed to 50s, or 1ms past a 330s roll), killing PowerShell before settlement can be observed; a clock jump backward keeps the wall-clock deadline from ever elapsing, so the loop never exits. The fix uses a monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) for the deadline and remaining budget, matching the sibling `isScheduledTaskDefinitionAbsent` in the same file.

- Problem: `prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` seeds its deadline and reads the remaining budget from the wall clock (`Date.now()`), while the consuming `spawnSync` timeout and `sleep` poll are monotonic timers — a cross-clock-domain budget.
- Solution: compute `deadline`, `remaining`, and the exit comparisons with `performance.now()` so the budget lives entirely on the monotonic clock.
- What changed: all six `Date.now()` usages inside `prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` in `src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.ts` became `performance.now()`, plus a new regression test and an update to the existing settlement test's clock mock.
- What did NOT change: the caller contract (`stopScheduledTask` / `restartScheduledTask`), the settlement result shape, and the default timeout constants all remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` is the only cross-clock-domain spot left in this file: its sibling `isScheduledTaskDefinitionAbsent` already computes `remainingTimeout()` and `expired()` from `performance.now()`, and the file's other deadline helpers use `performance.now()` too. The settlement deadline is a purely process-internal closure variable — never serialized, persisted, or compared across processes — so a full switch to the monotonic clock is safe and keeps the budget aligned with the monotonic timers that consume it. No new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface is introduced. The existing `schtasks.settlement.test.ts` clock mock was moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` while preserving the test's intent (settlement exhausts the full stop budget without a false restart).

## User Impact

Windows Gateway stop/update no longer stalls or fails spuriously when the system clock is adjusted (NTP resync, manual set, DST), because the settlement deadline is no longer skewed by wall-clock jumps. The settlement still waits the full configured stop budget before declaring the task unavailable, and still refuses a restart only when settlement genuinely cannot be confirmed.

## Evidence

**Real shipped command, real runner (before/after)**: a `windows-latest` runner installs a real Scheduled-Task Gateway (`openclaw gateway install`), then runs the actual shipped `openclaw gateway stop --force` while a preload steps the wall clock (`Date.now()`; `performance.now()` stays monotonic) between the settlement deadline seed and budget read — exactly the NTP/manual-set/DST incident. Both builds drive the real `schtasks.exe`/PowerShell subprocess; the only difference is the clock source of the settlement deadline (`Date.now()` pre-fix vs `performance.now()` post-fix):

| wall-clock jump | pre-fix (Date.now deadline) | post-fix (performance.now deadline) |
|---|---|---|
| +280s (forward, in-roll) | `openclaw gateway stop` ok (50s budget) | ok (full 60s budget) |
| +380s (forward, past roll) | **stop FAILS** (1ms budget → settlement unavailable → unverified) | ok (full 60s budget, inert) |
| -280s (backward) | ok (inflated budget, over-waits) | ok (inert) |

Proof artifact + workflow: `SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof` [run #40486854535](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof/actions/runs/40486854535).

**Raw CLI output (inline, current head `e804ccc7dcd`)** — verbatim, redacted to service/port only (no IPs, keys, endpoints):

```console
$ # post-fix (performance.now deadline): clock +280s between deadline seed and budget read
$ openclaw gateway stop --force --json
stop exit=0 elapsed=6.4801074s
{ "action": "stop", "ok": true, "result": "stopped",
  "service": { "label": "Scheduled Task", "loaded": true, "loadedText": "registered" } }
[proof-inject] settlement Date.now reads stepped: 5   # wall clock jumped, deadline monotonic -> inert
VERDICT[post-fix-forward]: STOPPED bounded completion in 6.4801074s

$ # pre-fix (Date.now deadline): same command, clock +380s (past the 330s roll) collapses remaining to 1ms
$ openclaw gateway stop --force --json
stop exit=1 elapsed=4.443505s
{ "action": "stop", "ok": false,
  "error": "Gateway stop failed: Error: Task settlement unavailable; stop unverified.",
  "hints": ["Run openclaw gateway status --deep to inspect the service, then retry."] }
VERDICT[pre-fix-forward-380]: STOP_REFUSED exit=1
```

Under the same wall-clock jump the pre-fix build fails the very `openclaw gateway stop` that succeeds on the post-fix build: the collapsed 1ms budget times out the real PowerShell probe, settlement reports `unavailable`, and `terminate()` refuses to confirm the stop. The backward jump is equally inert post-fix (`stop exit=0 elapsed=5.41s`).

**Unit regression (forward wall-clock skew)**, pre-fix RED / post-fix GREEN:

```console
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts   # pre-fix (reverted to Date.now)
AssertionError: expected 50000 to be 60000   (280000 ms)
AssertionError: expected 1 to be 60000        (380000 ms)
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts   # post-fix (monotonic)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  18 passed (18)
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks.settlement.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  37 passed (37)
```

Full daemon shard: 118 files / 1943 tests passed.

Beyond the clock budget, the settlement state machine and its JSON parsing are not re-tested here: they are covered by the existing 37-test settlement suite (unchanged apart from its clock-mock alignment).

**Open PR collision check**: no open PR touches `schtasks-state-probe.ts` / `schtasks.settlement.test.ts` (searched open PR topics `settlement`/`schtasks`/`monotonic clock` and changed-file lists).

Per review: added a real-Windows proof (forward + backward clock steps, before/after table) and fixed the new regression test's floating-promise lint by returning the `withMockedPlatform` promise from the test callback (CI `check-lint-core-2`).

prs.title: fix(workers): verify prepared projects before image capture
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prepared project images can retain obsolete Git seeds and manifests, and capture can proceed without verifying the prepared project, including stale manifest memos after a repository refresh.

## User Impact

Crabbox verifies and normalizes the project after preparation/scrubbing and before capture. Cleanup covers machine HOME and prepared HOME, preserves completion/current artifacts, and refuses unsafe entries before deleting anything. Teardown cannot initiate a fresh unverified project checkpoint. Failure diagnostics identify a bounded check/cache kind and rebuild action without paths/output. Ordinary enrolled-workspace inspection remains read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing source-preparation and runtime/capture owners with a host-bound snapshot capability and one complete multi-root removal plan. Validation precedes all deletion, within the existing lifetime budget. Fresh capture admission is guarded after existing-operation handling, preserving retained recovery/warnings and normal non-project teardown. No new manager, state store or schema; no old Azure SDK snapshot backend, external verifier settings or image-generation receipts. Worker-code reuse remains a separate independent lane.

## Evidence

### Exact-head status and required acceptance

Head **`36d1357b9ecec790a887956e6d6b3385d52b96ba`**, tree `1690c8861c9ac8036ba3494a2c68d69f2169716d`, was published on13 Nov through the native signed **source-for-proof** route. Its ordered parents are prior hosted `24f888eacd2b046e88ec5e0f8697c0de0436c035` and captured official main `a48a3175600e3cad5554128a4cf0012c4e65d9ad`; history was not rewritten. The remotely fetched commit/tree, all22 scoped paths and blobs, signature, and exact Galin/Vyctor coauthor trailers match the reviewed candidate. PR author remains @galiniliev. prs.title: fix: node directory listing pages until the gateway stops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node directory listing stops after 32 pages so one oversized directory cannot pin the gateway. Bootstrap discovery used that stop to skip the directory, then still loaded a sibling, but it recorded no diagnostic. A configured `*/AGENTS.md` file inside the oversized directory disappeared with `diagnostics: []`.

## Evidence

Head `b06896ea3a7` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1. The production trace below was run on `055d09e2943`. `b06896ea3a7` merges current main and adds the 112-line test grant. It does not change the listing or the diagnostic. A real directory held 131073 empty names, which is one past 32 pages of 4096. Its sibling `keep/AGENTS.md` contained `kept instructions`. Production `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` listed that tree. Each `dir.list` call went to production `handleDirList` on that directory, not a scripted page payload. `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` then loaded `*/AGENTS.md`.

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 stat=0 fetch=1
```

`dir.list` ran 34 times: one page for the root, 32 pages for the oversized directory, and one page for the sibling. `file.fetch` read the sibling once. The oversized directory is named in the diagnostic and its instructions were not loaded.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bootstrap discovery skips one directory after the real 32-page listing cap, records that skip, and still loads a sibling `AGENTS.md`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, head `055d09e2943` in `/tmp/oc-165805`, then merged forward as `b06896ea3a7` without changing the listing or the diagnostic. The directory was a local folder with 131073 names. The node command handler and the gateway bridge ran in one process.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Created the oversized directory and `keep/AGENTS.md`. Called `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` with `invoke` dispatching to `handleDirList`, `handleFileStat`, and `handleFileFetch`. Called `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` for `*/AGENTS.md`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that production path:

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 fetch=1
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The sibling file was loaded. The oversized directory produced one `io` diagnostic, `Directory listing exceeded 32 pages`, after 32 real listing pages.
- **What was not tested:** A second OS process enrolled as a node over the gateway websocket. The same handlers ran in-process.

## Summary

A directory past the listing page budget is still skipped, and its sibling still loads. The skip is now a diagnostic instead of a silent omission.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): bound the sandbox scp transfer with a deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sandbox media staging shells out to `scp`, and that spawn had **no deadline**: a hung transfer (dead peer, wedged ssh, a dropped TCP session that never resets) left the child process alive indefinitely and the caller awaiting a promise that never settles — one leaked `scp` per stalled staging attempt, with no bound on how long the turn could hang.

This gives the transfer a bounded deadline **through the shared process-lifecycle runner rather than by owning the spawn directly**, which is the direction #98141 was closed toward: that PR was closed as "superseded by the current process-lifecycle architecture, not because the linked defect is fixed" — so the timeout belongs on the existing runner call, not on a locally-owned `child_process.spawn`.

## Evidence

The change is two files:

```
src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts          |  8 +-
src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts | 101 ++++++++++++++++++-
```

- `stage-sandbox-media.ts` derives the per-transfer budget (`resolveScpTransferTimeoutMs()`: size cap / supported throughput, 30s floor, `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX_SCP_TIMEOUT_MS` override) and passes it as `timeoutMs` on the existing shared-runner invocation — the runner already owns deadlines and descendant-tree termination.
- The test suite asserts the deadline reaches the runner (`expect.objectContaining({ timeoutMs: SCP_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_MS })`) so the wiring cannot silently regress, and adds a real-process hang case: a fake `scp` on `PATH` that spawns a descendant, ignores `SIGTERM`, and never exits. The assertion is that the transfer is rejected by the deadline and **both the parent and the descendant are gone afterwards** (via the repo's existing `test-utils/process-tree` helpers), plus a negative control that a normal transfer still succeeds unchanged.

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  13 passed | 2 skipped (15)
```

## Verification

The deadline wiring and the normal-transfer assertions run and pass here; the two skipped cases are the POSIX-only hang cases (`it.runIf(process.platform !== "win32")`) — this machine is Windows, so the process-tree termination assertion itself is **not exercised locally**. I am stating that rather than implying it: it needs a POSIX CI lane to run, and that is the one part of this change I could not observe directly.

Partial fix for #98468: the deadline wiring, the revised budget, and real timeout recovery (process tree + temporary cleanup) are verified here; the remaining unobserved part is a real multi-hour suspend/transfer scenario on a POSIX lane, which CI's Linux lane runs via the committed cases.

## Context worth knowing before review

- Three prior attempts exist on this issue: #98141 (closed as superseded by the lifecycle architecture — see above), #101473 (long review loop, closed), #132552 (merged, but that was the *cancellation* half of staging, not the transfer deadline).
- The issue currently also carries `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`. If the automated fix lane produces a PR for the same deadline, take that one — the intent here is to have the fix available in the architecture the maintainer pointed at, not to race a bot.

## Revision 2 — revised transfer budget + real transport proof (head `8707115c920`)

**Decision answer (the question the review asked): revise the deadline instead of an unconditional 30s cutoff.**
`resolveScpTransferTimeoutMs()` derives the per-transfer budget from the size cap and the slowest throughput still called supported, keeps it bounded, and is overridable:

| Case | Budget |
|---|---|
| 50 MiB cap at the 256 KiB/s supported floor | **200s** |
| review example: 40 MiB at 1 MiB/s (~40s) | **160s** (the old fixed 30s could never allow it) |
| small transfers | 30s floor |
| `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX_SCP_TIMEOUT_MS` | operator override (tests use it to reach the deadline in seconds) |

The deadline remains an absolute, bounded value owned by the shared runner, so an unattended hang still dies; it just no longer kills a slow-but-healthy copy. A deadline kill is also no longer retried (one bounded wait instead of three): retrying a copy that stopped progressing only re-waits the whole budget. If maintainers want a different number, or a config field instead of the env override, name it and I'll switch it.

### Real behavior proof (no mocks: real spawned transport through staging, Windows)

A compiled stand-in transport is spawned through the same argv/PATH path the runner uses, so the real spawn, deadline, tree kill, and temp cleanup all execute:

```
[proof] slow transfer staged=1 elapsed=7965ms
[proof] staged bytes=real transport bytes
[proof] hung transport pid=22892 alive=true
[proof] descendant pid=54128 alive=true
[proof] reaped by deadline: parent=true descendant=true
[proof] surface={"value":{"staged":{}}}
[proof] attempts="attempt\n"
[proof] temp dir removed=true
 ✓ windows real transport proof > publishes a real slow transport that finishes inside the budget 8044ms
 ✓ windows real transport proof > kills a real hung transport tree on the deadline without retrying 8507ms
```

Both Windows-native cases pass (17 passed | 3 skipped with the scratch cases in place) and the same file without them is **15 passed | 3 skipped, exit 0**; `oxfmt --check` clean on both files. The three skips are the POSIX-gated cases (they spawn a shebang script), which is why the Windows run above uses a compiled stand-in. `oxlint` produced no verdict for explicit paths in this junction worktree, so I am not claiming a lint verdict — CI's lint lane judges.

The new committed cases: the derived-budget unit math (including the 40 MiB / 160s case), a real slow transfer that publishes, and the hung tree + descendant reaped on the deadline with one attempt and the temp dir removed.

prs.title: feat(ui): save per-agent model favorites in the chat picker
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Large model catalogs need a personal shortlist that can be edited while choosing a model. ## User Impact Click the star to add or remove a favorite without selecting a model or closing the picker. Favorites belong to the signed-in profile and agent, persist through existing user preferences, and do not change model availability or selection policy. A favorite identifies the model across runtime choices. Older model/runtime entries are read without losing saved models and normalized on the next write. Default and the current model stay ahead of favorites; ordering remains stable while the picker is open and updates on reopen. The Favorites rail entry appears when the current catalog contains a saved favorite and more than one provider. A favorite temporarily absent from the catalog stays saved without leaving an empty Favorites tab. Desktop stars appear on hover/focus or when selected; phone stars remain visible at the row end. ## Why This Change Was Made This is the final layer after #192135, #192137, #192142, and #192145. The existing preference owner handles conditional writes and invalidation; the picker owns presentation, keyboard navigation, and bounded rendering. ## Evidence - Desktop and phone source-UI flows passed for starring without model selection, close/reopen, and reload. Desktop additionally verified agent isolation and independent authenticated-profile contexts. Failed reads recover through Retry; conflicting writes reconcile to authoritative favorites without dropping them. - During four search-query changes, observed preference RPC totals stayed at **7 → 7 reads** and **2 → 2 writes** in both viewports. There were **0 model-selection requests**. This measures query updates, not a claim of zero reads across every open or reconnect. - The UI runs against the official mock Gateway preference owner. These results do not prove database durability or live authenticated Gateway behavior. Same-document profile changes are covered by unit tests only; the incomplete captured-hello replay is not product evidence. - Matching dark captures below compare the parent cooldown implementation with the final favorites candidate at the same viewport and synthetic conversation. Finite transitions were settled before capture. No inference, real credentials, or physical mobile device was used. - The focused test set covered 88 cases through the initial run and targeted repair replays; 11 E2E cases passed. UI/test types, lint, formatting, stylelint, locale validation, and the test-line budget passed. The final independent review found no actionable issues. - A final shared-consumer pass repaired five existing tests that still assumed model rows were native buttons. prs.title: fix: keep restored chat model labels readable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a fitting chat model name can become truncated in WebKit after the composer transitions from saved model metadata to a live runtime label and back to the same saved model.

## User Impact

The restored model name stays readable without resizing the composer or hiding legitimate runtime metadata. Narrow layouts retain the bounds that keep model and effort controls separate. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the model summary's circular percentage-width dependency with an owner-specific automatic width, while keeping its maximum width bounded. A real-browser regression updates the retained production composer and verifies identical saved markup, label-node identity, label readability, composer geometry, and no width-persistence callback.

## Evidence

- WebKit baseline regression: the same saved label changes from 242px visible / 242px natural width to 225px / 242px after the round trip, while the composer remains 524px wide. The capture-free regression passes with this repair.
- WebKit regression and overflow consumers: 15 passed; rerun after the CI repairs, 15 passed again. Chromium regression also passes after the repairs.
- Chromium affected picker, effort, overflow, and mobile suites: 56 passed across five files before the CI-only refinements.
- Bundled `/chat` synthetic reconnect and narrow picker layouts: 6 passed in Chromium and WebKit before the CI-only refinements.
- Broader WebKit affected run: 53 passed and four failed. All four failures were independently reproduced with baseline production CSS: reverse-Tab focus in chat/new-session and Access busy-focus true/false. They are not reported as passing.
- Scoped lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Local typecheck remains blocked by the supported checkout-boundary guard on a shared `tsrs` declaration input; it did not pass. No actual native-host verification was performed.
- Independent read-only review found no actionable findings. Original full-candidate canonical autoreview through P2 completed `scoped-clean`, including regression/fixture/render-helper quality, against base `a3d5baaabd2ce88ace4b5d1c45a9577a61dbc08a` and source `7083a9a30949977ef2493d66ab573763a578c032`.
- Hosted run `43518993336` exposed two PR-caused issues: a required `defaults.contextTokens` fixture field was missing, and the added CSS rule increased raw CSS by 85 bytes against a 64-byte differential allowance. The fixture now supplies its existing synthetic context size without changing assertions; the selector now addresses the picker's native direct-child summary. A local production-build comparison measures +63 raw CSS bytes, within the unchanged allowance. No budgets, baselines, or guards were weakened.
- The two-line CI repair delta received a fresh canonical API autoreview through P2: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Reviewed source `15a4399c1e3c25072564217049e61793b35e8e5b`, tree `384eebe888af1af1eadecdda1bbc2aabc9af5c1f`. Current native published head is `a1c030c08f103a3c978b63903047a133de9867d6`.
- Exact-head run [43521248648](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43521248648) completed with failure. Both repaired gates now pass: `control-ui-performance` records +63 raw CSS bytes, and all selected production/test typecheck jobs pass. `security-fast` also passes on this exact head. The remaining failed jobs are `checks-ui (1/3)`, `(2/3)`, `(3/3)`, `checks-ui-e2e (1/7)`, `(5/7)`, and their downstream `openclaw/ci-gate`; none is reported as passing.
- Remaining component failures have matching outside-PR signatures in completed run [43518448291](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43518448291), head `3f6229d951f7cea37a2be140a57c75438c849e85` for merged PR #192137: missing Anthropic credential label, draft account-group/context-window controls, extra mounted-view label work, and the identical WebKit activation assertion (`expected null to match object { hidden: false }`). Independent log comparison, not matching shard names, establishes the signatures. A focused local replay on actual CI base `9d419014f53d2430e44696a2d8de146eba849755` also reproduces all seven unit failures (52 pass); the isolated WebKit activation test passes locally, so that passing replay is not claimed as a repair.
- Remaining bundled-flow failures have matching signatures in completed run [43521735149](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43521735149), head `f3062e7c56f019826fd9f0d7cad523fcc4dd723d` for merged PR #192142: hidden provider auth metadata at 1280/390px; missing native-runtime selection options in confirm/cancel/mandatory cases; duplicate OpenCode runtime locator on send/confirm; chat-only metadata at line 84; and missing shortcut number in model-catalog geometry. Independent hosted logs match the exact assertions/selectors. Focused local actual-base replay also fails all eight selected cases (12 skipped); local source-map line attribution differs, so the independently matching hosted signatures establish inherited attribution. Unrelated failures remain defects, not passes.
- Hosted ClawSweeper reviewed exact head `a1c030c08f103a3c978b63903047a133de9867d6`: no correctness/security findings and no before-merge findings; ready for maintainer review. Its advisory proof gap is retained: the supplied images show the synthetic production-composer case, not a captured saved → live → saved transition through the built `/chat` route. No duplicate review was requested.

### Before and after

Inspected, synthetic production-composer captures in WebKit after the same saved → live runtime → saved round trip. Both composers are 524px wide. The screenshots are crops of genuine recorded browser frames: ordinary Playwright WebKit still capture toggles a stylesheet to synchronize animations and forces a relayout that temporarily repairs the baseline defect. Recording preserved the unmodified stale geometry for the baseline capture. The capture harness is not part of this PR, and the committed regression remains capture-free.

![Before: restored model label is truncated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46ccfbf7-a278-4b12-8d3f-046cdd1a8a42)

prs.title: fix(outbound): honor blockedHostnames for all outbound media downloads
prs.body:
Related: #197855

## Summary

When OpenClaw downloads a remote media URL to send to a channel, it skips the operator's `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.blockedHostnames`. A model-selected URL can therefore fetch a host the operator has denied, and the bytes get posted to the channel.

This PR applies the deny list to every outbound media download:
- message-tool attachments;
- message-tool `send`/`thread-reply` media;
- channel reply media;
- hosted-media staging;
- plugin media tools.

The host's `OutboundMediaAccess` carries the deny list, and the shared outbound loader enforces it. Only the deny list applies: web_fetch's private-network opt-ins never reach outbound media, and nothing changes for deployments that don't set `blockedHostnames`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw downloads and posts outbound media from hosts listed in `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.blockedHostnames`. This happens when the model sends an attachment or media URL, or when a channel delivers reply media.

## What was wrong

1. **Message-tool attachment hydration** (`src/infra/outbound/message-action-params.ts`) built loader options with no `ssrfPolicy` in either the host or the sandbox branch.
2. **Plugin-side downloads** never received the deny list. These are message-tool `send`/`thread-reply` media, channel reply media and hosted media.
   - They load through `buildOutboundMediaLoadOptions` / `loadOutboundMediaFromUrl` / `prepareUrl` (`src/media/load-options.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/outbound-media.ts`), which had no policy input.
   - A few plugins call the loader directly instead: the Discord slash-command replies, WhatsApp auto-replies, Tlon, the Matrix avatar and Feishu docx uploads.
3. `loadWebMedia` passes on only a policy the caller supplies, so `fetchWithSsrFGuard` ran with no hostname deny list.

The built-in private, loopback, link-local and metadata blocking, DNS pinning and per-redirect checks were unaffected. The exposure is limited to public hosts the operator explicitly blocked.

## User Impact

Operators who set `blockedHostnames` now get those hosts, including redirect hops, refused for all outbound media downloads, with `Domain policy: Blocked hostname (configured blocklist)`. Operators who don't set it see no change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One owner for the policy.** `resolveOutboundMediaAccessForConfig(cfg)` (`src/media/load-options.ts`) is the only reader of the config path.
  - The agent-scoped media access resolver (`src/media/read-capability.ts`) adds the deny list to host `mediaAccess`.
  - `resolveOutboundMediaAccess` keeps it.
  - `buildOutboundMediaLoadOptions` turns it into the loader's `ssrfPolicy`.
- **Host-provided capability, no ambient read.** Plugins that already forward the host `mediaAccess` (about 18 sites) get enforcement with no code change.
  - Plugin reply paths that held only config now pass `resolveOutboundMediaAccessForConfig(cfg)`.
  - Direct loader calls add only `ssrfPolicy`, leaving their local-root handling untouched.
- **Pass only the deny list.** `dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork`, `allowedHostnames` and the RFC 2544 and IPv6 ULA opt-ins never reach outbound media, so this cannot widen what outbound downloads can reach.
- **No config surface change.** The schema and defaults are unchanged, and no migration is needed.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path × mode | Before | After (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| **Real model + real Discord, `send` action**: `openclaw agent --local` (isolated state, real `gpt-5.4-mini`, a private Discord test channel), PNG from `www.google.com` with `blockedHostnames: ["www.google.com"]` | Narrow-fix build `f0a69e2` (attachment hydration only): **posted**. Discord shows the bot's message with the 5,969-byte PNG | Blocked in the Discord plugin's delivery path: `[security] blocked URL fetch … configured blocklist: www.google.com`, `OutboundDeliveryError`. No new post in channel history |
| Real model + real Discord, `send` action, allowed control (only `example.com` blocked) | — | Delivered. The Discord API read-back shows the PNG attachment |
| **Real model + real Discord, `upload-file` action**, same blocked PNG | Base `b4da3463d3a`: **posted** with the 5,969-byte attachment | Blocked before any request; no new post |
| Real model + real Discord, `upload-file` action, allowed control | — | Delivered. The Discord API read-back shows `googlelogo_color_272x92dp.png` (`image/png`) |
| Real model, `upload-file`, Docker sandbox mode (`openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim`), `example.com` blocked | Base: request sent to the blocked host (`HTTP 404 … Example Domain`) | Blocked before any request |
| Unit: central resolver → builder → `loadWebMediaRaw` → guard (`src/media/read-capability.test.ts`) | — | Rejected with `configured blocklist`; `fetch` was never called. Covers both resolver branches |
| Unit: `runMessageAction` `sendAttachment`, host and sandbox branches | Fails on base: the blocked URL is fetched and the handler is invoked | Rejected; neither `fetch` nor the handler was called |
| No `blockedHostnames` configured | — | Unchanged: no `ssrfPolicy` is added, and the existing suites stay green |

In the Discord rows, the model chose the tool call itself and delivery was real. Each "before" run used the stated commit's code.

Commands and results:
- **Core:** `pnpm vitest run` over the media options, read-capability, plugin SDK outbound media, hydration, outbound payload contract and gateway send suites: 13 files, 245/245.
- **Outbound delivery:** `deliver*`, `message-action-runner*`, `message-action-send*`, `delivery-queue*`: 54 files, 590/590.
- **Touched plugins:** the directly affected tests in each, all passing. Three tests that checked exact arguments were updated for the new field.
  - Discord, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Feishu and Mattermost: 26 files.
  - iMessage, Matrix, QA Channel, Signal, Tlon, X, Zalo and Zalo Personal: 25 files.
- **Typecheck:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` pass. The only extension errors are in the untouched `qa-lab/src/mantis` files, which can't resolve `@openclaw/crabbox-provider` in this local build.
- **Lint and format:** oxlint and oxfmt are clean on all 40 changed source files; `pnpm format:docs:check` and `git diff --check` are clean.
- **SDK exports:** `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports` is clean.

## SDK / caller upgrade contract

- **Additive only.** `OutboundMediaAccess.blockedHostnames?` and `resolveOutboundMediaAccessForConfig` (exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/outbound-media`) are new; `buildOutboundMediaLoadOptions` may now return `ssrfPolicy`. No existing signature changed.
- **Third-party plugins that forward the host `mediaAccess`** to `loadOutboundMediaFromUrl`, `buildOutboundMediaLoadOptions` or `prepareUrl` get enforcement automatically.
- **Plugins that build their own loader options** without it keep their current behavior until they adopt the helper.

## Boundary decisions requested from owners

1. **Config help wording (config owners).** The config help text still describes `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` as web_fetch-scoped. This PR documents the outbound coverage in `docs/tools/web-fetch.md` and the channel SDK media docs, to avoid regenerating the help baseline.
2. **Tlon link fallback (Tlon owners).** When a download fails and no byte cap is set, Tlon posts the original URL as a link. That still holds for blocked hosts; the gateway never fetches them.
3. **Operator-configured Matrix startup avatars (Matrix owners).** These are left out of scope, because the URL comes from operator config rather than the model.

## Testing

New tests:
- `carries the configured hostname deny list into plugin media downloads` (`src/media/read-capability.test.ts`);
- `applies only the configured deny list to outbound media options` (`src/media/load-options.test.ts`);
- `denies configured blockedHostnames before fetching host and sandbox attachment URLs` (`src/infra/outbound/message-action-params.attachments.test.ts`).

Everything else listed above is unchanged and green.

prs.title: feat(diagnostics-prometheus): let plugins add metric families to the scrape route
prs.body:
Closes #197880

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that wants operator metrics has to serve its own HTTP route, so operators add a second Prometheus scrape job for one Gateway, and that plugin's series skip the exporter's label and series budget.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can register counters, gauges and histograms that `diagnostics-prometheus` serves from `/api/diagnostics/prometheus`. Operators then scrape one route with the existing auth, and plugin series share the existing cardinality protection. Nothing changes for installs that do not enable a diagnostics exporter or whose plugins do not call the new API.

Risks:

- The type change is additive and optional. Plugins built against this host that use `api.metrics?.` run unchanged on older hosts, where the field is absent.
- Samples recorded during `register()` are dropped, because the exporter service starts after registration. Plugins record from their runtime paths (routes, services, hooks).
- Reloading a plugin resets its counters in the scrape: the Gateway disposes the previous instance before it registers the replacement, so the old series are dropped and new ones start at zero. Prometheus treats this like any counter reset.
- The gate reads each exporter's enablement as a bundled plugin. An exporter installed from npm or ClawHub and enabled only through `plugins.allow` (no `plugins.entries.<id>.enabled: true`) runs, but `api.metrics` stays undefined. Owners can keep this gate, resolve it from the discovered exporter record, or define `api.metrics` in every live registry and let samples drop while no exporter listens.
- Plugin label values are checked only against the character policy, not redacted. A plugin could still put an identifier in a label; the 128 series cap per family bounds the cardinality cost of that mistake.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197880 is marked as needing a product decision; this PR is a concrete proposal for that contract, with working code.

`api.metrics` is a small optional field on the plugin API:

```ts
const metrics = api.metrics?.register({
  families: [
    { name: "retain_total", type: "counter", help: "Retains by outcome", labels: ["outcome"] },
    { name: "recall_seconds", type: "histogram", help: "Recall latency", buckets: [0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5] },
  ],
});
metrics?.counter("retain_total").inc({ outcome: "ok" });
metrics?.histogram("recall_seconds").observe({}, 0.12);
```

- Namespace: the host sets it. Every family becomes `openclaw_plugin_<plugin id>_<name>`, so a plugin cannot claim another plugin's names. The issue proposed a plugin-chosen `namespace`; this is the main point for owners to decide.
- Budget: plugin families get no reserve. They draw from the existing shared pool, keep at most 128 label sets per family, and drops appear in `openclaw_prometheus_family_series_dropped_total{family="openclaw_plugin_..."}`. Core reserves do not change.
- Lifecycle: declarations are admitted under the existing plugin lifecycle authority (`capturePluginLifecycleAuthority`, captured when `register()` runs), and samples are delivered only while the recording instance is the published one (`isPluginRecordActive`, the same check the session attachment path uses). There is no separate fence for metrics. A replacement instance can register the same families during a reload, but what it records before the reload commits (from `register()` or a service started in the preparation scope) is dropped and cannot reset the live instance's series. A previous instance that a failed reload resumes keeps its series and recorders without registering again. A family leaves the scrape only when no remaining registration of the plugin declares it: when the same instance registers again without it, or when its owning instance is disposed. When the exporter stops, plugin series reset with the core series.
- Exporter gate: `api.metrics` exists while any diagnostics exporter plugin (`diagnostics-prometheus` or `diagnostics-otel`) is enabled, using the same exporter list that already decides who receives `internalDiagnostics`. Only `diagnostics-prometheus` reads the families today, so with only the OTel exporter on, samples are accepted and dropped. Whether OTel should export them, and whether this gate is the right one, is an owner decision.
- Consumer: [`@etzelm/openclaw-memory-hindsight`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@etzelm/openclaw-memory-hindsight), a memory slot plugin, serves its own Prometheus route (`/plugins/hindsight-native/metrics`) today, so operators add a second scrape job. With this API it would register `recall_total`, `retain_total`, `recall_skipped_total`, `retain_queue_replays_total`, `retain_queue_drops_total` (counters), `retain_queue_depth` (gauge), and `recall_duration_seconds`, `retain_duration_seconds`, `recall_injected_memories`, `recall_injected_chars` (histograms), labelled by agent, bank and fixed outcome or reason enums, and drop the route.

Owners can accept this shape or redirect it; the registration, namespace and allocation choices are theirs to make.

<details><summary>Admission, delivery and SDK surface details</summary>

- `api.metrics` is defined only for the live full registration, and only while a diagnostics exporter plugin is enabled in config. Otherwise it is `undefined`, so `api.metrics?.` is the whole opt-in. Samples recorded while no exporter listens are dropped.
- The plugin id is lowercased and other characters become `_`, so two ids can still map to one exported name (`a-b` and `a_b`, or plugin `foo` family `bar_baz` and plugin `foo_bar` family `baz`). The second registration of such a name throws at load, so the clash is loud but depends on load order. A histogram also reserves its `_bucket`, `_sum` and `_count` names, so histogram `lat` and gauge `lat_count` cannot both register, in one plugin or across plugins (plugin `a` histogram `x` blocks plugin `a_x` gauge `count`).
- `register()` checks names, counter `_total` suffixes, declared label names and histogram buckets, and throws during plugin load on bad input. A sample whose labels differ from the declaration is dropped with one warning per family on the plugin logger. Label values outside the low-cardinality policy (`[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`, at most 120 characters) are exported as `other`.
- Each `register()` result is one registration owned by its plugin instance. The first call binds teardown to the instance (`lifecycle.onDispose`) and captures the instance's lifecycle authority; `register()` throws when that authority cannot be minted (a disposed, retired or not-yet-published instance outside its own registration). Recorders publish only while their registration is held, the authority still holds and the record is published, so an instance paused by a reload drops samples until it resumes, and an uncommitted replacement's samples (including ones recorded inside the reload preparation scope, where the authority itself still allows calls) are dropped until publication.
- Re-registration by the same instance replaces only that instance's families and retires the ones no other instance of the plugin declares; recorders from the earlier call go quiet. Disposing an instance retires only names no remaining instance declares, so neither a disposed nor an older instance can evict the live instance's families. If a family's type, help, labels or buckets differ between instances, the exporter drops the old series once the new shape is published: when the previous instance is disposed after the reload commits, or at the first published sample of the new shape, whichever comes first. The scrape keeps one `TYPE` block per name, and a failed replacement never reaches this step.
- Delivery follows the existing exporter listeners (`onGatewayWsMetrics`, `onWorkerRequestMetrics`): a new trusted `internalDiagnostics.onPluginMetrics` listener, offered only to the trusted diagnostics exporters and bound to the service capability lease. Core keeps no metric values.
- No new SDK export names. The types are reachable as `NonNullable<OpenClawPluginApi["metrics"]>`. The SDK surface changes only by the new optional `metrics` field on `OpenClawPluginApi` and the optional `onPluginMetrics` on the service context's `internalDiagnostics`.
- Docs: a "Plugin metric families" section in `docs/gateway/prometheus.md` and one row in the SDK overview field table.

</details>

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway (`openclaw.mjs gateway run`, token auth, `diagnostics-prometheus` enabled) with a small standalone fixture plugin that calls `api.metrics?.register(...)` and records one counter, gauge and histogram sample per request to its route. Two requests, then one scrape:

| Build | `api.metrics` | Scrape | `openclaw_plugin_` lines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Reload through the same Gateway: a manifest fixture whose gauge records which registration served the request. A config edit replaces the plugin; a second edit sets `fail: true`, so the replacement's `register()` throws right after `api.metrics.register()`, and the Gateway restores the previous registration (it registers the previous code and config again, "registration 4" in the log). Sample lines per scrape (7 = counter, gauge and 5 histogram lines):

The other recovery path, a reload that fails early and resumes the paused previous instance without registering it again, is not reachable from a config edit; the "keeps the live instance's families when a reload fails and the instance resumes" test drives it through the real registry, lifecycle authority and `PluginInstance` pause/resume, and fails on the previous revision.

prs.title: feat(plugins): tell agent hooks when the turn read network content
prs.body:
Related: #197881 (agent hooks only; tool hooks stay open there), #107069, #196857

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that stores turn content (memory, logging) cannot tell whether the turn read network-sourced tool results, so it stores text from a fetched web page with the same trust as text the user typed. Core already tracks this per turn and records its own memory writes as `untrusted` when it is set.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can read `ctx.turnTainted` on agent hooks and lower trust or skip storing content from turns that read network-sourced tool results. The field is optional and read-only. Nothing changes for plugins that do not read it, and there is no new enforcement. Until #197940 is fixed, `agent_end` handlers do not run after turns that call Tool Search `dispatch_action`; `before_agent_finalize` and `llm_output` carry the field on those turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The field reuses the one per-turn flag core already keeps (`createAgentTurnTaintState`), the same getter that makes memory writes record `untrusted` (see "Freeform edits and quarantine" in `docs/concepts/memory-provenance.md`). There is no second tracker. This implements the minimal informational contract recommended in the issue triage; the coverage and semantics below are the proposal for the SDK and security owners.

- `PluginHookAgentContext.turnTainted?: boolean` (readonly). The embedded runtime reads the flag each time it builds a hook context, so the value matches the turn at that point. It is set on `before_prompt_build`, `llm_input`, `llm_output`, `before_agent_finalize`, `agent_end`, and the run loop's own `before_compaction` / `after_compaction`.
- The shared harness context builder (`buildAgentHookContext`) now forwards the field. It copies fields one by one, so without this `agent_end` and `before_agent_finalize` would not receive it. External harnesses that use the same SDK helpers can pass it too.
- It is absent, not `false`, when the runtime does not report it: CLI backends, other harnesses that do not pass it, and the session-level compaction hook that only carries `sessionKey`. So the issue's `before_compaction` ask is met for compaction the run loop owns, not for that session-level hook.
- Memory-flush maintenance runs (`trigger: "memory"`) start with the flag `true` when the source turn was tainted or the sender was not the owner, so on those runs `true` does not require a network tool result in that run. The flag stays set across retries of the same turn.
- `false` is not a trust attestation. It only means core saw no network-sourced tool result in this turn. The user's own message, channel input, and tool results not marked as network content leave it `false`. The docs and the type comment say to treat the flag as informational provenance.

Shape differs from the issue sketch (`turnTaint: { untrustedContent, sources }`). Core records only "a non-presentation tool result had `resultContentSource: "network"`", not which source, so a `sources` list would need new tracking. The boolean keeps the name core already uses (`turnTainted` in transcript metadata). A structured object can still be added later if core starts recording sources.

Not changed:
- When the flag is raised. #196857 (Code Mode catalog search raising it with no network call) still applies, and plugins now see the same value core uses, which makes that case visible.
- Input provenance. `ctx.inputProvenance` is unchanged; #107069 is separate.
- Tool hooks. The issue asks for them too, but they take a different context type (`PluginHookToolContext`), and a per-call value needs its own timing rule (before or after this call's result is counted). That is left for a follow-up, so this PR covers the agent hooks only and #197881 stays open for tool hooks.

## Evidence

Real Gateway on each side: built from the tree, isolated state, loopback, a local OpenAI-compatible model, and a small fixture plugin that logs whether `turnTainted` is present on each hook. Two turns through the Gateway's `/v1/chat/completions`: one asks for `web_fetch` of `https://example.com/`, one asks for `read` of a workspace file. The `after_tool_call` rows show which tools ran (tool hooks are not changed, so they never carry the field).

origin/main (7602443):

```
turn=network  hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=web_fetch
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=dispatch_action
turn=network  hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=network  hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=local    hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=local    hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=read
turn=local    hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=local    hook=agent_end            has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolResults=read
turn=local    hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
```

This branch (8f0bbfa; later revisions change only docs, a type comment and tests):

```
turn=network  hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=web_fetch
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=dispatch_action
turn=network  hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=true
turn=network  hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=true
turn=local    hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
turn=local    hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=read
turn=local    hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
turn=local    hook=agent_end            has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false toolResults=read
turn=local    hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
```

Known limitation, tracked in #197940: in our runs (2/2), after an embedded turn that called Tool Search `dispatch_action`, plugin `agent_end` handlers failed with `Plugin invocation scope is closed` before running. That is why the `web_fetch` turn above has no `agent_end` row: the model also called `dispatch_action`. With Tool Search off, `web_fetch`, `read` and `session_status` alone each ran `agent_end` normally.

This blocks the issue's main use case, retaining at `agent_end` after a network turn, whenever the turn used `dispatch_action`, until that bug is fixed. Tool Search is on by default, so that is common. The new field itself is correct on `before_agent_finalize` and `llm_output`, which run after the tools and are not affected, and a plugin can use those meanwhile. The `lifecycle-hook-helpers` test below covers `agent_end` handlers getting the field through the shared builder, and the `read` turn above shows it live on `agent_end`.

Tests (red on origin/main, green here):
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/agent-hook-context.test.ts`: the hook context reports the real `createAgentTurnTaintState` flag (false, false after a local result, true after a network result), and omits the field when the runtime gives no getter.
- `src/agents/harness/lifecycle-hook-helpers.test.ts`: `agent_end` and `before_agent_finalize` handlers receive `turnTainted` as `true` or `false` from the harness context, and no field when the harness does not report it.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts`: run-loop compaction hooks read the flag when they fire (false before, true after).

The `lifecycle-hook-helpers` test fails with the harness forwarding line removed (`expected [ undefined, undefined, undefined ] to deeply equal [ true, false, undefined ]`).

Gates on the current head (rebased on origin/main 126e63bf05b):
- `pnpm test` on the three files above plus `hook-context`, `turn-taint-state` and `agent-end-side-effects` tests: 6 files, 36 tests passed.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`: 23 passed. This is the test that failed CI on the previous head; it was broken on main by #197697 and fixed by #197976 (fails on 2035b0730f8^, passes on 2035b0730f8), so the rebase picks up the fix.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: every step passed except the dead export scan, which reports the same unused exports in `scripts/lib/` and `extensions/` on unmodified origin/main 126e63bf05b; this PR touches neither.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- `pnpm check:docs`: passed.

On 6417045 (same source; later revisions change only docs, a type comment and tests):
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff --base 7602443 --head 6417045`: exit 0. The only declaration change is the added `readonly turnTainted?: boolean;` on `PluginHookAgentContext` (2 reachable declarations, 183 exports that reach the type). Additive, no removals.

Risks: low. It is an additive optional field on a hook context. A plugin that treats a missing field as "not tainted" would be wrong on CLI backends; the docs say the field is absent there. A plugin that treats `false` as "trusted" would also be wrong; the docs say `false` only means no network-sourced tool result was seen.

prs.title: feat(plugins): let manifest configSignals test a config value
prs.body:
Closes #197882

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin authors cannot hide a tool while its config flag is `false`, because manifest `configSignals` can only test whether a value is present. The tool is still offered to the model.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can list a tool only while a feature is actually on, for example `"equals": { "knowledgeBase.enabled": true }`, so the model no longer sees tools the plugin will refuse to run. Existing manifests behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each `configSignals` entry now accepts an optional `equals` map from a dot path to a literal string, number, or boolean. It follows the issue triage: literal equality only, with inequality left out until a plugin needs it. The issue is marked as needing a product decision; this PR implements the recommended contract so that decision can be made on concrete code.

The contract, stated in the docs and covered by tests:

- **Missing value:** a missing or `null` path fails. Comparison is strict, so `"true"` does not equal `true`.
- **Overlays:** paths are read from the same effective config as `required`, after `overlayPath`. With `overlayMapPath`, each map entry is checked on its own, so `equals` and `required` must pass on the same entry.
- **SecretRefs:** never resolved. A path holding a SecretRef does not equal any literal, even when the secret has that value.
- **Older hosts:** they ignore `equals` and drop a signal that has nothing else, so the tool falls back to its other config or auth signals, and with none it stays listed, which is today's behavior. The docs tell plugins that rely on `equals` to set `openclaw.install.minHostVersion`.
- All fields of one signal must pass together. `required`, `requiredAny`, and `mode` are unchanged, so `false` still counts as present for `required`.

Generation provider metadata shares the same evaluator, so it gets the same field. Docs cover the field, its rules and a flag-gating example.

## Evidence

Real agent turns from the shipped CLI: `openclaw agent --local --model claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5 --json`, each with a fresh isolated state dir and config, `tools.profile: "full"`, and a small fixture plugin that registers two tools unconditionally:

- `kb_search`: `configSignals: [{ rootPath: "plugins.entries.kb-demo.config", equals: { "knowledgeBase.enabled": true } }]`
- `kb_status`: `configSignals: [{ rootPath: "plugins.entries.kb-demo.config", required: ["knowledgeBase.enabled"] }]` (presence only, unchanged control)

Prompt: list every tool whose name contains `kb_`, then call `kb_search` once if it is available, otherwise reply "kb_search unavailable". The tool columns come from the run's own tool list (`meta.systemPromptReport.tools.entries`, the tools sent to the model):

| Build | `knowledgeBase.enabled` | Tools sent | `kb_search` | `kb_status` | Model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main (`92e16d25ce01`) | `false` | 62 | sent | sent | called `kb_search`: "kb_search fixture result: ok" |
| main (`92e16d25ce01`) | `true` | 62 | sent | sent | called `kb_search`: "kb_search fixture result: ok" |
| this branch | `false` | 61 | not sent | sent | listed only `kb_status`, replied "kb_search unavailable" |
| this branch | `true` | 62 | sent | sent | called `kb_search`: "kb_search fixture result: ok" |

On main, `equals` is an unknown field, so the signal is dropped and the model can call `kb_search` while the flag is off. The presence-only `kb_status` stays listed in every run, because `false` counts as configured. On this branch the only difference between the two flag values is `kb_search`.

Redacted model reply, this branch, `knowledgeBase.enabled: false`:

```text
kb_status
mcp__openclaw__kb_status

kb_search unavailable
```

(The Claude CLI runtime also exposes OpenClaw tools under `mcp__openclaw__` names, so the model lists each tool twice.)

Regression tests (red on main, green here):

- `src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.test.ts`: on main 7 failed, 23 passed (30). Covers `true`, `false`, the string `"true"`, `null` and a missing path; `overlayPath`; `overlayMapPath` where `equals` and `required` must pass on the same entry; and a SecretRef that is never resolved.
- `src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts`: on main 1 failed, 65 passed (66). Loads a real manifest: the normalizer keeps `false` and `0`, trims paths, and drops non-scalar values, empty paths and a signal whose only `equals` entry is invalid.

Checks run on this branch (based on main `92e16d25ce01`):

- `pnpm test` on the two files above plus consumers (`tools.optional`, `tools.inspection`, `manifest-command-aliases`, `tool-policy`, `tool-policy-pipeline`, `tools-effective-inventory` (6 files)): 13 files, 286 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check`, `pnpm build`: pass.
- `src/plugins/bundled-plugin-categories.test.ts` fails on main `92e16d25ce01` and on this branch with the same message, `perplexity: expected exactly one purpose category`. The perplexity manifest has listed two categories since #195641; this branch does not touch it.

Risks: low. The field is optional and additive, and no existing branch of the evaluator changed. Older hosts drop the unknown field and fall back to the tool's other signals, which is today's behavior; the docs point plugin authors to `openclaw.install.minHostVersion`.

prs.title: fix(agents): agent denies finished setup after BOOTSTRAP.md is removed
prs.body:
Closes #196403

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent says setup is unfinished, and that it deleted `BOOTSTRAP.md` without reading it, on the turn after it followed and removed that file.

## User Impact

After a custom or stock bootstrap finishes, the agent no longer asks the user to restore `BOOTSTRAP.md` or redo setup that was already done.

## Why This Change Was Made

While setup is pending, `BOOTSTRAP.md` reaches the model through the system prompt. Once OpenClaw records setup as complete, the prompt drops the file and the "Bootstrap Pending" section, but the earlier turns that followed it stay in history, so the model sees a codeword exchange with no visible source. Since #196411, a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md` reliably stays pending until the agent removes it, which is exactly this state.

Routing (`resolveWorkspaceBootstrapRouting`) now reports recorded completion (`setupCompletedAt`) for primary sessions, and the bootstrap prompt section replaces the pending text with a two-line note. The note states OpenClaw's recorded state and does not claim each step was verified.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- The note depends only on recorded completion and the session key, never on the turn trigger or run kind, so the prompt prefix stays stable within a session. It appears in place of the pending section, so completion changes the prompt once, as it already did.
- Workspace preparation (`ensureAgentWorkspace`) records completion before routing on both turn paths (`command/prepare.ts`, `reply-workspace.ts`), so the first turn after the file disappears already carries the note.
- The bootstrap section builder moves from `system-prompt.ts` into `bootstrap-prompt.ts`, unchanged apart from the new branch, because `system-prompt.ts` and `cli-runner/prepare.ts` are over the line cap. The CLI helper takes the routing result instead of a separate mode for the same reason.
- A failed state read is not swallowed: `ensureAgentWorkspace` reads the same row earlier in the turn and would fail first.
- Cost: two fixed lines in the system prompt of primary sessions whose workspace completed setup. Removing a completed `BOOTSTRAP.md` from the prompt (#82463) is unchanged.

</details>

## Evidence

Live run of the reporter's flow through an isolated loopback Gateway (`POST /v1/chat/completions`, session `agent:main:main`) on main `8ae9d35bd53` and on this branch `ba176e52584`. A fresh baseline workspace gets a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md` (ask for the lighthouse codeword, delete this file, confirm). Then: greeting, Gateway restart, another message, the codeword, "Thanks. Is your setup finished?". Model inputs were captured with a logging proxy between the Gateway and the model server.

The model is the built-in runtime on a local Ollama model (`ollama/qwen3:4b`), not `claude-cli`: the Claude CLI login was unavailable on this host. The prompt code changed here is shared by both runtimes.

On both runs the model asks for the codeword on turns 1 and 2, deletes `BOOTSTRAP.md` with a tool call on turn 3 and replies "Setup complete. Codeword received: HALCYON-42". Turn 4's preparation records `setup_completed_at`. The built-in runtime keeps the first system prompt for prefix caching and sends later section changes as a "System prompt update" on the turn. Turn 4's update:

```text
main (8ae9d35bd53):
  System prompt update. The sections below replace their earlier versions; everything else in the system prompt is unchanged.
  ...
  ## Bootstrap Pending
  (removed)

  ## <workspace>/BOOTSTRAP.md
  (removed)

this branch (ba176e52584):
  System prompt update. The sections below replace their earlier versions; everything else in the system prompt is unchanged.

  ## Bootstrap Complete
  OpenClaw recorded workspace setup as complete; earlier BOOTSTRAP.md instructions are no longer shown.
  Missing BOOTSTRAP.md is expected. It and blank optional profile files do not mean setup was skipped.
  ...
  ## Bootstrap Pending
  (removed)

  (removed)
```

On main the model is told only that the bootstrap instructions were removed; with the fix it is told setup was recorded complete. The omitted `...` lines are unchanged `## Related` doc-link sections, identical in both runs.

`qwen3:4b` answered turn 4 "Yes, your setup is complete" on both main and this branch, so this model does not reproduce the reporter's Claude denial; the evidence here is the model input, not a changed reply. Turns 1 to 3 and Gateway restart behave identically on both.

```text
<<< Before we begin: what is the secret codeword for the lighthouse?

<<< Before we begin: what is the secret codeword for the lighthouse?

>>> USER: The lighthouse codeword is HALCYON-42.
<<< Setup complete. Codeword received: HALCYON-42
    [workspace: AGENTS.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md] [completed=-]
>>> USER: Thanks. Is your setup finished?
<<< Yes, your setup is complete. I'm ready to help with your next task!
    [workspace: AGENTS.md IDENTITY.md SOUL.md USER.md] [completed=2026-11-13T23:03:37.558Z]
```

</details>
