- `pnpm test src/agents/bootstrap-routing.test.ts src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts`: 3 failed / 71 passed with the production changes reverted, 74 passed with them.
- 277 tests across 13 affected files pass, including `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `system-prompt.cache-prefix`, `session-reset-prompt`, `helpers.system-prompt`, and the embedded bootstrap and CLI `prepare` suites.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, scoped oxlint, format, line-cap ratchet, test-lines ratchet and `git diff --check` pass.
- Not run: the same flow on `claude-cli` (login unavailable on this host). `prepare.existing-session` and `prepare.native-compaction` hit the warm Claude session host-memory check on main and on this branch.

prs.title: fix(agents): private CLI completions lose delivery under restrictive profiles
prs.body:
Related: #121661

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a private subagent result can fail to reach the user when the requester uses a restrictive tool profile such as `coding`, or a CLI backend that does not retain the full requester tool surface.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified private completion can relay its result to the requesting conversation through `message`, while its final answer stays private. Explicit tool denies, frozen policies, channel action gates, and grant revocation remain authoritative.

An additional completion messaging grant is restricted to sends in the original channel, account, conversation, and thread, and cannot become general messaging authority for spawned children or cron jobs. Existing requester permissions are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main already restores the normal Claude CLI requester tool surface. The remaining repair uses the explicit `privateCompletion` flag, carries source restriction independently of automatic final-reply delivery, and keeps the admitted completion allowance through the actual Gateway tool projection. The same policy merge helper preserves explicit denies and frozen allowlists at both stages.

The earlier destination-scope rationale in this PR was incorrect. This revision uses the existing source-reply guard for the additional grant. It also follows the current media contract: #176594 permits source-conversation photos and attachments through normal media validation; this PR does not restore the obsolete text-only restriction.

Integrated main at `650091daacdc10aa374e82a6327e8beffe136072` to resolve the stale branch conflicts and preserve current runtime selection and requester-tool retention.

## Evidence

At `bed203a26ff9c7aac301f0bff632b97d23895318` (tree `30b8d9d69f3d1a9983b45bc4f12f445b877763dc`):

- Production typecheck passed (`tsconfig.core.json`).
- Focused typecheck of all four changed test entrypoints, extending the repository root-test configuration, passed. It caught and fixed the current-main MCP startup API change.
- Type-aware lint passed for changed production files, tests/support, and the CI inventory; formatting, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet passed.
- The test-line ratchet still reports **51 inherited lines over budget**. At the integrated base the measured total is 6,551,687 and the effective ceiling is 6,551,636. This change adds exactly 663 test/support lines and a separate 663-line allocation, preserving that pre-existing difference. No shared baseline increase is included.

The complete Gateway → private parent completion → CLI runner → minted MCP grant → message tool → Telegram transport fixture passed **5/5** in [CI job 128116367053](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116367053). Only model decisions and external Bot API responses are synthetic. CI checked merge `328504c21532c5402858ade03a23c749cf1aa84e`, combining this head with main `9651d6347b1ab99453e8e6b5105d10d7800d82dc`.

| Scenario | Verified result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary private completion | Exactly one send containing the child result |
| Coding profile | Exactly one allowed send; other chat/thread and non-send probes rejected |
| Explicit operator deny | No completion message tool or child-result send |
| Disabled Telegram send action | Tool error and zero child-result sends |
| Revoked grant | HTTP 401 and zero child-result sends |

The five reported case durations total 122.7 seconds. This expensive composition stays in the release-only tier except for changed-file CI because admission-only tests miss authority lost between projection and dispatch.

The [CLI attempt suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116366616), including the new private/coding/other-CLI cases, and [MCP grant-context suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116366918) also passed. CI lint and all five core test-type stripes passed.

Full CI is red on an unrelated current-main defect: [production type checking](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116569548) and some asset-building jobs cannot resolve `extensions/deep-research/browser/client.js`. The browser directory has identical filenames and blob SHAs in main `9651d634` and the tested merge; both lack that module. This PR does not change those files.

The [CI baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116365654) also confirms the same inherited test-line debt on main `9651d634`: total 6,552,688, ceiling 6,552,637, over by 51, PR net delta +663. The separate allocation covers exactly the PR's +663; all other ratchets passed.

Local runtime attempts did not start tests: the worker compiler exceeded a 3 GiB cgroup limit, including a retry with a smaller Node heap; a narrow unit selection needed the same compiler and was stopped. The CI run supplies current-head GREEN proof. A fresh full-flow RED control, a real Gemini process, and Telegram Test Server were not run; the older-head live trace is not treated as evidence for this implementation.
Independent Codex source review covered the production and regression changes against `650091daacdc`: no actionable findings. This was an independent source review, not an autoreview or ClawSweeper execution. The existing private-delivery owner cases cover suppression of nonempty private final text; the new integration fixture itself returns `NO_REPLY`.

Simplification retained the existing runtime-selection and policy owners and removed unused photo/document assertions. Against the integrated base: production +38 net lines, regression tests/support +663. The exact 663-line test allocation is justified by the end-to-end authority boundary: admission-only tests miss a grant lost during CLI projection. The expensive integration is release-only except when selected by changed-file CI; the shared test baseline is unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

The model picker dropped Gateway cooldown details. Unavailable models did not explain when their cooldown would end, and a pinned Default could remain selectable.

## User Impact

Models in cooldown remain disabled, including pinned defaults and alternate runtimes. When an entire provider is cooling down, one status chip appears in its header. For a partially affected provider, only the affected rows show the chip. Cooldown replaces context information on those rows, and unavailable choices expose their status to assistive technology.

The countdown disappearing does not enable a model. Only an updated Gateway catalog can make it selectable. This change does not add credential-expiry UI.

## Implementation

Rebased onto `main` after #192135, #192137, and #192142 landed. The existing model availability owner remains authoritative; the picker only presents its cooldown deadline.

## Validation

- Two Chromium source-UI flows passed at 1280px and 390px with synthetic Gateway fixtures and a simulated clock.

prs.title: fix(macos): offer OpenClaw ID recovery after this Mac is removed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After **Settings › Remove this Mac**, the Mac forgets its OpenClaw ID enrollment and clears its primary connection, but then leaves the person stranded. The dashboard shows the generic "Dashboard unavailable · Gateway not configured" page with a Reload button that cannot help, Settings › Connection hides the OpenClaw ID section entirely, and the menu bar says "Gateway not configured". Found in the live sign-in-first test on 2026-11-12: there was no in-app way back short of a fresh profile. A Mac removed from another device ends up in the same place, with no explanation.

## User Impact

- The dashboard window shows a calm page instead of an error: "This Mac was removed from <claw>" (or "no longer has access", when another device removed it), with **Sign in with OpenClaw ID…**, **Set up a different connection** and **Close**.
- Settings › Connection always offers **Sign in with OpenClaw ID** when the build has an OpenClaw ID configuration, with a removal note when one applies.
- The menu bar offers **Sign in with OpenClaw ID…** when unconfigured and shows the removal.
- All entry points open the same sign-in → claw picker → approval flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `MacOpenClawIDDeviceStore` owns one local-retirement path for both a local removal and a verified remote one: stop the operator route, deselect the node, forget enrollment/session/keys, clear the primary connection, and record `{hostname, time, origin}`. The record is display context only, never authority; it clears on a new enrollment or when another primary connection is configured.
- A remote removal is recognized only from a verified snapshot that no longer admits this Mac's owner key (`notAdmitted`). Missing local trust data now reports `trustUnavailable` instead of `notAdmitted`, so it is not mistaken for removal; network errors never retire.
- A removal in progress on this Mac keeps "here" wording even when its lost-response verification observes the removal first.
- The sign-in sheet moves from the Settings model to one shared presenter used by Settings, the dashboard page and the menu.

Stacked on #197630.

## Evidence

- Real SwiftUI/HTML renders with fixture data (screens below).
- MacBook Pro (macOS 26.5.1, Xcode 26.6), isolated HOME/state, sandbox: `swift build --build-tests` passed; `OpenClawIDRemovalTests`, `DashboardFailurePageTests`, `StatusMenuDescriptorTests` 26 tests passed; `OpenClawIDRemovalRenderTests` passed.
- Pinned SwiftLint strict (macOS config, and iOS config for the shared file): 0 violations. SwiftFormat: clean. `pnpm native:i18n:verify`: passed.
- Not yet proven live: the OAuth → picker → approval round trip from each entry point, and a real remote removal. Both are in the next live test.

Screenshots: [inspected before/after comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197977#issuecomment-6866365581).

prs.title: fix(github): recover saved repository publications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repository-backed sessions can publish against their selected source branch instead of the current default branch, and saved publication requests cannot recover from pre-effect outages or retained-worker reconnects. Native integration also forwarded the selected personal publisher credential to the worker instead of using the normal execution identity. Capture failures could bypass bounded recovery and leave a request pending indefinitely.

## User Impact

Publication integrates the accepted checkpoint with one observed target tip in private worker Git state while preserving later edits, the editing index, the original request and existing PR metadata. Explicit retries revalidate the original requester and publisher; they never force-push or adopt an unmatched external head.

Repository-only publication requires the normal worker execution account to read the source/head and target/base roles: one repository in the common case, or fork and upstream when applicable. Actual read checks remain mandatory. My GitHub stays Gateway-held for final API/ref/PR writes and attribution. Missing execution credentials or access fail closed without personal-token fallback, anonymous fallback, new App requirements or broader grants. Ordinary worker Git/PR/issue capabilities are unchanged.

New capture still requires authoritative disk custody. Installed-upgrade and live private-provider/model qualification remain unperformed; these specific limitations were explicitly acknowledged in the landing direction below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing checkpoint, receipt, placement/runtime recovery, transfer and native Git owners. Capture holds editing custody; merge work stays private. Failure receipts retain bounded transport facts, not command output. Worker execution credentials have a bounded publication-operation lifetime independent of the API publisher, with acquisition rotation, committed selection, expiry, requester and placement checks. Native drain joins private publication and awaited cleanup outside the editing queue.

Reclaimed recovery carries the publication's existing live startup reader through the normal placement owner, without fabricating a chat turn or substituting credentials after denial. Capture errors use the existing cooldown and three-attempt/one-hour terminal policy. Healthy checkpoint waits remain exempt; busy work preserves previous failures. Terminal settlement rereads the current receipt under workspace exclusion without recapture or Git replay. The existing operation signal reaches placement and reconnect waits. No database schema, protocol extension, broader grant or new recovery owner was added.

Contributors: @galiniliev and @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1f24e3f3-e7d6-4966-b666-e5868987619d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/27a39a1f-33f6-4d65-89b8-6c389123648e)
- [Gateway process-restart implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/22f538c2-5ae4-4ca1-a35a-8279c9423ebf)
- [Bounded capture recovery implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/783b84dd-d80e-4e12-8a62-2c79c84912b8)

## Evidence

### Exact T and independent landing disposition

Published head **`0feb33f12155b29bb824b6ecaf2d707067be9698`**, tree **`119568553410ac8ed89106d60e92f3ed23635533`**. All85 scoped modes/blobs, signatures, ordered parents and both human trailers were verified. Historical source-for-proof receipt **`3acf53eaea9e14f4d0ef9025875d6030c7c2e942`** retains its original review **`1fde21bc0a30cb7946ff5265c6346110e3260a3f`**; it was not restamped as landing proof.

On November13 at22:29UTC the requester explicitly directed landing with the named installed-upgrade, live-private recovery and full-helper qualification gaps acknowledged, at the actual hosted3/3/4. A fresh independent ordinary correction review considered that new scope, current green CI and the actual source-bound evidence. Its verdict is **READY FOR /prepare-pr**, review OID **`8913c2a135c58314f4a80375bd49ee3cfdf0fcda`**, SHA256 **`fd550aafa1907c9760ac6ec2137127e198c8c348488d8bf03bde54c7bd7b8a33`**. Unmodified canonical validation passed before and after installation. This is independent review disposition, **not a claim that native preparation or merge has completed**; current authority, source, CI/security and landing checks still apply.

The reviewer traced permitted behavior/authority/credential/drain owners and inspected actual execution evidence:57 manifest entries,54 CI-log hashes and201 named proof lines. The behavioral assessment was completed; no new runtime test execution was claimed. All37 historical finding IDs across42 retained reviews, including originalR1–R5/NCI1, have explicit dispositions. Installed/live/helper gaps remain honestly recorded; the three investigated local HTTP failures remain `tests.result:fail` with their investigation records. No denied source was accessed, and no review/policy/receipt bypass was used.

### CI and hosted review

[Exact-T CI43492565015/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43492565015) **PASSED November13 at19:54:52UTC**:108 jobs,81 success/27 skipped/zero failed or active. Both required CI-gate forms and sensitive/dependency statuses succeed. The terminal post-review rollup has182 contexts:116 success/65 skipped/1 neutral. No rerun, new allocation credit or CI exception was used.

The [exact-T hosted assessment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193873#issuecomment-6674780143), revision11, remains **3/6 readiness · 3/6 proof · 4/6 patch**, **zero concrete code findings; Security:None**. Receiver43498247711/1, job132136926198, reviewed at20:11:26.361UTC. The single request6863558487 was accepted/completed; finalizer43499508888 was not another review. No higher rating is claimed or requested.

prs.title: fix(ui): reconcile remote access setup's relay step and offer profile linking
prs.body:
Closes #198464

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the **Turn on remote access** dialog shows two yellow warnings after a setup that actually worked. **Connecting <claw>** shows one when the relay connects a few seconds after setup. **Setting up your access** shows one when the Gateway restarted between OpenClaw ID sign-in and setup.

## User Impact

User impact: the completed setup card now shows the real state. **Connecting <claw>** spins and then turns green once the relay is online. A profile that couldn't be linked gets a note under the steps, with a **Link your profile** button when signing in again will fix it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dialog read relay status once, right after commit, and kept that answer. It now keeps checking while it is open: it spins for up to 30 seconds before warning, and still turns green if the relay connects later. The profile link is a separate step from setting up the claw's access, so its outcome moves out of that row. When the Gateway no longer holds the browser's sign-in (`sign_in_not_held`, for example after a restart), the note offers the same device sign-in that Settings → Profile uses.

## Evidence

Real Chromium render of the completed card. The synthetic Gateway answers commit with `profileLink: "sign_in_not_held"` and reports the relay offline at first, then online.

**Before (main):** both warnings, which stay after the relay connects.

![Before: Setting up your access and Connecting studio both show warnings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b02e0fda-bcd2-4973-9582-1510a991ae45)

**After, just finished:** access step done, relay step still connecting, profile note with Link your profile.

![After: relay step spinning and a profile-link note with a Link your profile button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24161541-02c1-437b-bba5-6f59735a8b9c)

**After, relay online:** the relay step turns green on its own.

![After: all four steps done, profile-link note remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3714f7da-e26a-4d8c-851f-21ae10ce0b57)

Tests:
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/lib/openclaw-id ui/src/components/openclaw-id ui/src/pages/profile`: 33 files, 261 tests pass
- New cases cover the relay coming up late, the grace-period warning, stopping when the dialog closes, each profile-link outcome, retrying the link, and ignoring a sign-in that finishes after setup closes
- The incident in #198464 had relay online 8 s after commit and `link_profile failure code=sign_in_not_held`; the reporter confirmed the Gateway restarted between sign-in and setup, and that linking from Settings → Profile then worked

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes foreground node actions remaining pullable after the requesting OpenClaw ID device or member is removed.

prs.title: fix(cli): surface capability flag-guard remedies in --json failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A script or agent that runs a capability CLI command with `--json` and mistypes a flag gets no actionable output. `openclaw capability model run --prompt hi --thinking turbo-mode --json` prints `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` plus `For help, run openclaw doctor.` on stderr — the remedy the guard already composed ("Invalid thinking level. Use one of: off|minimal|low|…") never reaches the terminal, even though the JSON envelope on stdout carries it. The same command *without* `--json` prints the remedy. The failure lane that automation reads is therefore the one lane that hides the advice, and the hint sends the operator to the wrong next step: `doctor` cannot repair a mistyped flag.

- Problem: eleven argument guards in `src/cli/capability-cli/` raise their operator remedy as a plain `Error`. `runCommandWithRuntime` rethrows plain errors when JSON output is active, and the root renderer prints a message only for expected CLI errors, so `capability` failures fall back to the generic title plus the Doctor hint.
- Solution: raise those eleven sites through the canonical `throwExpectedCliError` / `ExpectedCliError` owner in `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`, message text verbatim.
- What changed: `shared.ts` (3 guards), `model.ts` (3), `tts.ts` (3), `image.ts` (1), `tts-runtime.ts` (1) — production +18/-11. Regression assertions folded into existing cases in the four capability suites, net **-8** test lines, no new test file.
- What did NOT change: every message string, the exit code (1), the `--json` envelope bytes, and text-mode output. No guard became stricter or looser; only the error envelope changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer already distinguishes the two kinds of failure: `formatCliFailureLines` prints `humanOutput` verbatim when `isExpectedCliError` holds, and otherwise prints the generic title plus `For help, run openclaw doctor.` unless the command path is in a small show-reason whitelist (`update`, `connect`, `node run`, …). `capability` is not in that whitelist, and `runCommandWithRuntime` deliberately rethrows in JSON mode so the envelope and the stderr block stay owned by the root renderer. A plain `Error` therefore loses its advice exactly once: in JSON mode. Converting the guard sites to the owner class makes the capability CLI agree with every other operator-facing CLI remedy, which is the shape merged in #192127, #190366 and #196710 and what the four currently open per-site siblings (#198333, #198329, #191233, #191237) adopt.

Alternatives considered and rejected: adding `capability` to the renderer's show-reason whitelist would print raw reasons for every capability failure including provider and runtime faults, a larger blast radius than one guard family needs. Doing the conversion in the renderer or in `runCommandWithRuntime` would re-derive, at a shared boundary, a contract the error owner already owns. A new error class is unnecessary — `throwExpectedCliError(message)` sets `message`, `humanOutput` and `machineOutput` to the same string, which is exactly what these single-line remedies need.

One guard was deliberately left alone: `src/cli/capability-cli/tts-runtime.ts:242` ("--agent is only supported with local TTS provider inspection.") stays a plain `Error` because open PR #194702 deletes that gate; converting a line that is being removed would only manufacture a rebase conflict.

## User Impact

`--json` callers of `capability model run`, `capability image generate|edit` and `capability tts …` now see the flag remedy on stderr instead of a Doctor pointer, in the same words the text lane already used. Machine consumers are unaffected: the envelope is byte-identical before and after. Successful invocations, exit codes and non-JSON output are untouched.

## Evidence

Thirteen guards — the eleven converted, the unchanged `tts-runtime.ts:242` control, and an already-correct numeric-option control — each run twice (text, `--json`) on both arms: frozen `origin/main` `afa871c6e91` and this head `dd73d491fc3`. Both arms use the shipped source entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`) with `HOME` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` on a scratch directory holding a minimal config, so no real state is touched; inputs reach the guards before any network or provider work, so no mocks are involved. All 52 runs exit 1.

| Guard (with `--json`) | Before (`origin/main` `afa871c6e91`) | After (this head `dd73d491fc3`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 `capability model run --prompt ' '` | generic title + Doctor hint | `--prompt cannot be empty or whitespace-only.` |
| 2 `capability model run --prompt hi --thinking turbo-mode` | generic title + Doctor hint | `Invalid thinking level. Use one of: off…ultra.` |
| 3 `capability model run --prompt hi --prompt-stdin` | generic title + Doctor hint | `Use exactly one of --prompt, --prompt-file, or --prompt-stdin.` |
| 4 `capability model run --prompt hi --local --gateway` | generic title + Doctor hint | `Pass only one of --local or --gateway.` |
| 5 `capability model run --prompt hi --model not-a-provider/` | generic title + Doctor hint | `Model overrides must use the form <provider/model>.` |
| 6 `capability model run --prompt hi --agent ' '` | generic title + Doctor hint | `--agent must not be blank` |
| 7 `capability image generate --prompt p --aspect-ratio 16x9` | generic title + Doctor hint | `--aspect-ratio must be a W:H ratio of positive numbers, like 16:9` |
| 8 `capability tts convert --text hi --model gpt-4o-mini-tts` | generic title + Doctor hint | `TTS model overrides must use the form <provider/model>.` |
| 9 `capability tts convert --text hi --provider xiaomi --model openai/gpt-4o-mini-tts` | generic title + Doctor hint | `TTS --provider must match the provider in --model.` |
| 10 `capability tts set-persona --local` | generic title + Doctor hint | `--persona is required unless --off is set` |
| 11 `capability tts set-provider --local --provider ''` | generic title + Doctor hint | `--provider is required` |
| control: text lane, same 11 inputs (no `--json`) | remedy printed | remedy printed, `cmp` byte-identical to before |
| control: `capability tts providers --gateway --agent main` (guard left plain) | generic title + Doctor hint | generic title + Doctor hint, byte-identical |

After, guard 2 verbatim:

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts capability model run --prompt hi --thinking turbo-mode --json
stderr: Invalid thinking level. Use one of: off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|adaptive|max|ultra.
stdout: { "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error",
        "message": "Invalid thinking level. Use one of: off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|adaptive|max|ultra." } }
(exit 1)
```

Before, same command (stdout line unchanged, stderr line replaced):

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts capability model run --prompt hi --thinking turbo-mode --json
stderr: [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
        [openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
stdout: identical JSON envelope as above
(exit 1)
```

Contract preserved, measured rather than asserted: `cmp` over all 13 guards shows the `--json` **stdout** byte-identical between arms (the envelope already carried the message, so scripts that parse it keep working) and the **text-mode stderr** byte-identical between arms (the lane that already worked is untouched). Only JSON-mode stderr changes, and only from generic to remedy. The `tts-runtime.ts:242` control stays generic on both arms, which is the carve-out above, not a missed site.

Unit lane, same tests with the five production files reverted to `origin/main` and restored by recorded blob — a mutation test on the fix itself:

```console
FAIL src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts > capability cli > rejects invalid model run options [ '--thinking', 'turbo-mode' ] before dispatch
AssertionError: expected Error: exit 1 to be an instance of ExpectedCliError

FAIL src/cli/capability-cli.image-options.test.ts > rejects malformed image generate --aspect-ratio 16x9 before dispatch
AssertionError: expected Error: exit 1 to be an instance of ExpectedCliError

 Test Files  3 failed | 1 passed (4)   Tests  16 failed | 165 passed (181)   # production reverted
 Test Files  4 passed (4)             Tests  181 passed (181)                # this head
```

Consumers were run, not reasoned about. Every suite that imports the changed modules — the four edited files plus `capability-cli.help`, `capability-cli.lazy`, `capability-cli/shared`, `capability-cli/model.state-owner`, `model.auth-status`, `model.resources`, `local-account-secrets`, `command-secret-resolution.coverage`, `program/register.subclis`, `capability-cli/local-runners.account-secrets` and the root `failure-output` renderer suite: **14 files, 259 tests, green on this head**. `src/cli/capability-cli/shared.test.ts` needed no change and stays exactly as on `origin/main`; the `--local`/`--gateway` and blank-`--agent` guards it already exercises are also covered through the shipped CLI in the table above, so no second unit copy of them was added.

Gates: `git diff --check` clean; the repository formatter reports "All matched files use the correct format" on all 9 touched files; no `config/test-lines-allocations/` entry is needed because the test delta is **-8**; no test-only export was added and no new test file created.

Open PR collision check (submission-day sweep, 2026-11-14). Changed-file comparison over the recent open-PR snapshot plus keyword lanes (`throwExpectedCliError`, `capability-cli`, `aspect-ratio`, `thinking level`, `prompt-stdin`) found four same-family per-site PRs with **zero** file overlap (#198333 `models-cli.ts`, #198329 `nodes-cli`, #191233 `security-cli`, #191237 `worktrees-cli`), and two open PRs that touch my files without touching my semantics: maintainer PR #198294 (credential owner) overlaps only the `model.ts` import block — `git merge-tree` against its head conflicts on that one import line and nothing else — and #195363 (symlink image inputs, open since 11-08, currently `DIRTY`) re-indents the `model run` block that contains guards 1-3, a whitespace-only rebase conflict. Neither converts any capability guard, so this change is not superseded; both resolve mechanically on the next rebase. Gate 2.5: the fourteen commits touching `src/cli/capability-cli/` in the last 14 days (#198214, #198141, #196816, #195206, …) route state ownership and failure-output formatting, none asserts that a flag guard must stay a plain `Error`, and #196816 in fact narrows the generic-line path. The defect is still live: re-run against `origin/main` `68542b21d0d`, six commits past the arm above, `capability model run --prompt hi --thinking turbo-mode --json` again exits 1 with only the generic title and the Doctor hint on stderr, and `git merge-tree` of this head against that tip reports no conflict.

What was not tested locally: the repository lint wrapper refuses this worktree's symlinked install ("Declaration input escapes checkout"), and direct `oxlint` cannot load its `solid-lint` JS plugin here, so lint is left to CI on this head. A targeted `tsc` over the nine touched files produced no diagnostic in any of them; the six errors it printed are pre-existing module-resolution noise from the shared `node_modules` symlink (`libphonenumber-js`, `qrcode` types, `JSON.rawJSON`) in files this change does not touch. `openclaw capability … --json` was not run against a live Gateway, which these guards never reach: all thirteen inputs fail in argument validation before any transport call.

prs.title: fix(agents): auth refresh fails after its plugin call ends
prs.body:
Related: #196199

## What Problem This Solves

An auth change can queue a model-runtime refresh that runs after the plugin call has ended. That refresh then fails with `Plugin invocation scope is closed`.

## User Impact

Changing authentication can refresh the available models even after the original plugin call finishes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run the queued refresh in the existing detached async context. Keep the queue, owner, generation and retired-plugin checks.

## Evidence

Current head: `df942f3b031a7773f173e32018e3c1c0669809f8`, rebased onto main `f3957e8653e50e6f43d976fd0c0e9cf472606a0b` at the maintainer's request. The rebase was conflict-free. All three patch files are byte-identical to the preceding public head `232daa0d0313c7512178a575da782661050e2ec0`; `git diff --check` passed. Range comparison confirms that only the base and commit attribution changed, not the patch.

- Source review of auth publication, plugin invocation scope, drain/queue ownership, shutdown lifetime and retired-generation admission found no additional correctness blockers. Publication still uses the existing queue and lifecycle checks; it does not revive retired plugin instances.
- The preceding head's [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43388128647) failed two BTW context assertions in `checks-node-changed-compact-large-29`. Main now includes [08103c5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/08103c5df8b87969bdb69ce0a8977ed402a3d09a), which repairs the exact shared assertion used by both failures. That repair is included in this rebase. No separate baseline test run was performed during this review.
- Prior-head validation reported all 20 auth-recovery tests passing, including publication after the triggering call closes and refusal to revive a retired plugin registry; agents-root test typecheck, scoped lint, formatting and whitespace checks also passed. These remain prior-head evidence, not newly rerun checks.
- The earlier independent review found no remaining P0–P2 issues. Earlier checks also covered 23 eager-import wrapper tests and 29 core test-type graphs; those are prior-head evidence.

Current-head [CI run 43516263849, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43516263849) completed with failures; it is not green. Its only non-aggregate failed jobs are the two baseline-matched failures below. Current-head production/test typechecks and `security-fast` passed. No local fork-code execution or new end-to-end experiment was performed for this mechanical rebase.

The full Gateway experiment requested in review is still incomplete. Its first agent request failed with `Agent creation cannot capture another pending native opener`, before reaching auth refresh or the provider. The tests use synthetic credentials. This PR does not claim to explain every delegated-child failure in #196199.

### Authorized landing limitations

Sally explicitly authorized landing this reviewed exact head with both limitations documented:

1. **Pre-existing unrelated CI failures remain failed.** Attempt 2 has two non-aggregate failures, each directly signature-matched to scheduled main run [43510639112, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43510639112) at `649ca5f879f1e4349a2c5cf9872e30366962a595`:
   - [PR visitor-access job 132200172808](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43516263849/job/132200172808) matches [main job 132180373603](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43510639112/job/132180373603): the visitor-policy repair case expects `GatewayOperatorAccessDeniedError` but receives `GatewayOperatorAccessUnavailableError` at `agent.visitor-access.test-utils.ts:471`.
   - [PR ClawRouter job 132200172846](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43516263849/job/132200172846) matches [main job 132180366684](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43510639112/job/132180366684): the unsupported-chat expectation rejects with `FailoverError` / `model_chat_unsupported` instead of resolving an unsupported result, at `utility-completion.clawrouter.test.ts:223`.
   - The failing tests and inspected source inputs are unchanged between the scheduled-main baseline and this PR. The failed `openclaw/ci-gate` aggregate is downstream of these two jobs. Landing uses the native protected pre-existing-CI exception, not a claim of passing CI, and does not waive required review or security checks.
2. **Full real-Gateway end-to-end proof is still missing.** The experiment stopped at the separate native-opener error described above before exercising auth refresh. Source review and the reported focused tests do not replace that proof; no red-on-base demonstration or full resolution of #196199 is claimed.

prs.title: fix: templates add rejects publisher-qualified references for unscoped packages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw templates add @publisher/slug` rejects Templates whose stored package name is an unscoped slug, and the running-Gateway path cannot match them to the catalog.

## User Impact

User impact: the OpenClaw CLI accepts the publisher-qualified command shown on ClawHub, including creator-published Templates stored under an unscoped name. Local directory and CLAW.md sources are unchanged.

This requires the ClawHub registry change in https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4616 (merged and deployed). https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4622 handles deleted scoped predecessors found during live verification. This PR does not publish an npm release by itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the human-facing reference against the current publisher, then bind the plan, trust and archive checks to the registry's stored package identity. A live exact package name takes precedence; another publisher cannot claim the alias. When the Gateway owns local state, match the catalog's publisher-qualified reference and send its stored package name to the existing Add plan/apply handlers.

## Evidence

- Before: new gateway-owner regression failed on the base revision; candidate passed. Unscoped metadata returned for the publisher-qualified request previously failed identity validation.
- After: the built CLI at `fc3f8851a6e` ran `templates add @ameliomansour/openclaw-music-manager --dry-run --json` against live production in disposable state. Exit 0, `readiness.ready: true`, no blockers or diagnostics. The registry returns stored name `openclaw-music-manager`; archive verification and dependency planning completed.
- Focused source-acquisition and gateway-owner tests: 68 passed. Coverage includes publisher mismatch rejection and keeping archive/trust identity bound to the stored name.
- `pnpm check:changed`: changed-file formatting, lint, core/test typechecks, import-cycle and other guards passed. The full-tree dead-export scan failed on unchanged QA/Telegram/release-script exports; these are outside this patch (full results retained locally). PR CI is the broad verification gate.

No operator Gateway or live agent state was modified. The original CLI proof below was a dry-run; actual Gateway verification and its limitations follow.


### Real Gateway Add verification

The exact candidate ran `openclaw templates add @ameliomansour/myfitnessclaw --agent-id publisher-qualified-proof --json` against production ClawHub and a disposable running Gateway with isolated HOME/config/state. Catalog resolution, bound review, config commits and declared workspace-file copies completed. Readback shows MyFitnessClaw identity/description plus AGENTS.md, IDENTITY.md, SOUL.md, avatar, skills, reference and templates.

The CLI returned exit 1 / `status: partial`, `agentRetained: true`, **without** `initializationPending`: its opening greeting could not authenticate to the AI service because this clean runtime intentionally had no model credentials. This is installed-state and actual Gateway routing proof, not a successful model greeting. No Add was replayed; both disposable Gateways were stopped.

An earlier disposable test exposed an inherited macOS workspace-alias defect: an admitted `/tmp` path is compared against canonical `/private/tmp` and yields `workspace_collision`. A bounded planner probe reproduced that distinction; `src/templates/lifecycle.ts` and `gateway-add-apply.ts` are unchanged from main. The separate canonical-path test passed that boundary. The original partial agent was retained, not duplicated.

ClawHub backend deployment [43518722749](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/actions/runs/43518722749) succeeded at `8a0fe3b64f210c6f04fdaeda64c69890f877a15f`, including rollout restore verification. Production qualified myfitnessclaw returns 200, wrong publisher 404, live scoped hopper 200 with its exact stored name.

prs.title: fix: archived conversations are missing from Cmd+K search
prs.body:
Related: #195574

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes archived conversations missing from Cmd+K when stored titles or available indexed messages match, without allowing newer weak metadata matches to hide an older exact title.

## User Impact

Cmd+K finds active and archived conversations, labels archived results, and prefers active sessions only when relevance is equal. Metadata relevance is applied before the ten-result cutoff. Opening preserves archived/read-only state, sidebar exclusion and Unarchive. Section-editor membership stays active-only.

Cold-stored messages remain unsearchable until restored; stored titles remain searchable without restoration. Existing access, owner/participant and discovery exclusions remain unchanged. The feature adds no database schema/migration, dependency, persisted configuration, retention or product resource-budget change. The authorized base integration inherits upstream changes; it does not execute migrations or modify live state. The RPC adds explicit `sortBy: "relevance"`; ordinary chronological ordering remains unchanged. No Involving me toggle is introduced.

**Not merge-ready:** the original 20% performance gate remains failed, first-use qualification is unresolved, and current-head broad CI is pending. The generated-file conflict is resolved and GitHub reports mergeable, but blocked. Publication was authorized without a performance waiver. No PR merge, release, deployment or live-node operation has occurred.

## Why This Change Was Made

Archive inclusion belongs to the palette discovery scope; ranking, access, navigation and sidebar owners retain their responsibilities. Search avoids unused facets, repeated selections, duplicate serialization and unnecessary snippet work. SQLite reads bounded hits/snippets in one snapshot using existing prepared builders and the admitted full-text owner; PostgreSQL retains its single-query path.

The verified P2 was a cutoff-order bug: ten recent archived prefixes hid an older exact title before browser ranking. The palette now requests explicit relevance ordering. Existing Gateway selection applies shared normalized exact/prefix/substring ranking before partition/global limits, then active status, recency and stable key ties. It reuses bounded top-k merging and the field cache: no fetch-all browser roster, extra metadata RPC, increased result limit or cross-request authority cache. `source` remains diagnostics-only.

## Evidence

### Current published reconciliation

- **Head:** `6cb418ef18284a596b4cb189f63cc6762e477841`; tree `e9a9e4a76c756defef59607afae5c86e9e9ba2ee`, identical to reviewed local commit `812d6bf33c07c0f81d120f8b4bafa8badb0f6ea0`. Clean worktree verified after publication.
- Integrated pinned main `a846d93c689358a86cebeba091d937bbc05539fe` to resolve the actual generated-predicate conflict. Canonical main output bootstrapped the generator, then `gateway:validators:gen` and `gateway:validators:check` regenerated and verified the final file. No hand-edited predicate content. Obsolete imported-planner allocation removed because planner tooling is now inherited from main.
- **81/81 focused tests**, eight files: 27 Gateway selection/search/order/startup, 20 protocol, two broker and 32 palette tests. Current test accounting is **488/488** net lines against pinned main (400 ordinary +88 existing P2 allowance); no increased limits or weakened assertions.
- **Real production-UI/isolated-Gateway flow 1/1 passed** after full rebuild: 225 synthetic sessions, five agents, 22 queries. The older exact active Heron appears first among ten metadata results with nine archived prefixes and zero transcript matches. Archived navigation, active-sidebar exclusion, section membership, access/discovery exclusions and cold conservation pass. Served production-entry SHA matches built assets.
- Core/UI types, scoped lint/format, generator determinism, source i18n verification and diff checks pass. Current inherited i18n baseline: 12,334 keys and 63 existing raw-copy entries. No baseline exception added.
- **Fresh independent AutoReview, GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2:** two passes over the candidate against pinned main, no actionable scoped findings. Supplied-context limitations remain explicit; this does not certify performance. Prior ClawSweeper review on `49255ada` reports Findings None and confirms the cutoff P2 resolved; it is historical, not a review of this new head.

### Reproduction and visual evidence

The P2 was independently reproduced on `c292a06`: ten newer archived Heron notes titles filled the metadata response, hiding the eight-day-old active exact Heron, with zero transcript hits. The real product regression failed before and passed after repair. Tests also cover offsets/totals, exclusions, equal-rank active preference, archived exact versus active prefix, rename invalidation and unchanged chronological mode.

[Overflow before/after proof and review response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198421#issuecomment-6865157170) and [original archive-discovery proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198421#issuecomment-6862668476) were inspected, delivered in Team, uploaded as `roboclaw-bot`, and verified by exact asset IDs, bytes and rendered images. The rebuilt current UI screenshot was also inspected; authored reconciliation changes do not alter the demonstrated outcome. Existing evidence was not reuploaded.

### UI asset-size gate — separate from search latency

The old-head manual run found attributable UI byte growth. Equivalent ranking loops, removal of a redundant empty-field filter and forwarding the optional sort in the existing request object reduce bytes without changing relevance or limits.

The first local comparison had mismatched generated plugin inventories (packaged versus standalone settings-only); that failure and attribution are retained, not counted as a pass. The canonical checker then compared matching standalone artifact classes against pinned main, with the task-owned packaged directory restored afterward:

- startup gzip: 90,850→90,850 B;
- chat boot gzip: 1,314,886→1,314,913 B (+27);
- new boot gzip: 816,355→816,402 B (+47);
- CSS gzip: 332,471→332,464 B (-7); raw CSS and request counts unchanged.

**Qualified owner check passed with the existing 64-byte relative allowance unchanged.** Existing main absolute-size warnings remain. This is not RPC latency acceptance.

### Current-head CI

Normal PR CI now starts following conflict resolution. The observed complete inventory for `6cb418ef` initially contains 48 checks/statuses: 11 passed, 21 skipped/neutral and 16 pending, no observed failures at that snapshot. This is an evolving inventory, not final broad validation. [Current checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198421/checks); [normal CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43514566999). Dependency and security-sensitive reviews pass; aggregate CI remains pending. No prior-head result is counted as a current-head pass.

### Retained predecessor failures and proof

The manually dispatched [run 43510060715](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43510060715) verified workload checkout `49255ada` (workflow source was different), selected 267 jobs, and was cancelled once when replacing the obsolete run through base reconciliation; 180 jobs were cancelled. **It is not green.** Five completed failures remain recorded:

- strict release i18n fallback drift; source PR i18n verification passes, generated release locale output was not committed;
- UI asset gate, addressed locally by the qualified comparison above;
- exports/static analysis, including a proxy export removed by inherited upstream `49c99cf91a4df47`; new-head CI must validate the complete lane;
- Node broker child exit-code failure and Gateway startup sessions.list timeout. Their Bun siblings and current focused local Node replays pass, but a causal fix or identical hosted-runtime reproduction is **not established**. No timeout increase or assertion weakening.

On older `c292a06`, 162 statuses settled: 90 success, 68 skipped, one neutral, three failed. Four PostgreSQL conformance jobs, build, architecture/ratchets, three UI shards, two UI E2E shards and types/lint passed. [Planner validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43497186742/job/132133254224) passed 26/26. Initial proof was 46/46; native-owner repair 30/30, sidebar 118/118, isolated PostgreSQL search 4/4; cutoff repair 73/73 plus real UI 1/1. These remain historical.

Those three older reds were the [Talk shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43497186973/job/132134210459) and two aggregate gates. Four after-cancel signatures match [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43482629206/job/132083526517). Automatic classification remained unknown because its newer comparison run lacked that job name. Manual evidence did not override classification; `ALLOW_KNOWN_MAIN_RED` was false. No Talk repair or gate waiver is claimed.

### Performance — original gate remains failed

Baseline `4ab02e3c0879aa5efb51e664b5e57c092144c9ed`; five serial source-pinned pairs, **5,160 authenticated RPCs**, 100 warm samples/source/scope/query. Corpus: 3,500 sessions (500 active/3,000 archived), five agents, 3,495 indexed messages and five physically cold transcripts. Two-worker/heap limits unchanged; exact results/caps and zero cold restoration verified. Measurements predate repairs; no current-head latency pass is claimed.

| Query | Original active median / p95 ms | Measured candidate all median / p95 ms | Original 20% gate |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Common metadata | 0.488 / 3.192 | 0.424 / 4.070 | **Fail: p95 +27.5%** |
| Archive metadata | 0.352 / 3.342 | 0.344 / 4.000 | Pass; p95 +19.7%, near threshold |
| Common indexed | 8.525 / 16.341 | 7.830 / 16.479 | Pass |
| Archive indexed | 5.447 / 11.348 | 7.307 / 11.941 | **Fail: median +34.2%** |
| Absent indexed | 4.535 / 10.849 | 3.236 / 8.638 | Pass |
| Cold-only | 4.284 / 9.943 | 3.219 / 7.669 | Pass |

**4/6 primary cells pass; overall acceptance does not.** Archive-message medians rose in all five pairs, four by at least 20%. Returning 25 hits versus zero adds work but does not waive the gate. First-use **63.786→536.248 ms** mixes two process-first and three process-second observations per source; it is not an eightfold measured startup regression. Adverse second-request and first-use results remain unresolved.

Preparation includes changed-owner source pins and explicit `--metadata-sort relevance` for the palette workload. After full base integration, future qualification must use complete baseline/current source cohorts, not old selective overlays. Source-only preflight is not timing proof. No new matrix was run on an unqualified host.

**Exact isolated-capacity blocker:** configured ASCII Box failed before lease acquisition because `ASCII_BOX_API_KEY` was unavailable. Existing managed-node placement requires an operator update/reconnect that remains unauthorized. No paid fallback or live-node change was attempted. Read-only investigation identified standard public GitHub-hosted compute as a possible future route, but no existing workflow runs this archive-search experiment; reviewed orchestration and cost/artifact qualification would be needed. That route was not implemented or dispatched and is not claimed as qualified capacity.

<details>
<summary>Retained measurement limitations</summary>

Historical quantiles were reproduced from 7,440 RPC samples. A 1,960-RPC same-source null failed cached p95 by +265.1%, largely after dispatch with zero owner tasks. A separate client loop demonstrated coupling, but another 1,960-RPC null still failed cached p95 (+37.3%, +39.1%) and first-use cells. These constrain attribution, never waive failures. Whole-process CPU is not request-self CPU; kernel flush is unobserved. Later early cache retirements were metadata invalidations, not TTL expiry; earlier retirements remain unattributed.

No filtering, greener retry, threshold change, worker/heap increase or TTL extension was accepted. Rejected SQL/batching/cold-count/ordering/identity-startup prototypes were restored after adverse results. Retained preparation reduces warm builder calls 7→1 (hit)/6→0 (miss), but does not clear acceptance. The separate UI asset check is not the search-latency gate.

</details>

## Attribution

Requested and scoped by @hannesrudolph; AI-assisted implementation and verification by RoboClaw.

prs.title: fix(update): 2026.9.x updates report failure after installing the next release
prs.body:
Related: #197526

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: updating from published 2026.9.x releases (including the current extended-stable 2026.9.37) to current main fails with `post-update-failed` and "Shared state migration did not finish: expected schema 40, found missing", even though the update installed and the Gateway is healthy.

## User Impact

User impact: 2026.9.x users, including everyone on extended-stable 9.36/9.37, can update to the next release without a false failure, a `state-migrated-no-rollback` outcome, or a manual `openclaw update repair`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197526 made the candidate's schema-version reply for released drivers keep only rows with known ownership, so plugin stores such as Workboard stop failing the 2026.11.3 verifier. Published 2026.9.x drivers parse the candidate's discovery plan with a schema that only knows `spellings`, so the ownership fields are stripped before they send the plan back to the candidate's `versions` worker. The filter then dropped the shared row (and agent rows), and the 9.x verifier reported the shared schema as missing.

The candidate's own discovery is the authority for ownership. The update-state worker's `discover` mode (the cross-version entry released drivers call) now writes a small private ownership record into the driver-supplied staging root; the `versions` worker rehydrates stripped ownership from it (the shared database always counts as global), so the unchanged #197526 filter keeps shared and agent rows and still excludes Workboard. In-process discovery (backups, current inspection) is unchanged and writes nothing. The record's filename is allowlisted for abandoned-snapshot reclamation so a crashed inspection tree stays reclaimable. 2026.10.x drivers round-trip `owners` but not `registeredPaths`; the same rehydration restores their registered agent databases, and 2026.11.x drivers are unaffected.

## Evidence

All proof below ran on the exact final head **`daaf24724a8`** (fix commits merged with `origin/main` `3f3769a9355`, including #198148, which touches the same discovery function), unless a row says otherwise. `src/infra/update-candidate-state.ts` is byte-identical to main; discovery writes and versions reads the ownership record only in the update-state worker (the cross-version boundary).

- **Regression found** by the daily update matrix on main `a48a3175600`: published 9.9, 9.36 (`--channel stable`), 9.37 (`--channel stable`) and 9.5 updaters ended `rc=1 post-update-failed` (Gateway healthy on the new version). All passed on `46350dafd29` the day before #197526 landed.
- **Unit, head `daaf24724a8`** (Linux box checkout): red/green against the base production files from `3f3769a9355`. The new stripped-plan regressions (with and without a discovery record), the absent-shared-state case and the reclamation case fail on base and pass on the head; 30 of 31 tests in the three touched test files pass on the head. The one failure, `budgets schema inspection for configured cache`, fails identically on base and is environmental (box `umask 0002` makes its temp ancestor group-writable); the same file passes 19/19 on macOS. Locally on the same head: 64 tests across local-schema, reclamation, budget, `update-database-backup-engine` and `backup-database-resources` pass; type-aware oxlint on every changed file, the max-lines ratchet, oxfmt and `tsgo:core` are clean.
- **Native, Crabbox AWS, published updater → `daaf24724a8` packaged as 2026.11.30:**

| Published updater | Base `a48a3175600` | Head `daaf24724a8` |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.9.36 `--channel stable` | rc=1 post-update-failed | rc=0, 432 s, Gateway ready |
| 2026.9.37 `--channel stable` | rc=1 post-update-failed | rc=0, 439 s, Gateway ready |
| 2026.11.3 (owners path, control) | rc=0 | rc=0, 276 s, Gateway ready |

  Earlier native runs on pre-merge head `82355274715` also passed 2026.9.9 (rc=0, 435 s) and 2026.9.5 (rc=0, 186 s).
- **Review on head `daaf24724a8`:** autoreview scoped-clean (P0–P2) and an independent Codex review with no findings. Earlier rounds found and fixed: publishing every stripped row would still fail 9.x installs that have Workboard (fixed by the ownership record); the record blocked abandoned-tree reclamation (allowlisted); writing it from in-process discovery broke backup callers with uncreated or owned staging roots (moved to worker discovery only); the first CI run's lint shards failed in runner setup (Git upgrade lacked `--no-lazy-fetch`), but local type-aware oxlint then showed a real `max-lines` overflow in `update-candidate-state.ts` from this diff, fixed by moving rehydration into the worker; a madge type-import cycle that move introduced (caught by CI `check-guards-architecture` on `fb1c671b0d7`) is removed with a structural generic type. CI `ci-gate` passed on `daaf24724a8`.

prs.title: chore: stabilize SQLite lifecycle verification during deletion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SQLite lifecycle verifier can race with its own agent run while deleting a session. Gateway correctly rejects the changed session, but the verifier fails before checking the final state.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. This repairs internal lifecycle verification needed by #197334 without weakening the final-state assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wait for that owned run to settle and retry deletion once, only for the exact, correlated `session-changed` response. Other errors and a second rejection still fail. The verifier still requires successful deletion, stable session absence, and empty history. Superseded-history handling lives in the shared proof helper.

This changes test support only. Following review, the callback-only replay tests and redundant CLI fixture rename were removed.

## Evidence

On `fdbc70597`, the canonical runtime build, UI build, CLI transcript cases (9/9), SQLite helper cases (6/6), and the real Gateway built-CLI lifecycle proof (1/1) passed. The initial missing-UI setup timeout and successful same-head rerun are recorded in the [qualification report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197609#issuecomment-6823923953).

Current head `bc08a4c7c` only removes the reviewed redundant tests/allocation and restores the upstream CLI fixture. Both real verifier source files are byte-for-byte unchanged from that qualified head. The resulting cleanup passed the CLI cases (9/9), formatting, and test-line budget; it has not received a new full local build or a successful additional native autoreview.

[Exact-head CI run 43237911264](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43237911264) passed all 31 non-skipped jobs, including the real Gateway built-CLI lifecycle proof (1/1), build artifacts, type checks, and lint. [ClawSweeper's exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197609#issuecomment-6817957829) found no actionable defects. [Security Review attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43239220762/attempts/2) passed after recovery from the first attempt's GitHub API 503.

The race remains in the verifier on main `2f6061c9bc760d2137ac1dd7abc3a11a2d613220`; the [recorded failure on #197334](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43271819026/job/131371035235) matches the narrow retry. Review of the full two-file change found no blocking correctness issues. No additional local runtime proof was run during maintainer review; exact-head CI supplies that evidence.

Related: #197334. That naming PR no longer carries this test repair.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in screenshot fallback, a Browser panel action waits a fixed 350 ms before the refresh, even when the action itself was slow.

## User Impact

User impact: fallback frames refresh sooner after an action. Typing, clicks, wheel and a live screencast are unchanged. No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: feat(macos): sign in with OpenClaw ID and approve this Mac as your device
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Mac can join an OpenClaw ID claw only as a node with a separate invite, and nobody signs in. That isn't how a person uses their own Mac. Josh approved sign-in-first enrollment on 2026-11-11: the person signs in and the Mac becomes their own device.

## User Impact

- **Sign in with OpenClaw ID** in onboarding (and Settings for an existing Tailscale/token/SSH Mac) now does this:
  1. Signs in natively.
  2. Lists the person's claws.
  3. Makes this Mac an **owner device** of the chosen claw, either by comparing six digits with a device that already has access or by entering the recovery kit.
- The Mac then reaches chat and the dashboard over OpenClaw ID with its own key and runs tools through its bound node. There's no VPN and no Gateway token.
- Settings → Connection gets an OpenClaw ID section with these actions:
  - Stop using this Mac for tools, or use it again.
  - Remove this Mac.
  - Sign in again, shown when a tools-off Mac's Discovery session has ended.
  - Switch to OpenClaw ID (migration from a Tailscale, token or SSH connection).
- Migration *replaces* the existing connection and clears its saved Gateway token and password. Tailscale itself is untouched, and going back means Change connection… with a new setup code.
- The headless node-invite path (#196759) is unchanged and is still offered as "Use a node invitation".

**Not live-testable yet:**
- The staging Mac OAuth client is registered (`DulSrXtaYtPaLEnzEyHGuAHpVNWmaNbf`), but Discovery staging only accepts its tokens after openclaw/discovery#14 is deployed.
- The node binding in `start` and `add_owner_device` needs openclaw/discovery#13 and this protocol stack (#197573) deployed.
- Until then, sign-in reaches the issuer, and every Discovery call is refused.

**Stacking:** stacked on #197585 (`feat/ocid-mac-ocid-connection`). The protocol side is #197573 (`node` on the SAS `start` and on `add_owner_device`, and the approver UI).

**Member invite join is not in this PR.** It goes in a second stacked PR to keep this one reviewable. A member account that picks a claw here gets "Ask for an invite" instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mac follows the protocol's "Owner device node" design (enrollment.md). It holds three keys, each in its own Keychain service, and none of them ever goes over the node bridge:
- D_mac signs.
- W_mac is its owner peer key, used for chat and the dashboard.
- W_node is the only key the node worker sees, and it never carries human authority.

Enrollment works like this:
- **SAS.** The Mac is the new-device side of the owner-browser SAS. `start` carries `node {peer_key: W_node, description}`, so the compared digits bind all three keys and the tool surface. Before the Mac opens the sealed handoff, the person must confirm the digits on the Mac too. The handoff's binding must then verify under its root for this claw and hostname, and its cert must name this D and W.
- **Recovery kit.** R is derived in-process from the typed code or a kit file. If fp(R) isn't the descriptor's root, nothing is signed. R signs `OwnerDeviceCert` and `add_owner_device {cert, node}` at snapshot seq + 1, and they're sent as a `root_statement`. A `seq_conflict` notice is answered by re-signing at the re-read verified snapshot's seq + 1 (up to 3 times).
  - R is dropped when the attempt ends: admitted, refused, cancelled or after 2 minutes. The deadline is checked again right before every signature.
  - R is never stored, logged or sent. CryptoKit-held key bytes can't be explicitly zeroed (the same limit as the browser's WebCrypto key); the seed and decoded secret are zeroed. The typed `String` can't be zeroed either.
- **Admission.** The Mac is admitted only when the claw's K_gw-signed snapshot lists W_mac as an owner peer key and W_node in `node_peer_keys`. The existing join-completion owner then switches the primary connection and opens the dashboard.

The Swift ports (JCS statements, kit decode, R derivation, SAS commitment, transcript, code, AES-GCM handoff and peer-key proof) are checked byte for byte against vectors generated from the TypeScript protocol at #197573.

## Evidence

All build and test runs were on the Mac Studio in a separate checkout, built with `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1`.
- Builds: `swift build --build-tests` for `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` and for `apps/macos` (both green).
- Shared tests: `OpenClawID` filter, 45 tests in 6 suites, 8 consecutive green runs at `3d4dabcb9221`.
  - `OpenClawIDOwnerEnrollmentTests` checks the kit, root, SAS and statement vectors.
  - It also covers: the handoff must name this claw and device; kit seq_conflict re-sign; wrong kit or invalid code signs nothing; SAS opens the handoff only after the code is confirmed on the Mac (a mismatch aborts and pins nothing); a declined request.
- App tests: 45 tests in 9 suites green, run in the sandbox (`sandbox-exec`: no network or Keychain).
  - Includes the new `OnboardingOpenClawIDSignInTests`: build config, the callback's state and issuer checks, claw routing by relationship, no claws, cancelled sign-in, invalid kit installs nothing, the automatic approval wait, and switching to the kit cancels the wait.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` and `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` are clean. The native i18n baseline was regenerated.
- Inherited from the base: `OnboardingPageTests` "verified node setup…" hangs in the sandbox inside `DashboardManager.shared` init. It hangs the same way on #197585's head.
- Review:
  - **pr-simplify:** no architecture removed. One owner per responsibility: crypto port, Discovery account calls, enrollment client, route refresh, owner actions, sign-in, device store, Settings model.
  - **Astra autoreview:** 5 findings, all verified and fixed. P0: confirm the SAS code on the Mac before opening the handoff. P1: reconcile a self-removal whose answer is lost. P1: Sign in again for a tools-off Mac. P2: the route re-reads the node key and session on every verification. P2: kit deadline across awaits.

Renders are real views with fixture data from the sandboxed render harness; screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197630#issuecomment-6818359924 (local copies: `~/.openclaw/workspace/reports/ocid-mac-sign-in-first-mockups/impl/`). Recovery-kit entry can't be rendered there: `NSSecureTextField` blocks on the window-server lookup the sandbox denies. Its render is the mockup of the same view.

### Live-proof checklist (blocked on discovery#13 + #14 deploy)
- [ ] Sign in on staging; the claw picker lists the owned claw.
- [ ] SAS approve from the original local Control UI. The approval dialog shows "will also be able to run tools", the codes match on both screens, and the Mac pins and connects.
- [ ] Expected chat attribution: on main every OpenClaw ID owner device maps to the **shared Owner profile** (`gateway-owner-profile.ts`, `openclawIdOwner`). The Mac's chat should land there with owner/admin scopes, not as an accountless person. Personal-profile mapping is OCF-510, out of scope.
- [ ] The node connects with W_node, and Access shows it as this device's node.
- [ ] Recovery-kit enrollment works. Owners see "Recovery kit used". A wrong kit shows "That recovery code didn't work".
- [ ] Settings: stop tools, then use tools again; remove the Mac (connection ends, keys and primary cleared).
- [ ] Migration from a Tailscale connection: the token is cleared and Tailscale is still running.

### Known gaps
- Member invite join comes in the stacked follow-up PR.
- A Mac with tools off reads the claw with the person's 12-hour Discovery session. After it ends, Settings offers Sign in again; chat reconnects fail until then.
- Self-removal whose answer is lost is reconciled from Discovery's snapshot. If that also can't be read, Settings shows an error rather than guessing.
- The token is kept only as a Discovery session in the Keychain. The ID token itself is never stored.

Screenshots: [inspected before/after comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197630#issuecomment-6866363619).

prs.title: feat(ios): open matching chats from push notifications
prs.body:
Related: #193113

## What Problem This Solves

An ordinary iOS push notification opens the app but does not take someone to the chat the notification is about.

## User Impact

A push with an optional session destination can open that existing chat on the currently connected Gateway, after checking the current profile's access, without sending a message. Notifications without a destination keep their existing behavior. Missing, inaccessible, or wrong-Gateway destinations leave the current screen unchanged; taps do not automatically switch Gateways.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing `push.test` path and `openclaw nodes push --session <key>` rather than adding a general notification operation or arbitrary deep links. The Gateway resolves the destination and supplies its own identity. APNs sends revalidate through the existing session-read owner, and iOS resolves the destination on its current authenticated route before calling the existing `openChat` owner. Cold-launch handoff and reconnect use existing lifecycle owners, with duplicate-tap suppression and Watch/approval precedence preserved.

This does not add counters, registrations, or background wakes. The public changes in #193491 (unread badges) and #193033 (main-chat discovery) were inspected; this change preserves those owners. The API direction is presented for maintainer review, not as an already accepted product decision.

## Evidence

- Red/green regression: the new optional destination was rejected by the original closed request schema; it passes with the schema and generated runtime validators updated.
- **100 focused tests passed across five files:** protocol schema, APNs payload/refusal behavior, Gateway push handling, existing session visibility, and CLI option forwarding. The CLI test wrapper also completed its runtime build. These are synthetic/mocked boundary tests, not real APNs or iPhone acceptance.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed using workspace-local Node 26.12.1.
- Targeted typed lint passed for all eight changed TypeScript files; TypeScript/Markdown formatting, the documentation index, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review, P0–P3: the initial finding was fixed; a fresh review reported no actionable findings. The final handler suite was rerun after the lint repair.

**Ready for review / acceptance remains pending:** the retained signed integration below reproduces the exact effective source tree used for the Mac integration proof; the subsequent CI repair changes only comments and test-budget metadata. Real APNs/iPhone foreground/background/cold-launch tap flows and revoked-pairing behavior remain unverified for this PR, and there are no device before/after captures. Exact published-head CI and owning acceptance remain outstanding. This PR is ready for review; auto-merge remains off.

### Mac validation and signed source update

Signed integration head: `81b5e47967a092c610bdcb456549a7a633270f36`; source tree: `dbb3179fcbe0cafc9113fa1f37a9f80d5570b550`, exactly matching the retained native-tested candidate. The contributor’s original head and ancestry are preserved. Existing results are reused through verified tree equality; no new native run is claimed.

The local candidate incorporates main `154d60ec2bc612db80a39c13b61466a64acfc527`, preserves main's removal of the dead delegate URL queue, and addresses three findings:

- Retain a selected notification tap when a socket failure resumes its RPC before the model receives disconnection. An actual identity-RPC disconnect reproduced the original loss.
- Return synchronous send parameters from the prepared session reader, then await APNs outside that callback. A regression using the real prepared-read owner failed before this repair with “Session row read consumers must remain synchronous.” Final-send authority checks remain intact.
- Reconcile the initial agent roster through the existing chat-routing restore task before applying notification focus. The matched cold queued-tap control opened the destination and then lost both visible and saved focus when retiring the previous agent; the concurrent-tap variant passed in that control observation.

Validation:

- **5/5 expanded native delivery cases passed, zero skips:** both disconnect/reconnect paths, authoritative refusal, cold queued-tap retirement, and a tap during roster hydration. This is three Swift Testing functions, not five functions. The matched roster control had one pass and one intended failure.
