prs.title: feat(message): let operators confine group-turn sends to the current conversation
prs.body:
Related: #190557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a group turn's `message` send can reach the owner's DM or another chat when the operator wants group turns kept in their own conversation, because the existing `crossContext` switches confine every kind of turn or none.

## User Impact

User impact: existing configs behave exactly as on main; no default changes. An operator who sets `tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes: ["group", "channel"]`, globally or per agent, gets group and channel turns that can only send to their own conversation. Any other target, on the same provider or another one, fails with `message_cross_context_denied` before a transport call. DM turns keep their current permissions. Separately, under the existing `allowWithinProvider: false`, a Telegram forum-topic send or poll that names the chat id with the current topic's `threadId`, or inherits it, is no longer denied. Other actions from a topic turn, such as renaming a topic, still have to name the current topic, as on main. Two deliberate tightenings apply under `allowWithinProvider: false`, or when group turns are confined. A turn in a Telegram forum topic can no longer create a forum topic in that chat, even through its own topic target, which main allows; the new topic is a sibling conversation in the base chat, and a turn bound to the chat itself still can. Telegram topic creation and topic edits that name another chat through `chatId`, `chat_id` or `channel_id` are denied. In every mode, a target that disagrees with one of those fields is refused as conflicting input. A numeric `target`, `to` or `channelId` is now read as its string, so it follows the same rules as the string: with a target the target wins, and alone it is the destination the check judges. Before, a numeric `channelId` skipped the check and Telegram acted on it, and a numeric `to` or `target` was dropped for the current conversation. A number that is not a safe integer is refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision (4b90fc67b80) flipped the shipped `allowWithinProvider` default to deny. That was the wrong shape. It reversed a deliberate default (#149875, #150157), it broke the required-delivery and context-isolation fixtures, and it changed bound broadcasts. My claim in the old body that broadcasts were exempt was wrong: child sends carry `toolContext` into the same check. Review also found a real matcher bug: the same-provider check ignored `threadId`, so a same-topic Telegram send could be denied.

This revision keeps the default and adds an opt-in inside the existing owner, `enforceCrossContextPolicy`:

- `confineChatTypes` keys on the conversation kind the host reports for the turn (`toolContext.currentChatType`). A listed kind may only target its own conversation; this overrides both `allowWithinProvider` and `allowAcrossProviders`. Unlisted kinds, and turns with no reported kind, keep those flags. A `POST /tools/invoke` call bound by the conversation headers reports the bound target's kind, so it is confined like a turn from that conversation. A per-agent list replaces the global one through the existing per-agent merge; `[]` lifts it.
- Broadcast child sends already go through this check, so a confined broadcast delivers the current conversation and reports a denial for every other target. There is no runner change.
- When same-provider sends are restricted, the check resolves the thread the send will actually use, with the same `resolveAndApplyOutboundThreadId` that delivery uses (on a copy of the params), and names the destination with the channel's own `resolveCurrentChannelId`. Policy and delivery now judge the same destination. Only `send` and `poll` are judged by that thread alone, because the runner delivers them into it. Other guarded actions only hand the thread to the plugin, so they are judged on their requested target as on main, and a thread they carry can only narrow that. `topic-create` must also name the current conversation through its parent chat, resolved with the channel's own conversation grammar (core's `resolveSessionConversation`, which asks `messaging.resolveSessionConversation`), because Telegram creates the topic in the base chat whatever topic or thread the request names. Telegram declares `chatId`, `chat_id` and `channel_id` as delivery-target aliases for `topic-create` and `topic-edit`, because its handler takes the chat from them ahead of the target. Normalization therefore canonicalizes them before the check, the same way the thread spellings are folded. Normalization also stringifies exact integer values of `target`, `to` and `channelId` before folding them: Telegram's chat reader accepts numbers, while the fold and the check read only strings.
  - When a Telegram target's encoded topic and an explicit `threadId` disagree, the check follows Telegram's delivery precedence: the explicit thread wins. Telegram's `resolveCurrentChannelId` now goes through `formatTelegramDeliveryTarget`, the helper Telegram already uses to name a delivered send (moved unchanged into `targets.ts`).
  - The shared param readers accept each key's snake_case form, and Telegram's handler reads `messageThreadId` or `message_thread_id` before `threadId` or `thread_id`. Action normalization now folds every one of those four spellings into one string `threadId` before any check, including a numeric `threadId`, which core's string reader would otherwise skip. Values that disagree are refused, and so is any value alongside an explicit `threadId: null`. On any channel, an action carrying only an alias, or a numeric `threadId`, gets that value as its string `threadId`.

What changed since `1cb5e029db3` (2026-11-10): `POST /tools/invoke` now reports the kind of the conversation its headers bind it to, so `confineChatTypes` applies to header-bound direct calls as it does to a turn from that conversation (`9aadc2bbc5c`). The Bot API traces at `1cb5e029db3` showed the gap: with only `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` set and the topic-A headers, all nine direct calls were delivered, including a `sendMessage` to the owner DM and `editForumTopic` and `createForumTopic` on it. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` now sets `currentChatType` on the direct-invocation surface from the bound target, with the resolver outbound target resolution already uses, `inferChatTypeFromTarget` (now exported from `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`; for Telegram it asks the plugin's `parseTelegramTarget`). Calls without the headers, the RPC `tools.invoke` and the MCP loopback surface are unchanged. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` fails on `1cb5e029db3` (`promise resolved "{ content: [ { …(2) } ], …(1) }" instead of rejecting` for a sibling-topic send from a header-bound call) and passes on this head; `92aee940aa8` raises the test-line allocation by its 62 lines.

pr-simplify: compared with the first revision, the default flip and its three default-denial tests are gone. No new plugin API, no runner or broadcast changes. Every remaining test group fails on a named control (below). The remaining growth is one config field (4 schema paths), the denial reason text, thread-aware matching, the tests (493 net test lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/message-cross-context-confine-chat-types.txt`), and one qa-lab scenario. Against main `9a5df3d60f1`, which this branch is rebased on:

- production source +194 −37 (`outbound-policy.ts` +86 −11; `tool-resolution.ts` +11 −1 and `targets.ts` +2 −1 for the direct-invocation kind; Telegram `targets.ts`, `channel.ts` and `action-runtime.ts` +40 −24 for the moved delivery-target helper and `channel-actions.ts` +11 for the topic chat aliases; `message-action-normalization.ts` +33; +11 across schema, help and labels)
- tests +493 (`tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` +62)
- qa-lab scenario +172
- docs +18, plus the regenerated config baseline counts and hashes

## Evidence

Focused suite (measured at `470c81210da` against its merge base `19aff5bfd42`; the current head's checks are below): `outbound-policy.test.ts`, `message-action-routing.send-policy.test.ts`, `message-action-runner.broadcast.test.ts`, plus the existing context-isolation fixtures in `message-action-routing.context.test.ts`.

- With the change: 51 of 51 pass, and the 15 context-isolation fixtures pass.
- `outbound-policy.ts` at the merge base: 8 fail, 43 pass.
  - The confined cross-provider, confined same-provider, and confined broadcast cases fail. The broadcast case gets `expected [ 'first', 'second' ] to deeply equal [ 'first' ]`.
  - 5 of the 6 Telegram topic cases fail: the chat id with the current `threadId`, and the chat id inheriting the topic, are falsely denied (`target="telegram:-1001234567890" while bound to "telegram:-1001234567890:topic:42"`). Another `threadId`, another topic target, and `topLevel: true` are let through.
  - The in-band current-topic target passes either way.
- Default flipped to deny (the first revision's shape): 6 of the 51 fail.
  - The existing `preserves required delivery when message-tool-only sends target another conversation` gets the denial instead of `missing reconcileUnknownSend`.
  - The default-delivery cases for sends and broadcasts fail, and so do the direct, untyped and per-agent `[]` cases.
  - 3 of the 15 existing context-isolation fixtures also fail with `Cross-context messaging denied`: `allows directchat target mismatch`, `allows localchat target mismatch` and `blocks cross-context UI handoff for thread-reply to another workspace channel`.

The Telegram cases run the bundled Telegram plugin's real threading code (dry run), under both `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` and `allowWithinProvider: false`.

Conflicting thread inputs (review P1), bound to topic 42:
- `-1001234567890:topic:42` with `threadId: "99"` is denied; on `7742e779d2e` it resolved.
- `-1001234567890:topic:99` with `threadId: "42"` is allowed; on `7742e779d2e` it was denied with `target="telegram:-1001234567890:topic:99" while bound to "telegram:-1001234567890:topic:42"`.
- A topic-42 target with `messageThreadId: "99"` is denied; on `5afec105d94` it resolved.
- A topic-42 target with `message_thread_id: "99"` is denied; on `470c81210da` it resolved. A dry run of the bundled Telegram plugin against a loopback Bot API delivered that send into topic 99 (`sendMessage` with `message_thread_id` 99) in 5 of 5 runs at `470c81210da`.
- A topic-42 target with a numeric `threadId: 99` is denied; on `ee49182a9c1` it resolved (`promise resolved "{ kind: 'send', …(9) }" instead of rejecting`). Through the message tool the schema already turns that number into a string, so this covers callers that pass a number to `runMessageAction`.
- Normalization: `message_thread_id`, `thread_id` or a numeric `threadId` alone becomes a string `threadId`. `{threadId: "42", messageThreadId: "99"}`, `{threadId: "42", message_thread_id: "99"}`, `{thread_id: "42", messageThreadId: "99"}` and `{threadId: null, message_thread_id: "99"}` are refused. The spelling cases fail on `470c81210da` (7 failed, 43 passed). One of them, `threadId` with `messageThreadId`, was already refused there and fails only on the new error text. `thread_id` alone was never a bypass, because core already read it. The numeric cases fail on `ee49182a9c1` (2 failed, 50 passed), and all 52 pass here.

Effect-scoped judgement (review P1) and Telegram chat aliases, through the bundled Telegram plugin under both `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` and `allowWithinProvider: false` (the Telegram table is now 30 rows x 2 switches):
- `topic-create` to `-1001234567890` with `name` from a turn bound to topic 42 is denied; on `561a13dd1af` it was allowed (the review repro), and main denies it under `allowWithinProvider: false`.
- `topic-create` through the topic-42 target, with or without `threadId: "42"`, is denied; main and `af58c646aea` allowed it. From a turn bound to the chat itself, `topic-create` to the chat id is allowed and through a topic-99 target is denied, as on main.
- `topic-edit` naming topic 42 but `chatId` or `channel_id` of another chat is refused as conflicting input; `topic-edit` or `topic-create` with only `chatId` of another chat is denied. All four were allowed on main and on `46c40dc35e6`. A same-chat `chatId` stays allowed. That Telegram acts on the other chat comes from reading the handler; a recorded non-dry handler run shows that chat reaching it.
- Numeric target keys (review P1 at `3a79b762bb7`): from a group turn bound to `-1001234567890`, `topic-create` with target `-1001234567890` and numeric `channelId: -1009999999999` now reaches Telegram's handler with only the chat target; a recorded non-dry handler run shows `channelId` dropped (at `3a79b762bb7` and on main it carried the other chat). Numeric `channelId` of another chat alone is denied for `topic-create` and `topic-edit`; the same chat's numeric id stays allowed. Normalization turns numeric `target`, `to` and `channelId` into strings and refuses `2 ** 60` and `1.5`. Through the model's message tool the agent loop already coerces the number to a string before `execute`, and Tool Search and Code Mode reject it, so a real-Gateway dry run sent `editForumTopic` to the turn's own topic. This covers callers that hand a number to `runMessageAction` or call the tool's `execute` directly (the Gateway's tool-invoke path and in-process callers), as with the numeric `threadId` case.
- Red: 3 of 29 at `561a13dd1af`, 2 of 33 at `af58c646aea`, 4 of 39 at `46c40dc35e6`, 9 of 78 at `3a79b762bb7` (normalization and send-policy tests together); all pass now. Ten mutation controls (dropping each rule or alias, making the parent check always deny or parent-only, leaving `channelId` numeric, or stringifying inexact numbers) are each caught.
- Action by action, under a restricting switch: `send` and `poll` are judged by the resolved thread; `sticker`, `edit`, `delete`, `topic-create` and `topic-edit` by the requested target plus any thread it carries (and `topic-create` also by its parent chat); `react`, `read`, `emoji-list` and `sticker-search` are not guarded.

qa-lab, `qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario message-cross-context-confine-group` (qa-channel, real gateway child, mock-openai):

- With the change: pass, at `79dbe06abbe`, `3a79b762bb7`, `561a13dd1af` and `ee49182a9c1` (merged with main), `470c81210da` and `7742e779d2e`.
  - With no config, a group turn's send reaches the DM.
  - After `config.patch` sets `confineChatTypes: [group]`, the same send returns `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target="dm:alice" while bound to "group:qa-confine-group" (channel=qa-channel). tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes keeps group turns in their current conversation.`, and 0 DM deliveries follow.
  - The group's own sends and a DM turn's send to another group still deliver.
- Policy reverted: fail at the confined step. The DM was delivered.

Checks at `92aee940aa8` (on main `9a5df3d60f1`), 2026-11-10, macOS arm64:

- Focused suites under Node 26.12.1 (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`): `message-action-normalization`, `message-action-routing.send-policy`, `message-action-runner.broadcast`, `outbound-policy`, `schema.help.quality`, Telegram `action-runtime`, `channel-actions.contract` and `targets`, and the new `tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement`: 9 files, 0 failures. The 21 test files that import `tool-resolution.ts` or `outbound/targets.ts`, plus the five `tools-invoke` suites and the four focused `infra/outbound` suites: 30 files, 509 tests, 0 failures.
- `tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` on `1cb5e029db3`: 1 failed, 2 passed (the sibling-topic send from a header-bound call resolves). On this head: 3 of 3.
- CI's ratchets in PR form (`check:baseline-ratchets --base 9a5df3d60f1 --no-merge-base` with `RATCHET_PR_HEAD_SHA`): 10 of 10 ok, line-cap "16 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth", `Test lines OK: 6573693; ceiling: 6573741; slack: 48.` The allocation is exact: 494 is refused (`Test line allocation credit 494 exceeds allowed ceiling growth 493.`). Merged locally with current main `401a1de38b9` (the two generated config-baseline files conflict and were regenerated with `config:docs:gen`): 10 of 10 ok, `Test lines OK: 6629169; ceiling: 6629170; slack: 1.`
- `pnpm tsgo:all` passes. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the changed files. Import cycles: `0 runtime value cycle(s)`, madge `0 cycle(s)`. `config:docs:check`, `config:schema:check` and `plugins:inventory:check` OK.

The pushed head `c4bb370f344` merges main `401a1de38b9` into `92aee940aa8`. The only conflicts were the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` and `config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `config:docs:gen` (`config:docs:check` OK); the merged tree is the one the main-side ratchets above ran on, and it merges with main `6d811790acb` (2026-11-10 18:4xZ) with no conflicts.

CI on `c4bb370f344` (run 42878956154): 56 jobs pass, including `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (`Test lines OK: 6634898; ceiling: 6634908; slack: 10.`), `check-prod-types`, `check-lint` and `checks-node-changed`; the new test passes 3 of 3 in `checks-node-changed-compact-large-20` (Bun shard). Two QA smoke jobs fail, and `ci-gate` fails because they do: `QA Smoke CI (profile 2/6)` on `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` and `profile 3/6` on `subagent-empty-completion-recovery`, both `timed out after 60000ms; final bus-event kinds=[inbound-message,outbound-message,outbound-message]`. Main fails both the same way: built and run locally as CI runs them, 2 of 2 on main `401a1de38b9` for each (measured for #155273), and all 8 PR CI runs that ran those two profiles between 14:11Z and 18:49Z 11-10 (of 275 PR runs in that window) failed them, across four authors' PRs. Filed as #196899: the two scenarios first fail at `e230abd098e` (#196570), whose parent passes them 2 of 2.

- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `message-action-normalization.test.ts` 25.0 s (cold worker cache, 20.7 s of it compiling) and 5.6 s wall, 45 ms and 44 ms of tests; `message-action-routing.send-policy.test.ts` 16.6 s and 11.6 s wall, 7.6 s and 3.3 s of tests; `message-action-runner.broadcast.test.ts` 10.6 s and 10.1 s wall, 2.7 s and 2.6 s of tests; `outbound-policy.test.ts` 5.5 s and 5.5 s wall, 19 ms and 20 ms of tests. ## Bot API traces (2026-11-10)

On this head `92aee940aa8`, built alone, a topic-A turn under `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` puts its same-topic poll and topic rename into topic A. The sibling-topic, other-chat, alias and topic-create calls make no Bot API request at all: after each refusal, the only request is the turn's own reply in topic A. Direct calls through the Gateway's `POST /tools/invoke` that carry the conversation headers for topic A are confined the same way: under `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` alone, and under `allowWithinProvider: false`, every call that names another topic or chat is refused with no Bot API request, where main `9a5df3d60f1` (this branch's merge base) sends the numeric ones to topic 99 or acts on another chat. I ran everything twice, and both runs made the same Bot API requests (method, chat, thread, status) with the same results in all 49 recorded turns and calls.

Setup:
- The real Gateway with the bundled Telegram plugin, built from this head alone (`pnpm build`, buildstamp head `92aee940aa8`, `inputsClean: true`), and main `9a5df3d60f1` built the same way. Every Gateway log line in both runs, 2,981 of 2,981, reports runtime `node` `26.12.1` (macOS arm64).
- The Gateway polls a loopback Bot API (Crabline 0.2.0) through a recording proxy that logs each Bot API request the Gateway sends, with all of its parameters. These are HTTP requests from the Gateway, not the plugin's dry-run mode. Crabline has no `sendPoll`, so the proxy answers that one method itself, with a poll message in the requested chat and thread.
- The model is QA Lab's mock OpenAI provider, in its own process, playing a fixed list of `message` tool calls per turn. Each turn starts from a user message in topic A (thread 42) of a forum supergroup; topic B is thread 99. Chat ids are replaced with `<group>` (the supergroup) and `<owner-dm>` (a private chat).
- Run 1 18:06:58Z to 18:12:07Z, run 2 18:12:07Z to 18:17:13Z.

What these runs also showed, and what they do not cover:
- At `1cb5e029db3` the `confineChatTypes` column was all delivered: with only `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` set and the same headers, all nine calls went out, including a `sendMessage` to `<owner-dm>` and `editForumTopic` and `createForumTopic` on `<owner-dm>`, because `/tools/invoke` reported no conversation kind. `9aadc2bbc5c` makes it report the kind of the conversation its headers bind it to, which gives the refusals above.
- Without the conversation headers, `/tools/invoke` has no current conversation on either build (`Action send requires a target. This turn has no current conversation; pass an explicit target, or reply in normal text.`), so no `crossContext` switch applies. This is unchanged by `9aadc2bbc5c`: in both runs on this head, under `confineChatTypes`, a `threadId` of 99, string or number, went to topic 99, as it does on main. `topic-edit` with `channelId` `<owner-dm>` acted on `<owner-dm>` as a string on both builds, and as a number on this head; main refused the number with that "requires a target" error.
- The Bot API is a loopback, not Telegram. The traces show what the Gateway sent, not how Telegram would answer.

prs.title: fix(telegram): stop Plugin SDK deprecation warnings blamed on the bundled Telegram plugin
prs.body:
Closes #191786
Closes #191785
Related: #174937, #190243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway logs `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` warnings blamed on "Plugin telegram", and the Plugins catalog marks Telegram as using APIs that retire on Dec 31, 2026, when the bundled Telegram plugin loads, or when a Telegram group message from another member steers an active run under collaborative steering.

## User Impact

User impact: Telegram operators no longer see the startup deprecation warning, the `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warning on steering, or the retiring-API notice those two cause. A Telegram group message that steers another member's run under collaborative steering still logs `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint` and `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project`, and those still show as a catalog notice; that read is out of scope here (see "Not in this PR"). Discord, Slack, Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, iMessage, Signal and WhatsApp sessions now list `nativeApprovals` in the agent Runtime capabilities, and Telegram keeps it. Approval authorization, routing and delivery are unchanged. For those 8 channels the Runtime line gains one token, so their system prompt changes once after upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Telegram was the last bundled caller of the sync `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability`. It now uses `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapabilityAsync`, as #174937 did for Discord; `isNativeDeliveryEnabled` wraps the same check.
- `channelPluginHasNativeApprovalPromptUi` read only `native` and `nativeRuntime`. The async factories expose `nativeAsync` and `nativeRuntimeAsync`, so moving Telegram alone would have dropped `nativeApprovals` for Telegram, as it already had for 8 channels. The check now reads all four.
- `prepareFollowupRunToolAuthorityFingerprint` re-read its prepared fingerprint through the deprecated plugin-facing `fingerprint()`. Steering runs in the channel plugin's frame, so the warning and the deprecated-API record landed on Telegram. Core now uses a module-private reader with the same checks; plugin callers of `fingerprint()` still warn.
- Not in this PR: core's sync placement `getMany` (10 call sites, several inside synchronous commit guards; its warning has no fixed removal date), and the collaborative steering read that still calls `projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`. Both need their own core reader and proof.

pr-simplify: no production code removed. One test assertion on a statically defined factory output was removed. No new state, exports or test-only hooks. Production +30 -11 in 3 files; tests +117 -4; three test-line records totaling exactly the 113 net added test lines.

## Evidence

### Gateway run (2026-11-09)

A real Gateway from a built `dist` (`node --trace-deprecation dist/index.js gateway run`, Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64; Vitest also on Node), a local fake Telegram Bot API that grammY talks to as its transport, and a scripted Responses provider that records the `Runtime:` line of every request. Base: main `3855c896edd`. Head: this PR merged onto that main (`git merge-tree --write-tree 3855c896edd d096fe01a3c` = `8f366fba0b5`, no conflicts, same patch-id as this PR's diff). `messages.queue.mode: "steer"`. `channels.discord` and `channels.slack` are `{ enabled: true }` with no tokens, so the Gateway loads both plugins (`5 plugins: discord, memory-core, qa-lab, slack, telegram`) and `channels.status` shows both accounts `configured: false, running: false`. Two runs per scenario per build.

Steering. A run is held open at the provider and a second Telegram message arrives while it is active. In every run the second message is injected into that run (session controller `injection-outcome: consumed`, no "steering rejected" record), the provider gets it in the same session, and Telegram receives both answers.

| scenario | build | DEP_PLUGIN_SDK warnings, all "Plugin telegram" | `plugins.list` notices (of 268 plugins) |
|---|---|---|---|
| group, a second member steers, `allowCollaborativeSteering: true` | main | `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` (startup); at the steer `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint`, `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`, `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` | telegram, those 4 APIs |
| same | this PR | at the steer `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`, `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` | telegram, those 2 APIs |
| DM, the sender steers their own run | main | `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` (startup) | telegram, that 1 API |
| same | this PR | none | none |

Stacks from `--trace-deprecation` on main:
- `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint`: `fingerprint <- read <- prepareLegacyReplySteeringAuthority <- prepareReplyMessageJoin <- runActiveReplySteer`. Gone here.
- `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`: `<- read <- prepareCurrent <- prepareCurrent <- beginPreparedReplyMessageInjectionTarget`. Same stack here.
- `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project`: called from inside that `projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`. Same here.
- Startup: `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability <- channel-*.mjs` module load. Gone here.

Two things this shows that the description had wrong or left out:
- On main, a message from the run's own sender does not reach `fingerprint()` at all. A plain message is a `continue-existing` steer, which goes through `prepareReplyMessageContinuation` (since #177698) and never calls the deprecated reader. The fingerprint warning needs the legacy steering path, which a second member's message reaches under collaborative steering.
- On that collaborative path this PR leaves two warnings in place, `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint` and `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` (the second comes from inside the first), and both still put a retiring-API notice on Telegram in the catalog. The first is the collaborative read already listed under "Not in this PR".

Runtime capabilities. The provider's view of `channel=<id> | channel_capabilities=...`, the same in every run of a build. Discord and Slack turns come from the Gateway `agent` RPC with `channel` set and `deliver: false`, on fresh sessions:

| channel | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| telegram (DM and group turns) | `inlinebuttons,nativeapprovals` | `inlinebuttons,nativeapprovals` |
| discord | `threadbound-acp-spawn,threadbound-subagent-spawn` | `nativeapprovals,threadbound-acp-spawn,threadbound-subagent-spawn` |
| slack | `none` | `nativeapprovals` |

Telegram keeps `nativeApprovals` after moving to the async factory, and Discord and Slack gain it.


- At this head the three changed test files pass 37 of 37 (26 + 7 + 4). With the three source files from `19aff5bfd42`, they fail 1 of 26, 5 of 7 and 1 of 4.
- Red on base, green here, each with only that commit's source file reverted:
  - `extensions/telegram/src/approval-native.test.ts`: 5 failed / 2 passed vs 7 passed; the new test receives the deprecation message.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.test.ts` (follow-up read): fails with the `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` usage record vs passes.
  - `src/channels/plugins/approvals.test.ts`: `expected false to be true` vs 4 passed. Dropping either async field alone fails its own assertion.
- `--trace-deprecation` over the message-join and fallback-steering suites (101 tests): `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warnings 3 -> 0.
- All 9 bundled approval capabilities: `channelPluginHasNativeApprovalPromptUi` true for 1 of 9 on base, 9 of 9 here.
- Prompt consumers 16 files / 174 tests, Telegram and Discord approval suites 9 files / 218 tests, core steering and authority suites 19 files / 371 tests: all pass. `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap, assertion-safety and test-lines ratchets pass against `19aff5bfd42`. If CI's test-lines job is red, that is main's own overage (main has been over its ceiling since `2a32ab046f2`, #191638); this branch adds 113 test lines and 113 lines of allocation.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `approval-native.test.ts` 26.1 s (cold worker cache, 20.2 s of it compiling) and 6.6 s wall, 413 ms and 376 ms of tests; `reply-tool-authority.test.ts` 8.8 s and 7.8 s wall, 1.3 s and 1.2 s of tests; `approvals.test.ts` 10.0 s and 6.2 s wall, 11 ms and 9 ms of tests. CI run 41606285186, Bun: `approval-native.test.ts` 744 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1`); `reply-tool-authority.test.ts` 9.0 s Vitest duration, 1.6 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-7`); `approvals.test.ts` 50.1 s Vitest duration, 17 ms of tests (`checks-node-changed-channels`).
- Not covered end to end: real Telegram, Discord or Slack. The Discord and Slack sessions above came from the Gateway `agent` RPC with their plugins loaded and no accounts running, not from those services. Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, iMessage, Signal and WhatsApp were not run.

prs.title: fix(agents): cache drop warnings blame max_completion_tokens when only the output cap changed
prs.body:
Closes #191648

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `[prompt-cache] cache read dropped` warnings blame `provider-input-change:parameters:max_completion_tokens` when the prompt prefix is unchanged and only the per-request output cap moved.

## User Impact

User impact: on Chat Completions routes, a cache drop with an unchanged prompt prefix now reads `provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix` with `providerPrefix=prefix-match`, so the warning points at the provider instead of an OpenClaw request change that did not happen. Prompt, tool, message and other parameter changes are still attributed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Chat Completions transport clamps `max_completion_tokens` (or `max_tokens`) to the remaining context budget on most requests (`openai-completions-params.ts:511`). `describeProviderPrefix()` compared every tracked request parameter, so the cap alone turned `prefix-match` into `parameters:max_completion_tokens`. An output cap bounds the completion; it does not change the prompt tokens a prefix cache keys on.

The parameter comparison now leaves out `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens`:
- A cap-only change keeps `prefix-match`.
- When something else changed as well, the warning names only that: `parameters:temperature`, or `system`.

`docs/reference/prompt-caching.md` and `docs/logging.md` say so.

The provider-prefix description, with this filter, now lives in `prompt-cache-provider-prefix.ts`. With current main, `prompt-cache-observability.ts` would otherwise pass its 700-line cap; the functions moved unchanged.

Accepted edge case: if the cap changed and the only other difference is the JSON key order of the remaining parameters, the `order` signal is not reported.

## Evidence

- Production (details in #191648): on two hosts running a 2026.10.10-beta.5 based build, all 66 and all 83 drops labeled `parameters:max_completion_tokens` had equal `prefixHash` and `routeHash`. 35 and 17 of them went to 0 cached tokens.
- Unit: one new table in `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` with 5 cases:
  - `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens` alone -> unchanged prefix.
  - Cap plus `temperature` -> `parameters:temperature`.
  - Cap plus changed instructions -> `system`.
  - On base `19aff5bfd42` all 5 fail. The received values are `provider-input-change:parameters:max_tokens`, `...:max_completion_tokens`, `...:max_output_tokens`, `parameters:temperature+max_completion_tokens` and `system,parameters:max_completion_tokens`. With the fix the file passes 22/22.
- Consumers: 14 test files that use the observer pass (276 tests).
- End to end: an isolated `openclaw agent --local` turn against a scripted local Chat Completions server. Request 1 makes a tool call with 22560 cached tokens; request 2 reports 0. The bodies differ only by the two appended messages and `max_completion_tokens` (44468 -> 41385).
  - Base build: `provider-input-change:parameters:max_completion_tokens ... providerPrefix=parameters:max_completion_tokens`
  - This branch: `provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix ... providerPrefix=prefix-match`
- Checks:
  - `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files pass.
  - Against current main `3855c896edd`, with this branch merged locally:
    - CI's baseline ratchets (`ci-baseline-ratchets.mts --base 3855c896edd --no-merge-base`) pass 9 of 9, and the line-cap ratchet passes with `RATCHET_PR_HEAD_SHA` set. Before `a18dac5b480` it failed: `prompt-cache-observability.ts: 700 -> 712 counted lines (cap 700)`, because #192944 left that file at exactly its cap.
    - Test lines: main's test-line ratchet is now at its ceiling (slack 0; this branch measured 410 against its base), so `b094f0248d4` adds `config/test-lines-allocations/191649-cache-drop-output-cap.txt` with 30 lines, the net growth of the new table in `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts`, which is the regression test for this fix. The ratchet reads `Test lines OK: 6592398; ceiling: 6592398; slack: 0.`, and 31 is refused.
    - `check:changed --base 3855c896edd`: 35 of 36 lanes pass. The other, `changelog attributions`, reports the same 20 lines on unmodified main, in changelog files this PR does not touch.
    - The 12 test files that import the changed modules pass 191 of 191, under Node 26.12.1 and under Bun.
  - Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` 32.1 s (cold worker cache, 20.2 s of it compiling) and 12.8 s wall, 7.2 s and 7.4 s of tests. CI run 41574334778, Bun: `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` 36.0 s Vitest duration, 7.5 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-40`).
  - The new cases run in 1-2 ms each.
- Not covered: a live provider run. The qa-lab mock serves only Responses and Messages and reports no cached tokens, so it cannot produce a cache drop.

prs.title: improve(auto-reply): name the model whose connection failed
prs.body:
Closes #191299

## What Problem This Solves

When a model call fails to connect, the reply says "Couldn't connect to the AI service." (#168247) but not which model. With a fallback chain or several providers, the user can't tell which endpoint is down without the gateway logs.

## User Impact

User impact: the connection-failure reply starts with the failing model, e.g. `⚠️ gpufarm/qwen3.8-27b request failed: Couldn't connect to the AI service. ...`. The rest of #168247's copy is unchanged, including the completed-work caution. A failure without a provider or model reads exactly as before, and raw error text stays hidden.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveReplyFailoverFacts` already has the failover error's provider and model; the connection copy just didn't use them. It now prefixes the copy with the failing model through `modelKey`, which keeps a model id that already carries its provider as is (`openrouter/auto` is not doubled). Terminal replies and incomplete-turn replies both read `requestFailureText`, so both get the name.

When the error carries fallback attempts, the name comes only from the attempts whose own error is a connection failure, joined with ", " when there are several. A chain summary keeps the last attempt's model while its message joins every attempt's error, so taking the top-level model would blame a backup that connected and then timed out (ClawSweeper's P2 on the first head).

This partly reverses #163381 (#163368), which removed provider details from default errors to keep them short. For a connection failure, though, the failing model is the next recovery step (which server to check), not a diagnostic. Only the connection copy changes; rate-limit, auth and server-error replies are untouched. If maintainers want to keep #163381's rule here too, closing this is fine.

## Evidence

- New qa scenario `connection-failure-reply-names-model` (in this PR): real gateway, qa-channel, mock-openai with the provider's `baseUrl` set to `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`, so every model call is refused. It sends a DM and reads the terminal reply from the bus. The reply is `isError`, so it is read directly rather than through the failure-aware transport waits, the same way `a2a-allowlist-denied-cross-agent-send` reads its expected warning.
  - main at `70c93a29f17` (this PR's base): fails with `unexpected connection-failure reply: ⚠️ Couldn't connect to the AI service. Check your connection, then try again. ...`
  - This branch at `a798fb3485e` (the scenario now requires two distinct named models before "request failed"): passes with `reply: ⚠️ mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna, mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt request failed: Couldn't connect to the AI service. Check your connection, then try again. For details, open Settings → Logs in the Control UI or run `openclaw logs --follow`. Check the conversation for any completed work before trying again.` qa-lab configures `gpt-5.6-luna-alt` as the fallback, both on the refused provider, so this is the real fallback-chain path, and both refused models are named. The first head named only the last one: with its `request-error-facts.ts`, the scenario fails on `⚠️ mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt request failed: ...`.
  - Command: `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario connection-failure-reply-names-model --concurrency 1 --fast`, after `pnpm build`.
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`: 22 passed.
  - "names the model whose connection failed" covers the named copy, a provider-prefixed model id, and the unchanged copy without facts. With main's `request-error-facts.ts` it fails with `Received: "⚠️ Couldn't connect to the AI service. ..."`.
  - "names only the fallback attempts that failed to connect" builds the error with the real `throwFallbackFailureSummary`: the primary is refused and the backup times out, then both are refused. With the first head's code it fails with `Received: "⚠️ backup/llama3.3 request failed: Couldn't connect ..."`.
- 34 related test files at `e40cb6903e0`: 1,053 passed, 0 failed. They are the 13 that assert this copy or call `resolveReplyFailoverFacts` (`agent-runner-failure-reply`, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e`, `incomplete-turn*`, `settled-turn-finalization*`, `payloads.errors`, `session-lifecycle-run-failure`, `server-methods`, `assistant-error-format` and others), plus `model-fallback*` and `agent-terminal-snapshot`.
- qa-lab scenario catalog tests (19 files): 145 passed, run at `fc2d656c3bc`. The scenario file is unchanged since.
- `pnpm tsgo:all` exits 0. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Test lines: main's test-line ratchet is now at its ceiling (`3855c896edd`: slack 0), so `35ed4298bdd` adds `config/test-lines-allocations/191301-connection-failure-names-model.txt` with this PR's exact net test-line growth, 61 lines. They are the tests that pin this change: Connection-failure replies name the fallback models that failed to connect. Merged onto `3855c896edd`, `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 3855c896edd --no-merge-base` reads `Test lines OK: 6592429; ceiling: 6592429; slack: 0.`, and an allocation of 62 is refused. This is not a fix PR, so per the openclaw-testing guide the record needs a maintainer's approval; could a maintainer approve it?
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts` 27.7 s (cold worker cache, 21.9 s of it compiling) and 6.5 s wall, 15 ms and 16 ms of tests. CI run 41570533435, Bun: `agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts` 4.4 s Vitest duration, 20 ms of tests (`checks-node-changed-4`).
- Gap: the end-to-end proof is mock-openai against a closed local port. The refused-then-timed-out chain is covered by the unit test only; I did not build an end-to-end case for it. My fork runs the same naming on two bots with local models; I have not captured a live provider outage with this exact build.

prs.title: fix(process): avoid Gateway fork stalls in detached commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway pauses when detached callbacks start Git, exec-tool commands, or container helpers from a large Node process.

## User Impact

Linux Gateway commands continue using the existing small spawn broker after their request async context has ended. Command output, exit codes, environment, working directory, cancellation, deadlines, and process-tree ownership keep their existing contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The broker belongs to the Gateway lifetime, but its lookup only consulted request async context. Both shared spawn adapters therefore fell back to native spawn for detached work even when the broker was healthy. Register the ready broker at its existing owner and clear it after successful host cleanup. Explicit native-only scopes and scoped broker overrides retain precedence.

Production growth is 14 lines for the lifetime registration and cleanup hook. No configuration, cache, schema, or duplicate command implementation. Native transport remains for CLI/other runtimes, host-owned descriptors and explicit synchronous launch-authority boundaries.

## Evidence

Both regressions fail on exact parent `649ca5f879f1e4349a2c5cf9872e30366962a595`: detached commands have the main process as parent, and the real exec fixture completes without using its ready broker. Candidate owner, exec, transport and Gateway shutdown coverage passes; the lifecycle batch is 62 tests. The new owner test takes about 1.1 seconds of test time; compilation is excluded from that figure.

Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate is scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. Core test typechecks and scoped script checks pass after fixture corrections. `pnpm check:changed` passes every gate except unused exports; those failures reproduce unchanged on a clean exact-parent checkout:

- `TELEPORT_PT`, `QA_UX_STREAM_END_MARKER`: introduced in #198293 (`858b5b01338e`).
- `adoptTelegramDmTopicMessage`, `TELEGRAM_DM_TOPIC_ADOPT_WINDOW_SEC`: introduced in #169444 (`90c620b8e554`).
- `RELEASE_VALIDATION_WAIVERS`: introduced in #173437 (`2a1285197991`); no external reader in its symbol history.

These are recorded main regressions, not passing checks.

Linux proof uses the committed `scripts/perf/durable-spawn-measure.ts` workload, source-frozen parent/candidate bundles, a 9.11 GiB resident parent including 4 GiB V8 heap, five alternating pairs and identical-source A/A controls (250 commands per source per owner). All 750 native host spawns become zero.

| Owner | Native blocking median / p95, ms | Main-thread CPU median, ms/command | Wall median / p95, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Buffered Git | 39.803 / 97.065 → 0 / 0 | 23.924 → 0.610 | 42.750 / 116.405 → 2.362 / 25.603 |
| Guarded exec | 32.002 / 50.819 → 0 / 0 | 18.073 → 0.586 | 32.438 / 51.288 → 2.358 / 14.410 |
| Container helper | 32.648 / 59.934 → 0 / 0 | 19.458 → 0.677 | 46.529 / 101.649 → 14.007 / 44.034 |

Median allocation per command: Git 514,667 → 342,058 bytes; guarded exec 120,356 → 187,833 bytes; container 747,066 → 360,073 bytes. The guarded path adds about 66 KiB (+56%) through existing broker admission/IPC while reducing main-thread CPU by 96.8%. A/A wall medians were 42.324/42.856 → 2.318/2.429 ms for Git, 32.461/32.416 → 2.394/2.336 for guarded exec, and 46.009/46.917 → 14.059/13.976 for container helpers.

Separate CPU profiles (50 commands/source/owner) attribute 1,396 ms of Git and 1,503 ms of guarded-exec samples to native `spawn` before, with no native-spawn samples after. Timing acceptance uses unprofiled runs.

This is transport-owner proof in an isolated local Linux VM (ARM64, Node 26.12.1, overlayfs), not complete Gateway throughput or btrfs coverage. The commands do not read the database or workspace; the synthetic fixture matches resident heap and mapping cost without copying production data. The broker remains about 80–84 MiB RSS.

prs.title: fix(node): warn when MSIX computer control targets an isolated desktop
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Related: openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging#245
Packaging guidance counterpart: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging/pull/258

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes silent desktop-target confusion when the Windows MSIX CLI advertises computer control or screenshots from its isolated agent desktop.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

Users receive a visible stderr warning that starting the packaged alias from their terminal does not select their signed-in desktop. Windows Hub is the supported interactive-user Windows desktop node route, but **Hub does not currently implement `computer.act`**, tracked in openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#1871; this PR does not promise end-to-end Hub computer use. A separately installed interactive-user npm CLI node remains an unsupported workaround.

Isolation, command advertisement/admission, pairing, connection and exit behavior stay unchanged. This source change is not automatically included in the MSIX package's currently pinned payload; the packaging owner must consume a future core bundle containing it.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The node runner owns its filtered, advertised command manifest. It warns once per node-host run on Windows when the launcher's existing `CLAWCTL_GATEWAY_ISOLATION=enabled` contract is present and `computer.act` or `screen.snapshot` is actually advertised, including later availability updates. The existing redacted stderr writer keeps machine-readable stdout untouched. A warning preserves legitimate isolated non-desktop nodes and existing automation instead of rejecting every packaged `node run`.

The bundled guide now states the MSIX exception at requirements, setup and recovery. No packaging argument parser, isolation escape, native driver update, Hub feature, new CLI owner, setup automation or approval bypass is added. `desktop.stream` is an explicit node-local RFB relay, so a generic `screen` capability or stream declaration alone is not treated as native computer control.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Local regression environment: Windows x64, Node 26.13.0; production runner and real manifest/runtime preparation with synthetic config/plugin I/O and a captured Gateway transport. This fixture is separate from the real installed-MSIX probe below and does not claim a live desktop action.

- Base `480389e1ca1ef7595ea5c5ece0f14d75ef8b83a5`: `node scripts\run-vitest.mjs src\node-host\runner.inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'MSIX isolated desktop diagnostics'` reproduced 3 missing-warning failures and 4 passing negative controls. The wrapper also reported an artifact-cache rename `EPERM` after the test verdict; that cleanup error is not the behavioral reproduction.
- Same focused command after the fix: **7 passed**, testing each advertised command, silent stdout, unchanged command availability and successful first connection/exit 0, non-MSIX Windows, Linux, non-desktop nodes, filtered commands, and later manifest changes.
- `node scripts\run-vitest.mjs src\node-host\runner.inventory.test.ts src\node-host\runner.test.ts src\node-host\runner.shutdown.test.ts src\node-host\runner.auto-update.test.ts src\cli\node-cli\register.test.ts src\cli\node-cli\identity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --isolate`: **99 passed across 6 files**, 144.95s wrapper wall time. The changed file's tests took approximately 0.9s in that run; the full infra shard including identity tests took 31.18s including import/setup. CI seconds are pending.
- **Unresolved local harness failure:** the initial six-file run without `--isolate` exited its shared worker after 38 passing runner tests, before completing the remaining files. A narrower `runner.auto-update.test.ts runner.shutdown.test.ts` reproduction passed 7 auto-update tests then exited its shared worker before shutdown tests (exit 0 instead of the earlier exit 1). The isolated six-file run above covers every requested file, but does not establish a fix or baseline attribution for this cross-file worker-exit defect. No tests, assertions, baselines or runner configuration were weakened.
- `node scripts\run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts\tsgo-cache\core.tsbuildinfo`: **passed**.
- `node scripts\run-tsgo.mjs -p test\tsconfig\tsconfig.core.test.infra.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts\tsgo-cache\infra-test.tsbuildinfo`: **passed**.
- `node scripts\run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json src\node-host\runner.ts src\node-host\runner.inventory.test.ts`: **passed**.
- `node scripts\run-format.mts --check src\node-host\runner.ts src\node-host\runner.inventory.test.ts docs\nodes\computer-use.md` and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- `pnpm docs:list` (pinned pnpm entry), `node scripts\check-docs-mdx.mjs docs\nodes\computer-use.md`, `node scripts\docs-link-audit.mjs`, and `node scripts\check-docs-config-examples.mjs`: **passed** (1 edited MDX page; 16,622 internal links / 0 broken; 1,404 config fences validated).
- `pnpm check:env-var-count`, `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` (using the repository loader through the pinned pnpm entry), and `node scripts\check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs`: **passed**.

Author simplification retained one reused runner-local warning and the existing stderr/manifest owners: production +22/-1, tests +86/-1; no new module, export or production testing seam. Documentation table alignment is formatter-generated.

Full committed-range local ClawSweeper review was refreshed after the installed probe, on base `480389e1ca1ef7595ea5c5ece0f14d75ef8b83a5` through head `b1f73d448ec808d9253b2d9bd1f2a925d993791a`, using the clean upstream runner at `1e5b21e063e064b8ab4dc259e2743c54631c0b01` and normal `review -- --local-range` coverage (no priority filter). It completed at 21:57 UTC with verified checkout access, clean source/runner, **zero correctness or security findings**, and **real behavior proof sufficient** (`shipped_entry_point`; proof A, patch B, overall B). The review explicitly accepts the real installed-alias trace below as resolving the earlier local F proof gap. These are local results, not a hosted-rating or CI/security waiver.

The [completed hosted re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198416#issuecomment-6862650223) accepted the new installed proof on this exact head at 22:03 UTC: **overall 4/6, proof 5/6, patch 4/6, zero findings, no Before-merge items** ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/43515356765)). This resolves the initial 1/6 proof request. The source and installed-proof section are unchanged since that verdict; the gate-status section below records subsequent CI/security outcomes, not a new code or runtime claim.

The immutable normal package for that proof is now complete:

prs.title: fix(node-host): Windows node commands cannot use the allowlist or auto-review because of the cmd.exe wrapper
prs.body:
Closes #157930

## What Problem This Solves

On a Windows node host, every `system.run` command is wrapped as `cmd.exe /d /s /c <command>`. The node intentionally treats that wrapper as an allowlist miss (`windowsShellWrapperBlocked`), because cmd.exe changes the meaning of quotes and builtins. As a result, no allowlist entry or durable approval can ever apply on a Windows node: every command needs a human approval, even an absolute-path executable that is explicitly allowlisted.

## User Impact

An operator can now allowlist an executable on a Windows node (for example `C:\Users\me\.local\bin\claude.exe`) and the agent can run it with varying arguments without an approval each time. Commands that genuinely need cmd.exe (operators outside quotes, builtins, `.cmd`/`.bat` scripts) keep the existing wrapper and the existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

#157930 suggests binding and reviewing the inner command of the canonical wrapper. This PR takes the narrower route of not sending the wrapper when it is not needed: when a Windows command has no cmd.exe operator outside quotes, no builtin as its first word, and no `.cmd`/`.bat` target, the Gateway sends it to the node as a direct argv. The `windowsShellWrapperBlocked` rule is untouched, and the node's existing direct-argv path, allowlist and approval binding apply unchanged.

Splitting follows both Windows command-line rules (`CommandLineToArgvW` and the current C runtime) and only accepts a command when both yield the same argv; otherwise it keeps cmd.exe. Characters such as `& | < > ^ ( ) % !` and newlines are literal inside quotes and stay on the direct path; `%VAR%` is not expanded there, and the approval card shows the exact argv that runs. The Gateway approval precheck evaluates that same argv, so it never authorizes more than the node does.

## Evidence

- Unit tests for the splitter: eligible commands, every cmd.exe metacharacter inside and outside quotes, escaped quotes and backslash runs, doubled quotes, newlines inside quotes, builtins, `.cmd`/`.bat`, shell wrappers.
- Gateway tests for the argv sent to the node on both paths and for equality between the approved text and the executed argv.
- Real Windows integration test through the node handler: the child receives `a & b | c < d > e ^ f (g) 50% %PATH% !x! say "hi"` plus a newline exactly; `allow-always` is offered for an ordinary executable and reused.
- Real behavior proof: on a Windows 11 node paired with a Linux Gateway, with `claude.exe` in the node allowlist, the agent ran `claude.exe -p "<prompt with ( ) & % ? and accents>" --permission-mode plan` with no approval prompt, and Claude Code answered the full prompt. Before this change, the same calls required an approval each time and logged `Exec auto-review skipped: dispatch chain cannot be bound`; after it, that line no longer appears.
- Not run locally: the full test suite.

prs.title: fix(update): supervised PostgreSQL updates ignore server recovery captures and orphan them on finish
prs.body:
Closes #198401
Supersedes #198435

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `database.postgres.recoveryCaptures: "server"`, supervised `openclaw update migrate` exported every PostgreSQL store to local files while the Gateway was stopped, extending downtime, and `update finish` would orphan server-side captures if they were made.

## User Impact

User impact: supervised PostgreSQL updates honor the configured server recovery captures (shorter stopped window, no local export copies), and finishing the update retires those server captures instead of leaving `restore_<uuid>` schemas behind. Cleanup stays best effort: if retirement fails, the update still succeeds, the backup is kept, and a warning says to retry `update finish`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on @qingminglong's #198435, which forwards the existing setting to the supervised migrate backup, matching the native updater. That alone would keep rows in server schemas whose only references are the local backup manifests, and `update finish` deletes those manifests without dropping the schemas. Finish now retires them through the existing `discardPostgresSchemaCaptures` owner (the same one the native updater uses) before removing the backup directory; a failure keeps the manifests so a retry can finish, and `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS` keeps retries idempotent. Doctor's capture pruning cannot reclaim these because supervised captures lack its prefix marker.

Rolled-back (restored) receipts keep their captures under the existing rollback retention contract; no retention policy change.

## Evidence

- New finish regression in `update-command-migrate.test.ts` (real finish command, discard owner mocked at its module boundary): **red** on #198435's head (discard never called), **green** with the fix; covers ordering before directory removal, discard failure keeping the directory with a warning, and retry.
- `update-command-migrate.test.ts` 22 passed (including #198435's tests); `update-command-database-retention.test.ts` 15 passed.
- The PostgreSQL migrate→finish lifecycle case **ran and passed against a real PostgreSQL service in CI**, not skipped: [PostgreSQL conformance (1/3), run 43512134482](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43512134482/job/132185832402), `retires server captures through supervised migrate and finish` (13.124 s). The adjacent existing exact-capture→rollback→retirement test also passed (6.696 s), preserving the frozen capture and row verification. This remains in-process boundary proof (Doctor is stubbed), not an installed CLI upgrade.
- All 52 PR checks passed on `95500ea9c4c879cb4f302cb6e8e3f09615da982a`. Remaining gap: no installed v2026.11.3→candidate supervised CLI upgrade with existing portable captures. No schema, receipt format, or default-policy change is introduced; portable defaults and shared-state exceptions remain unchanged.
- Type-aware oxlint and format check of touched files, `git diff --check` pass.

Thanks @qingminglong for spotting the missing option and the parity test; your commit is kept as-is with authorship.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.body:
## Summary

Adds the **XingChen-AGI** provider plugin for OpenClaw, exposing the **Xing4.1-Preview** model (China Telecom AI Technology Co., Ltd.) through its OpenAI-compatible API.

- Provider id: `xingchen-agi`
- Package: `@openclaw/xingchen-agi-provider`
- Auth env var: `XINGCHEN_API_KEY`
- API: `openai-completions`
- Base URL: `https://api-maas.teleai.com.cn/v1`
- Default model: `xing4.1-preview`

## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw user who wants to use Xing4.1-Preview currently has to hand-configure an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and model metadata. This PR adds a ready-made provider plugin plus documentation, so the model becomes selectable as `xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview` once the plugin is installed and `XINGCHEN_API_KEY` is provided.

## What's included

- `extensions/xingchen-agi/` - provider plugin (`index.ts`, `openclaw.plugin.json`, `package.json`)
- `docs/providers/xingchen-agi.md` - provider docs page
- `docs/providers/index.md` - registered in the provider directory

## Manifest

Uses the current provider schema (`setup.providers[].envVars`, declarative `modelCatalog` with `discovery: static`) and the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-entry` SDK entry point.

## Model

| Model ref | Input | Context | Max output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview` | text | 1,000,000 | 192,000 |

- Reasoning: supported (deep-thinking mode; no `reasoning_effort` tiers exposed)
- Pricing (USD / 1M tokens, off-peak): input $0.11 / cached input $0.0022 / output $0.45 (peak = 2x)

## Verification

- Endpoint reachable over HTTPS from outside mainland China (tested: TCP 443 / TLS / HTTP 200, median latency ~120 ms)
- Auth is standard `Authorization: Bearer` (unauthenticated request returns a business 401, not a signature error)

## Evidence

Validation was run end-to-end on OpenClaw `2026.11.3` (`847611d`), Windows, Node `v24.18.0`, with the plugin from this PR installed. All output is redacted (the API key is masked as `sk-****`). Two layers are covered: local one-shot inference through the plugin, and a full Gateway agent turn using a saved credential profile with the standard plugin set loaded.

### Real behavior proof

Verified end-to-end against OpenClaw `2026.11.3` (`847611d`) on Windows, Node `v24.18.0`. The plugin from this PR was installed in link mode, the model catalog resolved, credentials resolved from `XINGCHEN_API_KEY`, and real one-shot model turns returned responses.

$ openclaw infer model run --model xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview --local --json \

prs.title: fix: Access page missing until restart after enabling OpenClaw ID
prs.body:
Related: #198468

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the OpenClaw ID Access page is missing from the Control UI when OpenClaw ID is turned on while the Gateway is already running, which is the normal flow on a fresh install.

## User Impact

User impact: turning on OpenClaw ID now loads the Access page right away; turning it off removes the page. Before this change, the page only appeared after a Gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundled `openclaw-id-access` plugin is only chosen when plugins load (`activation.onConfigPaths: ["gateway.openclawId.enabled"]`). Changes to `gateway.openclawId` were hot-applied without any reload action, so the plugin was never loaded. The catalog refresh that followed then read the startup registry, which never contained the plugin. This change adds a narrower reload rule so `gateway.openclawId.enabled` triggers `reloadPlugins`. Other `gateway.openclawId.*` settings keep their current behavior: hot-applied with no plugin reload.

This does not cover the allowlist case described in #198468, where an existing nonempty `plugins.allow` that omits `openclaw-id-access` keeps the plugin disabled. That needs separate reconciliation of the allowlist, so this PR does not close the issue.

## Evidence

- New test in `src/gateway/config-reload-plan.test.ts`: turning OpenClaw ID on or off produces `reloadPlugins: true, restartGateway: false`, and `relayUrl` edits still do not reload plugins. The test fails without the fix and passes with it; all 30 tests in the file pass.
- Live check on an isolated dev Gateway, without a restart:
  - Before enabling, `plugins.controlUi.list` returned `["deep-research"]`.
  - `openclaw config set gateway.openclawId.enabled true` logged `Plugin replacement applied: openclaw-id-access` and `config hot reload applied (gateway.openclawId.enabled)`.
  - `plugins.controlUi.list` then returned `["deep-research","openclaw-id-access"]`.
  - Setting it back to `false` hot-reloaded the same way.
- An independent review traced rule precedence, re-selection of plugins on reload, and the order of the `plugins.changed` and `plugins.controlUi.changed` broadcasts. It found no issues; `config-reload-plan`, `config-reload` and `config-reload.operation-policy` tests pass (244 tests).

prs.title: fix(active-memory): warning repeats on every turn when the memory provider lacks private transcript recall
prs.body:
Closes #198437

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Active Memory logs the same "does not support protected private transcript recall" warning on every eligible turn when Remember across conversations is on and the memory slot owner does not support it.

## User Impact

User impact: operators see the warning once per memory provider and agent instead of on every turn. Later repeats go to the debug log. Recall behavior does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Whether the slot owner supports protected transcript recall is fixed by config, so repeating the warning adds nothing. The plugin keeps a set of provider and agent pairs it has warned about; the first skip warns, later skips log the same line at debug. The set lives in the plugin registration, so a plugin reload or config change that re-registers Active Memory warns again. The other skip warning ("... is unavailable"), which depends on the turn's tool authority, is unchanged.

## Evidence

Real Gateway, before and after. Both builds came from source (`pnpm build`) and ran as an isolated local Gateway on loopback, each with its own state dir, config, and token. The model and the LanceDB embeddings came from the repo's QA `mock-openai` server, so no provider keys were used.

Setup, identical on both builds:

- `plugins.slots.memory: "memory-lancedb"`. LanceDB does not declare `supportsPrivateTranscriptRecall`.
- Active Memory is enabled with `agents: ["personal"]`.
- `memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations: true`.
- Three private turns to agent `personal` over Gateway `chat.send` on session `agent:personal:main` (webchat, direct). The turns are neutral messages with no recall intent.
- Logging at debug.

| Build | Version | `does not support protected private transcript recall` at WARN | same line at DEBUG | recall runs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main `eae12351406` | OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (eae1235), macOS arm64 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| this PR `c8df4c6e622` | OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (c8df4c6), macOS arm64 | 1 | 2 | 0 |

Gateway log excerpt, this PR (redacted):

prs.title: feat(android): sign in to Gateways protected by browser-session proxies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android native connections do not inherit a browser-session reverse-proxy login. The onboarding flow could also wait indefinitely for optional phone-node access after operator chat was already authorized.

**Published source:** [6cde97f4079e2a2ca0c806c9aa572ee207a99bc5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6cde97f4079e2a2ca0c806c9aa572ee207a99bc5). GitHub commit/tree readback confirms tree b993b3a3201c2167c0f06adeebffe649dccdee28 and all 42 feature source/test/documentation files. This includes the browser-lifecycle/consumer corrections and the exact non-test WebView shadow registration needed for complete JUnit discovery. Current-head CI and hosted/maintainer review remain separate gates; no merge or deployment.

## User Impact

- Enter one full Gateway URL: HTTPS defaults to 443, explicit ports win, and the existing local HTTP, IPv6, path and bare-host port18789 contracts remain intact.
- After verified native operator admission, browser authentication returns to the original native flow automatically. A legitimate device-pairing requirement can hand back to native approval; cookies, HTTP200 or a matching URL alone never confirm login.
- An operator-ready connection can continue to chat while optional phone-node access remains pending. Node capabilities still require their separate consent and Gateway approval; companion-only readiness is not operator login.
- Explicit replacement/signout retires only that Gateway's app browser authority, role grants and locally cached conversations. Other Gateways and the persistent device identity remain intact. Saved-session signout is reachable on the persistent Settings → Gateway card after automatic return.
- Renderer loss disposes only its owned browser and retires unadmitted work without revoking an already-admitted native session. Late callbacks cannot revive a retired attempt. Actual platform profile calls require MULTI_PROFILE support.
- Browser capture stays protected in ordinary debug and release builds. Recording requires an explicit debug-only build flag.

## Why This Change Was Made

One app-private WebView-profile owner supplies cookies for actual native HTTPS request URLs, with exact-origin/port and browser domain/path selection. Native admission, profile/attempt/cookie epochs, cancellation and target-bound runtime state own progress. Pending role grants and subsequent consumers cannot inherit a different browser principal's acceptance. Accepted-profile rotation/restart preserves its credential scope; explicit account replacement does not reuse it.

There is no LDAP client, JS credential bridge, TLS bypass, external-browser cookie copying or automatic device/node approval. Gateway shared-secret and trusted-proxy enforcement remain separate. Signout is local app-session retirement, not a promise of IdP-wide logout or LDAP-account revocation.

Related: #147061, #147307, #147305. Existing Cloudflare CustomTabs/service-header work is not recreated. Main's merged identity-disclosure fix #195997 and native fixture work #197407 are preserved in the integrated base.

## Evidence

### Published reviewed source

- Frozen public base: 4aa0168e1f2a17608fa6dbb8d7d07a406794fd96.
- Verified published Git tree: b993b3a3201c2167c0f06adeebffe649dccdee28; **42 authored source/test/documentation files** relative to that base, not incoming-main baseline files.
- Final full patch SHA-256: 59c6ca3474d044b1fc806ccedd839dea46700fa0a0649952ede9ec3cf81e593e.
- **336 affected Android tests passed; 0 failures/errors/skips** on implementation tree51577115f95e35853e74fba73cc92c803cf4d6b3, including real GatewaySession + NodeRuntime TLS fixtures, browser admission/profile lifecycle, scoped cache retirement, resolver/settings/onboarding, saved grants and capture protection. That is earlier implementation evidence, not a claim that336tests ran on the final source. The current source has the additional verification below.
- **192 targeted tests passed; 0 failures/errors/skips on implementation tree 78849d7080d6271512109f238e7283f78670f8aa:** 15 relevant browser/native Gateway/epoch/signout/UI suites in each Play and third-party flavor. This includes all three previously stale UI consumer suites.
- **Full Android Lint passes in both debug flavors:** all15reported errors are gone; two unchanged informational findings remain per flavor. Configured scoped Gradle ktlint and whitespace checks pass.
- Four renderer/capability regressions failed against the unfixed production behavior and pass after repair. The positive HTTPS-return/native-admission path and synchronous preference-commit success/failure contract also pass. The new Activity test suite takes about2.8seconds per flavor, excluding Gradle setup/compilation.
- Focused repository Gradle ktlint passed; MDX validation passed for 1,442 files; diff whitespace check clean.
- Fresh bound Auto Review, native OpenClaw engine, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, two completed chunks and no findings, covering the complete eight-file correction from506750967efc5f72b13c4c8c16faba9c56f2a013 to implementation tree 78849d7080d6271512109f238e7283f78670f8aa. The old reviewed snapshot reproduced the account leak and unreachable signout; the candidate passes. No assertion/timeouts/trust checks were weakened.

### CI locale-isolation correction

The initial new-head [preflight](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43461807947/job/132010368842) rejected source changes mixed with apps/.i18n/native/ru.json. ### Native CI consumer and browser-lifecycle corrections

The [Play test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43464440950/job/132021298342) exposed three consumers still expecting Host/Port or redundant transport controls. Their replacements retain fold/focus/draft/Back, credential masking, French large-font completeness and required-TLS assertions while exercising the actual URL flow.

The [combined lint job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43464440950/job/132021298347) and [Wear job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43464440950/job/132021298266) exposed15phone-app Android Lint errors; Wear tests/lint themselves passed. The fix checks WebView capability at SDK effects, handles renderer death and late callbacks, and preserves the existing synchronous commit Boolean. Provider JavaScript remains deliberately enabled under the existing HTTPS/TLS/no-bridge/file/content/mixed-content restrictions, with a narrowly explained lint exception—not a disabled security gate or baseline.

Current-head CI must complete independently. Old-head failures, skipped jobs and local proof are not represented as a passing final CI gate. No current-source physical-device sign-in, provider-profile-isolation or real renderer-process-kill claim is made.

### Complete JUnit discovery correction

The subsequent [Play failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43498627170/job/132139216258) and third-party job failed before test execution: unsandboxed JUnit Vintage discovery reflected an Android-only WebView shadow and could not load ViewRootImpl.CalledFromWrongThreadException. Robolectric still loads it through the real lifecycle test configuration; no test class, test method or assertion is excluded.

- An earlier mixed dry-run invocation accidentally executed the full Play suite and hit local native-thread limits before interruption; that attempt is not passing proof. The corrected single-flavor discovery checks and focused actual runs are the evidence above; broad runtime proof remains current-head CI.

### Current-head CI result

[CI for6cde97f4079e2a2ca0c806c9aa572ee207a99bc5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43510336675) is green: **47 passed,0failed,0pending,49skipped/neutral** in the fresh PR readback.
