prs.title: feat(subagents): warn when live children share an explicit working directory
prs.body:
Supersedes #135480 (auto-closed for inactivity; branch re-merged with current main).

## What Problem This Solves

Two live subagents explicitly pointed at one checkout can overwrite each other's uncommitted files and move the same Git HEAD. `subagents list` showed both runs but gave the parent no collision signal, so a parent coordinating concurrent children had no way to see that two of them were writing to the same directory. The signal has to cover native and ACP children, canonicalize aliases, and stay bounded at supported swarm sizes — an unbounded warning would itself consume the model context it is meant to protect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Persist an explicit ACP `cwd` through the same `resolveExplicitSpawnedCwd()` contract native children already use.
- Report only directories a spawn request actually chose. A run that inherited its workspace is exempt, and so is a sender-restricted helper that was *handed* the requester's root by policy — both are expected sharing with nothing for an operator to change. The discriminator is already persisted: `senderRestricted` is `ctx.inheritedToolPolicySource === "sender"` at both owners, and both owners refuse any `cwd` that is not the requester root for such a sender, so a restricted helper's `spawnedCwd` is always the policy root and never a chosen directory. `inheritedToolPolicySource` is a hot `SessionEntry` field the advisory already reads, so no new field crosses a Gateway boundary and no protocol `closedObject` changes.
- Group only live, unended runs by the directory the child is actually using — `SessionEntry.acp.cwd` when the ACP backend reported one, `spawnedCwd` otherwise — with canonical on-disk identity and a lexical fallback when a recorded directory no longer resolves.
- Read the child metadata the list builder has already selected, under the same key the selection is stored by; the advisory performs no session I/O of its own.
- Emit each shared directory once in a bounded top-level summary. Only the sampled member rows carry `sharedCwdGroupId`; all other rows are unchanged.
- Cap the advisory at eight groups, three sampled run IDs per group, and 72 characters per displayed path, with `sharedCwdGroupTotal` and each group's `runCount` preserving exact counts even when display details are omitted. Order by stable keys before the caps apply, so identical live state always produces identical output.
- Surface the same bounded summary through both the structured `subagents` tool and native `/subagents` text.

The advisory is informational; it does not refuse or cancel a spawn.

**Why the exemption is reader-side rather than at the spawn owners.** The obvious owner-side shape — clearing the inherited `cwd` to mark explicitness — breaks the restriction that put it there: `prepare.ts` resolves a session's run cwd from `spawnedCwd`, so clearing it drops a restricted helper back to `resolveAgentRunCwd` and out of the guarded root. Both approaches were built and measured separately rather than argued (controls below).

## User Impact

One shared directory produces one summary and at most three row references regardless of child count. A 50-child case split across 25 colliding directories reports the exact total but emits only eight summaries, and the same eight every time. A `collect` swarm inheriting one workspace, and a restricted sender's helpers confined to that sender's root, both stay silent. An operator can identify concurrent writers without the warning growing with the swarm.

## Evidence

**Tested head: `3bc860565be95faa6c1d0ef40da0cfdff12a640a`** (= `origin/feat/subagent-shared-cwd-advisory`). Everything below was measured today, 2026-11-13, not carried over from an earlier body. The Round 3, Round 2 and Round 1 captures were taken at the parent `9a861a7aebe18f897bce634f5232f740104916ea`; `3bc860565be` changes exactly one file — the committed proof harness `scripts/proof-135480-subagent-shared-cwd-advisory.ts`, for review feedback on its path assertions — and no runtime source, so those captures still describe this head's production code. The harness itself was re-run at this head; see "Proof-harness portability" below.

### Round 3 — the installed production Gateway, real spawns, the shipped `subagents` tool

This capture is from the operator's long-running production Gateway (a systemd user service, built `dist`, started 2026-11-12 22:26 MST), not from a script. That build is a fork integration commit (`59fa16a3c82`) that carries this branch; the five runtime source files this PR changes (`src/agents/spawned-context.ts`, `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-list.ts`, `src/agents/subagents/spawn/acp-spawn.ts`, `src/agents/tools/subagents-tool.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-subagents/action-list.ts`) are byte-identical there to tested head `3bc860565be` (`git diff --quiet` per file; the latest commit changes only the proof script).

From a Discord direct session, the agent spawned real children with the shipped `sessions_spawn` tool and then called the shipped `subagents` tool with `action: "list"`. Children A and B were given `cwd: /tmp/r3-shared-cwd/work`, child C `cwd: /tmp/r3-shared-cwd/other`, and six unrelated working children had no `cwd` (inherited workspace). A ran on the Claude CLI runtime and B on the embedded runtime (an OpenRouter model), so the group spans two runtimes. Output is trimmed to the relevant fields; nothing else was edited.

```ts
 * so working-directory readers see it like a native child", and "keeps a
 * restricted same-agent ACP helper in the requester's root"); what this script
 * proves is that an ACP-shaped child session written through the production
 * writer is grouped and reported by the production readers, and that the same
 * child WITHOUT the persisted field — i.e. current `main` — is not.
 *
 * Scenarios:
 *   1. Pre-fix control: two ACP children in one directory, no `spawnedCwd`
 *      persisted (current `main`) — no advisory. This is the reported bug.
 *   2. Post-fix: the same two ACP children with the field persisted — both
 *      refer to one directory summary in tool JSON and `/subagents` text.
 *   3. Cross-runtime: one native child and one ACP child in one directory —
 *      both refer to the same group.
 *   4. Symlink alias: two children reach one checkout by different paths —
 *      grouped, and the canonical directory is reported.
 *   5. Inherited workspace (no explicit cwd) — silent.
 *   6. Distinct directories — silent.
 *   7. Deleted directory — canonicalization fails, lexical fallback still
 *      groups rather than throwing or dropping the row.
 *   8. Model-context bound at the supported child maximum: 20 live children in
 *      one long-pathed directory. Measures the real model-visible payload the
 *      `subagents` tool emits for `action: "list"` and asserts the advisory's
 *      whole-response contribution is capped — the P0 regression. Also drives
 *      25 shared directories across 50 children to prove only eight directory
 *      summaries are model-visible, and that permuting that equal-timestamp
 *      cohort leaves the ids, samples, and reported directories identical.
 *   9. The reader/advisory metadata key contract. `readSubagentListSessionEntries`
 *      keys its selection by run id, not by child session key, because raw child
 *      session keys repeat across agents
 *      (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166550). Feeds the real
 *      reader's own selection object straight into `buildSubagentList`, so a
 *      producer/consumer key disagreement cannot pass.
 *      The cross-agent raw-key case itself needs an admitted database for a
 *      non-default agent, which this offline harness does not stand up; it is
 *      covered by `subagent-list.test.ts` ("groups by each run's own metadata
 *      when two agents share one raw session key") through the supported test
 *      state.
 *  10. Sender-restricted helpers. A restricted sender's helper is handed the
 *      requester's root as `spawnedCwd` even when the request named no cwd,
 *      because both owners refuse any other directory for it. Asserts the
 *      enforced directory is still on the entry, that two such helpers produce
 *      no advisory in either the structured list or the `/subagents` text, and
 *      — as the control — that the identical directory without the policy
 *      marker is still reported.
 *
 * Every reported directory is compared through `expectedSharedCwdPath()` — the
 * same helper the owner suites use — because the advisory keeps only the last 72
 * characters of a long directory, which a deep temporary root reaches.
 *
 * Run: node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/proof-135480-subagent-shared-cwd-advisory.ts
 */
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import fs from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";

type SpawnedContextModule = typeof import("../src/agents/spawned-context.js");
type SessionAccessorModule = typeof import("../src/config/sessions/session-accessor.js");
type SubagentListModule = typeof import("../src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-list.js");
type SubagentRegistryQueriesModule =
  typeof import("../src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-queries.js");
type SubagentsCommandModule =
  typeof import("../src/auto-reply/reply/commands-subagents/action-list.js");
type SubagentListTestSupportModule =
  typeof import("../src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-list.test-support.js");
type SubagentRunRecord =
  import("../src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.types.js").SubagentRunRecord;
type SubagentRunReadRecord =
  import("../src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-read.types.js").SubagentRunReadRecord;
type OpenClawConfig = import("../src/config/types.openclaw.js").OpenClawConfig;

let failures = 0;

function check(label: string, run: () => void): void {
  try {
    run();
    console.log(`   ✓ ${label}`);
  } catch (error) {
    failures += 1;
    console.log(`   ✗ ${label}`);
    console.log(`     ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`);
  }
}

function makeRun(suffix: string, now: number, options?: { ended?: boolean }): SubagentRunRecord {
  return {
    runId: `run-${suffix}`,
    childSessionKey: `agent:main:subagent:${suffix}`,
    controllerSessionKey: "agent:main:main",
    requesterSessionKey: "agent:main:main",
    requesterDisplayKey: "main",
    task: `work inside ${suffix}`,
    cleanup: "keep",
    createdAt: now - 120_000,
    execution: options?.ended
      ? {
          status: "terminal",
          startedAt: now - 120_000,
          endedAt: now - 60_000,
          outcome: { status: "ok" },
        }
      : { status: "running", startedAt: now - 120_000 },
  } as SubagentRunRecord;
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const root = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "openclaw-proof-135480-"));
  process.env.OPENCLAW_HOME = path.join(root, "home");
  await fs.mkdir(process.env.OPENCLAW_HOME, { recursive: true });

  const { resolveExplicitSpawnedCwd } =
    (await import("../src/agents/spawned-context.js")) as SpawnedContextModule;
  const { upsertSessionEntryCore } =
    (await import("../src/config/sessions/session-accessor.js")) as SessionAccessorModule;
  const { buildSubagentList, captureSubagentListReadContext, readSubagentListSessionEntries } =
    (await import("../src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-list.js")) as SubagentListModule;
  const { buildSubagentRunReadIndexFromRuns } =
    (await import("../src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-queries.js")) as SubagentRegistryQueriesModule;
  const { handleSubagentsListAction } =
    (await import("../src/auto-reply/reply/commands-subagents/action-list.js")) as SubagentsCommandModule;
  // The advisory's own display contract: the owner suites assert reported
  // directories through this helper, so the proof must not hand-roll the cap.
  const { expectedSharedCwdPath } =
    (await import("../src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-list.test-support.js")) as SubagentListTestSupportModule;

  /**
   * Captures the read context the same way the production caller does. This
   * script never registers runs with the in-memory subagent registry, so the
   * read index and "full runs" map are always empty — the advisory itself
   * only reads persisted `spawnedCwd`, not registry state.
   */
  const buildReadContext = (runs: SubagentRunRecord[], recentMinutes: number) => {
    const readIndex = buildSubagentRunReadIndexFromRuns<SubagentRunReadRecord>({
      runs: new Map<string, SubagentRunReadRecord>(),
      inMemoryRuns: [],
    });
    return captureSubagentListReadContext(
      runs,
      readIndex,
      new Map<string, SubagentRunRecord>(),
      recentMinutes,
    );
  };

  /**
   * Writes a child session entry through the production writer using the exact
   * creation patch `acp-spawn.ts` now builds for an ACP child (or the native
   * equivalent — both owners resolve `spawnedCwd` through the same contract).
   */
  const createChildSession = async (params: {
    storePath: string;
    sessionKey: string;
    requestedCwd?: string;
    /** Set false to reproduce current `main`, which persists nothing for ACP. */
    persistCwd?: boolean;
    /**
     * Adds the two fields both owners stamp for a sender-restricted helper.
     * The cwd then names the requester's root because policy put it there, not
     * because the request asked for it.
     */
    senderRestricted?: boolean;
  }) => {
    const spawnedCwd = resolveExplicitSpawnedCwd(params.requestedCwd);
    await upsertSessionEntryCore({ storePath: params.storePath, sessionKey: params.sessionKey }, {
      spawnedBy: "agent:main:main",
      completionOwnerSessionKey: "agent:main:main",
      parentSessionKey: "agent:main:main",
      ...(spawnedCwd && params.persistCwd !== false ? { spawnedCwd } : {}),
      ...(params.senderRestricted
        ? { inheritedToolPolicySource: "sender", sessionRoot: spawnedCwd }
        : {}),
      inheritedToolPolicyVersion: 1,
    } as never);
    return spawnedCwd;
  };

  const listFor = async (storePath: string, runs: SubagentRunRecord[]) => {
    const cfg = { session: { store: storePath } } as OpenClawConfig;
    const context = buildReadContext(runs, 30);
    const list = buildSubagentList({
      context,
      sessionEntries: await readSubagentListSessionEntries(cfg, context),
    });
    // The `/subagents` command surface, driven for real off the same build.
    const text = await handleSubagentsListAction({
      params: { cfg },
      readContext: { list: context },
    } as never);
    return { list, text };
  };

  const groupFor = (list: ReturnType<SubagentListModule["buildSubagentList"]>, runId: string) => {
    const groupId = list.active.find((item) => item.runId === runId)?.sharedCwdGroupId;
    return list.sharedCwdGroups.find((group) => group.id === groupId);
  };

  const now = Date.now();

  console.log("── scenario 1: PRE-FIX CONTROL — ACP children with no persisted cwd ──");
  {
    const store = path.join(root, "sessions-acp-prefix.json");
    const dir = path.join(root, "acp-shared");
    await fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
    const runs = [makeRun("acp-prefix-a", now), makeRun("acp-prefix-b", now)];
    for (const run of runs) {
      await createChildSession({
        storePath: store,
        sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
        requestedCwd: dir,
        persistCwd: false,
      });
    }
    const { list } = await listFor(store, runs);
    console.log(`   two live ACP children in ${dir}, field not persisted`);
    check("no advisory — this is the false negative the PR fixes", () => {
      assert.equal(list.active.length, 2);
      for (const run of runs) {
        assert.equal(groupFor(list, run.runId), undefined);
      }
    });
  }

  console.log("── scenario 2: POST-FIX — the same ACP children, cwd persisted ──");
  {
    const store = path.join(root, "sessions-acp-postfix.json");
    const dir = path.join(root, "acp-shared-post");
    await fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
    const runs = [makeRun("acp-post-a", now), makeRun("acp-post-b", now)];
    for (const run of runs) {
      await createChildSession({
        storePath: store,
        sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
        requestedCwd: dir,
      });
    }
    const { list, text } = await listFor(store, runs);
    const first = groupFor(list, runs[0]!.runId);
    console.log(`   run ${runs[0]!.runId} group: ${JSON.stringify(first)}`);
    check("both ACP rows refer to one exact group summary", () => {
      assert.deepEqual(first, {
        id: 1,
        path: expectedSharedCwdPath(dir),
        runCount: 2,
        runIds: runs.map((run) => run.runId),
      });
      assert.equal(list.active[0]?.sharedCwdGroupId, 1);
      assert.equal(list.active[1]?.sharedCwdGroupId, 1);
    });
    check("the /subagents text surface emits the directory once", () => {
      const rendered = JSON.stringify(text);
      assert.equal(rendered.split(expectedSharedCwdPath(dir)).length, 2);
    });
  }

  console.log("── scenario 3: cross-runtime — one native child, one ACP child ──");
  {
    const store = path.join(root, "sessions-cross-runtime.json");
    const dir = path.join(root, "cross-runtime-shared");
    await fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
    const nativeRun = makeRun("native-child", now);
    const acpRun = makeRun("acp-child", now);
    for (const run of [nativeRun, acpRun]) {
      await createChildSession({
        storePath: store,
        sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
        requestedCwd: dir,
      });
    }
    const { list } = await listFor(store, [nativeRun, acpRun]);
    check("the native and ACP rows refer to the same group", () => {
      assert.equal(list.active.find((item) => item.runId === nativeRun.runId)?.sharedCwdGroupId, 1);
      assert.equal(list.active.find((item) => item.runId === acpRun.runId)?.sharedCwdGroupId, 1);
      // The sample is ordered by run id, not by which runtime was seen first.
      assert.deepEqual(
        groupFor(list, nativeRun.runId)?.runIds,
        [nativeRun.runId, acpRun.runId].toSorted(),
      );
    });
  }

  console.log("── scenario 4: symlink alias to one real checkout ──");
  {
    const store = path.join(root, "sessions-alias.json");
    const realDir = path.join(root, "alias-real");
    const linkDir = path.join(root, "alias-link");
    await fs.mkdir(realDir, { recursive: true });
    await fs.symlink(realDir, linkDir, "dir");
    const canonical = await fs.realpath(realDir);
    const realRun = makeRun("alias-real-run", now);
    const linkRun = makeRun("alias-link-run", now);
    await createChildSession({
      storePath: store,
      sessionKey: realRun.childSessionKey,
      requestedCwd: realDir,
    });
    await createChildSession({
      storePath: store,
      sessionKey: linkRun.childSessionKey,
      requestedCwd: linkDir,
    });
    const { list } = await listFor(store, [realRun, linkRun]);
    console.log(`   ${linkDir} -> ${canonical}`);
    console.log(`   alias group: ${JSON.stringify(groupFor(list, linkRun.runId))}`);
    check("aliased runs group together and report the canonical directory", () => {
      assert.deepEqual(groupFor(list, realRun.runId), {
        id: 1,
        path: expectedSharedCwdPath(canonical),
        runCount: 2,
        runIds: [realRun.runId, linkRun.runId].toSorted(),
      });
      assert.equal(list.active.find((item) => item.runId === linkRun.runId)?.sharedCwdGroupId, 1);
    });
  }

  console.log("── scenario 5: inherited workspace stays silent ──");
  {
    const store = path.join(root, "sessions-inherited.json");
    const runs = [makeRun("inherited-a", now), makeRun("inherited-b", now)];
    for (const run of runs) {
      await createChildSession({ storePath: store, sessionKey: run.childSessionKey });
    }
    const { list } = await listFor(store, runs);
    check("no advisory for children that named no directory", () => {
      assert.equal(list.active.length, 2);
      for (const run of runs) {
        assert.equal(groupFor(list, run.runId), undefined);
      }
    });
  }

  console.log("── scenario 6: distinct directories stay silent ──");
  {
    const store = path.join(root, "sessions-distinct.json");
    const runA = makeRun("distinct-a", now);
    const runB = makeRun("distinct-b", now);
    const dirA = path.join(root, "distinct-a-dir");
    const dirB = path.join(root, "distinct-b-dir");
    await fs.mkdir(dirA, { recursive: true });
    await fs.mkdir(dirB, { recursive: true });
    await createChildSession({
      storePath: store,
      sessionKey: runA.childSessionKey,
      requestedCwd: dirA,
    });
    await createChildSession({
      storePath: store,
      sessionKey: runB.childSessionKey,
      requestedCwd: dirB,
    });
    const { list } = await listFor(store, [runA, runB]);
    check("two different checkouts are not reported as a collision", () => {
      assert.equal(groupFor(list, runA.runId), undefined);
      assert.equal(groupFor(list, runB.runId), undefined);
    });
  }

  console.log("── scenario 7: deleted directory falls back to lexical grouping ──");
  {
    const store = path.join(root, "sessions-deleted.json");
    const dir = path.join(root, "deleted-tree");
    await fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
    const runs = [makeRun("deleted-a", now), makeRun("deleted-b", now)];
    for (const run of runs) {
      await createChildSession({
        storePath: store,
        sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
        requestedCwd: dir,
      });
    }
    await fs.rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    const { list } = await listFor(store, runs);
    console.log(`   ${dir} removed after spawn; advisory still resolves`);
    check("grouping survives an unresolvable directory without throwing", () => {
      for (const run of runs) {
        assert.equal(groupFor(list, run.runId)?.path, expectedSharedCwdPath(dir));
      }
    });
  }

  console.log("── scenario 8: model-context bound at the supported child maximum ──");
  {
    // The advisory attaches to every row of `subagents list` AND to the rendered
    // text view, so naming every peer made one ordinary call grow as O(runs^2).
    // This scenario drives the real tool payload shape and measures it.
    const PATH_MAX = 72;
    // A realistically long checkout path, as the finding calls out.
    const deepDir = path.join(
      root,
      "home/operator/projects/worktrees/openclaw-feat-subagent-shared-cwd-advisory/packages/agent-core",
    );
    await fs.mkdir(deepDir, { recursive: true });
    assert.ok(deepDir.length > PATH_MAX, "scenario needs a path longer than the display cap");

    const measure = async (childCount: number) => {
      const store = path.join(root, `sessions-bound-${childCount}.json`);
      const runs = Array.from({ length: childCount }, (_unused, i) =>
        makeRun(`bound-${childCount}-${String(i).padStart(2, "0")}`, now),
      );
      for (const run of runs) {
        await createChildSession({
          storePath: store,
          sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
          requestedCwd: deepDir,
        });
      }
      const { list } = await listFor(store, runs);
      // Exactly what subagents-tool.ts emits for `action: "list"`: structured
      // rows with `line` stripped, plus the rendered text view.
      const modelVisible = JSON.stringify({
        sharedCwdGroupTotal: list.sharedCwdGroupTotal,
        sharedCwdGroups: list.sharedCwdGroups,
        active: list.active.map(({ line: _line, ...view }) => view),
        recent: list.recent.map(({ line: _line, ...view }) => view),
        text: list.text,
      });
      return { list, runs, modelVisible };
    };

    const at20 = await measure(20);
    const at50 = await measure(50);
    for (const [childCount, m] of [
      [20, at20],
      [50, at50],
    ] as const) {
      console.log(
        `   ${String(childCount).padStart(2)} children sharing one cwd: ${m.modelVisible.length} B model-visible, ${m.list.sharedCwdGroups.length} directory summary`,
      );
    }

    check("one summary reports the exact group size with a fixed run-id sample", () => {
      assert.equal(at20.list.sharedCwdGroups.length, 1);
      assert.equal(at20.list.sharedCwdGroups[0]?.runCount, 20);
      assert.equal(at20.list.sharedCwdGroups[0]?.runIds.length, 3);
      assert.equal(at50.list.sharedCwdGroups.length, 1);
      assert.equal(at50.list.sharedCwdGroups[0]?.runCount, 50);
      assert.equal(at50.list.sharedCwdGroups[0]?.runIds.length, 3);
    });
    check("only the sampled members carry row-level group references", () => {
      assert.equal(
        at20.list.active.filter((item) => item.sharedCwdGroupId !== undefined).length,
        3,
      );
      assert.equal(
        at50.list.active.filter((item) => item.sharedCwdGroupId !== undefined).length,
        3,
      );
    });
    check(`the reported directory is capped at ${PATH_MAX} characters`, () => {
      const reported = at20.list.sharedCwdGroups[0]?.path ?? "";
      assert.ok(reported.length <= PATH_MAX, `reported path was ${reported.length} characters`);
      assert.ok(reported.startsWith("..."), `expected a truncation marker: ${reported}`);
      assert.ok(reported.endsWith("packages/agent-core"), `lost the path tail: ${reported}`);
      // The untruncated path must not leak into the payload anywhere.
      assert.ok(
        !at20.modelVisible.includes(deepDir),
        "the full path reached the model-visible payload",
      );
    });
    check("the text view emits the group once with its true size", () => {
      assert.ok(at20.list.text.includes("[cwd 1] 20 live runs:"));
      assert.equal(at20.list.text.split(at20.list.sharedCwdGroups[0]!.path).length, 2);
    });
    // Sibling checkouts identical for their first 100+ characters, differing
    // only past the display cap: grouping must still keep them apart.
    const alphaDir = path.join(deepDir, "openclaw-worktree-alpha");
    const betaDir = path.join(deepDir, "openclaw-worktree-beta");
    await fs.mkdir(alphaDir, { recursive: true });
    await fs.mkdir(betaDir, { recursive: true });
    const siblingStore = path.join(root, "sessions-bound-siblings.json");
    const alphaRuns = ["sib-alpha-a", "sib-alpha-b"].map((suffix) => makeRun(suffix, now));
    const betaRuns = ["sib-beta-a", "sib-beta-b"].map((suffix) => makeRun(suffix, now));
    for (const [runs, dir] of [
      [alphaRuns, alphaDir],
      [betaRuns, betaDir],
    ] as const) {
      for (const run of runs) {
        await createChildSession({
          storePath: siblingStore,
          sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
          requestedCwd: dir,
        });
      }
    }
    const siblingList = (await listFor(siblingStore, [...alphaRuns, ...betaRuns])).list;
    const alphaAdvisory = groupFor(siblingList, alphaRuns[0]!.runId);
    const betaAdvisory = groupFor(siblingList, betaRuns[0]!.runId);
    console.log(`   sibling alpha reports: ${alphaAdvisory?.path}`);
    console.log(`   sibling beta  reports: ${betaAdvisory?.path}`);
    check("sibling checkouts past the display cap remain distinct groups", () => {
      assert.equal(alphaAdvisory?.runCount, 2);
      assert.equal(betaAdvisory?.runCount, 2);
      assert.notEqual(
        alphaAdvisory?.path,
        betaAdvisory?.path,
        "the display cap collapsed two distinct directories into one label",
      );
    });

    const manyStore = path.join(root, "sessions-bound-many-groups.json");
    const manyRuns: SubagentRunRecord[] = [];
    for (let groupIndex = 0; groupIndex < 25; groupIndex += 1) {
      const dir = path.join(root, `many-group-${String(groupIndex).padStart(2, "0")}`);
      for (let runIndex = 0; runIndex < 2; runIndex += 1) {
        const run = makeRun(`many-${groupIndex}-${runIndex}`, now);
        manyRuns.push(run);
        await createChildSession({
          storePath: manyStore,
          sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
          requestedCwd: dir,
        });
      }
    }
    const manyList = (await listFor(manyStore, manyRuns)).list;
    check("50 children across 25 shared directories emit only eight summaries", () => {
      assert.equal(manyList.sharedCwdGroupTotal, 25);
      assert.equal(manyList.sharedCwdGroups.length, 8);
      assert.equal(
        manyList.active.filter((item) => item.sharedCwdGroupId !== undefined).length,
        16,
      );
      assert.ok(manyList.text.includes("shared working directories (8/25 shown):"));
    });

    // `sortSubagentRuns` compares start timestamps only, so this
    // same-millisecond cohort reaches the advisory in whatever order the
    // caller's array had. With 25 groups against a cap of 8, that order used to
    // decide the group ids, the samples, and which directories were reported at
    // all. Permuting it must now leave the whole report unchanged.
    const summarizeMany = async (input: SubagentRunRecord[]) => {
      const list = (await listFor(manyStore, input)).list;
      return JSON.stringify({
        total: list.sharedCwdGroupTotal,
        groups: list.sharedCwdGroups,
        // Sorted so the comparison isolates group assignment from the row
        // ordering the permutation legitimately changes.
        assignments: list.active
          .map((item) => `${item.runId}=${item.sharedCwdGroupId ?? "none"}`)
          .toSorted(),
      });
    };
    const inOrderSummary = await summarizeMany(manyRuns);
    const reversedSummary = await summarizeMany(manyRuns.toReversed());
    const interleavedSummary = await summarizeMany([
      ...manyRuns.filter((_unused, i) => i % 2 === 1),
      ...manyRuns.filter((_unused, i) => i % 2 === 0),
    ]);
    console.log(
      `   reported directories: ${manyList.sharedCwdGroups.map((group) => path.basename(group.path)).join(", ")}`,
    );
    check("permuting equal-timestamp runs leaves the whole report identical", () => {
      assert.equal(reversedSummary, inOrderSummary);
      assert.equal(interleavedSummary, inOrderSummary);
    });
  }

  console.log("── scenario 9: the reader/advisory metadata key contract ──");
  {
    // The defect this round fixed was invisible to every scenario above that
    // asserted only an end result: the advisory read the reader's selection by
    // child session key while the reader stores it by run id, so every ordinary
    // child resolved to `undefined` and the advisory went silent. Drive the real
    // reader's own selection object through the owner, not a reconstructed one.
    const store = path.join(root, "sessions-key-contract.json");
    const dir = path.join(root, "key-contract-shared");
    await fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
    const runs = [makeRun("key-contract-a", now), makeRun("key-contract-b", now)];
    for (const run of runs) {
      await createChildSession({
        storePath: store,
        sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
        requestedCwd: dir,
      });
    }
    const cfg = { session: { store } } as OpenClawConfig;
    const context = buildReadContext(runs, 30);
    const selection = await readSubagentListSessionEntries(cfg, context);
    console.log(
      `   reader selection keys: ${[...selection.keys()].join(", ")} (run ids: ${runs
        .map((run) => run.runId)
        .join(", ")}; session keys: ${runs.map((run) => run.childSessionKey).join(", ")})`,
    );
    // Same selection object the production callers pass, consumed by the owner
    // under test — so a producer/consumer key disagreement cannot pass here.
    // The key shape itself is not asserted separately: this call detects the
    // disagreement, and `subagent-list.test.ts` covers cross-agent raw keys.
    const list = buildSubagentList({ context, sessionEntries: selection });
    check("the advisory consumes that selection under the same key", () => {
      assert.equal(list.sharedCwdGroupTotal, 1);
      assert.equal(list.sharedCwdGroups[0]?.runCount, runs.length);
      assert.ok(list.active.every((item) => item.sharedCwdGroupId === 1));
    });
  }

  console.log("── scenario 10: sender-restricted helpers are not an explicit request ──");
  {
    // Both spawn owners refuse any cwd that is not the requester's own root
    // for a restricted sender, then hand the child exactly that root as
    // `spawnedCwd` so the restriction stays enforceable. Two such helpers
    // therefore always name one directory, with nothing the operator could
    // change — the inherited-workspace case the advisory exempts. The control
    // below writes the identical directory WITHOUT the policy marker, so this
    // measures the marker rather than the path.
    const store = path.join(root, "sessions-restricted.json");
    const requesterRoot = path.join(root, "restricted-root");
    await fs.mkdir(requesterRoot, { recursive: true });
    const restricted = [makeRun("restricted-a", now), makeRun("restricted-b", now)];
    for (const run of restricted) {
      await createChildSession({
        storePath: store,
        sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
        requestedCwd: requesterRoot,
        senderRestricted: true,
      });
    }
    const cfg = { session: { store } } as OpenClawConfig;
    const restrictedContext = buildReadContext(restricted, 30);
    const restrictedSelection = await readSubagentListSessionEntries(cfg, restrictedContext);
    console.log(
      `   restricted entries persist spawnedCwd=${restrictedSelection.get(restricted[0]!.runId)?.spawnedCwd} inheritedToolPolicySource=${restrictedSelection.get(restricted[0]!.runId)?.inheritedToolPolicySource}`,
    );
    check("the enforced working directory is still on the entry, not cleared", () => {
      for (const run of restricted) {
        assert.equal(restrictedSelection.get(run.runId)?.spawnedCwd, path.resolve(requesterRoot));
        assert.equal(restrictedSelection.get(run.runId)?.sessionRoot, path.resolve(requesterRoot));
      }
    });
    const { list: restrictedList, text: restrictedText } = await listFor(store, restricted);
    check("two restricted helpers in one root produce no advisory", () => {
      assert.equal(restrictedList.sharedCwdGroupTotal, 0);
      assert.deepEqual(restrictedList.sharedCwdGroups, []);
      assert.ok(restrictedList.active.every((item) => item.sharedCwdGroupId === undefined));
      assert.equal(restrictedList.text.includes("shared working directories"), false);
      assert.equal(JSON.stringify(restrictedText).includes("shared working directories"), false);
      assert.equal(JSON.stringify(restrictedText).includes("shared cwd group"), false);
    });

    const controlStore = path.join(root, "sessions-restricted-control.json");
    const control = [makeRun("restricted-control-a", now), makeRun("restricted-control-b", now)];
    for (const run of control) {
      await createChildSession({
        storePath: controlStore,
        sessionKey: run.childSessionKey,
        requestedCwd: requesterRoot,
      });
    }
    const { list: controlList } = await listFor(controlStore, control);
    check("the same directory without the policy marker is still reported", () => {
      assert.equal(controlList.sharedCwdGroupTotal, 1);
      assert.equal(controlList.sharedCwdGroups[0]?.path, expectedSharedCwdPath(requesterRoot));
      assert.equal(controlList.sharedCwdGroups[0]?.runCount, control.length);
    });
  }

  await fs.rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true });

  if (failures > 0) {
    console.log(`\n${failures} runtime assertion(s) FAILED.`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log("\nAll runtime assertions passed.");
  process.exit(0);
}

await main();
```

</details>

This head merges current main (`8408f1b5755`) into the branch; the focused suites and the proof above were run at it. The PR stays draft until the full gates re-run.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing canonical family metadata on native Anthropic generated and discovered models outside the shipped manifest, which prevents requester-visible catalogs from reliably identifying their model family.

## User Impact

User impact: native Anthropic models such as Fable retain their authoritative family through configured-model completion and catalog publication without guessing a family for unknown deployments or other compatible hosts. No configuration migration or new user action is required. This PR does not deploy or reload a running Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing native producers now carry the family declared by their owning provider manifest. Capability, compatibility, model identity, routing, and authentication behavior remain unchanged. Tests cover native generation, authenticated discovery, configured completion through catalog publication, and negative host/model boundaries. The discovery fixture uses the actual auth provenance type, and the CLI-only scope test rejects reads through either credential resolver.

The change stays in six existing files: five production lines, focused regression coverage, and documentation. No new runtime abstraction or test-only production hook was added. The author completed the repository simplification and test-quality audit.

## Evidence

Reviewed source: `739d76b0ecaf9a47d395bb88a23f10518181dba4`, parent `a3d5baaabd2ce88ace4b5d1c45a9577a61dbc08a`, tree `80612fb08aa5ca25a57c9b349250af420bf13690`.

- Red/green regression: removing the two production fixes produced 9 failed / 9 passed touched-file tests; restoring them passed all 18 touched-file tests.
- Affected catalog, requester, persistence, and manifest siblings: 134 passed with one profile-sensitive Doctor-string failure. That sibling passed 3/3 with the inherited profile unset.
- After the review repairs, `extensions/anthropic/live-discovery-auth.test.ts` passed 4/4 (48.14 seconds wall time, about 1.04 seconds test execution). Production bytes and other test inputs were unchanged.
- Formatting, diff checks, core changed-file lint, plugin boundaries, import cycles, assertion/mock ratchets, and the other completed guards passed. The two selected Doctor declaration tests passed after restoring their pinned workspace dependency links.
- Canonical API review: complete, scoped-clean initial P0–P2 review plus complete, scoped-clean P0–P3 review of the auth-fixture/custody correction with the full changed test, auth contract, and determining catalog owners. Initial coverage is carried only for unchanged source; the final source tree matches the correction review exactly. The route reported `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`; medium reasoning and fast service were requested, not independently verified as server-effective controls.
- Independent peer review found the invalid auth provenance and weakened custody assertion; both were repaired. The peer accepted the final source commit/tree with no new findings.

**Remaining validation limits:** full local `check-changed` is not green. Compiler/declaration containment guards reject the canonical shared dependency layout, blocking the relevant typechecks and extension lint. A production dead-export scan reports `readPendingInputSource`; its owner/reference inventory matches the base, but no equivalent exact-base scan was run, so this is not claimed as a proven baseline failure. Raw `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --noEmit --incremental false` completed with exit 2: zero diagnostics in the six changed files or native Anthropic directory, but thousands elsewhere, including absent unrelated dependencies. The peer independently observed zero native Anthropic diagnostics and an overall failing typecheck. These are not green typing or CI results.

Broad build/type/security/check proof remains owned by exact-published-head PR CI. The evidence above is source-level validation, not live-provider or deployed-runtime proof.

prs.title: fix(subagents): completion review no longer repeats a result the user already saw
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the parent agent sends a subagent's result (text and images) to the user a second time when the subagent, or the parent itself, already delivered it through the message tool.

## User Impact

User impact: a background subagent that sends its result directly to the user is no longer followed by a parent reply that repeats the same text and re-attaches the same files. Observed on WebChat, where the user saw every image and text twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The default completion review instruction in `buildAnnounceReplyInstruction` said:

> Otherwise send a truthful user-facing update unless this exact result is already visible to the user in this same turn.

A completion announce always runs as a new requester turn, so "in this same turn" never matches. A result the child already sent with the message tool, or the parent sent earlier, still looks unseen, and the parent repeats it.

The instruction now says to send only what the user has not seen yet. If the result's text or files were already delivered earlier in this conversation, by the parent or by the subagent, the parent must not repeat them or re-attach the files, and at most confirms in one short sentence.

This PR deliberately does **not** reintroduce `NO_REPLY` guidance into the completion instruction. #162567 removed internal silence guidance so that silence could not hide unfinished work, and the existing failure-findings test still asserts the token is absent. The generic system prompt's silent-reply rule still applies when the model has nothing to add. On this path, a silent reply is already safe: `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` passes `sourceTool: "subagent_announce"`, and `subagent-announce-direct-response.ts` settles a successful, non-yielded `subagent_announce` completion without a visible payload as delivered ("Consuming child findings settles delivery; the parent owns any later answer"). That check runs before the result-required and message-tool checks. `buildAnnounceReplyInstruction` has a single caller; private (`completionTarget: "parent"`), nested-subagent and `subagent_settle` completions use their own instructions and are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New focused test in `subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts` asserts that the user-facing parent's completion context names "already delivered … earlier in this conversation" and "do not repeat it or re-attach its files", and contains neither "in this same turn" nor `NO_REPLY`.
- Red on base / green with the fix:

  - Base `8ef78ec2d` with the fix reverted, `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "resend a result"`: **1 failed** (received) context still contained "unless this exact result is already visible to the user in this same turn").
  - With the fix rebased onto `91046f7bb`, whole file `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **31 passed (31)**, including the existing failure-findings case that asserts `NO_REPLY` stays out of the completion context.
- A local probe through `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (not committed) confirmed a silent requester result for a `subagent_announce` completion settles as `delivered: true` on both a WebChat session origin and a Telegram route.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both touched files: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- Not run: a live Gateway reproduction with a real model and channel. The change is prompt text only, and model compliance with it is not proven by these tests.

prs.title: fix(update): honor server recovery captures in supervised migrations
prs.body:
Closes #198334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: during a supervised migration (`oc update` migrate path), the database backup is created without the `postgresSchemaCaptures` setting, so a configuration with `database.postgres.recoveryCaptures: "server"` produces local exports for non-state PostgreSQL stores and leaves behind an ambiguous recovery set instead of the server captures the recovery inventory expects.

## User Impact

When recovery captures are configured as `server`, a supervised migration now backs up non-state PostgreSQL stores on the database (server captures), matching what the native update path already does and what the recovery inventory expects to find. No configuration change, migration, or user action is required; behavior is unchanged for every other `recoveryCaptures` setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native update path passes `postgresSchemaCaptures: source.config.database?.postgres?.recoveryCaptures === "server"` to `createUpdateDatabaseBackup`, but the supervised migration path (`updateMigrateCommand`) omitted the flag entirely. The two paths therefore disagreed about where non-state PostgreSQL stores live after a backup: the migration wrote local exports while recovery tooling expected server captures, which surfaces as ambiguous recovery sets and failed Doctor finalization during update repair. The fix forwards the same flag from the same config source, restoring parity between the two update paths; no other backup options or migration steps are touched.

## Evidence

- [x] Regression tests red→green: "honors the configured recovery captures in the migration database backup (server)" and "(portable)" in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrate.test.ts` fail on main (expected `postgresSchemaCaptures === true`, received `undefined`) and pass with the fix. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrate.test.ts` — before: 2 passed / 16 failed; after: 4 passed / 16 failed (the same 16 failures, unchanged).
- [x] Related targeted suites: the other 16 failures in that file are pre-existing and unrelated to this change — they fail identically before and after the fix with local-filesystem environment errors (`FsSafeError` `path-mismatch`, a `linkedom` `entities/decode` export resolution error) on this Windows contributor machine; the failing set is byte-identical across the red and green runs, which is the relevant comparison.
- [x] Behavior verification: the new tests assert `createUpdateDatabaseBackup` receives `postgresSchemaCaptures: true` when `recoveryCaptures: "server"` in both server and portable configurations; on main the option arrives as `undefined`, with the fix it arrives as `true`.
- [x] Scope: one production file (`update-command-migrate.ts`, 4 added lines forwarding the existing config flag) plus two regression test cases (31 added test lines). The native update path, backup implementation, and all other migration steps are untouched.
- [x] Repo checks: `oc.sh check` — oxlint 0 errors on changed files; `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` reports 63 errors vs the documented 64-error baseline (none in changed files); test-lines ratchet vs `upstream/main` passes.

prs.title: test(qa): two QA lab end-to-end tests fail on main
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: two QA lab end-to-end tests fail on `main`, so every pull request whose CI selects them is red for a reason it did not cause.

- `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/telegram-model-picker-prepared-gateway.e2e.test.ts` fails with `Could not resolve built prepared-model-runtime- module`.
- `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-timeout-recovery-subagent.e2e.test.ts` fails because the expected child reply never arrives.

## User Impact

User impact: none. This changes two test files. Contributors stop seeing these two failures on unrelated pull requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both tests were left behind by product changes that are correct. No assertion, timeout, or retry changes.

**Model picker test.** It found hashed `dist/` chunks by searching for export text that contained spaces. #197801 turned on compact build output, so chunks now read `export{startGatewayServer,truncateCloseReason}` and the search stopped matching. That change updated the same kind of marker in four scripts and missed this test. The test now parses candidate chunks and matches the names its bootstrap script imports, so bundler formatting no longer matters.

**Timeout recovery test.** Its mock provider read only the last request item to decide whether the parent had received the child's completion. Since #198100 a prompt update item is appended after the turn's input, so the completion was no longer last and the mock answered as a plain retry. The Gateway still delivered the completion once. The mock now reads everything after the previous assistant reply, the rule #198177 already applied to `src/gateway/server.subagent-prompt-recent.gateway.test.ts`.

## Evidence

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files>`, which builds `dist/` itself.

| Tree | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `main` at `858b5b0` and at `90c620b`, unmodified | Model picker: 1 failed, 2 passed. Timeout recovery: 1 failed, expected `["…PARENT-OK", "…CHILD-OK"]`, received `["…PARENT-OK", "…PARENT-OK"]`. |
| This branch on `main` at `746135b` | Both files pass, 4 of 4 tests. |

The timeout recovery test passes on `81daea9`, the parent of #198100, and fails on #198100 itself.

prs.title: test(codex): worker command test fails on fork pull requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `extensions/codex/src/node-app-server.runtime.test.ts` fails on pull requests from forks, so their CI is red for a reason they did not cause.

The case "gates native resource readiness, resumes exact state, and retains failed-cleanup custody" expects a worker `command/exec` to exit 0 and gets exit 1 with empty output.

## User Impact

User impact: none. This changes one test file. Fork contributors stop seeing this failure on unrelated pull requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test sent `command/exec` with no sandbox policy, so Codex applied its default policy and wrapped the command in `bwrap`. Where unprivileged user namespaces are denied, the command exits 1 with `bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace`. #198140 moved fork pull requests to GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runners, which restrict those namespaces, and the case began failing there. No product code changed.

The case proves that a worker gates `command/exec` on resource readiness and then forwards it. It does not set out to prove that the host can run Codex's sandbox. The request now asks for `dangerFullAccess` for this one command, as `run-attempt.test.ts` and `thread-lifecycle.test.ts` already do. The assertion is unchanged.

Tradeoff: this case no longer exercises Codex's default Linux sandbox. Same-repository pull requests still run where `bwrap` works, so a future test that depends on the default sandbox would fail only for forks.

## Evidence

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/node-app-server.runtime.test.ts`

| Where | Test file | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node:24.20.0-bookworm` arm64 container, `main` at `858b5b0` and at `bd02bf9` | unmodified | 1 failed (`exitCode: 1`, `stdout: ""`) |
| Same image with `--privileged` | unmodified | 1 passed |
| Same container | with this change | 1 passed |
| macOS | with this change | 1 passed |

In CI the same check passed on #197922 before #198140 and failed in both runs after it. The hosted runner's own stderr was not captured; the `bwrap` message comes from the container.

The container and macOS runs with this change predate the move onto `main` at `746135b`, which touched no Codex file. This pull request's own CI runs the case on the hosted runner where it failed.

The format check and `git diff --check` pass. The test file was read in full; nothing was removed.

No autoreview pass: the helper could not run on the authoring machine.

prs.title: feat(msteams): send private and shared channel files to the channel's own SharePoint site
prs.body:
Closes #185926

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bots cannot send files in Microsoft Teams private or shared channels unless an operator configures a single central `sharePointSiteId`, which exposes every private channel's files to that site's members and still shows "request access" to channel members.

## User Impact

User impact: in private and shared channels, file sends now land on that channel's own SharePoint site, where exactly the channel's members already have access, and the file card opens without extra permissions. No organization-wide sharing link is created for those files. Standard channels, group chats and explicit `sharePointSiteId` keep their current behavior. No new Graph permissions and no config changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on #189339. Teams keeps a private/shared channel's site membership in sync with the channel, so the channel's own site is the only upload target that preserves the channel audience. For a non-standard `membershipType`, the resolver reads `GET /teams/{groupId}/channels/{channelId}/filesFolder`, then `GET /drives/{driveId}?$select=sharePointIds` (drive resources spell it `sharePointIds`; driveItems use `sharepointIds`), and builds the site ID `{hostname},{siteId},{webId}`. Results are cached per account, tenant, bot, team and channel, like the team-site cache.

`resolveMSTeamsSharePointSiteId` now returns `{ siteId, memberScoped }`. Member-scoped uploads skip `createLink`: the organization link that channel sends create would let anyone in the tenant holding its URL read a private-channel file, and channel membership already grants access through the file card's `webDavUrl`. An incomplete drive response fails closed before upload.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests:** `vitest` msteams config, 92 files / 943 tests pass. New cases run the real send paths (proactive and reply) against stubbed Graph `fetch`: private and shared channels upload to the channel site, never call `/groups/.../sites/root` or `createLink`, and cache the channel site (one `filesFolder` call across two sends); member-scoped uploads create no link; incomplete `sharePointIds` fails closed.
- **Static:** `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: typecheck (extensions and extension tests), lint, plugin boundaries and the other guards pass. The dead-export scan fails only on `src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-prepared-read.ts` (`retireControlUiSessionPrState`), unrelated to this change.

### Real behavior proof (production)

Multi-team production deployment, private channel, `sharePointSiteId` absent.

**Before** (#189339's behavior; private channels rejected). Gateway file log, redacted:

```
14:00:01Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 3 rows of test data"
          conversation: 19:<private-channel-id>@thread.tacv2;messageid=<id>
14:00:01Z [msteams] dispatching to agent
14:02:57Z [tools] tool_call failed: msteams file send failed: Automatic SharePoint site discovery
          supports standard channels only. Set channels.msteams.sharePointSiteId to upload to a specific site.
14:03:02Z [msteams] dispatch complete — counts: { tool: 0, block: 0, final: 1 }
```

The user received a text-only reply. No file reached the channel.

**After** (this change, backported onto the deployed release). Same private channel, first file send after a gateway restart (empty cache):

```
11:24:17Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 4 rows of test data"
11:24:17Z [msteams] dispatching to agent — sessionKey: agent:main:msteams:channel:19:<private-channel-id>…
11:24:36Z [msteams:send] sent native file card — fileName: <report> 1.csv
```

Graph check after the send (bot application credentials):

- `<folder>/<report> 1.csv` (created 11:24:35Z) sits on the private channel's own site (`/sites/<team>-<private-channel>`).
- Item permissions are only the channel site's Owners / Members / Visitors groups. No `organization` link.
- The parent team site has no entry for this send.
- The requester opened the file card from the channel.

During rollout, the first build read `sharepointIds` from the drive and failed closed ("incomplete SharePoint IDs") without uploading anything; Graph returns `sharePointIds` on drive resources. A later build still created the organization link; Graph showed it on the item, which is why member-scoped uploads now skip `createLink`.

### Access check (member, non-member, removal)

Same private channel. Each person opened the file's direct document URL in a browser, signed in with their own work account. Times are UTC.

| Step | Who | File | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Channel member | `<report-1>.csv`, sent by the bot | Opens (09:14) |
| 2 | Owner of the parent team, not a channel member. Also tried with their admin account | `<report-1>.csv` | Access denied (09:16) |
| 3 | The step 1 member, removed from the channel about 6 minutes earlier | `<report-1>.csv` | "You need access" (09:24) |
| 4 | Bot sends a new file in the same channel. No gateway restart, so the channel site comes from the cache | `<report-2>.csv` | Lands on the channel site (09:23). Inherits the library permissions; no sharing link |
| 5 | The removed member | `<report-2>.csv` | "You need access" (09:26) |
| 6 | A channel owner | `<report-2>.csv` | Opens (09:25) |

The removed user left the channel site's Members group without any bot action (checked 09:18). Access follows Teams channel membership.

Before step 1, an organization link on `<report-1>.csv` was deleted. A manual "Copy link" in the Teams client had created it, not the bot. After that, both files grant access only to the channel site's Owners, Members and Visitors groups (checked through SharePoint REST as a channel owner).

prs.title: fix(daemon): name the refused Scheduled Task action shape
prs.body:
Fixes #198287

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, when the `OpenClaw Gateway` Scheduled Task action is a `.vbs` path used directly as the `Command` (no `wscript.exe` prefix), service-definition inspection refuses the action and every surface collapses to the bare sentence `Effective Scheduled Task service command could not be inspected.` The cause was computed and then dropped: `readScheduledTaskCommand` catches the launcher refusal and re-throws the generic message, so an unsupported action shape is indistinguishable from a missing binary, an unreadable file, or malformed task XML. `openclaw gateway status --deep --json` reported `service.command: null` with `service-runtime-inspection-failed`, and `doctor` printed the same bare line in three sections.

The refusal now names the reason and the shapes the inspector accepts. A follow-up commit on this branch makes the recovery text agree with the reader that refused the shape: the CMD example now uses the doubled quoting Task Scheduler actually stores, and a refused Startup entry no longer receives Scheduled Task examples.

## User Impact

The refusal names the reason and the shapes the reader accepts:

```
Effective Scheduled Task service command could not be inspected. The task action was
refused: Unrecognized Scheduled Task launcher. Accepted Scheduled Task action shapes:
a native .exe; cmd.exe with Arguments /d /s /c ""<launcher>.cmd"";
wscript.exe with Arguments "<launcher>.vbs".
```

- The `cmd.exe` example is the exact `Arguments` value the registered-launcher matcher accepts. The previously advertised single-quoted form took the native-executable path instead: `service.command` became `cmd.exe /d /s /c <launcher>` with `sourcePath: null`, so the launcher was never read and no failure was reported.
- A refused Startup entry now says `The startup entry was refused: Unrecognized Startup launcher. Accepted Startup entry shapes: start "" /min cmd.exe /d /c "<launcher>.cmd".` It previously received the Scheduled Task action examples, although that reader only accepts the generated wrapper and rejects a native `.exe`.

Only closed, fixed refusal strings are surfaced — never a launcher path, its arguments, or a credential — so the existing redaction contract is unchanged. Refusals unrelated to the action shape still return the original bare message.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: name the observed action and the accepted shapes. The refusal text already exists at each rejection site as a closed string; the fix carries the matching one into the surface diagnostic instead of discarding it at the catch boundary.

Review then pointed out that one message cannot serve two readers: the CMD matcher requires `/d /s /c ""<launcher>.cmd""` (doubled quotes), and `readStartupEntryCommand` reaches the same throw with a Startup entry that is not a Task action at all. Both readers are unchanged here — only the recovery text and its selection by entry kind.

## Evidence

![real CLI A/B: refusal naming and the shape each reader accepts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/198374/proof-198374-action-shape.png)

### 1. Recovery text now matches the reader (previous head `c8795192` → this commit)

Windows 11 host, real objects, shipped CLI `node openclaw.mjs gateway status --deep --json` on a `gatewayWatch` build with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and port 28793. Tasks were registered with `Register-ScheduledTask` and deleted after the captures.

| case | real object | before `c8795192` | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Task `Command=<rig>\gateway.vbs`, no `Arguments` (the reporter's shape) | advertises `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<launcher>.cmd"` | advertises `cmd.exe with Arguments /d /s /c ""<launcher>.cmd""` |
| B | Task `Command=cmd.exe`, `Arguments=/d /s /c ""<rig>\gateway.cmd""` (the newly documented form) | inner command inspected, `sourcePath=gateway.cmd` | inner command inspected, `sourcePath=gateway.cmd` |
| D | Task `Command=cmd.exe`, `Arguments=/d /s /c "<rig>\gateway.cmd"` (the previously documented form) | `command=cmd.exe /d /s /c <launcher>`, `sourcePath=null`, no failure | same behavior; the diagnostic no longer advertises this form |
| C | Startup entry `%APPDATA%\...\Startup\OpenClaw Gateway.cmd` holding one plain node line | `The task action was refused: ... Accepted Scheduled Task action shapes: ...` | `The startup entry was refused: ... Accepted Startup entry shapes: start "" /min cmd.exe /d /c "<launcher>.cmd".` |

Raw captures (`gateway status --deep --json`, service block only):

```
# A, previous head
"detail": "... The task action was refused: Unrecognized Scheduled Task launcher. Accepted Scheduled Task action shapes: a native .exe; cmd.exe /d /s /c \"<launcher>.cmd\"; wscript.exe \"<launcher>.vbs\"."

# A, this commit
"detail": "... The task action was refused: Unrecognized Scheduled Task launcher. Accepted Scheduled Task action shapes: a native .exe; cmd.exe with Arguments /d /s /c \"\"<launcher>.cmd\"\"; wscript.exe with Arguments \"<launcher>.vbs\"."

# B, this commit (following the documented example restores inspection)
"command": { "programArguments": ["C:\\Program Files\\nodejs\\node.exe", "C:\\Services\\Gateway\\openclaw.mjs", "gateway", "--port", "28793"], "sourcePath": "C:\\Users\\lucien\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\proof198374b\\svc\\gateway.cmd" }
"runtime":  { "status": "unknown" }

# D, this commit (the old example bypasses resolution: cmd.exe is the service)
"command": { "programArguments": ["C:\\Windows\\System32\\cmd.exe", "/d", "/s", "/c", "C:\\Users\\lucien\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\proof198374b\\svc\\gateway.cmd"] }
"sourcePath": null

# C, previous head
Startup service command could not be inspected. The task action was refused: Unrecognized Startup launcher. Accepted Scheduled Task action shapes: ...

# C, this commit
Startup service command could not be inspected. The startup entry was refused: Unrecognized Startup launcher. Accepted Startup entry shapes: start "" /min cmd.exe /d /c "<launcher>.cmd".
```

Case C has no shipped CLI surface: `gateway status --deep` reads Startup entries only through the deep inventory, and it discards inventory errors, so the same built `dist` reader was called directly on a real file in a redirected `%APPDATA%` Startup folder.

### 2. The original refusal naming (main → branch)

![real CLI A/B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/198287/proof-198287.png)

A real Scheduled Task with the reporter's action shape — `Command=...\gateway.vbs`, no `Arguments` — driven through the shipped CLI. One variable differs between runs: this change.

| build | `service.command` | `service.runtime.inspectionFailure.detail` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | `null` | `Effective Scheduled Task service command could not be inspected.` |
| this branch | `null` | same sentence + `The task action was refused: Unrecognized Scheduled Task launcher.` + the accepted shapes |

### Tests and gates

- `src/daemon/schtasks.test.ts`: 45 passed (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/daemon/schtasks.test.ts`). The table test asserts the exact surfaced text for three refused Task shapes, and a new test drives the production `readStartupEntryCommand` with an unrecognized Startup launcher and asserts the Startup-specific guidance.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on both files, `check:line-cap-ratchet` OK, `check:test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main`: net test lines +50, allowance 400.

The throwaway Scheduled Tasks and temp directory were removed after the captures.

## What was not tested

- The reporter's exact 2026.11.3 `pnpm add -g` install was not reproduced: the same production read path was exercised from source on this host, against real Task definitions. `openclaw doctor` / Control UI update surfaces were not re-run; they consume the same `service-runtime-inspection-failed` detail.
- Case C calls the built `dist` reader rather than a CLI command, because no shipped command prints Startup inventory errors. The Startup entry used is a real file in the Startup folder; the generated wrapper itself was not re-run through the full startup control path.
- A `.vbs` whose body *is* the generated launcher shape (used directly as `Command`) still inspects as before — that path is unchanged, and is not covered by the new message.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): approve an app's node together with its owner device
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Mac app is moving to sign-in-first OpenClaw ID enrollment: the owner signs in and approves the Mac as an owner device. Its node (running tools on the Mac) should come from that same approval, not a separate node invite and six-digit ceremony.

## User Impact

- When an owner approves a new device that also asks to run tools, the Control UI approval dialog names the claw and says "<device> will also be able to run tools for <claw>: <surface>. Its own permissions still apply." One compared number and one click approve both the device and its node.
- Approval copy now says "device" instead of "browser".
- Owners get a toast when the recovery kit was used to add a device ("Your recovery kit was used to add <device>"), with a link to Your devices.
- Your devices tags such a device "Runs tools". The remove confirm says its node goes too.
- Access lists the node as "<device> · Your device", with a visible **Stop using for tools** action. That removes only the node; the device stays.

## Why This Change Was Made

Protocol (unshipped v1-draft):
- `MembershipChange` `add_owner_device` gains an optional `node { peer_key, label, description }`. The node is listed in `node_peer_keys` (tunnel and relay admission unchanged) as `NodeRecord { owner_device: fp(D) }` with no `invite_id`. Auto-pairing is bounded by the approved `description`, as for invited nodes.
- The node key can never be a human key (R, any D, any owner or member peer key, including the new device's) or another node's key. A device has at most one node.
- `remove_node` removes only the node. A re-add with `node` turns it back on.
- Revoking the device (directly or through the device that approved it) or dropping it for inactivity removes its node.
- SAS `start` gains an optional `node { peer_key, description }`, covered by the commitment and transcript, so the compared code binds the node key and the surface shown. Starts and changes without `node` are byte-identical to before.
- The node is in the change rather than the owner cert because the approved surface could push the cert past Discovery's 16 KiB owner-certificate header limit.
- `isNodeDescription` is exported for approvers.

Gateway: the owner link view exposes `ownerDevice` on nodes and `nodePeerKey` on owner devices.

Supersedes the operator-key approach of #197413 (closed). Discovery re-vendor: openclaw/discovery#13. Design: sign-in-first Mac enrollment (Josh, 2026-11-11).

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src`: 224/224.
  - New `owner-device-node.test.ts`: binding, human-key refusal, remove_node keeps the device, self re-add, revocation and approver cascade, inactivity cascade, kit path with `kit_used`, and a stolen node key.
  - SAS commitment binding test.
  - New fixture vector "owner approves a device with its node".
- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/owner-approval.test.ts`: 15/15. New: node approved in the change; browser unchanged; malformed node ignored; kit-used notice names the device.
- openclaw-id UI, lib, access-extension and Gateway authority/people suites: all pass.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:extensions` clean. `pnpm check:changed`: pass (exit 0).
- Not yet: the Mac side (stacked separately), live staging proof, and Control UI screenshots (mockup renders exist; real before/after screenshots will be added before ready).

prs.title: feat(sessions): add creator-only and named-audience confidentiality
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People sharing an OpenClaw server need to choose who can find and use each conversation.

## User Impact

A conversation can be personal to its creator and administrators, shared with named people, or open to server users who already have the required permissions. This audience is separate from collaboration modes. Existing sessions without access metadata keep their previous behavior; roles and creation permissions still apply.

For attended Control UI conversations, the creator can be bound on creation or the first message when the creator-only default is enabled. “Open to the server” does not mean anonymous access. This PR does not add an invitation UI or Telegram group-membership discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audience check needs to apply to discovery, history, updates and media, rather than hiding rows only in the sidebar. Restricted history can be forked only by its direct creator or a direct administrator. Native system input keeps its provenance so it cannot silently become an attended human message.

The branch incorporates upstream `e60207216` and regenerates configuration and protocol output with the normal generators. The CI follow-up fixes the attachment-test import, keeps actual exports in the profile mock, and moves Pi integration tests out of the core-only type graph. Shared types now live with their neutral owners so they do not create import cycles.

## Evidence

The integration passed **47 protocol/access tests** on tree `7ebdc9f0`. The CI repair passed **76 affected tests in four files**, the core/extension boundary check, formatting, and the mock/assertion guards against frozen `e602`.

Final core types and the full import-cycle scan pass. The last cycle fixes change types only; all five affected production modules emit the same normalized JavaScript as their public parent. The 76-test run preceded those final type-only edits. Independent review found no P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI and maintainer security review remain separate.

These real screenshots use synthetic admin, Alice and Bob accounts from an **earlier isolated notebook build with local overlays**. They illustrate the behavior, not this public head or real LDAP logins. [Full context](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187836#issuecomment-6635034742).

![Synthetic admin, Alice and Bob session visibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/master/187836-qa-20261104/qa-187836-1e24780-visibility.png)

![Synthetic Alice allowed and denied histories](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/master/187836-qa-20261104/qa-187836-1e24780-alice-history.png)

[Earlier integrated upgrade checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187836#issuecomment-6815411364) are separate evidence. Current real-user acceptance and the broader confidentiality policy still need maintainer review. A local integration of the feature is running; it is separate from this public head. Telegram group discovery has its own request, #198188, and [upstream follow-up #198282](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198282).

prs.title: feat(macos): OpenClaw ID primary connection + dashboard proxy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Lets the macOS app use OpenClaw ID as its primary connection to a claw, with the dashboard served through an app-owned loopback proxy. This is the base for the sign-in-first Mac enrollment PRs. It extracts the reusable parts of draft #197421 and keys them to a generic in-process OpenClaw ID human peer key, owner or member, plus a claw hostname. A future enrollment owner supplies both through `MacOpenClawIDOperatorRoute.shared.enrollment`. Nothing on this branch sets it yet, so the route stays inert until the stacked enrollment PR lands.

## Stacking

**Stacked on #196759** (`openclaw-e3b/macos-live-ocid`, head `d7ca1ae95d11`), which sits on #196445 and #194201. This PR's base branch is `openclaw-e3b/macos-live-ocid`, so the diff shows only these four commits. `main` has no Swift OpenClaw ID code; the tunnel, WebSocket session, worker bridge and node-invite path all come from that stack. #196759's node-invite path is kept unchanged as the headless path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Josh approved sign-in-first Mac enrollment. A Mac signs in with OpenClaw ID and becomes an owner or member device, so it doesn't join as a node with a separate operator key (W_op). #197421 built the connection, proxy and onboarding fixes on top of the superseded node-invite plus W_op flow. This PR keeps those fixes and drops the enrollment they were tied to.

## Changes

- `MacOpenClawIDOperatorRoute`: tunnel over a supplied human key, plus the dashboard proxy. It re-verifies the claw before each dial, and a relay move invalidates the route.
- Primary Gateway over the tunnel: `GatewayEndpointStore` publishes the OpenClaw ID session with a nil token and password, so saved Gateway secrets never reach the claw.
- `MacOpenClawIDDashboardProxy`, the loopback proxy, enforces:
  - an exact Host check
  - a per-launch HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, held in a nonpersistent `WKWebsiteDataStore`
  - an exact-origin cookie content rule
  - Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checks
- WebSocket upgrades:
  - The proxy upgrades only the root `/`, and the Control UI always dials the Gateway root.
  - The worker bridge stays `/__openclaw__/worker`.
  - The codec takes a path parameter.
- The conversation WebView and the reading tabs both stay on the operator store.
- Dashboard ingress auth: a `remote-ingress` hello signs the dashboard challenge with no credential. Ingress never issues a reusable device token, so this case used to throw.
- Dashboard resolution: a joined claw resolves through the endpoint store instead of the saved-config shortcut, so the dashboard route matches the tunnel route.
- `MacOpenClawIDJoinCompletion` sets the order: mark setup complete, close onboarding, switch the primary, refresh the endpoint, then open the dashboard.
- Joined-claw onboarding: no AI setup page, an unfinished first run finishes into the dashboard, and the handoff opens the normal dashboard.
- Scope gates via `GatewayConnection.grantsScope`:
  - Pairing polls need `operator.pairing`.
  - The post-update system-event wake needs `operator.admin`.
- Error copy: a superseded dashboard open (CancellationError) reads "Reconnecting to the Gateway", with OpenClaw ID guidance for a joined claw.

## Dropped from #197421

These parts are superseded by sign-in-first enrollment:

- the W_op operator key (`OpenClawIDNodeIdentityKeychainStore(operatorKey:)`) and `operator_peer_key` redemption
- the trust target's `nodePeerKeys`
- the node-invite chat opt-in
- the "Add this Mac to a claw…" Settings entry
- the `openclaw-node://join` URL scheme and deep link
- the node-invite onboarding sheet

Because the OpenClaw ID onboarding sheet isn't on `main`, the onboarding-view guard that ignored a mode change after a finished join isn't carried either. Completion now closes onboarding before it switches the primary, so that guard isn't needed.

## Evidence

All runs were on a macOS Studio in a separate checkout, with `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1`:

- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-tests`
- `swift build --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --build-tests`

Focused tests at the rebased head `92649f3a2ba8` ran in the sandboxed runner (`sandbox-exec`, network denied except Unix sockets):

- App (327 tests in 32 suites): every OpenClaw ID, node-invite, onboarding, control-UI auth, bridge and proxy suite passed. That includes the new tests:
  - joined-claw first run
  - join ordering
  - page order
  - failure copy
  - `remote-ingress` dashboard signing
  - root-only upgrade
  - cookie rules
- App failures are pre-existing:
  - `PostUpdateBundledRuntimeTests` (1 issue)
  - `OnboardingViewSmokeTests` remote page order, from #196759's onboarding (1 issue)
  - 41 sandbox `EPERM` issues on loopback TCP fixtures in `DashboardGatewaysTests`, `DashboardTokenlessRouteTests` and `GatewayConnectionMediaAuthorityTests`
- Shared (139 tests): only `GatewayNodeSessionDashboardAuthTests` failed, on sandbox `EPERM`.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` and `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` are clean.

Native i18n baseline regenerated with `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`.

Gaps:

- There's no end-to-end proof against a live claw. Nothing on this branch supplies an enrollment, so the route is unreachable until the sign-in PR lands; that PR owns the live proof.
- The endpoint store's nil-secret publication and the `immediateDashboardEndpoint` exclusion have no unit test. Both need a live route or isolated config.

## What Problem This Solves

The composer model picker needs stable provider navigation and readable model details.

## User Impact

Providers sit in a rail at the left of the picker, with drag and Alt-arrow reordering saved as a browser UI preference; while a tab is dragged, the other tabs dim. The rail scrolls with soft edges when providers don't fit, and is hidden with a single provider and while searching.

The panel has a fixed 350 px height, sits 8 px above the model chip, and keeps that height when a search finds nothing. The header shows the provider name, a neutral chip with the credential (for example "API key") and a quiet gear, without tooltips. Model names use the strong text colour, Default is a neutral chip, and context sizes and the check sit flush right under the gear. Long names truncate and show the full name in a tooltip after a short hover. "All models (N)" stays collapsed.

The panel fades in from the chip, the list fades when switching provider, and selection colours ease; reduced motion turns these off.

## Why This Change Was Made

Updates the picker structure while retaining the existing search, virtualization, selection and account owners. The rail replaces provider disclosures. The branch is merged with current main, keeping main's provider names and artwork, runtime availability and label fixes.

Landing order: **1/4 Structure (this PR) → 2/4 Runs on, context and accounts (#192137) → 3/4 States and phone sheet (#192142) → 4/4 Cooldown (#192145)**. This PR targets main. Do not merge out of order.
