prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Telegram group can appear in the Web UI sidebar but fail to open with “Couldn't load this conversation”. DMs with a user's personal agent can be missing too.

## User Impact

Linked users can open Telegram groups and topics they belong to, read history, and continue the conversation when their existing role permits writing. They do not become Gateway owners.

Older personal DMs whose keys omit the bot account need an explicit `session.sharing.legacyDirectAccess` grant. It is limited to the specified profile, agent, account and peer, including that conversation's threads. Removing the grant or unlinking the identity revokes access.

Owner-private sessions, private audiences, incognito restrictions and read-only roles remain protected. Approval replay still requires the existing reviewer, device, role and scope checks.

**Depends on #187836.** The main-based diff includes that prerequisite's privacy changes until it lands. GitHub still reports conflicts after main advanced again; this is for feature review, not a merge-ready claim. Related: #198188. Supersedes https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/pull/6.

## Why This Change Was Made

The UI opens a message subscription before reading history. Reuse the verified channel-aware access checks for that first subscription, history, replies, media and avatars, instead of rejecting a legitimate member with a second generic visibility check.

## Evidence

Public head: `2f8285a2b64c`, after merging main `309d415c3155`.

- Core types, generated config checks, scoped lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- Focused checks passed: 31 authority tests, 42 membership/media/avatar/operator-policy tests, and the targeted revocation RPC test. Membership is mocked in these tests; they do not prove live Telegram media behavior.
- The deployed V13 integration passed real Gateway protocol checks for two linked LDAP users: a group topic and a personal-agent DM each returned 80 history messages. Read-only scopes worked; owner-private sessions stayed hidden. Temporary QA tokens were revoked.
- The operator also confirmed browser access using an employee account. This is acceptance of that deployed integration, not a standalone live test of this public head. The newer media/avatar follow-up still needs live acceptance.

Hosted CI is blocked pending maintainer approval of this revision: dependency review passed, security-sensitive review is pending, and the CI gate reports “A maintainer must approve the current PR revision.” [Security Review run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43507946982). The before-fix screenshot below is retained; an after-fix browser screenshot is still pending.

prs.title: fix(plugins): surface dropped prompt-build context
prs.body:
Supersedes #118555 (auto-closed for inactivity; branch re-merged with current main).

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins use `before_prompt_build` to add context that can determine what an agent does next. When that contribution is lost, the prompt looks exactly as it would if the plugin had nothing to report — the plugin's block is simply absent. An agent whose work queue arrives through the hook therefore cannot distinguish "no ready work" from "the ready-work block was dropped", and silently does nothing.

On `main` the loss is operator-log-only. `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-helpers.ts` wires `before_prompt_build` through a `logHookFailure` that warns and returns `undefined`, and the caller treats `undefined` identically to "contributed nothing"; `src/agents/harness/prompt-compaction-hook-helpers.ts` does the same for the harness and the authorized phase. Per-handler losses inside the chain reach only `handleHookError` in `src/plugins/hooks.ts`, with no callback that lets a caller observe a discarded contribution.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a contribution is dispatched and then lost, the runtime appends one bounded, redacted `<dropped_plugin_context hook="before_prompt_build">` marker to the turn's `appendContext`, naming the affected plugin and a fixed reason code (`handler-failed` or `dispatch-failed`).

Existing policy is preserved: prompt-build hooks stay fail-open, surviving contributions still reach the prompt, error details stay in operator logs and never enter model context, and authority-only handlers are reported only by the authorized phase that can run them. Raw plugin identities are counted before labels are sanitized and truncated, so display collisions cannot understate the loss count. The marker lists at most five entries, is capped at 640 bytes, and accounts for omissions with `+N more`. Failures *before* dispatch (history load, hook-context assembly) are deliberately unmarked: nothing was dropped, and telling the agent to re-read context that never existed is the same misleading instruction the marker exists to prevent.

The two prompt-build dispatch phases were extracted into `src/plugins/hooks-prompt-build.ts` and `src/agents/cli-runner/hook-prompt-build.ts` to stay under the line-cap ratchet. The CLI helper returns `ResolvedPromptBuildHookResult | undefined`, the contract `prepareCliTurnPromptContext` requires, so the extraction does not narrow the caller's static type.

### Changed during this re-merge — one sub-behavior removed

Upstream retired the prompt-build re-entrancy guard in `0301614ddd9` ("refactor(plugins): simplify transient cleanup bookkeeping (#174872)"), which deleted `AsyncLocalStorage` and `beforePromptBuildDispatch` from `src/plugins/hooks.ts`; `runBeforePromptBuild` now dispatches unconditionally. The branch's third reason code, `nested-prompt-build`, therefore has no premise left. Rather than resurrect the retired guard, this merge **removes** that reason code, its 2 unit tests and proof scenarios [4] and [8], which are marked RETIRED in the proof header with the remaining scenario numbers left stable. The docs reference and the proof script's "WHAT IS REAL" description no longer promise nested-prompt-build suppression or a surviving re-entrancy guard.

## User Impact

Agents can distinguish "the plugin had nothing to add" from "the runtime lost the plugin's context", which prevents false empty-queue conclusions, without exposing exception text, credentials, endpoints, or plugin-authored prompt injection. No configuration or public plugin SDK change.

## Evidence

Measured on this head, `1650afd3378e5acad1021962802bc0f2d637ab87`, today (2026-11-13).

### Real behavior proof — real dispatcher, real CLI/harness/embedded prompt assembly

Command (exactly, from the branch worktree):

```
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/proof-prompt-build-drop-marker.ts
```

Key lines of the real output (`EXIT 0`, 46 assertions; full capture below):

```
[1] healthy contribution reaches the prompt and adds NO marker
  ok  healthy: block present in assembled prompt
  ok  healthy: no drop marker (marker is not unconditional)

[2] throwing handler: reason code only, healthy plugin survives
[plugins] [hooks] before_prompt_build handler from proof-beads failed: bd ready --json failed in /repo: AUTH_TOKEN=*** https://internal.invalid/v1/queue
  ok  throw: marker names proof-beads with a fixed reason code
  ok  throw: no error-derived text reached the prompt
  ok  throw: healthy plugin's contribution survives

[9] CLI consumer end to end: prepareCliRunContext prompt
  ok  cap/cli: overflow summary counts the 25 unlisted drops
  ok  cap/cli: marker is 516 bytes, within the 640-byte cap

[11] CLI boundary asymmetry: a pre-dispatch failure is log-only, never marked
[agent/cli-backend] cli prompt-build hook preparation failed: Error: pre-dispatch preparation failed: AUTH_TOKEN=*** https://internal.invalid/v1/queue
  ok  pre-dispatch: the CLI prompt still opens with the untouched base ask
  ok  pre-dispatch: no drop marker — nothing was dispatched, so nothing was dropped
  ok  post-dispatch: a real dropped contribution still yields exactly one marker
  ok  post-dispatch: the marker names the plugin whose contribution was actually lost

All runtime assertions passed. (46 checks)
```

**What is real:** `createHookRunner` and `initializeGlobalHookRunner`/`getGlobalHookRunner` with production options (the real dispatcher, the real per-hook timeout, the real `handleHookError` fail-open path); all three production prompt consumers — `resolveAgentHarnessBeforePromptBuildResult`, `resolvePromptBuildHookResult`, and `prepareCliRunContext` driven end to end so the CLI scenarios assert on `params.prompt`, the exact string handed to the backend; the real `createEmptyPluginRegistry`/`setActivePluginRegistry` activation seam; and real `prepareSystemAgentRunAdmission` admission via `withTestRunAdmission`, so the CLI path's live-authority assertions run.

**What is stubbed or constructed:** the hook registration records (same `{pluginId, hookName, handler, priority, timeoutMs}` shape the loader produces), the CLI backend descriptor, and an on-disk temp session file. Nothing between a handler and the assembled prompt is stubbed. The capturing logger in scenario [6] is an instrument, not a stub.

### Installed-plugin + provider-boundary proof: previously green, now blocked by main on Linux

`scripts/proof-118555-installed-plugin-provider-request.ts` (also committed here) installs each fixture through the real `installPluginFromPath`, loads it with the real `loadOpenClawPlugins` through the loader's real conversation-hook consent gate, and asserts on the **stdin of a real spawned provider process** reached through `runCliAgent`. On PR #118555 it passed 26 assertions and failed on pristine `origin/main` at the "exactly one loss notice" assertion — the silent drop this PR fixes, observed at the provider boundary.

Re-run on this head today it no longer reaches the provider boundary, for a reason that is not about this PR: current `main` added `acquireLinuxChildSubreaper` (`src/process/supervisor/linux-child-subreaper.ts:39`), which refuses child ownership when the owning process has source-loader hooks. Every `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` proof is such a process, so the spawn is rejected before the recorder starts:

```
  ok  healthy-only: loader registered before_prompt_build for every INSTALLED fixture (1)
  ok  healthy-only: the installed plugin's CLI backend is the resolved provider
[process/supervisor] spawn failed: runId=proof-118555-healthy-only reason=AggregateError: Linux child ownership requires a process owner without source-loader hooks
PROOF FAILED after 2 checks: AggregateError: Linux child ownership requires a process owner without source-loader hooks
```

The two assertions that do run still confirm the installed plugins loaded off disk, passed the consent gate, and that the installed plugin's CLI backend was the resolved provider. The marker assertions beyond that point are unverified on this head.

### Built shipped-CLI capture on an isolated identity — healthy, failing, overflow

This is the entry-point run the review asked for: the **built production CLI**, plugins installed
through the real `openclaw plugins install` CLI, and the three cases captured off the **bytes the
runtime sent to a model provider over HTTP**, not off an in-process return value.

What the binary is: `<openclaw-build>/dist` + `openclaw.mjs`, a real production build reporting
`OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (59fa16a)`. That is **a build of our fork's `integration` branch, which contains
this PR branch merged**, not a build of this PR alone. Across this PR's production files the build and
this head are identical except for one file, `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, which the build has
**3 insertions / 20 deletions** ahead of this head — and both hunks belong to *other* open branches that
also touch that file (`fix/native-capture-warm-refusal-e2m1` contributes `refuseNativeCapture(...)`;
`fix/zai-agent-sdk-setup-entry` contributes the `resolveApiKeyForProviderCore` backend-auth fallback).
Neither hunk is in this PR's diff, and **every line this PR changes is byte-identical in the build**,
including all of `src/plugins/prompt-build-drop.ts`, `src/plugins/hooks-prompt-build.ts`,
`src/agents/cli-runner/hook-prompt-build.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-helpers.ts`
and `src/agents/harness/prompt-compaction-hook-helpers.ts`. Verified with
`git diff --stat origin/integration origin/fix/prompt-build-drop-marker -- <this PR's production files>`.

Isolation: every run got a fresh `HOME`, a fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, a fresh `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`,
its own workspace, and its own loopback port (18911-18913). Nothing touched `~/.openclaw`, the operator's
config, or the Gateway on 18789.

Per scenario the harness: writes fixture plugin packages in the shape npm ships; installs each one with
`node openclaw.mjs plugins install <dir> --force --accept-capabilities` (real CLI, real install root —
`Installing to /tmp/cap197114-run/<scenario>/state/extensions/<id>…` / `Installed plugin: <id>`);
writes operator config granting `plugins.allow` plus `hooks.allowConversationAccess`; then runs one real

on-disk install root, real off-disk plugin discovery and the loader's real conversation-hook consent gate,
real `before_prompt_build` dispatch, the real embedded prompt assembly this PR changes, and a real HTTP
request to a model provider — the assertions read the JSON body the CLI put on the socket.

(`stub-provider.cjs`, 50 lines) is registered as a normal custom provider via `models.providers.stub.baseUrl`,
records each request body, and answers with a fixed completion. Nothing between a plugin handler and the

`stub-provider.cjs` — the only stub: a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint that records every request body:

```js
// Minimal OpenAI-compatible stub model endpoint.
// Records every request body it receives, then answers with a fixed completion.
// Usage: node stub-provider.cjs <out-dir> <port>
const http = require("node:http");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

const outDir = process.argv[2];
const port = Number(process.argv[3]);
fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
let seq = 0;

const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  let body = "";
  req.on("data", (chunk) => {
    body += chunk;
  });
  req.on("end", () => {
    seq += 1;
    const slug = req.url.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]+/g, "_");
    fs.writeFileSync(
      path.join(outDir, `req-${String(seq).padStart(2, "0")}-${req.method}${slug}.json`),
      body || "{}",
      "utf-8",
    );
    if (req.url.includes("models")) {
      res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" });
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ object: "list", data: [{ id: "stub-model", object: "model" }] }));
      return;
    }
    res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" });
    res.end(
      JSON.stringify({
        id: "chatcmpl-stub",
        object: "chat.completion",
        created: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
        model: "stub-model",
        choices: [
          {
            index: 0,
            message: { role: "assistant", content: "STUB-OK" },
            finish_reason: "stop",
          },
        ],
        usage: { prompt_tokens: 10, completion_tokens: 2, total_tokens: 12 },
      }),
    );
  });
});
server.listen(port, "127.0.0.1", () => {
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, "stub.ready"), String(port), "utf-8");
  console.log(`stub provider listening on 127.0.0.1:${port}`);
});
```

```js
// Self-checking assertions over the provider requests the BUILT OpenClaw CLI
// actually sent to the local stub model endpoint, one capture per scenario.
// Exits non-zero on any failed invariant.
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

const ROOT = "/tmp/cap197114-run";
const MARKER_OPEN = '<dropped_plugin_context hook="before_prompt_build">';
const MARKER_CLOSE = "</dropped_plugin_context>";
const SECRET = "sk-FIXTURE-SECRET-must-not-reach-the-prompt";
const HEALTHY = "HEALTHY-CTX-FROM-cap-healthy";

let failed = 0;
let checks = 0;
function ok(cond, label) {
  checks += 1;
  if (cond) {
    console.log(`  ok  ${label}`);
  } else {
    failed += 1;
    console.log(`  FAIL ${label}`);
  }
}

function userPrompt(scenario) {
  const capDir = path.join(ROOT, scenario, "capture");
  const file = fs
    .readdirSync(capDir)
    .filter((n) => n.startsWith("req-") && n.includes("chat_completions"))
    .sort()[0];
  if (!file) throw new Error(`${scenario}: the stub endpoint recorded no chat-completions request`);
  const body = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(capDir, file), "utf-8"));
  const first = body.messages.find((m) => m.role === "user");
  const content = typeof first.content === "string" ? first.content : JSON.stringify(first.content);
  return { file, content, body };
}

function markerSlice(prompt) {
  const start = prompt.indexOf(MARKER_OPEN);
  if (start < 0) return undefined;
  const end = prompt.indexOf(MARKER_CLOSE, start);
  if (end < 0) throw new Error("marker opened but never closed");
  return prompt.slice(start, end + MARKER_CLOSE.length);
}

console.log("[1] healthy: one installed plugin contributes, nothing is dropped");
{

  console.log(`      capture: healthy/capture/${file}`);
  ok(content.includes(HEALTHY), "the healthy contribution reached the provider request");
  ok(!content.includes(MARKER_OPEN), "no drop marker is present when nothing was dropped");
  ok(content.includes("latest ask from the operator"), "the operator's own ask is still in the prompt");
}

console.log("[2] failing: a healthy and a throwing plugin, both installed");
{

  console.log(`      capture: failing/capture/${file}`);
  const slice = markerSlice(content);
  ok(content.includes(HEALTHY), "the healthy contribution survived its sibling's failure");
  ok(Boolean(slice), "a drop marker reached the provider request");
  ok(

    "exactly one drop marker block",

  ok(slice.includes("cap-failing"), "the marker names the plugin whose contribution was lost");
  ok(slice.includes("handler-failed"), "the marker carries the handler-failed reason code");
  ok(!content.includes(SECRET), "the thrown exception's secret text never reaches the provider");
  ok(!content.includes("ready-work query failed"), "no exception message text reaches the provider");
  ok(content.includes("MISSING from this prompt"), "the marker tells the model the context is missing, not empty");
  ok(Buffer.byteLength(slice, "utf-8") <= 640, `marker block is bounded (${Buffer.byteLength(slice, "utf-8")} bytes <= 640)`);

console.log("[3] overflow: one healthy plugin and eight throwing plugins");
{
```

### Proof limits, stated plainly

- The built-CLI capture above runs a **build of our fork's `integration` branch that contains this PR**, not a build of this branch alone; the one production-file difference and its attribution to two other branches are stated with the command that measures it. A build of this branch in isolation was not affordable in this pass.
- The model endpoint is a local stub, so the captures prove what the runtime **sends**, not how a real model reacts to the marker. No API keys, IPs, phone numbers or non-public endpoints appear: the provider is `http://127.0.0.1:1891x/v1` with a dummy `stub-key`, and the fixture secret is the synthetic literal `sk-FIXTURE-SECRET-must-not-reach-the-prompt` (which the assertions prove never reaches the request).
- A from-source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`) proof can no longer spawn a provider child on Linux at all: `acquireLinuxChildSubreaper` refuses a process owner with source-loader hooks (`src/process/supervisor/linux-child-subreaper.ts:39`). That is why the entry-point capture uses a built CLI; it is a property of current `main`, not of this PR.
- The in-process proof asserts on the assembled prompt string a production consumer returns, not on bytes leaving the process.
- No API keys, IPs, phone numbers or non-public endpoints appear in the captures: the fixture secret is a synthetic `AUTH_TOKEN=sk-live-9f3c-PROOF` with an `internal.invalid` endpoint, and the runtime's own log redaction prints it as `AUTH_TOKEN=***`.

prs.title: fix(agents): node tools with an unverified plugin owner can pass plugin-ID tool policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a node tool that claims a plugin owner it is not registered under can pass a tool policy that allows tools by plugin ID, when the tool was first admitted through a broad plugin grant.

## User Impact

User impact: a plugin-ID entry in a tool allowlist now admits only tools whose ownership was verified when the node tool was materialized. The same holds for the tools a cron job captures from its creator, and for descriptors that use a case or whitespace variant of the reserved owner name without being genuine node-MCP descriptors. Exact tool-name grants, broad plugin grants, registered owners and genuine node-MCP descriptors behave as before. Deny rules still match on the claimed owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node-tool materialization already distinguishes verified from claimed ownership, but that distinction was lost in policy metadata, in caller snapshots and in cron creator-tool capture. The reserved-owner exception also normalized the ID without checking that the descriptor really has the node-MCP shape. The ownership decision is now made once, during materialization: the reserved exception requires the core MCP command and non-empty server and tool metadata, and unverified ownership is carried through the policy and cron projections. Plugin-ID allows and intersections expand using verified owners only.

## Evidence

Run with Node 24.22.2 and pnpm 12.15.0. Transport is mocked; no remote tool is invoked.

- The regression in `src/agents/node-plugin-tools.test.ts` uses real node publication, materialization, policy filtering and cron creator selection. Replayed unchanged against `main` it fails 7 of 25 cases; on this branch all 25 pass.
- A second, separately written test set covering the policy pipeline, caller snapshot, cron creator selection and reserved-owner variants: 19 failed / 6 passed on `main`, 25 passed on this branch.
- Changed-scope suites (policy, cron, caller and delegated authority, node snapshots, effective-tool reporting, embedded construction, prompt-prefix stability): 20 suites, 359 tests passed.
- Full build and all test typechecks passed. Scoped lint reported no warnings or errors across the ten changed TypeScript files; formatting, policy guards, import cycles and the test-line budget check passed. The per-change test allocation is 140 lines.

Gap: the broad `pnpm check` passed production, UI, extension, script and root-test types and script lint, then extension lint reported two line-limit errors in unchanged Tlon and Crabbox tests that also occur on an untouched `main`; the remaining core lint scan was stopped there, so the full check is not claimed green locally.

### Running Gateway with a connected node

A real built Gateway and a real built node host were started from each revision, with device and node pairing approved through Gateway RPC. Synthetic external plugins supplied harmless marker tools. A loopback MCP HTTP server stood in for the node-MCP far end, and a loopback Responses endpoint stood in for the model, recording the tool names it was offered. Neither is a hosted service or a real model. No product source was changed and the same driver ran on both builds.

- Base: `b382a29a688a`. Head: `3d064663c293`. Node 24.22.2, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, private-QA build.
- Policy: `tools.allow = ["policy-owner", "node-mcp", "policy_exact", "automations"]`, full profile, Code Mode and Tool Search off. `node.list` confirmed the published descriptors. Offered tools were read from `tools.effective` and from the requests of a completed turn, which agreed.
- In that turn the model stand-in created a cron job through the product's `automations` tool; `cron.get` returned the persisted tool cap. The policy was then replaced through `config.patch` with `["policy_exact", "automations"]` and the job was run with `cron.run`.

| Synthetic tool | Base: offered | Base: in cron cap | Head: offered | Head: in cron cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `policy_verified` (registered, verified owner) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `control_probe` (genuine node MCP) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `policy_claimed` (claims `policy-owner`, not registered under it) | **yes** | **yes** | no | no |
| `policy_exact` (exact-name grant) | yes | yes | yes | yes |

After the plugin-ID entries were withdrawn, the cron run was offered only `policy_exact` on both builds.

Not observed: a non-MCP descriptor using a case variant of the reserved owner could not be published through the normal node-plugin loader on either build (the manifest loader rejects the reserved ID case-insensitively), so that case is covered by the unit regression only.

Limits: local stand-ins for the MCP far end and the model; offerings and the cron cap were observed, not execution of an excluded tool; restart and crash recovery were not exercised.

prs.title: fix(ui): show video compression errors and honest preparation progress
prs.body:
Related: #194249 (closed report; no closing-fix evidence was available).

## What Problem This Solves

In Chrome, including the reported mobile case, failed video compression shows a generic retry action without an inline cause, and post-encoding attachment reads can appear to restart compression progress.

## User Impact

The existing tile shows an actionable, sanitized failure reason and bounded stage/error code. Encoding and attachment preparation have distinct progress labels, and failed tiles can wrap recovery text without clipping the controls. Original-file retry, cancellation, queued work, staged-file ordering, and negotiated batch admission remain owned by the existing lifecycle.

**Draft qualification:** real mobile rendering, inspected before/after screenshots, and hardware WebCodecs behavior remain unqualified. The reported encoding failure remains unreproduced and unroot-caused; a smaller successful resend is not proof that it works. This website change is not deployed and is not part of an Android APK.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep failure and phase state with the current worker wrapper, reader/controller, and tile rather than introducing another upload path. Diagnostics contain only fixed stage/category values, never codec exceptions, URLs, filenames, or recording contents. Codec negotiation and size caps are unchanged. Integration retains current main's separately indexed CSS action selectors.

## Evidence

- Static performance audit acceptance rule: compare the exact tested base 4aa0168e1f2a17608fa6dbb8d7d07a406794fd96 with this unchanged candidate using the repository comparison script, one installed toolchain and its fixed build identity. Attribute largest-JS, total-CSS and route-boot bytes against both base and unchanged thresholds; do not treat absolute overages as PR-introduced without a matched baseline. This is bundle-size evidence, not browser latency or codec proof.
- Integrated through the supported managed base refresh onto official main 4aa0168e1f2a17608fa6dbb8d7d07a406794fd96; its single CSS conflict was resolved and the refresh finished cleanly.
- Fresh current-lockfile run: **85 tests passed across 7 suites**, exercising production controller/rendering, wrapper/worker failure paths, retry/cancellation/queue behavior, budgets with staged files, and ownership/handoff settlement. Controlled injections are not real WebCodecs proof.
- Production UI typecheck, ui-chat and ui-e2e-chat test type graphs, targeted lint/style/catalog/format/whitespace checks passed.
- Actual production UI build completed successfully after installing the current frozen lockfile. A portable real-frontend preview package was assembled with the hashed compression worker/assets, source, manifest, licenses, a local-only real-Gateway launcher and test matrix. Integrity checks and 32 static entry/worker HTTP requests passed; these are not browser or Gateway/model proof.
- Fresh independent local review against the exact managed base covered P0 through P2 and returned scoped-clean with no actionable findings.
- Current-day browser prerequisites remain blocked at the sandbox proc-fdinfo chroot operation (EPERM). No sandbox/TLS weakening, private recording, or paid runner was used.
- Static audit: the exact tested base and candidate have identical manifests, lockfile, Vite configuration and performance reporters. The unmodified paired harness stopped before either build because extracting the 64,714-file base exhausted its 1 GiB temporary filesystem (tar: No space left on device). A report-only read of the retained candidate confirms the absolute overages below; no measured base or PR-attributable delta is available. Neither inherited debt nor PR-caused regression is asserted. Thresholds and source are unchanged.
- **Remaining Draft holds:** screenshots/device qualification and performance-report overages. No budgets or assertions were weakened. An earlier pre-assertion native abort remains unresolved; the current bounded passing run is not claimed as its repair.

<details>

Largest JavaScript gzip: 558.4 KiB versus 553.7 KiB; total CSS gzip: 324.2 KiB versus 318.9 KiB; total CSS raw: 1666.1 KiB versus 1642.8 KiB; chat boot JavaScript gzip: 1280.4 KiB versus 1273.2 KiB; New Session boot JavaScript gzip: 794.1 KiB versus 787.0 KiB. The production build reports these without rejecting the build; performance-gate clearance is not asserted.

</details>

prs.title: fix(macos): retain Peekaboo generation across refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Routine macOS capability refreshes rebuild the Peekaboo computer-use descriptor. A new generation on every read makes the unchanged provider look like a replacement and causes unnecessary node reconnects.

## User Impact

An unchanged Peekaboo provider keeps its node connection identity across routine refreshes. Changing providers still rotates the generation and invalidates the old route.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS node coordinator owns the Peekaboo generation for its provider lifecycle and changes it only when the selected provider changes. Existing connect-option equality and route invalidation remain in place.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `openclaw/openclaw:main` at `ec46689460eca425f101ef9366b6f28f881bcd54`; resolved the two conflicts while preserving the upstream bounded-native-bridge test.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Current-head checks for `110847813b25b57dc47f722d63c3ddec5b5523d6` are running: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43507960134). This repair session did not run the native tests locally.
- Historical hosted macOS proof for the prior head `1df0eda5b877f3032b803974e9105e011b311d74` against base `ce7788f5a24e5e2d0ef146a5dcea3ef4d0bb0983` passed 82 tests across 4 suites: [previous run](https://github.com/aashish254/openclaw/actions/runs/42691454605). That result predates this rebase and is not current-head proof.
- The native tests use an in-process `GatewayTestWebSocketSession`; they do not launch an interactive OpenClaw.app or connect to a separate live Gateway process.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the crowded model-picker button when a model without tool support displays an unstyled “No tools” warning above its label.

## User Impact

The selected model button no longer shows the warning icon or “No tools” badge. Tool availability, screen-reader capability information, and the explanation inside the model menu are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the badge rather than adding more chrome to the composer, as requested by @vyctorbrzezowski. The change deletes nine production lines and updates the existing regression tests without adding new state or styling.

## Evidence

- Regression failed on the original UI because the trigger visibly contained “No tools”; all 12 model-runtime tests pass after removal.
- Focused Chromium Control UI E2E passes, including switching to a tool-capable model and back, retained menu help, and a 390px mobile menu.
- UI TypeScript check, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Before/after screenshots below use the actual production-built Control UI with a synthetic model catalog (light theme, desktop). The E2E also checks the menu at 390px.
- Simplification/self-review: removal only; production −9 lines, tests net zero. No tool capability or execution-policy changes.

### Before

![Composer before removing the No tools badge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f9ab658-5bb7-4c8a-8d47-ca88e0d079b3)

### After

![Composer after removing the No tools badge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c26bfad6-a6b7-44b2-b657-b608d26366d6)

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: feat: confine native node worker filesystem access
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OCE OpenClaw node workers cannot safely use writable OpenShell PVC ancestors unless model-controlled processes are also prevented from replacing them.

## User Impact

Adds opt-in `nodeHost.workerRuns.isolation: "filesystem"` for Linux workers, alongside the scoped writable-ancestor exception. The worker and its descendants can write their admitted workspace, model HOME and scratch directory, but cannot replace those roots through their parents. Unsupported kernels/helpers reject launch; existing defaults remain unchanged.

**Dependency gate before merge:** [proc-safe #39](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/39) merged. The latest published proc-safe (0.5.0) does not export `filesystem-launch`. OpenClaw also needs an fs-safe release containing [#1079](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1079) and [#1081](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1081) after the [0.28.0 rollback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194589). Update both pins and the lockfile once suitable packages are published. Operators must stop existing workers and exclude all other unconfined untrusted writers, including same-UID processes, for the entire workspace lifetime. A dedicated Pod or PVC alone is insufficient.

The [current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193823#issuecomment-6673503877) also flags writable grants overlapping trusted runtime directories or shared scratch. [Stacked #198073](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198073) implements the overlap checks against this branch. Land and verify that repair on this branch before merging into main. Fresh-install and stable-upgrade proof with released dependencies is still outstanding.

At [`1a639e0`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1a639e0e6d3b2f6fd25849071efb37a4a4841af7), the default supervisor loads the filesystem launcher only when filesystem isolation is selected. With the PR’s locked proc-safe 0.4.2 and fs-safe 0.27.1, 27 Linux worker supervisor and workspace retention tests passed, including launching a downloaded worker through the standalone executable. With a locally packed proc-safe launcher and fs-safe 0.28.0, all three Linux filesystem supervisor tests passed. The latter run used local packages and does not qualify a published install.

At [`2d3e3d4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2d3e3d4e3bfc28f649dad6840dee113c07aa98c2), the Git cancellation test expects the existing `-c core.fsmonitor=false ls-files` invocation. The manifest suite reproduced the CI failure on the parent and passed all six cases on Linux after this test-only change ([CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43506279639)).

## Why This Change Was Made

Pre-exec Landlock confinement covers model-launched subprocesses while keeping existing Git transfer/publication APIs and process ownership. Descriptor-relative fs-safe I/O could harden its own operations, but subprocess and lifecycle integration would still need additional work. This approach requires Linux Landlock ABI 3+; inherited descriptors and other sandbox boundaries remain the caller's responsibility.

The real repository path also needs named-device dispatch to preserve its profile and use existing device eligibility. Trusted Git inventory disables repository fsmonitor/lazy fetch; anonymous credential checks retain explicit hostname selection without ambient `GH_HOST`. No new recovery manager or state is introduced.

## Evidence

- Synchronized with main at `3bd03dafb94` in `b1f3d73d551` to resolve the generated config baseline conflict. Regenerated and passed `pnpm config:docs:check`. [Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43491101538).

- At `fdd1f60b497`, fixed the missing filesystem-policy module in the PR tooling source inventory. Replayed the import graph (one missing file before, none after) and passed the repo’s `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts` on Node 24.19.0. [CI for the updated head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43489710410).
- At `9f0963a`, accounted for two additional environment names (`OPENCLAW_NODE_TRUSTED_WRITABLE_ANCESTORS` and the worker-private `OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_WORKER_TMPDIR`) in the inventory. Using the repository’s source counter, verified 463 names against the proposed budget of 463. The +2 is submitted for repository-owner review.

- With Josh’s stacked [#198073](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198073) at `d1cb924` applied to `8383df2`, all 41 tests passed on Linux arm64 in `node-worker-filesystem`, `node-worker-supervisor.filesystem` and `node-worker-supervisor.device-folder`. This included admission of an approved device folder with its assigned private HOME, refusal when a folder changed during admission, and preserving IPC and process cleanup with the filesystem launcher. Same candidate dependency setup as below. These focused suites do not establish a full managed OpenShell E2E on this combined tree.

- At `8383df24c18`, merged upstream main `f5c5984f734`, regenerated the config baseline, and passed `pnpm config:docs:check`. Linux arm64 ran all 44 tests from the workspace-admission, worker-supervisor runtime, and temp-directory suites using fs-safe 0.28.0 and locally packed proc-safe with the native artifact from [proc-safe #39 at 6ab653c](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/actions/runs/43487021774). The macOS tooling checkout had mismatched fs-safe native dependencies and its test run failed. [Hosted CI for this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43488320015).
- The normal install still pins fs-safe 0.27.1 and proc-safe 0.4.2. [Production typecheck on this commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43488320015/job/132104255086) reports TS2307 for the missing launcher subpath and TS2353 for the unsupported ancestor option. The first published fs-safe version containing the ancestor option (0.28.0) was [rolled back after CI regressions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194589). Qualify a published version with the upstream [lock](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1079) and [error handling](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1081) repairs before adoption. The proc-safe launcher also needs a release containing #39.

- Cleanup repair `1632274c789`: a real worker under UID 10001 leaves an unreadable scratch subdirectory; the old code rejects its extinction promise with EACCES, while the fix warns and preserves the confirmed exit. All three filesystem-owner cases pass on the final code. Startup/idle coverage also passed during the repair (50 tests total), with affected type graphs, formatting and lint passing. The same three independent reviewers rechecked the repair. Scratch cleanup reuses the existing best-effort owner; it does not weaken native extinction requirements.

- Before the cleanup repair, head `54a6fe3e1269a14520d3c39412885218c2b4b8ac`: 185 Linux arm64 tests across 12 files, affected type graphs, formatting and lint passed. Three independent source reviews found no draft blocker. Local autoreview was unavailable for the configured account; no machine-clean report is claimed.
- The retained source-built OpenShell test composition (`32b437c` plus this filesystem feature, the OCE bridges, merged fs-safe #1073 and the unpublished proc-safe helper) passed real model/exec, same-UID write/rename positive control followed by confined EACCES, Git publication, Gateway file readback, fresh-workspace restoration, cleanup and normal Pod/Gateway restart. This is local composed-runtime evidence, not current production or isolated current-head E2E proof.
- At `54a6fe3`, `pnpm build:docker` and `pnpm ui:build` passed with the reviewed local source dependencies, including required Darwin fs-safe assets; the packaged Linux launcher resolved and passed an execution smoke in the qualification container. UI bundling emitted three non-blocking size-budget overages (0.3–0.7 KiB), recorded separately from build success. A current-main OCE E2E still requires reconciling the retained setup-renewal bridge with newer node enrollment/transport/lifecycle owners; that broader runtime upgrade is not included here. Hosted CI, dependency release/pins and owner review remain required.
- **Known crash limitation in the retained fixture:** hard node-host termination replaced the OpenShell Pod and left capacity reserved because durable descendant-extinction evidence was missing. No unsafe resume occurred. The unchanged native owner passed a separate real parent-loss test, but matched full OpenShell baseline crash control has not run. Full abrupt-crash recovery and causality are not claimed; launcher/recovery work is deferred.

prs.title: fix: repository refresh failures hide Git diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: #197849
Follow-up to #197862.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed repository refresh failures still hide Git's underlying error when reading, preparing, or updating refs, even after the clone/fetch diagnostic repair.

## User Impact

Users receive a diagnostic ID that survives the retained session error summary; operators can match it to the failed Git operation, exit status, and process output. Raw Git output stays out of the shared conversation.

Credentials, authentication classification, cancellation policy, retry behavior, and checkout cleanup are unchanged. The original production clone/cancellation cause remains unknown, so this PR does not close the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Refresh preparation and ref updates bypassed the diagnostic path added in #197862. Reusing that same logger removes four generic error constructions rather than adding another diagnostic owner. A malformed packed-refs file and an existing ref lock reproduce the missing diagnostics with native Git.

Production delta: +12/-15 lines; regression tests: +60 lines. The existing documented diagnostic-ID and same-session recovery contracts remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Two native-Git regressions fail on base `fa155ff6f53e18f426d7b97ba3407976959380a0` because the errors contain no diagnostic ID. With this fix, the complete clone-runtime file passes **25/25** (39.06 s command wall time including compiler preparation; approximately 0.5 s test execution).
- Regressions cover corrupt ref inventory and blocked ref publication, matching operator log details, intact IDs in bounded session summaries, and successful retry of the same checkout after correcting only the fixture fault.
- **Actual isolated Gateway:** authenticated WebSocket `sessions.create` → native Git ref-lock failure → `chat.send` failed retry in the same retained session. Both `chat.history` responses retained distinct complete IDs matching the Git lock error in operator logs. No Git/preparation mocks; no model execution was reached. One temporary runtime proof passed (21.3 s test; 233.25 s command including runtime build).
- Core and affected-test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. E2E runtime build passed.
- Independent Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, P0–P2), base above → final two-file working-tree snapshot: **scoped-clean**, no findings. The reviewer inspected the diff and supplied unchanged owners; it did not independently execute tests.
- Refresh/default-base sibling selection: **13 passed, 3 failed**. One fixture was refused by the sandbox's shallow-history safeguard. Two partial-clone assertions expected Git exit 1 but received 128; both reproduce identically with the production patch removed. They remain unresolved and were not weakened.
- Broader workspace preparation suite on unchanged base: **9 passed, 9 failed**; worktree allocation was blocked by the sandbox's 1 GiB temporary filesystem versus the 4 GiB reserve. This does not invalidate the separate passing failure/retry proof, but successful Gateway worktree recovery was not verified here.

Hosted CI/job-second accounting is not yet available. No UI layout change or credential/configuration changes to the running installation.

Worked on by: Anmol

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/cdbd6901-9090-4a7a-b3b8-8f5493cd79c2)

## Worked on by

- @anmol0b

prs.title: fix: project memory misses its budget on large Knowledge vaults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes avoidable project-memory omissions when a large Knowledge vault exhausts the one-second recall budget.

## User Impact

Warm recall does less repeated work while preserving successful prompt bytes. If the budget still expires, the existing diagnostics stream records an explicit skipped outcome, including its reason and budget, for the existing tracing exporter. Cold index loading and queued work can still exceed the unchanged deadline. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scanner statted every entry twice and candidate selection revalidated approval metadata already validated by the scan. Reuse the observed stat and the validated facts owned by the existing, file-stamp-invalidated scan snapshot. This adds no independent cache or invalidation policy.

Production code grows by 23 lines: 11 for the skip event and 12 for the scan-owned approval facts and stat reuse.

## Evidence

Regression tests fail on the exact parent and pass on this head: repeated approval validation is removed, unchanged records receive one stat, eligible candidates remain identical, and budget omissions emit the trusted diagnostic event. Focused Knowledge vault/link/provider/save-cost tests and 43 core/audience/prefix/compact tests pass. Runtime build and Codex autoreview pass. An isolated Gateway with a real model returned a random phrase available only in approved project memory.

Controlled native Linux/btrfs A,A,B,A,B,B,A,B,A,B runs (50 warm samples per arm) on 62,000 memories / 2,000 projects, a separate 62,000-file / 1.1 GB workspace, and a synthetic 35.7 GiB agent DB with 5,001 sessions:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm wall p50 / p95 | 776 / 892 ms | 280 / 314 ms |
| Process CPU p50 / p95 | 929 / 1,369 ms | 303 / 343 ms |
| Sampled storage allocations per call | 793 MB | 219 MB |
| File stats per warm call | 124,022 | 62,022 |

All 100 successful native prompts have the same SHA-256. The initial A/A medians differ by 0.42%; the full baseline median range is 676–810 ms versus 261–306 ms after the fix. Allocation sampling ran separately in A,B,A,B processes (10 calls each); repeat averages differ by 0.69% before and 0.13% after. These direct-storage allocation samples exclude transport and caller allocation. Native timings use the default writes-enabled provider path; the attribution probe uses writes-disabled storage. Queue wait p95 stays below 0.03 ms, and main-thread CPU p95 stays below 2.6 ms.

Cold reopen settlement remains about 27 seconds in both arms, so this does not solve initial index loading. All five fixed cold skips emit the new diagnostic, versus none before. No warm sample skipped. A separate oversized-import fixture exposed an existing Git change-batch string-size limit; that setup failure is excluded from the results.

Measured production bytes are at 53c8b9048c0b88aae9c015d48ed16e4c7ed3fba2 against parent cda18427ad31e2f1a09945b5c1a3b55794d82244. The subsequent CI repair only binds benchmark instrumentation to its instances; production is unchanged. Initial CI rejected benchmark lint suppressions; all three are removed, and the failed policy test, script typecheck, and script lint pass locally. The probe also snapshots cold phase counters before explicit warmup; reported warm statistics and cold wall/CPU measurements are unaffected.

`pnpm check:changed` passes its selected checks except inherited dead-export failures, independently reproduced on the exact parent cda18427ad31e2f1a09945b5c1a3b55794d82244. These are main regressions, not passing checks:

- `TELEPORT_PT` and `QA_UX_STREAM_END_MARKER`: introduced by 858b5b01338e598af8bbcc6d4cc0b8c46a157394 (#198293).
- `RELEASE_VALIDATION_WAIVERS`: remaining consumers removed by b9f1e62e00d81cf1048af24aaecb47c97afe15c1 (#198274).
- Production-only scan: `adoptTelegramDmTopicMessage` and `TELEGRAM_DM_TOPIC_ADOPT_WINDOW_SEC`, introduced without external production consumers by 90c620b8e554becc8d0da785c16fea9935bd0681 (#169444).

The same first CI run also failed the audience integration test's first case (4.98 s; subsequent cases ~0.2 s). That test now preloads the runtime before checking real lineage semantics, keeping cold module loading outside this audience assertion. The fixed test passes under Bun with a fresh transpiler cache. The exact-parent replay passed too, so this is **not** claimed as a proven inherited failure or an admin-merge exception. Fresh CI is required.

prs.title: improve(ui): trim redundant tooltips and show working shortcuts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Many tooltips in the Control UI and the macOS app repeat what the icon or label already says, or explain it in a long paragraph.

## User Impact

User impact: hovering shows fewer, shorter tooltips. Tooltips stay where they teach a working shortcut, explain why something is disabled, show clipped text, or carry information the screen doesn't show. Accessible names for screen readers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each tooltip was either removed, shortened, or given the shortcut that already works for that action. No new shortcuts, panels or other UI were added. Where a long sentence is also shown as visible notice text (for example the read-only admin notices or the incognito note), the notice keeps its wording and only the tooltip copy changed.

## Every tooltip that changed (136)

prs.title: fix(gateway): OpenClaw ID nodes re-prompt for approval right after enrollment
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Mac node that joins through an OpenClaw ID invitation immediately asks for approval of "updated capabilities," even though it was just approved automatically and requests nothing new.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenClaw ID node enrollment completes without a spurious approval prompt. Reconnects that declare the same or less access stay prompt-free. A node that later adds commands, capabilities or newly granted OS permissions still needs operator approval, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenClaw ID auto-approval saved the node's owner-reviewed commands and capabilities but not the OS permission states the node reported. The next connection check found those permissions marked granted, with no approved permission set to compare them to, so it treated them as an upgrade and asked for approval. The approval now records the first connection's permission states, as other first-time approvals (setup link, SSH-verified) already do. The signed OpenClaw ID description has no permission field, so those first-connect states become the baseline. Commands and capabilities remain limited to what the owner reviewed.

<details><summary>Technical detail</summary>

- `approveOpenClawIdNodePairing` (`src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-pairing.ts`) now passes connect `permissions` to the worker, which stores them on `nodeSurface`.
- `src/gateway/node-connect-reconcile.ts` already allows narrowing reconnects. Without a stored permission map, any permission declared `true` read as widening, so it created a pending `node.pair` request.
- The macOS command count dropping from 30 to 18 after enrollment is not the app shrinking its list. The Gateway withholds 12 commands that are blocked by default (`DEFAULT_DANGEROUS_NODE_COMMANDS`), and that behavior is unchanged.
- The `node pairing changed after dispatch` errors came from approving that spurious request. Approval bumps the pairing generation and aborts in-flight invokes, which is correct for real approvals and unchanged here.

</details>

## Evidence

- New test `records first-connect OS permissions so the same or a narrower reconnect needs no approval` in `src/gateway/server.auth.openclaw-id-node-pairing.test.ts`. It fails on main (stored permissions `undefined`) and passes with the fix. It checks that the first connect and a narrowing reconnect create no pending request, and a newly granted permission does.
- `server.auth.openclaw-id-node-pairing`, `node-connect-reconcile` and `openclaw-id/authority.nodes` tests: 24/24 pass. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Before the fix (live isolated Gateway, 2026-11-12/13): after OpenClaw ID auto-approval, the paired Mac node record had no permissions. A pending request declaring `canvas`, `computerControl` and `notifications` as `true` appeared 44 ms later, and the macOS approval panel opened.
- After the fix (live, 2026-11-13): a test Gateway with this change auto-approved the OpenClaw ID Mac node with its permissions recorded. No pending re-approval appeared after enrollment, recovery-kit re-enrollment or reconnects.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(telegram): message_sent plugin hooks lose the session key
prs.body:
Closes #197669
Related: #197186

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin `message_sent` hooks get no `sessionKey` for Telegram sends, so plugins that match a send to its session (alongside `agent_end`, `llm_output` or `message_sending`) cannot correlate Telegram replies.

## User Impact

User impact: plugins observing `message_sent` now receive the session key for Telegram replies, finalized previews and native plugin command sends, the same as on the core outbound path and Slack. Sends without a session are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`emitTelegramMessageSentHooks` already receives the session key from every caller and uses it for the internal `message:sent` hook, but left it out of the canonical context that feeds the plugin hook. It now passes `sessionKeyForInternalHooks` through: the canonical runtime session key, with no policy-key fallback, as established for shared outbound hooks in #73706. It's the same key core and Slack pass to `message_sent`, and the one #197519 forwards to `message_sending`, so both hooks correlate on one value.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway proof (isolated mock-Gateway harness, two runs each).** I ran the source Gateway the same way the Telegram e2e runner's `--source-gateway` mode does: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway`, `plugins.load.paths` → `extensions/telegram`, `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR` set, isolated state, fake bot token. The only stand-in was Telegram's Bot API, a local HTTP server reached through `channels.telegram.apiRoot`. A real plugin loaded from disk registers `/plug` and a `message_sent` hook that records what it receives. A DM `/plug` update arrives through the real polling ingress, is dispatched as a native command, and is answered with `sendMessage`:

  | Run | Telegram send | Plugin `message_sent` `ctx.sessionKey` / `event.sessionKey` |
  |---|---|---|
  | main (fix line removed), runs 1 and 2 | `sendMessage` chat `4242` "Choose a deployment", success | absent / absent |
  | this PR, runs 1 and 2 | `sendMessage` chat `4242` "Choose a deployment", success | `agent:main:main` / `agent:main:main` |

  The same `/plug` command was registered through `setMyCommands` in every run. Removing the one fix line is the only difference between the rows.

  <details><summary>Redacted after-fix trace (this PR)</summary>

  ```
  [telegram] [default] starting provider (@proof_sut_bot)
  [telegram] [diag] isolated polling ingress started account=default
  bot-api  setMyCommands  commands include "plug"
  bot-api  getUpdates  -> update_id=1 message chat=4242 text="/plug" entities=[bot_command]
  [telegram] [diag] isolated polling worker batch received queued=1
  [telegram] [diag] isolated polling batch spooled updateId=1
  bot-api  sendMessage  chat_id=4242 text="Choose a deployment"
  plugin   message_sent ctx={channelId:"telegram", conversationId:"4242", sessionKey:"agent:main:main"} event={sessionKey:"agent:main:main", success:true, content:"Choose a deployment"}
  ```

  On main, the same trace ends with no `sessionKey` in either `ctx` or `event`. Chat and user ids are synthetic; the token and local ports are omitted.
  </details>

  Live gap: the repo's Telegram Test Server userbot proof uses Convex-leased team credentials, which I don't have access to as an outside contributor. Happy for a maintainer to run it if needed.
- Regression: the existing native-command delivery test ("settles a progress edit once") now also asserts the plugin hook context's session key. On main it fails (`expected [ undefined ] to deeply equal [ 'agent:main:main' ]`); with this change the file passes 19/19. Net 0 test lines.
- Related Telegram suites pass (96 tests across 7 files): delivery (paragraphs, media resolution), finalized-preview lifecycle, dispatch transcript, native-command concurrency and send recovery.
- `check:changed` ratchets pass (line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race, test-mock-exports), plus format and oxlint. Locally on Windows the oxlint wrapper falls back to non-type-aware linting, so type-aware lint is left to CI.
- Typecheck: the Telegram package and the changed test file (under the extension-test config) report 0 errors.
- Local review: autoreview isn't set up here. Reviewed manually instead: traced all four `emitTelegramMessageSentHooks` callers, confirmed the internal `message:sent` hook is unchanged, and checked the field against `PluginHookMessageContext.sessionKey`.

prs.title: fix(telegram): pass the runtime session key to message_sending hooks
prs.body:
Closes #197186
Closes #197669

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram `message_sending` and `message_sent` plugin hooks get no `ctx.sessionKey` for replies Telegram delivers itself, so plugins cannot match those sends to the session's `agent_end`, `llm_input` and `llm_output` events.

## User Impact

User impact: plugins that key on `ctx.sessionKey` now see the session key on Telegram's `message_sending` and `message_sent` hooks, the same as on the core outbound path and Slack. Sends with no session still omit the field.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram's reply delivery already carries the canonical runtime session key (`sessionKeyForInternalHooks`) and passes it to the internal `message:sent` hook, but left it out of both plugin hook contexts. Both contexts now pass that same key. The policy session key stays out, because it can name an acted-on session rather than the delivery destination.

This PR also carries the `message_sent` half from #197670, so both hooks are fixed and tested together. One regression covers both hooks, so the separate test-line allocation file is removed. The branch merges current `main` (no conflicts).

## Evidence

- **Live Telegram Test Server, real user DM, built Gateway, mock model.** A small test plugin records `ctx.sessionKey` from both hooks for three bot replies (plain, plain, quoted reply).
  - `main` at `8ebe740925ca`: `message_sending` and `message_sent` both reported `sessionKey: null` for every bot reply.
  - This head `a7aa32abca76`: both hooks reported `sessionKey: "agent:main:main"` for all three replies (`PONG:one`, `PONG:two`, `PONG:three`); all three replies were delivered to the user.

prs.title: fix(codex): omit unavailable question-tool and redundant mode guidance
prs.body:
Closes #187061

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary managed Codex sessions receive Default-mode boilerplate and native question-tool guidance even when OpenClaw deliberately disables that tool.

## User Impact

Managed collaboration guidance matches the effective question capabilities without advertising unavailable mode switching. Explicit native-question opt-ins and native-supervised modes remain supported; `ask_user` retains its own contract. Existing history is not rewritten. This is a prompt-quality change, not a measured latency, cost, or answer-quality improvement. No new configuration or dependency is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex's model catalogue can override caller-supplied collaboration text. Ordinary managed sessions therefore suppress native collaboration rendering and carry concise capability-aware guidance through the existing compaction-safe developer-instruction owner. Resume handoffs supersede retained mode guidance; supervision, cron, native modes, approval boundaries, and OpenClaw base-policy replacement retain their existing owners.

The branch resolves current-main conflicts without restoring retired configuration or prompt owners. Canonical snapshots were regenerated with the maintained generator, and replacement-policy consumer assertions were updated for the new instruction placement while retaining the base-replacement checks.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `194616e1e5ac2d7360aeb3f02161f00b04ba346c`. Verification: November 13, 2026. Pinned integration baseline: `fa155ff6f53e18f426d7b97ba3407976959380a0`.

- [Exact-head CI run 43503853665, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43503853665) completed successfully for this head. The initial fork-workflow approval requirement was satisfied through normal Actions approval; it was not a rerun to chase green.
- Eleven confirmed current-main conflicts were resolved while preserving the current `thread_policy` frame, OpenClaw base-carrier placement/reporting, latest-frame persona inspection, incognito guards, and system-prompt replacement boundaries. Managed resume still supersedes retained Plan/native-question guidance; supervision and cron retain their existing owners.
- The refreshed exact source passed all ten selected affected files across five Vitest shards, covering real pinned Codex four-surface and native-handoff checks, lifecycle/native-config consumers, policy framing, continuity, canonical descendants, prompt-prefix stability, and prompt snapshots. The two projection consumers passed 131 checks in a separate recheck. Duplicate snapshot reporter summaries are not counted as separate coverage.
- Both extension typecheck lanes, targeted TypeScript lint, formatting, generator-driven snapshot regeneration/check, whitespace checks, and the test-line ratchet passed. The signed native successor was verified source-identical to the reviewed and tested working tree; no generated output was hand-edited and no test allowance was increased.
- Fresh local autoreview covered the product diff at P0–P2 in one scoped-clean pass with no actionable findings. Independent source review also found no issues and checked the current frame/projection owners. Local ClawSweeper remained unavailable because its runner checkout was dirty; the autoreview's unchanged-file context limitation is not presented as runtime proof.
- Previous-head CI [42738190827](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42738190827) belongs to `a547ba94` and is historical, not proof for the refreshed head. The November 10 isolated red/green run demonstrated the original four native capability cases failing at the intended catalogue-owned guidance assertion against `d85ebfe8`, then passing with the fix.

Native boundary tests use a real pinned Codex app-server with fixture-provider responses, not newly executed live-model inference. No fresh live-model or stable native-thread continuity claim is made.

Earlier real Gateway/model and upgrade evidence is retained below as historical evidence, not relabeled as proof executed on the final head. Its native-thread continuity limitation remains explicit.

Original implementation and historical Gateway proof: @lastguru-net. Conflict repair, consumer updates, and final verification were prepared at @jalehman's request.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dc501594-9838-4aec-8ea1-25d9c7bf7787)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1ab55dbe-f237-4be7-b04f-dc944467d672)

<details>
<summary>Historical contributor evidence — October 29–30, 2026</summary>

Historical head: `adb0f8db5e18955d503aaea8f5ab035f5d1663b6`. Base: `1a881c5ff7850f03c8e8f1ada9302ba7fd939dab`. Validation dates: October 29-30, 2026.

### Review and CI repairs

- Updated successful managed-lifecycle configuration fixtures to include the `origins` map required by the native protocol. Production handling was not weakened to accommodate incomplete fixtures.
- Corrected canonical prompt reconstruction to use the developer instructions actually returned by thread configuration, including the managed collaboration policy. Regenerated snapshots through the existing generator and added two focused assertions.
- Fixed a related diagnostic undercount exposed by the consumer tests: prompt reports and trajectory rendering now consume the assembled developer instructions, including the collaboration block. Removed a now-duplicate configured-MCP notice from trajectory assembly.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40948797727) is green: 58 successful checks, 55 conditionally skipped, none pending or failed. Both previously failing jobs now pass: [canonical prompt snapshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40948797727/job/123711976572) and [changed extensions bundle 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40948797727/job/123711976931).
- Local verification includes all 14 app-inventory consumer checks, 13 snapshot checks, the unchanged prompt-report regression after its repair, current generated snapshots, relevant project typechecks, targeted lint/formatting, both line-budget checks, and a complete `pnpm build`.

### Native request-boundary proof

The repository-pinned real Codex **0.164.0** app-server was exercised with a local fixture provider. These tests use synthetic model metadata and fixture responses, not a live model.

- **Red/green:** the original prompt-owner code failed because captured developer input still contained the catalogue-owned Default policy; the fixed implementation passed.
- **Four question surfaces:** neither question tool; callable OpenClaw Ask User with native questions disabled; native registration without Default eligibility; and explicit Default eligibility. Only the last receives native-question usage guidance. All four omit the catalogue-owned Default announcement while preserving skill delivery.
- **Retained history and controls:** native replay retains the earlier Plan message, verifies that a later managed-resume notice supersedes it without another Default heading, and confirms that a native-owned sibling still receives native mode guidance. WebSocket refresh and native compaction cases also pass.
- The original native/policy run passed all 10 checks. The reorganized lifecycle/turn-parameter suites passed 191 checks; all 14 prompt-prefix stability checks and two selected canonical-fork cases also passed. These are overlapping focused runs, not a full-suite total.

### Real Gateway/model output

These are selected fields from captured real Gateway RPC, native requests and persisted native developer messages, not expected-output examples. Replies are actual Gateway payload text with whitespace trimmed. Every model turn used **GPT-6 Luna** with native ChatGPT authentication and principal-match checks; no provider responses were mocked. UUIDs identify disposable fixtures.

The observer's `nativeCollaborationInstructions` field records `config.include_collaboration_mode_instructions`; `nativeToolEnabled` records `config["tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled"]`. Null means the request did not supply an override, not false. `askUserDeclared` is derived from the actual dynamic-tool names. Only known collaboration-policy lines are retained, not the full developer prompt.

**Fresh managed session.** Real native Codex **0.164.0** received this request surface. The same quoted policy sentence was read back from that thread's native developer message:

```json
{
  "request": {
    "method": "thread/start",
    "nativeCollaborationInstructions": false,
    "nativeToolEnabled": false,
    "askUserDeclared": true,
    "optionalNativeQuestionGuidance": false,
    "collaborationExcerpt": [
      "Prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. Ask the user directly when required input prevents progress; silence is not an answer or approval."
    ]
  },
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "ORANGE-314"
  }
}
```

**Latest-stable upgraded retained OpenClaw session.** Registry `latest` was independently checked as **2026.10.9** for both OpenClaw and `@openclaw/codex`. The official stable runtime used native **0.160.0**. After a real seed turn, the fixture stopped, selected the fixed core/bundled plugin/native **0.164.0**, and ran supported `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` against its retained state (exit 0). Service repair was disabled for the fixture. This exercises a retained-state runtime upgrade, not the update installer.

The second input asked for the previous marker without supplying it again. Actual replies and identities:

```json
[
  {
    "phase": "stable-seed",
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "BLUE-271",
    "threadId": "01a189c7-f180-7d20-9972-88f5ef1a4d94",
    "action": "started",
    "sessionId": "b7da0c91-3a6a-4d9c-b997-0c31e304cd0b"
  },
  {
    "phase": "stable-upgraded-retained",
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "BLUE-271",
    "threadId": "01a189c9-94d0-7170-991e-61d16fa90021",
    "action": "started",
    "sessionId": "b7da0c91-3a6a-4d9c-b997-0c31e304cd0b"
  }
]
```

Stable's actual persisted collaboration excerpt:

```json
{
  "collaborationExcerpt": [
    "Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>"
  ]
}
```

Fixed Gateway request for the retained OpenClaw session; its persisted native developer message independently contains the same new sentence:

```json
{
  "method": "thread/start",
  "nativeCollaborationInstructions": false,
  "nativeToolEnabled": false,
  "askUserDeclared": true,
  "optionalNativeQuestionGuidance": false,
  "collaborationExcerpt": [
    "Prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. Ask the user directly when required input prevents progress; silence is not an answer or approval."
  ]
}
```

**Upgrade limitation:** the OpenClaw session ID and history survived, but the native thread was recreated (`action: "started"`). The strict upgrade test exited 1 because it required an unchanged native thread ID; that failure is preserved in `upgrade-evidence.json`, not relabeled as a passing native-resume test. Later assertions in that test were not reached; the excerpts above come from independently captured request/rollout records. Existing runtime/tool-catalogue rotation guards are unchanged by this PR, and both surfaces changed between stable and fixed versions; the exact first rotation trigger was not logged. This evidence establishes a retained OpenClaw-session upgrade, **not native-thread continuity across versions**.

**Same-build cold native resume.** A separate successful run stopped/restarted the fixed Gateway and retained both identities while recalling the earlier marker:

```json
[
  {
    "phase": "fresh-managed",
    "sessionId": "5f0a0cbd-f477-4558-80c7-be84d5ba7b72",
    "threadId": "01a189c3-422e-71d1-9aa3-eef40e47f891",
    "action": "started",
    "actualReply": "ORANGE-314"
  },
  {
    "phase": "retained-managed",
    "sessionId": "5f0a0cbd-f477-4558-80c7-be84d5ba7b72",
    "threadId": "01a189c3-422e-71d1-9aa3-eef40e47f891",
    "action": "resumed",
    "actualReply": "ORANGE-314"
  }
]
```

**Explicit native-question opt-in.** A separate fresh control set both `features.default_mode_request_user_input=true` and `tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled=true`. The captured request did not override native questions to false. Its actual persisted developer-policy observations and real reply were:

```json
{
  "policy": {
    "managedPolicy": true,
    "optionalNativeQuestionGuidance": true,
    "oldModeAnnouncement": false
  },
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "NATIVE-OPT-IN-OK"
  }
}
```

This control verifies authored configuration/guidance with a real completed turn. It does not claim execution of a blocking question or same-thread opt-in refresh.

**Native-supervised control.** A separate real native seed was continued through `sessions.catalog.continue`. The Gateway completed a real turn with lifecycle action `forked`. Native collaboration rendering was not disabled, the turn did not impose managed Default mode, and the persisted native policy remained native-owned:

```json
{
  "request": {
    "method": "thread/fork",
    "nativeCollaborationInstructions": null,
    "managedPolicy": false
  },
  "nativeDeveloperPolicy": {
    "managedPolicy": false,
    "oldModeAnnouncement": true,
    "collaborationExcerpt": [
      "Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>"
    ]
  },
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "action": "forked",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "SUPERVISED-NATIVE-OK"
  }
}
```

This control passed separately; it was not reached by the strict upgrade test. Native questions remained disabled by the existing tool-selection policy; this checks collaboration-prompt ownership, not native question-tool callability.

**Build provenance:** the checkout and final build stamps identify `adb0f8db5e1`. Generic `dist/build-info.json` retains `d39a5cc5daf8` from build start before the follow-up commit. A read-only reconstruction of the canonical Codex-plugin compiler fingerprint matches current clean source, and all **180** stamped Codex output hashes match. The attached verifier/result document that scope; no metadata was rewritten and no whole-Gateway artifact-equivalence claim is made.

The supplemental 
[openclaw-187856-live-proof.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34158233/openclaw-187856-live-proof.zip)
 contains sanitized per-run records, exact prompt excerpts, source harness/observer/companion modules, package provenance and reproduction instructions. Runs are reported separately, including the strict upgrade failure. No credentials, account identifiers, IP addresses, private endpoints or full private prompts are included. Existing user Gateway/channels/sessions were untouched.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce focused checks and inspect test cost</summary>

Native request-capture and policy tests:

```sh
pnpm test \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.skills.native.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.handoff.native.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-policy.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Recorded original result: 3 policy checks plus 7 native checks passed; 111.95 seconds total runner wall time, including worker preparation.

Lifecycle and turn-parameter checks:

```sh

  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts \

```

Recorded original result: 91 unit checks and 100 lifecycle checks passed; 102.67 seconds total runner wall time. Existing test groups were moved to focused sibling modules without changing their bodies, avoiding growth in already oversized suites.

Review-failure reproduction and snapshot verification:

