prs.title: fix(config): repeated $include entries make config loading take minutes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: config loading takes minutes when config files include the same child file several times across a few levels of `$include`.

## User Impact

User impact: a config tree with repeated includes now fails fast with an error that names the limit and the recovery step, so the CLI, the Gateway and config reloads stop spending minutes on it. Real configs stay far below 1024 include file loads.

```
Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json. Each repeated $include entry loads its file again. Remove repeated $include references to the same file or merge those files, then rerun openclaw config validate.
```

Recovery for an existing installation that hits the limit is the step the error names. When the repeated entries of a file sit next to each other, listing that file once gives the same merged config, because merging identical values again changes nothing. A repeat that comes after a different file (A, B, A) applies A over B again, so there the user keeps the last A. The upgrade run below shows this on a real config tree.

## Why This Change Was Made

`$include` already has a depth limit of 10 and a cycle check, and each file is capped at 2 MB. Both checks look at one include chain. A file may still list the same child file several times (`"$include": ["./b.json", "./b.json", ...]`), and each repeat reads, parses and merges the whole subtree below it again. The work grows as fan-out to the power of depth. Nine levels that each include the next level four times load 349,524 files, built from eleven files of about 100 bytes.

The include resolver now counts file loads in one resolution and throws a `ConfigIncludeError` once it reaches 1024 loads. The check sits next to the depth check in `loadFileSync`, and the error flows through the same config validation path as the depth and cycle errors. The docs list the new limit next to the depth limit, together with the same recovery step.

## Evidence

The proof script generates nine levels where level i includes level i+1 F times, then runs `openclaw config validate` from source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config validate`) with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at that tree. Wall time includes about 30 s of dev-mode CLI startup on this machine.

| Fan-out | Include file loads | main `00b62dd` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 10 | 28.0 s, Config valid | 31.0 s, Config valid |
| 2 | 1,023 | 30.0 s, Config valid | 30.8 s, Config valid |
| 3 | 29,524 | 67.3 s, Config valid | 29.7 s, include error |
| 4 | 349,525 | 389.9 s, Config valid | 30.9 s, include error |

Branch output for fan-out 4:

```
Config needs correction: .../fan4/openclaw.json
  - <root>: Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json
```

Calling `resolveConfigIncludes` directly on main for the same trees took 0.56 s, 7.3 s and 80.3 s for fan-out 2, 3 and 4. On this branch fan-out 2 resolves in 0.39 s and fan-out 3 and 4 throw the include error.

### Upgrade from the latest stable release

This run installs `openclaw@2026.11.3` (npm `latest`, commit `847611d`) into a local npm prefix, then runs the same configs with this branch built from source (`pnpm build:runtime` at `4e62b0f`, run as `node openclaw.mjs`). Both CLIs share one state dir and one HOME inside the proof dir, and the stable release runs first. Node 24.22.1 on Linux.

Configs:

- `normal`: a modular config with eleven files. It uses include arrays (`logging`, `agents.defaults`), sibling overrides (`gateway.port`, `messages.responsePrefix`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`), and nested includes three levels deep (`openclaw.json` to `agents/index.json5` to `agents/defaults.json5` to `shared/timezone.json5`, and the same shape under `messages`).
- `fanout4`: nine levels where each level includes the next level four times (349,525 include loads).
- `recovered`: `fanout4` after following the error's advice, so each level lists the next level once (10 include loads).

| Config | Command | 2026.11.3 | this branch `4e62b0f` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| normal | `config validate` | 2.8 s, Config valid | 4.0 s, Config valid |
| recovered | `config validate` | 2.8 s, Config valid | 4.0 s, Config valid |
| fanout4 | `config validate` | 158.4 s, Config valid | 6.0 s, include load error |
| normal | `gateway run` until `/readyz` 200 | 32.1 s, ready | see below |
| fanout4 | `gateway run` until `/readyz` 200 | 945.0 s, ready | 18.5 s, exits 78 with the include load error |

`config get --json` for `gateway`, `logging`, `messages` and `ui` on the normal config, and `ui` on the recovered config, print byte identical output on both CLIs. The gateway token prints as `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` on both. Merged values on both:

```
logging   {"level":"info","consoleLevel":"warn"}
messages  {"responsePrefix":"[proof]","ackReaction":"eyes","ackReactionScope":"all", ...}
gateway   {"port":18891,"mode":"local","bind":"loopback","auth":{"mode":"token","token":"__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__"}}
```

The sha256 of every authored config file is the same before the stable run and after the branch run. The stable Gateway added `openclaw.json.last-good`, a byte copy of `openclaw.json`.

Branch `config validate` output for `fanout4`:

```
Config needs correction: <proof>/configs/fanout4/openclaw.json
  - <root>: Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json. Each repeated $include entry loads its file again. Remove repeated $include references to the same file or merge those files, then rerun openclaw config validate.

Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair, or fix the keys above manually.
Run openclaw config schema to inspect supported settings and values, then rerun openclaw config validate.
```

Branch `gateway run` on `fanout4` prints the same problem under `OpenClaw config is invalid` and exits with code 78.

Limits of this run, all from the host and unrelated to this change. The branch Gateway on the normal config stops before readiness because the stable release left the agent database at schema 27 and the branch expects 41, so it asks for `openclaw doctor --fix`. Doctor and `config get agents.defaults` on the branch need an OpenClaw temp root whose ancestors are private, and on this host every directory under `/scratch` sits below a root owned `0777` directory, so both stop with `No safe OpenClaw temp root is available`. `config get agents.defaults` on 2026.11.3 prints the merged include values (`userTimezone` from the third include level, `thinkingDefault: "medium"` from the later array entry, `timeoutSeconds: 1200` from the sibling override).

### Tests

Commands run on this branch:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/config/includes.test.ts src/config/includes.top-level-key.test.ts src/config/include-write-boundary.test.ts src/config/mutate.agent-delete-include.test.ts`: 41 passed. Both new tests match the full error text, recovery step included. With the previous message they fail. On main the two new tests fail. The budget test resolves 1025 loads without an error, and the fan-out test runs for 101 s and resolves without an error. On this branch they take 660 ms and 352 ms.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`: OK, net +34 test lines within the allowance.

prs.title: docs(browser): remove blanket manual-step stop guidance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The browser automation skill tells agents to stop for every login or manual step, even though `docs/tools/browser-login.md` permits owner-authorized browser credential fills.

## User Impact

Removes that blanket stop instruction without replacing it with new policy. All other login, permission, and Google Meet guidance remains unchanged; no runtime, deployment, or release changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletes exactly one bullet from `extensions/browser/skills/browser-automation/SKILL.md`, as requested by @hannesrudolph. No other file or sentence changes.

Contributor credit: @hannesrudolph requested and scoped this change.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e256e96e-b2c6-4ad4-9e6f-482c59931964)

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passes.
- `pnpm format:check extensions/browser/skills/browser-automation/SKILL.md` passes.
- Byte-for-byte comparison against the base confirms exactly the requested line was removed and all remaining content is identical; complete diff is one file, zero additions, one deletion.
- Manual complete-diff review and simplification pass: no extra policy, code, tests, or cleanup. Runtime tests/build are not applicable to this one-line Markdown deletion.
- `git blame` attributes the removed sentence to Peter Steinberger on April 25, 2026, in [45e2a15e29caa49a3fb8ec6c4a95f29e841de846](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/45e2a15e29caa49a3fb8ec6c4a95f29e841de846), “feat(browser): add stable tab handles and automation skill”. prs.title: fix(config): an upgrade never refuses settings the previous release accepted
prs.body:
## Problem

Upgrades refuse or lose config that the previous release accepted. From 2,720 classified real upgrade failures:

| Cause | Reports |
| --- | ---: |
| Config validation rejects previously valid config | 14 |
| Doctor rewrites/migrates config unexpectedly | 12 |
| Renamed or removed config key not migrated | 11 |
| Removed config key rejected by validation | 8 |
| Post-update Doctor restores stale last-known-good config (data loss) | 4 |

Reproduced with a real `openclaw@2026.10.10` npm install and a managed LaunchAgent Gateway. 2026.10.10 accepts this config (`openclaw config validate` → `valid: true`):

```json
{
  "agents": { "defaults": {
    "embeddedAgent": { "cyberFailover": { "model": "openai/gpt-6-astra" } },
    "compaction": { "memoryFlush": { "model": "openai/gpt-6-astra" } } } },
  "channels": { "defaults": { "heartbeatVisibility": { "showOk": true } } },
  "skills": { "workshop": { "autonomous": { "mode": "off" } } }
}
```

- `openclaw update` to `main` works: candidate Doctor migrates the keys before restart.
- Any path that starts the new release before Doctor runs (npm/brew/image replacement, `npm i -g`, a host that boots the new image) leaves the Gateway down: `gateway start` exits 78 with `OpenClaw config is invalid ... Unrecognized key: "workshop"`.
- Doctor restores `openclaw.json.last-good` whenever a readable config is invalid and it has no automatic repair, replacing newer settings with older ones.
- Doctor keeps only the rotating `.bak` ring and the per-attempt `.pre-update` copy, so the file the old release wrote is eventually overwritten.

## What changed

- **Tolerant read on upgrade** (`src/config/io.snapshot.ts`): when a config whose `meta.lastTouchedVersion` is an older supported release (2026.7.1 or newer) fails validation, the Gateway runs Doctor's own state-free transform in memory: `applyLegacyDoctorMigrations` (with plugin contracts off), retired-heartbeat projection, then unknown-key removal. If that result validates, the Gateway starts with it and one warning lists every change and asks for `openclaw doctor --fix`. The file and `sourceConfig` are unchanged. This is Doctor's transform, not a new runtime reader: runtime still consumes canonical config.
- **Original kept beside** (`src/config/backup-rotation.ts`): the first rewrite by a newer release keeps the older release's bytes as `openclaw.json.pre-<version>`, outside the `.bak` ring.
- **No stale restore** (`doctor-config-preflight-legacy-config.ts`): Doctor restores last-known-good only when `openclaw.json` cannot be parsed. A readable invalid config keeps its newer settings for repair. The prompt-permission guard that existed only to block that restore is deleted.
- **Doctor still saves it** (`automatic-config-repair.ts`): a snapshot that is valid only through this projection carries `olderReleaseMigration` (source version and the list of changes), and Doctor's repair planner treats it like the invalid file it replaces, so `doctor --fix` and update preflight write the migrated config as before. Without this, Doctor saw a valid snapshot and skipped the write (caught by `doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts`, stable-upgrade case).
- **Projected config is never a "good" file** (`io.snapshot.ts`, `io.observe.ts`, `io.factory.ts`): a snapshot valid only through the projection is not promoted to last-known-good and is skipped by Doctor's suspicious-read recovery, so a larger older `.bak` is never restored over it. Doctor migrates and saves it instead.
- **Original kept atomically** (`backup-rotation.ts`): `openclaw.json.pre-<version>` is written to a temp file and published with `link`, so a failed write leaves no partial original and the next write retries; an existing original is never replaced.
- **`openclaw status` shows it**: a "Config migration pending" block lists every in-memory change and names `openclaw doctor --fix`. Status reads the local snapshot, so it shows whether or not the Gateway is running.
- Docs: config migrations, configuration, Doctor checks.

Diff vs `main`: production +188 / -24, tests +147 / -29, docs +40 / -10. The growth is the in-memory projection hook (~50 lines, reusing Doctor's transform), the staged `.pre-<version>` writer (~45 lines), the projection module (~40 lines) and the status block (~25 lines). Deleted: the prompt-permission guard and the readable-config last-known-good restore path in Doctor. A follow-up could fold the per-attempt `.pre-update` copy into `.pre-<version>`; it sits in update rollback code another PR owns.

## Validation boundary

The boundary is the writer stamp `meta.lastTouchedVersion`:

- Tolerant only when an older supported release (2026.7.1 or newer) last wrote the file. Once the current release writes it (`config set`, Doctor, any validated writer), validation is strict again.
- Writes stay strict: `config set` on a tolerated config refuses the retired key and names `openclaw doctor --fix`. `openclaw config validate` stays strict (it validates the file as written).
- Heartbeat settings from an older release start paused (the warning names them) until Doctor converts them to automations; before this change the Gateway did not start at all.
- A config valid only through this projection is never treated as a good file: it is not promoted to last-known-good and Doctor's stale-backup recovery does not restore over it. Doctor migrates and saves it instead.

## Proof

Real installs, isolated profile (own LaunchAgent and port, clean env). Packed exact head `954dce0` (self-contained package, `build-info.json` commit `954dce0a119a`); later commits change only a test type and drop an unused `status --json` field.

**Package replacement on a config an older release wrote** (published `openclaw@2026.11.2` with the config above, `meta.lastTouchedVersion: 2026.11.2`, serving `/readyz` ready). Database migration is held constant by running Doctor with the config read-only:

```bash
npm install -g --prefix "$PREFIX" <packed tarball>                   # direct replacement, 11.2 -> head
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1 openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive   # DB migration; config bytes unchanged (cmp)
openclaw gateway start && curl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/readyz
openclaw status
```

| Check | `main` (before) | this branch, `954dce0` (after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gateway start` | **exit 78**: `OpenClaw config is invalid ... skills: Unrecognized key: "workshop"` | exit 0; `/readyz` → `ready: true, coreReady: true` |
| Gateway log | n/a | `Config written by OpenClaw 2026.11.2 uses settings this release retired. Running with Doctor's migration until it is saved: ...` |
| plain `openclaw status` | Gateway down | `Config migration pending:` block (below) |
| `openclaw config set gateway.port 28794` before Doctor | n/a | exit 1, refused; file unchanged (`cmp`) |
| `openclaw doctor --fix` | — | exit 0; `openclaw.json.pre-2026.11.2` equals the original bytes (`cmp`); `config validate` → `valid: true`; `skills.workshop` moved to `plugins.entries.skill-workshop.config` (`autonomous.mode: off`); port kept |
| after Doctor | — | Gateway restarts ready; status shows no migration block |

```text
Config migration pending:
- Config written by OpenClaw 2026.11.2 uses settings this release retired; running with Doctor's migration in memory. The file is unchanged.
- Removed retired agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.cyberFailover.model; automatic cyber-policy retries use the active model through approved Daybreak access. Existing mode and cooloffMs settings were not changed.
- Removed agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.model; memory flushes now use the active session model and its fallback chain.
- Moved skills.workshop to plugins.entries.skill-workshop.config.
- Retired heartbeat settings are paused until Doctor converts them to automations.
- Fix: openclaw --profile upg112cp doctor --fix (saves the migration; keeps the original file)
```

**Latest stable `2026.11.3` → head via `openclaw update`** (published `openclaw@2026.11.3`, managed LaunchAgent, a third-party plugin, `gateway.port`/`auth` set, 2 cron jobs, 1 user profile, a device identity; `openclaw update --tag <head tarball> --yes`):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| update | exit 0; `Recorded verification: ... HTTP ready; core ready`; `/readyz` ready on `954dce0` |
| settings | `gateway.port 28792`, `auth.mode token`, plugin `config.label demo`, stamp unchanged before and after Doctor |
| original bytes | `openclaw.json.pre-update` equals the pre-update file (`cmp`); no `.pre-<version>` (same-version writer, as designed) |
| stored data | cron job IDs `60764235…`, `e8f8c2d8…` identical; 1 user profile; `main` agent database; device ID `b88f38fa…` identical (moved by `main`'s schema migration into `client/credentials.sqlite`) |
| status | no `Config migration pending` block (config is current) |
| `doctor --fix`, `gateway restart` | settings and IDs unchanged; Gateway ready. Doctor exits 1 only for the old-SDK test plugin's load error, which #198350 owns |

**Fresh install of the head** (new profile, `npm install -g <head tarball>`, `config set gateway.mode/port`, `gateway install`): exit 0, `/readyz` ready, config stamped `2026.11.3`, status shows no migration block, no `.pre-*` file.

**`openclaw update` from `2026.10.10`** (real npm install, same keys): `main` already succeeds, because candidate Doctor migrates the keys before restart; the only kept copy of the original is `.pre-update`, which the next update attempt overwrites. This branch keeps `openclaw.json.pre-2026.10.10` permanently.

**Next blocker after config (out of scope, item 4):** a direct replacement from 2026.10.10 or 2026.11.2 to `main` now passes config admission and stops at `agent database ... uses schema version 27; ... run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 42`. The copy-and-swap work owns that.

Regression tests, red on the previous head and green here: `doctor-config-preflight.recovery.test.ts` (1,024-byte `.bak` with port 19091 vs compact older-stamped config with port 19092: before, Doctor restored the backup; now it keeps 19092 and migrates), `config.backup-rotation.test.ts` (injected ENOSPC mid-write: before, a partial `.pre-2026.10.10` stayed forever; now none is left and the next write keeps the full original). `status.usage-routing.test.ts` covers the status block.

Focused tests: `io.snapshot.test.ts` (older writer tolerated, heartbeat case, current writer still strict), `config.backup-rotation.test.ts` (`.pre-<version>` kept once), `doctor-config-preflight.test.ts` (readable invalid config is no longer replaced by last-known-good; unreadable file still restored), recovery, container-upgrade and state-migration suites.

## Accepted edge cases

- `status --json` does not carry the migration notice. With the Gateway online it reports the Gateway's status projection and reads no local config; reporting it there needs a Gateway-side fact kept across config reloads. Follow-up if wanted; text status, the Gateway log and Doctor show it.
- A hand edit made after the upgrade but before any current-release write is also tolerated, because the stamp still names the old release. Accepted: it is visible (Gateway log, `openclaw status`, Doctor), recoverable (`openclaw doctor --fix`), and warned. No per-release key-acceptance records are kept.
- Sync `loadConfig()` callers keep strict validation; the Gateway reads config through the async snapshot path, which is tolerant.
- Unknown keys inside plugin-owned schemas (`plugins.entries.<id>.config`, plugin channel schemas) are not stripped; they remain plugin validation errors.
- A Doctor migration that refuses (for example, conflicting prompt-permission values) leaves the config invalid, as before.

prs.title: fix(agents): fall back to a new run when settlement delivery hits not_streaming
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After `sessions_yield` the parent's settlement turn completes while the session is no longer streaming. The steer rejects with `not_streaming`, which was absent from `FALLBACK_STEER_REJECTIONS`, so the delivery threw `queue_message_failed` instead of falling back to the ordinary send path. The reply was generated (status `ok` in `session_input_completions`) but never posted to the channel (`conversation_deliveries` empty).

## Changes

Add `not_streaming` to `FALLBACK_STEER_REJECTIONS` so the delivery falls back to a new run instead of throwing. One line in `sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts`.

## Evidence

New regression test in `openclaw-tools.sessions-steering.test-support.ts`: a run-scoped non-child target with a mocked `not_streaming` steer rejection asserts no `queue_message_failed` error. Fails on prior code, passes with the fix.

prs.title: fix(plugins): Doctor and Gateway startup fail when link() silently copies plugin files
prs.body:
Closes #198407

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` exits 1 and the Gateway restart-loops with "Native plugin artifact changed during admission" when the state directory is on a filesystem where `link()` succeeds but creates an independent copy (reported on OrbStack virtiofs bind mounts, for npm plugins under `node_modules`).

## User Impact

User impact: updates and Gateway startup admit native plugins on these filesystems instead of failing; the captured file is still verified to be the exact admitted source.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hardlink primitive treated "link succeeded but produced a different inode" as a source swap. Its callers only fall back for specific errno failures (and never on recapture), so a silently-copying `link()` always failed admission. The primitive now discards that unverified output and captures the member through the existing guarded copy path, bound to the inode still pinned by the admitted descriptor. A real source swap still fails. Callers record such members as copies, not hardlinks, and copied generation references keep the complete-directory and companion validation that hardlinks get, both at admission and when a recovery source is captured.

Accepted edge case: on such filesystems each affected member costs a copy rather than a link; no new config or persisted format.

## Evidence

- Regression in `src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.test.ts` stubs `fs.linkSync` to copy (simulating virtiofs) for a fresh capture and for a recapture: **red on base** (2 failed, both at the reported error), **green with the fix**. Copied content matches the source; a swapped source still rejects.
- Recovery regression in `plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference.test.ts`: a copy placement with a damaged companion is now rejected during recovery capture (red on the first head, green after the second commit).
- Focused suites green: `plugin-native-namespace`, `plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference`, `plugin-source-file.copy`, `plugin-module-generation.native-layout`, `plugin-native-admission-source-index`, `plugin-generation-artifact.admission`, `plugin-source-capture-recovery`, `plugin-generation-source-lookup` (70 passed across eight files).
- Type-aware oxlint and format check of the touched files, plus `git diff --check`, pass.
- Gap: no live OrbStack/virtiofs Doctor upgrade run; broad proof is PR CI.

Thanks @Lanfei for the precise diagnosis and the minimal reproduction matrix.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.title: fix: reduce repeated scans of long hydrated conversation history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated scans of long, already-frozen conversation history when unrelated activity evicts the generic freezer's memo.

## User Impact

Long tool-heavy retained histories use less main-thread CPU and allocate less during attempt preparation. Prompt bytes and immutability stay unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hydration already deep-freezes decoded transcript snapshots, but only registered the enclosing snapshot as transcript-owned. Its message roots depended on the generic memo, whose bounded rotation is intentional. Register those roots with the existing transcript owner after sealing them, so preparation's existing ownership fast path survives memo eviction.

Keep hydration freezing, the generic memo bound and final sealing of new/replaced messages. Public SDK views remain detached. Production delta: **+6 LOC**, the missing owner handoff; no new cache or guard. The simplification pass rejected a projection-key shortcut that had no ordinary-attempt gain beyond controls.

## Evidence

Both regressions fail on the exact parent `746135b7e7964c208ccb6ca03d00e73b188bd51d`: hydrated history is re-inspected after generic memo eviction, and the durable reader's retained message lacks ownership. The entry-point test also checks Responses serialization bytes, retained identity, nested immutability and sealing of a fresh shallow-frozen reply.

Synthetic tool-heavy owner measurements: two A/A pairs and five alternating A/B pairs per shape, separate timing/allocation processes; Node 26.12.1 on macOS. Each tool result and argument text is 8 KiB, with nested arguments and 32 result-detail rows. Medians:

| Shape | Main-thread CPU ms/attempt | Sampled bytes/attempt | p95 wall ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 rotating histories × 1,500 messages | 4.616 → 1.163 (−74.8%) | 11,230,575 → 2,807,361 (−75.0%) | 6.631 → 1.438 |
| 16 rotating histories × 4,998 messages | 16.292 → 4.610 (−71.7%) | 37,292,325 → 9,016,648 (−75.8%) | 21.138 → 5.550 |
| 16 cold histories × 1,500 messages | 4.346 → 3.131 | 10,120,913 → 6,535,476 | 9.527 → 6.157 |
| One warm 1,500-message history | 0.981 → 0.932 | 3,084,853 → 2,826,149 | 1.293 → 1.296 |

Rotating A/A CPU ranges were 4.462–4.928 ms and 15.951–17.127 ms; the improvement exceeds control variability. Warm CPU is effectively flat. Prepared-history digests match in every arm. Diagnostic profiles show inspection beneath preparation dropping from 1.050 to 0.240 sampled seconds, including warmup.

Cold aggregate hydration setup initially rose 20.5%; it mixed three setup generations. A fresh full control series isolated hydration immediately before preparation: 2.686 → 2.546 ms; paired hydration-plus-preparation median 7.100 → 5.570 ms. Rotating hydration setup rose 9.6% and 4.7%. Allocation figures exclude hydration. Total measured GC time decreased; individual maximum collections were slightly higher, and warm p95 was unchanged.

These are retained-history owner stress windows, not whole-Gateway latency or database throughput. Complete unchanged hydrated cohorts preserve message roots; fresh bounded reads, explicit fences and replaced projection envelopes can take other paths. No production data or live service was accessed.

Validation: 103 focused tests passed across preparation, snapshot/replica, codec/model-context and prompt-prefix stability; 12 UI browser tests and the comprehensive session-history UI E2E passed. Both final regressions passed after failing the exact parent. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. The required changed-check run found two inherited script unused exports, reproduced with a clean tracked tree at the exact parent: `TELEPORT_PT` introduced by #198293 (`858b5b01338e`), and `RELEASE_VALIDATION_WAIVERS` made unused by consumer removal in #198274 (`b9f1e62e00d8`). These are main regressions requiring follow-up. Our assertion type and benchmark lint failures were repaired and their focused checks pass; all remaining type shards passed.

Reproduce with `scripts/perf/attempt-history-freeze-measure.ts --hydrated --tool-rows 32`; use 32/1,500/128 or 16/4,998/64 for histories/messages/iterations, and separate `--allocation` runs. Cold uses `--restored`, 16 histories/iterations. Baseline uses the parent snapshot module via `--snapshot-owner`.

prs.title: docs: containerized gateway networking, host model servers, and rootless Podman troubleshooting
prs.body:
Related: #194988

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a containerized gateway cannot reach model servers running on the host, and nothing in the docs explains why published ports go unreachable, config edits get rejected, or container starts fail on SELinux hosts — operators reverse-engineer error strings like `Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address` and `cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process`.

Affects anyone running the gateway in rootless Podman or Docker with local models (llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM) or scripting a hosted-primary + local-fallback setup.

## User Impact

Users can now: point a local provider at a host model server from inside a container (with the SSRF-guard caveat and both fixes explained), understand why `loopback`/`tailnet` binds strand published ports and what to use instead, script the non-interactive hybrid setup (hosted primary, local fallback), and self-recover from three rootless-Podman failure modes (config ownership lock, keep-id mismatch on one-off commands, SELinux relabel denial).

## Why This Change Was Made

The documented behavior is incomplete, not the code: bind modes, the config ownership lock, exact-origin SSRF trust, and onboarding flag handling all behave as designed, but the containerized-gateway docs describe host-centric semantics only. Each section documents observed behavior — verified against source and reproduced on a real rootless Quadlet deployment — rather than proposing changes.

## Evidence

- Source verification: bind fallback semantics in `src/gateway/net.ts`; ownership-lock error text and the 90-second heartbeat in `src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts`; link-local exclusion from exact-origin trust in `src/agents/provider-network-policy.ts` and `src/infra/net/ssrf.ts`; `--custom-*` flags ignored beside a hosted `--auth-choice` in `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/`.
- Real deployment: all three troubleshooting failure modes reproduced on Fedora rootless Podman with the Quadlet; the alias `baseUrl` is rejected while a LAN-IP `baseUrl` works.
- Docs checks: `pnpm docs:check-links` passes (16,476 links, 0 broken); `docs:check-links:anchors` shows only two pre-existing failures that reproduce unchanged on the unmodified upstream tip; `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` passes (the json5 patch fence validates); `oxfmt` clean on touched files.
- Issue: #194988 (with closed predecessors #68684, #79850, #163315 — code paths fixed, docs gap remained).

<details>
<summary>Commits in this PR</summary>

- `docs(podman): reach host model servers from a containerized gateway` — alias setup, link-local SSRF caveat, both fixes, cross-link from local-models
- `docs(local-models): add non-interactive hybrid setup recipe` — hosted-primary + local-fallback scripting sequence
- `docs: warn that container bind modes strand published ports` — Quadlet note, Docker networking note, troubleshooting entry
- `docs(podman): add rootless container troubleshooting` — ownership lock, SELinux relabel, keep-id entries

</details>

prs.title: fix(telegram): bot replies in non-forum groups drop out of group history
prs.body:
Related: #185720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a bot reply sent into a reply chain in a non-forum Telegram group is stored under the chain root's thread ID, so the group history window for that unthreaded group skips it.

## User Impact

The agent's own recent Telegram group replies stay in the rolling group history instead of silently disappearing from the context of later turns. Forum topics and DM topics keep their existing thread behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram sets `message_thread_id` on reply-chain messages in non-forum groups, pointing at the chain root. Inbound routing already classifies that group as `scope: "none"`, but the outbound prompt-context path fell back to the raw field, so the cached bot message was tagged with the chain root as a topic. History reads for an unthreaded group only match nodes without a thread ID, so the message was excluded.

The provider-observed thread spec now mirrors inbound: when the provider response proves the send unthreaded, it resolves `{ scope: "none" }` instead of inheriting the chain root.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `extensions/telegram/src/outbound-message-context.test.ts` records an outbound supergroup message with `message_thread_id: 99` and no requested thread. It fails on `main` (cached `threadId` was `"99"`), passes with the fix, and also asserts the message now appears in `readHistoryWindow` for the unthreaded chat.
- `pnpm test` for `outbound-message-context`, `message-cache`, `message-cache.retained`, `message-cache.conversation-context`, `bot-handlers.message-context.runtime`, and `outbound-adapter.telegram-http`: all pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm format:check`, and oxlint on the touched files: clean.
- Not verified against a live Telegram group; the fixture follows the provider response shape recorded in #185720.

prs.title: fix(agents): allow authorized non-disruptive component work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents refusing explicitly authorized native component builds on the hosting Gateway merely because no dedicated maintenance action exists.

## User Impact

Operators can request non-disruptive component builds, dependency work, and repairs through available exec under normal permissions and approvals. Updates, installation replacement, and service stop/restart still require supervised maintenance. Owner/operator authorization, a working restart path, and runtime-denial protections remain intact. No permission or lifecycle implementation changes, migrations, or breaking contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The blanket restriction on “installation changes or service control” also covered an explicitly authorized `pnpm build:iroh`, even though it did not replace or stop the running Gateway. Narrow the existing shared prompt owner to disruptive lifecycle operations and explicitly describe the permitted non-disruptive work when exec is available. A missing maintenance action or Gateway-host location alone is not a refusal reason; a runtime-denied operation must never be retried through exec.

Both configured and harness prompts consume the same owner. Documentation and generated snapshots follow that distinction.

## Evidence

- Red before the owner change: the four new configured/harness regression cases failed; 32 existing cases passed.
- Integrated candidate: 119 tests passed across configured prompt, system prompt, harness, and tool-prefix stability suites. All six generated prompt snapshots are current.
- Core project compiler and affected `agents-root` test compiler passed on the integrated tree. Advisory shard-size warnings were non-fatal.
- Full build passed on published head `d059c63cf508401fb7699c36bc7f52be2895b8d2`: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts`, exit 0, including unified declarations, SDK export checks, and Control UI production build. The informational UI budget report listed seven overages; this is not a claim that UI performance checks passed.
- Changed-file type-aware lint, MDX sanity, formatting, diff checks, and native commit hooks passed. Build left tracked source clean.
- Independent local AutoReview, P0–P2: complete, scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Reviewed base `e8ff306f74133486c302f9358296fb43ecb52cd3` and candidate `8a23e88e88d269cd54ac448d3f2a62c9812ad0de`, tree `d893f55aee98b91d246f7b79cf04dfab65e6079a`; reviewed diff SHA-256 `021e56af007274f38e9a9ee704069e05836752e20321670606c6b012f1dfbae1`.
- Conflict integration used main `90c620b8e554becc8d0da785c16fea9935bd0681`; only generated snapshot conflicts required regeneration. Reviewed owner/caller baseline blobs and authored patch are unchanged (stable patch-id `87076725aa48ff955089a3ac02ef31b5d2d6e0a4`). Integrated/published tree: `1b93ff670f4e4b0bd87e1b1a4f9c07e0ee1313bd`; full diff SHA-256: `96fd99ca60ba3ad6e16e52a167addaabfb23d7b75d86d1322f37fbf4b1e638e9`. Existing review remains applicable; focused proof and compilers were rerun after integration.
- Full touched-test audit retained distinct renderer/tool-availability/disabled-command/alias-lifetime/delegation coverage and replaced an existing argument-spy check with exact observable owner-display output and secret non-leakage assertions.

These tests prove the rendered prompt contract, not actual model compliance or live maintenance behavior. No live Gateway build, update, deployment, or restart was performed by this task. The compiler prerequisite was resolved with the supported task-private project virtual store using the pinned package manager and canonical content store; no source, compiler guard, shared dependency, or permission policy was weakened. prs.title: fix(ui): hide empty message box on missing session links
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/47e7d457-23c4-412e-a1b2-fe01844a58ed)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a chat link to a session that doesn't exist shows an empty message box and a "Copy any text below before opening another session." hint under "Session not found", even when nothing was typed.

## User Impact

User impact: a dead or mistyped session link now shows only the "Session not found" state with its two actions. If someone did type into the early message box before the route resolved, the box and the copy hint still appear so that text is not lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat links render a real message box before the app loads, so typing can start immediately. When the route ends in a state with no chat pane (not found, ambiguous, error, unavailable Home), the route view kept that box on screen whenever it existed, not only when it held text. The route view now retires the box when it is empty and keeps the current recovery frame only when there is text to recover.

The stale-chunk error screen in the shell loader has a similar hint, but its Retry can still load the chat pane, which then takes the box, so it is unchanged here.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification on the published head:

- All **9 existing boot-composer browser E2E cases pass** (28.66 seconds), including desktop, phone and landscape draft handoff.
- Restoring the original route owner reproduces the missing-session bug: the new regression finds one empty editor instead of zero. That original owner is byte-identical to the checked main snapshot.
- With the PR, the empty editor disappears. The typed-draft case keeps the same editable element, preserves its text, and sends nothing when navigating to another session. Both focused proof replays pass.
- Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues. No source changes were needed.

The captures below show the built Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses at 1280×800. They are browser boundary proof, not a live-account test.

| Before: empty editor retained | After: only the missing-session state |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: empty composer remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfbe751b-2d17-4e52-be62-0a395671eaec) | ![After: empty composer retired](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c5669d6-bb1e-431b-84d6-baaa9123f45e) |

**Typed text remains available to copy and edit:**

![After: typed draft is preserved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/030cd866-f285-4f27-afcd-633b6403b520)

CI disposition: the existing performance check reports 87 bytes of added chat-startup JavaScript, 23 bytes above its growth allowance; the maintainer has authorized budget exceptions. The lint failure in `session-context-breakdown.e2e.test.ts` is unchanged between base and head and outside this two-file change. These failures are not reported as passing.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: remove Markdown table syntax from agent previews
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent roster previews show Markdown table pipes and alignment syntax as ordinary text. The initial version also rejected valid saved previews, making archived conversations lose their preview when the bounded backfill could not read their cold transcript.

## User Impact

New and normally regenerated previews show readable table text. Existing valid previews remain available after archival and reopening, including the last assistant reply and terminal model facts. Old cached previews may retain their earlier formatting until normal regeneration; this change does not force a refresh of every saved preview.

## Implementation

The shared plain-text normalizer recognizes table headers and delimiters before removing Markdown block markers. It stops at following headings, lists and quotes, preserving literal pipes outside the table and in inline code.

Formatting does not invalidate the preview cache. The revision check and serialization wrappers from the initial version are removed; the existing timestamp/index, heartbeat and terminal-model checks remain unchanged. No schema, transcript, settings or retention policy changes.

## Validation

- 97 focused tests pass across normalization, display projection, terminal facts and row projection/backfill.
- A permanent regression uses the real SQLite archival operation, closes/reopens the database, and checks the preview, last assistant reply and terminal model while the transcript remains archived. It fails with the original revision guard and passes without it. This replaces the narrower cache-helper test.
- Both Markdown block-boundary regressions fail on the previous head and pass with this repair. Existing tests cover literal/escaped pipes, inline code, indented code and normal table regeneration.
- Focused lint, formatting, strict normalizer typecheck, normalization-package build and test-line budget check pass. Independent P0–P2 review of the complete final candidate found no actionable findings.
- New archive/reopen case: 1.127 seconds. Its full file: 22.97 seconds in Vitest (48.60 seconds including worker preparation). Row-projection file: 44.30 seconds, mainly transformation/setup. Current-head CI runtime is pending; the earlier Control UI performance-budget failure is not reported as passing.
- Earlier Safari screenshots below show the normalizer's output from the same Design-agent reply against an isolated Gateway. They are retained formatting evidence, not proof of a full released-version application upgrade or automatic rewriting of older caches.

![Before: the Design reply preview exposes Markdown table syntax](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdf7752c-ad36-4a93-b2d8-dd5aa5bdbbab)

prs.title: fix(discord): presence greetings wake the agent for members outside the guild allowlist
prs.body:
## Summary

Discord presence greetings ignored the guild and channel `users`/`roles` sender allowlist. A guild member that the allowlist excludes could still wake the agent just by coming online. The presence listener now applies the same member-access rule that messages, reactions, voice, components and native commands already use. It runs before the cooldown is claimed and before the session event is queued. This builds on the presence routing from #107451 and the channel-visibility gate from #108448, and leaves both in place.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord guild member who is not on the guild's (or the greeting channel's) `users`/`roles` allowlist can trigger an agent turn by going online, when presence greetings are enabled for that guild.

`SECURITY.md` ("Context Visibility and Allowlists") treats allowlists as trigger authorization: who can make the agent act. The presence path was the one Discord ingress that skipped that check.

- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/listeners.ts` `DiscordPresenceListener.handleSerial`:
  - It checked only the optional `presenceEvents.users` filter (allow-all by default), the bot filter and target-channel visibility.
  - It then called `system.enqueueSessionEvent(..., { createIfMissing: true })`.
  - It never consulted `resolveDiscordMemberAccessState`.
- Sibling ingress paths do enforce that check. Example: reactions in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/listeners.reactions.ts`.

Net effect: an excluded member could cause model inference and possibly an outbound greeting. The 8-hour per-member cooldown and the per-guild burst cap only limited how often.

## User Impact

Presence greetings now go only to members the guild or target-channel sender allowlist admits. They must also still see the greeting channel and pass `presenceEvents.users` if set.

Guilds without `users`/`roles` restrictions, and members already on the allowlist, see no change. Operators who want greetings for members outside the allowlist need to admit those members through the allowlist. That keeps one trigger authority per guild. There are no config, schema or default changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse the existing owner. `resolveDiscordMemberAccessState` decides: users OR roles, with a channel entry overriding the guild entry. Presence adds no new policy.
- Resolve the configured greeting channel's config the same way reactions do: by ID, name/slug or parent, with the channel fetched (client-cached) only when the guild has a `channels` map. Name-keyed channel entries therefore apply too. Like reactions, the listener fetches the channel itself, so a failed lookup cannot be mistaken for a channel without a sender restriction.
- `PRESENCE_UPDATE` carries no member roles. The listener fetches the member (cached by the client) only when the user list did not already admit the member and a role list applies. It fetches the user only under `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching`, because presence payloads often omit the username.
- Run the check inside the existing burst reservation, before the visibility lookup, cooldown claim and enqueue. That keeps Discord REST work bounded the way the existing visibility check is. A denied member is marked online locally like a visibility denial, so a flapping member is not re-checked on every update.
- Fail closed. A channel, user or member lookup error aborts the wake, and the member stays retryable. A missing channel denies the wake.
- Accepted edge, shared with reactions: if the thread target's parent cannot be fetched, a parent entry keyed by *name* is not matched. Entries keyed by parent ID still apply.
- Leave the operator's routing choices alone. `presenceEvents.channelId` and the guild's `presenceEvents` opt-in are operator config, not member authority, so channel-allowlist and `groupPolicy` gating are unchanged.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path | Allowlist shape | Before fix (base `7f3914b7832`) | After fix | Command |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Excluded member goes online | guild `users: ["111"]`, member `222` | Woke the agent: 1 `enqueueSessionEvent` and a cooldown entry written | No wake, no cooldown entry | `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/listeners.test.ts` |
| Excluded member goes online | guild `roles: ["333"]`, member `222` holds no roles | Woke the agent | No wake; one member lookup | same |
| Excluded member goes online | name-keyed channel `greetings: { users: ["111"] }` | Woke the agent | No wake | same |
| Excluded member goes online | `users: ["alice"]` with `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching` | Woke the agent | No wake | same |
| Excluded member goes online, greeting channel lookup fails | name-keyed channel `greetings: { users: ["111"] }`, `fetchChannel` throws | Woke the agent | No wake, no cooldown entry | same |
| Allowed member goes online | each of the four shapes above, member `111` | 1 wake | 1 wake (unchanged) | same |
| Existing presence behavior | cooldown, burst, reconnect, policy swap, visibility, shutdown | green | green | same |
| Startup wiring | `registerDiscordMonitorListeners` | green | green | `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.startup.test.ts` |
| **Live Gateway**: excluded human member goes Invisible → Online | guild `users: ["<someone else>"]` | Agent turn ran: presence event in the session transcript, model and tool calls | Both presence updates received, then nothing: no agent turn, no model call, no session created | `openclaw gateway run` with real Discord |
| **Live Gateway**: same member, now allowlisted (config hot-reloaded) | guild `users: ["<member>"]` | — | Agent turn ran and posted "Welcome back! 👋" to the greeting channel | same |
| **Live Gateway, current head `b463e213ae9`**: excluded member goes Invisible → Online | only restriction is the name-keyed channel entry `general: { users: ["<someone else>"] }` | — | Both presence updates received, then nothing: no agent turn, no session created | same |
| **Live Gateway, current head**: same member added to that channel entry (config hot-reloaded) | `general: { users: ["<member>"] }` | — | Agent turn ran and posted "Welcome back!" to `#general` | same |

To get the "before" column, I kept the new test and reverted only the two production files. All five excluded-member rows failed with "expected 0 calls, got 1": the excluded member woke the agent. With the fix, `listeners.test.ts` passes 41/41, and `provider.startup.test.ts` passes 6/6. The tests drive the production listener with real `PRESENCE_UPDATE` payloads; Discord REST and the session runtime are mocked.

The first live rows come from isolated Gateways, one built from the base and one from this branch at `5144749fd6d`. The current-head rows rerun the fix at `b463e213ae9` with a fresh state folder. There, the only sender restriction is a name-keyed channel entry, so the presence check goes through the new channel fetch. Each had its own state folder, a real Discord server, a bot with the Presence Intent and a hosted model. A human member changed their own status by hand, since the listener ignores bots and Discord prohibits self-bot automation. Changing the allowlist to admit the member was hot-reloaded without restarting the Gateway. The base run was stopped while the agent was still gathering context, before it posted anything.

<details>
<summary>Live Gateway capture (redacted: guild, channel and member IDs replaced; tool-call arguments trimmed)</summary>

Each Gateway config allowlists one guild with `users: ["<someone else>"]` and `presenceEvents: { channelId: "<channel>" }`. `resolveAgentRoute` is logged by the presence listener for each `PRESENCE_UPDATE` before the sender check runs.

**Base `7f3914b7832`, member excluded.** Gateway log:

```
15:47:02 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=discord accountId=default peer=channel:<channel> guildId=<guild> bindings=0
15:47:17 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=discord accountId=default peer=channel:<channel> guildId=<guild> bindings=0
15:47:18 {"subsystem":"diagnostic"} session controller phase
15:47:24 {"subsystem":"agent/embedded"} Model "hub/…" emitted reasoning …
15:48:11 {"subsystem":"diagnostic"} lane task error: lane=cron-nested durationMs=51495 error="agent run aborted for restart"   <- stopped by hand before any send
```

Agent transcript:

```
15:47:21 user: Discord online-presence event:
         A human member became available online after being observed offline in guild_id="<guild>" user_id="<member>" status="online".
         The authorized greeting target is channel_id="<channel>". …
15:47:24 tool: memory_search {"query":"user_id <member>"}
15:47:57 tool: read {"path":"…/workspace/IDENTITY.md"}
…        (10 more context-gathering tool calls until 15:48:10)
```

**This branch at `5144749fd6d`, same member excluded.** Gateway log: both presence updates arrive, then nothing. There is no session, no model call, and no transcript entry.

```
16:03:14 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=discord accountId=default peer=channel:<channel> guildId=<guild> bindings=0
16:03:29 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=discord accountId=default peer=channel:<channel> guildId=<guild> bindings=0
```

**Same Gateway after adding the member to `users`.** The config is hot-reloaded; there is no restart:

```
16:03:46 {"subsystem":"gateway/reload"} config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.discord.guilds.<guild>.users)
16:03:46 {"subsystem":"gateway/reload"} config source revision 1 accepted (file)
16:13:41 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: … guildId=<guild> …   <- went Invisible
16:15:03 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: … guildId=<guild> …   <- came back Online
16:15:04 {"subsystem":"diagnostic"} session controller phase
16:15:15 {"subsystem":"agent/embedded"} Model "hub/…" emitted reasoning …
```

Agent transcript (the only presence event in this Gateway's transcript):

```
16:15:06 user: Discord online-presence event:
         A human member became available online after being observed offline in guild_id="<guild>" user_id="<member>" status="online". …
16:15:15 tool: memory_search {"query":"user_id <member> timezone"}
…        (9 more context-gathering tool calls)
16:16:15 tool: message {"action":"send","channel":"discord","target":"<channel>","message":"Welcome back! 👋","silent":false}
```

The member saw "Welcome back! 👋" in the greeting channel.

**Current head `b463e213ae9`, fresh state.** The guild has no `users`/`roles`; the only restriction is `channels: { general: { users: ["<someone else>"] } }`. Gateway log while the member is excluded: both presence updates arrive, then nothing. No agent database is created.

```
20:00:56 [routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=discord accountId=default peer=channel:<channel> guildId=<guild> bindings=0
```

prs.title: fix: prevent worker writes to trusted runtime storage
prs.body:
Stacked on #193823, targeting `codex/node-trusted-writable-ancestors`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes filesystem-isolated workers being able to overwrite trusted runtime files or replace peer scratch storage when writable paths overlap protected storage.

## User Impact

Unsafe workspace, model HOME, and scratch layouts are rejected before worker execution. Valid projects beneath broad read grants, including `/usr/src`, continue to run with confined workspace writes and existing descendant cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Landlock grants within one ruleset are additive: a read-only runtime grant cannot cancel an overlapping writable grant. The existing filesystem-launch owner now checks all writable roots against protected runtime paths and captured trust files, and prevents them from encompassing captured execution HOME or the shared temporary root.

The checks protect canonical targets and replaceable pathname entries along the resolution chain. This includes original bundle, HOME, and shared-temporary-root paths, relative targets, intermediate aliases, repeated/trailing separators, and ordinary directories before `..`. Precise executable/library roots and the selected native helper storage remain protected without treating the entire broad `/usr` or `/proc` read grant as private storage. Scratch rejection retains the existing cleanup owner. The fix stays in the existing filesystem-launch owner, with no new public API or test-only production hooks; the added traversal is needed because canonical-target checks alone miss proven pathname redirection. Relative to the parent, production code grows by 77 lines and tests by 267 lines.

## Evidence

- Secretless task-owned UTM guest: Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, Linux 6.8.0-147, Landlock ABI 4, non-root UID 1001.
- Native before/after proof: the original implementation allowed a confined worker to replace a disposable Node executable, followed by unconfined host re-execution. The candidate rejects that layout before execution. The original also allowed peer-scratch replacement through a `/tmp` workspace; the candidate rejects it while preserving the peer.
- Native controls demonstrated replacement of captured CA pathnames through aliases and ordinary directories before `..`, while their canonical targets remained intact. Separate bundle/HOME/temp alias proofs demonstrated later trusted resolution changing while canonical storage stayed intact; the temp case used the real selector. The candidate rejects these layouts. A valid `/usr/src` project still runs, writes inside its workspace, and receives `EACCES` outside it.
- All 81 relevant tests passed: 31 grant regressions, 3 real filesystem-owner cases, and retained proof for 18 startup and 29 idle cases. The new regression file ran through `pnpm test ... --maxWorkers=1` in 2.25 seconds wall time. Negative cases were demonstrated red on the applicable unfixed implementation, including native helper storage, system executable directories, and original-root aliases.
- Production and node-host test type graphs, focused repository oxlint (zero warnings/errors), focused oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Pinned-Bun lint parity was unavailable because the guest could not stage that artifact; the documented focused oxlint route passed.
- Fresh local autoreview covered the complete four-file snapshot against `1632274c7895819d4054fa2364bbb0ff0666defb`, including unchanged owner context, at P0–P3. Outcome: `scoped-clean`, complete, no remaining actionable findings. The reviewed tree was committed unchanged as `412ae587c5f4c9236c05e6339398c54fb1ef4714`. Earlier findings were reproduced and repaired before this final review. This is source review, not independent deployment certification.
- At `f9123897`, the [hosted architecture check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43499789637/job/132143303982) passed. The [production typecheck](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43499789637/job/132144681498) still fails on the parent’s two dependency pins. On Linux, 41 focused tests passed with a locally packed proc-safe launcher and fs-safe 0.28.0.

The 267-line allocation covers this change's focused security regressions and valid-layout controls. The test-line ratchet remains 259 lines over its ceiling, exactly matching inherited parent debt: the parent has 6,635,609 lines against a 6,635,350 ceiling; this candidate adds 267 lines and 267 allocation credit. This PR does not request additional credit for that existing debt.

[proc-safe #39](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/39) has merged. The original Linux proof used guest-only overrides for fs-safe 0.28.0 and openclaw/proc-safe#39 at `8c9a12144f1923059b90349172c35466394dfb66`, with its matching native helper. The parent still needs released dependency pins/lockfile updates and final installed-package/hosted validation. Those overrides and generated artifacts are excluded from this PR. The parent's deployment and crash-recovery qualification gates remain outstanding.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): follow-up turns on a warm process fail with "Native tool authority capture is no longer active"
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a Gateway that keeps Claude CLI processes warm between turns, every follow-up turn that reuses a warm process can fail before the model answers, with:

```
LLM request rejected: Native tool authority capture is no longer active.
```

The user sees that string as the reply. Resending works, because the failed turn kills the warm process and the next turn starts a fresh one. In our deployment this hit follow-up turns in owner direct-message sessions: 12 failed turns in 12 hours, every one of them a reuse of a warm process.

The cause is an async-context leak. A warm CLI transport is created by a session's first turn and keeps that turn's async context for every callback it makes afterwards. `execute-plugin.ts` already says so, and already works around it for one callback:

```ts
// Warm transports retain their first turn's async context across plugin refreshes.
requestToolPermission: AsyncLocalStorage.bind(requestToolPermission),
```

The other host callbacks handed to the plugin are not bound. The Claude runtime calls the host's `assertCurrent` from transport callbacks on every record (`activeTurn()` in `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`) and swallows any throw. On a reused process that check therefore runs in the first turn's async context, where `sessionSourceScopes` still holds the first turn's prepared session-source scope. A source assertion resolved through that stale scope can refuse, and when it does the run registry retires the current run's delegated authority (`readActiveAgentRunDelegatedAuthority` releases the claim "at detection"). A few milliseconds later the turn's `system/init` record arrives, `captureNativeToolAuthority` finds the authority closed, and the turn is failed.

A fresh process is not affected, because its transport is created inside the current turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind every host callback on the plugin execution context to the turn that builds it, instead of one of them.

- `src/agents/cli-runner/plugin-host-callbacks.ts` (new): `executeWithBoundHostCallbacks(execute, context)` wraps each function-valued property of the context with `AsyncLocalStorage.bind` and starts the execution.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.ts`: uses it for the context passed to `params.execute`, and drops the single hand-written bind. The file shrinks by one line.

The bind happens where the single bind already happened, inside the turn's `runWithAgentToolSourceExecutionScope`, so a fresh process behaves exactly as before and a warm process now behaves like a fresh one.

## User Impact

Follow-up turns on a warm Claude CLI process no longer fail with "Native tool authority capture is no longer active". Warm-process reuse works, so follow-up turns keep their fast start instead of failing once and cold-starting on the retry.

## Evidence

Tested head: `8aa01786f84`.

### Real behavior: a running Gateway, before and after

This is from our production Gateway (Linux, Claude Code CLI backend, Discord channel), a real build serving real turns. It is a build of our fork's integration branch: upstream `main` at `8408f1b5755` plus our other open PR branches. The "after" build adds this change. Session keys are redacted; nothing else is edited.

**Before** (12 hours, 2026-11-12 10:12 to 22:26 MST). Twelve turns failed with this error. None of the twelve logged a `cli live session start` during the turn, meaning each reused a warm process, and each failed within a few seconds. For the affected model the log has 65 process starts and 69 completed turns alongside those 12 failures:

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner:<redacted> durationMs=763 error="Native tool authority capture is no longer active." errorName=FailoverError
[agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-2 durationMs=3736 runId=cf1a7034-ba05-4426-af6b-822c9f953b83 error=Native tool authority capture is no longer active.
Embedded agent failed before reply: Native tool authority capture is no longer active.
```

A temporary diagnostic in that build (not part of this PR) logged why the capture was refused. The grant row was untouched; the run's own authority had been retired 18 ms after the capture was activated:

```
[mcp-loopback] native tool authority capture refused: reason=authority-closed+capture-assertion(admitted run authority is no longer active) run=ab7ad29f-1b83-4af2-b3f2-158ce686d0bb session=<redacted> lastWrite=activate-capture lastWriteRun=ab7ad29f-1b83-4af2-b3f2-158ce686d0bb lastWriteAgeMs=18 phase=probe
```

**After** (same Gateway rebuilt with this change, 14 hours from 2026-11-12 22:26 MST). Zero occurrences of the error. For the affected model the log has 18 process starts, 32 completed turns and no failed turns, so at least 14 turns completed on a reused process. The first reuse after the restart:

```
22:28:36.880 [agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-2 activeSessions=2
22:29:13.403 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-2 durationMs=36529 outBytes=709
22:29:49.738 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-2 durationMs=23403 outBytes=1436
```

The second `cli turn` has no `cli live session start` before it: it ran on the process started at 22:28:36. That exact sequence (a follow-up turn seconds after the first) failed every time before the change.

### Regression test

`src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.warm-context.test.ts` runs two turns through the real `executePluginOwnedProcess`. The plugin calls the host's `assertCurrent` through an async context captured during the first turn, the way a warm transport does, and the test records which turn's context the host assertion observed.

Without the change (`origin/main` `execute-plugin.ts`):

```
 ×  unit-fast  src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.warm-context.test.ts > plugin-owned CLI warm transport callbacks > runs host assertions in the current turn's async context, not the first turn's
   → expected [ 'turn-1' ] to deeply equal [ 'turn-2' ]
      Tests  1 failed (1)
```

With it:

```
 ✓  unit-fast  src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.warm-context.test.ts > plugin-owned CLI warm transport callbacks > runs host assertions in the current turn's async context, not the first turn's
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Also run at this head: `execute-plugin.test.ts`, `execute-plugin.policy.test.ts`, `execute-plugin.steering.test.ts`, `execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts`, `cli-live-session-registry.test.ts` and `extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime.test.ts` (187 tests passed), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, and the test-lines ratchet (the new test's 43 lines are funded in `config/test-lines-allocations/cli-warm-callback-async-context.txt`).

### Proof limits

- The before/after Gateway is a fork build that also carries our other open PR branches, not a clean build of `main` plus this change.
- We did not capture which session-source assertion refused in production. The diagnostic that would have named it shipped in the same build as the fix, and no refusal has happened since. The chain from "stale async context" to "authority retired" is read from the code; what is measured is the stale context (the regression test), the retired authority (the diagnostic line), and the failures stopping (the Gateway logs).
- The failure did not reproduce in `gateway-cli-backend.live.test.ts` with a warm process on the unfixed code. Those runs have no owner or operator session source, which is consistent with the explanation above but is not proof of it.
- The regression test proves the callbacks now run in the current turn's context. It does not itself drive the registry to retire an authority.

*Written by Tank (Claude), an AI agent operated by Eddie Abrams (zeroaltitude).*

prs.title: fix(auth): configured primary account blocks CLI fallback
prs.body:
Closes #158421. Thanks to @HerbertHuerto for the corrected report and @aoclaw-glitch for the per-agent reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A configured primary `model@profile` is treated as a conversation-wide account pin. After that primary fails, ordinary Chat or event-Cron fallback can reject the destination CLI before launching it because the primary account belongs to another provider.

## User Impact

Fallback can select the destination runtime's account while genuine user and user-link pins remain strict. Scheduled inference keeps its recorded-account requirement. Preparation waits retain the current session intent and saved credential; native login identity stays separate from forwarded credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing auth owner carries configured-account provenance as a runtime-only fact through the reply and Cron paths. New explicit intent clears that provenance even when its account values match. CLI preparation and final dispatch use the existing session, credential and cancellation owners.

This normal integration preserves main's shared preference and compatibility owners, native model/context facts, turn audiences, native-tool policy and requester construction. It maps the original configured-default condition to the shared preference's `origin`, instead of restoring the former inline precedence implementation. Both author and current-main Gateway lifecycle controls remain.

The public V1 registration signatures remain source-compatible with the shipped v2026.11.3 contract. The additive V2 types require deferred execution admission. The compatibility window remains owner-controlled and undated; this author update does not settle the remaining V1 deferred-effect decision or enforced owner approvals.

## Evidence

Current author head `7a2a868f0cd23bc9ca6c348b5e12180fa8b740fb`, tree `24d87bd3136d62c4ca86f36a27bd11210fb43dad`, normally merges original author `d61a1c17c521e3816f62ddebc25e396bfdf8f437` and official main `5dc668341a3d83a5fad2d33fa8db359b63eaf360`. The complete proposal matches the fixed local source and independent review.

- **Actual owning-entry before → after:** production source exactly at main `5dc66834`, with the original process fixture and its database-worker classification, produces one intended Chat failure: Google CLI rejects the configured Anthropic account and no owned child launches. The scheduled missing-recorded-account refusal passes. Wrapper cost: **415.797 seconds**; 15 other cases are unselected. The candidate's unchanged complete **17-case** normal-entry file passes in **884.238 seconds** (Vitest 645.26 seconds), including ordinary Chat/event-Cron, scheduled refusal, native account selection and late user/user-link pin edits. These use real configuration, canonical isolated storage, admission/placement and actual owned Node child I/O. Their contract spans asynchronous preparation and effect ownership; selector mocks do not establish it. They are not vendor CLI or operator-Gateway acceptance.
- **Supplementary owner and adapter checks:** The five core owner files have 122 distinct passing cases: selection 7, Gateway lifecycle 38, Cron DTO 8 and the latest ordered credential/history replay 69 (397.187 seconds). The separate plugin-runtime file passes 3 cases (129.105 seconds); both complete Anthropic adapter files pass 96 cases (176.574 seconds). The adapter tests cover cold/warm deferred admission, current credentials, private input, retained callbacks and process cleanup through owned Node simulators. Together with the 17 entry cases, these are 238 distinct cases in 9 files; replayed attempts are not added again.
- **Types and tooling:** production types pass (68.692 seconds); the canonical changed-test selector passes six relevant core test graphs (650.050 seconds); the representative Anthropic product/test consumer passes with canonical extension settings and ambient declarations (31.200 seconds). Type-aware lint passes on all changed core production paths, the six corresponding core test groups and all changed Anthropic product/test consumers. Format, mock-export, line-cap and main-relative whitespace guards pass. Canonical standalone SDK declarations pass in **337.242 seconds**; the canonical SDK export check also passes.
- **Budget:** the absolute native test-line gate passes at **6,656,788 / 6,656,788, 0 LF slack**. Exact main passes at **6,655,499 / 6,655,499**, so no inherited debt is funded. The original annotated 1,277-LF record and shared scalar stay unchanged; a distinct 12-LF record makes total credit **1,289 LF**, exactly this proposal's net regression growth under the current fix-owned allocation rule. These tests protect real fallback versus explicit pins, recorded scheduled accounts, credential publication/replacement/SecretRef/cancellation, final execution/input authority and V1/V2 consumers. One duplicate raw-pin DTO row is removed; the stronger session controls and all 17 entry cases remain.
- **Fresh independent source review:** two desktop reviewers inspected the complete **80-file main-relative proposal**, split into disjoint 35-file core and 45-file caller partitions with cross-owner tracing. Both verified the fixed tree and whole diff SHA256 `a2498a491a01ded3da1188d687c9b98a80aca959b8b7d6de465858c63c87570f`; no actionable P0–P2 findings. This is read-only source/evidence review, not maintainer approval or reviewer-executed tests.
- **Execution scope:** actual executable auditing observes zero Codex CLI executions in the controls and 17-case collection. The adapter fixtures use isolated state and owned Node protocol simulators. The standalone declaration build and every serial recovery command also have zero observed Codex CLI executions. Validation uses Node24.22.1/pnpm12.15.0, matching the actual branch manifest.

Natural [CI run 43026451913](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43026451913), attempt 1, is **completed/success**, observed at `2026-11-11T21:48:06.170871+08:00` (Asia/Shanghai). The complete observation has **89 jobs: 62 successful and 27 skipped**; skipped scopes are not executed proof. The native test-line job passes at **6,660,180 / 6,660,181, 1 LF slack**. Its actual tested merge `6d16dcc6d613cb7462ecfcbedb9bfc03ea783b74` combines main `93e4800f6df9c6c0e3f3de2e7b8b1071fd170598` and this author head; fresh official commit objects and checkout logs agree. The Actions CI-gate job passed. The separate [maintainer approval workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43030594409) still publishes pending dependency/security-sensitive statuses and a classic CI-gate failure awaiting approval; those are not test failures or approvals granted. Owner acceptance and the proof gaps below remain separate merge requirements.

### Retained local failures and their investigation

The first main control omitted the fixture's database-worker membership and failed before reaching account behavior. That two-failure attempt remains invalid control evidence; the corrected production-main result above supplies the defect proof. A HEAD-relative whitespace check also included canonical upstream Gradle CRLF changes; the artifact is byte-identical to main, and the actual PR-range check passes without changing it.

The first supplemental collection reports **121 passing cases and one global post-case cleanup-hook timeout** across five files. The synchronous credential case and setup bytes match the compared sources, but that does not establish inherited failure or flakiness. Retained transformed setup maps the timeout to the global `afterEach` at canonical `test/setup-openclaw-runtime.ts:382–403`; the unfinished lazy import/drain/reset/retirement step remains unclassified. The same two files, in the original order and with the unchanged timeout, subsequently pass all 69 cases in 397.187 seconds after standalone SDK preparation and serial scheduling. That is replay evidence, not a claimed hook repair; the original unfinished await remains unknown. The fail-fast scheduler left plugin-runtime and both Anthropic files unstarted; the results above describe their separate runs.

The first source-lint command failed before lint diagnostics because automatic SDK-boundary declaration preparation exceeded its existing 300-second deadline. The canonical standalone declaration producer completed on the same source; the subsequent validation retains its original timeouts. No source change or timeout increase is claimed as a repair for either infrastructure/setup failure.

## Remaining Proof and Review

Arbitrary legacy V1 deferred I/O still needs its SDK/security compatibility decision and effect-boundary evidence. Real bundled vendor CLI/account behavior, installed latest-stable upgrade preserving settings/sessions, paired-node execution, Windows and release behavior remain separate, uncovered requirements. Earlier Gateway proofs keep their original source and authorization; they do not transfer to this revision. SDK/listed-owner acceptance and applicable enforced security-sensitive/dependency checks remain separate from author validation and natural CI. No author dependency override, protocol/SQLite schema change, release or upstream merge is proposed.

<details>
<summary>Earlier source-qualified validation and failures, retained with their original inputs</summary>

Closes #158421. Thanks to @HerbertHuerto for the corrected report and @aoclaw-glitch for the per-agent reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A primary model configured with `@profile` can block Chat or event-Cron fallback to another CLI provider by treating the configured account as a conversation-wide pin.

## User Impact

Fallback can use the destination runtime's account. Explicit user/user-link pins retain priority and are checked after preparation waits. Scheduled inference keeps its recorded-account and current-credential checks. Explicit native CLI account adoption remains supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth owner records configured-account provenance as a runtime-only fact and distinguishes a native login's selected identity from a forwarded credential ID. Existing admission and dispatch owners carry those facts to the final effect. Legacy V1 CLI registration signatures remain source-compatible; the additive V2 execution contract carries the required admission capability. The compatibility window remains owner-controlled and undated.

Literal saved CLI credentials join a known pending credential publication before launch. Admission rechecks the conversation pin and the same saved record after that wait; SecretRef-backed records retain refusal behavior, and the owning turn or process can cancel the wait.

## Evidence

Current author head `d61a1c17c521e3816f62ddebc25e396bfdf8f437` (tree `cd0a09d6128e0d5ac7272d43f71e7f646ebef600`) includes the reviewed saved-credential publication repair `7973e98be502`.
