- **Original CI failure:** the two saved-account Gateway failures in [run 42198633248](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42198633248/job/127828654052) were reproduced before the production repair. The repaired four-case Gateway replay and its 73-case owner scope retain their recorded `7973e98be502` qualification; they are not claimed rerun in this fixture-only revision.
- **Current regression proof:** the first consolidation passed 257 cases in nine related suites. After the typed observation-flow correction, the four affected suites passed 100 cases; unchanged suite evidence retains its earlier test-tree binding. The before runs passed 69 authority/native-history cases and 190 preparation/steering cases. These counts overlap and are not added together.
- **Checks and review:** all nine affected test type graphs, typed lint, formatting, line caps and whitespace pass. Fresh native P0-P2 review covers this complete nine-file test delta. The preceding independent production review remains bound to the unchanged `7973e98be502` source.
- **Budget:** no allocation or shared scalar change. Common backend cleanup and credential fixtures remove 58 literal test newlines while retaining the replacement-during-wait, SecretRef, cancellation, current-account and pin controls. Net growth against official `a6ee6a18a5d748a8ed8e395b63c4a5d2a6e02982` is 1,295 LF, below the prior 1,298 maximum; the existing 1,277-LF allocation remains unchanged. The exact current-main merge preview passes with 40 lines spare.

Validation used Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0. Current-head PR CI supplies broad integration proof after this push. Installed latest-stable upgrade with the bundled vendor CLI, SDK-owner direction, security approval and dependency approval remain separate review items.

<details>
<summary>Earlier author integration and proof, with their original head qualifications</summary>

Previous author head `187f8c07b720ef84fd72e1a24122fe29cbe45b80` normally merges official main `982f3b1ee2b668afafe69c352d48baef470d2d20` into author head `a03c06e`, preserving earlier contributor history and the prior `669193e` integration. This resolves an actual CI semantic merge: a newly added Anthropic test helper still referenced the V1 type name after the SDK import migrated to V2. November 6 maintenance integrates official main `7302f00ac3eea8d12f84b3591fb451564a7fed7e`. The saved-account branch retains both the session pin check and the existing credential authority. Standard and personal credential readers are prepared by their owners and asserted synchronously after the session pin read at local target launch and input, bundled Claude target and first prompt, and the paired-node dispatch authorization gate.

- Omitting the inherited target-spawn check reproduced the existing refusal case failing. The integration passed 157 cases in 7 focused files, plus four persisted owner lifecycle cases and two personal credential owner cases. The four persisted-owner cases were repeated after the lint-only explicit return of the existing terminal error call.

Fresh independent review covered the retained account paths, fallback-stop behavior and metadata-only process view. The current author maintenance preserves the V1 and V2 SDK declarations from the preceding author revision.

Current committed tree `ee890ea01c49eeace583561c6f999e60032f8c46` matches the reviewed candidate.

Prior head-linked [CI run41976118069](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41976118069) completed **success** at2026-11-05 06:20:05 UTC (14:20 Asia/Shanghai). The ratchet job records actual test merge `b0f904096a7346d4c1caa46928a8c750c45d0ef6`, combining official main `57382781c4c0620e672644f2a187163f79ec67db` with187f. Its native test-line result is6,480,836 /6,480,842,with6 LF spare. This is a different source execution from the pinned982f local controls below; no author allocation or shared baseline was raised to obtain it. Maintainer dependency/security authorization still remains pending, so this is not an all-green merge gate.

The following failures remain recorded for the pinned main982f / standalone candidate comparison. Their assertions, budgets and outcomes were not weakened or retroactively relabeled by the later merged-CI success:

prs.title: fix(auth): configured primary account blocks Claude CLI fallback
prs.body:
Closes #158421. Replaces #165583 with a smaller fix at the same owner; that PR's author is credited as co-author.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the configured primary model carries an account (`openai/<model>@openai:<account>`) and that primary fails, the configured Claude CLI (or Gemini CLI) fallback never runs. The turn fails with `CLI backend "claude-cli" cannot use auth profile "openai:<account>" owned by "openai"`.

## User Impact

User impact: a configured primary account no longer blocks a cross-provider CLI fallback; the fallback answers with its own account. Accounts the user pinned on the session (`/model …@profile`, person-linked pins) still fail closed before the CLI starts, as before. Scheduled runs keep their recorded-account rule (unchanged path).

## Why This Change Was Made

Each turn resolves the configured primary account with the same strength as a session pin, so the reply path cannot tell them apart. The embedded fallback candidate and the command path already keep a configured account with its own provider. The reply path's CLI candidate passed the raw selection to the CLI auth owner so that session pins can fail closed there, and that also caught the configured account.

The CLI candidate now passes the raw selection only when it is the session's own pin. Otherwise it uses the existing provider-scoped selection (`resolveRunAuthProfile`), which is what the embedded candidate uses. No new state or fields.

Accepted edge case: if the session pin is cleared while the turn is in flight, that turn uses the provider-scoped selection.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway from source (own HOME, state, profile and port). Primary `openai/gpt-5.6-sol@openai:acct-a` with a synthetic invalid OpenAI key (OpenAI returns 401). Fallback `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime, with real Claude Code through the shared CLI proxy (the host subscription is at its weekly limit). One `chat.send` on `agent:main:main`.

| Build | Primary | Fallback decision | Fallback result | Chat history |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main `34600e99e21c` | 401, `fallback_model reason=auth` | `next=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` | `Embedded agent failed before reply: CLI backend "claude-cli" cannot use auth profile "openai:acct-a" owned by "openai".` No Claude turn. | "Model switched…" notice only, no reply |
| this PR | 401, `fallback_model reason=auth` | `next=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` | `cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5`, `candidate_succeeded` | `FALLBACK-OK` from `claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5` |

Tests: `agent-runner-execution-cli-auth.test.ts` adds "selects CLI credentials after the configured primary account fails over". It fails on main and passes here. The session-pinned rejection case still passes. `agent-runner-execution-{state,session-events,probes,cli-auth}`: 45 passed. oxfmt and oxlint are clean.

pr-simplify: the fix uses the existing provider-scoped owner. It adds no runtime provenance field, so no Cron/DTO/SDK threading. Production: +11/−1 in one file. Tests: +23/−2 (one new case; the existing rejection case now puts the pin on the session, which is where real pins live). Test-line allocation: 21.

prs.title: fix(tasks): recompute terminal retention after lost-task recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a task loses its backing session, maintenance marks it `lost` and stamps the
short 24-hour lost-window retention (`cleanupAfter = lostAt + 24h`). When the
durable ledger later records a real terminal result, maintenance recovers the task
to `succeeded`/`failed` but never recomputes `cleanupAfter`, so the recovered
record keeps `lostAt + 24h` instead of the standard 7-day terminal retention from
its actual `endedAt`. If recovery happens more than 24h after the lost-mark
(Gateway down overnight, long-running job), the recovered terminal record is
pruned on the very next sweep — the user never sees the recovered outcome,
defeating the recovery feature's purpose of preserving finished work across
Gateway restarts (#145940). Even on quick recovery, the record gets only the
remainder of the short lost window instead of the documented 7-day terminal
retention (#126063, #126095).

## Why This Change Was Made

The defect is in `applyTaskRecordPatch` (`src/tasks/task-registry-records.ts`),
the lifecycle owner that stamps `cleanupAfter` for terminal records: it only
recomputed when `cleanupAfter` was missing, so the numeric lost-window value
survived a `lost` → terminal transition. Recovery paths (`markTaskRecovered` /
`projectTaskRecovered` in `src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.ts`) also
preserved the numeric value.

The fix recomputes the terminal retention whenever a terminal status is reached
from `lost`, and makes the `projectTaskRecovered` projection always recompute.
The invariant: the short lost-window retention applies only while the record is
still `lost`; once recovered, the standard terminal retention from the recovered
`endedAt` applies. Files changed: `src/tasks/task-registry-records.ts` and
`src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.ts` (fix), `src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts`
and the `test/fixtures/task-registry-recovery-restart.ts` fixture (regression
tests). No new dependencies, configuration options, or schema changes.

## Review-followup fixes

- **Exclude unchanged `lost` status from the recovery predicate (P2).**
  `isTerminalTaskStatus("lost")` is true, so the recovery recompute also ran when
  a still-`lost` record received a metadata-only or cleanup-only update
  (e.g. `setTaskCleanupAfterById`), silently replacing the explicit deadline the
  retention owner honors with `endedAt + 24h`. The predicate now requires a
  *different* terminal status (`next.status !== "lost"`): only a real recovery
  recomputes, and a still-`lost` record keeps its existing deadline. A regression
  test ("preserves an explicit lost-task deadline on a cleanup-only update")
  covers this: it fails on the pre-fix predicate (deadline 45260000 replaced by
  88400000) and passes with the fix.
- **Prove persistence across real OS process restarts, not just reload (proof
  followup).** The previous proof reloaded the registry from SQLite inside one
  process, which is not independent proof of an operating-system process
  restart. The committed subprocess regression test now spawns the fixture as
  three genuinely separate OS processes (`node --import tsx`, distinct PIDs)
  sharing one SQLite state dir: seed → recover → verify, then the parent reloads
  and runs the next sweep. The corrected deadline demonstrably survives real
  process restarts, and the next sweep keeps the recovered record.

## User Impact

Recovered terminal cron tasks now keep the documented 7-day retention from their
recovered end time, so their outcome stays visible in task history instead of
being pruned shortly after recovery. Tasks that are never lost are unchanged;
`lost` records still use the 24-hour window (and still honor an earlier explicit
lost-task deadline).

## Evidence

- **OS-process-restart recovery proof (before/after).** The real task-registry
  module chain runs against one real SQLite state dir across three genuinely
  separate OS processes (each a distinct `node --import tsx` child), so
  persistence is proven across real process restarts — the same boundary a
  Gateway restart crosses — not just an in-process registry reload. A lost cron
  task whose 24h lost-window deadline has already expired is written by process
  1, recovered by process 2, and read + swept by process 3. Timestamps and PIDs
  are redacted below; each phase printed from a distinct process.

  **Before (pre-fix source):** recovery keeps the expired lost-window deadline,
  so the very next sweep prunes the recovered record (`pruned: 1`,
  `still-present: false`) — the recovered outcome is lost.

  ```
  [seed]    seeded lost task: status=lost cleanupAfter=... (2026-09-17T05:41:39.953Z) expired=true
  [recover] reload saw: status=lost cleanupAfter=... stale-expired=true
  [recover] recovered: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... corrected-in-future=false corrected=false
  [sweep]   reload saw: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... preserved-across-restart=false
  [sweep]   sweep: maintenance={"reconciled":0,"recovered":0,"cleanupStamped":0,"pruned":1} still-present=false
  ```

  **After (fixed source):** recovery restores the standard 7-day terminal
  retention from the recovered `endedAt`; the corrected deadline survives all
  three process restarts and the next sweep keeps the record
  (`pruned: 0`, `still-present: true`).

  ```
  [seed]    seeded lost task: status=lost cleanupAfter=... (2026-09-17T05:42:28.485Z) expired=true
  [recover] reload saw: status=lost cleanupAfter=... stale-expired=true
  [recover] recovered: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... (2026-09-23T15:42:38.378Z) corrected-in-future=true corrected=true
  [sweep]   reload saw: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... preserved-across-restart=true
  [sweep]   sweep: maintenance={"reconciled":0,"recovered":0,"cleanupStamped":0,"pruned":0} still-present=true
  ```

  `RESULT: PASS` — the corrected deadline survived 3 real process restarts and
  the recovered record is not pruned. The before/after traces are from the same
  script and state dir; the only difference is the two fixed source files.

- **Subprocess regression test (committed).** The same OS-process-restart flow is
  committed as a real persisted-SQLite regression test in
  `src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts` ("persists the corrected deadline
  across real OS process restarts and survives the next sweep"). It spawns the
  fixture `test/fixtures/task-registry-recovery-restart.ts` three times via
  `node --import tsx` (seed → recover → verify) against one
  `withOpenClawTestState` state dir, then reloads and runs the next maintenance
  sweep in the parent. On the pre-fix source this test fails
  (`expected <expired lost-window deadline> to be greater than <now>`); with the
  fix it passes.

- **Regression tests** in `src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts`:
  - a `lost` record with the short lost-window `cleanupAfter` is recovered via
    `markTaskTerminalById({ status: "succeeded", ... })`; the recovered record's
    `cleanupAfter` equals the standard terminal retention from the recovered
    `endedAt` and is greater than the stale lost-window value (fails on the
    original code, passes with the fix);
  - a still-`lost` record keeps an explicit deadline on a cleanup-only update
    (P2 followup, fails on the pre-fix predicate);
  - the reload + next-sweep proof (fails on the PR base);
  - the OS-process-restart proof above (fails on the pre-fix source).
- Existing suites pass locally: `task-registry.store.test.ts` (59),
  `task-registry-records.test.ts`, `task-retention.test.ts`,
  `task-registry.maintenance-projection.test.ts`. `oxfmt` and `git diff --check`
  clean.
- Production LOC delta: net +4 — no new dependencies, config, protocol, or schema.
- AI-assisted: yes

The test helper previously accepted PID receipt text with a valid numeric prefix, such as `42stale`, because `parseInt` stopped at the first non-decimal character.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the complete trimmed receipt as a positive safe decimal integer before returning it, while preserving the existing AbortSignal lifecycle. Rebased onto current `main`; commits carry the corrected author identity (`qingminglong`).

## User Impact

Test and CI cleanup helpers no longer treat contaminated PID receipts as real process identifiers.

## Evidence

### Real caller trace (red → green)

Direct `waitForPidFile` invocation from a cleanup-caller perspective, against a real temp-dir receipt file (unredacted terminal output, no credentials involved):

- **Base `main` helper** (bug reproduced):

  ```text
  BASE: receipt="42stale" -> resolved PID 42  (contaminated text accepted!)
  ```

- **This head** (fix applied):

  ```text
  receipt="42stale" -> rejected: aborted waiting for pid in ...\Temp\pid-probe-...

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts test/helpers/process-wait.test.ts`

- **Red** (base `test/helpers/process-wait.ts`, this PR's tests): `3 failed | 13 passed (16)` — exactly the malformed-receipt cases `42stale`, `42`, and `4.2` fail.
- **Green** (this head): `16 passed (16)`, including real process-death observation cases.

- `oxfmt --check test/helpers/process-wait.ts test/helpers/process-wait.test.ts` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Proof boundary

This proves complete PID receipt parsing in the shared test helper and regression fixtures only; it makes no production runtime or platform-specific claim.

prs.body:
Related: #174317 (landed as [eb6a328b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/eb6a328b7e8da71878e8be44cc54e6c7352a0fc3)).

## What Problem This Solves

Generated private Telegram topic names can stay tied to the opening message after a conversation settles on a more specific task. This is the separate Telegram follow-up to Peter's narrowed Dashboard implementation.

## User Impact

With existing `autoTopicLabel` enabled, newly generated private topic names receive one refinement attempt after six follow-up task messages. Control-only, unknown, and disabled skill commands do not count. A failed attempt consumes the attempt and preserves the name. Observed manual topic names, manual session names, legacy topics without generated provenance, reset sessions, group forums, and channel Direct Messages remain protected.

## Implementation and Scope

Telegram uses its existing account/metadata-owner-scoped topic cache, persists the countdown before inference, and rechecks the session and observed name before editing. It shares Dashboard task classification and the bounded 40-message/32 KB context reader. No transcript excerpts or database schema are added.

The SDK addition is two helpers and their state type through existing `reply-dispatch-runtime`: `advanceConversationLabelRefinement` and `readConversationLabelRefinementSource`. Neither writes state nor invokes a model. No new subpath, RPC, settings, or configurable threshold is introduced. Later automatic Telegram renaming and this narrow SDK surface still need a maintainer decision; landing Dashboard does not imply acceptance.

The branch integrates landed main `192947de`, preserves contributor history, and leaves #174317's branch untouched. Remaining feature diff: **13 files, +390/-68**, including the database-worker test registration. Current head: `1cd8d4e00a9815056e7ffdbbdbe03219468ff5ed`.

## Evidence

- All 56 focused cases passed on the integrated runtime tree: 39 Dashboard, 13 Telegram metadata/cache, and four dispatch regressions.
- Final fixture bytes pass all four cases in the **database-worker lane**, including sixth-task refinement, effective skill filtering, reopen persistence, manual rename during inference, session reset, and metadata-owner isolation.
- Prior-head [CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40178276834/job/121123855003) exposed missing host-broker admission for the new persistence test. The test now belongs to the existing database-worker lane; typed spies also resolve its unbound-method lint errors.
- Core and Telegram package types, the exact extension test-type gate, targeted core/Telegram lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass under Node 24.22.1.
- Full supported-runtime build passed in 16m 32.6s, including CLI metadata, runtime postbuild, and all 160 SDK export checks. Subsequent commits change only test routing/fixtures. The transferred runtime declares build `421a0af`; its production source is byte-identical to final head `1cd8d4e`. UI asset diagnostics reported 100 B startup gzip and 76 B total CSS raw over budget while the build exited successfully.
- Built Telegram import screening passes; Windows cannot qualify process-group closure, which remains an explicit screening limitation.
- Original-dispatch red proof: at `8bc21e5`, the sixth follow-up retains `Topic label` instead of `Fix release signing`. Disabled-skill countdown also has observed red/green proof.
- **Exact-head [CI 40181000819](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40181000819) passed**, including full test types and both extension bundles. All eight companion workflows also passed. Earlier runs exposed the repaired fixture issues and a repeated cron failure; the final run is green without rerunning or changing cron code.
- Independent narrative review found no remaining actionable P0–P2 issue after the metadata-scope, bounded-read, skill-filter, and integration repairs.

## Live Proof Still Pending

The existing HP QA source runtime has been refreshed to the published source, with its previous files/config preserved for recovery. Its established local model broker and QA bot are reachable. A full HP build refused the available memory before removing output. Supported narrow AI/package builds passed, but the source-Gateway route found stale old runtime bundles and a retained agent database requiring schema 31→34 migration. The Gateway/model smoke exited before inference. The passing Windows-built JavaScript artifacts were checksum-verified, extracted into the same stopped QA candidate, and verified to load on Linux as `2026.10.7 (421a0af)`. Previous runtime and state are preserved for recovery. The narrower session-import command reported zero targets and left schema 31 unchanged with `quick_check=ok`; broad Doctor repair awaits approval. The original QA configuration was restored byte-for-byte, and no candidate Gateway/poller or heavy HP build remains running.

**No live Telegram refinement, model-flow verdict, latest-stable upgrade verdict, or screenshot is claimed yet.** Telegram desktop interaction approval timed out before a QA message or deliverable screenshot; the required retained-database schema repair also awaits approval. Existing mocked transport/model tests and older proof packets do not replace that evidence. Current npm stable was verified as `2026.10.7`.

prs.title: feat(sessions): keep useful names after context resets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resetting context should not destroy a useful conversation name. Commands such as `/model` should never become its title.

## User Impact

The first real message gives a new Telegram topic or Dashboard conversation a name. This includes Telegram’s **New Thread** flow, where sending a message creates an implicitly named “New Chat”.

After six follow-up user messages, the utility model compares the opening message and those follow-ups with the current name. After `/reset`, it compares the first real message with the existing name. A fitting broad name such as “YouGile” stays exactly as it is for related work; the model replaces it only when the subject no longer fits.

Commands, bot replies and child-agent output do not count. Manual edits win over naming attempts already in flight.

## Why This Change Was Made

I usually reset a topic to continue the same work with fresh context. Having to restore its old name by hand defeats that workflow.

Naming now starts from approved, recorded user input, without waiting for the agent’s answer. Blocked or hidden input cannot trigger it. Queued messages count individually when their approved text is unchanged; if a hook rewrites the combined input, only that approved result is used. Opening media stays associated with its accepted message.

Related: #184821, #174317, #183368. Reassessing a manually chosen title changes the stable-title policy from #185337 and needs a maintainer decision.

## Evidence

The approved-input follow-up passed **113 focused tests in six files**, core types, five affected test type graphs, scoped lint, formatting and line budgets. It was then merged with main at `e60207216`. On the resulting tree `9f86524d`, **36 transcript and queue tests**, core types, formatting and scoped typed lint passed. An independent review of the three manual conflict resolutions found no P0–P2 issues. A later test-only follow-up removes duplicated fixtures while retaining the in-flight “New Chat” race: 15 lifecycle tests, formatting and the test-line budget against frozen `e602` passed. Hosted CI for the current head is separate.

These screenshots are from the earlier integrated build `b2b6eb7`, **not this public head**:

First real message:

![Automatic title after the first user message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/0f27d894bfa282460f9d5bdb1fbe7d4cdde95a59/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-12/telegram-first-message-b2b6eb7-header.png)

Reset, model selection and the same subject:

![The existing title remains for the same subject](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/0f27d894bfa282460f9d5bdb1fbe7d4cdde95a59/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-12/telegram-reset-same-b2b6eb7-header.png)

Reset and a different subject:

![A new title for a different subject](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/0f27d894bfa282460f9d5bdb1fbe7d4cdde95a59/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-12/telegram-reset-different-b2b6eb7-header.png)

[Messages, timings and limits](https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/blob/0f27d894bfa282460f9d5bdb1fbe7d4cdde95a59/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-12/telegram-naming-b2b6eb7.md).

The lifecycle retains bounded excerpts of the opening input and up to six follow-ups; that retention proposal needs maintainer review. Older lifecycles without those excerpts use a bounded transcript fallback. Delayed Telegram title edits retain the existing arrival-order behavior; the original live manual-rename mismatch was not captured well enough to prove its cause.

The behavior is now running in my local integration `644e178`; that build also carries other patches. This is separate from exact-public-head live acceptance and hosted CI. The manual-title policy and bounded input retention still need maintainer review.

Related: #196199, #190670, #170562, #194024.

## What Problem This Solves

Our earlier Gateway logs showed children losing tool access or failing to return results after the parent yielded. Accepted work could still inherit the plugin call that had just ended.

**Current-main status:** the maintainer's real Telegram test with a Codex parent and child passed. Merged #197658 fixes a separate failed-child announcement path and is already installed here. A normal user-path reproduction for the broader failure on current main is still missing.

## User Impact

Keep accepted child work, completion cleanup and parent wake running after the originating call ends. The original caller's authority, revocation, reload self-hold and generation checks remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Detach accepted work and queued lifecycle events from the finished invocation. Carry live self-hold facts through admission, then release them. A stale event cannot settle a replacement run.

## Evidence

Public revision: `57afbb83cb76d1beb0ce95195ff9200f3d9c34b7`.

- Focused checks passed: five event/registry/SQLite cases, three reload self-hold cases, and a real registered-tool write followed by revocation.

A linked Telegram user with staff access should be able to ask for a personal reminder without becoming a Gateway owner.

prs.title: feat(workboard): let a board run more than one card per owner at once
prs.body:
Closes #198354

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard runs only one card at a time per owner, so several independent cards for one agent run one after another, and all unassigned cards (which share the `workboard-dispatcher` owner) run one at a time across every board.

## User Impact

A board can set `orchestration.maxActivePerOwner` (1 to 20, default 1) to let one owner run that many cards at once. Boards without the setting behave exactly as before. The Workboard docs describe what actually occupies an owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Setting:** `maxActivePerOwner` is stored with the board's other orchestration settings (`orchestration_json`), so there is no schema change.
- **How it counts:** a card on the board may start while its owner holds fewer active cards than the limit. Active cards are counted across all boards, as before; only the threshold comes from the card's board.
- **Where it is enforced:** in the same two places as the existing one-card rule, the dispatcher's selection and the atomic claim (`claimIfOwnerAvailable`), which takes `{ ownerId, now, limit }`.
- **Agent tool:** `maxActivePerOwner` is also added to the `orchestration` parameters of the `workboard_board_create` tool. That schema is strict, so without the field agents could not set the limit on a board; the Gateway method `workboard.boards.upsert` accepts it without a schema change.
- **Docs:** they said an owner is blocked by "running or review work on the board". The code counts cards that are `running`, whose run is still marked running, or whose claim has not expired, on any board. So a card in `review` blocks its owner only until its claim expires. `docs/plugins/workboard.md` and `docs/cli/workboard.md` say this and document the setting.

The per-pass `maxStarts` cap (default 3) is unchanged. A pass still tries one card per owner before starting extra cards for the same owner.

## Evidence

- New test in `extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher.test.ts`: a board with `maxActivePerOwner: 2` and three unassigned ready cards starts two, and a second dispatch starts none while the third stays `ready`. It fails on the base branch (only one card starts) and passes with this change.
- Targeted tests: `dispatcher`, `dispatcher-compensation`, `store`, `store.attempts`, `sqlite-store-batch-read`, `sqlite-store.lifecycle`, `sqlite-store-policy`, `tools`, `postgres-store` and `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability`: 190 passed, 11 skipped. The skipped tests are the PostgreSQL store tests, which need a PostgreSQL server.
- Typecheck: `tsconfig.extensions.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` pass. `oxfmt --check` is clean on the changed files.
- Real Gateway proof in a disposable VM on `eff2d30273ff90ef8c73aa8aaf7634cbea791dc2`: 11/11 checks passed. Upgrade from `2026.11.3` preserves existing board summaries and full card records exactly; limit 2 admits two same-owner workers, defers the third and counts activity across boards; the default remains 1. Real local Ollama inference backed the active sessions; a transparent proxy held responses for observation. [Gateway and upgrade evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198358#issuecomment-6861117460). Exact-head CI remains held for maintainer approval (`action_required`).

prs.title: fix(openclaw-id): Copy link uses the tailnet address when opened through OpenClaw ID
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: **Copy link** on a session copies a link to the Gateway's configured public address (for example its tailnet hostname) when you opened the Control UI through OpenClaw ID remote access.

## User Impact

User impact: a claw member who reaches the claw through OpenClaw ID now copies session links on the claw's own address, so the link opens for members who reach the claw the same way. Preview links and public-share links are unchanged and keep the public address.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI builds copied links from the address the Gateway advertises in its hello, which was `gateway.publicOrigin` for every connection except plugin remote ingress. The hello now also carries the linked claw's Control UI address on OpenClaw ID tunnel connections, as a new optional field `controlUiClawUrl`, and the direct **Copy link** action prefers it.

`controlUiUrl` keeps its meaning. The tunnel admits members only, so preview links and anonymous public-share links must stay on the publicly reachable address; replacing `controlUiUrl` would have broken them for recipients who are not members.

The field is absent when the connection did not come through the tunnel, when no claw is linked, or when the Control UI is disabled.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.setup-completion.test.ts src/gateway/openclaw-id/claw-origin.test.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-sharing.test.ts`: 5 files, 134 tests passed.
- New Gateway tests cover the tunnel, disabled Control UI, non-tunnel and unlinked cases, and assert that `controlUiUrl` does not change. A new UI test covers direct links moving to the claw address while preview links stay public.
- `pnpm protocol:check` passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane passed except the dead export scan, which reports `RELEASE_VALIDATION_WAIVERS` in `scripts/lib/release-validation-waivers.mjs` and `resolveAuthoritativeSharedOAuthCredentialUnderLock` in `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-store.ts`. This PR does not touch either file; both are identical to the base commit `a48a3175600e`.

prs.title: fix(telegram): forum approval drops the topic when the live turn omits it
prs.body:
Closes #125166 ## What Problem This Solves With `execApprovals.target: "channel"`, an exec or plugin approval started in a Telegram forum topic is sent to the approver's private DM instead of the topic. The topic shows nothing, so the user in the topic does not see that the tool is waiting. ## User Impact The approval card is posted in the forum topic where the request started, as `target: "channel"` promises. A live turn from a different topic still does not match the stored route, so no card goes to a topic the request did not come from. ## Why This Change Was Made The origin check compares the live turn target with the stored session route and refuses the origin when they differ. Both carry the same topic, but in different shapes: - live turn: parsed to `{ to: "", threadId: 3 }`; - stored session route: `{ to: "telegram::topic:3", threadId: 3 }`, because the session resolver only ran `normalizeTelegramChatId`, which rejects the `:topic:` form. The pair never matched, the origin resolved to null, and the planner fell back to the approver DM. The live turn does carry its topic, so the omitted-thread theory in the first revision did not match the real flow. The Telegram adapter now normalizes the live turn and the stored session through one parser (`toTelegramOriginTarget`). The public `reconcileDivergentTargets` callback, its core plumbing and docs from the first revision are removed, so there is no SDK change. A stored target that cannot be parsed still has to disagree with the live turn. ## Evidence Live Telegram Test Server E2E, real Gateway + deterministic mock model, leased QA user, run-owned forum (`--create-forum`), `execApprovals: { enabled: true, approvers: [], target: "channel" }`, `tools.exec.mode: "ask"`. The user sends `EXEC:/usr/bin/touch ...` in the forum topic and taps **Allow Once**. The Bot API proxy log shows where each `sendMessage` went. - `main` at `8ebe740925ca`: the card `Approval required ...` went to the private chat (`chat: private`, no topic). The topic only got `Working / Exec running`, and the tap found no button. The same happened for a plugin approval (`before_tool_call` → `requireApproval`). - A debug build of `main` logged the origin check inputs: live turn `{"to":"-100…","threadId":3}`, stored session `{"to":"telegram:-100…:topic:3","threadId":3}`. - This head `ff04a839e875`: the exec approval card was posted in the forum topic, the **Allow Once** tap edited that card, the command ran and `EXEC_DONE` arrived in the topic. A plugin approval (`🛡️ Plugin approval required`) was also posted in the topic and resolved by a tap there. Nothing went to the private chat. - Regression: `approval-native.test.ts` stores the real `telegram::topic:` route; the same-topic case fails on `main` and passes here, the different-topic control stays null.

Working\n🛠️ Exec runnin'
18:15:08  editMessageText  chat=group topic=-  'Working\n🛠️ Exec'

prs.title: fix(browser): stop sending credentialed CDP wsUrl to the model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #158966.

With a loopback CDP profile whose `cdpUrl` carries HTTP Basic credentials or a query token (as used by Browserless/Browserbase-style endpoints), `browser action=tabs` and `browser action=open` hand the model a fully usable, credentialed `wsUrl`. Every tool action addresses tabs by `targetId`, so the model never needs the connectable socket URL, and its credentials leak into model-facing (and page-adjacent untrusted-content-wrapped) output.

This carries forward the unresolved problem from #137756, whose implementation PR was retired at the author's request without the underlying defect being fixed. Independent code reading against current `main` confirms the same root cause the retired PR identified, at the same two call sites (line numbers shifted slightly since that PR's base commit, behavior identical).

## Root cause

- `formatAgentTab` (`extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.actions.ts`) explicitly copies `source.wsUrl` onto the agent-visible tab it builds for `action=tabs`.
- `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata` (`extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-session-tabs.ts`) is documented as removing internal metadata before model output for `action=open`, but only stripped `ownership`/`resolvedProfile`, leaving `wsUrl` and its paired `wsLookup` intact.
- `normalizeCdpWsUrl` (`extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.ts`) deliberately propagates the configured endpoint's credentials onto the per-tab socket URL — that part is correct, it's needed for the runtime's own connection. The defect is only that the derived value then reaches the two model-facing formatting paths above.
- The declared output contract (`BrowserToolOutputSchema` in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.ts`) does not include `wsUrl` at all, and `client.types.ts` already documents `wsLookup` as "omitted from model-facing summaries" — `wsUrl` was never supposed to survive to model output either.

## Fix

Stop copying `wsUrl` in `formatAgentTab`, and strip both `wsUrl` and `wsLookup` in `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata`, matching the class of internal CDP connection metadata that already gets removed for other fields (`ownership`, `resolvedProfile`) and already gets redacted elsewhere in the codebase (`chrome.diagnostics.ts` calls `redactCdpUrl` before diagnostics output).

No other call site reads `wsUrl`/`wsLookup` back off a tool result — every consumer (screenshot capture, snapshot, page sessions) reads `tab.wsUrl` internally before the tool formats its result — so removing it from the two output paths changes nothing else.

## Evidence

New regression test `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts` drives the real, unmocked `executeTabsAction` and `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata` production functions with a synthetic credentialed CDP URL built through the real `normalizeCdpWsUrl`, then asserts the credential and the `wsUrl`/`wsLookup` keys are absent from the serialized model-facing result.

Confirmed the test fails without the fix — reverted the two source files to `HEAD~1` (pre-fix) and reran:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

 × browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=tabs model output
   → expected '{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"\n…' not to contain 's3cr3t-pass'
   Received: ...\"wsUrl\": \"wss://admin:s3cr3t-pass@chrome.example.net/devtools/page/AAA111?token=<redacted len=22>\"...

 × browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=open model output
   → expected '{"targetId":"AAA111","title":"Inbox",…' not to contain 's3cr3t-pass'
   Received: {"targetId":"AAA111","title":"Inbox","url":"https://mail.example.com","type":"page","wsUrl":"wss://admin:s3cr3t-pass@chrome.example.net/devtools/page/AAA111?token=<redacted len=24>...

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed (2)
```

Restored the fix and reran — both pass, plus the full existing browser-tool suite:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

 ✓ browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=tabs model output
 ✓ browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=open model output
 ...
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  277 passed (277)
```

Lint, typecheck and format on the changed files:

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.actions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-session-tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

(clean)

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
(clean)

$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.actions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-session-tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

## What was not tested

No real Chrome/CDP proxy end-to-end run — this fix and its test operate at the same production-function boundary (`executeTabsAction`, `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata`) as the issue's own real-behavior proof, using a synthetic credentialed URL built through the real `normalizeCdpWsUrl`. The retired PR #137756 previously ran a full real-Chrome/authenticating-proxy round trip proving the same before/after behavior; that evidence is preserved in its history for reference.

prs.title: fix(codex): shed abandoned cleared bindings at namespace capacity
prs.body:
Related: #125910.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server thread-binding namespace rejects new bindings after 50,000 rows accumulate, leaving later requests unavailable until the state database is cleaned manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier revisions of this PR moved the namespace to evict-oldest, which let the SQLite store delete binding rows it cannot read: retirement fences, legacy-clear provenance, live leases, and active sessions all ranked the same as garbage. This revision keeps reject-new everywhere and puts capacity recovery at the binding domain boundary.

`session-binding-overflow.ts` wraps the composed binding store's `mutate` and `withLease`, the insert and lease-admission paths. When an insert fails with a row-count limit error, the wrapper pages the worker-backed handle on the same namespace with `entriesInKeyRange` (512-row pages, storage-side ordering, decode in the storage worker) and sheds up to a few strictly validated disposable rows per failure through `observe` + `compareAndApply`, then retries. A lexical cursor persists across calls and wraps at the end of the namespace, so spaced failures keep advancing instead of re-reading the same protected prefix, and rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered. Destructive eligibility is decided on the raw record, not the tolerant codec: a lease in any malformed shape, a retirement marker in any shape at all, and any non-object row are preserved as ambiguous. Everything else (active bindings, retirement fences, live leases, `conversation:legacy-` provenance) fails closed with the original limit error. Recovery is gated on the current host's required capabilities; a host that lacks them cannot run the sweep and keeps reject-new behavior.

The sync store stays exactly where it was: hot reads. Listing and deletion during recovery run on the worker side of the store broker, so a full namespace never turns into a whole-table decode on the Gateway thread.

Sidecar migration keeps its main-branch reject-new store: at capacity the existing failure path retains the source, and no live row can be displaced by an import.

## User Impact

A namespace clogged with abandoned cleared rows recovers on its own instead of hard-failing every new session. Fences, leases, legacy-clear provenance, live bindings, and every ambiguous existing record are never shed; when nothing strictly disposable exists the limit error surfaces unchanged.

## Evidence

- `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` (16 tests; runs in the database-workers shard on the forks pool for the broker): recovery sheds an abandoned cleared row while an older live binding survives; fail-closed when the namespace holds only a retirement fence plus a live binding; a live lease is never shed; legacy-clear provenance survives recovery while an abandoned row next to it is shed; a cleared row with a non-object lease is preserved while a strictly valid abandoned row next to it is shed; a namespace of only ambiguous rows rejects with both rows intact; a host without ranged listing propagates the limit error with no inline scan; recovery through `createLazyCodexAppServerBindingStore(state, undefined, recoveryState)`, the exact production composition; a scan stalls mid-prefix under a one-page budget and the next insert resumes from the persisted cursor and succeeds (goes red when cursor persistence is broken); rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered.
- `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` (new): the real extension entry boots and builds the binding store plus the lazy recovery adapter from `api.runtime.state` itself; the openers delegate to the plugin-state test factories (same worker-backed SQLite stores, fixture module resolution; production additionally needs the Gateway host broker no in-process test has), with the binding namespace cap clamped 50,000 -> 3 as the only knob. Through that registered assembly: a fresh session's lease admission overflows, recovers, starts exactly once, and sheds exactly the disposable cleared row while the live binding and a held row survive; a caller whose authority is revoked at admission gets zero deletes with the disposable row intact; and a real `resolveCodexSessionBinding` authority whose `previousSessionId` changes between observe and `compareAndApply(delete)` is rejected at final worker admission with one delete attempt and the disposable row preserved.
- Real run, isolated state dir, production plugin-state store plus the production lazy composition over real SQLite at capacity (3/3: retired fence, live-leased cleared row, abandoned cleared row): the insert recovers, only the abandoned row is shed, both protected rows survive, and a fresh store handle on the same database still shows fence + lease + the new binding afterwards. Verbatim output is in the review reply below.
- `doctor-contract-api.overflow.test.ts`: at capacity the sidecar source is retained, nothing is imported, and the pre-existing row is intact (limit error injected through the production registration path); a revisited legacy sidecar cannot resurrect its cleared thread because the canonical cleared marker wins and the source archives without its row.
- Sibling Codex checkout inspection (`../codex`, origin/main 286d4ecf44): threads persist durably as rollout files plus the state db with paged listing and no retention eviction (`codex-rs/rollout/src/state_db.rs:352`, `codex-rs/rollout/src/maintenance.rs`), so shedding an abandoned OpenClaw binding row can never delete native Codex data.
- Before the final test-lint and format-only follow-ups, the full `extensions/codex` suite, `check-changed` lanes, and fresh `$autoreview` were clean with no actionable findings.
- At prior head `e721d349d2b6c9dca567e240c681829378c8fc45`, the registered-path test lint findings and the two overflow files' formatting were addressed without changing recovery behavior. PR CI at that head was green, including `check-test-types`. The xAI type failure seen at `f8d62fcb212d7adb73e5a51f89a3be618be7623f` was fixed upstream by #177830, and this PR does not change xAI.
- At current head `58efcd3c65f944499b2ff7454f05787e4ecadccc`, the final-delete negative control now starts revocation only after the unbound observation completes, limits rejection to caller-bound stores, and asserts exactly one `compareAndApply(delete)` attempt before rejection while preserving the disposable row. The strengthened assertion failed with zero attempts before the timing correction and passes with one after it. The low-value source-snippet inventory was removed; the registered production-path behavior test remains.
- Current head `acd84820f892ff2517adc6853e19cf6a9bb192e7`: `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` passed 16/16 and `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` passed 2/2 through `node scripts/test-projects.mts`; oxlint passed on the changed test file. `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passes after merging current `upstream/main`, and `test/scripts/pr-dependency-cache.test.ts` passes 41/41 locally, resolving the darwin workflow/source mismatch seen before that merge. Full extension-test typecheck passed with the already-landed #177830 xAI baseline fix temporarily overlaid and then restored. Without that overlay, the local branch reports only the known xAI baseline error, not an error in this PR's changed files.

Remaining evidence gaps: this head strengthens the final-delete negative control but does not supply a shipped Gateway fresh-session recovery trace with real session reset/reassignment lineage, a latest-stable upgrade run, or the maintainer's retention-policy decision. Those gates remain open and are not represented as complete here.

## What this PR is not

This is a partial fix with one open policy decision and no claim to close the underlying issue's storage architecture. Shedding strictly validated abandoned cleared rows is a durable-retention change, and it needs an explicit maintainer decision before merge; the review thread carries the full inventory. The store-level eviction primitive (storage-side disposal by policy rather than a domain-side sweep) remains the owner's call, as does any broader migration of the sync binding reads onto the async handle.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope the JSONL transcript usage estimate to the live window across boundaries
prs.body:
Refs #150579

## What Problem This Solves

A compacted session's transcript usage report (the JSONL artifact seam behind diagnostic reads) counted the whole append-only archive as live context. Content superseded by a compaction or reset stays in the file, and the chars-based estimate summed every user/assistant message ever written, so the reported total kept growing across clean compactions while the model's actual context stayed small.

A second gap sat next to it: once the estimate restarted at a boundary, eligibility was re-derived only from model-tagged assistant entries in the retained window. A summary-only window (the cut names an entry outside the message window) or a retained-user-only window (overflow compaction with a pending user message as its tail) lost the estimate until the next assistant reply, even though the summary and retained text were sitting in the model context.

## Root cause

`aggregateSessionTranscriptUsage` fills `totalTokens` from a chars estimate when no per-call usage snapshot provides one. `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` feeds it the full JSONL transcript, and the estimate accumulated `estimatedTranscriptChars` over the whole scanned set with no notion of boundary markers or the retained window they name. The boundary restart also reset `sawEstimateModelIdentity` from the retained entries alone, while `finish()` requires that flag, so any window without a surviving model-tagged assistant reported no estimate at all.

## Fix

- The JSONL reader passes `compaction`/`reset` boundary records through with their `summary`/`firstKeptEntryId` fields, and forwards each entry's id, instead of skipping markers.
- The accumulator keeps per-entry char counts for the current window. At a boundary it keeps the retained tail named by `firstKeptEntryId` plus the compaction summary, matching the model-context contract (compactionSummary + retained entries + post-boundary messages) and the transcript tree selector's fallback (an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window). The previous revision restarted the estimate at zero, which undercounts a compacted session that retains a large summary or window.
- A boundary leaves the window estimate-eligible whenever it holds counted text. A compaction or reset marker is only written by a live model session, so requiring a model-tagged assistant to survive the cut only masked reads taken between the boundary and the next reply.
- Usage snapshots (input/output/cache/cost) still aggregate over the whole record, and a fresh per-call `totalTokens` snapshot still wins over any estimate, unchanged.

## Scope

This change lives entirely in the JSONL artifact seam: `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` reads bounded transcript artifacts and its callers are diagnostic paths. The live budget-preflight path from #150579 reads the SQLite seam, which already scopes to the active context and is untouched here; that preflight symptom stays with #150579 and the PRs addressing it directly. This branch does not close the issue.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `session-usage-estimate.test.ts`: a compaction keeps its 500-char summary plus the 2000-char retained message named by `firstKeptEntryId` while dropping the 4000-char superseded prefix; a reset keeps its named retained tail; an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window but still counts the summary. Three further regressions end the transcript right at the boundary (summary-only window, compaction retaining only user messages, reset retaining only user text), covering the read between the boundary and the next assistant reply; earlier versions of these tests appended that reply, which masked the eligibility drop.
- Red/green: the boundary-terminal three fail on the previous head (no estimate reported). The consolidated table preserves all 10 independent scenarios, including snapshot precedence, reset boundaries, retained-user-only windows and the structural anchor.
- Runtime proof on a real compacted session (regenerated after the earlier /tmp artifact expired): isolated Gateway plus embedded agent against the scripted provider; a real injected 400 `context_length_exceeded`, one committed auto-compaction, then one more turn. The committed marker carries a 464-char summary and names a retained 91-char user message as `firstKeptEntryId`, so the boundary leaves a summary-plus-retained-user window. The artifact is the session's real settled transcript events serialized back to legacy JSONL, with redacted variants that drop usage fields and the model-snapshot entry so the chars estimate is what gets measured. The after-fix reader reports `totalTokens: 139` on the redacted prefix ending at the boundary (ceil((464 + 91) / 4), the summary plus the retained user text) and `176` on the full redacted artifact (ceil((464 + 91 + 56 + 90) / 4), adding the post-boundary assistant and user text). On the usage-carrying artifact the reader still reports the real provider aggregates (input 105 / output 25, latest context snapshot 120 total and available), so the estimate path and the snapshot path stay separate.
- Current head `dcfc49a70dfb`, including upstream main `3f2e7078de23`: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/session-usage-estimate.test.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-derived-readers.usage.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.transcript-usage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 4 files and 50 tests. oxfmt and direct type-aware oxlint pass on the consolidated test; the net PR diff passes `git diff --check`.
- Shipped diagnostic builder proof on `591ef68b2e9`: the real settled Gateway compaction events drive the production `buildReplyDiagnosticsPayload` raw diagnostic path through `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptAsync`, not just a direct reader call. With usage fields removed, the boundary-terminal artifact emits `total=139` and the full artifact emits `total=176`. The measured control emits `input=105`, `output=25`, `cacheRead=0`, `cacheWrite=0`, `total=120`. The probe prints only the session usage block, with no transcript text, credentials or endpoints. This builder-level evidence does not satisfy Revision 17's separate shipped CLI/Gateway diagnostic request gate; that proof requirement remains open.
- Test budget: the four repeated retained-window fixtures now share one table helper, preserving all 10 scenarios while reducing the new test file from 157 to 145 lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/session-usage-active-window.txt` grants exactly those 145 added lines. The full-index ratchet on current head `dcfc49a70dfb`, using hosted CI's current main `3f2e7078de23` with `--no-merge-base`, reports `Test lines OK: 6561328; ceiling: 6561328; slack: 0.` An earlier sparse local run omitted 566 tracked test lines and produced a false slack result; materializing those files reproduced hosted CI's over-10 failure before this consolidation.

prs.title: feat(browser): let users take over the agent's browser from the Browser panel
prs.body:
Closes #197902

## What Problem This Solves

When you step into the Browser panel to solve a CAPTCHA, finish a login or fix a form, the agent can click, type or navigate over you in the same browser, and it doesn't know you are there. The only way to stop it is to stop the whole run.

## User Impact

- Nothing changes for anyone who doesn't click the new button. Agents keep using the browser exactly as before.
- When you click or type in the Browser panel, the agent's browser results over the next minute say you just used the browser, so it can check the page before acting.
- **Take control** in the Browser panel toolbar pauses browser actions from everyone else (the agent's `browser` tool, the `openclaw browser` CLI, other Control UI windows) on that browser. The agent gets a normal tool result saying you have taken over, and its turn continues. Snapshots and screenshots still work, and an action that had already started may finish.
- Control ends when you click **Release control**, when the Control UI window closes or loses its connection, or after 5 minutes without input from you. The panel then says control was released.
- Browsers on the Gateway host only. The button is hidden for node-routed browsers.
- No new config option.

## Why This Change Was Made

The check sits in the browser plugin's shared route boundary that every browser caller goes through (agent tool, CLI, `browser.request`), so the lock holds on the real action path rather than in status or extension state. It mirrors desktop computer control (`hasController` in the desktop session registry), including the wording "Browser input paused while the operator has control".

- **Who holds control:** the Control UI connection that took it. Its Gateway connection id already reaches the routes through `browser.request`. The agent's in-process calls and the CLI carry no connection id, so they are refused.
- **What it locks:** control belongs to the browser, not the profile name. Several profiles that reach the same browser through the same `cdpUrl` share one lock. Existing-session profiles without a `cdpUrl` key on their Chrome user data dir. Duplicate `cdpUrl` configs stay allowed.
- **What the agent sees:** the browser tool turns the route's refusal into a normal result (`status: "user_has_control"`) for tab actions and `start`/`stop`, so the turn is not treated as a failed tool call.
- **Where it's offered:** default routing can send the panel's requests to a browser node, which has no takeover. The take-control status reports whether the request reached the browser with a Control UI connection (`available`), and the panel asks for it on each route, both when it loads tabs and when it follows an agent's tab. It offers **Take control** only when the answer is yes.
- **What counts as use:** the Browser panel marks its deliberate input (clicks, keys, text, scroll, back/forward, navigation, new tabs). Only marked input feeds the agent's note and keeps a takeover from going idle; the panel's automatic requests, such as page-metrics reads and viewport fits, do not.
- **Batched panel input:** the panel now sends clicks, keys and typing in batches through `/operator/input`; that request carries the same user-input mark.
- **What stays the same:** without a takeover, requests pass through untouched. The activity note is added only to host-local browser results.
- **State:** control is in memory. It ends with the browser runtime and does not survive a Gateway restart.

Relation to #143015 (mobile browser handoff): that PR reserves a profile for a handoff link. This covers the same-machine case with the user's own Control UI connection as the controller, and does not touch the handoff reservation; the handoff could reuse this check. #44615 proposed a lock kept in Chrome extension and status state.

Accepted edge cases, named instead of handled:
- One browser address spelled two ways (`localhost` and `127.0.0.1`) gives two locks.
- Session-scoped dashboard actions return the plain refusal message, not the friendly result.

## Evidence

Live run: an isolated Gateway with the managed browser (headless), the real Control UI and the real `browser` tool, with a local stand-in model that issues the tool calls.

Before, on `main`: the toolbar has no Take control button. The user clicked once in the panel, and the agent's click went through right after, with nothing telling the agent the user was there:

![Main: no Take control button; the agent's click lands while the user is in the panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ee34b743e036d49f3ab7f9a749910e22bb42e687/images/2026/11/03e31078-26a9-4889-a488-cd4b06c5fdfe.png)

With this change, the user clicked once in the panel. The agent's next click result carries the note:

![Agent's browser result notes that the user used the browser 5 seconds ago](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/08284199534c706d53eeaeadd98a4a6925b5cf34/images/2026/11/dbeedc63-d215-4ec5-9b91-d62e97c3f9e9.png)

After **Take control**, the agent's click is not run. Its tool result says the user has taken over, the tool call isn't marked failed, and the page is unchanged:

![Agent told the user has taken over the browser; page unchanged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/08284199534c706d53eeaeadd98a4a6925b5cf34/images/2026/11/deb49a68-188a-4dfd-b228-eb25467449f7.png)

With no input for 5 minutes, control was released (after 297 s). The panel shows the notice and **Take control** again:

![Panel notice that control was released after 5 minutes without input](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/08284199534c706d53eeaeadd98a4a6925b5cf34/images/2026/11/692cd463-701f-4670-96f4-ef5d12169f59.png)

The agent's next click works ("Clicked 3 times"):

![Agent's click succeeds after the idle release](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/08284199534c706d53eeaeadd98a4a6925b5cf34/images/2026/11/2db5115d-a40f-4e77-bba3-f22d688e623a.png)

Tests through the real route dispatcher (`routes/operator-control.test.ts`) and the browser tool (`browser-tool.operator-control.test.ts`):
- Others' input is refused while control is held: act, navigate, open tab, stop. The holder's own input is admitted, and disconnecting releases control.
- Control is released after 5 minutes idle. Marked panel input restarts the window; automatic page-metrics reads and viewport fits don't.
- The panel keeps checking control across navigation and shows when the Gateway released it.
- Take control is offered only when the Gateway confirms it: yes on a host browser and no on a node, both with default routing and after following an agent's tab.
- A second profile name pointing at the same browser is held too. A profile on a different browser is not.
- Only a Control UI connection can take control.
- The tool answers `act` and `stop` during a takeover with `user_has_control`.
- The alias, idle-release, control-check, takeover-availability and `stop` tests fail without their fixes.

Suites run: browser routes, browser Gateway handlers and browser tool: 456 + 52 passed; 59 skipped (existing opt-in Chromium suites). Browser panel UI tests: 286 passed. Typecheck is clean for the browser plugin, its tests and the UI; changed-files lint and the assertion-safety ratchet pass.

prs.title: fix(memory): CLI-backed sessions never flush memory before native compaction
prs.body:
Related: #137613

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sessions on a CLI backend (for example `claude-cli`) never save durable memory before Claude's native auto-compaction, because the pre-compaction memory flush is skipped for CLI runtimes.

## User Impact

User impact: CLI-backed agents now write their pre-compaction memory notes the same way embedded sessions do, re-arming every 256 KiB of transcript growth. Native compaction stays owned by the backend. Existing sessions need no migration; rows written before this change never suppress a flush.

## Why This Change Was Made

Branch rewritten on current `main` (the previous head was ~27k commits behind and conflicted with the memory-flush restructure).

- Reply and command turns reach the flush only through the preflight-compaction `beforeCompaction` hook, and preflight returned before calling it for CLI sessions. CLI sessions now run that hook before returning to native compaction (codex and other non-CLI native owners are unchanged).
- CLI compaction counts never advance, so the compaction-cycle dedup would lock after one flush. CLI sessions dedup on a transcript-byte window persisted as `memoryFlush.cliRearmBucket`; only a `succeeded` record suppresses.
- The flush dispatches through the CLI backend with a `read`/`write` allowlist, and the host-minted `memoryFlushWritePath` is carried through CLI dispatch → loopback grant → gateway tool resolution, so the writer stays append-only to the prepared target (a memory trigger without one still fails closed). Provider-owned tool plans keep the original skip.
- The private flush prompt stays out of the CLI dispatch transcript.
- Threshold and CLI byte-window rules live in `memory-flush-cycle.ts` so `agent-runner-memory.ts` does not grow past its line cap.

## Evidence

**Live run** (OpenClaw 2026.11.2 with the equivalent change applied to the packaged dist, `claude-cli` runtime, Claude Code 2.1.296, `forceFlushTranscriptBytes` temporarily set to 4096 for the run):

```
15:48:13 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user          # turn 1, transcript below threshold
15:48:19 dispatching embedded run through CLI backend: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5
15:48:19 ... unavailable here: memory-triggered compaction runs expose only read and append-only write.
15:48:19 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 trigger=memory      # turn 2: flush via CLI
15:48:22 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=true
15:48:25 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=true   # turn 3: no flush (same window)
session memoryFlush: {"kind":"succeeded","compactionCount":0,"cliRearmBucket":0}
```

Before the preflight-hook change, the same three turns produced no `trigger=memory` run. The flush model chose not to write for that filler transcript, so this run shows the bounded grant but not an actual append; the append-only writer is covered by the existing writer tests.

**Tests:** `agent-runner-memory.cli-flush.test.ts` (flush through CLI dispatch with the bounded grant; flush from the preflight hook without compacting — fails without the hook change; same-window suppression; re-arm on a new window; failed records do not suppress), `memory-flush-cycle.test.ts`, session-shape round trips for the bucket (including bucket-free older rows), CLI dispatch and grant-context forwarding. 48 related test files / 538 tests pass; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt and the line-cap ratchet pass.

**Limits / decision needed:** this still needs the maintainer call from the earlier review — recurring CLI memory maintenance at a fixed 256 KiB re-arm interval. Each re-arm costs one flush turn on the configured memory-flush model.
