prs.title: fix(codex): prevent native subagent continuation loss after sessions_yield
prs.body:
Related: #167410 (not a claim to close all reported timeouts).

## Current rebase validation — 2026-11-13

Head `3c0812c5f7367c18a89d6772aedcce5b98bd10dc`, reviewed against main `90c620b8e554becc8d0da785c16fea9935bd0681`. The five-commit rebase preserves upstream verified-local-home resolution and workspace-owned session metadata; pending-completion custody is rechecked after the metadata await. Earlier reviews below are historical and do not transfer to this conflict resolution.

- Fresh focused validation: **146 distinct tests across 11 files passed** (487.99 seconds), including native continuation, Gateway final-effect authority, catalog/workspace behavior and suite ownership. Duplicate tooling summaries counted once.
- Four type lanes, core/plugin targeted lint, formatting, line-cap and test-line budget checks passed on this head. All 12 preparation/validation lanes exited zero.
- Fresh local autoreview (Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2): **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings, exact base/head above. Code review is not execution proof.
- Main advanced during validation; no changed PR file overlaps the inspected advance to `77a0a8426513a024f2220c78085ddbd5731a059c`. Evidence remains bound to the reviewed base, not an untested latest-tip rebase. Hosted CI is separate and pending after publication.

### Separate stable 2026.11.3 qualification

Stable 11.3 still lacks all four retained backport fixes. Two are already on main; this PR retains only its remaining main delta. Custom source `529bac2e3a66d91ab0bf1be4cbfac1032ae6908f`, stable base `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`:

- 280 distinct tests in 16 files and source checks passed. Stable source review was reused under proven patch equivalence, not a fresh review.
- Canonical packaging passed, including archive integrity, inventory and import graph. Archive SHA-256: `4280b1a571ad9af43e4121d639d9daf178d603469420c44943411b798ceeef4b`.
- Isolated installation matched 9,522 core and 25 bundled Codex files. Native Codex 0.164.0 retained its prior digest.
- Network-disabled scripted-provider runtime: five distinct completed turns on one original child, three persisted yields, three once-only automatic consumptions; 102.59 seconds.
- Operator artifact/predecessor/Node checks and exact no-restart dry-run passed. No production installation or restart occurred. Dry-run does not prove retained-state admission.

No fresh stock 11.3 runtime comparison, real-model OAuth acceptance, live plugin-selection or browser/reload acceptance is claimed. Stable package proof is not certification of this upstream PR build. Historical false-delivery warnings and active-work blockage remain separate, unverified cases.

## What Problem This Solves

Preserve a managed native parent's saved tool declarations while its last terminal child's completion is still awaiting delivery. This fixes a distinct gap after execution protection correctly ends: rebuilding the catalog for the completion turn could rotate the parent thread and make a follow-up to its original child fail lineage validation.

The PR also retains the original delayed-completion authority regression. Current main already owns that async-lifetime behavior; no stable-only lifetime patch is added to main.

## Try it on stock 2026.11.1: native Codex continuation

**Use a fresh OpenClaw conversation backed by the native Codex plugin**, with native `spawn_agent`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, and OpenClaw `sessions_yield` available. An embedded model, Claude CLI, standalone Codex CLI, or `sessions_spawn` child does not exercise this same path. Use an isolated test installation, not an in-place downgrade of your working instance:

```sh
npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.1
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/codex@2026.11.1
openclaw plugins inspect codex --runtime --json
```

Complete normal Codex authentication/configuration and start that test Gateway. Confirm the **running** Gateway is stock 2026.11.1 and the official Codex plugin is loaded; merely installing the package does not replace an already-running Gateway. The controlled stock result below used native Codex 0.164.0. Record the actual build/plugin/native versions when reporting a result.

### Copy/paste prompt — first four turns

```text
Run a native Codex child-continuation reproduction. Use exactly ONE native
child throughout, created with native spawn_agent (not sessions_spawn).
Use native followup_task to start later turns on that SAME child. If the
required native tools or OpenClaw sessions_yield are unavailable, stop and
report that this setup cannot exercise the test; do not substitute tools.

1. Spawn a child named continuation_repro with fork_turns="none". Ask it to
   return exactly NORMAL_ONE. Wait with native wait_agent, and consume its
   actual completion once. Record the returned child identity.
2. Send that same child a followup_task asking it to return exactly
   NORMAL_TWO. Wait with native wait_agent, and consume the actual result.
3. Send the SAME child a followup_task asking it to wait 30 seconds using
   its shell or sleep tool, then return exactly AUTO_THREE. Immediately
   call OpenClaw sessions_yield to end this parent turn while awaiting that
   completion. Do not wait_agent, poll, sleep in the parent, schedule a
   reminder, or ask the user to wake you. Continue only when the child's
   completion automatically resumes you.
4. On automatic receipt of the actual AUTO_THREE completion, consume it
   once and immediately send the SAME original child a followup_task:
   wait 30 seconds, then return exactly AUTO_FOUR. Again immediately call
   sessions_yield, with no polling or manual wakeup. On its automatic
   completion, consume AUTO_FOUR once and report the results so far.

Do not create a replacement child, retry through another session, or read
transcript files to obtain a missing result. Do not treat the marker text
in this prompt as a received result. If a completion has no current child
identity/result, or followup_task rejects the original child, report the
actual error instead of repairing the test.

Report: original child identity, actual completed turns, confirmed yield
acknowledgements where observable, automatic resumptions, and consumed
results. Mark anything unobserved as unknown, not passed. Duplicate notices
must not cause duplicate followups or consumption. Stop after AUTO_FOUR;
wait for my separate fifth-turn prompt.
```

**Do not send a ping while waiting.** A delayed result must resume the parent without user input. A parent that merely says it will wait has not demonstrated a successful yield. If the child finishes before the yield and it returns `nothing_pending`, that run did not exercise the required boundary; repeat in a fresh conversation with a longer child delay. An acknowledgement replaced by `aborted by user` is not a successful native yield acknowledgement.

### Only after AUTO_FOUR arrived automatically: fresh user follow-up

```text
Continue the same reproduction with the SAME original native child. Send
it a followup_task asking it to wait 30 seconds and return exactly
AUTO_FIVE. Immediately call sessions_yield. Do not poll, wait_agent, create
a replacement child, or ask me to ping. On the automatic completion,
consume the actual AUTO_FIVE result once and report the final totals:
five completed turns on one child, three confirmed yields, three automatic
delayed-result resumptions, and each result consumed once. Report missing
or unobservable evidence honestly rather than inferring success.
```

### Expected result versus observed stock failure

Expected: one original child remains usable through all five turns; turns 3–5 each have a persisted native `yielded` output and automatic once-only consumption, with no user input between a yield and its completion. The second prompt is sent **after** turn 4 succeeds, not to rescue it.

**Observed on official stock 2026.11.1 on 2026-11-06:** the same child reached three turns, but the first native yield output became `aborted by user after 0.1s`. Automatic completion started a different native parent and omitted the current child identity/result. No delayed result was consumed; turns 4 and 5 were never reached. The failing assertion was `Current event must identify original child`. This is more specific than “the parent did not wake up”: a wakeup occurred, but continuation context/ownership was lost.

For a manual failure report, preserve the child's completed result, the yield/tool outcome, the automatic wake event (if any), and any original-child follow-up error. If nothing arrives after several minutes, preserve the trace before sending another message; a stall alone does not establish which boundary failed. Native parent-ID retention and persisted yield outputs require runtime/native-history evidence, not just the model's summary.

**Evidence boundary:** the stock result above was reproduced with installed official Gateway/plugin/native binaries and a deterministic local scripted Responses provider, not by running these exact natural-language prompts against a live model. The prompts express the same sequence, but model adherence and timing can vary; one passing manual attempt does not rule out the race. Stock archive SHA-256: `611282534d576e12f10b0ac5a1ac0d2825aac360637e92815a56eb71fb5a0301`; release commit: `4ffdd2047d192dd65554de3c8c46c0e0197c6e2a`. This demonstrates the remaining stable-release failure, not independent causality for every stable backport patch or qualification of the current upstream PR head.

## Reproduction and scope

A packaged Gateway + packaged native Codex test on the prior PR head completed two ordinary turns on one child, then genuinely yielded while the third result was pending. Automatic delivery resumed with a changed tool catalog, started a second native parent, and the original-child follow-up failed lineage checks. The provider was deterministic local scripted Responses, not a real model or OAuth acceptance test.

The new regression exercises the real harness lifecycle with a nonempty native tool catalog, holds terminal-child delivery after the execution pin releases, and admits the completion with no current executors. With only the catalog owner restored to the prior implementation, it fails with two native thread starts instead of one. With the repair, it preserves the original parent and rejects execution of the old tool.

## Follow-up: preserve terminal yield acknowledgements

A fresh live run on the separate stable candidate completed five original-child turns and automatically resumed all three delayed results, but two yield acknowledgements became `aborted by user`. It was not counted as a full acceptance pass.

The native dynamic-tool `item/completed` event precedes the handler's return. Interrupting at that point can replace the model-visible result with cancellation, even after OpenClaw has recorded terminal release. Waiting a JavaScript event-loop tick does not establish native output commitment.

The lifecycle owner now waits for matching `rawResponseItem/completed` function/custom output receipts in its existing model-response inventory. These prove recording in native model history before interruption. Nested Code Mode waits for the outer output; web/image calls are not incorrectly required to emit function outputs. No new protocol, timer, persisted state, or authority relaxation is introduced.

## Ownership and safety

- Read pending-delivery custody from the existing completion owner; no new custody registry or persistent state.
- Require the same physical native client, current assignment/history ownership, and the existing claimed delivery owner.
- Recheck catalog eligibility after reading native metadata.
- Keep execution pins released at terminal completion; never restore old executors.
- Release declaration eligibility when delivery settles, is abandoned, or loses custody.
- Share the existing child-execution predicate between its two monitor consumers; the oversized monitor file shrinks.

## Historical evidence — main refresh, 2026-11-01

Source: `9b99b76361370209209833996856e7080a5eb5c6`, rebased onto pinned main `72a691e5f732b04a53ffd9e83f96a61bc16d2016`. All four original commits remain patch-identical (`git range-diff` reports `=`); a fifth bookkeeping commit adds the exact 570-line regression allocation required by current main policy. No continuation behavior or assertion changed.

- Initial refreshed head `a5ac73f00f1c8c0769caf6e7a8f02d8faf1c98e9` on `5342923d897ad8a8021bdf586753f8cd38cd3094`: 218 successful test executions across 12 files in 437.79 seconds wrapper wall, including Gateway final-effect authority, catalog custody, original-child follow-up, lifecycle/steering, real native output-before-interrupt, and test-plan ownership. The 55 configuration cases execute on both test runtimes.
- Final head: 13 cases across four files passed in 140.65 seconds wrapper wall, covering the intervening upstream MCP data-directory change, pending-completion catalog preservation, direct/nested recorded-output ordering and real native output-before-interrupt.
- Final-head production plugin types and scoped extension test types passed (23.11 s / 13.14 s). Targeted type-aware lint with pinned runtime parity passed (74.01 s); formatting (0.43 s), pinned-base line-cap (1.10 s), and test-line allocation/budget (3.51 s) passed.
- The first lint invocation passed into the parity step but could not stage pinned Bun in the offline environment. Canonical online dependency staging resolved that prerequisite; the complete lint wrapper then passed offline. No gate, source assertion or timeout was weakened.
- Independent native source review of the full final range found no P0–P2 findings and independently verified the 570-line allocation. This is a source review, not CLI autoreview or live acceptance. The reviewed previous-series evidence remains historical; the exact final base/head are pinned above.

Hosted CI for this exact head has settled: 132 check runs (67 successful, 62 skipped, 1 neutral, 2 cancelled), with zero failed or pending checks. The aggregate CI gate and dependency/security-sensitive review statuses are successful. Earlier CI and live stable-backport evidence below belongs only to its named sources/artifacts; the separately qualified 2026.10.9 package is described next. No deployment, restart or merge was performed.

## Stable 2026.10.9 backport qualification — 2026-11-01

This is a separate release-based custom artifact, not a package of the upstream PR head or certification of stock 2026.10.9.

- Base `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`; custom source `eac766eb5d61e8a5b670d1dca9b3b2234bf11c99`. Four existing custom patches remain patch-identical; upstream filesystem-policy changes are preserved. Independent source review found no P0–P2 findings.
- Build `2026.10.9-custom-continuation-eac766eb5d6-20261101`; archive SHA-256 `ea691831432719785870299aabd3a1be7d12a9c43c5dc905123f69eb3a2f64cd`.
- 722 successful test executions across 28 distinct files (736.8 seconds wrapper wall), scoped core/plugin production and test types, separate type-aware lint, and formatting passed. Controlled removal of the native-output barrier reproduced both expected premature-interruption failures; the candidate was restored and its source is clean.
- Canonical build/inventory/tarball/import-graph checks passed (566.8 seconds). Fresh exact-archive installation passed (45.77 seconds), followed by offline Doctor and bundled Codex selection checks. Installed identity matched 8,911 core files, 22 Codex files and native Codex 0.160.0.
- Exact installed package, Docker networking disabled, synthetic state and scripted local Responses provider: five distinct completed turns on one original child, three persisted yielded acknowledgements and three automatic once-only result consumptions passed (61.98 seconds). No replacement child, manual completion wakeup or polling drove continuation.

Five stable line-cap failures remain explicitly recorded as unchanged backport exceptions: +13, +1, +45, +13 and +3 counted lines. No live state was mounted and no deployment, restart or release was performed. All qualification workers finished and their task-owned containers were removed through their own automatic teardown.

## Historical evidence — CI repair rebase, 2026-10-29

Source: `22540643f20c845ff5fea04408b89549d8448bbb`, rebased onto pinned main `02e19a39282d6af1cc93e01d7045681d0124b433`. All four PR commits are patch-identical to the previous series (`git range-diff` reports `=` for each); no continuation behavior or test assertion was changed in this refresh.

The previously failing [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40962090873/job/123758008168) and the [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40965138477) both succeeded. The live 10.7/10.8 backport acceptances and stock-versus-patched Docker comparison below remain evidence for their named artifacts, not a new package or live-model acceptance of this rebased upstream head.

## Historical source validation — 2026-10-28 upstream head

Source: `9c948da8a43477fb375ba8c7e5c08b14ef4b8ec2`, rebased onto pinned main `a919e5ecc4f6c579e16ab21499ccda3acaa1fb07` on 2026-10-28.

- At source-equivalent predecessor `d2b9766017ba75a56c419f8a316214201a145bdc`, 108 targeted cases across ten files passed in 215.03 seconds wrapper wall time, including delayed-completion authority, pending catalog custody, same-child follow-up, lifecycle/steering/output receipt tests and the real native-process yield test.
- Production plugin types, scoped extension-test types, targeted type-aware lint (including pinned Bun parity), formatting, pinned-base line-cap and test-line budget checks passed.

The original production/test patch is unchanged; the old test-budget-only increase was removed because upstream now owns a larger shared ceiling. - The real native case uses pinned Codex 0.164.0 and synthetic inference. Historical controlled-failure evidence below still documents the patch mechanism; neither a new full packaged upstream acceptance nor hosted CI success is claimed for this rebased head.
- The initial lint attempt on the preceding base could not stage the pinned Bun parity runtime in an offline container. Canonical staging resolved the tooling prerequisite; no lint gate or parity check was bypassed.

### Full-suite registration correction and hosted CI

That pre-rebase head added only the missing `run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.output-receipt.test.ts` entry to the database-worker test plan. Hosted CI on the predecessor caught that direct test selection was insufficient to prove full-suite discovery. The exact final head passed 54 configuration cases on both test runtimes plus four receipt cases (112 executions, 215.31 seconds wrapper wall), and scoped lint/format. [Failing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40791343185/job/123177622310). No gate or baseline was weakened.

## Historical source validation — pre-rebase head

Source: `7ac126cd15dc6f67d14944b4b4a97c1b8697313e`, based on pinned main `58bf6decb46a946365900bb6d2f93b96e9b52f69`.

- Controlled original-controller comparison: both new direct/nested receipt regressions fail on premature native interruption; candidate bytes restored afterward.
- 57 lifecycle/steering/receipt/native cases passed across four files (67.60 seconds total wrapper wall time). Existing fixtures now explicitly model recorded output; no assertions were weakened. Two native-sibling cases moved out of the oversized suite.

`f8699fea349def102ef4377b5009a556819583ac` passed 52 targeted tests plus packaged continuation in a fresh isolated installation: one parent, one original child, five persisted child turns, three genuine yields and three once-only automatic consumptions (96.19 seconds). It is historical after the acknowledgement repair, not a rebuilt-package or real-model/OAuth acceptance claim. ## Evidence — live 2026.10.7 backport acceptance

On 2026-10-28, a fresh uninterrupted live native acceptance run passed against installed custom build `2026.10.7-custom-continuation-e7de3d6695e-20261028`, backport commit `e7de3d6695e0b4881b109291c666e60121989580`. The running Gateway reported `2026.10.7` and pointed to that installed package.

These live results apply to the **stable custom backport**, not the upstream PR head. [Live acceptance report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184848#issuecomment-6480604481).

## Evidence — live 2026.10.8 backport acceptance

On 2026-10-29, fresh live native acceptance passed on the installed custom 2026.10.8 backport. The reachable running Gateway reported `2026.10.8`; session status identified build `55e31f3`, matching the qualified custom source `55e31f3e44f82154a6ffdabe58e725bec094a09c` (`2026.10.8-custom-continuation-55e31f3e44f-20261028`). | Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Turns completed with the same native child | 5/5 |

No polling during delayed checks, manual wakeups, replacement children, or user interruptions. No `nothing_pending` or interrupted yield acknowledgements were counted. Mirrored completion notices surfaced for turns 3–5 and were ignored after the first consumption, as in the 10.7 acceptance: once-only consumption is demonstrated, not transport-level exactly-once delivery.

This is additional **stable custom backport** evidence, not certification of the upstream PR head, unmodified 2026.10.8, or a new stock-versus-patched controlled comparison. No installation, restart, configuration change, or merge was performed for this acceptance. At that live acceptance, the upstream source head was `9c948da8a43477fb375ba8c7e5c08b14ef4b8ec2`; later rebases are separately qualified.

## Evidence — stock versus patched 2026.10.8 Docker control

On 2026-10-29, **stock failed and the custom stable backport passed the same continuation-focused probe**. These were real installed Gateway and native Codex processes with scripted local Responses inference, not live-model/OAuth acceptance or a rebuilt upstream-head test.

### Pinned inputs

- Stock: npm `openclaw@2026.10.8`, release commit `dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`; archive SHA-256 `7e36685a0b5fd9c8c3afcfa93ee33fad871f7c6c8b6e695cae6720d14a765f18`, also checked against registry SHA-512 integrity. Matching official `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.8` installed via the supported plugin CLI, with trusted-official registry ownership verified.
- Patched: custom stable source `55e31f3e44f82154a6ffdabe58e725bec094a09c`; archive SHA-256 `192509e3911ae9bba6437dc1f1f7dbac96525d612fc3f3ade82ceefef6b10f55`, using its bundled Codex plugin.
- Both: Node 24.22.1 and native Codex 0.160.0, identical native binary SHA-256 `12eb3e81114588aca3b7998f4f19e8997b056aca08e57a7ca7c8a3ec8c652aad`.
- Separate synthetic state; dependency staging online, execution with Docker networking disabled. No production credentials/state or Docker socket mounted. Installed packages owned Gateway/plugin execution; a read-only source client supplied only Gateway RPC transport.

| Check | Stock 2026.10.8 | Custom 2026.10.8 |
|---|---|---|
| Original-child completed turns | 3; stopped at first delayed continuation | 5/5 |
| Persisted confirmed yield outputs | 1 | 3/3 |
| Automatic completion wakeup | Observed after turn 3 | All 3 |
| Native parent identity retained | No | Yes |
| Current delayed-result payload supplied | No | Yes |
| Delayed results consumed once | 0 | 3/3 |
| Runtime phase, including setup/cleanup | 89.68 s; exit 1 | 54.31 s; exit 0 |

### Observed failure boundary

The stock child persisted three completed turns. Its original parent persisted `status: yielded` before the delayed third result was released. Automatic completion then arrived under a **different native parent ID**, carrying the inter-session wakeup placeholder without the current child-result payload. Both provider-visible instructions and input were inspected: the result marker occurred only in quoted earlier task/history text, not as the delivered completion. The current original-child event assertion failed before a fourth child turn could be requested. This was not merely failure to wake the parent or a timeout.

The patched control retained one parent and one original child, five distinct persisted completed child turns, three persisted `yielded` outputs, and three once-only delayed-result consumptions. No polling or manual wakeups drove delayed completion. A separate ordinary user turn requested the fifth child action only after the fourth result was consumed.

The old custom-package probe assumed bundled Codex; stock requires the official plugin installation above. Its first setup verification failure is excluded from behavior evidence. A separate strict assertion about inbound context residing in top-level provider instructions also failed before child execution: stock carries that context in input messages. That request-layout difference is **not counted as a continuation failure or missing-context proof**. A separately identified continuation-focused variant records the layout fact without blocking child execution; all payload, identity, yield and consumption assertions remain intact. Identical variant bytes were used for both compared packages, without modifying runtime implementations.

This comparison supports the continuing need for the **combined stable backport** in this scenario, not the independent necessity of every patch or certification of this PR's current upstream head. Registry-versus-bundled plugin packaging differs; this is not a single-change causal experiment. The narrower controlled regressions above remain the evidence for individual repair mechanisms. All eight task-created containers were removed by recorded creation IDs; production Gateway identity and availability were unchanged.

## Limits and operational impact

No live installation, restart, configuration change or merge is part of this PR-body update or the live acceptance run. The stable 2026.10.7 and 2026.10.8 backports remain separate from the upstream PR; both installed custom packages passed the respective live acceptance above. That does not certify a rebuilt package of the upstream PR head. The observed duplicate native notifications and intermediate visible-reply warnings are not claimed fixed by this acknowledgement patch. No claim of production restart recovery, provider/OAuth recovery, or all-plugin test-type coverage.

## Test-line budget

The shared scalar is unchanged. The refresh adds `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-native-continuation.txt` for exactly 570 net counted test lines, as required by current main policy. prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

Continuing a Claude CLI session that lives on a paired headless node fails on the first Web turn. The node is connected and advertises `claude-cli-skills-v1` and `agent.cli.claude.run.v1`, but the turn ends with "Your request couldn't be completed." and the Gateway logs:

```
Paired node needs claude-cli-skills-v1. Upgrade OpenClaw on the paired node, restart its node host, and retry this turn.
```

Cause: agent turns run in a detached request scope that carries the Gateway resolver but deliberately drops the direct request context. The two paired-node readers (`prepareNodeClaudeSkillRuntime` and `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun`) read only `getPluginRuntimeGatewayRequestScope()?.context`, so they see no Gateway and report the node as unusable before Claude starts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both readers now use the existing request-scope owner accessor `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext()`, which resolves through the live Gateway resolver (and falls back to the direct context when there is no resolver). A retired resolver still returns nothing, so the turn fails before any node lookup or dispatch. Command policy, expected connection, pairing generation, placement and skill-lifecycle checks are unchanged.

Maintainer follow-up on the contributor branch:
- merged current main (clean);
- reduced the change to the two reader substitutions. The earlier revision also re-checked resolver identity at dispatch; that guarded a theoretical retirement race already covered by the node connection and pairing-generation checks, so it and its two tests were removed;
- the existing invocation suite now runs on the detached resolver path instead of mocking the scope module, so every case exercises the real failure; the retired scope mock is pruned from `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`.

## User Impact

Adopted Claude CLI sessions on a paired node continue from the Web composer: the turn runs on the node and the reply appears.

## Evidence

Real end-to-end on this host: an isolated Gateway and a separate real headless node host (`openclaw node run`, own HOME, state and profile, `nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled`), paired through the normal flow. A short native Claude CLI session was created on the node, listed with `sessions.catalog.list`, adopted with `sessions.catalog.continue`, then continued with `chat.send` using full operator scopes, as the Control UI does. Claude Haiku 5.5. The real Claude Code binary ran through a shared Anthropic-compatible proxy because the host subscription is at its weekly limit.

| Build | Node row | `chat.send` "Reply with exactly: continued" | Second turn |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `c19ae286a00c` | `canContinue: true` | "Your request couldn't be completed." — `Paired node needs claude-cli-skills-v1` | n/a |
| branch `2705a5fe9190` (head `9dc9b4ea2744` adds only the mock-baseline prune) | `canContinue: true` | `continued` (node ran `claude -p … --resume <thread>`) | `second` |

Tests:
- `src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` + `src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts`: 15 passed on the branch; 14 of 15 fail with the production files reverted to main.
- Format check on changed files: clean. All baseline ratchets pass locally (mock-exports, test-lines, max-lines and the rest).

Production delta vs main: 2 files, +4 −4 (two import and two reader lines). Tests: +24 −21.

prs.title: fix(web): self-hosted web tool endpoints can redirect requests to other hosts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a self-hosted web tool endpoint (for example a private search instance) can redirect a request to a different host, and the request follows it with private-network access still enabled.

## User Impact

User impact: requests to a self-hosted web tool endpoint now stay on the hostname that was configured, on every redirect hop. Configured private endpoints and same-host redirects keep working.

Required action for some deployments: if a self-hosted endpoint relies on redirecting to a different hostname, configure that destination hostname directly. Such redirects are now rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Self-hosted endpoints need private-network access, but the shared self-hosted policy granted it without restricting the destination hostname. The policy is now derived from the configured endpoint URL using the existing URL hostname allowlist helper, together with the private-network grant. The allowlist is applied on each redirect hop, including environment-proxy dispatch. No new parser, guard or transport was added, and the helper's signature is unchanged for its consumers.

## Evidence

Run with Node 24.22.2 and pnpm 12.15.0. No live endpoint, provider or proxy was contacted; DNS and transport are mocked.

- The new regression (`src/agents/tools/web-guarded-fetch.redirects.test.ts`) calls `withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint` with the real redirect and network guards. On `main` it fails 2 of 5 cases: in both direct and proxy mode, a same-host hop followed by a hop to another host returns that host's response. On this branch all 5 pass, including private DNS, IPv4 and IPv6 endpoint controls.
- A second, separately written test set through the same helper: 41 failed / 13 passed on `main`, 54 passed on this branch. Off-host requests stop before the second transport call; private-service and same-host controls succeed.
- The affected consumer suites (guarded fetch, web search provider common, Brave, Firecrawl, web fetch tools): 100 tests passed.
- Full build, test typechecking, scoped lint, formatting and the test-line budget check passed. The regression adds 57 test lines with an equal dedicated allocation.

Gap: the broad `pnpm check` reports 22 line-cap errors outside this change, which reproduce with identical diagnostics on an untouched `main`. Live provider and proxy integration were not exercised.

### Real network dispatch (loopback)

The exported `withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint` helper was run from source with real DNS, real HTTP servers and the real transport. Nothing is mocked: no DNS or fetch replacement, no injected policy or dispatcher.

- Base: `b382a29a688a` (merge-base with `main`). Head: `a2c15cc68999`. Node 24.22.2.
- Server A is the configured endpoint at `localhost`. Server B is a different hostname, `127.0.0.1`, on another port. Both listen only on loopback inside a network namespace with no external interface.
- A serves `/control` (200), `/same-host` → `/same-host-result` (302 then 200), and the chain `/search` → `/next` → B `/result` (two 302s). B logs every TCP connection and request.
- Proxy mode points `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` at a local forward proxy that supports CONNECT and logs what it forwards.

| Scenario | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Direct, private control | 200 from A | 200 from A |
| Direct, same-host redirect | 200 from A | 200 from A |
| Direct, redirect to other host | **B receives `GET /result`; callback gets B's response** | rejected after A's second hop; B receives 0 requests and 0 TCP connections; callback not called |
| Proxy, private control | 200 from A | 200 from A |
| Proxy, same-host redirect | 200 from A | 200 from A |
| Proxy, redirect to other host | **proxy opens a CONNECT tunnel to B; B receives `GET /result`; callback gets B's response** | rejected after A's second hop; no CONNECT to B; B receives 0 requests and 0 TCP connections |

Head rejection message in both modes: `Domain policy: Blocked hostname (not in allowlist): 127.0.0.1. Permitted hostname patterns: localhost.`

Limits: loopback fixtures over plain HTTP, not a real search provider or TLS endpoint; this exercises the shared helper boundary, not a full agent turn. No latest-stable upgrade run was done.

prs.title: fix(discord): removed DM senders can still message and run commands through an existing session binding
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord direct-message sender who has been removed from the allowlist, or who is no longer paired, can still message the agent and run commands when an earlier session binding exists for that conversation.

## User Impact

User impact: removing a sender from the DM allowlist or pairing takes effect for bound conversations too. Rejected senders reach the normal denial or pairing path, and command authorization follows the current access decision. Admitted senders keep their existing binding and routing. No configuration or storage migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

DM preflight treated the existence of a routing binding as an alternative access decision, and also ORed the binding into command authorization. The binding lookup and both overrides are removed from preflight, so admission and command authorization come only from the current ingress result. The existing routing owner still restores bindings for admitted senders. Production code removes 25 lines and adds two.

## Evidence

Run with Node 24.22.2 and pnpm 12.15.0. No live Discord connection was used; ingress decisions and transport are mocked.

- The new regression (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.bound-dm.test.ts`) calls the production `preflightDiscordMessage` entry point with an in-memory binding adapter. On `main` 3 of 4 cases fail (allowlist rejection, pairing rejection, and command authorization for an admitted sender); on this branch all 4 pass.
- A second, separately written test set against the DM preflight access resolver: 11 failed / 14 passed on `main`, 25 passed on this branch.
- DM authorization, pairing-decision, message-preflight and routing-preflight suites: 77 passed.
- Full build and full test typecheck passed. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap, test-line and mock-export checks passed.

To run the regression:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.bound-dm.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'bound direct messages'
```

Gap: the broad `pnpm check` is not green locally. Extension lint reports line-limit errors in the Tlon and Crabbox tests that reproduce on an untouched `main` with identical counts, and the run was stopped while core lint was still pending, so its later formatting and policy stages did not complete.

### Running Gateway (loopback Discord provider)

The real Discord plugin and Gateway were started from each built checkout through the repository's QA-lab suite runner with the Crabline loopback Discord provider and the mock model provider. No product module is patched or replaced. This is a local provider stand-in, not the Discord service, and the senders are synthetic IDs, not human accounts.

- Base: `b382a29a688a`. Head: `1ff91cc0ded1`. Node 24.22.2, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build` with private QA enabled.
- Two synthetic DM senders, A and B, each with an existing session binding. Provider-native `MESSAGE_CREATE` DM events are injected through the provider's authenticated local ingress. Policy changes go through the Gateway's `config.patch` RPC with `replacePaths: ["channels.discord.allowFrom"]`. Bindings are left in place throughout and re-read after every step.
- Each step sends one message and one command per sender and records whether it reached agent execution, whether the agent's marker reply came back, and whether the command took effect.

| Phase | Sender | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Both on the allowlist | A | message and command executed | message and command executed |
| 1. Both on the allowlist | B | message and command executed | message and command executed |
| 2. A removed from `allowFrom`, binding retained | A | **message reached the agent and was answered; command executed** | denied: no agent execution, no reply, command not executed |
| 2. A removed from `allowFrom`, binding retained | B | message and command executed | message and command executed |
| 3. `dmPolicy: pairing`, A unpaired, binding retained | A | **message reached the agent and was answered; no pairing request was created** | not delivered to the agent; pairing request issued; command not executed |
| 3. `dmPolicy: pairing`, A unpaired, binding retained | B | not reached (run stopped at A's step) | message and command executed |

On head the scenario completed with all three phases passing. On base it recorded the violations above in phase 2 and stopped in phase 3 because the expected pairing request never appeared.

Limits: provider-native events from a loopback stand-in are not genuine human-to-bot DMs, and native slash interactions were not exercised; commands were sent as message text. No production Discord behaviour is claimed.

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep cached context and cron notices in their owning topics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes private Telegram conversations picking up another topic's cached context, and auto-disabled automations notifying the default conversation instead of their saved creator topic.

## User Impact

Root DMs and private topics keep their automatic context separate. Auto-disable safety notices stay with the saved job owner, while legacy routing and the owning-agent fallback for a deleted parent conversation continue to work.

No configuration or schema changes are required. This does **not** infer missing Telegram thread IDs, rewrite existing routes, or change explicit failure-alert destinations.

## Why This Change Was Made

An absent cache thread was treated as a wildcard, and reply-reference expansion could reinsert a foreign-topic node after window selection. Scope both reads and the final conversation selection to the requested thread, including the root conversation. Explicit current replies retain their separate reply-chain/body path.

Auto-disable notification snapshots dropped `job.owner`; queue selection used only the legacy `sessionKey`. Preserve the owner and prefer its agent/session for safety notices. When that parent has disappeared, clear both saved session routes before falling back to its agent. The failure-alert routing branch is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Live Telegram Test Server E2E (maintainer, 2026-11-13)

Real Gateway + deterministic mock model, leased QA user, Threaded Mode on, a fresh DM topic, `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["telegram:<qa user>"]` (needed to create automations from chat). The mock answers `PING:x` with `PONG:x`; `CRONMAKE:one` creates a one-shot isolated automation whose run fails (provider 400), so the job auto-disables and queues its safety notice; the mock answers that notice turn with `NOTICE_SEEN`. Each provider request is logged with its session key, and `TOPICSECRET_*` markers are only ever typed inside the topic.

Context isolation:

- `main` at `8ebe740925ca`: both root-DM turns (`agent:main:main`, `PING:root1`/`PING:root2`) carried `TOPICSECRET_ALPHA` from the topic in their provider request.
- This head `53d8e0a173ce`: the root-DM requests carry no `TOPICSECRET_*`; the topic requests still carry their own topic messages.

Auto-disable notice owner:

- `main` at `8ebe740925ca`: the automation was created in topic 200574, the notice turn ran in `agent:main:main`, and `NOTICE_SEEN` landed in the root DM.
- This head `53d8e0a173ce`: the notice turn ran in the topic session `agent:main:main:thread:<user>:200600`, and `NOTICE_SEEN` landed in topic 200600.

<details>
<summary>Captured Telegram events (TDLib recorder on the QA user)</summary>

`main` (auto-disable notice):

```text
    0.3s  user  message topic 200574 msg#082625  PING:warm
   16.9s  bot   message topic 200574 msg#179776  PONG:warm
   17.1s  user  message root DM      msg#179777  PING:root1
   19.9s  bot   message root DM      msg#276928  PONG:root1
   20.1s  user  message topic 200574 msg#276929  CRONMAKE:one
   22.0s  bot   message topic 200574 msg#374080  Working / 🧩 Automations
   22.9s  bot   message topic 200574 msg#422656  CRON_ADDED:one
   26.1s  bot   delete  topic 200574 msg#374080  
   43.3s  bot   message root DM      msg#471232  NOTICE_SEEN
  150.4s  user  message topic 200574 msg#471233  PING:after
  153.3s  bot   message topic 200574 msg#568384  PONG:after
```

This head (both checks in one run):

```text
    0.2s  user  message topic 200600 msg#345601  TOPICSECRET_ALPHA PING:warm
    7.3s  bot   message topic 200600 msg#442752  PONG:warm
    7.5s  user  message root DM      msg#442753  PING:root1
   10.3s  bot   message root DM      msg#539904  PONG:root1
   10.5s  user  message topic 200600 msg#539905  TOPICSECRET_BETA PING:topic2
   12.3s  bot   message topic 200600 msg#637056  PONG:topic2
   12.5s  user  message root DM      msg#637057  PING:root2
   14.3s  bot   message root DM      msg#734208  PONG:root2
   14.5s  user  message topic 200600 msg#734209  CRONMAKE:one
   16.3s  bot   message topic 200600 msg#831360  Working / 🧩 Automations
   17.3s  bot   message topic 200600 msg#879936  CRON_ADDED:one
   20.5s  bot   delete  topic 200600 msg#831360  
   37.1s  bot   message topic 200600 msg#928512  NOTICE_SEEN
```

</details>

### Contributor evidence (synthetic production-path proof)

**Synthetic production-path proof, not live Telegram proof.** Base: `f8719a02abcdca4aba466b55730abd9d1d512138`; patch: `82dce647a3b764825667f4ff8acfa11e685af890`.

### Before / after example

The Telegram fixture records two topics, an older local message replying to message `10` in topic `88`, and a local reply to message `17`. The current request (`22`) has **no reply**. History limit is two.

| Case | Base, before the runtime fix | With the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh root DM | Includes `other topic 10` / `other topic 11`, plus unrelated local neighbors around that foreign target | Only local messages `15, 16, 17, 20, 21` |
| Private topic `77` | Cached reply lookup reinserts `other topic 10` from topic `88` | Only local messages `15, 16, 17, 20, 21` |
| Auto-disabled job with `owner.sessionKey = agent:ops:telegram:direct:123:thread:123:456`, no legacy session key | Enqueues to `main`, with `sessionKey: undefined` | Enqueues to `ops` and the exact saved topic session |
| Parent conversation deleted | Modern-owner case falls back to `main` | Falls back to `ops`, without trying to recreate the deleted parent |

The two Telegram regressions failed on base source before the fix. They drive real grammY ingress, cache, session selection, prompt composition, and loopback Bot API transport; the reply resolver is a fixture. The cron regressions failed before the fix through real `CronService.run` and post-persist notification dispatch, not just resolver-unit tests. The legacy controls pass.

<details>
<summary>Replay the failing examples on the base with the tests-only delta</summary>

From a checkout containing the PR commit:

```sh
base=f8719a02abcdca4aba466b55730abd9d1d512138
head=82dce647a3b764825667f4ff8acfa11e685af890
git worktree add --detach ../openclaw-topic-base "$base"
git diff "$base" "$head" -- \
  extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.prompt-context.test.ts \
  src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts \
  | git -C ../openclaw-topic-base apply
cd ../openclaw-topic-base
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.prompt-context.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 -t 'keeps automatic DM context'
pnpm test src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 -t 'notifies the'
```

The first command must fail both root/topic cases; the second must fail the modern-owner case while the legacy case passes. Run the same tests on the PR checkout for the green comparison.

</details>

### Validation

- **155 tests passed across 12 files**: six cron owner/notification/failure-route suites (93 tests), five Telegram cache/prompt/runtime suites plus prompt-prefix stability (62 tests).
- Final typed-fixture replay: **15/15** in `bot-message-context.prompt-context.test.ts`.
- Typechecks passed: core, cron test shard, canonical extensions, canonical extension tests.
- Targeted core/Telegram lint, formatting, diff whitespace, test-line allocation, line-cap, max-lines, and assertion-safety checks passed.
- Local wrapper wall times: cron six-file run **57.63s**; Telegram/prefix six-file run **104.11s**; final single-file prompt replay **61.16s** including cold compiler work. The original head passed the CI gate ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42481675723)); follow-up-head CI is tracked separately below.
- Independent native read-only review covered the complete final snapshot: **no actionable findings**. The autoreview CLI/skill was unavailable; this is not an autoreview-CLI claim.
- Author simplification pass: existing owners only; no new runtime abstraction or state. Production delta **+23/-10**; regression delta **+172/-56**. The separate 116-line allocation covers the original ingress/owner/deleted-parent regressions plus 35 net lines for the auto-disable authority controls; the retained-history topic control is preserved.

### Review follow-up: real Gateway/model boundary proof

Follow-up commit `16bb80351` changes only authority tests and their line allocation. The production patch remains identical to `82dce647a3b764825667f4ff8acfa11e685af890`.

A fresh, isolated **source Gateway with a real API-backed agent/model** consumed synthetic Telegram updates through its real polling worker, durable spool/drain, grammY ingress, cache, session selection, prompt construction, and outbound Telegram adapter. The Bot API was a loopback HTTP fixture, **not Telegram Test Server**. The provider proxy forwarded the actual requests to the configured real model; it did not fabricate responses.

Before startup, 20 synthetic observed-message rows were written through the production SQLite plugin-state owner, including stale local replies to foreign-topic targets. No real session history or private data was used. Unlike the earlier ingress fixture, this run did not mock the reply resolver or agent execution. Each case below made one real provider request and received one matching `sendMessage` at the fixture boundary:

```text
ROOT_CHECK: own history present; FOREIGN_ absent from provider request
  sendMessage(thread=root):
  ROOT_CHECK LOCAL_ROOT_15 LOCAL_ROOT_16 LOCAL_ROOT_17 LOCAL_ROOT_20 LOCAL_ROOT_21
TOPIC_CHECK: own history present; FOREIGN_ absent from provider request
  sendMessage(message_thread_id=77):
  TOPIC_CHECK LOCAL_77_15 LOCAL_77_16 LOCAL_77_17 LOCAL_77_20 LOCAL_77_21
AUTO_DISABLED_NOTICE:
  authenticated Gateway RPC created a one-shot command job with modern owner.sessionKey
  real timer ran /bin/false -> command exited with code 1
  persisted: enabled=false, lastRunStatus=error, consecutiveErrors=1
  persisted: autoDisabled.reason=consecutive-failures; saved owner is topic 77
  real model request contained that exact job's auto-disable notice
  sendMessage(message_thread_id=77): The automation "Synthetic owner-topic auto-disable proof"
    was auto-disabled after one consecutive run failure. ...
cleanup: owned children remaining=0; both loopback fixture listeners closed
```

The persisted cron state was checked through the read-only store owner after Gateway shutdown. The command failure is an intentional scenario input, not a failed validation. The outbound response content and thread were observed at HTTP I/O; this is stronger than an enqueue spy but **not live Telegram acceptance**.

### Review follow-up: live requester authority

Extended `src/gateway/server-cron-failure-repair.final-effect.test.ts` in its existing shared fixture. It now covers both the original repair entry and the auto-disable Gateway enqueue adapter. The handoff observer calls through and awaits the genuine receipt; admission, tool gates, cron handlers, and persisted writes are real. The model in this authority suite remains synthetic; these results are **not** Telegram-delivery proof.

| Auto-disable requester control | Observed final effect |
| --- | --- |
| Current owner | Automation description update persisted |
| Known foreign/non-owner | Owner-only update gated; original description retained |
| Owner revoked while queued | Intended owner-revocation guard fired; executionStarted=false, delivered=false; no mutation |
| Owner revoked after admission | Retired host capability refused the write; original description retained |

**12/12 passed** across the repair, auto-disable, and operator-source matrices. Final wrapper wall time **54.71s** (Vitest **51.96s**). Targeted Gateway-server test typecheck, lint, formatting, whitespace, test-line and assertion-safety checks passed. Fresh independent read-only review of this follow-up delta found no actionable findings. No production permission checks were added or weakened.

Destination and authority remain distinct: the notification snapshot selects the recipient; the Gateway reads the **live job** by `jobId` and captures its recorded requester through `captureCronJobTurnTarget`. A known non-owner does not inherit the recipient session's owner tools. Harmless safety notices are not universally forbidden for non-owners by the existing contract; the negative control proves refusal of privileged effects, not an invented blanket ban on notices. Queued revocation is separately proven to refuse the turn before execution/delivery.

**Remaining external proof gap:** Telegram Test Server readiness was retried with the canonical doctor. It reported no authenticated Convex launcher and no broker credential pair; no install/login was attempted. Therefore live Test Server/userbot delivery and live-channel revocation I/O remain unverified. This update closes the real-Gateway/real-model and direct auto-disable authority-test gaps, not that missing external access boundary. The installed Gateway, production configuration, jobs, and histories were not modified.

**Follow-up-head CI:** the [CI workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42484104547) completed successfully for exact head `16bb803512c500c5097d9699a061f762e0d61d75`. Original-head CI is not represented as follow-up-head proof. Hosted re-review has been [requested once](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195214#issuecomment-6721975952); the prior verdict is not presented as a review of this follow-up.

<details>
<summary>Resolved validation setup failures</summary>

An initial cron fixture selected failure-repair rather than the auto-disable path; setting `failureAlert: false` exposed the intended routing failure before the patch. An initial Telegram batch caught the old wildcard expectation in the retained-cache suite and was also invalidated by concurrent source edits; the expectation now checks root and explicit-topic contracts, and the final frozen-source run passed. Early ad hoc typecheck scopes lacked generated SDK/ambient declarations; canonical typecheck lanes passed after correcting the test's nested reply type. None of these earlier attempts is counted as passing proof. The follow-up isolated-Gateway setup initially used a retired heartbeat key; removing that key fixed setup. An intermediate authority assertion tried to inspect an intentionally sanitized user-facing error; the final test instead captures the original admission exception and verifies the intended guard plus unchanged persisted state.

</details>

prs.title: fix(update): avoid duplicate database copies while the Gateway is stopped
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Schema-crossing updates keep the Gateway stopped while repeatedly copying large agent databases for read-only inspection.

## User Impact

Eligible stopped-writer inspections avoid redundant whole-database images while retaining the primary rollback payload and validation. The maintainer accepted the completed 14-arm performance result for landing: stopped migration/cleanup falls from **5.56 to 4.22 minutes**, CPU falls 12.82%, and outcomes match. The final head has green CI and a ClawSweeper review with zero open items.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing native updater maintenance lease and awaited worker handoff to checkpoint eligible WAL once, then capture source identities. Reuse the captured shared-state image and open drained, maintenance-owned sources immutably, including auth worker IPC. Preserve artifact-preserving scope, non-cacheable results and reader cleanup from #166857. A pinned reader/busy checkpoint, pending journal or unowned source retains the verified private-image path.

Activation-time capacity admission precedes checkpointing: successful preflight reserves no space. Full integrity/FK checks, hashes, durable publication, source-change fencing and recovery rules remain. No schema, product configuration, cache or online backup staging is added. Production LOC is net +76 versus the pinned main parent, primarily custody/IPC plumbing and the checkpoint/contention boundary.

## Evidence

Candidate `d342cc012364d2f29439bae60169fd76ca3d259e` versus main parent `84727572dd04bc769679e124b0bd5f26857ec640`, Node v26.12.1. Synthetic fixture: 30.08 GiB largest agent, 2.01 GiB shared state, seven agents, 10,003 sessions, 62,000 workspace files (~1.181 GB), and 128.9 MiB committed WAL including a real session-row update. The real native migration and cleanup run under maintenance custody, from schema 41 to 42. Preparation/outcome hashing are outside timing. Every arm cleans its source/staging files and compacts its private non-reflinking HFS+ image; native safety checks remain enabled. No operator data is used.

| Pair | Baseline stopped seconds | Candidate stopped seconds | Wall change | CPU change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 333.651 | 392.275 | +17.57% | +5.90% |
| 2 | 302.028 | 236.807 | -21.59% | -15.35% |
| 3 | 281.460 | 253.105 | -10.07% | -6.70% |
| 4 | 408.578 | 297.599 | -27.16% | -10.86% |
| 5 | 340.772 | 233.009 | -31.62% | -18.99% |

Four interleaved unchanged controls: 336.845, 405.163, 367.156 and 319.104 seconds. Median stopped migration/cleanup improves **333.651→253.105 seconds (-24.14%)**; total process-tree CPU improves **384.14→334.89 seconds (-12.82%)**. Wall p95 (nearest-rank) is 408.578→392.275 seconds. Parent sampled allocations are 6.046→6.065 GB (+0.31%, versus 0.75% A/A range); complete child allocation totals are unavailable.

The rule published before sampling requires median wall improvement ≥10% and greater than the A/A relative wall range, at least four improving pairs, CPU within the A/A relative CPU range, and identical outcomes. Four pairs improve, CPU passes and all canonical session/transcript hashes, committed WAL content, schema versions and migration receipts match. **The wall gate fails: 24.14% improvement is below 24.45% A/A variability.** The first negative pair is retained. The original threshold remains reported as failed. The maintainer explicitly accepted this 0.31-percentage-point miss as noise and directed landing based on the measured work reduction, matching outcomes and lower CPU; this is a maintainer decision, not a claim that the predeclared wall gate passed.

The backup owner median falls 117.788→62.675 seconds. File samples show three distinct full-agent readonly images on every baseline arm and one on every candidate. Both retain the primary recovery payload; the later reclamation inspection still uses a private image because Doctor has written new WAL. Five-second sampling is a lower bound. These timings exclude service-manager stop/start/readiness, use natural OS caches, and do not reproduce dense transcript scanning or Linux/btrfs latency. The prior 35 GiB and 30 GiB diagnostic series also failed their noise gates; they are not substituted for this result.

Focused proof includes 110 infra tests, 32 Doctor tests and 14 lint-suppression tests. The final capacity-order correction passes all 76 capture/engine/space tests on both Node and pinned Bun, `check:changed`, and independent Codex P0–P2 review. Its retained-WAL regression fails on 4e74381 because capture changes source sidecars before refusing space; after the fix, hashes and mtimes remain unchanged. The earlier auth regression failed on 463af25132b from changed SHM bytes and passes after immutable IPC handling.

[Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43466555599) hit the retained-copy test's 20-second publication deadline on Linux. It tested merge 8f31e918d onto main **68542b21d0d20ea368a1fb43d6b47aebf2e55d75**. The unchanged retained case passes on that exact parent on macOS (7.78 seconds), Linux ARM64 (10.45 seconds), and Linux x64 translated on ARM64 (20.73 seconds total). Both Linux full-file runs pass all five cases. Replaying CI's exact two compact groups with its runner, pinned Node 24.22.1/Bun, eight-CPU scheduling budget and two concurrent plans also passes the affected seven-file group: 53 passed, 11 skipped; retained case 22.37 seconds total. Translation and different hardware limit timing equivalence. An initial container lacking init failed orphan-PID assertions, so it was corrected and is not evidence of the publication failure.

The publication test is byte-identical since e68dfaf78a58 / #190918, which introduced its deadline and cold compiler settings. This identifies the deadline's owner, **not a proven introducing commit for the CI failure**. The actual parent's staging/copy implementations also match the candidate. The retained request has no maintenance custody and does not select the changed stopped-checkpoint or auth-row branches. A fresh independent Codex review of the complete final patch is P0–P2 scoped-clean and finds no new wait or import initialization barrier on that path. **The original timeout remains causally unattributed; passing replays are not a fix or an inherited-red waiver.** No timeout, assertion, or production change was made to chase green. [Ready-PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43485222161) now passes on the identical head and merge tree (56 successful jobs, 27 skipped, including the successful aggregate gate). Its [publication job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43485222161/job/132092816830) passes all five lifecycle cases; retained-copy total is 25.262 seconds, including retirement after publication. ClawSweeper Revision 6 reviews this exact head with **Before merge: None; Findings: None**, and explicitly retains the original timeout uncertainty. No inherited-red exception is used.

[Full manual validation on 3ef1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43442582104), before the final capacity-order correction, finished with 240 successful, 20 failed and 8 skipped jobs. The [published-driver job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43442582104/job/131956800636) passes: published 2026.11.3→candidate reaches readyz=200; the native systemd survivor passes; a separate intentional scoped migration failure restores schema 42→26, retains two outbox rows and preserves an unrelated write. Broader manual-run failures remain reported, not blanket-waived; PostgreSQL inventory regressions reproduce on exact main parent and trace to #190001/#195369.

Legacy transcript-label rewriting remains before activation because replay recognizes the new provenance marker. No production scan-speedup claim is made. Moving the primary backup before stop remains a separate, design-only recovery-contract change requiring maintainer acceptance.

**Design-only follow-up (B):** Stage a consistent recovery image with SQLite’s online backup API while the old release serves, then finalize the exact committed generation under the existing stopped-writer lease and durably publish it before migration. An observed 104.4 GB primary capture took 404 seconds inside the stop; moving those writes online could remove that component, but final catch-up, whole-file SHA-256, integrity checks and fsync still belong in the measured stop budget. At 115–250 MB/s, a genuinely incremental 1–10 GB catch-up projects 4–87 seconds before validation; writes from another connection may instead restart SQLite backup, so this is not a promised bound. Budget at least 104.4 GB plus WAL headroom, or 208.8 GB plus overhead if staging coexists with a fallback image. Preserve exact pre-migration recovery, later-write refusal, crash/cancel safety and retirement after update finish. Validate serving latency, total I/O, disk peak and recovery under concurrent WAL writes before accepting this material persistent-store change. **B is unimplemented and requires separate maintainer acceptance.**

prs.title: fix(codex): cold web-search support verdicts no longer rotate bound threads
prs.body:
Closes #174676

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: a Codex conversation's native thread is replaced — re-sending its full selected history — on the second turn after a Gateway cold start, because turn 1 recorded the web-search policy from a cold capability probe.

## User Impact
Conversations that start right after a Gateway start keep their native thread and prompt context. A cold "unsupported" capability read no longer forces a full history re-send once the provider's web-search support resolves (the issue measured ~1.2M characters re-injected on a lossless session).

## Why This Change Was Made
A cold app-server can answer `modelProvider/capabilities/read` before its model metadata hydrates, producing a definitive-looking "unsupported" verdict. The lifecycle persisted that verdict's disabled thread config as the binding's authoritative web-search fingerprint, so the first informed turn counted the change as a persistent policy change and rotated the thread.

The preflight now also computes the fingerprint an uninformed ("unknown") plan produces under the same config. When a binding's stored fingerprint equals that uninformed shape and the current plan is informed, the lifecycle adopts the informed fingerprint on the existing thread instead of replacing it. Genuine policy edits (allowed domains, provider opt-outs, persistent denial) move the plan away from the uninformed shape and still rotate as before; a first turn under an "unknown" verdict already keeps a provisional binding and is untouched.

The stored fingerprint alone cannot prove the plan was uninformed: an explicit `tools.web.search.enabled=false` turn writes the same disabled shape. The binding now also records whether the durable policy requested search (`webSearchRequested`, taken from `persistentWebSearchAllowed` with the effective value as fallback, so capability filtering such as domain-restricted management does not look like a denial). Cold-support settlement requires `webSearchRequested: true`, so re-enabling an explicitly disabled search remains a policy transition that rotates; bindings written before this field keep rotating exactly as before.

## Evidence
- Regression in `thread-lifecycle-web-search.test-support.ts` (registered from the binding suite): turn 1 under `nativeProviderWebSearchSupport: "unsupported"` persists the disabled fingerprint; turn 2 under `"supported"` keeps `thread-1` with exactly one `thread/start`. prs.title: feat(gateway): role definitions no longer turn on named-role enforcement without a default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway cannot hold role definitions without also switching on named-role enforcement for every operator sign-in. The presence of `gateway.roles` refuses device-token and setup-code sign-ins that have no verified identity, turns off browser-code pairing and owner ingress, and caps Tailscale and trusted-proxy users at the default role. OpenClaw ID needs role definitions on a personal claw without changing how its other sign-ins behave.

## User Impact

User impact: none for existing Gateways. Every valid config already has `gateway.roles.default`, so it keeps enforcement exactly as before.

`gateway.roles.default` is now optional. A config with `definitions` and no `default` defines roles as data and otherwise behaves like a Gateway with no `gateway.roles`.

Required action to be aware of: removing `default` from a team Gateway's config now turns named-role enforcement off, where it used to fail validation. `assignments.byGithubLogin` without a default is a validation error.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Named-role enforcement applies only when `gateway.roles.default` is set. One helper, `src/gateway/operator-role-enforcement.ts`, answers that question, and every enforcement gate that tested for `gateway.roles` now uses it: sign-in and pairing, owner and person ingress, HTTP profile requirements, session sharing, cron, web push, `send`, questions, tool invocation, and the bundled `mcp-relay` and `visitor-access` plugins.
- Code that reads definitions as data (model catalogs, role-name validation) still reads `gateway.roles.definitions`.
- Change detection still compares the whole `gateway.roles` object, so adding or removing a default reloads and re-checks connections.
- With no default, a profile resolves to no named role. `users.setRole` with a role name is refused and names `gateway.roles.default`; clearing with `null` works in every state.
- OpenClaw ID member policy is unchanged in all three states.

## Evidence

- New tests with definitions and no default: setup-code and device-token-only operator connects succeed; browser-code start and approval work; owner ingress is allowed; Tailscale identity scopes are not capped; `users.setRole` is refused and `users.list` shows no effective role; config validation accepts definitions alone and rejects an unknown default and assignments without a default.
- Focused run: 13 files, 387 tests pass. A broader 22-file run passed except one fixture that relied on definitions alone enabling enforcement; it now sets a default and its refusal assertion is unchanged.
- Four existing expectations changed, each only because `default` is no longer required: the schema rejection of definitions alone, role resolution with no default (denied to none), and two fixtures that gained an explicit default.
- Targeted typechecks, lint, format, config schema and docs checks, SDK boundary checks and line ratchets pass.
- An independent review listed 162 non-test references to `gateway.roles` across 66 files and found no missed or wrongly switched enforcement gate, and no P0 or P1.

Known gap, found by that review (P2): two Doctor checks in `src/commands/doctor/cron/execution-context-check.ts` and the replay script `scripts/dev/cron-context-replay.mts` still test for the presence of `gateway.roles`. With definitions and no default, Doctor can wrongly report that an automation will lose owner access. It only reports; it repairs nothing. #197785, later in this stack, fixes it.

Follow-up after first CI run:

- 17 more test fixtures relied on definitions alone enabling enforcement. Each now sets an explicit default; no assertion changed.
- The role-assignment eligibility check moved from `users.ts` to `users-profile-access.ts` to stay under the line cap, with unchanged behavior.
- The CI test-capacity planner keeps the Gateway core and client role tests in one compact group; without that its own floor test fails on this branch.

Live proof: 12 of 12 checks passed on head `433d3c32c5f6` in an isolated Gateway against the staging testnet (see the proof comment below).

Inherited CI failure: `checks-node-compact-small-9-1` fails in `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` (5 cases, UI end-to-end ownership counts). The CI merge base `97611bd5fb39` had two duplicate Home registrations in `test/vitest/vitest.ui-paths.mjs`, fixed on main by #198391. The test passes on this head alone (220), on current main (225) and on this head merged with current main (225); the CI base alone reproduces the same 5 failures. This PR touches neither file.

Not run: the full repository suite.

prs.title: improve(worktrees): reduce recovery snapshot overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large managed worktrees spend unnecessary time emitting object-validation replies before their recovery snapshot can be published. Related: #169690.

## User Impact

Recovery snapshots keep the same contents, validation and restore behavior, with less output overhead during cleanup. This is a small optimization; it does not eliminate filesystem scans or guarantee lower loose-object storage latency. No configuration, schema or retention changes. Production LOC delta: **0**.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot owner already supplies every object ID in one batch and waits for complete output. Git's default `cat-file --batch-check` writes each reply separately. Enable its documented `--buffer` mode while preserving the object-type checks, missing-object refusal and publication ordering. The existing restore scenario now spans multiple output buffers, including a partial final buffer.

## Evidence

- **41 focused tests passed** (`service.removal-safety.test.ts`, `service.retire-snapshot.test.ts`), 70.27 seconds wall time. Real native removal/restore also preserved the original HEAD, all 62,000 tracked paths and an edited provisioned file, with network protocols disabled during final restoration.
- Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Final targeted script typecheck/lint/format passed. Core/core-test typecheck and core lint passed within `pnpm check:changed`.
- Synthetic fixture: 62,000 tracked paths plus 62,000 ignored dependency files (1.143 GB), a hydrated local blobless partial clone and complete APFS clone. Maintenance/GC disabled. Two A/A controls, then five serial A/B process pairs, each with five warmups and five measured snapshots. Every arm produced the identical snapshot commit, including tree, parent, message and author/committer metadata.
- Acceptance fixed before qualification: preserve the exact commit and restoration; improve owner timing/CPU/allocation without a >20% regression. The committed benchmark command is `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-snapshot-measure.ts --native-repo <synthetic-checkout> --temporary-root <owned-scratch> --iterations 5 --warmup 5 --child-cpu`, adding `--base-file <pinned-owner-source>` for A. Never use the native benchmark on a user checkout.

| Qualified APFS partial-clone metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Owner wall, median of process medians | 985.989 ms | 899.692 ms |
| Owner wall, median of process p95 | 1,082.417 ms | 975.134 ms |
| Owner wall, worst observed sample | 1,363.570 ms | 1,034.617 ms |
| Object check, pooled median / p95 | 69.682 / 98.301 ms | 32.523 / 34.310 ms |
| Main + Git CPU per operation, median | 3,167.438 ms | 3,115.712 ms |
| Main V8 allocation per operation, median | 383.925 MiB | 372.220 MiB |

A/A block medians were 1,004.984 and 959.198 ms. Both arms issue 14 owner Git commands; the change removes per-object output writes, not validation or process launches. Native owner measurements exclude worker IPC, hydration, capacity admission and registry work. Child CPU has 10-ms resolution. Unforced end RSS increased 439.744 → 473.835 MiB; no peak/live-memory reduction is claimed. No large session/transcript DB is modeled because this owner does not read it.

<details>
<summary>Phase analysis, unsuccessful probes and inherited checks</summary>

Clean snapshots execute no add, private-index population or write-tree. Trace2 shows 62,000 tracked-file lstat calls, zero refresh content scans, and no maintenance/gc child. Status takes about 154 ms; other-path inspection about 436 ms; commit-tree and update-ref about 10 ms each. Those scans continue protecting hidden edits, nested repositories and private staged inputs. No fsync event appeared in Trace2; this is not syscall-level proof of no fsync.

Loose-object validation can dominate: short probes measured a 2.009-second median object check. Short loose-object controls were noisy: owner median 3.127 → 2.868 seconds, but worst sample 3.213 → 7.653 seconds; A/A itself ranged 2.726–6.954 seconds. These failed the tail gate and are not qualification or a loose-object speedup claim. Longer warmed APFS qualification is reported above. Omitting object-type reads was rejected because it would weaken damaged-object detection.

The real large-fixture candidate removal completed but hit the existing benchmark's 10-second timing assertion while broad local checks were running (21.238-second snapshot, host load 34–35 versus about 15 for the earlier baseline). That timing is not serial paired evidence and is not called passing. Its saved snapshot was subsequently restored and independently checked successfully. The initial worker profiling attempt also failed on an obsolete worker receipt; a separate owner CPU/Trace2 profile completed.

`pnpm check:changed` initially found benchmark-only type/lint issues; these were fixed and the affected checks passed on the final change. Its remaining script dead-export findings reproduce on exact main parent `28e2018dcdfb861c5f0b4b1178ff9fa6a72db151` with Knip 6.40.0:

- `TELEPORT_PT`: introduced as an unused export by `858b5b01338e` / #198293.
- `RELEASE_VALIDATION_WAIVERS`: its last consuming suite was deleted by `b9f1e62e00d8` / #198274.

These are identified main regressions, not ignored noise; no unrelated release/iOS change is included. The first parent probe lacked UI dependencies and was discarded; the qualified parent probe reproduces exactly these two findings.
</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native approval operations failing with an unsupported `--stdin` option when a packaged Mac app selects an older external CLI, especially on remote-only Macs without a seeded local Gateway runtime.

## User Impact

Packaged apps use their own matching approval CLI without preparing a local Gateway. The selected profile, state directory, and explicit config path remain intact. Broken bundled payloads report an error rather than falling back to another CLI. Unbundled development builds retain local CLI resolution. No migration or configuration change is required; installed apps need a build containing this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The private approval protocol must match the app, not whichever CLI happens to be discoverable. Reuse existing bundled-runtime validation and environment at the native approval owner; leave general Gateway/CLI resolution and approval authorization unchanged.

The stale-executable attribution in the originally affected app was not directly traced. A controlled baseline reproduction does invoke the older external CLI and fails with exit 64.

## Evidence

- Baseline child-process regression: explicit/default config cases selected the stale external CLI and failed with exit 64; broken packaged payloads did not reject resolution.

Actual subprocess execution verifies stdin, root profile arguments, state/config selection, inherited context, bundled SQLite selection, and no Gateway seed.
- Bundled-runtime siblings passed: relocated worker selection, incomplete/mismatched payload rejection (7 cases), and browser setup selection.
- Real packaged-policy boundary smoke also passed: the patched production launch builder selected an existing signed app's matching Bun/CLI/SQLite payload (`2026.11.2`, `b09f5e65212882bdc68df70fd1da833c9a9c8f33`) and completed real policy get → set-deny → get operations against disposable state with a named profile and explicit config. The saved hash/policy persisted; config stayed unchanged and no runtime seed appeared. This did not launch or modify the app, operator state, or any Gateway.
