prs.title: fix(ui): keep a Browser panel action's error visible through passive refreshes
prs.body:
Closes #198052

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Browser panel's error for a failed action, such as a navigation blocked by policy, disappears while the page keeps streaming, because the automatic viewport resize and passive panel refreshes clear it.

## User Impact

User impact: when an action in the Browser panel fails, its error stays visible until the person acts again, retries or refreshes, instead of vanishing on its own.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The automatic viewport sync runs as a passive action and no longer clears the shown error before it runs.
- A panel refresh keeps an error that came from the person's own action; it still clears errors from its own snapshot work.
- The person's next action, and an explicit Retry or Refresh, still clear the error, and any new error replaces it.

## Evidence

![The Browser panel still shows "Couldn't complete the browser action. Try again." about 10 seconds after a blocked navigation, while the page keeps streaming](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/f64e3f00b94ba3938400a5d18acea436e3af2aed/images/2026/11/ae8525d1-2aa6-4ac6-b259-5971ed3cf493.png)

Live run in an isolated VM, on a build that contains this change: about 10 seconds after a navigation blocked by policy and an automatic viewport resize, the panel still shows "Couldn't complete the browser action. Try again." while the page keeps streaming (live frame counter running). The expanded "Show details" text, which names the policy block, was not checked in that run.

Tests:
- New Browser panel streaming tests: an action's policy error survives 10 seconds of viewport sync and of a panel refresh while frames stream; both fail without this change. A second new test shows an explicit Refresh still clears an action's error.

prs.title: fix: restore Vue/Vite previews through native portals
prs.body:
Closes #198361

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes blank Vue/Vite app previews when the native portal rewrites development-module query strings.

## User Impact

Developers can load their local app and use hot reload through native portals without a separate reverse-proxy workaround. Existing portal authentication and cookie isolation are unchanged; no configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Calling `URL.searchParams.delete()` reserializes unrelated query parameters even when the bearer key is absent. For example, a Vue style request ending in `?vue&type=style&lang.css` becomes `?vue=&type=style&lang.css=`. Vite can answer with raw CSS labeled JavaScript, producing `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token`.

Remove only reserved portal-auth query segments and preserve every remaining segment verbatim. The shared authorization path covers both HTTP and WebSocket upgrades, including encoded/duplicate reserved names. The patch adds no helper, API, configuration, dependency or unrelated cleanup (production +8/-2 lines; tests +15/-2).

## Evidence

- Real loopback HTTP and WebSocket checks against the actual exported production handlers: **2 failures on the base, 2 passes with the fix**. No authentication/proxy mocks in that proof; it covers unauthorized rejection, cookie authentication, encoded/duplicate launch-token stripping, Vue bare flags, encoded app values and WebSocket query preservation.
- A real Vite app behind the patched native handlers returns byte-identical entry/client/Vue-style JavaScript compared with direct Vite; module syntax checks pass. Actual Vite HMR WebSocket upgrade through those handlers returns **101 Switching Protocols**.
- Added owner-suite HTTP regressions for Vue and encoded app queries under cookie and query-bearer authentication; expanded the existing local/worker WebSocket cases with byte-sensitive HMR query values.
- Targeted formatting and direct non-type-aware oxlint checks passed. Staged secret scan and the normal commit hook passed.
- Fresh independent native Codex review of the complete two-file change against `1904c27817b7eb8d1b9d09de8c7f46b5226d6780`: no actionable findings. No local ClawSweeper/autoreview CLI run is claimed.

**Draft / validation gap:** The canonical focused command `pnpm test src/gateway/portals/portal-http-proxy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` could not reach test execution on this constrained host: worker/artifact preparation terminated with exit 143 in the bounded Node run; the default Bun run was stopped under memory pressure. A direct repository-wrapper attempt also failed during compiled-worker preparation. The repository lint wrapper began a large SDK artifact preparation and was stopped to protect the running Gateway/app; full typecheck and the canonical Vitest suite are therefore **not verified**. The real-handler and live-Vite checks above are narrower proof, not a claim that the full suite passed. Please run the focused suite and normal CI on a qualified host before marking ready/merging. No installed OpenClaw runtime was patched or restarted, and browser rendering through the isolated test proxy was policy-blocked; live module/HMR verification is transport evidence, not viewer-rendering proof.

prs.title: feat(mcp-events): receive MCP events by poll without a public callback
prs.body:
Related: #166586

## What Problem This Solves

MCP Events can only deliver by webhook today, so an Automation can't react to an MCP server's events unless the Gateway has a public HTTPS callback route. Most Gateways run on a laptop or a private network, bound to loopback.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can enable `mcp-events` without `callbackOrigin`, and event Automations receive their events by polling the MCP server (`events/poll` from SEP-3415), with no public route to the Gateway. Each event runs the Automation once, as with webhook delivery.

`callbackOrigin` becomes optional. Configs that set it keep webhook delivery for events that offer it, and webhook subscriptions saved by earlier versions are kept as they are. An event that offers only webhook still needs `callbackOrigin`, and its source reports that. Adding or removing `callbackOrigin` later replaces affected subscriptions with the other mode; as when a source is replaced, events still queued for the old subscription don't run, and the replacement starts from now.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's review of #166586 recommended starting with polling: extend the existing host capability and plugin, and prove cursor recovery and replay deduplication. It also asked for a maintainer decision on that direction, which this PR still needs. SEP-3415 (status: Accepted) defines the poll profile. This PR implements poll only; push (`events/stream`) is not included.

Poll reuses the webhook path from the queue onward. Webhook callbacks and poll results go through one admission step into the same durable ingress queue, so deduplication by event ID, the `maxPendingEvents` budget, the drain and Cron's `runEvent` handoff are shared. The shared ingress code now lives in `ingress.ts`, which keeps `service.ts` under the line cap. Following the SEP's client guidance, OpenClaw uses webhook when `callbackOrigin` is set and the event offers it, and poll otherwise.

Poll behavior, per the SEP:

- One poll loop per event Automation, on the existing Gateway scheduler. The first poll sends `cursor: null` ("start from now").
- The returned cursor is persisted in plugin state after the batch is queued. A crash re-polls the batch and the queue drops repeated event IDs. After a restart, polling resumes from the saved cursor.
- `hasMore: true` with events polls again at once. Otherwise OpenClaw waits `nextPollMs`, with the SEP's 1-second floor and a one-hour ceiling. Editing other Automations doesn't pull a scheduled poll forward.
- Events in a batch run in the server's order.
- `NotFound` or `Unsupported` rediscovers the event type and starts again from now, dropping events still queued for the old subscription and backing off if the server keeps refusing. Other errors, including `Forbidden`, retry with backoff capped at five minutes while the Automation is enabled, as webhook sources do.
- Events over 256 KiB, or failing envelope or `payloadSchema` validation, are skipped with a warning, so one bad event can't block the Automation's queue.
- Poll keeps no server-side subscription, so removing or pausing the Automation just stops polling.

The host capability accepts `events/poll` only for the Automation's own persisted event name and arguments, the same rule `events/subscribe` follows. Two small SEP alignments also apply to webhook mode: discovery accepts the `io.modelcontextprotocol/events` extension entry as well as the earlier top-level `events` key, and requests that carry an event name send the `Mcp-Name` header (Base64 form for non-ASCII names). The Automation editor's catalog now lists events that offer poll; push-only events stay hidden.

Not included: `maxAgeMs`. After a long outage a saved cursor replays everything the server still retains, one run per event, bounded by `maxPendingEvents`. Webhook refresh behaves the same today.

## Evidence

- Focused tests, all passing with `--maxWorkers=1`: `extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts` (20), `src/agents/mcp-event-request.headers.test.ts` (4, new), `src/plugins/service-mcp-events.test.ts` (27), `src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-events.test.ts` (8). The plugin suite's test time is about 3 s of a 17 s run; the rest is compile time. The 16 existing webhook tests pass unchanged.
- New plugin tests cover: poll without a callback across a restart (cursor resumed, one queue row per event, `hasMore` and `nextPollMs` honored); a cursor write that fails after the batch is queued (the next poll resends the old cursor and the queue keeps one row); a webhook binding stored in the pre-change shape (kept, same binding ID, no new subscribe, and its refresh sends the same callback URL and cursor); and poll errors, rediscovery and its backoff.
- Three defects found while building this have tests that fail with the fix disabled and pass with it: events in one poll batch shared a queue receipt time and could run out of order; any Automation change re-polled every poll subscription at once, ignoring `nextPollMs`; and a restart after a recovered failure waited out the old backoff before polling.
- ClawSweeper found that a full poll batch (100 events at the 256 KiB limit) could exceed the MCP HTTP transport's 10 MiB response cap. The transport rejected it before parsing, the cursor didn't move, and the backlog stalled. Polls now ask for at most 32 events (8 MiB). A test in `src/agents/mcp-event-request.headers.test.ts` sends a full 32-event batch through the real transport, and shows a 100-event batch is rejected with `MCP HTTP response exceeds 10485760 bytes`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: everything this change touches passes, including type checks, format, the line-cap ratchet, the config baseline (regenerated because `callbackOrigin` is no longer required) and lint for `extensions/mcp-events`. Local gaps are listed below.
- Live run on macOS, isolated Gateway (own home, state and profile, loopback), on commit 7408fdf028c (the later commits only clear the stored retry time after a recovered poll, lower the poll batch to 32 events, and add or move tests and docs), against the MCP Events bridge (disclosure below) running in poll mode, with a real model (`anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). No `callbackOrigin`. The Automation's instruction was "Reply with only the comment_id value from the event data", so each run's reply shows which event it received. A pass-through recorder between the Gateway and the server logged each request:
  - The plugin's requests were `server/discover`, `events/list` and `events/poll` (37 polls). Every poll carried `Mcp-Name: proof.comment.created`. The server also saw `initialize` and `tools/list` once per run: each agent run loading the server's tools.
  - The first poll sent `cursor: null`, and each later poll sent the cursor the previous one returned. The server asked for `nextPollMs: 2000`, and polls ran 2.16 to 2.46 s apart.
  - Two signed test events, `comment_id` `one` and `two`, started two Automation runs. Both completed (`ok`) and replied `one` and `two`.
  - With the Gateway stopped, a third event (`three-while-stopped`) was sent. After restart, the first poll sent the cursor saved before the restart and returned that event. Its run completed and replied `three-while-stopped`. The subscription kept its binding ID.
  - Removing the Automation stopped polling. No subscription remained and nothing was unsubscribed.
- Upgrade from 2026.11.3 (installed from npm) with a live webhook subscription, on macOS with an isolated Gateway, the same server and model, and a public HTTPS tunnel as `callbackOrigin` (2026.11.3 accepts only a bare origin):
  - On 2026.11.3 the Gateway subscribed by webhook, and a signed test event ran the Automation (`ok`, replied `c_stable`).
  - `openclaw doctor --fix` on this branch's build (commit 30a364fc483) migrated the state databases, with backups, as `openclaw update` does.
  - This branch's Gateway then loaded the subscription 2026.11.3 had saved: same binding, `delivery: "webhook"`, one subscription, and no `events/subscribe` before its scheduled refresh.
  - At the refresh time 2026.11.3 had stored, this branch's build refreshed it: same callback URL and saved cursor; the server rotated the signing secret and extended the same remote subscription.
  - A signed test event after the upgrade ran the Automation (`ok`, replied `c_after-upgrade`).
  - In the saved record only refresh fields changed (`secret`, `previousSecret`, `cursor`, `cursorRevision`, `refreshBefore`, `nextAttemptAt`, `updatedAt`). `bindingId`, `callbackUrl`, `remoteId`, `status` and the stored event `definition` (still without a `delivery` field) were unchanged.
- Gaps:
  - `pnpm check:changed` failures local to this machine, rerun on 7e139abb007: the SQLite worker ratchet needs `rg`, which isn't installed; and the dead export scan flags `acquireConfiguredGatewayPostgresOwner` in `src/infra/gateway-postgres-owner.ts`, which this PR doesn't change.
  - Local review: local ClawSweeper (`review --local-range` against `origin/main`, head 30a364fc483) found no findings, cleared security, and rated the patch correct (patch tier C). Its proof tier is F because the offline range review sees only commits; the execution evidence it lists as missing is the live poll run and upgrade run above. Before that, two independent agent reviews (one using ClawSweeper's PR-review prompts) and the repo's `pr-simplify` pass led to the 256 KiB event limit, the rediscovery backoff, the floor for empty `hasMore` batches, the restart-after-recovery fix, the crash-window and stored-binding tests, and the queued-events note above. Left as is, on purpose: `Forbidden` retries with backoff like other errors, as enabled webhook sources do; no `maxAgeMs`; and a poll result without a cursor clears the saved one, because the SEP says an absent cursor means `null`.

Disclosure: I work at Hookdeck. The server in the live run is the [MCP Events bridge](https://github.com/hookdeck/mcp-events-bridge), an open-source MCP server I work on that turns webhooks into MCP events. It serves `events/poll` from webhooks stored in Hookdeck's Event Gateway. The test events were signed webhooks from a synthetic sender, not a real service.

prs.title: fix(plugins): plugins update --all keeps installing plugins and hook packs after Ctrl+C
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198378

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after Ctrl+C, `openclaw plugins update --all` keeps updating the remaining plugins and hook packs.

- With plugins to update, it goes on installing the next plugins until the CLI is killed by signal 9, and the kill leaves an install staging directory in the state directory.
- With only hook packs to update, it downloads and extracts the next hook pack after Ctrl+C, then exits 130.

## User Impact

User impact: Ctrl+C during `openclaw plugins update --all` now starts no further plugin or hook pack update, and the command exits 130 without being killed. As before, an interrupted run leaves the installed versions unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Neither bulk update loop read the command's cancellation signal. Each loop now stops before the next plugin or hook pack once the signal fires, and the CLI passes its existing interrupt signal to both. The update already in progress is left to the existing interrupt handling.

This follows https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198163, which did the same for `openclaw skills update --all`. The loops could instead call the install transaction's existing ownership check at their head. That check throws where this change ends the loop quietly, and it would also change the `openclaw update` and doctor callers, which were not run here.

## Evidence

Tested at this PR's head (base `main` `a48a3175600e`).

**Setup:**

- The built CLI on Linux x64 (Node 24.22.1) runs in a real PTY. Each run has its own `HOME`, state directory, config and npm cache.
- npm points at a local registry stand-in. The stand-in serves the packages, logs every request, and holds the first tarball download until released.
- Each run installs the packages at 1.0.0 (`openclaw plugins install npm:<name> --force --accept-capabilities`), offers 1.1.0, and runs `openclaw plugins update --all`. Ctrl+C is sent 0.2 s after the hold, and the download is released 300 ms later.
- Two package sets:
  - Plugin runs: three plugins `proof-plugin-a`..`c` and one hook pack `proof-hooks-d`. The held download is `proof-plugin-a`'s.
  - Hook pack runs: two hook packs, `proof-hooks-d` and `proof-hooks-e`. The held download is `proof-hooks-d`'s.
- All runs on both sides use the same driver script, packages and stand-in.
- Every run on both sides also prints two lines that are not part of this change:
  - "log file append failed", once. It refers to the default log file, which the isolated `HOME` does not move.
  - "Plugin manifest id ... differs from npm package name", once per plugin. It comes from the proof plugins' naming.

Before (base `main` `a48a3175600e`), plugins. `...` marks omitted lines, and `$RUN` stands for the run directory:

```text
== update --all with Ctrl+C during the first download
[driver] wrote Ctrl+C at +3.96s
[driver] released the held download at +4.27s
killed by signal 9 after 6.03s
---- terminal output ----
...
Installing proof-plugin-a into $RUN/before-1/state/npm/projects/.openclaw-install-stage-BA41mC…
...
^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
...
Installing proof-plugin-b into $RUN/before-1/state/npm/projects/.openclaw-install-stage-gM05Tw…
...
Installing proof-plugin-c into $RUN/before-1/state/npm/projects/.openclaw-install-stage-dnbfIb…
...
---- install staging directories left in the state dir ----
  npm/projects/.openclaw-install-stage-dnbfIb
---- installed plugin records (openclaw plugins list --json) ----
  proof-a: version 1.0.0
  proof-b: version 1.0.0
  proof-c: version 1.0.0
---- registry requests during update ----
...
1794588940.878 GET /-/tarballs/proof-plugin-a-1.1.0.tgz
1794588940.878 HOLD proof-plugin-a-1.1.0.tgz
1794588941.433 RELEASE proof-plugin-a-1.1.0.tgz
1794588941.888 GET /proof-plugin-b
...
1794588942.465 GET /-/tarballs/proof-plugin-b-1.1.0.tgz
1794588942.858 GET /proof-plugin-c
1794588943.154 GET /proof-plugin-c
```

After (this PR), plugins, with the same omission marks:

```text
== update --all with Ctrl+C during the first download
[driver] wrote Ctrl+C at +3.70s
[driver] released the held download at +4.01s
exit code 130 after 4.44s
---- terminal output ----
...
Installing proof-plugin-a into $RUN/after-1/state/npm/projects/.openclaw-install-stage-PLibH2…
...
^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
...
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: This operation was aborted
...
---- install staging directories left in the state dir ----
  (none)
---- installed plugin records (openclaw plugins list --json) ----
  proof-a: version 1.0.0
  proof-b: version 1.0.0
  proof-c: version 1.0.0
---- registry requests during update ----
...
1794586283.817 GET /-/tarballs/proof-plugin-a-1.1.0.tgz
1794586283.817 HOLD proof-plugin-a-1.1.0.tgz
1794586284.372 RELEASE proof-plugin-a-1.1.0.tgz
```

Before (base), hook packs, from the interrupt line to the end of the terminal output (temp directory names shortened to `...`):

```text
^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
Extracting /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-hook-pack-.../proof-hooks-d-1.1.0.tgz…
Installing to $RUN/before-hooks-1/state/hooks/proof-hooks-d…
Downloading proof-hooks-e…
Extracting /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-hook-pack-.../proof-hooks-e-1.1.0.tgz…
Installing to $RUN/before-hooks-1/state/hooks/proof-hooks-e…
Failed to update hook pack "proof-hooks-d": failed to copy hook pack: AbortError: This operation was aborted
Failed to update hook pack "proof-hooks-e": failed to copy hook pack: AbortError: This operation was aborted
```

After (this PR), hook packs, the same span:

```text
^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
Extracting /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-hook-pack-.../proof-hooks-d-1.1.0.tgz…
Installing to $RUN/after-hooks-1/state/hooks/proof-hooks-d…
Failed to update hook pack "proof-hooks-d": failed to copy hook pack: AbortError: This operation was aborted
```

**Observed result:**

- **Plugins, on base:** after Ctrl+C the CLI went on to `proof-plugin-b` and `proof-plugin-c`, and the stand-in logged their requests after Ctrl+C.
  - The process was killed by signal 9 during `proof-plugin-c`'s install.
  - Run 1 was killed after 6.03 s, 2.07 s after Ctrl+C. Run 2 was killed after 5.94 s, 2.09 s after Ctrl+C.
  - Each run left an install staging directory in the state dir.
- **Plugins, at the head:** the stand-in logged no request after `proof-plugin-a`'s.
  - The CLI exited 130: run 1 after 4.44 s (0.74 s after Ctrl+C), run 2 after 4.46 s (0.77 s after Ctrl+C).
  - No staging directory was left.
- **Hook packs:**
  - On base, the CLI downloaded and extracted `proof-hooks-e` after Ctrl+C, then exited 130 (3.52 s and 3.59 s).
  - At the head, the stand-in saw no request for `proof-hooks-e`, and the CLI exited 130 (3.38 s and 3.31 s).
- On both sides every package stayed at 1.0.0, on disk and in the records.
- **Without Ctrl+C,** the same head build:
  - updated all three plugins and the hook pack to 1.1.0 and exited 0;
  - updated both hook packs in the hook pack set.

Full captures:

- Before, plugins: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261113-198163-plugins-update-all-ctrl-c/before.txt
- After, plugins: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261113-198163-plugins-update-all-ctrl-c/after.txt
- After, plugins, uninterrupted: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261113-198163-plugins-update-all-ctrl-c/after-uninterrupted.txt
- Before, hook packs: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261113-198163-plugins-update-all-ctrl-c/before-hooks.txt
- After, hook packs: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261113-198163-plugins-update-all-ctrl-c/after-hooks.txt
- After, hook packs, uninterrupted: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261113-198163-plugins-update-all-ctrl-c/after-hooks-uninterrupted.txt

**Checks:**

- `src/plugins/update.test.ts` "starts no plugin update once interrupted" and `src/hooks/update.test.ts` "starts no hook pack update once interrupted": an aborted signal starts no install and returns no outcome. Both fail on base.
- `src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts`: the bulk `update --all` test now runs inside a work scope. It expects that scope's signal in both the plugin and the hook pack update call, and it fails on base.
- There are four changed lines: the two loop checks and the two CLI `signal` lines. Reverting any one of them alone turns its test red.
- Consumer tests pass: 29 files, 509 tests. They include:
  - `src/plugins/update-cohort.test.ts`;
  - the `src/cli/update-cli*.test.ts` files and `src/cli/hooks-cli*.test.ts`;
  - the `src/cli/plugins-update-command.*.integration.test.ts` files;
  - the doctor plugin-install repair tests.
- `pnpm check:changed`:
  - format, lint, typecheck and the repository guards pass;
  - the dead export scan fails on `scripts/lib/release-validation-waivers.mjs` (`RELEASE_VALIDATION_WAIVERS`) and `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-store.ts` (`resolveAuthoritativeSharedOAuthCredentialUnderLock`). This PR does not touch either file, and both exports are on base.
- Size against base: production +13 lines. Test lines are net −2, because three single-use test helpers were inlined at their only call site.
- The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

Test cost, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local:

| File | Tests | Local wall | Vitest | New or changed test | CI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/plugins/update.test.ts` | 90 | 14.44 s | 9.89 s | 5 ms | |
| `src/hooks/update.test.ts` | 7 | 11.50 s | 6.85 s | 719 ms | |
| `src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts` | 27 | 18.83 s | 14.28 s | 365 ms | |

Local review: autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, high), base `a48a3175600e` to head `e81fd39f9419`, priority P0–P1. Its context was the cancellation scope, the CLI local-state owner, both update loops and the plugins update command. Result: scoped-clean, no findings.

<!-- openclaw-preflight:v1
{"v":1,"repo":"openclaw/openclaw","base":"a48a3175600e3cad5554128a4cf0012c4e65d9ad","head":"e81fd39f9419562055188cc2e4425078baff2c09","tool":{"name":"autoreview","version":"source-a120e048f9fc"},"completion":"complete","summary":"Threshold P1; lower priorities not assessed; status scoped-clean; accepted 0; priority-filtered 0; scope/attribution-rejected 0; missing-required 0. Self-reported; see native report."}
-->

**Not covered:**

- The update already in progress is unchanged. It still meets the existing interrupt handling, the command still prints "The CLI command failed. Reason: This operation was aborted", and the run's changes are not kept.
- Two other callers of the plugin update loop pass no signal and are unchanged:
  - the plugin step of `openclaw update` (`src/plugins/update-cohort.ts`);
  - the doctor repair of missing configured plugin installs (`src/commands/doctor/shared/missing-configured-plugin-install.repair.ts`).

  They are separate commands that bring plugins in line with a release or a config. Whether to stop them partway is a separate decision, and neither was run here.
- The registry was a local stand-in, not npmjs.com. ClawHub-sourced plugins were not run.

prs.title: fix: dashboard stays on the shared token profile after Tailscale Serve recovers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS dashboard switches to the Gateway's shared token profile (default theme, no pinned shortcuts) and stays there until the app is relaunched, after managed Tailscale Serve briefly drops and recovers.

## User Impact

User impact: after a Tailscale restart or Serve recovery, the dashboard returns to the Serve sign-in address and the user's own profile on its own. During the outage it still falls back to the shared token profile, so it keeps working. No data was lost before this fix either: the user's profile rows stayed intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway advertises `controlUiIdentityUrl` in an operator hello only while a managed Serve route is published. When the route is withdrawn or replaced, it already closes identity-bearing operator sockets with 1012 so they reconnect and get a fresh hello. The reverse case had no equivalent. A hello sent while Serve was unpublished, during startup or a recovery, kept its identity-less answer for the life of the connection. The Mac app reconnected during the outage, correctly rebuilt the dashboard with native token auth, and never received another hello once Serve came back.

Eligible identity-less hellos now bind to a "next Serve publication" signal owned by `tailscale-published-origin.ts`. When managed Serve publishes again, those connections close with 1012 and reconnect with the identity route. On the Mac side, the existing reconnect path already moves the dashboard back to browser identity (`remote dashboard uses verified browser identity across tunnel reconnects`), so no Swift change is needed. Only operator hellos that could actually use Serve identity subscribe: `auth.allowTailscale` set, auth mode not `none`, Control UI enabled, and no origin published at all. Trusted-proxy, funnel, node-role and `allowTailscale: false` connections are untouched.

Accepted edge case: for the length of the outage, the dashboard shows the shared token profile. The Gateway has no way to tell a transient outage from an intentional removal, and a working dashboard is the better fallback. Telling the two apart would need a protocol addition.

## Evidence

**Incident (2026-11-12, Mac app 2026.11.2, Gateway 2026.11.3), from read-only log inspection:**
- 20:38:02Z: Gateway logged that the `serve route claim exited`; all `auth=tailscale` browser sockets dropped, along with the app's native operator socket.
- 20:38:02.9Z: the app's native socket reconnected while Serve was still down, so its hello carried no identity URL. At 20:38:03.6Z a new dashboard page connected as `client=openclaw-macos … auth=token`.
- 20:38:11Z: Gateway logged `serve enabled`. Nothing renewed the app's hello, so the page stayed on the token profile.
- WebKit's log shows the old WebContent process was not a crash. Its page was closed by the document replacement and WebKit reaped it about 10s later. The crash-recovery path (`webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` → Reload) wasn't involved in this event. It resolves through the same `windowConfiguration(for: .primary)` as launch.

**Regression test (real WebSocket, real `startGatewayTailscaleExposure` publication):** `renews a hello announced while managed Serve was unpublished once its route returns`. An operator gets an identity-less hello, managed Serve then publishes, and the test expects a 1012 close followed by a renewed hello carrying `https://gateway.tailnet.ts.net/`.
- Red on base `4efd662`: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ 1012, Anything ]`, 0 calls.
- Green with the fix.

**Overreach control:** the existing `advertises the personal dashboard for resolved $mode auth with $tailscale` table publishes a Serve origin after each hello and expects no close for rows that cannot use Serve identity. I checked it by mutation: subscribing every operator hello fails 6 of those rows.

**Checks on this head:**
- `pnpm vitest run` on every consumer of the published-origin and identity modules (`server-tailscale`, all `server/ws-connection/*`, `mcp-app-standalone`, `portal-service`, `provider-browser-auth/*`, `models-auth-login`): 41 files, 611 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: format, lint and the other guards OK. The dead-export scan reports `src/gateway/trusted-proxy-git-coauthor.ts`, which is already on main and unrelated.

prs.title: fix: preserve outcome guidance after native subagent completion
prs.body:
Related: #190582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing outcome guidance when a native Codex subagent finishes and wakes a detached OpenClaw parent.

## User Impact

The parent receives the existing guidance to compare the child result with the original request and continue in-scope work when needed. This corrects instruction delivery; it does not guarantee a model will follow that guidance or that a retained child can be resumed.

Maintainer edits are enabled on the fork branch, including the associated access to GitHub Actions workflows and any fork secrets.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared harness completion owner now composes the canonical subagent outcome instruction with either the default reply guidance or a caller's custom guidance. Native Codex supplies a custom instruction, so changing the default alone would not cover that path. Route-specific guidance and the separation of child results as conversation data are retained; no permissions, custody, retry, or session-lifecycle behavior is changed.

#190582 updates the shared outcome wording and other handoff prompts; its current draft does not change this completion-delivery boundary. This fix uses the existing shared policy rather than introducing another wording owner.

## Evidence

**Fresh live delivery passed on `7b6d41f85aa80994188decd68acb79146ff8cbcb` on November 11, 2026.** The isolated Gateway and bundled Codex exercised one detached native child completion on the pinned build. Docker, the wrapper, and Vitest exited 0. One test passed, and a separate verifier passed all 13 checks against the captured records.

- [Sanitized initiating case](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ekinnee/1284778ef4b89b34c821ea8a9fc7e0f5/raw/e4270c7cc2aa610bc817678c31a99d76602259ee/initiating-case.json)
- [Full sanitized transport trace](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ekinnee/1284778ef4b89b34c821ea8a9fc7e0f5/raw/0031dd41efdd36b7f19c18112c7cde7f8a8afc07/transport.jsonl)
- [Actual accepted parent input](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ekinnee/1284778ef4b89b34c821ea8a9fc7e0f5/raw/be793eea10efd7b41ec4851778ac42a1b58fa59e/actual-parent-input.txt)
- [Evidence bundle with replay instructions](https://gist.github.com/ekinnee/1284778ef4b89b34c821ea8a9fc7e0f5) · [SHA-256 manifest](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ekinnee/1284778ef4b89b34c821ea8a9fc7e0f5/raw/188fa49f0b286aa66853c7345b1529bc57b5b635/SHA256SUMS)

The initiating request reached the original Codex thread. The parent completed with `PARENT_RETURNED` while its child was still active. After latch release the same child turn completed with `NATIVE_REVIEW_BLOCKER_47`. The captured Gateway `thread_ready` records link the original and follow-up physical threads to the same logical parent. The follow-up `turn/start` included the child's actual identity and result, the complete canonical outcome instruction, and the full native reply guidance. Codex acknowledged that request and emitted matching `turn/started` and `turn/completed` notifications.

Inspect lines 25, 74, 77, 103 and 126 for the initiating request and parent/child sequence. Lines 127, 130, 133 and 165 contain the follow-up input, acknowledgment, start, and completion. The trace retains all 156 JSON-RPC frames in order. Proof IDs use consistent aliases, and ancillary configuration, account, model and reasoning payloads are redacted. The accepted-input file matches line 127, and the bundle includes an offline replay script.

Runtime used Node 24.19.0, Vitest 5.0.5 and bundled Codex 0.164.0. The live fixture body took 30.069 seconds. The isolated access-only routing preflight exited 0 after preserving the stored `last_refresh` timestamp required by Codex to load its bearer token. The operator auth was unchanged, refresh credentials stayed excluded, and the disposable home and container were removed.

**Earlier attempts:** the November 4 live fixture exited 1 and the archived capture passed offline verification. On November 11, the first fresh attempt exited 125 at Docker startup. The second recorded Vitest exit 1 and wrapper exit 124 after an account-routing 401, before any turn started.

**Reused regression/source evidence:** original base `0a6aaf50f6c5c4e906dd906dd52b9539e4bf93be`; original production candidate `43436be32a650d15deed27f5e055699f413fa393`. Default, custom, and detached native composition regressions failed on unchanged base production code for the missing canonical instruction: 3 failed, 16 skipped. With the fix, 57 tests across four files passed. The red native object match failed before its later route assertions; those later assertions are not claimed as red-run proof. The moved suite passed all 19 cases on `7d68fd5...`; `960f410...` added only two isolation annotations, removed their obsolete mock ledger entries, and adjusted the allocation. Local original-candidate source review and local ClawSweeper inspection found no actionable findings; the latter did not assess PR proof acceptance. The latest hosted review on `7b6d41f...` reports no code findings and confirms the earlier core graph issue is resolved; acceptance of the new delivery evidence is pending.

<details>
<summary>Red/green commands and observed totals</summary>

The historical runs used an isolated Vitest cache and log redirection; the cache path and redirects are omitted below. The red command ran with the test-only changes present on the base; the green command ran with the production fix present and was followed by the byte-identical original commit. The revised candidate moves that same suite to the top-level integration test path.

```sh
# Before: base production code with the new test-only changes
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-completion.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'preserves outcome guidance|delivers a detached Codex'

# After: original candidate 43436be
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-completion.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.completion-delivery.test.ts src/agents/internal-events.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# Revised candidate: complete moved suite and the affected type-graph boundary
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/agent-harness-completion.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm run lint:tmp:tsgo-core-boundary
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json --incremental
```

```text
Before: 1 test file failed; 3 tests failed | 16 skipped; exit 1.
  Default and custom reply instructions did not contain the shared outcome instruction.
  Detached native completion's captured event did not contain that instruction.
After: 4 test files passed; 57 tests passed; exit 0.
Moved suite: 1 file passed; 19 tests passed; exit 0.
Core type-graph boundary and root-test typecheck: exit 0.
```

The candidate adds 72 test lines (70 regression lines and two mock-isolation comments), recorded in its own test-line allocation; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged. The original-base test-line and line-cap checks passed locally. That earlier-base result does not establish a pass against the newer CI merge base.

</details>

**Proof scope:** one detached completion delivered through a real Gateway and native Codex runtime with synthetic task content. Model compliance, retained-child revision, other custody and recovery paths, and deployment remain unverified.

## CI status

The [additional-boundaries job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41754662646/job/126328502284) passed at the pinned head. The [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41754662646/job/126328501234) and [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41754662646/job/126331684226) remain red. CI counted 6,447,061 test lines against a ceiling of 6,446,916, an inherited overage of 145. The PR adds 72 lines and a matching 72-line allocation. The positive delta activates the ratchet while leaving the overage unchanged. The mock-export ratchet passed.

prs.title: fix: avoid repeated config copies after hot reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated full-config cloning during reply preparation and tool construction after a live configuration reload.

## User Impact

Reloaded configurations retain the existing shared capture, avoiding redundant allocation on subsequent turns. Configuration values, provider requests, and transcript ownership are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Secrets activation publishes a private config snapshot, but reload handed the pre-activation, value-identical object to prepared replies and committed-config consumers. Those objects missed the canonical capture fast path. Carry the published reference forward at the reload boundary, including neutral reloads and committed policy callbacks.

Production LOC is unchanged (+11/-11). No new cache, config option, schema, or hydration change. One existing mixed-plugin test moved into its support module to satisfy the line-cap ratchet without losing assertions.

## Evidence

- The real Gateway startup/file-reload test fails on the parent at both new identity assertions and passes with the fix.
- Reload handler suite: 110 tests pass, including publication rollback, plugin replacement, service handoff, and removed-agent database fences. Managed-secrets and real Gateway reload suites also pass.
- Isolated dev Gateway, synthetic 5,000-session/eight-agent fixture and 40 plugin registrations, real chat.send/reply/tool construction against a local model stub: after a logging-only reload, two captures/four cloned payloads per subsequent turn become zero. A/A instrumented baselines: 0.853 / 0.831 ms main-thread clone CPU and roughly 0.59–0.66 MB sampled capture allocation per turn become zero at these owners.
- Canonical startup A/A controls and a built-runtime probe already showed zero clones. The defect requires reload publication; this is not a separate module instance or a turn-specific overlay.
- Ordinary session-store worker reads in this flow were already canonical. Static tracing identifies a committed-config worker caller, but this experiment does not establish that it is the caller in a production CPU profile.
- Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Prompt-prefix suite: 14 tests pass. Line-cap/format proof passes; All final check:changed checks pass except the three exact-parent unused-export failures described below; exact-head hosted checks remain required before landing.

The fixture does not model a 35 GiB database or 62,000-file workspace. Whole-turn CPU/GC is noisy under profiling and concurrent local checks; no end-to-end speedup claim is made.

The initial changed-file run found a line-cap violation and parameter-reassignment lint error; both are fixed and their focused checks pass. It also reported three unused exports reproduced on exact parent 858b5b01338e598af8bbcc6d4cc0b8c46a157394: TELEPORT_PT and QA_UX_STREAM_END_MARKER were introduced by that parent (#198293), and RELEASE_VALIDATION_WAIVERS by 2a1285197991490df98f847f425f2c7fdb41d433 (#173437). These are recorded as main regressions, not ignored. The final changed-file run completed with only those three inherited failures; every other changed-file check passed. Exact-head CI remains required before landing.

prs.title: fix(browser): name both accepted upload sources when a path matches neither root
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes [#197015](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/197015): `browser` `action:"upload"` rejects a path outside both managed upload roots with only the inbound-media error (`Invalid path: must stay within inbound media directory (~/.openclaw/media/inbound)`). The message suggests only chat attachments can be uploaded and hides the fact that a file staged under `<tmp>/uploads` is also accepted, so an agent that generated a file has no hint of the working recovery path.

`resolveUploadPaths` (`extensions/browser/src/browser/paths.ts`) already tries the uploads directory first and then the inbound media root, but when both checks failed it returned only the inbound error.

## Solution

When the inbound media check also fails, append guidance naming the uploads directory as the other accepted source:

```
<inbound error>. Uploads must be placed in the uploads directory (<tmp>/uploads) or reference a direct inbound media file
```

No permission surface changes; the same two roots remain the only accepted sources.

## Evidence

### Regression test (real tool dispatch)

`browser-tool.upload-rejection.test.ts` drives the shipped `createBrowserTool().execute("upload", …)` path with a file matching neither managed root. No browser, node, or gateway mock is involved; `resolveExistingUploadPaths` runs for real, so the thrown error is exactly what an agent sees in production.

- GREEN (this PR): the test passes — the real error names both sources.
- RED (pre-fix resolver): the same test fails — the real error names only the inbound directory and contains no "uploads directory".

The full `paths.test.ts` suite (which covers the resolver fixture matrix, including the outside-root rejection) and the new real-dispatch test pass together (13/13); related `browser-proxy-upload.test.ts` and `pw-tools-core.upload-paths.test.ts` also pass (34/34 total).

- `tsc --noEmit -p extensions/tsconfig.json`: 0 errors in the changed files (1951 pre-existing errors are all in other extensions).
- `node scripts/run-format.mts` clean; `git diff --check` clean.

Closes #197015
### Real behavior proof — shipped CLI entry point (RED → GREEN)

Executed through the **shipped CLI** (`openclaw browser upload <paths...>`), the real product entry point, with the checkout's browser plugin loaded — no mocks, no test harness, no helper invocation.

**GREEN (this PR's head, `openclaw browser upload /tmp/openclaw/downloads/x.pdf`):**
```
$ openclaw browser upload /tmp/openclaw/downloads/x.pdf
Error: Invalid path: must stay within inbound media directory (/home/0668000622/.openclaw/media/inbound). Uploads must be placed in the uploads directory (/tmp/openclaw/uploads) or reference a direct inbound media file
```

**RED (same CLI command against the pre-fix resolver):**
```
$ openclaw browser upload /tmp/openclaw/downloads/x.pdf
Error: Invalid path: must stay within inbound media directory (/home/0668000622/.openclaw/media/inbound)
```

The CLI upload action (`extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.ts:311`) calls `resolveExistingUploadPaths` before any gateway or file-chooser hook, so this is the exact production path a user hits. The error message now names **both** accepted sources — the uploads directory (`/tmp/openclaw/uploads`) **and** direct inbound media (`media/inbound`) — fixing #197015's complaint that the message hid the uploads root. Output contains no IPs, API keys, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints.

prs.title: fix(discord): Activity hangs on npm installs because the SDK asset returns 404
prs.body:
Related: #127421

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Discord Activity iframe spins forever when the Discord plugin is installed from npm or ClawHub, because the Activity shell's Embedded App SDK request returns 404.

## User Impact

User impact: Discord Activities load their SDK again on standalone plugin installs. Source checkouts and bundled dist builds keep working as before. This PR covers only the asset half of #127421. The Entry Point command deletion in `reconcileGlobalCommands` is left alone, because ClawSweeper routes that half to coordination with the open Activities work first, so the issue stays open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The published `@openclaw/discord` package copies the generated SDK to `dist/assets/embedded-app-sdk.mjs` (`openclaw.build.staticAssets`), but `registerDiscordActivities` resolved `assets/embedded-app-sdk.mjs` against the plugin root. That path exists in a source checkout and in the bundled dist layout (`dist/extensions/discord/assets/`), and not in the standalone package. Registration now resolves both candidates and uses the one that exists, the same two-layout lookup `extensions/diffs/src/plugin.ts` uses for its viewer runtime. When neither exists, it keeps the old path, so the vendor route still answers 404 and retries the read on the next request.

## Evidence

- Red first. Test commit 013848773c2 adds a case to `extensions/discord/src/activities/interaction.test.ts` for each layout. Each registers the plugin against a temp root holding the SDK in that layout, then fetches `/discord/activity/vendor/embedded-app-sdk.mjs` through the registered route handler. With only the test commit applied, the standalone-package case fails with `expected 404 to be 200` (1 failed, 18 passed). With the fix (d086ab61e08), 19/19 pass.
- Published artifact. With the unpacked `@openclaw/discord@2026.9.8` tarball from `npm pack` as the plugin root, the same route returned `404` (9 bytes) with main's `register.ts` and `200` (159348 bytes, contains `DiscordSDK`) with this branch. The tarball has `dist/assets/embedded-app-sdk.mjs`, and its `assets/` holds only `icon.png` and `activity.svg`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/activities`: 6 files, 54 passed. `oxfmt --check` clean and `oxlint` 0 warnings and 0 errors on the 2 changed files. `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` (through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`) exit 0. `check-line-cap-ratchet --base upstream/main` OK on the 2 changed files.
- Test cost. `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/activities/register.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on 4bee5b11580 (before the rebase): 13 passed, 8.2s wall on a warm run (vitest reports 6.46s, 77% of it transform), 15.9s on a cold run. The 13 tests take 50ms in total; the two new layout tests take 18ms and 5ms. In CI the file ran in `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` (job 111259868399), inside the `vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` shard of 7 files and 72 tests, which took 31.85s (86% transform); the file's own tests add about 0.05s of CI time.
- Not verified: a real Discord client opening the Activity. Even with the SDK served, the client handshake still depends on the Entry Point half of #127421.

AI disclosure: an AI agent (Claude Code) reproduced the 404 against the published package, wrote the test and the fix, and ran the gates above: `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/activities/register.test.ts`, `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/activities`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt --check`, and `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main`.

Rebased 2026-10-27 onto main 183f52b9cd7 (head d086ab61e08). Main's #184882 deleted `activities/register.test.ts` and moved its route registration test into `interaction.test.ts` on the shared `createRegisteredActivityFixture` helper. The two layout tests moved there too, and the helper's `vendorAssetPath` argument now also accepts a resolver function so a test can map each relative path into its temp root. No change to the fix in `register.ts`. On d086ab61e08: `interaction.test.ts` 19/19 with the fix and 1 failed, 18 passed without it; the activities directory 4 files, 52 passed; oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files; `tsc --noEmit -p extensions/discord/tsconfig.json` reports no errors in `activities/` (2 errors elsewhere, in `outbound-payload.ts` and `voice/audio-worker-thread.ts`, which this PR does not touch). Not rerun on this head: the packed-tarball HTTP proof, the test-cost timings, tsgo, and autoreview.

## Maintainer verification

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes. Additional packed-artifact HTTP proof, source/bundled Gateway controls, live-call outcome, and the offline standalone-install trust limitation are recorded in [this handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164439#issuecomment-5973429815). A maintainer must confirm via a real ClawHub install or accept the handler-boundary evidence; standalone Gateway acceptance is not claimed.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep silent replies in replay so the session prefix stays append-only
prs.body:
## Problem

A deliberate silent reply (`NO_REPLY`) broke the prompt cache prefix on role-alternating transports.

- Replay dropped the silent assistant row, so the user turn before it and the next user turn became adjacent.
- OpenAI Chat Completions and Bedrock Converse merge adjacent user turns. The merge rewrote an already-sent user message, and every later request missed the cache from that point.
- Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses and Google kept the turns separate, so they did not break.

## Fix

- Replay keeps a silent reply. It drops one only when another assistant turn follows, which keeps the #99620 protection: two assistant turns are never merged into one message.
- A silent reply that is the newest stored row is also kept. The current prompt is appended after replay, so dropping it on that request and keeping it on the next would itself change the prefix.
- The decision depends only on the row after the silent reply. That row is fixed once written, so a sent prefix never changes.

## One invariant across five transports

New fake servers (`test/helpers/fake-model-transports.ts`) speak the five wire formats: `anthropic-messages`, `openai-responses`, `openai-completions`, `google-generative-ai` and `bedrock-converse-stream` (Bedrock uses a hand-built AWS event stream). Each transport has its own e2e file that runs one Gateway scenario:

first turn → background exec → subagent spawn and completion → inter-session send → skill install → workspace `AGENTS.md` edit → silent turn → next turn → compaction → turn after compaction.

The test canonicalizes each request (cache markers removed) and asserts **exactly one prefix break, at compaction**.

| Transport | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic Messages | pass | pass |
| OpenAI Responses | pass | pass |
| OpenAI Chat Completions | **break at silent turn** | pass |
| Google Generative AI | pass | pass |
| Bedrock Converse | **break at silent turn** | pass |

## Design references

- Hermes treats prompt caching as an invariant, with compression as the only exception (`AGENTS.md:18-21`), and asserts breaks with `prefix_breaks` (`tests/e2e/core/history/_helpers.py:214`). The e2e assertion here copies that shape: count breaks and allow exactly one, at compaction.
- Pi keeps system prompt and tools as the leading log entry, and sends later system changes as deltas (`packages/agent/src/agent.ts:78-87`, `packages/ai/src/types.ts`). OpenClaw already sends in-history system updates and retained runtime context this way; the fake matrix shows that path holds on all five transports.
- Not copied: Pi's per-transport `collapseSystemMessages` rebuild (`packages/ai/src/utils/transcript.ts`). Rebuilding the system block on transports without mid-conversation system messages would change the prefix.

## Evidence

- Unit: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts` 60/60.
- E2E (fake servers): all five transport files pass on this head. On `main`, Chat Completions and Bedrock fail at the silent turn.
- Real provider routes were not measured for this change. Proof is request-byte stability against the fakes, not provider `cacheRead` numbers.

## Not in this PR

- Google managed explicit caching still opts out of retained runtime context (`buildGoogleGeminiReplayPolicy`). Removing that needs a live Gemini cache measurement.
- Remote worker turns still render the system prompt each turn. Pinning them needs a worker protocol change.

prs.title: fix(acp): relay exec approvals when Claude CLI and MCP tool call IDs differ
prs.body:
Closes #197829

## What Problem This Solves

In `openclaw acp` with an agent on the `claude-cli` runtime, an exec approval never reaches the ACP client. The Gateway creates the approval and the bridge receives `exec.approval.requested`, but the bridge never sends `session/request_permission`. The turn stalls until someone resolves the approval in the Control UI, a channel, or `openclaw approvals resolve`.

Cause: the bridge matched raw approval events by tool call ID. Claude CLI streams its own ID (`toolu_…`), while the OpenClaw MCP loopback exec request carries a fresh `mcp-<uuid>` ID, so the IDs never match and the relay drops the approval silently.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already stores the requesting run on every exec approval (`request.runId`; for agent runtimes it is the runtime-verified run). The bridge now matches a raw approval by that run ID against its pending prompts, and only within the same session key. Approvals without a run ID keep the existing tool-call matching. A run ID that matches no active prompt in that session is not relayed (fail closed).

The Gateway approval handlers are unchanged. An earlier revision of this PR added a second, runtime-only `runId` field to the approval event. That field is not needed: the relay only selects which ACP client is asked, the decision is still resolved through the Gateway with the client's own authority, and a caller that can create approvals can already target a session's single pending prompt by omitting the tool call ID. Matching the stored run ID gives the same routing with less code.

## User Impact

ACP clients (for example T3 Code) get the normal permission prompt (Allow once / Allow always / Deny) for `claude-cli` exec requests, and the turn continues after the decision.

## Evidence

Real end-to-end on this host: isolated Gateway (own state, port and profile), `claude-cli` runtime with Claude Haiku 5.5, exec policy `security=allowlist ask=on-miss`, and a minimal stdio ACP client against `openclaw acp` (`initialize`, `session/new`, `session/prompt` "Use your shell tool to run exactly: date"). The client answers any `session/request_permission` with Allow once. The real Claude Code binary ran through a shared Anthropic-compatible proxy because the host subscription is at its weekly limit.

| Build | Streamed tool ID | Approval tool ID | `session/request_permission` | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main `c19ae286a00c` | `toolu_01UXDF8…` | (Gateway approval created) | 0 in 135 s | prompt still open; client timeout cancels; approval fails with `run-aborted` |
| this branch `2df9d19bc066` | `toolu_01HjeeeT…` | `mcp-db289ab7-…` | 1 (allow-once, allow-always, deny) | Allow once → `date` output, `stopReason: end_turn` in 28 s |

Tests:
- `src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts`: new regression (two concurrent ACP turns, different tool IDs, stale run and other-session events ignored, approval routed to the second turn). Red on the base, green on the branch; all 11 tests pass.
- `src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts`: 4 passed.
- Type-aware oxlint on the changed files: clean.

Accepted edge case: if a runtime ever records a run ID that differs from the ACP prompt's run, the approval is not relayed (same fail-closed behavior as today).

Maintainer follow-up on the contributor branch: replaced the Gateway event field with the stored run ID (net change now touches only `src/acp`), kept the contributor's regression test shape.

prs.title: perf(gateway): share policy decisions across session lineage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A deep session/child lineage re-enters the same access-policy plugin at every level of an admitted source check. The repeated async-context entry allocates and burns main-thread CPU on GitHub actions. The separate internal-error/false-revocation repair has landed in #198245.

## User Impact

The candidate shares one successful matching policy decision within each synchronous admitted source check. It preserves every captured person, source signal, session restriction and plugin-scope check, and checks authority again before later asynchronous effects. It does **not** share authorization across requests or across awaits.

**The delegated performance owner explicitly accepted the two measured shallow-check tails.** The complete controlled campaign reduces median CPU 64–72% and allocation 65–68%, while depth-1 active and model maximum segments regress. The acceptance is quoted verbatim below; the causes remain unestablished. Landing still waits for final-head ClawSweeper zero open items and native exact-head gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

The access owner identifies an uninterrupted grant by exact policy object, configuration object and captured person/role/grant inputs. Reuse additionally requires the same plugin scope and call. The registration owner admits the ambient scope on every visit; quiesced/retired instances use ordinary invocation. Unclassified callbacks always execute. The synchronous decision list is cleared in finally on both success and failure.

Generic source-callback deduplication and an async-store early return are deliberately avoided: opaque callbacks can alter authority, and plugin listener mutations must remain isolated. `PluginInstance`, `PluginInvocationScope` and the generic source assertion owner are unchanged. The role owner also uses `Object.keys` instead of allocating every key/value pair with `Object.entries`; own-key matching, precedence and case handling are preserved without a role cache.

Production delta **+131 LOC**: the synchronous decision owner and precise person/grant/plugin-context identity account for growth. Tests +125; benchmark +92 net. No schema, configuration or cross-request cache change.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule recorded before the first run:

- Measure active admitted checks, prepared model checks, GitHub edit inspection and GitHub edit at depths 1/4/16/64. Record plugin entries, source assertions, main-thread CPU, allocated bytes, elapsed time and maximum segment.
- Separate untraced timing, allocation, instrumented census and profiles. At least five interleaved AB process pairs, with an AA pair inside each arm; report medians, p95 and spread, pinned source and host load.
- Repeated plugin entries must become constant per matching decision, and depth-16/64 CPU and allocation must improve at least 20%. A 20% regression in depth-1 cost, action latency or maximum segment stops landing for investigation.
- Cross-user identity, one unauthorized deep source and changed/revoked grants must still refuse before external writes. Internal errors preserve the recovery behavior from #198245.

### Pinned workload

Head `d280895843dbf8533463bdabe45e75944ed90112`, integrated main parent `2ca47150600a6946f638dfd9de73f8707830258c`. All performance owners and runner are byte-identical to measured candidate `c3855348adcebee8621900e60ac37aaf1d57dcc3`. Baseline `5a1c9b58767f360a5823c0c8c5be9057bd987b71`.

Committed runner: `scripts/perf/github-action-scope-measure.ts`, SHA-256 `145fed3f7b3995709f7d146419e69d042969cf13dc69e00f8849f2825190e1d1`.

```sh
TMPDIR=/mnt/lane2458/testtmp node scripts/perf/github-action-scope-measure.ts \
  --capsule "$CAPSULE" --output "$OUTPUT" --lineage --pairs 1 --runs 0 \
  --roles 2000 --sessions 5000 --large-fixture /mnt/lane2458
# Separate runs add exactly one of: --counts, --allocation, --cpu-profile
```

Five baseline/candidate pairs run serially, each with two warm observations per cell. Linux/aarch64, Node 26.12.1, btrfs; synthetic agent DB 37,581,508,608 bytes with 5,000 indexed sessions; 62,000 files/1,116,000,000 bytes inside the actual action workspace; 2,000 role assignments. No production data. Fixture generation completed through the native owner, but no clean deferred-integrity-verification receipt is claimed.

The workload constructs actual session-principal/admitted chains and invokes the registered `sessions.github.action` handler with synthetic GitHub I/O. This is registered-handler/owner performance, not live GitHub-network or standalone Gateway performance. A separate real Gateway WebSocket functional probe at 64 actual lineage levels passes: one policy callback per active assertion, retryable policy error, same retained lineage recovers, then a real grant revoke closes the socket. It is functional transport proof, not timing evidence or a live-model campaign.

### Entry frequency

| Operation | Parent entries at 1/4/16/64 | Candidate entries |
|---|---|---|
| Active assertion | 1 / 4 / 16 / 64 | 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 |
| Prepared model assertion | 2 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 |
| GitHub edit inspection | 111 / 432 / 1716 / 6852 | 111 / 113 / 113 / 113 |
| GitHub edit | 141 / 546 / 2166 / 8646 | 141 / 143 / 143 / 143 |

The final separate instrumented census measures every entry count above on both pinned sources. Model admission performs two independent synchronous checks. GitHub operations retain fresh checks across effects, hence constant entries greater than one. Opaque source assertions remain depth-dependent: 10d active, 20d−5 model, 1070d−260 inspection and 1350d−326 edit in this fixture.

### Complete controlled timing and allocation

**Performance-owner acceptance (verbatim):**

> Lead decision (perf owner for this campaign; Peter delegated these decisions): ACCEPTED. The two depth-1 batch-maximum regressions (+2.643 ms and +6.412 ms on synthetic registered-handler maxima, causes unestablished) are accepted against median CPU −64–72% and allocation −65–68%, plus one policy callback per active check, proven on the real Gateway WebSocket.

**Post-deploy follow-up:** After deploy, watch Team stall logs for any authorization-path stall ≥50 ms attributed to the shallow check. This is a follow-up note, not a deployment or restart request.

All five allocation pairs and all five controlled timing pairs completed. CPU is `threadCpuUsage`; sampled allocation includes objects collected by major/minor GC, not retained heap deltas. Active/model maximum segment is the largest individual synchronous call in each batch; GitHub maximum segment is a 1 ms timer-gap upper bound. Identical Node/JIT flags are used in both arms; they are not asserted to match production flags.

Controlled timing starts each process below physical-host load 16 on 32 logical CPUs, after all task-owned compiler/tests/allocation jobs finish. Actual sampled host load ranged 9.06–20.09, aggregate process CPU 599–3136%. Every started sample is retained even if load rises.

Depth-1 maximum-segment p95 is 3.023 → 5.666 ms for active assertions (+87%, +2.643 ms), and 3.623 → 10.036 ms for model assertions (+177%, +6.412 ms). Deep-chain and GitHub-action segments improve. prs.body:
## Problem

Plugin problems still fail updates and make a healthy Gateway look broken. From 2,720 classified real upgrade failures (plugin layer):

| Cause | Reports |
| --- | ---: |
| Plugin runtime deps not installed after update | 23 |
| Plugin built for an older host / SDK API changed | 17 |
| Bundled channel plugin externalized without migration | 17 |
| Plugin target unavailable for update | 10 |
| Plugin data upgrade left pending | 8 |

Reports with reason `plugin-errors` show the shape: the new Gateway was serving, one plugin failed to load, and the update was rolled back (`Failing check pluginErrors (plugin-errors); plugin discord ...`).

Reproduced on current `main` with a real `2026.10.10` npm install, a managed LaunchAgent Gateway, and a third-party plugin built against the 2026.10.10 SDK (it imports `openclaw/plugin-sdk/heartbeat-runtime`, which `main` removed). After `openclaw update --tag <main tarball>` the Gateway serves without the plugin, but:

- the `gateway restart --preserve-definition --json` an updater runs (with `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS=1`) fails: `"ok": false, "error": "Gateway restart failed: activated plugins reported load errors."`, exit 1. Immutable activation, interruption recovery, and failed-update triage apply the same plugin-health requirement.
- plain `openclaw status` shows nothing about the plugin (`Plugin compatibility: none`); only `status --deep` and `doctor` name it.

## What changed

A plugin that cannot update, load, or migrate stays off for that Gateway boot with a notice. Its config and data are kept, and the next start or update retries it. The update and the Gateway proceed.

- **Restart health**: plugin load errors never make the Gateway unhealthy and never produce the `plugin-errors` wait outcome. They stay in the snapshot (`activatedPluginErrors`) and in update warnings.
- **Update readiness**: plugin-owned Doctor checks (memory-core's semantic-index check) no longer register as post-plugin readiness gates. Core config validation and security checks keep their readiness role.
- **Triage**: pending plugin data migrations and plugin load errors no longer keep a verified update unresolved; they stay warnings in `openclaw update status`.
- **Status**: `openclaw status` shows a **Plugins not loaded** row (`failedPlugins` in JSON), naming the plugin and `openclaw doctor`.
- Docs: updating, status, triage, doctor lint.

## What got deleted

- `requirePluginHealth` on every restart-health caller (lifecycle, update readiness, immutable verification, interruption recovery, triage, successor handoff, Doctor maintenance, diagnostics) and the `plugin-errors` wait outcome. The flag also chose which callers must own the listener before a probe counts; that rule keeps its callers under its own name, `requireOwnedListener`. Immutable activation and interruption recovery can now verify identity over HTTP like the other expected-version callers, since they no longer need plugin errors from RPC.
- The update-readiness tagging for bundled plugin health registrations.
- Pending-migration blocking in triage resolution.
- `test/update-memory-inspection.test.ts`, which covered the removed memory-core readiness gate.

Diff vs `main`: production +58 / -112, tests +79 / -517, docs +19 / -9.

## Proof

Real entry point, isolated profile (`--profile upg8cp`, own LaunchAgent and port, clean env), real `openclaw@2026.10.10` npm install, fixture plugin built with `openclaw.build.openclawVersion: 2026.10.10`.

```bash
npm install -g --prefix /tmp/upg8/prefix openclaw@2026.10.10
openclaw plugins install npm-pack:acme-openclaw-heartbeat-1.0.0.tgz --force --accept-capabilities
openclaw gateway install --port 28789
openclaw update --tag /tmp/upg8/pkg/openclaw-fix8.tgz --yes          # this branch, packed
OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS=1 openclaw gateway restart --preserve-definition --json
openclaw status
```

| Check | `main` (before) | this branch (after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw update` 10.10 → candidate | succeeds, 1 plugin activation error | succeeds, 1 plugin activation error |
| Gateway `/readyz` | 200, `coreReady: true` | 200, `coreReady: true` |
| updater `gateway restart` with update marker | **exit 1**, `activated plugins reported load errors` | exit 0, `ok: true`, `healthy: true`, error listed in `activatedPluginErrors` |
| `openclaw status` | no plugin notice | `Plugins not loaded │ acme-heartbeat · data kept; retried on next start · run openclaw doctor` |
| `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` | names the load error | names the load error (unchanged) |

Latest stable, exact head (`c8bb297`, packed): `openclaw@2026.11.3` with the same plugin loaded (11.3 still exports the SDK subpath), then `openclaw update --tag <branch tarball>`: update exit 0, `Recorded verification: ... core ready; 1 plugin activation error(s)`, `/readyz` ready, status shows `Plugins not loaded │ acme-heartbeat`, the update-marker `gateway restart --preserve-definition --json` returns `ok: true, healthy: true` with `activatedPluginErrors: [acme-heartbeat]`, and `plugins.entries.acme-heartbeat.config.label` still reads `demo`.

Retry and data: after installing a fixed `1.0.1` of the plugin and restarting, the plugin loads (`loaded 1.0.1`), the status row is gone, and `plugins.entries.acme-heartbeat.config.label` still reads `demo`.

The Control UI update panel already shows the run's `plugins` check from the recorded `pluginErrors`; this PR does not change the UI.

Focused tests: restart-health probe/client/progress/deadline/attribution, lifecycle readiness, status scan and overview rows, bundled health checks, triage resolution, update service/command/repair, status summary, fresh Doctor, post-plugin readiness. `pnpm tsgo:core` passes.

## Accepted edge cases

- A required channel plugin that fails to load leaves that channel down until the next start or update fixes it. The Gateway reports ready for core work; `/readyz` channel checks are unchanged.
- Standalone `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` still exits 1 for plugin load errors; updater-invoked Doctor already records them as warnings.
- Failure records written by earlier updaters keep the public `plugin-errors` code.
- Observed while testing, not fixed here: the `2026.9.4` updater fails `global install swap` with a local tarball (`Exit code: 1; very is unverified`) before any plugin work.

prs.title: fix(ui): Gateway event listener errors while chat Details updates are pending
prs.body:
Related: #196820 (found while investigating that freeze; this error is not known to cause it)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: while a chat Details update is waiting on async data, the Control UI logs `[gateway] event listener handler error: Error` for every Gateway event, and Details Automations misses cron updates.

## User Impact

Cron events reach Details Automations even while a chat update is pending, and those console errors no longer appear. "Show more" and "Retry" in Automations also stop throwing in that state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The automations inventory checks each Gateway event against its session binding by reading the parent's props inside the event callback. Details passes `sessionKey` as a conditional expression, and the Solid compiler turns that into a new memo on every read. While an async frame holds the parent's props write, that new memo has no committed value, so an untracked read throws `NotReadyError`. Its message is empty, so the console shows only `Error`. The event guard and the Show more/Retry handlers now read the inventory's own memos, which return the committed binding. Event fencing across session and Gateway changes is unchanged.

## Evidence

The new test in `chat-summary-automations.test.tsx` renders the real component under a parent that passes `sessionKey` the way Details does, holds a props write behind a pending read, then delivers a cron event and clicks Show more.

- **Red on base `68542b21d0`:** fails with `NotReadyError`. The stack is `serve` → `read` ← `sessionKey` getter ← `current` (`chat-summary-automations.tsx:224`) ← `subscribeEvents` callback (`:245`). The production report showed the same frames.
- **Falsifiers on base:** the same held write with a plain getter (`details()?.sessionKey`) does not throw. The conditional getter with nothing pending does not throw either.
- **Each half is needed:** with only the guard fixed, the Show more click still rejects with `NotReadyError`. With only the handlers fixed, the event still throws.
- **Green:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-summary-automations.test.tsx` passes 40/40. The existing session/reconnect fencing test (`fences late pages on session and same-client reconnect boundaries`) still passes.
- **Lint:** the file has the same three `solid(reactivity)` warnings as base, shifted two lines by the new comment.

**Gap:** I couldn't reproduce this in a browser E2E with the mock Gateway. I tried holding `progressCard.get`, `sessions.messages.subscribe`, `session.reactions.list`, and `models.list` across a session switch, and `artifacts.list`, `sessions.processes.list`, `progressCard.get`, and `cron.status` while opening Details and then refreshing its props. None of them staged the Details props write. Which read keeps a frame held in the reporting Mac app is still unknown. The unit test uses the real component and the real Solid runtime.

No UI changes, so no screenshots.

prs.title: fix: PR auto-fix stops following review and CI feedback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes enabled PR auto-fix missing fresh review feedback, repeating already-handled work, and losing attempt state when a scheduled payload fails.

## User Impact

PR auto-fix follows fresh feedback and exact-head checks for the selected PR, and reconciles pending publication requests without replaying them. AutoFix, AutoMerge, and AutoArchive remain separate opt-ins; enabling repairs does not grant merge authority. Existing jobs require explicit re-enabling to install the new revision—there is no implicit migration.

**Status:** open and ready for review, not merged. The real isolated Gateway/model repair→publication→original-request reconciliation→fresh same-PR feedback flow and sanitized UI captures remain unproven. Native GitHub Bot/App eligibility is the integration boundary; a separate branded RoboClaw deployment is not an additional requirement. Local boundary regressions use synthetic GitHub/model I/O and do not close the live-proof gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses the existing native Cron, selected-PR reader, publication receipt, and retry-history owners rather than introducing another watcher. Feedback remains untrusted data. Authority, cancellation, revocation, selected-target checks, and self-only cleanup are retained. App feedback is eligible only with same-head, same-repository native evidence; an outside human PR author is verified by stable integer account ID, not login spelling.

Successful no-op and explicit not-actionable feedback remain deduplicated until the exact revision changes or an observed resolved-to-unresolved thread transition requires reassessment. Both bounded inventory and mandatory fresh rereads reconcile the existing exact-revision receipt owners, including when inventory has advanced to a different thread. Fired payload-failure attempts, retries, and cooldowns survive at the scheduler boundary while cancelled, interrupted, and stale-owner runs remain excluded.

The change verifies the complete attempt-head→accepted-published-head changed-file range and freshly paginates exact-head check contexts beyond the first 100 with bounded consistency/failure handling. Repeated checks from the same App retain one eligible App identity rather than overflowing persisted trigger state; all check records and paging/count/head/repository qualification remain intact. Explicit authenticated Control UI enable of a historical source-less job uses the existing authority-capture owner. Loading or disabling that job does not capture authority, and there is no implicit migration.
