prs.title: fix: prevent Perl child processes from loading workspace-selected modules
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Perl child processes can load workspace-selected modules through `PERLLIB` even when `PERL5LIB` is blocked.

## User Impact

Workspace `.env` files and command environments can no longer redirect Perl library lookup or select its Windows shell using `PERLLIB` or `PERL5SHELL`. Ordinary environment variables remain allowed. Workflows relying on these two variables must supply their runtime configuration through another supported mechanism.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add both variables to the existing shared host environment policy, which covers workspace `.env` loading, inherited host execution environments, and command overrides. Regenerate the macOS policy mirror and update the policy coverage baseline. No new policy owner or configuration option is introduced.

## Evidence

Validated head: `b689a0ba3f452d7121bc623bea1d7770b8e9c958`.

- Focused Vitest run: `src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts src/infra/dotenv-workspace-blocklist.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.pager.test.ts src/infra/dotenv.test.ts`: **48/48 passed** across four files. The same regression assertions failed with the base policy.
- Linux with real `/usr/bin/perl`: the unsanitized environment loads a fixture `strict.pm` and prints `shadowed`; after `sanitizeHostExecEnv`, Perl runs successfully with no fixture output. The unwanted module is not loaded.
- The workspace `.env` production loader drops `PERLLIB`, `PERL5LIB`, and `PERL5SHELL`, while preserving benign `PERL_PROJECT_NAME`; override diagnostics reject the newly blocked keys.
- `pnpm check:host-env-policy:swift`, touched-file formatting, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` passed.

Environment limitations: disk capacity prevented an independent dependency install. The recorded test run used an existing same-base dependency install through a temporary link and a focused Vitest configuration without the unrelated Solid UI plugin; lint likewise omitted the UI-only override. Temporary configuration and links were removed. Full typecheck, macOS app execution, Windows Perl shell execution, and a live Gateway/model flow were not run. The focused proof exercises the real environment sanitizer and workspace loader, including a real Perl subprocess.

Simplification: the production policy grows by two entries; remaining changes are its generated mirror, coverage baseline, and regressions for subprocess execution and workspace loading (45 additions, 2 deletions overall).

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep DM topic approvals in their conversation
prs.body:
Closes #197907

## What Problem This Solves

An exec or plugin approval requested inside a private Telegram bot topic is sent to the root DM, not to the topic. The topic only gets "Approval required. I sent the approval request to Telegram DMs, not this chat." The user has to leave the conversation to find the card.

## User Impact

When the requester is also an approver on the same Telegram account, the approval card and its result stay in the topic where the request started. Other approvers still get their usual DM card. The requester gets one terminal result, whichever approver card is processed first.

This screenshot shows the original bug, before the fix:

![Approval sent outside its private bot topic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/333ff77343c75779e6d844aed454014f26c94525/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-13/telegram-dm-topic-approval.png)

## Why This Change Was Made

With `execApprovals.target: "dm"`, the delivery plan uses only approver DM targets. The approver DM target for the requester is the bare chat id, so the topic was dropped.

- The Telegram approver-DM resolver now carries the origin topic onto the requester's own DM target, only when the bot account and the numeric private chat both match the request origin.
- The redirect notice is not sent when the card already went to the origin topic.
- The terminal-result fallback waits for a later origin card in the same fan-out before it sends a separate result to the topic, so a requester that is processed second does not get two results. A failed edit of the topic card still sends one replacement result.

## Evidence

Live Telegram Test Server E2E, real Gateway + deterministic mock model, leased QA user, Threaded Mode on, `execApprovals: { enabled: true, approvers: [<qa user>], target: "dm" }`, `tools.exec.mode: "ask"`. The user sends `EXEC:/usr/bin/touch ...` inside a fresh DM topic, then taps **Allow Once**.

- `main` at `8ebe740925ca`: the card `Approval required ... /approve <id> allow-once` was posted in the root DM (no topic). The topic got `Approval required. I sent the approval request to Telegram DMs, not this chat.`, and the tap could not find the button in the topic.
- This head `b358a299a60b`: the card was posted in the topic (`topicId=200489`). The tap edited the same card to `Exec approval resolved / Allowed once`, the command ran, and one `EXEC_DONE` reply arrived in the topic. No redirect notice and no message in the root DM. A later `PING:after` in the topic was answered there.

Captured Telegram events (TDLib recorder on the QA user; `msg#` is the tail of the TDLib message id, so equal ids are the same message):

<summary>main 8ebe740925ca (before)</summary>

```text

   97.7s  user  message root DM      msg#985857  PING:rootctx
   97.7s  user  message topic 198770 msg#034433  EXEC:/usr/bin/touch /tmp/c-topics-approval-base
  100.1s  user  tap     Allow Once -> failed
  104.3s  bot   message root DM      msg#131584  PONG:rootctx
  107.2s  bot   message root DM      msg#180160  Approval required. /  / Run: /  / /approve ec14bb47-0f7c-499c-b392-fe0
  108.2s  bot   message topic 198770 msg#228736  Working / 🛠️ Exec running
  109.2s  bot   message topic 198770 msg#277312  Approval required. I sent the approval request to Telegram DMs, not th
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>this head b358a299a60b (after)</summary>

```text
    0.2s  user  message topic 200489 msg#953665  PING:warm
    8.4s  bot   message topic 200489 msg#147968  PONG:warm
    8.6s  user  message topic 200489 msg#147969  EXEC:/usr/bin/touch /tmp/c-topics-approval-fix
   12.4s  bot   message topic 200489 msg#245120  Working / 🛠️ Exec running
   13.4s  bot   message topic 200489 msg#293696  Approval required. /  / Run: /  / /approve fda16bf4-fd1b-4571-9cf5-56f
   13.7s  user  tap     Allow Once -> completed
```

- Regressions red on `main`: with this head's test files on `main` source, 15 cases fail (`approval-native`: matching private-chat approver keeps the origin topic, saved account binding; `approval-handler.runtime`: terminal results on the private topic for every outcome, and all six requester-first/requester-second/expiry/failed-edit fan-out orderings). All pass on this head.
- Focused tests (78 pass on this head): `approval-native`, `approval-handler.runtime` (requester-first, requester-second, expiry and failed-edit orderings), `approval-native-route-coordinator`, `approval-handler-runtime`.

prs.title: fix(imessage): group activation mode now controls replies
prs.body:
Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iMessage groups continuing to use static `requireMention` after an owner runs `/activation mention` or `/activation always`. The command could report success and persist the new mode while iMessage ingress ignored it.

## User Impact

iMessage group owners can change reply behavior with `/activation mention` and `/activation always` without editing channel config, matching Telegram and WhatsApp.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate resolved `requireMention` only from channel config. It now reads `groupActivation` from the exact routed session and uses a valid persisted mode as the per-group override.

If the session read fails or contains no valid activation mode, iMessage preserves the existing configured `requireMention` policy. This change does not introduce a new fail-closed fallback contract. Explicit bot-thread mention policy and authorized control-command admission remain unchanged.

## Evidence (exact head)

- Exact signed head: `21df6ff29c9610a1e34337fabbc1f26bcbafc9ff`
- Frozen base: `466a4b6f5073b5fe83b6a0b479a6dfc8392c82e4`
- Clean merge tree: `065c19a15148006d3d01b2e6fc1f68a53be0b592`
- Focused proof: `pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.activation.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session.activation.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **24/24 passing** across three shards.
- Behavior regression: the exact six-case iMessage test is **6/6 green** on this head and **2/6 red** on the frozen base. The base failures are the missing persisted `mention` and `always` overrides; both session-read-failure fallback cases pass on base and head.
- Static proof: `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, touched-file `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Latest-stable compatibility: `v2026.11.3` (`847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`) already stores `groupActivation` and `groupActivationNeedsSystemIntro`; this branch changes no session schema or migration.
- Canonical pre-PR receipt ran on this exact head for 404 seconds. Every branch-relevant gate passed, including SQLite worker/dialect ratchets, extension typechecks/lint, plugin boundaries, database-first guards, and import cycles. Its only failure was the repository-wide dead-export scan; the exact same three untouched exports fail on the frozen base.
- The iMessage regression test exercises the production ingress decision through the injected session runtime and mock Gateway admission. It does **not** claim live Apple Messages transport proof.
- Live Messages proof remains externally blocked because the isolated macOS pilot is not signed into Messages. No production Gateway, Messages account, or channel state was changed for this repair.

Hosted CI and maintainer review on this exact head remain authoritative.

prs.title: fix(mcp): mcp login prints an unusable sign-in link when the client ID is a JWT
prs.body:
Closes #197356

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw mcp login` prints a sign-in link that cannot be opened when the MCP provider issues a JWT as the client ID. ClickUp's hosted MCP server does this.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can sign in to OAuth MCP servers such as ClickUp from the link `openclaw mcp login` prints, and tools that read that link from the command's output get a working one.

Before, the middle of `client_id` was replaced with `…`, and the provider answered `401 invalid_client`. No error was shown by OpenClaw.

One behavior to know: the link line is now written to stdout as plain text in every console style. With `logging.consoleStyle: "json"`, that one line is no longer a JSON log line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The login printed the authorization URL through the console logger, which masks token-shaped text. A JWT client ID matches that mask. The URL holds no secret (client ID, PKCE challenge, state, redirect, scope), and it is printed for a person to open, so it now goes straight to stdout the way other commands write output that must reach the caller unchanged. Everything else the command prints is unchanged.

## Evidence

Head `cdadc1b492bc54a49ed127fb2a4070f97b966851`, rebased on `main` at `de6dc6249746de070d49c0ed521f39addd63cbb6`. The live output, tests and checks below were rerun at this head.

Since the first revision (`ec60bef41a9`): the source change is the same; the new test was shortened from +29 to +7 test lines after the test-lines ratchet failed in CI, and the branch was rebased.

**Live, real CLI path.** `openclaw mcp set` then `openclaw mcp login` run from source (`src/entry.ts`) in a fresh home against `https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp`, with real discovery and dynamic client registration. `state` and `code_challenge` are replaced below; nothing else is edited.

Before (`src/cli/mcp-cli-oauth.ts` as on `main`):

```
Open this URL to authorize "clickup":
https://mcp.clickup.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=mcp-client-eyJhbG…Nu1I&code_challenge=<challenge>&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Foauth%2Fcallback&state=<state>&scope=read+write&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.clickup.com%2Fmcp
After approval, run openclaw mcp login clickup --code <code>.
```

After (this branch):

```
Open this URL to authorize "clickup":
https://mcp.clickup.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=mcp-client-eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjEifQ.eyJ0b2tlblR5cGUiOiJqd3RfY2xpZW50X2lkIiwidXJpX2hhc2hlcyI6WyJlZWxHRHBqekpOTU9yZ0FJLW5JWTlBIl0sImlzcyI6ImNsaWNrdXAtbWNwLXNlcnZlciIsImlhdCI6MTc5NDQ5NzEzOH0.nYKl0LbVhLkKQUA4ZmxciuCZOEW-BBSu62tTdZfHeMg&code_challenge=<challenge>&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Foauth%2Fcallback&state=<state>&scope=read+write&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.clickup.com%2Fmcp
After approval, run openclaw mcp login clickup --code <code>.
```

The masked link sent to ClickUp's authorize endpoint returns `401 {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Invalid client_id"}`. The client ID shown is a throwaway registration for a callback at `example.com`.

**Tests.** `pnpm test src/cli/mcp-cli.login-loopback.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.oauth.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.oauth-integration.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 56 passed in 4 files (Node 24.22.2, Linux arm64). An existing loopback test now gives the login a JWT-shaped client ID, asserts that `redactSensitiveText` would change that URL, and asserts the URL is written whole. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +7; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0.`

**Checks.** `pnpm check:changed` (Node 24.22.2, Linux arm64 container): 32 of 34 steps pass, including format, lint, `typecheck core`, `typecheck core tests`, the tsgo graph boundary, import cycles and plugin boundaries. The two that fail do so identically on unmodified `main` at `de6dc624974` in the same container, and neither touches a file in this PR:

- `dead export scan`: `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.pending-inputs.ts: bindSessionPendingInputMentionInvitation` and `src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-source.ts: readPendingInputSource` are reported unused.
- `SQLite worker ratchet`: the tool stops with `An error was suppressed during disposal` and outcome `failure` (a tool error), not `rejected` (a finding). This PR adds no SQLite call.

Format and lint of the changed files pass inside `check:changed`.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): admins turn on remote access over a verified personal sign-in
prs.body:
Linear: OCF-511. Builds on #198323 (OCF-530, merged), whose held-sign-in check this uses.

## What Problem This Solves

Turning on remote access (the root ceremony) only worked on direct loopback, so setting up a remote claw needed an SSH tunnel to it.

## User Impact

With the OpenClaw ID lab on, an **admin** who reaches the claw through a verified personal sign-in (Tailscale Serve, Cloudflare Access or another trusted proxy, an enterprise principal) can choose **Turn on remote access** from the identity menu. The dialog is unchanged (Name → Recovery kit → Linking → Done). The person running it is proven on both sides, so setup also links their OpenClaw ID to their profile, and their owner devices arrive as them rather than as the shared owner. **Publish new keys** is offered to them too.

These are refused:
- shared token or password connections over the network;
- members, and people whose current role is not admin. They see "Only an admin can turn on remote access for this claw.";
- anything over the OpenClaw ID tunnel.

**Move to new keys** and owner reset stay machine-local.

## Why This Change Was Made

Such an admin can already change config and run commands on the host, so the ceremony adds little power. Requiring a personal identity and the admin role keeps other tailnet users from claiming the claw (Josh, 2026-11-11).

- **One gate** (`openclaw-id-remote-access.ts`) admits a ceremony step for the loopback operator, or for a personal connection that holds `operator.admin` under its current role policy, with a live source, the same profile and Labs on. Only these actions use it: `check_name`, `prepare`, `commit`, their `account_link_code`, and `publish`. They still run on the protocol's `local_operator` ceremony channel. The connection's own client channel is unchanged, so a personal admin does **not** become an owner client: People, membership writes, invites, device mail and rebind all stay as they were.
- **Live authority is checked at the durable write.** Prepare and commit pass the caller's guard into the authority's store write. An admin who loses the role, changes profile or disconnects mid-ceremony pins no root and admits no device.
- **Setup links the runner's profile.** At commit, the browser's ID token is accepted only if this Gateway redeemed it for the same profile (OCF-530's `verifyHeldOpenClawIdSignIn`, not a second device code). It is then linked through the OCF-510 store, and the owner display claims are kept. A refused link never undoes the commit: "Setting up your access" shows a warning and points to Settings → Profile.
- **Audit.** Each ceremony step, and each refusal the handler makes, writes a Gateway log line (a socket without `operator.admin` is refused earlier, at method dispatch): `openclaw-id: remote access <step> <outcome> code=… route=… via=<auth method> profile=… user=…`, and a trusted `security.event` with hashed IDs.
- **Re-bind decision: loopback only.** Re-bind is a recovery path. It works with remote access off, for lost or leaked keys, and like owner reset it is how the machine's operator takes the claw back if remote access was misused. Allowing it remotely would let a misused remote admin seat move the claw's keys. Nothing in the done-when needs it remotely.
- **Owner reset** is not implemented in the Gateway yet (OCF-319). Re-running the root ceremony on a linked claw stays `already_linked`, and the docs say reset stays on the machine.

## Evidence

**Live against staging OpenClaw ID, Discovery and relay.** A throwaway Gateway built from this branch, with fresh state (a new claw), ran on a disposable lab host behind same-host trusted proxies, driven by headless Chromium. The build was made before rebasing onto main after #198323 landed; the rebase changed nothing in the OpenClaw ID, profile-link or UI paths. alice was an admin (`identityScopes`), bob a person without admin, and a third browser had only the shared password and no personal identity. Nothing else on the host was touched, and everything was removed afterwards.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Non-admin personal sign-in: **Turn on remote access** disabled, "Only an admin can turn on remote access for this claw." | pass |
| Non-admin `check_name` / `prepare` refused; `remoteAccessSetup: null` | pass (refused at dispatch: `MISSING_SCOPE`) |
| Shared password, no personal identity, over the network | pass (refused at connect: `AUTH_UNAUTHORIZED`) |
| Admin personal sign-in: **Turn on remote access** enabled | pass |
| Ceremony completes; the link code comes from the signed-in account; **Setting up your access** ✓ (profile linked) | pass |
| Claw linked at `ocf511-bbf9de-hf2kg.crabd.xyz`, published at Discovery, relay online; the admin is still not an owner client | pass |
| `link_status`: the runner's OpenClaw ID is linked to their profile **and is the claw's owner account** (so owner devices arrive as them) | pass |
| Over the personal sign-in: `rebind_prepare` → `not_local_operator`; `openclawId.people` → `not_owner`; a second `prepare` is refused | pass |
| Gateway audit lines | `openclaw-id: remote access {link_code,prepare,commit,link_profile} success route=personal_admin via=trusted-proxy profile=… user=alice@example.test` |

The final menu screenshot in the run timed out because the done dialog was still open; the status RPC above covers that state. The second `prepare` was refused at Discovery (`code_invalid`, a dummy code) before the authority's `already_linked` check; unit tests cover `already_linked`.

Screenshots (test identities only; the recovery kit step is never captured): [non-admin/admin menus, name step and done step](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198349#issuecomment-6858127773).

**Test budget repair:** ClawSweeper's only actionable finding was the missing allocation for 654 net test lines, not a missing regression or a correctness/security defect. Added `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-remote-admin-setup.txt` with 254 lines beyond the default 400. These preserve focused authorization/refusal, durable-write, profile-link and UI eligibility coverage across distinct owners. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main` now passes: +654, allowance 400, credit 254. This repair changes no source or test inputs; prior behavior proof, focused tests, type checks and lint remain applicable at their recorded heads.

**Tests:** `pnpm test src/gateway/openclaw-id ui/src/components/openclaw-id/{account-menu,make-reachable-dialog}.test.tsx ui/src/lib/openclaw-id ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-openclaw-id.test.ts ui/src/pages/profile src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-{sign-in,rebind}.test.ts packages/openclaw-id-protocol` all pass on `9ea5073240af` (714 tests); the published source-equivalent head was `a59879eb`. New tests:
- `remote-access-setup-handler.test.ts` covers:
  - the admin ceremony, profile link and audit;
  - refusals for non-admin, lowered role, token, password, tunnel and rebind;
  - no owner-client widening;
  - publish and link code;
  - status.
- `authority.ceremony-guard.test.ts` shows the root write refused once the caller is gone.
- UI tests cover the menu for admin and non-admin users and the dialog's profile-link warning.

`pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui` and oxlint on the changed files are clean. Autoreview found:
- P1, the guard was not at the durable write: fixed;
- P2, prepare was not guarded: fixed;
- P2, missing audit for link codes and refused publishes: fixed;
- P2, a tunnel owner can publish: kept, because that is the existing owner capability and publish is not a root ceremony.

**Not covered live:** a new owner browser enrolling over the tunnel and then reconnecting as the linked profile. That is OCF-510's resolution path; this PR proves that the link setup creates the owner account.

prs.title: fix: only label scheduled heartbeat alerts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving an event-driven completion through the heartbeat dispatcher could see it mislabeled as their “First heartbeat alert.” The same event delivery could also consume the state marker, preventing the next genuine scheduled heartbeat alert from receiving the onboarding context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first-alert preamble and its persisted delivery markers now apply only to scheduled heartbeat runs: explicit `interval` wakes and the existing source-less scheduled compatibility path. Explicit event, manual, hook, and other non-scheduled wakes keep their original text and do not advance scheduled-heartbeat onboarding or dedupe state.

A regression test covers the user-visible sequence: an exec completion is delivered unchanged and leaves heartbeat state unset; the following scheduled heartbeat receives the first-alert preamble and persists its state.

## User Impact

Background task and event completion messages are no longer presented as heartbeat onboarding alerts. Users still receive the onboarding explanation on their first genuine scheduled heartbeat alert.

## Evidence

- Regression demonstrated red on unmodified main: the event-driven delivery included the first-heartbeat preamble.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.structured-delivery.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.isolated-session-mirror.test.ts` — 83 passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/heartbeat-dispatch.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/heartbeat-dispatch.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent P0/P1 targeted review — clean after two identified state-ownership edge cases were fixed.

Full local core/test typecheck did not produce a terminal result: one attempt encountered a stale artifact lock left by an interrupted check, and a subsequent run exceeded the local tool timeout. Exact-head CI remains the source of truth for the complete typecheck lanes.


## Production reproduction (2026-09-10)

A real Telegram DM on the contributor's OpenClaw `2026.9.3` runtime reproduced the reported pre-fix behavior at `2026-09-10 15:16:08 GMT+8`.

A background `openclaw doctor` completion was delivered through the heartbeat path and incorrectly received the scheduled-heartbeat onboarding prefix:

```text
First heartbeat alert: your bot runs periodic background checks and messages you only when something needs attention. Set agents.defaults.heartbeat.target: "none" to keep these internal.
补充检查结果：`openclaw doctor` 未成功跑完（退出码 1）……
```

This is user-visible production evidence for the bug mechanism: a background/event completion can be mislabeled as the first scheduled heartbeat alert. It supplements the red-on-main regression test. It is intentionally not claimed as exact-head after-fix proof; the remaining acceptance proof is the bounded Telegram Test Server sequence on `8bc954f7c103b8fa5512e3449acb09c58e1ed42a`: event delivery without onboarding or marker consumption, followed by the first scheduled alert with onboarding, then a later scheduled alert without repeated onboarding.

prs.title: fix(cli): publish CoreDNS config atomically with preserved permissions
prs.body:
Closes #184888

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `openclaw dns setup --apply` rewrites an existing CoreDNS `Corefile` (and its `.server` files) by truncating in place, so a crash or ENOSPC mid-write destroys the operator's DNS configuration with no backup and no recovery copy (the file lives outside OpenClaw's state dir).

## User Impact
A failed publication no longer destroys the previous Corefile or `.server` contents. An existing Corefile keeps its mode, its uid/gid, and its parent directory's mode across the rewrite instead of silently taking the invoker's group or the helper's restrictive defaults. CoreDNS setups that use a symlinked `Corefile`, a symlinked `conf.d`, or a chain like `Corefile -> Corefile.link -> missing file` publish to the final file and keep working; the previous revision of this PR aborted setup on the dangling-chain shape.

## Why This Change Was Made
`writeFileSudoIfNeeded` called `fs.writeFileSync` on the final path (and `sudo tee` as fallback), which truncates before any content is written. It now uses `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s `replaceFileAtomicSync` (temp-file + rename): a failed publication leaves the previous bytes exactly as they were. Options chosen deliberately: `preserveExistingMode: true` so existing rwx bits survive, `dirMode` pinned to the immediate parent's current mode so helper defaults cannot tighten existing directories, and `mode: 0o666 & ~process.umask()` for new files. The `sudo tee` fallback is unchanged.

Two review findings against the earlier revision are fixed at the same owner rather than at call sites:

- `resolvePublicationTarget` walks the whole symlink chain (bounded at 40 hops, reporting `ELOOP`) before publishing. The earlier revision handed a dangling chain's link itself to fs-safe, which rejects a symlink destination and aborted setup where `writeFileSync` used to create the final target. A missing parent still fails like `writeFileSync` instead of creating the directory tree.
- `preservePublicationOwnership` runs in fs-safe's `beforeRename` hook and restores the destination's uid/gid on the staged file, because a rename publishes a new inode and `preserveExistingMode` carries only rwx bits. If the invoking user cannot restore them (`EPERM`), the pre-existing privileged fallback takes over — it edits the existing inode, so the owner is not lost.

The branch was rebuilt as one commit on current `main` because the earlier head merged against a newer main whose test harness had been refactored; the regression tests now use that harness.

## Evidence
Level B (registered `dns setup --apply` CLI entry driven in-process against a real temporary filesystem, with `darwin` platform and `brew`/`sudo` subprocesses mocked):
- Atomic publication: with a rename of the Corefile forced to fail, setup rejects and the previous bytes are byte-identical. Red on `main` (`promise resolved instead of rejecting`), green with this change.
- Operator metadata: an existing Corefile at mode `0640` in a `0755` directory whose gid differs from the publisher's is published with the same gid, mode, and directory mode. Red on the earlier revision of this PR (`expected [ 1000, 416 ] to deeply equal [ 10, 416 ]`), green with this change.
- Symlinked/dangling publication: a `Corefile -> Corefile.link -> missing` chain and a symlinked `conf.d` both publish to the final file. Red on the earlier revision (`Serialized Error: { code: 'symlink', category: 'policy' }`), green with this change.
- All 11 cases in `src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts` pass: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts`.
- Local lanes for this head: core oxlint on both changed files (0 errors), `node scripts/run-format.mts --check`, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety ratchets, and `git diff --check`.
- Test-line budget: the three regressions add 57 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/184888-dns-atomic-corefile.txt` (the ratchet's allocation mechanism), so this PR adds no unaccounted test lines. The branch is rebased on current `main`; the local ratchet now reports `Test lines OK ... slack: 1`, which clears the earlier `over by 16` inherited from the older merge snapshot.
Real shipped-CLI run on this head (`node openclaw.mjs dns setup --domain proof.test --apply`, `OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (a15387c)`), Linux host with an isolated loopback netns carrying a `100.64.0.1` tailnet address, a documented `process.platform` preload selecting the macOS-gated path, and `brew`/`sudo` shims (no real Homebrew, sudo, or CoreDNS service):

| fixture | observed |
|---|---|
| `Corefile -> Corefile.link -> missing.conf` (dangling chain) | exit 0; `missing.conf` created with `import .../conf.d/*.server`; both links intact |
| existing Corefile mode `0640` in a `0755` directory | exit 0; mode, uid, gid, and directory mode unchanged, import block appended |
| publication forced to fail by `RLIMIT_FSIZE` (1.5 MB Corefile, 2 MB write limit) | CLI rejects; Corefile byte-identical (same sha256), no temp files left |
| control: the previous `writeFileSync` writer under the same limit | file truncated to exactly 1,048,576 bytes |

Evidence files: `~/openclaw-evidence/pr185017-cli-atomic/{scenario-a2,scenario-b,scenario-c}.log` and `SUMMARY.txt`.

- Known boundaries disclosed deliberately: fs-safe's `applyDirectoryMode` chmods the parent directory even when its mode already matches and does not restore it on failure; the group assertion is guarded and only runs when the test process has an assignable foreign group; the `mode: 0o666 & ~umask` path for a newly created Corefile is implemented but not asserted by the trimmed regression set; the privilege-escalation fallback (`sudo tee`) is unchanged and out of this fix's scope.
- Not obtained: an installed-macOS trace against a real CoreDNS install, including an upgrade from the latest stable. The host is Linux, so the macOS path ran behind a disclosed platform preload and `brew`/`sudo` shims; the gid-preservation case was not exercised because no second group is assignable without root.
- Not run locally: tsgo/extension-boundary lanes (the local checkout uses a shared dependency install that tsgo rejects); CI runs the type lanes for this head.
- Review status for this head: no autoreview helper verdict was produced — the helper's reviewer route failed as unavailable on the authoring host. The ClawSweeper verdict still describes `4154ed2`, the earlier revision; the two P2 findings it lists (ownership, dangling chains) are implemented and regression-covered on this head and need the fresh review to confirm.

prs.title: fix(models): disclose recorded provider failures behind refreshFailed
prs.body:
Fixes #194330

## What Problem This Solves

When a model catalog refresh fails for a provider, the published catalog carries the aggregate `refreshFailed: true` flag without any provider outcome explaining which discovery failed. Channel clients then show a generic "Could not refresh models. Tap Refresh to try again." over a fully populated catalog with no actionable scope. In plain terms: the system says "something failed" but never says what, so users cannot tell whether their configured provider is broken.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recorded acquisition failures go through `createCatalogAttemptReporter.failed()`, which only books providers into the attempt's failure scope; no `ProviderCatalogOutcome` is written for them, so the models.list projection forwards a bare flag. The published catalog now discloses those providers as `status: "unavailable"` outcomes alongside any real discovery outcomes, live with the attempt: settling a provider (successful renewal) withdraws the synthesized disclosure, and a provider that already has its own determinate outcome is never shadowed. Model availability decisions are unchanged — the decision layer gates only on `auth-rejected` outcomes, and ready-only consumers ignore unavailable rows.

## User Impact

Clients reading `models.list` receive the failing provider scope behind `refreshFailed` (e.g. `providerOutcomes: [{provider: "unreachable", status: "unavailable"}]`) and can show which provider failed instead of an unexplained retry notice. No availability or eligibility change.

## Evidence

- Regression: `prepared-model-runtime.publication-events.test.ts > "discloses recorded acquisition failures as unavailable provider outcomes"` — a recorded failure surfaces `{provider: "unreachable", status: "unavailable"}` on the published catalog, the healthy provider's real `ready` outcome is untouched, and `published(["unreachable"])` withdraws the disclosure. Suite 4/4 green.
- Adjacent consumers unchanged: `models-list-result.provider-outcomes.test.ts`, `models-list-result.access-programs.test.ts`, `model-catalog-access-programs.test.ts`, `model-catalog-decisions.test.ts`, `model-catalog-decisions.account-access.test.ts` all green (37 tests).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean; oxfmt clean.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the repository test harness to analyze issue #194330, trace the missing outcome path in prepared-model-runtime.publication-events.ts, and implement the disclosure merge. The implementer understands the code: the synthesized outcomes are disclosure-only and the decision layer's availability gates consume only auth-rejected outcomes. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep streaming replies in view and stop the jump when they finish
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with the keyboard up, a long reply streams below the composer and the reader never sees it; when it finishes, the view jumps to the end or, in about half the runs, stays blank above the "Done in" line until the user scrolls. With the keyboard hidden, every reply visibly jumps up 42 pt the moment it finishes.

## User Impact

Replies stay in view while they stream with the keyboard up, and the finished reply no longer jumps. The "working" status line now sits below the streaming words (where the "Done in" recap appears) instead of above them.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Follow the reply (keyboard up).** The transcript relied on `defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom, for: .sizeChanges)`, which left the scroll offset at 0 while the reply grew thousands of points below the composer; streamed words change no timeline revision, so nothing re-scrolled. The follow modifier now also pins the bottom edge (`ScrollPosition.scrollTo(edge:)`) on every content-height change while following. Edge scrolling does not depend on estimated row heights, and it runs in the modifier, outside the transcript body.
- **One update for the swap.** When the saved reply lands, two things used to happen in different layout passes: the bubble hid itself in its own observation scope, and the transcript added the row. Now the transcript decides whether the bubble shows (from the live-content shape it already reads), and `replaceMessages` shows any paced words still held back so the exact-match suppression sees the same text. Before, the saved row and the bubble were on screen together for a frame (11,600 pt of content), and the bottom anchor jumped into the doubled content, which is what left the transcript blank.
- **No 42 pt jump.** The working indicator sat above the streaming words and vanished when the reply finished. It now sits below them, so the final row takes the bubble's exact position.
- Behavior cases: `stream-turn` and `stream-follow` become guards. `stream-follow` gates on following the reply while it streams; when a row changes height, the grader now reads motion on an edge the reader can see, since a reply taller than the screen can change height above the fold without visible motion. A row that keeps its height still counts as a whole move, so a long reply spanning the screen is still measured (re-grading the last run: `scrolled-up` holds read 0 pt drift with a spanning row in every frame).

Known remaining glitch, reported by the harness rather than gated: in about one run in three, as the final row replaces the bubble, the transcript flashes to the top for one or two frames (`LazyVStack` measures the run group at ~0 for one layout pass, and the bottom anchor follows that). In about one run in three the view also ends scrolled away from the reply until the reader scrolls (main: about half). The harness reports both; tracing the finish swap is the follow-up.

UI change: cc @vyctorbrzezowski for the working-indicator position.

## Evidence

Keyboard up, 6 s into a 12 s reply. Before: the view stays at the top while the reply grows out of sight. After: the newest words sit above the composer.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: keyboard up, reply streams out of view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f813c40b-f18c-4207-958a-6c9ac9c5e4ca) | ![After: keyboard up, reply followed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4df82b4-ae9c-4820-9107-a5f304f8ec37) |

Keyboard hidden. The working status now sits below the streaming words (it was above the first heading), so nothing shifts when the reply finishes.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: keyboard hidden, status above the reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22d22a60-3175-4767-9c43-e6a6eac42c38) | ![After: keyboard hidden, status below the reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c13ee33d-96ff-427f-a0cd-fbf6f0fba347) |

`pnpm ios:behavior`, iPhone 17 simulator, 3 samples per case:

| Case | Kind | Gates (3 samples) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stream-turn` | guard | all 3/3 |
| `stream-follow` | guard | all 3/3 (reply followed while streaming) |
| `scrolled-up` | guard | all 3/3 |
| `keyboard` | guard | all 3/3 |
| `relaunch` | guard | all 3/3 |

Exit 0 with this PR's grading. Reported, not gated: in 2 of 3 `stream-follow` samples the reply ended scrolled away from view after it finished (the known finish glitch below).

On `main` (with #198293) the same `stream-follow` follow gate fails in every sample (p95 ~5,600 pt hidden) and `stream-turn` drifts 42 pt in every sample.

- New regression test `a durable reply retires the live bubble while pacing holds its last words` fails on the base and passes here; `ChatStreamPresentationTests` and `ChatStreamReplayTests` pass.
- `test/scripts/ios-behavior-grade.test.ts`: 6 passed. tsgo, oxlint, SwiftFormat, SwiftLint, native i18n inventory: clean.

Merge danger: two-way door. Revert restores the previous scroll and indicator behavior; no state, config or protocol change. Blast radius: the shared chat transcript on iOS and macOS.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PostgreSQL conformance silently omitting newly added suites until a separate completeness check catches their missing registration.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Developers no longer need a second registration edit for `.postgres.test.ts` suites under `src` or `extensions`. Existing non-suffix suites, directory targets, explicit overrides, and shard budgets remain intact.

The existing #198118 PG16 runtime hold is not waived; this candidate needs its own PostgreSQL execution evidence before landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three independent feature changes added four suites without updating the manual inventory. Discover suffix suites from the checkout and remove their redundant registrations instead of adding another list entry. Keep the independent repository completeness assertion, and add a real-CLI regression for future unregistered suites, overlap, deletion, and explicit overrides.

## Evidence

- Original [job 131944722956](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43442683384/job/131944722956), exact `b4da3463d3`: four omitted suites. Native Node 24.22.1 reproduces exactly those four omissions.

- Controlled future-suite experiment: original selector omits both new suites; candidate includes both without registration. Ordinary tests remain excluded, directory coverage is not duplicated, deletion removes the target, and explicit overrides remain unchanged.
- Four-file pinned format, scoped lint, native syntax checks and diff checks pass. Independent P0–P2 source review found no actionable defects.

The production Team host cannot perform their unqualified build/compiler preparation; the configured remote proof route remains unavailable. prs.title: fix(ios): VoiceOver finds an unnamed chat message editor
prs.body:
Fixes #195775

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unnamed message editor and a redundant placeholder announcement when VoiceOver users navigate the iOS chat composer.

## User Impact

VoiceOver users get a persistent, localized “Message” name for the editor, including after entering a draft, without encountering the decorative placeholder as a second accessibility element. No layout, input behavior, configuration, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native editor owns its accessible name; the SwiftUI placeholder only supplies the visual hint. This reuses the existing “Message” translations rather than adding another naming path.

The contributor’s focused patch is preserved: five production lines (including comments), one assertion in the existing native-editor test, and one regenerated localization-inventory entry. Simplification review found no extra machinery to remove; no unrelated tests were added.

## Evidence

- Source: [@saariuslystoned’s commit 5071eba4973475d92220d1d6e52533907a2350f2](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/5071eba4973475d92220d1d6e52533907a2350f2), from `fix/ios-chat-editor-voiceover-name`, applied to pinned upstream main `37365600bf67cab28ef5e180c5dfbfb400d88f83`. Original merge base: `465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82`. The stable patch ID matches the contributor’s complete four-file diff; all three Swift files are unchanged upstream between those bases.
- **Ran in the Linux sandbox:** `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` regenerated exactly the contributor’s inventory addition; `pnpm native:i18n:verify` and `git diff --check` passed. The existing iOS catalog contains “Message” in English plus 21 translated locales.
- **Pre-existing failures, reproduced without the patch on the exact pinned base:** `pnpm native:i18n:check` reports four missing native Apple translation IDs across 21 locales; `pnpm apple:i18n:check` reports the stale macOS `Localizable.xcstrings` catalog. Neither aggregate check is claimed passing; unrelated locale artifacts were left untouched.
- **Contributor-provided, original-head evidence:** [issue #195775](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/195775) reports that the regression fails on main and passes with the fix. The source commit preserves the production-factory accessibility-label assertion. The issue and commit do not include an exact Apple test command, execution log, or device/Simulator result, so this is reported evidence, not independently reproduced proof on this rebased candidate.
- **Independent review:** bound Auto Review, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, reviewed all four changed files against the pinned base with P0–P2 coverage; result `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. This was source review, not runtime validation.
- **Coverage gaps:** Swift/Xcode, SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, iOS tests, and VoiceOver traversal with empty/populated drafts and translated locales were not run here because Apple tooling is unavailable. Native-test wall time and CI seconds are unavailable. Published ready for review as explicitly requested without waiting for Apple-toolchain reruns; CI and maintainer review remain outstanding. This changes accessibility metadata only, so no visual before/after screenshots are claimed.

### CI follow-up (2026-11-10)

At unchanged head `04858f7d603a539bbcbbc6c3a52201d26e1629e0`, the four failed checks in run `42578397803` are a tool-download infrastructure failure and its dependent missing-report failures, not a reported source/test failure:

The download returned HTTP 504 through all three built-in retries, then curl exited 56 before project generation or the iOS index build. The log does not identify which of the script’s two archives failed.
- [Scan iOS dead code](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42578397803/job/129033757937) and [Scan shared kit from iOS](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42578397803/job/129033758055): report-completeness gates failed with `REPORT_COMPLETE=false` and empty scan-result outputs; these are not dead-code findings.

The installer and workflow are unchanged by this PR. No source repair, CI rerun, or toolchain installation was performed for this attribution; the iOS Periphery checks remain incomplete, not passing. Rechecked the local tree against the published head (identical) and `git diff --check` (passed). The existing P0–P2 source review still covers this unchanged diff.

prs.title: fix(ios): VoiceOver skips question option descriptions
prs.body:
Fixes #195776

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: VoiceOver omits the explanation beneath a question option when an agent asks the user to choose an answer.

## User Impact

User impact: an option such as “Pizza” with the description “Fast” now exposes “Pizza, Fast” as its accessible label. Missing or blank descriptions keep the original label, and selection-state announcements remain unchanged in the code. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared native question button overrides its accessible label with only the option title. Include a trimmed, nonblank description in that same label without changing the visual layout, selection behavior, or submission path. This shared component also serves macOS.

The contributor’s two-file patch and regression test are preserved unchanged. Simplification review retained the small label helper and existing-suite test: production +9/−1 lines, tests +8 lines; no unrelated tests, localization repairs, or new state.

## Evidence

- **Contributor-reported, original-head evidence:** [the issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/195776) states that a test fails on main and passes with the fix. [Source commit 8c422ac87e7552b1ca4f4c0eca2fad44e6ca9a29](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/8c422ac87e7552b1ca4f4c0eca2fad44e6ca9a29) adds helper assertions for a description, no description, and whitespace-only description. The inspected issue/commit provide no Apple command output or simulator/VoiceOver run; this is contributor-reported evidence, not a rerun on this PR head.
- **Ran in the isolated Linux sandbox:** `git diff --check` and `pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` passed. Byte comparison confirmed both applied files exactly match fork HEAD and both pre-change files match the contributor merge base. Static inspection confirmed the rendered button uses the new helper and retains the selected-state accessibility value. These checks do not establish runtime VoiceOver behavior.
- **Independent Auto Review:** OpenClaw engine, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Reviewed the complete two-file local candidate against `37365600bf67cab28ef5e180c5dfbfb400d88f83`; that unchanged candidate was committed locally as `b8d81800469ca803c06eca5997c2a05d56ba546e`. prs.title: fix(msteams): avoid stalls on unfinished outbound mentions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long stalls when outbound Microsoft Teams text contains many unfinished mention markers.

## User Impact

Teams messages with malformed mention-like text are formatted promptly. Valid mentions, escaped display names, and documentation examples retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the repeated regular-expression search with a forward scan in the existing activity builder. This removes repeated scans of the same suffix while retaining Teams ID validation and matching mention entities. The necessary parser growth is 26 net production lines; the regression adds 14 test lines across four distinct malformed-input shapes.

## Evidence

Head: `b4b6b570a3ada366c0600c37b2a5e6e3fe428f10`.

- Focused Vitest run of `extensions/msteams/src/mentions.test.ts`: 8/8 passed. Each hostile-input case uses 32,000 repeats, verifies unchanged malformed text and a valid preceding mention, and completes below 250 ms.
- The same tests against the base parser: all four new cases failed the 250 ms bound (4.4–12.7 seconds); the four existing cases passed.
- Differential comparison against the previous regex: 300,000 random inputs produced identical text and entities.
- Focused formatting, lint, and strict TypeScript checks passed; `git diff --check` passed.

Environment: Linux, using matching pinned tooling from an existing checkout because this source-only worktree lacks installed dependencies. No live Teams delivery was exercised. Additional runtime evidence below covers the shipped final-reply controller and SDK through an isolated HTTP connector. Remaining regression risk is mention-syntax compatibility, covered by existing cases and the differential comparison.


### Additional final-reply runtime evidence

At the same head, an isolated Linux harness bundled the current production reply controller, formatter, mention builder, and workspace packages, and used the installed Microsoft Teams `HttpStream` with a loopback HTTP connector. Each scenario emitted a final message, received HTTP 201, preserved the `29:abc` mention entity, and matched canonical Markdown rendering:

```text
unclosed-name: 96,013 final bytes; 832 ms; passed
empty-open: 64,013 final bytes; 740 ms; passed
unclosed-id: 192,013 final bytes; 683 ms; passed
benign control: 26 final bytes; 605 ms; passed
```

These oversized synthetic cases exercise local formatting and SDK delivery; the loopback endpoint accepts them without claiming that the live Teams service accepts oversized messages. A supplementary backslash-heavy case reached the connector with correct rendered text and mention entities but exceeded the harness's 10-second full-path budget. That broader formatting/streaming cost remains a limitation; the direct activity-builder regression cases all pass. No live Teams credentials or shared Gateway state were used.

prs.title: feat(compaction): let one agent use its own compaction model
prs.body:
Related: #196207, #52732

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway with several agents can set only one compaction summarization model, `agents.defaults.compaction.model`, for all of them. Agents that chat on different providers then share a summarizer that fits one of them and fails for another: in our deployment an agent running on a local model had every `/compact` refused by the shared hosted summarizer, while the other agents needed that hosted model for their large contexts.

## User Impact

Operators can set `agents.entries.<id>.compaction.model` to give one agent its own summarization model. It takes precedence over `agents.defaults.compaction.model` for that agent's sessions and accepts the same values (`provider/model-id` or a configured bare alias). Omitting it changes nothing. This adds one config key; no migration, state change, or default change.

## Why This Change Was Made

#196207 reopened `agents.entries.<id>.compaction` for the summary limit. This adds the model beside it and nothing else: thinking level, provider, timeout, and the other compaction settings stay shared.

The model was read in three places: target selection, the gate that keeps an explicit model off the session fallback chain, and ChatGPT V2 eligibility. All three now call one resolver, so an agent-scoped model behaves exactly like the shared one. It is used as configured, without the fallback chain, and it keeps provider-native V2 compaction out. A model-locked session still summarizes with its own model.

A caller that supplies neither an agent id nor a session key keeps the shared default; it does not guess an agent.

<details>
<summary>Scope notes</summary>

- Doctor's model-ref repair and the configured-model-ref collector already read `<agent>.compaction.model`, so the key needs no new Doctor code.
- Not changed: the Codex app-server warning about ignored compaction overrides still names only the shared keys.
- The key stays in the advanced config tier; `agents.defaults.compaction.model` remains the common-tier entry.

</details>

## Evidence

The change was written on `2f95bd3c3a5` and then rebased onto `a48a3175600` (this commit, `b88f9400940`). The only conflict was the generated config baseline, which I regenerated (core paths 2654 → 2655).

Red before the change, green with it, same four assertions (measured on `2f95bd3c3a5`):

| Test | Base | With change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `zod-schema.agent-defaults.test.ts` › accepts a per-agent compaction model | `Unrecognized key: "model"` | pass |
| `compaction-runtime-context.test.ts` › prefers the session agent's compaction model | resolved the shared model | pass |
| `chatgpt-v2-compaction.test.ts` › keeps explicit opt-outs … out of V2 | V2 stayed eligible | pass |
| `compact.hooks.test.ts` › never falls back from an explicit agent compaction.model | fell back to the session chain | pass |

Run on `b88f9400940` (after the rebase):

- Changed test files, each with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `zod-schema.agent-defaults` 9/9, `compaction-runtime-context` 37/37, `chatgpt-v2-compaction` 20/20, `compact.hooks` 89/89.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` (all shards) pass.
- `config:docs:check`, `config:schema:check`, `docs:check-config-examples`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (+36 net test lines) pass.
- `oxfmt --check` on the changed files and `oxlint` on the 14 changed TypeScript files are clean.

Run on `2f95bd3c3a5` plus this change, not repeated after the rebase:

- Consumers of the changed call sites, 40 files, all passing: config schema suites (13 files), compaction preparation, admission, queued and summary-fallback (6), prompt phase, prompt helpers and attempt session (5), `agent-runner-memory*` (11), CLI compaction (2), `runtime-llm.runtime`, `model-resolution-consistency`, `server.sessions.compaction`.
- `server.sessions.compaction.test.ts` failed once with an RPC timeout in `sessions.patch waits for terminal compaction before archiving the session` while other jobs loaded the host; the file passed 21/21 on its own rerun. The test does not exercise the changed code.
- `pnpm lint:core` exited 1 with 23 `max-lines` errors, none in a file this PR touches. The full `pnpm lint` wrapper timed out twice in the `plugin-sdk boundary dts` preparation step on a loaded host.
- `plugin-sdk:surface:check` failed on the export budgets (for example 3888 > 3867 public exports). This PR changes no file under `src/plugin-sdk` and no package export. I did not run the check on the base commit alone.
- `plugin-sdk:api:diff` did not finish locally; I stopped it after more than 75 minutes on a loaded host. The public config type gains the optional `agents.entries.<id>.compaction.model` field; no SDK export is added or removed.

Live run, on a Gateway running a 2026.11.3 backport of this change (`agents.defaults.compaction.model` is `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, one session of one agent, `openclaw sessions compact`, debug logging on for the two runs):

```
[compaction-diag] start … sessionKey=agent:developer-verifier:compaction-proof-a … trigger=manual provider=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 attempt=1 maxAttempts=1
[compaction-diag] end   … provider=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 … outcome=compacted
# openclaw config set agents.entries.developer-verifier.compaction.model anthropic/claude-opus-4-7
[compaction-diag] start … sessionKey=agent:developer-verifier:compaction-proof-a … trigger=manual provider=anthropic/claude-opus-4-7 attempt=1 maxAttempts=1
[compaction-diag] end   … provider=anthropic/claude-opus-4-7 … outcome=compacted
```

`openclaw config validate` accepts the key and still rejects a misspelled sibling (`agents.entries.main.compaction: Unrecognized key: "modell"`). The config write was applied as a hot reload without a Gateway restart.

Not covered: the live run used the 2026.11.3 backport, not this branch on `main`; no run on `main` against a real model. The consumer suites and the plugin SDK checks above were not repeated on the rebased commit.

prs.title: fix: keep links intact across streamed reply chunks
prs.body:
Fixes #151147

## What Problem This Solves

Long links can break when a streamed reply is split into separate message chunks.

## User Impact

Links that fit the channel's delivery limit stay intact across streamed chunks. Explicit chunk limits remain hard ceilings; oversized links still split so delivery can continue.

Default delivery may emit a fitting link beyond the preferred chunk size, up to the channel limit. The optional `hardMaxChars` contract and that default behavior still need streaming/SDK-owner acceptance. Existing SDK callers that omit it retain their current ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chunker needs to distinguish a preferred split point from the absolute delivery limit and recognize unfinished links across deltas. This uses the shared Markdown parser for complete links and buffers incomplete destinations, while preserving paragraph separators, reference citations, decimal boundaries, tables and code fences.

The reconciliation incorporates main at `632f7ffaf51409229e6ebcabad07d9d7615bf70e`, including #187434, #190710, #196039 and #183707. Both internal callers of the parser's definition metadata were updated together; that helper is not exported by the package.

## Evidence

Candidate: `a7b871bfaacfabce13cae2eaabd838fd17dd9483`.

- Two integration regressions reproduced before repair and passed afterward: a fitting link discarded preceding visible paragraph separators; a reference-definition destination was treated as complete while still streaming.
- 80 tests passed again after the lint repair across the utils/link-span, table and mutable-preview suites (15.17 seconds Vitest; 23.78 seconds including the runner). These used a prepared dependency graph with version drift, so they are diagnostic results, not frozen-lock acceptance.
- Syntax, repository formatting and whitespace checks pass. The test-line check passes: 419 net test lines with the standard 400-line allowance plus a documented 19-line allocation. That allocation preserves distinct link, explicit-ceiling and paragraph/source-boundary regression coverage.
- Independent manual review of the conflict/repair delta found no further P0-P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper completed the full committed range from `632f7ffaf51409229e6ebcabad07d9d7615bf70e` to `5ebefc7deacf5b08343869d6444e6315ab8bdc06`, with no concrete correctness or security findings. Its recommendation is keep open pending real-channel delivery proof; it did not run tests or establish merge readiness. A fresh independent source review of the subsequent two-file lint/allocation repair found no actionable P0-P2 findings; the full range was not re-reviewed.
- Main chunker and block-streaming config suites failed during setup before assertions because subprocess compilation could not resolve workspace dependencies, including `quickjs-wasi` and `@lancedb/lancedb`; `smol-toml` was also unresolved.

[CI run 43453539329](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43453539329) at `5ebefc7deacf` passed 38 jobs, including production/test typechecks and all selected test jobs. It failed the map-copy lint rule and the test-line budget. This follow-up removes the unnecessary object copies and records the exact 19-line allocation. [Fresh CI run 43466111388](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43466111388) completed successfully at `a7b871bfaacfabce13cae2eaabd838fd17dd9483`: 43 successful jobs, 29 skipped and no failures, including production/test types, lint, baseline ratchets and the aggregate CI gate. prs.title: fix(chat-ui): keep a budget-rejected voice note recoverable
prs.body:
Closes #193813

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: finishing a voice note in a nearly full attachment draft destroys the recording. `addVoiceNoteAttachment` deleted the capture file in an unconditional `defer`, the aggregate-budget rejection from `stageAttachment` was ignored, and the recorder returned to idle — so removing another attachment could not recover the note, and the only copy of the recording was gone.

## User Impact

User impact: a capture the aggregate budget rejects is now retained with its file and surfaced in the composer as a retry/discard row. Removing an attachment retries it automatically (the issue's recovery case), the Retry button re-stages against the current budget, and Discard deletes the file explicitly. Successful staging still removes the temporary file, and the upload limit itself is unchanged. Recordings over the per-note 5 MB limit or unreadable files are still discarded, since no amount of freed budget can admit them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recorder handoff now retains a capture the draft cannot admit instead of destroying it. The retained note (`OpenClawRetainedVoiceNote`, module-internal: recording URL, duration, and the exact localized rejection message captured at retention time) belongs to the draft that recorded it:

- The draft pins its owner (`isAttachmentOwnerPinned`, send paths, and programmatic `send()`) until the note is staged or discarded, so a pending session switch cannot strand it; `syncSession` completes after the note resolves.
- Removing an attachment retries staging synchronously through the MainActor retry guard; the voice-note button is disabled while a note is retained, so there is never more than one retained capture and no supersession races.
- Retry validity is identity-based (`retainedVoiceNote?.recording == recording` re-checked after every await), so a discarded note's bytes cannot reappear; the rejection banner is cleared by exact message match, which is locale-safe.
- Discard deletes the file explicitly; staged transfers delete it; a fresh `readAndStageVoiceNote` failure with a superseded or cleared retention leaves the draft untouched.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `ChatFileAdmissionTests.swift`: the retained note keeps the draft pinned ("Keep this recording with the draft" scenario — pending session switch waits, auto-retry after removal admits the note into the original draft, then the switch completes) and a short-budget retry keeps the note until discard. The parametrized `all staging paths count existing attachment bytes` voice branch pins retention plus explicit-discard deletion; aggregate enforcement stays pinned; the success/oversize/malformed-duration tests pass against the retained signature.
- Two independent review rounds drove the implementation (a compile-level setter visibility defect, a locale-dependent error-prefix match, and lifecycle/concurrency gaps including discard-retry resurrection and duplicate staging); the final design replaces the generation counter with draft ownership plus identity re-validation, reviewed to confirmation.
- Local gates on this commit: `swiftc -parse` clean on all nine touched Swift files, `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` reports 0/514 files needing formatting, `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes (inventory carries the new apple-surface strings). This host has Command Line Tools only — no full Xcode — so the SwiftUI SDK macro plugins cannot load and the native build/test gate is the iOS/macOS CI on this PR, consistent with `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md`.

## Current review status

Draft: the repair for the published revision's build failure is pushed as the current head. Remaining before ready, per the review plan: hosted iOS/macOS build lanes on this head, the focused regression suites in CI, and isolated iOS simulator evidence covering recording, rejection, retry, and discard.

prs.title: fix(goals): require a note to resume a blocked goal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resuming a blocked goal with an empty note made it active again and queued another pursuit turn. The operator had not said what changed, so the same blocker came back. A blocked goal now stays blocked until the resume includes a note. Paused, limited, and completed goals can still resume without one.

The command table and the blocked-status paragraph still told people that a bare `/goal resume` makes a blocked goal active. Those two lines now say the note is required, and that an empty resume leaves the goal blocked.

## Evidence

Head `834bd8c1ed7` on macOS. An isolated loopback Gateway served the Control UI. Session `agent:main:main` held a blocked goal whose objective was `Read the operator inbox.`

In the browser, Resume with an empty note showed `Enter what changed before resuming.` The Gateway did not receive `sessions.goal.update`.

Typing `The mail grant is still missing, so stop this goal.` and choosing Resume called the Gateway. The card changed from `Goal blocked` to `Pursuing goal`, and the same run started a model turn.

```console
[ws] res ok sessions.goal.update 65ms runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
[ws] event agent run=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49 agent=main session=main stream=lifecycle phase=start
[openai-transport] responses start provider=xai model=grok-4.7 sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A blocked goal cannot resume from the Control UI until the operator enters what changed. That noted Resume is admitted by `sessions.goal.update` and starts the model continuation. An empty note stays on the card and does not call the Gateway.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.12.1, worktree `/tmp/oc-192883`, head `834bd8c1ed7`. Loopback Gateway and its Control UI in Chromium. Model `xai/grok-4.7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Open the chat for `agent:main:main` with a blocked goal. Choose Resume with an empty note. Enter a note and choose Resume again. Read the Gateway log for `sessions.goal.update` and the following model turn.
- **Evidence after fix:** Control UI text and Gateway log:

  ```console
  empty note: Enter what changed before resuming.
  after note: Pursuing goal
  [ws] res ok sessions.goal.update 65ms runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
  [ws] event agent run=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49 stream=lifecycle phase=start
  [openai-transport] responses start provider=xai model=grok-4.7 sessionKey=agent:main:main
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The empty Resume stays on `Goal blocked` and does not call the Gateway. The noted Resume returns `sessions.goal.update`, switches the card to `Pursuing goal`, and starts the `grok-4.7` turn.
- **What was not tested:** A goal database written by the latest stable package, then opened by this build. The blocked goal in this run was created on this head.

## Summary

A blocked goal stays blocked until `/goal resume` or the Control UI Resume includes a note. The command table and the blocked-status paragraph say that. Paused, limited, and completed goals can still resume without a note.

prs.title: fix: sessions keep using an old fallback model after the default model is changed
prs.body:
Part of #88372 (the stale-catalog and Google 401 symptoms in that issue are not addressed here)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat that was moved to an automatic fallback model by v2026.4.26 through v2026.6.0 keeps sending every turn to that fallback, and keeps announcing the old model as the one selected, after the configured primary is switched to a different model. This happens both on channel and Control UI replies and in `openclaw agent`, the gateway `agent` method and the embedded TUI (`openclaw chat`, `openclaw terminal`, `openclaw tui --local`).

## User Impact

After changing `agents.defaults.model.primary`, those sessions go back to the configured primary on their next message, without deleting session state or running `/model default`. Explicit `/model` pins, locked sessions and self-origin subagent selections keep their model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Those builds stored the fallback as `modelOverrideSource: "auto"` together with the primary it fell back from. Recovery only ever probes that recorded origin, so once the origin is no longer the configured primary there is no probe to run and nothing clears the pin. Heartbeats already treated that case as stale; ordinary turns skipped the check entirely. The stale-origin check in `stored-model-override.ts` now applies to ordinary turns too, as ClawSweeper's review of the issue suggested, and both owners of stored-override selection use it: the reply path resets through the existing reset in `createModelSelectionState`, and agent command selection (`src/agents/command/model-selection.ts`) resets through its existing session repair, next to the no-origin legacy repair. Both keep the auth profile pin. For that, agent command selection resolves the primary (default or channel model override) before the repair instead of after it; the block moved unchanged. Ordinary turns only reset a real fallback: an entry whose override equals its origin is a self-origin subagent selection (`hasSessionActiveAutoModelFallback`) and stays. The heartbeat branch and the no-origin legacy path are unchanged, so the function is renamed from `isStaleHeartbeatAutoFallbackOverride` to `isStaleAutoFallbackOverride`. `docs/concepts/model-failover.md` gets one sentence for the new rule. Nothing in the closed cross-references tried this path; #115808 (open) handles auto pins that have no origin metadata, and this handles the ones that do.

## Evidence

**Real turns on Windows 11:** `getReplyFromConfig` (reply path) and `agentCommandFromIngress` with the embedded TUI's arguments (agent command path), no mocks, plugins disabled, a real on-disk session store, and two local OpenAI-compatible providers that log each request. Config primary is `newprov/new-model`; the session was seeded the way those builds left it, on `oldprov/fallback-model` with source `auto`, then sent two turns.

| Seeded origin | Path | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `firstprov/first-model` (primary since changed) | reply | both turns sent to `oldprov/fallback-model`, turn 1 says "Model Fallback: oldprov/fallback-model (selected firstprov/first-model; selected model unavailable)", pin still stored | both turns sent to `newprov/new-model`, no fallback notice, override cleared from the store after turn 1 |
| `firstprov/first-model` (primary since changed) | agent command | both turns sent to `oldprov/fallback-model`, pin still stored | both turns sent to `newprov/new-model`, override cleared after turn 1 |
| `newprov/new-model` (still the primary) | reply | turn 1 probes `newprov/new-model`, turn 2 on `oldprov/fallback-model` | same |
| `newprov/new-model` (still the primary) | agent command | turn 1 probes `newprov/new-model` and clears the pin, turn 2 on `newprov/new-model` | same |
| `oldprov/fallback-model` (self-origin) | both | both turns on `oldprov/fallback-model` | same |

- `model-selection.resolved-pin.test.ts` adds an ordinary-turn case that resets a fallback whose origin is no longer the primary (asserting reason `stale`) and one that keeps a self-origin selection; `get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts` checks that an ordinary turn with a replaced origin reaches directives on the primary; `model-selection.configured.test.ts` checks that agent command selection picks the primary and clears the stored override. With main's four source files the reset, get-reply and agent command cases fail (2 failed, 40 passed for the two reply files; 1 failed, 21 passed for the agent command file); the self-origin case passes on both.
- `--maxWorkers=1`: those three files plus `model-selection.test.ts` and `agent-runner-auto-fallback.test.ts`, 150 passed. `model-selection.turn-model-differential.test.ts`, 9 passed. `src/commands/agent.test.ts`, 70 passed and 1 timed out at 120 s ("rejects a missing harness-owned session before local CLI dispatch"); that test has no session entry, and it times out the same way run alone with main's source files.
- Test cost, `--maxWorkers=1` wall per file on a busy laptop: `model-selection.resolved-pin.test.ts` 97 s, `model-selection.configured.test.ts` 74 s, `get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts` 148 s, mostly transform; the new tests take 82 ms, 10 ms, 11 ms and 413 ms. No timers, sleeps or gateway boots. In CI (Ubuntu, Node 24.21.0), after the 09-28 merge from main, each file passed in full in its own shard: `model-selection.resolved-pin.test.ts` 21 tests in job checks-node-changed-compact-large-3-4, the new ones in 21 and 8 ms; `model-selection.configured.test.ts` 27 tests in job checks-node-changed-compact-large-31, the new one in 10 ms; `get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts` 14 tests in job checks-node-changed-compact-large-16, the new one in 53 ms.
