prs.title: fix(memory): keep backfilled snippets tied to their sources
prs.body:
Closes #157827

## Current Status - October 31

**Draft; blocked on reinforced legacy evidence handling.** Fresh-store staging proof does not qualify an existing reinforced store. No maintainer decision has been posted in response to the October 4 migration concerns, and the proposed migration remains unapplied.

Proposed decision for the memory owner: retain ambiguous legacy rows and their original support without redistribution, but exclude them from new promotion until their provenance is resolved. This is a proposal, not an implemented retention or promotion change. Previously promoted `MEMORY.md` content requires separate validation; this PR does not repair it or claim verified corruption.

Before ready: accept the legacy policy, implement it in the existing store/promotion owner, resolve conflicts, and exercise pre-fix reinforced state through backfill and actual promotion, including edited text at the same location, multiple legacy rows, and already-promoted state. No new code or tests are claimed on October 31; head remains `1c91be19e628e548f1b1e8ecc16aeeefeeec09fe`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading source citations when `memory rem-backfill --stage-short-term` stages a REM summary drawn from several nonadjacent lines but attaches only the first line's location.

## User Impact

Freshly staged short-term memories retain each contributing source location together with the text it supports. Coalesced atomic claims stay compact instead of absorbing transient details from the surrounding source line.

There is no configuration or persisted-format change, but per-source snippets change persisted claim hashes and entry keys. Rerunning backfill regenerates grounded-only entries, not all previously staged entries. It does not rewrite existing `MEMORY.md` content. The reported final wrong-citation outcome in `MEMORY.md` remains unverified, as clarified on the issue.

## Open Upgrade Blocker

The September 27 review identified a valid gap: `removeGroundedShortTermCandidates` retains an old merged entry if it has any recall or daily support. The new per-source keys do not replace that reinforced entry. The real CLI proof below covers fresh and repeated grounded-only staging, not this upgrade case. This PR is not merge-ready until existing-store handling is resolved and proved.

Deleting reinforced entries or copying their aggregate counts into each new source would lose or misattribute valid evidence. No such migration or retention change has been made. The next scoped proof must seed a pre-fix SQLite row with recall/daily support, run backfill, and verify preserved evidence without a promotable misleading citation; final promotion also needs examination because it rehydrates candidates from live source ranges.

October 4: source-reviewed the proposed upgrade patch and [reported two concrete risks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157912#issuecomment-5979542710): transferring old support to unrelated text edited at the same location, and losing accumulated counts when multiple legacy entries reuse a stale replacement snapshot. The proposal has not been applied or executed. Existing evidence retention/promotion policy and a real final-promotion regression remain unresolved; the branch also needs conflict resolution before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Staging now resolves every reference against the same scratch copy used for the preview. Joined summaries use the corresponding source snippet; recognized atomic claims retain the existing extraction rules. Source resolution finishes before replacing the prior grounded candidates.

The unchanged Markdown parser is shared with staging through a sibling module, keeping normalization and line numbering consistent without growing the already over-cap evidence file. Preview rendering, promotion policy, scores and day buckets are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Red on the base: the registered backfill CLI persisted one merged entry for two nonadjacent short preferences. A second regression caught display-time colon trimming retaining merged text at the first location.
- After rebasing onto `b9dc1ac9b366`: 96 evidence/promotion tests passed, then all 3 CLI regressions passed after adapting their mocks to the current host SDK imports. The earlier head also passed 268 focused tests and its full changed-file gate.
- The three new CLI cases use real temporary Markdown and SQLite state, covering per-source text/locations, repeated backfill, coalesced atomic claims and live-source rehydration. Deleting a source rejects its candidate. Configuration and manager acquisition are mocked; this is not a full Gateway E2E claim.
- Real CLI proof: `pnpm openclaw memory rem-backfill --path <isolated-workspace>/memory/2025-01-01.md --stage-short-term --json`, using isolated home/state/config and `memory.search.provider: none`, exited 0. The supported wrapper rebuilt the current source. No command, manager, or persistence mocks were used. Direct read-only inspection of the resulting SQLite store verified the rows below. Running the same CLI again reported 2 staged and 2 replaced entries.
- Fresh new-file cost: all 3 cases passed in 33.11s wrapper wall (29.79s Vitest, 21.39s compiler preparation; 799ms case execution).
- Fresh checks passed: production extension typecheck, formatting, line/maximum-line/assertion ratchets, plugin boundaries, doctor contract tests, dependency checks, and `git diff --check`. The all-extension test typecheck was stopped after 8m47s under local memory pressure; the remaining changed-file checks and refreshed full CI are not claimed green.
- Independent review found only the obsolete staged test imports; the reviewed working-tree correction has been staged. No other actionable P0-P2 finding. This proves CLI staging, not a Gateway/model run or the unverified final `MEMORY.md` corruption claim.

Sanitized rows read from the actual CLI-created `plugin_state_entries` store:

```json
[
  {"path":"memory/2025-01-01.md","startLine":2,"endLine":2,"snippet":"Always use UTC.","groundedCount":2},
  {"path":"memory/2025-01-01.md","startLine":4,"endLine":4,"snippet":"Prefer tea.","groundedCount":2}
]
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: empty or invalid `parameters.retry_after` metadata on an outer error prevents the shared channel retry runner from honoring a valid hint in its response or nested error. For example, it can retry after the 400 ms backoff despite a nested response requesting one second.

## User Impact

Channel requests using the default hint reader wait for the available provider-requested delay even when an earlier wrapper contains incomplete metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the first finite hint in the existing root, response, nested-error order. Missing or invalid hints fall through; finite hints, including zero, retain their precedence. The existing runner continues to own retry admission, injected readers, backoff, jitter, and delay caps. No public signatures, configuration, or exports change.

## Evidence

The earlier baseline reproduction had six fake-clock timing failures on the original production code. The repair retains ten distinct cases for invalid outer metadata, nested fallback, finite and zero precedence, and default backoff alongside main's newer coverage.

- Follow-up review removed two duplicate cap tests. The existing table still covers a 45-second hint capped at 30 seconds by default and allowed at 45 seconds with an explicit 60-second retry-after cap.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/retry-policy.test.ts src/infra/retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 38 tests passed across both owning files, 4.79 seconds wrapper wall time.

Validation gaps: no live channel/provider/Gateway trace with real transport, full build/test, or broader production/test type graphs were run. Fake-clock proof does not claim a live provider result. Exact-head CI is pending on the follow-up cleanup.

## What Problem This Solves

Shell preflight drops intentionally empty quoted option values. `env --argv0 "" python3 bad.py` then loses its interpreter position and bypasses the Python source check; Node target extraction similarly misses a preload following empty inline code. This repair also addresses the reported POSIX backslash-newline discrepancy in the same permissive shell tokenizer.

## User Impact

Shell analysis keeps empty words and their comment boundaries. Outside single quotes, permissive shell parsing removes backslash-LF without creating an argument or starting a word. The public process-command parser retains its existing empty-entry/backslash behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict is reconciled using main's existing word-start state rather than adding a second tracker. Strict raw-syntax rejection remains intact: both strict tokenization and the actual `planShellAuthorization` entry point continue refusing line continuations. Permissive preflight normalization does not establish execution approval.

prs.title: fix(telegram): first DM message lands in root chat when the client creates the topic separately
prs.body:
Closes #169443

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the first message of a new private bot topic is answered in the main chat, and the new topic stays empty, when the Telegram client creates the topic and sends the message as two separate updates.

## User Impact

User impact: a new private topic started from such a client (Telegram for Android, for example) gets its first reply, typing indicator, session and auto label inside that topic. Later messages sent to the main chat still stay in the main chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bot receives `forum_topic_created` for the new topic, then the user's first message without `message_thread_id`. Nothing linked the two, so the message ran in the main DM session.

The receiving account's ingress monitor now links them once, at admission: a threadless private message from the same user, with a larger message id, within 3 seconds of a topic that user created, joins that topic. The decision is stored on the spooled update (`adoptedDmThreadId`), so the lane, authorization, session, delivery and restart replay all read the same topic. Bot-created topics, groups and channel direct-message topics are unchanged. Old spool rows without the field replay unchanged.

Accepted edge case: if Telegram itself drops the new topic (as during the 2026-11-09 Bot API incident), the reply fails loudly with "message thread not found" instead of silently landing in the main chat. That matches the existing rule not to retry topic sends without topic metadata.

## Evidence

- Live Telegram Test Server E2E, before and after, real Gateway + deterministic mock model, leased QA user, Threaded Mode on:
  - Scenario: the QA user creates a topic with TDLib `createForumTopic`, then ~200 ms later sends `PING:adopt` to the main chat (the exact two-update shape from #169443).
  - `main` at `8ebe740925ca`: reply `PONG:adopt` arrived in the main chat; session `agent:main:main`. The new topic stayed empty.
  - This head `cb3709c0e1f3`: reply `PONG:adopt` arrived in the new topic (`topicId=199227`); model request session `agent:main:main:thread:<user>:199227`. Controls in the same run: a later main-chat message `PING:rootlater` was answered in the main chat (session `agent:main:main`), and `PING:infresh` sent inside the new topic was answered in that topic.
- Focused tests: `dm-topic-adopt`, `thread-spec`, `telegram-ingress-drain` (admission, account isolation, failed-append redelivery, restart replay, legacy rows) and the native-pipeline inbound-handler cases. The restart-replay case fails without the durable restore.
- The branch is merged with current `main` (conflicts with the widget-tap topic preparation from #198022 resolved by keeping both payload fields).
- Earlier production Bot API evidence from the author (topic sessions, `requireTopic` isolation, disabled-topic replay, upgrade from `2026.11.1`) remains in the PR history.

prs.title: fix: hide non-chat models from chat selection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Non-chat models could appear as chat choices, saved selections could fail with a misleading missing-model error, and deterministic provider HTTP 400 failures triggered three compaction attempts.

## User Impact

Chat choices now exclude models without declared chat support. Existing selections stay saved and receive an instruction to pick another model, including through the pre-run channel reply path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared discovery now requires declared chat/text support or an exact catalog declaration. Explicit audio-only or disabled-chat declarations win; unfamiliar ID-only rows remain hidden until support is declared. Negative facts use the existing route-bound `inference.chat` contract. Anthropic capability trees and oMLX model types are translated by their provider owners; Bifrost/oMLX setup selects only supported chat rows. Upstream snapshots and OpenAI projections preserve the result.

Existing pins remain saved and receive “This model doesn't support chat; pick another model.” A public Gateway probe also exposed an execution handoff bug: adding prompt-project fields cloned the prepared snapshot and lost its WeakMap-keyed admitted catalogs. Captured facts now travel on the immutable snapshot, preserving the admission generation through both chat and compaction projections. The two identity-keyed catalog maps are removed.

Compaction uses its existing structured HTTP failure classifier and skips deterministic request retries. The missing-model matcher now distinguishes an absent model from an absent service ID mentioned in the same error. No provider/model is hardcoded; no new config, cache, manifest, or database schema is added.

Picker publication also excludes a configured non-chat row reintroduced by wildcard policy, after preserving capability metadata from the selected physical route. Two regressions reproduce those bypasses before the repair.

The current public models.dev feed has four text-output TokenHub models and no IndexTTS-2. The publisher already filters for text output. Tencent documents its authenticated model list as IDs/names/status without capability metadata; the actual authenticated incident listing was not captured. Filtering only explicit audio declarations would leave that ID-only gap open.

## Evidence

- Discovery regression fails on exact base `777c036d592`; the snapshot-projection regression also fails before its repair. Both pass with the fixes.
- Initial 224 focused tests passed. Follow-up consumer and pin tests passed (171), and the snapshot repair passed all 35 focused lease, native-picker, configured-route and capture tests.
- Real loopback HTTP 400, warmed paired A/A/B/B/A/B: three requests before versus one after; median wall 1,907 → 576 ms. Sampled allocation increases from 8.58 → 10.24 MB; this is not a memory optimization.
- Synthetic 4,000-row catalog with 400 audio-only rows: 4,000 → 3,600 chat choices. Paired median CPU 7.99 → 10.08 ms/projection and sampled allocation 10.02 → 11.16 MB. A/A wall-time noise is substantial. These owners do not open session databases or scan workspaces; this is not a full large-database Gateway stress claim.
- Public Gateway replay with a synthetic authenticated loopback provider: `models.list` retains only declared text models; one turn against the saved audio pin returns the actionable `model_chat_unsupported` error with `retryable: false`, zero provider POSTs and no compaction attempts. All data and credentials were synthetic.
- Dashboard `chat.send` replay: one visible terminal error in `chat.history`, unchanged saved user pin, 298 ms runtime, zero provider POSTs and no compaction. The channel-boundary regression failed before the fix; all 46 reply tests pass afterward.
- Fresh Codex autoreview is scoped-clean, including the pre-run error handling and its extraction into the existing sibling utility module. The full follow-up `check:changed` completed with only the two inherited failures below; the final four-file publication check completed. It caught an import-shadow lint error in the new fixture; that test-only alias was corrected, formatted and linted successfully, with a fresh clean Codex review. The line-cap hook caught growth in the directive module; extracting its existing model-error handling resolved it, with focused tests, core typecheck and Codex review repeated.

Production delta is +108 lines. The growth supplies generic capability classification, provider setup migration, pin-preserving errors and snapshot facts; it adds no competing discovery owner.

- Latest-stable upgrade: created synthetic chat and speech sessions with published 2026.11.3, then used native Doctor and started the candidate against the same isolated state. Session IDs, labels, thinking settings and user pins remain intact. The candidate picker returns only `chat` and `fresh-chat`. The speech turn produces exactly one visible actionable terminal error in 264 ms, zero provider POSTs and zero compaction attempts; the chat turn returns `ready` through one provider POST. Native Doctor applied existing config/database migrations; this PR adds none. Doctor reported an unavailable whole-state recovery copy on the external-volume staging ancestor, while per-database migration backups were created. This is a synthetic compatibility proof, not certification of that host backup setup.
- Final picker regressions: two expected failures before publication filtering, all 19 route/visibility tests green afterward, fresh Codex autoreview scoped-clean.

## Inherited Main Regressions

The SDK surface budget and unused `acquireConfiguredGatewayPostgresOwner` export reproduce on exact base `777c036d592808418f95da97cf6b4ee6af614bbc`. The wildcard was introduced by #176886, the additional public entrypoint by #195641, and the PostgreSQL export by #196237. These remain failed checks.

Final-head CI run 43462915679 tests merge `dd5d27878c14`, with exact main parent `c19ae286a00c`. The catalog-reload assertion and all four Talk cancellation assertions reproduce on that parent with unchanged test and owner inputs. #197784 (`76385fd77e3f`) began persisting accepted catalogs, so the reload proof's old expectation of an image-less fallback fails in its same-route-account-switch scenario. #198100 (`bf0b8002c2b9`) introduced the append-only history guard that rejects the Talk follow-up. prs.title: fix(voice-call): prevent long initial readings from disconnecting calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes premature disconnection when a response-mode voice call starts with a long reading and generated audio outruns telephone playback.

## User Impact

Long initial readings are requested in short passages, with the next passage waiting for carrier playback acknowledgment. The existing bounded-buffer safeguard remains enabled. Short openings and continuous/native-delegation providers retain their existing paths; no configuration migration is required.

**Draft: package/runtime SDK compatibility corrected; human-answered live retry failed.** This only segments the initial message; subsequent `speak` requests remain unsegmented.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing pacer closes the carrier stream with WebSocket code 1013 when its bounded queue overflows, discarding queued speech. Raising the cap would only postpone the failure.

A plugin-local coordinator splits the initial text into roughly 480-character passages. It waits for successful generation completion and a unique carrier playback mark before requesting the next passage. Provider failure, playback reset, replacement speech, or close stop the reading. Character limits bound requested text, not arbitrary audio a noncompliant model might generate, so overflow protection remains enabled.

### ClawSweeper follow-up

Restored the intent of opening-greeting protection: caller audio and provider barge-in clears cannot cancel the segmented opening, including between responses and while awaiting final carrier playback acknowledgment. The segmented owner supplies its actual lifetime to the existing audio controller; normal caller input and interruption resume after the final acknowledgment. There is no longer a separate caller-speech cancellation policy for long openings. Short/continuous openings use the original policy.

Simplification retained one sequencing owner and existing pacer/mark plumbing. Transcript helpers move unchanged into their existing module; shared handler-test setup avoids growing oversized files. The exact 355-line net test allocation covers ordering, protected opening/input resumption, cancellation, unchanged short/continuous paths, long-audio replay, and shared fixture extraction.

## Evidence

- Opening-protection regression run against the previous PR head `2e26ba6a3eb1158cae9dbb3fd976aa0ca55ae929`: **1 failed / 5 passed**, with the reading losing its first playback mark after injected caller speech. Repaired real-WebSocket handler coverage verifies protection during generation and pending playback, then restored input and barge-in after final acknowledgment.
- Deterministic synthetic replay exercises the production session facade, reading coordinator, pacer and Twilio frame adapter: **180 seconds / 1,440,000 bytes** generated at **4x playback speed**. Without sequencing, the same workload overflows at 39–41 simulated seconds and discards over 119 seconds of generated audio. With sequencing, every byte arrives in order, subsequent generation waits for delayed playback acknowledgments, and no audio/acknowledgments remain pending. This is an unsegmented negative control through the current production composition, not a whole old-checkout replay.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-reading.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-reading-overflow.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-call-session-control.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-audio-pacer.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **64 passed / 5 files**, 14.82 seconds wrapper wall time (12.40 seconds Vitest). The replay itself took 67 ms in its initial focused run; opening coverage about 299 ms. CI timing not measured.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/voice-call/tsconfig.json --pretty false`: **passed** for the entire voice-call production package.

prs.title: fix(telegram): steered answers quote the wrong input
prs.body:
### Current CI repair — November 13

Head `148aa18a3ab3c9ea941916a7ab378a1162654702` adds the existing `home-readonly.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` to the canonical real-Gateway inventory. It previously ran in the parallel bundled UI lane despite starting a real Gateway. The existing selector now routes it to the serial real-Gateway lane; the scenario, assertions and 120-second timeout are unchanged. This corrects a verified scheduling omission; a passing new CI run is still required to establish the timeout is resolved.

New-head [CI run 43454717466](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43454717466) is `action_required` and has not run its jobs: upstream workflow approval is required. The available account has no upstream write/admin permission.

Previous run [43440680720](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43440680720) had two failing jobs:
- Home reader timed out after 120 seconds with `agents.list` pending. The same scenario passed on scheduled main in [job 131944718121](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43442683384/job/131944718121), taking 117.5 seconds in the bundled lane.
- The four native Talk after-cancel assertions also fail on scheduled main `b4da3463d3a78dc7fd0e553dfe33e49bfa1e2e3c`, [job 131944723210](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43442683384/job/131944723210), with the same expected completion versus fallback text. This is independently reproduced upstream, not evidence of passing Talk behavior.

Validation for this one-line change: `git diff --check` and manual inspection of canonical inventory consumers. Local ownership test did **not run**: the initial isolated environment failed Bun setup because curl was absent; the subsequent Node-only environment could not register before the retention lock timeout. No local test success or full CI success is claimed. Earlier proofs below retain their original commit scope.

Closes #178120.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can quote the wrong input when an embedded run consumes another message while an earlier answer is buffered. Capture each assistant message’s consumed input synchronously, retain it through buffered delivery and native transcript persistence, and preserve its implicit reply classification through final threading and pending-final payload preparation.

## User Impact

Answers retain the input they consumed. Implicit targets respect `off` / `first` / `all`; explicit quotes and quote suppression retain precedence. Legacy transcript JSON remains readable. The optional source fact needs no configuration or database migration.

## Evidence

### Telegram Test Server E2E (exact head `3662dc8280a9`, this branch merged with main)

Real Gateway built from this head and from `main` `8ebe740925ca`, Telegram Test Server DM driven by a userbot, scripted model, `replyToMode: "all"`. The user sends `Please answer STEERA`. The model answers `STEERA answer text` and starts an exec tool (`sleep 12`). Six seconds later the user sends `Please answer STEERB`, which is steered into the same run, and the next model call answers `STEERB answer text`.

| Reply | `main` 8ebe740925ca | this PR 3662dc8280a9 |
|---|---|---|
| `STEERA answer text` | replies to the STEERA message | replies to the STEERA message |
| `STEERB answer text` | replies to the **STEERA** message (quote "Please answer STEERA") | replies to the **STEERB** message |

- On this head the STEERB reply carries no automatic quote excerpt; on `main` the wrong-target reply quoted the STEERA text.
- Merge with main resolved one conflict in `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.types.ts` (both sides add optional subscribe params).


Current head: `92943dc42b1c90ab5c224a0ac63b5c7d424dd64c`. Integrated main: `11091f0bf62f93465c03aae211a3ae185cde88ae`.

### Conflict and regression-budget update — 29 October

Main #185730 intentionally replaced restart reconstruction/replay with ordinary resumed input and deleted `main-session-recovery`. This update honors that deletion instead of restoring the old 5,000-line test or its removed dependencies. The contribution's now-obsolete “retries a persisted implicit-source final before transport enqueue” case is removed with that owner. It is **not** claimed to run on the replacement restart architecture. The three consumed-input subscriber cases, including actual transcript persistence/readback, and the six pending-final/threading/legacy-transcript cases remain byte-identical to the previous head. Their historical passing results retain their old heads.

The stream projection fixture now forwards the optional `getUserTranscriptContexts` fact in its legacy comparison object, matching the explicit production subscription. This is a one-line fixture-contract correction, not a claim to fix the reported theme-initialization failure.

The prior head's [test-line gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40648149883/job/122682129777) reported net +274 test lines. The current contribution is net **+241 LF bytes** against the integrated main: 159 for consumed-input capture/persistence, 81 for implicit/explicit threading and legacy transcript cases, and one for the existing projection fixture. Following the documented test-line allocation policy, a separate `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-consumed-input-reply-source.txt` grants exactly 241 lines for these regressions. The shared scalar and all pre-existing allocation records are unchanged. No assertion, coverage or timeout was weakened to satisfy this gate; the new native ratchet result awaits CI.

The other prior-head [Bun check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40648149883/job/122682130556) failed `attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts` → “projects only subscriber facts while preserving real stream reads and effects” with `Theme not initialized. Call setTheme() first.` The failing test source was byte-identical to integrated main before the optional-callback fixture correction. This has **not** been reproduced on a baseline locally, is **not** claimed inherited or fixed, and remains for upstream validation. No blind rerun was requested.

Current-tree static checks: syntax-only parsing of all **18 TypeScript/MJS contribution files** using the existing Node 24.18.0 executable; contribution whitespace; relative-import path existence; exact preservation of the remaining regression bodies and upstream fixture except for the optional callback. Node 24.18.0 was used only as a parser, without importing or executing contribution source; it is below the current source-checkout runtime requirement and supplies no supported-runtime or SQLite qualification. No dependency installation, compiler/typecheck, lint/format runner, native ratchet, behavioral test, model/Gateway/Telegram scenario, or CI rerun was performed. Local `autoreview` is unavailable; direct source review only, without subagents. Current-head CI and maintainer validation remain pending.

### Conflict resolution — 28 October

The branch now incorporates the integrated main while retaining the consumed-input reply-source correction. Upstream moved `PrepareEmbeddedAttemptStreamInput` into `attempt-stream-prepare.types.ts`; the optional transcript-context getter now lives on that owner. The stream implementation retains the complete upstream explicit-field subscription construction, with only the existing getter forwarding added. No duplicate local type is retained.

The pending-final fixture retains the complete upstream consolidated test body. Its six contribution cases (implicit first/all threading, explicit inline quote, and three old/new transcript cases) are byte-identical to the previous head. The two older standalone checks already covered by upstream's tables were not restored.

Static checks on this exact tree: Node **24.18.0** syntax-only parsing of all **18 contribution paths**, `git diff --check`, exact comparison of the upstream stream/type owners except for the callback, and exact preservation checks for the upstream fixture and six contribution cases. The other contribution paths match Git's automatic merge output. The PATH-selected Node 26.8.2 failed TypeScript syntax-check setup; the explicitly selected existing Node 24.18.0 parsed all paths successfully. No contribution source was imported or executed.

**Not rerun:** compiler/typecheck, behavioral tests, lint, packaged survivor, Gateway/model/Telegram scenarios, or CI. The shared `autoreview` executable remains unavailable; this update received direct source review, without subagents. Current-head CI and maintainer validation remain pending. Historical evidence below retains its original heads and is not transferred to this tree.

### Historical import correction — 27 October

Head `08a9bf18e915da011656e59624632c436a9d67b5` corrected the remaining test-only `UserTranscriptContext` import to its canonical `attempt-llm-boundary.types.ts` owner. This addressed the [parent native test-type TS2459 diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40283649836/job/121442958765); the two production imports had been corrected on parent `54a02a08cae7141b5ac453c48f7e77176a0926c6`. The canonical imports are retained by this merge.

That parent also had a distinct [model-switch assertion failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40283649836/job/121442639836) in `agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts`, involving `supportsReasoningEffort: true`. It remains separately recorded: this contribution has not changed that file or reproduced the failure locally, and does not claim to have fixed it or established inheritance.

### Historical validation before the 25 October branch update

Historical head: `09517e7ab48747e2935ffbab41d3c90d2bde4202` had its earlier conflict with main `94dacc48dfb325197481e95cc0fe3fd863eec645` resolved. The pending-final test retains the entire upstream consolidation plus this contribution’s six regressions. The native database-worker inventory retains both the reply-source case and upstream update-repair cancellation case, once each. Independent review found no actionable resolution defect.

On this exact resulting tree, secretless Linux containers with Node 24.22.0 and dependencies installed from the new frozen lockfile pass:

- **32 focused native cases:** all three subscriber source cases, all 28 pending-final owning-file cases, and the real persisted implicit-source retry case. The other 194 restart-recovery cases are excluded by an explicit name filter, not claimed as executed.
- Production core types and all three affected native test-type graphs: `core-test-agents-root`, `core-test-agents-sessions`, `core-test-messaging`.
- Native type-aware core and test-inventory lint, formatting on all 17 contribution paths, and contribution whitespace checks.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.reply-source.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts -t 'retries a persisted implicit-source final before transport enqueue' --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-agents-root","core-test-agents-sessions","core-test-messaging"]' --concurrency 1
```

Parent `eb3874c1` had separately passed 94 focused cases across capture/persistence, final recovery, payload production, transcript reading and reply threading, with one existing Windows-only case skipped on Linux. That is parent evidence, not 94 additional current-head cases. Earlier red/green proof establishes the implicit-source recovery regressions against the reviewed producer/threading implementation. The subscriber fixture persists captured assistant messages and reads their actual source IDs through the native database worker.

The shared `autoreview` executable is unavailable and was not run. Native compiler, lint, format and test budgets were not changed.

## Packaged update and CI scope

The complete native published-package `sqlite-volume` survivor recipe **passes** in [run 39504398170](https://github.com/ChuLaiTheGreat/openclaw/actions/runs/39504398170), job `118909878709`, completed 20 October 2026 at 22:49 UTC. Candidate package source is `09517e7ab48747e2935ffbab41d3c90d2bde4202` (tree `fb409e5571e51267017a43b478f9052f5ce886c3`); the actual mounted E2E tooling is public PR #178801, `637db088c3fb0edcf516c74d63892becbbd7466e` (tree `10e70ebae01184a134d2b01eefffebb37f3f5bdc`, sole parent `5a0b5006`). The native entry point is `bash scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh`, installing the complete candidate tarball through the shipped updater from published `openclaw@2026.10.5`.

- Full native publishable package: **122,402,366 bytes**, SHA-256 `80bef2833f9ee9f8327a32f16d9ab6ec2d78ee084bb684802827d4c4f903799e`. Complete registry source/version/integrity validation passes for all four required packages.
- The update succeeds in **1,444.545 seconds** against the unchanged **1,500-second command budget**. Docker/lane budgets remain **2,280 seconds / 2,580,000 ms**, with the original 12 GiB / four-CPU fixture, original assertions and volume quotas.
- The real index is still oversized: **1,063,044 raw bytes**, including 1,060,022 plugin-array bytes and 2,314 install-receipt bytes. The required projection is **14,353 bytes**, preserving complete receipts and 76 plugin entries. This is a fresh run of the unchanged scenario, not a claim that the earlier 1,063,050-byte failed artifact was recovered.
- All **49 named phase end states pass**, including automatic migration, survival, Gateway history, Doctor idempotence, Gateway restart, post-restart history and final restarted survival. The synthetic volume retains 4,800 sessions, 23,890 events and 2,200 cron jobs. Gateway RPC verifies eight conversation samples across two agents before and after restart; their complete exported sample arrays and message digests are identical.
- The actual changed Doctor-budget consumer runs: persisted totals are 4,803 sessions / 23,893 events / 2,203 cron jobs / nine enabled distinct plugin roots, yielding the native **717-second** budget. Doctor idempotence completes in **276 seconds** and the native assertions pass afterward. The three additional baseline records explain the difference from the volume-only counts above.

Selected redacted native terminal output (the full job log is linked above):


The job is terminal success, with native driver exit 0 and successful final phase receipts. The four explicitly inspected host-owned package/image/mount/registry containers settle at exit 0 without OOM or a remaining PID; no unavailable inner-container inspect receipt is invented. Exported summaries are tail-limited and redacted, so the conclusion also uses the complete phase entries, valid targeted Gateway/budget receipts and native terminal result. The earlier `26fe6036` runtime-only success and `39491732163` partial updater success remain historical. ## Remaining proof / review

Live Telegram Test Server proof remains unexecuted. The exact-head Gateway/model controls below use a trusted credential-resident relay and a synthetic Bot API; they do not supply a live Telegram lease or delivery proof. The complete package survivor, post-restart history retention and idempotence proof is supplied above. ### Exact runtime follow-up — October 21

The unchanged head `09517e7ab48747e2935ffbab41d3c90d2bde4202` now has its own successful native `qaRuntime` build in [run 39621479405](https://github.com/ChuLaiTheGreat/openclaw/actions/runs/39621479405). ### Quote-off model control — 22 October

The unchanged head `09517e7ab48747e2935ffbab41d3c90d2bde4202` now passes one additional isolated built-Gateway scenario with the selected real model and the native Telegram adapter. The Bot API and sender identities are synthetic. All 58,307 tracked source blobs and both clean native build stamps match this head.

Two fresh inputs are durably admitted while the first model response is held. The model emits only `RESULT-A` and `RESULT-B`, with no explicit reply directives. The two final transport payloads refer respectively to input A and input B. The Gateway and actual container both exit 0, with PID 0 and no OOM; the container is removed and the finite validation cycle closes successfully. Only that fixture option was removed. The passing run retains an initial startup-unavailable observation followed by native durable completion, without a manual resend. **Limits:** this is synthetic Bot API boundary evidence, not live Telegram or installed-candidate acceptance. It adds no new persisted-history assertion or fresh baseline regression result. The complete live quote-policy matrix remains open; earlier negative results and the separate upgrade-survivor evidence retain their original scope. Two fresh native Gateway/webhook scenarios add real-model evidence without repeating the accepted steering or implicit quote-off cases. These are **synthetic Bot API boundary checks**, not live Telegram acceptance. The `first` check has one final payload and does not prove the multi-payload first-only limit. prs.title: chore(ios): measure chat scroll and streaming stability on the simulator
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

There is no repeatable way to see whether the iOS chat transcript jumps, drifts or rebuilds rows while a reply streams, while the reader is scrolled up, when the keyboard moves, or after a relaunch. Chat jank reports could only be checked by eye.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers and agents get `pnpm ios:behavior`, which drives the real app on a simulator against an isolated Gateway with a scripted model and prints position and count gates per case.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Scripted model:** the QA `mock-openai` provider gains a paced reply (`UXSTREAM chunks=<n> interval=<ms>`): mixed markdown deltas written that far apart, so every run streams the same reply.
- **Probe:** `ChatBehaviorProbe.swift` records, only in DEBUG builds launched with `--openclaw-behavior-probe`, the on-screen top and bottom of each tagged row, the live bubble and the composer on every frame where something moved, plus mounts, scroll phases, bubble body evaluations, sends and keyboard show/hide. Release builds compile it out; other DEBUG launches skip it.
- **Runner:** `scripts/ios-behavior.mts` pairs a fresh simulator through onboarding, runs five cases three times each and deletes the simulator. Each case is a `guard` (every gate passes in every sample) or `bad` (reproduces an open bug in at least one sample); there is no majority vote. Gates are positions and counts, not wall-clock limits; times are reported for A/B comparison only. Prompts are pasted, never typed: typing through a UI driver makes iOS treat the simulator as having a hardware keyboard and hide the software one for good.
- Docs: `.agents/skills/ios-e2e/BEHAVIOR.md`.

Two cases are `bad` on `main` and stay that way until the fix PR flips them:

- `stream-follow`: with the keyboard up, the growing reply is not followed. It streams up to ~5,700 pt below the composer, then either jumps to the end or, in about half the runs, leaves the transcript blank above the "Done in" recap until the user scrolls. The follow relies on `defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom, for: .sizeChanges)`, which does not hold a growing `LazyVStack`, and streamed words change no timeline revision, so nothing re-pins.
- `stream-turn`: when a reply finishes, its final row replaces the live bubble 42 pt higher, so the reply visibly jumps up.

`relaunch` also reports an intermittent jump (about 1 in 3 cold launches shows the top of history for one frame); it is a reported metric, not a gate, because it does not reproduce reliably.

## Evidence

Full run on this branch (main `f86e06de8c7` behavior), iPhone 17 simulator, 3 samples per case:

| Case | Kind | Gates not passing in every sample |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stream-turn` | bad | sent turn holds still, reply included (≤1 pt) 0/3 |
| `stream-follow` | bad | no teleports 2/3; no backward motion (≤1 pt) 2/3; end in view (≤4 pt hidden) 1/3 |
| `scrolled-up` | guard | all gates 3/3 |
| `keyboard` | guard | all gates 3/3 |
| `relaunch` | guard | all gates 3/3 |

Exit 0: guards pass, both bad cases still reproduce.

- `pnpm test test/scripts/ios-behavior-grade.test.ts`: 5 passed (grader boundaries: teleport and backward motion, sub-point rounding, live-bubble handoff, user-drag exclusion, remounts).
- `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai`: 13 files, 200 tests passed.
- `tsgo:scripts`, `tsgo:extensions`, oxlint, oxfmt, SwiftFormat and SwiftLint at the repo pins, iOS Debug simulator build: clean. The probe is `#if DEBUG && os(iOS)`; macOS compiles the no-op branch (left to CI).
- Gap: absolute timing, hitches and hangs need a physical device; this harness reports simulator times for A/B only.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes: the only shared file is root `package.json`, which gains one script.

Merge danger: two-way door. Revert removes the script, probe and mock scenario; no state, config or published contract changes. Blast radius: DEBUG builds launched with the probe flag, and QA mock prompts containing `UXSTREAM`.

prs.title: fix: recover OpenAI sessions after compaction item conflicts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes OpenAI conversations that permanently reject every turn with `item_conflict` after replaying a compaction checkpoint.

## User Impact

Affected conversations can resume on their next turn after upgrading, without editing or discarding their saved history. Any remaining item conflict gives recovery guidance instead of a generic failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The real Responses API accepts a compacted window with `store:true` once, then rejects replay of that checkpoint. Removing all item IDs still fails; replaying the unchanged checkpoint with `store:false` succeeds, including after it was stored. The shared payload policy now selects stateless replay for compaction input on the native public OpenAI endpoint.

Checkpoint contents remain intact. Ordinary requests keep stored HTTP continuation; compacted requests replay their bounded window instead of using stored `previous_response_id`. Azure and custom endpoint policies remain unchanged. No new configuration, cache, retry wrapper, database change, or migration is required.

## Evidence

The policy regression fails on the original code. Live official API probes distinguish the conflict from ordinary message/reasoning/tool ID replay and confirm that stripping IDs cannot fix it. A live test deliberately wedges a synthetic checkpoint, then runs the real agent loop for four successful turns across two reloads of unchanged saved state. Each turn makes one HTTP request and correctly recalls a random marker retained only in compacted tool history.

Focused policy, failure-copy, compaction, continuation and prompt-prefix tests; Chromium failure-notice tests (5) and terminal-reload UI E2E tests (3). Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The changed-file check completed; proof-harness type errors were corrected and both affected typechecks now pass. CI on the initial head exposed five stale admission/replay golden assertions; the only corrected fixture field is `store:false`, matching the live-proven contract. The affected suite now passes all 17 tests, and the follow-up independent review is clean. Exact-head CI [43466589308](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43466589308) passed on `15bee219b67f72fc4642dd3573eb8513d57d2a7a`; ClawSweeper reviewed the same head with zero findings and zero open items.

CI run 43462361673 subsequently found a real-Gateway Home test incorrectly assigned to the ordinary parallel UI lane: Gateway startup took 157.7 seconds against the test’s 120-second limit. #196902 introduced the test without its canonical real-Gateway registration. This PR adds that inventory entry and a red/green routing regression proving serial local ownership, ordinary-lane exclusion, and exactly-once dedicated Gateway coverage. The unchanged behavior test passes in the corrected serial project (27.097 seconds); timeouts and behavior assertions remain intact. Independent Codex review of this repair is clean. No inherited-CI bypass is used.

`pnpm check:changed` exposed an unrelated script unused-export regression: #198274 removed the final importer of `RELEASE_VALIDATION_WAIVERS` in `b9f1e62e00d8`. The same unused-export failure reproduces on clean exact parent `af10e5594d38`; this is a main regression, not a passing check.

The committed policy benchmark uses a synthetic 2,000-item active history, five A/A controls and five interleaved A/B pairs. Median wall/CPU µs per request: compacted 0.0058/0.0188 → 0.1155/0.1325; ordinary 0.0058/0.0181 → 5.1141/5.1232. Added sampled allocation is approximately 56 bytes/request. A/A wall controls are 0.0056–0.0057 µs. The owner performs no database or workspace reads; this is a bounded request-input scan, not a session-inventory scan or an end-to-end speedup claim.

Runtime production delta: +34 lines for endpoint-scoped storage policy and shared recovery copy. The additional benchmark and live proof are separate tooling/tests; no state machinery was introduced.

<details>
<summary>Redacted execution evidence</summary>

Observed from synthetic requests to the real public OpenAI Responses API:

```text
compact-first-replay          HTTP 200  completed
compact-exact-repeat         HTTP 200  SSE item_conflict / invalid_request_error / input
compact-without-message-ids   HTTP 200  SSE item_conflict / invalid_request_error / input
compact-without-checkpoint-id HTTP 200  SSE item_conflict / invalid_request_error / input
compact-all-idless            HTTP 200  SSE item_conflict / invalid_request_error / input
```

Terminal excerpts from the real agent/transport and shared failure-copy runs:

```text
✓ src/agents/openai-responses-compaction.live.test.ts > recovers a stored compaction checkpoint on the next agent turn and after reload 15120ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed (1)

✓ gives compacted-history recovery guidance for structured and terminal item conflicts
Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

The committed live test asserts the initial stored success, subsequent `item_conflict`, unchanged serialized checkpoint across reloads, four successful real agent turns, exactly one HTTP request per turn, `store:false`, no `previous_response_id`, and correct recall of compacted tool memory. Run it with `pnpm test:live src/agents/openai-responses-compaction.live.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` using an approved OpenAI API key. prs.title: fix(process): Doctor and spawn-broker cleanup fail when the host denies process-group signals
prs.body:
Closes #198130

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` and spawn-broker shutdown fail when OpenClaw runs on a Linux host that denies process-group signals, such as inside an OpenShell sandbox.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenClaw inside an OpenShell sandbox (or under any seccomp rule that denies `kill(2)` with a negative PID) can finish Doctor maintenance and shut its spawn broker down again. OpenClaw Enterprise holds Agent startup until Doctor reports settled maintenance, so this unblocks Agents that could not start after an upgrade ([openclaw/openclaw-enterprise#5706](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/issues/5706)). Hosts where group signals work are unchanged. No config, state or schema changes, and no update steps.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenShell's child seccomp filter returns EPERM for every process-group signal, including the signal 0 probe. Two probes treated that EPERM as "still alive" forever: `isChildProcessTreeAlive()` (command scopes, Doctor process custody, update handoffs) and the spawn-broker `groupGone()`. Every wait ran to its deadline and failed.

`isProcessGroupGone()` now makes that decision for both. The kernel probe still runs first. Only when the host itself denies the call (the same call against a group id above `PID_MAX_LIMIT`, which the kernel always answers with ESRCH, is refused too) does the `/proc` census decide, and it fails closed: a live member, a census error, or a `/proc` from another PID namespace keeps the group alive. A kernel EPERM from a member owned by another user keeps the old answer. When a broker group signal is denied, cleanup signals each member by PID after rechecking its pgid and start time, reusing the drain's existing per-member step.

Accepted edge cases, named rather than coded around:
- Under the deny, each poll does a synchronous `/proc` scan. That is cheap in a sandbox (the OpenShell workload we checked has 6 processes) but scales with retained detached groups; sharing one census per tick is a possible follow-up.
- A member that forks and exits in the middle of one scan can be missed, the same race the existing drain census accepts.
- `hidepid` or a restricted `/proc` under the deny can still hide a member.

Follow-ups, not in this PR: agent-core `killProcessTree` group signals (used by exec-spawn stop, exec-termination, command custody, provider-local services, and a detached child lost with the broker before its group identity is recorded) still only signal the group, so under the deny those paths can now confirm extinction but cannot kill survivors.

Overlap: #189415 changes the same `terminateBrokerProcessGroup` confirmation for zombie-only groups and leaves permission handling alone. Its `brokerGroupHasLiveMembers` calls `groupGone()`, which this PR replaces with `isProcessGroupGone()`, so whichever lands second needs a one-line rename.

## Evidence

### Review follow-up on 2026-11-13

Rebased onto `main` at `6eb8095ae971f51bfa547644d4d249c21ebb8335`. Both original production commits remain patch-identical after the rebase. [Follow-up commit `1435ab73daa5adf`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1435ab73daa5adf104f489b4c2f88a915eb8083a) addresses ClawSweeper's remaining P2 finding: the Node-only broker scenario now uses `resolveTestNodeExecPath()` for both `execFile` and `resolveRuntimeWorkerArgv`. All existing shutdown and child-extinction assertions are retained.

Focused proof on secretless AWS Linux, Node 24.22.1, with the rebased candidate's exact source tree verified before execution:
- Pinned Bun fork: `pnpm test src/process/spawn-broker/group-custody.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **3/3 pass**, including the real kernel seccomp scenario. Wall time 54.45 s, including 43.15 s of cold worker compilation; test bodies total 1.09 s.
- Node: the same suite plus `cleanup-group.test.ts`, `service-child-group-ownership.test.ts`, and `exec-spawn.test.ts` — **70/70 pass across 4 files**, 13.86 s wall time.
- Final formatting, targeted oxlint, and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json --incremental` — **pass**. The final formatting-only adjustment leaves the tested behavior unchanged; the final checked source tree matches the pushed commit.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of the launcher-repair delta from rebased head `985779b9ea9aea9`, before mechanical formatting — **no actionable findings**. The existing full-PR ClawSweeper review covers `041b1b2509b`; its sole remaining finding is addressed above. New-head broad CI is separate from these focused results.

### Current-head CI and inherited failure

CI run [43438047021, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43438047021) tested head `1435ab73daa5adf104f489b4c2f88a915eb8083a` in merge checkout `b14d600d19758cb6aed4ceb911ffa4401c973a88` against main `64fd44bdaae8434611e841f4fb50d2443c9461f6`. All 10 executed Node test shards and the executed lint, type, and security checks passed. CI remains **failed**, not green: [checks-ui-e2e (1/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43438047021/job/131929016095) timed out after 120000 ms in `Read-only Home real Gateway > opens existing Home for a reader without granting writes and hides denied targets` (`ui/src/e2e/home-readonly.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts:45`), making the downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` fail.

The same test, timeout, and suite stack already fail in [scheduled main run 43425732822, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43425732822/job/131887280121) at `777c036d592808418f95da97cf6b4ee6af614bbc`. The test, its shared suite support, and `src/gateway/server.ts` are byte-identical between that baseline, the CI main parent, and the tested PR merge; this PR changes no UI or Gateway source. This qualifies as an inherited unrelated CI failure for the authorized landing exception. Its underlying UI cause is not repaired or claimed to be a proven flake. No CI rerun or branch refresh was made solely to seek green.

### Contributor runtime and upgrade proof at `041b1b2509b`

Red on the original merge base `664a791058e`, green on `041b1b2509b`, all under a real BPF filter that returns EPERM for `kill()` with a negative PID (the OpenShell rule; wrapper in the linked issue):

| Check | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive`, isolated `HOME` | exit 1: "Command cleanup could not confirm that owned work stopped" | exit 0: "Doctor complete." |
| `SpawnBrokerHost` close with an attached / detached child | fails after 7.4 s: "Spawn broker group cleanup could not be confirmed … kill EPERM" | closes in ~420 ms |
| Command scope settlement | `CommandProcessCleanupError` after 10 s | settles in 30 ms |
| `settleCommandProcessGroups` custody | `cleanup: "uncertain"` after 10.3 s | `cleanup: "normal"` |

Upgrade from the latest stable: the published `openclaw@2026.11.3` npm release (registry integrity verified) was upgraded to the packed build at `041b1b2509b`, with an isolated `HOME`, and Doctor ran under the same filter. On 2026.11.3, `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exits 1 with "Command cleanup could not confirm that owned work stopped" (exit 0 without the filter). After the upgrade, it exits 0 with "Doctor complete.", applies main's pending state and agent database migrations, and keeps the profile's four settings and all workspace files byte-identical. A rerun is clean. Steps, snapshot diff and redacted output: [upgrade proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198132#issuecomment-6854180192).

Committed regressions, each red on the pre-fix source:
- `group-custody.test.ts` runs a real broker in its own Node process under the repo's kernel seccomp fixture (`installKillGroupSeccompFilter`) and checks that close settles and a detached descendant dies.
- `exec-spawn.test.ts` covers scope settlement under a denied probe, that a kernel EPERM keeps the group alive without a census, and that the census never runs when the kernel probe works.
- `service-child-group-ownership.test.ts` and `cleanup-group.test.ts` cover the census contract and per-member signalling (late joiners get SIGKILL, one unsignalable member does not stop the others, errors retry until the deadline, a foreign `/proc` signals nothing).

Contributor local checks at `041b1b2509b` on Linux with Node 24 (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`; the pinned Bun fork could not be staged on that host): 61 test files across `src/process/spawn-broker`, the supervisor service-child suites and every `isChildProcessTreeAlive` consumer pass. `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, `check:test-mock-exports`, both import-cycle guards and `check:docs` pass. `pnpm check` passes every guard and typecheck lane. Its lint lane fails only on untouched files (mostly `ui/`), because of the plain-oxlint fallback without the Bun fork, and fails the same way on the base. `proxy-retention.test.ts` ("releases completed command proxies after the host closes") is flaky on main without this change (2 of 3 runs fail).

Size against the rebased merge base: production +229/-78 in three existing owners (`child-process-tree.ts`, `service-child-group-ownership.ts`, `spawn-broker/cleanup.ts`), tests +389 net, docs +4. The drain's own per-member signalling moved into the shared step rather than being duplicated.

prs.title: fix(backup): stop removing further schedules after Ctrl+C
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after Ctrl+C, `openclaw backup disable` (which removes every matching backup cron schedule) keeps removing the remaining schedules until the CLI is force-killed.

## User Impact

User impact: Ctrl+C during `openclaw backup disable` now lets the schedule being removed finish with its removal confirmed, starts no other removal, and reports the schedules that were never reached as interrupted. Schedules that were not reached keep their cron entry — so for a disable they remain scheduled, and the acknowledgement no longer falsely claims "Scheduled backups disabled."

## Why This Change Was Made

`backupDisableCommand` removes one cron job per Gateway RPC in a loop that never reads the command's cancellation signal. The CLI now forwards its existing AsyncWorkScope interrupt signal through the loop and stops starting further removals once it fires. An already-admitted removal keeps its reply (the mutation RPC carries no abort signal, so its receipt settles), and when the loop stops early the acknowledgement reports the not-reached schedules as interrupted instead of printing the all-disabled message.

This follows the admitted-mutation handling and bulk-loop cancellation applied to `sessions archive/delete` (#198314) and `sessions import` (#197508).

## Evidence

Shipped CLI Ctrl+C proof, synthetic loopback WS peer speaking the real OpenClaw wire protocol (answers `cron.list` with two schedules, **holds then releases** the first `cron.remove` after SIGINT), source CLI in a real PTY targeted at the peer via `--port`:

- BASE `c0def7c89648` (review finding on the interrupted acknowledgement unfixed): the admitted removal's receipt is **kept** and the second removal never starts, but the CLI still prints `Scheduled backups disabled.` even though offsite-job remains scheduled — the misleading-success defect the review called out.
- HEAD `8a20a85bc47c` (this PR): the admitted removal settles, the second removal never starts, and the CLI reports `Scheduled backups disabled before completion: 1 schedule(s) not reached (interrupted).`

Both heads show one removal request and one released reply (the admitted receipt is kept; later removals stay unstarted).

Discriminant test: `stops removing further backup schedules once interrupted` asserts only the first schedule is removed, the mutation RPC carries no abort signal, and the interrupted acknowledgement is printed (red on the review finding, green with the fix).

Evidence bundle (receipts, raw PTY logs, harness): https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/backup-disable-signal/proof/backup-disable-signal/EVIDENCE.md

issues.title: Dream only sees the first 1000 characters of each cumulative checkpoint in history.jsonl

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Since HKUDS/nanobot#5610, each compaction appends the whole cumulative checkpoint to `memory/history.jsonl`, but `build_dream_prompt` still keeps only the first 1000 characters of each entry. Whatever lands later in a checkpoint never reaches Dream, and the cursor then moves past it for good. On my workspace, 69.8% of conversation journal text has never been shown to Dream. Nothing is logged; `/dream` reports a normal completion.

Code at `eb8546c32`:

1. Cumulative checkpoint appended whole: [`agent/memory.py#L954-L955`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/eb8546c32111b157759132eefb020545cc196e69/nanobot/agent/memory.py#L954-L955)
2. Per-entry head truncation: [`agent/memory.py#L521`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/eb8546c32111b157759132eefb020545cc196e69/nanobot/agent/memory.py#L521) → [`utils/helpers.py#L394-L398`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/eb8546c32111b157759132eefb020545cc196e69/nanobot/utils/helpers.py#L394-L398)
3. Cursor advances past the batch: [`command/builtin.py#L433`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/eb8546c32111b157759132eefb020545cc196e69/nanobot/command/builtin.py#L433), [`cli/gateway_runtime.py#L655`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/eb8546c32111b157759132eefb020545cc196e69/nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py#L655)

The cap dates from HKUDS/nanobot#5114, when entries were incremental and short; `test_truncates_long_entries_at_1000_chars` pins it.

### Steps to Reproduce

Both files are on [`shakewingo:fix/dream-cumulative-truncation-repro`](https://github.com/shakewingo/nanobot/tree/fix/dream-cumulative-truncation-repro), one commit on top of `eb8546c32`: [`tests/agent/test_dream_cumulative_truncation.py`](https://github.com/shakewingo/nanobot/blob/0d68a3995620afc83c3e4cbf647ab7132682cd35/tests/agent/test_dream_cumulative_truncation.py), [`scripts/dream_history_audit.py`](https://github.com/shakewingo/nanobot/blob/0d68a3995620afc83c3e4cbf647ab7132682cd35/scripts/dream_history_audit.py).

**Deterministic test** (scripted model; real code from `archive()` to `build_dream_prompt()`). The same 40 facts written as incremental checkpoints all reach Dream; written as cumulative checkpoints, only the first 13 do:

```text
$ pytest tests/agent/test_dream_cumulative_truncation.py -q
AssertionError: history entry lengths [769, 1559, 2349, 3139]; Dream sees only facts [0, 1, ..., 12]
1 failed, 1 passed
```

**Audit any workspace** (standard library only; prints aggregate counts, no entry text or session ids):

```bash
SNAP=$(mktemp -d)
cp ~/.nanobot/workspace/memory/{history.jsonl,.cursor,.dream_cursor} "$SNAP"/
python3 -I scripts/dream_history_audit.py "$SNAP"
```


### Expected Behavior

Every journal entry reaches Dream in full before the cursor passes it. Entries that do not fit in one run wait for the next run instead of being cut.


### Relevant Logs

My workspace, 2026-11-13 (the journal keeps about the last 1000 entries, about three weeks here; Dream had consumed all but the 2 newest):

| | conversation | heartbeat |
|---|---:|---:|
| entries > 1000 chars | 63 / 104 (61%) | 539 / 898 (60%) |
| text past the first 1000 chars of its entry | **69.8%** | 15.5% |
| distinct fact lines never in any entry's first 1000 chars | 315 / 556 (56.7%), incl. 15 `[correction]` | 84 / 1156 (7.3%) |

- The 69.8% does not depend on fact order or format. The fact-line count is an upper bound: it matches lines exactly, so a reworded fact seen elsewhere still counts as unseen.
- Conversation data is almost all from one long session (100 of 104 entries).

<details><summary>Full audit output</summary>

```text
entries: 1002
write cursor / Dream cursor: 2168 / 2166
entries not yet consumed by Dream: 2

== conversation
time range: 2026-10-25 14:21 .. 2026-11-13 05:25
entries / sessions: 104 / 3
entries per session: [100, 3, 1]
[RAW] fallback entries (no fact lines): 26
entries > 1000 chars: 63 (61%)
longest entry: 16029 chars; median: 1487
characters past the first 1000 of their entry: 69.8%
adjacent same-session verbatim fact-line overlap: median 0.00 over 69 pairs
distinct fact lines: 556
never inside the first 1000 chars of any entry: 315 (56.7%) {'durable': 228, 'ephemeral': 70, 'correction': 15, 'permanent': 2}

== heartbeat
time range: 2026-10-25 10:34 .. 2026-11-13 06:25
entries / sessions: 898 / 1
entries per session: [898]
[RAW] fallback entries (no fact lines): 86
entries > 1000 chars: 539 (60%)
```

### Bug Description

OpenAI retired `gpt-image-1` on October 23, 2026, and `dall-e-3` and `dall-e-2` on May 12, 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations). Requests that name them now fail, but nanobot still offers all three in the OpenAI image model list:

- https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/ce3f36983d6bee40d1f4cee58f71f3a1888ea648/nanobot/providers/image_generation.py#L1096 (`OpenAIImageGenerationClient.model_options`, which the WebUI settings show as the OpenAI image models)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In the WebUI settings, pick OpenAI for image generation.
2. Choose `gpt-image-1`, `dall-e-3` or `dall-e-2` from the model list.
3. Generate an image. The request fails because OpenAI no longer serves that model.

### Expected Behavior

The list offers only models OpenAI still serves. The default, `gpt-image-2`, still works, so dropping the three retired ids fixes it. OpenAI's replacement for `gpt-image-1` is `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, if you want to offer one of those instead.

### Environment

Not environment-specific: found by reading the code at commit ce3f369. Provider: OpenAI. Models: `gpt-image-1`, `dall-e-3`, `dall-e-2`.

---
Found by [Since](https://since.dev), which watches code for model and API retirements and opens the fix before the date. It's free for open source, and I work on it. Full scan of this repo: https://since.dev/scan/HKUDS/nanobot

Happy to open a PR if that helps.

issues.title: QQ: outbound attachments over ~2MB randomly fail with 'media upload failed: empty response' (botpy default 5s HTTP timeout, no retry)
issues.body:
### Bug Description

On the QQ channel, sending a moderately large attachment (2.4 MB PDF) fails roughly one time in two with:

```
[botpy] 请求超时，请求连接: https://api.sgroup.qq.com/v2/users/<openid>/files
ERROR | qq | media upload failed: empty response
```

and the user only receives the fallback text `[Attachment send failed: <filename>]`.

Root cause looks like a client-side timeout in nanobot's own botpy setup, not a QQ-side limit:

- `nanobot/channels/qq/runtime.py` builds the botpy client as `super().__init__(intents=intents, ext_handlers=False)` and never passes `timeout`.
- botpy's `Client.__init__` defaults to `timeout: int = 5`, and `BotHttp` applies it as `aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=self.timeout)` — i.e. **the whole HTTP request, including the base64 upload body**, gets a 5 s budget.
- Uploading a 2.4 MB file means a ~3.3 MB base64 JSON body to `api.sgroup.qq.com`; that request legitimately takes 5–8 s from a cloud host, so it lands right on the edge of botpy's default.
- When it does time out, botpy does not raise; it logs the warning and returns `None`, so `_post_base64file` yields nothing, `_send_media` logs `media upload failed: empty response`, returns `False`, and `send()` substitutes the `[Attachment send failed: ...]` text. There is no retry.

Same file, same filename, retried ~1 minute later → succeeded (`media sent: <filename>`). Calling `/v2/users/<openid>/files` directly with the same payload also returns 200, so neither the file nor the filename (`+` characters, Chinese text) is the problem — only the tight client budget is.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the QQ channel (`channels.qq`) with a valid appId/secret.
2. Send an outbound attachment of roughly 2 MB or more, e.g. have the agent call `message(media=["/path/to/2.4MB.pdf"])`.
3. Roughly half the attempts fail with `media upload failed: empty response`; the recipient gets `[Attachment send failed: <filename>]` instead of the file. Retrying the identical file often succeeds.

### Expected Behavior

The attachment is uploaded and delivered; a transient upload timeout should be retried (or the client timeout should be large enough for a multi-MB base64 body), rather than silently degraded to a `[Attachment send failed: ...]` text.

### Relevant Logs

```
2026-11-13T19:02:34.426+0800 | INFO  | Tool call: message({"content": "...", "media": ["/srv/nanobot/workspace/lab/courses/2026170832+高正扬+计算机技术049班.pdf"]})
2026-11-13T19:02:40.016+0800 | WARNING | [botpy] 请求超时，请求连接: https://api.sgroup.qq.com/v2/users/63E4F833.../files
2026-11-13T19:02:40.016+0800 | ERROR   | qq | media upload failed: empty response
2026-11-13T19:02:40.0xx+0800 | (user received "[Attachment send failed: 2026170832+高正扬+计算机技术049班.pdf]")

# identical file, retried a minute later
2026-11-13T19:03:16.376+0800 | INFO  | Tool call: message({"content": "...", "media": [".../2026170832-高正扬-计算机技术049班.pdf"]})
2026-11-13T19:03:22.916+0800 | INFO  | qq | media sent: 2026170832-高正扬-计算机技术049班.pdf
```

File: 2,574,579 bytes → 3.27 MiB base64 body.

### nanobot Version

0.3.5

### Python Version

3.12

### Operating System

Linux

### Channel / Platform

QQ

### LLM Provider

Other (opencode Go / deepseek-v4.1-flash)

### Configuration (Optional)

```yaml
channels:
  qq:
    enabled: true
    msgFormat: markdown
    # no timeout knob exists for the botpy HTTP client
```

### Additional Context

Suggested fix (either or both):

1. Pass an explicit `timeout=` when constructing the botpy client in `_make_bot_class` (e.g. 30 s), ideally configurable via `channels.qq`.
2. Retry the upload once (or twice, with a short backoff) in `_send_media` when `_post_base64file` returns an empty/`None` result. A timed-out upload produces no `file_info`, so retrying is safe.

Relevant code: `nanobot/channels/qq/runtime.py` — `_make_bot_class()` (`super().__init__(intents=..., ext_handlers=False)`), `_send_media()`, `_post_base64file()`.

Note the 5 s default also covers every other botpy API call (text send, ack), so this may bite slower links well before the file upload does.

issues.title: Tool parameter validation silently skips $ref / anyOf / oneOf schemas and crashes on tuple-form items
issues.body:
`Tool.validate_params` / `Schema.validate_json_schema_value` (nanobot/agent/tools/base.py) never resolve local `$ref` fragments and never evaluate `anyOf`/`oneOf` branches. Those are exactly the shapes MCP servers emit for model-typed and union parameters (e.g. a FastMCP tool built from `def book(addr: Address, count: int | str)`), so for such parameters local validation is a no-op:

- `addr` given as `{"zip": "98101"}` (missing required `city`, `zip` not an integer) → `validate_params` returns `[]`
- `addr` given as the string `"Seattle"` instead of an object → `[]`
- `count` given as a dict matching neither the integer nor the string branch → `[]`

The invalid arguments are forwarded to the MCP server unchecked, instead of producing the recoverable "invalid parameters" error other parameter shapes get.

Separately, an array parameter whose `items` is a list (draft-07 tuple form; `prefixItems` positions have the same problem) crashes both `cast_params` and `validate_params` with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`. That happens inside `ToolRegistry.prepare_call`, outside the tool-execution error handling, so one such tool schema turns every call into an unhandled exception rather than a tool error the model can react to.

Root cause: the validator reads `schema.get("type")`, which is absent for `$ref`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` fragments, and returns without checking anything; the array branch passes `schema["items"]` into the recursion assuming it is always a dict. The existing validation tests only use flat, native-type schemas, so none of these shapes are covered.

I have a fix with regression tests ready (validation resolves `$defs`/`definitions` refs and evaluates the composition branches; tuple/`prefixItems` elements are validated and cast positionally) and would like to open a PR.

prs.title: feat(agent): integrate mst-python as a metasearch provider
prs.body:
This PR adds the Meta-Search Tool (mst) as a new web search provider for nanobot.

## What it is

MST aggregates results from multiple search engines (DuckDuckGo, Google, Brave, Bing, etc.) simultaneously and merges them using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). This gives richer coverage than any single provider alone.

Inspired by [SearXNG](https://github.com/searxng/searxng) — MST brings the same metasearch concept to Python code directly, without needing a separate web server or Docker container. Package at https://github.com/openmtx/meta-search-tool.

## Changes

- **`nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`** — added `mst` as a new search provider with `_search_mst()` method. Supports:
  - `mst_engines` config / `MST_ENGINES` env var to select which engines to query (defaults to all ready engines)
  - `mst_weights` config / `MST_WEIGHTS` env var for per-engine ranking weight overrides
  - Graceful fallback when `mst-python` is not installed
- **`nanobot/webui/settings_api.py`** — added JSON parsing and validation for `mst_engines` and `mst_weights` in the WebUI settings API
- **`pyproject.toml`** — moved `mst-python` to `[project.optional-dependencies] mst` (optional, not installed by default)
- **`tests/tools/test_search_tools.py`** — 6 new tests covering success, missing package, env vars, config priority, and timeout
- **`tests/webui/test_settings_api.py`** — 4 new tests for MST engine/weight validation in the settings API

## Usage

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "web": {
      "search": {
        "provider": "mst",
        "mst_engines": ["ddg", "google", "brave"],
        "mst_weights": {"google": 2.0, "ddg": 1.0}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Or via env vars:
```bash
export MST_ENGINES="ddg,google,bing"
export MST_WEIGHTS="{\"google\": 2.0}"
```

Install with: `nanobot plugins enable mst` (or `uv pip install 'nanobot-ai[mst]'`)

## Testing

- All existing web search tests pass
- 10 new unit tests cover MST-specific functionality

## Problem

Stable PyPI uploads require a maintainer credential and manual artifact selection. Start PyPI Trusted Publishing when a maintainer publishes an approved GitHub Release. Keep a manual workflow for testing and recovery.
