prs.title: fix(webui): scope remote health checks to visible demand
prs.body:
## Why

After opening a remote host, retained views kept triggering directory reads every five seconds—even after switching to Local or hiding the browser tab. Each read also checked every established remote connection. Tie health checks to visible demand instead of retained iframe lifetime.

## What changed

- Check only the active remote host, or established connections while the host menu/management page is visible. Pause when hidden or no longer needed; revalidate on return without discarding frames, drafts or shared tunnels. Steady polling uses the targeted response to update the directory without a separate snapshot read; existing connections remain eligible for checks after errors.
- Make ordinary directory reads snapshot-only. Explicit `check` targets use the existing gateway lifetime lock and reuse completed checks for five seconds, including overlapping requests from other tabs.
- Count distinct failed samples rather than cached responses, reject stale results after connection changes, and preserve a queued wake even if the previous request fails.

## Scope

Remote-host health observation only. No changes to chat execution, SSH/WebSocket lifetime, other settings polling, or compatibility negotiation; no new push framework.

Contributes to [NAN-338](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-338/减少-webui-空闲轮询以状态变更通知和重连同步替代重复查询)

## Tradeoffs

Unobserved hosts can have stale displayed health until revisited. Observed checks can reuse a result up to five seconds old; explicit connect/repair validation remains separate. A check already in flight may finish after hiding the tab.

## Blast Radius

The local remote-host UI and `/api/remote-instances` contract change together under the same-version WebUI/gateway support policy. Authentication, loopback restrictions, gateway/view identity checks and the existing 12-second health budget remain intact. Disconnect/Forget still own transport teardown.

## Verification

- **Before/after:** with one retained remote view and Local selected, the original hook made **6 reads / 30 simulated seconds**; the new hook makes **0**. Both new demand-scope tests fail against the original hook for the intended reasons and pass here. [Regression scenarios](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/666edb77e3bd64d40ae8e880bf9a1b48ea48107c/webui/src/tests/host-sessions.test.tsx).
- **Real Chromium visibility:** a complete isolated browser run used actual tab switching, without overriding visibility. Each steady observation lasted 6.2 seconds: hidden tab **0** new reads; Local with a retained iframe **0**; active remote **1** targeted request; open host menu **1** periodic targeted request. Showing the tab caused an immediate targeted request. The same iframe and both drafts survived. Directory/RPC/remote content were synthetic; this is not live SSH or production traffic measurement.
- Frontend remote/host suites: **199 passed across 8 files**. Backend instances/pairing/proxy suites: **239 passed**, including targeted requests, concurrent/fresh-result reuse, replacement, cancellation and shutdown safety.
- Follow-up verification: steady observed polling uses **1 request / 5-second cycle instead of 2**, discovers connections from returned snapshots, and keeps checking after setup/identity errors without reviving a mismatched view. The frontend suites, TypeScript, touched-file ESLint and `git diff --check` passed on this update.
- Backend tests, Ruff, backend basedpyright, client import boundaries, production build and browser sampling passed on `90fe91a`; they were not rerun for this two-file frontend follow-up. Vite reported large-chunk warnings.
- Live SSH acceptance and cross-version behavior were not tested. No running user gateway or remote host was changed.

prs.title: fix(webui): keep history loading until content is ready
prs.body:
## Why

Pulling for earlier history can return a bookkeeping-only page or an incomplete turn fragment before any additional content is ready to display. Treating that first response as completion makes the nine-square indicator retract too early. Keep the pull pending until display content is admitted, history is exhausted, or a read fails.

## What changed

- Continue latest-history and navigation reads within one loading operation. Use the message list's activity filtering and include visible fork boundaries in the readiness comparison, without treating usage or timing updates as new content.
- Preserve completion metadata across discarded bookkeeping pages, in both navigation directions. Reuse the event projector with one retained terminal record per fragmented turn instead of accumulating skipped raw pages.
- Route real Blocks-button and boundary-gesture retries to the failed cursor. Publish navigation pages through one synchronous owner so a history response cannot overwrite trace details arriving in the same React batch.
- Rebase the reading anchor when delayed layout hits a scroll bound, so a later prepend cannot restore an obsolete offset and jump the conversation.
- Add pagination and geometry regressions plus an opt-in browser fixture for slow, fast, multi-page, and failed reads.

## Scope

WebUI only: no gateway, protocol, persistence, or dependency changes. Reuse the existing Blocks indicator and spring; add no production delays or minimum loading duration. Deferred Markdown, images, and highlighting remain layout work rather than additional completion gates.

## Tradeoffs

One gesture may fetch several cursor pages when they add no display content. Navigation keeps a three-page raw window plus the retained terminal record for each fragmented turn. Failed reads preserve the readable window and accepted metadata and retry the failed cursor; self-contained pages extend that readable window rather than evicting it through intervening bookkeeping pages.

## Blast Radius

Latest-history pagination, reconnect fragment recovery, prompt navigation, deferred activity details, fork dividers, and reading-position compensation. Verification includes interactions with command-session snapshots and trace-detail expansion.

## Verification

Run from `webui/` on the final integrated changes:

- `bun run test src/tests/useSessions.test.tsx src/tests/usePromptHistory.test.tsx src/tests/useReconnectRuns.test.tsx src/tests/useNanobotStream.test.tsx src/tests/thread-viewport.test.tsx src/tests/thread-shell.test.tsx src/tests/thread-messages.test.tsx src/tests/thread-display-projection.test.ts` — 507 passed.
- `NANOBOT_BROWSER_TEST_PORT=4196 bun run test:browser browser/history-boundary.spec.ts browser/exec-session.spec.ts --workers=1` — 32 passed. Covers continuous loading across non-display pages, desktop wheel and mobile touch, real button/gesture retry, fast completion, exhaustion, reduced motion, bounded navigation, delayed layout, and command activity.
- Review regressions cover hidden task-create activity, completion metadata after more than three bookkeeping fragments and failed continuation, backward terminal-record retention, same-batch detail expansion, and fork-marker-only pages in both directions with their rendered divider (including loading parent history from the first child prompt).
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run build`, and `git diff --check` — passed. Build retains the existing large-chunk warning.
- The top-bound layout regression reproduced a roughly 160 px jump before the anchor fix; the passing browser test requires less than 1 px drift.

Interactive fixture: `/browser/fixture.html?case=history-boundary&preview=pages&lang=zh-CN` on the local Vite server. Browser verification uses simulated responses, not a live authenticated gateway. Full frontend suites were not run.

Resolves [NAN-303](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-303/让-webui-历史加载头连续下拉揭示松手停靠并随用户滚动退出)

prs.title: feat(webui): stabilize session transitions and add a Mac-style goal notch
prs.body:
Resolves [NAN-443](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-443/稳定-webui-session-切换的输入框布局并加入消息区淡出淡入)

## Why

Session changes should replace the conversation without making the composer jump or compete with running subagent activity. Goal details belong in a quiet, separate surface, and dismissing an informational overlay should return users to the control they were using rather than unexpectedly moving focus to a header button.

## What changed

- Add interruptible, latest-navigation-wins session transitions: fade thread content, preserve unscaled composer text and stable anchors, coordinate with theme transitions, and skip unchanged desktop panes and reduced-motion captures. Closing the active temporary chat commits its replacement immediately, without animation, so route cleanup cannot override the destination.
- Move Goal out of the composer into a Mac-style top notch with continuous inverse corners and sidebar-derived materials. Active goal details have a fixed Markdown-sized heading, independently scrolling feathered content, a 25dvh height limit, reversible expansion/collapse, and narrow-screen header controls that remain reachable. Clamp long headings to leave the objective readable on portrait and landscape screens.
- Keep blocked goals visible using the existing gateway state (`active: false`, `status: blocked`). Show the blocking reason rather than the goal title, with a muted red circular alert icon and matching text; retain the objective in expanded details. Soften the expanded shadow and add a localized, interactive Goal preview to the component gallery. A live block returns open details to the reason; loaded Markdown retains the same color as the alert icon.
- Restore Escape focus according to the actual opener across Goal, model selection, session/source information, prompt search, workspace selection and feature settings. Preserve keyboard focus indicators, outside-click targets and dialog handoffs. When saving disables the feature switch that opened a dialog, restore focus to Configure instead. Add `webui --dev-port` for isolated previews.

- Remove the unused Goal close-button translations across all 10 locales; retain the blocked-state text used by screen readers.

## Scope

Frontend presentation and focus ownership, plus the development launcher. Goal execution, gateway policy, wire contracts, persistence formats and dependencies are unchanged. The running subagent dock stays beside the composer.

## Verification

History is organized into two commits: `9ab5562b9` adds `--dev-port`; `5168166cd` contains the WebUI changes and follow-up fixes. The final Git tree is identical to pre-squash head `4059e9712`; the evidence below retains its original commit identities, and tests were not rerun solely for this history rewrite.

prs.title: fix(agent): project safe execution activity across channels
prs.body:
## Why

Native `exec_session` observer waits were presented as completed user operations, exposing internal handles and inflating activity counts even while the command was still running. Project owner-observed execution facts at the shared public progress boundary so WebUI and other channels receive meaningful command status instead of internal control calls.

Refs [NAN-262](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-262).

## What changed

* Add opt-in execution contracts and typed return-point facts to native shell tools. Preserve model-facing results and execution ownership; successful waits, input management and inventory calls remain silent, while real results and control failures remain visible.
* Derive public text and structured activity together, preserving mixed-tool order and existing progress/hint settings. Apply the same read-only projection before history detail, summary and count calculation.
* Render localized execution activity in WebUI. Keep core protocol 1 with optional `webui.execution-activity.v2`, safe legacy text fallback and a separate optional `execution_detail` field.
* Follow-up `ffb5f36fc` / `4f67ca784`: reuse public batching, remove duplicate history filtering, lazily stop soft-page counting at its budget, and reuse wire events only for the requested detail group. These changes remove **15 net production lines** versus the initial PR; the new regression checks protect complete delivery with bounded projection work. Synchronize five existing test-double/expectation modules with the new internal registry contract, fixing the initial Python CI failures without production fallbacks or timeout increases.
* Channel follow-up `baa78d967`: discriminate public execution items before interpreting ordinary tool fields. Linear sends native thoughts (running states ephemeral, outcomes persistent); opt-in Weixin sends native text items using the shared command-status formatter. Preserve ordingoary tool actions, Linear redaction/retry identities, and Weixin causal order, shared run ID, progress cap and final-reply quota reservation. Replace the duplicated Telegram real-shell scenario with a focused send-adapter/HTML-escaping/topic test; real execution remains covered once at the shared boundary.

## Scope

Covers native command launch/control activity, shared channel delivery, WebSocket live events and WebUI history/replay. Does not rewrite saved conversations, filter assistant prose, copy stdout into progress, or introduce background command monitoring. No dependencies or configuration defaults change.

## Tradeoffs

Terminal status is reported when an existing tool return observes it; an unobserved background command does not gain an automatic completion push. Legacy records without typed terminal facts cannot recover precise historical exit results. Historical compatibility adds a public projection pass; measurements below do not establish a universal zero-regression guarantee.

## Blast Radius

Touches tool-result reporting, progress hooks, Linear/Weixin native progress adapters, Telegram delivery tests, WebSocket activity classification and WebUI transcript projection. Ordinary and third-party tools retain their default presentation, including tools with the same names that have not opted in. Mixed records retain causal order and stable replay identities. Detail-event retention is request-local and restricted to the requested group; ordinary history responses do not retain those payloads.

## Verification

Latest published source: `baa78d9673d28cf707ad4db2015ac06b579b892c`, direct parent `4f67ca7842a36f61ea7ac104caf98dcd637b104a`. This follow-up changes only two channel adapters and three channel test modules; shared execution/projection, WebUI/history, dependencies and defaults are unchanged.

Fresh channel-follow-up verification:

* Regression-first: 13 expected failures against the pre-fix adapters, with the narrowed Telegram test already passing. Final related matrix: **561 passed**, exit 0, covering the three channel packages, real shared shell/progress, runner integration, channel manager and WebSocket outbound delivery. Adapter cases include started-vs-end, completion, exit 7 with incomplete output, timeout, stop and control failure; Weixin mixed progress retains the cap, run ID and final reply.
* Full Ruff, Python import boundaries (10 rules / 167 files) and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh full backend BasedPyright remains **FAIL: 1025 errors**, normalized added/removed 0/0 against the recorded local diagnostic baseline.
* Latest-head [CI run 39229504997](<https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39229504997>): **in progress** after a bounded 300-second observation. Linux 3.11, Linux 3.14 + coverage (including strict BasedPyright), Docker and Windows process compatibility passed; WebUI and Windows full-suite jobs were still running at readback. No background watcher is retained.

Inherited performance/shared/UI evidence below retains its original snapshot identity. Performance-follow-up source: `4f67ca7842a36f61ea7ac104caf98dcd637b104a`. Benchmark source is its clean automatic integration with main `af68da3280c87316f00240de62b1f27056892ab1`, tree `80521d843f0427ab9b2fc1e144c8547f966812bb`; exported Python files were compared with that exact tree. Main already includes PR HKUDS/nanobot#6301, so its navigation-cache improvement is not attributed here.

* Previous-head focused Python integration/regression matrix: **559 passed, 1 skipped**, exit 0. The skip is unavailable Windows symlink creation. Includes all affected runner/hook fixture modules, real shell waits/results, complete/deferred history, counts, WebSocket delivery and the Telegram send adapter.
* Previous-head separate serial CLI matrix: **163 passed, 1 skipped**, exit 0; the skip is unavailable Windows `termios`. Full Ruff, Python import boundaries (10 rules / 167 files) and `git diff --check` passed.
* Previous-head [CI run 39222769201](<https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39222769201>) **passed**: Python minimum 3.11, latest 3.14 + coverage including strict BasedPyright and serial CLI, Windows 3.14, Windows process compatibility, WebUI tests/browser regressions/build, and Docker.
* Five interleaved benchmark rounds per snapshot, 80 synchronous handler requests per round/workload plus real authenticated loopback HTTP. Ordinary response payloads were semantically identical across snapshots; legacy-control removal was checked separately. In a 300-call dense turn, stored projection calls fell **901 → 339 per page** with complete deferred-detail delivery. Detail serialization is now once per event; the regression test checks actual delivery as well as work counts.
* Real native shell: five rounds of 100 zero-duration observations and two actual one-second waits, then successful completion. No measured observer slowdown; running observations emitted no public wait activity. This evidence uses the unchanged native execution/progress files from the final source.
* HTTP RTT varied substantially even on unchanged prompt/304 paths. Final dense-page CPU medians were main 22.85 ms / initial PR 28.71 ms / follow-up 25.59 ms, with overlapping run ranges; the remaining main-versus-head difference is recorded rather than presented as zero regression. Full latency, output/error counts, CPU ranges and separate memory/profile evidence are recorded in the [NAN-262](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-262/阻止内部执行协议文案泄露到-webui-和其他-channel-的用户消息) implementation document.

Unchanged frontend evidence inherited from initial head `3a3ec064b`: 262 focused Vitest tests across eight files, frontend import checks/self-tests, lint and production build passed; that head's WebUI CI also passed. The later changes are Python-only. Initial isolated gateway/browser acceptance covered completion, exit 7, stop, actual eight-second timeout, stale-handle failure, two real observer waits per scenario, live/history agreement, Working/Stop, refresh/reconnect and desktop/narrow layouts. Frozen protocol-1 client parsing accepted actual current-host history for all five scenarios; deferred-field compatibility used an explicit fixture, not an old graphical browser.

The initial local full-project checks failed with unchanged baseline diagnostics: backend 1025/1025 (the local environment lacks channel dependencies) and frontend 471/471, normalized added/removed 0/0. Initial-head strict backend CI passed with installed channel dependencies, while its Python tests failed on the 18 now-repaired contract/fixture cases. Final-head CI results are recorded separately above; these earlier local failures are not relabeled as passes.

Limits: no real-model performance or multi-user/p99 guarantee is claimed. The isolated gateway uses a deterministic local provider. Native real-shell execution is checked at the shared owner/progress boundary. Telegram, Linear and Weixin exercise their real send adapters against fake external API boundaries; real external delivery remains unverified. Collector/incomplete-output categories have typed test coverage rather than live fault injection. User visual feedback remains pending. The original preview was stopped under the recorded request to shut down all test instances; this follow-up did not restart it.

prs.title: fix(webui): clarify command session activity
prs.body:
## Why

Repeated `exec_session` checks currently expose an internal session ID and can make a completed check look like a completed command. Show the source command when it is already available and distinguish operations from the last observed process state.

## What changed

- Resolve source commands from already-loaded activity within the current chat or subagent; preserve separate calls and update the lookup at relevant tool, history and detail boundaries rather than on ordinary streamed text.
- Present the observed status and input/stop operations explicitly. Fold consecutive passive checks for the same session behind an expandable disclosure without hiding individual results.
- Preserve expanded details in fragmented history and prevent a stale detail request from being reused after switching chats away and back.

## Scope

This is a WebUI-only improvement. It adds no command polling, requests for unloaded history, or changes to execution, waiting or cleanup. It does not complete the issue's cross-channel, typed-execution scope.

Contributes to [NAN-262](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-262)

## Tradeoffs

The existing protocol exposes formatted result text, so the final formatter footer is parsed on a best-effort basis; optional reason lines are not typed facts and arbitrary output can be ambiguous. An ambiguous termination reason is presented as a neutral exit with its code. Command redaction is heuristic: common `-u`, `--user` and `--proxy-user` credentials are covered, but not every possible way to place a secret in a command.

On Windows, production `AgentActivityCluster` renders were compared on base `3f65a8f86` and this change using the same single-trace fixture, 10 interleaved measured samples after two warmups, measuring synchronous React commit plus layout. With 500 consecutive passive checks, collapsed DOM nodes were 22 → 24; p95 initial mount was 2.1 → 3.9 ms and p95 append/update 1.0 → 2.7 ms. At 10 checks, p95 mount was 1.5 → 1.6 ms. Explicitly expanding all 500 checks produced 5,513 nodes and took 75.3 ms p95; it is an on-demand cost. A separate 100,000-character command probe (six samples) measured p95 mount of 1.1 → 3.1 ms with four checks, and 1.1 → 1.7 ms with five checks folded. These are component measurements, not end-to-end latency or a claim of zero overhead. A focused streaming test verifies that 100 ordinary text deltas retain the same command-source snapshot.

## Blast Radius

The changes affect WebUI thread and subagent activity, including loaded history and deferred trace details. State parsing and command previews depend on the existing formatter and redaction rules described above.

## Verification

- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports` (42 passed), `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run`, and `bun run build`.
- Seven focused Vitest files (489 passed), covering result states, source lookup, ordering, redaction, history windows, deferred details and switching chats.
- `bun run test:browser -- browser/exec-session.spec.ts --trace=retain-on-failure`: 2 synthetic-fixture Chromium tests passed (1280 px and 360 px).
- A local full browser run was intentionally stopped after 112/529 completed tests, before the final source snapshot, due to host memory pressure and a subsequently fixed output-ambiguity case. A local coverage run was also stopped when further review findings required source changes. Neither is a full-suite pass; complete WebUI coverage and browser suites are delegated to PR CI.

prs.title: fix(tools): validate $ref/anyOf/oneOf schemas and tuple-form items
prs.body:
Fixes #6485.

Tool parameter validation skipped exactly the schema shapes MCP servers emit for model-typed and union parameters: `validate_json_schema_value` never resolved local `$ref` fragments and never evaluated `anyOf`/`oneOf`, so a missing required nested field or a wrong-typed value passed unchecked and was forwarded to the server. Array parameters with tuple-form `items` (or `prefixItems`) crashed validation and casting with `AttributeError` inside `prepare_call`, escaping the tool-error contract.

This change resolves `$defs`/`definitions` refs during validation (threaded from the tool's root schema through the recursion), evaluates `anyOf` (at least one branch must match) and `oneOf` (exactly one), and validates/casts array elements positionally for tuple-form `items` and `prefixItems`. Casting behavior for union and referenced parameters is intentionally unchanged: the cast layer keeps abstaining where a branch choice would be a guess, and validation is the boundary that rejects bad input.

Six regression tests in tests/tools/test_tool_validation.py cover nested `$ref` enforcement, non-object values for referenced parameters, JSON-string input surfacing a validation error, `anyOf` branch matching, and positional tuple/`prefixItems` handling. They fail on main and pass here; the tests/tools, tests/agent and tests/cron suites show no new failures against an unmodified-main baseline (identical pre-existing environment failures on both sides).

prs.title: fix(grep): search text declared by a byte-order mark
prs.body:
## Summary
Grep treated UTF-16 and UTF-32 text as binary because those encodings contain NUL bytes, and it left a UTF-8 byte-order mark on the first line. `read_file` already decodes all three, so an anchored search such as `^Hello` found nothing in a file the user could read.

Decode a leading byte-order mark before the binary check. Invalid marked bytes are still skipped. Plain UTF-8 and real binary files are unchanged.

## Test
On base `3bd6725`:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_search_tools.py::test_grep_searches_bom_marked_unicode_text -q --tb=line
```

Before: 3 failed (`utf-8-sig`, `utf-16`, `utf-32`). Each reported no matches for `^Hello`; UTF-16 and UTF-32 also reported a skipped binary file.

After `7341ccc7a067f01330274796973f3fe91c8c5db0`: 3 passed. `tests/tools/test_search_tools.py`: 87 passed.

prs.body:
## Summary

- Add a character offset to `web_fetch` and return `nextOffset` and `totalLength` for extracted text.
- Keep the untrusted-content banner on every page. Preserve existing image and network-policy behavior.
- Count retries per URL and offset so the agent can read a third page without hitting the repeated-lookup guard. Repeated calls for the same page still stop after the existing retry budget.

Related to #6316.

## Compatibility

The default offset is zero. Existing callers keep their first-page behavior. Each call fetches the URL again; content or extractor changes can shift offsets. No page snapshot or server cache is added. The tool schema changes once with the new optional parameter; it does not change as pages are read. Stored conversation history is unchanged.

## Verification

251 focused tests passed for fetch extraction, Jina privacy, URL and redirect guards, network policy, tool execution, and prompt-cache structure. The full AgentRunner-to-tool test reproduced the third-page block before the fix. It now reads all three pages and still blocks repeated calls for the same offset. Serialized request prefixes and tool schemas remain stable across those calls. HTTP and model responses are deterministic test doubles.

Scoped Ruff, BasedPyright, import-boundary checks, and diff checks passed. Current-head CI is tracked separately.

prs.body:
Thanks for merging #5047, which added the Parallel Search preset.

A stable project User-Agent lets Parallel measure aggregate usage from this integration so we can understand adoption and support it. prs.title: fix(models): route image input by preset capability
prs.body:
## Why

Image-aware routing lets a chain of text-only and vision models handle image requests while preserving the user's original input.

Resolves [NAN-442](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-442/模型请求失败时保留图片输入移除静默去图重试)

## What changed

- Add `supportsImages` to model presets, enabled by default. Named presets, the implicit default, and inline fallbacks each keep their own setting through save/load, migration, and runtime refresh.
- Route image requests through image-enabled presets in the configured primary and fallback order. If every candidate is text-only, return an image-input error before sending. Text requests use the full configured order.
- Preserve the original messages and images during transient retries, and return API validation errors directly. This replaces the previous image-stripping retry behavior and also preserves image blocks during DeepSeek content conversion.
- Add an **Image input** switch below the model picker using the existing settings controls and help hint. New presets start enabled; saved values stay with their preset, and cancelling discards a new draft. Include translations and configuration documentation.

## Scope

Covers preset configuration, shared provider retry and fallback selection, and the model settings UI/API.

## Tradeoffs

Users declare image capability per preset, including custom models. Enabled presets send images to their provider, which applies its image-format requirements and returns validation errors directly.

## Blast Radius

Regression coverage focuses on independent preset values, explicit `false` persistence, runtime refresh, capability-aware candidate selection, and original input/error preservation.

## Verification

Current-head local checks:

- All agent, provider and config tests plus settings API/edit-admission suites: **4052 passed, 8 skipped**.
- Focused CI-repair regression suite: **181 passed**. Attribution tests cover successful image requests and direct HTTP 400 errors with preserved input; governance and model-override mocks exercise their scripted primary/fallback paths.
- Full-project Ruff, BasedPyright, import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

Frontend checks carried forward from the implementation revision; frontend sources are unchanged by the test-only CI repair:

- WebUI model-settings and i18n tests: **107 passed**. `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, and `bun run build`: passed.
- Playwright preset-settings checks at 390px and 1280px: **2 passed**, covering keyboard toggling, cancellation/reset, and layout. Rendered Chinese desktop/light and narrow/dark synthetic previews and the help hint were also inspected.

Local checks use synthetic settings and controlled provider responses. Full-project verification runs in CI.

prs.title: fix(webui): prevent single-dollar math from crossing code spans
prs.body:
## Problem

The WebUI's single-dollar math scanner can start at prose such as `$ref` and consume the `$` inside a later inline code span such as `` `$defs` ``. This sends prose to KaTeX and destroys the intervening bold/code formatting. The reported full message, spaced code such as `` `$defs / definitions` ``, and preceding Windows paths are covered by regressions.

## Parsing rule

A tentative single-dollar formula must not end inside a complete CommonMark code span. Reuse micromark's `codeText` tokenizer to find the span boundary, then let the existing math scanner find its unescaped closing dollar. If that closer lies inside the code span, reject the math candidate and let Markdown parse the code normally.

This replaces the earlier identifier-tail regular expression and TeX-command guessing with a boundary check. Spaces, punctuation, and Windows paths no longer change code precedence. Ordinary formulas such as `$n$th` and `$x$2`, and backticks wholly contained within a formula such as ``$\text{`value`}$``, remain supported. The streaming fixture covers the reported reply's partial code span and completion.

When math and code delimiters cross, code wins. For example, `$th` is code in:

```text
A $x`$th`
```

An author intending a backtick inside math followed by Markdown code can use explicit TeX delimiters:

```text
A \(f(`x')\)th`code`.
```

This is a deliberate precedence choice, not an attempt to infer every author's intent. In particular, two bare dollar-prefixed identifiers without code spans remain outside this fix. Existing currency and explicit/display-math parsing rules are unchanged.

## Verification

- Focused renderer/streaming tests: 199 passed. The three added common-code regressions failed before the implementation change and passed afterward.
- Full WebUI unit suite: 205 files / 3,755 tests passed.
- Typecheck, lint, and production build passed.
- Full Chromium suite, with retries disabled: 522 passed / 1 failed. Both desktop/narrow Markdown streaming/completion cases passed, including the spaced-code and Windows-path regressions. The failing test is `history-hydration.spec.ts:319`, touch live-first history retry: `scrollTop` remained 114 instead of at most 1. Its cause is not attributed; no scroll changes or passing reruns are included in this PR.
- An initial browser command failed before tests ran because PowerShell expanded the reporter's comma. Quoting `--reporter=list,json` corrected the command; the full-suite result above is the completed run.

Earlier intermediate revisions had un-attributed full-suite failures (two `app-layout` unit cases, and `apps-connection-layout` / `history-hydration` browser cases). Their results are not reused as current-revision verification.

prs.title: fix(tools): validate arguments with jsonschema without coercion
prs.body:
## Why

Fixes #6485. This is an alternative implementation to #6486, building on the bug report and reproductions from @xiong-wei1.

The hand-written tool validator silently skips references and composition keywords, and positional array schemas can crash call preparation. Use the established `jsonschema` library instead of extending our own JSON Schema implementation. Incorrect arguments should produce actionable tool errors so the model can correct them, not be silently converted into different values.

## What changed

- Replace the hand-written validator with cached `jsonschema` validators and actionable errors, including instance paths and union-branch failure details.
- Validate MCP arguments against the server's original `inputSchema`, independently of provider-facing adaptations. This preserves nullable referenced models and handles Notion-style `oneOf` / `const` discriminators.
- Remove automatic argument casting and nested JSON-string decoding. Invalid arguments return errors; corrected calls execute without rewriting model/session history.
- Stop cron's action-specific checks when schema validation fails. Adapt already-valid JSON integers such as `2.0` to Python integers at built-in indexing/pagination boundaries, including file reading/editing, search, cron history and shell output limits.
- Return recoverable tool errors for unsupported or malformed explicit `$schema` declarations. Use draft 2020-12 only when the declaration is absent.
- Extend decimal `multipleOf` validation with exact rational arithmetic over decimal spellings, without an epsilon tolerance. Use the mature `regex` engine for Unicode string `pattern` constraints such as FastMCP's `^\p{L}+$`.
- Update the architecture documentation and avoid assertions tied to a dependency's exact error wording.

## Scope

This intentionally changes argument handling for built-in tools, MCP tools, and entry-point plugins: strings such as `"123"` are no longer converted to numbers, numbers are no longer converted to strings, and serialized nested objects/arrays are not unpacked. The removed `cast_params` hook is no longer part of tool call preparation. Parsing the outer provider JSON arguments envelope is unchanged. Built-in Python index adaptation does not change the original tool-call arguments or MCP submissions.

Validation defaults to draft 2020-12 and honors supported explicit dialects, including draft-07 tuple-form `items`. Legacy tuple schemas must declare their dialect; invalid schemas return a tool error. Provider-facing nullable/ref adaptations remain unchanged and are not the validation contract.

## Tradeoffs

Declare `jsonschema>=4.21.0`, `referencing`, and `regex` directly; all were already transitive dependencies. Testing 4.20.0 exposed its incorrect nested enum equality for booleans versus 0/1, fixed upstream in 4.21.0, so the lower bound now requires that fix rather than duplicating equality logic.

Error wording comes from `jsonschema` with small compatibility extensions for decimal multiples and Unicode string patterns. Other keyword handling remains library-owned. Unicode regex compatibility here is scoped to string `pattern`; object-key regex keywords retain the library's default implementation. Nanobot retains rejection of non-finite JSON numbers and disables external HTTP/file reference retrieval.

## Blast Radius

Callers that relied on argument coercion must supply the declared JSON types. Error results identify the offending field and reason so the model can retry. Existing agent retry/history behavior is retained, with real in-memory MCP coverage for correction and unchanged call history.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest tests/tools tests/agent tests/cron tests/providers --ignore=tests/tools/test_exec_platform.py -n 4 --dist loadfile -q --tb=short`: **5251 passed, 109 skipped**. Windows native process compatibility remains for CI.
- Focused regressions across schema/MCP, built-in file/search/web/shell and cron paths: **305 passed**.
- Minimum supported `jsonschema==4.21.0`, covering MCP, schema/registry/plugin validation and cron contracts: **423 passed, 3 skipped**.
- Real FastMCP in-memory tests and stdio acceptance: `4.02` with `multipleOf: 0.01` and `北京` with a Unicode letter pattern succeed; `4.021` and `123` are rejected locally. Earlier argument-correction/history integration remains covered by the broader suite.
- Repository Ruff checks, import boundaries and `git diff --check`: passed. Strict BasedPyright on all changed production modules: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- Full BasedPyright still **fails with the same four previously reproduced Windows FileLock return-type errors** in `mcp_oauth.py`, `gateway/runtime.py`, `process_runtime.py`, and `providers/xai_oauth.py`. Those files and their dependencies are unchanged by this follow-up; the errors remain unresolved.
- Full-project platform/build checks are left to this PR's CI for the updated head.

issues.title: gateway: a poweroff SIGTERM takes the restart-drain path, so restart_drain_timeout stalls every shutdown past the user manager's 2-minute stop timeout

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Summary

On a stock Linux systemd install the gateway runs as a **user** unit inside `user@<uid>.service`.
That manager ships a hardcoded `TimeoutStopSec=120s` (`/usr/lib/systemd/system/user@.service:33`,
systemd 262.2, KillMode=mixed). The generated `hermes-gateway.service` sizes its own
`TimeoutStopSec` from `agent.restart_drain_timeout` with no awareness of the enclosing manager, and
`gateway/run_bootstrap.py:210` classifies *every* SIGTERM/SIGINT as a **planned** gateway stop —
including the one systemd sends at poweroff.

So a documented, legal config value produces a shutdown that:

1. runs the full 120 s the user manager allows,
2. is SIGKILLed mid-drain,
3. leaves `previous_unclean_exit` in the lifecycle ledger,
4. logs nothing that explains the wait.

This is the *outward* variant of #105517 (which covers the same class of inversion *inward*: unit
budget vs. the shutdown-watchdog leash). Here it is unit budget vs. the **enclosing** supervisor's
budget. Nothing in the codebase ever compares the two.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.23.1 (2026.9.24), stable, commit `3b4215785882`, install method git
- Arch Linux, kernel 7.3.4-zen2-1-zen, systemd 262 (262.2-1-arch)
- `hermes-gateway.service` as a **user** unit (`~/.config/systemd/user/`), `WantedBy=default.target`
- Enclosing manager: `user@1000.service`, `TimeoutStopUSec=2min`, `KillMode=mixed`, `KillSignal=15`
- `agent.restart_drain_timeout: 600` in `config.yaml`; generated unit carries `TimeoutStopSec=630`

## Observed

Three for three, every shutdown in the retained journal:

| Boot | systemd begins stopping `user@1000` | gateway SIGTERM | last non-gateway unit stopped | `user@1000` SIGKILL | idle tail spent on the gateway alone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11-14 06:29 | 06:29:10 | 06:29:10 | 06:29:40 (cloudflared) | 06:31:10 | +90 s |
| 11-14 07:39 | 07:39:13 | 07:39:13 | 07:39:44 (openrazer) | 07:41:13 | +89 s |
| 11-14 07:51 | 07:51:44 | 07:51:45.896 | 07:52:15 (cloudflared) | 07:53:44 | +89 s |

Full detail for the last boot:

```
07:51:44      systemd[1]: Stopping user@1000.service...
07:51:45.896  hermes[1600]: WARNING gateway.run: Shutdown context: signal=SIGTERM under_systemd=yes
                             parent_pid=1363 parent_name=systemd loadavg_1m=3.48
07:51:45.899  hermes[1600]: INFO gateway.run: Stopping gateway...
              ... no further gateway.run line of any kind for 118 s ...
07:52:10.208  hermes[1600]: ERROR ... [Discord] transport closed (socket_closed, 1/2); forcing reconnect
07:52:10.210  hermes[1600]: INFO gateway.run: discord queued for background reconnection
07:52:52.009  hermes[1600]: INFO ... [Ntfy] Reconnecting in 2s...
07:53:09.011  hermes[1600]: INFO ... [Ntfy] Reconnecting in 5s...
07:53:29.013  hermes[1600]: INFO ... [Ntfy] Reconnecting in 10s...
07:53:44      systemd[1]: user@1000.service: State 'stop-sigterm' timed out. Killing.
07:53:44      systemd[1]: user@1000.service: Killing process 1600 (hermes) with signal SIGKILL.
              (+26 more: dbus-broker, 16x postgres, uv, python, node, tirith, bridge-mcp-ghid)
07:53:45      systemd[1]: user@1000.service: Failed with result 'timeout'.
07:53:45      systemd[1]: user@1000.service: Consumed 10min 17.982s CPU time over 5min 54.730s
                             wall clock time, 17.9G memory peak.
```

On the next boot the ledger correctly reports the cost:

```
07:55:36.905 WARNING gateway.lifecycle_ledger: Previous gateway life (pid=1600, ...) exited
             UNCLEANLY (no exit path ran — SIGKILL / OOM / VM death ...). suspected_oom=False
```

## Root cause

1. **Poweroff is indistinguishable from a restart stop.** `gateway/run_bootstrap.py:210` logs
   `Received %s as a planned gateway stop — exiting cleanly` for any SIGTERM/SIGINT. A poweroff,
   a `systemctl --user restart`, and a `hermes gateway stop` all land on the same planned path, so
   all three get `restart_drain_timeout`.
2. **The unit budget is sized against nothing.** `resolve_systemd_timeout_stop_sec()`
   (`gateway/restart.py:355`) = `max(60, max(drain, cron+10) + 30)` (`SYSTEMD_STOP_HEADROOM_S=30`).
   With `drain=600` that emits `TimeoutStopSec=630` — 5.25x the enclosing manager's 120 s.
3. **`hermes gateway install` does not look up.** It writes 630 into a unit that is a child of a
   120 s manager, and reports success.
4. **The shutdown watchdog cannot save it.** `resolve_shutdown_watchdog_delay()` = `drain + 60`
   (`DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_WATCHDOG_GRACE_S=60`) = 660 s > 630, so the watchdog is unreachable — the
   #105517 inversion, stacked on top of the outward one. `logs/gateway-shutdown-watchdog.log` does
   not exist on this host; there is no faulthandler dump for the hang.

## Why the existing safety nets miss it

- **#105517** (open, P2, PR #105518 open since 2026-09-08 with no review) covers unit-vs-watchdog.
  It does not consider a third deadline: the parent manager's.
- **#64155** (closed, fixed by #65084) bounded the **unexpected-signal** interrupt grace to 1 s. The
  planned path was deliberately left alone, and a poweroff takes the planned path.
- **`check_systemd_timing_alignment`** compares the installed unit against
  `resolve_systemd_timeout_stop_sec()` — the same function that generated it — so a "correct" 630 s
  unit reports `mismatch=False`.
- **The docs caution** (`website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`, "Gateway Restart Drain") tells
  you to re-run `hermes gateway install` after raising the value. Following the documentation is
  exactly what produces the un-stoppable unit.
- **The drain is silent** (#148281): the timeout warning prints `_running_agent_count()`, which
  excludes `managed_turn_count`, so a drain held open by managed/uncounted work reports zero. On
  this host no drain line was emitted at all — the 118 s gap contains no `gateway.run` output.
  A `ps` snapshot taken at SIGTERM shows an untracked child chain under the gateway:
  `hermes(1600) → uv(12850) → python(12925)` at **89.4 % CPU**.

## Reproduction

Pure config, no code changes:

```yaml
agent:
  restart_drain_timeout: 600
```

```bash
hermes gateway install          # writes TimeoutStopSec=630 into a user unit
systemctl --user show -p TimeoutStopUSec hermes-gateway.service   # 10min 30s
systemctl show -p TimeoutStopUSec user@$(id -u).service           # 2min
# trigger any in-flight turn, then poweroff and time the shutdown
journalctl -b -1 | grep "user@1000.service: State 'stop-sigterm' timed out"
```

Every shutdown costs exactly 120 s and ends in SIGKILL. Reducing the value only moves the number:
`drain=30` → 70 s unit (under the 120 s ceiling, so no SIGKILL, but 70 s of every shutdown is still
spent draining a turn the machine is about to kill anyway).

## Proposed fix

1. **Detect the shutdown case.** On a planned stop, check whether the stop is a system poweroff/reboot
   (`systemctl is-system-running` == `stopping`/`offline`, or a pending `shutdown.target` /
   `systemd-poweroff.service` / `systemd-reboot.service` job) and if so use a short bounded drain
   (e.g. `min(restart_drain_timeout, 10)`) instead of the full budget. A machine going down will
   never let the turn finish; holding it for ten minutes is strictly worse than interrupting it.
2. **Make the installer parent-aware.** Before writing `TimeoutStopSec`, read the enclosing
   supervisor's deadline (`user@<uid>.service` `TimeoutStopUSec`, or the system manager's for system
   units) and clamp/warn. A generated unit whose stop budget exceeds its parent's is a footgun that
   `hermes gateway install` should refuse to write silently.
3. **Compare all three deadlines in one place** — unit budget, watchdog leash, parent budget — and
   assert the ordering instead of re-deriving each from a separate constant. That would also retire
   #105517 rather than fixing it twice.
4. **Print the real drain occupants** (#148281) so the 118 s silence has an explanation in the log
   the next time this happens.

issues.title: [Feature]: Per-turn client identity on prompt.submit (which app and device sent this turn)

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: comp/gateway

labels.name: P3

issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

One session is reached from several clients: Desktop on a Mac, a browser tab on a
phone, the official mobile app, the TUI. The model and plugins cannot tell which
one sent the current turn.

- `platform` on `pre_llm_call` is per agent, so every dashboard client reports `gui`.
- `session.create` `client` (`session-client-v1`) names the client that CREATED the
  session. A session created on the Mac and continued from the phone still reports
  the Mac on every later turn.

What this costs:
- Formatting: an agent sends wide tables, local file paths and `hermes://` links to a
  phone, where none of them work.
- Plugins: per-device state has no key. A time plugin that stores the device time
  zone per profile lets two devices in different zones overwrite each other.
- Debugging: when a turn's result lands on a different client after a reconnect, the
  transcript has no record of which client sent the turn.

### Proposed Solution

`gateway/session_surface.py` already models a per-turn fact. `surface` (`hud`,
`voice-live`) is admitted on `prompt.submit`, committed as `surface_v1`, carried to
managed workers by `restore_surface`, and rendered as a note on the model input. The
module says "A surface is a fact about ONE turn, never about the session". The
creating client's label lives in `gateway/session_client.py`, with a validator
(`client_problem`) and a stated rule: attribution only, no prompt text.

1. Two optional `prompt.submit` fields, committed with `surface_v1`:
   - `client`: the same label shape as `session.create` `client`
     (`{"name", "version"?}`), checked by the same `client_problem` validator.
   - `form_factor`: a closed enum, `desktop`, `tablet` or `phone`.
2. `pre_llm_call` receives them as `turn_client` (`{"name", "version"?,
   "form_factor"?}`, or `{}`). Narrow legacy hook signatures never see the new
   field, because hook dispatch already passes only declared names.
3. Core renders no prompt text from them, matching the `session_client` rule.
   Plugins decide what to do with the label.
4. Capability gating, the same way as `clarify_batch`: `runtime.describe` lists
   `turn-client-v1`, and `client.capabilities` returns `turn_client: true`. An older
   owner refuses unknown submit keys, so clients send the fields only when advertised.
5. Desktop sends `client.name` `hermes-desktop` (native) or `hermes-web` (browser
   host), and a form factor from `(pointer: coarse)` plus the screen's short side.
   The mobile apps can send the same fields.

Trust: the client reports these values itself, unauthenticated. They are information only
and must never gate approvals, tool scopes or permissions. Both fields have closed
shapes with no free text, so neither can carry model input.

Non-goals: no hostnames, IP addresses, user agents or device fingerprints.

Related:
- #109455: proposed per-turn metadata including a `client_surface` field. The voice
  half has since landed as `surface` / `voice_turn`; the client half has not.
- #148596: api_server accepting the `surface` fields (the same fields could ride there)
- #149395: `turn_env` on `prompt.submit`, a separate per-turn field for tool
  environments. It touches the same submit contracts, so whichever lands second rebases.
- #118010: device nodes umbrella

### Alternatives Considered

- Reuse `session.create` `client`: it names only the creating client, and the
  creation request is frozen, so it cannot follow a session to another device.
- Infer the device from the connection (peer address, user agent): `pre_llm_call`
  does not see the connection, NAT and shared networks make it wrong, and it puts
  fingerprint-like data where a closed label is enough.
- One combined enum (`desktop-mac`, `web-phone`, ...): simpler, but it mixes which
  app sent the turn (useful for debugging) with what device it ran on (useful for
  formatting), and every new app multiplies the values.

### Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

A PR with this shape is ready: admission, contracts, the `pre_llm_call` field,
Desktop, tests and docs.

### Debug Report (optional)

_No response_

issues.body:
## Summary
When a steer / redirect message is injected mid-turn, its user row is created in memory without a `"timestamp"`. At the end of the turn, flushing to `state.db` fills in the missing timestamp with `time.time()` *after* the final assistant message already has its completion timestamp — leaving the user message permanently stamped milliseconds **newer** than the assistant reply that answered it.

Unlike `#141351` (where Force Reload fixes the UI order because the DB rows are already ordered), here the persisted SQLite timestamps themselves are inverted, so **reloading Desktop/Web UI or exporting the session keeps the reply above the prompt**.

## Observed timeline & SQLite evidence
- **Prompt accepted:** `2026-11-13 5:36:19 PM PT`
- **WS disconnect / reconnect while `terminal` awaited approval:** `6:21:52 PM PT`; tool approval timed out at `6:22:03.450 PM PT` (`id=14440`), and `/steer` delivered at `6:22:03.457 PM PT`
- **Persisted rows at turn end (`6:23:59 PM PT`):**
  - `id=14441` (`display_order=14441`, `role=user`, `display_kind='steer'`): `timestamp = 1794623039.304960`
  - `id=14442` (`display_order=14442`, `role=assistant`): `timestamp = 1794623039.302891`
  - `id=14441` is **2.07 ms newer** than `id=14442` despite sitting before it in `display_order`.

## Root cause & suggested fix
Checked on local commit `3b42157858` and verified unchanged on `main` (`4b40ffb0ad`):
1. `steer_user_row(steer_text)` in `agent/prompt_builder.py:586-592` builds `{"role": "user", "content": format_steer_marker(steer_text).lstrip(), "display_kind": STEER_DISPLAY_KIND}` with no `"timestamp"`.
2. Neither `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:3702` (`messages.append(steer_user_row(...))`) nor `agent/turn_iteration_prep.py:291` (`messages.insert(..., steer_user_row(...))`) attaches a timestamp when the steer enters `messages`.
3. `agent/turn_final_response.py:404, 408` appends `final_msg` (which already carries a completion timestamp) and flushes via `hermes_state_messages.py:666-690`, where `_coerce_timestamp(msg.get("timestamp"), now_ts)` backfills `id=14441` using a later `time.time()` than `final_msg`.

*(Distinct from `#117137` / `#117142`, which fixed live-dict copy-back but left `steer_user_row()` unstamped.)*

**Fix:** Set `"timestamp": time.time()` inside `steer_user_row()` (or clamp backfilled missing timestamps in `hermes_state_messages.py` to stay `<=` subsequent already-stamped rows).

## Environment
- `NousResearch/hermes-agent` local `3b42157858`, verified unchanged on `main` (`4b40ffb0ad`)

issues.body:
## Environment

- Hermes Agent checkout at `4b05f764fa` (same code still present on `main` at `8f21606116`)
- Windows 11 (x64), Python 3.14.7
- Reproduces on C:, D: and E: NTFS volumes — platform-wide, not volume-specific

## Symptoms

On Windows, after any full (complete, pagination-free) `read_file`, a `write_file` to the same path is refused **forever**:

- `ERROR: was last read with offset/limit pagination` — even though the read was a complete full read;
- re-reading the whole file does not clear it; and for files the agent created itself, `write_file` refuses with `has not seen its full current content`.

Only `patch` keeps working, so edit sessions degrade into patch-only loops.

## Root cause

`tools/file_tools_read_tracking.py::_file_version()` builds a metadata tuple from `os.fstat(fd)` and requires it to be **equal** to a tuple built from `os.stat(path)` (`st_dev, st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns, st_ctime_ns`).

On Windows, `os.stat()` and `os.fstat()` report `st_ctime_ns` from **different sources** (NTFS change time vs last-write time). The two only coincide for a file whose metadata has not been touched since creation; after any rewrite, `os.utime`, or atomic-replace write they diverge and the equality check fails.

For such files `_file_version()` returns `None` permanently, which means:

- a full read gets stamped `partial=True` by the read tracker (so `write_file` sees a partial view), and
- `_mark_full_write_baseline()` can never record a baseline.

Observed on Windows 11:

```
fresh file, single write:   stat.st_ctime_ns == fstat.st_ctime_ns      (passes by luck)
after os.utime:             stat ...998450700 != fstat ...149930300    (mismatch)
after in-place rewrite:     stat = change time, fstat = write time     (mismatch)
```

Freshly created files can slip through when the timestamps happen to coincide — the failure looks intermittent, but any file that gets edited more than once fails 100% of the time (exactly the file `write_file` is needed for).

## Expected behavior

A complete read clears the partial/stale state and `write_file` succeeds when the file is unchanged since that read — on all platforms.

## Fix

A fix + regression test (in `tests/tools/test_file_staleness.py`) are ready — PR incoming.

issues.title: [Bug]: Shared webhook adapter drops profile-bound (--route-profile) deliveries at durable admission (route_digest not_found)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: platform/webhook
labels.description: Webhook / API server

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
### Bug Description

On a multiplexed gateway, a dynamic webhook subscription bound to a secondary profile (`--route-profile`) passes ingress but every delivery then fails durable admission with `RuntimeStoreError('not_found')`. The coalesced path returns 202 and later logs `Coalesced delivery … was not admitted`, so the sender sees success and the event is silently lost.

Cause: the **shared** webhook adapter reloads its dynamic-route table from `get_hermes_home()`. Ingress resolves that to the listener owner's home. Admission runs under the routed profile's scope, so it resolves to the secondary profile's home. There the subscriptions file is absent, the shared adapter's routes are cleared, and the following lookup fails.

This started on our install with the update from `d923a5eb48` to `5b147ab036`. We counted 33 rejected deliveries in about 11 hours before we noticed.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable the webhook platform and `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, serving a secondary profile (`watcher`).
2. In the listener owner's (default) home, run `hermes webhook subscribe monitor-alert --route-profile watcher …` with a secret, an agent prompt, `deliver: log`, and optionally `coalesce: {key: …}`.
3. Leave `profiles/watcher/webhook_subscriptions.json` absent. This is the documented layout (webhooks.md §route profile binding).
4. Send a correctly signed POST to `/p/watcher/webhooks/monitor-alert`.
5. Admission fails: see the traceback below.

Offline reproducer. It uses the installed adapter's real reload/digest methods against throwaway fixture homes and touches no live state:

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from unittest.mock import patch
from gateway.platforms.webhook import WebhookAdapter, _WebhookDeliveryIdentity
from gateway.platforms.webhook_delivery import route_digest
from hermes_state_runtime import RuntimeStoreError

with TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    root = Path(td); sec = root / 'profiles' / 'watcher'; sec.mkdir(parents=True)
    store = root / 'webhook_subscriptions.json'
    store.write_text(json.dumps({'monitor-alert': {'secret': 'fixture', 'profile': 'watcher',
                                                    'deliver': 'log', 'coalesce': {'key': 'k'}}}))
    a = object.__new__(WebhookAdapter)
    a._static_routes, a._dynamic_routes, a._dynamic_routes_stat, a._routes = {}, {}, None, {}
    a._global_secret, a._host = '', '127.0.0.1'
    chat = _WebhookDeliveryIdentity.from_parts('watcher', 'monitor-alert', 'x').session_chat_id
    with patch('hermes_constants.get_hermes_home', return_value=root):
        a._reload_dynamic_routes(); assert 'monitor-alert' in a._routes   # ingress: OK
    with patch('hermes_constants.get_hermes_home', return_value=sec):
        try: route_digest(a, chat)
        except RuntimeStoreError as e: print('REPRODUCED:', e)            # admission: not_found
```

Output on v0.22.3 / `5b147ab036`: `REPRODUCED: not_found`. Moving the subscription into the secondary home fixes admission but removes the route from ingress, because the listener then finds nothing in its own home.

### Expected Behavior

Ingress and admission resolve the route against the same subscription authority, the listener owner's file, whatever the execution profile. Wrong-profile URLs should still be refused. In our test they are: `Route … is not authorized for profile 'default'` / `'kirby'`.

### Actual Behavior

Every delivery to the profile-bound route is accepted at ingress (202 on the coalesced path) and then dropped at admission.

### Affected Component

Gateway (webhook platform, durable admission)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Webhook

### Debug Report

Not attached for privacy. Versions are below; the reproducer above runs standalone against the installed package.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 (Linux 7.0.0-38-generic)

### Python Version

Hermes venv (installed by the stable installer)

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.22.3 (2026.9.24) · stable · local `5b147ab036d6`

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```
ERROR gateway.platforms.webhook: [webhook] Coalesced delivery <id> on route xyops-failure was not admitted
  webhook_ingress.admit_producer → _prepared → session_envelope.prepare_native
  → _snapshot_native (session_envelope.py:224) → webhook_delivery.route_digest (webhook_delivery.py:18)
  RuntimeStoreError: not_found
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

- `gateway/config.py:313-315`: webhook is a shared-listener mirror, so secondary profiles have no adapter of their own. `WebhookAdapter.connect` (283-289) serves `/p/<profile>/webhooks/...` on the primary adapter.
- `_resolve_route` reloads from the root home before auth: correct.
- `webhook_ingress.producer_scope` (41-43) then enters the routed profile's scope. `session_envelope._snapshot_native` (217-224) calls `route_digest` on the same shared adapter.
- `route_digest` (webhook_delivery.py:9-18) calls `_reload_dynamic_routes()`, which builds the path from the **current** `get_hermes_home()` (webhook.py:442-450). The secondary file is absent, so the shared adapter's dynamic routes are cleared and `.get(route)` is None.

`webhook_delivery.py`, `webhook_ingress.py` and `session_envelope.py` are byte-identical on `main` @ `4e58c721c8cf` (checked 2026-10-22), so this looks unfixed there. Source comparison only; we haven't run main live.

Interim workaround that works for us: a symlink `profiles/<secondary>/webhook_subscriptions.json → ../../webhook_subscriptions.json`. `stat()` follows it, so both scopes see the same file and stat key, and root CLI atomic-rename writes are still seen. Deliveries were admitted again immediately with no restart. This is a stopgap and changes nothing in core.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Have the shared adapter remember the home it was connected under, and use that in `_reload_dynamic_routes` instead of the ambient `get_hermes_home()`. Alternatively, make `route_digest` read the adapter's snapshot without reloading. Suggested regression test: a route bound to a secondary profile with the subscription only in the owner's home, covering immediate and coalesced admission, retained reply validation, interleaved deliveries to different profiles, and wrong-profile URLs still refused.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Not right now. Happy to test a fix on this setup.

---
*Investigated and drafted with AI assistance (Hermes agents), verified on the installed release by the reporter's agents.*

issues.body:
## Problem
On v0.23.1 (3b42157), `hermes chat -q` gets a ticket over the control socket, then dials `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/ws` on an ephemeral port (`gateway/run_api.py` `start_gateway_api(host="127.0.0.1", port=0)`, via `start_gateway_runtime_api`). The port can only be fixed with `webapp.enabled: true` (`WebappSettings.bind` returns port 0 otherwise), which also serves the Webapp. The same setup worked on v0.22.2 (d923a5e); I have not bisected the change.

I run the CLI under a macOS `sandbox-exec` profile: outbound only to one loopback model endpoint, Unix sockets only in one private 0700 directory. The control socket works there. The session socket fails with `Gateway connection failed; no local fallback`. SBPL network filters accept only `localhost` or `*` as the host, and the port is chosen after the profile is written, so the only rule that works is `(remote ip "localhost:*")`. That opens every loopback service, including unauthenticated ones such as a browser's remote-debugging port. `HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL` does not help, because that path sends no ticket.

## Proposal (opt-in, default unchanged)
1. A setting, e.g. `gateway.session_socket: unix`, that serves `/api/ws` on a 0600 AF_UNIX socket in the control socket's directory and returns its path in the session-ticket answer; the client connects with `websockets` `unix_connect`. Tickets stay required. Note: `GatewayRuntimeAPI` treats a peer as native only when `ws.client.host` is 127.0.0.1 or ::1. A Unix-socket peer has no address, so it would need to count as native, ideally with the control socket's peer-uid check. Windows can keep TCP.
2. Fallback: `gateway.session_port: <n>` that pins the port without enabling the Webapp and fails startup if the bind fails (no silent fallback to an ephemeral port).

## Test idea
With the setting on, the gateway opens no TCP listener; a ticketed `unix_connect` attaches; an unticketed one is refused.

issues.title: webapp launch page conflates redeem-refused with ticket-expired (four dated witnesses)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: area/auth
labels.description: Authentication, OAuth, credential pools

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

issues.body:
## Symptom

`http://127.0.0.1:9120/webapp/launch#ticket=<fresh>` on a **virgin browser profile** consumes the ticket (*"Opening Hermes"*, fragment still riding the URL) and ~5 s later prints **"The sign-in link was already used or has expired."** The sentence conflates two different failures:

1. *ticket spent or sixty seconds stale* (the honest case the copy describes), and
2. ***redeem refused for this browser*** — the server's `_peer_is_server_user` check rejecting the exchange because the webapp's process uid doesn't match the session user (e.g. webapp serving under a container service uid like s6's `hermes`, browser session under the host uid).

Case 2 reports as case 1, so the only page the human looks at lies about *which* failure it is. Every forensic path in our session had to shell out to `ps`/`ss` and read server code to discover the refusal.

## Evidence (four dated witnesses, 2026-11-14, Hermes v0.23.1, rig container, single listener per port, store 18/18 healthy)

- ~01:45Z — host chromium (uid 1000), fresh 43-char mint, rig :9120 webapp (server uid `hermes`/10000): consume → conflation sentence.
- ~02:20Z — same dance, same container generation, same sentence.
- ~02:35Z — fresh mint against a force-recreated container (`a475923a…`), virgin storage, no pre-seeding: consume → *"Opening Hermes"* → sentence ~5 s later.
- Control: a *warm* profile that already holds a browser credential passes the same URL end-to-end — the page cannot distinguish "this browser holds a session credential" from "this ticket is still valid," so the failure looks browser- and time-dependent.

## Suggested fix

Two distinct sentences (or a reason code the launch page renders): **"sign-in refused from this browser"** (server-side peer/uid rejection — actionable: use the dashboard door, or run the webapp at your uid) vs **"ticket spent or stale"** (re-mint). One word-count change upstream; it collapsed what would otherwise be an hour of process-table archaeology per attempt.

## Context

Found while demoing the `myfarm-advisor` plugin on a dev rig (dashboard :8644 vs webapp :9120). Not blocking: the dashboard door passes natively. Filed on behalf of the rig room by @borealBytes/research-desk.


## Update (2026-11-14, ~03:2xZ): the root cause is worse than conflation — the page starts guilty

Two further witnesses (one 200-proven crossing, one HTML fetch) reframe the diagnosis:

1. **The failure sentence is the launch page's INITIAL visible state.** `GET /webapp/launch` with *no ticket at all* returns HTML whose body already contains "The sign-in link was already used or has expired." The client script only *replaces* that text on success. So every non-happy path — dropped URL fragment, single-use re-submit, a refused exchange — converges on a sentence that was **already rendered before any script ran**, indistinguishable from a server verdict. The copy doesn't just conflate two failures; it *pre-accuses*.
2. **A refused exchange also wears this sentence:** `POST /webapp/window-session` without an `Origin` header (i.e., any bare HTTP client) answers 403 with an honest body naming the same-origin requirement — but the *launch page* only shows the conflation sentence, so browser-less forensics and human users see different truths at the same moment. The endpoint itself is fine; the page discards the server's explanation.

**Cleaner remedy than the original two-word split:** render an initial state of *"Opening…"* (or empty) and let each failure mode replace it with the server's own reason — *refused from this browser* (peer/uid rejection), *ticket spent* (single-use consumed), *ticket stale* (>60 s), *no ticket received* (fragment dropped by the browser/paste). The one-use and same-origin enforcement are both correct behavior; the only defect is that the page reports its resting state as a verdict.

**Control that also explains the "warm browser passes" witness:** the session credential returned by a successful `window-session` exchange is **generation-reusable** — a re-exchange of a fresh ticket returns the *same* token — so a browser that has ever crossed once holds `sessionStorage` papers and passes without any ritual, masking every failure mode for everyone who tests with a warm profile.

prs.title: One malformed MCP tool no longer parks the whole server (salvage #101804, fixes #101669)
prs.body:
One MCP tool with a definition the SDK rejects now costs only that tool, instead of parking the whole server with zero tools.

Salvage of #101804 by @hyeonsang010716 (their commit cherry-picked, authorship kept), slimmed to the salvage bar. Same fix class as anomalyco/opencode#58350 ("skip malformed MCP tools instead of failing the server").

Fixes #101669

## What changes

| Server offers | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `good_echo` + `broken_tool` (no `inputSchema`) | `hermes mcp test` → `✗ Connection failed: 1 validation error for ListToolsResult tools.1.inputSchema Field required`; agent log: `failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking`; 0 tools | `✓ Tools discovered: 1 (good_echo)`; WARNING `dropping tool 'broken_tool' … (inputSchema: Field required); the server's other tools remain available` |
| 312 tools, one with a shape the SDK model rejects (#101669) | all 312 gone | 311 load, the bad one is named in the log and in `get_mcp_status()["dropped_tools"]` |
| Custom/extension method whose result happens to carry a `tools` list | passed through | passed through, unchanged |

**Root cause:** the mcp 2.x SDK validates a `tools/list` page as a whole against the negotiated protocol version's wire schema, so one invalid tool fails the response and Hermes parks the server.

## How

- `tools/mcp_listing_guard.py` wraps the session's stream pair between the transport and `ClientSession` (both the stdio and HTTP/SSE sites in `mcp_tool_transport.py`, so discovery, `tools/list_changed` refreshes, the keepalive fallback and `hermes mcp test` are all covered).
- The write proxy records each outbound request's method by id; the read proxy only touches the response to `tools/list`, validates each tool alone against the SDK's own per-version `Tool` model (`mcp_types.methods.SERVER_RESULTS`), and drops just the failing ones. Anything unexpected passes through as before.
- Dropped tools are recorded on the server (`_dropped_tools`, reset on rediscovery/refresh) and surfaced by `get_mcp_status`.

OpenCode does the same at its transport `onmessage` hook (validate the page with the tools stripped, then each tool alone via the SDK's era codec). The Python SDK has no such hook, so the guard sits on the anyio streams instead.

## Salvage notes

- `95a751fff00`: @hyeonsang010716's commit, cherry-picked onto current main (28k commits of drift; conflicts in `__slots__` and `_refresh_tools` resolved additively).
- `72c71663de7`: slim pass. Guard 321 → 178 lines (dropped mcp 1.x root-model unwrapping since Hermes pins mcp 2.x, the separate ledger class, and pragma-no-cover try/excepts); tests 627 → 92 lines, two invariants through a real `ClientSession`. `get_mcp_status` reads `_dropped_tools` with `getattr` like its `_registered_tool_names` neighbour (two status tests use `SimpleNamespace` servers).

- `c1647382008`: guard verdicts are cleared inside the RPC lock right before the fetch they belong to, so a queued `tools/list_changed` refresh can't leave a stale drop entry (review finding).

## Verification

- **Live repro (real `hermes chat -q`, OpenRouter `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, scratch HERMES_HOME, raw stdio MCP server offering `good_echo` + a tool without `inputSchema`):** main answered `NOTOOL` (server parked, `registered 0 tool(s) from 0 server(s) (1 failed: badsrv …)`); this branch answered `echo:{"x": "ping"}` after a real `mcp__badsrv__good_echo` call. Each leg used a fresh backend process.
- Sabotage: disabling the `_isolate` call turns `test_invalid_tool_is_dropped_by_name_and_the_rest_load` red.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp*.py`: 101 files, 887 passed, 0 failed locally (CI is the verdict).
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.

## Infographic

![mcp-skip-malformed-tools](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab06345/0CVdmbSb6LgIFs_Rvalzb_ZcIPieHd.png)

prs.title: fix(agent): DirectSDK overflow compresses instead of wait and /retry
prs.body:
Claude subscription (DirectSDK) sessions now compress and retry when Claude says "prompt is too long", instead of failing every message with "wait a moment and /retry" until `/new`. Fixes #129153, closes the residual of #149555, supersedes #129157.

## Before

Hermes decided "is this a local server?" from the base URL:
- DirectSDK's URL is `process://claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental`. Its host has no dots, so `is_local_endpoint()` read it as a LAN machine name.
- A local server can be busy with another request, so on an uncounted context overflow Hermes told the user to wait and retry. DirectSDK is a hosted model behind a child process, so waiting never helps, and the session stayed stuck.
- The same misreading gave DirectSDK its 900 s stall patience by accident: a buffered call to opus or sonnet-5-5 was still cut at 240 s, while haiku waited without limit.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  O[prompt is too long, no count] --> U{is_local_endpoint of the URL}
  U -->|process:// reads as a LAN host| W[wait and /retry, every message]
```

## After

A new sibling, `agent/process_transport.py`, decides by the provider profile's `auth_type == "external_process"`, never by the URL:
- An external-process provider is not a local server: an uncounted overflow compresses and retries, and the startup probes for Ollama and llama.cpp skip it.
- It keeps a local server's patience on purpose: 900 s for a stream.
- A buffered call to it is bounded by its request timeout (1800 s unless set), for every model. An explicit `providers.<id>.stale_timeout_seconds` is used as-is on both paths.
- The dashboard judges an auxiliary pin with the selected profile's plugins, not the launch profile's.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  O[prompt is too long, no count] --> A{provider auth_type}
  A -->|external_process| C[compress and retry]
  A -->|HTTP| U{local server?}
  U -->|yes| W[wait and /retry]
  U -->|no| C
```

## What the user sees

| Situation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| "prompt is too long" (no count) on DirectSDK or an `acp://` provider | the turn fails with "wait and /retry", on every message until `/new` | compress and retry |
| Stream stall budget, DirectSDK | 900 s, from the URL | 900 s, from `auth_type` |
| Buffered-call stall, opus or sonnet-5-5 | 240 s | the request timeout (1800 s) |
| Buffered-call stall, haiku | no wall-clock limit | the request timeout (1800 s) |
| A buffered call to an ACP child that stops reading the prompt | hangs | ends at the request timeout |
| `stale_timeout_seconds: 180` on an external process | stream 900 s, buffered 240 s | 180 s on both |
| Dashboard `?profile=B` with a process provider installed only in B | B's pin judged with the launch profile's plugins | judged with B's |
| An auxiliary task pinned to DirectSDK after the main model switches | not listed as a stale pin | listed (it bills a subscription) |

## Not in this PR

- Sites that apply only to Codex Responses, or that have no provider in scope and are never reached for `process://`, still read the URL.
- One trade-off: a buffered haiku call to a child that keeps sending events but never finishes now ends at 1800 s, where `main` had no limit. DirectSDK streams, so it takes this path only as a fallback.

## Live verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| The PR's own test files plus the adjacent stale-timeout and ACP client suites, on this head | pass |
| `scripts/check` on this head | pass |
| A DirectSDK session at ~72.6K tokens with `compression.threshold_tokens: 20000` | compressed to ~12.3K through two summaries on `process://`, then answered |

No screenshot pair: the only screen change is the "wait and /retry" message turning into compress-and-retry, and that needs an uncounted overflow from Claude, which cannot be triggered on demand. The threshold run above proves compression works end to end on `process://`; the overflow branch itself is covered by the unit test, red on `main`.

Builds on #129157 by @dskwe, cherry-picked with authorship kept. Its `process://` prefix check is replaced by the `auth_type` rule, which also covers `acp://`.

## Follow-ups

- Move the remaining Codex-only `is_local_endpoint` sites to the same rule when one of them gains a provider in scope.
