prs.title: feat(update): hermes update --force stops the gateways at once instead of draining
prs.body:
Before, `hermes update` waited for every gateway to finish its running work (up to 30 minutes by default) before updating, and there was no way to say "stop everything now". `hermes update --force` now stops every gateway right away (naming what each was running), interrupts its turns, background subagents and processes, kills anything still alive after about 12 seconds, then updates and restarts the gateways as usual. | | Output (live rig: real `gateway run` under a scratch home, a live chat turn running `sleep 900`, a background `sleep 900`, a background delegation) | |---|---| | main `hermes update` (from code + the red-on-main test, not run live on the rig) | `⏳ Waiting up to 1875s for in-flight turns on gateway PID … to finish before the update...` (drain request, then the full budget) | | `hermes update --force` | `⏹ gateway PID 2151595: stopped by --force, interrupting 3 unit(s): chat turn agent:main:api_server:dm:rig-session-1 … [model fake-rig-model, tool terminal]; api run …; background delegation deleg_dd01af2d … [rig child: sleep in foreground]`
`⚠ gateway PID 2151595 still running 12s after the stop — SIGKILL`
`elapsed 12.1s; gateway alive: False` | **Root cause:** the POSIX pre-swap pause (`update_cmd_posix_pause._stop_gateways`) only knew the drain path; `--force` existed but meant only the Windows `hermes.exe` check. **What changed** - `hermes_cli/update_cmd_force_stop.py` (new): per gateway, reads `active-work` (live verb, else the state file), records the stop as sent, asks for the force stop on the control socket (`pause-for-update {"force": true}`, accepted only when the ACK carries `force: true` — the contract the companion gateway lane adds), else planned-stop marker + SIGTERM (main's immediate `stop()`), prints one line, SIGKILLs survivors after 12 s, then stops the supervisor so it cannot respawn on the old tree. The normal paused-set resume starts the gateways on the new code. - `_stop_gateways` dispatches to it when the run's token carries `force`; `arm_pause(force=)` and `_UpdateOptions.force` plumb `args.force`. - `--force` help, `updating.md` and the CLI reference describe the new meaning; the Windows `hermes.exe` meaning stays under the same flag, `--force-venv` is unchanged. **Live repro:** before (main) the pause sends the drain request and waits the restart budget; after (`--force`) the live gateway with 3 active units was gone in 12.1 s, the gateway log shows `Received SIGTERM as a planned gateway stop`. Recorded-call rig (gateway functions called directly against a `gateway run --force` under a scratch HOME/HERMES_HOME/lock dir; no systemctl, no host update). **What survives `--force`:** on this rig the gateway did not finish its own `stop()` within 12 s and was SIGKILLed, so the background `sleep 900` started by the terminal tool kept running: it lives in its own `hermes-worker-proc_*.scope` (systemd) and is not a child of the gateway. A gateway whose `stop()` completes kills it through `process_registry.kill_all`. Follow-up: give `--force` a cleanup pass over the profile's `processes.json` after a SIGKILL. **Tests:** `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_force_stop.py` (2): the force pause never sends the drain request and a SIGTERM-ignoring gateway is gone within the bound (red on main: main waits the budget, then SIGKILLs); the line names what was interrupted. `test_update_posix_pause.py`, `test_update_target_identity.py`, `tests/ci/test_docs_drift.py` green. Tests changed by ruling: none. **NOT_COVERED:** the systemd/launchd branches of the force stop (`_disarm` → `systemctl stop` / `launchctl bootout`) were not run live; Windows is unchanged (its pause still drains then tree-kills); the post-update fleet restart's drain (`_restart_one_systemd_gateway_unit`) is unchanged, since a `--force` run has already stopped and restarted the paused set. Out of scope here (follow-up): the non-force update still SIGKILLs / blunt-restarts a gateway when the drain budget runs out. ## Infographic ![update-force](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab26424/j7UWC1cYk-JScTJA4q8Wl_JAZhTdWn.png)

prs.title: fix(security): flag Unicode TAG characters in the shared threat scan
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening (not a boundary).

**Problem:** `tools/threat_patterns.py` `INVISIBLE_CHARS` omitted the Unicode TAG block U+E0000–U+E007F, so TAG-encoded ("ASCII smuggling") text in memory entries, context files and cron prompts scanned clean while a single U+200B was flagged.

**Fix:** add the TAG block to `INVISIBLE_CHARS` (cron shares the set). Subdivision-flag emoji (U+1F3F4 + lowercase/digit tags + CANCEL TAG) are exempted in both `scan_for_threats` and the cron stripper; the exemption excludes spaces/punctuation so it can't wrap a sentence. Mirrors the existing handling in `tools/ansi_strip.py`.

**Tests:** TAG payload flagged (scanner + cron), Scotland flag allowed, flag-shaped wrapper still flagged; red on base.

Fixes #148815

**Exemption scope:** only the three RGI subdivision flags (England, Scotland, Wales) are exempt; any other TAG character, including flag-shaped sequences, is flagged. **Known limits / follow-ups:** `tools/skills_guard.py` keeps its own invisible-character list without the TAG block (open PR #78952 should reuse this list); `tools/ansi_strip.py` has a looser any-length flag exemption with the same chaining issue.

prs.title: feat(gateway): add hermes gateway tickets for clients that reach the gateway over SSH
prs.body:
> **Stacked on #155320.** This branch contains #155320's two commits; review the commits after them. #155320 merges first.

## ELI5

Apps that reach a Hermes machine over SSH (Desktop and mobile "SSH mode") can already open a chat connection to the gateway with `hermes gateway attach`, but they had no supported way to get the one-time passes the gateway asks for on every other web request. This adds `hermes gateway tickets`: one quick question ("does this machine support it?") and one command that stays open and hands out a fresh pass each time the app asks. A request can ask for a pass for any profile that gateway serves, and for the two special passes that creating, renaming and deleting a profile need, so an app on this path can do what the Desktop app does on its own machine. It can also ask for the chat connection's pass in the form the Desktop app uses, which lets one chat connection work in every profile instead of only the one it was opened for. It never starts a gateway and nothing that exists today changes.

## What does this PR do?

**Stacked on `feat/gateway-attach-windows-start-context` (PR 2). Base pinned to its head `b3f25e2d8279`; merge that one first.** Every count and diff below is against that base.

Adds `hermes gateway tickets`, the public way for an SSH-tunnel client to get `native-http` tickets (until now only reachable through the private `hermes_cli.gateway_client._session_ticket`, which the spike had to import by hand).

- `hermes gateway tickets --probe --json` starts nothing, contacts no gateway, exits 0 and prints `{"protocol":1,"purposes":["native-http","native-profile-create","native-profile-registry","interactive"],"windows_service_session":false}` (`windows_service_session` is PR 2's `windows_service_session()`, the value `attach --json` reports in `start_context`). On a host without this PR the command exits 2 with no JSON on stdout, which is the client's fallback signal.
- `hermes gateway tickets --serve --json` finds the running gateway for the profile with the same discovery `attach` (no flags) uses, never starts one, prints a hello line, then answers each stdin line with exactly one stdout line until stdin closes (exit 0).
- A request line may add `"profile": "<name>"`. Without it the reply is exactly what it was (a ticket for the profile the command runs in). With it, the ticket is for that profile of the same gateway.
- `--serve` mints four purposes: `native-http`, `native-profile-create` (`POST /api/profiles`), `native-profile-registry` (`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/profiles/<name>`) and `interactive` (the WebSocket's ticket, host-scoped; see below).

Why profiles and the two management purposes: a gateway serves every profile of a host and binds each ticket to one. A client that sends every request with the launch profile's ticket gets `403 profile_scope_mismatch` for any other profile, and can never create, rename or delete a profile, because those routes only take their own purposes (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/native_http.py`). SSH-mode users can do all of that today, so a client could not move to this path without them.

How it mirrors Desktop's local connection (`apps/desktop/electron/local-gateway.ts`, `routedGatewayEndpoint` / `mintLocalGatewayTicket` / `nativeGrantPurpose`): same `session-ticket` verb on the same control socket, `profile_id` = the named profile's home, the launch gateway's `instance_id`, the same three purposes, no `scope` (so `profile`, as Desktop's non-interactive tickets), the store's own 30 s TTL. The profile name is resolved with the functions the gateway uses for `?profile=` (`validate_profile_name`, `profile_exists`, `get_profile_dir`). Nothing here can get a ticket a local same-user process cannot already get from the control socket, and `hermes -p <name> gateway tickets --serve` already minted `native-http` for a served sibling.

Why `interactive`: the ticket `hermes gateway attach` returns is bound to the profile it ran in (`mint_ticket` asks with no `scope`, so `profile`), and the gateway answers `profile_mismatch` to every frame on that socket that names another profile (`gateway/session_controls.py:187`). A live Android run against this branch at `c4d1af6f1066` hit exactly that: a chat turn in `beta` failed with "This conversation belongs to another profile", and the profile editor could not load a non-default profile. Desktop's local connection does not have the problem because it asks for a host-scoped interactive ticket. `--serve` now mints that same ticket; `attach` is untouched.

What a host-scoped interactive ticket grants, and why this adds nothing:

- Desktop asks for it the same way: `apps/desktop/electron/local-gateway.ts:621-623` (`ticketScope`: `scope: 'host'` for `interactive` only) sent at `:664` as `{verb: 'session-ticket', params: {profile_id, instance_id, purpose, scope}}`; the Windows path is `apps/desktop/electron/local-gateway-python.ts:41-42` (`_session_ticket(home, endpoint, purpose=..., scope='host' if purpose == 'interactive' else None)`). `--serve` calls that same `_session_ticket(home, endpoint, scope="host")` for the launch profile's home: the same verb, the same four params, the same control socket.
- The gateway decides, not the caller: `gateway/control_socket.py:382-383` requires the same-user peer, `:404-406` passes `scope` to the store, and `gateway/runtime_bootstrap.py:42-44` refuses `host` for any purpose but `interactive`. TTL is the store's `TTL_SECONDS = 30` (`runtime_bootstrap.py:26`) for every ticket; the redeem deletes it (`:75`).
- The WebSocket takes it at `gateway/run_api.py:493` (`redeem(..., purpose='interactive')`) and copies the grant's scope into the connection at `:538` (`'profile_scope': grant.get('scope', 'profile')`). The only readers are `host_scoped` (`gateway/session_controls.py:174-177`) and its five uses: sibling routing for a frame's `profile` among the profiles this process serves (`session_controls.py:187`, `:215`), a staged upload's source home among those same profiles (`gateway/session_ancillary.py:191`), and the group controls (`gateway/session_group_controls.py:93`, `:375`). Capabilities are the purpose's (`runtime_bootstrap.py:54`), the same set a profile-scoped interactive ticket carries.
- So the serve-minted ticket is the grant local Desktop gets (Desktop names the home of the profile it is showing, `--serve` the home it runs in; both are homes that gateway serves, and the reach is the same set of served profiles), from the same socket any same-user local process can already ask. A profile the gateway does not serve is still `profile_mismatch`.

The mint is the existing `_session_ticket`, unchanged. Its error mapping (already inside `attach_gateway`) moved into `mint_ticket` so both commands share it; an attach still calls `_session_ticket(home, endpoint)` with no `purpose` and no `scope` argument, as on the base.

## Related Issue

No issue. Spike evidence: chat over SSH through the gateway works on main today; REST needs per-request `native-http` tickets and there was no public command for them.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_tickets.py` (new, 166 lines): `cmd_gateway_tickets` (probe and serve), the bounded line reader, the per-line reply, the profile lookup and the routed mint.
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/gateway.py`: registers `tickets` with a required, mutually exclusive `--probe` / `--serve` and `--json`.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_attach.py`: `mint_ticket(home, endpoint, *, purpose="interactive", scope=None)` holds the mint and its `TicketUnavailable` mapping; `attach_gateway` calls it. Same calls, same exceptions.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_tickets.py` (new): 56 behaviour tests that run the real CLI as a subprocess. Five of them start a real gateway (four a multiplexing one with named profiles; two of those dial its WebSocket).
- `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-ssh-clients.md` (new): the client contract (both commands, the line protocol, a "Profiles" section saying which purpose and profile each HTTP request needs, a "The WebSocket ticket" section, the six client rules (rule 4: dial the WebSocket with a serve-minted `interactive` ticket when the probe lists it, otherwise with the ticket `attach` returned); rule 2 now matches PR 2: never suggest `hermes gateway install`). Linked from the sidebar, `reference/cli-commands.md` and the `hermes gateway attach` section of `gateway-internals.md`.

### JSON shapes

Probe (one line, exit 0):

```json
{"protocol":1,"purposes":["native-http","native-profile-create","native-profile-registry","interactive"],"windows_service_session":false}
```

A host that lists `native-profile-registry` accepts `profile` in a request. A host that lists `interactive` mints the WebSocket's ticket.

Serve, first line when a gateway is attachable (`endpoint` is the object `attach --json` returns as `endpoint`):

```json
{"endpoint":{"api_origin":"http://127.0.0.1:<port>","authority_epoch":1,"capabilities":["..."],"code_sha":"...","control_home":null,"instance_id":"...","profile_id":"...","runtime_protocol":1,"supervisor":"none"},"protocol":1,"type":"hello"}
```

Serve, first and only line when there is none (exit code is `hermes gateway ensure`'s for that verdict, 5 when absent):

```json
{"error":{"code":"absent","message":"gateway absent: not ready","reason_code":null},"type":"error"}
```

`code` is the discovery state, `reason_code` the reason `attach` reports (or null), `message` the text `attach` shows.

Request lines (`profile` is optional on the three HTTP purposes and forbidden on `interactive`) and the one reply each gets:

```json
{"id":7,"purpose":"native-http"}
{"id":7,"purpose":"native-http","profile":"beta"}
{"id":7,"purpose":"native-profile-create"}
{"id":7,"purpose":"native-profile-registry","profile":"beta"}
{"expires_in":30,"id":7,"ok":true,"ticket":"<ticket>"}
{"error":{"code":"ticket_unavailable","message":"..."},"id":7,"ok":false}
```

The WebSocket's ticket (no `profile`; dial `attach`'s `url` with the subprotocols `hermes-gateway-v1` and `hermes-gateway-ticket.<ticket>`), and the refusal when the key is present:

```json
{"id":8,"purpose":"interactive"}
{"expires_in":30,"id":8,"ok":true,"ticket":"<ticket>"}
{"id":8,"purpose":"interactive","profile":"beta"}
{"error":{"code":"invalid_request","message":"an interactive ticket takes no profile: it serves every one"},"id":8,"ok":false}
```

| HTTP request | `purpose` | `profile` |
|---|---|---|
| selects a profile (`?profile=`, JSON body `profile`, `/api/profiles/<name>/...`, `recents_profile` on the sidebar route) | `native-http` | that name |
| selects none | `native-http` | omit |
| `POST /api/profiles` | `native-profile-create` | omit |
| `PATCH` / `DELETE /api/profiles/<name>` | `native-profile-registry` | `<name>` |

Error codes: `invalid_request` (not a JSON object with an integer or string `id`, nested too deeply to parse, or longer than the line limit: the reply's `id` is null; or `profile` is present and not a valid profile name, `null` included, or present at all on an `interactive` request: the reply carries the `id`), `unsupported_purpose`, `unknown_profile` (no such profile on the host), `profile_not_served` (the profile exists but the running gateway does not serve it; decided by asking the same gateway's `identify` after its refusal: only the same `instance_id`, `state: ready` and a `served_profiles` list of `{profile_id: <string>}` entries that has the launch profile and not this one counts; a replaced instance, a draining or starting gateway, or a malformed list stays `ticket_unavailable`), `ticket_unavailable`. A bad line never closes the channel, and a refused `profile` never falls back to the launch profile's ticket.

Line limit: a request line may be at most 65536 bytes (64 KiB), its LF or CRLF excluded (a 65536-byte line is answered with either ending, a 65537-byte one refused with either). A longer line is dropped as it is read (never held in memory) and gets exactly one `invalid_request` reply; the next line is answered normally.

## Compatibility

Additive. A request line without `profile` and with `purpose: native-http` is answered as before this change. `gateway tickets` is new in this PR, so `purpose: interactive` turning from `unsupported_purpose` into a ticket changes nothing that is on main. The ticket `attach` returns is the one main returns: profile-scoped, and still `profile_mismatch` for another profile (a test pins it against a real gateway). `hermes gateway attach` and `ensure` print what they printed on the base; `attach_gateway`, `TicketUnavailable`, `GatewayAttach` and `_session_ticket` keep their names, signatures and behaviour (the existing attach and bootstrap suites pass unchanged). No config keys, no gateway-side change: the control socket and the HTTP ticket check are untouched. `gateway tickets` was an unknown subcommand before (exit 2).

## How to Test

Before (main without this PR):

```
$ hermes gateway tickets --probe --json
hermes gateway: 'tickets' is not a `hermes gateway` command.
Run `hermes gateway --help` to see all commands.
rc=2
```

RED for the profile work: the final `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_tickets.py` run on the previous head of this branch (`0dd25c7af018`, before profiles) -> 14 failed, 20 passed. The real-gateway failures are the reported break: `GET /api/config?profile=beta` with the only ticket that head can mint answers 403, and `native-profile-create` / `native-profile-registry` are `unsupported_purpose`.

RED for the attach call shape: on this stack before commit `675c86070726`, PR 2's own `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_attach_start_context.py` -> 7 failed, 2 passed (`TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'purpose'`); after it, 9 passed.

RED for the review fixes (`c4d1af6f1066`): its `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_tickets.py` against the module as of `a36e0fa22098` -> 9 failed, 39 passed. The 9: the CRLF line of exactly 65536 bytes (refused), `"profile": null` (a launch-profile ticket was minted), and seven identify answers reported as `profile_not_served` (`served_profiles` `{}` or `[]`, `[]` while draining, `state` draining / starting / missing, a non-string `profile_id`). The other new cases already passed there and pin behaviour: both LF boundaries, the CRLF line one byte over, four more malformed lists, and a replaced `instance_id`.

RED for the interactive ticket (`0f7775e80a84`): its `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_tickets.py` against `hermes_cli/` as of `c4d1af6f1066` -> 8 failed, 48 passed. The 8: the probe's `purposes`, the mint against a real ticket store (`unsupported_purpose`), the five `profile` values on an interactive request (`unsupported_purpose`, not `invalid_request`), and the real-gateway socket test (no ticket to dial with). The ninth new test, attach's ticket against a real gateway, passes on both: it pins what main does.

After (head `0f7775e80a84`):

1. `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_tickets.py --file-retries 0` -> 56 passed, 0 failed. Among them, against a real multiplexing gateway serving `default` and `beta`:
   - one serve-minted `interactive` ticket opens `/api/ws`; on that one socket `session.create` with `profile: beta` commits a session in beta's `state.db` (and `session.list` with `profile: beta` shows it), `session.create` with no `profile` and with `profile: default` commit in the root's, neither store holds the other's session, and `profile: nobody` is `profile_mismatch`. Dialing again with the same ticket is refused at the upgrade, and the HTTP API answers 401 to an unspent one.
   - the ticket `hermes gateway attach --json` returns opens `/api/ws`, `session.create` with `profile: beta` is `profile_mismatch` and creates nothing in beta, and `session.create` with no `profile` commits in the root's store.

   And against a real multiplexing gateway serving `default`, `beta` and `gamma`:
   - a `profile: beta` ticket gets 200 on `/api/config?profile=beta` and `/api/profiles/beta/soul`, and 403 `profile_scope_mismatch` on `?profile=default`, `?profile=gamma` and `/api/profiles/gamma/soul`; a ticket without `profile` gets 200 on `/api/config` and 403 on `?profile=beta`.
   - `native-http` tickets get 403 on `POST /api/profiles` and on `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/profiles/beta`; a create ticket gets 401 on `GET /api/config` and on `PATCH`/`DELETE`; a registry ticket gets 401 on reads and on `POST /api/profiles`, and 403 on another profile's `DELETE`; then create (200), rename `gamma` -> `delta` (200) and delete `beta` (200) succeed with their own tickets, after which `profile: beta` is `unknown_profile`.
2. `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_tickets.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_attach.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_attach_start_context.py tests/gateway/test_native_http_auth.py tests/gateway/test_native_profile_registry_grant.py tests/gateway/test_native_profile_create.py tests/gateway/test_session_a2a.py tests/gateway/test_runtime_bootstrap.py tests/gateway/test_ticket_profile_scope.py tests/gateway/test_native_http_secondary_profile_binding.py --file-retries 0` -> 10 files, 82 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped.
3. Every non-Docker test file that mentions the attach module, the tickets module, `_session_ticket` or `windows_service_session`, plus the native-http auth, profile-create and profile-registry gateway files: 26 files, 256 passed, 0 failed (measured at `a36e0fa22098`, not rerun since).
4. `tests/docker/test_tui_gateway_startup.py`: 4 passed (measured at `a36e0fa22098`, not rerun since).
5. `python scripts/check` -> 18 checks, ok. `python -B scripts/boundary_lint.py --check` -> exit 0. `python -m scripts.code_health --base b3f25e2d8279 --head HEAD` -> 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

prs.title: fix(gateway): two RPC failure paths log their error instead of dropping it
prs.body:
A pool-routed RPC handler that raises, and the backend's parse-error reply, now leave a log line instead of disappearing.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  H["pool handler raises"] --> R["-32000 reply"]
  H -->|after| L["gateway log: method, id, traceback"]
  P["-32700 reply, id null"] -->|before| D["dropped by handleFrame"]
  P -->|after| C["onUncorrelatedError: Desktop console, TUI protocol log"]
```

- `tui_gateway/rpc_dispatch.py`: the pool `run` wrapper logs with `logger.exception` before answering, like the inline WebSocket and stdio paths.
- `apps/shared/src/json-rpc-channel.ts`: an error frame with no request id goes to a new `onUncorrelatedError` option, passed through `JsonRpcGatewayClient`; Desktop logs it to the console and the TUI client to its protocol log. The pending-response branch moves into `settleResponse` to keep `handleFrame` under the complexity limit.

**Tier:** T1 (logging only; replies and routing unchanged).

| Check | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `test_rpc_dispatch_pool_errors.py` | fails (no log record) | passes |
| `json-rpc-channel.test.ts` uncorrelated error case | fails | passes |
| `apps/shared` tests + typecheck; Desktop `src/api` tests + typecheck; TUI gateway-client tests | | 222 / 200 / 42 passed |
| Anti-slop ratchet; `python scripts/check` | | no net-new findings; 14 checks ok |

**Not verified:** the web dashboard's `GatewayClient` does not pass the new sink, so it still ignores such frames.

Fixes #150533

prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump hermes-teammates to 1.7.0
prs.body:
Give your agent a fixed team. You define each specialist's instructions, toolsets and model once, and the agent picks only a name. On Hermes' Kanban board the team works linked cards one after another, and each finished card waits in Review for approval. 1.7 adds opt-in push completion: a finished run can wake the chat that assigned it, so an orchestrator doesn't have to hold its turn in `teammate_wait`.

This bumps the hermes-teammates entry from 1.6.0 to **1.7.0**, pinned to `7665be07c5e1ad64317211414bb37fbd9349fce6` (tag [v1.7.0](https://github.com/100yenadmin/hermes-teammates/releases/tag/v1.7.0)). Only `plugin-catalog/hermes-teammates.yaml` changes.

## What changes on the plugin's page
- **The pins:** the sha, `version: "1.7.0"`, and the banner and screenshot URLs all point at the v1.7.0 commit.
- **One Disclosure sentence is replaced.** "Completion-notice code exists but never injects on current Hermes" is no longer true. The new sentence says:
  - completion notices are off by default and never inject unless the operator turns on both `notify_on_completion` and `trust_notice_routing`;
  - with both on, a finished run sends one line (teammate name, run ID and status, never result text) as a user message to the chat it was assigned from, through `ctx.inject_message`;
  - that also needs Hermes' own `allow_gateway_injection` consent;
  - a run with no recorded chat gets no notice;
  - after `/new`, `/reset` or `/resume`, the line reaches that chat's current conversation.

  The rest of the description is unchanged, word for word.
- **Tools and hooks:** unchanged (eight tools, the same two hooks). `requires_hermes` stays `>=0.21.4`.

## What 1.7.0 adds
- **`trust_notice_routing`, off by default.** With `notify_on_completion` also on, each notice goes to the chat recorded when the run was assigned. Each chat gets only its own runs. With the setting off, everything behaves exactly as in 1.6.0.
- This was contributed by allanbell3d in 100yenadmin/hermes-teammates#136.

## Install
```bash
hermes plugins install 100yenadmin/hermes-teammates --ref 7665be07c5e1ad64317211414bb37fbd9349fce6 --enable
hermes tools enable kanban
```

## How to test
```bash
python3 -B scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/hermes-teammates.yaml
```
Manual check:
1. Follow the README's first steps (roster, `hermes tools enable kanban`), then send the quick-start message. Three linked cards go ready → running → review → done without another message.
2. Optional: set `notify_on_completion: true` and `trust_notice_routing: true` in the plugin's settings, and `allow_gateway_injection: true` on its entry. Assign a teammate from a gateway chat and end the turn. When the run finishes, a one-line notice starts a new turn in that chat.

## Disclosure
Updated as described above. 1.7.0 adds no tools, hooks, network calls or stored data. The only new behaviour is the opt-in notice, which carries no run output and goes through Hermes' own `inject_message` and consent check.

## Evidence
- **Validator:** `validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` reports `OK` for the whole directory. Upstream's `scripts/ci/catalog_validate_pinned_entries.py`, run locally at the pin, reports `PASS`.
- **Pins:** the sha and all image URLs pin the v1.7.0 commit; the banner and all six screenshots return HTTP 200.
- **Plugin CI:** the feature passed against pinned Hermes and Hermes main. A Claude reviewer and a Codex reviewer each reviewed it, and both re-reviewed the fix commit (MERGE).
- **Live on Hermes 0.23.1, fresh homes (`env -i`, no TTY):** with the setting on, a notice woke a gateway-hosted chat, and the agent read and relayed the result. With it off, nothing was sent. The README's quick-start chain finished all three cards.
- **Install by catalog name at this pin (Hermes 0.23.1, fresh home):** with the published catalog changed only in this entry, `hermes plugins install hermes-teammates --enable` installed v1.7.0 at `7665be0`, and the README's quick-start message finished all three cards (213 s, no failed tool calls).
- **Not proven here:** plugin runtime behaviour beyond the plugin's own CI and those runs.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop the /goal loop after a failed provider turn
prs.body:
This stops the classic CLI `/goal` loop from judging and re-queuing after a failed provider turn.

## What does this PR do?

On main, a credit cap hit mid-goal (HTTP 402) spends the whole turn budget on 402s plus one judge call per failed turn.

A failed turn has no model reply. `_maybe_continue_goal_after_turn` still reads the newest assistant row, which is the `FAILED_TURN_NOTICE` boundary row on main ("Your request was not processed...") and the previous turn's reply on v0.20.0. The judge reads that as progress, says continue, and the next turn fails the same way. The TUI already gates this with `_is_successful_goal_turn`. The CLI hook never reads `_last_turn_result`.

This came from production use of Hermes on my fleet of unattended `hermes chat` goal agents (v0.20.0, custom provider behind a daily credit cap). Across the fleet's tmux panes, the goal event right after a billing-failed turn was 91 continuations, 87 parks and 7 "goal achieved" verdicts, all judged on text the failed turn never produced. One pane logged "402, Continuing toward goal (n/20)" in a loop until the judge-error pause fired.

## Related Issue

Related to #63180, the gateway twin of this bug. #63187, #63203, #64337 and #74974 touch only `gateway/`. No open issue or PR covers the classic CLI hook. #118705 edits the empty-response check a few lines below and composes with this change.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/cli_loops_mixin.py` adds `_goal_turn_failed`. It applies the TUI contract to `_last_turn_result` and skips the judge. The contract is failed, interrupted, or `completed is False` that is not a max-iterations handoff, so #102213 keeps working.
- For `failure_reason` billing, auth or auth_permanent the hook also pauses the goal, because those repeat on every retry until the user acts.

- `locales/*.yaml` adds `cli.goal.paused_provider_failure` to all 17 catalogs (parity test).

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_goal_interrupt.py` adds 5 cases. Billing, auth and auth_permanent pause with no judge call and nothing queued. A transient server error skips the judge, spends no goal turn and leaves the goal active, while a max-iterations handoff still goes to the judge as before.

## How to Test

1. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_goal_interrupt.py -q` on main code with the new tests. The 4 failure cases fail because the judge runs on the failed-turn notice, and on this branch all 8 pass.

```
E   AssertionError: Expected 'judge_goal' to not have been called. Called 1 times.
E   Calls: [call('build a thing', 'Your request was not processed. Send it again if you still want me to carry it out.', ...)]
```

2. End to end, I drove the real `HermesCLI` (`chat()` plus the post-turn goal hook that `process_loop` runs) against a local fake OpenAI server. The `/goal` kickoff turn succeeds and every continuation turn gets the Nous 402 "Insufficient available credits" body. The judge always answers continue.

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| turns run | 20 | 2 |
| POSTs answered 402 | 19 | 1 |
| judge calls on failed turns | 19 | 0 |
| final goal state | paused, turn budget exhausted (20/20) | paused, provider turn failed (billing) |

3. The 15 goal, loop, i18n and TUI goal test files give 322 passed, 1 skipped on main and 327 passed, 1 skipped on this branch.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform (macOS 26, Darwin 25.6.0, Python 3.14.7)

The full `pytest tests/ -q` suite did not run on this machine, only the 15 related files listed under How to Test.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] N/A for README, `docs/`, `cli-config.yaml.example`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md` and tool schemas. No config key, workflow or schema changes.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered. The change is control flow in the post-turn hook with no file, process or terminal handling.

## Screenshots / Logs

```
main    RESULT {"turns": 20, "agent_402": 19, "judge_calls": 20, "judge_calls_after_failed_turns": 19, "goal_status": "paused", "paused_reason": "turn budget exhausted (20/20)"}
branch  RESULT {"turns": 2, "agent_402": 1, "judge_calls": 1, "judge_calls_after_failed_turns": 0, "goal_status": "paused", "paused_reason": "provider turn failed (billing)"}
  ⏸ Goal paused — the provider rejected the turn (billing). Fix credits or credentials, then use /goal resume to continue, or /goal clear to stop.
```

prs.title: fix(gateway): restart when idle — keep serving, never kill live work on a timer (salvage #115190, #147402)
prs.body:
Before, asking the gateway to restart froze it: for up to 30 minutes it turned away every new message, every background-job "done" notice and every subagent result, then killed whatever was still running. Now the gateway keeps working normally and restarts the moment it is idle; nothing running is killed because a timer ran out, and the wait says exactly what it is waiting on.

| | before (origin/main 4b40ffb0) | after (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| new session B during the wait | refused `runtime_draining` | admitted, ran (`b1 terminal/completed`) |
| follow-up on session A | `queued`, never ran | `terminal/completed` |
| background-process completion notice | `Watch notification not admitted … runtime_draining` | both notices admitted and ran as turns |
| at the 20 s cap | `wait timed out … proceeding to stop()`, held turn `interrupted`, 2 tool subprocesses killed, clean-shutdown marker skipped | `WARNING Restart still waiting after 20s; live work is NOT interrupted … Waiting on: [{'kind':'chat','session':…},{'kind':'process','process_id':'proc_269f09c28930',…}]`, keeps waiting |
| restart | exit 75, 23 s after SIGUSR1, work lost | exit 75, 61 s after SIGUSR1, once everything finished; held turn `completed` |

**Root cause:** `request_restart` set `_draining` (the admission-refusing state) up front and `_await_active_work_before_restart` treated `agent.restart_after_turn_timeout` as a hard deadline before `stop()` interrupts.

**What changed**
- `gateway/restart_when_idle.py` (new): restart-when-idle wait. Admission stays open until `stop()`; idle = no awaitable foreground work AND no live background delegation, notify-watched background process, or queued delegation completion. The cap now only warns (repeating) with every unit named. Wedged turns still never hold it.
- Force path: control verb `pause-for-update` with params `{"force": true}` (`pause_gateway_for_update(home, force=True)`); ack adds `"force": true` and `"waiting_on": [...]`. It escalates a waiting restart and zeroes the drain budgets so `stop()` interrupts at once. SIGTERM unchanged. Contract for `hermes update --force` (Lane C) is stable.
- `session_runtime_workers.uncounted_runtime_work_units` names each real unit (session id + route, mutation task, side-agent thread, managed worker) instead of padding `{'kind':'managed','pid':<gateway pid>}`; `_describe_active_work` adds delegations (id + parent session), processes (id, pid, command) and queued notices.
- Process watchers register in `runner._live_process_watchers` while running so the wait counts them.
- `agent.restart_after_turn_timeout` now means "warn after": DEFAULT_CONFIG comment + docs (updating.md, configuration.md, messaging/index.md) updated.
- Salvaged by cherry-pick (authorship kept): async-delegation accounting from #115190 by @Glucksberg and #147402 by @WenhuaXia (their duplicate counters merged into one `_active_async_delegation_count`).

**Live repro:** real `gateway.run` from each code root under scratch HOME/HERMES_HOME, loopback fake OpenAI provider, `restart_after_turn_timeout: 20`; session A starts `sleep 12`/`sleep 35` with `notify_on_complete`, session C holds a model call 60 s, SIGUSR1, then session B + A follow-up. Before: B refused, notice refused, C interrupted at 20 s, 2 subprocesses killed. After: B, A follow-up, C and both completion notices all `terminal/completed` in state.db `session_admissions`; restart at +61 s; wait log names `chat` + `process` units.

**Tests**: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on 16 restart/drain/notice files: 134 passed, 2 skipped. New: `test_restart_wait_never_interrupts_a_delegation_at_the_cap`, `test_request_restart_after_turn_cap_elapsed_keeps_waiting_and_serving` (cap keeps waiting; `force_restart` stops with drain 0).

## Tests changed by ruling
- `test_restart_drain.py::test_request_restart_is_idempotent`: `_draining is True` → `False` (refuse-new-turns-while-waiting).
- `test_restart_drain.py::test_request_restart_defers_stop_until_active_turn_finishes`: same assertion.
- `test_restart_drain.py::test_request_restart_after_turn_cap_elapsed_still_calls_stop` → replaced by `…_keeps_waiting_and_serving` (interrupt-at-cap).
- `test_restart_drain.py::test_restart_wait_for_async_delegation_is_bounded` (from #115190) → replaced by `test_restart_wait_never_interrupts_a_delegation_at_the_cap`.
- `test_restart_drain.py::test_request_restart_after_turn_timeout_zero_enters_stop_immediately`: removed (0 used to mean "force drain now"; force is now explicit).
- `test_managed_runtime_live_drain.py::test_managed_turn_finishes_inside_configured_restart_drain`: waited for identify to report `draining` while the turn ran; now asserts the pause ACK names the managed turn it waits on. The turn still completes and lands in state.db (passes locally).

**NOT_COVERED:** the force verb end-to-end over a real control socket (unit-tested via `force_restart` only); Windows; CLI-side wait budgets in `hermes_cli/gateway.py` (`_graceful_restart_via_sigusr1` still gives up after its budget and falls back to a service restart — Lane A/C files).

## Infographic

![Restart when idle](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab26488/LT4Sma8RBUxquTT9r3MC7_ZZ3pGATW.png)

prs.title: fix(agent): Anthropic 401 help names a key_cmd credential instead of Entra ID / az login (salvage #154860)
prs.body:
When an Anthropic-style provider that gets its token from a `key_cmd` returned 401, Hermes told you it was a Microsoft Entra ID key and to run `az login`, then told you to check `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `.env`. Now it names the real source (`key_cmd token (command)`), tells you to run your `key_cmd` and check the token it prints, and leaves out the env-var/OAuth advice, which only applies to string keys.

Salvages #154860 by @webtecnica (cherry-picked, authorship kept) for #154707 reported by @christianburrell, plus the `key_cmd` hint from @kvnloo's fork commit 771ea4b3 (cherry-picked, authorship kept). The labels come from the credential-source tag added in e7a81e75 (#140469).

## What was wrong
`agent/turn_recovery.py::_print_anthropic_401_diagnostics` branched on `is_token_provider(key)`, which is true for **any** callable. A `key_cmd` provider (`CommandTokenSource`), Vertex OAuth and MiniMax OAuth all got the Entra ID / `az login` text. The same key's banner already said `key_cmd token (command)`.

## Commits
1. **@webtecnica (#154860)**: branch on `credential_source(key) == ENTRA_ID`. Any other callable prints its `credential_label`.
2. **@kvnloo (771ea4b3)**: adds `Run the configured \`key_cmd\` manually and verify the token it prints.` for `KEY_CMD` sources, plus a source-matrix test in `tests/agent/test_credential_source_labels.py`. Conflict with (1) resolved by keeping (1)'s structure and adding the hint inside its labelled-callable branch.
3. **Ours**:
   - The Troubleshooting block (`ANTHROPIC_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `hermes auth add anthropic`, ...) now prints only for a **string** key. A callable key never came from those places, so the advice pointed users at credentials this provider doesn't read.
   - Swept the other places that label a callable key: `ApiErrorSummaryMixin._mask_api_key_for_logs` (request debug dumps) and the dashboard's `hermes_cli/web_server_oauth.py::_truncate_token` now render `<{source}-bearer>` from the tag (e.g. `<key-cmd-bearer>`). An untagged callable keeps `<entra-id-bearer>`, so `tests/agent/test_callable_api_key.py` on main is unchanged. `batch_runner` prints the source label instead of "Entra ID".
   - Moved the test into `tests/agent/test_credential_source_labels.py` and deleted the issue-numbered `tests/test_154707_*.py`. kvnloo's parametrized matrix covers both of webtecnica's cases, without invoking the callable.
   - `doctor`/`status`: grepped and found no callable-key labelling there (the doctor's Entra probe only runs for `azure-foundry` + `entra_id`), so nothing changed.

## Tests
- Red on base 095ba5b5 / green on head: `test_anthropic_401_diagnostics_labels_callable_source[vertex,key_cmd,minimax,unknown]`, `test_anthropic_401_env_and_login_advice_only_for_a_string_key[*]`, `test_masked_previews_name_the_source_not_entra[vertex,key_cmd,minimax]`. That's 12 failing cases on base, from the 2 invariant tests on the 401 help plus 1 on the previews.
- `tests/agent/test_credential_source_labels.py tests/agent/test_callable_api_key.py tests/agent/test_run_agent.py`: 310 passed on head. I ran them directly with the install's test interpreter under a scratch HOME; the shared test lock was queued.

## Live evidence (real `hermes chat -q`, scratch HERMES_HOME + fake HOME, real api.anthropic.com returns 401)
Config: `providers.corp` with `transport: anthropic_messages`, `api: https://api.anthropic.com`, `key_cmd: "echo sk-bogus-keycmd-token-123456789"`.

**main @ 095ba5b5** (tree from `git archive`, `hermes_cli.__file__` printed from the archive):
```
🔐 Anthropic 401 — authentication failed.
   Auth method: Microsoft Entra ID (httpx event hook)
   Run `hermes doctor` for credential-chain diagnostics, or
   `az login` if your developer session expired.
   Troubleshooting:
     • Check ANTHROPIC_TOKEN in …/hh/.env for Hermes-managed OAuth/setup tokens
     • Check ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in …/hh/.env for API keys or legacy token values
     … (5 more env/OAuth lines)
```
**head**:
```
🔐 Anthropic 401 — authentication failed.
   Auth method: key_cmd token (command)
   Run the configured `key_cmd` manually and verify the token it prints.
```
**Control on head** (`provider: anthropic` + bogus string `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`): unchanged from main. It still prints `Auth method: x-api-key (API key)`, `Token prefix: sk-ant-api03...` and the full Troubleshooting block.

NOT_COVERED: Entra ID live (no Azure tenant). The Entra branch is covered by the `[entra]` unit cases, which build the provider with the real `build_token_provider` against a stubbed `azure.identity`.

Credit: @christianburrell (report + probe runs on both candidate fixes), @webtecnica (#154860), @kvnloo (771ea4b3).

## Infographic
![Anthropic 401 help: before says cloud login, after names the key_cmd token](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab256c4/74wAAc8unfGt15QrUUmo-_eZpUKKtI.png)

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: fix(kanban): inherited worker card is read-only for a cron run fired from it
prs.body:
**Problem.** A cron run fired in-process from a Kanban worker (`cronjob run`) is fenced as non-dispatcher-owned (`non_dispatcher_owned_context`, #94351), but only `_default_task_id` checks the fence. `_enforce_worker_task_ownership`, `_own_task_env`/`_worker_run_id`, the `_worker_guard` run-id gate and the auto heartbeat still read raw `os.environ["HERMES_KANBAN_TASK"]`. A cron child that names the worker's card explicitly passes the ownership check and can complete/block/heartbeat/comment on it, with completions stamped with the **worker's** run id (#103883 has the board evidence).

**Fix.** `tools/kanban_tools.py`: a fence-aware `_owned_task()` now backs those gates. If the execution inherited `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` but does not own it, that card is read-only. Lifecycle tools and `kanban_comment` refuse it with an actionable message. Other cards keep the orchestrator path and `kanban_create` still works. The auto heartbeat skips the fenced cron context. A real dispatcher worker behaves as before.

**Hardening (SECURITY.md §3.2), not a boundary.** This applies inside one process. It does not cover the gateway-owned execution path: agent cron runs submitted via `cron.submit` carry no firing-card provenance (see the escalation note on the issue).

**Tests.** `tests/tools/test_kanban_inherited_task_readonly.py` checks refusal for complete/block/heartbeat/comment on the inherited card, that no worker run id or heartbeat is borrowed, that other cards stay mutable, and that the dispatcher worker can still complete its own card. 5/7 fail on base; all pass with the fix. The existing kanban/cron isolation suites pass (111 tests).

**Credits.** The fence-aware `_own_task_env` and heartbeat gate follow #103896 by @fangliquanflq (Co-authored-by). That PR's other hunks (stop nudge, turn finalizer, subprocess env scrub, comment injection) are already on main in another form.

Refs #149512
Refs #103883

**Scope — partial (Refs, not Fixes):** since `cdbe8c35ad`, agent cron runs without a bound owner execution go `run_job` → `run_canonical_job` → `cron.submit` and execute in the gateway owner process, where `HERMES_KANBAN_*` is stripped. That default path is **not** covered here: closing it needs a `firing_task` field carried through `CronRunParams`/admission/journal into a ContextVar — a canonical gateway contract change left to a maintainer (#149512 stays open). This PR hardens the in-process path. **Behaviour change:** inside the fence, a cron run naming a *different* running card now completes it with `expected_run_id=None` (base refused with "worker is scoped to…"); `kanban_link` no longer borrows the worker's run id.

- New: a lock/version floor test (`tests/pm/test_git_package.py`) and a Windows-marked ucrt64 PATH-derivation test.
- Updated: the candidate-list test and a bundle-audit exemption row.

prs.title: fix(gateway): no typing indicator or processing reactions for a sender admission will drop
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening (no new boundary): pre-admission outbound activity leaked to senders the gateway then drops.

**Problem.** `_process_message_background` starts the typing refresh and the `on_processing_start` hook before `_handle_message`, where the runner authorizes. With Signal linked as a secondary device on the owner's number, every contact got `sendTyping` as the owner; adapters with processing reactions (Telegram, Discord, Feishu, Matrix, Photon, relay) also sent 👀/✅ to unauthorized senders.

**Fix.** Ask the runner's own `_is_user_authorized_for_source` verdict before that activity:
- `typing_refresh_wanted` gates `_start_typing_refresh` (salvaged from #149030 by @kouyichi, authorship kept).
- `sender_may_see_activity` gates `_run_processing_hook`, caching the verdict on the event so typing, start and complete agree and the runner is asked once.
Internal events skip the probe; a missing runner or a raising probe keeps the old behaviour.

**Tests.** `tests/gateway/test_typing_indicator_authorization.py` drives the real `_process_message_background`: unauthorized → no typing loop, no hooks; authorized → both; internal/no-runner/probe-error keep typing. Red on main (typing) and on the salvaged commit alone (reactions).

Fixes #149024

Also gates the BlueBubbles read receipt (owner's own Apple ID) on the runner's authorization verdict. **Known limits (bot accounts, follow-up):** Telegram's pairing/decline reply re-arms typing via `_retrigger_typing`; Matrix `_background_read_receipt` and opt-in WhatsApp read receipts still fire before authorization (contradicts `whatsapp.md:306`). Discord: unauthorized senders now skip the backfill ledger, so a later scan may re-dispatch (and re-drop) those messages up to 3 times.

prs.title: fix(gateway): no typing indicator to a sender admission will drop
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The typing indicator could be shown to a sender the gateway then drops as unauthorized.
`BasePlatformAdapter._process_message_background` starts the refresh loop *before*
`_handle_message`, and the runner authorizes inside that handler, so the first `sendTyping`
went out before the verdict — with Signal linked as a secondary device on the owner's own
number (the single-number / Note-to-Self setup), every contact who messaged the owner saw
the owner "typing…" after each of their own messages, and nothing was ever read or answered.

`_start_typing_refresh` now asks `gateway.platforms.helpers.typing_refresh_wanted`, which
resolves the runner (the adapter's `gateway_runner`, else the owner of its message handler)
and reads the same verdict the handler will. A sender admission drops therefore gets no
indicator, and the indicator can no longer disagree with admission.

Kept exactly as before:

- `typing_indicator: false` still suppresses it (the check moved into the helper).
- Scheduled heartbeats still get none — proactive work has nothing to say yet.
- Internal events (background-process notices) are admitted without an allowlist, so the
  probe is skipped for them.
- An adapter with no runner (a plugin adapter built outside `_create_adapter`, hand-built
  test adapters) and a verdict that raises both keep the indicator: this probe must never be
  the reason a conversation loses its status bubble.

## Related Issue

Fixes #149024

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/helpers.py` — new `typing_refresh_wanted(adapter, event)`: adapter
  config, heartbeat and internal-event gates plus the authorization probe, in one place.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py` — `_start_typing_refresh` delegates to it. The file is at its
  `FILE_LINES` cap, so the change is line-neutral: the three call-site lines replace the
  condition that was already there, and the rationale lives in the helper's docstring.
- `tests/gateway/test_typing_indicator_authorization.py` — new module; drives the real
  `_process_message_background` turn path with a stubbed refresh loop, so it asserts "was
  the indicator started" and never timing.

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_typing_indicator_authorization.py
```

On this branch: 6 passed.

Sabotage (both source files restored to the base commit, the new test kept): 3 failed,
3 passed, the reported case failing with the defect itself:

```
test_unauthorized_sender_never_sees_typing
>       assert adapter._keep_typing.await_count == 0
E       AssertionError: assert 1 == 0
```

The other two failures on the base are the tests that assert the probe ran at all
(`runner.sources` empty), and the three pass-through cases (internal event, no runner,
raising verdict) pass on both sides, as they should.

Every test module that references `_process_message_background`, `_start_typing_refresh`
or `_keep_typing` (41 files, the whole surface this change touches):
580 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped.

`python scripts/check --base upstream/main` → `14 checks, ok`.

## What this does not change

- Nothing else gates the pre-handler window: a message dropped for an ignored Slack channel
  or parked by startup restore can still show a brief indicator. Those gates live in
  `_hm_admit_event` and are not authorization; closing them means moving the indicator start
  after admission, a much larger change.
- The unauthorized-DM paths (`pair` / `decline` / owner notice) still run — only the
  indicator is withheld from a sender who is not authorized.
- Authorization is asked once more per turn (the handler asks it again): `_is_user_authorized`
  is a read-only peek, which is why it was safe to consult before admission.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added for the fixed behaviour
- [x] No formatting/cleanup unrelated to the issue
- [x] English comments and commit message

prs.title: fix(cron): a dashboard edit keeps a zero-tool toolset allowlist (#148886)
prs.body:
## Problem

A cron job deliberately locked to zero toolsets (`enabled_toolsets: []`) loses that allowlist on
the next Dashboard edit of any field — including a prompt-only edit — and the job starts running
with every toolset, MCP servers included.

Two steps on the dashboard write path collapse the distinction between "zero tools" and "no
restriction":

1. `web/src/lib/cron-job.ts::buildCronJobPayload` sends the whole form, and an empty toolset
   picker becomes `enabled_toolsets: null` (it cannot tell "no restriction" from "the stored
   allowlist is the zero-tool list this picker cannot render").
2. `hermes_cli/web_server_cron.py::_cron_string_list` collapsed that to `None`, and
   `cron/jobs.py::update_job` merged it over the stored `[]`.

`cronjob`'s own tool surface is already safe (it skips a `None` and documents `[]` as an explicit
zero-tool allowlist that is never widened back, #82010); the dashboard route bypasses that guard.

## Change

- `_cron_string_list(..., keep_empty=True)` keeps an explicit `[]` as `[]`. `context_from` keeps
  the old `[] -> None` collapse, where empty really does mean "clear".
- The create route uses it for `enabled_toolsets` too: a client that sends `[]` means zero tools,
  as documented, not "unrestricted".
- `_keep_zero_tool_allowlist()` drops a `null` `enabled_toolsets` from a dashboard update when the
  stored allowlist is exactly `[]`, because that is the one stored value the picker cannot display
  — writing it would widen the job to every tool. A non-empty stored allowlist still clears when
  the picker is emptied: the user can see and uncheck it.

`cron/jobs.py::update_job` keeps its generic contract (`None` writes "no restriction") for
programmatic callers; the loss happens in the dashboard adapter, so that is where it is fixed.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_cron_profiles.py` (existing profile-routing harness):
- `test_dashboard_normalizer_keeps_an_explicit_empty_toolset_list` — adapter unit: `[]` stays `[]`,
  `context_from: []` still collapses to `None`.
- `test_dashboard_prompt_edit_preserves_a_zero_tool_allowlist` — the reported path, end to end
  through `update_cron_job` with the dashboard's full form payload: prompt changes, `[]` survives
  both the response and the store.
- `test_dashboard_create_keeps_an_explicit_empty_toolset_list` — the create route's same collapse.
- `test_dashboard_cleared_picker_still_clears_a_non_empty_allowlist` — the capability that must
  not regress.

Red-first evidence (source reverted to `upstream/main`, tests kept):

```
=== Summary: 1 files, 44 tests passed, 3 failed ===
E       assert None == []      (x3, one per zero-tool case)
```

Green with the fix:

```
=== Summary: 1 files, 47 tests passed, 0 failed ===   tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_cron_profiles.py
=== Summary: 177 files, 1603 tests passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped ===   tests/cron
=== Summary: 4 files, 37 tests passed, 0 failed ===   dashboard cron route tests
scripts/check --base upstream/main -> 14 checks, ok
```

## Risks / not done

- A job whose stored allowlist is exactly `[]` can no longer be returned to "no restriction" by
  emptying the dashboard picker (that is the value the form can never display). Recreate the job,
  or edit `cron/jobs.json`. This matches `cronjob`'s existing contract, which has no clear path
  either.
- No front-end change: the picker still has no way to show "zero tools" as distinct from "no
  selection". That would be a UI feature (a tri-state control), not this bug fix.

Closes #148886

prs.title: fix(config): keep config.yaml backups owner-only
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`backup_config()` copied `config.yaml` with `shutil.copy2`, which preserves the source file's mode. A `config.yaml` left at 0644 by an editor or a non-atomic writer therefore produced world-readable backups containing the user's credentials.

Each new backup now gets the same `_secure_file` policy that `config.yaml` itself already gets: 0600, skipped when managed (activation sets 0640 group-readable) or in a container. Reusing the existing helper keeps one permission policy for the config and its copies instead of hardcoding a second chmod.

- `hermes_cli/config_backups.py`: call `_secure_file(dest)` right after the `shutil.copy2` in `backup_config()` (late import, matching how `config.py` late-imports this module).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_backups.py`: regression test: a 0644 `config.yaml` yields a 0600 backup.

1. `chmod 644 ~/.hermes/config.yaml`, then trigger a backup (e.g. `hermes setup`).
2. `stat -c '%a %n' ~/.hermes/backups/config/*`: on `main` the new backup is `644`; with this PR it is `600`.

prs.title: fix(cron): isolate kanban worker identity
prs.body:
## Summary

- make Kanban stop, ownership, run-stamping, heartbeat, comment, and budget-exhaustion gates honor the execution-scoped dispatcher ownership fence
- reject lifecycle mutation of an inherited worker task while preserving explicitly configured cron orchestrator access to other tasks
- scrub Kanban dispatcher identity from terminal and execute-code subprocess environments created by fenced cron executions

## Root Cause

Cron jobs fired inside a dispatcher worker already enter `non_dispatcher_owned_context()`, but several lifecycle gates read `HERMES_KANBAN_*` directly. Those reads bypassed the ContextVar fence, so the cron turn could receive the worker stop nudge, reuse its task and run IDs, heartbeat its claim, consume operator comments, or record the worker failure. Child-process environment builders likewise only recognized delegated-child lineage, allowing a fenced cron execution to copy dispatcher identity across a process boundary.

## Testing

- RED: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_cron_kanban_env_isolation.py -q` (2 new regressions failed before the production patch)
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_cron_kanban_env_isolation.py tests/agent/test_kanban_stop.py tests/tools/test_kanban_comment_injection.py -q` (26 passed)

prs.title: fix(file-safety): read-deny the live Google Workspace token files
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #38953 (write side) — noted there by @egilewski's review and tracked in the drift history of #89064.

`get_read_block_error()` blocks reads of the legacy `auth/google_oauth.json` path, but not the stores the Google Workspace skill actually uses: `HERMES_HOME/google_token.json` (live OAuth refresh/access token) and `HERMES_HOME/google_oauth_pending.json` (in-flight PKCE exchange state). A prompt-injected `read_file` can exfiltrate a live Google refresh token. The other credential surfaces already deny both (`_ROOT_CREDENTIAL_FILES` on delivery, `_SENSITIVE_MANAGED_FILE_BASENAMES` on the dashboard, and `build_write_denied_paths()` for writes once #38953 lands); the read guard was the last open one.

**The subtlety:** the sandbox mount gate in `tools/credential_files.py` deliberately reuses the read deny-list ("the mount surface cannot hand a skill what the read surface denies"), and the google-workspace skill declares `google_token.json` in `required_credential_files` — its own docstring cites that file as the canonical *legitimately mountable* service token. A blanket read-deny would therefore silently break the skill inside Docker/Modal sandboxes (`register_credential_file` would refuse the mount and the token would never reach the container).

So the fix is two-sided:

- read-deny both files (under the active profile home **and** the Hermes root, since profiles inherit root credentials);
- add a narrow, exact-path carve-out in the mount gate (`_MOUNTABLE_SERVICE_TOKENS = {"google_token.json"}`) so skill-declared service tokens stay mountable while master stores remain refused. `google_oauth_pending.json` gets no carve-out: nothing mounts it, and the in-flight PKCE verifier has no business inside a sandbox.

**Why the carve-out only resolves against `HERMES_HOME`, while the read deny-list covers both `HERMES_HOME` and the Hermes root:** it cannot be reached from anywhere else. `register_credential_file()` builds its host path as `hermes_home / relative_path` and then runs `validate_within_dir(host_path, hermes_home)`, so by the time the deny-list is consulted the resolved path is always inside the active `HERMES_HOME`. Matching the deny-list's two-location shape here would widen the carve-out to a location the gate can never see, which is the opposite of what a carve-out should do. `test_carve_out_is_exact_path_not_basename` pins the narrowness from the other side: a nested file that merely shares the basename gets no special treatment.

Trusted consumers are unaffected: `setup.py`, `google_api.py`, and `gws_bridge.py` read/write the token via direct file IO in their own processes, which never routes through the model-facing guard.

## Related Issue

Discussed in the #38953 review thread; part of the four-list drift documented in #89064.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] 🔒 Security fix
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/file_safety.py`: added `google_token.json` and `google_oauth_pending.json` to `credential_file_names` in `get_read_block_error()`; updated the docstring enumeration (which was also missing the already-blocked `cache/bws_cache.json`).
- `tools/credential_files.py`: new `_MOUNTABLE_SERVICE_TOKENS` frozenset and `_is_mountable_service_token()` helper (path-resolved exact match, so `./google_token.json` spellings neither dodge nor widen the carve-out); the refusal in `register_credential_file()` now exempts carve-out entries. Docstrings updated to state the carve-out explicitly.
- `tests/agent/test_file_safety_credentials.py`: parametrized read-deny tests for both filenames under the active `HERMES_HOME` and at `<root>/` + `<profile>/` while a profile is active; plus a negative case pinning that `google_token.json` *outside* HERMES_HOME stays readable (per-location gate, not per-basename).
- `tests/tools/test_credential_files.py`: `test_per_service_token_still_mounts` docstring now marks it as the carve-out regression test; new `test_pending_oauth_state_is_refused` (no carve-out for the pending file) and `test_carve_out_is_exact_path_not_basename`.

## How to Test

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest tests/agent/test_file_safety.py tests/agent/test_file_safety_credentials.py tests/agent/test_file_safety_cross_profile.py tests/tools/test_credential_files.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_credential_files.py tests/tools/test_write_deny.py -q
```

Without the `agent/file_safety.py` change, the 4 new read-deny cases and `test_pending_oauth_state_is_refused` fail; without the carve-out, `test_per_service_token_still_mounts` and the google-workspace skill mount tests fail. All pass with both.

prs.title: fix(file-safety): deny writes to Google Workspace and Bitwarden credential stores
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`get_read_block_error()` blocks *reads* of `<hermes>/auth/google_oauth.json` (Google Workspace OAuth token store) and `<hermes>/cache/bws_cache.json` (Bitwarden Secrets Manager plaintext disk cache), but `build_write_denied_paths()` only covers the *encrypted* cache variant (`cache/bws_cache.enc.json`), so neither read-blocked path was write-denied.

The plaintext Bitwarden cache is still live alongside the encrypted one (`agent/secret_sources/bitwarden.py`, `_DISK_CACHE`), so both files remained overwritable by `write_file`. A prompt-injected write can plant attacker-controlled OAuth refresh tokens or seed cached secret *values* that the next process reads back as if they came from BSM.

Per review (thanks @egilewski), the fix also covers the **live** Google Workspace stores at the `HERMES_HOME` root, which the original patch missed: `google_token.json` (written by the skill's `setup.py`, rewritten on refresh by `google_api.py`, consumed by `gws_bridge.py`) and `google_oauth_pending.json` (in-flight exchange state). Trusted setup/refresh writes are direct file IO inside the skill's own scripts and never route through the model-facing guard, so they keep working unchanged.

All paths are added to the exact-path write denylist under **both** the active profile's `HERMES_HOME` and the global Hermes root, the same widening already applied to `.env` and `.anthropic_oauth.json` (#15981), since every profile inherits root credentials.

Note: `gateway/platforms/base.py` (`_ROOT_CREDENTIAL_FILES`) and `hermes_cli/web_server.py` (`_SENSITIVE_MANAGED_FILE_BASENAMES`) already list all four filenames; `agent/file_safety.py`'s write denylist was the only one of the three lagging behind.

## Related Issue

None. Discovered by diffing the read-deny and write-deny lists in `agent/file_safety.py`; live-token coverage added per review.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] 🔒 Security fix
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/file_safety.py`: added `auth/google_oauth.json`, `cache/bws_cache.json`, `google_token.json`, and `google_oauth_pending.json`, each under both `hermes_home` and `hermes_root`, to the exact-path set returned by `build_write_denied_paths()`.
- `tests/tools/test_write_deny.py`: two parametrized tests over all four filenames, one for the active `HERMES_HOME` and one for `<root>/` while a profile is active (which also asserts the profile view stays denied). Both use `tmp_path` + `monkeypatch`, mirroring the existing `test_hermes_root_env_when_running_under_profile`.

The diff is purely additive: `+94 / -0`, two files, no reformatting of surrounding code. An earlier revision of this branch carried incidental `ruff format` churn in `agent/file_safety.py` and `tests/tools/test_write_deny.py`; that has been stripped, since `main` is not `ruff format`-clean on those files and the churn was unrelated to the fix.

Deliberately out of scope, both now tracked: the model-facing *read* guard for the same live token files is #89072, and folding the four hand-maintained credential lists (`file_safety.py` read + write, `_ROOT_CREDENTIAL_FILES`, `_SENSITIVE_MANAGED_FILE_BASENAMES`) into one shared constant is #89064. #89072 applies cleanly on top of this branch — they touch different functions of the same module.

## How to Test

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest tests/tools/test_write_deny.py tests/tools/test_credential_files.py tests/agent/test_file_safety.py tests/agent/test_file_safety_credentials.py tests/agent/test_file_safety_cross_profile.py -q
```

The eight parametrized write-deny cases fail before the `file_safety.py` change and pass after it. On the current rebase this is **97 passed**.

prs.title: fix(security): block google_token.json, google_oauth_pending.json, and pairing/ in read_file guard
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Aligns the `read_file` credential read-guard with the credential set the gateway media-delivery denylist already enforces.

`gateway/platforms/base.py::_media_delivery_denied_paths` classifies `google_token.json`, `google_oauth_pending.json`, and the DM-pairing tree as credential material, and its own comment states it *"mirrors the canonical read guard in agent/file_safety.py … so the delivery (read/exfil) side can't trail the write side."* But `agent/file_safety.py::get_read_block_error()` had drifted behind it — it blocked `auth.json`, `.env`, `auth/google_oauth.json`, `webhook_subscriptions.json`, `cache/bws_cache.json`, and `mcp-tokens/`, yet not those three. The write deny guard (`is_write_denied`) likewise already blocks the pairing tree.

Net effect of the gap: a prompt-injection (or a misdirected agent) reaching `read_file` could pull Google OAuth access/refresh tokens or DM-pairing approval state into the transcript, even though the exact same paths are denied on the write and media-delivery sides.

This restores the documented read↔write↔media "mirror" invariant. It is **defense-in-depth, not a security boundary** — the terminal tool runs as the same OS user and can still read these files; the guard returns a clear denial to tool-respecting models and leaves an audit trail. Same posture and wording as the existing `mcp-tokens/` block. `config.yaml` is intentionally left readable (covered by an existing test). The fix lives in the shared guard, so it also covers the ACP shim (`agent/copilot_acp_client.py`), which calls the same function.

## Related Issue

N/A — no existing tracking issue; internal credential-guard consistency hardening.

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [x] 🔒 Security fix

## Changes Made

- `agent/file_safety.py` — in `get_read_block_error()`:
  - Add `google_token.json` and `google_oauth_pending.json` as exact-file matches under HERMES_HOME and the global Hermes root (profile-aware, same as the existing entries).
  - Add the DM-pairing tree as a directory-prefix block, covering **both** the legacy `<home>/pairing` and the consolidated `<home>/platforms/pairing` layouts (`gateway/pairing.py` resolves the live dir via `get_hermes_dir("platforms/pairing", "pairing")`, so new installs use `platforms/pairing`).
  - Update the function docstring's credential list.
- `tests/agent/test_file_safety_credentials.py` — 9 new regression tests.

## How to Test

Run the credential read-guard suite:

    pytest tests/agent/test_file_safety_credentials.py -q
    # 28 passed, 1 skipped   (the skip is an environment-gated symlink test)

New cases added (all pass):
- `test_google_token_json_blocked`, `test_google_oauth_pending_json_blocked`
- `test_pairing_legacy_file_blocked`, `test_pairing_platforms_file_blocked`, `test_pairing_dir_itself_blocked`
- `test_non_pairing_dir_not_blocked`, `test_google_and_pairing_outside_home_not_blocked` (per-location gating, same principle as `auth.json`/`mcp-tokens`)
- `test_profile_mode_blocks_root_google_and_pairing` (profile + root widening)
- `test_read_file_tool_blocks_google_token` — drives the real `read_file_tool` against a HERMES_HOME `google_token.json` containing token markers and asserts the error is returned and **no token material leaks** into the result.

Sibling guard suite unaffected:

    pytest tests/agent/test_file_safety.py -q   # passes

Regression-safety: I baselined the affected test modules on this branch against pristine `main`. This branch adds exactly the 9 new tests above and introduces **zero new failures** — the failure/skip set is identical to `main` (the remaining failures are pre-existing and live in modules this PR does not touch, e.g. symlink-gated and OS-pseudo-path tests).
