prs.title: Add hive.yaml plugin configuration file
prs.body:
Adds **Hive** to the plugin catalog: <https://github.com/MFaiqKhan/hermes-hive> @ `665b3f06cf9c7e3139079b9929f59b04a101691e` (0.1.0).

## In plain words

Your agent hits an error and spends ten commands figuring out the fix. Next week it hits the same error and spends ten commands again: it does not remember. And every other Hermes user's agent does the same work, alone.

Hive is a memory for fixes. When your agent fixes an error, Hive notes "this error → this command fixed it", using the exit codes as proof. The next time that error appears, Hive puts the fix right under the error so the agent can use it at once. If you turn sharing on, the fix (with nothing personal in it) is published to Nostr, and another person's Hermes that hits the same error, on a different computer anywhere, sees it on its first failure, labelled as unverified text from anonymous peers. Hive only suggests; it never runs anything.

## What it does

Agents re-debug the same errors. Hive remembers which command fixed which error on this machine and, when that error comes back in any later session, adds the fix under the failed command's output:

```
datactl: error: cache index is corrupt or missing (code 17)
── Hive: this error has been fixed before ──
• On this machine (worked 2 times, last 2026-11-12):
    datactl sync --rebuild-index
Hive only suggests; nothing was run. Check it fits before running.
```

Fixes are learned from exit codes, not from a model: a command fails, something changes, and the same command (or a close variant) then succeeds. Look-around commands (`ls`, `cat`, `--help` …) and plain retries never count; failures hidden behind `| tee` / `| head` and `&&` chains are handled.

Opt-in, installs share verified fixes over **Nostr** (signed with a random per-install key, NIP-13 proof of work, no server of ours). Another install that hits the same error sees it labelled "Unverified text from N anonymous Nostr peers; check it before running anything" (no "suggested next step": that imperative wording is kept for fixes learned on the same machine). When the fix works there too, that install vouches for it, and when it does not, it says so.

```bash
hermes hive learn             # learn from past sessions (state.db read-only) + share of failures already fixed before
hermes hive list | show SIG   # learned fixes
hermes hive network off|read|share     # off by default
hermes hive outbox            # exactly what is or would be published
hermes hive sync              # publish / fetch now
/hive                         # status in chat
```

## Safety

Hive never runs anything; hints are text. A fix is never kept or shown if it pipes a download into a shell, runs encoded code, deletes whole trees, writes to disks, `/etc` or `~/.ssh`, opens a remote shell, force-pushes or turns off TLS checks. Votes from random keys cost nothing to fake, so they never vouch for a shape: a fix from another install is shown only when **every step has one of two allowlisted shapes**, however many installs report it: (1) a known installer installing packages named in the error, as whole words (`colorama` does not justify `color`), never from a URL, file or non-default index; (2) the exact command that failed on this machine, token for token, with plain flags added at the end (`npm install` → `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`), so a peer never chooses the program, the subcommand or an argument. A plain flag is a switch or a long switch with a number; values that could name a package, file, host or URL are refused, and so are switches that turn off TLS, signature, sandbox or permission checks. Shape 2 is never used for interpreters, shells, package runners or programs whose flags alone can run code, reach another machine or destroy files (`find`, `tar`, `ssh`, `rsync`, `awk`, `sed`, `docker`, `rm` …), never for fetch-and-run subcommands (`exec`, `x`, `dlx`, `create`, `init`, `run`, `start`, `test`, `download`, `wheel` …), and for package managers and build tools only for dependency-maintenance subcommands (`install`, `ci`, `update`, `cache` …). Everything else is refused (another program or subcommand, `npm exec x`, `go run m@latest`, `npx`, `uvx`, `python -c`, `bash ./x.sh`, paths, variables, `sudo`, any shell syntax). It also needs 2+ independent installs, more yes than no, valid signatures, NIP-13 proof of work and content that matches its own hashes. Fixes outside the allowlist are not published at all. The shared error line goes through the same secret screen as the fix steps. Tested: 14 fake votes from 14 keys for `npx …` / `bash ./…`, two fake peers offering `npm exec <pkg>` / `go run <mod>@latest` after an npm / go failure, a table of fetch-and-run commands for 23 package managers and build tools, and poisoned `pip install` / `curl … | sh` from three fake installs, are all refused.

## Hermes surfaces used

- Hook `transform_terminal_output` (declared in `provides_hooks`): reads command, output and exit code; appends a hint on a known failure.
- `ctx.register_cli_command` (`hermes hive`), `ctx.register_command` (`/hive`), `plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_data_dir`.
- No private core imports: Hermes's own secret patterns are used as a last check before anything is shared, through the published plugin API (`agent.redact:redact_sensitive_text`, guarded).
- No tools or middleware; no core overrides; no Python dependencies (pure-Python BIP-340 signatures; `websockets` comes with Hermes).

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Reads:** terminal command text, exit codes and output (through the hook); `state.db` read-only on `hermes hive learn`.
- **Writes:** its own SQLite store and a random install key under `plugin-data/hive`.
- **Network:** none by default. `network read`: error fingerprints (hashes) are sent to the configured Nostr relays (default nos.lol, relay.primal.net, relay.damus.io) to look up fixes. `network share`: also the normalized error line and fix commands. Home paths become `~`; fixes whose steps **or error line** mention private paths, non-public hosts, IPs, user names, e-mails or secret-looking text (API key prefixes, JWTs, long tokens) stay private and are never published. Thresholds are plugin settings (`hermes hive settings --min-peers N --min-pow N`), not environment variables. `hermes hive outbox` previews it.
- **LLM use, credentials, telemetry, background processes:** none (a background thread syncs with relays only when network is on).

## Testing

**Live demo (Hive installed from this repo at the pinned SHA, Hermes v0.23.1, free local model qwen3.5:4b, two separate Hermes homes, local Nostr relay):** machine A hit a `datactl` error whose message does not say how to fix it, fixed it once, and Hive learned `datactl sync --rebuild-index` and published it. Machine B, which had never seen the error, got it on its first failure, labelled as unverified text:

```
datactl: error: cache index is corrupt or missing (code 17)

── Hive: this error has been fixed before ──
• Unverified text from 1 anonymous Nostr peer; check it before running anything:
    datactl sync --rebuild-index
(Hive only suggests; nothing was run. Details: hermes hive show f8bb8a6494)
```

With this label, in 6 repeat runs on the final code B saw the text 6 times and finished the sync 6 times (the shown fix was its very next command in 5). On a machine's own learned fixes the "Suggested next step" line is unchanged.


On Hermes **v0.23.1** (installed from this repo with `hermes plugins install … --ref <sha>`):

- `hermes plugins validate`: passed, security scan safe, no warnings. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` on this entry: valid.
- `tests/test_hive.py`: 41 offline tests, incl. the review cases (fake votes for unsafe shapes, package managers that fetch and run code, the failed command plus plain flags only, code-running arguments, whole-word package names, secrets in the error line, settings in the plugin store, an install's own report never counted as a peer), three installs trading a fix over a local mock relay, the poisoning cases above, and the exact command sequences a live model produced (failures hidden by `| tee` / `; echo`, `fix && retry` in one command, tools called through a path, `$(which …)` or a variable).
- Live,  local model, two throwaway homes and a local relay: with the labelled network text the agent finished in 2 to 3 commands in 5 of 6 runs (see above). An earlier no-hint baseline (5–10 commands, gave up once in four runs) was measured with the previous demo tool, whose fix was a separate subcommand, and has not been re-measured with the current one.
- `hermes hive learn` on a home's own past sessions: 80% of its failures were errors it had already fixed before.
- Hook cost: under 0.1 ms per terminal command; no network on the hot path.
- Not tested yet: publishing to the public relays from this machine (verified signing against 10 real network events; publishing was tested on a local relay).

prs.title: fix(cron): dashboard edits keep a zero-tool toolset allowlist
prs.body:
Hardening (§3.2), not a boundary fix.

**Problem:** the dashboard cron editor PUTs the whole form; an empty toolset picker sends `enabled_toolsets: null`. `_cron_string_list` collapsed `[]`/None to None, so a prompt-only edit turned a stored `[]` (zero-tool allowlist, #82010) into "default toolsets". Create had the same `[]` → None collapse.

**Fix:** `_cron_string_list(keep_empty=)`; `enabled_toolsets` keeps `[]` on create/update; an incoming null is dropped when the stored value is `[]` (the picker cannot render `[]`); a non-empty allowlist stays clearable. Non-list shapes for `enabled_toolsets`/`context_from` on the free-form update dict return 400 instead of silently clearing.

prs.title: fix(tools): the unwrapped tool_call target keeps its own hooks and middleware
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening, not a new boundary.

**Problem.** `handle_function_call` unwraps the Tool Search `tool_call` bridge so downstream hooks see the real tool name. But the single-tool re-dispatch forwarded the caller's `skip_pre_tool_call_hook` / `skip_tool_request_middleware` / `skip_tool_execution_middleware`. The agent loop passes `skip_pre_tool_call_hook=True` after policing whatever name parsing produced. When the parse-time peel falls back to the wrapper name (resolve error or a swallowed exception), the real tool ran with no `pre_tool_call` hook and no request/execution middleware. A plugin guardrail keyed on the real tool name could not veto it.

**Fix.** Re-dispatch with all three flags `False`, the rule `dispatch_connector_batch` already applies per entry. The wrapper's hooks fire once for `tool_call`, and the inner tool gets its own single pass. The normal path (peeled at parse time) is unchanged.

**Tests.** `tests/tools/test_tool_call_bridge_hook_scope.py`: the hook sees the inner name, a veto blocks execution, and middleware sees and rewrites the inner call. All 3 fail on main and pass with the fix. Neighbouring tool-search/connector/guardrail suites are green.

**Credits.** Salvaged from @kouyichi's fork commit (authorship kept).

Fixes #147330

**Known limits:** on the fallback path (agent loop couldn't unwrap up front), plugins see `pre_tool_call` for both `tool_call` and the real tool, while `post_tool_call` fires only under `tool_call` — a plugin pairing events by name sees one unmatched pre (pre-existing shape, same as connector batches).

§3.2 hardening (file-tool guards are defense-in-depth, not a boundary).

**Problem:** the file-tool read deny-list covers `auth/google_oauth.json` but not the bundled google-workspace skill's live stores at the HERMES_HOME root: `google_token.json`, `google_client_secret.json`, `google_oauth_pending.json`. Agents read the refresh token during routine calendar requests (#149056); none of the three were write-denied either.

**Fix:**
- Salvaged #89072 (@exdsgift): read-deny token + pending state, and an exact-path `_MOUNTABLE_SERVICE_TOKENS` carve-out in `tools/credential_files.py` — the sandbox mount gate reuses the read deny-list, so without it the skill would lose its token in Docker/Modal.
- Follow-up: one `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CREDENTIAL_FILES` tuple feeds both read- and write-deny (active profile, sibling profiles, root); client secret added to the carve-out and to the gateway media-delivery and dashboard Files denylists.

Not done: denying every skill-declared `required_credential_files` generically (skill-controlled, open-ended); skill UX polish from the issue.

**Tests:** read/write deny on profile, root and sibling copies; declared files still mount, pending state does not; media delivery and Files API refuse the client secret. Red on main (13 failures), green with the fix.

Fixes #149056
Supersedes #89072, #52644, #38953

**Known limits:** the guard is path-based, so a hardlink to a Google Workspace file elsewhere is not read-denied (true of every credential store); `terminal cat` is out of scope by design; `session_search` can surface a token printed into an earlier transcript. The write-protected table in `website/docs/user-guide/security.md` doesn't list the three files yet (follow-up).

prs.body:
§3.2 hardening, not a new boundary.

**Problem:** `backup_config` uses `shutil.copy2`, which copies the source mode. A `config.yaml` left at 0644 therefore produces a 0644 backup in `backups/config/`, and that backup stays readable after the live file is re-secured. Legacy `config.yaml.bak.*` siblings swept into that directory also keep their old mode.

**Fix:** apply the existing `_secure_file` policy (0600; skipped when managed or in a container, same as `config.yaml`) to new backups and to swept legacy copies.

**Tests:** two behaviour tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_backups.py`, both red on main.

**Credits:** first commit cherry-picked from #148327 by @satvik8954. The legacy-sweep follow-up is mine.

## Summary of Changes
The bug was that configuration backups were created using `shutil.copy2`, which preserves the source file's permissions. prs.title: fix(pm): drop the revision from first-build PortableGit asset names
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`Git.fetch_url` always spliced `.{build}` into the PortableGit asset filename, but Git for Windows publishes the **first** build of a tag without the revision: `v2.56.0.windows.1` ships `PortableGit-2.56.0-64-bit.7z.exe`, not `PortableGit-2.56.0.1-64-bit.7z.exe` (while `v2.55.0.windows.5` does ship `PortableGit-2.55.0.5-64-bit.7z.exe`). Since the current pin template predates the last `.windows.1` release, every `hermes pm update git` / `hermes pm install git` against a `.windows.1` release ends in HTTP 404 during the pin phase. The fix omits the revision from the filename only when `build == 1`; the release **directory** keeps `.windows.{build}` in all cases.

The naming rule was verified against the actual releases:

- `v2.56.0.windows.1` → `PortableGit-2.56.0-64-bit.7z.exe`, `PortableGit-2.56.0-arm64.7z.exe`
- `v2.55.0.windows.1` → `PortableGit-2.55.0-64-bit.7z.exe`, `PortableGit-2.55.0-arm64.7z.exe`
- `v2.55.0.windows.5` → `PortableGit-2.55.0.5-64-bit.7z.exe`, `PortableGit-2.55.0.5-arm64.7z.exe`

## Related Issue

Fixes #127044

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pm/packages.py` — `Git.fetch_url`: build the artifact filename revision ("" when `build == 1`, ".{build}" otherwise) instead of always splicing `.{build}`; the directory component stays `v{tag}.windows.{build}`.
- `tests/pm/test_pm_core.py` — added `test_git_package_url_omits_first_build_revision` pinning the first-build (x64 + arm64) and later-build URL shapes.

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/pm/test_pm_core.py::test_git_package_url_omits_first_build_revision -q` — Observed result: `1 passed`.
2. Cross-check the constructed URLs resolve: the first-build URL now matches the asset names published under the `v2.56.0.windows.1` release (sha256 `ececb5e06…` for the x64 asset, per `gh api repos/git-for-windows/git/releases/latest`).
3. Full local run: `python -m pytest tests/pm/test_pm_core.py tests/pm/test_pm_bionic.py tests/pm/test_store_extract.py -q` — Observed result: 51 passed, 1 skipped, 1 pre-existing failure (`test_registered_bionic_stage_preserves_host_facts[python-None-True]`, a codesign cross-target staging failure that reproduces identically on unmodified `upstream/main` @ `b30bbe2f53`, unrelated to this change).

prs.title: fix(approval): make the reviewed artefact match what runs (#117815)
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening, not a boundary (SECURITY.md §2.2/§3.2).

- **Smart review**: salvages #117827 (@shoyann, @lolchocotaco). `#` is stripped only at an unquoted word start, quote state carries across lines, and heredoc/expansion-bearing input is kept verbatim, so `echo a#; <tail>` reaches the guardian whole.
- **Coalescing**: concurrent gateway approvals key on a sha256 of the executed command instead of the redacted display text.
- **approvals.deny**: also matches a shell quote-removed projection, so `git "status"` meets `git status`.
- **config.yaml block**: on host-local writes also compares file identity (`os.path.samefile`), so case variants on case-insensitive filesystems and hard links are refused. Hosted/SSH/container writes keep the string comparison only (their paths name backend files; the hosted no-host-touch contract forbids stat'ing them here).

The #121759 detection-lexer part of #117827 is left to #121761.

Tests: each new test is red on base and green with the change.

**Known limits:**
- A glob in the agent's command that expands to a denied path (`rm -rf /importan?` vs a `rm -rf /important*` rule) is still not caught; deferred.
- ANSI-C quoting (`git $'status'`) doesn't match a `git status` deny rule.
- Smart review passes a command through unchanged (comment included) whenever any shell marker appears, even quoted — fail-safe direction.
- The `samefile` config guard only helps when `config.yaml` already exists; on a fresh profile, a case variant on a case-insensitive FS can still create it.

Rebased onto main after #155241 (config hard-block keeps both `deny_key` and `samefile`). Re-run `tests/tools/test_approval_deny_rules.py` after #155258 lands.

Fixes #117815

prs.title: fix: honor title previews for attachment-only first turns
prs.body:
Fixes #155525

Part of the end-to-end Hermex large-paste title work tracked in [uzairansaruzi/hermex#1701](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1701).

## Root cause

The gateway accepts and persists `title_preview`, and turn context forwards it to title generation. However, `maybe_auto_title()` and `apply_instant_title()` checked `is_titleable_user_message(user_message)` without the preview. The attachment-only opener guard therefore returned before either title path could use the preview.

## Changes

- Let a non-empty explicit `title_preview` satisfy the topic-eligibility check for attachment-only first turns.
- Pass the preview through both instant-title and model-title eligibility gates.
- Count persisted preview metadata as a real user turn for historical/reconnect logic.
- Keep manual attachment-only turns without a preview excluded; machine-authored openers and existing title-source protections remain unchanged.
- Keep the preview out of the user message and main-model input.

## Tests run

On current `main` plus this patch:

- Title-generation/input/turn-context suite — **185 passed**.
- Gateway display-admission/submission-identity suite — **5 passed**.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

The Hermex client-side XCTest suite remains unrun here because this Linux host has no Xcode, Swift, or iOS simulator; its separate draft PR awaits macOS CI approval.

## Scope

This server change is metadata-only. It does not change attachment bytes, prompt text, main-model input, title-model assignment, or user-assigned titles. The iOS-facing behavior requires the separate Hermex client release as well as a Hermes Agent release containing this fix.

prs.title: fix(config): refuse to persist redacted credential masks
prs.body:
**Problem.** The agent only sees credentials as redactor / `mask_secret` output (`sk-pro...WXYZ`, `***`, `«redacted:…»`). When it "repairs" its own config via `hermes config set`, `save_config` or a `.env` writer, that mask is stored as the credential and the next model call 401s (#42727).

**Fix.** New sibling `hermes_cli/config_credential_values.py` recognises Hermes's own mask shapes. `save_env_value` refuses a mask for credential-named keys (`_is_secret_config_key` or `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS` `password: True`, e.g. `FAL_KEY`). The shared document writer `_write_config_state` (behind `save_config`, `atomic_config_replace/write`, `config set`) refuses a mask *newly* set on a credential leaf, nested dicts/lists included; a mask already on disk at the same location doesn't block unrelated saves (list entries are located by `name`/`id`/`key`, so `custom_providers` deletes/reorders are fine, while a stale mask never exempts a new one at another path). Context the redactor keeps (`Bearer ***`, `123456789:***`, `xoxb-***`) is stripped before matching. `${VAR}` references and empty values pass. Refusals are `ConfigValueError` (CLI exits 1, dashboard returns 400). `_check_non_ascii_credential` moves to the sibling to keep `config.py` under its line cap.

**Why here.** Three chokepoints cover every in-process writer without touching each caller: `save_env_value`, the document writer `_write_config_state` (config set, dashboard PUT /api/config, TUI `_save_cfg`, provider credential lifecycle, setup wizards) and the keyed writer `write_config_key(s)`/`write_changes` (TUI `config.set`, `cli.save_config_value`, gateway toggles, remote model switch). This is §3.2 hardening at the edge of output redaction, not a new boundary; agent shell/Python edits of the files stay out of scope (#28024), as do the credential-pool/`auth.json` writers.

**Tests.** `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_redacted_credentials.py` runs real writers against a temp `HERMES_HOME`, with masks derived by running `redact_sensitive_text` (both modes) and `mask_secret` over sample credentials; red on main, green here.

Based on #70454 by @asdlem (Co-authored-by).

Fixes #42727

**Not covered:** the credential pool / `auth.json` writers (`hermes auth add --api-key`, dashboard pool add), and the agent editing the files directly via shell or Python (separate request #28024).

**Known residuals:** list entries with no `name`/`id`/`key` (mainly `fallback_model` chains) share one location, so a stale mask on one entry still exempts the same mask on a sibling. Renaming an entry into a slot that already holds a dead mask inherits that exemption; this needs a deliberate rename plus delete, not the write-back scenario. For password-named credentials (`*password`/`*passwd`/`*passphrase`, e.g. `SUDO_PASSWORD`) ellipsis/star shapes such as `Hello...2026` or `****` are saved; they are refused only when they equal a mask of the password stored there now. Provider keys keep the full shape refusal.

Rebuilt from #70454 by @asdlem (co-author).

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- A password leaf stored as a `${VAR}` reference is not compared against masks of the referenced value, so writing such a mask replaces the reference. Provider keys are unaffected (full shape refusal).
- `save_env_value` looks up the stored value case-sensitively: a lower-case `sudo_password` mask writes a separate line and leaves `SUDO_PASSWORD` intact.

prs.title: fix(gateway): timing-safe inbound secret compares, replay windows, uniform webhook 404
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening (no new boundary claimed).

**Problem.** Several inbound adapters compared remote-supplied secrets with `==`/`!=` (Meet node RPC token, BlueBubbles webhook password, WeCom msg_signature); WeCom and Feishu verified signatures over a timestamp they never checked; A2A's `compare_digest(str, str)` and the `.encode()` compares raised on non-ASCII / surrogate-escaped header bytes (500 instead of 401). The generic webhook returned 401 for a known route with a bad signature but 404 for an unknown one, enumerating route names. BlueBubbles accepted a whitespace-only password, Twilio SMS replays of a signed POST dispatched twice, and Signal reacted 👀 to senders the gateway later refuses.

**Fix.** `gateway/platforms/_shared.py` gains `secrets_match` (compare_digest on UTF-8 `surrogatepass` bytes, fails closed on missing/unset) and `timestamp_fresh` (the existing 300 s webhook window); every inbound compare uses them, and WeCom/Feishu enforce the window. The Meet node protocol keeps an inline stdlib compare (module is gateway-free). Bad webhook signature → same `404 Unknown route` (docs en/zh updated). BlueBubbles strips the password; SMS dedupes `MessageSid` (24 h, carried across rebuilds); Signal's reaction consults `_is_sender_authorized`.

**Tests.** Per-adapter behaviour tests (good / wrong / hostile-byte secret, stale timestamp, blank password, replayed MessageSid, refused sender) — red on main, green here; existing webhook tests updated for 404.

**Credits.** Salvaged from #127902 (@jonpol01, shared helper commit), #108390 and #136766 (@Adolanium); #108354 (@Adolanium) is covered by the same protocol hunk, registry half already on main (588ec723d4).

Fixes #108353
Fixes #108388
Fixes #127901
**Known limits (predate this change):** route names can still be told apart by the 413 an oversized body gets before the signature check, and by `403 Route disabled: <name>` on a disabled route. Signal still sends its 👀 reaction if the auth check raises (deliberate legacy `is not False`). The SMS replay cache holds 2,000 SIDs, so above that in 24 h the oldest can be replayed.

Fixes #136768

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- Other adapters' pre-auth gates still call `_is_sender_authorized` without `is_bot` (bluebubbles attachments, buzz, feishu, email, teams attachments, telegram injected check/topic transfer, google_chat, simplex, matrix, discord). Whether each one is the same loop-guard gap depends on whether that platform can mark a sender `is_bot` (`bot_users`, or a native flag). Follow-up, not audited here.

prs.title: feat(qqbot): support at_sender in group replies and fix media reply_to fallback
prs.body: ### Summary This PR adds two important improvements for the QQBot platform gateway: 1. **Configurable `@sender` in group messages (`at_sender: true`)**: - QQ group messages now automatically prepend `` to group reply messages when `platforms.qqbot.at_sender` is set to `true` (defaults to `false` to preserve backward compatibility). - Accurately tracks member OpenIDs via both inbound message author parsing and an LRU cache mapping `msg_id -> sender_openid`. 2. **Fix media messages in groups failing as unauthorized passive messages**: - `_send_media()` now falls back to `self._last_msg_id.get(chat_id)` when `reply_to` is omitted, resolving Tencent API `400: 主动消息失败, 无权限` when sending images/media back into group chats. - Added HTTP 400 permission errors to `_PERMANENT_SEND_ERRORS` to prevent wasteful retries. ### Changes - **`gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py`**: - Add `at_sender` option to `QQAdapter`. - Capture sender OpenID from incoming group events. - Prepend `@` tag in group replies when enabled. - Automatically fall back to cached `_last_msg_id` in `_send_media()`. - **`tests/gateway/test_qqbot.py`**: - Add 7 comprehensive unit test cases (`TestQQBotGroupAtSender`) verifying at_sender behavior, DM bypass, LRU tracking, and media reply_to fallbacks. - **Documentation**: - Updated both English (`website/docs/user-guide/messaging/qqbot.md`) and Chinese (`website/i18n/zh-Hans/.../qqbot.md`) documentation with `at_sender` configuration usage. ### Verification - Full pytest test suite passing: `61 passed in 4.65s` (all 54 upstream tests + 7 new tests). - Ruff check: all checks passed with no warnings. - Tested and verified against live QQ Bot in real group chats.

prs.title: fix(desktop): load active Bot Mode roster before fleet discovery
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets Bot Mode show bots from the active connection while other saved gateways are still being discovered. On main, `fetchRosterSnapshot()` waits for the entire route inventory, then reads the active gateway, then waits for the aggregate agent inventory before publishing any rows. A slow unrelated gateway can therefore hold a healthy local roster off screen.

The active route lookup is now connection-scoped and runs alongside fleet discovery. A successful active-gateway response can populate an empty query cache immediately. Fleet results enrich that response when ready. An accessible, translated loading message stays visible while discovery is pending, and the pane waits before declaring an empty roster or no filter matches.

New active rows come from the server response and must match verified ownership on hosts with route discovery. Previously shown remote rows retain the existing retention behavior. Connection and cancellation checks guard reads, metadata reconciliation and publication. Canonical Bot Chat identity remains the server's exact `(profile, "Bot Chat")` registry. No persisted session pointer or presentation snapshot is added.

## Related Issue

No separate issue. Searched current PRs by the symptom and by `fetchRosterSnapshot`, `enumerateRegistryAgentSources` and `profileRoutes` before implementation.

- Closed #96728 addressed a previous roster architecture and explicitly requested a fresh current-main implementation with new proof.
- Open #139777 fixes active gateway attribution during reconnect. This change addresses the discovery waits and does not replace its attribution fix.
- Open #122681 proposes changing offline-row visibility. Existing retention behavior is preserved here.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- Add an optional connection ID to `host.profileRoutes()` through the SDK, preload and Electron bridge. Calls without it retain full-inventory behavior. Unknown connection IDs are rejected.
- Start active-source and fleet discovery together, publish verified active rows first, and keep late or cancelled work from publishing into another connection's view.
- Preserve alias indexes for connections outside the scoped refresh and retain rich canonical-session metadata.
- Add loading feedback in all registered Bot Mode locales and suppress premature empty/filter-no-match output.
- Move the existing source-deadline helper out of the oversized Electron entry point without changing its deadline behavior.

## How to Test

The reproduction uses the real roster query with an unresolved fleet promise and a ready active gateway. Before resolving fleet discovery, assert that the active bot and its canonical-session metadata are already available. Then resolve discovery and verify the combined roster. Other cases cover aliases, connection switches, cancellation, fleet failure and loading presentation.

Verified against main `43faacfb8de7b29548547a7fbdedad0cc6e7391c`:

- Nine focused UI regression cases fail on unchanged main production code.
- Eleven focused UI files pass with 158 tests, including routing, metadata, cached roster and canonical Bot Chat contracts. The two final cancellation/failure cases also pass after the final assertion cleanup.
- Three focused Electron files pass with 28 tests, including scoped connection selection and deadline cleanup. Total: 186 distinct passing tests, zero retries.
- CI follow-up: replaced the mention suite's hand-written query cache with a real TanStack QueryClient so cold discovery receives the production query context. Its 25 tests pass, including the cross-connection cold-mention regression. The four-file mention/roster/routing run passes all 71 tests. Total across focused verification: 211 distinct passing tests, zero retries.
- All 12 blocking `scripts/check` checks pass against that base.
- Full Desktop ESLint scope and renderer, Electron, E2E and builder-config type checks pass with lockfile-matched tools.
- Prettier passes for the other 17 changed files. Whole-file formatting flags `electron/main.ts` and `src/sdk/profile-routing.test.ts` on both base and head. Unrelated formatting churn is excluded.
- `git diff --check` passes.

Rebased onto main at `422ad186185` on 2026-11-13. Six files conflicted. Resolution notes:

- The pane keeps main's `listedCount` (bots plus gateway rooms) and takes this PR's discovery-pending state, so the loading banner and the empty state both account for rooms.
- The five extra locale strings moved into main's per-locale `group-surface-*.ts` files, where roster strings now live under a strict type.
- The local-only path keeps main's `claimDefaultHandles` step and passes this PR's ownership check.
- Both new roster suites are kept: main's unserved-profile suite and this PR's progressive suite.

Rerun on Windows with the pinned pnpm 12.15.0:

- `data.roster.test.tsx` against main's unchanged `data.ts`: **5 failed, 20 passed**. With this change: 25 passed.
- Every test under `src/plugins/hermes-bots`, the two touched Electron test files and `src/sdk`: **1712 passed, 17 skipped** across 167 files. Two more files (`bot-delete.test.ts`, `hidden-bots.test.ts`) time out in their module-load hook and do the same on main without this change.
- Renderer and Electron type checks, ESLint on the changed files and the code-health check against main: passed.
- Not rerun for the rebase: the e2e type check, the full ESLint pass, Prettier, and the other `scripts/check` gates.

The commands below predate main's move to pnpm; the equivalents are `pnpm exec vitest run <files>`.

Focused commands from `apps/desktop`:

```sh
npm run test:ui -- src/plugins/hermes-bots/data.roster.test.tsx src/plugins/hermes-bots/roster-pane-content.test.tsx src/plugins/hermes-bots/routing.test.ts src/sdk/profile-routing.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/data.cached-roster.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/data.bot-meta.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-chat-registry.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-chat-creation.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-chat-adopt-on-conflict.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/bot-row-opens-canonical-chat.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/hide-bot-chats.test.ts --maxWorkers=4 --retry=0
npm run test:desktop:platforms -- electron/plugin-profile-routes.test.ts electron/remote-oauth-ticket.test.ts electron/roster-enumeration-deadline.test.ts --maxWorkers=4 --retry=0
```

Tests ran on native Windows with isolated test state and synthetic transports. This proves publication ordering under a blocked sibling, not a packaged-app startup benchmark. Packaged interactive testing and Linux/macOS execution remain for review and CI.

prs.title: fix(agent): skip project context files that resolve outside the project
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening — not a new security boundary.

**Problem:** the startup context loader (`_read_context_file` and the `.hermes.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` finders in `agent/prompt_builder.py`) followed symlinks with no containment or read deny-list, so a cloned repo's `CLAUDE.md -> <file outside the project>` was injected into the system prompt. Subdirectory hints already applied `_resolved_hint_target` (5aca5406f0).

**Fix:** reuse `_resolved_hint_target` in every finder with the project root (git root, else cwd) and read the vetted resolved target. A root at or above `$HOME` narrows to the file's own directory (also for subdirectory hints with a `/` working dir). A refused file returns `None` and `/context` reports it as `skipped` without stat'ing the target. Docs updated.

**Tests:** parametrized symlink tests for all five file kinds (outside refused + `/context` skipped, inside link and regular file still load) and wide-root narrowing for startup and hints; red on main.

Salvaged from #126040 by @jonpol01 (authorship kept); follow-up adjusts one test for #76902 ($HOME working dir now disables hints).

**Behaviour change:** the nearest `.git` sets the containment root, so a submodule or sibling checkout whose `AGENTS.md` symlinks into the superproject / another checkout is now refused (warning + `skipped` in `/context`).

**Known limits:** a mid-path directory swapped for a symlink between check and read (local racing attacker; same window as the subdirectory-hint loader); hardlinks (git can't ship them).

Fixes #126038

prs.title: ci: pin wheel, pass install-e2e inputs via env, keep skills-index probe output single-line
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening (no current attacker: no caller passes setup-exe-url, and the index is our own docs site).

- `pyproject.toml`: `[build-system].requires` pinned setuptools but floated `wheel`; pin `wheel==0.48.0`.
- `install-e2e-windows-run.yml`: the four `windows-e2e.ps1` steps template-interpolated `inputs.*` (setup-exe-url unquoted) into PowerShell; they now read every input from `env:` / `$env:VAR`, so input text is never parsed as script.
- `scripts/ci/skills_index_probe.py`: stdout is appended to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`; CR/LF in remote `generated_at`, `source` keys or decode-error text could add a forged `status=ok` line. `_one_line()` flattens them.
- `skills-index-freshness.yml`: the "Report status" step template-interpolated the probe's `detail`/`summary` (built from remote values) into its bash `run:`; they now arrive via `env:`, like the issue-opening step.

Tests: `tests/ci/test_skills_index_probe.py::test_remote_newlines_cannot_add_output_lines` (red on base).

Credits: workflow + pin commits salvaged from #108384 by @Adolanium (its inline-Python hunk targeted code since moved to `scripts/ci/skills_index_probe.py`).

Not changed: the `check-catalog-cors` job also writes exception text to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`; it is outside this issue.

**Known limits (outside this issue):** `check-catalog-cors` writes a possibly multi-line `detail=$detail` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` (`skills-index-freshness.yml`); readers use `env:`, so the worst case is a forged output value, not code execution.

Fixes #108382

prs.title: fix(docker): seed auth.json owner-only from the first instant
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening, not a boundary fix.

**Problem:** `docker/stage2-hook.sh` seeds `auth.json` from `HERMES_AUTH_JSON_BOOTSTRAP` with a root-context redirect under the ambient umask, so the file exists as 0644 until `chmod 600` runs. That chmod is unguarded under `set -eu`, so if it fails the boot aborts and the refresh token stays world-readable on host-shared mounts.

**Fix:** create the file inside a `(umask 077 && printf ...)` subshell, so it is 0600 from the moment it exists. The re-tighten chmod now warns and continues.

The first-boot `.env` copy (`seed_one ".env" ".env.example"`, which later receives the generated `API_SERVER_KEY`) had the same window: it ran under the ambient umask and landed 0644 until the best-effort `chmod 600`. It now runs as `(umask 077 && seed_one ...)`.

Adjacent, non-credential: the `HERMES_GATEWAY_BOOTSTRAP_STATE` seed's `chmod 644 gateway_state.json` was unguarded under `set -eu` (same abort shape). It is now best-effort with a warning; the mode is unchanged.

**Tests:** four behaviour tests in `tests/tools/test_stage2_hook_seed_one_symlinks.py` run the real stage2 blocks in `sh` under `set -eu` / `umask 022`:
- `test_auth_seed_creates_credential_owner_only`: the auth.json write alone gives 0600 (chmod stubbed to a no-op).
- `test_auth_seed_survives_failing_chmod`: a failing chmod warns and boot continues, file still 0600.
- `test_env_seed_is_owner_only_under_ambient_umask`: the first-boot `.env` copy is 0600 straight from the seed.
- `test_gateway_state_seed_survives_failing_chmod`: a failing `gateway_state.json` chmod warns and boot continues.

All four fail on main or with their guard removed.

Credits: core fix by @liuhao1024 (#126957, cherry-picked with authorship kept); tests reworked from regex-on-source to behaviour tests.

Fixes #126950

prs.title: fix(approval): only a WHERE in the DELETE's own statement clears the DELETE FROM rule
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening of the approval heuristic (not a security boundary).

**Problem:** `\bDELETE\s+FROM\b(?![^\n]*\bWHERE\b)` cleared on any WHERE later on the line — in a `--`/`/* */`/`#` comment, a quoted literal or identifier, a `$$` body, a later `;` statement, or a later shell command.

**Fix:** bound the lookahead at newline, `; & |`, comment openers, quote openers and dollar-quote openers. Bare `$VAR`/`${VAR}` stay transparent so templated tables still clear. One regex, no SQL lexer; it fails closed (a real WHERE placed after a comment/quoted identifier now prompts).

**Why not #118655's masker:** same coverage for the issue's probes with one bounded regex instead of ~75 lines of position-preserving SQL/shell masking plus a new dispatch path.

**Tests:** `tests/tools/test_approval_sql_delete_where.py`, with the issue's 8 probes plus `$tag$`, `&&` and nested-carrier cases, legit WHERE clauses that must still clear, and an end-to-end cron-deny check. Red on base, green with the fix.

Tests adapted from #118655 by @beardthelion.

**Known limits / false positives:** a bare `WHERE` inside the DELETE's own statement still clears the rule (`DELETE FROM t RETURNING (SELECT 1 WHERE 1)`, `RETURNING [WHERE]`, a CTE `WITH x AS (DELETE ...) SELECT ... WHERE`). Quoted identifiers or a comment before the WHERE (`"users"`, `` `users` ``, `/* c */ WHERE`) now ask for approval — in cron `deny` mode that is a hard block.

Fixes #118654

prs.title: fix(plugins): pin liveness endpoint URL to loopback (salvage #125745)
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening (precondition: an installed, operator-reviewed plugin manifest); not a new boundary.

**Problem:** `liveness.endpoint_path` from an app manifest was appended verbatim to the loopback URL from the vendor's runtime `server.json`, then re-parsed and dialed with that file's bearer token. A path starting with `@host/` rewrites the authority, so the token goes to a manifest-chosen host. The same composed URL + token reaches the MCP transport via `AppResolver.endpoint()`.

**Fix:**
- declaration parse: `endpoint_path` must be a plain rooted path (`[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]`, no `..`); `liveness.path` rooted like `location`; `pid_key`/`url_key`/`token_key` identifier-shaped. Same rules in `tools/mcp_liveness.parse_liveness`.
- resolver: re-parse the composed URL and require http + loopback + same port + no userinfo; `_mcp_initialize` re-checks before sending the token. IPv6 loopback bracketed; runtime pids bounded.
- catalog: unreadable liveness renders `unknown`, not `present`.

Parse-time rejection is defence-in-depth; the dial-site check is what guarantees the token never leaves loopback, even for a directly constructed `AppDef`.

**Tests:** declaration, resolver, liveness and catalog behaviour tests; red on main (39 failures), green with the fix.

Credits: salvaged from #125745 by @beardthelion (authorship kept; rebased onto the multi-location `AppDef`), plus a lint follow-up.

**Compatibility:** third-party manifests whose `endpoint_path` has a query or percent-encoding, or with a relative `liveness.path`, now fail to load (nothing in `plugin-catalog/` or the bundled apps is affected).

Fixes #125744

prs.title: feat(plugins): catalog managed Rapid-MLX runtime
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds the community `rapid-mlx` model-provider plugin to the catalog. It gives Hermes Desktop and CLI a managed Rapid-MLX 1.0.2 runtime, public alias/repository pulls, a profile-scoped model library, authenticated loopback inference, and a generation-validated **Use** action that saves the profile default. Opening the library or provider picker does not install or start a process.

Owner submission from the public repository [raullenchai/hermes-plugin-rapid-mlx](https://github.com/raullenchai/hermes-plugin-rapid-mlx), pinned to commit `0287a4482bc18ae81d6308330ceb40f26b6e5d23` on `main`. Both `sha` and the README `docs_url` use that immutable pin. The plugin uses public provider-profile, model-selection, credential and Desktop SDK APIs.

## Related Issue

No issue is being closed. Follows the standalone managed-runtime approach of merged PR #150815 (`omlx`). Existing Rapid-MLX PRs were searched: #136903 concerns custom-endpoint documentation; #41894's first-class core provider was closed. This proposal adds only a catalog entry.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- Only `plugin-catalog/rapid-mlx.yaml` in hermes-agent, with community tier, macOS platform metadata, matching plugin version `0.1.0` and `>=0.23.0` compatibility floor.
- No declared tools, hooks, middleware or required external credentials.
- Explicit operational disclosure and known limitations in the entry and standalone README.
- Derived from the MIT oMLX plugin at `eb748caf0a3080cd3b8d9426eb995d2722ec3406`, preserving its copyright notices. This integrates a different inference runtime: a complete hash-locked PyPI venv, native Rapid-MLX alias-aware pulls into the shared Hub cache, and single-model lifecycle instead of an oMLX app bundle/private snapshots.

## How to Test

1. From a prepared Hermes checkout, run CI's whole-directory structural check (with `ruamel.yaml==0.18.17`): `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`.
2. Run CI's public-pin admission script with the checkout root as `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, `CHANGED_FILES=plugin-catalog/rapid-mlx.yaml`, and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`: `python3 -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/ci/catalog_validate_pinned_entries.py"`. Put the prepared Hermes dependency venv's `bin` directory on `PATH`, so isolated Python can import installed dependencies and `hermes` resolves to this checkout's PM environment. The script clones the public repository, checks out the exact pin and runs `hermes plugins validate --install-deps`, confinement, self-updater and executable-payload checks.
3. On an Apple Silicon Mac with Python 3.12, install the runtime, pull `qwen3-0.6b-4bit`, choose **Use**, and send a Hermes chat turn using provider `rapid-mlx` and canonical ID `mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit`.
4. Turn off → immediately Turn on → Turn off. Confirm only owned PIDs are stopped. The standalone `scripts/live_smoke.py` automates the backend/provider/CLI flow on a free port in 8480–8489 and cleans up in `finally`.

Final catalog checks on 2026-11-13, macOS 26.5.2 arm64, after `git fetch origin`, against Hermes `422ad1861856dd9b80b947fbad9f39d1580f6b41`:

- **Structural: PASS**, exit 0, **2,311 catalog files valid**. There are 16 existing warnings in other entries and none for `rapid-mlx`.
- **Public-pin admission: PASS**, exit 0. Anonymous HTTPS clone with global/system Git configuration disabled checked out `0287a4482bc18ae81d6308330ceb40f26b6e5d23`. All **16 plugin checks passed**, scanner **safe**, no admission warnings; confinement, no-self-updater and executable-payload gates also passed. Expected isolation verdict: **in-process only** for the live model-provider SDK client.
- Commands and scripts match `.github/workflows/plugin-catalog-ci.yml`; executed locally, not a hosted CI run. Structural Python was 3.9 with the CI-pinned YAML package; admission used the PM-prepared Python 3.14.9 environment on macOS, rather than CI's Ubuntu runner.
- Fresh branch `add-rapid-mlx-plugin` starts at fetched `origin/main`, with only the uncommitted `plugin-catalog/rapid-mlx.yaml` addition. No generated index is required by the catalog README.

Earlier plugin verification on the same Hermes base and exact plugin commit (retained evidence; not rerun during catalog finalization):

- **31 plugin tests passed** through Hermes's canonical test runner and isolated test environment.
- **All 16 plugin admission checks passed** on a clean export of the exact local commit, with dependency preparation, real provider registration, scanner `safe`, no warnings, no core overrides and a valid Desktop SDK surface.
- Real hash-verified private Rapid-MLX 1.0.2 installation; `pip check` and private CLI version check passed.
- Real alias resolution/pull reused 9 cached model files (351.4 MB); no fresh model-weight transfer is claimed.
- Authenticated loopback start and `/v1/models` worked; an unauthenticated request returned 401. Server startup used offline HF/Transformers mode with the model mirror disabled.
- The real **Use** backend validated generation and saved the isolated profile default. Both a guarded provider call and a separate Hermes CLI chat turn completed.
- Immediate stop/restart passed; managed PIDs 72289 and 73127 were stopped, final server state was empty and port 8480 was closed. Port 8477 was not contacted or signalled.
- Ruff, Python compilation, Node syntax and Git whitespace checks passed.

## Operational / Security Disclosure

- **Setup downloads/runs:** uses existing Python 3.12 to create `HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/rapid-mlx/runtime/1.0.2`, then private isolated pip installs Rapid-MLX 1.0.2 and every dependency in the committed SHA-256 lock from PyPI/`files.pythonhosted.org`, with `--require-hashes --only-binary=:all:`. No global install, shell installer, bundled executables, optional extras, plugin self-updater, or MLX packages in Hermes's environment. The base upstream distribution includes native MLX/Metal and vision/audio-related dependencies; this plugin exposes chat only.
- **Model network/storage:** explicit `rapid-mlx pull <alias-or-repo>` uses the official `models.rapidmlx.com` mirror and Hugging Face/CDNs. Alias companion artifacts may be included. Files reuse the standard shared HF cache; **Remove** forgets a library record and never deletes shared weights. Pulls consume disk/bandwidth; loaded models consume unified memory. Progress is indeterminate, with cancellable jobs and native logs.
- **Processes/ownership:** runs a long-lived `rapid-mlx serve` on `127.0.0.1` with a generated bearer key. Verifies PID birth, setup-observed interpreter, exact private CLI path, subcommand, profile and origin; refuses foreign listeners. Homebrew's framework Python may execute its installed framework binary, recorded at setup. A peer cannot stop another live Hermes owner's server. Child environments use a small allowlist and private HOME; inherited secrets/proxies and upstream telemetry are disabled. The local key is present in the upstream server process's argument list.
- **Hermes data/credentials:** reads config and saves explicit model selection only through public APIs. The generated key is saved via Hermes's credential API as `HERMES_RAPID_MLX_LOCAL_API_KEY` in the profile `.env` and read with `get_secret`; no direct credential-store reads and no keys in plugin state/REST responses. **Use** writes the profile default in `config.yaml`; existing chat selections are unchanged.
- **Transport:** loopback origin/ownership guard, no proxy inheritance or redirects, guard retained in SDK copies. Startup failure occurs at request time outside generic-client fallback. Inference startup uses cached models in offline mode; removed cache files require an explicit pull.
- **Limits:** macOS 15+ / Apple Silicon / existing Python 3.12; one served model at a time; in-process provider execution required. No audio/embedding claims. No real Desktop rendering is claimed because Desktop was unavailable locally.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] Read the Contributing Guide and plugin authoring/catalog requirements.
- [x] Prepared Conventional Commit message: `feat(catalog): add Rapid-MLX model provider plugin`; derivative-license attribution preserved. No catalog commit created during finalization.
- [x] Searched existing PRs and catalog/provider listings for duplicates.
- [x] The proposed core diff contains only this catalog YAML.
- [x] Focused plugin tests passed using the canonical `scripts/run_tests.sh` runner.
- [ ] Full `just test` — not run for a one-entry catalog proposal; 31 focused tests and native checks above.
- [ ] Full `just check` — not run; plugin lint/syntax, admission and catalog structural checks above.
- [x] Added runtime, transport, ownership, cancellation, profile and API persistence tests.
- [x] Tested on macOS 26.5.2 arm64 with isolated storage and real inference.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Standalone README documents setup, Desktop/CLI usage, disclosure, storage, dependencies and limits.
- [x] No core config/tool schema/architecture changes; associated housekeeping is N/A.
- [x] Platform requirements and in-process isolation limit are disclosed.

## Screenshots / Logs

Hermes Desktop was not runnable: `hermes desktop --skip-build --source` reported no `apps/desktop/dist`; no installed Hermes app or Desktop dependency tree existed. CLI evidence is provided instead:

```text
Loaded provider: rapid-mlx
/download complete mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit
Started verified PID 72289 at http://127.0.0.1:8480/v1
Unauthenticated /v1/models refused: 401
/activate complete {'model_id': 'mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit', 'scope': 'profile-default', 'live_chat_changed': False}
Use persisted profile selection: rapid-mlx mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit
☤ Hermes
Hello! I'm Hermes Agent. What can I help you with?
Turn off completed; restarting immediately
/start complete None
Restarted verified PID: 73127
Stopped managed PID: 73127 state: {}
Test port is closed
```

Earlier reproducible plugin evidence is in the pinned repository's [verification notes](https://github.com/raullenchai/hermes-plugin-rapid-mlx/blob/0287a4482bc18ae81d6308330ceb40f26b6e5d23/docs/verification.md), [CLI transcript](https://github.com/raullenchai/hermes-plugin-rapid-mlx/blob/0287a4482bc18ae81d6308330ceb40f26b6e5d23/docs/cli-transcript.txt), and [admission report](https://github.com/raullenchai/hermes-plugin-rapid-mlx/blob/0287a4482bc18ae81d6308330ceb40f26b6e5d23/docs/admission.json).

Final admission output:

```text
HEAD is now at 0287a44 feat(rapid-mlx): add managed Hermes local runtime plugin
✓ security scan — safe
✓ no core override — no runtime rebinds of Hermes core
✓ desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface
Validation passed.
✅ PASS: plugin-catalog/rapid-mlx.yaml
✅ PASS: all changed catalog entries validated at their pinned shas
```

AI assistance: Claude Code assisted with the original plugin and submission preparation; Codex assisted with final catalog pinning, validation and handoff editing. The submitting human remains responsible for reviewing the pinned code and disclosures.

prs.title: fix(update): importing a module never starts an update; updates leave other checkouts' gateways alone (salvage #131105)
prs.body:
Before: just importing one old-compatibility module started a full `hermes update`, and an update run from a test checkout could rewrite your real gateway service so it pointed at the test checkout, then restart your live gateway. Now the import does nothing unless an old updater is actually running, and an update only rewrites or restarts gateways that run the checkout and home it is updating.

Salvage #131105 by @Kyzcreig (cherry-picked, authorship kept), plus the checkout-scope fix the 2026-11-13 incident needed.

| | origin/main 4b40ffb0ad6d | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `import hermes_cli.psutil_android` (takeover `_run_child` patched to record) | `IMPORT RAISED SystemExit 0 takeover calls: [{'root': None, 'home': None}]` | `IMPORT OK, takeover calls: []` |
| Update from checkout B, HERMES_HOME = scratch under `~/.hermes`, unit + gateway serve checkout A | `↻ Updated gateway user service definition…` (ExecStart now `sys.path.insert(0, '<checkout B>')`), `→ hermes-gateway: update is running inside this gateway's process tree — signalling restart…`, EVENTS `daemon-reload`, `SIGUSR1 self-restart <pid>`, `reset-failed`, `start` | `unit rewritten: False`, `↷ hermes-gateway: systemd unit of another Hermes checkout (/home/…/hermes-agent) — left alone (not restarted)`, EVENTS `none` |
| Control: update from the checkout the unit/gateway run | rewrites the stale unit + restarts | rewrites the stale unit + restarts (same events) |

**Root cause:** the import shim called the takeover at module level, and update ownership was judged by home alone, where a scratch HERMES_HOME nested in `~/.hermes` resolves the account root so the real default home and every profile counted as "this update's", and no step compared the runtime's checkout with the updater's.

**What changed**
- `psutil_android.py` (from #131105): the import-time handoff only runs under a historical updater frame (`in_historical_update()`, the same gate `tools/lazy_deps.py` uses). Sweep of the same class: an AST scan of every module importing `_old_updater` turns up no other module-level `stop_for_relaunch()`. `managed_uv`, `npm_engine`, `old_updater_deps`, `old_updater_main`, `main_web_build`, `update_cmd_maint` and `tools/lazy_deps` all call it inside function bodies only. The frozen old-updater surface is unchanged (`tests/test_old_updater_compat_surface.py` passes).
- `update_cmd_fleet._restart_launchd_gateway_after_update` (from #131105): checks label ownership the way the sibling loop does.
- `update_fleet_scope.update_scope_homes`: a home nested inside an inventoried home owns only itself.
- `update_fleet_scope`: new `gateway_pid_foreign_checkout` (cmdline / VIRTUAL_ENV / status argv) and `definition_foreign_checkout` (ExecStart / ProgramArguments, including the `python -I -c "sys.path.insert(0, '<root>')"` launcher form). A runtime counts as foreign only when none of the checkouts it names is the updater's (`_updater_code_root`), and an unreadable one falls back to the home rule. Called from the launch-file refresh, `_systemd_unit_owned_by_update`, `_scoped_manual_gateway_pids` and `_drain_or_signal_gateway_for_update` (so the ancestor SIGUSR1 branch and the stale-survivor path are covered too). The skipped runtime gets the existing `left alone` notice.
- Review follow-ups: profile-mapped gateways of another checkout are never armed or SIGTERMed by the manual restart pass. One launchd ownership decision (`launchd_label_skip_notice`: foreign home or foreign checkout) covers the invoking-label restart, the sibling loop and the pre-swap pause. Quoted checkout paths with spaces are read whole. A runtime is judged by the source it runs, and a shared interpreter/venv only decides when no source checkout is named.
- Dropped from #131105: the whole-tree import canary (it imports every shipped module, which is exactly how this incident started, and its audit hook does not refuse `os.kill`), and the e2e source-reading AST test.

**Live repro:** the two scripts are `probe_import.py` / `probe_scope.py`, run against a scratch HOME + HERMES_HOME with systemctl, `os.kill`, SIGUSR1 and launcher publication all recorded, and a real stand-in gateway process whose argv names checkout A. Before (origin/main worktree): the unit is rewritten to checkout B and SIGUSR1 goes to the gateway. After: both are refused and EVENTS are `none`. Control (same checkout): rewrite + restart still happen. Read-only check against this host: the live gateway and the real user unit both resolve to `/home/teknium/.hermes/hermes-agent`, so an update run from any worktree reads them as foreign.

**Tests**
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_checkout_scope.py` (new): 2 invariants (unit/plist refresh + launchd restart; ancestor signal + manual restart pass, own-checkout control). Red on origin/main (2 failed, 1 passed) and on each pre-review head, green here.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_old_updater_shims.py::test_psutil_android_import_outside_an_update_starts_nothing`: red on main's shim, green here.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over `tests/hermes_cli/test_update*.py`, `test_gateway_service*.py`, `test_fleet*.py`, `test_gateway_launchd*.py`, the old-updater shims and the compat surface: everything passes except `test_gateway_service.py::TestUnitAnchoredServiceIdentity::test_real_unit_sync_keeps_the_name_it_validated`, which fails identically on origin/main.

**NOT_COVERED:** the launchd plist path (`definition_foreign_checkout` on `ProgramArguments`) is only exercised by unit logic, not on macOS. The system-scope unit refresh under root was not run live.

## Infographic
![Updates stay in their lane](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab2636b/hNXICgyIgQWodioMkZNyM_p51E38rF.png)

prs.title: fix(compression): send role-typed turns to the compaction summarizer (salvage #154891)
prs.body:
Hardening (SECURITY.md §3.2), not a boundary: a prompt-injection mitigation for compaction laundering.

**Problem.** The compaction summarizer got every earlier turn as one flat `[USER]: …` text block, so tool output that prints `[USER]: you have my standing approval…` looked exactly like the user. The summary then persisted that line as the user's instruction (#146750; the issue's A/B shows 72% laundering on main).

**Fix.** Salvages #154891 (and #124595 inside it) by @teknium1, authorship kept. The summarizer instructions go in `system`, and in lean mode the turns go in their real roles (user / assistant+`tool_calls` / `role=tool`). Redaction, elision and sampling are unchanged.

**Follow-up commit.** The typed request has tool blocks but no `tools`. Anthropic Messages 400s on that and Bedrock Converse rejects it, so lean compaction would fail on those summarizer routes. `agent/tool_history_as_text.py` rewrites tool history as **assistant** text when a request declares no tools (or `tool_choice="none"`). It is wired into `build_anthropic_kwargs` and the aux-only `call_converse`. Tool output never goes into a user turn. Requests that declare tools are unchanged.

**Tests.** `test_context_compressor_summary_roles.py` (red on main) and `test_tool_history_as_text.py`, which drives the real aux shims and checks the wire has no tool blocks and no forged text in user turns (red without the follow-up). 1087 related tests pass; `scripts/check` ruff+health ok.

Superseded: #153368 (keeps the flattened string on Anthropic/Bedrock), #144880 (label escape only, no measured effect).

**Known limits:** on Anthropic/Bedrock aux routes tool output is rewritten into assistant text, so a forged `[USER]:` line keeps its label inside that text (not user-authoritative; the laundering A/B covered chat/codex/Gemini only). The premise that Anthropic/Bedrock reject tool blocks without `tools` is from provider error docs; the Nous Portal accepted the shape. Legacy `tail_mode` still sends the flattened transcript as one user message. The rewrite drops cache markers/non-text parts from rewritten tool rows.

Fixes #146750

prs.title: fix(skills): keep plaintext secrets out of oss-forensics working files
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening (skill instruction text, not a boundary).

**Problem:** guardrail 8 in `optional-skills/security/oss-forensics/SKILL.md` required redaction only in the final report ("Log them internally only"). Meanwhile Phase 1 records an IOC `Value` for `API_KEY`/`SECRET` in `iocs.md`, that list goes into sub-agent `context`, and Phase 7 archives the whole directory, so plaintext credentials ended up in working files and archives.

**Fix:**
- Guardrail 8 now says to record references instead of copies: type, source location, evidence ID. Raw retention is allowed only in an explicitly authorized, access-controlled store that stays out of the archive.

prs.title: Sync with upstream/main (1095 commits) + forward-port magicform customizations
prs.body:
## Summary

- Merges ~1095 commits from `sipeed/picoclaw` `upstream/main` (last sync was at `7ea7bb0`).
- Forward-ports our 6 customization commits onto upstream's restructured layout: agent loop split into `agent_*.go`, tools reorganized into `pkg/tools/{fs,integration}/`, channel config moved to a map+Settings model.
- Drops the launcher subsystem (deps deleted upstream, MagicForm doesn't use it).
- Phase 1 of the multi-tenancy port: tenant hints from `bus.InboundContext.Raw` plumb onto `processOptions`. Phase 2 (effSessions/effProvider/effContextBuilder threading) is deferred to a follow-up PR.
- New `MAGICFORM_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md` indexes the fork's customizations by subsystem so future syncs are predictable.

## Commit shape (deliberately one-customization-per-commit for sync friendliness)

```
763e5690 docs: add MAGICFORM_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md sync index
9a0b2817 forward-port: multi-tenancy hint plumbing on agent processOptions (phase 1)
cd1720f4 forward-port: write size cap + crypto/rand temp suffixes in fs sandbox
94d28c1b forward-port: bound search response size with LimitReader
0c8ebde2 forward-port: register magicform channel in gateway init
93fb7b87 Merge upstream/main into sync/upstream-2026-05-07
```

## Notable upstream changes incorporated

- Agent loop split (#2585) — `pkg/agent/loop.go` → 30+ `agent_*.go` files. Multi-tenancy customization moved into a new isolated `agent_tenant.go` to minimise future conflict surface.
- Tool packages reorganized (`4c133dc2`) — `pkg/tools/{filesystem,web}.go` → `pkg/tools/{fs,integration}/`. Hardening re-applied at the new locations.
- Launcher migrated to `web/backend/` (#1275) — old launcher dropped (see below).
- Channel config switched to map+Settings model — `MagicFormConfig` rewritten as `MagicFormSettings` with `SecureString` token, registered alongside other channels in `config_channel.go`.
- `AgentDefaults.Model` deprecated field removed; `SessionConfig.DMScope` replaced by `Dimensions`; `Config.Bindings` replaced by upstream's legacy bindings migration.

## Things that changed in our fork

- **Launcher dropped.** Half its dependencies were deleted upstream (`auth_config.go`, `process.go`, `server_test.go`, etc.), and MagicForm doesn't use the launcher's HTTP API. Upstream's `web/backend/` is the replacement when an admin UI is needed.
- **Multi-tenancy split into phases.** Phase 1 (this PR) validates and plumbs tenant hints onto `processOptions`. Phase 2 (next PR) wires `effSessions`/`effContextBuilder`/`effProvider`/`effModel` through the turn execution path. Phase 1 is a no-op functionally for current MagicForm traffic (which doesn't yet send webhooks) but locks in the protocol so phase 2 is a clean diff against the agent loop only.
- **Workspace overlays using the deprecated `model` JSON key are now silently ignored.** Migrate them to `model_name`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` (excluding matrix, which has a Windows+CGO=0 libolm constraint that's environment-only and pre-existing)
- [x] `go test ./pkg/agent/` — tenant-extraction tests pass (4 happy-path/escape/no-boundary/CSV cases)
- [x] `go test ./pkg/pathutil/` — workspace-boundary resolver tests pass
- [x] `go test ./pkg/tools/integration/` — web tool tests pass
- [x] `go test ./cmd/picoclaw/internal/agent/` — workspace path validation tests pass
- [ ] CI build on Linux (matrix/libolm needs gcc + CGO; should be set up in CI)
- [ ] Manual smoke test of agent CLI: `picoclaw agent "hello" --workspace tenant-a` against a workspace_root config
- [ ] Manual smoke test of magicform webhook (deferred until MagicForm starts sending)

Two pre-existing test failures are environment-specific Windows issues unrelated to this PR (`TestSecurityPath` hardcodes Unix path separators; `TestHostRW_Read_PermissionDenied` uses Unix file modes).

## Out of scope (follow-up PR candidates)

- Phase 2 multi-tenancy: actual session/provider isolation per turn
- Forward-port launcher security hardening to `web/backend/` if/when MagicForm starts using it
- Documentation refresh (`docs/cli.md`, `docs/magicform-integration.md`) for new upstream features

prs.title: fix(channels): resolve a clicked card only after the host accepts the click
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The `channels` side of #4168: text-command answers and the web chat wait for the host too.

- **Problem**: WhatsApp (Baileys), iMessage and the local web chat answered a pending question themselves before the host decided. They closed the question and posted "✅ Approved by <name>" even when the host refused, so the approver could no longer answer.
- **Fix**: they wait for the host's outcome. Accepted: confirmed, question closed. Refused: question stays open, nothing posted (no private reply on these channels; the web chat shows the refusal only to the person who clicked). Closed: "No longer available". Ignored: the question stays open, since it may still be pending. The host decides once, so WhatsApp needs no answer queue. The web chat draws the resolution the server returns, and none for a card the host updates itself; when two tabs answer at once, the losing tab keeps the winner's answer. iMessage hands an answer to the host off its one inbound loop, so a slow answer holds no other chat; answers in one chat reach the host one at a time. An answer queued behind one that closed or replaced its question is dropped.
- **Any core**: on an older core `onAction` returns nothing, which counts as answered as before. The adapters type-check on `v2026.10.0` and `v2026.10.1-rc.2`.
- **Known gaps**: an expired approval answers "ignored", so a WhatsApp or iMessage question stays open after it; fixing that needs a core change. On a core from before #4168, two WhatsApp answers sent at the same instant are both confirmed (the old answer queue stopped that; a current host decides once). A Discord gateway card the host closes with nobody clicking (timed out, expired) keeps its buttons, as on main.

**How to review**: review #4168 first. This PR's own change is the adapter files (`whatsapp.ts`, `imessage.ts`, `local-web.ts`, `local-web-page.js`, +119/-40 lines, plus tests); the core files are byte copies of #4168's, except `chat-sdk-bridge.ts`, which differs only by main's send_card parts (#4292) that `channels` doesn't have yet. Squash on merge.

## Related work

Stacked on #4156 (base `fix/approval-card-length-channels`); merges with #4168, after #4156.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 4,957 passed. 3 git-heavy `scripts/update` tests timed out under load; that file passes 29/29 alone.
- New tests per adapter: a refused answer keeps the question and posts nothing; an accepted one is confirmed once; "ignored" keeps the question open; two WhatsApp answers at once reach the host, and only the accepted one is confirmed; the web chat returns the resolution to draw (none for a gateway card, "No longer available" when closed); an older core's empty return counts as answered; a clicked Discord card loses its buttons through the click, only after its edit has ended, also when Discord refuses that edit; a decided gateway card does too; an iMessage answer holds no other message while the host decides, and answers in one chat reach the host in order; a Discord thread from the raw message to the raw click, through the real adapter and coordinator (chat keyed by the parent, by the thread alone, both announcement cases). The web chat's guard for a second tab is checked by the page's asset test.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` clean. Codex adversarial review on the branch and each fix; real findings fixed. Left: the older-core gap above, and a web chat display race that needs a failed row delete first.

- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
WhatsApp, iMessage and the local web chat confirm an answer only after it is accepted; a refused answer leaves the question open.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Who may decide is unchanged (host checks only). These channels now show only what the host accepted.

prs.title: fix(channels): escape approval card text, and refuse a card a channel can't show
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Card text shows as typed on Slack, Google Chat and Discord. Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud refuse a card they can't show whole, instead of cutting it.

- **Problem**: card text could turn into links or mentions on Slack, Google Chat and Discord. Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud show a card as one message with a length cap, and cut or reject text past it.
- **Fix**: Slack, Google Chat and Discord escape card text (`escapeCardText`); Slack card titles keep link syntax inert. Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud set a fixed `maxCardTextLength` of 2,000, 4,000 and 1,024. Telegram also counts a question card the way it is sent and refuses it over 4,096. A longer card is refused and nothing posts, so a gateway approval fails closed, as today.
- **Limits**: Discord 4,000 keeps an embed under its 4,096. Telegram 2,000: MarkdownV2 escaping at most doubles plain text, and 2,000 is the agent's own question cap. Text that grows more (lists, links, email addresses, tables) is counted as sent. WhatsApp Cloud 1,024 is the platform's cap.
- **Google Chat**: its cards show Markdown as typed, so it drops the backslash a gateway card puts before a Markdown mark for the other channels. Cost: a backslash someone really typed before one of `` \`*_~[]()<>& `` is dropped too, so `a\_b` shows as `a_b`.
- **Scope** (Telegram): the count as sent covers every card with answer buttons, a custom renderer's too, so none is cut with its buttons kept. A card with no answer buttons is sent as before.
- **Any core**: the options go in through spreads, so the adapters still build on a core without them. The Telegram count needs `CardTooLongError`; on a core without it nothing changes.

## Related work

**MERGE HOLD**: lands together with #4147. This branch carries #4147's card text change until the next `main` -> `channels` sync. The Discord button removal on card edits moved to #4171 with the click rework. Out of scope: WhatsApp Cloud's 3 buttons with 20-character labels. No issue: found internally.

## Change kind

<!-- Check exactly one. -->
- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation
