issues.title: [Feature]: Auto-retry once in RetryChatModel when HTTP 200 stream completes with no answer content (empty / thinking-only EOF)
issues.body:
> **AI Disclosure:** This issue was drafted and submitted with AI assistance on behalf of `@djj532` after inspecting QwenPaw `v2.3.0` runtime behavior and source code. All referenced file paths, line behaviors, and observations have been verified directly against the codebase and runtime logs.

## Summary

Add an opt-in (or default 1-time) empty-turn recovery retry in `RetryChatModel` when an upstream model returns HTTP `200 OK` and completes normally without producing any visible answer content or tool calls (either completely empty or thinking-only EOF).

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

In QwenPaw `v2.3.0`, some upstream models and compatible gateways intermittently finish a streaming response with HTTP `200 OK` and a normal EOF (`is_last=True`), while emitting **no `TextBlock` (non-whitespace) and no `ToolCallBlock`** — for example, returning only a reasoning/signature block or `text: ""` with `finish_reason: STOP` (observed repeatedly during long multi-step tool-calling sessions across both Anthropic- and OpenAI-Responses-compatible upstreams).

Inspecting the current retry and stream-progress implementation:

1. **`qwenpaw/providers/retry_chat_model.py` (`_stream_with_retry`, around lines 1117–1124)**:
   ```python
   async for chunk in active_stream:
       emitted = emitted or (
           has_meaningful_stream_content(chunk.content)
       )
       yield chunk
   return  # stream completed without error
   ```
   `emitted` is currently only used to decide whether an **exception** can be safely replayed. When the stream closes cleanly without raising an error (`is_last=True`), it returns unconditionally even when `emitted` remained `False`.

2. **`qwenpaw/providers/stream_progress.py` (`_block_has_meaningful_content`, lines 36–43)**:
   `has_meaningful_stream_content` treats a non-empty `ThinkingBlock` (`bool(block.thinking)`) as meaningful content. As a result, a turn that emits only reasoning/thinking and then terminates with empty answer text and no tool calls is treated as having produced meaningful output.

3. **Relationship to #8521 and open PR #8676**:
   PR #8676 nicely addresses the UI silent-completion bug by adding `has_answer_content()` (excluding thoughts) and raising `RuntimeError("The model returned an empty answer. Please retry or switch models.")` so users know the turn failed.
   However, because #8676 checks this at the `QwenPawAgent._reasoning` boundary and does **not** retry inside `RetryChatModel`, every transient empty-EOF turn still aborts the ongoing ReAct tool loop and forces manual user intervention — even when an immediate single retry succeeds reliably.

## Proposed Solution

1. **Separate "visible answer / tool-call progress" from "thinking-only progress"** (consistent with `has_answer_content` in PR #8676):
   - Keep `has_meaningful_stream_content` for idle-timeout / liveness tracking if needed (so long thinking does not trip TTFT), **or** track a dedicated flag `answer_emitted` (`non-whitespace TextBlock`, `DataBlock`, or `ToolCallBlock`).
2. **Optional single auto-retry in `RetryChatModel` on empty normal EOF** (for both streaming and non-streaming):
   - When a stream finishes cleanly (`is_last=True`, no exception) with `answer_emitted == False` (and non-interrupted, non-`max_tokens` truncation), allow a configurable `empty_response_retries` (e.g., default `1`) before surfacing the final empty state / error to `QwenPawAgent`.
   - **Trade-off on thinking chunks**: Because `RetryChatModel` yields chunks immediately, if `ThinkingBlock` chunks were already streamed to the caller before EOF, replaying could duplicate thinking in the UI unless either:
     - (a) a small bounded pre-answer buffer (e.g., up to N bytes before the first `TextBlock`/`ToolCallBlock`) holds pre-answer chunks until the first answer/tool token arrives or buffer threshold overflows, or
     - (b) auto-retry triggers only when no chunks (`not emitted`) or no UI-visible blocks were yielded yet, while thinking-only turns with already-yielded thoughts fall back to PR #8676's explicit retry prompt (or a clear notice).
   - **Strict safety invariant**: Once any non-whitespace `TextBlock` or `ToolCallBlock` has been emitted (`answer_emitted == True`), **never retry**, preventing duplicate side effects / duplicate tool calls.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Plugin `on_model_call` middleware**: We implemented a scoped middleware plugin using a bounded pre-answer buffer (`BUFFER_FLUSH_BYTES`) and 1-time retry on empty/thinking-only EOF. Verified in real `v2.3.0` sessions: when an upstream returned a `0`-output-token turn (`371k` input tokens), the middleware caught the empty EOF and retried once, recovering normal tool-calling output immediately.
- Putting this directly into `RetryChatModel` (and unifying with #8676's `has_answer_content`) avoids duplicating provider-specific middleware plugins and ensures consistent behavior across all channels (Console, Feishu, DingTalk, etc.).

## Additional Context

- Tested on QwenPaw `2.3.0` (macOS arm64 Desktop).
- Related issue & PR: #8521, #8676.

issues.title: [Bug]: Hub model gateway instantly fails for Anthropic/MiniMax presets — provider_headers() calls missing request_headers()
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (latest release). Also present on `main` @ 19363e6069fb (2026-11-13): `src/qwenpaw/hub/model_service/provider_setup.py` is unchanged.

## Description

In QwenPaw Hub, any organization-model connection that uses the built-in `anthropic`, `minimax`, or `minimax-cn` preset fails instantly. The admin **Test** button returns HTTP 502:

```json
{"error": {"message": "Invalid or incomplete response from the upstream model.", "code": "hub_upstream_error"}}
```

and the request ledger (`hub_model_requests`) records `error=upstream_failed` with created→completed deltas of only **10–50 ms** — the request never leaves the Hub process (a TLS handshake to the upstream alone takes ~140 ms).

**Root cause:** `hub/model_service/provider_setup.py::provider_headers()` unconditionally calls `preset.request_headers()`:

```python
def provider_headers(connection: dict) -> dict:
    preset = supported_presets().get(connection.get("provider_id"))
    return preset.request_headers() if preset is not None else {}
```

but `AnthropicProvider` and its subclass `MiniMaxProvider` do not implement `request_headers()`. Enumerating all 31 presets returned by `supported_presets()`, exactly three lack the method:

| provider_id | class | request_headers |
|---|---|---|
| anthropic | AnthropicProvider | missing |
| minimax | MiniMaxProvider | missing |
| minimax-cn | MiniMaxProvider | missing |

All other presets (OpenAI/OpenRouter-derived) implement it. The resulting `AttributeError` is swallowed by `ModelGateway.call`'s generic `except BaseException`, settled as `upstream_failed`, and surfaced as a generic 502 — so it looks like a network/provider outage even though the upstream is perfectly healthy.

**Related PR(s):** #7779 (feat(hub): add model gateway, member governance and usage dashboard) introduced this code path.

**Security considerations:** none (no credentials involved in the failure path).

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0
- **OS:** Linux x86_64 (fnOS NAS)
- **Install method:** venv (fnOS app package)
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run QwenPaw Hub 2.3.0 and sign in as admin.
2. In organization model management, create a connection using the `minimax-cn` preset (MiniMax China), base URL `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`, with a valid API key.
3. Publish a model on that connection (e.g. `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` or `MiniMax-M3`).
4. Click **Test** (`POST /api/hub/admin/models/{model_id}/test`).

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** instant 502 `hub_upstream_error` ("Invalid or incomplete response from the upstream model."). Every recorded attempt fails identically in 10–50 ms (34/34 over 5 days in our ledger). Same failure with the `anthropic` preset.
- **Expected:** the test succeeds. A direct `POST https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1/messages` from the same host with the same key and model returns HTTP 200 in ~1.4 s (verified independently with curl and urllib; `MiniMax-M3` and `MiniMax-M2.7` also return 200).

## Logs / Screenshots

Raw traceback, captured by instrumenting `ModelGateway._prepare` (the gateway normally hides it behind the generic 502):

```
File ".../site-packages/qwenpaw/hub/model_service/gateway.py", line 169, in _prepare
    **provider_headers(connection),
File ".../site-packages/qwenpaw/hub/model_service/provider_setup.py", line 78, in provider_headers
    return preset.request_headers() if preset is not None else {}
File ".../site-packages/pydantic/main.py", line 1110, in __getattr__
    raise AttributeError(f'{type(self).__name__!r} object has no attribute {item!r}')
AttributeError: 'MiniMaxProvider' object has no attribute 'request_headers'
```

## Additional Notes

- **Suggested fix:** make `provider_headers()` defensive, e.g.
  ```python
  fn = getattr(preset, "request_headers", None)
  return fn() if callable(fn) else {}
  ```
  or implement `request_headers()` on the `Provider` base class / `AnthropicProvider` so all presets satisfy the contract.
- **Workaround:** create a *custom* connection without `provider_id` (protocol `anthropic`) with the same base URL and key — `provider_headers()` returns `{}` when no preset matches, bypassing the crash.
- Runtime-level (personal) MiniMax providers are **unaffected**; only the Hub model-gateway path is broken.
- Duplicate check: searched issues for `request_headers`, `MiniMaxProvider`, `provider_headers`, `upstream_failed`, `minimax hub`, `hub model failed` — no existing report of this bug. #7445 is a different problem (local/LAN URL reachability from containerized runtimes).

issues.title: [Feature]: Plugin-facing theme extension point (semantic token override layer)
issues.body:
## Summary

The Console theme system added in #7741 lets **users** pick a palette (6 built-ins) and customize accent / hover / background / surface / radius. But **plugins** still have exactly one theme knob: `window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.set(pluginId, { colorPrimary })`. Plugin authors who want deeper theming (backgrounds, glass / `backdrop-filter`, full palettes) have no official hook, so they end up injecting CSS.

Proposal (for discussion): add a **plugin-facing semantic token override layer**, built on QwenPaw's *own* semantic tokens rather than the upstream UI library's raw tokens — so plugins can theme deeply **without coupling to upstream upgrades**.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Problem / Motivation

1. **Plugin theming is one-dimensional today.** The plugin theme API only accepts `colorPrimary` (see `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` and `plugins/hostSdk/install.ts` → `themeFieldMap`). Everything else is unreachable from a plugin.
2. **The marketplace already proves both the demand and the fragility of the workaround.** Appearance plugins such as *QwenPaw Skin Studio*, *background-wallpaper*, and *No Glass (Flat UI)* all describe themselves as "pure frontend, zero-dependency" — i.e. they inject CSS and poke the DOM directly. That breaks whenever the Console's markup or styles change.
3. **Why not simply expose the upstream tokens?** Because `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` deliberately keeps the public surface stable *"across vendor upgrades"* — exposing the upstream UI library's raw tokens would couple every plugin theme to that library's token names. The layer worth opening is **QwenPaw's own semantic layer**, part of which already exists (see #7682).

## Proposed Solution

Two steps, in order:

1. **Own the layer.** Make the Console's theming go through **QwenPaw-owned semantic tokens** (semantic role names → mapped internally to whatever the underlying UI library expects). #7682 ("use semantic tokens in SettingsCenter") is already a step in this direction.
2. **Open the layer to plugins.** Add a plugin API to override those semantic tokens, with the same disposable / registration semantics as the rest of the plugin SDK, e.g.:

```js
const dispose = window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.overrideTokens("my-plugin", {
  "surface":         { light: "#ffffff", dark: "#1f1f1f" },
  "chat.background": { light: "#fafafa", dark: "#111111" },
  // ...any semantic token; both light & dark required, so an override
  // never goes illegible when the user flips the color scheme.
});
```

Because plugins override **QwenPaw's semantic names**, an upstream library upgrade only changes QwenPaw's internal mapping — plugin themes keep working. That removes the exact risk that motivates keeping the surface closed today.

Happy to start with a **minimal first cut** (e.g. the handful of tokens the Console already uses for surface / background / border / text) and grow from there, rather than a big-bang "full skin system".

## Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo — each plugin injects CSS.** Works, but fragile and duplicated; breaks on Console changes; no clean restore. (This is what marketplace appearance plugins do today.)
- **Expose the upstream UI library's raw tokens directly.** Rejected — couples plugins to upstream token names and contradicts the existing "do not expose vendor config" design intent.
- **Only widen the current scalar list** (accent / surface / radius / …). Helps a little, but still cannot reach backgrounds / glass / full palettes.

## Additional Context

- Related: #7741 (merged — 6 palettes + accent/hover/background/surface/radius), #7406, #5909, #6312 (superseded by #7741), #7287 (external frontend gateway — `not_planned`).
- **Reference design**: DeepSeek Harness ships exactly this — `ctx.theme.overrideTokens(source, tokens)` plus a `ThemeDefinition` type (alias-token overrides, light + dark required), documented as *"Third-party themes can register alias-token overrides through `ctx.theme`."*
- Marketplace plugins currently working around this: `@osier-yi/qwenpaw-dream-skin`, `@levodoubt/background-wallpaper`, `@erickcharles/qwenpaw-no-glass`.

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

---

### 中文摘要

Console 的主题系统（#7741）让**用户**能换 6 套预设、自定义 accent / 背景 / 表面 / 圆角；但**插件**目前只有一个主题接口 `chat.theme.set(id, { colorPrimary })`。插件想深度定制（背景、毛玻璃、整套配色）没有官方入口，只能注入 CSS —— 市场里的外观类插件（Skin Studio、背景壁纸、去玻璃化）都是这么干的，Console 一改版就失效。

建议：**在 QwenPaw 自己的语义 token 层上加一个面向插件的覆盖接口**（而不是暴露上游 `AgentScope Runtime WebUI` 的原始 token）—— 这样上游升级时插件主题不受影响（只需 QwenPaw 内部重新映射）。愿意在讨论通过后提 PR，可先做最小版本。

issues.title: [Bug]: Responses continuation summary still fails when a model's default reasoning consumes the 4000-token output budget

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

QwenPaw **2.3.0** (pip install, `site-packages`), Python 3.11, Linux (Docker).

## Description

Scroll generates the continuation summary with `disable_thinking=True`. On the OpenAI Responses protocol that flag currently **strips the `reasoning` field instead of expressing "no reasoning"**, and only re-adds an explicit `{"effort": "none"}` for six hard-coded OpenAI model IDs. For every other Responses model the request therefore carries no reasoning control at all, so the model falls back to its own default (often enabled, sometimes aggressive). That default reasoning then consumes nearly the entire `max_output_tokens` budget, the Markdown body is truncated mid-sentence, `parse_plain_markdown()` cannot find all five required headings, and the caller raises `empty or malformed plain Markdown summary` — twice, ~86 seconds wasted, with a misleading diagnosis.

What happens vs what I expected: compaction does run (eviction succeeds, context is preserved), but the semantic handover is never produced, and the error points at "malformed output" instead of "output truncated by reasoning budget".

This is the residual gap left by #6811 / PR #6818. That fix removed *inherited* provider-level `reasoning` leakage, but did not address the case where **the model's own default** enables reasoning and the model is not on the hard-coded allowlist.

**Related PR(s):** #6818 (partial fix for #6811), #8436 and #8358 (declared `ThinkingControl` direction, still Chat-only)

**Security considerations:** None. The logs below contain no credentials; gateway addresses and keys are redacted.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0
- **OS:** Linux (kernel 6.8, Docker container)
- **Install method:** pip (installed into `site-packages`)
- **Python version:** 3.11

Provider: custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `chat_model = OpenAIResponseModel`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash` served by Volcengine Ark (`/api/plan/v3`). The endpoint sits behind a self-hosted LiteLLM gateway that declares `reasoning_effort: {effort: max}`. The gateway amplifies the problem; case A in the evidence table shows the same failure class without it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an `OpenAIResponseModel` provider pointing at a reasoning-capable model that is **not** in `_NONE_REASONING_EFFORT_MODELS` (e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash` on Volcengine Ark).
2. Leave the model's default reasoning enabled (native default, or a gateway/LiteLLM `reasoning_effort` default).
3. Grow the session past the compaction trigger, or run `/compact` (note: manual `/compact` additionally bypasses decision-model compaction by design).
4. Watch the continuation-summary step fail; the session keeps the previous summary (or none).

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `_SummaryCandidateError: empty or malformed plain Markdown summary` after two attempts (~43s each). `summary_update_failed = true`, `continuation_summary = null`. Eviction itself succeeded (~291k → ~54k estimated tokens), so context is preserved but the handover summary is missing.
- **Expected:** the summary call disables reasoning for models whose declared thinking control supports `off`, or budgets enough output tokens for the reasoning overhead, and produces a valid 5-section Markdown summary.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
2026-11-13 23:34:28 | INFO  | Processing command: compact
2026-11-13 23:35:54 | WARNING | scroll: continuation summary update failed; preserving the previous valid summary
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py", line 1516, in _update_continuation_summary_inner
    updated = await self._validated_summary_attempt(...)
  File ".../qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py", line 1399, in _validated_summary_attempt
    raise _SummaryCandidateError(
qwenpaw.agents.context.scroll.manager._SummaryCandidateError: empty or malformed plain Markdown summary
2026-11-13 23:35:54 | INFO  | scroll: compact timing outcome=done total=85931.8ms persist=4.4ms prepare_input=0.1ms count_tokens=1.3ms split=4.1ms offload_dialog=0.4ms continuation_summary=85920.5ms index_evicted=0.1ms rebuild_context=0.3ms live_tokens=0.6ms
```

Session state after the run:

```json
{"summary_update_failed": true, "continuation_summary": null}
```

### Measured evidence (same real `build_update_prompt()` output, 5691 chars, Chinese continuation summary)

"Reasoning in request" = what actually reached the provider.

| Case | Endpoint | Reasoning in request | `reasoning_tokens` | `output_tokens` | Body length | `status` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Ark direct | *(omitted)* | 3089 | 3640 | 1240 | completed |
| B | Ark direct | `{"effort": "none"}` | **0** | 559 | **1240** | completed |
| C | LiteLLM gateway | *(omitted — QwenPaw stripped it)* | 3923 | 4000 | **194** | completed (hit limit) |
| D | LiteLLM gateway | `{"effort": "none"}` | **4000** | 4000 | **0** | `incomplete`, `reason=length` |
| E | LiteLLM gateway | *(omitted — QwenPaw stripped it)*, `max_output_tokens=8000` | 5775 | 6276 | **1122**, 5/5 headings | completed |

Two conclusions:

1. The model fully supports `reasoning.effort = "none"` (case B: `reasoning_tokens = 0`, body intact). QwenPaw never sends it for this model.
2. The 4000-token output cap leaves no room for reasoning. 3923 reasoning tokens left 77 tokens of body (case C); in case D the model spent 4000/4000 on reasoning and produced zero text. Raising the cap to 8000 made the identical request succeed with all five headings present (case E).

## Additional Notes

### Root cause

`src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py` (`_generate_plain_summary`, ~line 1184):

```python
response = await agent.model(
    messages=messages,
    tools=None,
    max_tokens=max_tokens,
    disable_thinking=True,
)
```

`src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py` (~line 1483) — hard 4000 cap, byte-identical on `main` at the time of this report:

```python
output_tokens = max(256, min(4000, context_size // 4))
```

`src/qwenpaw/providers/openai_response_provider.py` (~lines 138-141) — also byte-identical on `main`:

```python
if disable_thinking:
    merged.pop("reasoning", None)
    if _supports_none_reasoning_effort(model_name):
        merged["reasoning"] = {"effort": "none"}
```

`_NONE_REASONING_EFFORT_MODELS` is a hard-coded frozenset of six OpenAI IDs:

```python
{"gpt-5.5", "gpt-5.5-2026-04-23", "gpt-5.6", "gpt-5.6-luna", "gpt-5.6-sol", "gpt-5.6-terra"}
```

So `disable_thinking` currently means "delete the reasoning field". For a model whose default is *on*, deleting the field is indistinguishable from "enable reasoning with the default effort", and the summary path then races its own output budget.

`src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/continuation_summary.py` (`parse_plain_markdown`, ~line 633) turns the truncation into a formatting error:

```python
if unexpected_text or headings != list(_SECTIONS):
    return None
```

A truncated body misses `## Constraints` / `## Decisions` / `## Open Work`, so the parser returns `None` and the caller raises `empty or malformed plain Markdown summary` — although the real cause was `finished_reason = length`.

### Why #6811 does not cover this

- #6811 (fixed by PR #6818) addressed inherited provider-level `reasoning` (e.g. `generate_kwargs={"reasoning": {"effort": "xhigh"}}`) leaking into the summary request. The patch removed the inherited field.
- Removing the field is not the same as disabling reasoning. For `gpt-5.6` the patch compensates with an explicit `none`; for every other Responses model it silently falls back to the provider default.
- PR #8436 / PR #8358 already established the correct principle for Chat Completions: use the model's declared `ThinkingControl` wire mapping and never guess compatibility parameters. The Responses path still uses a six-model allowlist and is unaligned.

### Suggested fix

1. **Honor declared thinking controls on the Responses path.** Route `disable_thinking` through the model's declared `ThinkingControl` (same source of truth as PR #8436). If the model supports off, send an explicit `{"effort": "none"}`; if the control is unknown, do not silently omit — either fall back to a documented default or record the omission.
2. **Budget the summary output for reasoning, not only prose.** Raise the cap (8000 sufficed in case E), or add the model's expected reasoning overhead to `output_tokens` when thinking cannot be disabled. Keep the prompt-level 1500–2500 token guidance unchanged.
3. **Make the failure diagnosable.** `_generate_plain_summary` already sees `response.incomplete_details.reason`. When it is `length`, raise a distinct error (e.g. `SummaryTruncatedError` carrying `text_len` / `max_tokens`) and log it, instead of collapsing into "empty or malformed" after two 40-second attempts.

### Workaround

- Raise the summary output cap above the reasoning overhead (8000 was enough for a ~5.7k-char evidence prompt; 12000 is safer for long histories).
- Or remove the forcing `reasoning_effort` default from the gateway/model config so the stripped field yields a lighter default.
- Either way keep `summary_timeout_seconds` generous (the 2.3.0 default of 300 is adequate).

### Similar issues reviewed

- #6811 — same error message and same `disable_thinking` path, but scoped to inherited provider kwargs (fixed by #6818).
- #8417 — identical symptom, Chat Completions endpoint and duplicated disable flags (fixed by #8436).
- #8464 — manual `/compact` ignoring session-level model selection; unrelated.

issues.title: [Feature]: DingTalk channel: support interactive card callbacks in stream mode
issues.body:
> **Submitted by**: 狄仁杰·Repairer@QPQAT

## Summary

The DingTalk channel creates interactive cards with `callback_type="STREAM"`, but the stream client never subscribes to the card callback topic (`/v1.0/card/instances/callback`). As a result, user interactions on cards (single-choice selections, form submissions, button clicks) are silently lost — the agent can never learn what the user chose, and cards cannot be updated in place based on that answer.

Request: register a handler for `Card_Callback_Router_Topic` on the **same** stream connection and expose card callback events to the upper layer (custom handler registration and/or a config switch).

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Background

QwenPaw's DingTalk channel connects via the `dingtalk-stream` SDK (`dingtalk-stream>=0.24.3`) using a Stream (WebSocket) long connection, and already uses DingTalk interactive cards ("AI Card") to stream assistant replies back into the chat.

Two relevant facts about how that SDK works:

1. **Subscriptions are derived from registered handlers.** `DingTalkStreamClient.open_connection()` builds the `subscriptions` list of the connect request by iterating `self.callback_handler_map.keys()` (`dingtalk_stream/stream.py`, `open_connection`). A topic with no registered handler is therefore *never subscribed* — DingTalk will not even push those callbacks down the connection.
2. **Card interactions arrive on their own topic.** Interactive cards created with `callbackType="STREAM"` deliver user actions to `/v1.0/card/instances/callback`, exposed by the SDK as `dingtalk_stream.Card_Callback_Router_Topic` (`card_callback.py`) and `CallbackHandler.TOPIC_CARD_CALLBACK` (`handlers.py`). The payload is parsed by `CardCallbackMessage.from_dict()`, whose `content` field carries the user's selection / form values and whose `outTrackId` identifies the card instance.

## Current behavior

**Only the chatbot message topic is registered** — `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/dingtalk/channel.py` (lines 2851-2854 at `origin/main` @ `1cfaad4ef`, version `2.2.1b1`):

```python
self._client = dingtalk_stream.DingTalkStreamClient(credential)
...
internal_handler = DingTalkChannelHandler(...)
self._client.register_callback_handler(
    ChatbotMessage.TOPIC,          # '/v1.0/im/bot/messages/get'
    internal_handler,
)
```

There is no `register_callback_handler(Card_Callback_Router_Topic, ...)` anywhere in the channel.

**Yet the card is created asking for STREAM callbacks** — same file, line 3153:

```python
create_request = dingtalk_card_models.CreateCardRequest(
    card_template_id=self.card_template_id,
    out_track_id=card_instance_id,
    card_data=dingtalk_card_models.CreateCardRequestCardData(...),
    callback_type="STREAM",
    ...
)
```

So the sending side declares "call me back over Stream", while the receiving side never subscribes to that callback topic and has no handler for it. The link is a dead end:

- The connect request subscribes to `/v1.0/im/bot/messages/get` only, so card action callbacks are not delivered at all.
- Even if such a message did arrive, `route_message()` would find no handler in `callback_handler_map` and log `"unknown callback message topic"` before dropping it — with no ACK, which also means DingTalk-side retries/timeouts.

**Observable impact:** a card with buttons/radio/form controls renders fine and users can click it, but QwenPaw receives nothing. The conversation cannot continue from the card, and the card cannot be updated to reflect the user's choice.

## Expected behavior

1. On the existing stream client, register a handler for `Card_Callback_Router_Topic` so the connect request subscribes to `/v1.0/card/instances/callback`.
2. Parse the callback into a usable event (`CardCallbackMessage`: `outTrackId` / card instance id, `userId`, `content` with the user's selection or form values, `extension`).
3. Return a proper ACK (`AckMessage.STATUS_OK`) so DingTalk considers the callback handled.
4. Expose the event to the upper layer instead of swallowing it inside the channel — ideally via both:
   - a pluggable/custom handler registration hook (so agent or skill code can react to a specific card's answer), and
   - a config switch (e.g. `DINGTALK_CARD_CALLBACK_ENABLED`, default off for backward compatibility) so existing deployments see no behavior change unless they opt in.
5. Correlate the callback back to the originating card instance (the channel already tracks active cards in `self._active_cards` / `AICardPendingStore`) so the answer can be routed to the right session, and the card can then be updated in place — the update primitives are already there (`StreamingUpdateRequest` in `_stream_ai_card`, plus `CardReplier.put_card_data` in the SDK).

## Use case

**Interactive decision cards.** When an agent needs the user to pick between options — "which of these three fixes should I apply?", "approve / reject this change?", "which environment should I deploy to?" — the natural UX on DingTalk is a card with buttons or a radio group, not asking the user to type a number as a new chat message. Today the agent can send such a card but is blind to the click, so the flow has to fall back to free-text replies.

**Approval cards.** Human-in-the-loop gates (deploy approval, destructive-operation confirmation) benefit from an auditable, one-click card answer bound to a specific card instance and user id, rather than parsing chat text.

**Form-style parameter collection.** Collecting several fields at once (target version, region, flags) in a single card submission, then updating the same card to show "received: …".

## Constraint: one stream connection per client-id

DingTalk allows only **one** Stream long connection per `client-id`. If a second process opens a connection with the same credentials just to pick up card callbacks, the two connections compete for the same incoming traffic — chatbot messages get diverted to whichever connection receives them, and the main agent silently stops seeing user messages. That makes the workaround "just run a separate callback listener process" unviable for anyone who also wants normal chat to keep working.

The only correct fix is to add the subscription **on the same stream client instance** that already handles `ChatbotMessage.TOPIC`, i.e. inside the channel's existing connection setup.

## Proposed implementation sketch (optional)

```python
from dingtalk_stream import (
    CallbackHandler, CallbackMessage, AckMessage, Card_Callback_Router_Topic,
)

class DingTalkCardCallbackHandler(CallbackHandler):
    def __init__(self, channel, main_loop):
        super().__init__()
        self._channel = channel
        self._loop = main_loop

    async def process(self, callback: CallbackMessage):
        # CardCallbackMessage.from_dict(callback.data) gives
        # outTrackId (card instance), userId, content (user's answer)
        await self._channel._on_card_callback(callback.data)
        return AckMessage.STATUS_OK, "OK"

# in the same place where ChatbotMessage.TOPIC is registered:
if self.card_callback_enabled:
    self._client.register_callback_handler(
        Card_Callback_Router_Topic,
        DingTalkCardCallbackHandler(self, self._loop),
    )
```

Notes:
- Registering before `start_forever()` is what makes `open_connection()` include the topic in `subscriptions`; no extra connection is needed.
- Keep it behind a config flag, default off, so the connect request of existing deployments is unchanged.
- The handler runs on the SDK's stream thread; hop to the channel's asyncio loop the same way `DingTalkChannelHandler` already does, and keep `process()` fast (hand off heavy work) so ACKs are not delayed.

## Alternatives considered

- **Separate process with the same client-id** — rejected: splits chatbot messages across connections (see Constraint), breaks the main agent.
- **HTTP callback endpoint instead of Stream** — requires a publicly reachable URL and a different DingTalk app configuration; Stream is already the channel's model and needs no new inbound port.
- **Free-text replies instead of card interactions** — the current de-facto workaround; loses the one-click UX, is ambiguous to parse, and cannot be bound reliably to a specific card instance.

## Additional context

- QwenPaw version checked: `2.2.1b1` at `origin/main` @ `1cfaad4ef` (latest tag `v2.2.0-beta.7`).
- SDK: `dingtalk-stream` 0.24.3; relevant symbols `Card_Callback_Router_Topic`, `CardCallbackMessage`, `CallbackHandler.TOPIC_CARD_CALLBACK`, `AckMessage.STATUS_OK`.
- Related SDK facilities already available but unused by the channel: `CardReplier.create_and_deliver_card`, `CardReplier.put_card_data`, `AICardReplier`.
- DingTalk interactive card callback topic: `/v1.0/card/instances/callback`.

## Willing to Contribute

We are a QA team running QwenPaw in a multi-agent test setup. We are not opening a PR for this right now, but we can help verify a fix end-to-end in our own DingTalk test environment (card with radio/form controls → callback received → card updated in place), and we can supply logs/payload captures from the current dead-end behavior if that helps.

issues.title: [Bug]: /model 在渠道内无法切换会话级钉住模型（只改 agent 默认），钉住模型故障时无法自救
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0

## Description

### 现象

在渠道（飞书 / 钉钉等）对话框里，对**已经钉住了会话级模型**的会话执行 `/model <provider>:<model>`，命令返回 "Model Switched" 成功，但**当前会话实际使用的模型不变**，再发 `/model` 查看也仍显示原来钉住的模型。用户无法在渠道内把当前会话切换到别的模型——即使钉住的那个模型已经故障、整条会话无法对话。

### 实际复现案例（生产实测）

- 某飞书会话此前通过 Console 模型选择器钉住了会话级模型 `provider-b:model-b`（写入 `chats.json` 的 `meta.runtime_context.model`）。
- 该模型所属网关整体连接失败（`Connection error`），会话无法正常对话。
- 在飞书对话框发 `/model provider-a:model-a`：
  - 服务日志出现 `/model switch: agent=default provider=provider-a model=model-a`（命令执行成功）；
  - `agent.json` 的 `active_model` 确实被持久化为 `provider-a:model-a`；
  - 回执为 "Model Switched"，附带一句英文提示 "This conversation keeps its session override: provider-b:model-b ..."。
- 紧接着发普通消息，builder 日志仍为 `built agent for session=... model=provider-b/model-b`——会话依旧用钉住的故障模型。
- 再发 `/model` 查看，显示的仍是 `provider-b:model-b`（session override）。
- 期间还发了 `/new`：会话重建后**仍用** `provider-b/model-b`（`/new` 不清会话级钉住）。
- 关键：slash command 本身不经过 LLM（模型故障时 `/model` 依然能执行成功），所以这本该是模型故障时的自救通道，但因为改不动会话钉住而失效。

### 期望行为

在渠道对话框内，`/model <provider>:<model>` 应能切换**当前会话**实际使用的模型；或至少提供一个命令（如 `/model reset` / `/model unpin`）能清除当前会话的会话级模型钉住，让会话回落到 agent 默认，从而在钉住模型故障时用户能在渠道内自救。

### 实际行为

`/model <provider>:<model>` 只更新 **agent 级默认**（`agent.json` 的 `active_model`），完全不触碰当前会话的会话级模型钉住（`chats.json` 的 `meta.runtime_context.model`）。由于会话级优先级更高，当前会话的显示与实际调用都不变。`/model reset` 同样只清 agent 级、不清会话钉住。渠道内没有任何命令能设置 / 清除会话级模型。

### 根因分析（源码链路）

1. **模型选择优先级**：`qwenpaw/services/session_thinking.py` 的 `select_chat_model()` = 请求级 override > 会话级 override（`session_model(meta)` 读 `meta.runtime_context.model`）> 无。会话级钉住优先于 agent 默认。
2. **`/model` 显示与实际调用都走会话级优先**：`qwenpaw/runtime/commands/control/model_handler.py` 的 `_current_model()` 先调 `_conversation_model()`（读会话 override），有则直接返回；builder 构建普通消息时同样应用会话 override。
3. **`/model <spec>` 只写 agent 级**：`_switch_model()` 仅 `agent_config.active_model = new_slot` + `update_agent_config_async(...)` 持久化到 `agent.json`，**不调用** `set_session_model()`，不改 `meta.runtime_context.model`。成功回执里的 `_override_notice()` 只是"提示"会话仍用旧 override，并不改变它。
4. **`/model reset` 同样只清 agent 级**：`_reset_model()` 把 `agent_config.active_model = None`，也不触碰会话 override。
5. **会话级模型的唯一写入入口不在渠道命令**：`qwenpaw/app/chats/manager.py` 的 `set_session_model(chat_id, model)` 只被 `qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py` 的 `PUT /{chat_id}/model`（Console）与 `qwenpaw/app/routers/console.py` 调用。渠道侧 control 命令（/model /stop /skills /checkpoint /approval）与渠道命令（/new /compact）均无法设置 / 清除会话级模型。

**结果**：一旦某会话在 Console 钉住了模型，渠道内就再也无法用命令改它的模型；钉住模型故障时，用户在渠道内无自救手段，只能回到 Console（或直连 API）处理。

## 与既有 issue 的关系

- **#8464（已修复 / completed）**：`/compact` 无视会话级模型、固定用 agent 级默认——官方已让 `/compact` 继承会话当前模型。本 issue 是**同族互补缺口**：`/model` 作为"模型管理"命令，却反而**无法管理当前会话的模型**（只能改 agent 默认）。两者都源于"slash command 与 `meta.runtime_context.model` 会话级 override 的交互不完整"。
- 区别于 #8310（Console 切换弹窗 UX / 思考控制），本 issue 专指**渠道内 `/model` 命令无法切换 / 清除会话级模型**。

## 修复建议

让 `/model` 在渠道会话内使用时作用于**当前会话**，任选其一或组合：

- 选项 A：`/model <provider>:<model>` 在有会话上下文时，同时调用 `set_session_model(chat_id, new_slot)` 更新当前会话 override（与 Console `PUT /{chat_id}/model` 同源），使显示与实际调用立即一致。
- 选项 B：赋予 `/model reset`（或新增 `/model unpin`）会话语义——清除当前会话的 `meta.runtime_context.model`（`set_session_model(chat_id, None)`），回落到 agent 默认。当前 `/model reset` 只清 agent 级，建议区分会话级。
- 无论哪种，成功回执应明确说明"当前会话已切换 / 已清除钉住"，而不是仅提示 "This conversation keeps its session override"。

## 影响

- 模型故障时渠道内无法自救，只能回 Console，违背"slash command 不经过 LLM、模型挂了也能用"的兜底设计初衷。
- "Model Switched" 成功回执与实际行为不符，易误导用户以为已切换。

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.3.0（Docker 部署）
- 渠道：飞书（其他渠道同理，凡支持会话级模型钉住 + slash command 的均受影响）

issues.title: [Feature] Support pre-condition rules in AGENTS.md for tool calls
issues.body:
## Problem

Agents sometimes skip critical verification steps before modifying files, even when rules are clearly defined in AGENTS.md. For example:

- Editing a date field in a Vue file without checking MEMORY.md for the correct date
- Modifying user-specific information (names, birthdays, config values) based on "memory" rather than verified data

The root cause is **behavioral, not capability-related**: the agent has access to memory tools and knows the rules, but the "get it done fast" tendency overrides "stop and check first". This is especially problematic when context gets long.

## Use Case

My agent manages a family app with hardcoded values (baby birthday, API endpoints, user preferences). When I ask it to fix a date value, it opens the file and edits directly **without querying MEMORY.md to confirm the correct value** — even though MEMORY.md contains the verified information on line 25.

This has caused real data errors (wrong birthday year) that were caught only by manual review.

## Proposed Solution

Support a `[pre-condition]` section in AGENTS.md that defines mandatory checks before specific tool calls:

```markdown
## Pre-conditions

[pre-condition:edit_file]
pattern: "*.vue", "*.ts", "*.js"
require: grep_search(MEMORY.md) OR memory_search
```

### Behavior

- Before executing `edit_file` on a file matching the pattern, the system checks if the required query has been performed **in the current turn**
- If not, the tool call is blocked with a message: "Pre-condition not met: please query MEMORY.md before editing this file"
- Only applies to `edit_file` (not `write_file` for new files)
- The check is lightweight — just verifying that a search call was made, not evaluating its result

## Why Prompt-Only Rules Are Not Enough

AGENTS.md already has rules like "check memory before modifying files". But these are treated as **reference**, not **mandatory**. The agent can and does skip them when it "feels confident" about the answer. Without enforcement, rules become suggestions.

## Why This Matters

- **Generic problem**: Any agent managing projects with personal/config data will face this
- **Low implementation cost**: Only needs a pattern-match + call-history check before tool execution
- **No performance impact**: Only activates for matching file patterns
- **Composable**: Users can define multiple pre-conditions for different tools/patterns

## Implementation Sketch

```python
def check_pre_conditions(tool_name, tool_args, config):
    rules = config.get("pre_conditions", {}).get(tool_name, [])
    for rule in rules:
        if file_matches_pattern(tool_args["file_path"], rule["pattern"]):
            if not has_called_in_turn(rule["require"]):
                return PreConditionError(
                    f"Please call {rule['require']} before editing this file"
                )
    return None
```

The key insight: we don't need to evaluate the *quality* of the search result — just enforcing that the agent **paused to look** is enough to break the "edit first, verify never" pattern.

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows sandbox ACL on a drive-root workspace can lock the volume

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

`2.2.2b2` (`main` @ `79f8e7d30e571d32fb4fe2e62ca714a8eeafa413`, 2026-09-18)

## Description

On Windows, the first sandboxed shell writes an inheritable ACE on `config.workspace_dir`. QwenPaw does not reject a drive root as cwd. If the workspace is `C:\` (or another volume root), that write is applied to the entire volume.

`_set_path_ace` uses `SET_ACCESS` + `SetNamedSecurityInfoW` with `(OI)(CI)`, and does not refuse a NULL DACL. Windows then re-propagates inheritable ACEs to existing children. A drive root has no parent; if the root DACL is missing or becomes sandbox-only, SYSTEM / Administrators / Users can disappear from the subtree and the drive becomes inaccessible.

This is not caused by the user's later shell commands. It happens when the sandbox is first created.

**Related PR(s):** N/A

**Security considerations:** Local filesystem ACL corruption. A drive-root workspace (especially `C:\`) can leave the volume unreadable even for an elevated Administrator. Elevated sandbox cleanup also falls back to `icacls <path> /reset`, which is dangerous on a volume root.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2b2 (`79f8e7d3`)
- **OS:** Windows Server (repro on a disposable `E:` volume). Field reports are on Windows 10 Pro, workspace `C:\`.
- **Install method:** from source
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a **disposable test volume only**. Do not run this on `C:\`.

1. Confirm `sandbox_enabled=true` (default whitelist AppContainer).
2. On a throwaway drive (e.g. `E:\`), optionally pre-set a NULL DACL on the volume root (this matches the failure mode when `GetNamedSecurityInfoW` returns `p_dacl == NULL`).
3. Set the workspace cwd to that volume root (`E:\`), not a subdirectory.
4. Send one message that runs a shell command, e.g. `cmd /c echo hello`.

Code references on current `main`:

- `src/qwenpaw/sandbox/windows_appcontainer_sandbox.py` `_apply_all_acls`: `_set_path_ace(..., _WC.SET_ACCESS)` on `config.workspace_dir`
- `src/qwenpaw/sandbox/windows_unelevated_sandbox.py` `_set_path_ace`: `SetNamedSecurityInfoW` with inherit flags; no NULL-DACL check
- `src/qwenpaw/sandbox/windows_elevated_sandbox.py`: `icacls ... /reset` cleanup fallback

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** After the first sandbox ACL write, `icacls E:\` can return access denied for an elevated Administrator; Explorer cannot open the drive; the Security tab cannot display the DACL. Remaining trustees may be only the sandbox SID (`S-1-15-2-*`).
- **Expected:** QwenPaw should not treat a volume root as a workspace grant root, should not replace a missing DACL with a sandbox-only DACL, and should not reset DACLs on a drive root.

issues.title: [Bug]: Upgrade does not migrate built-in channel plugins; installed Matrix stays on old source and 2.3.0 fixes never apply

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (PyPI, released 2026-11-11)

## Description

Upgrading from an earlier release to 2.3.0 leaves `~/.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix` on its old source. The Matrix fixes in 2.3.0 — #8559 (install E2EE dependencies with the channel), #8558, #8584, #8599, #8411 (session and device-key recovery) — exist only in the bundled `official_channels/matrix-0.1.0.dev0.zip`. Nothing installs it over the existing plugin directory.

The upgrade completes, the plugin does not, the fixes never apply, and there is no update entry point: `qwenpaw plugins` has no `update` subcommand, and both Console's update check and the extension market exclude built-in channel plugins.

In this instance the old plugin's `state.py` imports `qwenpaw.plugins.matrix_legacy`, which 2.3.0 removed, so it fails at startup with `ModuleNotFoundError`. Three agents with Matrix enabled fail to start.

Mechanism:

- `plugins/official_channels.py:455` seeds a bundled channel only when `loader.find_installed_plugin_dir(plugin_id) is None`.
- `plugins/official_channels.py:312` does the same during `prepare-upgrade`; an installed plugin only goes through `preflight_backend()`, which checks and installs dependencies but does not replace source.
- `plugins/loader.py:3518` raises `Official source already exists` when a seed is attempted for an existing directory. The comment at `plugins/loader.py:3531` states the intent: `Reuse A first-copy/publication, never replacement.`
- `official_channels/index.json` records matrix as `version: 0.1.0.dev0` with `sha256: 114e9e32...`. No code compares that hash or version against the installed directory.
- Console → Installed plugins → check updates queries `https://download.qwenpaw.agentscope.io/metadata/plugins/index.json` (31 entries, no `matrix`). The extension market has no entry for it either.
- `qwenpaw plugins` has no `update` subcommand; `install --force` is the only entry point.

**Related PR(s):** #8559, #8558, #8584, #8599, #8411

**Security considerations:** None. No credentials or auth paths are involved; the failure is confined to local plugin loading.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-42-generic
- **Install method:** one-line install (`curl -fsSL https://qwenpaw.agentscope.io/install.sh | bash`)
- **Python version:** 3.12.14 (uv-managed venv at `~/.qwenpaw/venv`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On 2.2.x, enable the Matrix channel for at least one agent and confirm it connects. `~/.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix` now exists with `matrix-nio>=0.25.0` in `requirements.txt`.
2. Upgrade to 2.3.0 with the official installer.
3. Start the service and open Console → Channels → Matrix.
4. The channel fails to start.
5. Stop the service and run `qwenpaw plugins prepare-upgrade`. It exits successfully, but `~/.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix/requirements.txt` is unchanged.
6. Open Console → Extensions → Installed plugins → check updates, then the extension market. Matrix is not listed in either.
7. Only `qwenpaw plugins install /path/to/unpacked/matrix --force` restores it.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** After upgrading to 2.3.0, the installed Matrix plugin remains on its old source and the 2.3.0 channel fixes are not applied. This instance fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'qwenpaw.plugins.matrix_legacy'`, and all three agents with Matrix enabled fail to start. `prepare-upgrade` does not fix it, Console's update check and the extension market provide no entry for the plugin, and the CLI has no update command.
- **Expected:** Upgrading QwenPaw should migrate built-in channel plugins. At minimum, compare `official_channels/index.json` `sha256` against the installed directory (`version` is currently fixed at `0.1.0.dev0` and cannot serve as a criterion), replace it after backing up, and preserve channel configuration. Alternatively, include built-in channel plugins in Console's update detection and provide an entry in the extension market for one-click update.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'qwenpaw.plugins.matrix_legacy'
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/execution/worker.py", line 230, in connect
  File ".../.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix/qwenpaw_channel_matrix/driver.py", line 41, in start
  File ".../.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix/qwenpaw_channel_matrix/platform.py", line 204, in <module>
  File ".../.qwenpaw/plugins/matrix/qwenpaw_channel_matrix/state.py", line 15, in <module>
```

```text
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'matrix' marked FAILED after startup:
channel 'matrix' failed: job@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED;
jiuhu@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED;
fairy@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
```

After force-reinstalling the bundled source, the same three agents connect within two seconds, and the new plugin logs the recovery path that only exists in the 2.3.0 source:

```text
MatrixChannel: homeserver lost E2EE device keys; re-uploading the existing identity
platform_state: connected
```

## Additional Notes

This is not Matrix-specific. `official_channels/index.json` contains 18 bundled channel plugins; 17 of them are versioned `0.1.0.dev0`. Whenever a release changes their code or the host APIs they import, the same stale-source problem applies, and none of it is covered by the current update detection.

Recovery for affected users is a manual `qwenpaw plugins install <unpacked plugin directory> --force`.

issues.title: execute_shell_command: a resource-protection termination hides the result from the model, which then repeats the call
issues.body:
## What happens

With `QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=128`, a 400 MB probe process is terminated
correctly. The tool result visible in the log and in the Console reads:

```
exit code 15. [resource protection] Shell memory limit exceeded (RSS 134881280 bytes > 134217728 bytes)
```

The model, however, does not receive that result. It re-issued the identical
call, and governance approved the same `Bash` invocation **14 times** between
`09:09:10` and `09:10:22` (one every 6–7 seconds); the user had to press stop
twice. From the model's side the call simply produced no result, so repeating
it looked like the only option.

## Why

`_with_shell_guard` is the only place in `agents/tools/shell.py` that turns a
completed call into `ToolResultState.ERROR`:

```python
if guard.failure:
    result.state = ToolResultState.ERROR
    result.content.append(
        TextBlock(type="text", text=f"[resource protection] {guard.failure}"),
    )
```

Every other failure path in the same tool — non-zero exit code, timeout —
returns `ToolResultState.SUCCESS` and puts `Command failed with exit code N`
into the text (`shell.py` lines around `1608` and `1663`). Those results reach
the model normally.

`agents/middlewares.py` documents the difference:

> The coordinator stops driving this generator as soon as it sees an
> ERROR/INTERRUPTED ToolChunk (no ToolResponse follows), so the terminal chunk
> itself is the only record of how the call ended.

So the `[resource protection] ...` text is recorded for observability but never
becomes a tool response, and the model is left with an empty result for a call
that actually ran.

## Expected

The model should see exactly what the user sees: the command ran, was
terminated by resource protection, and why. A terminated command is a completed
call, not a broken tool, and the same tool already reports every other failure
that way.

## Proposed fix

Keep the state the command produced (`SUCCESS` for a terminated process) and
append the reason, instead of overriding it with `ERROR`:

```python
if guard.failure:
    result.content.append(
        TextBlock(type="text", text=f"[resource protection] {guard.failure}"),
    )
```

`tests/unit/agents/tools/test_shell_resources.py` asserts `SUCCESS` now and
still requires the reason plus the original stderr to be present. With the one
line removed the same tests fail (4 failed), so the assertion pins the
behaviour.

## Second observation — explained, not a defect

While reproducing, a bare script that set `QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=96`
before importing `qwenpaw` still ended up with `ShellGuard.from_environment`
returning `None`, and a 300 MB process ran to completion.

The cause is `load_bootstrap_envs()`: at import time it replays
`$QWENPAW_HOME.secret/envs.json` over `os.environ` with `overwrite=True`, and
that file contained `"0"` for this key, so the value set by the script was
replaced (96 → 0). Setting the variable **after** the import creates the guard
as expected (96 MB, kills a 300 MB process).

That is documented behaviour — "persisted values override existing
process/system values" — and the Console path writes through the same store, so
a limit configured there is applied correctly. I am recording it only so the
reproduction in this issue can be run; it is not a defect.

issues.title: Creator: Windows source-intelligence write path still derives its directory from the raw source_id (write-side root cause split from #8547)
issues.body:
## 背景

从 #8547 的修复 PR(xuanrui-L/QwenPaw#254)CR 中拆出的**写侧根因**。#8547 修的是读/导入侧,本 issue 跟踪写侧。

## 问题

Windows 上 Creator 素材理解(source-intelligence)的写路径仍拿 raw `source_id`(形如 `source:<uuid4 hex>`,生成点 `services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:3282`)当落盘目录分量:

- `services/source_analysis/service.py:2077-2082`:`relative_uri = PurePosixPath("assets", "source-intelligence", job.source_id, f"{job.intelligence_version_id}.json")`
- publish 时 `AssetFileStore` 按该 `relative_uri` mkdir 父目录

`:` 是 Windows 非法字符,因此 Windows 上**新建素材理解、或对导入项目的素材重跑理解**,publish 阶段 mkdir `source:<id>` 会失败。读路径不受影响(一律经 `IndexedFile.relative_uri` 解析,见 `services/media/source_observation.py:401`、`services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:9384`、`services/project_files/assets.py:412`)。

代码路径推断,未 Windows 真机复现;复现成本不高,建议认领时先补一条 Windows 矩阵的发布用例。

## 与 #8547 的关系

- #8547 / PR #254 修的是**解包侧**:Windows 提取归档时把含非法字符的成员名 sanitize 成合法名,并把 `IndexedFile.relative_uri` 重写到与落盘一致;逻辑标识(source_id、`sources.items` 键、`order`)不动。
- 写侧根因非该 PR 引入,也不被该 PR 解决。PR body 中"落盘路径只经 relative_uri 解析"的论断已按 CR 修正为**仅读路径成立**。

## 建议修法(二选一,认领时定)

1. **publish 时 sanitize**:`AssetFileStore` 落盘前统一映射非法字符,并把 sanitized 结果写回 `relative_uri`,保持注册表与落盘一致(与 PR #254 的解包侧 sanitize 复用同一函数,保证幂等);
2. **生成点不再拿 raw source_id 当路径分量**:目录名改用 uuid/hash 形态,`source_id` 仅保留为逻辑标识。需要为存量 `relative_uri` 做迁移或兼容读。

方案 1 改动面小、与现有 sanitize 一致;方案 2 更彻底但带迁移成本。

## 验收标准

- Windows 真机/CI:新建素材理解、对导入示例素材重跑理解,publish 均成功;
- Linux/macOS 导出、Windows 导入的归档,`relative_uri` 与落盘路径一致,导入后写路径可继续追加文件。

## 关联

- #8547(读/导入侧症状)
- xuanrui-L/QwenPaw#254(读/导入侧修复)
- 历史读侧修复 `4f71f44e5`(#165,1.1.2 发布)与回归点 `f6ed7362c`(#185 重构 example_routes 时丢失 sanitize)
- 另一独立动作(不在本 issue 范围):按 #165 复审结论重建并重传 `cat-perspective-0803` 归档(合法目录名 + 更新 manifest sha256),让内置示例的运行时重写变 no-op,顺带绕开"在途事务归档 + Windows 导入"时重写改变语义 etag 致 recovery 基线失配的窄边缘(`services/project_files/recovery.py:419/461`)。该动作需要 OSS 发布权限。

issues.title: Support mounting the Console and API under a configurable runtime base path
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

- Reproduced with `qwenpaw==2.3.0` from the published wheel.
- Rechecked against current `main` (`19363e6069fb349afaef46e093e91d20dfedd1f0`).

## Description

A standard pip/uv/Docker installation cannot currently be mounted cleanly below a reverse-proxy URL prefix such as `/app/qwenpaw/web/` without rewriting response bodies in the proxy.

The backend registers its API, static assets, and SPA fallback at root-level paths. The prebuilt Console also contains root-relative entry, public asset, API, and navigation URLs. As a result, a proxy that preserves the prefix encounters requests such as `/assets/...` and `/logo-light.svg`, and frontend navigation can escape to `/chat`.

Setting Uvicorn `root_path` or forwarding `X-Forwarded-Prefix` is not sufficient: those mechanisms cannot change absolute URLs already embedded in the prebuilt HTML and JavaScript.

`VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME` from #8316 covers a separately built Console. This request is for the complementary runtime case, where rebuilding the frontend for each installation is not practical.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install QwenPaw from the published wheel and start `qwenpaw app`.
2. Mount it behind a reverse proxy at `/app/qwenpaw/web/`, preserving the prefix without modifying HTML or JavaScript response bodies.
3. Open `/app/qwenpaw/web/` and then a deep link such as `/app/qwenpaw/web/chat`.
4. Inspect asset requests, login navigation, dynamic module requests, and page refresh.

## Actual Behavior

- HTML entry and public assets can be requested from root-level paths.
- SPA navigation can escape the deployment prefix.
- Deep-link refresh and dynamically loaded modules are unreliable without proxy-specific response rewriting.
- Uvicorn `root_path` alone does not correct the prebuilt frontend URLs.

## Expected Behavior

An optional runtime setting such as `QWENPAW_BASE_PATH=/app/qwenpaw/web` should consistently cover:

- FastAPI routes and URL generation;
- HTTP and WebSocket mounting;
- the Vite entry and dynamic imports;
- public files including logos and fonts;
- API and readiness requests;
- router basename, login redirects, and deep-link refresh.

An empty or `/` value must preserve the existing root and `/console` behavior. Requests outside a configured prefix should not silently fall back to the root application.

The proxy should be able to preserve the prefix and forward HTML, JavaScript, and CSS without guessing string replacements in minified output.

## Proposed Implementation

I have prepared a focused implementation and am willing to submit it as a PR:

- validate and mount the application below `QWENPAW_BASE_PATH` using standard ASGI `root_path` semantics;
- use a root-compatible HTML entry whose document base and JSON-encoded runtime prefix are set by the backend;
- use relative Vite entry/module URLs and runtime-aware public asset, API, router, login, and readiness URLs;
- leave JavaScript and CSS response bodies byte-identical;
- update English and Chinese deployment documentation.

Verification includes backend ASGI/static/auth regressions, the complete Console Vitest suite, production builds, and real Chromium login plus deep-link refresh under `/app/qwenpaw/web/`. An empty-prefix control run and `vite preview` are also covered.

## Related Work

For context only: #1853, #8177, and #8316. This new issue is specifically about runtime support for standard prebuilt installations; it does not require reopening, commenting on, or closing those older issues or pull requests.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Console
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CI/CD

## Security Considerations

The configured prefix must be validated as an absolute URL path. Protocol-relative values, query/fragment input, encoded separators, and dot segments must be rejected so generated URLs cannot escape to another origin or path.

issues.title: [Bug]:  [2.3.0] WeChat channel cannot start (`ACCOUNT_IN_USE`) and successful sends are reported as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Environment

| item          | value                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| QwenPaw       | 2.3.0 (PyPI latest at time of report; no 2.3.1 available)    |
| agentscope    | 2.0.10                                                       |
| openai SDK    | 2.33.0                                                       |
| Python        | 3.12.13                                                      |
| OS            | Linux (Manjaro, x86_64), systemd system service              |
| wechat plugin | `wechat` 0.1.0.dev0 (bundled with 2.3.0, `publish: false`)   |
| Channel setup | single agent `default`, wechat enabled with an existing iLink bot token (`bot_token`, no `bot_token_file`) |

## Bug 1 — WeChat channel never starts: `ACCOUNT_IN_USE` (critical)

### Symptom

On every boot (6+ restarts, always identical — unrelated to restart count):

```
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/api.py:688 | Plugin 'wechat' Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
ERROR qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py:1076 | Failed to start new workspace instance for default: Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: channel 'wechat' failed: default@...:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
```

The plugin then gets unregistered (`Unregistered channel 'wechat'`), so the workspace no longer has a wechat channel at all and the bot is silently offline.

`GET /api/config/channels/wechat/health` → `404 {"detail": "Channel 'wechat' is not running."}`

### Traceback

```
manager.py:1602  start_one
manager.py:1671  _start_one_unlocked
manager.py:1342  _reserve_channel_auth
wechat_auth_custody.py:117  _reserve_wechat_auth_evidence
    raise ManagementError("ACCOUNT_IN_USE")
```

Line 117 is the loop that treats **another agent profile** as a competing owner of the same WeChat credential:

```python
scopes, others = evidence
for runtime_key, configured, other_scopes in others:
    if (
        configured or any(lease.key == runtime_key for lease in leases)
    ) and (scopes.intersection(other_scopes)):
        raise ManagementError("ACCOUNT_IN_USE")
```

### Root cause

`_read_wechat_auth_evidence()` skips "myself" with a case-sensitive id comparison:

```python
for agent_id, profile in root.agents.profiles.items():
    if agent_id == workspace_id:
        continue
```

but the workspace id that `manager._reserve_channel_auth()` resolves and passes in is **`Default`** (capital D), while the profile key in `config.json` is **`default`**. The guard therefore never skips itself and evaluates `default` as "another profile". Instrumenting the guard shows the conflict is with the very same workspace, with identical scope hashes:

```
BLOCK workspace_id=Default other=<WORKING_DIR>/.copaw/workspaces/default
      configured=True lease_hit=True overlap=True
      own=['260b8fc0ee','c52f3d47c7','d7162d88f8']
      other_scopes=['260b8fc0ee','c52f3d47c7','d7162d88f8']
```

Note also that with `bot_token_file` left empty, `wechat_auth_scopes()` derives the token paths from `WORKING_DIR`, so **any** profile is guaranteed to hash to the same scopes — meaning a second (even dormant, non-wechat) agent profile is enough to trip this check once the id comparison fails.

### Suggested fix

Normalize identity instead of comparing raw strings; e.g. casefold both sides and/or compare resolved workspace directories. A `workspace_dir` parameter is already available at both call sites.

```python
if str(agent_id).strip().casefold() == str(workspace_id).strip().casefold():
    continue
if own_dir is not None and Path(profile.workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve() == own_dir:
    continue
```

## Bug 2 — Plugin recovery deadlocks on a leaked custody-only lease (critical)

### Symptom

After the plugin has been probed once in a process, it can never be (re)enabled:

```
ERROR loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: ...
POST /api/plugins/wechat/enabled {"enabled": true}
→ 500 {"detail": "Failed to update plugin enabled state: Plugin 'wechat' recovery failed; needs_restart: Recovery has runtime resources; unload first"}
```

`POST /api/plugins/wechat/unload` returns `clean: true, quiescent: true`, yet the next enable still fails, and the `_recovery_blocked` entry is never cleared for the lifetime of the process.

### Root cause

`loader._has_runtime_custody()` is just `bool(registry.runtime_owners.leases(plugin_id))`. Probe reservations are made with `custody_only=True` and **no stop adapter**, and `RuntimeOwners._invoke()` refuses to attest a stop for them:

```python
async def _invoke(entry):
    if entry.stop is None:
        return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")
```

`release()` then returns `False` for that lease, so the entry stays in `_entries` forever → recovery sees "runtime resources", blocks, and caches the error.

### Suggested fix

A custody-only reservation owns no process, so it can always be released:

```python
if entry.stop is None:
    if entry.custody_only:
        return RuntimeStopReceipt(True, "CUSTODY_ONLY_NO_PROCESS")
    return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")
```

## Bug 3 — Successful sends reported as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`; replies dropped (critical)

### Symptom

Inbound works and the agent produces a reply, but the user never receives it:

```
INFO  channel _consume_with_tracker: chat_id=... session=wechat:...        (message received)
INFO  builder: built agent for session=wechat:... model=...
INFO  Usage for session wechat:...: {'input_tokens': 142422, 'output_tokens': 102}
ERROR base.py:1040 | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN
WARNING isolated_proxy.py:637 | Channel diagnostic: RESPONSE_FINISH_FAILED
qwenpaw.app.channels.isolated_proxy.ChannelDeliveryError: PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN
```

`qwenpaw channels send --channel wechat ...` fails the same way (`500` on `/api/messages/send`).

### Reproduction of the platform side

Calling the iLink API directly with the same bot token and the stored `context_token`:

```
POST https://ilinkai.weixin.qq.com/ilink/bot/sendmessage
{"msg": {"to_user_id": "...@im.wechat", "message_type": 2, "message_state": 2,
         "context_token": "<token>", "item_list": [{"type": 1, "text_item": {"text": "test"}}]},
 "base_info": {"channel_version": "0.1.0"}}

→ HTTP 200  {"message_id": <MESSAGE_ID>}
```

**A successful send returns only `message_id` — no `ret`, no `errcode`.**

### Root cause

`plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py:406`:

```python
@staticmethod
def _check_result(response, sent):
    if not isinstance(response, dict) or not (
        {"ret", "errcode"} & response.keys()
    ):
        raise WeChatDeliveryError(
            "PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN",
            side_effect_possible=True,
        )
```

Every successful send is therefore classified as an unknown result and the reply is discarded (the proxy also marks `_reply_unknown`, so there is no retry).

### Suggested fix

Accept `message_id` as success (and/or fall back to the HTTP status):

```python
if isinstance(response, dict) and response.get("message_id"):
    return
```

## Bug 4 — `top_k` / `repetition_penalty` from per-model `generate_kwargs` crash the model call (major)

With an OpenRouter model whose stored `generate_kwargs` contain `top_k` and `repetition_penalty`:

```
TypeError: AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'top_k'
  File ".../openai/resources/chat/completions/completions.py", line 2714, in create
```

OpenAI-compatible endpoints generally expect these in `extra_body`; the SDK signature does not accept them as top-level kwargs. Removing them from the model's `generate_kwargs` (`PUT /api/models/{provider}/models/{model}/config`) fixed it. Suggestion: filter known-unsupported keys into `extra_body` in the OpenAI-compatible wrapper instead of passing them through.

## Observation (not necessarily a QwenPaw bug)

While testing, `openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free` repeatedly returned an empty stream while its connection test reported `status=available, verification=live`:

```
WARNING retry_chat_model.py:1201 | LLM stream failed (attempt 1/4):
        LLM stream for openrouter:nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free produced no content
```

Switching the agent's chat model to `deepseek-custom/deepseek-flash` produced normal replies, so this looks model/provider-specific, but the retry loop silently consumed 4 attempts without surfacing a user-visible error.

## Minimal patch set that made the channel usable (for reference)

```diff
--- a/qwenpaw/app/channels/wechat_auth_custody.py
+++ b/qwenpaw/app/channels/wechat_auth_custody.py
 def _read_wechat_auth_evidence(config, workspace_id, working_dir,
+                               workspace_dir=None):
     for agent_id, profile in root.agents.profiles.items():
         if agent_id == workspace_id:
             continue
+        # NEW: the resolved workspace id may differ in case from the profile key
+        if str(agent_id).strip().casefold() == str(workspace_id).strip().casefold():
+            continue
+        # NEW: or point at the very same workspace directory
+        if workspace_dir is not None and (
+            Path(profile.workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+            == Path(workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+        ):
+            continue

--- a/qwenpaw/plugins/ownership.py
+++ b/qwenpaw/plugins/ownership.py
     async def _invoke(entry):
         if entry.stop is None:
+            if entry.custody_only:
+                return RuntimeStopReceipt(True, "CUSTODY_ONLY_NO_PROCESS")
             return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")

--- a/plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py
+++ b/plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py
     def _check_result(response, sent):
         if not isinstance(response, dict) or not ({"ret", "errcode"} & response.keys()):
+            if isinstance(response, dict) and response.get("message_id"):
+                return
             raise WeChatDeliveryError("PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN", side_effect_possible=True)
```

After these three changes (plus removing `top_k`/`repetition_penalty` from the model's `generate_kwargs`):

- `GET /api/config/channels/wechat/health` → `{"channel":"wechat","status":"healthy"}`
- plugin → `status: active, diagnostics: ["channel_validation_passed"]`
- inbound messages are consumed, replies are delivered, no `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`

## Additional notes

- A zero-downtime agent reload (triggered by any config change) can leave the previous wechat channel handle undelivered: subsequent `POST /api/config/channels/wechat/restart` returns `CHANNEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` indefinitely, and a stale `shared_worker.py` keeps polling (reported `platform_state: connected`) while its messages no longer reach the app. Killing the stale worker unblocks the drain.
- Plugin source edits require `POST /api/plugins/wechat/unload` + `enabled=true` to take effect; `channel restart` fails with `SOURCE_REVISION_MISMATCH`.
- With a large wechat session (142k input tokens per turn) replies take 60–90 s end-to-end, which may be close to the iLink reply window.

issues.title: [Bug]: Attachments cannot be resolved when the workspace path contains #
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

Reproduced on `main` (`fc1db1a4568b44c74094aa2a748ee0eba70d1990`) and with the same source-level probe on `v2.2.2`.

## Description

On Windows, an attachment saved under a workspace directory containing `#` cannot be resolved after QwenPaw converts its local path into a message. The converter copies the raw `#` into the file URI, where the reader interprets the remainder as a fragment. This affects both image and file blocks.

Related investigation: #8655 and [the reproduction comparison](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8655#issuecomment-6819991930). This report covers the reproducible fragment case. It was also present in `v2.2.2`, before the beta release discussed in #8655.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows
- **Install method:** source-level offline probe
- **Python:** 3.12.14
- **AgentScope:** 2.0.10

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an installed source checkout, run the snippet below. It creates a synthetic attachment under a temporary workspace.
2. Compare the raw Windows path used by the converter with the encoded URI control. The two inputs point to the same file.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from types import SimpleNamespace

from qwenpaw.app.channels.utils import file_url_to_local_path
from qwenpaw.runtime.message_convert import _request_input_to_msgs

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory, "workspace#draft", "media", "sample.png")
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    path.write_bytes(b"synthetic attachment")
    for value in (str(path), path.as_uri()):
        part = SimpleNamespace(type="image", image_url=value)
        [message] = _request_input_to_msgs(
            [SimpleNamespace(role="user", content=[part])]
        )
        resolved = Path(file_url_to_local_path(str(message.content[0].source.url)))
        print(resolved == path, resolved.is_file())
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The raw path resolves only as far as `workspace`. The encoded URI control resolves to the full file.
- **Expected:** Both inputs resolve to the same existing attachment. A literal `#` in the local path is encoded as `%23` when forming the URI.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
workspace with spaces | raw path | image + file: same_file=True, exists=True
workspace#draft       | raw path | image + file: same_file=False, exists=False
workspace#draft       | encoded  | image + file: same_file=True, exists=True
```

## Additional Notes

I would like to work on a focused fix in the shared local-path converter. The reproduction uses no channel connection or model credentials. AI assistance was used for investigation.

prs.title: fix(pawapp): disable proxy buffering on chat and tool-call SSE streams

## Description

Follow-up to #8522, which added `X-Accel-Buffering: no` to the `/api/console/chat` SSE responses. Two more SSE endpoints that the Console consumes still lack it:

- `POST /chat/stream` in `pawapp/app.py` (used by the pawapp SDK host)
- `GET /tool-calls/{session_id}/{tool_call_id}/stream` in `app/routers/tool_calls.py` (used by `console/src/api/modules/toolCalls.ts`)

Behind nginx with the default `proxy_buffering on`, their events are held until the buffer fills or the response ends, so the stream arrives late or all at once — the same symptom as #8516.

prs.title: fix(hub): expose request_headers on AnthropicProvider presets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hub model connections that use the built-in `anthropic`, `minimax` or `minimax-cn`
preset fail instantly with HTTP 502 `hub_upstream_error`, and the request never
leaves the Hub process.

`hub/model_service/provider_setup.py::provider_headers()` calls
`preset.request_headers()` for every presets-based connection, but
`AnthropicProvider` never defined that method (`OpenAIProvider` and
`OpenRouterProvider` do). Because `MiniMaxProvider` subclasses
`AnthropicProvider`, three of the 31 presets returned by `supported_presets()`
raise `AttributeError: 'AnthropicProvider' object has no attribute
'request_headers'`.

`ModelGateway` catches it with its generic `except BaseException`, settles the
ledger row as `upstream_failed`, and surfaces
`Invalid or incomplete response from the upstream model.` — so a broken call
site looks like a provider outage even though the upstream is healthy.
`provider_headers()` returns `{}` for custom connections, which is why only
preset-based connections are affected.

Fixes #8718.

## Change

Implement `request_headers()` on `AnthropicProvider`, mirroring the existing
implementations on `OpenAIProvider` and `OpenRouterProvider`:

```python
def request_headers(self) -> dict:
    """Return provider headers for an externally owned HTTP transport."""
    return self._build_default_headers()
```

`MiniMaxProvider` inherits the method, so all three affected presets are fixed
by one definition.

I did not add a `getattr` fallback in `provider_headers()`: that would silence
the crash while silently dropping attribution and session headers for any
future preset that forgets the method. Keeping the contract callable makes a
missing implementation fail in tests instead.

## Evidence

Before the patch, calling `provider_headers({"provider_id": ...})` for every
preset:

| provider_id | class | result |
|---|---|---|
| anthropic | AnthropicProvider | `AttributeError` |
| minimax | MiniMaxProvider | `AttributeError` |
| minimax-cn | MiniMaxProvider | `AttributeError` |
| openai | OpenAIProvider | `{}` |
| openrouter | OpenRouterProvider | headers returned |

After the patch all 31 presets return a dict.

The new regression test is parametrized over `supported_presets()`, so it covers
every built-in preset rather than only the three known-bad ids:

- unpatched tree: `3 failed, 69 passed` (fails exactly for anthropic, minimax, minimax-cn)
- patched tree: `72 passed`

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/unit/providers/test_hub_provider_reuse.py` — 72 passed
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/providers` — 1191 passed, 1 skipped
- Pre-commit: all hooks passed (ast, docstring-first, encoding, private key,
  whitespace, trailing commas, mypy, black, flake8, pylint)
