prs.title: feat(crons): per-job thinking_level override
prs.body:
## Description

Cron jobs currently inherit the agent's `thinking_level` wholesale. A
pipeline job (data collection, report generation, format conversion)
that only needs the agent's tools pays full reasoning latency and
reasoning tokens on every scheduled run — or the operator has to clone
the agent just to turn thinking off. #8439 reports 21 of 29 cron jobs
in exactly that situation, with single model calls stretching from
20 seconds to 9.5 minutes while `relay_reasoning` is on.

This adds a per-job `thinking_level` to the cron `JobRuntimeSpec`,
resolved through the existing request-scoped thinking precedence, so a
job can disable thinking (or force a specific effort) without touching
the agent's defaults.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8439

**Security Considerations:** None — the override only shapes model
generation kwargs for the job's own execution; it adds no tool, network
or config surface. It rides the same `request_context` channel the
executor already uses for `approval_level`.

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter runs 29 cron jobs, 21 of them pure pipeline tasks. Today a
job can only follow the agent's global thinking setting:

- Turning thinking off to save tokens/latency requires creating a
  separate lightweight agent per job and repointing `agent_id` — error
  prone at scale and explicitly rejected by the reporter.
- Keeping thinking on means every scheduled run pays the full reasoning
  chain (measured 20 s – 9.5 min per call).

After this change a job opts in directly: `off` for pipeline jobs,
`inherit` (default, fully back-compatible) for everything else, or an
explicit effort level for jobs that genuinely need deep reasoning.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/app/crons/models.py`:

- `JobRuntimeSpec` gains `thinking_level: Literal["inherit", "off",
  "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"]`, default
  `"inherit"`. Existing jobs validate unchanged and keep the agent's
  setting.
- The field reuses the agent-level value space instead of the
  issue-proposed `off/inherit/enabled` triple: the thinking machinery
  resolves a concrete preference against each model's control surface
  (`ThinkingLevel` has no provider-independent "on" — the wire mapping
  differs per protocol). Sharing one vocabulary keeps a single meaning

  and an explicit effort level expresses "force thinking on".

  carries it in `request_context["thinking_level"]`, next to the

  request payload as before.

- New `request_thinking_override()` reads that request-context key,
  accepting dict and object requests and both the direct and the
  nested-under-`meta` context forms (the same shapes
  `request_model_override` already supports). Absent and `"inherit"`
  values mean "no override".
- `apply_chat_model_settings()` accepts an optional
  `request_preference` and resolves the final thinking with the
  precedence its docstring already promises: request > session >
  agent defaults. A request override wins over a session preference;
  with no override, session and agent behavior are byte-identical to
  before. The override lands on the per-request agent snapshot taken

prs.title: feat(console): preview docx, xlsx and pptx files in the file drawer
prs.body:
## Description

The Console file drawer only previews images, PDF, Markdown, HTML and CSV, so `.docx` / `.xlsx` / `.pptx` files that agents produce show "Preview is unavailable" and have to be downloaded to be read.

This adds a read-only, client-side preview for those three formats:

- **docx** – converted to HTML with [mammoth](https://github.com/mwilliamson/mammoth.js) (new dependency, BSD-2), sanitised with DOMPurify (scripts, event handlers, inline styles and live links removed) and shown with the existing Markdown typography.
- **xlsx** – read directly from the zip container with the already-bundled `jszip` (no spreadsheet engine added). Shared/inline strings, numbers, booleans and date-formatted cells are resolved; each sheet gets a tab; rows/columns are capped at 500 × 50 (same limits as CSV) with a note showing the real size.
- **pptx** – slide text in presentation order (resolved through `presentation.xml`, not file names), with a note that layout/images/charts need the download.

The parsing code is in `officeDocument.ts` and is imported lazily, so mammoth/jszip land in their own chunk (confirmed in a production `vite build`) and only load when an Office file is opened. Files over 25 MB, corrupt archives and failed downloads fall back to the existing "preview unavailable" message. Legacy `.doc` / `.xls` / `.ppt` are unchanged.

New UI strings are added to all seven locale files. `vitest` is aliased to mammoth's browser build so tests run the same entry point Vite bundles.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8404

**Security Considerations:** Document HTML is untrusted, so it goes through DOMPurify with `href`, `target`, `style` and `<style>` removed before `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; xlsx/pptx content is rendered as plain text nodes only. Files are fetched with the existing authenticated blob loader.

prs.title: fix(auth): don't skip auth for loopback peers forwarding proxy headers
prs.body:
Fixes #8695

## Description

`AuthMiddleware._should_skip_auth()` skips token validation when the resolved client IP is in `security.allow_no_auth_hosts` (default `127.0.0.1`, `::1`). `_resolve_client_ip()` only honours `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-IP` when the TCP peer is in `security.trusted_proxies`, which is empty by default. Behind a same-host reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy, 1Panel) the resolved IP is therefore the proxy's own `127.0.0.1`, and the loopback defense-in-depth check passes too because the peer really is loopback. Every proxied request was treated as a local CLI request and skipped auth.

In the loopback branch of `_should_skip_auth()`, the skip is now refused when the peer is not a configured trusted proxy and the request carries `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP` or `Forwarded`. This is the first fix suggested in the issue. Direct loopback requests without proxy headers (the CLI path) still skip auth, and a deployment that lists its proxy in `trusted_proxies` resolves the real client IP as before.

This is a narrower change than #2840, which removes the localhost bypass altogether; it does not conflict with it.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8695

**Security Considerations:** Closes an auth bypass in the default config behind a same-host reverse proxy. A local client that sends one of those headers itself now has to authenticate; no other request path changes.

prs.title: fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes the **run-cleanup half** of #8173: a chat run whose completion callback hangs or is cancelled never releases its entry in `TaskTracker._runs`, so the run stays `running` forever.

### Root cause

`TaskTracker._producer` clears its `_runs` entry and pushes the end-of-stream sentinel at the end of a `finally` block, *after* awaiting the `on_finished` completion callback. Two paths meant that cleanup never completed:

1. **The callback hangs.** `on_finished` is `ChatManager.mark_chat_finished`, which persists a completion marker under a lock shared with ~24 other manager methods. Lock contention or a stalled repo suspends the producer task *inside its own `finally`*. The task is then not done **and** the entry is still registered, so every status reader reports `running` — workspace reload is blocked and inbound messages are dropped with HTTP 409.
2. **The producer is cancelled mid-callback.** `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the `except Exception` guard and skips cleanup entirely, leaving subscriber streams without their sentinel.

### The fix

- Run the callback through `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...))` bounded by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT`, so a hung callback is logged and given up on rather than holding the run open.
- Move the cleanup into a nested `finally` so it always runs.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8173

Deliberately *not* `Fixes` — see the scope note below.

### Scope — what this does **not** fix

This addresses the cleanup leak only. The other items from #8173 are **not** implemented here: the post-spawn connection health probe, the idle watchdog, `force` semantics on the reload/disable-enable paths, and in-channel hints for `/new` and `/stop` on backends that do not support them. Those are larger design questions and I would rather land the narrow fix first.

Note that the wedge is now **bounded** by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT` rather than eliminated: the run stays `running` while the callback runs, because `test_attach_or_start_reports_completion_before_becoming_idle` pins that ordering deliberately (it asserts `get_status == "running"` from inside the callback). Reordering the pop ahead of the callback would break that contract.

### What the new tests cover

New `tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py` (6 tests) covers a hung callback, a callback that raises, a callback that raises `TimeoutError`, a producer cancelled mid-callback, and `request_stop` against a slow callback. Waits are event-based rather than fixed sleeps.

Against unmodified source these fail on behavioural assertions (`run entry survived a hung completion callback`, etc.), not on import or attribute errors.

### Security Considerations

Not applicable — no change to channel auth, credentials, or config handling.

## Evidence

Verification is a real failure on unmodified source followed by the **same command** against the patched tree. Base is `5c56644a` (`main`), patch is `e2b7b8be`.

**1. Unmodified baseline — the new tests genuinely fail.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_hung_completion_callback_does_not_block_new_messages
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_completion_callback_timeout_is_logged_not_raised
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_cancellation_during_callback_still_clears_the_run
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_request_stop_with_a_slow_callback_does_not_wedge_the_run
4 failed, 1 passed in 8.32s
```

**2. Same command with the patch — all green.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
.......................                                                  [100%]
23 passed in 0.49s
```

**3. Full `tests/unit/app` with the patch — no regression.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app
3118 passed, 1 skipped, 12 warnings in 58.77s
```

One caveat worth stating plainly: the baseline run pins the module source with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at a pristine checkout. The venv's editable install points at the patched worktree, so simply `cd`-ing to the unmodified tree would still have imported the patched code and produced a false green — that happened on the first attempt and the baseline above is from the corrected invocation.

prs.title: fix(console): repair CJK emphasis boundaries in chat Markdown
prs.body:
## Description

### What Problem This Solves

The chat message body renders Markdown through the vendor `Markdown` component, whose parser follows CommonMark's emphasis "flanking" rules. Those rules classify CJK sentence punctuation as Unicode punctuation, and CJK text is written without inter-word spaces. A closing `**` that sits immediately after CJK punctuation and immediately before CJK text is therefore judged "not a valid closer", and the raw markers leak into the bubble:

```
**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。
```

The reader literally sees `**没有改动任何设置。**` instead of bold text. This is a common pattern in Chinese/Japanese/Korean replies, so it shows up frequently.

### Fix

Add `normalizeCjkEmphasis` in `console/src/utils/markdownCjk.ts`, which moves the trailing CJK punctuation run outside the delimiter (`**中文。**后` becomes `**中文**。后`), and apply it to the deferred content inside `AssistantMarkdown` — the shared deferred Markdown renderer used by host bubbles — before the text reaches `<Markdown>`.

`AssistantMarkdown` has two render paths (plain, and plugin-backed stable code blocks); the normalization is applied once to `displayContent` and both paths consume it, while the streaming comparison keeps using the raw deferred value.

The repair is deliberately conservative and display-oriented:

- only `*`, `_`, `**`, `__`, `***`, `___` are considered;
- only `。！？；：，、…` plus full-width trailing closers (`”’」』】》〉）〕］`) are moved;
- only when the delimiter is immediately followed by Han / Hiragana / Katakana / Hangul;
- fenced, indented and inline code, escaped delimiters, CRLF endings and unrelated unfinished Markdown are preserved verbatim.

The helper is a pure, idempotent string transform, so applying it to a streaming (partial) value is safe — the result converges to the same text once the message completes.

## Evidence

Rebased onto `main` (`27d22cd1`); the deferred-rendering block this originally patched was moved into `AssistantMarkdown` by the host-bubble refactor, so the patch now lives there.

- `npx vitest run src/utils/markdownCjk.test.ts src/pages/Chat/AssistantMarkdown.test.tsx src/pages/Chat/HostBubbles.render.test.tsx` -> **37 passed** (3 files; 15 of them new in `markdownCjk.test.ts`).
- `tsc -b --noEmit` -> exit 0, no diagnostics.
- `npx eslint` on the three changed files -> exit 0.
- `npx prettier --check` on the three changed files -> "All matched files use Prettier code style!".
- Direct checks:
  - `normalizeCjkEmphasis("**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。")` -> `"**没有改动任何设置**。所有内容保持不变。"`
  - `normalizeCjkEmphasis("**重点**后接中文")` -> unchanged
  - fenced code block containing `**代码。**后` -> unchanged
  - `**内容。**latin` -> unchanged (follower must be CJK)

## Notes

- Targeted, display-oriented repair rather than a general Markdown parser; ASCII punctuation and non-CJK followers are out of scope by design.
- Related: CommonMark discussion `commonmark/commonmark-spec#650` on CJK-friendly emphasis.

---

> **Note:** this supersedes #8068, which the PR Spam Gate auto-closed on 2026-10-01 (author had >10 open PRs at the time). Same branch, same diff; GitHub refused to reopen the original, so this is a fresh PR.

prs.title: feat(plugins): support CLI commands and extension points
prs.body:
## Description

Adds plugin CLI commands to the existing Click command tree and connects them to the plugin registry, dependency checks, and resource lifecycle.

### 1) Key CLI features

- Register root commands, nested commands, or complete Click groups through `ctx.register_cli(CliSpec(...))`. Native commands retain priority.
- Installed, enabled plugins expose their commands. Disable/uninstall removes them. Core commands remain available without plugins.
- Plugin commands run without starting the App. Root help uses static declarations; selecting a command checks dependencies and loads its implementation.
- Invocation cleanup completes before resources and source leases are released, including after Ctrl-C. No dedicated session thread or process is added.
- Core `models`, `channels`, and `doctor` commands discover plugin contributions. Unavailable implementations retain their saved configuration without becoming executable.

### 2) Supporting plugin-core changes — review requested

The design separates application declarations, capability registration, driver execution, and resource ownership, following OS concepts.

#### 2.1 Shared registration, independent receiver execution

Previously, `entry.descriptor` and `entry.backend` were mutually exclusive. They can now coexist under one plugin instance and rollback ledger.

Simplified flow:

    App loading:
        register static channel metadata
        register lightweight public contributions

    Plugin CLI:
        load the public entry and selected command

    Enabled workspace receiver:
        start the existing channel worker

This lets a channel plugin also provide CLI or client Tools without requiring its receiver to run. Global plugin disablement still blocks execution. Public registration failure rolls back the combined registration; per-capability failure isolation is not implemented.

#### 2.2 Capability dependencies and invocation side effects

Package-wide dependencies remain supported. Named `optional_dependencies` and per-contribution `requires` distinguish lightweight operations from SDK-dependent operations:

    status.requires = []
    send.requires = ["transport"]

    install/update/repair:
        prepare packages referenced by declared capabilities

    selected command:
        check requires -> build implementation -> execute -> clean up

This prevents an unrelated SDK prerequisite from gating a lightweight command. Authors must keep the public entry lightweight and defer SDK imports themselves.

CLI execution also skips installation callbacks and backend provision commits. It reuses registration and runtime cleanup without rewriting existing Tool/Skill configuration.

#### 2.3 Update: reduce plugin CLI startup and cleanup overhead

Cleanup previously imported memory/model implementations just to inspect resource ownership. The existing memory registry now lives in a lightweight module, preserving public imports and the shared registry instance.

    Before: cleanup -> public memory API -> memory/model imports
    After:  cleanup -> lightweight ownership registry

Dependency observation now retains only file paths matching imported modules while still validating every RECORD row. Existing dependency checks, cache invalidation, and ownership protection remain in place.

For the same local Hello command, median peak RSS fell **214.77 → 193.69 MiB (-21.08 MiB)** and runtime fell **2.656 → 2.385 s (-10.2%)**.

The fixed plugin still uses **17.86 MiB / 0.591 s more** than the native reference. This includes shared-environment inspection and loader/SDK setup. Runtime environment inspection remains a current design tradeoff; reducing it further requires the environment-management work described below.

### 3) Reviewer decisions and TODOs

- [ ] Approve version choices: proposed SDK `1.1.0`, new API `since` values, and channel versioning/schema changes.
  - Channel descriptor schema v3 adds named `requires`; schema v2 remains supported.
  - Review compatibility and migration policy. The worker IPC protocol version is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(chat): add append-only session storage, paginated history and native Turn forks
prs.body:
## Description

Long conversations previously depended on mutable session snapshots and loading large history windows. That made historical Turn forks, runtime recovery, and reconnect behavior difficult to keep consistent. This branch introduces durable per-session SQLite history with append-only facts and rebuildable projections, and bounds the Console's history and replay work.

This draft covers the complete branch, including:

- Store message/content facts and immutable context revisions separately from current message/runtime projections. Rebuild projections without rewriting historical facts; reuse state component references for usage-only revisions and avoid redundant block events.
- Migrate legacy JSON sessions and history databases, preserve available historical messages, reconstruct legacy runtime where possible, and retain provider session/Turn mappings.
- Fork completed Turns with their historical runtime boundary. Codex/Qoder branches use native provider interfaces and stored Turn mappings rather than rebuilding third-party context. Failed native restoration/reset must not silently create a fresh context.
- Add stable history pagination, bounded rendering, message-directory navigation, streaming/reconnect replay, and safe session switching/deletion.
- Integrate storage with clear/new, compact, dump/load, Scroll/Recall, cloning, backup, checkpoints, statistics, and PawApp/SDK session access. Preserve reset and checkpoint restoration semantics; roll back failed/cancelled compaction.

## Issues addressed

- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/3915 — measured virtual rendering, incremental history loading, scroll anchoring, and bottom-follow behavior.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/3923 — bounded Console history reads and windowed rendering address the full-history/full-DOM paths. This does not claim a measured memory result for the reporter's exact dataset or include all optional bundle-size suggestions.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8134 — durable display history is independent of the model's compacted context.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/6542 — completed turns persist their final messages and session state. This covers the real-time archival proposal, not zero loss of uncommitted output after a forced process termination or external notebook synchronization.

## PRs superseded after merge

The following PRs can be closed manually as superseded after this PR merges. This is a functional replacement assessment, not a claim that every change from those PRs was incorporated:

- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7361 — history pagination and virtual rendering.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7542 — access to pre-compaction history through paginated durable transcripts. Retention changes are outside this PR's scope and are not a prerequisite for replacing the pagination implementation.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/6704 — use the completed-Turn Fork implementation, including the latest completed turn, rather than adding a second whole-session fork path.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8091 — route-driven active-chat tracking also covers sidebar navigation and cached sessions.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/1481 — metadata updates exclude messages without mutating the caller's session.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/803 — per-agent last-chat persistence and route restoration replace the older global storage-key approach.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/1489 — backend cancellation, cancellation-state persistence, and history/reconnect handling replace the older cancel-endpoint approach.

Some of these behaviors are inherited from main and retained by this branch; they are not all new contributions of this PR. PR #7413 / issue #7410 are already addressed by main's #8212, and the workspace-owned HistoryStore work in #8471 is superseded by #8482 and subsequent maintenance. Those are independent cleanup items, not closure claims of #8532.

**Security Considerations:** Session ownership and active-session deletion checks remain part of history access. This PR does not include local databases, conversation exports, screenshots, profiling dumps, or environment credentials. Provider contexts remain provider-owned.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactoring
- [x] Breaking change (session storage representation changes; legacy data is imported)
- [ ] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console
- [x] Channels (Console streaming/reconnect)

- [ ] Full default test configuration is green (see known failures below)
- [ ] Documentation published in this repository
- [ ] Ready for review / merge

## Testing

Focused implementation-audit validation on **2026-11-06**, against HEAD **95bc9c73e8108a7645332087149c209d56a2a14c**:

- Frontend: **111 passed** across 10 files covering measured/history windows, route gates, bottom follow, large-session handling, ownership, transitions, initialization, and replay parsing.
- Backend: **207 passed** across the selected persistence, migration, projection-rebuild, Fork/catalog, replay, task, and lifecycle tests. This includes the regression test from #7413 run from a temporary file, without adding it to this PR.

Earlier branch validation retained for context (not rerun as a full suite at the HEAD above; groups overlap and should not be summed as unique coverage):

- TypeScript noEmit, changed-file pre-commit checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Frontend full single-worker run: **657 files passed / 2 failed**; **8475 tests passed / 1 failed / 2 expected failures / 9 skipped**. This was not a green default full run.
  - JobDrawer JSON validation did not display its error within `waitFor`; the unchanged complete file passed on isolated retry (**29 passed**).

Earlier behavior checks (not repeated in the 2026-11-06 focused audit):

- A database generated by the previous implementation containing four `block.committed` events was rebuilt twice: messages, runtime, and original events remained unchanged.
- Eight database command scenarios and sixteen Fork boundaries verified state preservation, with Codex/Qoder native reset failure protection probes.

prs.title: fix(channels): accept WeChat send receipts that only carry message_id
prs.body:
Part of #8709 (bug 3 only: successful sends reported as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`). Bugs 1, 2 and 4 are not addressed here.

## Description

A successful iLink `sendmessage` response is HTTP 200 with a JSON object that contains only `message_id`. `WeChatPlatform._check_result` treated any body without `ret` or `errcode` as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`. `send_parts` runs that check after each fragment, so the first accepted send aborted the rest of the reply and the channel reported the delivery as unknown.

When `ret` or `errcode` is present, those fields still decide the result, including when `message_id` is also present: a non-integer status stays `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`, `ret == -2` stays `CONTEXT_TOKEN_INVALID`, and any other non-zero `ret` or `errcode` stays `PLATFORM_SEND_FAILED`. A body with neither status field is a success only when `message_id` is non-empty. An empty `message_id`, a missing one, or a non-dict body stays `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`.

This change is only that result check (bug 3 in the report). It does not change account custody, plugin recovery, or model `generate_kwargs`.

**Related Issue:** Part of #8709 (bug 3)

**Security Considerations:** None. The check does not read credentials or log the response. A non-zero `ret` or `errcode` is still a failure when `message_id` is present.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation

- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [ ] Official channel changes are covered in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` (startup, shutdown and message delivery)
- [ ] Shared host/process changes are covered in `test_channel_host.py` / `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py`
- [ ] Console changes retain the built-in contract checks in `tests/contract/channels/`

## Reproduction

The platform call is `POST /ilink/bot/sendmessage`. A successful body observed for that call is `{"message_id": "test-123"}` with no `ret` and no `errcode`. No live iLink call is required: the same object is passed to `_check_result`, and `send_parts` is driven with a stub client that returns that object for two text parts.

On the current main branch the first object raises `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN` and the second text part is never sent. `{"ret": 0}` and `{"errcode": 0}` stay success. `{"message_id": "test-123", "ret": 1}`, `{"message_id": "test-123", "errcode": 4}`, and `{"message_id": "test-123", "ret": -2}` stay failures.

## Testing

`pytest tests/unit/channels/test_wechat_send_result.py -q --noconftest`

Before the change: 2 failed, 3 passed. `test_message_id_only_is_a_successful_send` and `test_message_id_receipt_does_not_drop_the_next_part` raise `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`. After the change: 5 passed. The three cases that were already green stay green: zero `ret`/`errcode`, status errors that must still win beside `message_id`, and bodies with no status and no message id.

## Evidence

```text
pytest tests/unit/channels/test_wechat_send_result.py -q --noconftest
.....
5 passed
```

Before the change, the same command reported:

prs.title: fix(desktop): persist early startup errors and show native error dialogs
prs.body: ## Description QwenPaw Desktop can fail before the main window exists. Some of these early startup failures currently leave no visible window, no actionable message, and no log entry. The regular desktop logger is only initialized during Tauri setup, while earlier startup errors were only written to `stderr`, which Windows release builds do not show. This PR adds startup diagnostics that start at the very beginning of the desktop shell's startup path: - Write an independent startup log before Tauri builds the app. - Primary location: the app's local data directory, under `logs/startup/`. - Fallback: the system temporary directory. - Each process gets its own log file, so concurrent launches do not overwrite each other. - Record startup stages, the failing operation, relevant paths, OS errors, the error source chain, and a diagnostic backtrace. - Flush and sync fatal errors to disk before showing a dialog. - Show a native error dialog for desktop startup failures, with the failed stage, the reason, and the saved log location. - Windows uses `MessageBoxW`. In our Windows testing, the task-dialog path shortened long log paths in the middle (e.g. `C:\Use...\startup-xxx.log`), so users could not see where the log was; `MessageBoxW` displayed the full path. - macOS and Linux use `rfd`. - Report errors returned from Tauri setup. Tauri runs setup inside the event loop and panics on setup errors, so these failures previously bypassed the normal `build()` error path. They are now logged, shown, and followed by exit code `1`. - Record `Desktop ready` only after setup completes successfully. - Add path and operation context to early errors in installation coordination, shared-runtime directory setup, and installer process inspection. - Never show a dialog for `--agent-host` failures; they are logged only. The update admission and installer waiting rules are unchanged. While an installer is still running, a newly launched desktop process still waits quietly, as before. The only addition is that the wait start, the end, and the elapsed time are now recorded in the startup log. **Related Issue:** Relates to #8616 **Security Considerations:** - The startup log does not dump environment variables, `runtime.json`, runtime tokens, user configuration, or command lines. - Logs are written under the current user's local app data directory, or the system temporary directory as a fallback. On Unix-like systems, new log files are created with `0600` permissions. - Old startup logs are cleaned up only when they match this feature's log naming pattern and are no longer in use. Symlinked log entries are not followed. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [ ] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [ ] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy Affected area not listed above: desktop shell (`console/src-tauri`). ## Checklist - [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [ ] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ## Testing Commands run on Windows: ```powershell pre-commit run --files ` console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml ` console/src-tauri/Cargo.lock ` console/src-tauri/src/lib.rs ` console/src-tauri/src/backend/runtime.rs ` console/src-tauri/src/updates/coordination.rs ` console/src-tauri/src/updates/windows.rs ` console/src-tauri/src/startup_diagnostics.rs cargo test --locked --manifest-path console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib cargo clippy --locked --manifest-path console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets ``` I also built a Windows release desktop shell from this change and ran it in Windows Sandbox. To match the packaged build, I used `STATIC_VCRUNTIME=true` and `tauri/custom-protocol`. The backend and other bundled resources were copied from an existing beta.4 installation. Scenarios checked: 1. **Failure before any window is created.** I made the working directory path an existing file. 2. **Background supervisor failure** (`--agent-host`). 3. **Default startup log directory not writable.** 4. **Tauri setup failure.** I made the regular desktop log directory path a file. 5. **Normal startup.** 6. **Launch while an installer handoff is still active**, then let the installer exit. ## Evidence ```text pre-commit run --files check toml...............................................................Passed detect private key.......................................................Passed trim trailing whitespace.................................................Passed (other hooks skipped: no matching files) ``` ```text cargo test --locked --manifest-path console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib running 66 tests test result: ok. 66 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out ``` ```text cargo clippy --locked --manifest-path console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets exit code: 0 No warnings in the changed files. ``` Windows Sandbox results: | Scenario | Result | | --- | --- | | Failure before window creation | Native error dialog shown. It includes the stage, the full path with Chinese characters and spaces, `os error 183`, and the full log path. The log was saved before the dialog closed. Exit code `1`. | | Background supervisor failure | No window shown. The failure is written to the startup log. Exit code `1`. | | Default log directory unavailable | The log is written to the temporary directory, together with the reason the primary directory failed. | | Tauri setup failure | Native error dialog shown with stage `Initialize desktop logging and backend attachment`. The log is saved to the fallback directory. Exit code `1`. `Desktop ready` is not recorded. | | Normal startup | Main UI rendered. Backend ready. No error dialog shown. `Desktop ready` is recorded after setup completes. | | Active installer handoff | No extra prompt or window while waiting. The wait is recorded in the startup log. The main window appears after the installer exits, and the stale handoff record is removed. | Screenshots: - Tauri setup failure dialog - Early startup failure dialog ## Additional Notes - This PR improves startup observability and gives users actionable failure information. It does not claim to fix the unconfirmed root cause reported in #8616. - For the setup-failure case, the stage is reported, but the regular log plugin's own error does not include the target directory path.

prs.title: feat(creator): release 2.0.5 with safe assets and audio updates
prs.body:
## Description

Release QwenPaw Creator **2.0.4 → 2.0.5**, including only work completed **after the previous upstream release** at `d09c34f6c` (merged 2026-11-02 from fork head `df983dd5d`). The previous release's non-DashScope transport, probe-origin hardening, and medium-neutral visual guidance are already upstream; this Description covers their new follow-ups and the newly merged asset/audio work, not a repetition of the 2.0.4 notes.

**Fork sync completed first.** This PR comes directly from **`xuanrui-L:dev/creator`** at `b5b555c272ff1aa14796d521148e06f1d171fab5`. Before opening it, the latest upstream `main`, `14b02c597aee1b314f9bd12f8813e01543c3c328`, was merged through https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/251 using a **merge commit**. The previous upstream squash and its fork head have byte-identical plugin trees, and upstream has made no later plugin edits. Eight squash-history conflicts were resolved against the exact prior fork release head; the complete integrated tree equals the clean reference merge `012c71c1440c7d660f4c4c2d418343a41d2971c9`.

**Scope: 52 Creator plugin files, +8,870 / −518.** The entire plugin tree is unchanged from the pre-sync fork head `55f972ba5`; every file outside `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/` equals the recorded upstream baseline. No host application, Console, other-plugin, dependency declaration, or CI/release workflow changes are contributed by this upstream PR.

### What's new since 2.0.4

- **Source asset deletion and content reuse.** The asset library now offers confirmed deletion and removes unreferenced source, thumbnail, native-media, and intelligence files along with their metadata. Shared files remain protected. References from both active timelines and snapshots block ordinary deletion, with structured `ASSET_IN_USE` details. A separately confirmed force-delete can detach references that an element can survive without and mark affected element/final outputs stale; required audio/edit or sole-content references remain blocking. Force deletion also changes affected snapshots, so it does not promise that deleted inputs can later be restored from history. Duplicate local content reuses an existing compatible, healthy source version instead of creating another file/identity, and the UI reports reuse. Post-delete refresh failures no longer masquerade as deletion failures, while late responses cannot rebind a different project or clear a newly selected asset.
- **Cancellation and conversation recovery stay consistent.** Deleting a source cancels its in-process specialist and standalone observation, source-memory, and video-reader workers as well as settling persisted task state. Admission, initialization, repeated cancellation, and shutdown paths share protected terminal cleanup so work is not left falsely running or allowed to publish a result for a deleted source. Agent Dock avoids cascading scroll during event replay while honoring manual scroll-up; project changes replay full event history rather than truncating terminal-state evidence, and manual older-history loading remains usable when SSE is unhealthy.
- **Qwen-Audio 3.1 TTS and voice-correct narration reuse.** Register the 3.1 Flash/Plus models with model-specific voice lists, correct the 3.0 voices and Plus entry, and expose provider availability to the model picker. The unsupported non-realtime instruct model is no longer advertised. Explicit invalid voice requests still fail before synthesis; a stale deployment default resolves to a valid voice for the selected model. Synthesis and narration reuse use the same resolved model/voice identity, avoiding another paid generation when a retry can reuse existing audio. Agent-facing voice lists are bounded rather than dumping the entire table. Connection probes distinguish read-only voice listings from actual audio evidence.
- **Aliyun Token Plan follows its actual media channels.** Image/video reference inputs use shared, bounded inline-image downscaling instead of an unavailable temporary-upload route; image edit/translation remains explicitly unsupported on this path. ASR production and probing share one route selector, including the Qwen-Audio family. Because Creator's normal source transcription consumes local audio and Token Plan requires public audio URLs, Token Plan is removed from the ASR picker and local-audio configurations get actionable refusals. TTS uses the plan's WebSocket synthesis endpoint and its supported model; the endpoint is bound per synthesis instance rather than mutating the SDK's process-global URL. The plan's TTS connection test synthesizes a short sample rather than calling unsupported voice-management routes. Grounding no longer rejects the plan's Responses search channel at save time, and a fallback LLM roster remains available when the host registry has no configured plan models.

**Version and dependencies.** The already merged fork version bump is included: `plugin.json`, `ui/package.json`, and both package-lock root-version fields all read **2.0.5**. The host minimum remains **2.1.0**. No Python or npm dependency changes are introduced relative to current upstream. Publication remains governed by the unchanged version-driven main-branch workflow; no immutable artifact is being overwritten.

**Related Issue:** Release follow-up to https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8529. Included source changes: https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/240, https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/242, https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/249, and the version bump https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/246.

**Security Considerations:** No credentials, user projects, generated media, or runtime directories are committed. Deletion checks actual references, protects shared files, and uses existing project/path validation; force-delete is explicit and does not bypass indispensable references. Provider endpoint changes remain local to the configured request rather than leaking across later synthesis calls. Real provider connection tests, including Token Plan TTS, may consume provider quota; this release validation made **no paid-provider calls**. Browser testing used only a synthetic project in a temporary data root. Existing host authentication and secure download boundaries are unchanged.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

- [ ] Documentation (website)

- [x] Scripts / Deploy — plugin version metadata only
- [x] Creator app plugin (`plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/`)

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes — not claimed; every applicable hook passed locally over the complete release delta.
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks — no auto-fixes were needed.
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass — 2,372 backend tests and 422 UI tests.
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed) — model/prompt guidance and bilingual UI descriptions are updated; no website documentation change is required.
- [x] Ready for review

Channel-specific checklist: not applicable; this upstream diff contains no host channel changes.

## Testing

Tested the synchronized tree in a fresh **Python 3.11.12** environment with its own upstream host test extras (`agentscope==2.0.10`) and Creator requirements. UI used the committed lockfile. Local Node was **25.9.0**; CI uses upstream `.nvmrc` (**22.23.4**), so local/CI version parity is not claimed.

```bash
# From Creator backend on this macOS machine:
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 \
QWENPAW_CREATOR_MOTION_BROWSER="/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" \
  python -m pytest tests -q --timeout=120

# From Creator UI:
npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build

# From repository root:
git diff --name-only -z upstream/main HEAD | xargs -0 uvx --python 3.11 pre-commit run --files
git diff --check upstream/main HEAD
python scripts/pack/generate_plugin_metadata.py \
  --plugins-root plugins --dist dist/plugins \

```

The initial backend run failed in HTTPX client initialization because this machine's inherited `NO_PROXY` included the bracketed IPv6 entry `[::1]`, which HTTPX parsed as an invalid port. A test-process-only normalization made client initialization and the entire suite pass. No source, assertion, system proxy setting, or provider security check was changed to suppress those failures. The supported system-Chrome override covered caption rendering; the separate bundled-Chromium motion-clip test remained skipped.

**Browser behavior proof:** a live Vite UI used real asset API routes against an isolated temporary project. Uploading identical synthetic text under two request IDs returned `reused=false` then `reused=true` with the same asset version and one source. Cancelling deletion kept the card; confirming deletion removed the card/selection, source/file index entries, and the actual file on disk. The TTS model dropdown rendered Qwen-Audio 3.1 Flash and Plus from the backend capability API without uncaught JavaScript errors. The harness bypassed model-config binding and disabled Agent upload notifications, so no model was invoked; session/conversation reads returned expected 404s because no Agent session was started. This focused asset/settings smoke is **not** a claim of full production-runtime or paid-provider E2E coverage. Temporary servers and the browser were stopped afterwards.

## Evidence

Results on integration commit `8c5df425b`; the merged PR head `b5b555c27` has the exact same tree:

```text

Browser/API: duplicate-content reuse, cancel/delete, actual disk cleanup,
  and Qwen-Audio 3.1 model-picker visibility verified
ZIP: 391 entries; CRC, manifest entries, required resources,
  runtime exclusions and four matching 2.0.5 fields PASS
ZIP SHA256: ac51de94210c5fade25e91d4db1fd4446f145ce38361d4dc4c99c6bb1a9dd76f
```

prs.title: fix(wechat): prevent false bot conflicts and isolate workspace state
prs.body:
## Description

WeChat could return `ACCOUNT_IN_USE` during startup or Console QR login because the host treated saved credentials and shared file paths as evidence of a running Bot. This could happen with a disabled channel or with a single agent whose workspace ID differed in case from its profile key.

- Check for duplicate Bot credentials against active runtime leases. Disabled channels and shared token file paths no longer trigger a conflict on their own.
- Check the new credential when Console QR authorization is confirmed. If it is in use, stop polling and show the conflict. On successful save, release the QR session lease before scheduling the agent reload.
- Default the Bot Token file and reply context cache to `<workspace>/wechat/`. Explicit `bot_token_file` paths remain supported. Users who relied on the old root-level token file can point `bot_token_file` to it or scan again. Incoming messages rebuild the reply context cache.

Fixes #8693. Addresses the WeChat startup failure reported as Bug 1 in #8709.

## Testing

- Python regression suite covering WeChat, the channel host, configuration, and CLI.
- Console tests covering the channel drawer and QR authorization.
- Isolated QwenPaw instance with a simulated iLink service.

## Evidence

```text
./scripts/check-channels.sh wechat
14 passed
All channel checks passed.

Python regression suite
282 passed, 17 skipped

Console tests
3 test files passed, 93 tests passed
```

With a duplicate token in a disabled agent's config, the Console QR endpoint returned HTTP 200. Confirming and saving the QR authorization wrote the new token to `agent.json`, and the reloaded worker used it to poll iLink. A separate worker-initiated login wrote its token to the workspace's `wechat/` directory.

prs.title: feat(console): support runtime base-path deployment
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8714.

Related context only: #1853, #8177, and #8316. This PR does not reopen, comment on, or close those older issues or pull requests.

Add an optional `QWENPAW_BASE_PATH` runtime setting for serving the standard prebuilt Console and API below a reverse-proxy prefix such as `/app/qwenpaw/web`.

#8316 covers custom builds through `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME`. This PR covers the complementary runtime case: pip/uv/Docker users should not need to rebuild the Console or have a proxy rewrite minified JavaScript. Uvicorn `root_path` alone cannot solve the absolute URLs already present in that prebuilt output.

### What changed

- Add a validated base-path ASGI middleware using standard `root_path` semantics for HTTP, mounted static files, and WebSockets. The bare prefix redirects to a trailing slash; requests outside the prefix return 404.
- Inject only two explicit deployment values into `index.html`: its `<base href>` and a JSON-encoded runtime prefix. JavaScript and CSS response bodies are not rewritten.
- Build default Console entry and module URLs relative to the document base; resolve public assets, API calls, router/login navigation, and chunk-readiness probes against the same runtime prefix.
- Preserve the existing root and `/console` behavior when the setting is empty or `/`. Existing build-time `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME` and desktop behavior remain separate.
- Document runtime proxy configuration in English and Chinese. Proxies must preserve rather than strip the configured prefix.

The current login flow uses a Bearer token in `localStorage`, so no authentication-cookie path change is needed.

prs.title: fix(media): downscale oversized images and mark stripped media as omitted
prs.body:
## Scope

Type: A (single-point fix) — media handling on the freezing, request-normalization
and agent-recovery paths. No public API or configuration changes.

## What Problem This Solves

An oversized image is sent verbatim and rejected by the provider; the recovery
then strips every image from the request while the tool text still says
`Image loaded: x.png`, so the model answers as if it had seen an image it
never received.

## Description

Two defects on the media path share one real-world trigger: an agent loaded a
9000px-wide PNG through `view_image`, the provider rejected the payload
("You have uploaded an unsupported image"), and QwenPaw's recovery stripped
**every** image from the request. The model then answered from a tool result
that still read `Image loaded: timeline_states_48h.png` — it was told it had
seen an image it never received.

**1. Oversized images are downscaled on the request copy only**

`freeze_image_bytes` enforced the byte cap but never checked dimensions, so a
wide-but-lightweight PNG (line art, timeline charts) passed straight through
and was rejected downstream. Freezing now keeps the original bytes, and
`downscale_oversized_images` (`agents/utils/image_resize.py`) shrinks the
cloned request inside `normalize_messages_for_model_request`. History, memory
and any later explicit request for the same media keep full resolution.

The helper:

- keeps the source format when it can carry alpha, so a transparent WebP no
  longer becomes a multi-megabyte PNG;
- if the re-encoded payload still exceeds the byte limit, steps quality down
  and then halves the dimensions; if every attempt fails it returns the
  original bytes, never a larger payload;
- detects animation with `n_frames > 1` **before** resampling and passes it
  through untouched (GIF, animated WebP, APNG) instead of keeping only the
  first frame;
- applies `ImageOps.exif_transpose()` before `thumbnail()`, so a rotated JPEG
  is scaled along its displayed axes.

**2. Stripping media now leaves an explicit marker**

When only some blocks of a `tool_result` were stripped, the surviving text was
kept as-is — that is how the model ended up holding an "Image loaded" claim
with no image behind it. The blanket "this model supports no media" strip now
appends `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_PLACEHOLDER` to the surviving output, in the same
shape as its siblings (dict for 1.x blocks, block object for 2.0).

Targeted strips (audio / video / document / empty) are deliberate per-modality
decisions, so they keep their current output shape. This is a deliberate
behaviour change and is covered by an updated assertion in
`test_react_agent_media_strip.py::test_nested_media_in_tool_result_stripped`.

## Evidence

Before / after, same input (9000x60 PNG):

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stored message | 9000x60 | 9000x60 (unchanged) |
| request copy | 9000x60, sent verbatim | 8192x55 |
| provider payload | rejected as unsupported | accepted |
| tool result text after strip | `Image loaded: x.png` | `Image loaded: x.png` + `[Media content removed - model does not support this media type]` |

Regression tests, grouped by the module they cover:

- `tests/unit/agents/utils/test_image_freezing.py` — an oversized image stays
  byte-identical after freezing; an in-limit image is not re-encoded.
- `tests/unit/agents/utils/test_image_resize.py` — oversized side is
  downscaled with the aspect ratio preserved; transparent WebP stays WebP with
  alpha; animated WebP and APNG keep every frame; EXIF orientation is applied
  before resizing; the normalizer shrinks the request copy while the stored
  message keeps its bytes.
- `tests/unit/agents/test_message_request_normalizer.py` — a partial strip
  yields the full output list `["Image loaded: a.png", placeholder]`; an
  all-media strip collapses to the placeholder string.

Checked the tests are not vacuous: with the `src/` changes stashed the same
files report 2 failed (freezing still downscales, normalizer does not
rescale), and pass again once restored.

## Follow-up direction

The other two halves of the same bug. They are deliberately left out because
both need an interface decision first, and neither is required for this fix:

- **Per-provider media capability table** (max side / max bytes / accepted
  formats). Today the limit is inferred from a 400 response; with a declared
  table the request could be shaped correctly instead of being repaired after
  a rejection. It touches provider registration and the formatters.
- **Rejection-site attribution.** If each image carried an id, a rejection
  could name the offending one, and the recovery could transcode and retry
  *that* image instead of stripping every image in the request.

Happy to open an issue with the exact failure shapes and take either item once
the owning layer is agreed.

## Test scope

- Target: `test_image_freezing.py`, `test_image_resize.py`,
  `test_message_request_normalizer.py` — 81 passed.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents -k "image or media or normalizer"` — 488
  passed, 3 skipped.
- Lint: `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — all hooks passed (black 23.3.0,
  mypy, pylint, flake8, add-trailing-comma, docstring-first, AST,
  private-key, encoding-pragma, trailing-whitespace).

prs.title: fix(providers): read a gateway-reported status from the error text
prs.body:
## Description

`extract_status_code()` reads a status from the exception's `status_code`, `code`, `response`, and `body`/`details` fields, and falls back to the message text for one narrow gateway format — `Streaming response failed: [503] ...`.

An OpenAI-compatible gateway that fails mid-stream can instead report the status only inside the message text, for example `status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)`. The OpenAI SDK raises a base `APIError` for such a response: no `status_code`, no `response`. The real status is present in the text, but the fallback does not recognise that shape, so `classify_model_error()` returns `unknown` — no same-model retry, no cross-model fallback, and the turn or scheduled job dies. The same upstream failure wrapped as a real HTTP 502 is `transient` and does fall back, so identical failures behave differently only because of how the gateway phrased them.

This adds one more narrow pattern for gateway error text, keeping the same deliberate narrowness the existing fallback documents: only `4xx`/`5xx` are read, so a success code quoted in a message (`expected status_code=200`) is never mistaken for a failure, and unrelated three-digit numbers in provider messages are still ignored.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8505

**Security Considerations:** None — this only affects how a provider error is classified, never what is sent to a provider.

prs.title: fix(scroll): recognize url-referenced media in tool-result folding
prs.body:
## Description

When a chat session accumulates enough turns to trigger context compression, historical completed tool results are inspected by `ScrollContextManager._tool_result_fold_candidates()` to collapse long or media-carrying results into compact pointer stubs (`[scroll folded] ...`).

Previously, `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` only checked for `source.get("type") == "base64"` or `source.type == "base64"`. URL-referenced media blocks (`source.type == "url"`), such as video, audio, or image outputs generated by `send_file_to_user` and similar tools, were not recognized as inline media. Consequently, these media tool results failed the `has_media` check and, having short text captions (<= 200 chars), were skipped by `_tool_result_fold_candidates()`.

As a result, uncollapsed media blocks were carried over across turns and re-spliced verbatim into rebuilt request payloads after compression. Subsequent model API requests failed repeatedly with errors such as `400: Video count 2 exceeds limit 1 per request`, permanently hanging the session for that channel.

This change extends `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` to recognize `source.type == "url"` with non-empty URL values for both dictionary-based and object-based sources.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8474

**Security Considerations:** None.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the issue happens

In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`:

```python
    @staticmethod
    def _tool_result_has_inline_media(block: Any) -> bool:
        ...
        for item in output:
            if ScrollContextManager._block_type(item) != "data":
                continue
            source = (
                item.get("source")
                if isinstance(item, dict)
                else getattr(item, "source", None)
            )
            if isinstance(source, dict):
                if source.get("type") == "base64" and source.get("data"):
                    return True
            elif getattr(source, "type", None) == "base64" and getattr(
                source,
                "data",
                None,
            ):
                return True
        return False
```

When a tool output provides a data block with a URL source (`source={"type": "url", "url": "https://..."}`), `_tool_result_has_inline_media` returned `False`.

In `_tool_result_fold_candidates`:

```python
    has_media = self._tool_result_has_inline_media(block)
    if (
        not has_media
        and self._tool_result_text_chars(block) <= _PRE_TRIM_MIN_CHARS
    ):
        continue
```

Because `has_media` was `False` and media tool results generally have little or no text characters (`<= 200`), the block was skipped and never folded. During context compression and payload rebuild, the raw media block remained in the active payload.

## The change

1. In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`, `_tool_result_has_inline_media` now also checks:
   - For dict sources: `source.get("type") == "url" and source.get("url")`
   - For object sources: `getattr(source, "type", None) == "url" and getattr(source, "url", None)`
2. In `tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py`:
   - Added `test_tool_result_has_inline_media_recognizes_url_sources` to test both base64 and URL sources across dict and object representations as well as negative cases.
   - Added `test_pressure_fold_recognizes_url_media_independently_of_text_length` to verify that tool results carrying URL media bypass the text length restriction and fold into pointer stubs under context pressure.

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

Verified with pytest on the scroll context manager suite:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py -k 'test_tool_result_has_inline_media_recognizes_url_sources or test_pressure_fold_recognizes_url_media_independently_of_text_length' -v

======================= 2 passed, 83 deselected in 1.26s =======================
```


prs.title: feat(console): support runtime base-path deployment
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8714.

Related context only: #1853, #8177, and #8316. This PR does not reopen, comment on, or close those older issues or pull requests.

Add an optional `QWENPAW_BASE_PATH` runtime setting for serving the standard prebuilt Console and API below a reverse-proxy prefix such as `/app/qwenpaw/web`.

#8316 covers custom builds through `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME`. This PR covers the complementary runtime case: pip/uv/Docker users should not need to rebuild the Console or have a proxy rewrite minified JavaScript. Uvicorn `root_path` alone cannot solve the absolute URLs already present in that prebuilt output.

### What changed

- Add a validated base-path ASGI middleware using standard `root_path` semantics for HTTP, mounted static files, and WebSockets. The bare prefix redirects to a trailing slash; requests outside the prefix return 404.
- Inject only two explicit deployment values into `index.html`: its `<base href>` and a JSON-encoded runtime prefix. JavaScript and CSS response bodies are not rewritten.
- Build default Console entry and module URLs relative to the document base; resolve public assets, API calls, router/login navigation, and chunk-readiness probes against the same runtime prefix.
- Preserve the existing root and `/console` behavior when the setting is empty or `/`. Existing build-time `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME` and desktop behavior remain separate.
- Document runtime proxy configuration in English and Chinese. Proxies must preserve rather than strip the configured prefix.

The current login flow uses a Bearer token in `localStorage`, so no authentication-cookie path change is needed.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

### Components affected

- [x] Console

prs.title: fix(sandbox): never write a sandbox ACE on a volume root
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows, sandbox ACLs are **inheritable** and are written on the
workspace, on every mount (including the session project directory, which
is mounted writable) and on every deny path. A volume root has no parent,
so writing one there re-propagates it to every existing child of the
volume. When the root DACL is missing (a NULL DACL) it gets replaced with
a sandbox-only DACL, and SYSTEM / Administrators / the user vanish from
the subtree — the drive becomes inaccessible even to an elevated
Administrator, and the sandbox-only ACE has to be removed by hand.

This closes every path that could create that state:

1. **A volume root is never a sandbox grant root** — `SandboxConfig`
   collects them (`volume_root_paths`) across `workspace_dir`, any mount
   (read-only mounts get an inheritable ACE too) and any `deny_paths`
   entry, and warns. `create_sandbox` then downgrades such a config to
   `SandboxMode.NONE` and logs a warning, so **the command still runs**
   while the volume stays usable. One check covers the AppContainer,
   elevated and unelevated backends.
2. **Never fill a NULL DACL** — `_set_path_ace` and `_add_traverse_ace`
   refuse instead of letting `SetEntriesInAclW` produce a DACL that holds
   only the sandbox SID.
3. **Never rewrite a volume root's DACL** — both DACL-reset fallbacks
   (`icacls /reset` in the elevated backend and
   `_reset_dacl_to_inherited` in the unelevated one) skip volume roots.
4. **A second guard in `_set_path_ace`** — it is the single point where
   sandbox ACEs are written (the AppContainer and elevated backends both
   delegate to it), so no caller can reintroduce the write.

The console warns before the user picks such a directory
(`ProjectSelectModal`), so the loss of the sandbox is not silent.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7943

**Security Considerations:** This tightens, rather than loosens, the
sandbox — no auth or config surface is added. Two judgement calls worth
flagging:

- **Fail-open on the volume root.** The sandbox is *skipped* rather than
  the session failing, because the reporter's expected behaviour is
  "command runs in the host / volume stays usable". That means a
  volume-root workspace runs **unsandboxed**; the backend logs a warning
  and the console asks the user first. If you would rather refuse
  outright (fail-closed), it is a two-line change — happy to switch.
- **The volume-root check is platform-independent**, so a POSIX
  `workspace_dir` of `/` also falls back. The ACL hazard is Windows-only,
  but "a volume root is not a usable workspace" holds everywhere. Happy
  to scope it to Windows if you prefer.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

No real reproduction is included on purpose: reproducing the original
report means locking a drive. The guards are covered by unit tests that
mock the Win32 layer, and each guard is proven to bite by reverting it
(see Evidence).

```bash
# backend
pytest tests/unit/sandbox tests/unit/governance \
    tests/integration/test_sandbox_module.py -q
# 573 passed, 26 skipped

# console
cd console && npm run test:run
# 472 files / 4778 tests passed
```

## Evidence

**Backend — `tests/unit/sandbox` (Python 3.12, Windows):**

```bash
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/sandbox -q
258 passed, 23 skipped in 2.22s
```

**Backend — wider run (sandbox + governance + sandbox integration):**

```bash
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/sandbox tests/unit/governance \
    tests/integration/test_sandbox_module.py -q
573 passed, 26 skipped in 11.72s
```

prs.title: fix(security): guard inline Office COM automation before unsandboxed fallback
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows, with approval level `auto` and the security sandbox off, an
agent-authored inline Office COM command is executed instead of denied. The
Office COM servers (`PowerPoint.Application`, `Excel.Application`,
`Word.Application`, `Outlook.Application`) are single-instance, so `Quit()`
on an inline-constructed object terminates the user's already-open app.

The command matched no signature in `dangerous_shell_commands.yaml`, was
classified `SANDBOX_FALLBACK` by `GovernancePolicy.evaluate`, and — with the
sandbox off — was rewritten to `ALLOW` by `ResourceGovernor`
("running unsandboxed"), so it ran silently.

This PR adds a CRITICAL detection rule (`TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION`)
covering the inline-construction verbs against the four Office ProgIDs:

- `New-Object -ComObject <App>.Application` (PowerShell)
- `GetActiveObject(...)` / `[Marshal]::GetActiveObject(...)`
- `CreateObject(...)`
- `win32com.client.Dispatch` / `DispatchEx(...)`
- `[Type]::GetTypeFromProgID(...)` (used by `[activator]::CreateInstance`)
- `Activator` + `CreateInstance`

The CRITICAL finding surfaces in Phase 1, so the call is held for approval
*before* the unsandboxed fallback, instead of running silently.

**Related Issue:** Refs #8002

**Security Considerations:** Local impact only — a shell command the agent is
already allowed to run can no longer silently close the user's Office
process. Ordinary shell commands are unaffected.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` locally and it passes
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest`) and they pass
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

The new rule is matched through the real loader
(`load_rules_from_yaml` → `RuleBasedToolGuardian`) and through
`GovernancePolicy.evaluate`, not by re-declaring the patterns in the test.

Verified behaviour with a default policy (`execution_level` = smart / auto):

| command | decision | finding |
|---|---|---|
| `New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application` | ASK | `TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` |
| `win32com.client.Dispatch('Word.Application').Quit()` | ASK | `TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` |
| `echo hello` | SANDBOX_FALLBACK (unchanged) | — |

`ASK` maps to the approval card, so in `auto` + sandbox-off the command is
now held for the user instead of closing their PowerPoint.

## Evidence

```bash
$ pre-commit run --files \
    src/qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/rules/dangerous_shell_commands.yaml \
    tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_office_com_rule.py
check python ast.........................................................Passed
check yaml...............................................................Passed
check docstring is first.................................................Passed
detect private key.......................................................Passed
trim trailing whitespace.................................................Passed
Add trailing commas......................................................Passed
mypy.....................................................................Passed
black....................................................................Passed
flake8...................................................................Passed
pylint...................................................................Passed

$ pytest tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_office_com_rule.py -q
41 passed

$ pytest tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_office_com_rule.py \
         tests/unit/governance/test_policy.py -q
141 passed
```

## Additional Notes

Approval (`ASK`) rather than a hard `DENY` is deliberate. Per
`policy.py`, severity alone does not hard-deny — only rule IDs listed in
`resolve_auto_denied_rules()` do (default:
`SAFETY_CHECKS_DESTRUCTIVE_COMMAND`). `ASK` is the right outcome here
because legitimate COM automation that drives a *private* instance should
remain approvable, while an accidental `Quit()` on the user's open app can
no longer slip through. If a hard deny is preferred, adding
`TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` to the default auto-denied set is a
one-line follow-up — happy to do it if that's the intended policy.

prs.title: fix(shell): report a resource-protection termination instead of an ERROR chunk
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A command terminated by resource protection does return a complete result:
`Command failed with exit code 15` plus `[resource protection] Shell memory
limit exceeded (RSS …)`. But `_with_shell_guard` then overrode the result state
with `ERROR`, and `agents/middlewares.py` documents what that means:

> The coordinator stops driving this generator as soon as it sees an
> ERROR/INTERRUPTED ToolChunk (no ToolResponse follows), so the terminal chunk
> itself is the only record of how the call ended.

So the reason stayed in the terminal chunk and never became a tool response.
The model was left with an empty result for a call that had actually run, and
repeated it — governance approved the identical `Bash` call 14 times in 70
seconds, and the user had to press stop twice.

Fixes #8712.

## Scope

Type: A (single-point fix) — one branch in `_with_shell_guard` and the
assertion that pinned the old state.

## Evidence

Before / after, same probe with `QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=96` and a 300 MB
process:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| result state | `ERROR` | `SUCCESS` |
| content | `Command failed with exit code 15` + `[resource protection] …` | unchanged |
| model sees it | no — ERROR chunk produces no ToolResponse | yes — normal tool response |

This is what the same tool already does for every other failure: a non-zero
exit code and a timeout both return `SUCCESS` with the exit code in the text.
The change only aligns the terminated case with them; a terminated command is a
completed call, not a broken tool.

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/unit/agents/tools/test_shell_resources.py` — **11 passed, 4 skipped** (real process killing, skipped only where the platform does not support it).
- Red/green: with the `shell.py` change stashed the same file gives **4 failed** (memory and output limits, sandboxed and not), and **11 passed** once restored.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents/tools` — **969 passed, 17 skipped**.
- Lint: `pre-commit run --files` — all hooks passed (black 23.3.0, mypy, pylint, flake8, add-trailing-comma, docstring-first, AST, private-key, encoding-pragma, trailing-whitespace).

issues.title: [Bug]: the Seatbelt profile's "user home dotfiles" read rule is mis-escaped (`\\.`), so toolchains and configs under `~/.cargo`, `~/.nvm`, `~/.pyenv`, `~/.local` fail with "Operation not permitted" under the default macOS sandbox; the fix must not hand the sandbox `~/.ssh`
